body: Without hub diagonal, 2 X_h (L + beta) + 2 eps L P = 2 (L + beta)(X_h + eps P) - 2 eps beta P, so Y = X_h + eps P is a hub whose conditional density given the light coordinates is at most 1 and depends on them only through P. For Q = 2 Y (L + beta) + lambda (V - v_c(L, P))^2 + F(L, P) with such a hub, L, V, P orthonormal projections of independent coordinates with densities at most 1, t = l + beta, c = 2 sqrt 2 |lambda|^{-1/2} and a(l, p) = sup_v rho_{L,V,P}(l, v, p): ||p_Q||_inf <= 1/2 + int int_{|t| <= 1} min(rho_{L,P}(l, p), c a(l, p) |t|^{1/2}) dl dp/(2|t|). Proof: given X' the form is affine in Y; for fixed (l, p) the bathtub step of Proposition S bounds int f(y|p) dv/(2|t|) by sqrt 2 (|lambda| |t|)^{-1/2}; |t| > 1 contributes at most 1/2. Windowed corollary: 1/2 + int r(p)(2 + 2 log_+(c a(p)/r(p))) dp with r, a the suprema over |l + beta| <= 1. This covers the single hub with no hub or light diagonal and linear terms in span(w, v, q^), uniformly in eps. The windowed form is NOT bounded under the (0.1) leverage condition alone: w = (e1+e2)/sqrt2, q^ = (e1-e2)/sqrt2, v = (e3+e4)/sqrt2 and two combs with incommensurate spacings of order N^{-1/2} give int r = 3.9, 7.5, 22.6, 83.7 at N = 64..4096, while the sharp form stays bounded (V independent of (L, P)) and Proposition 3.15 covers that configuration. Open: is the sharp form bounded uniformly under w_i^2 + v_i^2 + q^_i^2 <= 1/2? A yes settles the no-diagonal single hub for every eps.

[Lemma last two rows are equal of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have $p_{n-1,j}=p_{n,j}$ for all $1\leq j\leq n$.
    \begin{proof}
        We present a combinatorial argument. Card $n$ is drawn first and placed by itself. Now card $n-1$ goes on top, respectively on the bottom, of card $n$ with probability $1/2$. Hence, cards $n$ and $n-1$ move as a block in the shuffle with both orderings equally likely. Therefore, given a position, they are equally likely to end up there. One can also argue by computing the transition probabilities and using Pascal's identity and symmetry.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma last two rows are equal of arXiv:2507.10294

body:
[Lemma prob0 pure of arXiv:2604.20660, 'The Legendre structure of the TAP complexity\\ for the Ising spin glass'] Assume that $\xi$ is pure $p$-spin. Let $\varepsilon>0$. Let $u\in(0,1)$, $q\in(0,1)$, $f\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $\zeta\in \mathrm{Prefix}_2(u,q)$ where $\mathrm{Prefix}_2$ is as in Definition (def:nprefix of the paper).
		
		Let $\delta\in[\varepsilon,1)$ and $\mathbf{m}\in[-1+\delta,1-\delta]^N$. Suppose moreover that $q_\mathbf{m}\in (q-\varepsilon,q+\varepsilon)$ and
		$\mathrm{dist}\!\bigl(\zeta_\mathbf{m},\,\zeta|_{(q,1]}+\zeta([0,q])\,\delta_q\bigr)<\varepsilon$.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item  The gradient $\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})$ is a non-degenerate Gaussian vector in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Its log-density at $0$, tilted by
			\[
			u\!\left(\frac1p\langle \mathbf{m},k_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})\rangle-\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)-N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)-Nf\right),
			\]
			satisfies
			\begin{multline}
				\log \varphi_{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})}(0)
				+u\!\left(\frac1p\langle \mathbf{m},k_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})\rangle-\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)-N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)-Nf\right)
				\\
				=
				\frac{1}{2}N\xi(q)u^2
				-\frac{1}{2}N\xi''(q)\!\left(\int_q^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t\right)^{\!2}
				-\frac{1}{2\xi'(q)}
				\Vert \partial_m h_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})-u\xi'(q)\mathbf{m}\Vert^2
				\\
				-\frac{N}{2}\log(2\pi \xi'(q))
				+\frac{N(p-1)}{2p\,\xi'(q)\,q}
				\!\left(
				\frac{1}{N}\langle \partial_m h_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m}),\mathbf{m}\rangle
				-\xi'(q)\int_0^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t
				\right)^{\!2}
				\\
				-u\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)+N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)+Nf\right)
				+O\!\left(N\frac{\varepsilon}{\delta}\right).
			\end{multline}
			
			\item  Suppose moreover that
			\begin{equation}
				\langle \partial_m h_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m}),\mathbf{m}\rangle
				=
				N\xi'(q)\int_0^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t+O(N\varepsilon)
			\end{equation}
			and
			\begin{equation}
				\sum_{i=1}^N\bigl(h_\zeta(q,m_i)-\partial_m h_\zeta(q,m_i)m_i\bigr)
				+N\int_0^q t\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t
				+\frac{N}{2}\int_q^1 t\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t
				=
				-Nf+O(N\varepsilon).
			\end{equation}
			Then the squared term in (equation eq:pure-prob0-main of the paper) is $O(N\varepsilon)$, so that 
			\begin{multline}
				\log \varphi_{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})}(0)
				+u\!\left(\frac1p\langle \mathbf{m},k_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})\rangle-\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)-N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)-Nf\right)
				\\
				=
				\frac{1}{2}N\xi(q)u^2
				-\frac{1}{2}N\xi''(q)\!\left(\int_q^1 \zeta([0,t])\,\mathrm{d} t\right)^{\!2}
				-\frac{1}{2\xi'(q)}
				\Vert \partial_m h_\zeta(q,\mathbf{m})-u\xi'(q)\mathbf{m}\Vert^2
				\\
				-\frac{N}{2}\log(2\pi \xi'(q))
				-u\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^N h_\zeta(q,m_i)+N\mathcal U_\zeta(q)+Nf\right)
				+O\!\left(N\frac{\varepsilon}{\delta}\right),
			\end{multline}
			and, on the event $\{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=0\}$,
			\begin{equation}
				F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=Nf+O\!\left(N\frac{\varepsilon}{\delta}\right).
			\end{equation}
		\end{enumerate}

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked; reduction plus asserted conditional, not a solution] Svante Janson's Problem 18.39 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510, asks whether Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability is possible in the condensation regime 0 < nu < lambda. Janson conjectures that it is not possible for the full sequence and, more strongly, that there are always epsilon > 0 and a subsequence along which Y_(1) >= epsilon n w.h.p. (Example 18.36 gives Y_(1)/n -> 0 in probability along a subsequence.) Setting: let w_k >= 0 with w_0 > 0, let Phi(z) = sum_k w_k z^k have radius rho in (0,infinity) with Phi(rho) < infinity, and put pi_k = w_k rho^k/Phi(rho), a law with generating-function radius one and finite mean nu > 0. Let m_n/n -> lambda > nu. (Y_1,...,Y_n) is n i.i.d. pi variables conditioned on sum m_n, Y_(1) = max_i Y_i, and M = (lambda-nu)n. Heuristic rate: carrying M in r = M/a boxes of size a has class weight binomial(n,r) pi_a^r up to the bulk's fluctuation, giving log P = M Lambda(a) + o(M) with Lambda(a) = [log pi_a + log(a/(lambda-nu)) + 1]/a. For pi_k ~ c k^(-beta) and for pi_a = exp(-a^gamma), 0<gamma<1, Lambda increases on large a, so the optimum is a = M (one box), matching the known condensation picture. Since limsup_a Lambda(a) = 0 and Lambda < 0 for large a, Lambda has infinitely many upper records a_1 < a_2 < ... (Lambda(a_j) > Lambda(a) for all a < a_j). The record asserts, as author-checked and with no proof given beyond reference to an analogous step for Problem 18.40 in a companion memo, the following Proposition: if for some epsilon > 0 and every C, along infinitely many records, Lambda(a_j) - max_{a <= epsilon a_j} Lambda(a) > C a_j^(-1/2), then along n_j = a_j/(lambda-nu), P(Y_(1) >= ((lambda-nu)/2) n_j) -> 1, so the conjecture holds. Caveat: the only derivation offered is the heuristic rate with an o(M) error, which is coarser than the order sqrt(a_j) resolution this hypothesis requires, so the record does not establish the Proposition. The record poses the open Question whether, for every law pi on Z_{>=0} with radius one and finite mean, [log pi_a + log a]/a has infinitely many records with gap exceeding a_j^(-1/2) below max_{a <= epsilon a_j} for some fixed epsilon > 0. This is not a proved equivalence with the conjecture. A negative answer would only give a candidate counterexample, still requiring proof that the allocation spreads. The Question's normalisation and fixed threshold also differ from the Proposition's hypothesis. The problem remains open. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The allocations are defined along sizes with positive conditioning probability.
0 < nu < lambda and the boundary-tilted law pi has generating-function radius one.

body: [Lemma lem:star-recoloring of arXiv:2609.02845, 'Degeneracy bounds, stability, and a sharp gap for $B$-colorings'] Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $u\in V(G)$, and let $\mathcal C$ be a set of colors.  Suppose that $\varphi$ is a $B$-coloring of $G-S_u$ with colors from $\mathcal C$.  For each $x\in N_G(u)$, let $L_x\subseteq\mathcal C$ be the set of colors not used on any old conflict edge for $ux$. If the family $\{L_x\colon x\in N_G(u)\}$ admits a system of distinct representatives, then $\varphi$ extends to a $B$-coloring of $G$ with colors from $\mathcal C$.

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2603.13798, 'Iterated Graph Systems (I): random walks and diffusion limits'] $\Psi:\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^K\to \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^K$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{(Monotonicity).}
If $\mathbf x\le \mathbf y$ coordinatewise, then
$
\Psi(\mathbf x)\le \Psi(\mathbf y).
$

\item \textbf{(Homogeneity).}
For all $t\ge 0$,
$
\Psi(t\mathbf x)=t\Psi(\mathbf x).
$

\item \textbf{(Continuity).}
The map $\mathbf x\mapsto \Psi(\mathbf x)$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)^K$.
Moreover, for $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^K$ the limit
$
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow 0}\Psi(\mathbf x+\varepsilon\mathbf 1)
$
exists and defines an extension of $\Psi$ to $\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^K$.

\item \textbf{(Concavity).}
For all $\lambda\in[0,1]$ and all $\mathbf x,\mathbf y\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^K$,
\[
\Psi(\lambda\mathbf x+(1-\lambda)\mathbf y)
\ge
\lambda \Psi(\mathbf x)+(1-\lambda)\Psi(\mathbf y).
\]

\item \textbf{(Superadditivity).}
For all $\mathbf x,\mathbf y\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0}^K$,
$
\Psi(\mathbf x+\mathbf y)\ge \Psi(\mathbf x)+\Psi(\mathbf y).
$
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.21597, 'Random Hazard Forests'] \emph{
The RHF split statistic for splitting a node $A_j$ into regions
$A_{j,1}$ and $A_{j,2}$ is
\Eq
S(A_{j,1},A_{j,2})
=
V_{j,1}\log\!\left(\frac{V_{j,1}}{U_{j,1}}\right)
+
V_{j,2}\log\!\left(\frac{V_{j,2}}{U_{j,2}}\right),

\EndEq
and the associated empirical risk reduction is
\Eq
\D_n(A_{j,1},A_{j,2})
=
V_{j,1}\log\!\left(\frac{V_{j,1}}{U_{j,1}}\right)
+
V_{j,2}\log\!\left(\frac{V_{j,2}}{U_{j,2}}\right)
-
(V_{j,1}+V_{j,2})\log\!\left(\frac{V_{j,1}+V_{j,2}}{U_{j,1}+U_{j,2}}\right).

\EndEq
If $R_n(F_s)$ is the empirical risk for the current working log hazard
and $R_n(F_{s+1})$ is the risk after the split, then
$R_n(F_{s+1})=R_n(F_s)-\D_n(A_{j,1},A_{j,2})$.}
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.21597

[Lemma lemma_catenarycase1_primary of arXiv:2609.04000, 'The type and cardinality of minimal presentations of \\ numerical semigroups with embeddin'] Suppose that $S$ is primary. Consider $(-\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3) \in V$ satisfying
    $$ \lambda_0d_0 + \lambda_1d_1 = \lambda_2d_2 + \lambda_3d_3$$
    with $\lambda_i \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, and $ \lambda_0 \geq a_{00}$ or $ \lambda_1 \geq a_{11}$. If $a_{00}d_0 \neq a_{11}d_1$, then $\lambda_0d_0 + \lambda_1d_1 \notin \textup{Betti}(S)$. Otherwise, if $a_{00}d_0 = a_{11}d_1$, then $\lambda_0d_0 + \lambda_1d_1 \in \textup{Betti}(S)$ and $\varphi^{-1}(\lambda_0d_0 + \lambda_1d_1) = \mathcal{F} \cup \{(0,0,\lambda_2,\lambda_3)\}$, where 
    $$\mathcal{F} =   \{(\lambda_0 + \lambda a_{00},\lambda_1 - \lambda a_{11},0,0) \mid \lambda \in \mathbb{Z}, \lambda_0 + \lambda a_{00} \geq 0, \lambda_1 - \lambda a_{11} \geq 0 \}. $$ 
    An analogous statement holds for $(\lambda_1,-\lambda_2,\lambda_3)$ and $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,-\lambda_3) \in V$.

body:
[Lemma 3 (Regeneration at a level) of arXiv:2608.10992, '2608.10992'] Suppose that the $t$-avalanche has finite range $I$. Conditionally on
$\mathcal H_t$, its terminal fitnesses are independent and have the form
\[
        F_x=t+E_x,\qquad x\in I,
\]
where the $E_x$ are independent $\operatorname{Exp}(1)$ variables,
independent of $\mathcal H_t$. Consequently, when the threshold is raised
above $t$, the next triggering level occurs at rate $|I|$, its location is
uniform on $I$, and the subavalanche attached there is independent of
$\mathcal H_t$ and has the law of an avalanche at the triggering level.

[Theorem thm:OGP of arXiv:2605.10911, 'The stochastic block model has the overlap graph property for modularity'] [\bf Modularity has OGP] 
Fix real numbers $a>b>0$, and integer $k\geq 3$.
For any $\nu\in \left(\frac{1}{2(k-1)}, \frac{1}{k}\right)$ and {$\varepsilon>0$}, there exist $\mu = \mu(\nu)$ and $c=c(\varepsilon)$ such that the following holds for $n$ large enough.

Let $p=p(n)=\omega\; a / n$ and $q=q(n)=\omega \; b/n$ be such that $\omega>c$, and let $G \in \mathcal{G}(n,k,p,q)$ with planted partition $\mathcal{P}$. Then with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$, for every $k$-part partition $\mathcal{A}$ with 
\begin{equation}

q_\mathcal{A}(G) \ge \frac {a-b}{a+(k-1)b} \left( 1 - \frac {1}{k} - \frac {2}{k^2} \right) - \mu,
\end{equation} 
either $d(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{P}) \le \frac {{1}}{2(k-1)}$ or $d(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{P}) \ge \nu$.
Moreover, there are partitions $\mathcal{A}$ satisfying the latter. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemm l:conditional-variance-variational of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $X$ be a square-integrable random variable and let $Y$ be a random $d$-dimensional vector on the same probability space, for some $d\in\mathbb{N}$.
    Then
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}[\Var(X|Y)]
        = \mathbb{E}[(X-\mathbb{E}[X|Y])^2]
        = \inf_f \mathbb{E}[(X-f(Y))^2],
    \end{align*}
    where the infimum is over all measurable functions $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(Y)$ is square-integrable. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemm l:conditional-variance-variational of arXiv:2607.18194

[Definition 24 (Polyhedrally sofic THP) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] A unimodular random rooted infinite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedron
\((P,f)\) is called \emph{polyhedrally sofic} if there exists a
sequence of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra \(P_n\), with
\[
    |F(P_n)|\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
such that, after choosing \(f_n\) uniformly from \(F(P_n)\), the finite rooted marked dual triangulation of $P_n$ satisfy
\[
    \bigl(G(P_n),\rho_n,\Theta_{P_n}\bigr)
    \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}
    \bigl(G(P),\rho,\Theta_P\bigr)
\]
in the local topology of rooted marked graphs.

Equivalently, \((P,f)\) is polyhedrally sofic if its ADT is a Benjamini--Schramm limit of the finite rooted marked dual triangulations of uniformly
face-rooted finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra.
title: Polyhedrally sofic THP

Consequently, if $\lambda_n\to\lambda$, there is a constant $B\ge1$ such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and all integers \(u\ge0\),
\[
        \Pbb(E_n=u)u!p^u\le B^u.
\]

body:
[Proposition 40 (Gaussian concentration implies quantitative blowing-up, \cite{CMRU}) of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] \leavevmode\\
Let $Y$ be an ergodic random field with law $\nu$, and assume $Y$ satisfies the Gaussian concentration bound \eqref{def-GCB} with constant $C$. Then $Y$ has the blowing-up property. More precisely, for any 
$\Lambda\Subset\Z^d$ and any $E\subseteq B^\Lambda$ with $\nu(E)>0$,
\begin{equation}
\nu([E]_\varepsilon)\ \ge\ 1-\exp\!\left[-\,\frac{|\Lambda|}{2C}\left(\,\varepsilon-\sqrt{\frac{2C}{|\Lambda|}\,\log\frac{1}{\nu(E)}}\,\right)^{\!2}\,\right],
\end{equation}
whenever $\displaystyle \varepsilon>\sqrt{\frac{2C}{|\Lambda|}\,\log\frac{1}{\nu(E)}}$\,. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Gaussian concentration implies quantitative blowing-up, \cite{CMRU}

body: Publication record. Problem 11 of N. N. Ganikhodzhaev and U. A. Rozikov, Quadratic stochastic operators: results and open problems (2009), asks whether their Theorem 6 (a strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on three types has a unique fixed point, and it is not attractive) extends to more types. Y. Shmalo, Fixed points of strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators in four or more types (September 2026) shows that it does not extend to four or more types; uniqueness at four types is left open and reduced to one determinant inequality by an index count. Here G_f(mr, r, p, q) (Definition 1) has mr vertices in r clusters of exactly m vertices each; two vertices of the same cluster are joined with weight p, any other two with weight q < p; and a^(l)_ij is the (i, j) entry of A^l, the l-th-order proximity matrix of the (weighted) adjacency matrix A.

\[
\theta_n=\frac{\alpha+1}{\alpha+2}\varepsilon+o(\varepsilon),
\]
and
\[
\phi_n''(\theta_n)=\frac{\alpha+2}{\alpha+1}+o(1).
\]
For \(T_n\) defined in (equation equ-def-tn of the paper), we have
\[
T_n=(1+o(1))\,C_\alpha\,\varepsilon^{-2}\log(\varepsilon^3 n),
\qquad
\frac{\theta_n\ell(d_n)}{T_n}\to\infty.
\]

body:
[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] Suppose there exists a function $g: E \to [0,\infty)$ such that for all $f \in \Fc$, there exists a constant $a_f \in \R_+$ s.t. $|f| \leq a_f g$. In addition, all functions in $\Fc$ are continuous, or $\Fc$ is at most countable. Assume further $\gamma^*$ is the optimizer of the constrained problem:
$$
\min_{\gamma \in \Pi_{\Fc}} \int c d \gamma =  \int c d \gamma^* \in \R.
$$
Then $\gamma^*$ is $c$-monotone.

body:
[Theorem lucesec of arXiv:2605.10452, 'A secretary for Messrs. Luce and Mallows'] Consider the secretary problem for a
$P_n^{\mathcal{L}_\text{inv};\{\theta_j\}_{j=1}^n}$-type Luce
  distribution in the case that the smallest number is of highest rank.
For  $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
\begin{equation}
P_n^{\mathcal{L}_\text{inv};\{\theta_j\}_{j=1}^n}(\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M))=
\begin{cases}\frac{\sum_{i=1}^M\theta_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n\theta_i}\sum_{j=M+1}^n
\frac{\theta_j}{\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}\theta_i},\ M\in\{1,\cdots, n-1\};\\
\frac{\theta_1}{\sum_{i=1}^n\theta_i},\ M=0.\end{cases}

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem lucesec of arXiv:2605.10452

Fix $\eps\in (0,\gamma)$. Consider observing the graph $\bC^{(3)}_{\alpha,\delta,\eps}(1)$ without vertex labels, and fix $\varepsilon>0$. It is possible to construct a confidence set $K=K(\varepsilon)\subset V\left(\bC^{(3)}_{\alpha,\delta,\eps}(1)\right)$ not depending on $n$ such that 
    \begin{align*}
        \Prob{1\in K(\varepsilon)}>1-\varepsilon.
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem colour_position_symmetry_step of arXiv:2412.03370, 'TASEP with a general initial condition and a deterministically moving wall'] Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, $\{Z_n\}_{n \in I} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and let $(x^{\textup{step},Z_n}(t),t\geq 0), n \in I,$ be coupled by basic coupling. 	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary cor:finite-profile-transfer of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $H\geq1$ and $k\geq2$, and let $G$ be a nontrivial torsion-free abelian
group.  The following four collections of truncated profiles are identical:
\[
 \bigl\{(|jA|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:A\subset G,\ |A|=k\bigr\},
 \quad
 \bigl\{(|jB|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:B\subset\mathbb Z,\ |B|=k\bigr\},
\]
\[
 \bigl\{(|P^{\times j}|)_{1\leq j\leq H}:
       P\subset\mathbb Z_{>0},\ |P|=k\bigr\},
 \quad
 \bigl\{(H_{C_B}(j))_{1\leq j\leq H}:
       B\subset\mathbb Z,\ |B|=k\bigr\},
\]
where $P^{\times j}$ is the $j$-fold product set and $C_B$ is the projective
monomial curve attached to $B$ over an arbitrary field.  More strongly,
equip the subgroup generated by an additive realization with a
translation-invariant linear order.  Its complete equality-and-order table
through degree $H$ then has an integer exponent representative.  The
resulting sumset, product-set, and monomial-curve exponent models have
identical ordered tables, active ranks, and relation-birth degrees through
$H$.

Every such table has a primitive integer representative
$B=\{0=b_0<\cdots<b_{k-1}\}$ with
\begin{equation}
 b_{k-1}\leq dH^{d-1}\prod_{i=1}^r p_i
 \leq(k-1-r)H^{k-2},
 \qquad d=k-1-r,
\end{equation}
where $r$ and $p_i$ are its active rank and birth degrees through $H$.
The universal exponent $k-2$ for preserving the complete truncated table is
best possible.

body:
[Proposition tightness condition of arXiv:2411.15485, '\bf\Large Stochastic Volterra Equations for Local Times of Spectrally Positive L\'evy Proc'] For a sequence of c\`adl\`ag stochastic processes $\{X^{(n)}\}_{n\geq 1}$ defined on a common probability space with $\sup_{n \geq 1}  \mathbf{E} \big[|X^{(n)}(0)|^q\big] < \infty$ for some $q>0$, it is $C$-tight if the following two conditions hold for any $T\geq 0$ and some constant $\beta>2$.
 \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(1)] 
  There exist some constants $C>0 $, $p\geq 1$ and $\rho,\alpha>0$ such that for any $\delta\in(0,1)$ and $n\geq 1$,
  \begin{eqnarray*}
   \sup_{t\in[0,T]} \mathbf{E}\Big[\big| X^{(n)}(t+\delta)-X^{(n)}(t)\big|^{p}\Big] 
   \leq C\cdot \Big(  \delta^{1+\rho}+ \frac{\delta}{n^\alpha}\Big).
  \end{eqnarray*}
 		
  \item[(2)] 
  $\displaystyle\sup_{k=0,1,\cdots,[Tn^\beta]} \sup_{\delta\in[0,1/n^{\beta}]} \big|  X^{(n)}(k/n^\beta+\delta) -X^{(n)}(k/n^\beta)\big|  \overset{\rm p}\to 0$  as $n\to\infty$. 
 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary c1 of arXiv:2411.19433, 'Singular mean-field backward stochastic Volterra integral equations in infinite dimensiona'] Let condition $(A_{2})$ satisfy. Then, for every \( \Psi(\cdot) \in L^2_{\mathcal{F}_{b}}(r, \delta; H) \), the stochastic Fredholm-type integral equation (equation 3.6 of the paper) admits a unique adapted solution

\[
(\Psi_{\delta}(\cdot), \aleph(\cdot, \cdot)) \in L^2_{\mathcal{F}_{\delta}}(r, \delta; H) \times L^2(r, \delta; L^2_{\mathcal{F}}(\delta, b; L_0^2)).
\]

The second special case of (equation f3.4 of the paper) is as follows: Let \( r = \delta \), and define

\[
X(t) := \lambda(t, t), \quad t \in [\delta, b], \quad \aleph(t, s) := \mu(t, s), \quad (t, s) \in [\delta, b]^2.
\]

Then equation (equation f3.4 of the paper) becomes

\begin{align}
X(t) = \Psi(t) + \int_t^b \eta(t, s, \aleph(t, s), \mathbb{E}[\aleph(t, s)]) \, ds - \int_t^b \aleph(t, s) \, dB_{s}, \quad t \in [\delta, b].
\end{align}

This is a specific case of a singular MF-BSVIE (equation r3 of the paper), where the generator \( \eta \) is independent of \( X(s) \) and \( \aleph(s, t) \). We can define \( \aleph(t, s) \) for \( (t, s) \in [\delta, b]^2 \) by using the martingale representation theorem:

\[
X(t) = \mathbb{E}[X(t) | \mathcal{F}_{\delta}] + \int_{\delta}^t \aleph(t, s) \, dB_{s}, \quad t \in [\delta, b].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Cor universal-p-comparison of arXiv:2609.03856, 'Consensus time for asynchronous $\ell^p$ relaxation: graph dependence'] For every finite connected graph, every $2\le p<\infty$, and every
$0<\varepsilon\le1/2$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathsf T_p(G,\varepsilon)
  \le C_p\log\!\left(\frac{en}{\varepsilon}\right)
          \mathsf T_2(G,\varepsilon).
  
\end{equation}
Thus the worst-profile $p$-consensus time on every graph is at most the
quadratic worst-profile time times one logarithm and a $p$-dependent
constant.

body: Consider an autonomous C^1 planar vector field dx/dt = f(x) on an open subset of R^2, and a forward trajectory that stays inside a compact set for all t >= 0. The Poincare-Bendixson theorem states that its omega-limit set is nonempty, compact, connected, and is either a fixed point, a periodic orbit, or a union of finitely many fixed points joined by homoclinic or heteroclinic orbits; in particular, if the omega-limit set contains no fixed point, it is a single periodic orbit. The result is specific to the plane and fails for flows in dimension 3 or higher. Due to Henri Poincare and Ivar Bendixson.
title: Poincare-Bendixson theorem

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let Condition $\sH_\sigma^g$ holds.
		
			(i) For any $f$ in $L_{p}(\mR^d)$ with $1\leq p\leq p'\leq \infty$, the following inequality holds for all $r<t\leq 1$
		\be 
		\|T_{r,t}f\|_{p'}\leq N(t-r)^{\frac{d}{2p'}-\frac{d}{2p}}\|f\|_{p},
		\ee 
		where $N$ depends only on $d, p, p',c_0, C_1$.
		
	(ii) For any $f$ in $L_{p}(\mR^d)$, where $p,p'\in (d/\beta\vee 1,\infty]$and $p\leq p'$, the following estimate holds for all $0\leq r<t\leq 1$
		\be 
		\|{F_{r,t}^nf}\|_{p'}\leq N\|f\|_{p}[(t-r_n)^{\frac{\alpha}{2}-1 +\frac{d}{2p}-\frac{d}{2p'}}+(t-r_n)^{-\frac{\beta}{2}+\frac{d}{2p'}-\frac{d}{2p}}],
		\ee
		where $N$ is a constant that depends exclusively on the dimensions  $d$, the exponents $p, p'$, and the constants $c_0, C_1$ associated with Condition $\sH_\sigma^g$.

body:
[Theorem Main result of arXiv:2604.09509, 'An Improved Bipartition Cover Bound for the Multispecies Coalescent Model'] For $\ell\geqslant 2$, let $p_\ell(T)$ denote the probability that the lineages descending 
from a balanced $\ell$-taxon tree, with all branch lengths equal to $T$, coalesce to a single 
lineage. Then $n$ independently sampled gene trees form a bipartition cover with probability at least $q$ whenever
\[
    \sum_{\ell=2}^{k-2}\bigl(1-p_\ell(T_{\min})\bigr)^n\leqslant 1-q.
\]
In particular, it suffices that
\[
    n\geqslant
    \frac{\log\!\left(\frac{k-3}{1-q}\right)}
         {-\log\!\left(1-p_{k-2}(T_{\min})\right)}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main result

body:
[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2605.09459, 'Multipoint connectivity in the branching interlacement process'] Let $n \leq 5$. Let $X^{(1)},\dots,X^{(n)}$ be $n$ independent random walks indexed by infinite critical trees starting respectively from $x_1, \dots, x_n$. Let $\sigma_u, \sigma_u^{(1)},\dots,\sigma_u^{(n)}$ be $n+1$ independent interlacements with law $\mathrm{Poi}(u,W^*)$ and independent from $X^{(1)},\dots,X^{(n)}$. For $1 \leq i \leq n$, denote by $(A_i^{(j)})_{j\geq 1}$ the visible sets associated to $X^{(i)}$ and constructed with the interlacement $\sigma_u^{(i)}$. There exist constants $c > 0$, $R_0 < \infty$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, such that, for any $r > \max(\|x_1\|,\dots,\|x_n\|)$ and $R > R_0$, satisfying $r^{d-4} \leq \varepsilon R$, we have
  \[
    \P\left(\exists\,\gamma \in \mathrm{Supp}(\sigma^u_{r,R}) : \gamma \text{ connects } A_1^{(k_1)}(r,R), \dots, A_{n-1}^{(k_{n-1})}(r,R) \text{ and } A_n^{(1)}(r,R)\right) \geq c.
  \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 32 of arXiv:2605.09459

[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2608.27433, 'Scalar curvature on K\"ahler blow-ups and systolic inequalities'] Let \(F^r\) be a smooth rationally connected manifold, and let \(\alpha\in\mathcal K(F)\) be a K\"ahler class.  Define
\[
        m_F(\alpha)
        :=
        \inf\{\alpha\cdot C\mid C\subset F\text{ a rational curve}\}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
        m_F(\alpha)
        \frac{c_1(F)\cdot\alpha^{r-1}}{\alpha^r}
        \le
        r+1.
\end{equation}
Moreover, equality in \eqref{eq:mori-length-final} holds if and only if \(F\cong\mathbb P^r\).

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] [\textbf{Convergence of the Dynkin martingale}]
Let $H \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$. The sequence of martingales $\big\{ \big(  \mathcal{M}_t^n(H)  \big)_{0 \leq t \leq T}, \; n \in \mathbb{N}_+\big\}$ converges with respect to the Skorohod topology of $\mathcal{D}([0, T], \mathbb{R})$ to a mean zero Gaussian process $\mathcal{M}(H)$, as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Furthermore, $\mathcal{M}(H)$ is a continuous martingale on $[0, T]$ whose quadratic variation is $\langle \mathcal{M}(H) \rangle_t = t D_3 \mathcal{P}^{ \gamma} H$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 11 of arXiv:2604.03777

[Theorem 1 (Pfaffian identity for the representation defect) of arXiv:2609.03238, 'Representation Defects and Cassels Pairings for Congruent Number Curves'] Let $n$ be a positive squarefree integer and suppose that $s_2(n)$ is even.  For any
basis $\mathcal B$ of $\Sel_2'(E_n)$, let $C_{\mathcal B}(E_n)$ be the Gram matrix of
the Cassels pairing.  Then
\[
2\sigma_Q(n)2^{s_2(n)/2}\mid \Delta_Q(n)
\]
and
\begin{equation}
\mathcal D_Q(n)=\Pf\bigl(C_{\mathcal B}(E_n)\bigr)\in\F_2.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the two sides are equal to $1$ if and only if
\[
\rk E_n(\Q)=0,
\qquad
\Sha(E_n)[2^\infty]\cong(\Z/2\Z)^{s_2(n)}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition def:genbackoff of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a \emph{send sequence}  
$\overline{p}$, a non-negative integer~$\tau$, and 
a distribution~\newsym{D-cal-0}{birth distribution}{\mathcal{D}} on non-negative integers. 
Fix a (possibly random)
tuple $\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(\tau)$ of disjoint sets 
$\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(\tau) = (\mathbf{arr}^Z_{1}(\tau),\mathbf{arr}^Z_2(\tau),\ldots)$ where
each $\mathbf{arr}_i^Z(\tau) 
\subseteq \mathcal{B}(\tau)$.
A \emph{generalised backoff process}~\newsym{Z-roman}{generalised backoff process, Definition~(def:genbackoff of the paper)}{Z} with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$\tau$,
birth distribution~$\mathcal{D}$, and 
initial population $\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(\tau)$ is defined as follows: First,
$\mathbf{b}^Z_0(\tau) = \emptyset$ and,
for all positive integers~$j$,
$\mathbf{b}^Z_j(\tau) = \mathbf{arr}^Z_j(\tau)$.
For each time step~$t>\tau$ and each bin $j\geq 0$, the process has random variables 
\newsym{Bjz-bf}{population of bin~$j$ in~$Z$ just before sends at $t$}{\mathbf{B}^Z_j(t)}, 
\newsym{sjz-bf}{balls that send from $j$ at $t$ in $Z$}{\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)},
\newsym{ejz-bf}{balls that escape from $j$ at $t$ in $Z$}{\mathbf{e}^Z_j(t)}, and 
\newsym{bjz-bf}{population of bin~$j$ in~$Z$ just after step $t$}{\mathbf{b}^Z_j(t)} of respective sizes 
\newsym{Bjz}{$|\mathbf{B}^Z_j(t)|$}{B^Z_j(t)}, 
\newsym{sjz}{$|\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t))|$}{s^Z_j(t)}, 
\newsym{ejz}{$|\mathbf{e}^Z_j(t)|$}{e^Z_j(t)}, and 
\newsym{bjz}{$|\mathbf{b}^Z_j(t)|$}{b^Z_j(t)}.
By analogy to backoff processes, 
$\mathbf{b}^Z_j(t)$ is the population of bin~$j$ just after step~$t$ in~$Z$, 
$\mathbf{B}^Z_j(t)$ is the population of bin~$j$ just before the sends at step~$t$,
$\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)$ is the set of balls that send from bin~$j$ at step~$t$, and $\mathbf{e}^Z_j(t)$ is the set of balls that escape from bin~$j$ at step~$t$.
The process evolves as   follows for $t>\tau$.
\begin{itemize}

\item   The quantity \newsym{n-z}{$|n^Z(t)|$}{n^Z(t)} is drawn from~$\mathcal{D}$.  If $n^Z(t) = 0$ then $\mathbf{n}^Z(t) = \emptyset$. Otherwise,
the set 
$\newsym{nz-bf}{set of balls born at $t$ in $Z$}{\mathbf{n}^Z(t)} = \{\mathcal{B}(t,0,1),\ldots,\mathcal{B}(t,0,n^Z(t))\}$.

\item $\mathbf{B}_0^Z(t) = \mathbf{n}^Z(t) \cup \mathbf{b}_0^Z(t-1)$.   
For $j\geq 1$, $\mathbf{B}_j^Z(t) =  \mathbf{b}_j^Z(t-1)$.   

 
\item    
For all $j\geq 0$,  the set $\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)$ is formed
by taking each element of $\mathbf{B}_j^Z(t)$ independently with probability~$p_j$. 
$\newsym{sz-bf}{set of balls that send at $t$ in $Z$}{\mathbf{s}^Z(t)} = \cup_{j\geq 0}\ 
\mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)$
and $\newsym{sz}{$|\mathbf{s}^Z(t)|$}{s^Z(t)} = |\mathbf{s}^Z(t)|$.
 

\item For all $j\geq 0$, 
a random subset $\mathbf{e}^Z_j(t)\subseteq \mathbf{s}^Z_j(t)$ is drawn from some distribution (to fix a particular generalised backoff process this distribution will be specified).   
 

\item $\mathbf{b}^Z_0(t) = \mathbf{B}^Z_0(t) \setminus \mathbf{s}^Z_0(t)$.

\item Fix a (possibly random) tuple 
$\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(t)$ of disjoint sets

entries $(X_{ij})_{i\le j}$ on and above the diagonal.

$X_{ij}\sim N(0,\frac{1}{N})$ for $i\ne j$ and
$X_{ii}\sim N(0,\frac{2}{N})$.

body: In mathematical analysis, the Weierstrass approximation theorem states that every continuous function defined on a closed interval [a, b] can be uniformly approximated as closely as desired by a polynomial function. Because polynomials are among the simplest functions, and because computers can directly evaluate polynomials, this theorem has both practical and theoretical relevance, especially in polynomial interpolation. The original version of this result was established by Karl Weierstrass in 1885 using the Weierstrass transform.
title: Stone–Weierstrass theorem

[Theorem 3 (Positive maximum principle) of arXiv:2609.01403, '2609.01403'] Let $n\ge2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $B_r(x_0)\subset\mathbb R^n$, and
$c\in L^\infty(B_r(x_0))$. Assume
$u\in\mathcal L^{2s}(\mathbb R^n)$,
$u\ge0$ a.e. in $\mathbb R^n$, and
\[
    \mathscr{L}_su+cu\ge0
    \qquad
    \text{in }\mathcal D'(B_r(x_0)\setminus\{x_0\}).
\]
If
\[
    u\ge m>0
    \qquad
    \text{a.e. in }
    B_r(x_0)\setminus B_{r/2}(x_0),
\]
then
\[
    u\ge\alpha m
    \qquad
    \text{a.e. in }B_r(x_0)\setminus\{x_0\},
\]
where
\[
    \alpha
    =
    \alpha\!\left(
        n,s,
        r^{2s}\|c^+\|_{L^\infty(B_r(x_0))}
    \right)>0,
    \qquad
    c^+=\max\{c,0\}.
\]
In particular, if $0<r\le1$, then $\alpha$ may be chosen to depend only
on $n$, $s$, and
$\|c^+\|_{L^\infty(B_r(x_0))}$. If $c\le0$, it may be chosen
independently of both $r$ and $c$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Positive maximum principle

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.30898, 'Necessity of Ladyzhenskaya \& Ural'tseva's sufficient conditions in nonuniform ellipticity'] Let $n\ge 2$ and $2<p<\infty$. There exists a bounded domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$ with smooth boundary, and a function $v_{0}\in C^{\infty}(\bar{\Omega})$ such that the unique solution $v\in v_{0}+W^{1,1}_{0}(\Omega)$ to Dirichlet problem
\eqn{pd}
$$
v_{0}+W^{1,1}_{0}(\Omega)\ni v\mapsto \min_{w\in v_{0}+W^{1,1}_{0}(\Omega)}\mathcal{A}_{p}(w;\Omega),
$$
and unique generalized minimizer of $\mathcal{A}_{p}$ in class $v_{0}+W^{1,1}_{0}(\Omega)$, satisfies $v\in C^{0,1-\frac{2}{p}}(\bar{\Omega})\cap W^{1;\frac{p}{2},\infty}(\Omega)\setminus W^{1,\infty}_{\loc}(\Omega)$. In particular, the set of non-Lebesgue points of $Dv$ has positive $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$-measure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$, 
and for $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, 
the mapping
$(\lambda,\mu)\mapsto S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$,
is continuous with respect to the Hausdorff metric $d_H$.

\begin{proof} Fix $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\ge0$.
Recall the notation \eqref{e:lam.mu.delta.ball}, and suppose
$(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda$ and 
 $(\lambda,\mu)\in B_\delta(\lambda',\mu')$. Given $\YY'\in S_\star(\lambda',\mu';\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$, we will construct $\YY\in S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$ which is $o_\delta(1)$-close to $\YY'$. We set $\vwww$ as in Lemma~\ref{l:D.mu.continuity.w}, so that we have the bound $\|\vwww-\vwww'\|_1 \le \delta/\iota^2$. Recalling Lemma~\ref{l:p.polytope.bd.local.aux}, we see that
 $\vwww,\vwww'$ are confined to a compact domain $[0,9/\iota_0]^s$.
The $\Budget$ function is uniformly continuous on the compact domain
$[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}\times\Lambda$, so
	\[\sup\bigg\{
	\begin{array}{l}
	|\Budget(\YY;\mu)
	-\Budget(\YY';\mu')|
	:\YY,\YY'\in[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s},
	(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda,\\
	\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
	\|\mu-\mu'\|_\infty \le \delta,
	\|\YY-\YY'\|_1 \le \delta/\iota^2
	\end{array}
	\bigg\} \le o_\delta(1)\,,
	\]
where $o_\delta(1)$ denotes an error tending to zero as $\delta\to0$. 
For the purposes of this proof, let us abbreviate
	\begin{align*}
	c(\YY;\lambda)
	&\equiv \Cost(\YY;\lambda)
	+ \epsilon_1\alpha^2\iota^2(\|\vBBb\|_2)^2\,,\\
	g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)
	&\equiv c(\YY;\lambda) - \Budget(\YY;\mu) - \epsilon_2\,.
	\end{align*}
Then we can similarly bound
	\[\sup\bigg\{\begin{array}{l}
	|c(\YY';\lambda)
	-c(\YY';\lambda')|
	: \YY'\in[0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}, 
	(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')\in\Lambda,\\
	\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad
	\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_\infty \le \delta,
	\end{array}
	\bigg\}
	 \le o_\delta(1)\,.
	\]
Combining the above bounds gives
	\beq
	c(\YY';\lambda)
	-\Budget(\YY;\mu) - \epsilon_2
	\le g (\YY';\lambda',\mu') + o_\delta(1)
	\le o_\delta(1)\,,
	\eeq
uniformly over 
$(\lambda,\mu),(\lambda',\mu')$ in $\Lambda$ within distance $\delta$,
and
$\YY,\YY'\in [0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}$ within distance $\delta/\iota^2$.
If the above left-hand side is in fact $\le0$ then we are done, since we can then set
$\YY=(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$
 to achieve
$g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)\le 0$. If the above left-hand side is
 strictly positive, then it remains to choose 
 $\YY=(\vBBb,\vvvv,\vUUu,\vwww)$
 close to 
 $\YY(0)\equiv(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$ to make $g(\YY;\lambda,\mu)\le 0$.
In this case, consider the path in $\cD_\mu$ given by the line segment joining $\YY(0)\equiv(\vBBb',\vvvv',\vUUu',\vwww)$
to $\YY(1)\equiv(\vec{0},\vvvv'-\vUUu',\vec{0},\vwww)$. If we parametrize this segment as a linear function $\YY(t)$ of $t\in[0,1]$, then along the segment we have
	\[\Cost(\YY(t);\lambda)
	-\Cost(\YY(0);\lambda)
	=-(\lambda,\vBBb'+\vUUu')t
	\equiv -A(\YY')t\,.
	\]
Recall from \eqref{e:surplus.small.error.bound} that at the start of the line segment we have $g(\YY(0);\lambda,\mu) \le o_\delta(1)$.  Let $\eta = g(\YY(0);\lambda,\mu)$. We then divide into several cases:
\begin{itemize}
\item If  $A(\YY')\ge\eta^{1/2}$, then we can choose $t_0= \eta / A(\YY') \le \eta^{1/2}$ such that
	\[
	g(\YY(t_0);\lambda,\mu) 
	\le  \eta^{1/2} - A(\YY') t_0 
	\le 0\,,
	\]
and (since $\YY,\YY' \in [0,9/\iota_0]^{3r+s}$) $\|\YY(t_0)-\YY(0)\|_2 \lesssim \eta^{1/2}$. In this case, we can conclude by setting $\YY = \YY(t_0)$.
\item Otherwise, if 
$A(\YY')\le \eta^{1/2}$, then
assumption~\eqref{e:def-Lambda} implies that 
\[
    \max\Big(\|\vBBb'\|_1,\|\vUUu'\|_1\Big) \le \frac{\eta^{1/2}}{\iota}\,,
\]
so that we have 
\[

\]

[Theorem thm:one-dimensional-phase-diagram of arXiv:2608.05105, 'Cluster-Cluster model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$'] For the fully occupied one-dimensional Cluster-Cluster model ($p=1,d=1$), the following bounds hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(\alpha>0\), then \(T_\alpha=\infty\) and
\[
   \mu(t) := \mathbb{E}[|\mathfs{C}_0(t)|]\asymp (1+t)^{1/\alpha}.
 \]
\item If \(\alpha=0\), then \(T_0=\infty\) and 
\(\mu(t)=e^t\). 
\item If \(-1<\alpha<0\), and let $q=-\alpha$, then \(0<T_\alpha<\infty\). More explicitly,
 \(\exists \kappa_q>0\) such that
\begin{equation*}

    \frac1q
    \le
    T_q
    \le
    \min\left\{
        \frac1{\kappa_q},
        \frac1{1-2^{-q}}
    \right\}.
\end{equation*}

\item If \(\alpha=-1\), then \(T_{-1}=1\) and
\(\mu(t)=(1-t)^{-1}\).
\item If \(\alpha<-1\), then \(T_\alpha=0\).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:one-dimensional-coding of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $T:Z\to Z$ be a Borel automorphism of a standard Borel space.
There is a Borel family of sets
\[
    z\longmapsto P_z\subset\mathbb R
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
the sets $P_z$ are uniformly Delone;

\item
\[
    P_{Tz}=P_z-1
    \qquad
    (z\in Z);
\]

\item
if $z,w\in Z$ and $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
\[
    P_w=P_z-u,
\]
then
\[
    u\in\mathbb Z
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    w=T^u z;
\]

\item
for every $z\in Z$,
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{P_z}
    =
    4\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }(-1,1)
\]
in the sense of tempered distributions.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-dimensional coding theorem

[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $f:\Omega\to \Omega'$ and let  there be given a $\sigma$-field $\FF$ on $\Omega$ and a $\sigma$-field $\FF'$ on $\Omega'$. 
	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
		\item If $A'\subset\Omega'$ is such that $f:\Omega\to A'$, then $f\in \FF/\FF'$ iff $f\in \FF/(\FF'\vert_{A'})$. 
		\item For $A\subset \Omega$, if $f\in \FF/\FF'$, then $f\vert_A\in (\FF\vert_A)/\FF'$.
		\item If $(A_i)_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence in $\FF$ with $\Omega=\cup_{i\in \mathbb{N}}A_i$ then: $f\in \FF/\FF'$ $\Leftrightarrow$ ($f\vert_{A_i}\in \FF\vert_{A_i}/\FF'$ for all $i\in \mathbb{N}$). 
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 14 of arXiv:2604.01685

[Corollary cor:poisson-noisy of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda>0$.
Fix a send sequence $\overline{p}$. Fix a real number $W\geq 1$.  Let $S$ be a set of positive integers such that, for every $k\in S$, $W_k \geq W$. Let $\{ P_k : k\in S\}$ be a set of   independent Poisson variables 
such that, for each $k\in S$,
$\mathbb{E}(P_k) \ge  \lambda W_k/10$.   Then \[
\mathbb{P}\big(\sum_{x \in S} P_xp_x < \lambda |S|/20\big) \le \exp(-\lambda |S| W /80).
    \]

[Definition 76 (Connes--Kreimer extraction-contraction coproduct) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] The \emph{Connes--Kreimer extraction-contraction 
co\-product} $\DeltaCK: \spanF \to \spancFminus \otimes \spanF$ is defined by 
\begin{equation}
  
 \DeltaCK(\Gamma) = \Gamma\otimes\unit + \unit\otimes\Gamma 
+ \sum_{\substack{\unit\neq\overline\Gamma\subsetneq\Gamma, \overline\Gamma \in \Fminus}} 
\overline\Gamma\otimes(\Gamma/\overline\Gamma)\;, 
\end{equation} 
where the sum ranges over all \emph{divergent} subgraphs $\overline\Gamma$, and 
$\Gamma/\overline\Gamma$ denotes the graph obtained by replacing $\overline\Gamma$
by a single vertex. The subgraphs have to be \emph{full}, in the sense that if an edge
$e$ belongs to $\overline\Gamma$, all edges connecting the same vertices also belong 
to $\overline\Gamma$.
title: Connes--Kreimer extraction-contraction coproduct

[Proposition prop:periodic-finite-volume-compatibility of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] The process \(\Xi_{L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}\) is obtained from the finite-volume
periodic ideal Bose Feynman--Kac measure
(equation eq:periodic-spatial-permutation-measure of the paper) by decomposing the
permutation into cycles, disintegrating each cycle into a rooted Brownian
loop, describing the marks defined in
(sssec:periodic-rooted-loops-marks of the paper), and adding independent uniform
labels.  Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item the unmarked cycle-count marginal is
  (equation eq:periodic-canonical-cycle-law of the paper);
  \item conditionally on the cycle counts, the marks attached to distinct
  cycles are independent;
  \item for a cycle of length \(j\), the single-loop mark has law
  \[
    (R,Y_{L,j},\zeta_{L,j})
    \sim
    \mathsf J_{L,j}^{\mathrm{per}}
    =
    \mathsf H_{\mathbb T^d}\otimes
    \mathsf G_{L,j}\otimes
    \mathsf B_{j/V_L};
  \]
  in particular, the rescaled root, the scaled winding endpoint, and the
  winding-corrected bridge fluctuation are independent;
  \item cutting each rooted loop of duration \(\beta j\) into its \(j\)
  consecutive time-\(\beta\) legs and forgetting the marks recovers the
  spatial-permutation measure
  (equation eq:periodic-spatial-permutation-measure of the paper).
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition prop:tailrl-centered-target of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] For $N\geq2$, let
\begin{equation}
\bar\omega
:=
\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\omega\bigl(r(x,z_i)\bigr),
\qquad
\hat g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)
:=
\sum_{i=1}^N
\Bigl(\omega\bigl(r(x,z_i)\bigr)-\bar\omega\Bigr)\,S(x,z_i).

\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}_{z_{1:N}}\!\left[\hat g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)\right]
=
\nabla_\theta J_{\mathrm{TailRL{}}}^{(N-1)}(\theta;x).

\end{equation}

body:
[Lem lem-monotone-lim of arXiv:2411.06301, 'Inverting the operation of conditioning a branching process on extinction'] Let $\lambda \in [0,\infty)^d$.
If there exists $ m \in \mathbbm N$ such that $g^{(m)}(\lambda) < \lambda$, then $\lim_{n\to\infty} g^{(n)}(\lambda) = 0$. 
Moreover, if there exists $m \in\mathbbm N$ such that $g^{(m)}(\lambda) > \lambda$, then $\lim_{n\to\infty} |g^{(n)}(\lambda)| = \infty$.
title: Lem lem-monotone-lim of arXiv:2411.06301

body:
Aldous and Janson, The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II (arXiv:2303.02529), Open Problem 14 (pp. 54-55) asks to prove that L_n, the expected drawn length of DTCS(n) under their recursion (73) l(chi_m) = l(chi_i) + l(chi_{m-i}) + 2 + |h(chi_{m-i}) - h(chi_i)|, grows roughly like n log^4 n. Our result (id P0340, 2026-09-08): the drawn length is Theta(n), so the conjecture is FALSE. For every full binary tree the drawn length is at most the sum of all leaf depths, because the increment 2 + |h_R - h_L| is at most n_L + n_R (a full binary tree with k leaves has height at most k-1); with the authors' own Theorem 3 (the expected depth of a random leaf is asymptotic to (1/(2 zeta(2))) log^2 n = 3 pi^-2 log^2 n) this gives E[drawn length] <= n E[leaf depth] ~ (3/pi^2) n log^2 n = o(n log^4 n). The heuristic's error is a missing factor m: their heuristic (75) uses n a(n,m) as the mean count of size-m subclades where the correct count is (n/m) a(n,m); with the wrong count the conjecture is reproduced exactly, with the right one the scale sum converges (sum log^3 m / m^2) instead of diverging (sum log^3 m / m). Verification as the source words it: machine-checked in P0340.lean, together with the exact decomposition drawn(T) = sum of internal subtree heights + height(T); simulation gives L_n/n = 4.71, 4.78, 4.84, 4.83, 4.86 at n = 10^3 to 4 x 10^5 - flat across a 400x range while log^4 n grows 12x - with the sampler validated first against the paper's own clade counts and leaf-depth law. Prior art not cleared.

body: [Lemma reduction of arXiv:2607.24528, 'On Feige's conjecture'] Let $\delta>0$, let \(F\) be a merger, and let \(\alpha\in[0,1]\). Suppose that \[ F(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\leq\alpha \] whenever \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\geq 0\) and \[ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\geq n+\delta. \] Then, for any independent nonnegative random variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with expectation one, \[ \mathbb P\left(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i<n+\delta\right)\geq 1-\alpha. \]

[Corollary 34 (Conditional convergence) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Let either $W(\mu):=\mu(\varphi_0)$, with $\varphi_0\in\Cc$, $\varphi_0\not\equiv0$, fixed
and $\eps$ admissible in the sense of Theorem~\ref{thm:restricted} and small
enough that $\bN(\mu(\varphi_0)>\eps)>0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:PZ}); or
$W(\mu):=\mu(\R^d)$, with $\eps>0$ arbitrary --- every $\eps$ being admissible
here, since $\mu(\R^d)$ has no atoms under $\bN$ and
$\bN(\mu(\R^d)>\eps)\in(0,\infty)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:totalmass}). Then
\[
\bP\bigl(\mu_n\in\cdot\;\big|\;W(\mu_n)>\eps\bigr)
\;\xRightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\;
\bN\bigl(\,\cdot\,\big|\;W(\mu)>\eps\bigr)
:=\frac{\bN(\,\cdot\,;\,W(\mu)>\eps)}{\bN(W(\mu)>\eps)}
\]
weakly as probability measures on $\cM$, and
$n^{2}\,\bP\bigl(W(\mu_n)>\eps\bigr)\to\bN\bigl(W(\mu)>\eps\bigr)\in(0,\infty)$.

[Definition of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] We say that $Z \in_R \mathbb{R}^d$ is \emph{symmetric about zero} if for any measurable $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $\mathbb{P}(Z \in E) = \mathbb{P}(Z \in -E)$. 
If $Z - w$ is symmetric about zero (for some fixed $w \in \mathbb{R}^d$) then we say $Z$ is \emph{symmetric about $w$}. 
We say that $Z$ is \emph{symmetric} to mean that it is symmetric about \emph{some} $w$; 
we say that $Z$ is \emph{asymmetric} if it is not symmetric about \emph{any} $w$.

[Theorem 6 (Information-theoretic lower bound for exact quantile regret) of arXiv:2608.22227, '\fontsize{18pt}{20pt}\selectfont \bf Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning with Smoothed Q'] Fix a target quantile level \(\tau\in(0,1)\), and assume \(A\ge2\) and \(H\ge2\). Then there exist constants \(c_0,c_1>0\), depending at most on the fixed target level \(\tau\), such that for every \(\rho\in(0,\frac{\min\{\tau,1-\tau\}}{8}]\), every
\(T\ge c_0\,\frac{A}{\rho^2}\), and every possibly randomized learning algorithm that, at each episode \(t\),
outputs a deterministic history-dependent policy
\(\pi^t\in\Pi_{\mathrm{det}}\), there exists a finite-horizon episodic MDP \(\mathcal M=(\mathcal S,\mathcal A,H,P^\star,r)
\) with deterministic rewards \(r_h(s,a)\in[0,1]\),
\(
|\mathcal S|=2\), \(|\mathcal A|=A\), such that the root-level plateau constant of this instance satisfies $\rho_\tau=\rho$, and 
$\mathbb E\!\left[\Reg_\tau(T)\right]
\ge c_1\,\frac{H} {\rho_\tau}\sqrt{AT}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:abstract-sharp of arXiv:2609.03637, 'On the abstract approach to spectral constants:\\ a proof of the Clou\^atre--Ostermann--Ra'] Let \(\mathcal A\subset C(X)\) be a uniform algebra, let
\[
 \theta:\mathcal A\longrightarrow B(\mathcal H)
\]
be a bounded unital homomorphism, and let
\[
 \alpha:\mathcal A\longrightarrow\mathcal A
\]
be a bounded unital antilinear map.  Define
\begin{equation}
 \Phi(h)
 =\frac12\bigl(\theta(h)+\theta(\alpha(h))^*\bigr),
 \qquad h\in\mathcal A.
 
\end{equation}
If \(\Phi\) is contractive, then
\begin{equation}
 \left\lVert \theta\right\rVert\leq2.
 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2608.30743, 'Perspectives on the Bott spectral sequence for Lie groupoids'] Consider a vector bundle $b: V \rightarrow M$. Furthermore consider an action $K$ of $G$ on $p': N \rightarrow G_0$. Now consider an invariant map $f: N \rightarrow M$. Then there is a natural linear action of $G$ on $f^* V$ covering the action on $N$ and the map
	\[
	f^* : \Gamma(M, V) \rightarrow \Gamma(N, f^* V)
	\]
	has its image contained in $(\Gamma(N, f^* V))^G$.

[Lemma lem:ineqs of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Let $H_n$ be integer-valued and let $N_n(h),L_n(h)$ be nonnegative random
variables such that
$$
\{H_n\ge h\}=\{N_n(h)\ge1\},
\qquad
\{L_n(h)\ge1\}\subseteq\{H_n\ge h\}.
$$
If $\mathbb{E}[N_n(h_n)]\to0$, then $\P(H_n\ge h_n)\to0$. If
$L_n(h_n)\to\infty$ in probability, then $\P(H_n\ge h_n)\to1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 25 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] A measurable function $u:[0,1]\times \mR^d\mapsto\mR$ is considered a solution to Eq. (\ref{EquationA.1}) if $u\in \mH_{1,p}^q([0,1])$, $\partial_su\in \mH_{-1,p}^q([0,1])$, $u(1,\cdot)=0$ and Eq. (\ref{EquationA.1}) holds in $\mH_{-1,p^*}^{q^*}([0,1])$. Specifically, for every $\phi\in\mH_{1,p^*}^{q^*}([0,1])$, the following equality must be satisfied
	\be
	\int_{0}^{1}\langle(\partial_t+a^{i,j}\partial_{i,j}+\sL_{\upsilon,R}^g)u_t,\phi_t\rangle_{\mH_{-1,p}(\mR^d),\mH_{1,p^*}(\mR^d)} dt=\int_{0}^{1} \langle f_t,\phi_t\rangle_{\mH_{-1,p}(\mR^d),\mH_{1,p^*}(\mR^d)} dt.
	\ee 
	
	Likewise, a measurable function $v:[0,1]\times \mR^d\mapsto\mR$ is considered a solution to Eq. (\ref{EquationA.2+1}) if $v\in \mH_{1,p^*}^{q^*}([0,1])$, $\partial_sv\in \mH_{-1,p^*}^{q^*}([0,1])$, $u(1,\cdot)=0$ and Eq. (\ref{EquationA.2+1}) holds in $\mH_{-1,p}^{q}([0,1])$. Specifically, for every $\phi\in\mH_{1,p}^{q}([0,1])$, the following equality must be satisfied
	\be

	\ee

body:
[Theorem thm:CM_OU of arXiv:2510.18106, 'Law equivalence for Ornstein--Uhlenbeck dynamics\\ driven by L\'evy noise'] Let $B$ generate a $C_0$-semigroup and let $h\in\mathcal{H}_{B,T}$. Then
\[
        \mathcal{L}\big(Y_B(W)+h\big)\sim \mathcal{L}\big(Y_B(W)\big)
        \quad\hbox{on }D_{H,T}.
\]
Equivalently, if $h=\mathcal{R}_{B,T}u$ for some $u\in L^2(0,T;H)$, the shift is implemented by the usual Cameron--Martin density. If $u$ is random but independent of $W$, the same conclusion holds after conditioning on $u$; no unconditional Novikov estimate is needed in this conditional situation. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cameron--Martin theorem for OU convolutions

[Thm 1 (Jiang-Qi) of arXiv:2604.13134, '\bf From Gaussian to Gumbel: extreme eigenvalues of complex Ginibre products with exact ra'] Let $k_n$ and $\alpha_n$ be defined as above. The following holds.

(a). If \(\alpha=+\infty\), then 
\[\sqrt{\alpha_n \log \alpha_n}\big( n^{-k_n/2} \max_{1 \leq j \leq n} |Z_j| - 1 \big) - (\log \alpha_n - \log(\sqrt{2\pi} \log \alpha_n))\]
converges weakly to the Gumbel distribution.

(b). If \(\alpha \in (0, \infty)\), for any $x>0,$ we have 
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(\max_{1 \leq j \leq n} |Z_j|\le x n^{k_n/2})=\prod_{j=0}^{+\infty}\Phi(\frac{j}{\sqrt{\alpha}}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\alpha}}+2\sqrt{\alpha}\log x).\] 

(c). If \(\alpha=0\), then
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(\max_{1 \leq j \leq n} \log |Z_j|\le  \frac12 k_n \psi(n)+\frac{x}{\sqrt{2\alpha_n}})=\Phi(x).\]
Here, $\Phi$ is the distribution function of standard normal and $\psi(n)$ is the digamma function. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Jiang-Qi

[Theorem thm:BCSVH of arXiv:2606.14687, 'Lehner's operator norm formulas, semidefinite programming, and spiked matrix models'] For $\bm X$ defined as in (equation eq:X-gauss of the paper), define the quantities
\begin{align*}
\sigma(\bm X)^2
  &\colonequals \|\mathbb{E}(\bm X - \mathbb{E} \bm X)^2\| \\
  &= \left\| \sum_{i = 1}^n \bm A_i^2 \right\|, \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \\
v(\bm X)^2
  &\colonequals \|\mathbb{E} \mathsf{vec}(\bm X - \mathbb{E} \bm X)\mathsf{vec}(\bm X - \mathbb{E} \bm X)^{*}\| \\
  &= \left\|\sum_{i = 1}^n \mathsf{vec}(\bm A_i) \mathsf{vec}(\bm A_i)^*\right\|, \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}  \\
\sigma_*(\bm X)^2
  &\colonequals \sup_{\|\bm u\| = \|\bm w\| = 1}\mathbb{E}[|\bm u^{*}(\bm X - \mathbb{E} \bm X)\bm w|^2] \\
  &= \sup_{\|\bm u\| = \|\bm w\| = 1} \sum_{i = 1}^n \left| \langle \bm u, \bm A_i \bm w \rangle \right|^2, \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}  \\
  \widetilde v(\bm X)^2
  &\colonequals
v(\bm X) \cdot \sigma(\bm X). \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation}
\end{align*}
    There is a universal constant $C > 0$ such that
    \[
        \left|\mathbb{E}\lambda_{\max}(\bm X) - \Lambda_{\mathsf{sc}}(\bm A_0, \bm A_1, \dots, \bm A_n)\right|
        \leq
        C \,\widetilde{v}(\bm X) (\log d)^{3/4}.
    \]
    Also, if $\bm X = \bm X^{(d)} \in \mathbb{C}^{d \times d}_{\mathsf{herm}}$ is a sequence of such random matrices with $\bm X^{(d)} = \bm A_0^{(d)} + \sum_{i = 1}^n g_i\bm A_i^{(d)}$ for some $n = n(d)$, and one has, as $d \to \infty$,
    \[
        \widetilde{v}(\bm X^{(d)})(\log d)^{3/4} \to 0,
    \]
    then the following convergence in probability holds as $d \to \infty$:
    \[
        |\lambda_{\max}(\bm X^{(d)}) - \Lambda_{\mathsf{sc}}(\bm A_0^{(d)}, \bm A_1^{(d)}, \dots, \bm A_n^{(d)})| \to 0.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary holub-1-Y-reflexive of arXiv:2609.00794, 'On operators whose adjoints or second adjoints attain their norms'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces. 
\begin{enumerate}
        \itemsep0.25em
        \item If $\operatorname{NA}(Y,X^*) = \mathcal{L}(Y,X^*)$, then $\operatorname{NA}_1 (X,Y^*) = \mathcal{L}(X,Y^*)$.
\item If $\operatorname{NA}_1(Y,X^*) = \mathcal{L}(Y,X^*)$, then $\operatorname{NA}_2 (X,Y^*) = \mathcal{L}(X,Y^*)$.
        \end{enumerate}
If $Y$ is reflexive, then the converses of both implications also hold. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2604.19738, 'Phase Transitions in the Fluctuations of Functionals of Random Neural Networks \\'] Let $\widehat \kappa_L$ be as in \eqref{defkappahatL} and assume either \Cref{ass::CRI}, $\kappa'(1)>1$ and $\kappa'(b)\neq 0$, or \Cref{ass:cri-pot}. Then the following asymptotics holds for fixed $q\in\N$, $q\ge2$.

\smallskip
\noindent
If $q<d/(2\nu)$, as $L\to\infty$ we have
	\begin{equation*}
		\int_{-1}^1 \widehat \kappa_L(u)^q\,\di \mu(u)
		= v_L^{q}\Big(\beth_q+o(1)\Big)\,
	\end{equation*}
where
    $$\beth_q = \frac{1}{\beta_0^q} \int_{-1}^1 \widehat \beta(u)^q  \di \mu(u)\,,\,\,\,\qquad \widehat \beta:=\beta-\int_{-1}^1\beta(u)\di\mu(u)\,.
    $$
Moreover,  $\beth_q=0 \iff \kappa$ and $q$ are both odd.

\smallskip
\noindent
If $q\ge d/(2\nu)$ and $q$ is even whenever $\kappa$ is odd we have
$$ \int_{-1}^1 \widehat \kappa_L(u)^q \di \mu (u)\asymp
\begin{cases}
			v_L^q \log(v_L^{-1})&\textnormal{if } q=\frac{d}{2\nu} \\
			v_L^{d/(2\nu)}
            &\textnormal{if } q>\frac{d}{2\nu}
		\end{cases}\,\,\,\,\,\,.
        $$

\smallskip
\noindent
Moreover, we always have (with no restrictions on $q,\kappa$)
$$ \int_{-1}^1  |\widehat\kappa_L(u)|^q \di \mu (u)\lesssim
\begin{cases}
v_L^q &\textnormal{if } q<\frac{d}{(2\nu)} \\
			v_L^q \log(v_L^{-1})&\textnormal{if } q=\frac{d}{2\nu} \\
			v_L^{d/(2\nu)}
            &\textnormal{if } q>\frac{d}{2\nu}
		\end{cases}\,\,\,\,\,\,.
        $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2505.21774, 'The friendship paradox for trees'] {\bf [Correlations of vertex types for infinite trees]}

\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] 
Let $\mathcal{T}_\infty$ be the infinite Galton-Watson tree with offspring distribution $p$ satisfying \eqref{eq:pcond}. Then, for each $\tchi,\chi \in S$, there exists $f^{\tchi\chi}$ such that 
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty} \frac{N_m^{\tchi\chi}}{N_m} = f^{\tchi\chi} \quad \PP\text{-}\mathrm{a.s.}
\] 
\item[(b)] 
For $k \in \N$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
f^{\tchi\chi} &= \sum_{\tk \in \N_0} \sum_{k \in \N_0} \tilde{p}_{\tilde{k}}\, p_k\,
\PP\Big({\rm sign}\big[\tX+{S}_{\tilde{k}-1}+k-\tilde{k}(\tilde{k}+1)\big]=\tchi\Big)\\
&\qquad \times \PP\Big({\rm sign}\big[\tilde{k}+S_k-k(k+1)\big]=\chi\Big),
\end{aligned}
\]
where $S_k$ and $\tilde{X}$ are as defined in Theorem \ref{thm:densities-on-infinite-trees}.

[Lemma lem:t0-asymptotics of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] Fix $\lambda_*>0$.  Uniformly for all $\lambda\geq\lambda_*$ and all
admissible solutions $(f,g)$ at $t=0$, with $u=\log g$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \lambda\|f\|_{C^0}=O(\alpha^{-1}),
 \qquad \|u\|_{C^0}\leq C,
 \qquad
 \frac{\|\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C} f\|_{C^0}}{\alpha}=o(1)
 \quad (\alpha\to\infty).
\end{equation}
More precisely,
\[
 \sup_{\lambda\geq\lambda_*}
 \sup_{(f,g)\in\mathcal S_{\alpha,\lambda}}
 \frac{\|\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C}f\|_{C^0}}{\alpha}
 \longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{as }\alpha\to\infty,
\]
where \(\mathcal S_{\alpha,\lambda}\) denotes the set of admissible
solutions at \(t=0\).

[Dfn of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The product functor}]
  Fix $N \in \mathbb{N}$.
  Let $(\tau^{(k)})_{k=1}^{N}$ be 
  a sequence of functors.
  The \textit{product functor} $\tau = \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}$ is defined as follows:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$, 
      we set $\tau(S) \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau^{(k)}(S)$.
      We equip $\tau(S)$ with the max product metric (cf.\ (equation 2. eq: max product metric of the paper)).
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      we set $\tau_{f} \coloneqq \prod_{k=1}^{N} \tau_{f}^{(k)}$, that is, 
      $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$ is a distance-preserving map given by 
      \begin{equation}
        \tau_{f}\bigl( (a_{k})_{k=1}^{N} \bigr) \coloneqq \bigl( \tau^{(k)}_{f}(a_{k}) \bigr)_{k=1}^{N}.
      \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}

[Prop prop-single-type of arXiv:2411.06301, 'Inverting the operation of conditioning a branching process on extinction'] Let $X= \{X(n)\}_{n \geq 0}$ be a single-type branching process started from a single individual and let $f$ be its generating function. Assume that 
\begin{enumerate}[I.]
\item $X$ is subcritical, i.e., $\mathbbm E[X(1)] < 1$.  
\item We have $\mathbbm P[X(1) \geq 2] > 0$.   
\item $f$ is continuous from $(0,\infty]$ to $(0,\infty]$ (with $(0,\infty]$ equipped with the topology of a half-open interval). 
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a unique conjugate branching process for $X$. Equivalently, there exists a unique value of $ q > 1$ for which $f(  q) =  q$.

[Definition 29 of arXiv:2511.02725, 'Mixing of general biased adjacent transposition chains'] Let $\cB=\{B_1,\dots,B_\ell\}$ denote any collection of subsets of $[N]$ where $\bigcup_i B_i=[N]$.  
The heat-bath block dynamics 
is the {discrete-time} Markov chain which, from a configuration $X_t$, chooses a block $B_i$ with probability $|B_i|/(\sum_i |B_i|)$ from $\cB$, and resamples the entire configuration $X_t(B_i)$

[Lemma 11 (Local variation of the transformed tail) of arXiv:2608.20101, '\bfseries Largest bulk gap of the complex Ginibre ensemble'] Let \(r\to\infty\) and let \(h=h(r)\) satisfy \(h=O(r^{-3})\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \Psi(r+h)-\Psi(r)=r^3h+o(1).
\end{equation}
More generally, if \(r_n,s_n\to\infty\), both are of the same order, and
\(\Phi(s_n)-\Phi(r_n)\to y\), then
\(\Psi(s_n)-\Psi(r_n)\to y\).

[Theoremc 3 (Coordinate and diagonal extremizers for all smoothing times) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $1\le p<2$, $n\ge2$, and $t\ge0$. Then for every $\theta\in\sphere$,
\[
 \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\diag)
 \le
 \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\theta)
 \le
 \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(e_1).
\]
The right equality occurs exactly for coordinate directions $\{\pm e_i\}$, and the left equality occurs exactly for diagonal directions
\[
 \left\{\frac1{\sqrt n}(\pm1,\ldots,\pm1)\right\}.
\]
The same statement holds for the unstandardized profile $A_{p,n,t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem.mathcalYCN of arXiv:2605.11785, 'Regularization of a mean-field SDE by an additive common noise: the conditional expectatio'] There exists a unique probability measure $Q(d\bm{x}^0,d\bm{y}) = Q^{\bm{x}^0}(d\bm{y}) {\mathcal W}^{\overline\mu_0}(d\bm{x}^0)$ on $({\mathcal C}^2, \overline{\mathcal F})$ (with $Q^{\bm{x}^0}$ denoting the conditional law of $\bm{y}$ given $\bm{x}^0$ under $Q$),  such that 
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] under $Q(d\bm{x}^0,d\bm{y}) 
$, the process
$$
\Bigl( {\bm{x}}^0_t\; , \; \bm{y}_t-\bm{y}_0 - \int_0^t  \left(b(\bm{y}_s+{\bm{x}}^0_s,{\bm{x}}^0_s)ds - \overline b(s,\bm{x}^0_s,\bm{x}^0)\right)ds \Bigr)_{t\in[0,T]}, 
$$
 is a $2d-$dimensional Brownian motion starting from $(\overline\mu_0,0)$ for the canonical filtration generated by $(\bm{x}^0,\bm{y})$, and $\bm{y}_0$ is distributed according to $(Id-\overline \mu_0)\sharp \mu_0$, 
\item[(ii)] ${\mathcal W}^{\overline \mu_0}(d\bm{x}^0)\otimes dt$-a.e., 
  $\bm{y}_t\sharp Q^{\bm{x}^0}= \mu^{\bm{x}^0}_t$. 
\end{itemize}

[Corollary cor:jackson-rescale of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] For any $f\in C^k([-R,R])$ such that $f^{(l)}(-R) = f^{(l)}(R)$ for all $l\le k$ and $\norm{f^{(k)}}_\infty \le M$, there exists a trigonometric polynomial of the form 
\begin{align}
    T_D(x) &= \sum_{m\le D} a_m \cos\Big(\frac{m\pi (x+R)}{R}\Big) + b_m \sin\Big(\frac{m\pi (x+R)}{R}\Big), \text{ for } x\in [-R,R],  
\end{align}
such that $\norm{T_D - f}_\infty \le C_k D^{-k} M (R/\pi)^k$. 
Additionally, it holds that 
$$\sum_{1\le m\le D} |a_m| + |b_m| \le  \frac{2^{k+2}\,MR^k}{\pi^{k+1}} \sum_{1\le m \le D} m^{-k}.$$

[Corollary 106 (Corewise all-order continuity) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Fix $N\ge2$ and $R<\infty$, and assume that the operational exponent satisfies
$1/3<\eta\le\alpha$.  On $\mathcal C_R$, the geometric and It\^o
all-order readouts
\[
 x\longmapsto \mathbf S^{S,N}(x),
 \qquad
 x\longmapsto \mathbf S^{I,N}(x)
\]
are continuous.  The degree-$N$ geometric signatures of the smooth resolvent
paths converge uniformly on $\mathcal C_R$ to $\mathbf S^{S,N}$, and the
corresponding bracket-corrected towers formed with the trace-energy
approximations converge uniformly to $\mathbf S^{I,N}$.  More precisely, the
towers driven by $S_2(Y^{\eps_n})$ and $\mathsf E^{\delta_j}$ converge jointly
as $n,j\to\infty$, and hence along every prescribed diagonal.
For any exponent $1/3<\eta<1/2$, this hypothesis can be arranged by choosing
$\eta\le\alpha<\beta<1/2$ before constructing the cores.

[Prop 6 (Initial-tangent contact sets) of arXiv:2609.03296, 'Nonuniqueness of Model Potentials and Weak Geodesic Rays'] Let \((u_t)_{t\geq0}\) be a bounded weak geodesic ray emanating from zero and
let \((\widehat u_\tau)_{\tau\in\RR}\) be its Legendre transform.  As
observed in \cite[Section~5]{Darvas26}, for
every \(\tau\in\RR\),
\[
 \{\dot u_0\geq\tau\}
 =
 \{\widehat u_\tau=0\}.
 \tag{2.1}
\]
The pointwise initial tangent therefore records the zero-contact filtration
of the dual maximal test curve. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For all $\gamma>0$, there exists $C>0$ independent of $x_0$ and $N$ such that 
$$
\sum_{k,\alpha} (\theta_k^{N})^2 \|\sigma_{k,\alpha}^{N^{-1}}\|_{C^\gamma(B)}^2\leq C.
$$
In particular, $(\theta_k^{N}\sigma_{k,\alpha}^{N^{-1}})_{k,\alpha}\in C^\gamma(B;\ell^2)$ uniformly in $N\geq 1$ for all $\gamma>0$.

body:
Garg, Gunn and Wang, arXiv:2506.01854v2, Corollary 4: relative to any crypto oracle, there are no statistically secure pseudorandom codes robust to any constant rate of independent random binary errors. This already holds for secret-key zero-bit PRCs with negligible soundness and completeness errors and polynomial query complexity. Their noise parameter rho is correlation: N_rho refreshes each bit independently with probability 1-rho, equivalently flips each bit with probability (1-rho)/2; constant positive noise means rho is bounded away from 1. Section 1.1 interprets this as a fully black-box separation from primitives implemented by crypto oracles; footnote 3 specifies the additional PSPACE oracle used in that interpretation. The statistical oracle impossibility must not be read as an unconditional impossibility from existence of one-way functions.
Binary channel with a constant positive independent bit-flip rate below one half
Statistical security in the oracle model of the source
Polynomially many oracle queries and polynomial block length
Negligible completeness and soundness errors

Let (X, mu) and (Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces, 1 <= p < infinity, and F: X x Y -> [0, infinity] measurable for the product sigma-algebra. Then ( int_Y ( int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) )^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} <= int_X ( int_Y F(x,y)^p dnu(y) )^{1/p} dmu(x), both sides in [0, infinity]. Consequently, for complex measurable F with the right-hand side (computed with |F|) finite, int_X F(x,y) dmu(x) converges absolutely for nu-a.e. y and its L^p(nu)-norm is at most the right-hand side. In words: the L^p norm of an integral is at most the integral of the L^p norms. (For p = infinity the analogous statement with ess sup holds for F >= 0.)
(X, mu) and (Y, nu) are sigma-finite measure spaces
F is measurable with respect to the product sigma-algebra
F >= 0 (or the right-hand side is finite when F is complex)
1 <= p < infinity

body:
[Lemma lem:3.1 of arXiv:2604.19294, 'On the maxima of Littlewood polynomials on $[-1,1]$'] For $t\geqslant0$, define
\begin{equation} 
    f_{n,t}^{+}=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}f_n(e^{-t/n}),
    \qquad
    f_{n,t}^{-}=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}f_n(-e^{-t/n}).
\end{equation}
Then
\[
    \lVertf_n\rVert_\infty
    = \max\Big\{1,\ \sqrt n\sup_{t\geqslant0}|f_{n,t}^{+}|,\ \sqrt n\sup_{t\geqslant0}|f_{n,t}^{-}|\Big\}.
\]

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy' (prob environment labelled eq:tuple-of-Phis).] When $\phi$ is unital, Theorem~(thm:pre-LDP) says that the value $E_n$ gives the rate function in the large deviations principle obeyed by the random element
\[(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n] \in \S^\rm{u}_k(B_n).\]
The values $E_n'$ should have an analogous interpretation, but this time for the random $S$-tuples
\begin{equation}
\big((\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n\cup sB_n]:\ s \in S\big)
\end{equation}
taking values in the space
\[\Big\{(Q_s:\ s \in S) \in \prod_{s \in S}\S^\rm{u}_k(B_n\cup sB_n):\ (Q_s)[B_n]\ \hbox{is the same for all $s$}\Big\}.\]
If this is true, then both inequalities in Lemma~(lem:1-2-ineqs) become instances of the contraction principle.

I believe one can prove this along the same lines as Theorem~(thm:pre-LDP) without any really new ideas, but working with the the tuples in~(eq:tuple-of-Phis) is sure to be more complicated than working with $(\Phi^\pi_V)[B_n$ alone. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)

body:
[Lemma lem:LG-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}
  \sum_{r \le a_i} \sum_{r' \le a_j}
   \psi_{t, r, n_i}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with the
kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^m$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data and
$B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ as the propagator.

[Definition of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] A map $f\colon X\to Y$ of closed orthogonal $G$-spaces is called a \emph{$G$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalence} if $f({\mathcal{U}}_H)\colon X({\mathcal{U}}_H)\to Y({\mathcal{U}}_H)$ is a $\mathcal G_{H,G}$-weak equivalence for every $H\in{\mathcal{F}}$ and some (hence any) complete $H$-universe ${\mathcal{U}}_H$. 

    A map $f\colon X\to Y$ between general orthogonal $G$-spaces is called a $G$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalence if in some (hence any) commutative square
    \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            X'\arrow[d,"\sim"']\arrow[r,"f'"] & Y'\arrow[d,"\sim"]\\
            X\arrow[r,"f"'] & Y
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where the vertical maps are $G$-global equivalences and $X',Y'$ are closed, the map $f'$ is a {$G$-global ${\mathcal{F}}$-weak equivalence} in the sense defined above.

Own work draft, status independently checked proof, E0018-C3 v1 (w667 PASS, w668 PASS). For symmetric-rate switching of real 2x2 matrices Ai, set Bi=Ai-(tr Ai/2)I. The exponent obeys L_A(r)=L_B(r)+(tr A0+tr A1)/4. If one traceless part has nonzero imaginary eigenvalues +-i omega, a fixed real similarity and time scaling transform the traceless pair into J=[[0,-1],[1,0]] and eta H+sJ, H=diag(1,-1), eta>=0, s real; normalized rate rho=r/omega and the original traceless exponent equals omega times the normalized exponent at rho. For unscaled traceless matrices with spectral abscissae ki=sqrt(max(-det Bi,0)), there exist scalar shifts Ai=Bi-ai I making both individually Hurwitz with prescribed damping average abar iff abar>(k0+k1)/2. This places no requirement on the averaged matrix. No rate monotonicity or unimodality is asserted.

Status: proof (unaudited), 2026-10-14.

Let symmetric-rate switching alternate two real 2x2 matrices Ai. Put
Bi=Ai-(tr Ai/2)I, so Bi is traceless. Let tau=(tr A0+tr A1)/4.
The top Lyapunov exponent satisfies L_A(r)=L_B(r)+tau whenever one exists.
This is an exact pathwise scalar factorization plus the two-state occupation law.
If B0 has purely imaginary nonzero eigenvalues +-i omega, omega>0, then after a
single fixed real similarity and time scale omega the pair is
B0/omega=J=[[0,-1],[1,0]],
B1/omega=eta H+s J=[[eta,-s],[s,-eta]], eta>=0, s real, H=diag(1,-1).
The transformed switching rate is rho=r/omega. Thus (after removing traces) every
pair with a nonzero elliptic matrix reduces to two real parameters eta,s.

Proof of trace shift. Let c_i=tr Ai/2 and C(t)=integral_0^t c_{I_s}ds.
The fundamental matrix equals exp(C(t)) times the one for Bi: differentiate on
sojourns and use the commuting scalar factor and continuity at jumps.
The two-state symmetric occupation law gives C(t)/t->(c0+c1)/2=tau almost surely.
Fixed similarity preserves exponential norm growth since its condition number is
constant. Rescaling time t'=omega t divides both matrices and rate by omega and
scales the original exponent by omega.

Proof of elliptic canonical form. Cayley-Hamilton for a traceless real B0 gives
B0^2=-omega^2 I. Choose any real nonzero vector v; vectors v, B0v/omega are linearly
independent, since dependence would give a real eigenvalue. In that basis B0=omega J.
Every real traceless B1 in this basis decomposes uniquely into s0 J+R, where
s0=(B1_21-B1_12)/2 and R is symmetric traceless, R=[[a,b],[b,-a]].
Any real symmetric traceless R has eigenvalues +-eta0 with eta0=sqrt(a^2+b^2)>=0.
There is a determinant-one orthogonal matrix O (a plane rotation) with
O^T R O=eta0 H: select an orthonormal eigenbasis, flip its second eigenvector if
necessary to make determinant one. Every plane rotation commutes with J, so the
same O leaves B0 unchanged. Divide by omega to obtain eta=eta0/omega,s=s0/omega.
This transformation is fixed, independent of r, so preserves the full rate curve.

Exact diagnostic identities. Half the trace of (B1/omega)^2 equals eta^2-s^2;
half the trace of ((B0+B1)/(2omega))^2 equals [eta^2-(1+s)^2]/4.
Let k1=sqrt(max(eta^2-s^2,0)), kavg=(1/2)sqrt(max(eta^2-(1+s)^2,0)).
The symmetric occupation average of the individual spectral abscissae is k1/2.
Comparing these algebraic endpoints, kavg>k1/2 is possible only for s<-1/2
and eta>|1+s|; those two conditions are also sufficient. This statement compares
spectral abscissae only; it does not assert a stochastic slow/fast limit theorem.
For any traceless real Bi its eigenvalue spectral abscissa is sqrt(max(-det Bi,0)).
A scalar shift Ai=Bi-ai I is Hurwitz exactly when ai exceeds that abscissa.
Consequently a fixed scalar damping average abar can make BOTH Ai Hurwitz if and
only if abar>(k0+k1)/2: necessity by summing ai>ki; sufficiency choose
ai=ki+abar-(k0+k1)/2. No condition on the averaged matrix is required.

Non-result: the two-parameter curve is not proved unimodal. This reduction helps
separate an actual Hurwitz-only search from an unnecessarily stable-average search.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:383fff664b083531fd9875bbc9b5c71c0f80d084bc72a1271d76e6a30ea40474","revision_digest":"sha256:c800e2e5ac4a159efd0bbfbb4710f53f8c474e0744d25c16014a6e5d0f200358","source_id":"own-work:w658:E0018-C3-v1","source_revision":"owner-work://brain_workers/w658/proofs/E0018_C3_v1.md; exact v1 independently audited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Proposition 14 (Persistent supercritical misalignment) of arXiv:2608.20638, 'Provable Edge-of-Stability for Adam on a One-Dimensional Quadratic'] Suppose that $0<\beta_1<1$ and $w_{\max}>2$.  For every $v_0>0$ satisfying
$w_0=c\eta/(\sqrt{v_0}+\varepsilon)>2$, there exist $x_0\ne0$ and
$m_0\in\R$ such that
\begin{equation}
    x_t(m_t+cx_t)<0
    \qquad\text{for every }t\ge0.

\end{equation}
Along this trajectory,
\begin{equation}
    w_t\ge w_0,
    \qquad
    \abs{x_t}\le(w_0-1)^{-t}\abs{x_0},
    \qquad t\ge0.

\end{equation}
In particular, $(x_t,m_t,v_t)\to(0,0,0)$ and $w_t\to w_{\max}$,
although the trajectory remains uniformly supercritical for all time. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: The number of primes up to x satisfies pi(x) ~ x / log x, equivalently pi(x) ~ Li(x), as x grows. Proved independently by Hadamard and de la Vallee Poussin (1896) by showing zeta(s) has no zeros on the line Re(s) = 1; elementary proofs (Erdos, Selberg 1949) avoid complex analysis. The error term in the theorem is governed by the zero-free region - under the Riemann hypothesis the error is O(sqrt(x) log x).
title: Prime Number Theorem

[Lemma lem:prime-deleted-character-sum of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $X\geq2$ and $1\leq Y\leq X$.  Let $m,w,D\geq1$, and let $q,t\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $(t,D)=1$ and $wt\equiv q\pmod D$.
Let $P$ be a prime with $P\nmid D$, and put $\chi_m(\cdot)=(\frac{\cdot}{m})$.
Define
\[
\mathcal P(m;w,D,q)
=
\{\ell\mid m:\ \ell\text{ odd},\ v_\ell(m)\text{ odd},\
\ell\nmid q,\ (D,w,\ell)=1\}
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak m
=
\frac{m}{\displaystyle
\prod_{\ell\in\mathcal P(m;w,D,q)}(\sqrt\ell/2)}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\substack{M\in[X,X+Y]\\M\equiv t\ (\bmod D)\\P\nmid M}}
\mu^2(M)\chi_m(M)
\chi_m\left(\frac{wM-q}{D}\right)
&\ll
\sqrt X+\frac{\mathfrak mY}{mD}
+\frac{\log(2X)\sqrt{\mathfrak mY}}{\sqrt D},
\end{aligned}

\end{equation}
with an absolute implied constant.

In the Gaussian linear-regression setting y=<x,theta*>+z, with independent x~N(0,diag(v_1,...,v_d)) and z~N(0,sigma^2), let n,d be positive integers, v_i>0, sigma^2>0, and theta*_i nonzero. Put a_i=v_i(theta*_i)^2 and b=sigma^2/n. For coordinate learning rates 0<=eta_i<=1/v_i define the deterministic surrogate risk of equation (2), Rbar_eta(t)=sigma^2+sum_i [a_i(1-eta_i v_i)^(2t) +b(1-(1-eta_i v_i)^t)^2], for integer t>=1. For any prescribed integer t_*>=1, choose eta_i=[1-(b/(a_i+b))^(1/t_*)]/v_i. Then each coordinate summand attains its minimum at t=t_*, and Rbar_eta(t_*)=sigma^2+sum_i a_i b/(a_i+b), the global minimum over all admissible coordinate rates and integer stopping times. These are oracle rates using the true signal coefficients and feature variances. This statement optimizes the source surrogate; approximating the random finite-sample prediction risk requires the separate hypotheses and conclusion of Theorem 1.
