[Lemma 6 (Finite-chaos Stein estimate) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Fix positive integers $q_1,\ldots,q_d$.  Let
$F_{n,a}=I_{q_a}^{(n)}(f_{n,a})$, assume that the kernels are bounded,
and let $C_n=\Cov(F_n)$.  Put
\[
 \Gamma_{n,ab}
 =\ip{DF_{n,a}}{-DL^{-1}F_{n,b}}_{H_n}.
\]
There is a constant $c=c(q_1,\ldots,q_d)<\infty$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a,b=1}^d
 \norm{\Gamma_{n,ab}-C_{n,ab}}_2^2
 \le c\sum_{a,b=1}^d
 \sum_{\substack{1\le r\le q_a\wedge q_b\\
 (r,q_a,q_b)\ne(q_a,q_a,q_a)}}
 \norm{f_{n,a}\otimes_rf_{n,b}}^2.
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, if $Z_n\sim N_d(0,C_n)$, then for every $t\in\R^d$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\E e^{it\cdot F_n}-\E e^{it\cdot Z_n}\right|
 \le\frac{|t|^2}{2}
 \left(
 \sum_{a,b=1}^d
 \norm{\Gamma_{n,ab}-C_{n,ab}}_2^2
 \right)^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}

\[
  \Phi_k(\mathcal{B}_1) \;\subseteq\; \Phi_k(\mathcal{B}_2) \qquad \text{for every } k \geq 0\,.
\]

[Lem localconcentration of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Let $Z\sim N(0, \mathbf{1}_d)$ be a 
$d$-dimensional
standard Gaussian vector. 
Let $\Omega\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a measurable set with 
$\mathbf{P}[Z\in \Omega] \geq \frac{3}{4}$, and let $f: \mathbb{R}^{d}\to \mathbb{R}$ be a
function whose restriction to $\Omega$ is $L$-Lipschitz.
Then
$$
	\mathbf{P}[|f(Z)-\mathrm{med}(f(Z))| > \varepsilon] 
	\leq \mathbf{P}[Z\notin \Omega] + C e^{-c \varepsilon^2/L^2}
$$
for any $\varepsilon>0$, where $C, c>0$ are universal constants.

[Proposition 28 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The two estimates on which the critical compactness argument rests are the following.

\textup{(i)} Let $\phi_0>0$ be the normalized local Dirichlet principal eigenfunction. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\sigma_\varepsilon>0$ such that
\[
\cA_{\sigma,2,L}\phi_0+(\lambda_0+\varepsilon)\phi_0\ge0\;\hbox{in }(-L,L)
\]
for $0<\sigma<\sigma_\varepsilon$. Consequently $\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,2,L})\le\lambda_0+\varepsilon$.

\textup{(ii)} There exist constants $c_J,C_J>0$ such that
\[
c_J\min\{\eta^2,1\}\le1-\widehat J(\eta)\le C_J\min\{\eta^2,1\}\;\hbox{for all }\eta\in\R.
\]
Consequently, if $\sigma_n\to0$ and $u_n$ are supported in a fixed bounded interval with $\|u_n\|_2\le C$ and $E_{\sigma_n}(u_n)\le C$, then a subsequence converges strongly in $L^2(\R)$ to a function in $H^1(\R)$ supported in the same interval. The estimate is proved directly below from the Fourier symbol. In particular, the proof does not invoke the Sobolev-norm approximation/characterization theorems of \cite{BBM,Brezis02,PonceCV,Ponce}; retaining the zero-extension support is essential for recovering the missing inflow boundary condition in the advective problem.
For every such strongly convergent subsequence, with limit $u$, one also has the sharp lower-semicontinuity estimate
\[
d_J\int_\R |u'(x)|^2\,dx\le \liminf_{n\to\infty}E_{\sigma_n}(u_n).
\]

[Lem 62 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $q_0 \in [0,1)$, we have $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\BOGP}(\alpha,q_0)$.
\begin{proof}
    This is a consequence of Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main}.
    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$, where $L$ is sufficiently large depending on $\alpha,q_0,\epsilon$. Recalling \eqref{e:cM.Lip.q0}, this means there exists a sequence of $L$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA_j)^\circ$ (acting in $N_j$ dimensions) such that
    \begin{align} \nonumber 
    &\WERR( (\cA_j)^\circ,\mu)
 \le \epsilon\,,\\
        
   &     q_0(j)
        \equiv \chi_{ (\cA_j)^\circ}(0)
         \stackrel{j\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} q_0\,.
    \end{align}
    Let $(\cA_j)_{j\ge 1}$ be the perturbations of the $( (\cA_j)^\circ)_{j\ge 1}$ given by Proposition~\ref{p:wlogable}, which are also $L$-Lipschitz.
    Proposition~\ref{p:wlogable} further yields
    \[
        \frac{1}{N} \bbE \Big[\| (\cA_j)^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) 
        	- \cA_j(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\|^2\Big]
        \le \frac{2}{(1-q_0(j))L^2}\,.
    \]
Thus Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.approx} implies that for $c_0$, $C_1(\alpha)$ and $C_2(\alpha,L)$ given therein,
	\[
	\WERR(\cA_j,(\cA_j)^\circ)
	\le 
	\bigg\{
        C_1(\alpha) \cdot \frac{2}{(1-q_0(j))L^2} + C_2(\alpha,L) e^{-c_0N_j}
        \bigg\}^{1/2} 
        \le \epsilon \]
    where the last inequality holds if $L$ is sufficiently large depending on $\alpha,q_0,\epsilon$ (consistent with our assumptions), and $j$ sufficiently large depending on $q_0,\epsilon,L$. Hence, by omitting finitely many $j$, we can assume it holds for all $j$ that

for some fixed $\mu^\Ising \in \cP(\{\pm 1\})$.
    By passing to a further subsequence, we can assume (as in Theorem~\ref{thm:BOGP-hardness-main}) that $\chi_{\cA_j}$ converges to a limiting function $\chi$, both pointwise and in $L^1$.
    Since Proposition~\ref{p:wlogable} ensures

body: A graph is bipartite if its vertices split into two parts X and Y with every edge joining X to Y - equivalently, it contains no odd cycle (Konig). A matching is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges; it saturates a set S if every vertex of S is an endpoint of a matching edge, and it is perfect if it saturates every vertex. In a bipartite graph, Hall's marriage condition - |N(S)| >= |S| for every subset S of X, where N(S) is the neighborhood - is exactly the condition under which X can be saturated by a matching.
title: Bipartite Graph and Matching

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.00757, 'Improved bounds in Birch's theorem for forms in many variables'] Let \(d\geq5\), and let \(F\in\ZZ[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) be a form of degree \(d\).
Write \(\sigma\) for the affine dimension of the singular locus of the affine hypersurface \(F=0\) over \(\overline{\QQ}\).
Suppose that
\[
 n-\sigma\geq
 \frac34d2^d-2d-\left(3\cdot2^{d-3}-3\right),
 \qquad\text{for }d=5,6;
\]
or
\[
 n-\sigma>C_d,
 \qquad\text{for }d\geq7.
\]
Then the smooth Hasse principle holds for \(F\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.00757

body: In the mathematical discipline of graph theory, Menger's theorem says that in a finite graph, the size of a minimum cut set is equal to the maximum number of disjoint paths that can be found between any pair of vertices. Proved by Karl Menger in 1927, it characterizes the connectivity of a graph. It is generalized by the max-flow min-cut theorem, which is a weighted, edge version, and which in turn is a special case of the strong duality theorem for linear programs.
title: Menger's theorem

[Problem Average-energy Gaussian codes of arXiv:2607.14087, 'Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima: A Resolution of the Weak Simplex Conjecture'] \label[problem]{prob:average-energy}
For fixed $M$, ambient dimension, noise level, and average-energy budget $E$,
maximize the average probability of correct decoding over equiprobable
Gaussian codebooks satisfying
\[
  \frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M\lVert c_i\rVert^2\leq E.
\]
Characterize the optimizers as a function of the signal-to-noise ratio.  Can an
optimizer always be chosen from a family consisting of a lower-dimensional
regular simplex together with coincident zero signals, or are additional
geometries unavoidable? (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Average-energy Gaussian codes

Let X be an algebraic stack. The inertia stack of X, denoted I_X, is the fiber product I_X = X x_{X x X} X, where both morphisms are the diagonal Delta: X -> X x X. Fiberwise over a geometric point x in X, I_X(x) is isomorphic to the automorphism group scheme Aut(x).
X is an algebraic stack

  &:=\sup_{t\le T}\norm{m(t)}_{L^2}^2

  \\
  Z_T^\beta(m)
  &:=\int_0^T\norm{m(t)^3}_{B^{1-\beta}_{1,1}}\dd t.
\end{align}
Once \(m\) is fixed, we suppress its argument; the same convention will be
used for \(K_T^s(m)\) below.
Then
\begin{equation}

    +\left(\sup_{t\le T}[a(t)]_{C^\beta}\right)
       Z_T^\beta,
\end{equation}
where the implicit constant depends on the ellipticity and bi-Lipschitz
constants and on
\[
  \int_0^T\left[
    1+\norm{Q_\lambda(t)}_{C^\rho}^{\gamma/(\gamma-1)}
  \right]\dd t,
\]
but not on \(Z_T^\beta\).

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] For every \(0<\lambda\le 1\) (i.e.~\(-2\le c<0\)), there is a
unique probability law on compact connected sets
\(K\subset\overline D\) with
\(K\cap\partial D=\{a,b\}\) such that
\begin{equation}
        \mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf 1_{\{K\cap A=\varnothing\}}
        \exp\left\{-\lambda m_D(K,A)\right\}\right]
        =\mathbb P\left[\gamma_{\mathrm{BE}}^{D;a,b}\cap A=\varnothing\right],
\end{equation}
for every compact \(A\subset\overline D\) such that $A\cap\{a,b\}=\varnothing$ (with no requirement that \(A\) attach to \(\partial D\)).

For \(\lambda>1\) (i.e.~\(c<-2\)), no probability law on compact
connected sets satisfies~(equation eq:intro-main-id of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The Brownian loop-catcher

[Lemma lem:first_order_deterministic_equivalent of arXiv:2608.23938, 'Generalization, memorization, and overfitting \\for diffusion models trained in the lazy h'] Suppose that Assumptions~(ass:high_dim of the paper) and~(ass:input_dist of the paper) hold, and that \(\kappa^\star \geq c\) for some constant \(c>0\).

    \[
        \|\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{{\boldsymbol R}}(\vartheta)] - \widetilde{{\boldsymbol M}}(\vartheta)\|_\mathrm{F}  \lesssim \frac{1}{\kappa^\star\sqrt{d}} 
    \]
    Furthermore, for every deterministic \({\boldsymbol A}\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) with \(\|{\boldsymbol A}\|_\mathrm{F}\leq 1\),
    \[
      \left|{\rm Tr}({\boldsymbol A}(\widetilde{{\boldsymbol R}}(\vartheta)-\widetilde{{\boldsymbol M}}(\vartheta)))\right| \prec \frac{1}{\kappa^\star\sqrt{d}}.
    \]

\end{enumerate}

[Definition def: Berger_good_box_definition of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $Q$ be a $k$-block

    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=2.2em, itemsep=2pt]
    \item A $0$-block $Q$ is \textbf{good} if there is no directed edge $(u,w)$ with
    $u,w\in Q$ and $|u-w|>A_0/100$.

    \item For $k\ge1$, a $k$-block $Q$ is \textbf{good} if the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}, leftmargin=2.2em, itemsep=2pt]
    \item there is no directed edge $(u,w)$ with
    $u,w\in Q$ and $|u-w|>A_{k-1}/100$;
    \item among the $(k{-}1)$-blocks (children) of $Q$,
    all but at most one are good;
    \item for every
    $v\in\{0,\pm A_{k-1}/2\}^d$, the shifted inner block $Q^{\mathrm{int}}+v$
    also satisfies \textup{(b)} (i.e., among its $(k{-}1)$-subblocks, all but at most
    one are good).
    \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Lem 198 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\cA$ be an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm, and let $\bx(q_d)$ be as defined by
\eqref{e:x.q.mean}. Then
    \[
    \P\bigg(\bigg|
    \frac{(\bx(q_d),\bx(q_\ell))}{N}-q_{\min\{d,\ell\}}
    \bigg|\ge
    \frac{1}{N^{1/3}}\bigg) 
    \le \exp(-N^{0.1})\,.
    \]

\begin{proof}
This follows easily from gaussian Lipschitz concentration (see e.g.\ Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}).
Indeed note that $\|\cA(\bG,  \bg^\aux)\|_2\leq N^{1/2}$ almost surely, while by definition $\bx(q_d)$
is an $L$-Lipschitz function of the gaussian vector $(\bG(q_d),\bg^\aux(q_d))$. It follows that for $\ell \le d$, the normalized inner product
    \[\frac{(\bx(q_d),\bx(q_\ell))}{N}\]
is an 
 $O(LN^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz function of 
    \[\Big(\bG(q_\ell),
    \bg^\aux(q_\ell),
    \bG(q_d) - \bG(q_\ell),\bg^\aux(q_d) - \bg^\aux(q_\ell)\Big)\,.\]
 Therefore it concentrates around its mean by Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}, which gives the conclusion.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 198 of arXiv:2608.29416

body:
[Lemma 4 (Absolute Fourier estimate) of arXiv:2609.01413, 'Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field'] Fix a positive integer $m$ and a constant $c>1$, and put
    $$
    \beta_n:=\frac{c\log n}{n}.
    $$
    Let $V$ be an $m$-dimensional $\F_p$-vector space, and let
    $\mu_{ij}$, $1\leq i,j\leq n$, be arbitrary
    $\beta_n$-balanced probability measures on $\F_p$. Fix a nontrivial
    additive character
    $$
    \psi:\F_p\longrightarrow\C^\times,
    $$
    and write
    $$
    \widehat{\mu}_{ij}(u)
    :=
    \sum_{a\in\F_p}\mu_{ij}(a)\psi(ua),
    \qquad
    u\in\F_p.
    $$
    Then
    \begin{align}
        
        &p^{-mn}
        \sum_{\substack{g_1,\ldots,g_n\in V\\
        \Span_{\F_p}\{g_1,\ldots,g_n\}=V}}
        \ \sum_{\substack{h_1,\ldots,h_n\in V^\vee\\
        (h_1,\ldots,h_n)\neq(0,\ldots,0)}}
        \prod_{i,j=1}^n
        \left|
        \widehat{\mu}_{ij}\bigl(h_j(g_i)\bigr)
        \right|
        =
        o(1),
    \end{align}
    where the estimate is uniform over the choices of
    $\mu_{ij}$.

[Lemma stability of arXiv:2603.15323, '\Large \bf Small-time heat decay for stable processes on fractal drums'] {[vB87]}
Let $D$ be a bounded $C^{1,1}$ open set in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$ with characteristic $(R_0, \Lambda_0)$ and define for $0\leq q <R_{0}$,
$$
D_{q}=\{x\in D : \delta_{D}(x)>q\}.
$$
Then
$$
\left(\frac{R_{0}-q}{R_{0}}\right)^{d-1}|\partial D|\leq |\partial D_{q}| \leq \left(\frac{R_{0}}{R_{0}-q}\right)^{d-1}|\partial D|,
\quad 0\leq q < R_{0}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma stability of arXiv:2603.15323

body:
[Proposition properased of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $(T, d, \rho, \mu)$ be a rooted finitely measured Polish $\mathbb{R}$-tree, let $h \! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$ and let $\rho \! \in \!  \mathtt{t} \! \subseteq \! T$ be closed and connected. Then the following holds true. 
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$]  If $\mu (T\backslash \mathtt{t}) \! < \!  h$, then ${\cal E}_h \mu\! = \! {\cal E}_h \mathtt{P}_{\!\mathtt{t}} \mu$.  

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] For all connected components $C$ of $T \backslash \mathtt{t}$, 
${\cal E}_h \mu ( C)\! =\!  (\mu (C) \! -\! h)_+$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iii)$] ${\cal E}_h \mu (T\backslash \mathtt{t}) \! \leq \! \mu (T\backslash \mathtt{t}) $. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iv)$] $\mathtt{Span}\,  (\mathtt{Supp}\,   {\cal E}_h \mu)$ is the compact set $ T_{\! \mu, h+}$, 
which is the closure of $\, \bigcup_{h^\prime >h} T_{\! \mu, h^\prime}$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(v)$] $({\cal E}_h )_{h \in \mathbb{R}_+}$ is a semigroup on $\mathcal{M}_f (T)$, i.e.~ 
$ {\cal E}_h \!  \circ\!  {\cal E}_{h^\prime} \! = \!  {\cal E}_{h+h^\prime}$ for all $h,h' \! \in \!  \mathbb{R}_+ $.  

\smallskip

\item[$(vi)$] For all $h, h^\prime \! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$ and all $\mu \! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_f (T)$, $d_{\mathtt{var}} ({\cal E}_{h+h'}\mu, {\cal E}_h\mu ) \! \leq \!  3 \mu(T) h^\prime / h$, where for all $\nu, \nu'\! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_f(T)$ we have set $d_{\mathtt{var}} (\nu, \nu')\! = \!   \sup_{B \in \mathscr{B} (T)} | \nu(B)\! -\! \nu'(B) |$. 
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition Wigner Matrix of arXiv:2411.11341, 'Ultra high order cumulants and quantitative CLT for polynomials in Random Matrices'] By a Wigner matrix $X\equiv X(N)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}(x_{i,j})\in \mathbb{C}^{N\times N}$ we mean a self-adjoint random matrix, i.e., $x_{i,j}=\overline{x_{j,i}}$, with independent (up to symmetry) entries which satisfy the moment conditions $\mathbb{E}x_{i,j}=0$ for all $i,j$ and $\mathbb{E}|x_{i,j}|^2=1$ for $i\neq j$. We further make the following assumptions. 

\begin{itemize}

 

\item[$\diamond$]
the entries above the diagonal, $\{x_{i,j}\}_{i<j}$, are
identically distributed as a complex random variable $x_o$ whose odd  cumulants are all $0$, that is, $K_{2n+1}(x_o^{\epsilon_1},\dots,x_o^{\epsilon_{2n+1}})=0$ for any $\epsilon_i\in \{1,-1\}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Here $x_o^{1}=x_o$ while $x_o^{-1}=\overline{x_o}$ means its conjugate. We further assume $x_o\stackrel{d}= \overline{x_o}$. 

\item[$\diamond$] 
the diagonal entries, $\{x_{i,i}\}_{i}$, are identically
distributed as a real random variable $x_d$ whose odd cumulants are all $0$, that is, $K_{2n+1}(x_d)=0$ for any $n\in\mathbb{N}$;

\item[$\diamond$] For any $r$, any $i,j$ and $\epsilon_i\in \{1,-1\}$, 
$|K_r(x_{i,j}^{\epsilon_1},\dots,x_{i,j}^{\epsilon_r})|\leq \mathsf{C}^rr!$ for some constant $\mathsf{C}>0$. 

\end{itemize}
We call a Wigner matrix a  GUE if its off-diagonal entries are $\mathbb{C}\mathcal{N}(0, N^{-1})$ and the diagonal entries are $\mathcal{N}(0, N^{-1})$. We call a Wigner matrix a GOE if its off-diagonal entries are $\mathcal{N}(0, N^{-1})$ and the diagonal entries are $\mathcal{N}(0, 2N^{-1})$.
title: Definition Wigner Matrix of arXiv:2411.11341

[Corollary Asymptotic concentration on the two adjacent layers of arXiv:2609.02659, 'Dimension Dependent Correlation Gap Bounds under Restricted Independence'] Under the asymptotic regime
\[
n\to\infty,\qquad m=m(n)\to\infty,\qquad m(n)=o(n),
\]
let
\[
\delta_n
:=
j-\frac{n-1}{m}
=
\left\lceil\frac{n-1}{m}\right\rceil-\frac{n-1}{m}
\in[0,1).
\]
Then the distribution $\mbox{\boldmath $p$}_n^\star$ in (equation eq:pn_star of the paper) satisfies
\[
\Pr_{\mbox{\boldmath $p$}_n^\star}(|S|=j-1)
=
\delta_n+o(1),
\qquad
\Pr_{\mbox{\boldmath $p$}_n^\star}(|S|=j)
=
1-\delta_n+o(1).
\]

[Defi def:skew_gt_patterns of arXiv:2412.05999, 'Non-Archimedean GUE corners and Hecke modules'] For $\mu \in \Sig_n, \lambda \in \Sig_{n+k}$, we define $\GT_P(\lambda/\mu)$ to be the set of sequences of interlacing signatures $\mu = \lambda^{(0)} \prec_P \lambda^{(1)} \prec_P \cdots \prec_P \lambda^{(k)}= \lambda$. 

For $\lambda,\nu \in \Sig_n$, we define $\GT_{Q,k}(\lambda/\nu)$ to be the set of sequences of length $n$ interlacing signatures $\nu = \lambda^{(0)} \prec_Q \lambda^{(1)} \prec_Q \cdots \prec_Q \lambda^{(k)}=\lambda$. We refer to elements of either $\GT_P$ or $\GT_{Q,k}$ as \emph{Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns}.

For $T \in \GT_P(\lambda/\mu)$ with $\len(\lambda) = \len(\mu)+k$, set $\psi(T) := \prod_{i=1}^{k} \psi_{\lambda^{(i)}/\lambda^{(i-1)}}$. For $T \in \GT_{Q,k}(\lambda/\nu)$, set $\varphi(T) := \prod_{i=1}^{k} \varphi_{\lambda^{(i)}/\lambda^{(i-1)}}$. In both cases, let $wt(T) := (|\lambda^{(1)}|-|\lambda^{(0)}|,\ldots,|\lambda^{(k)}|-|\lambda^{(k-1)}|) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$.
title: Defi def:skew_gt_patterns of arXiv:2412.05999

body:
[Proposition traducvlawera of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $(h_p)_{p\in \mathbb{N}}$ be $\mathbb{R}^*_+$-valued and strictly  decreasing to $0$. Let 
$\mathbf m\! \equiv\!  (\mathbf T, \mathbf d, \rho, \mathtt m)$ and $\mathbf m_n\! \equiv\!  (\mathbf T_n, \mathbf d_n, \rho_n, \mathtt m_n)$, $n\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, be $\mathbb{T}^*$-valued r.v.s.
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$] The following assertions are equivalent. 

\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(a)$] $\mathbf m_n \! \to \! \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}^*, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(b)$] For all $h\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$, ${\cal E}_{h} \mathbf m_n \! \to \! {\cal E}_{h} \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(c)$] For all $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, ${\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m_n \! \to \! {\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$. 

\end{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] The laws of $(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ are tight in $(\mathbb{T}^*, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$ iff the laws of 
$(\langle \mathbf m_n \rangle)_{n\in \mathbb{N}} $ are tight in $\mathbb{R}_+$ and for all fixed $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, the laws of $(\mathtt{Ht} ({\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m_n))_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$  are tight in $\mathbb{R}_+$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iii)$] Let us suppose $(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ to be $\mathbb{T}$-valued and $\mathbf m_n \! \to \! \mathbf m$ in law in $(\mathbb{T}^*, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$. 
Then a.s.~$\mathbf m\! \in \!  \mathbb{T}$ (without necessarily implying that $\mathbf m_n \! \to \! \mathbf m $ in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$) 
iff
\begin{equation}

\forall \varepsilon \! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+, \quad \lim_{r\to \infty} \, \limsup_{p\to \infty} \, \sup_{n\in \mathbb{N}}  {\bf P} \big({\cal E}_{h_p} \mathbf m_n \big(T_n \backslash B_{T_n} (\rho_n, r)\big) \! > \!  \varepsilon  \big) = 0.  
\end{equation}

\item[$(iv)$]  Let us suppose that $(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ is a $\mathbb{T}$-valued sequence. Then $(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges in law in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$ iff the laws of 
$(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ are tight in $(\mathbb{T}, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{GP}})$ and $(\mathbf m_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges in law in $(\mathbb{T}^*, {\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{\mathtt{era}})$. In this case the limiting laws are concentrated on $\mathbb{T}$ and coincide. 
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma forward estimate of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $k \geq 0$ and let $v$ be a vertex that can create a forward $d$-dimensional simplex with a $(d-1)$-simplex $\sigma_k$ that is being explored at Step $k$. Then, given $\mathcal{X}_{k-1}$, the probability that $\sigma_k \cup \{v\}$ appears at Step $k$ is lower bounded by
\[  \tag{3.2.3}
p_k^F := \left( 1 - (k-1) \frac{\lambda}{n} - \sum_{\ell = 1}^{d-1} \sum_{\rho \subseteq \sigma_k, \dim(\rho) = \ell-1} \deg_{\ell-1, d-1}^{\mathcal{X}_{k-1}} (\rho)  p_{d, \ell}  \right) \left( \frac{\lambda}{n} + o(1) \right).
\]
In particular, if the given MRSC model is the Linial-Meshulam model, the probability is exactly $\lambda/n + o(1)$.
title: Lemma forward estimate of arXiv:2605.03151

body:
[Theorem thm:transport-cover of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] Let $0\leq L<\infty$.  Assume that $q$ is finitely supported and
\begin{equation}
 D\!\left(\mathcal L(U,Z)\middle\Vert\mathcal L(V)\otimes\mathcal L(Z)\right)\leq L.
\end{equation}
For $0<a<1$, define
\begin{align}
 \Lambda_a&=\{\chi\in\widehat G:|\widehat q(\chi)|\geq a\},
 \\
 K_{\rm cut}(a,L)
 &:=\exp\!\left(\frac{2(L+e^{-1})}{a}\right),
 \\
 M_{\rm tr}(a,L)
 &:=\left\lceil
 \frac{16K_{\rm cut}(a,L)}{a^2}
 \log\!\left(\frac{16eK_{\rm cut}(a,L)}{a^2}\right)
 \right\rceil.
 
\end{align}
There are characters $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_M\in\Lambda_a$, with
$1\leq M\leq M_{\rm tr}(a,L)$, such that every $\chi\in\Lambda_a$ has some
$j$ for which
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\arg_{\mathbb T}\chi(v_1)
 -\arg_{\mathbb T}\chi_j(v_1)\right\|_{\mathbb T}
 <\frac1{2N_1+1}.
\end{equation}
The bound on $M$ is independent of the rank and side lengths of $A$, the
support of $Z$, and the ambient group.

[Lemma lem:BR_Hilbert of arXiv:2601.08184, 'Wasserstein-p Central Limit Theorem Rates: From Local Dependence to Markov Chains'] Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space equipped with a
filtration \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge 0}\). Let \(H\) be a real separable Hilbert
space with norm \(\|\cdot\|\). Let \((d_k)_{k\ge 1}\) be an \(H\)-valued
martingale difference sequence, i.e., for each \(k\ge 1\),
\(d_k\) is \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, \(\mathbb{E}\|d_k\|<\infty\), and
\[
\mathbb{E}[d_k\mid \mathcal F_{k-1}]=0
\qquad \text{a.s.}
\]
Define
\[
M_n:=\sum_{k=1}^n d_k,\qquad n\ge 1,
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
M_0:=0.
\]
Then, for every \(p\ge 2\), there exists a constant \(C_p\in(0,\infty)\),
depending only on \(p\), such that for all integers \(n\ge 1\),
\[
\mathbb{E}\|M_n\|^p
\le
C_p\left\{
\mathbb{E}\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^n \mathbb{E}[\|d_k\|^2\mid \mathcal F_{k-1}]\Bigr)^{p/2}
+
\mathbb{E}\sum_{k=1}^n \|d_k\|^p
\right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem~4.1 in \cite{pinelis1994optimum}

body: [Lem 53 of arXiv:2606.13459, 'Symmetric Cooperative Motion in Higher Dimensions'] Suppose $\x, m \in \mathbb Z^d$ and $|\x_i| \le m_i$ with $\sum_{i=1}^{d} m_i = n-2$. Let $\lapconst := (8d^4)^{-1}$. If $2 \le n \le \lapconst|\x|^2$, then $${n(n-1) \over d^3} \sum_{i=1}^{d} {1 \over ((m_i+2)^2 - \x_i^2)} \ge 1 + {1 \over n}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

uniform in $\ell$.

[Theorem th:InfiniteVol-PhaseTrans of arXiv:2601.05798, '{I}mry-{M}a phenomenon for the hard-core model on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$'] Consider the hard-core model
	on ${\mathbb{Z}}^2$ with activity field $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$,
	$0\le \lambda_v<\infty$ for all $v$.
	The even and odd infinite-volume measures
	are well-defined as the (unique) local weak limits of finite-volume measures along any exhausting sequence $\Lambda \uparrow {\mathbb{Z}}^2$:
	\begin{equation}
		\mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2,\boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{e} = \lim_{\Lambda \uparrow {\mathbb{Z}}^2} \mu_{\Lambda, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{e} \,, \quad \quad
		\mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2,\boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{o} = \lim_{\Lambda \uparrow {\mathbb{Z}}^2} \mu_{\Lambda, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{o}. \vspace{-.2cm}
	\end{equation}
	Furthermore,
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[(i)]
		      If $\mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{o}(v\in I) = \mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{e}(v\in I)$ for every $v\in {\mathbb{Z}}^2$, then $\mathcal{G}_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}(\mathbb{Z}^2)$ is a singleton set.
		\item[(ii)] For any site $v \in {\mathbb{Z}}^2$, $
			      \mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{e}(v \in I) - \mu_{{\mathbb{Z}}^2, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}^{o}(v \in I)\ge 0$ if $v$ is even and $\le 0$ if $v$ is odd.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:internal-commutator-hierarchy of arXiv:2608.22910, 'A Commutator Framework for Selective Spectral Alignment in Deep Neural Networks'] The terminal internal commutator satisfies
\[
C_{L-1}^{\mathrm{int}}=[Q_{L-1},P_{L-1}]=0.
\]
For \(\ell=0,\ldots,L-2\), define
\begin{align}
T_\ell^{\mathrm{tr}}
&:=
\mathbb E_\mu
\bigl[
D_\ell W_{\ell+1}^\top C_{\ell+1}^{\mathrm{int}}
W_{\ell+1}D_\ell
\bigr],
\\
T_\ell^{\mathrm{imb}}
&:=
\mathbb E_\mu
\bigl[
D_\ell[\mathcal S_{\ell+1},\Delta_\ell]D_\ell
\bigr],
\\
T_\ell^{\mathrm{fluc}}
&:=
\mathbb E_\mu
\bigl[
D_\ell[R_{\ell+1},P_\ell]D_\ell
\bigr],
\\
T_\ell^{\mathrm{gate}}
&:=
\mathbb E_\mu
\bigl[
[D_\ell,P_\ell]S_{\ell+1}D_\ell
+D_\ell S_{\ell+1}[D_\ell,P_\ell]
\bigr].

\end{align}
Then each component is skew-symmetric and
\begin{equation}
C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}
=T_\ell^{\mathrm{tr}}
+T_\ell^{\mathrm{imb}}
+T_\ell^{\mathrm{fluc}}
+T_\ell^{\mathrm{gate}}.
\end{equation}

body:
[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2506.13347, 'Ergodic theorem for the differential equations with interaction'] Assume that for equation with Lipschitz coefficient $a: \mathbb{R} \times \mathfrak M_{0} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$,
$$
\left\{\begin{array}{l}
x\left(u,t\right)=a\left(x(u, t), \mu_{t}\right) d t \\
x(u, 0)=u \in \mathbb{R}, \\
\mu_{t}=\mu_{0} \circ x(\cdot, t)^{-1}
\end{array}\right.
$$
there exists a set $A$ of invariant initial measures,
that is $A=\left\{\mu \in \mathfrak M_{0}: \Phi_{t}(\mu)=\mu, \ t \geq 0\right\}$.
Then the measure $\varkappa$ on $\mathfrak M_{0}$ of the form
$$
\varkappa=\sum_{k=1}^{N} \delta \mu_{k} \cdot p_{k}, \quad \mu_{k} \in A
$$
is invariant with respect to $\Phi_{t}$ :
$$
\varkappa \circ \Phi_{t}^{-1}=\varkappa .
$$

body:
[Lem 17 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] Let \(x_n,y_n,x,y\in D([0,\infty),\bR)\).
Assume the following:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(x_n\to x\) on \(D([0,\infty),\bR)\) as \(n\to\infty\),
  \item \(y_n\) and \(y\) are non-decreasing, with
  \[
  y(0)=0,
  \quad
  y_n(\infty)=y(\infty)=\infty,
  \]
  \item \(y\) is strictly increasing,
  \item there exists a dense subset \(D\subset[0,\infty)\) such that
  \[
  y_n(u)\to y(u)
  \quad (n\to\infty)
  \]
  for every \(u\in D\).
\end{enumerate}
Then, for every \(t\ge0\) such that \(x\) is continuous at \(y^{-1}(t)\), we have
\begin{align}
x_n(y_n^{-1}(t))\longrightarrow x(y^{-1}(t))
\quad (n\to\infty),

\end{align}
where \(y_n^{-1}\) and \(y^{-1}\) denote the right-continuous inverses. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 17 of arXiv:2605.23659

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.02381, '\bfseries Viscosity Supersolution Barriers to a\\ Non-local Free Boundary Problem'] Let $\nu(dz)$ be a L\'evy measure on $\mathbb{R}_0$ with finite
large-jump intensity
$\lambda:=\nu(\{|z|>1\})<\infty.$

\begin{equation}
\beta:=\sqrt{\lambda}\,L_\gamma-(r+\rho)>0.

Then, for every finite horizon $T>0$, there exists a nonnegative global
viscosity supersolution
\[
v^T:\mathbb{R}\times[0,T]\to[0,\infty)
\]
of the PIDE \eqref{eq:bubble-pide}.

[Lemma 27 (KMS small-particle lemma in discrete time) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] Let $Q$ be a finite irreducible reversible transition kernel on $N\ge2$ states
with stationary law $\pi$, and assume $Q(x,x)\ge1/2$ for all states. Let
$t_{\rm meet}^Q$ be the worst-case expected meeting time of two independent
synchronous $Q$-walks, and let $t_{\rm mix}^Q$ be the total-variation mixing
time with threshold $1/4$. Put
\[
        \alpha_Q:=\frac{t_{\rm meet}^Q}{t_{\rm mix}^Q}.
\]
There are universal constants $a_0,c_0,C_0\in(0,\infty)$ such that, if
$\alpha_Q\ge a_0$, then the expected coalescence time of the synchronous
coalescing $Q$-walk process started from any initial configuration with at most
$c_0\alpha_Q\log\alpha_Q$ particles is at most $C_0t_{\rm meet}^Q$.

\end{equation}
The second identity is understood under the product isometry just chosen.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The covariant derivative satisfies $\nabla _{\xi } =\mathcal{L}_{\xi } -\sum_{k}e^{k}\wedge
\left( \phi e_{k}\right) \lrcorner $, where $\{\xi ,e_{k}\}$ is a local orthonormal frame of $TM$ with corresponding

[X\lrcorner ,L]=(\phi X)^{\flat }\wedge $ and $[X\lrcorner ,\Lambda ]=0$ as well as $[L,\nabla_X]=X^\flat\wedge\eta\wedge$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis: the Rankine-Hugoniot condition, and hence the whole notion of weak solution, is attached to a specific pair (conserved density, flux) — not to the PDE as an equation for smooth functions. Two equations with identical classical solutions can have different weak solutions. Counterexample: for smooth u, Burgers' equation u_t + (u^2/2)_x = 0 is equivalent to (u^2/2)_t + (u^3/3)_x = 0 (multiply the first by u; conversely divide where u ≠ 0). But a jump from u_l = 1 (left) to u_r = 0 (right) travels with speed [f]/[u] = (1/2 - 0)/(1 - 0) = 1/2 for the first form, and with speed (1/3 - 0)/(1/2 - 0) = 2/3 for the second: the two weak solutions are genuinely different. The same phenomenon makes the nonconservative form u_t + u u_x = 0 meaningless across a shock (the product u u_x is not a distribution for discontinuous u). Physically, the model must specify which quantity is conserved; numerically, only schemes written in the conservative form of the true conserved quantity (Lax-Wendroff theorem) converge to the correct shock speeds. Auditor's check: when a proof rewrites the flux (multiplying the equation by a function of u, changing variables u = φ(v), or using a chain rule), the manipulation is legitimate for smooth solutions only; across discontinuities it changes the answer.
Counterexample: u_t + (u^2/2)_x = 0 versus (u^2/2)_t + (u^3/3)_x = 0 with left state 1 and right state 0
Rankine-Hugoniot: σ = [flux]/[density], so both entries matter
Chain-rule manipulations of the flux are valid only where the solution is C^1
title: Pitfall: Shock Speeds Depend on Which Conservative Form Is Used

d_{TV}(\mathrm{Law}(X_{n},G_{n}),\mu_{*})\to 0,\ n\to\infty.
$$	
For all measurable 
functions $\phi:\mathbb{R}^{(N+1)d}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that 
\begin{equation}
|\phi(u)|\leq C(1+|u|)	
\end{equation} 
with some $C>0$,
\begin{equation}
E\left[\left|\frac{\phi(X_{1},G_{1})+\ldots+\phi(X_{n},G_{n})}{n}-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{(N+1)d}}\phi(u)\mu_{*}(du)\right|\right]\to 0,
\ n\to\infty.
\end{equation}
A fortiori, the averages converge in probability. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Tightness of the path via the exponential metric (Liouville first passage percolation) comparison. Result: The energy-minimising path between two points concentrates on paths of small total resistance, i.e. on near-geodesics of the discrete metric with edge weights e^{beta h}; this is the Liouville first passage percolation metric, whose scaling limit (the LQG metric) exists for beta below the critical value by Ding-Dubedat-Dunlap-Falconet and Gwynne-Miller. Tightness of P is then plausible via geodesic tightness in that metric, but P is not a geodesic: the current spreads over many paths and the minimiser of the quadratic energy is a flow, not a path; the notes' 'path' is the sampled path of the current. Its scaling limit would be a random path sampled from the limiting current, which requires the continuum current on LQG, an object not yet constructed. I record the reduction: existence of the limit of P is equivalent to existence of the continuum electrical current between boundary points on the LQG surface. Obstruction: No continuum electrical current on LQG has been constructed; the path is a functional of it.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0015-scaling-limit-of-the-current-minimising-path-in-the-dgff-network

At each fixed finite t for sparse critical parking on Z^d, d>=3, the common-Abel full-space potential V_t=lim_{a->1}G_a*(eta-(A_t-H_t)) exists in L2 and U_t-E U_t=V_t+M_t, where M_t is the C17 Green instruction martingale. The odometer mean is a harmonic mode; the two components are not asserted independent. In d4 the difference is well-defined although raw individual charge potentials diverge. Assumptions: Bounded sparse iid source law, 0<p<1/2; finite t; d>=3; Full-space discrete-time SRW, (I-P)G=delta; common Abel parameter; Source finite propagation gives finite-dependent centered U_t; C17 L2 Green instruction martingale. Limitation: No time-uniform potential variance, Gaussian law or independence; no nearest-distance conclusion. Novelty: KNOWN stationary Poisson/resolvent method; UNCHECKED exact parking decomposition. Status: proof (unaudited). The model is discrete-time uniform nearest-neighbor synchronous parking on Z^d with stationary capacity-one holes; A_t(x) is the active-particle count and H_t(x) the unfilled-hole indicator. In the sparse law eta(x) is initially +1 and -1 each with probability p, and zero otherwise, independently across sites. In this card V_t denotes the charge-difference potential, not the eligible-site indicator V_t in C23; these are separate local notations. No audit has been completed for this exact version. U_t(y) counts departures through time t, rho_j(y) is the destination of its jth used instruction, P is the nearest-neighbor averaging operator, G_a=sum_{n>=0}a^n p_n, and M_t(x)=L2-lim_{a->1}sum_y sum_{j<=U_t(y)}[G_a(rho_j(y)-x)-(P G_a)(y-x)].

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN stationary Poisson/resolvent

not assumed independent and no time-uniform variance bound follows.

For the sparse critical source process on Z^d, d>=3, 0<p<1/2, fix a
finite horizon t. Let S_t=A_t-H_t, m_t=E U_t(0), and

    N_t(x)=sum_y sum_{j<=U_t(y)}
                  [1{rho_j(y)=x}-p_1(x-y)].

This is accumulated arrival instruction noise. For 0<a<1 let
G_a(x)=sum_{n>=0}a^n p_n(x), the full-space discrete-time Abel Green
kernel. The limit

    V_t(x)=L2-lim_{a->1} [G_a*(eta-S_t)](x)

exists, and the exact centered identity is

    U_t(x)-m_t=V_t(x)+M_t(x),

where M_t is C17's deterministic Green-potential instruction martingale
with covariance m_t[2G(z-x)-1{x=z}]. All convolutions use the same full-space
SRW convention (I-P)G=delta. In d4 the raw eta and S_t potentials separately
have divergent variance (C24); their difference is regularized together.
The mean m_t is a spatially constant harmonic mode and cannot be recovered
by inverting I-P on mean-zero charges.

## 1. Exact finite-Abel algebra

Source conservation (19) and the definition of N_t give

    S_t=eta+(P-I)U_t+N_t,
    eta-S_t=(I-P)U_t-N_t.

At fixed t under the bounded sparse law, all local counts have a deterministic
finite bound. G_a is in l1, with total mass 1/(1-a), so these convolutions
are well-defined absolutely at a<1 and commute with P. Therefore

    G_a*(eta-S_t)=G_a*(I-P)(U_t-m_t)-G_a*N_t.

The constant was removed because (I-P)m_t=0. Expanding the arrival noise
and using symmetry of G_a shows

    (G_a*N_t)(x)=sum_y sum_{j<=U_t(y)}
                  [G_a(rho_j(y)-x)-(P G_a)(y-x)]
                =M_t^a(x).

The rearrangement is legitimate: at fixed t U_t(y) is uniformly bounded,
and the sum of neighbor Green weights is finite at a<1. C17 proves
M_t^a converges in L2 to M_t for d>=3.

## 2. Resolvent filter converges to the centered identity

Set Z_t=U_t-m_t. The field Z_t is stationary, square-integrable and
finite-dependent by source finite propagation from iid bounded initial
data and independent local motion randomness. Its covariance therefore
has finite support and an absolutely continuous spectral measure; in
particular there is no atom at frequency zero.

The SRW Fourier multiplier is lambda(theta)=d^(-1)sum_i cos(theta_i).
The filter G_a*(I-P) has multiplier

    b_a(theta)=(1-lambda)/(1-a lambda).

For lambda>=0, 0<=b_a<=1; for lambda<0 it is bounded by two.
At every frequency with lambda!=1 it tends to one as a tends to one.
The only frequency lambda=1 is zero, which has no spectral atom for Z_t.
Dominated convergence against its finite spectral measure yields

    G_a*(I-P)Z_t -> Z_t in L2.

Combining this with Step 1 and C17 gives convergence of the charge-difference
potential and the claimed identity. This also proves why centering is
required: b_a(0)=0 at every a and the mean mode is annihilated.

## 3. Scope of cancellation

The difference eta-S_t is a stationary current divergence; covariance
reindexing as in C19 shows its susceptibility is zero. This is consistent
with the existence of its potential even when the two individual raw
charge potentials diverge. It is not legitimate to subtract two separately
defined infinite-variance limits; the same Abel parameter regularizes their
difference before passing to the limit.

Both V_t and M_t depend on the same routing and final configuration.
No independence between them is claimed. The identity supplies a correct
potential decomposition at each finite time, not a bound on V_t as time
grows, a Gaussian approximation, or a conditional hole-influence estimate.
The remaining d4 nearest-distance problem still requires spatial control.

Primary source: Bou-Rabee--Panagiotis arXiv:2609.02820v1, (19), Lemma 4.3
and finite propagation. C17 supplies the Abel instruction martingale;

body: Two Latin squares of order n are orthogonal if superimposing them produces each of the n^2 ordered pairs of symbols exactly once; a family is a set of MOLS if every pair in it is orthogonal, and N(n) denotes the maximum size of such a family. For every n >= 2, N(n) <= n - 1, with equality whenever n is a prime power via the finite-field construction L_a(i, j) = a i + j over F_n for nonzero a. N(1) is infinite by convention, and N(2) = N(6) = 1.
title: Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares (MOLS)

\begin{multline*}
\left(
\fint_I \tvert{P_{2\tau}}_{A,B,q',q}\drm \tau 
\right)^\frac{2}{q}
\\
\leq 
\inf_{\omega\in\ell^\infty(X)}
\sup_{A}\euler^{-\omega}
\sup_{B}\euler^{\omega}
\left(
\fint_I
\tvert{P_\tau^\omega}_{A,A,2,q}^q
\drm \tau
\right)^\frac{1}{q}
\left(
\fint_I
\tvert{P_\tau^{-\omega}}_{B,B,2,q}^q
\drm \tau
\right)^\frac{1}{q}.
\end{multline*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:BKtoL of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Given the structure (A1-A5) one obtains (L1-L6) via the following:
\begin{enumerate}[(L1)]
\item $A^0=\cA$, $A^{0,1}=\Omega^1$, $A^{1,0}=\overline{\Omega^1}$, $A^2=\cA^\vee$.
The product $A^1\otimes A^1\to A^2$ is defined by
\begin{gather*}
A^{0,1}\otimes A^{1,0}\to A^2, \qquad x\otimes \overline{y}\mapsto -\sqrt{-1}h(\_ x,\overline{y}),     \\
A^{1,0}\otimes A^{0,1}\to A^2, \qquad \overline{x}\otimes y\mapsto \sqrt{-1}h(\_ y,\overline{x}).     
\end{gather*}
\item The differential $d\colon A^0\to A^1$ is $da=Da+\overline{Da^*}$ and the differential $d\colon A^1=A^{0,1}\oplus A^{1,0}\to A^2$ is 
\[
d(x,\overline{y})=\left(a\mapsto-\sqrt{-1}h(x,\overline{Da^*})+\sqrt{-1}h(Da,\overline{y})\right)
\]
where $x,y\in\Omega^1$ and $a\in\cA$.
\item $F=-2\eta\in\cA^\vee$.
\item $\tau=\operatorname{ev}_1\colon \cA^\vee\to\bC$.
\item The $*$-structure on $A^0$ and $A^2$ comes from the $*$-structure on $\cA$, and the $*$-structure on $A^1$ is given by $x^*=\overline{x}$ for $x\in A^{0,1}$.
\item See (L1).
\end{enumerate}

[Dfn 3. dfn: metric on frakMtau of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{The metrics $d_{\mathfrak{M}_{c}}^{\tau}$ and $d_{\mathfrak{M}}^{\tau}$}]  
  Let $\tau$ be a functor on $\mathfrak{M}$.
  For $\mathcal{S}=(S,d^{S}, \rho_{S}, a_{S}), \mathcal{T}=(T, d^{T}, \rho_{T}, a_{T}) \in \mathfrak{M}(\tau)$,
  we define
  \begin{equation} 
    d_{\mathfrak{M}}^{\tau} (\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{T})
    \coloneqq
    \inf_{f, g, M}
    \left\{
      \lHausdMet{M}{\rho_{M}} \bigl( f(S), g(T) \bigr) 
      \vee  
      d_{\tau}^{M,\rho_{M}} \bigl( \tau_{f}(a_{S}), \tau_{g}(a_{T}) \bigr)  
    \right\},
  \end{equation}
  where the infimum is taken 
  over all $(M, d^{M}, \rho_{M}) \in \mathfrak{M}$ 
  and root-and-distance-preserving maps $f : S \to M$ and $g : T \to M$.
  For a functor $\tau$ on $\mathfrak{M}_{c}$,
  we define $d_{\mathfrak{M}_{c}}^{\tau}$ similarly.

[Lemma 5 (right stabilizer of the free fibre) of arXiv:2609.03593, '\textbf{New Homogeneous Einstein Metrics from Detection}'] Consider either free $H$-orbit obtained from one simple factor of
$G=H\times H$.  The induced metric is left invariant on $H$ and, with
respect to the $Q=-B_H$ decomposition
\[
 \mathfrak h=\mathfrak q\oplus\mathfrak{sp}(p)\oplus\mathfrak{sp}(q),
\]
its metric endomorphism is scalar on each of the three displayed summands.
For a detected asymmetric metric one has $x_3\ne x_4$.  Consequently the
identity component of the subgroup of right translations preserving the
induced fibre metric is contained in $K=\Sp(p)\times\Sp(q)$.

body: Let (mu_n) be a sequence of probability measures on a topological space X equipped with its Borel sigma-algebra, and let (a_n) be a sequence of positive reals with a_n tending to infinity (the speed). A function I: X -> [0, infinity] is a rate function if it is lower semicontinuous; it is a good rate function if in addition every sublevel set {x in X : I(x) <= alpha}, alpha < infinity, is compact. The sequence (mu_n) satisfies a large-deviation principle with speed a_n and rate function I if, for every Borel set B, -inf_{x in int(B)} I(x) <= liminf_n (1/a_n) log mu_n(B) <= limsup_n (1/a_n) log mu_n(B) <= -inf_{x in cl(B)} I(x), where int(B) and cl(B) denote the interior and closure of B. [Dembo and Zeitouni, Large Deviations Techniques and Applications]
title: Large-Deviation Principle and Rate Function

[Lemma eq:l:FullDomain:0 of arXiv:2411.14936, 'Massive Particle Systems,\\Wasserstein Brownian Motions,\\ and the Dean--Kawasaki Equation'] Let~$k\in {\mathbb N}$,~$F\in \mcC_b^\infty({\mathbb R}^k)$, and~$\left(f_i\right)_{i\leq k}\subset \msD(\mssE)$. 
For every choice of everywhere defined $\nu$-representatives~$\tilde{f_i}$ of~$f_i$, the function
\begin{equation}
\tilde{u}\colon \mu \longmapsto (F\circ\tilde{\mbff}^\star)(\mu)
\end{equation}
is well-defined on~$\msP$ and $\mcQ_\pi$-square-integrable. Its class~$u\eqdef \class[\mcQ_\pi]{\tilde{u}}$ is independent of the choice of representatives for the~$f_i$'s and satisfies
\[
u\in \msD(\mcE_\pi)\qquad \text{and} \qquad \mcG_\pi(u)=\sum_{i,j}^{k,k} (\partial_i F\cdot\partial_j F) \circ \tilde{\mbff}^\star \cdot \mathsf{\Gamma}(\hat f_i, \hat g_j)^\star \quad \mcQ_\pi\text{-a.e.}\,\mathrm{.}
\]

\begin{proof}
It suffices to show the statement for~$\tilde{u} = \tilde{f}^\star$. The conclusion for~$\tilde{u}$ as in~(equation eq:l:FullDomain:0 of the paper) follows by the diffusion property for~$\mcG_\pi$.
Let~$\left(f_n\right)_n\subset \msA$ be $\mssE^{1/2}_1$-convergent to~$f$ and consider the sequence~$\left(f_n^\star\right)_n$.
By Theorem~(t:TransferP of the paper)(i:t:TransferP:2 of the paper), by~(equation eq:l:DiffusionP:0.1 of the paper), and since~$f\mapsto f^\star$ is linear on~$\msA$,
\begin{align}
\nonumber
\mcE(f^\star_n-f^\star_m)=&\ \widehat\boldsymbol\mssE_\pi\big({(f_n^\star-f_m^\star) \circ\mathrm{em}}\big)
\\
\nonumber
=& \int \boldsymbol{\mathsf{\Gamma}}^\mbfs\paren{\sum_i s_i (f_n-f_m)({\,\cdot\,}_i)}_{(\mbfs,\mbfx)} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\widehat\boldsymbol\nu_\pi(\mbfs,\mbfx)
\\
\nonumber
=& \int\!\!\!\!\!\int \sum_i s_i \mathsf{\Gamma}(f_n-f_m)_{x_i} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol\nu(\mbfx)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\pi(\mbfs)
\\
\nonumber
=& \int \sum_i s_i \int \mathsf{\Gamma}(f_n-f_m)_{x_i}\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\nu(x_i)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}\pi(\mbfs)
\\

=&\ \mssE(f_n-f_m) \,\mathrm{.}
\end{align}
Together with Lemma~(l:SimpleTridLp of the paper), the equality in~(equation eq:l:DomainCylinderF:1 of the paper) shows that~$\left(f_n^\star\right)_n$ is $\mcE^{1/2}_1$-fund\-amental.
As a consequence of Lemma~(l:SimpleTridLp of the paper)(i:l:SimpleTridLp:3 of the paper) there exists~$\lim_{n} f_n^\star= f^\star$, thus~$f^\star\in\msD(\mcE_\pi)$ by closability of~$(\mcE_\pi,\msD(\mcE_\pi))$.
The independence of~$\mcG_\pi(u)$ from the representatives~$\tilde{f_i}$'s is straightforward.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma eq:l:FullDomain:0 of arXiv:2411.14936

[Lemma lem:eq_split of arXiv:2505.09604, 'Exceptional force, uncountably many solutions in the KPZ fixed point'] The following holds on the event $\Omega_1$, for all $\xi \in \Xi$ and all $b \in \mathcal{F}^\xi$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
\item  For $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and all $x,y \ge \tau_t^{b,R}$, $b(y,t) - b(x,t) = W^{\xi +}(x,t;y,t)$. For all $x,y \le \tau_t^{b,L}$, $b(y,t) - b(x,t) = W^{\xi -}(x,t;y,t)$.
\item  If for all $t \in \mathbb{R}, \tau_t^{b,R}$ are finite, then for all $t,s \in \mathbb{R}$, 
\[
b(\tau_t^{b,R},t) - b(\tau_s^{b,R},s) =W^{\xi+}(\tau_s^{b,R},s;\tau_t^{b,R},t).
\]
\item   If for all $t \in \mathbb{R}, \tau_t^{b,L}$ are finite, then for all $t,s \in \mathbb{R}$, 
\[
b(\tau_t^{b,L},t) - b(\tau_s^{b,L},s) =W^{\xi-}(\tau_s^{b,L},s;\tau_t^{b,L},t).
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:eq_split of arXiv:2505.09604

[Definition def: BB Couplings of arXiv:2607.17393, 'Optimal Covariance Estimates for Schr\"odinger Semigroups with White Noise in $d=1,2$'] We take $B_1^{0,0}$ to mean a standard Brownian Bridge in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d\in\{1,2\}$ that satisfies $B^{0,0}_1(0)=B_1^{0,0}(1)=0$. For $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $t>0$, we define $B_t^{x,x}(u)$ by the coupling \[B^{x,x}_t(u) = x+\sqrt{t}B_1^{0,0}(u/t)\] In words, this is a Brownian Bridge from $x$ to $x$ in time $t$ with one specific choice of coupling over all $x,t$. Similarly, we use $\overline{B}^{y,y}_s$ to denote an independent Brownian Bridge,
with the same coupling over $y\in\mathbb R^d$ and $s>0$.
title: Definition def: BB Couplings of arXiv:2607.17393

body: [Definition d:included-curve of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $\gamma,\tilde{\gamma}$ be two curves which are of type $\operatorname{I}$ or $\operatorname{II}$. We say that $\tilde{\gamma}\preccurlyeq\gamma$ if there exists a bijective and increasing map $\tau:[0,1]\rightarrow[0,1]$, and such that, for every $t\in[0,1]$, $\tilde{\gamma}(t)\in\mathcal{L}_{\gamma\circ\tau(t)}$.

		solution for every $D$ and every length: a unique steady law,

		sign-changing equilibria of the unconstrained equation consists
		entirely of non-monotone profiles and therefore lies outside the
		probability cone: constrained to laws, the bifurcation diagram
		collapses to a single branch. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 9 (Weak sub-solution) of arXiv:2608.26834, 'Small-time annealed large deviations principle for one-dimensional diffusions in a random '] A nonnegative function $u$ on $(0,S)\times D$ is called a bounded weak sub-solution  of the differential equation
		\begin{equation}
			\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}={\mathcal L}_W u
		\end{equation}
		if
		\[
		u\in L^\infty((0,S)\times D) \cap L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,S);H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)),
		\]
		and, for every nonnegative $\varphi\in C_c^1((0,S);H_0^1(D)\cap L^\infty(D))$, one has
		\begin{equation*}
			-\int_0^S\!\int_Du\,\partial_s\varphi\,\dd \mu_W\dd s
			+\int_0^S\mathcal E_W(u(s),\varphi(s))\,\dd s\le0.
		\end{equation*}
		If equality holds for all such $\varphi$, then $u$ is called a weak solution.

\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (a)}]

\item   $(${\bf  $\mssW_{p, \mssd_\U}$-contraction}$)$ Let $1 \le p <\infty$.  {Then, $\mcT_t^{\U, \QP} \nu$ is well-defined for $\nu \in \overline{\mcP_{\Theta}}^{\mssW_{p, \mssd_\U}}$. Furthermore, for $\nu, \sigma \in \overline{\mcP_{\Theta}}^{\mssW_{p, \mssd_\U}}$,}

$$\mssW_{p, \mssd_\U}(\mcT_t^{\U, \QP} \nu, \mcT_t^{\U, \QP}\sigma) \le e^{-Kt}\mssW_{p, \mssd_\U}(\nu, \sigma)  \fstop$$

\item  $(${\bf  Wang's log-Harnack inequality}$)$ for every non-negative bounded Borel function $u: \U \to \R_+$ and $t>0$, 
\begin{align} 
T^{\U, \QP}_t\log u(\gamma) \le \log (T^{\U, \QP}_tu(\eta)) + \frac{{\mssd}_\U(\gamma, \eta)^2}{4I_{2K}(t)}\comma \quad \text{$\gamma, \eta \in \Theta$} \scolon
\end{align}
where $I_K(t) :=\int_0^t e^{Kr}\diff r=\frac{e^{Kt}-1}{K}$. 

\item  $(${\bf  $p$-Bakry--\'Emery gradient estimate}$)$    The Bakry--\'Emery $p$-gradient estimate $\BE_p(K,\infty)$ holds for every $1 \le p <\infty$$:$
 $$\cdc^{\U}(T_t^{\U, \QP}u)^{\frac{p}{2}} \le  e^{-pKt}T_t^{\U, \QP}\bigl(\cdc^{\U}(u)^{\frac{p}{2}}\bigr) \quad \text{$\QP$-a.e.~} \quad u \in \dom{\E^{\U, \QP}} \fstop$$

[Definition 4 (Martingale representation problem) of arXiv:2608.03412, 'A McKean--Vlasov semigroup and its application to a martingale representation problem'] Let $G:\Pc(\R^d)\to\R$ be given. A pair of Borel maps
\[
Y:[0,T]\times\Pc(\R^d)\to\R,
\qquad
Z:[0,T]\times\R^d\times\Pc(\R^d)\to\R^d
\]
is called a solution of the martingale representation problem associated with
$G$ if the following property holds.

For every initial time $e\in[0,T]$, every initial law $m\in\Pc(\R^d)$,
and every admissible conditional law flow $(\nu_r)_{r\in[e,T]}$ generated by
a bounded Lipschitz drift $\beta$, namely
\[
\mathrm{d}X_r
=
\beta(r,X_r,\nu_r)\,\mathrm{d}r
+\mathrm{d}W_r+\sigma_\circ\,\mathrm{d}W^\circ_r,
\qquad
\nu_r=\Lc(X_r\mid\Gc_r),
\qquad
\nu_e=m,
\]
the following integrability condition is satisfied:
\[
\E\left[
\sup_{r\in[e,T]} |Y(r,\nu_r)|
+
\int_e^T
\left(
|Z(r,X_r,\nu_r)|
+
\left|
\E[Z(r,X_r,\nu_r)\mid\Gc_r]
\right|^2
\right)\mathrm{d}r
\right]
<\infty,
\]
and, $\P$-a.s., for every $t\in[e,T]$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y(t,\nu_t)
=
G(\nu_T)
-
\int_t^T
\E\Big[
Z(r,X_r,\nu_r)\cdot\beta(r,X_r,\nu_r)
\,\Big|\,\Gc_r
\Big]\mathrm{d}r
-
\int_t^T
\E\Big[
Z(r,X_r,\nu_r)
\,\Big|\,\Gc_r
\Big]\cdot\sigma_\circ\,\mathrm{d}W^\circ_r .
\end{aligned}
\]
title: Martingale representation problem

Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: A finite-horizon input coupling suggests a cubic collision scale. Fix k tagged servers. Jobs arrive at rate Lambda=lambda*n/k and choose a uniform k-subset. If N is the number of tagged servers hit by an arrival, E[N(N-1)]=k*(k-1)*k*(k-1)/(n*(n-1)). Remove arrivals that hit at least two tagged queues and restore their lost marginal rates by independent Poisson streams. A union bound on removed events and added events is at most (3/2)*Lambda*T*E[N(N-1)], hence at most 3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)). The resulting streams are independent with the correct marginal rates. With independent task marks and queues initially empty, this also bounds total variation of their workload paths on [0,T]. Extending the credited source coupling to stationary starts gives TV<=2*k*r(T)+3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)), where r(T) is the stationary marginal emptying tail. With independent exponential service of rate mu>lambda, a stopped generator calculation gives r(T)<=(1+sqrt(lambda/mu))*exp(-(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2*T). Taking T=2*log(n)/(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2 gives sufficient k=o((n/log(n))^(1/3)). A conditional polynomial tail r(T)<=C*T^(-p) gives sufficient exponent p/(3*p+1). Check: The hypergeometric factorial moment follows by summing ordered pairs of tagged-server indicators. On N>=2, both 1<=N(N-1)/2 and N<=N(N-1), giving the factor 3/2. Small subset enumeration checks the moment exactly. Separate exact checks cover 77 hypergeometric/restoration cases, 81 generator identities, nine geometric exponential moments and five polynomial balancing identities. The complete packet explicitly checks stationary coupling, marginal rate restoration, PASTA and heavy-traffic limits; these are author checks, not independent review. [Lemma 14 of arXiv:2609.02581, '\bfseries Interior Curvature Estimates for the Graphical Scalar Curvature Equation in All '] Let \(B_1\subset\mathbb R^n\), and suppose that
\[
 u,v\in C^2(B_1)\cap C^1(\overline{B_1}),
 \qquad
 \kappa[v]\in\Gamma_2,
\]
with
\[
 v\geq u\quad\text{in }B_1,
 \qquad
 v=u\quad\text{on }\partial B_1,
 \qquad
 \lVert Du\rVert_{L^\infty(B_1)}\leq K.
\]
Set
\[
 \tilde{d}(x):=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial B_1)=1-|x|.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 0\leq v(x)-u(x)
 \leq (1+K)\left(\sqrt{2\,\tilde{d}(x)}+\tilde{d}(x)\right)
 \qquad\text{for every }x\in B_1.
 
\end{equation}

body:
[Definition def:FktdAJs of arXiv:2609.02588, 'Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games'] Let $k,t,d,s,r$ be positive integers with $t\geq d \geq 2$ and $k\geq r$,
let $\mathcal{A} \subseteq \binom{[t]\setminus \{1\}}{d-1}$
and $\mathcal{K}\in \binom{[t]\setminus \{1\}}{d-1} \setminus \mathcal{A}$.
We define $\mathcal{F}_s(k,t,d,\mathcal{A},\mathcal{K},r)$ to be the family of all 
$d$-uniform hypergraphs
$\mathcal{H}$ that satisfy the following property:
There exists a partition of the vertex set $V(\mathcal{H}) = V_1\cup \ldots \cup V_t$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $|V_i| = k$ for every $i\in [t]$,
\item[(ii)] $|e\cap V_i| \leq 1$ for every $i\in [t]$ and $e\in E(\mathcal{H})$,
\item[(iii)] for every $i\in [t]$, every vertex $v\in V_i$, 
every index set $J\in \binom{[t]\setminus [i]}{d-1}$ and every choice of sets
$A_j\in \binom{V_j}{s}$ for $j\in J$, we have 
$e_{\mathcal{H}}\big( \{v\}\cup \bigcup_{j\in J} A_j\big) \neq 0$,
\item[(iv)] for every $v\in V_1$ and every $J\in \mathcal{A}$ we have 
	$\mathcal{H}_v\big[ \bigcup_{j\in J} V_j \big] \cong H_{k,d-1,d-1}$,
\item[(v)] there exists a set $X_1 \in \binom{V_1}{r}$ such that 
	 $\mathcal{H}_v\big[ \bigcup_{j\in \mathcal{K}} V_j \big] \cong H_{k,d-1,d-1}$ for every $v\in X_1$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:FktdAJs of arXiv:2609.02588

[Prop pr.Topo of arXiv:2411.13099, 'Long time behavior of killed Feynman-Kac semigroups with singular Schr{ö}dinger potentials'] Let $(L_t,t\ge 0)$ be a purely jump Lévy process over $\mathscr R^d$ such that its  Lévy measure $\nu$ has full topological support over $\mathscr R_0^d$, i.e. for all $y\in \mathscr R^d_0$ and all $r\in (0,|y|)$, $\nu(B(y,r))>0$, and such that for some $\beta >0$, 
 $$\int_{|u|\le 1}|u|^\beta \nu(du)<+\infty.$$  Let $\mathscr O$ be a subdomain of $\mathscr R^d$. 
 Let  $T>0$ and $x,z\in \mathscr O$. Then,  for all $\epsilon>0$, 
 \begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_x[|L_T-z|<\epsilon, T<\sigma _{\mathscr O}]>0,
 \end{equation}
 where $\sigma_{\mathscr O}:=\inf\{t\ge 0, L_t\notin \mathscr O\}$. 
 In addition, if $\mathscr R^d\setminus \overline{\mathscr O}$ is nonempty, for all $x\in \mathscr O$, $\mathbb P_x[\sigma_{\mathscr O}<+\infty ]>0$.
title: Prop pr.Topo of arXiv:2411.13099

body:
[Prop number of components in MRSC of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $X_n \sim \MRSC_d(n; \bm{p})$ satisfying Assumption~(assumption: prob parameters of the paper). Let $C_n$ denote the number of $d$-dimensional connected components in $X_n$. Then, it holds that
\[
\frac{C_n}{s_{d-1}(X_n)} \overset{\mathbb{P}}{\to} \gamma_{\lambda} - \lambda \frac{d}{d+1} \gamma_{\lambda}^{d+1},
\]
where $\gamma_{\lambda}$ is the extinction probability of a branching process with offspring distribution $d \mathsf{Poi}(\lambda)$, i.e., $\gamma_{\lambda}$ is the smallest solution to $\gamma = e^{-\lambda(1 - \gamma^d)}$.
title: Prop number of components in MRSC of arXiv:2605.03151

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let $\Phi$, $A$, $\mathbf{P}$, $\mu$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $V$ be as in Theorem \ref{thm:polydifdrift} and let all conditions of Theorem \ref{thm:polydifdrift} except \eqref{prop:eq0} and \eqref{prop:eq2} be satisfied. Then a sufficient condition for \eqref{prop:eq0} and \eqref{prop:eq2} to hold is given by
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $\mathrm{deg} (\mathbf{B})\le 2m-2$, where $m=\mathrm{deg}(\Phi)$, and
\item[(ii)] $-\Phi_m(x)>0$ for every $x\in S^{d-1}:=\{x\in \R^d\,| \, \|x\|=1\}$.
\end{itemize}
In particular, Theorem \ref{thm:polydifdrift} applies and in addition, the regularized semigroup associated with the
$L^1$-closed extension of $(L^{\widetilde{\mathbf P}},C^\infty_0(\mathbb R^d))$
is conservative.

Positive-axis continuation and nonnegative coefficients give summability below the root; a noncanceled E-zero pole gives divergence at and above it. [Corollary Constant alternating regret for polyhedral OLO of arXiv:2608.24731, 'Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games\thanks{Authors are alphabetically'] \label[corollary]{cor:polytope}
Let $\mathcal X=\operatorname{conv}\{\boldsymbol{v}_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol{v}_N\}$ be a  polytope. Consider  linear losses $f_t(\boldsymbol{x})=\langle \boldsymbol{c}_t,\boldsymbol{x}\rangle$, with $f_t(\boldsymbol{x})\in[-1,1]$ for every $\boldsymbol{x}\in\+X$. Running (alg:main of the paper) with $\mu$ being the uniform distribution on $\{\boldsymbol{v}_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol{v}_N\}$ gives
\[
  \max_{\boldsymbol{u}\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{Reg}_{\mathrm{Alt}}^T(\boldsymbol{u})\le8\log N.
\]
In particular, for $\mathcal X=\Delta_d$ and $\boldsymbol{c}_t\in[-1,1]^d$, (alg:main of the paper) coincides with (alg:variance hedge of the paper) and recovers the bound $8\log d$.

[Lemma 106 (Proportional distinct-speed phase gap) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $\parvec$ satisfy \eqref{eq:parameter-vector}.  There exist
$\delta_0=\delta_0(\parvec)>0$, $N_{\mathrm{sp}}=N_{\mathrm{sp}}(\parvec)\ge2$,
and $c_{\mathrm{sp}}=c_{\mathrm{sp}}(\parvec)>0$ such that, whenever
\[
  |\ell|\sim N,\qquad N\ge N_{\mathrm{sp}},
  \qquad |q|\le\delta_0|\ell|,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
  |\omega_a(\ell+q)-\omega_b(\ell)|
  \ge c_{\mathrm{sp}}N,
  \qquad a\ne b.
\end{equation}
Every sum phase in \eqref{eq:two-frequency-phases} has the same type of lower
bound.  Consequently
\begin{equation}
  |\Phi_{a|b}^{\eps_1,\eps_2}(q,\ell)|
  \ge c_{\mathrm{sp}}N
\end{equation}
for every sign branch generated by a same-color block.  The constants
$\delta_0$, $N_{\mathrm{sp}}$, and $c_{\mathrm{sp}}$ depend only on the
dispersive parameters and the Littlewood--Paley support constants; they are
independent of $\mathfrak h_{\W}$ and $\mathfrak h_{\K}$.
title: Proportional distinct-speed phase gap

For each integer $j\in\llbracket0,s-1\rrbracket$ let the pair $(\l_{j,0},\l_{j,-1})\in (\mathbb N\cup\{0\})\times\llbracket0,m-1\rrbracket$ be such that 
$$\Big\lfloor\frac{l_{j+1}}{p^{j+1}}-(p-1)\sum_{i=1}^j\frac{l_i}{p^i}\Big\rfloor=m\l_{j,0}+\l_{j,-1};$$
e.g., $(\l_{0,0},\l_{0,-1})\in (\mathbb N\cup\{0\})\times\llbracket0,m-1\rrbracket$ is such that $\lfloor\frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor=m\l_{0,0}+\l_{0,-1}$. Let $b\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$ and let the pair $(\q_{s,b},\r_{s,b})\in \mathbb Z\times\llbracket0,m-1\rrbracket$ be such that $\delta_s(b-1)-\delta_s(b)=m\q_{s,b}+\r_{s,b}$.  Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} If either $a=[0]_m$ with $\delta_s(b)\ge 1$ (i.e., with $b\le p^s-2$) or $a\neq [0]_m$, then we have identities
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}\mu_X(a,b)=&\q_{s,b}+\Big\lfloor\frac{\delta_s(b)-1+\r_{-a}+\r_{s,b}}{m}\Big\rfloor-\Big\lfloor\frac{\delta_s(b)-1+\r_{-a}}{m}\Big\rfloor\\
=&\begin{cases}\q_{s,b}+1\quad\;\textup{if}\quad \r_{\delta_s(b)-1+\r_{-a}}+\r_{s,b}\ge m\\
\q_{s,b}\quad\quad\quad\textup{if}\quad \r_{\delta_s(b)-1+\r_{-a}}+\r_{s,b}<m.\end{cases}
\end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular, we have $\mu_X(a,b)=\q_{s,b}+1$ if and only if $\r_{s,b}\neq 0$ (i.e., $\r_{s,b}\in\llbracket1,m-1\rrbracket$) and $a\in [\delta_s(b)]_m+\{[i]_m|i\in\llbracket0,\r_{s,b}-1\rrbracket\}$.

{\bf (2)} We have identities 
\begin{equation*}
\q_{s,p^s-1}=\Big\lfloor\frac{\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor+1}{m}\Big\rfloor=\begin{cases}\l_{0,0}+1\quad\textup{if}\quad\l_{0,-1}=m-1\\
\l_{0,0}\quad\quad\;\;\,\textup{if}\quad \l_{0,-1}\in\llbracket0,m-2\rrbracket,\end{cases}
\end{equation*} 
$\r_{s,p^s-1}=\Big\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\Big\rfloor+1-m\Big\lfloor\frac{\lfloor \frac{l_1}{p}\rfloor+1}{m}\Big\rfloor$, and

\end{split}
\end{equation}

$$\mu_X([0]_m,p^s-1)\le\mu_X(a,p^s-1)\le \mu_X([0]_m,p^s-1)+1.$$

        S_\star\bigg(\lambda',\mu';
        	\frac\epsilon5,\frac\epsilon2-\delta_0
        	\bigg)\,.
    \end{align}
for all $(\lambda',\mu') \in B_{\delta_0}(\lambda,\mu)$.

        \subseteq S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;
        	\frac\epsilon5,\frac\epsilon2\bigg)
        =K_2\,.\]
Abbreviate $u_\mu\equiv (0^{3r},\mu)$, and recall from \eqref{e:D.mu.affine.closure} that the affine space $\mathcal{F}_\mu$ is defined by the constraint $(\YY,u_\mu)=1$. In the above definition of $P$, we can assume without loss that none of the $H_j$ have normal vector parallel to $u_\mu$: such $H_j$ are redundant because of the intersection with $\cD_\mu$.

        \cQ \equiv \bigg\{

    \]
must be a subset of the extreme points of $P$ (the points that cannot be written as a convex combination of two other points in $P$). Therefore, $\cQ$ is a discrete set.
    Moreover, Lemma~\ref{l:S.star.nbd.in.S.star.eps} implies

        S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] \subseteq

that we denote

	\tilde{P}_{\mu'}

	\]

If $\YY\in \mathrm{int}(\tilde{P}_\mu;\mathcal{F}_\mu)$, then for all $\YY'$ orthogonal to $u_\mu$ with $\|\YY'\|$ small enough, we must have $\YY+\YY' \in\tilde{P}_\mu$. body: In mathematics, specifically in homology theory and algebraic topology, cohomology is a way of attaching algebraic invariants to a topological space or other mathematical object that encode its properties in a way that is often computable. Cohomology is often related to questions of whether some local property of the space is obstructed when passing to a global property. For example, the Möbius strip is not the product space of a line segment with a circle, but locally on any segment of the circle it resembles an ordinary rectangle without the global twist. The obstruction to making the product structure global is encoded in the first cohomology of the underlying circle, which classifies the two inequivalent ways a line can twist around a circle. The fact that there are only two inequivalent ways of twisting a line around a circle is encoded in the relevant cohomology group which can be computed as isomorphic to the group where corresponds to an even number of twists, and to an odd number.
title: Cohomology

[Lemma lemma_time_scaling of arXiv:2411.08846, 'On the Number of Crossings and Bouncings\\ of a Diffusion at a Sticky Threshold'] [e.g.,~[Anagnostakis2022], Corollary~2.7]

The probability transition kernel of the sticky Brownian motion with respect to its speed measure 
$m_{\rho}(\mathrm{d} x) = \,\mathrm{d} x + \rho \delta_0(\mathrm{d} x)$ satisfies for
all $c,\rho,t>0 $ and $x,y\in \IR $
\begin{equation}
	p_{\rho}(ct,x,y)m_{\rho}(\mathrm{d} y)
	= p_{\rho/\sqrt{c}}(t,x/\sqrt{c},y)m_{\rho/\sqrt{c}}(\mathrm{d} y).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Review-only DRAFT of a worker-derived identity, not an accepted FEI proof. For Boolean f under uniform measure, let H be Shannon entropy in bits of squared normalized Walsh coefficients, and Delta_i=H(f)-[H(f_i^+)+H(f_i^-)]/2. For restriction coefficients u_T,v_T put w_T=(u_T^2+v_T^2)/2, p_T=u_T^2/(u_T^2+v_T^2), q_T=(u_T-v_T)^2/[2(u_T^2+v_T^2)]. Omit zero weights. Then sum w_T=1, Inf_i(f)=sum w_T q_T and Delta_i=sum w_T[1+h_2(q_T)-h_2(p_T)], where h_2 is binary entropy with zero endpoint terms. In particular 0<=Delta_i<=2. The extra imbalance term is nonnegative and cannot be dropped for an upper bound.

$$
V_{*}(A)<\alpha<\alpha_{*}=-\limsup_{K\to\infty}\frac{\log(\lambda_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}})}{K}\;.
$$
Let $\mathcal{T}(A,\,\alpha,\, K,\,({\underline N^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}}(\,\raisebox{0.4mm}{\scalebox{0.6}{\textbullet}}\,)))$ be the amount time a 
trajectory spends outside $A$ in the time interval 
$\big[0,\,\exp(K\,\alpha) \big]$, namely
$$
\mathcal{T}(A,\,\alpha,\,
K,\,({\underline N^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}}(\,\raisebox{0.4mm}{\scalebox{0.6}{\textbullet}}\,)))=\int_{0}^{\exp(K\,\alpha) }
\mathbbm{1}_{K*A^{c}}\big({\underline N^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}}(s)\big)\,ds\;.
$$
Then for any $\epsilon>0$
$$
\lim_{K\to\infty}{{\mathds P}}^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}}\left(\frac{\mathcal{T}(A,\,\alpha,\,
 K,\,({\underline N^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}}(\,\raisebox{0.4mm}{\scalebox{0.6}{\textbullet}}\,)))}{e^{\alpha\,K}}
\in\big[(1-\epsilon)\,\mu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}\big(K*A^{c}\big),\,
(1+\epsilon)\,\mu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}\big(K*A^{c}\big)\big]
\right)=1.
$$

	0, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition defn:core of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Take any $m\in \mathbb N$, $\vec \mathbf k \in \mathbb R^m_+ $, and $\vec \boldsymbol{\tau}\in \mathbb R^m$ such that $\boldsymbol{\tau}_1\le \cdots \le \boldsymbol{\tau}_m$, and denote $\mathbf Q_\ell = \sum_{\ell'=1}^\ell \mathbf k_{\ell'}$ for each $\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$.
We let
\[
\mathbf L_\beta(\vec\mathbf k, \vec\boldsymbol{\tau}) = \mathrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathscr K[\vec\mathbf k]} \exp\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^{m-1}
(\boldsymbol{\tau}_\ell-\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\ell+1}) \mathbf H(\mathbf Q_\ell)/2 \right)\mathbf I_{\beta,\vec\mathbf k}[\vec \mathbf p, \vec\boldsymbol{\upsilon}, \mathbf H] \mathrm d(\vec\mathbf p,  \vec\boldsymbol{\upsilon},\mathbf H),
\]
where the principal value integral is taken in the following sense.
For any small enough $\epsilon>0$, we let  $\mathscr K_\epsilon=\mathscr K_\epsilon[\vec\mathbf k]$ denote the space of all blocks $(\vec\mathbf p, \vec\boldsymbol{\upsilon}, \mathbf H)\in \mathscr K[\vec \mathbf k]$, such that for each $\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$, $\mathbf p^0$ is constant in $(\mathbf Q_{\ell-1}, \mathbf Q_{\ell-1}+\epsilon)$, and either $\boldsymbol{\upsilon}_\ell>\epsilon$, or $\boldsymbol{\upsilon}_\ell=\varnothing$.
We integrate over $\mathscr K_\epsilon$, then send $\epsilon\to 0+$.
title: Definition defn:core of arXiv:2411.10829

[Proposition 43 (Uniform shifted fourth-moment criterion) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Suppose that the shifted-profile expansions for \(m_f\) and \(q_f\) hold and that
\[
\lim_{R\to\infty}\limsup_{\delta\downarrow0}
\sup_{|s|\le\delta}
\E\bigl[|f(\zeta+s)|^4{\bf 1}_{\{|f(\zeta+s)|>R\}}\bigr]=0.
\]
Assume also that
\[
        \E |f(\zeta+s)|^4\longrightarrow \E |f(\zeta)|^4
        \qquad(s\to0).
\]
Then the shifted fourth-cumulant stability and shifted fourth-moment Lindeberg parts of Condition~\ref{cond:profile-admissibility} hold.

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph of maximal degree at most $\Delta$, and for each $(u,v)\in E$ we are given constants $\beta_{uv}$ where $|\beta_{uv}|\leq\beta$ for all edges. Fix an arbitrary external field $h=(h_u)_{u\in V}$, an arbitrary subset $A\subset V$ and configuration $\tau\in\{0,1\}^A$. Then whenever $\beta\leq\frac{1}{\Delta}$, the measure $\mu_{\beta,h}$ defined on $\{0,1\}^{V\setminus A}$ via
$$
\mu_{\beta,h}(\sigma)\propto\exp(\sum_{(u,v)\in E}\beta_{uv}\sigma_u\sigma_v+\sum_{u\in V\setminus A}h_u\sigma_u),\quad\forall\sigma\in\{0,1\}^V:\sigma|_A=\tau
$$satisfies approximate tensorization of variance and approximate tensorization of entropy with constant 2.

[Defn qcdens of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] [coornaert-pjm] 
For $(X,d)$ Gromov-hyperbolic, let $M(\partial_g X)$ denote the collection of positive finite Borel measures on $\partial_g X $. A $G$-equivariant map $X \to M(\partial_g X)$ sending $x \to \mu_x$ is said to be a $C$ {\bf quasi-conformal density} of dimension $v$ ($v\geq 0$), for some $C\geq 1$, if
\begin{equation}
	\frac{1}{C}\exp\big(-v\beta_\xi(y,x)\big)
	\leq
	\frac{{\rm{d}}\mu_{x}}{{\rm{d}}\mu_y} (\xi)
	\leq C \exp\big(-v\beta_\xi(y,x)\big)
\end{equation}
for all $x, y \in X$, $\xi\in \partial X$. If $C=1$, it is a {\bf conformal density}. Equivalently, we also call the family of measures $(\mu_x)_{x\in G}$ a (quasi)-conformal density.
title: Defn qcdens of arXiv:2411.14350

[Lemma lem:quotient-properties of arXiv:2609.02845, 'Degeneracy bounds, stability, and a sharp gap for $B$-colorings'] The false-twin quotient $Q$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item Every false-twin class is an independent set in $G$.
  \item Between two distinct false-twin classes there are either all
        possible edges or no edges.
  \item For every $X\in V(Q)$,
        \[
          \sum_{Y\in N_Q(X)}w(Y)=\Delta.
        \]
  \item Distinct vertices of $Q$ have distinct open neighborhoods
        in $Q$.
  \item The graph $Q$ is nonbipartite.
  \item The graph $Q$ is connected.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Prop bvp of arXiv:2411.05441, 'Sticky diffusions on star graphs : characterization and It\^o formula'] For every $\delta > 0$ and $f \in \bigoplus_{i=1}^N C_b([0,\delta))$, with $f_i(0) = f_j(0)$ for all $1 \leq i,j \leq N$, there is a unique $u \in \bigoplus_{i=1}^N C^2([0,\delta])$ such that
 \begin{equation}
  \begin{cases}
   L_i u_i(x) = f_i(x) \quad & \textnormal{for all } x \in (0, \delta), \, 1 \leq i \leq N, \\
	\eta L u (\mathsf{v}) - \sum_{i=1}^N \rho_i {u_i}'(0) = 0, \\
	u_i(\delta) = 0 \quad & \textnormal{for all } i \in \{1,\dots, N \}, \\
	u_i(0) = u_j(0) \quad & \textnormal{for all } i,j \in \{1,\dots, N \},
  \end{cases}
 \end{equation}
 given by
 \[
  u_i(x) = - \frac{\kappa_i  \alpha_i(x)}{\alpha_i(0)} - \beta_i(x) \quad \textnormal{for all } 0 \leq x \leq \delta,
  \]
  where
  \begin{align*}
  \kappa_i & = \left (\eta f(\mathsf{v}) - \sum_{j=1}^N \frac{\rho_j(\beta_1(0) - \beta_j(0))}{ \alpha_j(0)} \right ) \left (\sum_{j=1}^N \frac{\rho_j}{\alpha_j(0)} \right )^{-1} + \beta_1(0) - \beta_i(0) \\
  \alpha_i(x) & = \int_x^\delta \exp \left (-\int_0^y \frac{2b_i(z)}{\sigma_i^2(z)} dz \right) dy \\
  \beta_i (x) & = \int_x^\delta \left ( \int_0^y \frac{2 f(z)}{\sigma_i^2(z)} \exp \left (\int_0^z \frac{2b_i(s)}{\sigma_i^2(s)} ds  \right) dz \right ) \exp \left (-\int_0^y \frac{2b_i(z)}{\sigma_i^2(z)} dz \right) dy
 \end{align*}
 for all $1 \leq i \leq N$.
 Furthermore, we have 
 \[
  \max_{1 \leq i \leq N} \max_{x \in [0,\delta]} \left \lvert u_i''(x) \right  \rvert = O(1) \quad  \textnormal{as } \delta \downarrow 0,
 \]
 where the hidden constant only depends on $f$ through $\lVert f \rVert_{\infty}$.

body: In probability theory, Bernstein inequalities give bounds on the probability that the sum of random variables deviates from its mean. In the simplest case, let X_{1},..., X_{n} be independent Bernoulli random variables taking values +1 and −1 with probability 1/2 (this distribution is also known as the Rademacher distribution), then for every positive $\varepsilon$, $$\mathbb {P} \left(\left|{\frac {1}{n}}\sum _{i=1}^{n}X_{i}\right|>\varepsilon \right)\leq 2\exp \left(-{\frac {n\varepsilon ^{2}}{2(1+{\frac {\varepsilon }{3}})}}\right).$$

[Theorem 57 (\cite{Keller_Liverani}) of arXiv:2609.04153, '\vspace*{-3cm}Smooth autonomous fast dynamo action on the three-torus'] Let $(X,\|\cdot \|_{X})$ be a Banach space, embedding compactly into the Banach space $(Y,\|\cdot \|_{Y})$, so that furthermore $\|\cdot \|_{Y} \leq \|\cdot \|_{X}$. Let $(\mathcal{F},d_\mathcal{F})$, $(\mathcal{G},d_{\mathcal{G}})$ be two metric spaces, so that $(\mathcal{G},d_{\mathcal{G}})$ is compact.
Let $\{\cL_{u,g}\}_{u \in \mathcal{F},g \in \mathcal{G}}$ be a collection of bounded operators on $X$, which extend to bounded operators on $Y$, and so that for every fixed $u \in \mathcal{F}$, the map $g \mapsto \cL_{u,g}$ is continuous in the operator norm topology. Finally, assume that the $\cL_{u,g}$ satisfy the following: there exist constants $C,\alpha, M>0$, $\alpha <M$, so that for all $u \in \mathcal{F}, g \in \mathcal{G}$, $m \in \NN$ it holds 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\|\cL_{u,g}^m B\|_{Y} \leq CM^m\|B\|_{Y}$
    \item $\|\cL_{u,g}^m B\|_{X} \leq C\alpha^m \|B\|_{X}+CM^m\|B\|_{Y}$
    \item $\|\cL_{u,g} B-\cL_{v,g} B\|_{Y} \leq \eta(d_{\mathcal{F}}(u,v))\|B\|_{X} $, where $\eta: \RR_+ \to \RR_+$ is some monotone, upper-semicontinuous function that tends to zero as its argument tends to zero.
\end{enumerate}
Assume further that there exists $u \in \mathcal{F}, g \in \mathcal{G}$, and $\lambda_0 \in \sigma_X(\cL_{u,g})$ corresponding to an algebraically simple eigenvalue, with $\alpha <|\lambda_0|<M$. Then, there exists an open set $G \subset \mathcal{G}$ containing $g$, so that for all $h \in G$, $\cL_{u,h}$ has an isolated, algebraically simple eigenvalue $\lambda_h \to \lambda_0$ as $h \to g$. Furthermore, there exists $\delta_{\mathcal F}>0$ so that for all $v \in B_{\delta_{\mathcal F}}(u)$, $\cL_{v,h}$ similarly has isolated, algebraically simple eigenvalues $\lambda_{h,v}$, and it holds \emph{uniformly} for $h \in G$ that $\lambda_{h,v} \to \lambda_h$, as $d_{\mathcal{F}}(u,v) \to 0$.

[Lemma 32 (Monotonicity of angles) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix a finite graph $G$, some $\beta\in[0,\infty)$.
    Let $u$ denote some vertex, and let $E_u$ denote the set of edges incident to $u$.
    Pick
    \[
        \tau'=(\alpha',\omega',\eta')\in [0,\pi/2]^{V\setminus\{u\}}\times\{0,1\}^{E\setminus E_u}\times\{0,1\}^{E\setminus E_u},
    \]
    Let $\mu_{\tau'}$ denote the measure
    $\mu_{G,\beta}$ conditioned on \[\{\tau|_{(V\setminus\{u\})\times (E\setminus E_u) \times (E\setminus E_u)}=\tau'\}.\]
    Then the density of $\alpha_u$ on $[0,\pi/2]$ under $\mu_{\tau'}$
      is proportional to
    \begin{align}
        \textstyle
        \left(
        \prod_{\Gamma\in C(\omega')}
        \textstyle
        2\cosh(\beta\cos\alpha_u\sum_{v \in \Gamma}\cos\alpha_v')
        \right)
        \left(
        \prod_{\Gamma\in C(\eta')}
        \textstyle
        2\cosh(\beta\sin\alpha_u\sum_{v\in \Gamma}\sin\alpha_v')
        \right),
\end{align}
where $C(\rho)$ is the partition of $\{v\in V:v\sim u\}$ into $\rho$-connected components.

In particular, if $\mu^{\alpha_u}_{\tau'}$ denotes the law of $\alpha_u$ under $\mu_{\tau'}$, then
\[
    \tau'\preceq\tau''
    \qquad
    \implies
    \qquad
    \mu^{\alpha_u}_{\tau'}\leqstoch\mu^{\alpha_u}_{\tau''}.
\]

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, paired). The per-output long-only stack on the relative-metric error covariance was shrunk toward the pooled simplex weights, $w_d \\mapsto w_g + (1 - s)(w_d - w_g)$. The ceiling of the family - the amount chosen by five-fold cross-validation on the calibration rows - adds $+0.59$ percent on EMIT and $+0.20$ on OCO-2 at full calibration (28 of 40 and 26 of 30 cells). A positive-part James-Stein amount $s = \\min(1, \\sum_d \\operatorname{tr} V_d / \\sum_d \\|w_d - w_g\\|^2)$ with $V_d$ the naive $n$-out-of-$n$ bootstrap covariance of the long-only weights over 20 resamples recovers $+0.10$ / $+0.15$ (worst cells $-2.6$ / $-0.0$) with amounts $0.18$ against the cross-validated $0.14$ on EMIT: it overshoots, because the long-only weights have coordinates at the boundary and the naive bootstrap is inconsistent there (Andrews 2000; resampled fits flip members between zero and positive weight). The $m$-out-of-$n$ subsampling repair ($m = n/2$, variance scaled by $m/n$; Politis-Romano) gives amounts $0.11$ / $0.12$ against $0.14$ / $0.57$ and gains $+0.43$ / $+0.09$ (worst $-1.3$ / $-0.0$). Reading: the residual pooling amount is not recoverable from resampling to the accuracy the ceiling requires and remains the one cross-validated quantity in the neighbourhood of the long-only estimator, which alone sits within that ceiling

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] Suppose that $p \ll 1$ and let $G \subseteq K_n$ be a graph with $O(f \log(1/p))$ edges.
  Suppose further that either $\eps_H = \infty$ or $\eps_H < \infty$ and $p \gg n^{-1/\Delta - \eps_H} (\log(1/p))^K$ for some large constant $K$ that depends only on $H$.
  Then
  \begin{equation*}
    \Ex_G[X]-\Ex[X] \leq \sum_{J\in \cJ} \frac{|\Emb(J,H)|}{|\Aut(H)|} \cdot N(J,G)\cdot n^{v_H-v_J}p^{e_H-e_J}+o(n^{v_H}p^{e_H}).
  \end{equation*}
  Furthermore, if $p \le n^{-1/\Delta-\Omega(1)}$, then

    \Ex_G[X]-\Ex[X] \leq \sum_{J\in \cJ^*} \frac{|\Emb(J,H)|}{|\Aut(H)|} \cdot N(J,G)\cdot n^{v_H-v_J}p^{e_H-e_J}+o(n^{v_H}p^{e_H}).

Disjoint boxes centered at j(2r+1)e_1 are independent. The first matching box exists almost surely, so its environment-measurable center matches with probability 1. The location is unrestricted; no directional-transience or full-target counterexample is asserted.

[Lemma 14 (Uniform local bound for zero-truncated Poisson sums) of arXiv:2604.26298, 'The Expiring Coupon Collector\\ Sliding-Window Surjection Flux and Rare-Entry Laws'] Let \(N\ge2\), \(m\ge N+1\), and let \(\tau=\tau_{N,m}>0\) be the unique
solution of
\[
        \frac{\tau}{1-e^{-\tau}}=\frac{m}{N}.
\]
Let \(D_1,\ldots,D_N\) be iid zero-truncated Poisson variables with parameter
\(\tau\):
\[
        \Pbb(D_i=k)=\frac{\tau^k}{k!(e^\tau-1)},\qquad k\ge1.
\]
Write
\[
        \mu_\tau=\Ebb D_i=\frac{\tau}{1-e^{-\tau}},
        \qquad
        \sigma_\tau^2=\Var(D_i),
        \qquad
        B=N\sigma_\tau^2.
\]
Assume \(0<\tau\le C_0\log N\). If \(B\to\infty\), then
\[
        \Pbb(D_1+\cdots+D_N=m)
        =
        \frac{1+o(1)}{\sqrt{2\pi B}},
\]
uniformly in this range. Consequently, for some constants \(c,C>0\),
depending only on \(C_0\),
\[
        \Pbb(D_1+\cdots+D_N=m)\ge c\,m^{-C}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(N\). If \(B\) is bounded, the same polynomial
lower bound still holds.
