body:
Let (P_t) be the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup on L^p of the standard Gaussian measure on R^n. For 1 < p <= q < infinity, || P_t f ||_q <= || f ||_p for every f, PROVIDED e^{-t} <= sqrt( (p-1)/(q-1) ). The constant is exactly 1 - the semigroup is a contraction from L^p to the strictly larger L^q, not merely bounded - and the condition on t is sharp. Two consequences used constantly: taking p = 2 gives || P_t f ||_q <= || f ||_2 for e^{-t} = 1/sqrt(q-1); and restricting to the n-th Wiener chaos, where P_t acts as multiplication by e^{-nt}, gives the MOMENT COMPARISON || F ||_q <= (q-1)^{n/2} || F ||_2 for every F in the n-th chaos and every q >= 2. That comparison is dimension-free and is the reason all L^q norms on a fixed chaos are equivalent, with a constant depending only on the chaos order and q. GROSS'S THEOREM: hypercontractivity of (P_t) with these exponents is EQUIVALENT to the logarithmic Sobolev inequality Ent(f^2) <= 2 E|grad f|^2 for the same measure; each implies the other by differentiating or integrating the relation at q = q(t). The discrete-cube analogue with the noise operator is the Bonami-Beckner inequality, and the Gaussian case follows from it by the central limit theorem. [Nelson (1966, 1973); Gross (1975); see Bakry, Gentil and Ledoux, Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators, Chapter 5]

[Theorem 8 (Stationary singularity in the supercritical regime) of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] Fix $N\geq1$ and assume $A>A_c(N)$. Let $\pi_{A,N}$ be the nonzero invariant
  law of $X^{(N)}$. Let $\beta_{A,N}\in(0,N)$ be the unique
  positive solution of
  \begin{equation*}
    A^{-\beta}N^{\beta/2}2^{-\beta/2}
    \frac{\Gamma((N-\beta)/2)}{\Gamma(N/2)}
    =
    1.
  \end{equation*}
  Here $\bar\sigma_N$ denotes normalized surface measure on
  $\mathbb S^{N-1}$. Then there is a constant $c_{A,N}>0$ such that, for every
  Borel set
  $B\subseteq\mathbb S^{N-1}$ satisfying $\bar\sigma_N(\partial B)=0$,
  \begin{equation*}
    s^{-\beta_{A,N}}\pi_{A,N}\left(
      0<\norm{x}_2\leq s,\,
      \frac{x}{\norm{x}_2}\in B
    \right)
    \longrightarrow
    c_{A,N}\bar\sigma_N(B)
    \qquad \mbox{as } s\downarrow0 .
  \end{equation*}
  In particular,
  \begin{equation*}
    \pi_{A,N}\left(0<\norm{x}_2\leq s\right)
    \sim
    c_{A,N}s^{\beta_{A,N}}
    \qquad \mbox{as } s\downarrow0 .
  \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Bubeck and Sellke (2021): let (x_i, y_i), i = 1..n, be data with covariates x_i in R^d drawn from a distribution satisfying isoperimetry (Lipschitz functions of x concentrate like they do for a Gaussian; a mixture of such distributions is allowed) and labels y_i carrying genuine noise (conditional variance sigma^2 > 0 that no function of x can remove). Let F be a class of functions parametrized by p real parameters (more precisely, with log covering number of order p). Then with high probability every f in F that fits the data to within a constant fraction of the noise level (a fraction of the sum of the y_i's conditional variances remains unexplained) has Lipschitz constant at least of order sqrt(n d / p), up to logarithmic factors. Consequence: interpolating n noisy points in dimension d smoothly (Lipschitz constant O(1)) needs p of order n d parameters, a factor d beyond the n needed merely to memorize. The bound is vacuous without noise (a smooth interpolant can exist) and without the isoperimetry hypothesis on the covariates.
covariates satisfy an isoperimetric (concentration) inequality, e.g. Gaussian, uniform on the sphere, or a mixture of such
labels have irreducible noise of variance sigma^2 > 0
the model class has p parameters in the sense of a log covering number of order p
the model fits the data below the noise floor (an interpolation-type condition)
title: Bubeck-Sellke universal law of robustness (via isoperimetry)

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Cycle-flow rank lemma for a double edge cover of a connected loopless multigraph B. Every edge bears two distinct labels, the label multigraph G is connected and remains connected after any label is deleted, and each label subgraph B_t is nonempty, connected and bridgeless. If B has q vertices,e edges and v labels, then q-e+v<=2; if any B_t has cycle rank at least2, then q-e+v<=1. In raw cumulant diagrams with bridgeless local row-column graphs this gives the required strict suppression of all higher blocks, including odd blocks. General local graphs may have bridges, so the full asymmetric coefficient theorem and uniform remainder remain open. Supporting proof draft; novelty unestablished.
Finite loopless multigraph B, connected, with distinct parallel edges
Every edge has exactly two distinct labels, v>=2
Connected label graph G, with G-t connected for every label
Every label subgraph nonempty, connected and bridgeless
Real cycle spaces; for the strict bound at least one has dimension>=2

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:70f30bc77c3f6327d58902cbda49680b8fa9430d465a9be9f2b051d63e74a5b9","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/70/70f30bc77c3f6327d58902cbda49680b8fa9430d465a9be9f2b051d63e74a5b9.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:5b9f7179ba2c2e22072cbab7d7a8a73d7ac24334eed12464811cabe7931b35f8","bundle_entry_key":"odd-cumulants-bridgeless-double-cover-cycle-flow-rank-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-odd-cumulant-cycle-flow-rank-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Graph cycle spaces and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_010.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:odd-cumulants-bridgeless-double-cover-cycle-flow-rank-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A cycle-flow rank lemma for the odd-cumulant route

Target 1 supporting route lemma. Proof draft, UNAUDITED. Novelty is
unestablished. This does not prove the full asymmetric coefficient theorem,
and it does not supply a dimension-uniform Taylor remainder.

## Statement

Let B be a finite connected undirected loopless multigraph with e edges
and q vertices. Every edge has two distinct labels from a set of v>=2
labels. Let G be the multigraph on labels with one edge for each edge of
B, joining that edge's two labels. For label t let B_t be the subgraph
formed by all edges bearing t, retaining their endpoints. Assume:

1. G is connected, and G-t is connected for every label t (a single
   vertex is connected).
2. Every B_t is connected and bridgeless, with at least one edge.

Then q-e+v<=2. Moreover, if some B_t has cycle-space dimension at least
two, then q-e+v<=1.

Parallel edges are distinct edges throughout. Orient the edges of B
arbitrarily, once and for all. All vector spaces below are over R.

## Proof of the weak bound

The cycle space Z(B), the kernel of the oriented vertex-edge incidence
matrix, has dimension b=e-q+1. Since B_t is bridgeless, every edge of B_t
belongs to a cycle. Thus for each of its edges its coordinate functional
is nonzero on Z(B_t). A finite union of proper linear hyperplanes cannot
cover a real vector space. We may therefore choose f_t in Z(B_t) nonzero
on every edge of B_t, and extend it by zero outside B_t. Its extension
lies in Z(B).

Form the v by e matrix F with rows f_t. A column indexed by edge a of G,
with endpoints t,u, has precisely two nonzero entries f_t(a),f_u(a).
If lambda is in the left kernel of F, it satisfies

    lambda_t f_t(a) + lambda_u f_u(a) = 0.

Consequently one coordinate of lambda determines all the others along
paths in connected G. In particular the kernel dimension is at most
one, and any nonzero kernel vector has every coordinate nonzero.
Therefore rank F>=v-1. Since its rows lie in Z(B), b>=v-1, proving the
weak inequality.

## Strictness

Suppose b=v-1. For every choice of full-support flows, F then has rank
exactly v-1 and a one-dimensional left kernel with all coordinates
nonzero. Fix one such choice and a nonzero kernel vector lambda.

Fix a label t and replace only its flow by any other full-support flow
h in Z(B_t). The new matrix again has a nonzero left-kernel vector mu
whose coordinates are all nonzero. On every edge joining labels other
than t, the old and new equations give

    mu_u/lambda_u = mu_w/lambda_w.

Connectivity of G-t makes this ratio a common nonzero constant c for
all labels other than t. On each edge a joining t and u, subtracting
the two kernel equations now gives

    mu_t h(a) = c lambda_t f_t(a).

All edges of B_t bear a second label other than t. Hence h is a scalar
multiple of f_t on its entire support. Every full-support flow in
Z(B_t) is therefore on one fixed line. Full-support flows are the
complement of finitely many proper hyperplanes, a nonempty open dense
subset of Z(B_t). This is possible only if dim Z(B_t)=1. As t was
arbitrary, equality forces this dimension to be one for every label.
If any label has dimension at least two, the integer b must be at least
v, proving strictness. QED.

## Translation to the cumulant diagrams

In a Wick contraction, B has one vertex for each global row equality
class and each global column equality class, and one edge for each
Wick pair. It is bipartite and loopless, including when several edges
have the same endpoints. Its label graph is the tensor contraction
graph G. Thus q=c_i+c_j, and q-e+v is exactly the index exponent.
Connected local raw row/column graphs and connected G imply connected B.

Let H_t be the local graph before global equality identifications.
Each of its edges maps to a distinct edge of B_t. If H_t is bridgeless,
then B_t is bridgeless: an edge on a cycle maps to an edge on a closed
trail, so cannot become a bridge. Vertex identifications preserve or
increase cycle-space dimension, since they preserve edge count and
cannot increase the vertex count of a connected graph.

Every raw block has size at least two. Thus H_t has minimum degree two.
If any raw block has size at least three, its connected graph has
cycle rank at least two: writing d for its edge count and h for its
vertex count, 2d>=2h+1 implies d>=h+1 and d-h+1>=2. This applies to odd
degrees without an Euler circuit. The strict exponent bound therefore
holds for all diagrams whose local graphs are bridgeless and which
contain a higher raw block.

## The remaining bridge obstruction

Minimum degree two DOES NOT imply bridgeless. A connected bipartite
local graph can consist of two length-two parallel-edge cycles joined
by a single edge. It has five edges, degree sequence (3,2,3,2), and a
bridge. All cycle flows vanish on that bridge. The full-support choice
used in the proof is then impossible; the associated column of F can
have zero entries, so the kernel-propagation proof cannot be invoked.
Some global identifications can remove such bridges, but this is not
guaranteed term by term by the current assumptions.

The general route must either remove these bridge terms through an
additional exact entropy cancellation or control their missing flow
constraints by a separate graph argument. Neither has been proved here.
Even that extension would address fixed-order coefficients only.

Least trusted step for review: whether the global quotient diagrams
indeed have precisely the B and G incidence representation stated in
the translation. The abstract graph lemma itself uses only the stated
support, rank and connectivity conditions.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:301e329545fb9cbce0c61e9c86ce36ea4e49997d0ea2cebdf0dbce18c63eb19b","revision_digest":"sha256:d1d8b8da18a72cdf1fea56d6242b4fc19bbae7b328bd1e53b2d44073088268f5","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:odd-cumulants-bridgeless-double-cover-cycle-flow-rank-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

\begin{align*}
(a_i-a_j)\Big( \frac{\partial f}{\partial a_i}-\frac{\partial f}{\partial a_j}\Big)\geq 0.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let X be a square-integrable function of independent coordinates and X^L its value after an independent resampling of a block L, and suppose the pair (X, X^L) is exchangeable (automatic for independent block resampling). Then E[((X^L - X)^+)^2] = Var(X) - Cov(X, X^L). Proof in two lines from facts that hold separately: exchangeability gives E[(X - X^L)^2] = 2 Var(X) - 2 Cov(X, X^L), and the symmetry of X^L - X gives E[(X - X^L)^2] = 2 E[((X^L - X)^+)^2]; equate. Consequences: Cov(X, X^L) <= Var(X) always; summing over a partition of blocks turns Efron-Stein into the exact statement Sum_L E[((X^L - X)^+)^2] = Sum_L (Var(X) - Cov(X, X^L)), so bounding the positive-part functionals a resampling engine consumes is EXACTLY the problem of lower-bounding the block covariances. Numerically checked on a nonlinear functional (relative difference 0.008 at 200,000 samples).

	a quotient matrix of $M$ with respect to some partition.  Then the
	eigenvalues of $B$ interlace those of $M$.  Moreover, if the partition is
	equitable, then the largest eigenvalue of $M$ equals the largest
	eigenvalue of $B$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{Brouwer-Haemers}

body: In mathematics, the operator norm measures the "size" of certain linear operators by assigning each a real number called its operator norm. Formally, it is a norm defined on the space of bounded linear operators between two given normed vector spaces. Informally, the operator norm of a linear map is the maximum factor by which it "lengthens" vectors. It is also called the bound norm.

body:
[Thm main:IG of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] The following hold for all $\omega$ in a full $\mathbb{P}$-probability event and for all $\theta\in\Theta^\omega$.
\begin{enumerate}[label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}] \itemsep=1pt

\item
$\IG\theta$ is closed, nowhere dense, and has no isolated points.

\item
The connected components of the open set $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\IG\theta$ are all bounded, and distinct components have disjoint closures. Moreover, there are countably infinitely many such components. We call these components \emph{stability islands}.

\item Each island has a unique boundary point with minimal time, called the \emph{bottom}, and a unique boundary point with maximal time, called the \emph{tip}. The boundary of the island consists of two continuous space-time paths, the \emph{left boundary} and the \emph{right boundary}, each connecting the bottom to the tip. Except at the bottom and the tip, the left boundary lies strictly to the left of the right boundary.

\item The islands are dense in $\IG\theta$: for any $(x,s)\in\IG\theta$ and $\rho>0$, there exists an island whose closure is inside the ball of radius $\rho$ and center $(x,s)$.\vspace{2pt}

Let $\mathcal D^\theta$ denote the subset of $\IG\theta$ consisting of points that are not on the boundary of any stability island. Points in $\mathcal D^\theta$ are called \emph{dust points}.\vspace{4pt}

\item
$\mathcal D^\theta$ {\rm(}and hence also $\IG\theta${\rm)} is temporally bi-infinite: there exists an uncountable family of continuous bi-infinite space-time paths $\tau_\alpha:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $\tau_\alpha(\mathbb{R})\subset\mathcal D^\theta$ for all $\alpha$, the paths are pairwise disjoint
{\rm(}$\tau_\alpha(\mathbb{R})\cap\tau_\beta(\mathbb{R})=\varnothing$ for $\alpha\ne\beta${\rm)}, and each path is $\theta$-directed in both time directions, i.e.\ $t^{-1}\tau_\alpha(t)\to(\theta,1)$ as $|t|\to\infty$.

\item For any $s\in\mathbb{R}$, the set $\mathcal D^\theta\cap(\mathbb{R}\times\{s\})$ has no isolated points and is unbounded above and below. Moreover, for any $a<b$ such that $\IG\theta\cap((a,b)\times\{s\})\neq\varnothing$, the set $\mathcal D^\theta\cap((a,b)\times\{s\})$ is uncountable.

\item For each $(x,s)\in\IG\theta$, there exists at least one continuous bi-infinite space-time path through $(x,s)$ that remains on $\IG\theta$ and is $\theta$-directed in both time directions.

\item
$\IG\theta$ forms a path-connected graph: for any $(x,s),(y,t)\in\IG\theta$, there exist $z,z'\in\mathbb{R}$ and times $r<s\wedge t\le s\vee t<r'$ such that $(z,r),(z',r')\in\IG\theta$, and there are continuous space-time paths contained in $\IG\theta$ from $(z,r)$ to each of $(x,s)$ and $(y,t)$, and from each of these two points to $(z',r')$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional Finsler metric measure manifold. Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), claim w744-T368-wu-lemma9-missing-positive-part v2. Let n>=1 data (x_i,y_i) in R^d times {-1,+1} satisfy ||x_i||_2<=1. Assume a unit vector w_star and a fixed gamma>0 satisfy y_i <x_i,w_star> >= gamma for every i. Define ell(q)=log(1+exp(-q)), L(w)=(1/n)sum_i ell(y_i<x_i,w>), and full-batch GD w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k) with constant eta>0. Assume w_0=0. Put G(w)=(1/n)sum_i 1/(1+exp(y_i<x_i,w>)) and log_+(a)=max(0,log(a)) for a>0. For every integer t>=1, (1/t)sum_{k=0}^{t-1}G(w_k)<=[sqrt(2)+2log_+(gamma^2 eta t)+eta]/(gamma^2 eta t). The corresponding norm bound is ||w_t||<=[sqrt(2)+2log_+(gamma^2 eta t)+eta]/gamma. This corrects the printed unrestricted Lemma 9, which omits the positive part: n=d=1,x=y=w_star=gamma=1,eta=1/16,t=1 has left side 1/2 but its printed numerator sqrt(2)-8log(2)+1/16 is strictly below -181/48. The printed bound is therefore false at allowed small times. The replacement agrees with the original whenever gamma^2 eta t>=1, including the source phase-transition argument. No new optimization rate or refutation of source Theorem 1 is claimed.
Finite nonempty binary-labeled data with Euclidean feature norms <=1
Unit separating vector w_star and margin gamma>0
Averaged logistic risk and full-batch constant-step gradient descent
Zero initialization
Integer t>=1; log_+ argument gamma^2 eta t>0

Status: PROOF (UNAUDITED); source text and PDF p20 formula visually confirmed. This is a
source-statement correction, not a new optimization-rate result and not a solution
of the nonhomogeneous-network frontier target.

The primary arXiv:2402.15926 PDF p20 prints, under zero initialization and every
eta>0, for t>=1,

    mean_{k<t} G(w_k) <= [sqrt(2)+2 log(gamma^2 eta t)+eta]/(gamma^2 eta t).

Here G(w)=mean_i 1/(1+exp(y_i x_i dot w)). Take n=d=1, x=y=w_star=gamma=1,
w_0=0, t=1 and eta=1/16. These satisfy every boundedness/separability/initialization
hypothesis. The left side is exactly 1/2. The numerator on the right is
sqrt(2)-8log(2)+1/16 < 3/2-16/3+1/16 = -181/48 <0.
Use sqrt(2)<3/2 (squaring positive numbers) and log(2)>2/3, obtained by integrating
1/x >=4/3-4x/9 on [1,2], strictly except at x=3/2. The denominator is 1/16>0.
Thus the printed unrestricted small-time statement is false. No floating-point
estimate is used. The rendered formula in renders/arxiv2402.15926_p20.png was
inspected and confirms both the numerator and its unrestricted eta>0,t>=1 range.

A correct universal version replaces log(a) by log_+(a)=max(0,log(a)).
The data hypotheses, arbitrary eta>0 and t>=1 remain unchanged. Proof:

Write z_i=y_i x_i, p_i(w)=1/(1+exp(z_i dot w)), G=mean_i p_i, and
g=grad L=-mean_i p_i z_i. Source Lemma 7 uses u=u_1+u_2, where
u_2=eta w_star/(2gamma), and gives

    ||w_t-u||^2/(2 eta t)+mean_{k<t} L(w_k)
      <= L(u_1)+||w_0-u||^2/(2 eta t).

Indeed ||g||<=G<=1, g dot w_star<=-gamma G, so
2eta g dot u_2+eta^2||g||^2<=0. Convexity of L controls the u_1 term;
sum the squared-distance recursion over k. This holds for any u_1 and w_0.

For w_0=0 set a=gamma^2 eta t and u_1=log_+(a) w_star/gamma.
If a>=1, separability and log(1+exp(-q))<=exp(-q) give L(u_1)<=1/a.
If a<1 then u_1=0 and L(u_1)=log(2)<1<1/a. Consequently

    ||w_t-u||^2 <= ||u||^2+2/gamma^2,
    ||w_t|| <=2||u||+sqrt(2)/gamma
             =[2log_+(a)+eta+sqrt(2)]/gamma.

Finally z_i dot w_star>=gamma gives the perceptron progress inequality
(w_{k+1}-w_k) dot w_star>=eta gamma G(w_k). Telescope from w_0=0 and use
||w_star||=1, obtaining mean G<=||w_t||/(eta gamma t), exactly the corrected
bound. All divisions use eta,gamma,t>0. The logarithm's argument a is positive.
When a>=1, this reproduces the printed expression unchanged; in particular this
is the regime used in the source's finite phase-transition proof (Lemma 12).

Indeed, if eta>=1, tau>=60eta/gamma^2 implies gamma^2 eta tau>=60.
If eta<1, n>=1 gives (eta+n)/eta>2, so the logarithmic term in tau gives
gamma^2 eta tau>=60(eta+n)log((eta+n)/eta)>60log(2)>40>1.

The same positive-part choice also justifies the all-time parameter and averaged
risk estimates without using a negative comparator radius in a margin inequality.
It does not refute Theorem 1 or its acceleration corollary.

[Definition of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] Let $p$ be a semi-directed path from the origin to a point $(n,m)$. For $k=0,...,n$ let $f_p(k)\in \mathbb Z$ be such that $(k, f_p(k)) \in \mathbb Z^2$ is the first intersection of $p$ with the vertical line $\{k\}\times \mathbb Z$. In particular, $f_p(0)=0$. The points $(k, f_p(k)) \in \mathbb Z^2$ are referred to as \emph{pioneer points}. 
We also introduce the convention $f_p(n+1)=m$ (even though $(n+1,m) \not \in p$).
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'

body: [Dfn 22 (Strong Markovian coupling) of arXiv:2604.12853, 'Coupling Markov Chains \\with a Common Image Chain'] For two stochastic matrices $P_X\in\SM(A)$ and $P_Y\in\SM(B)$, a \textbf{strong Markovian coupling} (SMC) of $P_X$ and $P_Y$ is a stochastic matrix $P\in\SM(A \times B)$ such that, for all $\upalpha\in\PM(A \times B)$, the marginals of $\MC(\upalpha,P)$ are DTHMCs driven by $P_X$ and $P_Y$. In other words, $P$ lumps strongly under $\proj^1$ to $P_X$ and also lumps strongly under $\proj^2$ to $P_Y$.
title: Strong Markovian coupling

[Lemma lem:increment of arXiv:2511.17101, 'Central limit theorem for the range of critical branching random walk'] \begin{enumerate}
\item
The sequence $(\Delta C(i))_{i\ge 1}$ is i.i.d., taking values in $\{1,-1\}$ with probability $\frac 1 2$ each.
\item
When $\Delta C(i)=1$, $\Delta V(i)$ is a uniform unit vector independent of $\sigma(C(-\infty,i-1],V(-\infty,i-1])$.
\item 
When $\Delta C(i)=-1$, $\Delta V(i)$ is the vector from $u_{i-1}$ to $\overleftarrow{u_{i-1}}$, completely determined by $(C(-\infty,i-1],V(-\infty,i-1])$.
\item In particular, $u_{2i-1}$ is bad if and only if $\Delta C(2i-1)=1,\Delta C(2i)=-1$, and $-\Delta V(2i-1)=\Delta V(2i)$ is the vector from $u_{2i-2}$ to its parent. Therefore,
\[
\mathbb P\parsof{u_{2i-1}\text{ is bad}}{C(-\infty,2i-2],V(-\infty,2i-2]}=\frac 1{8d},
\]
and the event $\{u_{2i-1}\text{ is bad}\}$ is independent of the past $\sigma$-algebra  $\sigma(C(-\infty,2i-2],V(-\infty,2i-2])$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:increment of arXiv:2511.17101

[Proposition pr:hextension of arXiv:2604.21142, 'Gaussian fluctuations for Internal DLA on cylinders'] For $2 \leq k \leq N$, let $q_k > 0$ be the positive real number defined by
	\begin{equation}
	 \cosh(q_k) = 2 - \l_k\,.
	 \end{equation}
(By irreducibility and laziness, $\l_k \in [0, 1)$ for $k \geq 2$, so $2 - \l_k \in (1, 2]$ and $q_k > 0$.) Then, for every $h \in {\ensuremath{\mathbb Z}} $ and every sequence $(\a_k(h))_{2 \leq k \leq N}$ of real numbers, the function
	\[ \psi(x, y) = \sum_{k=2}^N \a_k(h)\, f_k^N(x)\, e^{q_k(y - h)} \]
is discrete harmonic on ${\ensuremath{\mathbb G}} _N$, decays exponentially as $y \to -\infty$, and satisfies $\psi(x, h) = \sum_{k=2}^N \a_k(h)\,f_k^N(x)$ on the line $\{(x, h) : x \in V_N\}$.

[Theorem thm:fullI of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] The full asymptotic expansion of the average of the random variable $T_{N,d}$ in the $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP) is given by  
\begin{align}
\mathbb {E}\left[T_{N,d}\right]=&\frac{H_N}{A_N}+\frac{B_N}{A_N^2}\nonumber \\
\sim& \frac{N}{d}\log N+\frac{\gamma}{d}N
+\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\bigl(\lambda_m(d)\log N+\nu_m(d)\bigr)N^{-m},\quad N\rightarrow \infty,

\end{align}
where the coefficients $\lambda_m(d)$ and $\nu_m(d)$ are defined in relations ((33a of the paper))-((38 of the paper)). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition of arXiv:2411.13505, 'Capacity of loop-erased random walk'] We define the two-sided loop-erased random walk $\hat\eta$ as the random variable on two-sided infinite paths in $\Omega$ such that $\hat\eta[0,\infty)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\eta$ with Radon-Nikodym derivative given by $\frac{X_\infty}{\mathbb{E}[X_\infty]}$. It was shown in [lawler19fourdimensional] that $(T\hat\eta)[0,\infty)\stackrel{d}{=}\hat\eta[0,\infty)$. Thus, we can extend $\hat\eta$ to the space of two-sided infinite paths by defining $\hat\eta[-a,b]\stackrel{d}{=}\hat\eta[0,a+b]-\hat\eta(a)$.

[Lem zygmundwithlogs of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Fix $k,l\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ and $u>0$, and let $s := \lceil k+ul\rceil$.
Let $h\in\mathcal{P}_q$ with Chebyshev expansion
$h(x) = \sum_{j=0}^q a_j T_j(K^{-1}x)$, and let
$f(\theta):= h(K \cos(\theta))$.  Then
$$
	\sum_{j=1}^q j^k (1+\log j)^l  
	|a_j| \lesssim
	\bigg(\frac{e^u}{u}\bigg)^l
	\sobnorm{f^{(s+1)}}{0}{[0, 2\pi]}.
$$

body:
[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.23989, 'Collision Properties in Discrete and Continuous Time on Bounded-Degree Graphs'] The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Let~$P$ be an irreducible Markov kernel on $\mathsf S$, reversible with respect to a measure $\pi$ satisfying
    \[ \sup_{x \in \mathsf S}\pi(x) <\infty.\]
    Then~$\Pp(\mathcal E^P_\mathrm{disc}) \in \{0,1\}$ for every common starting state.  
    \item Let~$Q$ be an irreducible~$Q$-matrix on~$\mathsf S$, reversible with respect to a measure~$\pi$ satisfying
    \[ \sup_{x \in \mathsf S} \pi(x) <\infty \qquad \text{and} \qquad \sup_{x \in \mathsf S}q(x) <\infty .\]
    Then~$\Pp(\mathcal E^Q_\mathrm{cont}) \in \{0,1\}$ for every common starting state. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.23989

[Lemma 8 (Campbell--Palm intensity identity) of arXiv:2608.20101, '\bfseries Largest bulk gap of the complex Ginibre ensemble'] For every Borel set \(A\subset D_1\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\mathcal E_n(r)(A)
 =\int_AK_n(a,a)q_n(a,r)\dd^2a.
\end{equation}
More generally, the same formula holds with \(r\) replaced by a measurable
location-dependent radius \(r(a)\).  In particular, the adaptive process in
\Cref{prop:LO} has intensity measure exactly
\(\kappa\dd^2z\) in unit-disk coordinates.

body:
[Lem 46 of arXiv:2510.22783, 'Universality of Cutoff for Riffle Shuffling'] Consider the set $\mathcal M$ of $(N-i+\iota(p)+y_{p,i}-1)\times K$ matrices with entries in $[k]_0$ such that:
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item The first $n^{\rem}$ rows start with $\p$.
            \item The first $n^{\rem}$ rows are lexicographically greater than or equal to $s_i$.
            \item Among the first $n^{\rem}$ rows, at least $y_{p,i}$ are equal to $s_i$.
            \item For every $t\in [K]$ and $j\in [k]_0$, the number of $j$-digits in the $t$-th column is exactly $n_j^{(t),\rem}$ .
        \end{enumerate}
        We then select uniformly at random a matrix from $\widehat{\mathcal{M}}$.
        For each\footnote{Note the fourth condition above with $t=1$ and $j=\p$ implies that \emph{only} the first $n^{\rem}$ rows begin with $\p$; recall $n^{\rem}=n^{(1),\rem}_{\p}$.} $j \in [n^{\rem}]$, denote by $\widehat{s}_j$ the $j$-th row of the selected matrix. 
        If we sort $\{\widehat{s}_j\}_{j \in [n^{\rem}]}$ into increasing lexicographic order, writing the result as $(\overline{s}'_j)_{j \in [n^{\rem}]}$, then we have
        \[
            (\overline s'_{1}, \ldots, \overline s'_{n^{\rem}}) \overset{\mathrm{law.}}{=} (s_{i-y_{p,i}+1},s_{i-y_{p,i}+2},\ldots,s_{\tau(p)})
            \text{\emph{ conditioned on $\mathbf a_i$,}}
        \]
        which gives a natural coupling between the two sequences of strings with $\overline{s}'_{j}=s_{j+i-y_{p,i}}$ for each $j \in [n^{\rem}]$, and thereby between the set $\{\widehat{s}_j\}_{j \in [n^{\rem}]}$ and the sequence $(\overline{s}_{j+i-y_{p,i}})_{j \in [n^{\rem}]}$. 
        We denote this natural coupling by $Q$.
        In particular, the distribution of $\left|\cI(B_x)\right|$ conditioned on $\mathbf a_i$ coincides with that of $\left|\{j \in [n^{\rem}] : \widehat{s}_j \in B_{x}\}\right|$.

[Definition Measure-theoretic upper expectation of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z})$ be a gamble space, and $X:\Omega\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ a measurable variable.
  Then we define
  \begin{align}
    \overline{\mathbb{E}} X &:= \sup_{P\in\Delta(\Omega)} \inf_{Z\in\mathrm{mdcl}(\mathcal{Z})} \mathbb{E}_P [X-Z]~,
  \end{align}
  and $\underline{\mathbb{E}} X := -\overline{\mathbb{E}}(-X)$.
  If $\mathbb{E}_P[X-Z]$ is not defined, we define it to be $\infty$.

body:
[Definition defi:interface of arXiv:2511.01851, 'Percolation on graphs of polynomial growth is local:\\analyticity, supercritical sharpness'] Let $\mathscr{I}\subset V$ be a finite set of vertices. We say that $\mathscr{I}$ is an \textit{interface} if it is $t$-coarse connected and either $o\in \mathscr{I}$ or $o$ lies in a finite connected components of $\mathscr{G}\setminus \mathscr{I}$. Let $\overline{\mathscr{I}}$ denote the set of vertices $x$ such that $d_{\mathscr{G}}(x,\mathscr{I})\leqslant 10N$. We say that an interface $\mathscr{I}$ \textit{occurs in $\omega$ at scale $N$} if
\begin{enumerate}
    \item every $x\in \mathscr{I}$ is bad,
    \item every $x\in V\setminus \mathscr{I}$ such that $d_{\mathscr{G}}(x,\mathscr{I})\leqslant t$ is good,
    \item the closed edges of $\overline{\mathscr{I}}$ form a bond-cutset between $o$ and $\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
When clear from context, we simply write that $\mathscr{I}$ occurs.
title: Definition defi:interface of arXiv:2511.01851

[Proposition eq:finite_size_criterion_1 of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{prop:finite_size_criterion}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 2$ and let $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ be a transitive kernel.
    
    Suppose that $G$ admits $A$-controlled nets for some $A \geq 1$.
    
    Let $\delta > 0$ and let $\beta \in \mathbf{R}_+$.
    
    Suppose that there exists $\nu > 0$ such that  for some $R \in \mathbf{N}$ we have
    
    \begin{equation}
    
        \mathbf{P}_{\beta}
        \left(
            \# 
            K_{R}^{\scriptscriptstyle (1)}
            \geq
            \nu
            \# B(R)
        \right) 
        \geq 
        1
        -
        \delta,
    \end{equation}
    
    and for any two sets $S_1, S_2 \subseteq B(10AR)$ with $d_G(S_1,S_2) \geq 2R$ and $\#S_1, \#S_2 \geq \nu \# B(R)$, 
    
    \begin{equation}
    
        \mathbf{P}_\beta
        \left(
            S_1 
            \sim 
            S_2 
        \right) 
        \geq 
        1
        -
        \delta
        .
    \end{equation}      
    
    If $\delta = c_G/(18 (8A)^d C_G)$ then $\beta > \beta_c(G,J)$.
    
    Further, $\mathbf{P}_{\beta} \left(K_{R}^{\scriptscriptstyle (1)} \leftrightarrow \infty \right) \to 1$ as $\delta \to 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-size criterion for $d \geq 2$

body:
[Cor Thom-space-po of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The diagram $((diag:thom-space-spectrum of the paper))$ is a pushout of presentably symmetric monoidal global $\infty$-categories. 
\begin{proof} 
    By Corollaries~(cor:global-spectra-smash of the paper) and (cor:gl-pointed of the paper) and the construction of the various maps, $((diag:thom-space-spectrum of the paper))$ is a commutative square in $\CAlg(\textup{Pr}^\textup{Glo}_\textup{Glo})$.
    It therefore suffices to show that for every presentably symmetric monoidal global $\infty$-category ${\mathcal{C}}$, 
    the square $((diag:thom-space-spectrum of the paper))$ induces an equivalence \[{\textup{Hom}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{gl}}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}  {\textup{Hom}}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_{\textup{gl},*}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}})\times_{{\textup{Hom}}({\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}}},{\mathcal{C}})}{\textup{Hom}}(\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{VRep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}}),\] where ${\textup{Hom}}({-},{-})\coloneqq {\textup{Hom}}_{\CAlg(\textup{Pr}^{\textup{Glo}}_{\textup{Glo}})}({-},{-})$ denotes the $\infty$-groupoid of symmetric monoidal left adjoints.  
  
    Fix a presentably symmetric monoidal global $\infty$-category ${\mathcal{C}}$.
    It follows from Proposition~(prop:slice-sym-mon-is-universal of the paper) and the universal property of group completion that restriction along ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\Spc}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}}\to \ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{VRep}^{\oplus}}$ yields an inclusion of path components \[ {\textup{Hom}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\Spc}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{VRep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}})\hookrightarrow {\textup{Hom}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\Spc}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}})\] with image those globally cocontinuous symmetric monoidal functors ${\mathpalette\ulhelper{\Spc}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}}\to {\mathcal{C}}$ which send elements in the Yoneda image of $\smash{\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}}$ to invertible objects.   
    By construction of the Thom space functor $\ul{\textup{th}}_\textup{gl}^\otimes$, this implies that the projection \begin{align*}{\textup{Hom}}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_{\textup{gl},*}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}})\times_{{\textup{Hom}}(\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{Rep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}})}{\textup{Hom}}(\ul\Spc_{\textup{Glo}/\ul\textup{VRep}^{\oplus}},{\mathcal{C}}) \to {\textup{Hom}}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_{\textup{gl},*}^{\otimes},{\mathcal{C}})\end{align*} is the inclusion of the components consisting of those globally cocontinuous symmetric monoidal functors which in every degree $G$ send all representation spheres to invertible objects. The map ${\textup{Hom}}(\Sigma^\bullet,{\mathcal{C}})\colon{\textup{Hom}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{gl}^\otimes,{\mathcal{C}})\to{\textup{Hom}}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_{\textup{gl},*},{\mathcal{C}})$ admits the same description by the universal property of global spectra (Corollary~(cor:global-spectra-smash of the paper)) and Corollary~(cor:SpR-sym-mon-univ-prop of the paper),  finishing the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor Thom-space-po of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
Let $K$ be symmetric positive definite with eigenvalues $w_1 \le \dots \le w_n$ and eigenvectors $U$, and let $G$ be symmetric positive semidefinite. The exact identity $V = \mathrm{Tr}(K^{-1} G K^{-1}) = \sum_k \tilde G_{kk} / w_k^2$ with $\tilde G = U^\top G U$ holds, but if $G$ is replaced by $G + E$ with $\|E\|_2 \le \varepsilon \|G\|_2$ (rounding of relative size $\varepsilon$ in the entries of $G$), the computed value changes by at most $\varepsilon \|G\|_2 \sum_k w_k^{-2} \le \varepsilon\, n\, \|G\|_2 / w_1^2$. When $\|G\|_2$ is comparable to $\|K\|_2^2 = w_n^2$ (as for $G = \Phi D \Phi^\top$ built from the same features as $K = \Phi\Phi^\top$), this is an absolute error of order $\varepsilon\, \kappa(K)^2$ per eigendirection, so the trace form is not a usable number once $\varepsilon \kappa(K)^2 \gtrsim 1$. If instead $G = \Phi D \Phi^\top$ and $K = \Phi \Phi^\top$ share a factor $\Phi$ with $D$ diagonal nonnegative, then $V = \sum_j D_{jj} \|K^{-1} \Phi_{\cdot j}\|^2$, and a perturbation $\Delta$ of $\Phi$ with $\|\Delta\|_F \le \delta$ changes $V$ to first order by at most $2 \sqrt{V}\, \sqrt{D_{\max}}\, \delta / w_1$: one inverse, and the error enters through a single factor of $1/w_1$ rather than $1/w_1^2$. Measured instance: Gaussian kernel on the sphere, $d=12$, $n=4096$, $\kappa(K) = 1.3\times 10^{10}$, $\varepsilon \kappa^2 = 4\times 10^4$: the trace form reads $3.09$, a factored form through an eigendecomposition of $G$ alone reads $25.7$ (the rounding directions of $G$ still divided by $w_k^2$), the shared-factor form reads $2.653$, and a Monte-Carlo evaluation of the same quantity reads $2.657 \pm 0.003$.
K symmetric positive definite
G symmetric positive semidefinite
rounding modelled as a symmetric perturbation E of G with spectral norm at most epsilon times the spectral norm of G

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.02019, '2609.02019'] Let $s>5/2$. Let  $J_n$ be the Friedrichs mollifier defined in \eqref{Define Jn}.
		Then we have
		\begin{equation*}
			\left|\IP{\mathcal{H} u\partial_x u, u}_{H^{s}}\right|
			\lesssim  (\|u_x\|_{L^\infty}+\|\mathcal{H} u_x\|_{L^\infty})\|u\|^2_{H^{s}},\quad u\in H^{s+1}.
		\end{equation*}
		and
		\begin{equation*}
			\sup_{n\ge1}\left|\bIP{J_n (\mathcal{H} u\partial_x u), J_n u}_{H^{s}}\right|
			\lesssim  (\|u_x\|_{L^\infty}+\|\mathcal{H} u_x\|_{L^\infty})\|u\|^2_{H^{s}},\quad u\in H^{s}.
		\end{equation*}
		Moreover, for all $u,v\in H^s$, all $n,m\ge1$, and every
		$\theta\in(3/2,s-1)$,
		\begin{align*}
			\left|\IP{J_n \left[\mathcal{H} J_n u\partial_x J_nu\right]-J_m \left[\mathcal{H} J_m v\partial_x J_mv\right],u-v}_{H^\theta} \right|
			\lesssim  \Big(1+\|u\|^4_{H^s}+\|v\|^4_{H^s}\Big)
			\left((n\wedge m)^{-2(s-1-\theta)}+\|u-v\|^2_{H^\theta}\right).
		\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition ``Categories'' of exceptional rows of arXiv:2509.02432, 'A threshold for online balancing of sparse i.i.d. vectors'] For each $t \in [T]$, define the sets ${\mathbf C}_{t,w} \subset [n]$ inductively via:
    \[
        {\mathbf C}_{t,0} = \Big\{i \in [n]\,:\, \big|\big\la \mathrm{row}_i(A),\, \widetilde \sigma \big\rangle_{[s]}\big| > \frac{1}{2}\cdot C_\text{\tiny{(alg of the paper)}} \, \log \log n, ~ \text{ for some $s \le t$} \Big\},
    \]
    and, for each $w \in \mathbb N$,
    \begin{align*}
        {\mathbf C}_{t,w} = \Big\{i \in [n]\,:\, &\exists\, \text{ distinct } j_1,j_2 \in \mathrm{supp}(\mathrm{row}_i(A))\cap[t] \, \text{ s.t. for both $u \in \{1,2\}$, } \\
        &\exists \, i_u \in \big({\mathbf C}_{j_u - 1,w-1} \cap \,\mathrm{supp}(\mathrm{col}_{j_u}(A))\big)\setminus\{i\}\Big\}.
    \end{align*}
title: ``Categories'' of exceptional rows

[Theorem scheme case of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $X$ and $Z$ are smooth connected separated schemes of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ of dimension $n$, and there is a projective contraction morphism $f : X \to Z$ where the exceptional divisor $E$ is a smooth irreducible Cartier divisor. Moreover, suppose there is a smooth closed irreducible subscheme $Y \subseteq Z$ such that $E \simeq f^{-1}(Y)$ set-theoretically, and $f : X \setminus E \xrightarrow{\sim} Z \setminus Y$. 
    
    Then, $f$ is the blowup of $Z$ along smooth center $Y$, i.e., $X \simeq \operatorname{Bl}_Y Z$. In particular, there is a vector bundle $V \to Y$ of rank $r := \operatorname{codim}(Y, Z)$ such that $(E, \mathcal{O}_{E}(-E)) \simeq (\mathbb{P}(V), \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}(V)}(1))$ where $\mathbb{P}(V)$ is the projectivization of $V$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem scheme case of arXiv:2609.04023

\[
\E_{x_m}[\tau_{S_\eps}]\ge c_*

In particular,

body: [Definition def:thin_quantum_wedge of arXiv:2412.04005, '$\SLE_{\kappa}(\rho)$ processes in the light cone regime on\\ Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $\gamma \in (0,2)$ and $W \in (-\gamma^2 / 2,  \gamma^2 / 2)$.  A quantum wedge of weight $W$ on ${\mathscr{S}}$ (with marked points at $-\infty$ and $+\infty$) is the random distribution $h$ on ${\mathscr{S}}$ that can be sampled as follows.  Let $Y$ be a $\mathrm{BES}^{\delta}$ process where $\delta$ is as in~(equation eqn:bessel_dimension_wrt_weight of the paper).  Let $\mathcal{H}_1({\mathscr{S}}),  \mathcal{H}_2({\mathscr{S}})$ be as before.  We sample a countable collection of distribution valued random variables $h_{e}$ on ${\mathscr{S}}$ indexed by the excursions~$e$ of~$Y$ from~$0$ and take the projection of $h_{e}$ onto $\mathcal{H}_1({\mathscr{S}})$ to be given by reparameterizing $2\gamma^{-1}\log(e)$ to have quadratic variation $2dt$ and the projection of $h_{e}$ onto $\mathcal{H}_2({\mathscr{S}})$ to be sampled according to the law of the corresponding projection of a free boundary GFF on ${\mathscr{S}}$ (with additive constant fixed so that its average on $[0,i\pi]$ vanishes) taken to be independent of the corresponding projection of the other excursions from $0$ of $Y$.  Note that $\delta \in (0,2)$ and in that case we call the quantum wedge \emph{thin} quantum wedge.
title: Definition def:thin_quantum_wedge of arXiv:2412.04005

body:
[Definition 15 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Let $\theta^0$, $\{b^t\}_{t \geq 0}$, and $\{g^t\}_{t \geq 0}$
be mutually independent scalar variables/processes on a filtered
probability space $(\Omega,\cF,\{\cF_t\}_{t \geq 0},\P)$, where
$\Law(\theta^0)$ is given by Assumption \ref{assump:dynamics}(c),
$\{b^t\}_{t \geq 0}$ is a standard $\cF_t$-adapted Brownian motion, and
\[\{g^t\}_{t \geq 0} \sim \GP(0,C_g)\]
is a continuous, mean-zero, $\cF_t$-adapted Gaussian process with a symmetric
positive-semidefinite covariance kernel $C_g:[0,\infty) \times [0,\infty)
\to \R$. Let $\{\theta^t\}_{t \geq 0}$ be the solution of the SDE
\begin{equation}
\d\theta^t=\left[f(\theta^t)+\int_0^t R_g(t,s)\theta^s ds+g^t\right]
\d t+\sqrt{2 \gamma}\,\d b^t, \qquad \theta^t|_{t=0}=\theta^0,
\end{equation}
where $R_g:[0,\infty) \times [0,\infty) \to \R$
is a response kernel satisfying $R_g(t,s)=0$ for $s>t$. Let
$\{\frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}\}_{t \geq s \geq 0}$ be the solution of the
response equation
\begin{equation}
\frac{\d}{\d t} \frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}=\left[f'(\theta^t)\frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}
+\int_s^t R_g(t,r)\frac{\d \theta^r}{\d g^s}\d r\right],
\qquad \frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}\bigg|_{t=s}=1.
\end{equation}
These kernels $C_g,R_g$, in conjunction with a pair of auxiliary kernels
$C_\theta,R_\theta:[0,\infty) \times [0,\infty) \to \R$,
are self-consistently defined from the laws of the above processes by the
fixed point conditions
\begin{align}
C_\theta(t,s)&=\E[\theta^t \theta^s]\\
R_\theta(t,s)&=\E\left[\frac{\d\theta^t}{\d g^s}\right]
\text{ for } s \in [0,t],
\quad R_\theta(t,s)=0 \text{ for } s>t,
\\
C_g(t,s)&=\sum_{p,q \geq 0} \kappa_{p+q+2}\,
R_\theta^{\ast p} * C_\theta * \bar R_\theta^{\ast q}(t,s),
\quad
\text{ where } \bar R_\theta(t,s)=R_\theta(s,t) \text{ for all } s,t \geq 0,\\
R_g(t,s)&=\sum_{p \geq 1} \kappa_{p+1}\,R_\theta^{\ast p}(t,s).
\end{align}
Here, $A*B$ denotes the standard convolution for kernels defined over
$[0,\infty)$,
\[[A \ast B](t,s)=\int_0^\infty A(t,r)B(r,s)\d r,
\quad A^{\ast p}=\underbrace{A \ast \ldots \ast A}_{p \text{
times}}, \quad A^{\ast 0}*B=B*A^{\ast 0}=B.\]
title: Definition 15 of arXiv:2607.10102

[Lem lem-geo-infty-ind of arXiv:2510.26123, 'Directed distances in bipolar-oriented triangulations:\\ exact exponents and scaling limit'] For $k\in\mathbbm Z$, let $\mathring M_{x_k,\infty}^L$ (resp.\ $\mathring M_{x_k,\infty}^R$) be the submap of $M_{0,\infty}$ lying to the left (resp.\ right) of the leftmost ${\operatorname{XDP}}$ geodesic $P_{x_k}$ of Lemma~(lem-geo-infty of the paper), including the vertices and edges lying on $P_{x_k}$.
Then $\mathring M_{x_k,\infty}^L$ and $\mathring M_{x_k,\infty}^R$ are independent. Furthermore, if $k\geq 0$ then $\mathring M_{x_k,\infty}^R \overset{d}{=} \mathring M_{x_0,\infty}^R$ and if $k\leq 0$ then $\mathring M_{x_k,\infty}^L \overset{d}{=} \mathring M_{x_0,\infty}^L$.
title: Lem lem-geo-infty-ind of arXiv:2510.26123

PRIVATE AUTHOR-CHECKED PARTIAL CANDIDATE; no independent review or novelty certification. For n FIFO queues, Poisson jobs at rate n*lambda/k choosing uniform k-subsets, and independent task marks, let r(T) be a stationary marginal M/G/1 emptying tail. The tagged k-workload law differs from its marginal product by at most 2*k*r(T)+3*lambda*T*k*(k-1)^2/(2*(n-1)) in total variation. Exponential services of rate mu>lambda give r(T)<=(1+sqrt(lambda/mu))*exp(-(sqrt(mu)-sqrt(lambda))^2*T), hence sufficient k=o((n/log(n))^(1/3)). A conditional polynomial tail T^(-p) instead gives sufficient exponent p/(3*p+1). Credits the prior finite-time coupling method; general service, optimal exponents and novelty remain unresolved.
Fixed 0<lambda<mu; n>=2 and 1<=k<=n
Independent iid marks including tasks of one job; independent uniform routing
FIFO work-conserving queues in stationarity
Exponential services only for the displayed exponential corollary

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:628459c8671c6293853cfa21127c6e93c0fc40c0f3cdd5206d26514029aee3cb","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/62/628459c8671c6293853cfa21127c6e93c0fc40c0f3cdd5206d26514029aee3cb.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ac94520dd14667574818c4e5bdd7d6df7d8846c54fdf5cf64184077d7f769f36","bundle_entry_key":"fork","bundle_id":"population.probability-hole-coefficient-and-forkjoin-partials-008","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-01a07a40/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.stochastic:limited-forkjoin-stationary-collision-emptying-bound","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Limited fork-join: a stationary exponential-service partial candidate

Status: private author-checked partial result for P0429. No independent review or novelty certification. The general finite-second-moment service question is not solved. The basic collision and empty-start coupling method is already in Wang et al., *Delay Asymptotics and Bounds for Multi-Task Parallel Jobs*, Sections 3-5, archived as `queues_limited_forkjoin_2018`. We credit that method and its $k=o(n^{1/4})$ theorem. This packet sharpens the marginal emptying-time step under an additional exponential-service assumption and restores thinned arrival rates explicitly.

## Model and candidate bound

There are $n\ge2$ FIFO servers. Jobs arrive as a Poisson process of rate $\Lambda=n\lambda/k$, independently select uniform $k$-subsets of servers, and place one task in each selected queue. Service requirements of all tasks, including different tasks of the same job, are independent and identically distributed, independent of routing and arrivals. Fix the marginal rate $0<\lambda<\mu$, with mean service $1/\mu$. Let $\pi_{n,k}$ be the stationary joint workload law at any specified $k$ servers, and let $\nu_k$ be the product of their marginal stationary workload laws. Total variation uses $\sup_A|\pi(A)-\nu(A)|$.

Write $r(T)$ for the probability that a stationary marginal M/G/1 workload has not hit zero by time $T$. The modular coupling bound is

$$d_{\rm TV}(\pi_{n,k},\nu_k)\le 2k r(T)+\frac{3\lambda T k(k-1)^2}{2(n-1)},\qquad T>0.$$

With exponential service of rate $\mu$, put $\rho=\lambda/\mu$ and $c=(\sqrt\mu-\sqrt\lambda)^2>0$. Then

$$r(T)\le(1+\sqrt\rho)e^{-cT},$$

so the candidate explicit stationary bound is

$$d_{\rm TV}(\pi_{n,k},\nu_k)\le 2k(1+\sqrt\rho)e^{-cT}+\frac{3\lambda T k(k-1)^2}{2(n-1)}.$$

Either right-hand side may also be capped at one. The constants are uniform in $n,k$ at fixed $\lambda,\mu$.

## Step 1: independent arrivals with exactly restored marginal rates

Fix the tagged set $K$ with $|K|=k$. For one job let $N$ count selected servers in $K$. Counting ordered pairs gives

$$\mathbb E[N(N-1)]=\frac{k^2(k-1)^2}{n(n-1)}.$$

Poisson marking decomposes the arrival stream into independent streams indexed by its selected tagged subset. Retain every singleton-tagged arrival, discard all arrivals hitting two or more tagged queues, and add independent Poisson arrivals to each tagged queue at the marginal rate removed from that queue. The resulting $k$ arrival processes are independent Poisson processes of rate exactly $\lambda$. Give added tasks independent service requirements with the original law, and use identical marks on shared singleton arrivals.

Over $[0,T]$, the probability of any discrepancy is bounded by the expected number of discarded job events plus the expected total number of added task events. These are bounded by

$$\Lambda T\left(\mathbb P(N\ge2)+\mathbb E[N\mathbf1_{N\ge2}]\right)\le\frac32\Lambda T\mathbb E[N(N-1)].$$

Here $1\le N(N-1)/2$ and $N\le N(N-1)$ when $N\ge2$. Substitution of $\Lambda=n\lambda/k$ yields the collision term in the stated bound. This argument is nonasymptotic and does not require $2k\le n$.

Start the original and modified queues empty. Until the first discrepancy their tagged workload paths agree, because they have identical tagged arrival times and task marks. Thus the same bound controls total variation at time $T$.

## Step 2: couple empty starts to stationary starts

For the original system, couple one copy with stationary workloads at time zero to a copy with empty workloads, using the same future routing, arrivals and service marks. The stationary workload is coordinatewise above the empty-start workload. Whenever a stationary coordinate hits zero, both copies have zero workload there and then agree forever at that coordinate.

Each stationary coordinate is a marginal M/G/1 queue with the same $\lambda$ and service law, even though coordinates are dependent. By a union bound, the probability that any of the $k$ coordinates has failed to couple by $T$ is at most $kr(T)$. The independent comparison system has the same marginal law, so its own stationary-versus-empty coupling has the same bound. The triangle inequality between these two comparisons and Step 1 proves the modular estimate. Independence of the original stationary coordinates is neither assumed nor required.

## Step 3: exponential-service emptying tail

Consider the marginal M/M/1 queue count $Q$ until its first hit $\tau_0$ of zero. For $q\ge1$, its generator applied to $h(q)=a^q$, with $a=\sqrt{\mu/\lambda}>1$, is

$$\frac{{\cal L}h(q)}{h(q)}=\lambda(a-1)+\mu(a^{-1}-1)=-(\sqrt\mu-\sqrt\lambda)^2=-c.$$

Stopping first at zero and at a finite upper count level makes the standard exponential generator martingale legitimate. Nonnegativity and Fatou's lemma upon removal of the upper stopping level give

$$\mathbb E_q\left[e^{c(T\wedge\tau_0)}a^{Q(T\wedge\tau_0)}\right]\le a^q.$$

On $\{\tau_0>T\}$ the integrand is at least $e^{cT}$, so $\mathbb P_q(\tau_0>T)\le a^qe^{-cT}$. Averaging over the stationary geometric queue count yields

$$\mathbb E[a^{Q(0)}]=\frac{1-\rho}{1-\rho a}=\frac{1-\rho}{1-\sqrt\rho}=1+\sqrt\rho.$$

A marginal workload is zero exactly when its queue count is zero. The count process here is used only to bound this marginal stopping time; the pathwise workload coupling in Step 2 remains driven by shared task marks. No erroneous identification of arbitrary coupled count and workload paths is needed.

## Consequences and limits

Taking $T=2\log n/c$ gives

$$d_{\rm TV}(\pi_{n,k},\nu_k)\le\frac{2k(1+\sqrt\rho)}{n^2}+\frac{3\lambda k(k-1)^2\log n}{c(n-1)}.$$

Hence the distance tends to zero when $k=o((n/\log n)^{1/3})$ under exponential service. This is a sufficient regime, not an optimal threshold, and says nothing at the boundary $k\asymp n^{1/3}$ by itself. Poisson arrivals see the stationary pre-arrival workload law by PASTA. The arriving job selects its uniform target set independently of that law; exchangeability makes its selected workloads have the law of the specified tagged set. Appending independent tagged-job service requirements and taking a maximum is a Markov kernel, so total variation contracts; the same error controls the job-delay distribution against the independent comparison.

More generally, if $r(T)\le C T^{-p}$ for some fixed $p>0$, the modular estimate gives an error of order $k/T^p+Tk^3/n$. Balancing at $T\asymp(n/k^2)^{1/(p+1)}$ gives the sufficient regime $k=o(n^{p/(3p+1)})$. This conclusion is conditional on the stated emptying-tail bound; no unproved implication from a service moment is used. For $p=1$, the source's finite-second-moment estimate recovers the known exponent $1/4$.

## Attempts to break the argument

The vulnerable points are the growing number of tagged queues, simultaneous multi-hit arrivals, the marginal rate after removing those arrivals, and the passage to stationarity. The proof restores lost marginal rates rather than silently comparing to lower-load queues. It uses a union bound over all $k$ queues and retains both empty-start errors. The exponential tail constant tends to zero as load approaches one, so this packet does not claim a uniform heavy-traffic result. Correlated within-job service marks are excluded. Exponential control of the stationary emptying time has not been proved here for general service laws.

The original paper already has the same broad finite-time/emptying-time proof structure and numerical experiments at larger exponents. The observation here could be a known or straightforward corollary; bounded search is not a novelty certificate. No full original open-problem solution is promoted. [Proposition 3 (Variance characterization of Bernoulli
convergence) of arXiv:2607.12365, 'Bernoulli--Doob representation, asymptotic limits and boundary behavior of bounded homogen'] Under assumptions \textnormal{(A1)--(A3)}, let
$v(t):=\var[Z_t]$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(i)] \textnormal{(Max-variance law.)}
      The generalised Bernoulli $\mathcal{B}(a,b,z)$ is the unique
      maximum-variance distribution on $[a,b]$ with mean $z$:
      \[
      \mathcal{B}(a,b,z)
      = \argmax_{\mathcal{L}\in\mathcal{P}(a,b,z)}\var[\mathcal{L}]\,,
      \]
      where $\mathcal{P}(a,b,z)$ is the set of distributions on
      $[a,b]$ with mean $z$.
\item[\rm(ii)] \textnormal{(Variance strictly increasing.)}
      $v(t)$ is strictly increasing as long as
      $\Pr(Z_t\in\{a,b\})<1$.

satisfying:

\smallskip
 $(i)$ for every $i\!\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$,
\[

C_i(x) \subset  \bigcap_{j=1}^n \big \{\xi\!\in U: \phi_{_F}(\xi,x_i) \le  \phi_{_F}(\xi,x_j)\big\},
\]

 $(ii)$ if $C_i(x)\neq \varnothing$ and $x_j=x_i$, then $C_j(x)= \varnothing$,

\smallskip
 \noindent is called an {\em $F$-Bregman--Voronoi partition} (or more simply a {\em Bregman--Voronoi partition}) induced by the $n$-tuple $x$.

Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space, 0 < p_0 < p_1 <= infinity, 0 < theta < 1, and define p by 1/p = (1-theta)/p_0 + theta/p_1. Then for every measurable f, ||f||_p <= ||f||_{p_0}^{1-theta} ||f||_{p_1}^{theta} (convention 0 * infinity = 0). Consequently L^{p_0} intersect L^{p_1} is contained in L^p for every intermediate p, and t -> log ||f||_{1/t} is a convex function of t in [0, 1/p_0] where finite. This is the 'trivial' (one-function) interpolation inequality; the operator analogue is the Riesz-Thorin theorem.

body:
Let (X,d) be a metric space and let f : X -> (-infinity, +infinity] be lower semicontinuous and bounded below. For each n define f_n(x) = inf over y in X of ( f(y) + n d(x,y) ). Then each f_n is real-valued and n-Lipschitz, the sequence is nondecreasing, f_n <= f for every n, and f_n(x) increases to f(x) at every x. So a lower semicontinuous function bounded below is the pointwise increasing limit of Lipschitz functions. On a Hilbert space with the quadratic kernel (1/(2t))||x-y||^2 in place of n d(x,y) the same construction gives the Moreau envelope of a convex f, which is convex, differentiable with Lipschitz gradient, and increases to f as t decreases to 0.
f lower semicontinuous AND bounded below (boundedness below can be relaxed to a linear minorant);
the approximation is from BELOW and increasing.
For an upper semicontinuous f bounded above the dual sup-convolution gives a decreasing sequence of Lipschitz functions.

The classical Aizenman-Burchard condition establishes tightness of random curves confined to a compact region (planar or spatial) under uniform power bounds P(N_{r, R}^x(gamma_n) >= N) <= K_N (r/R)^{lambda_N} with lambda_N -> infinity. Sequential tightness relaxes this by eliminating the requirement of power decay uniform over all moduli r/R: precompactness holds, for curves in a compact (geodesic) metric space X, under non-uniform regularity lim_{N -> infinity} sup_n P(N_{r, R}^x >= N) = 0 for each fixed annulus (compactness is needed: constant curves escaping to infinity cross no annulus yet are not tight), accommodating pathological curves (such as logarithmic spirals) where scale-invariant power bounds fail.
Curves gamma_n in P(X), X a compact (geodesic) metric space
Modulus non-uniformity allowed

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(L0)] $ \lim_{n\to\infty} \gamma_n=0$,
\item[(L1)] $ \exists \, L,\eps_{0}\in(0,\infty)$  $\forall \eps\in[0,\eps_0]:$ $\|\1+\eps H\|\leq 1-\eps L$ and 

\item[(L3)]  $\displaystyle{\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\gamma_n-\gamma_{n+1}}{\gamma_n^2}=0.}$
\end{enumerate}
Then the matrices $(\bar\Pi[m,n])_{1\le m\le n}$ converge to $-H^{-1}$ when letting
 $m,n\to\infty$ with $t_n-t_m\to\infty$. Furthermore,  the matrices $(\bar\Pi[m,n])_{1\le m\le n}$  are uniformly bounded.

body: [Lemma 20 of arXiv:2609.03951, 'Generalized Semi-Riemannian Submersions and Foliations'] Let $(M,g)$ be a semi-Riemannian manifold, and let $\mu: G \times M \to M$ be an isometric action such that $M / G$ is a manifold and $\pi: M \to M / G$ is a submersion. Then, the horizontal distribution $\mathcal{H}$ is locally generated by basic vector fields. Consequently, any regular homogeneous foliation is a generalized semi-Riemannian foliation.

body: [Definition 5 (Iterative directed graph process) of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Consider the vertex set $V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$, consider degree sequences $\d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ and $\d'=(d_1',\ldots,d_{n}')$ of non-negative integers with $m:=d_1+\ldots+d_n=d_1'+\ldots+d_{n}'>0$, and consider a set $X$ of forbidden arcs. We define $\widetilde{V}:=A \cup B$ with $A=\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}$ and $B=\{w_1',\ldots,w_n'\}$ disjoint, and $$\widetilde{X}:=\{(w_i,w_j'):(v_i,v_j)\in X\}\cup\{(w_i,w_i'):i=1,\ldots,n\}.$$ Consider sampling a bipartite graph from the iterative bipartite graph process on $\widetilde{V}$, $\d$, $\d'$, and $\widetilde{X}$. Identify any pair $w_i$, $w_i'$ with the vertex $v_i$ and any edge $(w_i,w_j')$ with an arc from $v_i$ to $v_j$. This results in a simple directed graph with out- and in- degree sequences $\d$ and $\d'$ and with no arcs from $X$.

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.03495, 'Spectral Characteristics of Autoencoder Parameters as a Vector Representation of Data'] Suppose that assumptions (B1)--(B6) hold. We introduce the notation ${\Delta_r := \|\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}^{data}(\mathbf{X}_1)-\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}^{data}(\mathbf{X}_2)\|_2,}$ where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}^{data}_{1:r}(\cdot)$ denotes the singular values of the data matrices $\mathbf{X}_c$ from the first to the $r$-th.

\noindent Then there exist constants \({C_0>0}\) and \({c_*>0}\) such that, for any \({\delta\in(0;\frac{1}{2})}\), for a sample size \(n\), with probability at least \({1-2\delta}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\big\|\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}^{model}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\psi}}_n(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_1))-
\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1:r}^{model}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\psi}}_n(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_2))\big\|_2
\ge c_*\Delta_r - C_0\Bigl(\sqrt{\tfrac{\log(1/\delta)}{n^2}} + \sqrt{\eta_n} + \tau_n\Bigr),
\end{aligned}
\]
where \({\tau_n := \max(\tau_n^1, \tau_n^2)}\) is the maximum of the optimization errors for models trained on samples of size $n$ using $\mathbf{X}_1$ and $\mathbf{X}_2$.

In particular, if \({\Delta_r>0}\) and \({\eta_n,\tau_n \to 0}\), then as \({n \to \infty}\), the right-hand side remains positive, and the vectors of the first \(r\) singular values remain separated by a nonzero gap with probability tending to 1. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.03495

[Lemma lem:lower_bound_gaussian_lim of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\bm{X}$ be a L\'evy process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with 
the characteristic triplet $(\bm{\gamma_X},\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{\Sigma_X}^{\scalebox{0.6}{$\top$}},\nu_{\bm{X}})$.
For $t\in (0,1]$, denote
$\bm{X}^t=(\bm{X}_{st}/\sqrt{t})_{s\in[0,1]}$. Moreover, let $\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{B}$ be the
Gaussian component of $\bm{X}$ in its L\'evy--It\^o decomposition~(equation eq:levy_ito_decomp of the paper) and define 
  $\bm{S}\coloneqq \bm{X}-\bm{\Sigma_X}\bm{B}$ with L\'evy--Khintchine exponent $\psi_{\bm{S}}$.\\
{\normalfont(a)} Pick any $\bm{u}_*\in\mathbb{R}^d_{\bm{0}}$ and define $C_*\coloneqq |\bm{u}_*|^{-1}|\psi_{\bm{S}_1}(\bm{u}_*)|>0$. Then, we have 
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{W}_1(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{\Sigma}_{\bm{X}}\bm{B}_1)
    \geqslant C_*\sqrt{t}+ \mathcal{O}(t^{3/2}),
\quad\text{as }t \downarrow 0.
\end{align*}
{\normalfont(b)} Let $\lambda$ be the largest eigenvalue of $\bm{\Sigma}_{\bm{X}}\bm{\Sigma}^{\scalebox{0.6}{$\top$}}_{\bm{X}}$. Suppose there exist $\delta\in[1,2)$ and vectors  $(\bm{u}_r)_{r\in(0,\infty)}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d_{\bm{0}}$ satisfying $|\bm{u}_r|=r$ and $c:=\inf_{r>1}r^{-\delta}|\psi_{\bm{S}}(\bm{u}_r)|>0$. Then for any $C_*\in(0,ce^{-\lambda/2})$ we have
\[
\mathcal{W}_1(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{\Sigma}_{\bm{X}}\bm{B}_1) \geqslant C_* t^{1-\delta/2}
\qquad\text{for all sufficiently small }t>0.
\]
title: Lemma lem:lower_bound_gaussian_lim of arXiv:2411.03609

body:
[Definition def:pseudo of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] For an initial law $\pi_0$, $\widehat\pi_0:=\binom{\pi_0}{0}$, set $\Phi_0:=B\widehat\pi_0$ and, for $z\in\mathbb{C}$,

\[
\Phi_z:=W_z\Phi_0\in\mathbb{C}^{2M}\quad(\text{the \emph{pseudo-wave}}),\qquad
\rho_z:=\Phi_z\Phi_z^{T}\in\operatorname{Sym}_{2M}(\mathbb{C})\quad(\text{the \emph{pseudo-density}}).
\]

The superscript $T$ is the plain transpose, with no complex conjugation, so
$\rho_z$ is complex symmetric and in general not Hermitian.
title: Pseudo-wave and pseudo-density

[Lemma 13 (Loss difference under operator-valued observations) of arXiv:2608.24426, 'Sequential operator learning under dependent data'] Let $\mdlspace$ be a real Hilbert space and, for each $i\in\range{\iteridx}$, let $\obsop_i:\obsspace_i\to\mdlspace$ be bounded and linear. Suppose that $\loss_i(\cdot,\observation_i)$ is twice Fr\'echet differentiable and $\alpha$-strongly convex for some $\alpha>0$, and that $R_\iteridx:\mdlspace\to\R$ is Fr\'echet differentiable and $\regfactor_\iteridx$-strongly convex for some $\regfactor_\iteridx>0$. Define $\Loss_\iteridx(\mdlop):=\sum_{i=1}^\iteridx\loss_i(\obsop_i^\adj(\mdlop),\observation_i)+R_\iteridx(\mdlop)$, and let $\widehat{\mdlop}_\iteridx$ minimize $\Loss_\iteridx$ over $\mdlspace$. Then, for every $\mdlop\in\mdlspace$,
\begin{equation}
    \frac{1}{2}\norm{\mdlop-\widehat{\mdlop}_\iteridx}_{\operator{H}_\iteridx}^2
    \leq
    \Loss_\iteridx(\mdlop)-\Loss_\iteridx(\widehat{\mdlop}_\iteridx)
    \leq
    \frac{1}{2}\norm{\nabla\Loss_\iteridx(\mdlop)}_{\operator{H}_\iteridx^{-1}}^2,
    
\end{equation}
where $\operator{H}_\iteridx:=\regfactor_\iteridx\idop+\alpha\sum_{i=1}^\iteridx\obsop_i\obsop_i^\adj$.
title: Loss difference under operator-valued observations

body:
[Lemma lem:deriveSPDE of arXiv:2608.27828, 'Scaling limit of the 3D abelian Yang--Mills Langevin dynamics'] On the time interval $t<\tau_\varepsilon$ where $\tau_\varepsilon$ is as in (equation e:def-tau of the paper), the DeTurck-gauge-fixed Langevin dynamics (equation eq:NParaDisc of the paper) can be written as
\begin{equ}

\partial_t \theta^\varepsilon(e)  
 = \Delta_\varepsilon \theta^\varepsilon
+ a_3 \, \varepsilon^4 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}_\varepsilon^* \,(\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}_\varepsilon \theta^\varepsilon)^3(e)

+ \varepsilon^{-2} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}_\varepsilon^* (\mathfrak{R}(\varepsilon^2 \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d}_\varepsilon \theta^\varepsilon))(e)
+\xi^\varepsilon
\end{equ}
where  $a_3 = -\frac16 h^{(4)}(0)$ and $\mathfrak{R}(z):=
    z-a_{3}z^3-h'(z)$.

Moreover, there exists $C>0$, independent of $\eps$, such that, for all $z\in [-\rho_0,\rho_0]$,
\begin{equ}[e:coeff-bounds]
|a_3|\le C,
\qquad
|\mathfrak R(z)|\le C|z|^5.
\end{equ} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:deriveSPDE of arXiv:2608.27828

[Theorem thm:radial-ig of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $\beta,\rho_1,...,\rho_n\in\mathbb{R}$, define $\alpha$ as in~(equation eq:radial-alpha of the paper),  and let $h$ be the GFF on $\mathbb{D}$ described  above. Then there exists a unique coupling between $h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ and a radial $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\beta(\underline\rho)$ process in $\mathbb{D}$ from $-i$ targeted at 0 with force points $x_1,...,x_n$ such that the following holds. For every $\eta$-stopping time $\tau$, the conditional law of $h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ given $\eta|_{[0,\tau]}$ is that of $\tilde h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ where $\tilde h$ is a GFF on $\mathbb{D}\backslash\eta([0,\tau])$ such that $\tilde h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ has the same boundary conditions as $h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ on $\partial \mathbb D$. If $\kappa\in(0,4)$, then $\tilde h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ has $-\alpha$-flow line boundary conditions on $\eta([0,\tau])$. If $\kappa'>4$, then $\tilde h+\alpha\arg(\cdot)+\beta\log|\cdot|$ has $-\alpha$-flow line boundary conditions with angle $\frac{\pi}{2}$ (resp.\ $-\frac{\pi}{2}$) on the left (resp.\ right) side of $\eta([0,\tau])$. 
	
	    In this coupling, $\eta([0,\tau])$ is a local set of $h$, and $\eta$ is measurable with respect to $h$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$

$
\end{enumerate}

For n>=64 let R_n be symmetric +/-1 and B_n an independent Bernoulli variable with p_n=exp(-sqrt(n)). Set X_n=n^{1/3}R_n+(n/4)(B_n-p_n), Y_n=3n/2+X_n. Then EX_n=0, n<=Y_n<=2n, and Var X_n=n^{2/3}+(n^2/16)p_n(1-p_n)~n^{2/3}. For this family define chi_a=inf{a: for some alpha>0, sup_n E exp(alpha|X_n|/n^a)<infinity} and chi_b=sup{b: for some c>0,N, Var X_n>=c n^{2b} for all n>=N}. One has chi_a=1/2 and chi_b=1/3. Thus a pure variance power law and uniform square-root exponential concentration do not by themselves identify the two fluctuation thresholds. Indexing by lattice endpoints with n=ceil(|v|) preserves the gap. This is an abstract random-variable family, not an FPP metric or iid-edge construction, and it does not refute P0110.

\begin{equation}
c\, d_U(x)\le \rho_U(x)\le C\, d_U(x), \qquad\text{and}\qquad 
|D^\alpha \rho_U|\leq C_{|\alpha|} d_U(x)^{1-|\alpha|} 
 \text{ for }\alpha \in \mathbb N_0^d,  
\end{equation}
where the constant  $ C_{|\alpha|}$  depends only on $d$ and 
 $|\alpha|=\sum_1^d \alpha_i$. In particular, $|\nabla \rho_U(x)|\le C_1$ and $\rho_U$ is globally Lipschitz on $U$, and its extension by $0$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus U$ is globally Lipschitz on $\mathbb R^d$.

Moreover, the construction is translation-covariant in the sense 
\begin{equation}
\rho_{U+z}(x+z)=\rho_U(x) \qquad\forall x\in U.
\end{equation}

Let X ~ N(0, I_n) and let f: R^n -> R be 1-Lipschitz. Let M be a median of f(X). Then for all t > 0, P(f(X) - M >= t) <= 1 - Phi(t) <= exp(- t^2 / 2), and for all t >= 0, P(|f(X) - M| >= t) <= 2 * exp(- t^2 / 2). At t = 0 the one-sided bound fails when f(X) has an atom at M (a constant f gives 1 against 1/2).
X ~ N(0, I_n)
f is 1-Lipschitz
M is a median of f(X)
t > 0 for the one-sided bound, t >= 0 for the two-sided one

	Under (ass4.1 of the paper), BSVIE ((1.1 of the paper))  admits a unique global adapted solution
	$(Y(\cdot), Z(\cdot,\cdot))\in L^\infty_{\mathbb{F}}[0,T]\times  {\cal Z}^2_{\mathbb{F}}(\Delta[0,T];\mathbb{R}^d).$  Moreover, there exist two positive constants

		\|Y(\cdot)\|_{L_{\mathbb{F}}^\infty[0,T]}\leqslant M_1\quad\hbox{and}\quad\ \|Z(\cdot,\cdot)\|^2_{{\cal Z}^2_{\mathbb{F}}(\Delta[0,T])}\leqslant M_2.
	\end{equation*}

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2605.05388, 'The Efron-Stein inequality for identically distributed pairs'] Let \(\epsilon\in \mathbb R\), let \(X_i\) be uniform on \([0,2\pi]\) and let \(Y_i\) equal \(X_i+2\epsilon\) mod \(2\pi\). Then \(X_i\stackrel{d}{=}Y_i\). Assume that the pairs \((X_i,Y_i)\) are independent as \(i\) varies. Let \(f(x_1,\ldots x_n)=\sin(x_1+\ldots +x_n)\), and let \(Z_i=f(X_1,\ldots X_{i},Y_{i+1},\ldots Y_n)\). Then the random variables \(Z_i\) (and hence the ratio on the left-hand side of \eqref{e}) depend on \(\epsilon\), and we have
\begin{equation}
\lim_{\epsilon\to 0} \frac
{E(Z_n-Z_0)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n E(Z_i-Z_{i-1})^2}=n.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 3 of arXiv:2605.05388

[Lem decomposition A-nu, B-nu, C-nu of arXiv:2608.23156, 'Disc counting statistics of the real Ginibre ensemble'] Under the assumptions of Lemma~(lem: generating func cN counting statistics of the paper), for every positive integer $\nu$, we have

        \mathbf{A}_N^{(\nu)}(R) &= \mathbf{M}_N(R) - (1-2^{-\nu}) \mathbf{E}_{N,1}(R),
        \\
        \mathbf{B}_N^{(\nu)}(R) &= \mathbf{L}_N(R) - \mathbf{M}_N(R) - \mathbf{E}_{N,2}(R). 
    \end{align} 
Consequently, the skew-orthogonal polynomial representations

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] Let $\mu,\nu\in\Delta(\Omega)$. The Kullback--Leibler divergence,
also called the relative entropy, of $\mu$ relative to $\nu$ is
\[
  \KL(\mu\|\nu)
  :=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}
     \mu(\omega)\log\frac{\mu(\omega)}{\nu(\omega)},
\]
with the conventions
$0\log\frac0y=0$ for $y\geq 0$ and $x\log\frac x0=+\infty$ for $x>0$.
title: Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.02017

Let $T>0$ and $u\in C^2_1(\mathbb R^n\times(0,T])\cap C(\mathbb R^n\times[0,T])$ satisfy $u_t-\Delta u=0$ in $\mathbb R^n\times(0,T)$ and $u(\cdot,0)=g$. If there are constants $A,a>0$ with $u(x,t)\le Ae^{a|x|^2}$ for all $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $0\le t\le T$, then $\sup_{\mathbb R^n\times[0,T]}u=\sup_{\mathbb R^n}g$ (maximum principle for the Cauchy problem). Consequently, for continuous $f$ and $g$, the problem $u_t-\Delta u=f$ in $\mathbb R^n\times(0,T)$, $u(\cdot,0)=g$, has at most one solution in $C^2_1(\mathbb R^n\times(0,T])\cap C(\mathbb R^n\times[0,T])$ satisfying $|u(x,t)|\le Ae^{a|x|^2}$ on $\mathbb R^n\times[0,T]$ with $A,a$ independent of $t$. The growth hypothesis cannot be dropped (Tychonoff's example).

body:
Backward uniqueness says the map from $u(\cdot,T)$ to $u(\cdot,0)$ is injective; it says nothing about continuity of that map or about its range, and both fail badly -- the backward heat problem is the standard ill-posed problem of Hadamard. (1) No stability: on $U=(0,\pi)$ with Dirichlet data, $u_k(x,t)=e^{-k^2t}\sin(kx)$ has $\|u_k(\cdot,T)\|_{C^m}\le k^me^{-k^2T}\to0$ for every $m$ while $\|u_k(\cdot,0)\|_{L^2}=\sqrt{\pi/2}$ is fixed. Hence there is no estimate $\|u(\cdot,0)\|\le C\|u(\cdot,T)\|$ in any pair of norms, and numerical backward continuation must be regularized. (2) No solvability: $e^{T\Delta_D}$ has range $\{\psi=\sum_kc_k\sin(kx):\sum_k e^{2k^2T}c_k^2<\infty\}$, a dense but meagre subspace of $L^2$; for instance $\psi(x)=\sum_{k\ge1}k^{-2}\sin(kx)\in L^2$ is not $u(\cdot,T)$ for any solution with $u(\cdot,0)\in L^2$, since that would require coefficients $e^{k^2T}k^{-2}$ at time $0$. Backward-in-time data must be analytic-like (exponentially decaying spectral coefficients). (3) What does survive is conditional stability of logarithmic or Holder type: under the a priori bound $\|u(\cdot,0)\|_{L^2}\le M$, log-convexity gives $\|u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^2}\le M^{1-t/T}\|u(\cdot,T)\|_{L^2}^{t/T}$ for $0<t<T$, with the estimate degenerating exactly as $t\downarrow0$. An auditor should flag any argument that uses backward uniqueness to produce a bound at the earlier time without such an a priori bound.
Injectivity of the solution map does not imply continuity of its inverse
The range of the forward solution operator is a proper dense subspace
Conditional (Holder) stability requires an a priori bound at the initial time and degenerates as t tends to 0
title: Pitfall: Backward uniqueness is not backward stability or backward solvability

[Lemma lem:Ofer-A4 of arXiv:2608.05262, 'The law of $(1+1)$D SOS with an area tilt in a wedge'] Fix $b,\delta,\eta>0$ and consider the area-tilted sequence $\{Y_i,  i \in I=[0,k]\}$ 
with $\mathbb Z$-valued {\sc{\lowercase{iid}}} increments 

from a zero-mean,  log-concave law of 
finite exponential moments and positive probabilities of $\{-1,0,1\}$-valued increments. 
For $C<\infty$,  $\kappa>0$ depending on $b,\delta,\eta$ and any $k \in [\eta N,2N]$,
\[
\mathbb P_{1,I;\infty,0}^{b,1;0,\star} \big( Y_k \ge N^{1/3+\delta} \big) \le C e^{- N^{\kappa}} \,. 
\]

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.11279, 'Flocking with Multiple Types: Competition, Fluid Limits and Traveling Waves'] We have the following:
    \begin{enumerate}[label = (\alph*)]
        \item  Suppose that Assumptions \ref{assumption0} and \ref{assumption2} hold. Then the sequence $\{\mu_n(\cdot)\!: n\in\nat\}$ is $\mathscr{C}$-tight in the space $\mathscr{D}\big([0, \infty), \mathscr{P}_1(\real\times \{+,-\})\big)$. 

        \item  In addition, suppose that Assumptions \ref{assumption3} and \ref{assumption4} hold. Then any subsequential weak limit point $\mu(\cdot)$ of $\{\mu_n(\cdot)\!: n\in\nat\}$ in $\DDD\big([0, \infty), \PPP_1(\real \times \{+, -\})\big)$ satisfies \eqref{originalMVE}, the McKean-Vlasov equation, for $t \ge 0$ and $f \in \HHH$. Moreover, there exists a $B_0 \in (0,\infty)$, depending only on $C_0$ in Assumption \ref{assumption3} and the jump distribution $J$ such that, almost surely, $\mu \in \TTT_{B_0}$.

        \item  Furthermore, if $\mu_n(0) \cpinf{n} \nu$ in $\PPP_1\bigparens{\real \times \{+, -\}}$, where $\nu$ is deterministic, then $\mu_n(\cdot) \cpinf{n} \mu(\cdot)$ in $\DDD\big([0, \infty), \PPP_1(\real \times \{+, -\})\big)$, where $\mu(\cdot)$ is the unique and deterministic solution to \eqref{originalMVE} in $\TTT_{B_0}$ with initial condition $\mu(0) = \nu$. 
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.11279

body: [Defn 7 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\sA=(A,\alpha:L\to A)\in \mathrm{PreLog}_{\sR}$. We denote by $\omega_{\sA/\sR}^*$ the log de Rham complex of $\sA$ over $\sR$. It is a (strict) cdga over $A$. Note that we have $\widehat{\omega}_{\sA/\sR}^* /p \simeq {\omega}_{\sA/p/\sR/p}^*$.

body:
[Corollary 4 (Exact posterior--prior reverse-path relative entropy) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Fix $T>t>0$.  On the reverse clock $u\in[0,T-t]$, let
$\mathbb Q^{r,\mathrm{rev}}_{[t,T]}$ and
$\mathbb P^{\mathrm{rev}}_{[t,T]}$ be the time-reversal pushforwards of the
forward OU path laws initialized from $q_t^r$ and $p_t$, respectively.
When the noised marginals are smooth and positive, they coincide with the
reverse processes \eqref{eq:posterior-reverse-sde} and
\eqref{eq:prior-reverse-sde}, initialized from $q_T^r$ and $p_T$.
Assume the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-r-entropy-dissipation} on \([t,T]\).  Then
\begin{equation}

\KL\!\left(
\mathbb Q^{r,\mathrm{rev}}_{[t,T]}
\middle\|
\mathbb P^{\mathrm{rev}}_{[t,T]}
\right)
=
\mathcal K_t(r)
=
\mathcal K_T(r)+
\int_t^T\E_{X_u\mid r}\|g_u(X_u,r)\|^2\,\dd u.
\end{equation}
Under the normalization $\dd X_t=-X_t\dd t+\sqrt2\dd W_t$, the coefficient of
the integral is one: the two reverse drifts differ by $2g_t$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact posterior--prior reverse-path relative entropy

body:
[Theorem 33 (Airy uniformisation and cubic Stokes multiplier) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let
\[
 H_3(x)=x^3-3x,
 \qquad
 \varphi_3(t)
 =
 \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \int_{\R}
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{x^2}{2}+itH_3(x)\right)\dd x .
\]
Then \(\varphi_3\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 27t^3(18t^2+1)y''
 +(486t^4+99t^2+1)y'
 +6t(18t^2+1)^2y=0.

\end{equation}

On a simply connected sector at \(t=0\) containing the positive real
axis, choose the branches for which \(t^{1/3}>0\) when \(t>0\), and put
\begin{align}
 z(t)
 &=
 \frac{1-36t^2}
 {12\,3^{1/3}t^{4/3}},
 \\
 C(t)
 &=
 \sqrt{2\pi}\,
 (3t)^{-1/3}
 \exp\!\left(\frac1{108t^2}-\frac12\right),
 \\
 \zeta(t)
 &=
 \frac23 z(t)^{3/2}
 =
 \frac{(1-36t^2)^{3/2}}{108t^2}.
 
\end{align}
Then the real Gaussian cycle is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \varphi_3(t)=F_0(t):=C(t)\Ai(z(t)),
 \qquad t>0.

\end{equation}
In particular, the local solution space of \eqref{eq:h3-airy-ode} is the
pullback, with gauge \(C(t)\), of the Airy equation
\[
 w''(z)=zw(z).
\]

Let \(\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}\) and define
\begin{align}
 F_+(t)
 &=
 C(t)e^{i\pi/6}\Ai(\omega z(t)),
 \\
 F_-(t)
 &=
 C(t)e^{-i\pi/6}\Ai(\omega^2 z(t)).
 
\end{align}
The functions \(F_+\) and \(F_-\) are the two lateral sectorial
realisations of the same dominant formal solution at the positive real
Stokes ray, and
\begin{equation}
 F_+(t)-F_-(t)=iF_0(t).

\end{equation}
Consequently, for
\[
 \mathcal Y_-=(F_0,F_-),
 \qquad
 \mathcal Y_+=(F_0,F_+),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal Y_+
 =
 \mathcal Y_-
 \begin{pmatrix}
 1&i\\
 0&1
 \end{pmatrix}.

\end{equation}
Thus the multiplier selected by the real Gaussian cycle is nonzero and,
in the normalisation \eqref{eq:h3-Fplus}--\eqref{eq:h3-Fminus}, equals
\(i\).  Reversing the orientation replaces \(i\) by \(-i\).

[Theorem thm:q-level-annular-decay-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Fix \(q\in(1,2)\) with \(\rho(q)<1\), and let
\[
    0<\beta<\beta_X(q)
    =
    -\frac1q\log_2\rho(q).
\]
Then, almost surely, there exists a finite random constant
\(C_\beta(\omega)<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{2^n\le |\xi|\le 2^{n+1}}
    |\widehat{\mu}(\xi)|
    \le
    C_\beta(\omega)2^{-\beta n}
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large \(n\).
