[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2609.03556, 'An Effective SPDE Model for a Schr\"odinger Equation with a Fluctuating Magnetic Potential'] \label[lemma]{lemma_ito_limit_martingales}
Let $v,v'\in H^1(\R^d)$ and $0\leq s\leq t\leq T$. Set
\begin{align*}
 a_k^v(r)&:=\langle \sigma_k\bar\psi_r,\nabla v\rangle,
 &b_{k,j}^v(r)&:=\langle (\sigma_k\cdot\sigma_j)\bar\psi_r,v\rangle,
 &c_{k}^v(r,r')&:=\langle A_r^n\cdot\sigma_k\bar{\psi}_{r'},v\rangle.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align}
    \langle\mathbb{E}\left[\Theta^n_t-\Theta^n_s\mid\mathcal{F}^n_s\right],v\rangle&=- \frac{1}{\sqrt{\tau_n}}\int_s^t e^{-r/\tau_n}\langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_r,\nabla v\rangle dr\notag\\ &- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{{\tau_n}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t \int_0^s e^{-(r-u)/\tau_n} a_k^v(r) dW^{k,n}_u dr,\\
        \langle\mathbb{E}\left[\Gamma^n_t-\Gamma^n_s\mid\mathcal{F}^n_s\right],v\rangle&=\int_s^t e^{-2r/\tau_{n}} \left\langle\frac{\wick{|A^n_0|^2}}{\sqrt{\tau_n}}\bar{\psi}_r,v\right\rangle dr\notag\\ & +\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\tau_n}\sum_{k\in I }\int_s^t\int_0^s e^{-2(r-u)/\tau_n} c_k^v(u,r) dW^{k,n}_u   dr,
\end{align}
and
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\!\left[
  \left|\left\langle
   \mathbb E[\Theta_t^n-\Theta_s^n\mid\mathcal F_s^n],v
  \right\rangle\right|\right]
 &\lesssim \sqrt{\tau_n}\,
  \sup_{r\in[0,T]}\|\bar\psi_r\|\,\|v\|_{H^1},
 \\
 \mathbb E\!\left[
  \left|\left\langle
   \mathbb E[\Gamma_t^n-\Gamma_s^n\mid\mathcal F_s^n],v
  \right\rangle\right|\right]
 &\lesssim \sqrt{\tau_n}\,
  \sup_{r\in[0,T]}\|\bar\psi_r\|\,\|v\|_{H^1}.
 
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{align}
 &\mathbb E\!\left[
  \langle\Theta_t^n-\Theta_s^n,v\rangle
  \langle\Theta_t^n-\Theta_s^n,v'\rangle
  \,\middle|\,\mathcal F_s^n\right]\notag\\
 &\qquad=\frac1{\tau_n}\sum_{k\in I}
  \int_s^t\!\!\int_s^t e^{-|r-r'|/\tau_n}
  a_k^v(r)a_k^{v'}(r')\,dr\,dr'
  +\rho_{s,t}^{1,n}(v,v'),\\
 &\mathbb E\!\left[
  \langle\Gamma_t^n-\Gamma_s^n,v\rangle
  \langle\Gamma_t^n-\Gamma_s^n,v'\rangle
  \,\middle|\,\mathcal F_s^n\right]\notag\\
 &\qquad=\frac2{\tau_n}\sum_{k,j\in I}
  \int_s^t\!\!\int_s^t e^{-2|r-r'|/\tau_n}
  b_{k,j}^v(r)b_{k,j}^{v'}(r')\,dr\,dr'
  +\rho_{s,t}^{2,n}(v,v'),\\
 &\mathbb E\!\left[
  \langle\Theta_t^n-\Theta_s^n,v\rangle
  \langle\Gamma_t^n-\Gamma_s^n,v'\rangle
  \,\middle|\,\mathcal F_s^n\right]
  =\rho_{s,t}^{3,n}(v,v'),
\end{align}
where
\begin{align*}
    \rho^{1,n}_{s,t}(v,v')&=\frac{1}{\tau_n}\int_s^t\int_s^t e^{-(r+r')/\tau_n} \langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_r,\nabla v\rangle \langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_{r'},\nabla v'\rangle dr dr'\\ & +\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^{s} e^{-(r+r'-u)/\tau_n}\langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_r,\nabla v\rangle a_k^{v'}(r') dW^{k,n}_u dr dr'\\ & +\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^{s} e^{-(r+r'-u)/\tau_n} a_k^v(r) \langle A^n_0 \bar{\psi}_{r'},\nabla v'\rangle  dW^{k,n}_u dr dr'\\ &+\frac{2}{\tau_n^2}\sum_{k,k'\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^s \int_0^s e^{-(r+r'-u-u')/\tau_n}a_k^v(r)  a_k^{v'}(r') dW^{k,n}_u dW^{k',n}_{u'}dr dr'\\ & -\frac{1}{\tau_n}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t \int_s^t  e^{-(r+r'-2s)/\tau_n} a_k^v(r)a_k^{v'}(r') dr dr',
    \\ \rho^{2,n}_{s,t}(v,v')&=\frac{1}{\tau_n}\int_s^t\int_s^t e^{-2(r+r')/\tau_n} \langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_r, v\rangle \langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_{r'}, v'\rangle dr dr'\\ & +\frac{\sqrt{8}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^{s} e^{-2(r+r'-u)/\tau_n}\langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_r, v\rangle c_k^{v'}(u,r') dW^{k,n}_u dr dr'\\ & +\frac{\sqrt{8}}{\tau_n^{3/2}}\sum_{k\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^{s} e^{-2(r+r'-u)/\tau_n} c_k^{v}(u,r) \langle \wick{|A^n_0|^2} \bar{\psi}_{r'}, v'\rangle  dW^{k,n}_u dr dr'\\ &+\frac{8}{\tau_n^2}\sum_{k,k'\in I}\int_s^t\int_s^t\int_0^s \int_0^s e^{-2(r+r'-u-u')/\tau_n} c_k^v(u,r) c_{k'}^{v'}(u',r') dW^{k,n}_u dW^{k',n}_{u'}dr dr'\\ & -\frac{2}{\tau_n}\sum_{k,k'\in I}\int_s^t \int_s^t  e^{-2(r+r'-2s)/\tau_n} b_{k,k'}^v(r) b_{k,k'}^{v'}(r') dr dr'   \\

$[0,(\log k)/4]$, for all sufficiently large $k$.

[Proposition 5 (Compactness and support convergence) of arXiv:2609.03916, 'Halfspace Theorems for Anisotropic Minimal Surfaces and Perimeter Minimizers'] Let $E_j$ be global $\Phi$-perimeter minimizers with locally uniformly
bounded perimeter, meaning that
$\sup_j|D\chi_{E_j}|(K)<\infty$ for every compact set $K$.  After passing to a
subsequence, there is a set $E$ of locally finite perimeter such that
\begin{equation}
  \chi_{E_j}\to\chi_E\quad\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}},
  \qquad
  D\chi_{E_j}\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}D\chi_E,
  \qquad
  |D\chi_{E_j}|\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}|D\chi_E|.
\end{equation}
The limit $E$ is a global minimizer, and
$\supp|D\chi_{E_j}|$ converges to $\supp|D\chi_E|$ locally in Hausdorff
distance. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Compactness and support convergence

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The real probability measures having as even moments/moments the central binomial coefficients, $D_k=\binom{2k}{k}$, are the measures
$$\alpha_1=\frac{1}{\pi\sqrt{4-x^2}}\,dx\quad,\quad\alpha_1'=\frac{1}{\pi\sqrt{x(4-x)}}\,dx$$
called arcsine laws on $[-2,2]$, and on $[0,4]$.

body: [Theorem 1.4 of arXiv:2512.17823, 'van den Berg-Kesten--type correlation inequalities for disjoint polymers in the KPZ univer'] There exist $C,c>0$ such that the following holds. Let $y\in\mathbb R$, $K,R\geq 0$, and $\mathsf{A}\subseteq\mathcal{C}([0,K],\mathbb R)$ be an increasing Borel measurable set. For any $t>0$, $M>0$, and a.e. $f\in\mathcal{C}([y-R,y],\mathbb R)$, (1.8) $\begin{split}&\mathbb P\Bigl(\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,2}|_{[y,y+K]}-Ct^{-1/3}\log M\in\mathsf{A}\ \Big|\ \hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}|_{[y-R,y]}=f\Bigr)\\ &\leq\mathbb P\left(\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}|_{[y,y+K]}\in\mathsf{A}\right)+\frac{3(K+1)t^{2/3}\exp(-cM^{2})}{\mathbb P(\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}|_{[y-R,y]}\geq f)}.\end{split}$ The same also holds when the conditioning is replaced by $\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}|_{[y-R,y]}\geq f$, in which case we may relax the continuity assumption and allow any $f:[y-R,y]\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}$ which is upper semicontinuous. All of the previous also hold under both conditionings when $+K$ is replaced by $-K$ and $-R$ by $+R$ simultaneously.

body:
Lojasiewicz gradient inequality. Let U be an open subset of R^n, f: U -> R real analytic, and p in U. There are an open neighbourhood W of p in U and constants theta in (0,1) and c > 0 such that |f(x) - f(p)|^theta <= c |grad f(x)| for every x in W. Consequence (finite length and convergence of bounded gradient trajectories). Let x: [0, infinity) -> U solve x'(t) = -grad f(x(t)) and suppose the trajectory {x(t): t >= 0} has compact closure in U. Then x has finite length, int_0^infinity |x'(t)| dt < infinity, and x(t) converges as t -> infinity to a single critical point a of f. Near a, the tail length obeys int_t^infinity |x'(s)| ds <= (c/(1-theta)) (f(x(t)) - f(a))^(1-theta), with c and theta the constants of the inequality at a. The same holds for gradient ascent x' = +grad f(x) with f replaced by -f. Critical points need not be isolated; smoothness alone is not enough (there are smooth functions with bounded gradient trajectories that spiral forever without converging).
f real analytic on an open set U in R^n
x solves the gradient flow x' = -grad f(x) on [0, infinity)
the trajectory has compact closure in U (precompact; bounded is enough when U = R^n)

body: A Hopfield network is a form of recurrent neural network, or a spin glass system, that can serve as a content-addressable memory. The Hopfield network, named for John Hopfield, consists of a single layer of neurons, where each neuron is connected to every other neuron except itself. These connections are bidirectional and symmetric, meaning the weight of the connection from neuron i to neuron j is the same as the weight from neuron j to neuron i. Patterns are associatively recalled by fixing certain inputs, and dynamically evolve the network to minimize an energy function, towards local energy minimum states that correspond to stored patterns. Patterns are associatively learned by a Hebbian learning algorithm.
title: Hopfield network

[Prop 60 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $m, r_1, r_2, s$ be positive integers. Let $M_1$ (resp.\ $M_2$) be a submatroid of 
$MQ_{r_1}(m)$ (resp.\ $MQ_{r_2}(m)$) containing a rank-$s$ Dowling subgeometry as a flat $F$.
Then the modular join $P_{F}(M_1, M_2)$ is a submatroid of $MQ_{r}(m)$, where 
$r \deq r_1 + r_2 - s$.

[Thm main of arXiv:2509.03065, 'Mathematical research with GPT-5: a Malliavin-Stein experiment'] For integers $p\neq q$, with $p$ odd, $q$ even, let
\begin{equation}
X = I_p(f), \qquad Y = I_q(g), \qquad Z = X+Y,
\end{equation}
satisfying $E[Z^2]=1$. Write $\kappa_4(Z)=\mathbb E[Z^4]-3$.
Then, we have
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Z,N(0,1)) \;\le\; \sqrt{6\,\kappa_4(Z)},
\end{equation}
with $d_{\mathrm{TV}}$ the total variation distance.
In particular, if $Z_n = I_p(f_n) + I_q(g_n)$ with $E[Z_n^2]=1$ and $\kappa_4(Z_n)\to 0$, then
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Z_n,N(0,1)) \;\longrightarrow\;0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Quantitative two-chaos fourth moment theorem

body:
[Theorem 98 (Evolution-family stochastic entrance and Galerkin stability) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $U(t,s)$ be a deterministic evolution family on a separable Hilbert space
$H$.  Let $N$ be a continuous square-integrable martingale on a Hilbert noise
space $U_0$, and let $K_s:U_0\to H$ be predictable.  For every terminal time
$t$ assume that $s\mapsto U(t,s)K_s$ is stochastically integrable and put
\[
 Z_r^{s\mid t}=\int_{(s,r]}U(t,a)K_a\,\mathrm dN_a,
 \qquad s\le r\le t.
\]
Assume locally in $t$ that the terminal-frame trace energies
\[
 \mathcal E_t^{(t)}
 =\operatorname{Tr}\langle\!\langle Z^{0\mid t}\rangle\!\rangle_t
\]
are finite.  Then the split degree-two increments
$\mathbf Z_{s,t}=(Z_t^{s\mid t},A_{s,t}^{(t)},Q_{s,t}^{(t)})$ are critical
entrances.  For a bounded spatial map $B$, write
$B_\#(x,A,Q)=(Bx,BAB^*,BQB^*)$.  With this convention they satisfy the
transported Chen law
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf Z_{s,t}
 =U(t,u)_\#\mathbf Z_{s,u}\circ\mathbf Z_{u,t},
 \qquad s\le u\le t.
 
\end{equation}
Here the early increment is first constructed in the terminal $u$ frame and
then pushed to the terminal $t$ frame.

Let $K^{(m)}$ be finite-rank Galerkin approximants.  For a fixed terminal
$t$, if
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}
 \langle\!\langle
  Z^{K^{(m)}-K,\,0\mid t}
 \rangle\!\rangle_t\longrightarrow0,
 
\end{equation}
then the corresponding first levels, areas, and brackets converge ucp on
$[0,t]$ in the critical split topology.  The estimates are uniform over a
family of deterministic terminal frames whenever their energy and error
bounds are uniform.  Joint ucp convergence in the terminal parameter requires
an additional terminal-frame continuity or maximal estimate.  Adding an adapted finite-variation drift whose range on each compact
interval is contained in a deterministic finite-dimensional subspace of $H$
changes the area only by trace-class terms and preserves the entrance.

For exact critical unshaped tanh K_next=q S_(n,q), v=1/(nq), V_next=1/(n K_next), small fixed q<=epsilon and sufficiently large n, E(V_next-v)=(2v+2)/n+[4v-4-5/(3v)]/n^2+r, |r|<=C[v/n^(5/2)+(1+1/v+1/v^2)/n^3+v exp(-cn)]. On each fixed0<q<=Q the global reciprocal first/second moment and coarse drift estimates stated in the proof hold. Assumptions: Gaussian iid rows, variance1/n, zero bias, no shaped-activation normalizer; q=1/(nv). Constants uniform in small q and depend on fixed Q for the global estimates. Inverse moments justified by C044, n sufficiently large. Model: K_(j+1)=n^-1 sum_(i=1)^n tanh(sqrt(K_j)Z_(j,i))^2, with independent standard Gaussian rows and layers, K0>0 fixed, no bias, Gaussian weight variance exactly1/n, and no width-dependent normalizer. Write Y_q=tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2/q, S_(n,q)=n^-1 sum_i Y_q(Z_i), q=K_j, v=1/(nq), V_next=1/(nK_(j+1)). Limit: Unaudited tail and remainder proof; exact symbolic coefficient checks are separate from a proof audit.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:3d0face865ebb1a496c1c5b8aa5a366d01d218fc34c2a57768d81c094b1ab539","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/3d/3d0face865ebb1a496c1c5b8aa5a366d01d218fc34c2a57768d81c094b1ab539.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b6b80062e37a23fca82e641d20dba351ce5b2a9b7c0adb121f8f3309c6a0ca51","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-next-reciprocal-drift","bundle_id":"population.t244-critical-tanh-reciprocal-mean-rate-016","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_016.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:t244-tanh-next-reciprocal-drift","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C044-C045: exact critical tanh inverse moments and next reciprocal drift

Version 1, 20 October 2026. Target3, kind moved. Proofs (unaudited).
Prior-work distinctions are C025: variance1/n, zero bias, unshaped tanh;
no shaped-activation variance multiplier. No literature novelty is asserted.

Write Y_q=tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2/q for q>0 and Z standard Gaussian, and
S_(n,q)=n^(-1)sum_(i=1)^n Y_q(Z_i), with iid rows.

## C044: uniform inverse sample moments and deleted tails

For every fixed Q<infinity and positive integer p, there is a finite
C_(Q,p) such that

    sup_(0<q<=Q, n>=4p) E[S_(n,q)^(-p)] <= C_(Q,p).            (1)

For any fixed sufficiently small eta>0, with m(q)=E Y_q and
G_(n,q)={|S_(n,q)-m(q)|<=eta},

    P(G_(n,q)^c)<=C_Q exp(-c_Q n),
    E[S_(n,q)^(-p);G_(n,q)^c]<=C_(Q,p)exp(-c_Q n/2), n>=8p.   (2)

Constants can be made explicit from the Gaussian expectations in the
proof. The sample mean is strictly positive almost surely. These are
exact-chain inverse moment estimates, in contrast with the ReLU atom and
near-collinearity obstruction.

Proof. tanh(x)/x decreases for x>0: tanh(x)-x sech(x)^2 has derivative
2x sech(x)^2 tanh(x)>0 and value0 at zero. Therefore Y_q>=Y_Q for q<=Q,
and Y_q<=Z^2. Let H=Y_Q>0 and phi(s)=E exp(-sH). For small y>0,

    P(H<=y)=P(|Z|<=arctanh(sqrt(Qy))/sqrt(Q))<=C sqrt(y),

using arctanh(w)<=2w for w<=1/2 and the bounded Gaussian density.
Increasing C_Q extends P(H<=y)<=C_Q sqrt(y) to every y>0.
Integration by parts gives phi(s)<=C'_Q s^(-1/2). Also for0<=s<=1,

    phi(s)<=1-c_Q s<=exp(-c_Q s), c_Q=E[H exp(-H)]>0,

and rho_Q=phi(1)<1. The Gamma identity and independence yield

    E[(n^(-1)sum_i H_i)^(-p)]
       =n^p/Gamma(p) integral_0^infinity s^(p-1)phi(s)^n ds.    (3)

Choose s0>=max(1,(2C'_Q)^2). On [0,1], (3) is bounded by c_Q^(-p).
On [1,s0], use rho_Q^n, giving at most
n^p s0^p rho_Q^n/(p Gamma(p)), uniformly bounded in n. On [s0,infinity),
for n>=4p,

    integral_(s0)^infinity s^(p-1)(C'_Q/sqrt(s))^n ds
      <= s0^p 2^(-n)/(n/2-p).

After multiplication by n^p/Gamma(p), this is uniformly bounded too.
This proves (1), since S_(n,q)>=n^(-1)sum H_i under the common-row coupling.

Uniform exponential integrability follows from0<=Y_q<=Z^2; m(q)>=E H>0.
Centered exponential-moment bounds and Chernoff give the first part of(2),
uniformly in q. Choose eta< E H/2 so G also stays uniformly away from zero.
Cauchy-Schwarz, (1) at order2p and the first bound in(2) prove its second
bound. All integrations use nonnegative integrands, so Tonelli applies.

## C045: full next drift of the exact reciprocal

Consider the exact scalar critical chain K_next=q S_(n,q) and
v=1/(nq), V_next=1/(n K_next). There are epsilon>0,C,c,n0 such that for
0<q<=epsilon and n>=n0,

    E(V_next-v)
      =(2v+2)/n + [4v-4-5/(3v)]/n^2+r_n(v),
    |r_n(v)|<=C[v/n^(5/2)+(1+1/v+1/v^2)/n^3+v exp(-cn)].     (4)

The exact inverse moments in C044 justify this unbounded observable.
In particular the singular next correction is negative. On any fixed
0<q<=Q, the following coarser estimates hold uniformly for sufficiently
large n (depending on Q and the indicated moment orders):

    E[(V_next/v)^j]<=1+C_(Q,j)(q+1/n), j=1,2,
    E[(V_next-v)^2]<=C_Q(v^2/n+1/n^2),                        (5)
    |E(V_next-v)-(2v+2)/n|
                         <=C_Q[q/n+1/n^2+v/n^(3/2)].         (6)

Proof of(4). Global Taylor inequalities for tanh, using boundedness on
|x|<=1 and polynomial domination on |x|>=1, imply

    m(q)=1-2q+(17/3)q^2+O(q^3),
    Var(Y_q)=2-16q+O(q^2),
    kappa_3(Y_q)=8+O(q).

For example tanh(x)^2=x^2-(2/3)x^4+(17/45)x^6+O(x^8), with a global
remainder bound C|x|^8. Similarly E Y_q^2=3-20q+O(q^2). Every fixed
positive row moment is bounded; its first variation is O(q) since
|Y_q-Z^2|<=Cq Z^4.

Taylor expand 1/S about m(q) through order four on G. The fifth absolute
sample-average moment is O(n^(-5/2)); it follows, for instance, from the
sixth moment bound for centered iid sample sums and Holder. The exact
sample-mean third moment is kappa_3(Y_q)/n^2, and its fourth moment is
3 Var(Y_q)^2/n^2+O(n^-3). Deleted inverse tails are exponentially small
by C044. Therefore uniformly on0<q<=epsilon,

    E S^(-1)=m^(-1)+Var(Y_q)/(n m^3)
              +[-kappa_3(Y_q)/m^4+3 Var(Y_q)^2/m^5]/n^2
              +O(n^(-5/2))+O(exp(-cn))
      =1+2q-(5/3)q^2+(2-4q)/n+4/n^2
              +O(q^3+q^2/n+q/n^2+n^(-5/2)+exp(-cn)).         (7)

Multiply by v, subtract v, and use vq=1/n. This gives(4).

For(5), the same good-event Taylor expansion through order two applied
to S^(-j), with C044 for the deleted tails, gives
E S^(-j)=m(q)^(-j)+O_(Q,j)(1/n). The function
[m(q)^(-j)-1]/q stays bounded on0<q<=Q, so its first assertion follows.
The Lipschitz estimate for1/S on G, and C044 off G, give
E(S^(-1)-m(q)^(-1))^2<=C_Q/n. Since m(q)^(-1)-1=O_Q(q), the second
assertion follows by v^2 q^2=1/n^2.

For(6), the second-order centered Taylor expansion has remainder
O(n^(-3/2)), and Var(Y_q)/m(q)^3=2+O(q). This yields
E S^(-1)=1+2q+2/n+O(q^2+q/n+n^(-3/2)) for small q, which gives(6).
On epsilon<=q<=Q, v<=1/(n epsilon); the error is O_Q(1/n), absorbable
in C_Q q/n. This completes the global extension.

body:
[Proposition 45 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in S_X$ be a homogeneous regular sequence, and set
\[
A \defeq S_X/(f_1,\ldots,f_r).
\]
Let
\[
\widehat Z
 \defeq 
V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\cap U_X
\subset
\operatorname{Spec}(A)
\]
and $Z\defeq\widehat Z/G_X\subseteq X$.

Then \(Z\) is HT-split.
In particular, if \(Z\) is smooth, then there is an isomorphism
\[
F_{*}\Omega^\bullet_{Z/k}
\simeq
\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\dim Z}
\Omega^i_{Z/k}[-i]
\]
in \(\mcalD_{\qcoh}(Z)\).
Consequently, the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of \(Z\)
degenerates at \(E_1\), and \(Z\) satisfies the
Akizuki--Nakano-type vanishing theorem.

body:
[Proposition prop:exact-density-Nterms of arXiv:2606.04859, 'Stein's method for the Wishart distribution'] Let $N\geq 2$, and let $\alpha_j > d-1$ and $\Sigma_j\in \mathcal{S}_{++}^d$ for all $j\in [N]$. Let $\mathfrak{G}_1, \ldots, \mathfrak{G}_N$ be independent random matrices such that $\mathfrak{G}_j\sim\mathcal{W}_d(\alpha_j, \Sigma_j)$ for all $j\in [N]$. Then $\smash{\mathfrak{T} = \sum_{j = 1}^N \mathfrak{G}_j}$ has density
\[
f_{\mathfrak{T}}(X) = \frac{|\Sigma_N|^{\alpha_{\bullet}/2}}{\prod_{j = 1}^N |\Sigma_j|^{\alpha_j/2}} \, f_{\alpha_{\bullet}, \Sigma_N}(X)\Psi(X), \qquad X\in \mathcal{S}_{++}^d,
\]
where $\alpha_{\bullet} \vcentcolon= \sum_{j = 1}^N\alpha_j$ and
\[
\Psi(X) \vcentcolon= \mathsf{E}\left[\mathrm{etr}\left\{-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j = 1}^{N-1} X^{1/2}(\Sigma_j^{-1}-\Sigma_N^{-1})X^{1/2}\mathfrak{U}_j\right\}\right],
\]
with $(\mathfrak{U}_1, \ldots, \mathfrak{U}_{N-1})\sim \mathrm{MatrixDirichlet}_{d\times d}(\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_N)$ [GuptaNagar2000].

[Definition 17 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] (Event-field denoising) Let $\mu$ be a distribution on $\{0,1\}^V$ and consider a collection of events $\mathcal{A}$. Denote by $\pi$ the joint distribution on $\{0,1\}^{V\cup\mathcal{A}}$ and let $(Y_t')_{t\in[0,1]}$ be the vertex-field denoising process for the marginal $\pi_{\mathcal{A}}$ with $\pi_{\mathcal{A}}=\operatorname{Law}(Y_1')$.
    Then event-field denoising process for $\mu$ through $\mathcal{A}$, which we denote by $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ is defined via
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Sample $Y_1\sim\pi_V(\cdot\mid Y_1')$,
    \item For $t\in[0,1)$, we set $Y_t=Y_t'$. 
\end{enumerate} In other words, the process follows the vertex field denoising process applied to the event indicators, and finally at $t=1$ projects onto the vertices in $V$ via the conditional law $\pi_V(\cdot\mid Y_1')$.
title: Definition 17 of arXiv:2605.02002

body:
[Prop curie-weiss of arXiv:2411.14236, 'Size of chaos for Gibbs measures\\of mean field interacting diffusions'] Suppose that $\mathcal X = \mathds R$ and the confinement potential is given by
\[
V(x) = \frac{\theta}{4} x^4 + \frac{\sigma}{2} x^2
\]
for $\theta > 0$ and $\sigma \in \mathds R$.
Suppose that the interaction is given by
\[
W(x,y) = - J x y
\]
for $J \in (0, J_\textnormal{c})$, where
\[
J_\textnormal{c} \coloneqq
\frac{\int_{\mathds R} e^{-V(x)} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x}
{\int_{\mathds R} x^2e^{-V(x)} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x}.
\]
Then Theorem~(thm:sharp of the paper) applies with
$m_*$ being the centered measure
$\propto e^{-V(x)} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x$ and
\begin{align*}
\rho &= \biggl(1 - \frac{J}{J_\textnormal{c}}\biggr)^{\!2}\rho_0,\\
\gamma &= \frac{64(1+\delta_N)^2J^2}{\lambda_N},\\
M &= 4J^2 \biggl( \frac{\delta_N}{\lambda_NN} + \frac{d}{\rho_0}\biggr),
\end{align*}
where $\rho_0$, $\lambda_N$, $\delta_N$ are given by
\begin{align*}
\rho_0 &=
\begin{cases}
\sigma, & \sigma \geqslant 1, \\
\exp \bigl( - 7(1-\sigma)^2\!/36\theta \bigr),
& \sigma < 1,
\end{cases} \\
\lambda_N &= \biggl( 1 - \frac{J}{J_\textnormal{c}}\biggr)\frac{\rho_0}{2}
- \frac{3\bigl(1/\sqrt{\min(J_\textnormal{c}/J-1,1)}+3\bigr)J}{N}, \\
\delta_N &=
3\bigl(1/\sqrt{\min(J_\textnormal{c}/J-1,1)}+3\bigr)\frac{dJ}{\rho_0},
\end{align*}
whenever $N$ is large enough such that $\lambda_N > 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop curie-weiss of arXiv:2411.14236

body:
[Lem mean-properties of arXiv:2609.03856, 'Consensus time for asynchronous $\ell^p$ relaxation: graph dependence'] For $p\in(1,\infty]$, the map $m_p$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item It is continuous and lies between the smallest and largest coordinate.
\item It is positively affine equivariant: for every $\alpha>0$ and
$a\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
 m_p(\alpha y+a\mathbf{1})=\alpha m_p(y)+a.
\]
\item It is coordinatewise monotone.  Consequently,
\[
 |m_p(y)-m_p(z)|\le \lVert y-z\rVert_\infty
\]
whenever $y$ and $z$ have the same number of coordinates.
\end{enumerate}

body: [Definition Complements and Zero Triples of arXiv:2609.01926, 'On Sum Ranges for $3n$-convergence'] An element $a$ in a sequence $A$ has a \emph{complementary pair} if there exist distinct $b,c \in A$ such that $a + b + c = 0$. Such a triple is called a \emph{zero triple}. If a sequence $A$ can be partitioned into zero triples, we say $A$ has a \emph{zero triple arrangement} (ZTA).

body:
[Lemma lem:remove0s of arXiv:2509.16541, 'Two-stage Bootstrap Percolation'] Consider two dynamics with the same initial configurations of $1$s and $2$s on ${\mathbb Z}^2$. 
    The first dynamics is the standard one on the full ${\mathbb Z}^2$, and denote by $A_f\subset {\mathbb Z}^2$ the set of vertices that are eventually occupied by $2$s in these dynamics. 
    For the second dynamics, we remove from ${\mathbb Z}^2$ all the vertices that are initially $0$s, then run the standard dynamics on the induced subset of ${\mathbb Z}^2$ and obtain the set $A_r$ of vertices that are eventually in state $2$. 
    Then $A_r\subset A_f$.

body:
Let (T(t)) be a C_0-semigroup on a Banach space X satisfying the growth bound ||T(t)|| <= M exp(omega t). Then there is an EQUIVALENT norm on X, namely |||x||| = sup over t >= 0 of exp(-omega t) ||T(t) x||, in which the semigroup satisfies |||T(t) x||| <= exp(omega t) |||x||| - that is, the constant M is normalised away and the semigroup becomes a quasi-contraction. The new norm satisfies ||x|| <= |||x||| <= M ||x||, so it is equivalent and the generator, its domain and its spectrum are unchanged; only the operator NORMS and the numerical range move. This is the standard reduction that lets one prove results for contraction semigroups and transfer them to general ones.
The uniform growth bound with constants M and omega, which every C_0-semigroup has by the uniform boundedness principle.
The renorming changes the geometry of the space - the new norm need not be, for instance, a Hilbert norm even if the original was, so any argument relying on inner-product structure must be checked rather than assumed to survive.

[Lem 13 of arXiv:2511.20322, 'Dissertation'] Suppose $Y$ solves \eqref{eq:linearRDE}.
Then $\tilde Y_t = Y_{tT}$ solves
\begin{equation}

d\tilde Y_t = \tilde A_t Y_t + \tilde b_t\,dt + \tilde \si_t\,d\tilde X_t, \quad \tilde Y_0 = Y_0.
\end{equation}
where
\[\tilde A_t = T A_{tT}, \tilde b_t = Tb_{tT} + \si_{tT} X_T, \tilde \si_t = \si_{tT},\]
and the driver $\tilde X_t = X_{tT} - tX_T$ is $1$-periodic.
Conversely, if $\tilde Y$ solves \eqref{eq:linearRDE1period} for $1$-periodic $\tilde X$ and we are given $X_T\in \R^d$, then $Y_t := Y_{t/T}$ solves \eqref{eq:linearRDE}, where
\[A_t = \frac1T\tilde A_{t/T}, b_t = \frac1T \tilde b_{t/T}- \tilde \si_t X_T, \si_t = \tilde \si_{t/T},\]
with $X_t = \tilde X_{t/T} + \frac t T X_T$ having $T$-periodic increments. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 7 (Convergence rate for L\'evy area) of arXiv:2512.04646, '\textbf{Canonical Rough Path over Tempered Fractional Brownian Motion: Existence, Construc'] Let $\mathbb{B}^{(N)}_{H,\lambda}$ be the piecewise linear
approximation of $\mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda}$ on a uniform partition of
$[0,T]$ with $N$ sub-intervals. For $H > 1/4$,
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{E}\bigl[|\mathbb{B}^{(N)}_{H,\lambda}(0,T)
  - \mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda}(0,T)|^2\bigr]^{1/2}
\le C(H,\lambda,T)\cdot N^{-2H},
\end{equation}
where
$C(H,\lambda,T) = \widetilde{C}(H)\cdot\max\{1,\lambda^{-2H}\}\cdot
T^{2H}$ with $\widetilde{C}(H)$ depending only on $H$. The rate
$N^{-2H}$ is optimal: no first-order piecewise linear scheme can
achieve a better rate.
title: Convergence rate for L\'evy area

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.26490, 'Bayesian methods and Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms for curve reconstruction and poin'] For a fixed $n=1,\dots,N$, let $r_n$ be a random position generated according to the sampling scheme in \cref{eq:un,eq:sn,eq:pi,eq:L}. Then \cref{eq:rn} follows.
\begin{proof}
Given a geometry $G$, the position $r_n$ specifies and is specified by a global coordinate $v_n$ that equals the arc-length from $h^1$ along the curve $\mathcal{G}$ encoded by $G$. Consequently, it suffices to show that $v_n$ is uniformly distributed over $[0,L^G]$ where $L^G=\sum_{k=1}^K L_k^G$ is the total arc-length of $\mathcal{G}$.

Conditional on $s_n$ and $u_n$, such global coordinate $r_n$ is obtained deterministically by
\begin{align*}
v_n|s_n,u_n
&\sim\delta_{C^G_{s_n-1}+u_nL_{s_n}^G},
\end{align*}
where the cumulative segment lengths are defined by
\begin{align*}
C^G_0&=0,
\\
C^G_k&=\sum_{k'=1}^K L^G_{k'},
&
k&=1,\dots,K.
\end{align*}
According to the law of total probability, we obtain the marginal
\begin{align*}
p(v_n)
&=
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
p(v_n|s_n,u_n)p(s_n,u_n),
\end{align*}
and, because of independence in \cref{eq:sn,eq:un}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
p(v_n)
&=
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
p(v_n|s_n,u_n)p(s_n)p(u_n)
\\
&=
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
\delta_{C^G_{s_n-1}+u_nL_{s_n}^G}(v_n)\pi_{s_n}^G
\\
&=
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
\frac{1}{L_{s_n}^G}\delta_{u_n}\left(\frac{v_n-C^G_{s_n-1}}{L_{s_n}^G}\right)\frac{L_{s_n}^G}{L^G}
\\
&=\frac{1}{L^G}
\sum_{s_n=1}^K\int_0^1du_n\,
\delta_{u_n}\left(\frac{v_n-C^G_{s_n-1}}{L_{s_n}^G}\right)
\\
&=\frac{1}{L^G}
\end{align*}
indicating that, indeed, $v_n$ is uniformly distributed over $[0,L^G]$ which completes our proof. Here, the last equality holds because, from the $K$ different summands $\int_0^1du_n\,
\delta_{u_n}\left(\frac{v_n-C^G_{s_n-1}}{L_{s_n}^G}\right)$, only one integrates over the singularity.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.26490

body:
[Corollary cor:Airy of arXiv:2411.15830, 'Deformations of biorthogonal ensembles and universality'] For any compactly supported continuous function $h:\mathbb{R}\to [0,+\infty)$, the limit
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathcal G_n^{\sigma_n}[h]=\mathcal G_{\rm Airy}^{\sigma}[h],
\]

is valid, { where $\mathcal G_{\rm Airy}^\sigma$ is the probability generating functional of the $\sigma$-deformation of the Airy point process,

\[

\mathcal G_{\rm Airy}^{\sigma}[h]=\det(\mathsf{1}- \sqrt h\mathbf K_{\rm Airy}^\sigma\sqrt h),
\]
}
with

\[
\mathbf K_{\rm Airy}^\sigma=\sqrt{1-\sigma}\mathbf K_{\rm Airy}(\mathsf{1}-\sigma\mathbf K_{\rm Airy})^{-1}\sqrt{1-\sigma},
\]

and $\sigma$ given by (equation def:sigmaedge1 of the paper)--(equation def:sigmaedge2 of the paper).
In particular, the deformed orthogonal polynomial ensemble $\mathcal X_n^{\sigma_n}$ converges weakly as $n\to\infty$ to the deformed Airy point process $\mathcal X_{\rm Airy}^{\sigma}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $T\colon (V,\|\cdot\|)\to (W,\|\cdot\|)$ be a linear map between vector spaces with diagonalizable norms.
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item Define an increasing $\bR$-filtration, $\cF^-(T)$, on $\operatorname{gr}V$ whose restriction to $(\operatorname{gr}V)_\alpha$ is 
        \[
        \left(\cF^-(T)_{\leq\beta}\right)_\alpha\coloneqq\left\{v\in (\operatorname{gr}V)_\alpha\mid\exists\text{ lift }\tilde{v}\in V:\|T\tilde{v}\|\leq e^{\alpha+\beta}\right\}.
        \]
        (Note the inequality can be written, for $v\neq 0$, as $\log(\|T\tilde v\|/\|\tilde v\|)\leq \beta$.)
        
        \item Define a decreasing $\bR$-filtration, $\cF^+(T)$, on $\operatorname{gr}W$ whose restriction to $(\operatorname{gr}W)_\alpha$ is 
        \[
     \left(\cF^+(T)_{\geq\beta}\right)_\alpha\coloneqq\left\{w\in (\operatorname{gr}W)_\alpha\mid\exists v\in V:Tv \text{ lifts }w,\|v\|\leq e^{\alpha-\beta}\right\}.
        \]
        (Note the inequality can be written, for $w\neq 0$, as $\log(\|Tv\|/\|v\|)\geq \beta$.)
        
        \item The \textbf{singular values}\footnote{They should really be called \textit{logarithms of singular values}, in analogy with the Archimedean case.} of $T$ are the numbers $\sigma_1\geq\ldots\geq \sigma_r$, $r=\operatorname{rk}T$, where the filtration $\cF^-(T)$ (equivalently: $\cF^+(T)$) jumps, where the multiplicity of the jump $\sigma_i$ in the descending list is  $\dim_\mathbf k\cF^-(T)_{\leq\sigma_i}/\cF^-(T)_{<\sigma_i}$.
    \end{enumerate}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2609.03268, 'Poincare Polynomials of Heavy-Light Hassett Spaces'] Let $p_n(x):=p_{\LM{n+2}}(x)$, with $p_0(x)=1$.
            \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=10pt]
                \item (\cref{thm:LM-ppoly-deg2-recursion}) $p_{n-1}(x)=(1+x)p_{n-2}(x)+x\sum_{j=1}^{n-3} {n-2\choose j} p_j(x)p_{n-j-2}(x)$.
                \item (\cref{cor:egf-ppoly-LM-space}) The exponential generating function $P(x,t):=\sum_{n\ge0}p_n(x)\frac{t^n}{n!} = \frac{1-x}{e^{(x-1)t}-x}$ is a solution to the differential equation $P_t=xP^2+(1-x)P$.
                \item (\cref{cor:deg1rec-ppoly-LM-space}) $p_n(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n {n\choose i} (x-1)^{i-1}p_{n-i}(x)$.
            \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:1ae190435e7b657c945d3a052b349474d8561c45b1e0a73355ca4689c9eb58a9","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/1a/1ae190435e7b657c945d3a052b349474d8561c45b1e0a73355ca4689c9eb58a9.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:1897088fd6bce2b41875bad2e316b72ce701bc5859c50a5af342efc251043f67","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c19","bundle_id":"population.t309-random-anisotropic-fixed-noise-bad-basin-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and diffusion objectives","draft":"w721/bundle_012.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:gaussian-mixture-ddpm-random-anisotropic-fixed-noise-bad-basin","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C19 v1; proof (unaudited); Target 2 route 12 auxiliary composition lemma.

# A constant random-initialization bad-basin probability at fixed high noise

This composes the unaudited C17 entry and C18 unrestricted local trapping lemmas. It is a fixed-noise population result for a particular anisotropic three-component teacher. It neither refutes annealed learning nor settles the well-separated K=3 target. No novelty finding is asserted.

## Statement

Let d>=2, E^T E=I_2, A=diag(1,3), and use the teacher (1/3)sum_j N(a E A u_j,I_d), where u_j are unit equilateral vertices. Optimize the canonical equal-weight identity-covariance mixture score by physical Euclidean unit-step GD on the single-time population DDPM excess risk, with all entries of the d-by-3 initial mean matrix iid N(0,3a^2/(2d)). There is a fixed positive constant c_* such that taking a^2=c_* d^(-420) gives probability greater than 79/600 that the unrestricted trajectory converges to a strict non-global local minimum. Entry into its trapping neighborhood takes O(d^420 log d) steps. The convergence assertion is asymptotic; no finite-time identification rate is claimed here.

The statement depends on C06, C17 and C18 as analytic proof drafts, not independently checked theorems. In particular the original well-separated means need not resemble the small noisy means displayed here, and the statement is not a result about changing noise levels, empirical gradients, bit complexity or every random initialization.

## 1. Fix angular margins before the noise level

Set beta=acos(-61/128) and p=1-beta/pi. Since -61/128>-1/2 and acos is strictly decreasing on (-1,1), beta<2pi/3, hence p>1/3. Also beta>pi/2, so p<1/2. Set

    g=p-1/3>0, delta=pi*g/18.

C18's three bad sectors in each determinant branch have endpoints

    l_j=beta/3+2pi*j/3,
    r_j=(2pi-beta)/3+2pi*j/3, j=0,1,2.

Each width is 2pi*p/3. The chosen delta is less than one fourth of this width, so it is allowed in C18. Erode each sector by 3delta at each endpoint. Their total uniform angular measure, divided by 2pi, is

    3[(2pi*p/3)-6delta]/(2pi)
       =p-9delta/pi=(p+1/3)/2>1/3.              (1)

The intervals are disjoint modulo 2pi. Thus this measure calculation neither double-counts labels nor treats the three sectors as independent events.

## 2. Match all entry hypotheses simultaneously

Choose K in C18 large enough for C17's bound ||b_N||<=C_0 a^4. With this K and the fixed delta above, C18 supplies a fixed normal radius rho_T and smallness threshold a_T. The constants are independent of d.

Near the compact orbit {E A O:O in O(2)}, the polar chart is uniformly Lipschitz in Frobenius norm, independent of d: its planar part is a two-by-two positive-definite polar map, and its perpendicular part is a projection followed by a two-by-two rotation. Therefore factor distance at most rho implies

    ||c-c_*||+||Y||<=C_chart rho.               (2)

C17 also gives actual-to-surrogate polar angle distance at most C_phase rho at time N, with the same determinant branch. Choose a fixed entry tolerance 0<rho<=1/100 so that C_chart rho<rho_T/4 and C_phase rho<delta. Shrink rho further if necessary to stay within the uniform chart. Since cbar_a(theta)-c_*=O(a^2) uniformly in theta, sufficiently small a makes

    ||(c_N-cbar_a(theta_N),Y_N)||<rho_T.         (3)

The O(a^2) section displacement is explicitly included here; covariance-orbit distance alone is not the normal hypothesis in C18.

For this fixed rho, choose the absolute constant c in C17's prescription a^2=c rho exp(-84(S+1)), S=10log(8000 sqrt(d)/rho), small enough to enforce a<a_T, (3) and all its own assumptions for every d>=2. This prescription is exactly a^2=c_* d^(-420) with a fixed positive c_*. Consequently the constants and tolerances are chosen before d, and the polynomial exponent does not hide dimension dependence.

## 3. Conditional uniform phase, not independence

Let G be C17's joint good event: its right-invariant shape event together with ||b_0||<=10. It satisfies P(G)>=79/200. Conditional on G and either determinant branch, the C16 surrogate phase at the deterministic terminal time N gamma is uniform. The terminal time depends on d and fixed constants only, not on the random trajectory. Both determinant branches have positive conditional mass by the reflection symmetry of the Gaussian initialization and G.

Let A_good be the event that this surrogate phase lies in one of the three eroded sectors in Section 1. Formula (1) gives

    P(A_good | G, branch)=(p+1/3)/2>1/3.

Summing over the two branches gives exactly the same conditional probability given G. There is no factor one half: in the negative branch C18 uses a fixed reflection J that permutes the equilateral vertices, so R_theta J U=R_theta U Pi, and the same angular sectors apply by label symmetry. Nor is A_good asserted independent of G; its conditional probability is supplied by right-rotation invariance.

On G intersect A_good, the actual phase differs from the surrogate by less than delta. Its distance from each bad-sector endpoint is therefore greater than 2delta. Equations (3) and the centroid bound meet the remaining C18 hypotheses. C18 then gives convergence to that sector's strict bad minimum. Thus

    P(converges to a strict non-global minimum)
       >=P(G) P(A_good|G)
       >=(79/200)*(p+1/3)/2
       >79/600>1/8.                            (4)

This multiplication is the conditional-probability identity with an established conditional measure, not a product of unproved independent bounds. Component-label sectors and determinant branches have both been accounted for.

## Scope, checks and the unpaid target

Fix a sufficiently small $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$.
Let $j$ be a sufficiently large integer. Fix an integer $\tau \ge 0$ and a tuple $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$.
Let $E^+$ be a constant-escape process on $[j]$ with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time $\tau$, end-of-step arrival rate $\nu_j^\mathrm{lo}$, and $\overline{\mathrm{arr}}_{[j]}^{E^+}(\tau) = \overline{a}$. 
Let $d \ge 0$ be real, and suppose $\overline{a}$ satisfies (Con(item:Con1 of the paper)) for $d$. 
Fix $t$ in the range $\tau \leq t \leq \tau + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$. Then, with probability at least $1-\exp(-450j/\lambda^2)$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E^+}(t)$ satisfies (Con(item:Con1 of the paper)) for $d+j^{21}$.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:2fb14c31740fa511acca049d47e110dfe0c184ccddfd618b8a81e7a016204d80","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/2f/2fb14c31740fa511acca049d47e110dfe0c184ccddfd618b8a81e7a016204d80.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7adb1b8cf4ebcfee20f4aa5d92ae35bd71b88962a5a3272563d5c82f8871c78b","bundle_entry_key":"random-comb-exit-scale-collision-count-lower-bound","bundle_id":"population.w664-i0012-conditional-extensions-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w664/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.random.walks:random-comb-exit-scale-collision-count-lower-bound","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0012-Q2 v1: almost-sure lower collision counts along geometric exit scales

NOVELTY: UNCHECKED (direct adapted-tail consequence of the conditional one-scale bound; no priority claim).
Status: proof (unaudited).

## Statement and scope

Assume the critical analytic inputs and nonempty window of notes/boundary_comb.tex. Let b>=2 be the integer scale multiplier and c>0 its deterministic one-scale constant. For two independent walks started at the backbone origin, let sigma_m be the first time either exits R_{b^m}((b^m)^(3/2)). Let C_T count backbone collision times from time 1 through T. Then in almost every environment,

    liminf_{m->infinity} C_{sigma_m}/log m >= c/log b, almost surely.

In particular the count is at least a positive multiple of log m along exit scales. This is a log log N lower bound when N=b^m. No almost-sure order log T, deterministic-time rate, or limiting coefficient is claimed. The inputs remain conditional, with the upstream caveats in UPSTREAM_CHECK.md.

## Adapted indicators

Fix an environment where Lemma B of the note holds. Beyond a finite deterministic index in this fixed environment, define I_m as the indicator of a backbone collision in [sigma_m,sigma_{m+1}). Let F_m be the pair filtration at sigma_m. Then I_m is F_{m+1}-measurable and

    E[I_m | F_m] >= a_m := c/(1+m log b).

The interval count includes the endpoint sigma_m, whereas C_T excludes time zero. Discard finitely many initial blocks so sigma_m>=1, and all remaining successful blocks yield distinct collision times counted by C_{sigma_{M+1}}.

## Lower-tail product

Fix a starting index M0 beyond that threshold. For lambda>0,

    E[exp(-lambda I_m) | F_m]
        =1-(1-exp(-lambda)) E[I_m | F_m]
        <=1-(1-exp(-lambda))a_m.

Iterated conditioning, using measurability of earlier indicators at F_m, gives for S_M=sum_{m=M0}^{M-1} I_m,

    E exp(-lambda S_M)
        <= product_{m=M0}^{M-1}[1-(1-exp(-lambda))a_m]
        <= exp(-(1-exp(-lambda)) H_M),

where H_M=sum_{m=M0}^{M-1}a_m. Markov's inequality therefore gives, for 0<theta<1,

    P(S_M <= theta H_M)
        <= exp(-[1-exp(-lambda)-lambda theta]H_M).

Choose lambda small enough that d:=1-exp(-lambda)-lambda theta>0; this is possible because (1-exp(-lambda))/lambda tends to one as lambda decreases to zero.

The harmonic sum satisfies H_M=(c/log b)log M+O(1), by comparison with the integral of c/(1+x log b). Hence the lower-tail probability is at most D M^(-d c/log b) for a fixed finite D in this fixed environment.

## Sparse subsequence and interpolation

Take M_j=ceil(exp(j)). The probabilities P(S_{M_j}<=theta H_{M_j}) are summable in j. The first Borel-Cantelli lemma, which needs no independence, implies that almost surely, eventually

    S_{M_j} > theta H_{M_j}.

For M_j<=M<M_{j+1}, monotonicity gives S_M>=S_{M_j}. Since log M<=log M_{j+1}=j+1+o(1) and H_{M_j}=(c/log b)(j+o(j)), it follows that

    liminf_{M->infinity} S_M/log M >= theta c/log b

almost surely. Intersect the probability-one events for a countable sequence of theta tending to one to obtain liminf S_M/log M>=c/log b.

Finally C_{sigma_M}>=S_M because each counted successful block is disjoint and ends by sigma_M. This proves the assertion.

## Limits

The finite-bounded-interval upper time for each successful collision does not itself give an upper bound on all exit times sigma_m. Thus replacing sigma_m by a deterministic power of b^m would require a separate quenched exit-time upper bound. Likewise a logarithmic expectation from Q1 does not imply concentration or an almost-sure logarithmic growth rate.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:2475b91ab27b6b8f749e21ccda38cde2a2d4e3e843fd0c376ab39677344d6132","revision_digest":"sha256:d3f6d5c434cc97d3f8a8304b8d7f4c51729782f8b317949de1e4112ab9638128","source_id":"own-work:w664:I0012-Q2:v1","source_revision":"v1; w667 and w668 PASS; upstream qualifications persist","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Corollary cor:dCoulomb of arXiv:2411.15830, 'Deformations of biorthogonal ensembles and universality'] Consider the discrete Coulomb gas ensemble (equation eq:discreteCoulomb of the paper) under Assumption~(assumption:dCoulomb of the paper). Scale it around a bulk point $x^*$ as in (equation eq:corrkerneldiscrete of the paper) and let $\sigma$ be as in (equation eq:sigmadsine of the paper).

For any compactly supported continuous function $h:\mathbb{R}\to [0,+\infty)$, the limit
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathcal G_n^{\sigma_n}[h]=\mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^{\sigma}[h],
\]

is valid, where $\mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}$ and $\mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^\sigma$ are the probability generating functionals of the discrete sine point process on $\Omega=\frac{\kappa_V(x^*)}{\rho(x^*)}\mathbb{Z}$ and its $\sigma$-deformation,

\[
\mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}[h]\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.5ex \lineskiplimit0pt
                     \hbox{\scriptsize.}\hbox{\scriptsize.}}}
                     = \det(\mathsf{1}- \sqrt h\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}\sqrt h),\qquad \mathcal G_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^{\sigma}[h]\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.5ex \lineskiplimit0pt
                     \hbox{\scriptsize.}\hbox{\scriptsize.}}}
                     = \det(\mathsf{1}- \sqrt h\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^\sigma\sqrt h),
\]
with

\[
\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^\sigma\mathrel{\vcenter{\baselineskip0.5ex \lineskiplimit0pt
                     \hbox{\scriptsize.}\hbox{\scriptsize.}}}
                     = \sqrt{1-\sigma}\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}(\mathsf{1}-\sigma\mathbf K_{{\mathrm{dsin}}})^{-1}\sqrt{1-\sigma}.
\]

In particular, the deformed discrete Coulomb gas $\mathcal X_n^{\sigma_n}$ converges weakly as $n\to\infty$ to the deformed discrete sine point process $\mathcal X_{{\mathrm{dsin}}}^{\sigma}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2509.02432, 'A threshold for online balancing of sparse i.i.d. vectors'] Let $T = n$, and let $X_1,\dots,X_T$ be independent and uniformly random $d$--sparse binary vectors. Then, for any $2 \le d \le n/2$, any online algorithm for assigning $\sigma \in \{-1,+1\}^T$ satisfies: w.h.p.,
    \[
        \big\|\sum_{i \in [T]} X_i\sigma_i\big\|_\infty \ge \max\Big(\frac{1}{8}\log\log n,\, \Omega\big(\sqrt{d}\big) \,\Big).
    \]
    On the other hand, for $d \le (\log\log n)^2 / \log\log\log n$, there is an explicit near-linear time online algorithm for assigning $\sigma$, satisfying: w.h.p.,
    \[
    \max_{t \in [T]}\,\big\|\sum_{i \in [t]} X_i\sigma_i\big\|_\infty \le 35\,\log\log n.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] Let \(Y\) be a subordinator with L\'evy measure \(\nu\) and Laplace exponent \(\psi\).
Let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(c\ge0\), and let \(K\) be a slowly varying function at \(\infty\).
Define
\[
h(x):=\frac{x^\alpha}{\Gamma(1-\alpha)K(x)}
\quad (x>0),
\]
and let \(g\) be the right-continuous inverse of \(h\), that is,
\[
g(\lambda):=\inf\{y\ge0 \mid h(y)>\lambda\}.
\]
Let \(Z^{(\alpha)}\) be the \(\alpha\)-stable subordinator characterized by
\[
E[e^{-qZ^{(\alpha)}_t}]=e^{-tq^\alpha}
\quad (q,t\ge0).
\]
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\left(\frac{Y_{\lambda t}}{g(\lambda)}\right)_{t\ge0}
  \xrightarrow[\lambda\to\infty]{d}
  \bigl(c^{1/\alpha}Z^{(\alpha)}_t\bigr)_{t\ge0}\) on \(D([0,\infty),\bR)\).
  \item
  \(\nu(x,\infty)\sim c x^{-\alpha}K(x) \quad (x\to\infty)\).
  \item
  \(\psi(q)\sim c \Gamma(1-\alpha) q^\alpha K(1/q) \quad (q \to 0)\).
\end{enumerate}

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Non-normal orbit quotients that are not normal quotients (October 2026), addresses Question 4.5 of Grimmett and Li, Self-avoiding walks and connective constants (arXiv:1704.05884): can a non-normal subgroup A of a transitive automorphism group of an infinite transitive graph G give a transitive orbit quotient G_A not isomorphic to G_N for any normal subgroup N of any transitive automorphism group, and does a free action of A matter? For every m >= 3 there is an infinite, connected, locally finite Cayley graph X whose automorphism group acts regularly, with a non-normal subgroup B acting freely, such that X_B is the complete graph K_m while no normal quotient of X is K_m. X is a graphical regular representation (Leemann and de la Salle) of F * F, with F = S_3 for m = 3 and F = A_m for m >= 4; B is the preimage of a point stabiliser under the projection onto the first factor. The quotient is finite; the infinite-quotient version and Question 4.6 are not addressed. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/nonnormal-orbit-quotients (commit b11def36f965). Not refereed.
title: Non-normal orbit quotients that are not normal quotients: K_m as a free orbit quotient of a Cayley graph with no K_m normal quotient, on Grimmett-Li Question 4.5 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/nonnormal-orbit-quotients)

[Lemma 6 (Moderate second-order expansion) of arXiv:2608.01674, '\textbf{Limit Theorems for Tempered Linear Processes with Innovations in the Domain of Att'] Assume $N\lambda_N\to\lambda\in[0,\infty)$.  For every $x>0$,
\[
 \frac{A_N(x)-L(N)}{\ell(N)}
 \overset{N\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} G_\lambda(x),
\]
where
\[
 G_\lambda(x)
 =\log x+\int_0^x\frac{\e^{-\lambda u}-1}{u}\dd u.
\]
The convergence is locally uniform for $x$ in compact subsets of
$(0,\infty)$.

body: A function holomorphic on an annulus 0 <= r < |z - c| < R has a Laurent series f(z) = sum over all integers n of a_n (z - c)^n, converging there; the coefficient a_{-1} is the residue of f at c. At an isolated singularity c the principal part (negative-index terms) classifies it: none => removable; finitely many, lowest index -m => pole of order m; infinitely many => essential singularity (near which f comes arbitrarily close to every value, Casorati-Weierstrass / Picard). The residue a_{-1} is what contour integrals of f pick up.
title: Laurent Series and Classification of Singularities

    $$\mathcal{L}_1(t,x_0,x,x_0',x')\leq C_S [G^{[2]}_t(d(x_0,x))+1][G^{[2]}_t(d(x_0',x'))+1]\left(\int_0^t k^1_S(s)ds\right),$$
    where $C_S$ depends on $\alpha$ and $M$.
title: Lemma 15 of arXiv:2603.26936

[Corollary cor:gumbel of arXiv:2608.04162, 'Correlation Matrices in High Dimensions:\\ The Elliptope as a Sample-Correlation Ensemble'] Let $C$ be uniformly distributed on $\mathcal{E}_n$, and let $M_n=\max_{1\leq i<j\leq n}|C_{ij}|$. Then, as $n\rightarrow\infty$,
$$
(n+1)M_n^2-\mu_n\overset{d}{\rightarrow}\mathcal{G},\qquad \mathcal{G}(t)=\exp\{-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{8\pi}}e^{-t/2}\},
$$
which is a Gumbel distribution. In particular, $\sqrt{(n+1)/\log n}M_n\overset{p}{\rightarrow}2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Gumbel limit

body:
In 1998, Keith Wolcott posed the question whether every cohomological Bousfield class in the category of harmonic spectra $\mathcal{H} = L_{\bigoplus K(p, n)} \operatorname{Sp}$ is homological (i.e. whether $\langle E \rangle^* = \langle X \rangle$ for some spectrum $X$). Barthel et al. (2026) answered this question negatively by establishing that cohomological classification is strictly stronger than homological classification and requires homological stratification.
\mathcal{H} is the harmonic stable homotopy category
title: Wolcott's Question on Harmonic Spectra

[Thm DL-infty of arXiv:2411.16376, 'Higher order approximations in arcsine laws for subordinators'] Let $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Let $X=(X_t)_{t\geq0}$ be a killed subordinator which is not identically zero. Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label={\upshape (\arabic*)}]

\item The killing rate $a$ is zero, and the tail $\Pi((x,+\infty))$ of the L\'evy measure  is regularly varying at $+\infty$ with index $-\alpha$.

\item The Laplace exponent $\Phi:(0,+\infty)\to(0,+\infty)$ (restricted over $(0,+\infty)$) is regularly varying at $0+$ with index $\alpha$. 

\item	
$\displaystyle \lim_{s\to+\infty}\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}\bigg(\frac{X_{T(s)-}}{s} \leq t\bigg)=\frac{\sin(\pi\alpha)}{\pi}\int_0^t x^{-1+\alpha}(1-x)^{-\alpha}\,dx$ for any $0\leq t\leq 1$.

\item 
$\displaystyle \lim_{s\to+\infty} s^{-1}\ensuremath{\mathbb{E}}[X_{T(s)-}]=\alpha$.

\item The law of $tX_{1/\Phi(t)}$ converges weakly to a stable law with index $\alpha$, as $t\to0+$. 

\item The distribution function $U([0,x])$ of the potential measure  is regularly varying at $+\infty$ with index $\alpha$.  
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: long-range Dynkin--Lamperti theorem

[Prop 42 of arXiv:2512.02286, 'Pfaffian Transition Probability and Correlation Kernel of TASEP in Half-space'] Let $m$ be a fixed integer and let $M$ be a fixed $2m\times2m$-dimensional skew-symmetric matrix such that the minors 
    \[[M]_{k,\ell}, \quad \text{for } 2j-1\leq k,\ell\leq2m\]
    are invertible for all $1\leq j\leq m$. Then $M$ has a \emph{skew-Borel factorization} of the form
    \begin{equation}
        M = R_{2m} J_{2m} R_{2m}^T,
    \end{equation}
    where $R_{2m}$ is an upper-triangular $2m\times2m$-dimensional matrix which is uniquely determined up to setting $\left[R_{2m}\right]_{2j-1,2j}=0$ and $\left[R_{2m}\right]_{2j,2j}=1$ for each $1\leq j\leq m$. Also where
    \[J_{2m} = \diag\left\{\left[\begin{array}{cc}
			0 & 1\\
			-1 & 0
		\end{array}\right],\dots,\left[\begin{array}{cc}
			0 & 1\\
			-1 & 0
		\end{array}\right]\right\}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 42 of arXiv:2512.02286

[Prop vela of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be compact oriented 		
	$4$-manifolds with  $b_1=0$ and $b_{+}\equiv 3\bmod 4$,
	and suppose that each of them is equipped with an almost-complex structure
	for which the corresponding   spin$^c$ structure 
	satisfies  $n_\mathfrak{c}\neq 0$. 
	Then, with respect to the canonical isomorphism 
			$$
			H^{2}(X\# Y\# Z, {\mathbb Z})  =   H^{2}(X, {\mathbb Z})\oplus H^{2}(Y, {\mathbb Z}) 
			\oplus H^{2}(Z, {\mathbb Z}) , 
             $$
	the cohomology classes 
	$$
	\pm c_{1}(X)   \pm c_{1}(Y)   \pm c_{1}(Z) 	  \in 
	H^{2}(X, {\mathbb Z})\oplus H^{2}(Y, {\mathbb Z}) 
			\oplus H^{2}(Z, {\mathbb Z}) 
	$$
	are monopole classes  on the connected sum 
	on $X\# Y\# Z$.
	Here the $\pm$ signs are arbitrary, and  are completely independent
	of one another. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:weakconvergence of arXiv:2411.15830, 'Deformations of biorthogonal ensembles and universality'] Let $(\nu_n)$ be a sequence of finite Borel measures over a fixed Euclidean space $E$, converging weakly to a finite Borel measure $\nu$ on $E$ as $n\to\infty$. 

\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item If $(f_n)$ is a sequence of uniformly bounded Borel measurable functions and $f$ is a bounded continuous function, for which
    
    $$
  \lim_{n\to\infty}  \|\mathsf{1}_B(f_n-f)\|_{L^\infty(\nu_n)}= 0,
    $$
    
    for any compact $B\subset \mathbb K $, then

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\int f_n \, \mathrm{d}\nu_n=\int f\, \mathrm{d}\nu.
$$

\item If $G$ is an open set for which $\nu(\partial G)=0$, then $\restr{\nu_n}{G}\stackrel{*}{\to}\restr{\nu}{G}$ as $n\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] Let $G$ be non-deterministic and $B>t_{0}(G)$. For any edge $e$ of the lattice, we define the \emph{detour height} as the distance to an edge with small passage time:
\[
k_B(e):=\min\left (k\ge 1 | \,  \min( \tau(e+(0,k)),\tau(e-(0,k)))< B\right).
\]
The \emph{detour} of $e$ is the path that starts at one edge of $e$, goes $k_B(e)$ edges upwards or downwards, passes the horizontal edge with weight less than $B$ and goes $k_B(e)$ edges down back to the other endpoint of $e$. The \emph{detour time} $dt_B(e)$ is the passage time of the detour.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'

[Lemma lem:resolvent-frechet of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Let $W$ be a real symmetric matrix and $M$ be a Hermitian matrix of the same dimensions that are functions of parameters that lie in an open subset of some vector space.
    Let $T$ be a constant matrix of the same dimensions.
    Let $D := W^{-1}$ and $X := M + D$ and $R := X^{-1}$.
    Suppose that there is a $\gamma > 0$ so that for all parameters of $W$ and $M$, $\min \Spec(|X|) \geqslant \gamma$ and $\ensuremath{\left\lVert M \right\rVert_\mathsf{op}} \leqslant C_1$.
    Then, letting $C_2 := (\gamma + C_1)\gamma^{-1}$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*), ref=\thetheorem(\alph*)]
        \item \[\frenorm{dR} \leqslant \gamma^{-2}\frenorm{dM} + C_2^2\frenorm{dW}.\]
        
        \item \[\frenorm{d(R^k)} \leqslant k\gamma^{-(k+1)}\frenorm{dM} + kC_2^2\gamma^{-(k-1)}\frenorm{dW}.\]
        
        \item \[\frenorm{d(DR)} \leqslant C_2\gamma^{-1}\frenorm{dM} + C_1C_2^2\frenorm{dW}.\]
        
        \item For $k \geqslant 1$,
        \[\frenorm{d(DR^k)} \leqslant kC_2\gamma^{-k}\frenorm{dM} + (kC_2-1)C_2^2\gamma^{-(k-2)}\frenorm{dW}.\]
        
        \item For $k \geqslant 2$, \[\frenorm{d(DR^kD)} \leqslant kC_2^2\gamma^{-(k-1)}\frenorm{dM} + (kC_2-2)C_2^3\gamma^{-(k-3)}\frenorm{dW}.\]
        
        \item For $k \geqslant 2$ and $1 \leqslant j \leqslant k-1$,
        \begin{align*}
            \frenorm{d(R^jDTDR^{k-j})} \leqslant  kC_2^2\gamma^{-(k-1)}\frenorm{dM}\ensuremath{\left\lVert T \right\rVert_\mathsf{op}} + (kC_2-2)C_2^3\gamma^{-(k-3)}\frenorm{dW}\ensuremath{\left\lVert T \right\rVert_\mathsf{op}}.
        \end{align*}
        
        \item For $k \geqslant 2$ and $1 \leqslant j \leqslant k-1$, and letting $T$ be variable for this bound only,
        \begin{align*}
            \frenorm{d(R^jDTDR^{k-j})} \leqslant{} &  kC_2^2\gamma^{-(k-1)}\frenorm[\to\infty]{dM}\schnorm{T} 
            \\&+ (kC_2-2)C_2^3\gamma^{-(k-3)}\frenorm[\to\infty]{dW}\schnorm{T} + C_2^2\gamma^{-(k-2)}\frenorm{dT}.
        \end{align*}
        
        \item When $\Im[X]$ is invertible, \[\frenorm{d((\Im [X])^{-1}\Im[R])} \leqslant 2\gamma^{-3}\frenorm{dM} + 2C_2^2\gamma^{-1}\frenorm{dW}.\]
        
        \item When $\Im[X] = bI \ne 0$,
        \[\frenorm{d(b^{-1}\Im[RDTDR])} \leqslant 6C_2^2\gamma^{-2}\frenorm{dM}\ensuremath{\left\lVert T \right\rVert_\mathsf{op}} + 2(3C_2-2)C_2^3\frenorm{dW}\ensuremath{\left\lVert T \right\rVert_\mathsf{op}}.\]
        
    \end{enumerate}
title: Bounds on derivatives of resolvent products

[Conjecture Conj: alpha_equals_d of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $d \ge 1$. Assume that $Q$ is a symmetric, translation-invariant, 
    heavy-tailed transition matrix on $\mathbb Z^d$ with exponent $\alpha = d$. 
    Consider the frog model on $\mathbb Z^d$ equipped with $Q$.
    For every particle density $\lambda > 0$ and particle lifespan 
    $\ell \in \mathbb N$, there exists $\theta = \theta(Q,\lambda,\ell) \in (0,1)$
    such that the following statement holds: for every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, 
    there exists $c = c(d,Q,\lambda,\ell,\varepsilon)>0$ such that
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb P\left( \mathrm{AT}(o,x) \ge c |x|^\theta \right) 
        \ge 1-\varepsilon,
        \qquad \text{for all } x \in \mathbb Z^d .
    \end{align*}
    Moreover, if $\ell > \ell_c(\lambda,Q)$, then the same exponent $\theta$ 
    also satisfies the following statement: for every 
    $\varepsilon,\rho \in (0,1)$, there exists 
    $C = C(d,Q,\lambda,\ell,\varepsilon,\rho)>0$ such that, for all sufficiently 
    large $L$,
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb P^+\left(
            \left|\mathcal{A}\left(C L^\theta\right) \cap B(L)\right|
            \ge \rho |B(L)|
        \right) 
        \ge 1-\varepsilon .
    \end{align*} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture Conj: alpha_equals_d of arXiv:2608.00399

For probability measures P and Q on one space, TV(P, Q) = sup_A |P(A) - Q(A)| and D = D(P || Q) is the Kullback-Leibler divergence in nats (+infinity unless P << Q). Then TV(P, Q) <= sqrt(1 - exp(-D)), and consequently 1 - TV(P, Q) >= 1 - sqrt(1 - exp(-D)) >= (1/2) exp(-D). Unlike Pinsker's bound sqrt(D/2), this never exceeds 1. In base-b units, exp(-D) = b^(-D_b). (J. Bretagnolle and C. Huber, 1979.)
P and Q are probability measures on one measurable space

	=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\operatorname{Tr}f\bigl(a(\theta)\bigr)\,d\theta .
	\]

[Corollary 12 of arXiv:2508.04938, 'Perfect t-embeddings of doubly periodic Aztec diamonds'] 1) The t-surface~$(\cT_N, \cO_N)$ of the Aztec diamond of size~$\ell N$ with $(2\times\ell)$-periodic weights (as shown on Figure~\ref{fig:aztec_2_l}) converges to a space-like surface in~$\mathbb R^{2,2}$ with zero mean curvature and with the boundary given by a quadrilateral in~$\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{R}$ with vertices at 
\[
(0,0), \quad
\left((a+\i)\sqrt{a^2+1},-(a^2+1)\right), \quad
\left(2a\sqrt{a^2+1} ,\,0\right), \quad

\left((a-\i)\sqrt{a^2+1},-(a^2+1)\right),
\]
and~$\ell-1$ cusps with apices~$P_1, \dots, P_{\ell-1}$;\\
2) In the scaling limit, each of the $4$ frozen regions collapses to one of the boundary points, and each of the~$(\ell-1)$ gas regions collapses to one of the inner points $P_i$ under the t-surface. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]

		\item $(\mathcal{L}(X,Y), \tau_c)^* = (\mathcal{L}(X,Y), \|\cdot\|)^*$.

Then, the implications (a) $\Rightarrow$ (b) $\Rightarrow$ (c) and (a) $\Rightarrow$ (d) $\Rightarrow$ (c) hold. body:
[Proposition 9 (Tiny Central Perturbations of Random Transpositions) of arXiv:2605.19084, 'Limit Profiles for Separation Distance'] Let $P_n$ be the random transpositions shuffle on $S_n$, let $C_n$ be any symmetric central random walk on $S_n$, and set $Q_n:=(1-\epsilon_n)P_n+\epsilon_n C_n$ with $\epsilon_n=O((n!)^{-1})$. Put $t_n(c):=\frac n2(\ln n+c)$. Then, for every fixed $c\in\mathbb R$,
$$\left|s_*^{Q_n}\left(t_n(c)\right)-s_*^{P_n}\left(t_n(c)\right)\right|\to0.$$

[Lemm 12 (Subsequence trick) of arXiv:2608.19104, 'Record times for coverage thresholds and maximal spacings'] Suppose $(U_{n,k},(n,k) \in \N \times \N)$ is an array of random
variables on a common probability space such that $U_{n,k} $ is
nonincreasing in $n$ and nondecreasing in $k$, that is,
$U_{n+1,k} \leq U_{n,k} \leq U_{n,k+1} $ almost surely,
for all $(n,k) \in \N \times \N$. 

       
	Let $c > 0$,  $\eps >0$. Suppose
$
\Pr[n U_{n, \lfloor  \eps \log n \rfloor } > \log n] \leq
c n^{-\eps},
$
        for all but finitely many $n$.
	Let $k \in \mathbb N$.
Then with probability 1, $ \limsup_{n \to \infty} n U_{n,k} /\log n \leq 1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.03112, '2609.03112'] Let $M$ be a discrete set and let $\lambda_m>0$ for $m\in M$.  For
$\psi_1,\psi_2\in C_c^\infty(\R_{>0})$ define
\[
 S_{j,X}(u)=X^{-1/2}\sum_{m\in M}
 \psi_j\!\left(\frac{\lambda_m}{X}\right)
 \e\!\left(\frac u2\lambda_m\right).
\]
For $h\in C_c(\R)$ set
\[
 \widehat h(s)=\int_\R h(u)\e(us/2)\,du.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \int_\R S_{1,X}(u)\overline{S_{2,X}(u)}h(u)\,du
 =\frac1X\sum_{m,n\in M}
 \psi_1\!\left(\frac{\lambda_m}{X}\right)
 \psi_2\!\left(\frac{\lambda_n}{X}\right)
 \widehat h(\lambda_m-\lambda_n).
\end{equation}
If $\lambda_m$ is a positive quadratic polynomial on a lattice coset, the
left side of \eqref{eq:theta-pair-identity}, with $v=X^{-1}$, is a finite
linear combination of integrals of products of the form
$\Theta_f\overline{\Theta_{f'}}(g_\alpha n(u)a(v))$.

[Lemma 27 (Multi-cluster history bound) of arXiv:2608.26259, 'Cutoff with an $O(1)$ window for Potts Glauber Dynamics\\on lattice at High Temperature'] Let \(a\in\{1,2\}\). 
Let \(D_1,\ldots,D_r\subseteq\Lambda\) be pairwise disjoint finite nonempty sets,
each of which is disjoint from every top set of a Green, Yellow, or Strong-Red
cluster revealed by \(\mathcal K\).
Let
\(Y_1,\ldots,Y_r\subseteq\Lambda\) be finite. Then under the condition of Lemma~\ref{lem:single_bound},
\[
\mathbb P\left(
        \bigcap_{i=1}^r
        \{D_i\in{\rm Red}^{(a)},\,
          \mathcal H_{D_i}^{(a)}\rightsquigarrow Y_i\}
        \,\middle|\,\mathcal K
\right)
\le
C_{\rm h}^r e^{-r(1-m)T}
\prod_{i=1}^r e^{-\lambda_{\rm P} W(D_i,Y_i)} .
\]

body:
[Corollary 2.9 of arXiv:2110.05374, 'When Janson meets McDiarmid: Bounded difference inequalities under graph-dependence'] Let f : Ω → R be c-Lipschitz and let the Ω-valued random vector X = (X_1, ..., X_n) be m-dependent for some m ≥ 1. Split [n] into consecutive blocks B_j := {k : (j−1)m + 1 ≤ k ≤ jm} for j ∈ [⌊n/m⌋] and, when m does not divide n, a last block B_{⌈n/m⌉} := [n] \ ∪_{j≤⌊n/m⌋} B_j. Then for every t > 0, P(f(X) − E[f(X)] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2t² / (Σ_{i=1}^{⌈n/m⌉−1} (Σ_{j∈B_i∪B_{i+1}} c_j)² + min_{i∈[⌈n/m⌉]} (Σ_{j∈B_i} c_j)²)). The blocks form a path on ⌈n/m⌉ vertices, and Theorem 2.1 is applied to it with block coefficients Σ_{j∈B_i} c_j. The paper prints the first sum over i ∈ [⌊n/m⌋]: the same range when m does not divide n; when m divides n the path has n/m − 1 edges, as the paper's own Remark 2.10 uses. With all c_i = c the denominator is at most 4mnc², so P(f(X) − E[f(X)] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−t²/(2mnc²)) (Remark 2.10).
c-Lipschitz (Definition 1.1 of the paper): Ω = Ω_1 × ... × Ω_n is a product of Polish spaces, c = (c_1, ..., c_n) ∈ R_+^n, and f : Ω → R is c-Lipschitz when |f(x) − f(x')| ≤ Σ_{i=1}^n c_i 1{x_i ≠ x'_i} for all x, x' ∈ Ω (Lipschitz for the c-weighted Hamming distance).
m-dependence (Definition 2.8 of the paper): (X_j)_{j=1}^i and (X_j)_{j=i+m+1}^n are independent for every i.

body: [Definition of arXiv:2504.06238, 'Infinite Boundary Friction Limit for Weak Solutions of the Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equati'] We define $C^{\infty}_{0,\sigma}(\mathscr{O};\mathbb{R}^2)$ as the subset of $C^{\infty}(\mathscr{O};\mathbb{R}^2)$ of functions which are compactly supported and divergence-free. $L^2_\sigma$ is defined as the completion of $C^{\infty}_{0,\sigma}(\mathscr{O};\mathbb{R}^2)$ in $L^2(\mathscr{O};\mathbb{R}^2)$, and $W^{1,2}_{\sigma}$ as the completion of $C^{\infty}_{0,\sigma}(\mathscr{O};\mathbb{R}^2)$ in $W^{1,2}(\mathscr{O};\mathbb{R}^2)$. Moreover we introduce $\bar{W}^{1,2}_\sigma$ as the intersection of $W^{1,2}(\mathscr{O};\mathbb{R}^2)$ with $L^2_\sigma$ and $\bar{W}^{2,2}_{\alpha}$ by $$\bar{W}^{2,2}_{\alpha}:= \left\{f \in W^{2,2}(\mathscr{O};\mathbb{R}^2) \cap \bar{W}^{1,2}_{\sigma}: 2(Df)\underline{n} \cdot \underline{\iota} + \alpha f \cdot \underline{\iota} = 0 \textnormal{ on } \partial \mathscr{O}\right\}.$$

body:
[Theorem dimHmu of arXiv:2505.11721, 'Variational principles for Hausdorff and packing dimensions of fractal percolation on self'] Suppose that the assumptions of Theorem~(sufcond2 of the paper)(1) hold, so that $\nu$ is non-degenerate. Let 
$$
\underline{d}(\nu)=\liminf_{N\to +\infty} d_N \text{ and } \overline{d}(\nu)=\limsup_{N\to +\infty} d_N. 
$$
where $d_N$ is defined as in (equation uN0 of the paper).  
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose that $\liminf_{N\to+\infty} N^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^NH(W^{(n)})=0$. With probability~1, conditional on $\{\nu\neq 0\}$, or $\nu$-almost every~$\boldsymbol{i}$ one has 
$$
\liminf_{N\to +\infty} \frac{\log(\nu(B_N(\boldsymbol{i})))}{-N}= \underline{d}(\nu)=0 \text{ and }\limsup_{N\to +\infty} \frac{\log(\nu(B_N(\boldsymbol{i})))}{-N}\le \overline{d}(\nu).
$$

\item Suppose that $\liminf_{N\to+\infty} N^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^NH(W^{(n)})>0$ and $\sup_{n\ge 1}\phi_{\widetilde W^{(n)}}(q)<+\infty$ for some $q \in \left(1,2\right]$.
With probability~1, conditional on $\{\nu\neq 0\}$, for $\nu$-almost every~$\boldsymbol{i}$ one has 
$$
\lim_{N\to +\infty}\left|\frac{\log(\nu(B_N(\boldsymbol{i})))}{-N}-d_N\right|=0,
$$
hence
$$
\begin{cases}
\liminf_{N\to +\infty}\displaystyle \frac{\log(\nu(B_N(\boldsymbol{i})))}{-N}= \underline{d}(\nu)\\
\limsup_{N\to +\infty}\displaystyle \frac{\log(\nu(B_N(\boldsymbol{i})))}{-N}= \overline{d}(\nu)
\end{cases}.
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition def:nf of arXiv:2608.27771, 'A normal form for the Thin Flat Surfaces category'] Let $f \colon n \to m$ be a connected viewable tf-cobordism with interval cycles
$\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_p$, where $\lambda_k$ involves $a_k$ incoming and $a'_k$
outgoing intervals, genus $g \geq 0$, and $c \geq 0$ holes.  Fix an ordering of the
cycles as in Section~(sec:ordering of the paper).  The \emph{normal form} of $f$ is the
tf-cobordism
\begin{equation}

  \mathrm{NF}(f)
  \;:=\;
  \Gamma(c,\, g)
  \;\circ\;
  \bar\rho(f)
  \;\circ\;
  K_p\!\bigl(\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_p\bigr)
  \;\circ\;
  \bar\sigma(f).
\end{equation}
For a general (not necessarily connected) viewable tf-cobordism $f = f_1 \otimes
\cdots \otimes f_c$ decomposed into connected components, the normal form is the
monoidal product
\[
  \mathrm{NF}(f) \;:=\; \mathrm{NF}(f_1) \otimes \cdots \otimes \mathrm{NF}(f_c).
\]
title: Normal form of a connected viewable tf-cobordism

Let U be an open subset of C, f holomorphic on U, and let the closed disc {|z - z_0| <= r} lie in U. Then for every a with |a - z_0| < r, f(a) = (1 / (2 pi i)) integral over the positively oriented circle |z - z_0| = r of f(z) / (z - a) dz, and for every n >= 0, f^{(n)}(a) = (n! / (2 pi i)) integral of f(z) / (z - a)^{n+1} dz. In particular a holomorphic function is infinitely differentiable and analytic. General form: for a closed piecewise smooth curve gamma in U that is null-homotopic in U and a point a in U not on gamma, n(gamma, a) f(a) = (1 / (2 pi i)) integral over gamma of f(z) / (z - a) dz, where n(gamma, a) is the winding number.

body: There are probability mass functions p and q on {1, 2, 3} and an event A with p(A), q(A) > 0 such that the conditional laws p(.|A) and q(.|A) are disjoint, so at total variation distance 1, while d_TV(p, q) = 1/2: take p = (1/2, 0, 1/2), q = (0, 1/2, 1/2) and A = {1, 2}. So disjoint conditional laws with p(A), q(A) > 0 do not imply d_TV(p, q) = 1; what holds is max(p(A), q(A)) <= d_TV(p, q) <= 1.

body:
[Theorem 11 (Dense-frequency separation) of arXiv:2609.01116, 'Vector-Carleson, Calder\'on, and Poisson--Atomic Criteria for\\ Generalized Hilbert Operat'] For every $2<p<\infty$ there is $\phi\in\Hol(\D)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $T_\phi:H^p\to H^p$ is bounded but not compact;
 \item every sufficiently large hard dyadic block is active and contains
 a consecutive frequency interval of length $2^{j-1}$;
 \item $\operatorname{supp}\widehat\phi$ is not an analytic
 $\Lambda(p)$-set;
 \item
 \[
  2^{-j/p'}\|\Delta_j\phi\|_{H^p}=1
  \qquad(j\ge j_0).
  \tag{4.4}
 \]
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the symbol lies outside the known sufficient class defined
by
\[
 \bigl(2^{-j/p'}\|\Delta_j\phi\|_{H^p}\bigr)_j\in\ell^t,
 \tag{4.5}
\]
and it is neither lacunary nor spectrally thin.

body: [Lem 22 of arXiv:2608.26698, 'Mapping class groups of simply connected closed spin 5-manifolds with no 2- and 3-torsion '] Let $M$ be a compact oriented 5-manifold, $S : S^2 \times D^3 \hookrightarrow M$ and $T : S^3 \hookrightarrow M$ be embeddings in the interior of $M$, and let $\mathbf{t}_{S, \beta}$ be the Dehn twist about $S$ and $\beta \in \pi_3(\mathrm{SO}(3))$. [Proposition 2 (Bijection of the vertex-labelled construction) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Fix $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathrm S_n$ be the set of sequences
\[
\left(\{u_1,v_1\},\ldots,\{u_{n-1},v_{n-1}\}\right)
\quad\text{with}\quad
0\le u_i< v_i\le i,\ \ 1\le i\le n-1.
\]
Let $\mathrm T_n$ be the set of bilabelled rooted trees with $n$ vertices: an
element of $\mathrm{T}_n$ is a rooted tree $T$ whose vertices are labelled by pairs
\[
(\ell(v),r(v))\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\times \mathbb Z_{\ge0},
\]
such that $\ell$ and $r$ are both standard labellings of $T$.
Then, the map $F:\mathrm S_n\to\mathrm T_n$ defined by the recursive algorithm

body: [Theorem 3 (Estimating the number of communities) of arXiv:2411.02835, 'Community detection with the Bethe-Hessian'] Assume that the average degree satisfies d ≥2 and Assumption 1 holds. For any ε > 0 small enough, the following holds with high probability for sufficiently large n: Nε( √ d) = N( √ d + ε) = r+ and Nε(− √ d) = N(− √ d −ε) = r−. The above is also valid when taking ε = εn = log(n)−c for any c > 0.

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), route failure, no novelty claim. For k>=2, two one-hot tasks with distinct disjoint k-parity labels on uniform x in {-1,+1}^{2k} can have nonzero population-gradient inner product in a shared two-layer ReLU network. In f=a ReLU(sum_j x_j+2k-1-c0/4+c1/4), at a=0 the conditional half-squared-loss gradients have inner product 15/(16*2^(4k))>0. All preactivations are at least 3/4 from zero. The expectation is over conditional task inputs at a fixed network state; averaging a sign-symmetric random initialization is a different statement. This refutes support-separation alone, not the intended random-training theorem.

half squared conditional task loss
explicit differentiable initialization; not a typical-initialization assertion

[Theorem thm:numerical-scaling of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] The following limits exist:
\[
    c_- := \lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\beta_k^-}{k^2}, \qquad c_\mathrm{typ}:=\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\beta_k^\mathrm{typ}}{k^2},
    \qquad
    c_+:=\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\beta_k^+}{k^2}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
    c_- < c_\mathrm{typ} < \frac12 < c_+.
\]
Quantitatively, 
\[
    \frac{1}{4} \le c_- \le 0.48867, \qquad 0.48934 \le c_\mathrm{typ} \le 0.49967,
    \qquad
    0.50547 \le c_+ \le 0.50568.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:multi of arXiv:2412.04328, 'The critical Karp--Sipser core of Erdős--Rényi random graphs'] Let $(m_n)_{n \geqslant 1}$ be a (deterministic) sequence of nonnegative integers such that $m_n=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{2}n+O \left( \sqrt{n} \right)$.
For $i \geqslant 2$, let $\mathbb{D}_i(n)$ be the number of vertices of degree $i$ in the Karp--Sipser core of $ \mathbb{G}(n, m_n)$. Then we have the joint convergence in distribution
	\[
	\left(\begin{array}{c}n^{-3/5} \cdot \mathbb{D}_{2}(n) \\  n^{-2/5} \cdot \mathbb{D}_{3}(n) \\ n^{-1/5} \cdot \mathbb{D}_4(n) \\ \mathbb{D}_5(n) \end{array}\right)  \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)} \left( \begin{array}{c} \frac{2^{9/5}3^{4/5}}{\mathrm{e}^{3/5}} \vartheta^{-2} \\  
	\frac{2^{16/5}3^{1/5}}{\mathrm{e}^{2/5}} \vartheta^{-3} \\ \frac{2^{13/5}3^{3/5}}{\mathrm{e}^{1/5}} \vartheta^{-4} \\ \mathrm{Poi} \left( \frac{48}{5} \vartheta^{-5} \right) \end{array}\right),
	\]
	where $\vartheta=\inf\{t \geqslant 0 : W_t=t^{-2}\}$ for a standard Brownian motion $W$ started from $0$. Moreover, with high probability, we have $\mathbb{D}_i(n)=0$ for all $i \geqslant 6$. Finally, conditionally on $\left( \mathbb{D}_i(n) \right)_{i \geqslant 2}$, the Karp--Sipser core is a configuration model. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:multi of arXiv:2412.04328

[Lemma lem:smooth_orthogonal_completion of arXiv:2607.04514, 'Boundary-layer asymptotics for Gaussian-smoothed singular measures'] Let \(\mathcal B\) be a contractible paracompact \(C^s\) manifold and let \(E\subset \mathcal
  B\times\mathbb R^d\) be a \(C^s\) rank-\(m\) subbundle, \(0\leqslant m \leqslant d\). Assume that
  \(E\) is equipped with a \(C^s\) orthonormal frame \(q_1,\ldots,q_m\). Then there are \(C^s\) maps
  \(n_1,\ldots,n_{d-m}: \mathcal B \to \mathbb R^d\) such that, for every \(b\in\mathcal B\),
  \(q_1(b),\ldots,q_m(b), n_1(b),\ldots, n_{d-m} (b)\) is an orthonormal basis of \(\mathbb R^d\).
title: Smooth orthogonal completion

body:
[Proposition prop:sbox-frame-condition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{F} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset)$ be an f-frame.
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
    \item $\mathfrak{F}$ is $\sqsubset$-strong iff it is $\sqsubset_\beta$-strong.
    \item If $\mathfrak{F}$ is $\Box$-p, then $\mathfrak{F}$ is $\sqsubset$-strong iff
          $\mathfrak{F} \vDash^e \varphi \to \Box \varphi$ for every $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$.
  \end{enumerate}
  \begin{proof}
    (1)
    ($\Rightarrow$)
    If $x \sqsubset_\beta y$, then there is $z \in W$ such that $x \sqsubset z \leq y$.
    Then $x \leq z \leq y$ by $\sqsubset$-strongness, so $x \leq y$ by the transitivity of $\leq$.
    Thus ${\sqsubset_\beta} \subseteq {\leq}$.
    ($\Leftarrow$) Trivial from the reflexivity of $\leq$.

    (2)
    ($\Rightarrow$) Suppose that $\mathfrak{F}$ is $\sqsubset$-strong, and let $\mathfrak{M}$ be an f-model based on $\mathfrak{F}$.
    Take $x, x' \in W$ and $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$ such that $x \leq x'$ and $x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$.
    For every $y \in W$ such that $x' \sqsubset y$, $\sqsubset$-strongness gives $x' \leq y$.
    Since $\mathfrak{F}$ is $\Box$-p, $\Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M}$ is $\Box$-persistent by Proposition~(prop:extrinsic-persistency of the paper);
    so $y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$.
    Therefore, $x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi$, and so $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi \to \Box \varphi$.
    ($\Leftarrow$) Suppose that $\mathfrak{F}$ is not $\sqsubset$-strong.
    Fix $x, y \in W$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $x \not \leq y$, and fix $p \in \mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}}$.
    Define a valuation $V$ by
    $V(p) = \set*{ z \in W; x \leq z }$ and $V(q) = \emptyset$ for every $q \ne p$,
    where each $V(r)$ is clearly upward closed with respect to $\leq$,
    and let $\mathfrak{M} = (\mathfrak{F}, V)$.
    Then $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} p$ and $y \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M} p$.
    Since $x \sqsubset y$, we have $x \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box p$,
    and consequently $x \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M} p \to \Box p$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:sbox-frame-condition of arXiv:2608.29708

body: In mathematics, the Banach fixed-point theorem is an important tool in the theory of metric spaces; it guarantees the existence and uniqueness of fixed points of certain self-maps of metric spaces and provides a constructive method to find those fixed points. It can be understood as an abstract formulation of Picard's method of successive approximations. The theorem is named after Stefan Banach (1892–1945) who first stated it in 1922.
title: Banach fixed-point theorem
