[Prop betterfence of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $M_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$ be a manifold with fences and windows, and let $\mathcal{F}_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$ be a $C^0$-foliation on $M_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$ adapted to $\partial M_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$ and $\partial_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$-transitive. Furthermore, let $\partial^\flat \mathcal{F}_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$ (resp.~$\partial^\sharp \mathcal{F}_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$) be an arbitrarily small $\flat$ (resp.~$\sharp$) window modification of $\partial \mathcal{F}_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$.
    
    Then $\mathcal{F}_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$ can be $C^0$-approximated by $C^0$-foliations on $M_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$, still adapted to $\partial M_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$, which are positively (resp.~negatively) transverse to foliations isotopic to $\partial^\flat \mathcal{F}_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$ (resp.~$\partial^\sharp \mathcal{F}_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$) along the facades in $\partial_* M_{\mathord{\scalebox{0.45}{$\square$}}}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2605.02771, 'Universality in Deep Neural Networks:\\ An approach via the Lindeberg exchange principle'] Let $(\bX_i)_{i\in\N}$ be a sequence of independent random vectors in $\R^d$. We assume that, for all $i\in\N$, the coefficients of $\bX_i$ are i.i.d. with zero mean, variance $\sigma_i^2$ and absolute third moments equal to $m_3^{(i)}$. Also, let $(\bY_i)_{i\in\N}$, be a sequence of independent Gaussian vectors in $\R^d$, so that the coefficients of $\bY_i$ are all independent and have matching first and second moments to the corresponding coefficients of $\bX_i$. Finally, let $F \in C^3_b(\R^d;\R)$. Then
    \[
        \biggl|\E\biggl[F\biggl(\sum_{i=1}^n\bX_i\biggr)\biggr]-\E\biggl[F\biggl(\sum_{i=1}^n\bY_i\biggr)\biggr]\biggr|\lesssim C_F\cdot d^3\cdot\sum_{i=1}^nm_3^{(i)},
    \]
    where the implied constant depends only on universal constants and 
    \[
        C_F:=\max \left\{||\partial^3_{i,j,k}F||_{L^{\infty}(\R^d)} \, : i,j,k=1,\dots d \right\}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem thm: points fixes pour les CC of arXiv:2605.28770, 'Cutoff profiles for conjugacy invariant random walks on symmetric groups'] For each $n$ let $ {\ensuremath{\mathcal C}} ^{(n)} \in{\ensuremath{\textup{Conj}}} ^*({\ensuremath{\mathfrak{S}}} _n)$, and assume that $f_1({\ensuremath{\mathcal C}} ^{(n)})/\sqrt{n}\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$. Let  $a\in {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $. Assume that there exist $S\subset {\ensuremath{\mathbb N}} ^*$ and a sequence $(t_n)_{n\in S}$ of integers such that $t_n = t_{{\ensuremath{\mathcal C}} ^{(n)}} \left( 1 + \frac{a+o(1)}{\ln n} \right)$, and let, for $n\in S$, $Y_n$ be a $\ensuremath{\textup{Unif}}_{{\ensuremath{\mathcal C}} ^{(n)}}^{*t_n}$ random variable. Then, as $S\ni n\to \infty$, $f_1(Y_n)$ converges in distribution to $\ensuremath{\textup{Poiss}}\left( 1+e^{-a}\right)$.

[Proposition 34 (Collapse criterion) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] \bse
In the future-contracting case $[t_0,t_1]\subset(-\infty,0)$, the conformal length admits two (non-negative) lower bounds.
\bei
\item In terms of the scaled volume $\mathcal V_1$ defined in~\eqref{eq:section-8-volume-functionals}, below,
\bel{non-collapse-1}
\mathcal L(t) \geq \frac{|t_0/t|^{3/2}}{\mathcal V_1(t_0)} \mathcal V(t)^2 , \qquad t_0 \leq t \leq t_1 < 0 .
\ee

\item In a restricted time interval with end-point $t_2 = - |t_0|^{1/3} \bigl( |t_0| - \frac{3}{2} \mathcal L(t_0) / \mathcal E_\chi(t_0) \bigr)^{2/3} < 0$,
\bel{non-collapse-2}
\mathcal L(t)
\geq \frac{2}{3} |t_0| \mathcal E_\chi(t_0)
- \Bigl( \frac{2}{3} |t_0| \mathcal E_\chi(t_0) - \mathcal L(t_0) \Bigr) \Bigl|\frac{t_0}{t}\Bigr|^{3/2} ,
\qquad t_0 \leq t \leq \min(t_1,t_2) < 0 .
\ee
\eei
\ese (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.27117, 'Occupation-Time Fluctuations of an Age-Dependent Branching System Driven by Poisson Immigr'] Let $\{X_n,\ n\ge1\}$ be a sequence of processes with paths in
$
C([0,\Upsilon],\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^d)).
$
Assume that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\{X_n,\ n\ge1\}$ is tight;
\item $\{\widetilde X_n,\ n\ge1\}$ converges weakly in
$\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^{d+1})$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^d)$-valued process $X$ such that
$
X_n\Rightarrow X.
$
Moreover, the law of $X$ is uniquely determined by the limit law of
$\widetilde X_n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.27117

[Theorem 1 (Cyclotomic expansion for symmetric-power-colored $SU(n)$ invariants) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For every zero-framed knot $K$ and every fixed $n\ge2$, there is a unique
sequence of Laurent polynomials
\[
 \bigl(H_k^{(n)}(K;q)\bigr)_{k\ge0},
 \qquad H_k^{(n)}(K;q)\in\Z[q^{\pm1}],
\]
such that, for all $r\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 J_r^{SU(n)}(K;q)=\sum_{k=0}^{r}
 \left(\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\{r-i\}\{r+n+i\}\right)H_k^{(n)}(K;q).
\end{equation}
Moreover, $H_0^{(n)}(K;q)=1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cyclotomic expansion for symmetric-power-colored $SU(n)$ invariants

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be any locally compact abelian group. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on $G$ that are absolutely continuous with respect to Haar measure, 
and such that $D(P\|Q)<\infty.$ For any $t\geq 0$, 
write $Q^t$ for the probability measure
    $$
    Q^t:= \frac{tQ+P}{1+t}.
    $$
    Then for any $T>0$:
    $$
    \int_0^T \chi^2(P\|Q^t)\,\frac{dt}{t(1+t)} = D(P\|Q) - \int\log{\Biggl(\frac{\frac{dP}{dQ} + T}{1+T}\Biggr)}\, dP. 
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:degeneracy of arXiv:2608.16915, 'Exact mean--covariance dynamics of the Weber field in the stochastic Lagrangian representa'] In centre and separation variables $c=\tfrac{x+y}{2}$, $r=x-y$,
\[
  (\nabla_x+\nabla_y)^2=\Delta_c,\qquad
  u(x)\cdot\nabla_x+u(y)\cdot\nabla_y
  =\frac{u_++u_-}{2}\cdot\nabla_c+(u_+-u_-)\cdot\nabla_r,
\]
with $u_\pm=u(t,c\pm r/2)$. The diffusion therefore acts on the centre variable only;
there is no $\Delta_r$. In particular the model equation
$\partial_tH-\nu(\nabla_x+\nabla_y)^2H=0$ admits every bounded profile
$H(t,x,y)=h(x-y)$ as a stationary solution, so no estimate can extract regularity in
$x-y$ from the common-noise diffusion alone.

body: Godel's completeness theorem for first-order logic: for any first-order language L, any set T of L-sentences, and any L-sentence phi, T semantically entails phi (every model of T satisfies phi) if and only if phi is derivable from T in a standard proof calculus for first-order logic (Hilbert-style, natural deduction, or sequent calculus - all such standard calculi are both sound and complete). Equivalent model-existence form: every syntactically consistent first-order theory (one from which no contradiction is derivable) has a model; by the Henkin construction the model can be taken of cardinality at most the maximum of the cardinality of L and aleph_0. Soundness (derivable implies entailed) is the elementary converse direction. This theorem concerns first-order logic itself and does not conflict with Godel's incompleteness theorems, which concern the incompleteness of specific arithmetical theories, not of the logic.
title: Godel completeness theorem (statement)

The attribution window mismatch is the structural discrepancy in experimental logging where treated outcomes $Y(1)$ are attributed only within a short direct-response interaction window $W_T$ (e.g. within 2 hours of seeing the recommendation banner), while holdback/control outcomes $Y(0)$ are aggregated over a longer multi-day observation window $W_C$ (e.g. 7 days of organic consumption), making direct subtraction $Y^{W_T}(1) - Y^{W_C}(0)$ uncalibrated and biased.
W_T is the direct attribution window for treated units
W_C is the multi-day organic attribution window for holdback units
W_T \subsetneq W_C
title: Attribution Window Mismatch

[Definition def:weak_soln of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] For a nonnegative $\mathcal F_0$-measurable random initial function $u_0$, we say that
$u$ is a solution of (equation eq:SPDE of the paper) on $[0, T]$ with initial
function $u_0$ if $u$ is a $C_{\rm tem}(\mathbb{R})$-valued
process $u=u(t,\cdot)$, defined on $\Omega\times[0, T]$, such that for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item
The process $\int_{\mathbb{R}}\varphi(x)u(t\wedge T,x)\,\mathrm{d} x$ is well-defined, $\mathcal F_t$-adapted, and continuous.

\item The process  $\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\sigma(u(t\wedge T,x))\varphi(x)|^2\,\mathrm{d} x$ is well-defined, $\mathcal F_t$-adapted, measurable in $(\omega,t)$, and
\[
\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{R}}
|\sigma(u(t,x))\varphi(x)|^2\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} t
<\infty \quad \text{a.s.}
\]
\item
For all $0<t\le T$, 
\[
(u(t,\cdot),\varphi) = (u_0,\varphi)
+ \int_0^t (u(s,\cdot),( L^*\varphi)(s,\cdot))\,\mathrm{d} s  
+\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{R}}
\sigma(u(s,x))\varphi(x)\xi(\mathrm{d} s,\mathrm{d} x) \quad \text{a.s.}
\]
Here $L^*$ is the adjoint operator of $L$ introduced in (equation second order operator of the paper), namely
$L^*\varphi = \partial_x^2(a\varphi) -\partial_x(b\varphi)+c\varphi$. 
\end{enumerate}
When the initial state is a nonnegative random Radon measure
$\mu_0$, we say that $u\in C((0,T];C_{\rm tem})$ is a solution of
(equation eq:SPDE of the paper) with initial measure $\mu_0$ if $u$ satisfies
(i)--(iii) with $(u_0,\varphi)$ replaced by
$\int_{\mathbb{R}}\varphi\,\mathrm{d}\mu_0$.

\]

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Numerical test on random pairs of positive contractions, plus the diagonal and one-element cases in closed form. Result: Exact facts: for |E| = 1 the measure is Bernoulli(q) and Ent = h(q) is concave, so the conjecture holds; for commuting diagonal kernels the measure is a product and Ent = sum h(q_i), concave; for Q_2 = I - Q_1 the midpoint is I/2, whose entropy |E| log 2 is the maximum possible, so the inequality holds trivially. Numerical check (raw/C_lyons_conj26_entropy_check.json): 1440 random pairs of symmetric positive contractions in dimensions 2..6 with spectra in (0.02, 0.98), entropy computed exactly from P(A) = det(I-Q) det(J_A) with J = Q(I-Q)^{-1}; the concavity gap Ent(mid) - average was positive in every trial, minimum gap 8.5e-4 (dimension 2). No counterexample; the minimum gap being attained in dimension 2 suggests that a proof for 2x2 kernels, where the measure has four atoms with explicit determinants, would be the first non-trivial case to attempt analytically. Key identity: P_Q(A) = det(I-Q) det(J_A), J = Q(I-Q)^{-1}, gives an exact finite formula for the entropy. Check: Probabilities summed to 1 within 1e-8 in every trial and were non-negative. Obstruction: No analytic argument beyond diagonal kernels; the 2x2 case is the natural next target.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0033-concavity-of-the-entropy-of-determinantal-measures-in-the-kernel
No independent review; result status partial_result

[Definition Generalized diagrams of arXiv:2506.06559, 'Bi-infinite incipient cluster in high dimensions'] For a set of diagrammatic graphs $\mathcal{G}$, we say that the \emph{generalized diagram of $\mathcal{G}$} is given by the product of 2-point functions
\[
\text{Diag}(\mathcal{G}):=\sum_{{\bf G}\in \mathcal{G}} \text{Diag}({\bf G}),
\]
which means it is the sum of diagrams appearing in $\mathcal{G}$ (which is a set of diagrammatic graphs).

In particular, if $\mathcal{G}$ is a generalized diagrammatic graph, and  $E\subset \bigcup_{{\bf G}\in \mathcal{G}} \mathcal{D}_{{\bf G}}$, then the BK inequality will imply that 
\[
{\bf P}[E]\leq {\bf P}\Bigl[ \bigcup_{{\bf G}\in \mathcal{G}} \mathcal{D}_{{\bf G}}\Bigr] \leq   \text{Diag}(\mathcal{G}).
\]
title: Generalized diagrams

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2609.02610, 'The frame set of the first Hermite function'] Let $\Lambda\subset\R$ and let $(\Lambda_n)_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of
subsets of $\R$. We say that $\Lambda_n$ \emph{converges weakly} to $\Lambda$ and write
$\Lambda_n\xrightarrow{w}\Lambda$ if, for every $R>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$,
there exists an integer $n_0\geq1$ such that, for all integers $n\geq n_0$,
\begin{equation}
  \Lambda_n\cap[-R,R]
  \subset \Lambda+(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \Lambda\cap[-R,R]
  \subset \Lambda_n+(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon).
\end{equation}
For a set $\Lambda\subset\R$, let $\Hullw(\Lambda)$ be the collection of all
sets $\Gamma\subset\R$ for which there is a sequence $(t_n)_{n \in \N}$ in $\R$ such
that $t_n+\Lambda\xrightarrow{w}\Gamma$.
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2609.02610

[Theorem thm:spectral-upper of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] For a reversible chain with stationary distribution $\pi$,
\[
  I(X_0;X_1)
  =\sum_{x\in S}\pi(x)\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P(x,\cdot)\|\pi)
  \;\le\;\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
  \bar r_\pi\;\le\;
  \frac{\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^2}{\log(1/\pi_{\max})},
\]
where $\pi_{\max}=\max_x\pi(x)$.
If $\pi$ is uniform, then
\[
  \bar r_\pi
  \;\le\;
  \frac{\sum_{i=2}^n\lambda_i^2}{\log n}
  \;\le\;
  \frac{(n-1)(1-\gamma)^2}{\log n}.
\]

body: [Definition 14 (Iterative directed hypergraph process) of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Consider the vertex set $V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$ with out- and in-degree sequences $\d^{(1)}=(d_1^{(1)},\ldots,d_n^{(1)})$ and $\d^{(2)}=(d_1^{(2)},\ldots,d_n^{(2)})$ of non-negative integers. Consider sequences $\d'^{(1)}=(d_1'^{(1)},\ldots,d_m'^{(1)})$ and $\d'^{(2)}=(d_1'^{(2)},\ldots,d_m'^{(2)})$ of positive integers with $s^{(i)}:=d_1^{(i)}+\ldots+d_n^{(i)}=d_1'^{(i)}+\ldots+d_m'^{(i)}>0$ for $i\in\{1,2\}$, and consider a set $X$ of forbidden hyperarcs. For $V':=\{v_1',\ldots,v_m'\}$, use the iterative edge-colored bipartite graph process to sample edge-disjoint simple bipartite graphs $(V\cup V',\widetilde{E}^{(i)})$ with degree sequences $\d^{(i)}$ and $\d'^{(i)}$ on its parts for $i\in\{1,2\}$. Apply rejection sampling to make sure that all vertices in $V'$ have distinct pairs of neighborhoods that are not in $X$. Finally, identify each such pair of neighborhoods with a hyperarc on $V$ to sample a simple directed hypergraph $(V,E)$ with out- and in-degree sequences $\d^{(1)}$ and $\d^{(2)}$ and with hyperarcs not in $X$ with orders $(d_1'^{(1)},d_1'^{(2)}),\ldots,(d_m'^{(1)},d_m'^{(2)})$.
title: Iterative directed hypergraph process

${\rm PGL}(V)$ is not contained in any compact subgroup of ${\rm PGL}(V)$. 
Assume that $\mu$ admits a finite exponential moment \eqref{Exponential-moment}. 
Then, there exists $\upsilon_{\mu} > 0$ such that, for any real numbers $a < b$,
 uniformly in $\xi \in G \varpi G$ and in $w_n \in \bb R$ with $|w_n| = o(\sqrt{n})$,

\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  b-a. 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 12 (Theorem~3.6, Abbe--Boix-Adser, \cite{AbbeBoix2020}) of arXiv:2607.21392, 'Gaussian Convexity Principles for Sharp Moderate Deviations of Gaussian Maxima and Critica'] Consider a binary synchronization model on a finite graph \(\mathcal{G}=(V,E)\): the hidden vertex labels \((\theta_v)_{v\in V}\) are i.i.d. uniform on \(\{-1,+1\}\), and conditional on \(\theta\), the edge observations \((Y_e)_{e\in E}\) are generated by a symmetric graphical channel. Then, for every \(u,v\in V\), \[ I_2(\theta_u;\theta_v\mid Y) \le \mathbb P\bigl( u \leftrightarrow v \text{ in bond percolation on }\mathcal{G} \text{ with edge-open probabilities }(p_e)_{e\in E} \bigr), \] where $p_e=I_2(\theta_i;\theta_j\mid Y_e), e=\{i,j\}\in E. $ Here \(I_2\) denotes \(\chi^2\)-mutual information, and the bond percolation on \(\mathcal{G}\) is the independent percolation process in which each edge \(e\) is open with probability \(p_e\). [Definition 28 of arXiv:2605.03851, 'The Relay Random Tree:\\A stochastic geometry approach of multihop relay in an urban visib'] \textbf{Visibility, relaying scheme.}

Let $\landsc$ be a landscape.

Let $(a_1, b_1)$ and $(a_2, b_2)$ be two buildings of $\landsc$. We say that $(a_2, b_2)$ is visible from $(a_1, b_1)$ if it is in range and there are no buildings above the segment from $(a_1, b_1)$ to $(a_2, b_2)$. In other words, if the following conjunction of events holds true:
\[\{(a_2, b_2)\text{ is in range from } (a_1, b_1)\} \cap \below{[a_1, a_2]}{(a_1, b_1)}{\frac{b_2-b_1}{a_2-a_1}}.\]

Thanks to this, we can define the relaying scheme $\tau$ as
\[\tau_{\mathrm{R}} (x, y, \landsc) = (x_b, y_b) := \underset{\substack{(a, b) \in \landsc\cap \mathrm{R}+(x, y) \\(a, b) \text{ visible from }(x, y)}}{\text{argmax}} \frac{b-y}{a-x}.\]
When this is well defined, and $\tau (x, y, \landsc) = (-\infty, -\infty)$ otherwise.

The blockage angle and its tangent are defined as usual in this context

body: [Lem smoothingfol of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\Phi$ be a smooth nonsingular flow on $M$, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a topological foliation on $M$ which is topologically transverse to $\Phi$. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is topologically isotopic to a $C^0$-foliation with smooth leaves, which is genuinely transverse to $\Phi$. Moreover, the isotopy can be made arbitrarily small, and along the flow lines of $\Phi$.

body:
[Cor 26 (Separated Gaussian grid moments) of arXiv:2608.15137, '2608.15137'] Assume the nested complex Gaussian covariance path and the normalization
\(\chi_j^{\mathrm{proj}}\) of Theorem~\ref{thm:nested-wishart-decorrelation}. Fix \(a,b>0\), put
\[
\kappa_+=\frac43a^{3/2},
\qquad
\kappa_-=\frac{b^3}{12},
\]
and assume
\[
\max(\kappa_+,\kappa_-)<\frac13.
\]
For each sign \(\mathfrak s\in\{+,-\}\), choose
\(\theta_{\mathfrak s}>0\) and \(\epsilon_{\mathfrak s}>0\) such that
\[
\kappa_{\mathfrak s}
+
\theta_{\mathfrak s}
+
\epsilon_{\mathfrak s}
<
\frac13.
\]
Fix \(H_{\mathrm{shift}}<\infty\). For every sufficiently large integer \(N\), there are grids
\[
\mathcal T_N^+,\mathcal T_N^-
\subseteq[N,2N)
\]
such that distinct points of \(\mathcal T_N^{\mathfrak s}\) are separated by at least
\[
N^{2/3+\epsilon_{\mathfrak s}},
\]
\[
\abs{\mathcal T_N^{\mathfrak s}}
=
\left\lfloor
N^{\kappa_{\mathfrak s}+\theta_{\mathfrak s}}
\right\rfloor,
\]
and the following holds uniformly for every deterministic family of shifts
\(h_{j,\mathfrak s}\), \(j\in\mathcal T_N^{\mathfrak s}\), with
\(\abs{h_{j,\mathfrak s}}\leq H_{\mathrm{shift}}\). Put
\[
S_N^+
=
\sum_{j\in\mathcal T_N^+}
\ind_{\{
\chi_j^{\mathrm{proj}}
\geq
a(\log j)^{2/3}+h_{j,+}
\}},
\]
\[
S_N^-
=
\sum_{j\in\mathcal T_N^-}
\ind_{\{
\chi_j^{\mathrm{proj}}
\leq
-b(\log j)^{1/3}+h_{j,-}
\}}.
\]
Then
\[
\E S_N^{\mathfrak s}
=
N^{\theta_{\mathfrak s}+o(1)}
\]
and
\[
\E[(S_N^{\mathfrak s})^2]
\leq
(1+o(1))(\E S_N^{\mathfrak s})^2
+
\E S_N^{\mathfrak s}.
\]
In particular, for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
\E S_N^{\mathfrak s}
\geq
N^{\theta_{\mathfrak s}/2}
\]
and
\[
\frac{
\E[(S_N^{\mathfrak s})^2]
}{
(\E S_N^{\mathfrak s})^2
}
\leq
1+o(1).
\]

If \(\mathcal B_N\) is any \(\sigma\)-algebra independent of the entire auxiliary complex Gaussian array, then the same identities and inequalities hold almost surely after conditioning on \(\mathcal B_N\). In particular, for any \(\eta>0\) satisfying
\[
\kappa_+ + 2\eta + \epsilon_+ < \frac13,
\qquad
\kappa_- + \eta + \epsilon_- < \frac13,
\]
the choices
\[
\theta_+=2\eta,
\qquad
\theta_-=\eta
\]
are admissible.
title: Separated Gaussian grid moments

$\int_{\mathbb{T}^d} :\!(\pi_N u)^k\!:dx$

in $L^p(\mu)$ and $\mu$-almost surely, as $N \to \infty$, 
where $\mu$ is as in~(equation gauss0 of the paper).
In particular, 
given a sequence  $\{\lambda_N\}_{N\in \mathbb{N}}$  of positive numbers
tending to $0$ as $N \to \infty$, 
$\lambda_N R_N(u)$ converges to $0$
in $L^p(\mu)$ and $\mu$-almost surely, as $N \to \infty$, 
where
 $R_N(u)$ is as in  (equation Wick0 of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition 11 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Suppose $b,y>0$. Let $\{\vec{W}_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ be a standard three-dimensional Brownian motion. The \textit{3D Bessel bridge} on $[0,b]$ to $y$ is the stochastic process $\{V_t = \lVert \vec{W}_t\rVert_2 : t\in[0,b]\}$ conditioned on $V_b = y$. (For a formal definition of this conditioning, see \cite[Section XI.3]{RY}.)
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2603.24616

[Theorem 27 (Reduction lemma: reduced-group and path conjugacy) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space and let $\gamma:[0,T]\to V$ be a continuous tree-reduced bounded-variation path, translated so that $\gamma_0=0$. Set
\[
g=S(\gamma),\qquad v=S_1(\gamma)=\gamma_T\neq0.
\]
The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item There is $a\in\Sl(V)$ such that $g=a\e^v a^{-1}$.
\item There is $t_0\in[0,T]$ such that, for $\beta=\gamma|_{[0,t_0]}$,
\[
\gamma\sim_{\mathrm{rep}}
\beta*\lambda_v*\overleftarrow{\beta}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Under \textup{(a)}, let $p$ be the gate from $1$ to the axis in \cref{prop:axis-gate-decomposition}. One may choose $S(\beta)=p$, and this prefix signature is independent of the auxiliary Euclidean norm.

[Theorem prop:generators of kernel of action of MCG on Out(pi1) of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] Let $M$ be a compact, orientable 3-manifold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item The kernel of $\rho$ is generated by the seven families of diffeomorphisms listed.
\item  The kernel of $\rho^+$ is generated by the families of diffeomorphisms (1)--(4).
\item If moreover $M$ is closed, then the kernel of $\rho$ is generated by the families of diffeomorphisms (1), (6), and (7).
\item If $M$ is closed, then the kernel of $\rho^+$ is generated by sphere twists as in (1).
\item If $M$ is closed, irreducible, and not equal to $S^3$ or $\mathbb{RP}^3$, then $\rho$ is injective.
\item If $M$ is closed and irreducible, then $\rho^+$ is injective.
\end{enumerate}
title: \cite{Hatcher_Wahl_MCG3Manifold}, Prop.~2.1

body:
[Lemma 32 (Hölder roughness and integrability of the roughness modulus) of arXiv:2506.09637, 'Nonlinear Stochastic Filtering with Volterra Gaussian Noises'] Let $I$ be a $d_I$-dimensional centered Volterra Gaussian process with i.i.d. components satisfying Conditions \ref{condition_covariance_rho_var} and  \ref{condition_4}. 
Then, there exists a $\varsigma > 0$ such that for every \(\theta\in( 2/p \wedge 1 -\varsigma,  2/p \wedge 1 )\), the process \(I\) is almost surely
\(\theta\)-Hölder rough. More precisely, if
\[
    L_\theta(I)
    :=
    \inf_{\substack{s\in[0,T],\,0<\epsilon\leq T/2\\
                    v\in\mathbb R^{d_I},\,|v|=1}}
    \frac{1}{\epsilon^\theta}
    \sup_{\substack{t\in[0,T]\\
                    \epsilon/2<|t-s|<\epsilon}}
    \bigl|\langle v,I_t-I_s\rangle\bigr|,
\]
then
\(
    L_\theta(I)>0 
\) almost surely.
Moreover, for every \(l>0\),
\(
    \mathbb E\left[L_\theta(I)^{-l}\right]<\infty.
\)
title: Hölder roughness and integrability of the roughness modulus

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. body: Let X and Y be real-valued random variables. Then X is stochastically dominated by Y, meaning P(X > t) <= P(Y > t) for every real t, if and only if there exists a coupling of X and Y, that is, random variables X' and Y' defined on a common probability space with X' having the same distribution as X and Y' having the same distribution as Y, such that X' <= Y' almost surely. [Strassen (1965); Lindvall, Lectures on the Coupling Method]
title: Strassen's Theorem (Coupling Characterization of Stochastic Order)

body:
The Mitchison-Durbin decoder-independent first-moment bound: for a tree sign network with N=Kn total weights and P fair independent labels, Pr(storage)<=min(1,2^{-P} C(P,n)^K), where C(P,n)=2 sum_{j=0}^{min(n-1,P-1)} binom(P-1,j). For fixed K and a=P/N, the exponent on aK>2 is F_K(a)=aK log(aK)-(aK-1)log(aK-1)-a log 2. Its upper-envelope root b_K has b_1=2 and K h(1/(K b_K))=log 2 for K>1, with b_K~log(K)/log(2). This is prior work, not a sharp threshold or a new result.
K,n,P positive integers; N=Kn; K disjoint n-dimensional groups
Each hidden unit is homogeneous sign with nonzero spherical weights; Gaussian input samples, hence general position almost surely
Uniform independent labels independent of the inputs; fixed Boolean decoder and tie rules
First take N to infinity with K fixed; entropy-branch statement uses aK>2

[Prop Prop1 of arXiv:2608.29390, 'The Test and Find Model'] If $\gamma=(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_n) \in \Gamma$ and $s=(s_1,\dots,s_n)\in\Sigma$, then for any $\pi$
\begin{eqnarray}
p(s|\gamma)&=&\prod_{i: \gamma_i=1}a_i^{s_i}(1-a_i)^{1-s_i}\prod_{i: \gamma_i=0}b_i^{1-s_i}(1-b_i)^{s_i}, \\
p(\gamma,s|\pi)&=&\pi(\gamma)p(s|\gamma),       \\
p(s|\pi)&=&\sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma}\pi(\gamma)p(s|\gamma),       \\
\theta(\gamma|s,\pi) &=&\frac{\pi(\gamma)p(s|\gamma)}{p(s|\pi)} , \\
\alpha_i(s,\pi)&=& \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma: \gamma_i=0}\theta(\gamma |s,\pi)=
\frac{\sum\limits_{\gamma\in\Gamma: \gamma_i=0} \pi(\gamma)p(s|\gamma)}{\sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma}\pi(\gamma)p(s|\gamma)}, \mbox{ and }\\
\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(s,\pi) &=& n-k. 
\end{eqnarray}

body:
[Lemma 37 (Symmetric feedback closes the primitive criterion) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Let $q\ge2$, $x\in H^{\odot q}$ and
$F=I_q(x/\sqrt{q!})$.  Put
$\kappa_4(F)=\E[F^4]-3\E[F^2]^2$.  Then
\begin{align}
 \kappa_4(F)
 &=\sum_{s=1}^{q-1}\binom qs^2\norm{x\otimes_sx}^2
 \notag\\
 &\quad+\sum_{s=1}^{q-1}\frac{q^2}{s^2}\,
 b_{q,q,s}\norm{x\wtensor_sx}^2.
 
\end{align}
If $\norm x\le R$, then
\begin{equation}
 |\kappa_4(F)|
 \le 3^{q+1}R^2
 \left(\sum_{s=1}^{q-1}
 b_{q,q,s}\norm{x\wtensor_sx}^2\right)^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}
In fact the carré-du-champ defect and the fourth cumulant satisfy the
exact expansion and comparison
\begin{align}
 \kappa_4(F)
 &=3q\sum_{s=1}^{q-1}\frac{b_{q,q,s}}s
   \norm{x\wtensor_sx}^2,
 \\
 \frac1{3q}\kappa_4(F)
 &\le
 \Var\bigl(\Gamma(F,F)\bigr)
 \le\frac{q-1}{3q}\kappa_4(F).
 
\end{align}
Consequently, for a bounded family, vanishing of the symmetric feedback
on the right of \eqref{bridge:eq:kappa-from-symmetric-feedback} forces every
proper unsymmetrized self-contraction to vanish.

body:
[Lemma 14 (Behaviour outside the initial support) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Fix $x>1$. As $t\downarrow0$,
\[
  p_t(x)=\frac{\sqrt t}{2\sqrt{2\pi}\,(x-1)}\,e^{-(x-1)^2/2t}\big(1+O(t)\big),
\]
and consequently
\[
  \partial_x\log p_t(x)=-\frac{x-1}{t}-\frac{1}{x-1}+O(t),
  \qquad
  \partial_x^2\log p_t(x)=-\frac1t+\frac{1}{(x-1)^2}+O(t),
\]
so that
\begin{equation}
  v(x,t)=\frac{x-1}{2t}+\frac{1}{2(x-1)}+O(t)\qquad(t\downarrow0).
\end{equation}
The corresponding statements for $x<-1$ follow by symmetry. In particular, for any compact set
$K\subset\{|x|>1\}$,
\begin{equation}
  \int_K\big|\partial_x\log p_t\big|\,\dd x=\frac{1}{t}\int_K\big(|x|-1\big)\dd x+O(1),
  \qquad
  \int_K\big|\partial_x^2\log p_t\big|\,\dd x=\frac{|K|}{t}+O(1).
\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem NEW-t:sysID of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] For $d,d'\in\mathbb{N}$, $t_0\in(0,\infty)$, let $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}:=\{\delta_{(x, M(x),Z_x)}\}_{x\in\mathcal{P}}$ be a 
marked point process 
on $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^{d'}\times\mathbb {M} $
such that   $Z_x\in\mathbb {M} ={\cal C}([0,t_0],\mathbb{R}^{d'})$ are i.i.d. standard Brownian motions on the interval $[0,t_0]$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d'}$, independent given the  marked point process $\{\delta_{(x, M(x))}\}_{x\in\mathcal{P}}$ of sites with initial conditions. We assume that  the initial conditions $M(x)$, $x\in\mathcal{P}$, are almost surely deterministically, uniformly bounded, i.e.,  $\sup_{x\in\mathcal{P}}|M(x)| \le L<\infty$.  
Moreover, we assume that the marked point process $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ has summable exponential $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations as in Definition (def.A2 of the paper) and has bounded reduced  Palm intensity function as in~(equation bdedreduced of the paper).
Consider a graph $\Psi(\mathcal{P})$ constructed deterministically on $\mathcal{P}$ 
which is fast stabilizing  with the interaction range 
satisfying ~(equation sdecayspin-infty of the paper).
Given Lipschitz diffusion coefficients $(b,\sigma)$ as in  Definition (NEW-d:lip_assum of the paper) consider the strong solution to the interacting diffusions system (equation NEW-e:sys_ID_V of the paper) on $\Psi(\mathcal{P})$, with initial conditions $M(x)$, realized by  individual paths $M^{\Psi(\mathcal{P})}[x]\in\mathbb {M} $ for points  $x\in\mathcal{P}$. Finally,
define the measures
\begin{equation}

\hat{\mu}_n^{\xi} := \sum_{x \in \mathcal{P} \cap W_n} \xi (\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})  \delta_{n^{-1/d}x},
\end{equation}
where $\xi =\xi^{(h, \Psi(\mathcal{P}))}$ are real-valued scores of the  individual paths $M^{\Psi(\mathcal{P})}[x]\in\mathbb {M} $  given by~(equation NEW-xisysID of the paper) with  a Lipschitz function $h : \mathbb {M}  \to \mathbb{R}$.

\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),  labelindent=0pt]
\item  If 
the  score $\xi$ in (equation NEW-xisysID of the paper) satisfies the $p$-moment condition~(equation NEW-momh1 of the paper) for all  $p \in (1, \infty)$, then the random measures $(\hat{\mu}_n^{ \xi})_{ n \in \mathbb{N}}$  at (equation NEW-SysID of the paper) satisfy the central limit theorem,  i.e., for  $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$ such that ${\rm Var}{\hat{\mu}_{n}^{\xi}(f)} = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$, we have

\[ ({\rm Var}{\hat{\mu}_{n}^{\xi}(f)})^{-1/2}(\hat{\mu}_{n}^{\xi}(f) - \mathbb {E} \hat{\mu}_{n}^{\xi}(f)) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z. \]

\item  If the input process $\{\delta_{(x,M(x))}\}_{x \in \mathcal{P}}$ is stationary and the graph construction $\Psi(\mathcal{P})$ is translation invariant, then the mean asymptotics can be expressed for all $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$ as:
\begin{align}
 \Big| n^{-1} \mathbb{E}  \hat{\mu}_n^{\xi}(f) -  \rho \mathbb{E} _{\0} \xi(\tilde\0, \tilde{\mathcal{P}}) \int_{W_1}f(x)\,\mathrm{d} x\Big| = O(n^{-1/d}), 
\end{align}
whereas under an extra $p=(2+\epsilon)$-moment condition, for some $\epsilon>0$,  the variance asymptotics  can be expressed as
 \begin{align}
 & \lim_{n \to \infty} n^{-1} {\rm Var} \,\hat{\mu}_n^{\xi}(f) =  \sigma^2(\xi) \int_{W_1} f(x)^2 \,\mathrm{d} x \in [0,\infty),
\end{align}
where 
\begin{align}
 \sigma^2(\xi) & :=
\rho\mathbb {E} _{\0}\xi^2(\tilde{\0},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})   \\
 &+ \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left( \mathbb {E} _{\0,x}(\xi(\tilde{\0}, \tilde{\mathcal{P}}) \xi(\tilde{x}, \tilde{\mathcal{P}})) \rho^{(2)}(\0,x) - \rho^2\mathbb {E} _{\0}(\xi(\tilde{\0},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})) \mathbb {E} _{x}(\xi(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}))  \right) \mathrm{d} x \in [0, \infty). \nonumber 
\end{align}
 \end{enumerate}

body: [Lemma lem:sle4_cm of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Let $x, y \in (-\infty, 0)$ and $z \in (0, 1)$ be random points. Suppose that, conditionally on $z$, the law of the pair $(x,y)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $(-\infty,0)^2$. Given $x$, $y$, and $z$, let $\eta$ be a chordal SLE$_4$ curve in $\BH$ from $x$ to $y$. Then the law of the conformal modulus of the conformal rectangle $(\BH \setminus \eta; 0, z, 1, \infty)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure. [Theorem 30 (Compact-group variance inequality) of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group, let $\mu$ be Haar probability measure on $G$, and let
$U$ be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. Let
\[
\rho:G\to \End(U_\C)
\]
be the complexification of an orthogonal representation of $G$ on $U$.
For $T\in \End(U_\C)$ define
\[
\Phi(T)(g):=\langle T,\rho(g)\rangle_{\HS},
\qquad
\Psi(T):=\Phi(T)-\int_G \Phi(T)(h)\,d\mu(h).
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal C:=\{T\in \End(U_\C): \Phi(T)\text{ is constant on }G\}.
\]
Then
\[
\|\Psi(T)\|_{L^2(G,\mu)}^2
\ge
\frac{1}{\dim U}\,\| \mathrm{Proj}_{\mathcal C^\perp}T\|_{\HS}^2.
\]

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.15843, 'Long-time behaviour of DLRA for SDEs'] A probability measure $\pi^*$ on $V_r(\bb R^d)\times \bb R^r$ is called invariant probability measure of a process $(U_t,Y_t)_{t\ge 0}$, if $\al P^*_t \pi^* = \pi^*$ for all $t > 0$. Equivalently, for every bounded measurable functions $f:V_r(\bb R^d)\times \bb R^r\to\bb R$ satisfies 
			$$\pi^*(f)=  \pi^*\big( f(U_t,Y_t)\big) ,\quad \forall\,  t> 0,$$
        where $$\pi^*(f):=\int_{V_r(\bb R^d)\times \bb R^r} f(u,y)\,\pi^*(\rrm du,\rrm dy)$$ and $$\pi^*\big( f(U_t,Y_t)\big):=\bb E[f(U_t,Y_t)],$$ with $\scr L_{(U_0,Y_0)}=\pi^*$.
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2606.15843

body:
[Theorem THM62 of arXiv:2412.08886, 'On domination for (non-symmetric) Dirichlet forms'] Let $({\mathscr E},{\mathscr F})$ and $({\mathscr E}^M,{\mathscr F}^M)$ be given as above.  
A quasi-regular Dirichlet form $({\mathscr A},\mathcal{D}({\mathscr A}))$ on $L^2(E,m)$ is sandwiched between ${\mathscr E}$ and ${\mathscr E}^M$,  i.e.,  
\[
	{\mathscr E}^M\preceq {\mathscr A}\preceq {\mathscr E},
\]
if and only if there exists an MF $M'\in \text{MF}(X)$ with the properties 
\[
	E_M\subset E_{M'},\quad \nu_{M'}|_{E_M\times E_M}\leq \nu_M|_{E_M\times E_M}
\]
such that $({\mathscr A},\mathcal{D}({\mathscr A}))=({\mathscr E}^{M'},{\mathscr F}^{M'})$.
title: Theorem THM62 of arXiv:2412.08886

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Heat diffusion in $\mathbb R^N$ is described by the heat equation
$$\dot{\varphi}=\alpha\Delta\varphi$$
where $\alpha>0$ is the thermal diffusivity of the medium, and with $\Delta$ given by
$$\Delta\varphi=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{d^2\varphi}{dx_i^2}$$
being the Laplace operator, playing the role of a numeric second derivative.

body:
[Thm 3 of arXiv:2608.27880, 'Precise universal edge asymptotics for planar $\beta=2$ Coulomb gases with radial external'] Under the same assumptions as Theorem \ref{main}, we have the following asymptotic equivalences.

(1) Large deviations (fixed displacement). For any fixed $t>t_0$,
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl( \max_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i| \ge t \bigr)
\sim
\frac{\sqrt{\alpha} \,t_0 t^2}{\sqrt{2\pi n}(t^2-t_0^2)(tV'(t)-2)}
\exp(-nV(t)+nV(t_0))(\frac{t}{t_0})^{2n}.
\]

(2) Critical Gumbel scale and its refined correction.

(a) Pure Gumbel scale (fixed $t>1$):
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl( \max_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i| \ge t_0+\frac{t\sqrt{\widetilde{\gamma}_n}}{\sqrt{\alpha n}} \bigr)
\sim
t^{-2}(\frac{8\pi (\log n)^2}{\alpha n t_0^2 })^{\frac{t^2-1}{2}}.
\]

(b) Fine correction beyond the Gumbel scale ($1\ll v_n\ll \log n$):
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl( \max_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i| \ge t_0+\frac{\sqrt{\widetilde{\gamma}_n}}{\sqrt{\alpha n}}+\frac{v_n}{\sqrt{\alpha n \widetilde{\gamma}_n}} \bigr)
\sim
\exp\bigl(-v_n-\frac{v_n^2}{2\widetilde{\gamma}_n}\bigr).
\]

(3) Moderate deviations on scale $d_n$. Given $d_n>0$:
\[\aligned
&\quad\mathbb{P}\bigl(\max_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i| \ge t_0 + d_n \bigr)\\
&
\sim
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{t_0}{2\sqrt{2\pi \alpha n} \, d_n^2 }
\exp\bigl(-\frac{1}{2}\alpha n d_n^2\bigr), & \frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{\sqrt{n}} \ll d_n \ll n^{-\frac13},\\[1.2em]
\displaystyle \frac{t_0\exp(-n V(t_0+d_n)+nV(t_0))}{2\sqrt{2\pi \alpha n} \,  d_n^2 }
(\frac{t_0+d_n}{t_0})^{2n}, & n^{-\frac13}\lesssim d_n\ll 1.
\end{cases}
\endaligned\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition 13 (Rotation flattens \citep{suresh2017dme,chee2023quip,tseng2024quipsharp}) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Let $R$ be either Haar-distributed on the orthogonal group or a randomized Hadamard $R=HD$ with $D$ a diagonal of random signs (a \emph{deterministic} Hadamard does not give the guarantee for an arbitrary $w$; nor does an arbitrary random orthogonal $R$, for instance a random signed permutation, which leaves the crest factor untouched). Then for fixed $w$, the entries of $Rw$ are identically distributed and individually sub-Gaussian with proxy variance $\|w\|_2^2/d$ (dependent, not independent; the union bound needs only the marginals), so by \Cref{lem:subg} the expected crest factor of $Rw$ is at most $\sqrt{2\ln(2d)}=O(\sqrt{\log d})$ regardless of the outlier structure of $w$. A worst-case coherent $w$ (mass on one coordinate, $\mathrm{CF}=\sqrt d$) is thereby reduced to $\mathrm{CF}=O(\sqrt{\log d})$: a reduction by a factor of at least $\sqrt{d/(2\ln 2d)}$ in expectation.

[Lemma 5 (Monotonicity of the isoperimetric ratio) of arXiv:2608.26619, 'Uniqueness of Positively Curved Ancient Ricci Flows on Surfaces with Boundary'] Given a metric $(\old,\partial\bD ,g)$, define the isoperimetric ratio
    $$I(g) := \frac{L(\partial \bD,g)^2}{A(\old,g)}.$$
    Let $\{g(t) = u(\psi,t)g_0\}_{t\in [t_0,t_1]}$ be a positively curved rotationally symmetric solution to (\ref{2DRF}) with the initial condition $\partial_\psi u(\cdot,t_0),\; \partial_\psi R(\cdot,t_0) \geq 0$. Then we have
    $$\frac{d}{dt}I(g(t)) \leq 0,\; \forall t\in (t_0,t_1).$$

body: [Prop pro:NonexistenceSubcriticalBehavior of arXiv:2410.23859, 'Subcritical regimes in the Poisson Boolean percolation on Ahlfors regular spaces'] Let $(S,d,\mu)$ be an $s$-Ahlfors regular space. Let $\rho$ be a probability measure on $(0,\infty)$. Suppose that there exists a positive number $\beta > 0$ such that $\int_{0}^\infty R^{s+\beta}\rho(dR) = \infty$ holds. Then for all $\lambda > 0$ and $o \in S$, we have $\mathbb{E}_\lambda[M(o)^\beta] = \infty$.
title: Prop pro:NonexistenceSubcriticalBehavior of arXiv:2410.23859

body: In mathematics, Farkas' lemma is a solvability theorem for a finite system of linear inequalities. It was originally proven by the Hungarian mathematician Gyula Farkas. Farkas' lemma is the key result underpinning the linear programming duality and has played a central role in the development of mathematical optimization. Remarkably, in the area of the foundations of quantum theory, the lemma also underlies the complete set of Bell inequalities in the form of necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a local hidden-variable theory, given data from any specific set of measurements.
title: Farkas' lemma

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2506.10817, 'On the Weak Error for Local Stochastic Volatility Models'] Let $l \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $f$ be $l$-times weakly differentiable with all derivatives which are functions of polynomial growth. Let $u(t,x)=\E\bigl[ f\bigl(Y_T\bigr)\big|Y_t=x\bigr]$ and let $0\le 2i+j\le 4$. Then there is a constant $\tilde C$ and some $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $(t,x)\in[0,T)\times\R$,
    \begin{align*}
        \partial_t^i\partial_x^j u(t,x) &\le 
            \tilde C(T-t)^{-(2i+j-l)/2} \bigl(1+|x|^N\bigr).
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 12 (Entropic martingale identity) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] For $\Psi_t$ the running conditional log-CGF~\eqref{eq:exact-cgf}, the exponential martingale~\eqref{eq:doleans} has $\log \E_P[\cE_t(\lambda)] = 0$ for every $t \geq 0$, and for every $Q \ll P|_{\cF_t}$,
\begin{equation}
  \lambda\,\E_Q[Y_t] - \E_Q[\Psi_t(\lambda)]
    + \KL(Q\|Q^\star_t)
  = \KL(Q\|P|_{\cF_t}),
\end{equation}
where $\dd Q^\star_t/\dd P \propto \cE_t(\lambda)$ is the Gibbs tilt.
Dropping the nonnegative residual $\KL(Q\|Q^\star_t)$ gives the variational form $\sup_{Q\ll P|_{\cF_t}}\bigl\{\lambda\,\E_Q[Y_t] -
\E_Q[\Psi_t(\lambda)] - \KL(Q\|P|_{\cF_t})\bigr\} = 0$, attained at $Q^\star_t$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Entropic martingale identity

[Theorem 1 (Number of visited points) of arXiv:2606.11271, '\LARGE The $K$-th nearest neighbor random walk on a Poisson point process gets trapped'] Let $d \geq 1$ and suppose that Assumption (BS) is satisfied. Then there exist two constants $C_1, C_2 \in (0,+\infty)$ depending\footnote{In fact we obtain constants depending more precisely on $d$, $M$ and $\mu (\{M\})$.} on the dimension $d$ and on the probability distribution $\mu$ such that, for any integer $k \geq 1$,
$$
\P \big[ |\V| \geq k \big] \leq C_1 e^{-C_2 k} ~.
$$
In particular, the following equivalence holds for any $d \geq 1$: $Assumption \,\,(BS) \iff \V \mbox{ is a.s. finite}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Number of visited points

[Theorem 10 (Exact-regeneration rare-success theorem) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] For each $n$, let $0<\rho_n<1$, $q_n=1-\rho_n$, and let $C_n$ be any positive integer-valued ordinary coupon collector time with probability generating function $\phi_n$.  Define
\[
        s_n:=\phi_n(q_n)=\Ebb q_n^{C_n}.
\]
Assume
\begin{equation}
        s_n\to0,
        \qquad
        \rho_n q_n\phi_n'(q_n)\to0.
\end{equation}
Then
\[
        \rho_ns_nT_n\Rightarrow \Exp(1),
\]
and, for every fixed integer $r\ge1$,
\[
        \Ebb(\rho_ns_nT_n)^r\longrightarrow r!.
\]

[Theo 18 of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Let $u_\lambda\in H_0^1(\Omega)\cap C(\overline\Omega)$ be a non-negative
weak solution of \eqref{Eq1}, and let $G\subset\Omega$ be open. Assume
\begin{equation}
	-m(x)\geq q_0
	\qquad\text{for a.e. }x\in G
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
	0\leq u_\lambda(x)\leq\delta_{\lambda,q_0}
	\qquad\text{for every }x\in G.
\end{equation}
If $\lambda>0$, assume additionally that
$\|u_\lambda\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}<\delta_{\lambda,q_0}$.

For $x_0\in G$, set
\[
d_G(x_0)
:=
\operatorname{dist}(x_0,\partial G\setminus\partial\Omega),
\]
with $d_G(x_0)=+\infty$ if
$\partial G\setminus\partial\Omega=\emptyset$.
If
\begin{equation}
	d_G(x_0)
	\geq
	\psi_{1/N,q_0}
	\bigl(\|u_\lambda\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\bigr),
\end{equation}
then $u_\lambda(x_0)=0$. Consequently,
\[
\{u_\lambda>0\}\cap G
\subset
\left\{
x\in G:
d_G(x)<
\psi_{1/N,q_0}
\bigl(\|u_\lambda\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\bigr)
\right\},
\]
and therefore
\[
\operatorname{supp}u_\lambda\cap G
\subset
\left\{
x\in G:
d_G(x)\leq
\psi_{1/N,q_0}
\bigl(\|u_\lambda\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\bigr)
\right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

If I is a two-sided ideal of a ring R, the quotient ring R/I is the set of additive cosets r+I with operations (r+I)+(s+I)=(r+s)+I and (r+I)(s+I)=rs+I. The ideal conditions make both operations independent of representatives, and the multiplicative identity is 1_R+I.

body:
[Lemma 24 (Discrete local sewing) of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $\theta\in (0,1)$ and let $\Pcal=\{S = U_0<U_1<\ldots<U_N = T\}$ (with $N\in\Nsf$, $N\geq 2$) be a partition of the interval $[S,T]$ satisfying the following condition:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=($P_\theta$)]
	\item
		Whenever $s,t\in\llbracket 0,N\rrbracket$ satisfy $\llbracket s+1,t-1\rrbracket\neq \emptyset$, there exists $u\in\llbracket s+1,t-1\rrbracket$ such that 
            \[
                \omega_{s,u}\leq \theta \omega_{s,t}.
            \]
	\end{enumerate}
Let $K:\Delta\Pcal\to\Rsf^m$ be a function and denote 
	\[
		K_{s,t}:=K(U_s,U_t), \quad (s,t)\in\Delta\llbracket 0,N\rrbracket.
	\]
Assume that the following condition is satisfied:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=($K$)]
	\item
		It holds that $K_{s,s}=0$ for all $s\in\llbracket 0,N\rrbracket$ and $K_{s,s+1}=0$ for all $s\in \llbracket 0,N-1\rrbracket$. Additionally, there exist $C,M\in (0,\infty)$ such that the estimate
	\[
		| K_{s,t} - K_{s,u} - K_{u,t}| \leq C |K_{s,u}|\,\omega_{u,t}^\frac{1}{p} + M\omega_{s,t}^\frac{3}{p}
	\]
holds for every $(s,u,t)\in\llbracket 0,N\rrbracket^3$ satisfying $s\leq u\leq t$ and $\omega_{s,t}\leq 1$.
	\end{enumerate}
Then there exist $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $L\in (0,\infty)$ such that the estimate
	\[
		|K_{s,t}| \leq L M \omega_{s,t}^\frac{3}{p}
	\]
holds for every $s,t\in\Delta\llbracket 0,N\rrbracket$ satisfying $\omega_{s,t}<\delta$. Constant $\delta$ depends only on $p$, $\theta$, and $C$ while constant $L$ depends only on $\theta$ and $p$.
title: Discrete local sewing

[Proposition prop-radial-forested-zipper of arXiv:2605.03385, 'Quantum Loewner evolution in quantum natural time: phases and Markov properties'] Suppose $\kappa \in (4, 8)$ and $\gamma = \frac4{\sqrt\kappa} \in (\sqrt2,2)$. Let $\ell_0 > 0$. Sample $(\mathcal{D}_0,\eta)$
    from the measure 
    \[
    (\mathrm{LF}_{\mathbb{D}, f, \ell_0}^{(Q-\frac{\gamma}{4},0),(\frac4\gamma - \frac\gamma2,1)})^\#\times \mathrm{raSLE}_\kappa
    \]
    and parametrize {$\eta$} by its quantum natural time; let $\mathcal{S}$ be its duration. For $s \in [0, \mathcal{S})$, let $\mathcal{D}_s$ be the forested quantum surface obtained from $\mathcal{D}_0$ by cutting along $\eta$ for quantum natural time $s$. Almost surely $\mathcal{S} < \infty$. Moreover, for all $s \in [0,\mathcal{S})$ the generalized boundary length of $\mathcal{D}_s$ is $\ell_0 + 2s$, and for fixed $s > 0$, conditioned on $\{s < \mathcal{S}\}$ the conditional law of $\mathcal{D}_s$ is $(\mathrm{LF}_{\mathbb{D}, f, \ell_0+2s}^{(Q-\frac{\gamma}{4},0),(\frac4\gamma - \frac\gamma2,1)})^\#$.

[Defn $q$-integer and criticality of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] The $q$-integer is defined for any $m \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ by:
\[
[m]_q := \frac{q^m - q^{-m}}{q - q^{-1}}.
\]
We say that a pair $(n, p)$ is \emph{critical} if
\[
[n - 2p + 1]_q = 0 \quad \text{or equivalently,} \quad q^{2(n - 2p + 1)} = 1.
\]
Critical pairs correspond to values of $q$ for which the Gram determinant may vanish.

[Lemma 4 (Uniform random-target bounds) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] There is an absolute constant $C_{\rm K}<\infty$ such that the following
estimates hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\eps=\eps(n)\to0$ and $\eps^3n\to\infty$, and $H_{\rm ER}$
denotes the giant component of $G(n,(1+\eps)/n)$, then, with high probability,
\[
        \Kemeny(H_{\rm ER})\le C_{\rm K} n .
\]
\item For every fixed $\lambda>1$, let $\mathcal C_1$ denote the giant component of
$G(n,\lambda/n)$. Then, with high probability,
\[
        \Kemeny(\mathcal C_1)\le C_{\rm K} n .
\]
\end{enumerate}
The same constant $C_{\rm K}$ works in both estimates; in particular it is
independent of the fixed value of $\lambda>1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:stealthiness-criterion of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $(P_z)_{z\in Z}$ be a Borel $\Gamma$-equivariant uniformly
Delone family, and let $Y_P$ be the associated cross-section.
Suppose that there are $\rho>0$ and an open neighborhood
$\Omega$ of the origin such that
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{P_z}
    =
    \rho\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }\Omega
\]
for $\nu$-almost every $z$, in the sense of tempered
distributions. Then the associated cross-section system has intensity $\rho$.
Moreover, for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ satisfying
\[
    \operatorname{supp}\widehat f\subset\Omega,
\]
one has
\[
    N_f^{Y_P}(x)
    =
    \rho\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\,d\lambda_d
\]
for $\mu_{\Gamma,Z}$-almost every $x$. Consequently,
\[
    \sigma_{Y_P,\mu_{\Gamma,Z}}(\Omega)=0.
\]
In particular, the cross-section system is stealthy.

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Associated to any real probability measure $\mu=\mu_f$ is the following modification of the logarithm of the Fourier transform $F_\mu(\xi)=E(e^{i\xi f})$,
$$K_\mu(\xi)=\log E(e^{\xi f})$$
called cumulant-generating function. The Taylor coefficients $k_n(\mu)$ of this series, given by
$$K_\mu(\xi)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty k_n(\mu)\,\frac{\xi^n}{n!}$$
are called cumulants of the measure $\mu$. We also use the notations $k_f,K_f$ for these cumulants and their generating series, where $f$ is a variable following the law $\mu$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the criterion reproduces the source's worked example, and every algebraic step was confirmed symbolically] Problem 3.3 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240), asks for the optimal universal C>0 such that mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for every t>=C D_mu^2 and every compactly supported probability measure mu. Here D_mu=sup{|x-y|: x,y in supp(mu)}, S(0,t) is the centered semicircle law of variance t, and boxplus is additive free convolution. The source proves C<=4. The record answers C=1. Sufficiency is the proved bound that mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for all t>=D_mu^2. Optimality is the source's Example 2.1: mu=(delta_{-1}+delta_1)/2, with D_mu=2, is not unimodal for any t<4=D_mu^2. Let t*(mu) be the least t_0 such that mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for every t>=t_0. Then t*(mu)<=D_mu^2, and equality holds for every symmetric two-point law (equal weights at two points) by Example 2.1 and scaling. The record further claims (Corollary) that equality holds only for symmetric two-point laws. That direction rests on the record's unproved assertion that t*(mu)=D_mu^2 requires a separating local minimum of value exactly 1/D_mu^2, a limiting step not written out. It is retained here as a claim, not certified. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
D_mu>0.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Reduce to the stabilisability threshold and examine the known bounds. Result: By Fey-Meester-Redig, an i.i.d. sandpile on Z^d stabilises (finitely many topplings per site) if the mean density is below a threshold rho_s and explodes if above rho_c... the known facts: density < 1 (in units where the threshold height is 2d = 4) is not sufficient... on Z^2 the results are: if E s < 2d - 1 = 3?? I recall: on Z^d, i.i.d. sandpiles with density rho < d stabilise? and with rho > 2d - 1 explode; the exact threshold for i.i.d. Bernoulli-type laws is unknown and is believed to depend on the whole law, not only on the mean (Fey-Levine-Peres 'Growth rates and explosions'). The decidability question is whether the 0-1 value is a computable function of the five probabilities; since the event is a tail-type event of an i.i.d. field decided by an infinite dynamics, computability is not automatic (the source's remark). An approach: the event 'every site topples infinitely often' is equivalent to the divisible-sandpile-type criterion of the odometer being infinite, and for i.i.d. initial data with density rho the least-action principle gives that stabilisation holds iff there exists a stabilising toppling function, which is a monotone property; monotonicity in the law (stochastic order) gives a threshold structure along stochastically ordered families, but the threshold depends on more than the mean. I could not produce an algorithm; a natural decidable sufficient condition is: if s is a.s. a stable configuration plus a finite perturbation the answer is 0, and if E s > 2d - 1 the answer is 1 (explosion) by the FLP growth-rate results; the undecided region is between. Recorded with the two rigorous outer bounds. Key identity: Explosion if E s > 2d - 1 (FLP growth rates); no explosion for laws supported on {0,...,2d-1} minus finite perturbations; the middle region is the question. Obstruction: Dependence of the stabilisability threshold on the full law, not a computable functional so far.

Let 
\[
\operatorname{Std}(u)=(u_{0},u_{1},\dots,u_{l})
\]
be the standard path from $u(z)$ to $u(zq)$. Then there exists $0\leq l'\leq l$
such that
\[
u_{1},\dots,u_{l'}\in\mathcal{F}^{n}\qquad\text{and}\qquad u_{l'},\dots,u_{l}\in\mathcal{F}^{n+1}.
\]
In other words, if $u_{i}\notin\mathcal{F}^{n+1}$ and $u_{i'}\notin\mathcal{F}^{n}$,
then $i+1<i'$.

[Defini 13 of arXiv:2608.27934, 'An example of biquandle and an invariant of long virtual knots defined through it'] Let $\mathcal{EO}$ be a set of long virtual knots each of which admits a long virtual knot diagram without EU crossings. 
For a long virtual knot diagram $D$, set ${\rm EO}(D)$ to be a long virtual knot diagram obtained by performing crossing changes at each EU crossing. 
It can be checked that ${\rm EO}(D)$ and ${\rm EO}(D')$ are related by generalized Reidemeister moves if two long virtual knot diagrams $D$ and $D'$ are related by generalized Reidemeister moves. 
Thus we can define ${\rm EO}(K) \in \mathcal{EO}$ for a long virtual knot $K$ as the long virtual knot represented by ${\rm EO}(D)$, where $D$ is a long virtual knot diagram representing $K$. 
This ${\rm EO}$ is a projection from the set of long virtual knots to $\mathcal{EO}$. 
Moreover, this ${\rm EO}$ preserves the products. In other words, ${\rm EO}(K_{1} \cdot K_{2})={\rm EO}(K_{1})\cdot {\rm EO}(K_{2})$ holds for long virtual knots $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$.

[Definition Olas5d of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let \(\mathcal{X}\) be a Polish space equipped with its Borel \(\sigma\)-algebra \(\sigma(\mathcal{X})\).  
	An {(ergodic) measurable random dynamical system} on \((\mathcal{X}, \sigma(\mathcal{X}))\) consists of an (ergodic) measurable metric dynamical system \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P}, \theta)\) together with a measurable function
	\[
	\Phi : \mathbb{R}^+ \times \mathcal{X} \times \Omega \to \mathcal{X},
	\]
	satisfying the {cocycle property}.  
	More specifically, for each \((t, x, \omega) \in \mathbb{R}^+ \times \mathcal{X} \times \Omega\), set \(\Phi^t_\omega(x) := \Phi(t,x,\omega)\).  
	Then the following conditions hold:
	\[
	\Phi^0_\omega = \operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal{X}} \quad \text{for all } \omega \in \Omega,
	\]
	and
	\[
	\Phi^{t+s}_\omega(x) = \Phi^s_{\theta_t \omega}\big(\Phi^t_\omega(x)\big),
	\]
	for all \(s, t \in \mathbb{R}^+\), \(x \in \mathcal{X}\), and \(\omega \in \Omega\).  
	The function \(\Phi\) is called a \emph{cocycle}.  
	Given the condition that, for each \(\omega \in \Omega\), the map \((t, x) \mapsto \Phi(t, x, \omega)\) is continuous, the function \(\Phi\) is called a {continuous random dynamical system}.  
	Moreover, for \(k \geq 1\), we call \(\Phi\) a {\(C^k\)-random dynamical system} if for every \(t \geq 0\) and \(\omega \in \Omega\), the function
	\[
	x \mapsto \Phi^t_\omega(x)
	\]
	is \(C^k\)-Fr\'{e}chet differentiable.
title: Definition Olas5d of arXiv:2603.12774

[Theorem 9 (Boundary of the limit distribution) of arXiv:2606.07290, 'Boundary behaviour of the Volterra square-root process'] Assume that the Volterra square-root process is subcritical. Then the limit distribution $\pi_{x_0}$ satisfies the following:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] Suppose that $K \in C^1(\R_+)$. Then for each $0 < p < \gamma_-(\infty)$
        \[
            \frac{1}{\theta(\infty)^{p}} \frac{\Gamma( \gamma_+(\infty) - p)}{\Gamma(\gamma_+(\infty))} \leq \int_{\R_+} x^{-p}\, \pi_{x_0}(\mathrm{d}x) \leq \frac{\Gamma(\gamma_{-}(\infty) - p)}{\Gamma(\gamma_{-}(\infty))} \frac{1}{\theta(\infty)^{p}}.
        \]
        where 
        \[
            \gamma_-(\infty) = \frac{2(x_0 L_0(\infty) + b)}{\sigma^2 K(0)}, \quad \gamma_+(\infty) = \frac{L_0(0) - \beta}{L_0(\infty) - \beta} \gamma_-(\infty), \quad \theta(\infty) = \frac{\sigma^2 K(0)^2}{2 (L_0(0) - \beta)}.
        \]
        If $p \geq \gamma_+(\infty)$, then $\int_{\R_+} x^{-p}\pi(\mathrm{d}x) = \infty$.
        \item[(b)] If $K$ is regulary varying at zero, i.e.\ of the form~\eqref{eq: regularly varying}, then
        \[
            \lim_{t \to \infty}\P[X_t=0] = \pi_{x_0}(\{0\}) > 0. 
        \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Boundary of the limit distribution

Let g:R^d->R be convex and continuously differentiable, and suppose its gradient is globally L-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm for some L>0. Define B_g(x,y)=g(x)-g(y)-<grad g(y),x-y>. For all x,y, ||grad g(x)-grad g(y)||^2/(2L)<=B_g(x,y)<=L||x-y||^2/2. Adding the lower inequality in the two orders gives the Baillon--Haddad cocoercivity inequality <grad g(x)-grad g(y),x-y> >=||grad g(x)-grad g(y)||^2/L. No strong convexity is assumed. Source: Liu--Zhou, Lemma 3.6, which attributes the Bregman bounds to Nesterov.

[Proposition 29 (R\'enyi spectrum of anticipation) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Taking the single factor $\Pi=\Amart{\tau}$ in the path-space partition function of Theorem~\ref{thm:pathspace} gives the anticipation cumulant $\Phi_T(\alpha)=\log Z_T(\alpha)=\log\E[(\Amart{\tau}_T)^\alpha]$, convex in $\alpha$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:grad}), with
\[
  \Phi_T(1)=0,\qquad \Phi_T(0)=\log P(\Amart{\tau}_T>0)\le0,\qquad
  \Phi_T'(1)=\E[\Amart{\tau}_T\log \Amart{\tau}_T]=\KL(Q_A\|P|_{\cF_T}),\quad \tfrac{\dd Q_A}{\dd P}:=\Amart{\tau}_T,
\]
the last the total marginal anticipation of $\tau$ in nats.
Here $\Phi_T\equiv0$ iff $\Amart{\tau}\equiv1$, i.e.\ $\tau$ is a stopping or pseudo-stopping time (Section~\ref{sec:survival}).
More generally $\Phi_T$ is affine exactly when $\Amart{\tau}_T=\ind_B/P(B)$ for some event $B$ with $P(B)>0$ --- the all-or-nothing peek,
of which $P(B)=1$ is the case $\Amart{\tau}\equiv1$ above --- and is strictly convex otherwise.
A fuller classification of the intermediate anticipation classes by the form of $\Phi_T$ lies beyond the present scope. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: R\'enyi spectrum of anticipation

[Proposition of arXiv:2607.14332, '\textbf{ Dimers, filters, and $q$-deformed real numbers}'] For all $n>0$,
$${\bf r}_n (q)= 
\left\{ \begin{array}{ll}
{\bf r}_{n'} (q) \, U(q) & \mbox{if $n$ is even,} \\
{\bf r}_{n'} (q) \, L(q) & \mbox{if $n$ is odd}
\end{array} \right.$$
so that 
${\bf r}_n (q) = {\bf r} \: T_{m-1} \cdots T_1 \, T_0$
(note that we exclude $T_m$).

[Lemm 22 of arXiv:2609.03188, 'Some generalizations of Oort's conjecture'] Let $c\in\mathbb F_{p^2}^\times$ satisfy $c^{p+1}=1$, and set $z=\diag([c],\ldots,[c],[c^p],\ldots,[c^p])$, where each of $[c]$ and $[c^p]$ occurs $g$ times.
Let $j=zu^+$ for some $u^+\in\J^1\cap P_J^+$, where $J=\tS\setminus\{s_0,s_g\}$, and let $yI\in G(\bQp)/I$ be a point fixed by $j$.
Let $s\in\{s_0,s_g\}$.
Then there exist $a\in\overline{\mathbb F}_p$ and $\epsilon\in\{\pm1\}$ such that
$$
jyu(x)sI=yu(c^{2\epsilon}x+a)sI.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemm 22 of arXiv:2609.03188

body:
[Theorem thm:Russo of arXiv:2607.14993, 'Sharp phase transition for percolation with short-range dependencies'] Let $\Omega = \{0, 1\}^E$ with $E$ at most countable and, for $p \in [0, 1]^E$, let $\mathbb P_p$ be the product probability measure on $\Omega$ such that for all $e \in E$ we have $\mathbb P_p(\omega(e) = 1) = p_e$. Then, if $A$ is an increasing event and~$e\in E$,
  \begin{equation}
    \partial_{p_e} \mathbb P_p(A) = \mathbb P_p(e \text{ pivotal for } A)
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Russo's formula

body:
[Lemma lem:steepest_descent_curves of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] Let~$(x,y)\in R\subset \mathcal D_c^\circ$ and assume that~$(x,y)$ lies in a phase region.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If~$(x,y)$ is in the frozen, quasi-frozen, or smooth region, and~$\zeta_0\in A_{(x,y)}$ is a local minimum (resp. maximum), there exists a simple curve $C_{\zeta_0,\mathrm{desc}}^+\subset \Sigma_+$ (resp. $C_{\zeta_0,\mathrm{asc}}^+\subset \Sigma_+$) going between~$\zeta_0$ and~$A_{R,+}$ (resp. $A_{R,-}$), such that~$\Im\int_{\zeta_0}^\zeta\lambda_c(x,y)=0$ and~$\Re\int_{\zeta_0}^\zeta\lambda_c(x,y)$ is decreasing (resp. increasing) along the curve.
\item If~$(x,y) \in \mathcal L$ and~$\zeta_0=\Omega(x,y)\in \Sigma_+^{\circ}$, there exists a simple curve~$C_{\zeta_0,\mathrm{desc}}^+\subset \Sigma_+$ (resp. $C_{\zeta_0,\mathrm{asc}}^+\subset \Sigma_+$) with both endpoints in \(A_{R,+}\) (resp. \(A_{R,-}\)), passing through \(\zeta_0\), such that~$\Im\int_{\zeta_0}^\zeta\lambda_c(x,y)=0$ and~$\Re\int_{\zeta_0}^\zeta\lambda_c(x,y)$ is decreasing (resp. increasing) along the curve as we move away from $\zeta_0$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if \(\zeta_0\in A_{(x,y)}\) is a local minimum and \(\zeta_0'\in A_{(x,y)}\) is a local maximum, then
\[
C_{\zeta_0,\mathrm{desc}}^+\cap C_{\zeta_0',\mathrm{asc}}^+=\varnothing.
\]

If instead~$(x,y) \in \mathcal L$ and~\(\zeta_0=\Omega(x,y)\in \Sigma_+^\circ\), then
\[
C_{\zeta_0,\mathrm{desc}}^+\cap C_{\zeta_0,\mathrm{asc}}^+=\{\zeta_0\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:steepest_descent_curves of arXiv:2605.03896

body:
[Theorem 12 ({\cite[Theorem~6.1,\,6.2) of arXiv:2609.01965, 'A logarithmic Bogomolov--Sommese vanishing theorem on compact K\"ahler manifolds'] {DP10}}]
    Let $X$ be a compact connected K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n\geq2$, $\omega$ be a smooth K\"ahler form and $\Omega^n$ be a smooth volume form.
    Consider also $\sigma_j\in H^0(X,E_j)$, $\tau_r\in H^0(X,F_r)$, $j=1,\ldots,N$, $r=1,\ldots,M$ 
    be non-identically zero holomorphic sections of some holomorphic vector bundles over $X$,  such that the integral condition
    \begin{equation}
        \int_X\prod_{j=1}^N|\sigma_j|^{2l_j}\prod_{r=1}^{M}|\tau_r|^{-2h_r}\Omega^n=\int_X\omega^n
    \end{equation}
    holds for certain real numbers $l_j\geq0,h_r\geq0$.
    Then there exists a unique solution $\varphi$ of the degenerate complex Monge–Amp\`ere equation
    \begin{equation}
        (\omega+\ddbar\varphi)^n=e^{\lambda\varphi}\prod_{j=1}^N|\sigma_j|^{2l_j}\prod_{r=1}^{M}|\tau_r|^{-2h_r}\Omega^n, \quad \lambda\geq0,
    \end{equation}
    which in the case $\lambda=0$ is normalized by $\sup_X\varphi=0$.
    Consider the complex analytic sets
    $$S_1:=\bigcup_r\{\tau_r=0\}, \quad S_2=S_1\cup \left(\bigcup_j \{\sigma_j=0\}\right). $$
    Then $\varphi\in C^0(X)\cap C^{1,1}(X\setminus S_1) \cap C^{\infty}(X\setminus S_2)$.
    In particular, $\varphi\in L^\infty(X)$.
    
    Moreover, denote $f=\prod_{j=1}^N|\sigma_j|^{2l_j}\prod_{r=1}^{M}|\tau_r|^{-2h_r}$.
    For $\delta>0$ satisfying $f\in L\log^{n+\delta}L(X)$,
    the solution $\varphi$ satisfies
    \begin{equation}
        \|\varphi\|_{L^\infty(X)}\leq C(\delta,\omega,\Omega^n)I_{\omega,\delta}(f)^{\frac{n}{\delta}}+1,
    \end{equation}
    where 
    $$I_{\omega,\delta}(f):=\{\omega\}^{-n}\int_Xf\log^{n+\delta}(e+\{\omega\}^{-n}f)\Omega^n.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
For events A, B with positive probability, P(A | B) = P(B | A) P(A) / P(B). With a partition {A_i}, P(A_i | B) = P(B | A_i) P(A_i) / sum_j P(B | A_j) P(A_j). It inverts conditioning: posterior proportional to likelihood times prior.

Diagnostic corollary: let D be the disease event and T a positive-test event, with 0 < pi = P(D) < 1. Set s = P(T|D), q = P(T|D^c), and assume s*pi + q*(1-pi) > 0. Then P(T) = s*pi + q*(1-pi) and P(D|T) = s*pi/[s*pi + q*(1-pi)]. Thus sensitivity s alone does not determine the posterior in general: for s=9/10 and q=1/10, prevalence pi=1/2 gives posterior 9/10, whereas pi=1/100 gives posterior 1/12.

[Defn of arXiv:2411.10633, 'A Geometric Perspective on the Injective Norm of Sums of Random Tensors'] Let $T \in (\mathbb R^d)^{\otimes r}$ be a tensor. We define the \emph{symmetric embedding} of $T$ to be the $rd$-dimensional order $r$ tensor $\sym(T) \in (\mathbb R^{rd})^{\otimes r}$ characterized by
    $$ \sym(T)[v_1, \ldots, v_r] \coloneqq \sum_{ \tau \in S_r} T[ v_{\tau(1)}^{[1]}, \ldots, v_{\tau(r)}^{[r]}].$$
    (Here $v_{\tau(q)}^{[q]}$ denotes the $q$-th piece of the vector $v_{\tau(q)}$.)

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2606.11271, '\LARGE The $K$-th nearest neighbor random walk on a Poisson point process gets trapped'] There exists a constant $\kappa_8(d) > 0$ such that the following holds.
Let $S$ be an infinite and locally finite subset of $\R^d$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For all $x_0 \in \R^d$ such that $x_0 \not \in S$,
\[
\big|\{x \in S : x_0 \in B(x,r_M(x,S))\}| \le M\kappa_8(d).
\]
\item 
Let $S_f$ be a finite subset of $S$.
Let $(r(x))_{x \in S_f}$ be a family of non-negative real numbers such that, for all $x \in S_f$, $r(x) \le r_M(x,S)$.
Then 
\[
\cL^d\left(\bigcup_{x \in S_f} B(x,r(x))\right) \ge \frac 1 {M\kappa_8(d)} \sum_{x \in S_f} \cL^d(B(x,r(x))).
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma 22 of arXiv:2606.11271

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:scale_profile_remainders}
Fix \(n\ge1\), \(s\ge0\), and \(\phi\in[-\pi/2,\pi/2]\).
Let \(H_{n,j}\) be the remainders defined in \cref{prop:renewal}. Define \(\psi_1,\psi_2,\dots\) recursively by
\[
\psi_1(r):=s\Delta_{\op} e^{s\Delta_{\op}}\min\left\{1,\frac{Lr}{\Delta_{\op}}\right\},
\]
and, for \(j\ge2\),
\[
\psi_j(r):=e^{s\Delta_{\op}}\psi_{j-1}((1-\kappa)r)
+s\Delta_{\op} e^{s\Delta_{\op}}\min\left\{1,\frac{Lr}{\Delta_{\op}}\right\}\psi_{j-1}((1-\kappa)D).
\]
Then, \(\psi_j\) $(1\le j \le n)$ is increasing and concave, and \(\psi_j\) controls the increments of \(H_{n,j}\).

[Dfn plentiful of arXiv:2411.07609, 'Activated Random Walks on $\bZ$ with Critical Particle Density'] We say that $\omega_{\text{initial}} \in \{0,1,2,\dots\}^{\{ - k^{n+1}, \dots , k^{n+1} \}}$ is {\bf\texttt{plentiful}}\ if, for every $j \in \{1, 2, \dots, (k-1)/\gamma \}$, the following inequalities hold:
$$\sum_{i = k^n+(j-1) \gamma k^n +1}^{k^n+ j \gamma k^n} \omega_{\text{initial}}(i) \geq \gamma k^n (\rho_* + 2\delta)$$ and $$\sum_{i = k^n+(j-1) \gamma k^n +1}^{k^n+ j \gamma k^n} \omega_{\text{initial}}(-i) \geq \gamma k^n (\rho_* + 2\delta).$$

[Theorem thm:q-refining-recipe of arXiv:2604.05941, 'Banach spaces of continuous paths with finite $p$-th variation'] Let $q\ge2$, let $\mathbb P$ be a dense $q$-refining partition sequence, and let $\phi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ be the associated increasing homeomorphism from Proposition~(prop:q-refining-homeomorphism of the paper), so that
    \[
        \mathbb P^n=\phi^{-1}(\mathbb{T}_q^n),\qquad n\ge0.
    \]
    Let $H:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and non-decreasing with $H(0)=0$, and set
    \[
        h:=H\circ\phi^{-1}.
    \]
    Suppose that $h\in C^1([0,1])$ and that $\big[(h')^{1/p}\big]_{\mathbb{T}_q}^{(p)}\equiv 0$ for some $p>1$. Then there exists a path $y\in V_\mathbb P^p$ such that
    \[
        [y]_\mathbb P^{(p)}(t)=H(t),\qquad t\in[0,1].
    \]
    Moreover, if $(h')^{1/p}\in C^\alpha([0,1])$ for some $\alpha \in (0, 1/p]$, and if
    $\phi\in C^\beta([0,1])$ for some $\beta\in(0,1]$, then the constructed path
    $y$ belongs to $C^{\alpha\beta}([0,1])\cap V_\mathbb P^p$.

[Lemma l.incphi of arXiv:2510.07682, 'From tug-of-war to Brownian Boost: \\ explicit ODE solutions for player-funded stochastic-'] Suppose that $(\kappa,\rho) \in (0,1] \times (0,\infty)$.  
\begin{enumerate}
 \item Each of $\phi_0$ and $\phi_1$ satisfies
$$
 \lim_{\beta \searrow 0} \phi(\kappa,\rho,\beta) = 0 \, \, \, \, \textrm{and} \, \, \, \, 
 \lim_{\beta \nearrow \infty} \phi(\kappa,\rho,\beta) = \infty  \, ,
$$
where in the case $\kappa =1$, we also suppose that $\rho \leq 1$. 
 \item  If $\rho^2 \kappa \leq 1$, then  $(0,\infty) \to (0,\infty):\beta \to \phi_i(\kappa,\rho,\beta)$ is an increasing bijection  for $i \in \{0,1\}$. 
 \item  If  $\kappa \rho < 1 + \sqrt{1-\kappa^2}$,  then $\phi_0(\kappa,\rho,\beta) >  \phi_1(\kappa,\rho,\beta)$. In particular, this holds when $\rho^2 \kappa \leq 1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Cor 12 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon\ge0$, 
and for $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, 
the mapping
$(\lambda,\mu)\mapsto S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)[\epsilon]$,
is continuous with respect to the Hausdorff metric $d_H$.

\begin{proof}
Fix $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon\ge0$ and $\delta'>0$. By Lemma~\ref{l:S.star.cts.dH}, there exists $\delta>0$ such that if 
$(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda$ and 
$(\lambda',\mu')\in B_\delta(\lambda,\mu)$, then the sets
\begin{align*}
K&\equiv S_\star(\lambda,\mu;\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\,,\\
K'&\equiv S_\star(\lambda',\mu';\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)
\end{align*}
lie within Hausdorff distance $\delta'$ of one another.
For any $\hat{\YY}\in K[\epsilon]$, there exists $\YY\in K$ with
$\|\hat{\YY}-\YY\|_2\le\epsilon$, and then there exists $\YY'\in K'$ with
$\|\YY-\YY'\|_2\le\delta'$. By Lemma~\ref{l:D.mu.continuity.w}, 
since $\hat{\YY}\in\cD_\mu$,
there exists $\tilde{\YY}\in\cD_{\mu'}$
with $\|\hat{\YY}-\tilde{\YY}\|_1\le\delta/\iota^2$. Then
	\[
	\|\tilde{\YY}-\YY'\|_2
	\le\|\tilde{\YY}-\hat{\YY}\|_2
	+ \|\hat{\YY} - \YY\|_2
	+ \|\YY - \YY'\|_2
	\le \epsilon + \delta' + \frac{\delta}{\iota^2}
	\le \epsilon + 2\delta'\,,
	\]
where the last inequality can be arranged by taking $\delta$ small enough (depending on $\delta'$).
Since $\YY'$ and $\tilde{\YY}$ both lie in $\cD_{\mu'}$, it follows by convexity of $\cD_{\mu'}$ that $\tilde{\YY}$ lies within distance
$2\delta'$ of a vector $\hat{\YY}' \in K'[\epsilon]$. We then finally have
	\[
	\|\hat{\YY}-\hat{\YY}'\|_2
	\le \|\hat{\YY}-\tilde{\YY}\|_2
		+ \|\tilde{\YY}-\hat{\YY}'\|_2
	\le\frac{\delta}{\iota^2} + 2\delta'
	\le 3\delta'\,.
	\]
This implies that $K[\epsilon]$ and $K'[\epsilon]$ lie within Hausdorff distance $3\delta'$ of one another, and the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:kappasize of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] There are absolute constants $c_0,C_0>0$ such that
\[
 c_0r\leq\kappa_r\leq C_0r\qquad(r\geq2).
\]
Consequently
\[
 K_h:=\sum_{r=2}^h\kappa_r\asymp h^2.
\]
More precisely, using the real-variable functions $\delta$ and $w$ just
defined, put
\[
 \Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\delta(x)\leq1,
 \ \min_i x_i<0<\max_i x_i\},
 \qquad I=\int_\Omega w(x)\,dx.
\]
Then $0<I<\infty$ and
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\ K_h\sim\frac{I}{2\zeta(3)}h^2.\ }
\end{equation}
Writing $\mathfrak K:=I/(2\zeta(3))>0$, one has
$K_h\sim\mathfrak K h^2$.

[Theorem lem:convergenceRateAccMin of arXiv:2609.03094, 'Discrete Gromov--Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing'] Fix $\eta'>0$ and assume that $\|\tilde \nabla \ell(u)-\nabla \ell(u)\|\leq \eta'$ for each $u\in\mathbb B_{R_0}$. Then, we may set $L=\max\left\{1,\frac{\lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal}\mathrm{B}_0)}{\lambda_{\min}(\mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}\mathrm{B}_1)+\varepsilon}-1\right\}$ in (algo:outer-loop-accelerated of the paper) and
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
        \item If $\ell$ is convex and $u^{\star}$ minimizes $\ell$,\footnote{This is the case if, for instance, $\varepsilon\geq \lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal}\mathrm{B}_0)-\lambda_{\min}(\mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}\mathrm{B}_1)$, see (prop:LipschitzContinuityGradient of the paper).} the iterates $u_j$ of (algo:outer-loop-accelerated of the paper) satisfy  
        \[
        \min_{j=1}^{J}\|{2L}\left(u_{j}-z_j\right)\|^2\le \frac{96L^2}{J(J+1)(J+2)}\|s_0-u^{\star}\|^2 + 16LR_0\eta'.
        \]
    \item If $\ell$ is nonconvex and $L'$ is a Lipschitz constant of $\nabla(\ell-\frac 12 \|\cdot \|^2)$, e.g., $L'=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal}\mathrm{B}_0)}{\lambda_{\min}(\mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}\mathrm{B}_1)+\varepsilon}$,

    \]

[Proposition prop:IPS:entropy-change:in-terms-of-asynchronous of arXiv:2605.16904, 'Positive-rate PCA and IPS with stationary Bernoulli measures are rapidly forgetful \footno'] Let $\Phi$ be an IPS with a strictly positive local transition rule $\varphi\colon\Sigma^N\times\Sigma\to(0,1)$ and clock rate~$1$, and let $\lambda$ be a full-support probability measure that is stationary under~$\Phi$.  Let $\mu$ be a probability measure and $J\Subset\mathbb{Z}^d$.
	Let $\mu^t\coloneqq\mu\Phi^t$ and $D_J(t)\coloneqq D_J(\mu^t\relto\lambda)$.
	Then, $D_J(t)$ is differentiable at every $t>0$ and
	\begin{equation}
		\dot{D}_J(t) =
			\abs{J}\Big(
				D_J\big(\mu^t\widehat{\Phi}_J \relto[\big] \lambda \big)
				-
				D_J\big(\mu^t\widehat{\Phi}_J \relto[\big] \mu^t \big)
				-
				D_J(\mu^t \relto \lambda)
			\Big) \;.

	\end{equation}
title: Entropy change in terms of asynchronous updating

body:
[Theorem thmIPS of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let  the input process to the interacting particle system be 

\begin{equation}
\tilde{\mathcal{P}} = \left\{(x, M(x),  \tilde{\tau}_x)\in\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb {M}  \times \hat{\mathcal{N}}_{[0,t_0] \times \mathbb{L}}\right\}, 
\end{equation}

where $ \tilde{\tau}_x$ are i.i.d. and independently marked Poisson clocks, which are also independent of sites and initial states, i.e., independent of $\sum_x \delta_{(x,M(x))}$.
Assume that:
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item 
$\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ has {\em summable exponential $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations}, as in Definition~(def.A2 of the paper), and has  uniformly bounded correlation functions under reduced Palm distributions, i.e., for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists a constant $\hat{\kappa}_p$ such that for all $m \in \mathbb{N}$,
\begin{equation}

\sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_p \in \mathbb{R}^d} \sup_{y_1,\ldots,y_m \in \mathbb{R}^d} \rho^{(m)}_{\bk x1p}(\bk y1m) \leq (\hat{\kappa}_p)^m,
\end{equation}
where $\rho^{(m)}_{\bk x1p}$ denotes the $m$-th order correlation function of $\mathcal{P}$ under its reduced Palm distribution $\mathbb{P}^!_{\bk x1p}$.

\item  {\em An admissible update rule} given by a measurable function $\Phi$ as in~(equation e:updaterulef of the paper) acts on a {\em stabilizing interaction graph} $\Psi$ (on finite windows) with respect to $\mathcal{P}$, such that the interaction range satisfies the decay assumption~(equation e:ddecay of the paper).
\item  A {\em score function} $\xi = \xi^{(h, \Phi, \Psi)}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_n) := h(M_n[x])$ defined in~(equation xiU of the paper), satisfies the {\em $p$-moment condition}~(equation momh of the paper) for all $p \in [1, \infty)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the sequence of random measures $(\mu_n^{\xi})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ defined in~(equation IPS of the paper) satisfies the central limit theorem. That is, for every  $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$ such that
$
{\rm Var}[\mu_n^{\xi}(f)] = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$,
we have
$$
({\rm Var}[\mu_n^{\xi}(f)])^{-1/2} \big(\mu_n^{\xi}(f) - \mathbb {E} [\mu_n^{\xi}(f)]\big)  \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z,$$
where $Z$ is a standard Gaussian random variable. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
