body:
[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2608.27450, 'Koszul duality and Morita categories'] Let $\sA$, $\sB$, and $\sC$ be stable presentable categories, and let $\sQ$, $\sR$, and $\sS$ be strongly positive coalgebras in the categories $\SSeqnu(\sA,\sA)$, $\SSeqnu(\sB, \sB)$ and $\SSeqnu(\sC, \sC)$ respectively.
    Suppose we are given bicomodules
    \[
    M \in \BcoMod_{(\sS, \sR)}(\SSeqnu(\sB, \sC)) \quad \text{and} \quad N \in \BcoMod_{(\sR, \sQ)}(\SSeqnu(\sA, \sB)).
    \]
    Then the limit defining the relative cobar construction $M \Box_{\sR} N$ is an $(n-1)$-skeletal totalization in arity $n$ for every $n \geq 1$.
    It follows that for every stable presentable category $\sD$, both composition functors
    \[
    \SSeqnu(\sA, \sC) \times \SSeqnu(\sD, \sA) \to \SSeqnu(\sD, \sC) \quad \text{and} \quad \SSeqnu(\sC, \sD) \times \SSeqnu(\sA, \sC)  \to \SSeqnu(\sA, \sD)
    \]
    preserve the limit defining the relative cobar construction $M \Box_{\sR} N$.

body:
Recall that a real function g on a topological space Z is of BAIRE CLASS ONE if it is the pointwise limit of a sequence of continuous real functions on Z. THEOREM (Baire for R x R; Rudin in this generality): let X be a METRIC space, let Y be a topological space (in particular a metric space), and let f: X x Y -> R be SEPARATELY CONTINUOUS, i.e. for each fixed y the map x -> f(x,y) is continuous on X and for each fixed x the map y -> f(x,y) is continuous on Y. Then f is of Baire class one on X x Y: there is a sequence of continuous functions f_n: X x Y -> R with f_n(x,y) -> f(x,y) for every (x,y). CONSEQUENCE (Baire's theorem on functions of the first class): if in addition X x Y is a Baire space - for instance if X and Y are both complete metric, or both locally compact Hausdorff - then the set of points at which f is JOINTLY continuous is a dense G_delta subset of X x Y, and its complement is meagre. So a separately continuous function is jointly continuous at 'most' points, in the sense of category. CLASSICAL EXTENSION: a function of n variables that is separately continuous in each variable is of Baire class n - 1 (Lebesgue); the case n = 2 is the theorem above. SHARP EDGES. (a) Separate continuity does NOT give joint continuity: f(x,y) = xy/(x^2 + y^2) with f(0,0) = 0 is separately continuous on R^2, indeed continuous on each line through the origin, and is discontinuous at the origin (it equals 1/2 on the diagonal). The theorem therefore cannot be strengthened to continuity anywhere in particular, only to a residual set of continuity points. (b) The metric structure of the first factor is essential to the proof, which builds a locally finite partition of unity on X; for arbitrary topological factors the statement requires extra hypotheses and should not be quoted in that generality. (c) The consequence about continuity points needs X x Y to be a Baire space; on a non-Baire domain 'dense G_delta' carries no information, and the conclusion is vacuous. (d) Baire class one is a statement about POINTWISE limits; it gives no uniform convergence, and the limit functions f_n constructed in the proof are not monotone in n. (e) The converse is false and is not being claimed: plenty of Baire class one functions on a product are not separately continuous.

Y is a topological space (metric suffices, and is the usual case)
f: X x Y -> R is separately continuous: continuous in each variable with the other held fixed
for the residual-set-of-continuity-points consequence, X x Y is a Baire space (e.g. X, Y complete metric)

[Lemma 34 (Rotational invariance for conformal martingales) of arXiv:2604.09365, 'Cotlar martingale transforms and related singular integrals'] Let $Z_t=X_t+iY_t$ be a conformal martingale on the Brownian filtration.   
Then for every $\theta\in\R$ and every $t\ge0$,
\[
X_t\cos\theta+Y_t\sin\theta \ \stackrel{d}{=} \ X_t,
\]
and consequently, for $1<p<\infty$,
\[
\|X\cos\theta+Y\sin\theta\|_p=\|X\|_p.
\]

Let (X, Y) be a jointly Gaussian random vector in R^a x R^b with means mu_X, mu_Y and covariance blocks A = Cov(X), B = Cov(X, Y), C = Cov(Y), so its covariance matrix is M = [[A, B], [B^T, C]], possibly singular; A^+ is the Moore-Penrose inverse, and a value x is compatible when x - mu_X lies in the range of A (the support of X). For every compatible x, the support of the conditional law of Y given X = x is an affine subspace of dimension rank K = rank M - rank A, where K = C - B^T A^+ B; it does not depend on x.

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $B$ be a compact metric space and let $\pi: E \to B$ be a 
Lipschitz vector bundle of dimension $d$ over $B$. 
Let $G$ be a locally compact group acting on $E$ by an isometric Lipschitz bundle action. 
Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
For any continuous section $s: B \to E$, define the operator $P_\mu$ by
\begin{align*}
P_{\mu} s (b) = \int_{G}  g^{-1} s (g b) \mu(dg), \quad b \in B. 
\end{align*}
Then $P_{\mu} s: B \to E$ is again a continuous section, and the operator $P_{\mu}$ is bounded on $\bf \Gamma^{0}(E)$. 

Assume furthermore that there exists a constant $\alpha >0$ such that $\bb E ({\rm Lip}_E(g_1)^{\alpha} ) < \infty$. 
Then, for any $\gamma \in (0, \alpha)$, 
the operator $P_{\mu}$ is bounded on $\bf \Gamma^{\gamma}(E)$. 
Moreover, if $(G, \mu)$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B} on $B$,
then for any $\gamma \in (0, \min \{ \delta, \alpha \})$, 
the operator $P_{\mu}$ has essential spectral radius strictly less than $1$ on $\bf \Gamma^{\gamma}(E)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2607.19873

[Defn 6 of arXiv:2605.25762, 'Brownian Convergence of Planar Domains and Stability of the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Pro'] The Hilbert transform of a real valued $2\pi$- periodic function
$f$ is defined by 
\[
H\{f\}(x):=PV\left\{ \frac{1}{2\pi}\int^{\pi}_{-\pi}f(x-t)\cot(\frac{t}{2})dt\right\} =\lim_{\eta\rightarrow0}\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\eta\leq|t|\leq\pi}f(x-t)\cot(\frac{t}{2})dt
\]
where $PV$ denotes the Cauchy principal value. The Hilbert transform
does exist a.e whenever $p\geq1$. However, it is a bounded operator
on $L^{p}_{2\pi}$ only when $p>1$. The case $p=1$ is irregular,
and $H$ becomes unbounded. For all proofs and properties of the Hilbert
transform, we refer the reader to \cite{butzer1971hilbert,king2009hilbert}.

denote $[W^u(a)]$ the cycle  corresponding  to $W^u(a)$, viewed an element in  $H_1(\Sigma,\mathbb{Z})$.
Assume $g=(g_a)_{a\in \mathsf{Crit}_1(f) }$ is a regular point of \[\left\{ \mathsf{Hol}_{\partial\mathcal S}(g)=1_G \right\}\]

Given two elements $(v_a)_{a\in \mathsf{Crit}_1(f)}$ and $(w_a)_{a\in \mathsf{Crit}_1(f)}$ in $\mathfrak{g}^{2\mathsf{genus}(\Sigma)}$ that we can identify with elements in the tangent space $T_{(g_a)_{a\in \mathsf{Crit}_1(f)}}\mathcal{M}_g$, the symplectic form writes:

\end{equation*}
where the quantity $\big[W^u(a)\big]\cap \big[W^u(b)\big] \in \mathbb{Z} $ is the oriented intersection number of the two cycles $[W^u(a)]$ and  $ [W^u(b)]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let lambda be the security parameter and let lambda<=n(lambda)<=poly(lambda). Start with a binary secret-key zero-bit PRC: polynomial-time KeyGen, randomized Enc and Dec, uniformly negligible false acceptance of every fixed key-independent input, and computational indistinguishability against probabilistic polynomial-time oracle adversaries of fresh encodings under one fixed key from fresh independent uniform n-bit strings. There exist absolute constants C0,Crob>=1 such that the following holds. Fix0<p0<1/(10*Crob), and assume the base code is robust to every(1/2-p0)-substitution-bounded channel: for each randomized channel C satisfying d_H(x,C(x))<=(1/2-p0)*n almost surely for every x, decoding the corrupted fresh encoding accepts except with negligible probability in lambda, averaged over key, encoder, channel and decoder coins. Fix an integer rho>=C0/p0. Put q=rho*n and m=ceil(n*ln2). The new secret key is(k,psi), where k is the base key and psi:[q]->[n] is an independent uniform map with exactly rho preimages per label. To encode, draw b from the base encoder, draw U uniformly from[n]^m, and let S0={i:b_i=1},S1=Unique(U). If |S0 minus S1|>=|S1 minus S0|, choose a uniform injection from S1 minus S0 into S0 minus S1 and relabel its domain in U by its image. Otherwise choose a uniform injection tau:S0 minus S1->S1 minus S0 and replace each occurrence of tau(a) by a. Call the result Y, and independently lift each Y_j to a uniform Z_j in psi^{-1}(Y_j). Decode any received q-ary word w by applying the base decoder to the binary occupancy vector D_psi(w), whose ith bit is1 iff some symbol of w maps to i. This is a zero-bit PRC on[q] with block length m<=n. It is robust to every polynomial-time sampleable channel E that, for every input x, changes x by a total of at most(1-Crob*p0)*|x| insertions, deletions and substitutions almost surely. The channel receives the input word, not the secret balanced map. This is the zero-bit, fixed integer-rho implementation of Theorem4.1.
Binary secret-key zero-bit PRC with repeated-encoding oracle security, soundness and the stated substitution robustness; lambda<=n<=poly(lambda).
Fixed p0>0 below1/(10*Crob); fixed integer rho>=C0/p0. All fresh encoder and lift coins are independent.
Uniform balanced psi is secret and independent of the base key. Edit channels are efficiently sampleable and see the word alone.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.01996, 'Baumslag--Solitar Subgroups Obstruct Model Companions for Fields with Group Actions'] Let \(\pi:\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow Q\) be a surjective group homomorphism and let \(K\) be a \(Q\)-field.
  Let \(K_\pi\) denote the \(\Gamma\)-field with the same underlying field and action
  \[
    \gamma\cdot a:=\pi(\gamma)(a).
  \]
  Then:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item \(K\) is \(\aleph_0\)-saturated as a \(Q\)-field if and only if \(K_\pi\) is \(\aleph_0\)-saturated as a \(\Gamma\)-field;
    \item \(K\) is p.e.c. as a \(Q\)-field if and only if \(K_\pi\) is existentially closed in every regular \(\Gamma\)-field extension of \(K_\pi\) on which \(\ker(\pi)\) acts trivially.
  \end{enumerate}

[Proposition 25 (Pointwise detection of the weak logarithmic scale) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Fix \(0<p<2\), \(r\geq1\), and set
\[
 \varphi_{p,r}(N)
 :=N^{-1/p}\bigl(\log(e+N)\bigr)^{(r-1)/p}.
\]
For a compact \(T\), the following are equivalent:
\begin{align}
 s_N(T)&=O(\varphi_{p,r}(N)),\\
 \mathcal N_T(R)&=O(e^{pR}(1+R)^{r-1}),\\
 \mathfrak F_T(a)&=O(a^p(\log(e+a))^{r-1}).
 
\end{align}
The same equivalence holds with every \(O\) replaced by \(o\).
Thus the positive determinant detects both the weak and little
logarithmic ideals, even when no asymptotic equivalent exists.

[Lemma 20 (Antidiagonal orthogonality for links) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Let $(K_k)_{k\ge0}$ and $(L_\ell)_{\ell\ge0}$ be finite-rank operators of
the shapes in \eqref{eq:link-definition}.  Suppose that the initial
projections
\[
 q_k:=\supp(K_k^*K_k)\in\cL(X)
\]
are pairwise orthogonal and that the terminal projections
\[
 p_\ell:=\supp(L_\ell L_\ell^*)\in\cL(Y)
\]
are pairwise orthogonal.  Set
\[
 T_{k,\ell}:=\operatorname{Link}_Z(L_\ell,K_k),
 \qquad
 U_j:=\sum_{k+\ell=j}T_{k,\ell}.
\]
Then, for every $j\ge0$, the nonzero singular values of $U_j$, counted with
multiplicity, are the disjoint union
\begin{equation}

 s(U_j)=\bigsqcup_{k+\ell=j}s(T_{k,\ell}).
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{align}
 \norm{U_j}_{\Sch_p}^p
 &=\sum_{k+\ell=j}\norm{T_{k,\ell}}_{\Sch_p}^p,
 &&1\le p<\infty,
 \notag\\
 \norm{U_j}_{\Sch_\infty}
 &=\max_{k+\ell=j}\norm{T_{k,\ell}}_{\Sch_\infty}.
 
\end{align}

[Definition 21 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Given an equilibrium measure $\boldsymbol{\mu}$, we will use the following terminology for each $h \in [H]$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[$\bullet$] A \emph{void} is a maximal (for the inclusion) and closed interval in $[\hat{a}'_h,\hat{b}'_h]$ where
$\mu_h(x) =0$.
\item[$\bullet$] A \emph{saturation} is a maximal closed interval in
$[\hat{a}'_h,\hat{b}'_h]$ where $\mu_h(x) = \frac{1}{\theta_{h,h}}$.
\item[$\bullet$] A \emph{band} is a maximal open interval in $[\hat a'_h,\hat b'_h]$ where $0<\mu_h(x)<\frac{1}{\theta_{h,h}}$.
\end{itemize}
We denote by $\amsmathbb{V}_{h}$ (respectively $\amsmathbb{S}_{h}$, $\amsmathbb{B}_{h}$) the union of voids (respectively saturations, bands) in $[\hat{a}'_{h},\hat{b}'_{h}]$. If we speak of a \emph{saturated segment} (respectively, a \emph{void segment}), we mean a segment included in a saturation (respectively, in a void) but not necessarily maximal.

[Proposition 13 (Stagewise perturbation margins) of arXiv:2608.22334, 'Recovering Weighted Tangent Geometry from a Single-Scale Score Field'] Let $\eta$ bound the recovered moments through order $K$, and write
$\gamma_K(\Lambda)=\lambda_{\min}^{+}(T_K)$.  Correct branch count is
guaranteed whenever
\begin{equation}
 \eta<\eta_{\rm count}:=\frac{\gamma_K(\Lambda)}{2(K+1)}.
 
\end{equation}
Conditional on that count, an angular tolerance $a_0$ is guaranteed if
the Rouch\'e inequality in \eqref{eq:rouche} with
$r\leq\sin(a_0/2)$ holds, and a weight tolerance follows from the
Vandermonde inequality in \eqref{eq:weightbound}.  Full geometric recovery
therefore has sufficient rank, root, and weight margins, whereas count uses
only the rank margin.  Replacing the geometry-dependent quantities by declared
class-level lower bounds turns these perturbation statements into uniform
certificates. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

In the spiked covariance model with noise level $\sigma^2$ and ratio $\gamma = p/n$, let $\hat\lambda$ be a sample eigenvalue lying above the bulk edge, $\ell := \hat\lambda / \sigma^2 > (1 + \sqrt{\gamma})^2$. Then the unique $\theta > \sqrt{\gamma}$ with $(1 + \theta)(1 + \gamma/\theta) = \ell$ is $$\hat\theta = \tfrac{1}{2}\Big( (\ell - 1 - \gamma) + \sqrt{(\ell - 1 - \gamma)^2 - 4\gamma} \Big),$$ and $\sigma^2 (1 + \hat\theta)$ is the consistent estimate of the population eigenvalue behind $\hat\lambda$. The discriminant is nonnegative exactly when $\ell \ge (1 + \sqrt{\gamma})^2$, so the formula is defined precisely for eigenvalues at or above the edge. The population value $\sigma^2(1 + \hat\theta)$ is always strictly less than $\hat\lambda$ (a sample spike is debiased downward), by the amount $\sigma^2 \gamma (1 + 1/\hat\theta)$.

Suppose that a vertex $v$ in $\mathcal{N}_{t}$, of type $c(v)$, carries $j$ marks at time $t$.

[Theorem thm:gen-frag-pos-recurrent of arXiv:2511.10223, 'Stochastic Reaction Networks Within Interacting Compartments with Content-Dependent Fragme'] Let $N$ be the coarse-grained model associated to (equation eq:general-content-dependent-fragmentation of the paper):
\begin{equation*}
\begin{tikzcd}
    \mathcal I_\mathcal K & &
    0\arrow[yshift=.5ex]{r}{\kappa_I}& C\arrow[yshift=-.5ex]{l}{\kappa_E} \arrow[yshift=.5ex]{r}{\kappa_FS_C}& 2C\arrow[yshift=-.5ex]{l}{\kappa_C} & &
    \mu.
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathcal A$ denote the generator of the associated chemistry $\mathcal I_\mathcal K$. Suppose there exists a linear function $f:\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d\to\mathbb R$ of the form $f(x)=w\cdot x$ for some $w\in\mathbb R_{>0}^d$, such that $\sup_x\mathcal Af(x)<\infty$, 
and that condition~(con:lambda finite of the paper) holds; that is, $\lambda<\infty$.
If $\kappa_C>0$ and $\kappa_E>0$, then the state with no compartments is positive recurrent for $N$, all states reachable from it are also positive recurrent for $N$, and all other states are transient with finite expected time to reach the set of positive recurrent states.

\begin{remark}
    If $f$ were a Lyapunov function witnessing (via Corollary (cor:lyapunov-positive-recurrence of the paper)) that $\mathcal I_\mathcal K$ was positive recurrent, we would have $\mathcal Af(x)\le-1$ outside some finite set. Similarly, if $f$ were witnessing that $\mathcal I_\mathcal K$ was recurrent, we would have $\mathcal Af(x)\le0$ outside some finite set. Either of these conditions would imply the assumption $\sup_x\mathcal Af(x)<\infty$ from the theorem. 
    
    The assumption $\sup_x\mathcal Af(x)<\infty$ is in fact \emph{strictly} weaker than having a Lyapunov function for recurrence, as we will see in Corollary (cor:spec-frag-pos-recurrent of the paper), when we apply it with the transient chemistry $0\to S$. However, the assumption $\sup_x\mathcal Af(x)<\infty$ is stronger than having a Lyapunov function for non-explosivity. Indeed, if $\sup_x\mathcal Af(x)<\infty$ and $f\to\infty$, then a suitable shift $g$ of $f$ will satisfy $\mathcal Ag(x)\le g(x)$.\hfill $\triangle$
\end{remark}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem (thm:gen-frag-pos-recurrent of the paper)]

Let $V(n)=C(n)+\alpha\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d} n_x (w\cdot x)$, for some constant $\alpha>0$ to be chosen later. 
The assumption that every coordinate of $w$ is strictly positive means that $V\to\infty$ in the sense of Corollary~(cor:lyapunov-positive-recurrence of the paper). 
Our goal is to show that $\mathcal L V(n)\le -1$ outside a finite set of states, which will then allow us to conclude positive recurrence via Corollary~(cor:lyapunov-positive-recurrence of the paper).

We next compute $\mathcal L V(n)$, the generator of $V$, and bound its growth term by term.
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal LV(n)
    &=\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d} \bigg[ \kappa_FS(x)n_x+\kappa_I\mu(x)(1+\alpha w\cdot x)+\alpha\sum_{\nu\to\nu'}n_x\lambda_{\nu\to\nu'}(x)\big(w\cdot(x+\nu'-\nu)-w\cdot x\big)\\
    &\quad\quad-\kappa_En_x(1+\alpha w\cdot x)-\kappa_C\binom{n_x}2-\mathop{\sum_{y\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d}}_{y\ne x}\kappa_C\frac{n_xn_y}2\bigg]\\
    &=\bigg(\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d} \kappa_FS(x)n_x-\alpha\kappa_En_x(w\cdot x)+\kappa_I\mu(x)(1+\alpha w\cdot x)+\alpha n_x\mathcal Af(x)\bigg)\\
    &\quad-\kappa_C\binom{C(n)}2-\kappa_EC(n)\\
    &\le-\kappa_C\binom{C(n)}2+\left(\alpha\sup_x\mathcal Af(x)-\kappa_E\right)C(n)+(\kappa_Fw_S^{-1}-\alpha\kappa_E)\bigg(\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^d}n_x(w\cdot x)\bigg)\\
    &\qquad+\kappa_I+\alpha\kappa_I(\max_j w_j)\lambda.
\end{align*}
Pick $\alpha$ large enough that $\alpha\kappa_E>\kappa_Fw_S^{-1}$ (here we used $\kappa_E>0$). Then we claim this upper bound is at most $-1$ outside a finite set of $n$. Indeed, the term $(\kappa_Fw_S^{-1}-\alpha\kappa_E)\left(\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^d}n_x(w\cdot x)\right)$ is non-positive by the choice of $\alpha$, so $\mathcal LV(n)$ is at most a polynomial in $C(n)$ (with no dependence on $n$ other than through $C(n)$) with negative leading term (here we used $\kappa_C>0$). So for large enough values of $C(n)$ we hav (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 2 (Calabi symmetry) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] A Kähler metric $g$ on $M^0 = \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}$ (with respect to the standard complex structure) has \emph{Calabi symmetry}, or $\mathrm{U}(n)$\emph{-symmetry}, if its Kähler form is
	
	\begin{equation}
		\omega \;=\; \sqrt{-1}\, \partial \bar{\partial}\, u(\rho), \qquad \rho = \log \|z\|^2 ,
	\end{equation}
	
	for a smooth function $u$ of $\rho$ alone satisfying
	
	\[
	u_{\rho} > 0, \qquad u_{\rho\rho} > 0 ,
	\]
	
	which are exactly the conditions for positivity of $\omega$.
title: Calabi symmetry

D_{m}({\rm e}_{j_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes{\rm e}_{j_{n}})\triangleq\begin{cases}

\]

\[
\bar\rho_d:=\frac1d\sum_{i=1}^d\rho_i.

\begin{equation}

\frac1d
\left\|(UDU^\top)_{\diag}-\bar\rho_d I_d\right\|_F^2

[Definition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] We say $\mathfrak{F} = (W, \sqsubset)$ is a \emph{Kripke frame (k-frame)} if $W$ is a non-empty set and $\sqsubset$ is a binary relation on $W$,
  and $\mathfrak{M} = (\mathfrak{F}, V)$ is a \emph{Kripke model (k-model)} if $\mathfrak{F}$ is a k-frame and $V: \mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}} \to \mathcal{P}(W)$.
  Such $\mathfrak{M}$ is said to be \emph{based on} $\mathfrak{F}$.
  For $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \sqsubset, V)$, we define a \emph{satisfaction relation} $\Vdash_\mathfrak{M}$ on $W \times \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ by:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item $x \nVdash_\mathfrak{M} \bot$
    \item $x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} p \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} x \in V(p)$
    \item $x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \land \psi_2 \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} (x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \mathrel{\text{\&}} x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2)$
    \item $x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \lor \psi_2 \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} (x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \mathrel{\text{or}} x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2)$
    \item $x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \to \psi_2 \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} (x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_1 \mathrel{\Rightarrow} x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \psi_2)$
    \item $x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \forall y \sqsupset x \, (y \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
    \item $x \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \varphi \mathrel{\;\ratio\Longleftrightarrow\;} \exists y \sqsupset x\, (y \Vdash_\mathfrak{M} \varphi)$
  \end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:Haar of arXiv:2609.00336, 'Critical points of point charge potentials along lines'] Let $p>0$, $\{(a_j,|b_j|)\}_{j=1,\ldots,N} \subset \mathbb{R}\times[0,+\infty)$ pairwise distinct, and set
		\[
		R_j(x)=(x-a_j)^2+b_j^2.
		\]
		Then, any nonzero linear combination of the $2N$ functions
		\begin{equation}
			R_j(x)^{-(p+2)/2},\qquad
			(x-a_j)R_j(x)^{-(p+2)/2},\qquad j=1,\ldots,N,
		\end{equation}
		has at most $2N-1$ distinct zeroes in $D=\mathbb{R}\backslash\{a_j \ | \ b_j=0\}$. In particular, when all $b_j>0$, the functions in (equation eq:Haar-family of the paper) form a Haar system on $\mathbb{R}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (S, d) be a metric space and \mu_n, \mu be probability measures on S. S is a metric space

Fix N>=1 data points, output dimension K>=1, real offsets b_i in R^K, and fixed matrices G_ij in R^(m by n). Define h(D)=N^(-1) sum_i ell_i(b_i+(<G_ij,D>)_(j=1..K)), where each ell_i:R^K->R is convex, nonnegative and twice continuously differentiable. This is the exact affine/NTK model, not an error bound for a nonlinear network. Let lambda>=0 and suppose h(D)+lambda||D||_* has a global minimizer. Let r>=1 satisfy r(r+1)/2>KN. For U in R^(m by r), V in R^(n by r), Q=[U;V], and P in S_+^(m+n), set F_P(U,V)=h(UV^T)+(lambda/2)(||U||_F^2+||V||_F^2)+<P,QQ^T>. For Lebesgue-almost every nonzero P in the full PSD cone (with ambient symmetric-matrix Lebesgue measure), every second-order stationary point of F_P is a global minimizer of F_P. The same almost-sure conclusion holds for any perturbation law absolutely continuous with respect to that measure, including laws supported in an arbitrarily small PSD ball. The conclusion does not cover deterministic P=0, a measure supported on a lower-dimensional face, or finite-iteration convergence of GD.

[Lem local expansion from Green function of arXiv:2603.27144, 'On the critical fugacity of the hard-core model on regular bipartite graphs'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be

walk $\boldsymbol{W}_{0},\dots,\boldsymbol{W}_{M_{0}-1}$ started

Then $G$ satisfies the local expansion property with parameters $C_{\mathrm{LE}}=C_{0}$
and $M_{\mathrm{LE}}=M_{0}$, by taking $\boldsymbol{T}$ to be the trace
of the walk $\boldsymbol{W}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Before a harmonic fluctuation calculation can support a low-temperature Riesz crystal argument, the chosen lattice must have a nonnegative displacement Hessian in the relevant directions. Force balance alone is insufficient, as the density-one simple cubic lattice has a finite-support negative second variation for every s>3. Even a valid finite infrared fluctuation integral in dimension three leaves the nonlinear control of defects, competing phases and a symmetry-breaking infinite-volume Gibbs limit open. This is a proof-route guard, not a solution of P0309.
Classical three-dimensional continuum Riesz crystal proof route
Reference to the counterexample at s>3 only
title: Stability prerequisite for a Riesz crystal harmonic expansion

[Thm conditional-rank-one-bound of arXiv:2607.21428, 'Subcritical percolation and network archaeology on random recursive tree substrate network'] Assume the rank-one comparison setup satisfies the edge bound, the
		maximum-weight bound, and the susceptibility bound.  Then, for every
		\(r>0\), there is \(C_r<\infty\) such that, for every \(L\geqslant0\), every
		\(t>0\), and all sufficiently large \(n\),
		\begin{equation}
			
			\mathbb P\left(
			\max_{\mathcal{D}:\,\mathcal{D}\cap[L]=\varnothing}w(\mathcal{D})>t
			\right)
			\leqslant
			C_r t^{-r}\sum_{i>L}w_{n,i}^r.
		\end{equation}
		In particular, if, for a fixed \(L\) with \(L+1\leqslant N_n\) eventually and
		some \(r_L>0\),
		\[
		\sum_{i>L}
		\left(\frac{w_{n,i}}{w_{n,L+1}}\right)^{r_L}
		\leqslant C_L
		\qquad\text{for all large }n,
		\]
		then
		\[
		\max_{\mathcal{D}:\,\mathcal{D}\cap[L]=\varnothing}w(\mathcal{D})
		=O_{\mathbb P}(w_{n,L+1}).
		\]
		Finally, suppose the weights are random.  Assume there are events \(E_n\),
		measurable with respect to the weights, with \(\mathbb P(E_n)\to1\), such that on
		\(E_n\), conditional on the realized weights, the deterministic rank-one
		comparison setup above holds with the same constants \(p,\beta,\nu\) and with
		a deterministic error sequence \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) in the edge bound.  If,
		for some \(r>1/p\),
		\begin{equation}
			
			\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
			\mathbb P\left(
			n^{-pr}\sum_{i>L}w_{n,i}^r>\varepsilon
			\right)=0
			\qquad\text{for every }\varepsilon>0.
		\end{equation}
		then
		\[
		\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
		\mathbb P\left(
		n^{-p}
		\max_{\mathcal{D}:\,\mathcal{D}\cap[L]=\varnothing}w(\mathcal{D})>\varepsilon
		\right)=0
		\]
		for every \(\varepsilon>0\).

body:
[Defn contFV of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] For $\alpha>0$, an \emph{$\alpha$-good potential} is a
    function $V:\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$,  $(h,\varphi)\mapsto V_h(\varphi)$ 
    which is twice continuously differentiable 
    
    with 
    \[
        \sup_{\substack{|h|\le C \\ \varphi\in\mathbb{R}}}
        \left| \frac\partial{\partial h} V_h'(\varphi)\right| < \infty
    \]
    for all $C>0$ and $V_h''(\varphi)\in[\alpha,\alpha^{-1}]$
    for all $h,\varphi\in\mathbb{R}$ (where  $V_h'$ and $V_h''$ are the first and
     second  derivatives of $V_h$ with respect to $\varphi$). In other words, this family of potential
    functions is smooth and uniformly strongly convex with Lipschitz
    gradient, and furthermore $V_h'$ is Lipschitz in $h$. For
    $\text{\boldmath $h$}\in\mathbb{R}^N$, we define the potential

    \begin{align*}
V_\text{\boldmath $h$}(\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}):=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{h_i}(\varphi_i)\, .
\end{align*}

    Given an $\alpha$-good potential $V$ and
    a weighted graph $G=(\text{\boldmath $B$},\text{\boldmath $h$})$ on $[N]$ with $\text{\boldmath $B$}\succ-\alpha\text{\boldmath $I$}$,
    we consider the Gibbs measure on $\mathbb{R}^N$ with base measure
    $e^{-V_\text{\boldmath $h$}(\text{\boldmath $\varphi$})}{\rm d}\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}$ and quadratic Hamiltonian
    $-\frac12\<\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}, \text{\boldmath $B$}\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}\>$ and denote its free energy density
    by

    \begin{align*}
F_V(G)=F_V(\text{\boldmath $B$},\text{\boldmath $h$})=\frac1N \log \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \exp\left( -\frac12
\<\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}, \text{\boldmath $B$}\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}\> \right) e^{-V_\text{\boldmath $h$}(\text{\boldmath $\varphi$})} {\rm d}\text{\boldmath $\varphi$}.
\end{align*}
title: Defn contFV of arXiv:2608.06500

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2608.20252, '2608.20252'] Under $\P_{\nu^N_{\rho_0(\cdot)}}$, the distribution of $\eta_t$ is the inhomogeneous product of Poisson measures $\prod_{x\in \T_N^d} \kappa_{\psi_{N,t}(x)}$ where

body:
[Thm 4 of arXiv:2605.28776, 'Limiting distributions of triangle counts in linear preferential attachment models'] The dominating term in the centered-edge decomposition of $T_n$, as in~\eqref{term:central0}--\eqref{term:central3}, is of fluctuation order 
 \begin{enumeratei}
 \item $\sqrt{\log n}$ and is given by $T_{n}^{(3)}$ when $\delta>0$,
 \item $(\log n)^2$ and is given by $\Delta_{n}$ when $\delta=0$,
 \item $n^{-\delta/(2m+\delta)}\log n$ and is also given by $\Delta_{n}$ when $\delta\in (-m,0)$.
 \end{enumeratei} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 4 of arXiv:2605.28776

body:
[Definition def:languages-formulas of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}}$ be the set of all propositional variables, and let:
  \begin{align*}
    \mathscr{L}_p  &= \mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}} \cup \set{ \land, \lor, \to, \bot },
      & \mathscr{L}_\Box &= \mathscr{L}_p \cup \set{ \Box }, \\
    \mathscr{L}_\Diamond &= \mathscr{L}_p \cup \set{ \Diamond },
      & \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}  &= \mathscr{L}_p \cup \set{ \Box, \Diamond },
  \end{align*}
  where $\bot$ is nullary, $\Box, \Diamond$ are unary, and $\land, \lor, \to$ are binary.
  We use $\top$ and $\neg \varphi$ as abbreviations for $\bot \to \bot$ and $\varphi \to \bot$, respectively.
  The formulas of each language are built from $\mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}}$ and $\bot$ in the usual inductive way using these connectives.
  For a language $\mathscr{L}$, by abuse of notation, we also write $\mathscr{L}$ for the set of all formulas in $\mathscr{L}$.
title: Definition def:languages-formulas of arXiv:2608.29708

[Lem l:4.10 of arXiv:2602.21277, 'A Limit in Law for the Cover Time and Last Visited Vertex of Wired Planar Domains'] If $\gamma$ is small enough, then, given any $0 < \eta' < \eta < \tfrac{1}{2}$ small enough (depending only on $\gamma$), for each $u \geq 0$, $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $k \geq 1$ there exists a probability measure ${\rm O}^{k,\epsilon}_u$ on $\mathbb{R}^{{\rm Q}(k)}$  such that 
\begin{equation}
\lim_{k \to \infty} \left[ \sup_{z \in \mathcal Z^{\eta'}_k[\mathcal T_k] }\Bigg\| \frac{{\rm d} {\rm M}^{k,\epsilon}_{u}(z,\cdot)}{{\rm d} {\rm O}_{u}^{k,\epsilon}} - 1 \Bigg\|_\infty\right]=0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem l:4.10 of arXiv:2602.21277

[Lemma app-L-1 of arXiv:2608.30548, 'Finite speed of propagation and waiting time phenomena for stochastic porous media equatio'] Let $ 1 \le r \le \infty$, $0< q <p$, $ m \in \mathbb{N}_+$
such that
\[
\frac 1r - \frac mN < \frac 1p \,.
\]
If $\mathcal{O} \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is bounded with piecewise smooth boundary,
then positive constants $c_1$ and $ c_2$ depending only on $\mathcal{O},
r, p, m$ and $q$ exist such that for any $u \in L^q (\mathcal{O})$
satisfying $ D^m u \in L^r (\mathcal{O})$, the following inequality holds:
\begin{equation}
\| u \|_p \le c_1 \|D^m u\|^a_r \| u \|^{1-a}_q + c_2 \| u \|_q

\end{equation}
where $a = \frac{\frac 1q - \frac 1p}{\frac 1q + \frac m N - \frac
1r}$.

Especially, if $\mathcal{O}=\mathbb{R}^N$,  then ((eq-GN of the paper)) holds
with constant $c_1=c(r,p,m,q)$ and $c_2=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma app-L-1 of arXiv:2608.30548

body: [Lemma 7 of arXiv:2512.10761, 'Special times for the point set process of the Brownian Net'] Almost surely a point $x\in\xi^\R_t$ is isolated from the left in the set $\xi^\R_t$ if and only there is an incoming path $l\in\mathcal{W}^l$ at $(x,t)$. An analogous statement holds if $x$ is isolated from the right. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 7 of arXiv:2512.10761

body:
The entropy method derives concentration inequalities by bounding the entropy functional Ent(exp(lambda * f)) via logarithmic Sobolev inequalities or modified log-Sobolev inequalities, which subadditively tensorize on product spaces. Integrating the resulting differential inequality on the moment generating function (Herbst's argument) establishes sub-Gaussian or sub-exponential concentration.
Logarithmic Sobolev or modified log-Sobolev inequalities on product spaces
title: The Entropy Method (Herbst's Method)

[Theoremb 2 (Positive-time heat-flow Schur convexity) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $1\le p<2$ and $t>0$. The map
\[
 \theta\mapsto \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\theta)
\]
is strictly Schur-convex as a function of $s(\theta)$. In particular, with
\[
 \diag=\frac1{\sqrt n}(1,\ldots,1),
\]
one has
\[
 \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\diag)
 \le \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(\theta)
 \le \widetilde A_{p,n,t}(e_1),
 \qquad \theta\in\sphere,
\]
with equality only for the corresponding signed-permutation orbits. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Positive-time heat-flow Schur convexity

=-\infty .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma 88 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Let $0<\delta<1$ with $\delta=o(1)$ and $\tfrac1{\delta}=O(\log\alpha)$. [Definition 9 of arXiv:2609.01965, 'A logarithmic Bogomolov--Sommese vanishing theorem on compact K\"ahler manifolds'] Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\{\alpha\}\in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$ a $(1,1)$-class on $X$. Let $L$ be a line bundle on $X$.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(1)] $\{\alpha\}$ is said to be nef if for every $\varepsilon>0$, 
        there exists a smooth function $\varphi_\varepsilon$ on $X$ such that $\alpha+\ddbar \varphi_\varepsilon\geq-\varepsilon\omega$.
        One defines the numerical dimension of $\{\alpha\}$ to be
        $$\nd(\{\alpha\})=\max\{k=0,\ldots,n~|~\{\alpha\}^k\neq0 \text{ in } H^{2k}(X,\mathbb{R})\}.$$
        $L$ is said to be nef if $c_1(L)$ is a nef class.
        In this case, we define its numerical
        dimension by $\nd(L)=\nd(c_1(L))$.
        A vector bundle $E$ is called nef if the line bundle $\mathcal{O}_E(1)$ on $\mathbb{P}(E)$, the projective bundle of hyperplanes in the fibres of $E$, is nef.
        \item[(2)] $\{\alpha\}$ is said to be pseudo-effective if there is a quasi-psh function $\varphi$ such that $\alpha+\ddbar\varphi\geq 0$ in the sense of currents.
        One defines the numerical dimension of $\{\alpha\}$ to be
        $$\nd(\{\alpha\})=\max\{k=0,\ldots,n~|~\langle \{\alpha\}^k \rangle\neq0 \}.$$
        Here $\langle \{\alpha\}^k \rangle:=\lim\limits_{\delta\to0}\{\langle T^k_{\min,\delta\omega} \rangle\}$ 
        where $T^k_{\min,\delta\omega}$ is the positive current with minimal singularity in the class $\{\alpha+\delta\omega\}$ and $\langle T^k_{\min,\delta\omega} \rangle$ is the non-pluripolar product.
        We refer to \cite{BEGZ10} for more precise argument.
        $L$ is said to be pseudo-effective if $c_1(L)$ is a pseudo-effective class. 
        In this case, we define its numerical
        dimension by $\nd(L)=\nd(c_1(L))$, and there is a singular Hermitian metric $h$ on $L$ such that $\image\Theta_{L,h}\geq 0$ in the sense of currents.
        \item[(3)] $\{\alpha\}$ is said to be big if there is a quasi-psh function $\varphi$ such that $\alpha+\ddbar\varphi\geq \varepsilon\omega$ for some positive continuous function $\varepsilon$ in the sense of currents.
        $L$ is said to be big if $c_1(L)$ is a big class. 
        In this case, there is a singular Hermitian metric $h$ on $L$ such that $\image\Theta_{L,h}\geq \varepsilon\omega$ in the sense of currents. 
        Note that a nef line bundle is big if its numerical dimension is $n$.
    \end{itemize}

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2609.00757, 'Improved bounds in Birch's theorem for forms in many variables'] Let \(d\geq5\), \(B\geq2\), \(\eps>0\), and \(1\leq Q\leq B\).
Let \(q\) be a positive integer, and suppose that \(\|q\alpha\|=|q\alpha-a|\) for some integer \(a\) with \((a,q)=1\).
Suppose that
\[
 q\leq B^2,\qquad \|q\alpha\|\leq B^{-1},
\]
and \(K_B(\alpha,q,Q)\leq B^\eps Q^{-1}\).
Then, with \(H_1=Q^{1/2^{d-4}}\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{|\h|\leq H_1B^\eps}|S_{\h}(\alpha;B)|
 \ll B^{n+O_{d,n}(\eps)}H_1^\sigma.
\end{equation}
The implied constant depends only on \(F,\omega\) and \(\eps\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 1 (Degree--parameter envelope) of arXiv:2608.30304, '2608.30304'] For all $n\in\Nzero$, all $\alpha,\beta\ge-1/2$ and all $x\in[-1,1]$,
\begin{equation}
 F_{n,\alpha,\beta}(x)\le C_*\,\mathcal E_n(\alpha+\beta+1),
 \qquad C_*=1.2\cdot10^5.
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\[
 F_{n,\alpha,\beta}(x)^2\le C_*^2
 \max\left\{1,S^{1/3},\frac{S^{1/2}}{(n+1)^{1/6}}\right\},
 \qquad S=\alpha+\beta+1.
\]
No attempt is made to optimise the numerical constant. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Mainthm t:1.2i of arXiv:2602.21277, 'A Limit in Law for the Cover Time and Last Visited Vertex of Wired Planar Domains'] There exists a coupling between
$\eta_{\rm D}$ from~(equation e:1.10i of the paper), $\mathcal Z_{\rm D}$ from~(equation eq:deflqgm of the paper) and $\overline{h}_{\rm D}$ from~(equation e:1.7p of the paper), such that $\eta_{\rm D}$ and $\mathcal Z_{\rm D}$ 
are related as in~(equation e:1.10i of the paper), $\mathcal Z_{\rm D}$ is measurable w.r.t. $\eta_{{\rm D}}$ and $\eta_{\rm D}$ is conditionally independent of $\overline{h}_{\rm D}$ given  $\mathcal Z_{\rm D}$. Under this coupling, if $(r_N)_{N \geq 1}$ satisfies~(equation e:1.11i of the paper) then
\begin{equation}

\big(\eta_{N,r_N},\, \overline{h}_N\,\big)
\underset{N \to \infty}\Longrightarrow \big(\eta_{\rm D},\, \overline{h}_{\rm D} \big) \,,
\end{equation}
with the underlying space for the first component taken as in~(equation e:1.10i of the paper). In particular, the joint law of $\eta_{\rm D}$, $\mathcal Z_D$ and $\overline{h}_{\rm D}$ in any such coupling is the same. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2511.14757, 'A weak convergence approach to the large deviations of the dynamic Schr\"odinger problem'] Assume Assumptions \ref{ass:b-sigma-local-properties}-\ref{ass:log-gradient-convergence} hold and fix $x,y$. For $F$ bounded and continuous, the sequence $\{ X^{\eta, xy} \} _\eta $ of bridge processes satisfies 
\begin{align*}
    \lim _{\eta \to 0} -\eta \log \mathbb{E} \left[ \exp\left\{ -\frac{1}{\eta} F(X^{\eta, xy}) \right\} \right] = \inf _{\varphi \in \calC _1} \left[ F(\varphi) + \inf _{\calU _\varphi} \frac{1}{2} \int _0 ^1 | \nu _s | ^2 ds  \right].
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

constant $C=C(K,r)$ such that

    \leq
    C\|f\|_2^2
\]
for every $r$-separated set $P\subset\mathbb R^d$ and every
$f\in PW_K$.

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2603.28212, 'Limit Laws for the Distance to Fr\'echet Means of Random Graphs'] Under the same conditions of Theorem \ref{Thm:Fn2}, we have the following.
\begin{itemize}
     \item[(i)] If $np(1-p)\to 0$ and $n^2p(1-p)\to \infty$, then
    \[
    F_n-\sqrt{\E[F_n^2]} \xrightarrow{D} N(0,1). 
    \]
    \item[(ii)] If $np(1-p)\to c$ for some non-integer constant $c>0$, then
    \[
    F_n-\sqrt{\E[F_n^2]} \xrightarrow{D} 
    N\left(0, \frac{c\big[4(c-\lfloor c\rfloor+1)^2+c\big]}
    {2\big[(c-\lfloor c\rfloor)^2+\lfloor c\rfloor+2c\big]}\right).
    \]
    \item[(iii)] If $np(1-p)\to \infty$, then
    \[
    \frac{F_n-\sqrt{\E[F_n^2]}}{\sqrt{np(1-p)}} \xrightarrow{D} 
    N\Big(0,\frac16\Big). 
    \]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 6 of arXiv:2603.28212

[Lemma lem:stopped-capped-arrays-martingales-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Fix \(
d\in\mathfrak D_{\xi,n}^{\mathrm{osc}}\), and set \(m=m_{\xi,d}\). Let
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{pre}}(d)
=
\left\{
(\ell,I,J):
0\le \ell<m,\ 
I\in\mathcal D_\ell^\circ,\ 
J\in\mathcal D_{\ell+1}^\circ,\ 
J\subset I
\right\},
\]
and choose a deterministic ordering \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{pre}}(d)=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_N\}\), by increasing generation, with any deterministic order within each generation, where \(\gamma_r=(\ell_r,I_r,J_r)\). With respect to the filtration \((\mathcal H_r^{\mathrm{pre}})\) generated by revealing the variables \(U_{J_r}\) in this order,
\[
S_r^{\mathrm{pre}}
:=
\sum_{q=1}^r
\mathbf 1_{\{\tau_n>\ell_q\}}
X_{J_q,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}(\xi,d,\ell_q),
\qquad
0\le r\le N,
\]
is a complex-valued martingale and \(S_N^{\mathrm{pre}}=\widehat F^{\mathrm{pre,cap}}_{\xi,d,n}\).

Moreover, for every \(L>m\), an analogous deterministic ordering of
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{post}}(d,L)
=
\left\{
(\ell,I,J):
m\le \ell<L,\ 
I\in\mathcal D_\ell^\circ,\ 
J\in\mathcal D_{\ell+1}^\circ,\ 
J\subset I
\right\}
\]
produces a complex-valued martingale whose terminal value is \(\widehat F^{\mathrm{post,cap}}_{\xi,d,n,L}\).

[Lemma lem:geod_IC of arXiv:2505.09604, 'Exceptional force, uncountably many solutions in the KPZ fixed point'] The following holds on the event $\Omega_1$. Let $\xi \in \mathbb{R}$, and $b\in \mathcal{F}^\xi$. Then for each $(x,t) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, either
\[
g_{(x,t)}^{b,L}(t) = g_{(x,t)}^{\xi -,L}(s) \quad\, \forall s \le t,\qquad\text{or}\qquad g_{(x,t)}^{b,L}(s) = g_{(x,t)}^{\xi +,L}(s)\quad\, \forall s\le t.
\]
The same holds for $R$ in place of $L$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:invariant of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] The Cauchy family is exactly invariant under the flow:
		$\mathrm{Cauchy}(m,\gamma) \mapsto \mathrm{Cauchy}(m,\gamma e^{-t})$,
		with reduced dynamics $\dot m = 0$, $\dot\gamma = -\gamma$ and exact
		entropy law $H = \log(4\pi\gamma)$, $\dot H = -1$. The Fisher--Rao
		metric of the family is
		\begin{equation}
			ds^{2} = \frac{dm^{2}+d\gamma^{2}}{2\gamma^{2}},
			
		\end{equation}
		a hyperbolic plane of curvature $-2$, and the flow traces its vertical
		geodesics at constant speed $1/\sqrt2$.

[Teo 9 of arXiv:2608.02103, '$p$-Adic Diffusion and Random Walks on $[0,1]$'] There exists a probability measure $p_t(x,\cdot)$, $t\geq 0$, with $x\in [0,1] $, on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $[0,1]$, such that the Cauchy problem (\ref{CauchyProblem}) has a unique solution of the form 
\[u(x,t)=\int_0^1 u_0(y)p_t(x,dy).\]
In addition, $p_t(x,\cdot)$ is the transition distribution of a strong Markov process, whose paths are right-continuous and have no discontinuities other than jumps.

body:
Small raw drift of derivative-power Loewner probes does not identify a Brownian variance if their positive exponents tend to zero. With deterministic driver W=0 and alpha_n=1/n, on a local interval with bounded derivative jets and h-prime bounded away from zero, (h-prime)^alpha_n tends uniformly to 1. For slit probes (x,s)=(1,1),(-1,1),(1,3), the initial raw relative drifts are alpha_n times (9/8,9/8,33/32), yet the variance rate is zero. At n=128 the maximum raw drift is 9/1024<1/100, while division by alpha_n leaves 9/8. Require a fixed positive common limiting exponent or exponent-normalized error control. Author-derived obstruction; independent review pending.

[Theorem 8 (Gaussian partial coloring relative to a subspace) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] There are absolute constants \(c,\eta,C>0\) with the following property. Let
\(H\subseteq\mathbb R^s\) be a linear subspace satisfying $\dim H\ge (1-\eta)s$, and let \(K\subseteq H\) be a symmetric convex set satisfying $\gamma_H(K)\ge \exp(-\eta s)$.
Then for every \(y\in(-1,1)^s\), there exists an increment \(x\in CK\) such that $y+x\in[-1,1]^s$ and $|\{i\in[s]: |y_i+x_i|=1\}|\ge cs.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.01485, 'On the Ramification of Quadratic Fields where the Torsion of a Rational Elliptic Curve Gro'] Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve. Assume $K$ is a quadratic number field such that there exists $P\in E(K)[\ell]\setminus E(\mathbb{Q})$, with $\ell\geq 3$ prime.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For every prime $p\neq \ell$ that ramifies in $K$, $E$ has additive reduction at $p$, i.e. $p^2|N_E$.
        \item If $p=\ell>3$  ramifies in $K$, $E$ has additive reduction at $p$, i.e. $p^2|N_E$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:ergo of arXiv:2505.14012, 'Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations'] \phantom{ }
\begin{enumerate}
\item An invariant measure $\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H)$ for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is called \emph{ergodic} if
\[Q_T(v,\cdot) \rightharpoonup \mu\]
as $T\to\infty$ for any $v\in H$ in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.
\item An invariant measure $\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H)$ for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is called \emph{strongly mixing} if
\[P_t(v,\cdot)\rightharpoonup \mu\]
as $t\to\infty$ for any $v\in H$ in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.
\item An invariant measure $\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H)$ for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is called \emph{exponentially ergodic} if there exists $\beta>0$ and a positive function $c:H\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for any $\varphi\in\operatorname{Lip}_b(H)$, all $t>0$, and all $v\in H$,
\[\left|P_t\varphi(v)-\int_H\varphi(z)\,\mu(dz)\right|\le c(v)e^{-\beta t}\operatorname{Lip}(\varphi).\]
\item An invariant measure $\mu\in{\mathcal M}_1(H)$ for the semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ is called \emph{exponentially mixing} if there exists $\beta>0$ and a positive function $c:H\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all $t>0$, and all $v\in H$,
\[\|P_t(v,\cdot)-\mu\|_{F-M}\le c(v)e^{-\beta t},\]
where
\[\|\nu\|_{F-M}:=\sup\left\{\left|\int_H\varphi(z)\,\nu(dz)\right|\;\colon\;\varphi\in \operatorname{Lip}_b(H),\;\|\varphi\|_{\operatorname{Lip}_b}\le 1\right\}\]
is the \emph{Forter-Mourier norm} (also called \emph{bounded Lipschitz norm}) of a signed measure $\nu$ on ${\mathcal B}(H)$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Ergodicity and mixing

body:
[Proposition prop: convergence of chaos for truncated noise of arXiv:2602.04429, 'Disordered systems and (subcritical) polynomial chaos\\ with heavy-tail disorder'] {}
	Let $\ensuremath{\mathbf{f}}$ be symmetric and infinitely differentiable function with compact support in~ $\Omega^{k,*} = \{ (x_1,\dots,x_k) \in \Omega^k \,, \forall i \neq j, x_i \neq x_j \}$. 
	Then for every $s > \frac{D}{2}$ the following joint convergence in distribution holds in $H_{\rm loc}^{-s}(\Omega) \times {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} $ as $\delta \downarrow 0$:
	\[ 
	(\zeta_{\delta}, X_{\delta}^{(a)}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{f}})) \xrightarrow{(d)} (\boldsymbol\zeta,{\ensuremath{\mathbf X}} ^{(a)}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{f}})) \,,
	\]
	where ${\ensuremath{\mathbf X}} ^{(a)}(\ensuremath{\mathbf{f}}) = \frac{1}{k!} \int_{\Omega^k} \ensuremath{\mathbf{f}}(x_1,\dots,x_k) \prod\limits_{j=1}^k \boldsymbol\zeta^{(a)}(\mathrm{d} x_j)$.

body:
[Lemma lem_collision of arXiv:2608.15344, 'A Harris recurrent continuous-time Markov process without wide-sense regenerative structur'] Let $Y$ be an $\mathcal{S}$-valued random variable, and let
\[
U=(U_1,\dots,U_N)
\]
be a random sequence of vertices in $\mathcal{V}$, where $N<\infty$ almost surely.
Conditional on $Y$, let $U^{(1)}$ and $U^{(2)}$ be independent copies of $U$. Suppose that\[
P(v\text{ occurs in }U)=0
\]
for every fixed $v\in\mathcal{V}$. If $Z$ is a $\mathcal{V}$-valued random variable independent of $Y$, then
\[
P(Z\text{ occurs in both }U^{(1)}\text{ and }U^{(2)})=0.
\]
No independence between $Z$ and the two sequences is required.

body:
[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.31008, 'Stability of gravitational instantons with a bounded Killing vector field'] On a Ricci-flat four-manifold, we have
\begin{align}
 dF=0,\qquad\delta F&=0,\quad \text{ and } \quad\iota_KF=-dV,\\
 \nabla^2V&=\frac12F\circ F-2\Rm(\,\cdot\,,K,\,\cdot\,,K),
 \\
 \Delta V&=-|F|^2,
 \\
 \cE_g(\kappa\otimes\kappa)&=\nabla^2V-F\circ F,
 
\end{align}
and for every smooth function $f$, we find
\begin{equation}
 \cE_g(\nabla^2f)=\nabla^2(\Delta f),\qquad
 \cE_g(fg)=(\Delta f)g.
\end{equation}

	\lim_{k\to \infty} \int_{X}m_2^2(\nu)\,{\rm d}\eta_k(\nu) = \int_{X}m_2^2(\nu)\,{\rm d}\eta(\nu) < \infty.

Then, for all $(\mu_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathcal{P}_2(H)$ such that $\mu_k \to \mu$ with respect to the weak topology of $P_2^w(H)$,
\[
	\lim_{k \to \infty} \int_X \mathcal{R}(\nu,\mu_k){\rm d}\eta_k(\nu) = \int_X \mathcal{R}(\nu,\mu){\rm d}\eta(\nu).
\]

body: In mathematics, the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means, or more briefly the AM–GM inequality, states that the arithmetic mean of a list of non-negative real numbers is greater than or equal to the geometric mean of the same list; and further, that the two means are equal if and only if every number in the list is the same.
title: AM–GM inequality

    \[\sup_{n\geq 0} \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{n^{d-1}}{k_n^d}\phi_{d+1}\left(T_{n}^{k_n} \right) \right)^p \,\right] < +\infty\]
title: Lemma borneLp of arXiv:2607.14792

body:
[Theorem 21 of arXiv:2608.26628, 'Open Problems in Mathematical Logic'] {[ZF $+$ there is an uncountable well ordered set
of reals].}

The following conditions on a countable (first order) $T$ are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $T$ is categorical in some cardinal $\aleph_{\alpha} > \aleph_0$,in $\mathbf V$, of course
        \item $T$ is categorical in every cardinal $\aleph_{\beta} > \aleph_0$,
        in $\mathbf V$, of course
        \item $T$ is, in $\mathbf L[T]$, totally transcendental
        (i.e. $\aleph_0$-stable) with no two cardinal models
        (i.e., for no model $M$ of $T$ and formula
        $\varphi(x,y) \in \mathbf L(\tau_T)$ and
        $\bar a \in {}^{\ell g(\bar y)}M$ do we have
        $\aleph_0 \leq |\varphi(M,\bar a)| < \|M\|$
        and $\|M\|$ is a cardinal, i.e. the set of elements of $M$ is well-orderable hence its power is a cardinal)
        \item If $\mathbf V' \subseteq \mathbf V$ is a transitive class extending
        $\mathbf L$, $T \in \mathbf V'$ and $\mathbf V'$ satisfies ZFC, then the conditions in (3) hold
        \item For some $\mathbf V'$ clause (4) holds.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 21 of arXiv:2608.26628

body:
The individual basic reproduction number R_0 is the expected total number of secondary infectious contacts (both global and local) produced by a single primary infective in an entirely susceptible population: R_0 = E[X_G] + E[X_L]. Because local contacts may be wasted on already infected household members, R_* <= R_0, with strict inequality whenever local spread occurs.
Single primary infective
title: Individual Basic Reproduction Number R_0

body:
[Thm 14 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Suppose that \(\beta, W\) and $\theta_k$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{assumption12}. Then, for every
\(m\geq1\) and every
\(\bm x_1,\ldots,\bm x_m\in\mathbb R^n\), the conditional law of
\(
    \bigl(
        \mathcal P_k^a(\bm x_1),\ldots,
        \mathcal P_k^a(\bm x_m)
    \bigr)
\)
given \(A_k\) converges weakly in probability to
\(\mathcal N_m(\boldsymbol 0,\bm K)\), where
\[
    \bm K_{bc}
    =
    K_{\beta,a}(\bm x_b,\bm x_c),
    \qquad 1\leq b,c\leq m.
\]
Consequently, the unconditional finite-dimensional distributions of
\(\mathcal P_k^a\) converge to those of the centered Gaussian
process with covariance kernel \(K_{\beta,a}\). In particular, for
every \(\bm x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
    \mathcal P_k^a(\bm x)
    \xrightarrow{d}
    \mathcal N\left(
        0,
        \operatorname{Var} 
            a(\bm Z^\top\bm x)
        +
        q_\beta
            \mathbb E^2
                a(\bm Z^\top\bm x)
    \right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 14 of arXiv:2608.12804

body:
[Lemma lem: fan gon of arXiv:2609.03755, 'The Scramble Number of Outerplanar Graphs'] Let $F_m$ be the fan graph on $m+1$ vertices. If $m = k^2+c$ for some $k\in {\mathbb Z}_{>0}$ with $0\leq c\leq 2k$, then
    $$\operatorname{sn}(F_m) = \begin{cases}
        \left\lfloor\sqrt{m} \right\rfloor+1 & \text{if } c\leq k+1\\ 
        \left\lfloor\sqrt{m} \right\rfloor+2 & \text{otherwise }\\
    \end{cases}.$$

body:
[Lemma lem:heavy-parent-children of arXiv:2608.26707, 'An Exponential Lower Bound for the Permanent\\of Random Bernoulli Matrix'] Fix $0\leq k<n$, condition on $\mathcal{F}_k$, and let $A\in\binom{[n]}{k}$ be $\lambda$-heavy.
Let $I\subseteq[n]\setminus A$.
After exposing row $k+1$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb{P}\!\left(
   \text{no }A\cup\{i\},\ i\in I,
   \text{ is }\lambda\text{-heavy}
   \,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_k
 \right)
 &\leq2^{-\left\lvert I\right\rvert},
 \\
 \mathbb{P}\!\left(
   \#\set{i\in I:A\cup\{i\}
        \text{ is }\lambda\text{-heavy}}<\frac{\left\lvert I\right\rvert}{3}
   \,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_k
 \right)
 &\leq e^{-\left\lvert I\right\rvert/18}.
 
\end{align}

  a_i,
  \qquad
  a_i+a_j\quad(0\le i<j<m,\ \{i,j\}\notin E(C_m))
\]

body:
[Theorem 19 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $\emptyset\ne \Omega \subset \RR^d$ be an open and bounded subset.
  Let $A_1,A_2\in \{B,F\}$.
  Let $s_1,s_2\in \RR$ and let $0<p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2 \le \infty$ (with $p_i<\infty$ if $A_i=F$).
  Assume that 
  \begin{equation*}
     s_1 > s_2 
     \quad \text{and} \quad
      s_1 - \frac{d}{p_1} > s_2 -\frac{d}{p_2}.
  \end{equation*}
  Let $\SC$ denote the unit ball of $(A_1)^{s_1}_{p_1,q_1}(\Omega)$
  and let $\XX = (A_2)^{s_2}_{p_2,q_2}(\Omega)$,
  endowed with the \mbox{(quasi-)}\allowbreak metric induced by
  $\norm{\cdot\mid (A_2)^{s_2}_{p_2,q_2}(\Omega)}$.
  Then $\md(\SC) = \frac{d}{s_1-s_2}$ and there exists a Borel probability measure on
  $\XX$ that is critical for $\SC$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 19 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Lemma lem:cauchy-positive of arXiv:2605.26688, 'Absolute moment inequalities under quadratic-form positivity'] Let \(D\in\mathcal B(\mathbb{R})\), let \(\mu\) be a measure on \(\mathcal B(D)\), let \(c:D\to(0,\infty)\) be measurable, and let \(\eta:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be measurable. If
\[
   \iint_{D^2}\frac{\left\lvert \eta(x)\eta(y)\right\rvert}{c(x)+c(y)}\mu(\,\mathrm{d} x)\mu(\,\mathrm{d} y)<\infty,
\]

[Lemma lem:optimisation of arXiv:2605.10911, 'The stochastic block model has the overlap graph property for modularity'] Let $0\leq t <1$.
Define $\mathcal{X}_k(t)$ to be the family of matrices $X=(x_{ij})_{1\leq i \leq j \leq k}$ such that
\begin{align}
\nonumber &x_{ij} \geq 0, &\mbox{for all $i,j \in [k]$},\\[0.5em]

 &\sum_i x_{ij}  =  1 &\mbox{for all $j \in [k]$},  \\

\nonumber &\sum_{i\neq j}x_{ij}  = t, \mbox{ and }\\
\nonumber &\sum_{i}x_{ii} \geq \max_{\sigma} \sum_i x_{\sigma(i)i}.
\end{align}

Let $g(X)$ be defined as in~(equation defn.gx of the paper). Then,

\[ \max_{X\in \mathcal{X}_k(t)} g(X) = k(k\!-\!1) - 2t \big( k\!-\!t(k\!-\!1)\big)\;\; \mbox{and} \;\; \arg\max_{X\in \mathcal{X}_k(t)} g(X) = \{ X_k^{(ij)}(t) \; : \; i\neq j \}, \] 
where, for $i\neq j$, $X^{(ij)}_k(t)$ is the $k\times k$ matrix with $x_{ij}=t$, $x_{jj}=1-t$, all other diagonal elements $1$ and non-diagonal elements~$0$ (i.e., $x_{aa}=1$ for all $a\neq j$ and $x_{ab}=0$ for all $a\neq b$ such that $(a,b)\neq (i,j)$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:optimisation of arXiv:2605.10911

body:
[Lemma lem:cole-hopf-plateau of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Let $0\le s<t\le1$, assume $\zeta((s,t))=0$, and set $\alpha:=\zeta([0,s])$.  Then
		\[
		U(r,x):=\exp\{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(r,x)\}
		\]
		solves the backward heat equation on $[s,t]$,
		\[
		\partial_r U(r,x)+\frac12\xi''(r)\partial_{xx}U(r,x)=0 .
		\]
		Hence, with
		\[
		p^{\mathrm{BM}}_{s,t}(x,y)
		:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi(\xi'(t)-\xi'(s))}}
		\exp\left\{-\frac{(y-x)^2}{2(\xi'(t)-\xi'(s))}\right\},
		\]
		we have
		\begin{equation}
			e^{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(s,x)}
			=\int_\mathbb{R} e^{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(t,y)}p^{\mathrm{BM}}_{s,t}(x,y)\,\mathrm{d} y .
		\end{equation}
		Equivalently, conditionally on $X_s=x$, the transition density of the Auffinger--Chen process on the plateau is
		\begin{equation}
			p_{s,t}(x,y)
			=\frac{e^{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(t,y)}}{e^{\alpha\Phi_\zeta(s,x)}}
			p^{\mathrm{BM}}_{s,t}(x,y).
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cole--Hopf identity on a plateau

[Proposition eq:Wulff-def of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Let $d\ge 1$.
Suppose that Assumptions~(ass:Omega of the paper) and~(ass:J of the paper)
hold, but without requiring that $h^{(\mu)},J^{(\mu)}$ satisfy
(equation eq:Q_d-1 of the paper).
For nonzero $x \in {\mathbb R^d}$,
define its \emph{surface tension} by $\sigma(x) = m_S  \abs x_S
= \mu_{\hat x} \cdot x $.
Then the \emph{Wulff shape} for $\sigma(x)$, defined by
\begin{equation}

\mathcal{W}
= \bigl\{ \mu \in {\mathbb R^d}    :     \mu \cdot x \le  \sigma(x)
	\text{ for all nonzero } x\in {\mathbb R^d}   \bigr\} ,
\end{equation}
coincides with $\overline \Omega$.

and let \(\Delta_j=S_j-S_{j-1}\) be its differences.

Assume that \(|\Delta_j|\le R\)
for

\[
    \sum_{j=1}^N
    \mathbb E[|\Delta_j|^2\mid\mathcal H_{j-1}]

almost surely.  Then, for every \(t>0\),
\[
    \mathbb P
    \left(
        \max_{0\le j\le N}|S_j|>t
    \right)
    \le
    4\exp
    \left(
        -\frac{t^2}{8(V+Rt)}
    \right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For real factors B of size m-by-r and A of size r-by-p, and differentiable product loss F(BA), put G_B=grad F(BA) A^T, G_A=B^T grad F(BA), and D=AA^T-B^TB. Simultaneous factor gradient descent with step eta has the exact identity D_next-D=eta^2(G_A G_A^T-G_B^T G_B); the first-order terms cancel. Thus ||D_next-D||F<=eta^2(||G_A||F^2+||G_B||F^2). If a fixed eta>0 additionally satisfies the sufficient-decrease inequality f_next<=f-a eta ||grad f||F^2 for f(B,A)=F(BA), some a>0, and f is bounded below by f_star along the iterates, summation gives ||D_t-D_0||F<=(eta/a)(f_0-f_star). This implication assumes descent; it does not establish it or prove arbitrary-step convergence. The trace identity (||B||F^2+||A||F^2)^2<=r[||AA^T-B^TB||F^2+4||BA||F^2] then converts bounds on imbalance and product into a factor bound. Du-Hu-Lee, Algorithmic Regularization in Learning Deep Homogeneous Models: Layers are Automatically Balanced, arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 2.2 gives continuous-time Gram invariance; Appendix B, Claim B.1 expands the discrete square-loss update. The conditional constant-step summation and trace inequality here are elementary method consequences, not their full GD convergence theorem. Their Theorem 3.1 instead uses small Gaussian initialization of both factors and decreasing steps.

body: For independent Bernoulli bond percolation with common parameter p, the conditional probability that an edge is open given all other edge states equals p almost surely. Hence the strict finite-energy hypothesis 0<P(edge open | other edges)<1 holds exactly for 0<p<1. At p=0 or p=1 that hypothesis fails; uniqueness conclusions at those endpoints can be checked directly. This corrects the application sentence that all Burton-Keane hypotheses hold for every p, without refuting its interior-parameter uniqueness conclusion. Correction draft: independent review pending.
title: Bernoulli finite energy requires an interior parameter

body:
[Theorem 29 (Geometric estimates from initial data) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] \bse
Fix an admissible Navier--Stokes triple $(\mathscr F,\chi,\mathscr B)$ as defined in \autoref{def-pot-admissible-triple}.
Let $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ with $\Phi=(\Jperp,\Jpar,\Pbb,\Qbb)$ and $\Psi=(\ell,\log\Omega,\Kpar)$ be a sufficiently regular dissipated-energy or particle-production Einstein--Navier--Stokes areal flow $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ on $[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^3$.  Denote the values at time $t=t_0$ by
\be
(\mathring\Phi,\mathring\Psi,\mathring\zeta) \coloneqq (\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)(t_0,\cdot) \quad \text{on } \Tbb^3 .
\ee
Then the following estimates hold, where implied constants depend on the Navier--Stokes potential $\chi$ and on $t_0,t_1$, but not on the relaxation structure~$\mathscr B$ nor on the solution $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$.
\bei
\item \emph{Spatial energy.} The fluid variables, and the first-order geometric variables $\Pbb,\Qbb$ have
  \bel{estimate-SE}
    \int_{\{t\}\times \Tbb^3} \Bigl( T_\chi^{00} + \Ebf_0(\Pbb,\Qbb) \Bigr) \dVtrois
    \lesssim \|\mathring\Phi\|_{\mathrm{energy}} , \qquad t\in[t_0,t_1] .
  \ee

\item \emph{Conformal length and volume.}
  \bel{estimate-LV}
  \aligned
  & \mathcal L(t) \leq \mathcal L(t_0) , \quad \mathcal V(t) \leq |t/t_0|^{3/4} \mathcal V(t_0) , \qquad t_0 \leq t \leq t_1 < 0 \quad \text{(future-contracting regime)},
  \\
  & \mathcal L(t) \geq \mathcal L(t_0) , \quad \mathcal V(t) \geq |t/t_0|^{3/4} \mathcal V(t_0) , \qquad 0 < t_0 \leq t \leq t_1 \quad \text{(future-expanding regime)}.
  \endaligned
  \ee
  Furthermore, the minimum conformal length $\mathcal L_{\min}=\min_{t\in[t_0,t_1]} \mathcal L(t)\geq 0$ is reached at $t=t_1$ in the future-contracting regime and at $t=t_0$ in the future-expanding regime.
\eei
In the future-contracting regime, subsequent estimates require the assumption that $\mathcal L_{\min}>0$ and depend on $1/\mathcal L_{\min}$, which is \emph{not bounded} by the initial data.  In the future-expanding regime $\mathcal L_{\min}>0$ is part of the initial data.
The constants $C_1,C_2,\dots$ below depend on $\mathcal L_{\min}$ and on the finite-energy and bounded-variation norms of initial data.
\bei
\item \emph{Both-sided bounds on conformal length and volume.}
  \bel{both-sided-LV}
  (C_1)^{-1} \leq \mathcal L(t) \leq C_1 , \qquad (C_2)^{-1} \leq \mathcal V(t) \leq C_2 .
  \ee

\item \emph{Bounded variation in space.} The lapse, twist and conformal length measure satisfy
  \bel{spatial-bv}
    \|\ell\|_{\BVac(0,1)} + \|(\log\Omega,\Kpar)\|_{\BVac(\Tbb^3)}
    \leq C_3 , \qquad t \in [t_0,t_1] .
  \ee

\item \emph{Temporal integrals.} The (not necessarily positive) spatial stress~$T_\chi^{11}$ admits integrals on constant-$x$ slices
\bel{temporal-stress}
\biggl| \int_{[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^2} \Bigl( T_\chi^{11} + E_0(\Pbb,\Qbb) \Bigr) \dVundeux \biggr|
\leq C_4 , \quad x\in\Sbb^1 .
\ee
\eei
Assume further that the potential~$\chi$ is torus-adapted (\autoref{def-NS-torus-adapted}) and the stress-tensor satisfies the \emph{coercive stress condition} (\autoref{def-Tchi-coercive}, below), and assume that the parallel momentum per particle is bounded at initial time in the sense that $2|T_\chi^{02}|+2|T_\chi^{03}|\leq C^\parallel\Numb_\chi^0$ for some constant~$C^\parallel>0$.
Then \eqref{temporal-stress} are completed to an $L^2$~control of the whole fluid momentum~$\Jbb$ along timelike slices, and the following estimates are satisfied.
\bei
\item \emph{Bounded variation in time.} The lapse, twist and conformal length measure satisfy
  \bel{bv-time-bound}
    \|\ell\|_{\BVac(\Interval)} + \|(\log\Omega,\Kpar)\|_{\BVac(\Interval\times\Tbb^2)}
    \leq C_5 , \qquad x \in \Sbb^1 .
  \ee
\eei
Altogether, under the assumed coercive stress condition, the finite-energy and bounded-variation norms \eqref{equa-flow-energy-norm}--\eqref{equa-flow-variation-norm} of the areal flow are bounded by a function of its initial data and, in the future-contracting regime, of~$\mathcal L_{\min}$.
\ese (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Geometric estimates from initial data

[Lemma lem:capture-disjoint-blocks of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Fix integers $B\ge1$ and $K\ge1$, and real $\lambda>2$. Let $r$ be a positive integer and $n_0=\lceil\lambda r\rceil$. Assume
\[
(8\lambda)^{2B}\le K,
\qquad
K\log K\le \frac r2.
\]
Let $J$ be a set of size $n_0$ and assume there are pairwise disjoint subsets
\[
\mathcal W_1,\dots,\mathcal W_K\subseteq J,
\]
each of size at most $B$. If $\Omega\subseteq J$ is chosen uniformly from $\binom Jr$, then
\[
\mathbb P\big(\forall s\in[K]:\mathcal W_s\not\subseteq\Omega\big)
\le
\exp(-\sqrt K).
\]

The condition $K\log K\le r/2$ keeps the sequential exposure of the $K$ blocks from depleting the sample. The condition $(8\lambda)^{2B}\le K$ ensures that the capture probability of one block, repeated $K$ times, gives exponent at least $\sqrt K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Capturing one of many disjoint witness blocks

[Lemma positive-weight of arXiv:2608.30212, 'A Painlev\'e equation for the H\"ormander-Bernhardsson constant'] Let $k$ be even and $c\in J_{k,0}$. Define $\lambda_{\ell,c}$ by
\[
\lambda_{\ell,c} = -\frac{\pi \gamma_{k,c}(x_\ell(c))}{q_{k,c}'(x_\ell(c))}
\]
Then $\lambda_{\ell,c}>0$ for $1\le \ell\le k$. Defining $\nu_c = \sum \lambda_{\ell, c} \delta_{x_\ell(c)}$, 
\[
\mathcal{L}_c[p] = \int pd\nu_c, \qquad (p \in \mathcal{P}_{2k-1})
\]
the measure $\nu_c$ is positive, and the largest zero in the interlacing belongs to $\gamma_{k,c}$.

[Theorem thm2 of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {\bf [Averaged stable-law attractor]}

Suppose that
\[
(\blacksquare) \qquad 
\begin{aligned}
&\mathbb{P}(X_1 > x) \sim A x^{-\alpha}, \quad x \to \infty,\\
&\big|g^{\neq}(x,y) - B(xy)^\beta\big| \leq K^{\neq}, \quad x,y \in \mathbb{R}_+,\\
&\big|g^{=}(x) - Cx^\beta\big| \leq K^{=}, \quad x \in \mathbb{R}_+,
\end{aligned}
\]
with $\alpha \in (0,\infty)$ a tail exponent, $\beta \in (0,\infty)$ a growth exponent, and $A,B,C,K^{\neq},K^{=} \in (0,\infty)$ constants. Suppose, in addition, that the law of $X_1$ is absolutely continuous. If $\alpha<\beta$, then there exists a coupling of $(X,Y)$ via a sequence $U$ of i.i.d.\ $\mathrm{UNIF}[0,1]$ random variables, written $(X(U),Y(U))$, such that  
\[
\lim_{\ell \to \infty} \sup_{L \geq \ell}\,\mathbb{E}_U\left[\Delta\Big(P(G^{(\ell)}[X(U)]),P(G_{\ell,\gamma,\delta,\eta}[Y(U)])\Big)\right] = 0
\]
with $\gamma = \frac{\alpha}{\beta}$, $\delta = B\big(A\Gamma(1-\gamma)\big)^{2/\gamma}$ and $\eta = C\big(A\Gamma(1-\gamma)\big)^{1/\gamma}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 14 (Rigidity) of arXiv:2607.23585, 'The one-period Kyle model has one equilibrium'] Let $V$ and $U$ be independent standard normal random variables.
	For every Borel-measurable map $\phi\colon\R\to\R$, let $P_\phi\colon\R\to\R$
	be a Borel version of the inverse regression
	\[
		P_\phi(y)=\E[V\mid\phi(V)+U=y]\,,
	\]
	and let
	\[
		F_\phi(x):=\E[P_\phi(x+U)]\,.
	\]
	The pointwise maximisation condition
	\[
		\phi(v)\in\argmax_{x\in\R}
		\bigl(xv-xF_\phi(x)\bigr)
		\qquad\text{for every }v\in\R
	\]
	holds if and only if $\phi=\id$.

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.10184, 'The sharp SAT/UNSAT phase transition in random ellipsoid fitting'] Let $x_1,\dots,x_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0,I_d)$ and let $p(n,d) = \mathbb{P}\{\exists S \succeq 0 :\ x_i^{\top} S x_i = d \ \forall i\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\rm (a)}] \textup{(Satisfiable phase.)} If $\ \limsup_{d \to \infty} n/d^2 < 1/4$, then $p(n,d) \to 1$.
\item[{\rm (b)}] \textup{(Unsatisfiable phase.)} If $\ \liminf_{d \to \infty} n/d^2 > 1/4$, then $p(n,d) \to 0$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem non-uniform-uniqueness of arXiv:2606.01627, 'The geometry of the giant component of random geometric graphs'] Fix $\lambda_0 > \lambda_c(d)$ and let $\phi_s \le s$ be an increasing
        function of $s$.  
        Then there exist $c(d,\lambda_0) > 0, C = C(d) > 0$
        such that the following holds.

        Let $\sigma$ be a metric on $\mathbb{R}^d$
        which satisfies
        \[
            \sigma(x,y) \le \|x - y\| \le 2\sigma(x,y)
        \]
        for all $x,y \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
        Let  
        $\nu$ be a measure on
        $\mathbb{R}^d$ which satisfies 
        $\frac{d\nu}{d\mathcal{L}} \ge \lambda_0$. 
        Let $G_s$ be the random geometric
        graph
        whose vertices are the
        points of a Poisson process on $[-s,s]^d$
        with intensity measure $\nu$
        and whose edge set consists
        of pairs of vertices with
        $\sigma$-distance at most 1.

        Then
        \[
        \mathbb{P}\left(
        \begin{array}{c}
            \mbox{Exactly one component of } G_s \\
            \mbox{ has Euclidean diameter at least } \phi_s
        \end{array}
        \right)
        \ge 1- C s^{d}\exp(-c \phi_s).
        \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 14 (Examples: averaged macroscopic-loop bounds) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\).

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item \textbf{Random regular graphs.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the random \(d\)-regular graph on \([n]\), with law \(p_{d,n}\).
    If $d>2c_{\theta,u}$, then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    p_{d,n}\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs.}
    Let \(G_n\sim G(n,\lambda/n)\). If $\lambda>2c_{\theta,u}$,
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Simple bounded-degree configuration model.}
    Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with
    degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\). Assume that
    \[
    1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
    \qquad\text{for all }i,n,
    \]
    and $\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho$. If $\rho>2c_{\theta,u}$,
    then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
    \[
    \Pbb\!\left(
    \frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
    \right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Examples: averaged macroscopic-loop bounds

[Proposition Th:hitting1 of arXiv:2411.08220, 'Nonlocal operators with Neumann conditions'] The following statements hold $\mathbb{P}_x$-a.s. for every $x>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $\alpha\in (0,1)$, then $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} X_{R_{2n}} = \lim\limits_{n\to\infty} V_n = +\infty$.
    \item If $\alpha\in (1,2)$, then $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} X_{R_{2n}} = \lim\limits_{n\to\infty} V_n = 0$.

    \]
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph of degree at most $\Delta$. Assume that Assumption \ref{primaryassumptionpaper} is satisfied for some $p_0\in(0,1)$, then with $\mathbb{P}_h$- probability at least $1-O_{\beta,\Delta,p_0}(\frac{1}{|V|})$ over the external field (here $O_{\beta,\Delta,p_0}$ denotes constants that may depend on $\beta$, $\Delta$ and $p_0$), the spectral gap of RFIM measure $\mu_G$ satisfies
    $$
    \mathbf{gap}_G\geq |V|^{-1}\exp\left(-\frac{16\beta\Delta\ln|V|}{\alpha_*}\right),
    $$
    and the $\epsilon$- mixing time of Glauber dynamics for $\mu_G$ is $$t_{mix}(P,\epsilon)=O\left(|V|^{1+\frac{16\beta\Delta}{\alpha_*}}\left(\beta\Delta|V|+\|h\|_1+\log(1/\epsilon)\right)\right).$$
Here $\|h\|_1:=\sum_{x\in V}|h_x|.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.02002

[Lemma lem:pigeonhole of arXiv:2601.04079, 'TV homogenization inequalities'] For $g:\mathbb{Z}\to[0,\infty)$
and $\mu\in\mathbb{R}$,
define
\[
  G := \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} g(k)
  \qquad
  J :=
  \sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} (k-\mu)^2\, g(k).
\]
If $0<G,J<\infty$, then
\[
  \sup_{k\in\mathbb{Z}} g(k)
  \;\ge\;
  \frac{G^{3/2}}{4\sqrt{J}+\sqrt{G}}.
\]

body:
[Proposition middle terms strategy of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] Let $n$ be even. Then, $I_{\frac{n}{2}}^*=I_{\frac{n}{2}+1}^*=\{n-1,n\}$, i.e. the player should guess card $n-1$ or card $n$ in positions $\frac{n}{2}$ and $\frac{n}{2}+1$. If $n$ is odd, card $n-1$ or card $n$ should be guessed in position $\frac{n+1}{2}$.
    \begin{proof}
        By Proposition $(guessing strategy symmetry of the paper)$ and Lemma $(last two rows are equal of the paper)$, it suffices to show that $n\in I_{\frac{n}{2}}^*$ and $k\notin I_{\frac{n}{2}}^*$ for $k\leq n-2$. We compute 
        \[p_{i,\frac{n}{2}}=\frac{\binom{i-1}{\frac{n}{2}-1}+\binom{i-1}{\frac{n}{2}}}{2^i}=\frac{\binom{i}{\frac{n}{2}}}{2^i}\]
        where the second equality is a consequence of Pascal's identity. Consider the sequence 
        \[a_i=\frac{\binom{i}{\frac{n}{2}}}{2^i}\]
        We note that $a_i=0$ for all $i\leq \frac{n}{2}-1$ and $a_i>0$ for all $i\geq \frac{n}{2}$. Now we examine the ratio of consecutive terms. Canceling factorials, we obtain
        \[R_i:=\frac{a_{i+1}}{a_i}=\frac{i+1}{2(i+1-\frac{n}{2})}\]
        Immediately, we have $R_{n-1}=1$ and $R_{i}<1$ for all $i\leq n-2$. This shows that $a_i$ is strictly increasing for all $\frac{n}{2}\leq i\leq n-1$ with $a_{n-1}=a_{n}$. This implies $a_{n-1}$ and $a_n$ are the unique maxima. But $a_n=p_{n,\frac{n}{2}}$, and the result follows. The construction for odd $n$ is nearly identical.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition middle terms strategy of arXiv:2507.10294

The independent set is \emph{maximal} if it is not a strict subset of another independent set, and it is \emph{maximum} if no other independent set has strictly more vertices. The abbreviation \emph{MIS} stands for a maximum independent set.

body:
Let d>=2 be an integer, let X=(a,b) have the standard Gaussian law on R^(2d), and let H_d={h_U(a,b)=sign(a^T U b): U in O(d)}. Define rho(h,g)=Pr[h(X)!=g(X)], and let D(H_d,rho,t) be its t-packing number. There is an absolute c>0 such that D(H_d,rho,t)>=(c/t)^(d(d-1)/2). Consequently any learner which, for each h in H_d, achieves disagreement error at most epsilon with probability at least 1-delta from n independent labeled examples must satisfy n >= (d(d-1)/2) log_2(c/(2epsilon)) + log_2(1-delta). This is useful for 0<epsilon<c/2 and fixed delta in (0,1). The class H_d is contained in the orthogonal orbit of f(x)=sign(sum_{i=1}^d x_i^2-sum_{i=d+1}^{2d} x_i^2). Thus an orthogonally equivariant learner of this single target under the standard Gaussian law has a fixed-confidence Omega(d^2 log(1/epsilon)) lower bound as epsilon decreases below an absolute constant. With expected disagreement risk epsilon, the corresponding explicit bound is (d(d-1)/2) log_2(c/(4epsilon))-1. This is an existing result of Li, Zhang and Arora, not new research; it concerns classification, not square-loss regression.
d is an integer >=2
Independent standard Gaussian input blocks a,b in R^d
Noiseless binary labels and disagreement loss
Independent training examples; randomized learners allowed
Orthogonal equivariance is required only for the single-target corollary
0<epsilon<c/2; fixed 0<delta<1 for the stated asymptotic; use epsilon<c/4 in the expected-risk formula

body:
Local escape bound (proof unaudited; no novelty or global burn-in claim). Fix n,m,d>=1, deterministic data ||x_i||<=1, y_i in {-1,1}, and a unit separator with margin gamma>0. Let phi be C1, phi(0)=0, alpha<=phi prime(z)<=1 for alpha>0, and phi prime beta-Lipschitz with beta>=0. For f_i=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x_i) and averaged logistic loss, train both layers simultaneously with actual GD step m eta, eta>0. Put v=phi prime(0) sum_i y_i x_i/(2n), b=||v||>=alpha gamma/2, h=eta b, Delta=min(h,2), and Lambda=1+h-Delta/4>1. Let P project each neuron block onto (1,v/b)/sqrt(2), Q=I-P, and R=||theta||. The GD map is M theta+E with expanding eigenvalue 1+h on P, complementary operator norm at most max(1,|1-h|), and ||E||<=eta(beta R^2/2+R^3/(8m)). For k>=1 and r>0 satisfying eta(beta r/2+r^2/(8m))sqrt(1+k^2)<=Delta/4, any theta_0 with 0<||Ptheta_0||, ||theta_0||<=r, ||Qtheta_0||<=k||Ptheta_0|| exits the closed radius-r ball by floor(log(r/||Ptheta_0||)/log Lambda)+1; the cone is invariant until exit. For delta in (0,1), put rho=(delta/2)^(1/m)/sqrt(exp(1)), k=sqrt(2(d+1)/delta)/rho, and choose such an r. If theta_0 has iid N(0,sigma^2) coordinates, sigma>0, sigma<=r sqrt(delta/(2m(d+1))), then with probability >=1-delta the exit time is <=floor(log(r/(sigma sqrt(m)rho))/log Lambda)+1. The probability proof uses an unconditional chi-square lower tail and a union bound. This does not cover unit-variance initialization in general or guarantee loss reduction or absence of returns after exit.
Both layers trained; fixed separable data; centered activation and positive leakage

[Proposition 9 (Loop equations) of arXiv:2511.05386, 'CLT for $\beta$-ensembles with Freud weights, application to the KLS conjecture in Schatte'] Let $p>2$. For all $N,q\geq1$, $\alpha\in[0,1]$, $z\in\C\setminus \R$, 
		\begin{align} 
			& \E_\alpha \left[ \left( 
			P_\alpha(z) + \frac{L_N(f_{\alpha,z})}{Nz} 
			+ \frac{1}{N}\left( \frac{2}{\beta}-1 \right) s_N'(z)
			\right) 
			P_\alpha(z)^{q-1} P_\alpha(\overline{z})^q \right] \nonumber \\
			& {} + \frac{2(q-1)}{\beta N^2 z} 
			\E_\alpha \left[ \left( 2s_N(z)+\frac{g_\alpha(z)}{z} \right)
			\left( \frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^N \frac{\lambda_k}{(\lambda_k - z)^3} \right)
			P_\alpha(z)^{q-2} P_\alpha(\overline{z})^q \right] \nonumber \\
			& {} + \frac{2q}{\beta N^2 z} 
			\E_\alpha \left[ \left( 2s_N(\overline{z}) + \frac{g_\alpha(\overline{z})}{\overline{z}} \right)
			\left( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k=1}^N \frac{\lambda_k}{(\lambda_k - \overline{z})^2(\lambda_k-z)} \right)
			P_\alpha(z)^{q-1} P_\alpha(\overline{z})^{q-1} \right]
			= 0. 
		\end{align}
