[Theorem 7 (Supercritical rigidity) of arXiv:2609.03339, 'Exterior Serrin Rigidity for the Homogeneous \texorpdfstring{$k$}{k}-Hessian Equation\\'] Let $\frac{n}{2}< k<n$, and let $\Omega\Subset\R^n$ be smooth,
		bounded, strictly star-shaped, and strictly $(k-1)$-convex.  Put
		\[
		\alpha=\frac{2k-n}{k},\qquad q=\frac{n-k}{k}=1-\alpha.
		\]
		For some $\mathfrak a>0$, suppose that the exterior  k-admissible 
		solution $u\in C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\overline E)$ satisfies
			\begin{equation}
			\begin{cases}
				\sigma_k(D^2u)=0&\text{in }~\R^n\setminus\overline\Omega,\\
				u=1& \text{on}~\partial\Omega,\\
				u(x)-\mathfrak a|x|^\alpha=O(1)&\text{as }|x|\to\infty.
			\end{cases}
		\end{equation}	
	
	
	
	
	
		If $u_\nu=|Du|=c>0$ on $\partial\Omega$, then for some
		$x_0\in\R^n$,
		\[
		\Omega=B_R(x_0),\qquad
		R=\left(\frac{\mathfrak a\alpha}{c}\right)^{1/q},
		\]
		and
		\[
		u(x)=\mathfrak a|x-x_0|^\alpha+1-\mathfrak aR^\alpha.
		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Supercritical rigidity

[Thm cltn of arXiv:2412.06480, 'A SIR epidemic model on a refining spatial grid \\ II-Central limit theorem'] ~\\
	Assume that $\sqrt{\mathbf{N}}\big( Z_{\mathbf{N},\varepsilon}(0)- Z_{\varepsilon}(0)\big) \longrightarrow 0 $, as $ \mathbf{N}\to \infty $.\\ Then, as $ \mathbf{N} \rightarrow + \infty$ , $\big\{\begin{array}{rl}  \Psi_{\mathbf{N},\varepsilon} (t) ,  \; t\geq 0   \end{array} \big\} \Longrightarrow \big\{\begin{array}{rl} \Psi_{\varepsilon}(t) , \; t\geq 0  \end{array}\big\} ,  $ for the topology of locally uniform convergence, where  the limit process
	$ \Psi_{\varepsilon}(t) := \left( \begin{array}{cl}
	U_{\varepsilon}(t)\\
	V_{\varepsilon}(t)\\
	W_{\varepsilon}(t)
	\end{array}
	\right) $ satisfies
	\begin{equation}
	\Psi_{\varepsilon}(t) = \int_0^t \nabla_{\!\!z} b_{\varepsilon}\big(r,Z_{\varepsilon}(r)\big) \Psi_{\varepsilon}(r)dr + \sum_{j=1}^{K}\int_0^t \sqrt{\beta_j\big(r,Z_{\varepsilon}(r)}\big)dB_j(r) , \quad t \geq 0, 
	\end{equation}
	and $ \displaystyle \{ B_1(t), B_2(t), \cdots, B_K(t) \}$ are mutually independent standard Brownian motions. \\
	More precisely, by setting $ A_{\varepsilon}=S_{\varepsilon} +I_{\varepsilon}+R_{\varepsilon}$, for any site $x_i$, the limit $(U_{\varepsilon}, V_{\varepsilon}, W_{\varepsilon})^{\mathtt{T}}$ satisfies the following system
	\begin{eqnarray}
	\hspace{-0.5cm}U_{\varepsilon}(t,x_i)
	&  = & \mu_{S} \int_0^t \Delta_{\varepsilon}U_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)dr -  \int_0^t \beta(x_i) \dfrac{I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)\big(I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)+R_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)\big)V_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}{A_{\varepsilon}^2(r,x_i)} dr\nonumber  \\
	&- & \int_0^t\beta(x_i) \dfrac{S_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)\big(S_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)+R_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)\big)U_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}{A_{\varepsilon}^2(r,x_i)}  dr
	+\int_0^t \sqrt{\beta(x_i)\dfrac{S_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}{A_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}}\; \; dB_{x_i}^{inf}(r)\nonumber  \\
	&- &\sum_{y_i \sim x_i}\int_0^t\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_{S}}{\varepsilon ^2} S_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}\; \; dB_{x_iy_i}^S(r) 
	+\sum_{y_i \sim x_i}\int_0^t\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_{S}}{\varepsilon ^2} S_{\varepsilon}(r,y_i)}\; \; dB_{y_ix_i}^S(r) \nonumber
	\end{eqnarray}
\begin{eqnarray}
V_{\varepsilon}(t,x_i)
&=& \mu_{I} \int_0^t \Delta_{\varepsilon}V_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)dr +\int_0^t \beta(x_i) \dfrac{I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)\big(I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)+R_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)\big)V_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}{A_{\varepsilon}^2(r,x_i)} dr\nonumber  \\
&+&\int_0^t\beta(x_i) \dfrac{S_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)\big(S_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)+R_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)\big)U_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}{A_{\varepsilon}^2(r,x_i)}dr-\int_0^t \alpha(x_i)V_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)dr\nonumber\\
&-&\int_0^t\sqrt{\beta(x_i)\dfrac{S_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}{A_{\varepsilon}^2(r,x_i)}}\; \; dB_{x_i}^{inf}(r)+\int_0^t\sqrt{\alpha(x_i) I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}\; \; dB_{x_i}^{rec}(r) \nonumber\\
&-& \sum_{y_i \sim x_i}\int_0^t\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_{I}}{\varepsilon ^2} I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}dB_{x_iy_i}^I(r)+ \sum_{y_i \sim x_i}\int_0^t\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_{I}}{\varepsilon ^2} I_{\varepsilon}(r,y_i)}\; \; dB_{y_ix_i}^I(r)  \nonumber 
\end{eqnarray}
\begin{eqnarray}
W_{\varepsilon}(t,x_i) 
& =& \mu_{R} \int_0^t \Delta_{\varepsilon}W_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)dr+ \int_0^t \alpha(x_i) V_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)dr-\int_0^t\sqrt{\alpha(x_i) I_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}\; \; dB_{x_i}^{rec}(r) \nonumber
\\[2mm]
&-& \sum_{y_i \sim x_i}\int_0^t\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_{R}}{\varepsilon ^2} R_{\varepsilon}(r,x_i)}\; \;dB_{x_iy_i}^R(r)+ \sum_{y_i \sim x_i}\int_0^t\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_{R}}{\varepsilon ^2} R_{\varepsilon}(r,y_i)}\; \; dB_{y_ix_i}^R(r), \nonumber 
\end{eqnarray} 
where $\{ B_{x_i}^{inf}: x_i\in \mathrm{D}_\varepsilon \}$ , $\{ B_{x_i}^{rec} : x_i\in \mathrm{D}_\varepsilon \}$ , $\{ B_{x_i y_i}^S   : y_i \sim x_i\in \mathrm{D}_\varepsilon \}$ , $\{ B_{x_i y_i}^I   : y_i \sim x_i\in \mathrm{D}_\varepsilon \}$ and $\{ B_{x_i y_i}^R   : y_i \sim x_i\in \mathrm{D}_\varepsilon \}$ are  families of independent Brownian motions. Own-work draft; T419-C013 v1, proof (unaudited), no novelty claimed; counterexample only to a specified formulation. Fix arbitrary m,p>=2, nonzero rank-one Delta in R^(m by p), s>0, sigma>0 and integer n>p+1. Let x_i iid N(0,I_p), z_i=Delta x_i+e_i with e_i iid N(0,sigma^2 I_m), and independent rank-one initialization b_0=0, a_0~N(0,s^2 I_p). Run simultaneous factor GD on sum_i ||b a^T x_i-z_i||^2/(2n), with any finite positive step eta chosen independently of initialization (it may be a measurable function of the data), held fixed in time. Then liminf_(t->infinity) E ||b_t a_t^T-Delta||F^2=infinity, whereas rank-one reduced-rank regression has finite expected population excess risk. This holds for arbitrarily large n and target condition number 1. The lower-limit risk is infinite on a positive-probability escape event. Deterministically, for C=XX^T/n positive definite, D=ZX^T/n nonzero, lambda=lambda_min(C), L=||D||op, the region ||a||^2,||b||^2>=6/(eta lambda), ||a||||b||>=2L/lambda is invariant and each factor norm grows by at least 2 per update. A Gaussian a_0 reaches its strict interior at iteration 1 on a nonempty open set. Fatou's lemma gives the expected-risk conclusion. This does not rule out high-probability results, initialization-dependent or adaptive steps, or finite statistical stopping; it does not settle the whole target.
Rank-one target and rank-one factors; arbitrary m,p>=2; n>p+1
Independent standard Gaussian inputs, positive-variance isotropic Gaussian label noise and nondegenerate Gaussian input-factor initialization
Finite positive constant step chosen independently of initialization; expectation includes initialization

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:4d16361291995c305d5f3644e2d820875067d5d12ba2dc11a25d2f99f8d68e32","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/4d/4d16361291995c305d5f3644e2d820875067d5d12ba2dc11a25d2f99f8d68e32.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:df3997f0310034279a485959cec33d2de0603a4e53a05f4c1618f49dd2d73aeb","bundle_entry_key":"expected-risk-escape","bundle_id":"population.t419-lora-all-scale-square-input-and-expected-risk-scope-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA factor gradient descent","draft":"w705/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-fixed-step-gaussian-initialization-expected-risk-divergence","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C013 v1: fixed-step unconditional expected-limit risk can diverge

Kind: route-failure (counterexample to a specified interpretation of Target 2). Target: 2.
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim. This concerns the fixed-positive-step, unconditional expected-limit-risk version, not all possible GD algorithms or the whole written target.

## Deterministic escape lemma, arbitrary input and output dimensions

Let X be a p-by-n full-row-rank design and Z an m-by-n residual-label matrix. Write C=XX^T/n, D=ZX^T/n and assume D is nonzero. Put lambda=lambda_min(C)>0, L=||D||op>0. For rank-one factors b in R^m and a in R^p, simultaneous GD with any fixed eta>0 on

 f(b,a)=(1/(2n))||b a^T X-Z||F^2

has the updates

 b_next=(1-eta a^T C a)b+eta D a,
 a_next=(I-eta ||b||^2 C)a+eta D^T b.

Define alpha=||a||, beta=||b|| and the closed escape region

 alpha^2>=6/(eta lambda), beta^2>=6/(eta lambda),
 alpha beta>=2L/lambda.

If an iterate is in this region, the next iterate satisfies

 ||a_next||>=2alpha, ||b_next||>=2beta.

To prove the b bound, eta a^TCa>=6 and the reverse triangle inequality give

 ||b_next|| >= (eta lambda alpha^2-1)beta-eta L alpha
             >= (eta lambda alpha^2/2-1)beta>=2beta,

where L alpha <= lambda alpha^2 beta/2 follows from alpha beta>=2L/lambda. For the a bound, every eigenvalue of I-eta beta^2 C is negative, and its least singular value is at least eta beta^2 lambda-1. Therefore

 ||a_next|| >= (eta lambda beta^2-1)alpha-eta L beta
             >= (eta lambda beta^2/2-1)alpha>=2alpha.

The escape region is invariant, so both norms grow at least by 2 per step. Since the product is rank one,

 ||b_t a_t^T||F=||a_t||||b_t||

grows at least by 4 per step. This argument does not require the factor directions to remain aligned, C to be diagonal or near identity, or a relation between the input and output dimensions.

## Positive-probability entry from the prescribed initialization

Initialize b0=0 and a0~N(0,s^2 I_p), s>0, independently of the data. Then

 a1=a0, b1=eta D a0.

Because D is nonzero, choose a unit vector w with ||Dw||>0. Taking a0=t w with t sufficiently large makes all three escape-region inequalities strict at iteration 1. By continuity they remain strict on a nonempty open ball around t w. A nondegenerate Gaussian law gives that ball positive probability. Thus for every fixed dataset with C positive definite and D nonzero, and every fixed eta>0, the prescribed initialization has strictly positive probability of entering the invariant escape region at its very first update.

The same argument permits eta to be any finite positive measurable function of the training dataset, provided it is chosen independently of a0 and then held constant throughout the iterations. It does not cover initialization-dependent or iteration-dependent step rules.

## Consequence for the named statistical target

Fix any dimensions m,p>=2, any nonzero rank-one signal Delta, any s>0, and Gaussian regression data

 x_i iid N(0,I_p), z_i=Delta x_i+e_i,
 e_i iid N(0,sigma^2 I_m), sigma>0,

with all inputs, label noises and initialization independent. Choose any n>p+1. The design has full row rank almost surely. Conditional on X, the sample cross matrix D has a nondegenerate Gaussian perturbation, so D is nonzero almost surely. Conditional escape probability is strictly positive almost surely, hence its joint probability is positive; no multiplication of unrelated probability bounds is involved.

On the escape event,

 R_t=||b_t a_t^T-Delta||F^2 -> infinity,

because R_t^(1/2)>=||a_t||||b_t||-||Delta||F. Isotropic population excess prediction risk equals R_t. Fatou's lemma for the nonnegative R_t gives

 liminf_(t->infinity) E R_t >= E[liminf_(t->infinity) R_t] = infinity.

In contrast, the global rank-one reduced-rank regression estimator has finite expected population risk at every n>p+1, by C002's exact-rank Gaussian-design specialization of Zindari-Mulayoff-Stich Theorem 2. Its inverse-covariance expectation is finite in this sample-size regime. Therefore no finite constant factor compares the limiting expected risk of this fixed-step GD to the reduced-rank estimator under these conditions.

This holds for arbitrarily large n, including n>=C0(m+p) for every proposed universal sample-size constant C0. The nonzero signal has condition number 1 because it has rank one. Hence the sample-size and target-condition-number requirements alone cannot rescue this version of Target 2. This is an infinite family with arbitrary input/output dimensions, not a scalar-only example or a zero-noise finite-time technicality.

## Exact limitation and relation to earlier claims

This does not rule out a high-probability guarantee, conditioning on a bounded initialization event, initialization-dependent steps, adaptive steps, clipping/restarts, or statistically chosen finite stopping. It does not claim that any of those alternatives achieves the target. It identifies assumptions that an unconditional fixed-step expected-limit-risk theorem must address.

C003 and C012 only assert high-probability convergence on explicit Gaussian initial events. Their positive-probability complements cannot be discarded when computing an unconditional expectation. The present escape result is compatible with both high-probability bounds.

Mu-Klabjan's norm-dependent step restriction in equation (8) is relevant prior context, but this escape proof is elementary and does not invoke their theorem or any unverified random-matrix limit. Existing-literature novelty is unresolved; a discovery search is recorded, not treated as evidence of absence. # Joint low-noise central-window bifurcation

T267 / Target 2 / C012 / proof draft (unaudited); novelty unestablished.
This is a local, rescaled noise-onset result in C010's restricted model.
It is not an exact global two-critical-noise-level theorem.

## 1. Precise scaling and result

Use C010's four-point stratified design, centered unit-norm ReLU teacher,
paired nonzero initialization with fixed nu in (0,1], both-layer GD with
step 1/2, and label-noise-averaged clean risk Q. Let alpha=alpha_e and
let b_h denote C009's full-kernel rates. Set

eta_e=(b2+b12)/b1 ~ e,
rho_e=kappa sqrt(eta_e), kappa>0 fixed,
sigma_e=2alpha sqrt(rho_e),
t0_e=log(1/sqrt(eta_e)).

Here sigma_e is the amplitude of independent symmetric label noise.
It is asymptotic to sqrt(kappa) e^(9/4). The network step size remains
1/2; eta_e in this proof is a spectral ratio, not that step size.

Let F_e(z) be the continuously interpolated frozen risk divided by
alpha^2. Define its central-time version
G_e(s)=F_e((t0_e+s)/b1). Then, uniformly on compact real s intervals,

G_e'(s)/(2 eta_e) -> H_kappa(s)
       =kappa exp(-s)-exp(-2s)-1,
G_e''(s)/(2 eta_e) -> H_kappa'(s)
       =-kappa exp(-s)+2exp(-2s).

Equivalently, the normalized value differences converge locally uniformly:

[G_e(s)-G_e(0)]/(2 eta_e) -> V_kappa(s)-V_kappa(0),
V_kappa(s)=-kappa exp(-s)+(1/2)exp(-2s)-s.

If kappa>2, define z_+=(kappa+sqrt(kappa^2-4))/2 and
z_-=(kappa-sqrt(kappa^2-4))/2. The frozen curve has a central strict local
minimum at scaled time tending to s_min=-log z_+, and a subsequent strict
local maximum at scaled time tending to s_max=-log z_-.
In small fixed neighborhoods of those two points there is exactly one
frozen stationary point of the indicated type for sufficiently small e.
The actual nonlinear discrete-GD risk has strict descent-rise-descent
witnesses near these points, with probability tending to one in the
iterated even-width-then-feature-scale limit. Its interval minimizers and
maximizers on these separate neighborhoods have the same scaled limits.
Its resulting central local peak obeys

b1 k_peak-t0_e -> s_max,
k_peak ~ (2pi/nu^2) e^(-1) log(1/e),

in that iterated probabilistic sense. The first assertion refers to every
maximizer in a chosen sufficiently small neighborhood of s_max; it does
not assert that all actual extrema are unique.

For 0<kappa<2, the FROZEN interpolated risk is strictly decreasing on any
fixed compact central s window for sufficiently small e. No monotonicity
of actual finite-width risk is asserted. At kappa=2 the leading derivative
has a degenerate zero; this proof does not resolve its finite-e unfolding.
Thus 2 is a threshold for this limiting central-window shape, not a proved
global critical noise level or a global absence theorem.

## 2. Uniform derivative limit

The exact frozen curve is
F_e(z)=rho_e(1-exp(-b0 z))^2
      +sum_(h=1,2,12)[exp(-2b_h z)+rho_e(1-exp(-b_h z))^2].
Its nonconstant h derivative with respect to z is
2 b_h q_h [rho_e-(1+rho_e)q_h], q_h=exp(-b_h z).
At z=(t0_e+s)/b1, q1=sqrt(eta_e)exp(-s). Therefore its contribution to
G_e'(s)/(2eta_e) is exactly
kappa exp(-s)-(1+kappa sqrt(eta_e))exp(-2s).

For h=2,12, b_h/b1=O(eta_e) and
q_h=1+O(eta_e log(1/eta_e)), uniformly on compact s sets. Their combined
contribution to G_e'(s)/(2eta_e) tends to -1, since their b_h/b1 weights
sum to eta_e. Differentiating with respect to s makes their contribution
tend to zero: the extra b_h/b1 factor is O(eta_e).
The constant-mode term and its s derivatives tend to zero after division
by eta_e. Indeed b0/b1 is of order 1/e, t0_e is of order log(1/e), and
exp[-(b0/b1)(t0_e+s)] decays faster than every power of e on compact s
sets. These exact formulas prove both uniform derivative limits.
Integration from zero proves the uniform value-difference limit.

## 3. Limiting stationary points and risk witnesses

Writing z=exp(-s)>0, H_kappa=kappa z-z^2-1.
For kappa>2 its roots are z_+>1 and z_-<1 with product one.
At s_min=-log z_+, H_kappa'=z_+ sqrt(kappa^2-4)>0;
at s_max=-log z_-, H_kappa'=-z_- sqrt(kappa^2-4)<0.
Thus V has a strict minimum then a strict maximum. Compact uniform
convergence of H and H' gives a unique frozen critical point near each,
of the same type; the derivative is bounded away from zero outside small
root neighborhoods inside a fixed central compact window.

Choose delta>0 sufficiently small. The four scaled times
s_min-delta, s_min, s_max, s_max+delta are increasing and have strict
limiting value inequalities descent-rise-descent. Rounded integer times
floor((t0_e+s)/b1) have scaled grid error at most b1, which tends to zero.
The associated frozen risk differences therefore have strictly positive
margins of order alpha^2 eta_e. The same value convergence provides a
strict gap away from the unique minimum or maximum in each separate
small neighborhood.

For 0<kappa<2, completion of the square gives
H_kappa=-(z-kappa/2)^2+kappa^2/4-1<0 for every z>0.
Its maximum is strictly negative, so compact uniform derivative
convergence implies the stated frozen decrease on each fixed compact
s window. This does not control scaled times escaping all compacts.

## 4. Actual nonlinear GD and order of limits

For each fixed e, rho_e, alpha_e and all interval endpoints are fixed
numbers, and all involved integer times lie below T_e=ceil(e^(-5/2))
for sufficiently small e. Labels remain bounded. C010's independent-pair
finite-horizon comparison therefore controls every involved actual risk
uniformly through T_e as width grows, including all sixteen noise
patterns. Multiplication of the error by the fixed positive factor
1/(alpha_e^2 eta_e) preserves convergence to zero for this FIXED e.
It follows, first taking width to infinity then e to zero, that the
actual risk value differences converge to the same V differences and
inherit the strict four witnesses. The positive local value gaps transfer
the interval minimizers and maximizers to s_min and s_max. No derivative
comparison for the actual nonlinear network is needed or claimed.

Finally eta_e~e, b1~nu^2 e/(4pi), so t0_e~(1/2)log(1/e) and the displayed
peak time follows. This theorem concerns a different joint-noise regime
from C011's fixed-rho phase comparison; neither proof exchanges limits.

## 5. Exact concrete witness certificate, kappa=5/2

Here z_+=2, z_-=1/2. Use z values 3,2,1/2,1/4 in decreasing order,
so the corresponding s=-log z and integer times increase. The primitive
values are respectively

-3+log 3, -3+log 2, -9/8-log 2, -19/32-2log 2.

Their required margins are
log(3/2), 15/8-2log 2, log 2-17/32, all strictly positive.
For fully checkable bounds, log(3/2)>1/3 and
7/12<log 2<3/4 follow from integrals of 1/t: the lower bound splits
[1,2] into [1,3/2] and [3/2,2] and uses right-endpoint rectangles.
For the upper bound write t=1+x and use
1/(1+x)<=1-x/2 on [0,1], strict in the interior, since the difference
has numerator x(1-x)/2. The margins exceed 1/3,3/8,5/96 respectively.
This certifies a specific joint-noise witness choice by exact rational
bounds, not a floating-point estimate of a bifurcation.

## Remaining scope

The exact finite-e global onset, the degenerate kappa=2 case, interaction
with the initial constant-mode transient, iid sampling, fixed-positive
noise and all-time nonlinear dynamics remain open. These restrictions
matter: a central-window derivative result cannot imply that no other
double-descent pattern occurs elsewhere in time. Pairing and finite
support remain as in C010. Dependencies C009/C010 and this argument
await independent mathematical review; specialist novelty is unestablished.
All restricted four-point, unit-norm centered-ReLU teacher and paired nonzero initialization assumptions of C010
Independent label noise amplitude sigma_e=c_e sqrt(kappa) eta_e^(1/4)~sqrt(kappa)e^(9/4)
Noise-averaged clean risk; simultaneous both-layer GD step 1/2; fixed nu in (0,1]
Even width limit precedes feature-scale limit; local windows only; eta_e is spectral ratio, not GD step size

[Theorem thm.ctfg of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] Assume that $E=G$ is a graph, $\mu$ is any measure on the vertices of $G$ and $\lambda_n\downarrow 0$ such that $F(n)^{-1}\leq \lambda_n \leq F(n-1)^{-1}$. Then, $X^{(\lambda_n)}$ converges weakly (after a suitable shift) to a nonempty point process on the extended boundary (say $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$) if and only if:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item $\restrict{F}{\mathbb N}$ is log-regularly-varying with positive index (say $b$),
			\item the probability measure $F(n)^{-1} \restrict{\mu}{B_n(\mathbf{o})}$ converges weakly to a probability measure on $\partial G$ (say $\nu_0$) as $n\to\infty$, and
			\item $\lim_{n \to \infty} \lambda_n F(n) = e^{b\xi}$ for some $\xi$. 
		\end{enumerate}
		If these conditions hold, then $(\Theta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ are i.i.d. points on $\partial G$ with distribution $\nu_0$ and $(\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ is an independent Poisson point process on $\mathbb Z$ with intensity measure $\beta^{(\xi)}(i)\coloneqq (p-1)p^{i-1+\xi}$, where $p\coloneqq e^b$. In addition, the corresponding Poisson--Voronoi diagrams also converge to the IPVT corresponding to $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$, {which we denote by ${\rm IPVT}_{\xi}(G)$}, \underline{without} any non-degeneracy condition. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsc{Full Convergence for Graphs}

[Lemma lem:write_mod_as_signature of arXiv:2605.10911, 'The stochastic block model has the overlap graph property for modularity'] [\bf Concentration of modularity]
Fix $a>b>0$ and integer $k\geq 2$. Let $p=p(n)=\omega\; a / n$ and $q=q(n)=\omega \; b/n$. For any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $c=c(\varepsilon)$ such that if $\omega>c$ for $n$ large enough, then the following holds with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$ provided $n$ is large enough.

Let $G \in \mathcal{G}(n,k,p,q)$. For all $k$-part partitions $\mathcal{A}$, 
\[ 
\left| q_\mathcal{A}(G) - \frac{a-b}{(a+(k-1)b)} \cdot \frac {g(X)}{k^2} \right| < \varepsilon, 
\]
where $X = X(\mathcal{A}) =(x_{ij})_{1\leq i,j \leq k}$ is the signature of $\mathcal{A}$ and $g(X)$ is defined  in~(equation defn.gx of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:write_mod_as_signature of arXiv:2605.10911

Then $\nu_{t}=\mu_{t}$, where $\mu_{t}$ is defined in $\text{\eqref{def misura inv}}$.

body: The Erdős–Straus conjecture is an unproven statement in number theory. The conjecture is that, for every integer $n$ that is greater than or equal to 2, there exist positive integers $x$, $y$, and $z$ for which ${\frac {4}{n}}={\frac {1}{x}}+{\frac {1}{y}}+{\frac {1}{z}}.$ In other words, the number $4/n$ can be written as a sum of three positive unit fractions.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2608.28410, 'Mean curvatures and symmetry\\of convex hypersurfaces'] Let $E\in Gr(n+1,\ol{m})$ with $\ol e:=P_Ee\ne0$. Then
$$
L^+_\xi(t)
=
\sup_{\substack{x\in\cl(\Omega)\\P_{\ol E}x=\xi}}
\left\{
\frac{\langle x,\ol e\rangle}{|\ol e|^2}+r(x)+tc(x)
\right\},
\quad
L^-_\xi(t)
=
\inf_{\substack{x\in\cl(\Omega)\\P_{\ol E}x=\xi}}
\left\{
\frac{\langle x,\ol e\rangle}{|\ol e|^2}-r(x)+tc(x)
\right\}.
$$
In particular, $L^+_\xi$ is convex and $L^-_\xi$ is concave in $t$, and, for each fixed $t$, the function $\xi\mapsto\ell_\xi(t)$ is continuous on $\inte(P_{\ol E}\Omega)$.

DRAFT own-work, proof (unaudited), w724-T321-C010 v1. No claim of novelty or a solved Poincare bound. For a fixed unit teacher v in R^d, set z_i=a_i.v, L(x)=mean_i((a_i.x)^2-z_i^2)^2, M=mean_i z_i^2 a_i a_i^T and K={v+h: |a_i.h|<=|z_i|/4 for all i}. Deterministically Hess L(x)>=(11/4)M for every x in K. If all z_i are nonzero, K is convex with v in its interior; if M is positive definite, K is bounded. For d>=2, a teacher v fixed independently of iid a_i~N(0,I_d), q=P(1<=|N(0,1)|<=2), and m>=512d/q, with probability at least 1-5exp(-qm/256), M>=(3q/32)I and Hess L(x)>=(33q/128)I simultaneously for every x in K. Hence Hess(beta L)>=(33q beta/128)I there for all beta>0 on that same event. No lower bound on Gibbs mass of K or local/global Poincare constant is supplied. The inradius can be tiny.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:0118877761d80afd07719e3bb9680b156a64c3b5cd34e3b1ad96e309124ec743","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/01/0118877761d80afd07719e3bb9680b156a64c3b5cd34e3b1ad96e309124ec743.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:5c44bd70031e38eabe177d1559e7c3719dcc3578819b2aabec320e8c0185599b","bundle_entry_key":"local-convexity","bundle_id":"population.t321-local-measurement-polytope-convexity-unaudited","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability and statistical learning","draft":"w724/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.functional.inequalities:phase-retrieval-local-measurement-polytope-convexity-w724-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A local convex region without global rank-two RIP

T321 Target 2, supporting local-well lemma. Status: proof (unaudited).
This supplies a local Hessian ingredient; no global or quotient Poincare bound
and no claim of novelty or scored frontier move is made.

DETERMINISTIC STATEMENT. Fix a unit v in R^d and measurement vectors a_i,
with z_i=a_i.v nonzero for every i. Put
 L(x)=mean_i((a_i.x)^2-z_i^2)^2,
 M=mean_i z_i^2 a_i a_i^T,
 K={v+h: |a_i.h|<=|z_i|/4 for every i}.
For x in K,

 Hess L(x) >= (11/4) M.                                (1)

Indeed Hess L(x)=mean_i[12(a_i.x)^2-4z_i^2]a_i a_i^T.
The defining inequalities give |a_i.x|>=3|z_i|/4. Hence each coefficient
is at least [12(3/4)^2-4]z_i^2=(11/4)z_i^2. Summing positive-semidefinite
rank-one forms preserves the order. This is a lower bound only; it does
not use any uniform empirical fourth-moment upper bound or matrix RIP.
K is convex, contains v in its interior and, if M>0, is bounded: its
defining inequalities imply h^T M h<=mean_i z_i^4/16. The inradius bound
min_i |z_i|/(4 max_i||a_i||)>0 is valid but can be very small.

GAUSSIAN STATEMENT. Let d>=2, v fixed before the sample, and a_i iid N(0,I_d).
Let q=P(1<=|Z|<=2)>0 for Z~N(0,1). If m>=512d/q, then, except on an event
of probability at most 5 exp(-qm/256),

 M >= (3q/32) I, and Hess L(x)>=(33q/128)I for all x in K. (2)

All z_i are nonzero almost surely, so K has nonempty interior. The assertion
is about the single sample event in (2), uniformly in x in K and beta>0;
it is not a product of rowwise conditional probabilities.

Proof of (2). Select I={i:1<=|z_i|<=2} and n=|I|. The indicators are iid
Bernoulli(q). For completeness, Markov applied to 2^{-n} gives
 P(n<=qm/2)<=exp(qm log(2)/2)(1-q/2)^m<=exp(-qm/8),
using 1-t<=exp(-t) and log(2)<=3/4. The latter follows by integrating
1/t on [1,2] and using its trapezoidal upper bound. On n>=qm/2 we have
n>=256d>=512.

Write a_i=z_i v+w_i. Conditional on all z_i, the selected w_i are iid
standard Gaussian on v-perp. Assemble the n-by-d selected-row matrix
D=[z W] in an orthonormal basis beginning with v. Choose a row-orthogonal
matrix Q taking z to ||z||e_1. Since Q depends only on z, conditional on z
the matrix QW is still iid Gaussian. Write its first row as w_0 and its
remaining (n-1)-by-(d-1) matrix as W_perp. We use the Gaussian singular
value estimate of Vershynin arXiv:1011.3027, Corollary 5.35, namely
 P(sigma_max(G)>sqrt(N)+sqrt(k)+t)<=2exp(-t^2/2),
 P(sigma_min(G)<sqrt(N)-sqrt(k)-t)<=2exp(-t^2/2)
for an N-by-k iid standard Gaussian matrix; the second bound is used
with N>=k. No conditional independence of the two estimates is required.

Applied to the (d-1)-by-1 column w_0 with t=sqrt(n)/8, the first estimate
gives ||w_0||<=sqrt(d-1)+1+sqrt(n)/8<=sqrt(n)/4,
except with probability 2exp(-n/128). Here sqrt(d-1)<=sqrt(n)/16 and
1<=sqrt(n)/16 follow from n>=256d and d>=2.
Applied to W_perp with t=sqrt(n)/4, the second estimate gives
sigma_min(W_perp)>=sqrt(n-1)-sqrt(d-1)-sqrt(n)/4>=sqrt(n)/2,
except with probability 2exp(-n/32). For the last inequality one may use
sqrt(n-1)>=7sqrt(n)/8 and sqrt(d-1)<=sqrt(n)/8; both follow from the
displayed dimension conditions. Thus the conditional failure probability
for these two events is at most 4exp(-n/128), by a union bound.

For a scalar a and b in R^(d-1), on those events,
 ||D(a,b)||^2=(||z||a+w_0.b)^2+||W_perp b||^2
 >= (n/2)a^2-(n/16)||b||^2+(n/4)||b||^2
 >= (3n/16)(a^2+||b||^2).
Here ||z||^2>=n, Cauchy-Schwarz bounds (w_0.b)^2, and
(s+t)^2>=s^2/2-t^2 follows from the identity
(s+t)^2-s^2/2+t^2=(s+2t)^2/2>=0.
The estimate is simultaneous in (a,b) because it follows from operator
norm and least-singular-value events, not a union over directions.

Since z_i^2>=1 on selected rows,
 M>=D^T D/m >=3n I/(16m)>=3q I/32.
Integrating the conditional failure bound on n>=qm/2 and adding the
binomial failure gives exp(-qm/8)+4exp(-qm/256)<=5exp(-qm/256).
Together with (1) this proves (2). The same event proves Hess(beta L)
>=(33q beta/128)I on K for every beta>0.

SOURCE AND LIMITS. Gaussian singular-value estimates are already sourced
in this worker's papers/1011.3027 PDF and the Target 1 proof. This argument
adapts that tool to a fixed-teacher weighted covariance using selected rows.
The source estimate is used conditionally only after preserving the iid
Gaussian law through a z-measurable orthogonal row transformation.

K is not asserted to contain a dimension-independent ball, most Gibbs
mass, or a typical low-temperature fluctuation. A local Hessian bound
alone supplies neither confinement nor a global quotient gap. A correct
convex-support Poincare theorem would turn this into a conditional local
gap; that functional-inequality step is not asserted as proved here.
The next unpaid step is to replace or enlarge this potentially narrow K
while preserving quantitative control, and then handle its complement.

CHECKS. The boundary factor 3/4 is retained before squaring, the Hessian
coefficient is exactly 11/4, the selected-row count is at least 256d,
and the covariance coefficient is 3q/32. Gaussian upper-tail and lower-tail
events are added, never multiplied. The teacher must be fixed; adaptively
choosing v after seeing a_i would invalidate the conditional Gaussian law.

body:
[Theorem 44 of arXiv:2606.16164, 'A Low-Regularity Semigroup Sewing Lemma via Quotient Structures'] Fix an admissible scale-dependent selection rule $\mathsf s$ on a domain $\D^{\mathsf s}_{\gamma}(\Delta_T^3;B_\alpha)$.  Let $p\in[1,\infty)$.
If $0<\gamma<1$ and $H\in L^p\big(\Omega; \D^{\mathsf s}_{\gamma}(\Delta_T^3;B_\alpha)\big)$, then $R^{\mathsf s}:=\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf s}_{S,\gamma,\alpha}H$ satisfies
\begin{equation}

\mathbb E\left[\norm{R^{\mathsf s}}_{\gamma,\alpha}^p\right]\le C^p \mathbb E\left[\norm{H}_{\gamma,\alpha}^p\right]
\end{equation}
and $\hdd R^{\mathsf s}=H$ almost surely.  For a family of individual random defects not lying in one fixed linear domain, the same estimate holds with the right-hand side replaced by
\[
C^p\mathbb E\left[\bigl(\norm{H}_{\gamma,\alpha}+C_H(\omega)\bigr)^p\right].
\]
If $H\in L^p\big(\Omega;\D^{\mathsf s}_{1}(\Delta_T^3;B_\alpha)\big)$, then $R^{\mathsf s}:=\hat\Lambda^{\mathsf s}_{S,1,\alpha}H$ satisfies
\begin{equation}

\mathbb E\left[\norm{R^{\mathsf s}}_{1,\log;\alpha}^p\right]\le C^p\mathbb E\left[\norm{H}_{1,\alpha}^p\right]
\end{equation}
and $\hdd R^{\mathsf s}=H$ almost surely.  Again, for individual defects one may replace $\norm{H}_{1,\alpha}$ by $\norm{H}_{1,\alpha}+C_H(\omega)$.

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2608.31145, 'Gauge-compatible tensors on statistical manifolds: splitting and submanifold geometry'] Let $(M,g,\nabla,\nabla^{*},\Theta)$ be a Levi-Civita-parallel
$\Theta$-statistical manifold. Assume that the tangent bundle admits the orthogonal decomposition
\[
TM=\ker\Theta\oplus\operatorname{Im}\Theta.
\]
Then both distributions are preserved by
\[
\nabla^{g},\ \nabla,\ \nabla^{*},
\]
and
\begin{equation}
K_XY=0
\end{equation}
whenever one of $X,Y$ belongs to $\ker\Theta$ and the other belongs to
$\operatorname{Im}\Theta$.

Consequently, every point of $M$ admits a neighborhood $U$ for which
\[
(U,g,\nabla,\nabla^{*})
\cong
(U_0,g_0,\nabla^{0},(\nabla^{0})^{*})
\times
(U_1,g_1,\nabla^{1},(\nabla^{1})^{*}),
\]
where
\[
TU_0=\ker\Theta,
\qquad
TU_1=\operatorname{Im}\Theta.
\]
Thus the two local factors inherit statistical structures.

body:
[Definition def:initialization-coupling of arXiv:2605.08052, 'Rapid phase ordering of Ising dynamics on $\mathbb Z^2$'] [Time-zero monotone coupling] Assign each vertex in $\mathbb Z^d$ at time $0$ two $\text{Unif}[0,1]$ random variables $(\mathcal U_{v,0}^\pi)_{v\in \mathbb Z^d}$ and $(\mathcal U^Q_{v,0})_{v\in \mathbb Z^d}$ independently. Start with an arbitrary enumeration $v_1,v_2,...$ of the vertices of $\mathbb Z^d$. 
    
    For any distribution $\pi_{\Lambda}^{\eta}$ where $\Lambda \subset \mathbb Z^d$ finite, and $\eta \in \{\pm 1\}^{\Lambda^c}$ is a boundary condition, draw a sample $\sigma \sim \pi_{\Lambda}^{\eta}$  and $Q\sim \bigotimes_{v\in \Lambda} \text{Rad}(p)$ as follows: iteratively, for $i\ge 1$, 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item let $\sigma_{v_i}$ be $+1$ if $$\mathcal U_{v_i,0}^\pi \le \pi_{\Lambda}^{\eta} ( \sigma_{v_i} =+1 \mid (\sigma_{v_j})_{j<i:v_j\in \Lambda})$$
        and $-1$ else. 
        \item let $Q_{v_i}$ be $+1$ if $\mathcal U_{v_i,0}^Q \le p$ and $-1$ else. . 
    \end{itemize}
    Once all vertices in $\Lambda$ have been processed, terminate.
title: Definition def:initialization-coupling of arXiv:2605.08052

body: [Proposition prop:h0-pairing-graph-merge-tree of arXiv:2608.29719, 'Persistence Pairing Graphs: Tracking Changes of Selected Homology Bases'] Under the preceding assumptions and a common tie-breaking order, the $0$th persistence pairing graph $\mathcal G^{(0)}(\mathfrak F)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal B_g$. Every edge has coefficient $1\in\Bbbk$. Consequently, if the component structure eventually stabilizes to one component, $\mathcal G^{(0)}(\mathfrak F)$ is a rooted directed tree whose edges are oriented toward its unique root. If several terminal components remain, it is a rooted directed forest with one root for each terminal component.

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{calYzero_sufficient}
Let $f \in \Sym$ with $\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{\supp(f)} \ge 3$. 
At least one of of the following holds: 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $H(f) > H(X)$
\item $g = \big(\sum_{k \in S^0} f(k)\big)^{-1} f \mathds{1}_{S^0} \in \Sym^0$ and $H(g) \le H(X)$.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
Note that $S^0 = 2 \mathbb{Z}$. 

By (large_median_at_zero of the paper), $c = \sum_{i \in 2\mathbb{Z}} f(i) > 0$, 
so $g \in \Sym^0$ by (lem:Sr_restriction_of_symmetrizers_produces_symmetrizers of the paper). 

If $c = 1$, $H(g) = H(f) \le H(X)$. 
Otherwise, $c \in (0,1)$ and 
$ f = cg + (1-c)h $,
where 
$ h = \frac{f-cg}{1-c}$ is a PMF according to (lem:Sr_restriction_of_symmetrizers_produces_symmetrizers of the paper). 

Noting that $h(0) = 0$, (large_median_at_zero of the paper) shows that $H(h) > H(X)$; by concavity of entropy, therefore, 
\[ H(f) > cH(g) + (1-c)H(h) > cH(g) + (1-c)H(X) .\] 
Thus either $H(f) > H(X)$ or $H(X) \ge H(f) > cH(g) + (1-c)H(X)$. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

squared norm with relative error at most $\eta$.

[Lemma 59 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $j \in \N,x^1, x^2 \in \R^d$, $\Gamma : [0,\infty) \to \R^d$ with $\Gamma_0=0$, $\gamma \in (0,1)$. Suppose that for some $\delta>0$,
    \[\|\Gamma\|_{\mathcal{C}^\gamma_t} \leq 2^{(\gamma \beta -1 - \delta) j}.\]
    Then there exists $ C(\alpha,\beta,\delta,d)>0$ such that if $j \geq C$, $M \geq 1$, letting $N^j$ be as in~\eqref{eq:Tj properties}, we have the bound,
    \begin{align*}&\P_U\big(\inf_{0 \leq t \leq {N^j2^{-\beta j}}} \inf_{\substack{s,r\in [0,t]\\|s-r|\leq 2^{-\beta j}}} |Y^1_s- Y^2_r| \leq 2^{1-j}\big) + \P_U\big(|Y^1_{N^j2^{-\beta j}} - Y^2_{N^j2^{-\beta j}}| \leq M2^{-j})  \\&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\leq C 2^{-C^{-1} j} + C \frac{2^{-j}}{|x^1 - x^2|} + C M 2^{ -j^{1/2}/2}.
    \end{align*}

body:
Let p and q be probability mass functions on a finite set, d = d_TV(p, q), A an event, u = sum over x in A of (p_x - q_x)_+ and v = sum over x in A of (q_x - p_x)_+. Over all maximal couplings (X, Y) of p and q (those with P(X != Y) = d), P(1_A(X) != 1_A(Y)) takes exactly the values from |p(A) - q(A)| to min(u + v, 2d - u - v) = d - |d - (u + v)|. Since |p(A) - q(A)| is the total variation distance between the laws of the two indicators, for every event A some maximal coupling of p and q is at the same time a maximal coupling of 1_A(X) and 1_A(Y).

[Lem 5 of arXiv:2605.15501, 'Well-posedness of the obstacle problem for generalized Dean--Kawasaki equation\thanks{ The'] Let $u\in H^{1}(\mathbb{T}^{d})$
be a nonnegative function, and $\chi$ be the kinetic function of $u$.
Then, for every $\phi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{d}\times(0,\infty))$,
\[
\int_{x,\xi}\nabla_{x}\phi(x,\xi)\chi(x,\xi)=-\int_{x}\phi(x,u(x))\nabla_{x}u(x).
\]
In particular, if $(u,\nu)$ is a stochastic kinetic solution in the
sense of Definition \ref{def:def of stochastic kinetic solution}, then almost surely for every $\phi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^{d}\times(0,\infty)\times[0,T])$,
\[
\int_{x,\xi,s}\nabla_{x}\phi(x,\xi,s)\chi(x,\xi,s)=-\int_{x,s}\phi(x,u(x,s),s)\nabla_{x}u(x,s).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
\int_0^R\!\!\int_{B(x_0,R)}|\Delta^F_\mu(x,r)|^{2/\alpha}\,d\mu(x)\,\frac{dr}{r}
\;\le\;H^{2/\alpha}\,c'\,R^n,
\]
where $c'$ is the constant in (equation eq:carleson of the paper).

If $(\rho_k)_k \subset \cP_p(\mathcal Y)$ converges weakly to some $\rho \in \cP(\mathcal Y)$,
$(\nu_k)_k \subset \cP_p(\mathcal Z)$ is precompact in $(\cP_p(\mathcal Z),\Wcal_p)$, and $\sup_{k} W(\rho_k,\nu_k) < \infty$,
then $\rho_k \to \rho$ in $(\cP_p(\mathcal Y),\Wcal_r)$.

[Theorem thm:lower_bound of arXiv:2411.11415, 'The ballistic limit of the log-Sobolev constant equals the Polyak--\L{}ojasiewicz constant'] Suppose $f\colon \R^d \to \R$
    is minimized by some $x_\star \in \R^d$
    around which it is Lipschitz continuous.
    Then, for any point $x \in \R^d$
    around which $f$ is continuously differentiable,
    we have
    $$
    f(x) - f(x_\star) \leqslant \frac12\, \Bigl(\liminf_{t\to 0^+}\frac{C_{\msf{LS}}(\mu_t)}{t}\Bigr) \, \|\nabla f(x)\|^2\,.
    $$
In particular, if $f$ is minimized by
some $x_\star \in \R^d$ and is continuously
differentiable everywhere,
then
 $$
 C_{\msf{PL}}(f) \leqslant \liminf_{t\to 0^+}\frac{C_{\msf{LS}}(\mu_t)}{t}\,.
 $$

Attributed source theorem, not independently audited here. Let x -> P_x be any channel. A simulator uses common randomness Z independent of the input, a transcript T with at most 2^Q possible values, and an output determined by (T,Z). Suppose its output has TV distance at most delta from P_x for every x. If the original channel has a one-shot code for 2^k equiprobable messages with average decoding error r and delta+r<1, then Q>=k-log2(1/(1-delta-r)). This bounds total transcript bits; real-valued score-query counts require a separate answer-information bound.
Uniform per-input TV bound delta
Common randomness independent of input
At most 2^Q transcript symbols
One-shot code with uniform 2^k messages, average error r, delta+r<1

[Theoremi thm_planar_ordering of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] Let $\Gamma$ be a set of topological lines of the plane, such that for all distinct $\gamma,\gamma'\in\Gamma$, the difference $\gamma\setminus\gamma'$ is a portion of $\gamma$. Then, for all distinct $\gamma,\gamma'\in\Gamma$, denoting by $\triangle$ the symmetric difference operator, the set
        \[J(\gamma,\gamma')\coloneqq\overline{\gamma\triangle\gamma'}\]
    is a Jordan curve. Furthermore, setting
        \[(\gamma,\gamma')_\Gamma\coloneq\{\sigma\in\Gamma\setminus\{\gamma,\gamma'\}:J(\gamma,\sigma)\subset\overline{\mathrm{Int}} J(\gamma,\gamma')\}\]
    for all distinct $\gamma,\gamma'\in\Gamma$, the ternary relation $\cdot\in(\cdot,\cdot)_\Gamma$ induces a \emph{betweenness} structure on $\Gamma$, that is, there exists a strict total order $<_\Gamma$ on $\Gamma$, unique up to reversal, such that for all distinct $\gamma,\gamma',\sigma\in\Gamma$,
        \[\sigma\in(\gamma,\gamma')_\Gamma\iff[\gamma<_\Gamma\sigma<_\Gamma\gamma'\text{ or }\gamma'<_\Gamma\sigma<_\Gamma\gamma].\]
    Finally, for all distinct $\gamma,\gamma',\sigma\in\Gamma$, $\sigma\notin(\gamma,\gamma')_\Gamma\iff J(\gamma,\sigma)\subset\overline{\mathrm{Ext}} J(\gamma,\gamma')$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Planar ordering

[Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] The \textbf{particle-production Einstein--Navier--Stokes model} associated with a Navier--Stokes triple $(\mathscr F,\chi,\mathscr B)$ is the Einstein--matter system
\bel{eq:pot-production-system}
G^{\alpha\beta}=T_\chi^{\alpha\beta},
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}=0,
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha A_\chi^{\alpha\beta\gamma}
=-\mathscr B^{\beta\gamma}.
\ee
The unknowns are the spacetime metric and the fields $(\beta,\zeta)$, representing the rescaled matter momentum and the relaxing field, respectively. The tensors $T_\chi$ and $A_\chi$ are defined from the potential according to~\eqref{eq:pot-currents}.

body: [Definition 15 (Multipoint connection following a spined tree) of arXiv:2605.09459, 'Multipoint connectivity in the branching interlacement process'] Let $X$ be a random walk indexed by an infinite critical tree $\mathcal{T}$. Let $1\leq m \leq n+1$, and $T \in \mathbb{T}_{m,n+1}$ with vertex set $x_0,\dots,x_n \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ rooted at $x_0$. We say that $X$ \textbf{connects} $x_0,\dots,x_n$ \textbf{following} $T$, if $X_\varnothing = x_0$, and there exist $v_1,\dots,v_n \in \mathcal{T}$  such that $X_{v_i} = x_i$ and $\mathcal{T}\langle \varnothing,v_1,\dots,v_n\rangle$ is isomorphic to $T$ with $v_i$ mapped to $x_i$, and preimages of elements of the spine of $T$ on the spine of $\mathcal{T}$.
title: Multipoint connection following a spined tree

\[

\]
This inequality is available for any $\ent$. Letting $\ent$ go to $\infty$, we get with $p=1$ and $\diamd=1$ (for the $\ell_\infty$-norm):
\[
{\cal W}_p^p(\mu, \nu) \le 2^{1-\frac{1}{d}}D^{\infty}(\mu,\nu)^{\frac 1d}
\]

\end{itemize}

[Lemma lem:filling-escape-final of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Consider the VEB setting, and let $\Psi = (g,\tau_g,j,\overline{z},\mathcal{S},\textup{filling}) \in \ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$ be a high-level state. Let
$S = \Upsilon_{j, \ge\widetilde{W}[j]} \setminus \Upsilon_{j, \ge j^2}$.
Suppose that $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$ is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning. Conditioned on the events $\Psi(\tau_g) = \Psi$ and $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(\tau) = \overline{a}$, with probability at least $1-\exp(-400j/\lambda^2)$, the 
following events occur.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(t)$ is a $(6j^{25},j^{27},2/(\xi j^3),2)$-RS-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g + j^{22} \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_g}(t)$ is a $j^7$-AF-good beginning.
\item For all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $\mathcal{N}_S^{E_g}(t+1) \le \lambda|S|/80$.

    \item For all $k\in [j]$ with $W_k \ge j^\chi$ and all $t$ in the range $\tau_g \le t \le \tau_g + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$, $p_kb_k^{E_g}(t) \le \lambda/80$.  

\end{enumerate}   Moreover, if these events do occur and $V$ is well-behaved, then the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(I)]
\item $\Psi(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $j$-refilling, $(j+1)$-advancing or $(j+1)$-filling state.
\item If $\Psi(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $j$-refilling state, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_{g+1}}(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $(6j^{25}, j^{27}, 2/(\xi j^3), 2)$-RS-good beginning.
\item If $\Psi(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $(j+1)$-advancing or $(j+1)$-filling state, $\overline{b}_{[j]}^{E_{g+1}}(\tau_{g+1})$ is a $(j+1)^7$-AF-good beginning.
 

\item For all $t$ with $\tau_g \le t < \tau_{g+1}$,   $\mathcal{N}^{E_g}_S(t+1) \le \lambda |S|/80$. Moreover, $S$ is non-empty.

\item For all $t$ with $\tau_g \le t < \tau_{g+1}$, 
and all $k\in [j-1]$ with $W_k\geq j^{\chi}$, 
$\{k\} \in \mathcal{S}$  and $\mathcal{N}^{E_{g}}_{\{k\}}(t+1) \le \lambda /80$.
Moreover, there is at least one such $k\in [j-1]$.

 

\end{enumerate}

body: [Lemma 18 of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] Let $\gamma$ be a continuous path in $\overline\BD$ from $-\ri$ to $\ri$ that meets $\partial \BD$ only at $-\ri$ and $\ri$, and fix $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$. Then there exist constants $c = c(\gamma, \varepsilon) > 0$ and $t_\ast = t_\ast(\gamma, \varepsilon) \in (0, \pi)$ such that for each $t \in (0, t_\ast]$, the following is true: Let $\eta|_{[0, \tau]}$ be an SLE$_4(-2t/\pi; 2t/\pi - 2)$ curve in $\BD$ starting from $-\ri$, with force points at $(-\ri)^-$ and $(-\ri)^+$, targeting $\ri$, and stopped at the first time $\tau$ at which it hits $B_\varepsilon(\ri) \cap \partial\BD$. (Since $-2t/\pi + (2t/\pi - 2) = \kappa - 6$, this curve is target invariant \cite{SLE-CoC}, so the law of $\eta|_{[0,\tau]}$ does not depend on the choice of target.) Then it holds with probability at least $ct$ that $\eta([0, \tau]) \subset B_\varepsilon(\gamma)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 18 of arXiv:2609.04139

[Proposition 14 (Optimal single-weight update; Optimal Brain Surgeon \citep{hassibi1993obs}; quantization form \citep{frantar2022obc}) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Assume $\HX$ invertible; in practice a small diagonal damping is added before inversion, both because $X^{\!\top}X$ is singular where a layer has dead input channels and, in \citeauthor{frantar2022gptq}'s implementation, because the repeatedly-applied inverse accumulates numerical error at scale (they add $1\%$ of the mean diagonal). Minimizing the layer proxy $\Delta w^\top \HX\,\Delta w$ subject to quantizing coordinate $q$ to value $w_q^{\mathrm q}$ (constraint $e_q^\top\Delta w = w_q^{\mathrm q}-w_q$) gives optimal remaining update
\begin{equation}
\Delta w \;=\; -\,\frac{w_q-w_q^{\mathrm q}}{[\HX^{-1}]_{qq}}\;\HX^{-1} e_q,
\qquad
\text{incurring cost}\quad
\frac{(w_q-w_q^{\mathrm q})^2}{[\HX^{-1}]_{qq}} .
\end{equation}

body:
[Thm Gr-oup-completion of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The map $i\colon\textbf{\textup{Gr}}\to\textbf{\textup{BOP}}$ is a global group completion.
    \begin{proof}
        For $f\colon V\to W$ in $\textbf{\textup{L}}$ and $n\ge0$, the map $\textbf{\textup{Gr}}_n(f)\colon\textbf{\textup{Gr}}_n(V)\to\textbf{\textup{Gr}}_n(W)$ is a closed embedding as it is a continuous injection between compact spaces; in the same way, one shows that ${-}\oplus W\colon\textbf{\textup{Gr}}_n(V)\to\textbf{\textup{Gr}}_{n+\dim(W)}(V\oplus W)$ is a closed embedding. With this established, it follows straight from the definitions that the orthogonal spaces $\textbf{\textup{Gr}}$ and $\textbf{\textup{BOP}}$ are closed. In light of the description of the equivalence $\Phi$ from Lemma~(lemma:id-g-fixed-points-vs-ev of the paper), the theorem therefore amounts to saying that for every complete $G$-universe ${\mathcal{U}}_G$ the induced map $i({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G\colon\textbf{\textup{Gr}}({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G\to\textbf{\textup{BOP}}({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G$ is a group completion in $\CMon(\Spc)$ (where we make $(-)({{\mathcal{U}}_G})^G$ into a symmetric monoidal functor ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}^{\text{closed},\otimes}\to\Spc^\times$ in the unique way).

        As the key step in the proof of [schwede2018global]*{Theorem~2.5.33}, it is shown that the induced map $H_*(i({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G;{\mathbb{Z}})$ on integral homology is a localization (in the ring-theoretic sense) at $\pi_0(\textbf{\textup{Gr}}({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G)\subset H_0(\textbf{\textup{Gr}}({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G;{\mathbb{Z}})$. In particular, $\textbf{\textup{BOP}}({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G$ is grouplike, and so $i({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G$ factors through a map $f\colon X\to\textbf{\textup{BOP}}({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G$ from the group completion. By the McDuff--Segal group completion theorem (see [nikolaus-group-completion]*{Theorem~1} for a proof in this language in generality), also the group completion $\textbf{\textup{Gr}}({\mathcal{U}}_G)^G\to X$ induces a localization on homology at the same classes, so that $f$ is a homology isomorphism. As both its source and target are grouplike h-spaces (and hence their fundamental groups act trivially on higher homotopy groups), $f$ is therefore already an equivalence by the homological Whitehead theorem.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm Gr-oup-completion of arXiv:2608.28504

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): Let beta = log2(4/3). (a) If every selected witness meets at most D remaining matching pairs, then kappa <= D/beta. (b) If every private row support has size at most s, then kappa <= (s-1)/beta. (c) A maximum-degree bound on the two-shadow graph implies the same conclusion, because every row support spans a clique in the two-shadow graph. ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Distinct invariant ergodic laws are mutually singular Result: For a fixed countable group action, two distinct invariant ergodic probability measures are mutually singular. In the Lebesgue decomposition of one relative to the other, the absolutely continuous part is invariant. Its density is invariant and hence constant under the second ergodic law; ergodicity of the first forces its absolutely continuous mass to be either zero or one. Nonzero overlap therefore forces equality. Check: The singular and absolutely continuous parts are preserved by the action by uniqueness of Lebesgue decomposition; this is the load-bearing invariance step. Obstruction: This handles forest laws admitting such an ergodic common action. Arbitrary networks may lack it; two distinct probability laws need not be singular in general.

[Thm uniqueness of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Let $1\le k\le d-1$.
  Then for every $p\in[0,1]$, the following holds $\mathbb{P}_p$-almost surely$:$
  If
  \[
  \gamma^-\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times(-\infty,0]\to\mathbb{R}^d
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \gamma^+\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}^d
  \]
  are backward and forward infinite open $k$-tubes, respectively, then there exists a bi-infinite open $k$-tube $\gamma\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that
  \[
  \gamma|_{\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times(-\infty,-T]}=\gamma^-|_{\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times(-\infty,-T]}
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \gamma|_{\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[T,\infty)}=\gamma^+|_{\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[T,\infty)}
  \]
  for some $T\ge0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm uniqueness of arXiv:2605.14910

[Lemma lem:port of arXiv:2509.23086, 'On Optimal Markovian Couplings of L\'evy Processes'] Let \( \{\mu_n\}_n \subset \Lambda(\mathbb{R}^d) \) be a sequence of Lévy measures, and let \( \mu \in \Lambda(\mathbb{R}^d) \). The following are equivalent:
	
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[(i)] \( \mu_n \xrightarrow{\Lambda} \mu \).
		
		\item[(ii)] For every lower semicontinuous function \( \varphi: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R} \) satisfying \( \varphi(x) \ge -C \min\{1, |x|^2\} \) for some \( C \ge 0 \), it holds that
		\[
		\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(x)\, d\mu(x) \le \liminf_{n \to \infty} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(x)\, d\mu_n(x).
		\]
		
		\item[(iii)] For every upper semicontinuous function \( \varphi: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R} \) satisfying \( \varphi(x) \le C \min\{1, |x|^2\} \) for some \( C \ge 0 \), it holds that
		\[
		\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(x)\, d\mu(x) \ge \limsup_{n \to \infty} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \varphi(x)\, d\mu_n(x).
		\]
	\end{itemize}

[Definition $C_b^\infty$ and its Fourier image of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Let
\[
C_b^\infty:=\{f\in C^\infty:\ \|\partial^\alpha f\|_{L^\infty}<\infty\ \forall \alpha\}
=\bigcap_{m\ge0}W^{m,\infty},
\]
be the space of smooth functions with bounded derivatives, which is equipped
with Fréchet seminorms \(p_\alpha(f)=\|\partial^\alpha f\|_\infty\).
Define
\[
\widehat{C_b^\infty}
:=\Bigl\{u\in\mathcal S':\ (i\xi)^\alpha u\in PM\ \text{for all multiindices }\alpha\Bigr\},
\]
with seminorms \(\|u\|_{PM,k}:=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\|(i\xi)^\alpha u\|_{PM}\).
Then \(\mathcal F:C_b^\infty\to\widehat{C_b^\infty}\) is a Fréchet isomorphism.
title: $C_b^\infty$ and its Fourier image

[Lemma l:conv_hitting0 of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\delta_1>0$, $\delta_2<2$, and $a,b$ be positive real numbers.  Suppose either
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $(S_x,x\ge 0)$ is a ${\rm BESQ}(\delta_1\, |_a \, 0 \, |_{b}\, \delta_2)$ process starting at $0$,
    or
    \item $(S_x,x\ge -a)$ is a ${\rm BESQ}(\delta_1\, |_0 \, 0 \, |_{b}\, \delta_2)$ process starting at $0$.
\end{enumerate}
In both cases, let $T_{a,b}:=\inf\{y\ge b: S_x=0\}$. The conditional distribution of $T_{a,b}$ given $\{S_{b}>0\}$ converges as $a\to 0$ to the distribution of $\frac{b}{A}$, where $A$ has the beta distribution $\mathcal{B}(\frac{2-\delta_2}{2},1)$.

Owner draft: independently checked proof (C010 v1). Let C be a compact full-dimensional convex body and p an interior point. If Unif(C) is a probability mixture of Unif(K_alpha), where every component is an inscribed compact full-dimensional convex body and p lies in its interior almost surely, then K_alpha=C almost surely. Averaging normalized mass of shrinking balls around p and applying Fatou yields E[1/vol(K_alpha)]<=1/vol(C); containment gives the reverse pointwise inequality, forcing equal volumes and equal bodies. Thus a nonsimplex C cannot be a mixture of inscribed uniform simplices sharing its centroid, even with overlap or an uncountable mixture. Singular atomic/vertex components are excluded from this obstruction.
C compact full-dimensional convex body
Probability mixture of measurable uniform-body kernels
Each component full-dimensional convex and contained in C
One fixed point interior to almost every component

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: the Christ–Kiselev lemma passes from an untruncated space-time bound L^p_t → L^q_t to its causal truncation ∫_{s<t} only when p < q strictly. At p = q the truncation can be unbounded even when the full operator is bounded. Concrete counterexample on L²(R): let K(t,s) = sin(t−s)/(t−s) (continuous, locally bounded). The full operator is convolution with the sinc kernel, whose Fourier multiplier is π·1_{[−1,1]}(ξ) (up to normalization), so it is bounded on L² with norm ≈ π. Its causal truncation is convolution with k(u) = 1_{u>0} sin(u)/u, whose multiplier is m(ξ) = ∫_0^∞ e^{−iuξ} sin(u)/u du; using ∫_0^∞ sin(u) sin(uξ)/u du = (1/2) log |(1+ξ)/(1−ξ)|, the imaginary part of m is −(1/2) log|(1+ξ)/(1−ξ)|, which is unbounded as ξ → ±1. A convolution operator on L²(R) is bounded if and only if its multiplier is in L^∞, so the truncated operator is unbounded on L²: p = q = 2 fails. Consequence for PDE: the retarded (Duhamel) Strichartz estimate at the double endpoint q = q̃ = 2 cannot be obtained from the untruncated estimate by Christ–Kiselev; it is exactly the case Keel–Tao had to prove directly. Any proof that claims the double-endpoint inhomogeneous estimate 'by Christ–Kiselev' is misapplying the lemma.
title: Pitfall: Christ–Kiselev Needs p < q Strictly

body:
[Definition 14 of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] Let $\mathbf{X}$ be a geometric $p$-rough path on $V$, with $p \notin \mathbb{N}$.  
The signature of $\mathbf{X}$ is the unique extension of $\mathbf{X}$ to a path
\[
S(\mathbf{X}) : \Delta_{[a,b]} \to T((V)),
\]
such that $S^{(n)}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X}^{(n)}$ for every non-negative integer $n \leq \kappa$ and the following properties hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item
for every integer $n > \kappa$  the $n$-th level of the signature satisfies the estimate 
\[
\left|S^{(n)}(\mathbf{X})_{s,t}\right |
\le
\frac{\omega_{\mathbf{X}}(s,t)^{n/p}}{\beta_p\,\Gamma(n/p+1)} \quad \text{for all } a \le s \le t  \le b.
\]
\item
$S(\mathbf{X})$ is multiplicative, that is,
\[
S(\mathbf{X})_{s,s} = \mathbf{1}, \quad 
S(\mathbf{X})_{s,u} = S(\mathbf{X})_{s,t}\otimes S(\mathbf{X})_{t,u}
\quad \text{for all } a \le s \le t \le u \le b.
\]
\end{itemize}
title: Definition 14 of arXiv:2605.08844

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.00642, 'Quantitative central limit theorem for an integrated periodogram via the fourth moment the'] Let $f,g\in L^{1}(-\pi,\pi)$ such that
\begin{align}
\begin{split}
f(\lambda) &= |\lambda|^{-\alpha} L_f(\lambda),\\
g(\lambda) &= |\lambda|^{-\beta} L_g(\lambda), 
\end{split}
\end{align}
where $L_f$ and $L_g$ are slowly varying functions at $0$. Assume that
\[
-1<\alpha, \beta<1,
\qquad
d:=\alpha+\beta < \frac12 .
\]
Then we get
\[
d_W(F_n,Z)\longrightarrow 0 \qquad \text{as } n\to\infty .
\]
Assume moreover that there exists $C>0$ such that, for all $\lambda,\omega$ satisfying
$|\lambda-\omega|<\tfrac{|\lambda|}{2}$,
\begin{align}
\begin{split}
|f(\omega)-f(\lambda)|
&\le C\, f(\lambda)\,|\lambda|^{-1}|\lambda-\omega|,\\
|g(\omega)-g(\lambda)|
&\le C\, g(\lambda)\,|\lambda|^{-1}|\lambda-\omega|.
\end{split}
\end{align}
Then, for every $\eta>0$, there exists a constant $C_\eta<\infty$ such that, for all $n$ large enough,
\[
d_W(F_n,Z)\le C_\eta\, n^{\,d-\frac12+\eta}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] When flipping a biased coin $n$ times in a row, we have
$$P(s\ {\rm heads}, n-s\ {\rm tails})=\binom{n}{s}p^s(1-p)^{n-s}$$
and your winning law, for heads, is the following probability measure,
$$b_{np}=\sum_{s=0}^n\binom{n}{s}p^s(1-p)^{n-s}\delta_s$$
called binomial law of parameter $p\in[0,1]$.

body: In the localized FPP problem on a finite region of Z^2 (weights restricted to a finite edge set), define G as the set of edges lying in EVERY geodesic between two fixed points. Then membership is Borel outright: e belongs to G if and only if the passage time computed with e forbidden strictly exceeds the unrestricted passage time, and both are continuous functions of finitely many weights. No measurable selection of a geodesic is needed for any argument consuming G, and geodesic non-uniqueness only SHRINKS G (more geodesics means more constraints), so uniqueness assumptions are unnecessary for upper bounds on |G|. Confirmed in independent review (2026-08-10) of an entropy-method derivation that had carried a measurable-selection caveat it turned out not to need.

[Defi 14 of arXiv:2608.30120, 'Graphs of operators as points in the Grassmann manifold'] Let $P$ be an orthogonal projection in $\j=\j_+\oplus\j_-$. Denote $P_+=P_{\j_+}$ and $P_-=P_{\j_-}$. Then $P$ belongs to the restricted Grassmannian $\p_{res}(\j_+)$  (induced by this decomposition) if and only if
\begin{itemize}
\item
$P_+P\big|_{R(P)}:R(P)\to \j_+ $ is a Fredholm operator;
\item
$P_-P\big|_{R(P)}:R(P)\to\j_-$ is  compact operator.
\end{itemize}
The index of $P$ is the index of the above Fredholm operator, and is given by
$$
{\rm ind}_{\j_+}(P)=\dim R(P)\cap\j_--\dim N(P)\cap\j_+.
$$
title: Definition 14 of arXiv:2608.30120

body:
TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). The smoothing transform concerns fixed points of the distributional equation W =_d sum_i T_i W_i, where (T_i) is a given, typically random, sequence of nonnegative weights and (W_i) are i.i.d. copies of W independent of (T_i); such fixed points arise as limits of branching random walk martingales, including derivative martingale limits, or of Mandelbrot multiplicative cascades, and their tail behavior, characterized by a power-law index alpha solving E[sum_i T_i^alpha]=1 or a related equation, governs the limit's regular variation. Durrett and Liggett characterized the solution set of the smoothing transform equation, establishing existence, uniqueness up to a scaling constant, and the precise tail index under moment conditions on (T_i), a result foundational for analyzing branching random walk boundary and derivative martingale limits and related models such as the random energy model. Separately, Poisson-Dirichlet distributions PD(alpha,theta) arise as the limiting law of ranked, normalized jump sizes of a subordinator, of ranked cycle lengths in random permutations, or of ranked masses in fragmentation and coalescent processes, characterized via the stick-breaking (GEM) construction or via a Poisson process of jumps of a stable subordinator normalized by its total mass. Neither result gives an explicit closed-form density for the general fixed point or limit; the smoothing transform's fixed point is typically characterized only implicitly, through its tail index and functional equation, and both results require specific moment or regular-variation conditions on the input weights or subordinator to hold. Typical failure: Assuming the smoothing transform has a unique nontrivial fixed point up to scale without checking that the characteristic equation E[sum T_i^alpha]=1 actually has a solution in the admissible range, or without the Durrett-Liggett/Biggins regularity conditions, particularly in boundary cases such as the critical branching random walk where the derivative martingale, rather than the ordinary martingale, is the relevant object; applying the generic smoothing-transform tail behavior in a boundary or degenerate parameter regime without re-deriving it is a common source of incorrect tail-index claims. Canonical reference: Durrett and Liggett, 1983, Zeitschrift fur Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete; Biggins and Kyprianou, 2005, Electronic Journal of Probability; Pitman and Yor, 1997, Annals of Probability.
for the smoothing transform: existence of alpha solving E[sum_i T_i^alpha]=1 in the admissible range, plus regularity conditions such as E[sum_i T_i^alpha log^+ T_i]<infinity from Durrett-Liggett/Biggins theory
for Poisson-Dirichlet: a well-defined subordinator, or fragmentation/coalescent structure, whose ranked, normalized jump sizes are being studied
independence of (T_i) from the i.i.d. copies (W_i) in the smoothing transform equation
non-degeneracy conditions ruling out the trivial Dirac-mass-at-0 solution
title: Technique: Poisson-Dirichlet Limits and the Durrett-Liggett Smoothing Transform

[Proposition 10 (Gelfand-Tsetlin facts, {\cite[Proposition 2) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] {NarSheffTao}}]
Let \(\lambda=(\lambda_1\geq \cdots \geq \lambda_n)\in\Spec_n\).  For
\(a\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(\GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}\) denote the real
Gelfand-Tsetlin polytope of triangular arrays
\[
        \Gamma=\{\lambda^{(k)}_i:1\leq i\leq k\leq n\}
\]
satisfying
\[
        \lambda^{(k+1)}_i
        \geq
        \lambda^{(k)}_i
        \geq
        \lambda^{(k+1)}_{i+1},
        \qquad
        1\leq i\leq k<n,
\]
with top row \(\lambda^{(n)}=\lambda\), and diagonal boundary condition
\[
        \sum_{i=1}^k \lambda^{(k)}_i
        =
        \sum_{i=1}^k a_i,
        \qquad 1\leq k\leq n.
\]
Let \(\GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel *}:=\bigcup_a\GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}\).
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), then the Schur--Horn relation
\(\diag(\lambda)\rel a\) holds if and only if
\(\GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}\) is nonempty.
\item[(ii)] The \(\binom n2\)-dimensional volume of
\(\GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel *}\) is \(V_n(\lambda)/V_n(\tau_n)\).
\item[(iii)] If \(A\) is Haar-uniform on the unitary orbit with spectrum
\(\lambda\), then the eigenvalues of the northwest principal minors of
\(A\) form a uniformly distributed point of
\(\GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel *}\). Its boundary vector \(a\) is the diagonal of
\(A\).
\item[(iv)] If \(\Lambda\in\Spec_n\) has large gaps,
\[
        \min_{1\leq i<n}(\Lambda_i-\Lambda_{i+1})
        >
        \lambda_1-\lambda_n,
\]
then for every \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) there is a volume-preserving linear
bijection
\[
        \GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}
        \longleftrightarrow
        H_n(\Lambda,\lambda;\Lambda+a).
\]
Under this bijection, a Gelfand-Tsetlin pattern
\((\lambda^{(k)}_i)_{1\leq i\leq k\leq n}\) is sent to the hive \(h:T_n\to
\mathbb R\) given by
\[
        h(i,j)
        =
        \Lambda_1+\cdots+\Lambda_j
        +
        \lambda^{(j)}_1+\cdots+\lambda^{(j)}_i .
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, the connective constant is a numerical quantity associated with self-avoiding walks on a lattice. It is studied in connection with the notion of universality in two-dimensional statistical physics models. While the connective constant depends on the choice of lattice so itself is not universal (similarly to other lattice-dependent quantities such as the critical probability threshold for percolation), it is nonetheless an important quantity that appears in conjectures for universal laws. Furthermore, the mathematical techniques used to understand the connective constant, for example in the recent rigorous proof by Duminil-Copin and Smirnov that the connective constant of the hexagonal lattice has the precise value ${\sqrt {2+{\sqrt {2}}}}$, may provide clues to a possible approach for attacking other important open problems in the study of self-avoiding walks, notably the conjecture that self-avoiding walks converge in the scaling limit to the Schramm–Loewner evolution.

For an integer n>=1, let X=(X_1,...,X_n) be a random vector on one probability space, with each coordinate taking values in a finite discrete alphabet. Let S_1,...,S_m be subsets of [n], repetitions allowed, and let k be a positive integer such that every i in [n] belongs to at least k of the selected subsets. With Shannon entropy computed consistently with any base b>1, define X_S=(X_i)_{i in S}. Then
k H(X_1,...,X_n) <= sum_{j=1}^m H(X_{S_j}).
The empty-projection entropy is zero. Independence of coordinates is not required. The stated finite-alphabet domain guarantees nonnegative finite Shannon entropies and valid chain rule.
n is a positive integer
the random vector is discrete; finite coordinate alphabets are a safe sufficient restriction
the cover multiplicity k is a positive integer
every coordinate occurs in at least k selected subsets
all entropy terms use one logarithm base greater than 1

PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let an infinite connected locally finite unit-conductance graph C contain a subdivision of a locally finite graph H, replacing each edge e by an internally vertex-disjoint path of length ell_e. If H has a unit flow f from a root to infinity with sum_e ell_e f(e)^2 finite, then C is transient. Lift the constant current along each replacement path; its energy is exactly that sum and its divergence is inherited at branch vertices. Uniformly bounded corridor lengths suffice whenever H is transient. A percolation argument must establish this quantitative energy condition, not only branching topology.
Connected locally finite unit-conductance graphs
An actual subdivision with disjoint path interiors
A specified root-to-infinity unit flow with finite weighted energy

[Prop weightstability of arXiv:2412.04918, 'On one dimensional weighted Poincar\'e inequalities for Global Sensitivity Analysis'] Under the notation and assumptions of Proposition (prop: upper bound of the paper), let fix $i\in \{ 1,\ldots, d \}$ and let $f$ be of the form $f(x) = u_i(x_{-i}) + h_i (x_i) v_i(x_{-i})$, where $u_i, v_i$ are functions depending only on $x_{-i}$, such that $u_i (X_{-i}) , v_i (X_{-i}) \in L^2$, and $h_i \in H^1(\mu_i,w_i)$ is centered with respect to $\mu_i$. Let further assume that there exists $\varepsilon \geq 0$ such that 
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[w_i(X_i) \left( h_i'(X_i)-g_i'(X_i) \right) ^2\right]\leq \varepsilon,
\]
where $g_i$ is a function saturating the weighted Poincar\'e inequality (equation eq: poincar\'eGSA of the paper). Then we have the following stability result:
\[
0 \leq   C_P(\mu_i,w_i)\frac{\nu_{i,w_i}}{\mathop{\rm Var}\nolimits(f(X))}-S_i^\mathrm{tot}\leq C_P(\mu_i,w_i) \, \frac{\mathbb{E}\left[v_i^2(X_{-i})\right]}{\mathop{\rm Var}\nolimits(f(X))} \, \varepsilon.\]
In particular, if $f$ has the form $f(x)= u_i(x_{-i}) + g_i(x_i) v_i(x_{-i})$, then (equation eq: prop upper bound of the paper) is an equality.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Assuming that $f,g:X\to\mathbb R$ are independent, we have
$$E(f^kg^l)=E(f^k)E(g^l)$$
and the converse holds, in the sense that this implies the independence of $f,g$.

[Theorem thm:biregular of arXiv:2411.07809, 'Pirogov--Sinai Theory Beyond Lattices'] Suppose $G$ is bipartite, one-ended, vertex transitive within each
  parity class, and has polynomial volume growth. Suppose also that
  $G$ has a $D$-bounded cycle basis $\mathcal B$. There is a
  $\lambda_{\star}=\lambda_{\star}(D,\Delta,C_{\text{iso}})$ such that if
  $\lambda_{\textsf{e}} \geq\lambda_{\star}$ and $\lambda_\textsf{o}\in \mathcal{U}$, then
  the free energy $f_G(\lambda_\textsf{e},\lambda_\textsf{o})$ is well-defined and
  independent of the vertex $v$ used in its definition. Moreover,
  there is a unique $\lambda_{\textsf{o},c}(G,\lambda_{\textsf{e}})\in \mathcal{U}$ such
  that
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item The function $f_G(\lambda_\textsf{e},\lambda_\textsf{o})$ is continuously
    differentiable at pairs of activities
    $(\lambda_\textsf{e},\lambda_\textsf{o} )$ different from 
    $(\lambda_\textsf{e},\lambda_{\textsf{o},c}(G,\lambda_\textsf{e}))$.
  \item The critical parameter $\lambda_{\textsf{o},c}$ satisfies
    $\log\lambda_{\textsf{o},c} = \frac{\Delta_{\textsf{o}}}{\Delta_{\textsf{e}}}
    \log\lambda_{\textsf{e}} + o_{\lambda_{\textsf{e}}}(1)$.
  \item If $\lambda_{\textsf{o}}\neq \lambda_{\textsf{o},c}$ there is a unique
    infinite-volume Gibbs measure.
  \item For the hard-core model on $G$ with activities
    $(\lambda_\textsf{e},\lambda_{\textsf{o},c}(G,\lambda_\textsf{e}))$ phase coexistence
    occurs, and $f_G$ fails to be continuously differentiable at such
    pairs.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:biregular of arXiv:2411.07809

[Theorem thm: martingale of arXiv:2511.08479, '\Large From disordered systems to the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow'] Let $\phi\in C^+_c({\ensuremath{\mathbb R}} ^2)$, $\psi\in C^2_b(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and $\vartheta\in\mathbb{R}$. Let
     $   \mathscr{Z}_t^{\vartheta,\phi}(\psi)
        :=\iint \phi(x) \, \mathscr{Z}_t^\vartheta(\mathrm{d} x, \mathrm{d} y) \, \psi(y) .$
    Then
    \begin{align}
        \mathscr{M}_t^{\vartheta,\phi} (\psi)
        :=
        \mathscr{Z}_t^{\vartheta,\phi}(\psi)
        -\int \phi(x) \psi(y) \mathrm{d} x \, \mathrm{d} y
        -\int^t_0 \mathscr{Z}_s^{\vartheta,\phi} \big( \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta \psi \big) \mathrm{d} s
    \end{align}
    defines a continuous martingale starting at $0$ at time $0$ and with quadratic variation
    $\langle \mathscr{M}^{\vartheta,\phi}(\psi) \rangle_t$ obtained as a suitable limit via
    regularisation. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm: martingale of arXiv:2511.08479

[Lemma 24 (The case $n=2$ is the case $n\ge 2$) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero.
    Let $D$ be a derivation of the form $D= \sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}$ where $f_i\in k(X)$ are nonzero rational functions.

    Then, $D$ defines an algebraically integrable foliation on $k(x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n,\ldots)$ if and only if 
    for each $1\le i<j\le n$ the derivation $E_{ij}=f_i(x_i)\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}+f_j(x_j)\frac{\partial}{\partial x_j}$ defines an algebraically integrable foliation on $k(x_i,x_j)$.

body: [Lemma 3 (Extremal envelopes) of arXiv:2602.20971, 'Does Order Matter : Connecting The Law of Robustness to Robust Generalization'] For $f\in\mathcal{F}_{L}$, define $f_{\rho}^{+}(x)=\sup_{\tilde{x}\in B_{\rho}(x)}f(\tilde{x})$ and $f_{\rho}^{-}(x)=\inf_{\tilde{x}\in B_{\rho}(x)}f(\tilde{x})$. [Defn de.2 of arXiv:2411.13099, 'Long time behavior of killed Feynman-Kac semigroups with singular Schr{ö}dinger potentials'] Let  $\mathbf F: \mathscr V\to [1,+\infty]$ be a measurable function. 
   We say that  $(Q^{\mathfrak X}_t,t\ge 0)$ is    $\mathbf F$ {\rm compact-ergodic} over $\mathscr V$   if:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[\textbf 1.] There exists a unique q.s.d.  $\rho$ for  $(P^{\mathfrak X}_t,t\ge 0)$ in   $  \mathcal P_{\mathbf F}(\mathscr V)$.  
 \item[\textbf 2.] 
  For all $t>0$, $Q^{\mathfrak X}_t:b\mathcal B_{\mathbf F}(\mathscr V)\to b\mathcal B_{\mathbf F}(\mathscr V)$ is compact and there exists $\lambda\ge  \inf_{\mathscr V} \mathbf V$   such that $\mathsf r_{sp}(Q^{\mathfrak X}_t|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf F}(\mathscr V)} ) =e^{-\lambda t}, \ \forall t>0$. 
  Furthermore,  $\rho    Q^{\mathfrak X}_t =e^{-\lambda t}\rho$, for all $t\ge 0$, and $\rho (O)>0$ for all nonempty open subsets $O$ of $ \mathscr V$. In addition,  there is a unique   function $\varphi \in \mathcal C_{b\mathbf F}( \mathscr V)$   such that  $\rho   (\varphi )=1$ and $
      Q^{\mathfrak X}_t \varphi= e^{-\lambda  t} \varphi  \text{ on } \mathscr V, \forall t\ge0$.  
 Moreover, $\varphi>0$   everywhere on $\mathscr V$.
\item[\textbf 3.] There exist   $\mathfrak m_1>0$, and   $\mathfrak m_2\ge 1$, s.t.  for all  $t>0$ and all   $\nu\in \mathcal P_{\mathbf F  }( \mathscr V)$:
$$
\sup_{\mathcal A\in\mathcal B(\mathscr V)}\big |  \nu P^{\mathfrak X}_t(\mathcal A)-\rho  (\mathcal A)\big |\le \mathfrak m_2 \, e^{-\mathfrak m_1 t} \frac{\nu(\mathbf F )}{\nu(\varphi)}.
$$
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.07365, 'A pathwise Ito formula \\for weakly differentiable functions'] There exists a constant $C_d$ such that if $f\in W^{1, 1}(\Rr^d)$ and its derivatives are defined at every point by \ref{2eq:values}, and $x, y\in\Rr^d$ be such that $|f(y)|, |f(x)| <+\infty.$ If $x, y\in Q$ then
\[
|f(y)- f(x) |\leq C_d\left(\int_Q \frac {|\nabla f(z)|} {|x- z|^{d-1}} dz\,+\, \int_Q \frac {|\nabla f(z)|} {|y- z|^{d-1}} dz\right).
\]
Similarly for $f\in W^{2, 1}(\Rr^d)$, and $x, y\in Q$ with $|f(y)|, |f(x)|, |\nabla f(x)| <+\infty$ 
\[
|f(y)- f(x) - \nabla f(x) (y-x)|\leq C_d\left(\int_Q \frac {|\nabla^2 f(z)|} {|x- z|^{d-2}} dz\,+\, \int_Q \frac {|\nabla^2 f(z)|} {|y- z|^{d-2}} dz\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop eq:lesmom of arXiv:2603.21634, 'Individual-based stochastic model with unbounded growth, birth and death rates: a tightnes'] Let $p \geq 1$, and under the \hyperlink{ren}{renormalized setting}, assume in addition that
\begin{align}
    \underset{K \in \mathbb{N}^{*}}{\mathrm{sup}} \hspace{0.1 cm} \mathbb{E}\left(\left(E_{0}^{K} +N_{0}^{K} + \Omega^{K}_{0}\right)^{p}\right) < + \infty.
    
    \end{align}
Then, for all $T \geq 0$, we have
\[ \sup_{K \in \mathbb{N}^{*}} \mathbb{E}\left( \sup_{t \in [0,T]}\left(E_{t}^{K} +N_{t}^{K} + \Omega^{K}_{t}\right)^{p} \right) < + \infty. \]
This immediately implies that for every $\varphi \in \mathfrak{B}_{1+\mathrm{Id}+\omega}(\mathbb{R}^{*}_{+})$, we have
\[ \sup_{K \in \mathbb{N}^{*}} \mathbb{E}\left(\underset{t \in [0,T]}{\mathrm{sup}} \left|\langle \mu^{K}_{t}, \varphi \rangle\right|^{p} \right) < + \infty. \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop eq:lesmom of arXiv:2603.21634

Let d>=1, sigma>0, and let f be a measurable deterministic classifier or a measurable input-dependent distribution on a finite label set Y of size K>=2. Its internal randomness is averaged together with independent Gaussian noise epsilon~N(0,sigma^2 I_d). Define g(z) as a class maximizing P(f(z+epsilon)=c), using any fixed rule to resolve ties. Fix x in R^d and cA in Y. Suppose 0<pB<pA<1 and P(f(x+epsilon)=cA)>=pA, while max_(c!=cA) P(f(x+epsilon)=c)<=pB. With Phi the standard normal CDF, set R=(sigma/2)*(Phi^(-1)(pA)-Phi^(-1)(pB)). Then simultaneously for all delta with ||delta||_2<R, cA is the unique most probable class at x+delta and g(x+delta)=cA. In the binary case, taking pB=1-pA for pA>1/2 gives R=sigma*Phi^(-1)(pA). The inequalities are bounds on smoothed probabilities; the certificate does not require them to be exact or the base classifier to be continuous.
Finite label set and measurable classifier or Markov classification kernel
Gaussian noise variance sigma^2 I with sigma>0, independent of classifier randomness
Bounds at one fixed x: top-class probability at least pA and every competitor at most pB
Interior nontrivial case 0<pB<pA<1; strict open perturbation ball
No assumption on input distribution or base network architecture
