[Lemma 47 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \((U,h)\) be a smooth Riemannian manifold, and let
\(H_i,H:U\to\R^k\) be smooth maps with
\(H_i\to H\) in \(C^\infty_{\rm loc}\).  Suppose that \(0\) is a regular
value of \(H\), and set \(S=H^{-1}(0)\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.4em]
\item If \(K\Subset\operatorname{int}K^+\Subset S\) are compact
domains, then, for all large \(i\), \(H_i^{-1}(0)\) contains a small
normal graph \(K_i\) over \(K\), and \(K_i\to K\) smoothly.
\item If \(S\) is compact and is the entire zero set of \(H\) in a
precompact tubular neighbourhood \(U_0\Subset U\), then, for all large
\(i\), \(H_i^{-1}(0)\cap U_0\) contains a compact boundaryless normal
graph \(S_i\) over \(S\).  Moreover, \(S_i\to S\) smoothly and
\(S_i\cong S\).
\end{enumerate}
If Riemannian metrics \(h_i\) on \(U\) converge smoothly to \(h\), the
induced metrics and volume forms on these graphs converge smoothly. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 47 of arXiv:2609.02878

body:
[Openquestion 34 (Reversal amplitude) of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Fix a tie convention.  Among all pairs with $\mathbb{E}[\tau_U]\ge \mathbb{E}[\tau_V]$, how large can the head‑to‑head advantage of $U$ over $V$ be?  Define the \emph{reversal gap}
\[
\Delta_{L_1,L_2}(p)\;:=\;\sup_{|U|=L_1,\,|V|=L_2,\ \mathbb{E}[\tau_U]\ge \mathbb{E}[\tau_V]}\Bigl(\Pr(U\!>\!V)-\tfrac12\Bigr).
\]
Determine (or bound) $\Delta_{L_1,L_2}(p)$ and its maximisers; relate them to border polynomials.
In particular, for fixed $(L_1,L_2)$ and $p$, can $\Delta_{L_1,L_2}(p)$ be bounded away from $1/2$, or can it approach $1/2$ (i.e.\ can a ``slower'' string win with probability arbitrarily close to $1$)? (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Reversal amplitude

[Theorem th:intro-HALFGODHALFSOUVLAKI of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] (Theorem (HALFGODHALFSOUVLAKI of the paper))
  Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$
  and $0 < \theta < 1$. Assume that for every finite $r$ we have
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N^{\theta}} \log \mathbb{E} [H
    \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A), \ldots, \lambda_N
    (A))] = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is a smooth function in a complex neighborhood of $0$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$. Then, for every $k \in
  \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th moment of the random measure $N^{- \theta} \sum_{i =
  1}^N \delta \left( N^{- 1} \lambda_i (A) \right)$ converges in
  probability to $\dfrac{\Psi^{(k)} (0)}{(k - 1)!}$, as $N \rightarrow \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:corners of arXiv:2608.11378, 'On the most likely geodesic in last passage percolation'] Suppose the weight distribution satisfies Assumptions~(ass:lower-tail of the paper) and (ass:tiltable of the paper). Write
\[
\Gamma^\ge_n = \set[\big]{\gamma \in \Gamma_n : \mathbb{P}(\gamma \in \Gamma_n^*) \ge \mathbb{P}(\gamma^{\raisebox{-0.5ex}{$\scriptstyle\ulcorner$}} \in \Gamma_n^*)}
\]
for the set of paths which are at least as likely to appear as geodesics as $\gamma^{\raisebox{-0.5ex}{$\scriptstyle\ulcorner$}}$. For any $\epsilon > 0$, it holds for all $n$ large enough that
\[
\abs{\Gamma^\ge_n}\leq e^{\epsilon n} \quad \text{and} \quad \frac{\abs{\Gamma^\ge_n}}{\abs{\Gamma_n}} \le d^{- d n (1 - \epsilon)}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop Sgn of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $g\ge 2$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\mathcal S_{g,n}=\emptyset$ for $n>2g+2$.
\item For $g+2<n\le 2g+2$, the locus $\mathcal S_{g,n}$ is empty unless $n\in\{2g+1,2g+2\}$, and then it consists of the single point $y^n=x^2-1$, which lies in the hyperelliptic locus.
\item Let $3\le n\le g+2$ and $\mathcal S_{g,n}\ne\emptyset$. Then the datum $\mathbf C_{g,n}$ has $m\ge 3$. If $3\mid g+2$, then $\mathcal S_{g,g+2}$ contains the non-hyperelliptic curve $y^{g+2}=x^3-x$.
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 12 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Follow the same setup and notation as \Cref{lem:subgaussian-kahane-khintchine} with $H \coloneqq H^1(\mathcal{I};\mathbb{K})$ and $\mathbb{K} = \R$ or $\C$. 
There exist $c,C>0$ such that for all $m\in\N$ and $u\geq0$, we have
\begin{align}
        \P\Big(
        \max_{0\le k\le m}\|S_k\|_\infty>u
        \Big)
        \le
        Ce^{-cu^2/\sigma_m^2}\,.
\end{align}
where we use the convention that $1/\sigma_m^2 \coloneqq 0$ when $\sigma_m = 0$.
Moreover, for all $\lambda,K>0$, there exists $C_\lambda<\infty$ (also depending on $K$) such
that whenever $\sigma_m \in [0,K]$, we have
\begin{align}
        \E\big[\exp( \lambda \max_{0\leq k\leq m} \|S_k\|_\infty)\big]-1
        \leq
        C_\lambda\sigma_m .
\end{align}

[Proposition 5 (\cite{DunlopNewman1975}) of arXiv:2512.05340, 'The rate of convergence of the critical mean-field $O(N)$ magnetization via multivariate n'] Fix $N \geq 2$. Let $\sigma$ be distributed via~\eqref{eq:mean-field O(N) measure} with $\beta=N$, and let
  $W_{n} = n^{-3/4}\,S_{n}(\sigma)$. Let $Y$ be a random vector in $\RR^N$ whose distribution has Lebesgue density

    \item $\EE|W_{n}|^{k} \leq C_{k} < \infty$, for all integer $k\ge0$ and $n\ge 2$
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Asymptotic total length of finite SIRSN samples structural attempt Result: A local truncation argument gives the lower bound liminf E length/k>=ell. Tile the bulk of the large square by unit cells. For fixed R and M, retain in each cell only the length, truncated at M, of routes between sampled endpoints within distance R of that cell. Its local binomial point configuration converges in total variation to the corresponding rate1 Poisson configuration. The retained length is bounded by M, so its expectation converges. Summing disjoint unit-cell contributions and then taking k to infinity gives the Poisson local truncated expectation as a lower bound. Let M and then R increase: monotone convergence recovers the full sampled-network intensity ell. Check: Only a bounded endpoint region is used before taking k to infinity; its binomial count tends to a Poisson count and conditional positions have the same uniform law. Truncation avoids any unproved uniform-integrability step. Boundary cells are an asymptotically negligible fraction for fixed R. Obstruction: This proves no upper bound on total length. Rare paths can leave the sampling square by a large distance, and their exterior contribution is absent from the local lower-bound argument. Controlling those excursions remains necessary for equality.

[Lemma G-global-spectra-tensoring of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The smash product $\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*\times\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}\to\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ is a left Quillen bifunctor for the $\mathchoice{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}$-model structure on $\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*$ and the $G$-global model structure on $\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$. Moreover, if $X\in\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*$ is $\mathchoice{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}$-cofibrant, then $X\smashp{-}$ is fully homotopical, and if $Y\in\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ is flat, so is ${-}\smashp Y\colon\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*\to\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$.
    \begin{proof}
        The pushout product axiom for cofibrations follows from Lemmas~(lemma:restr-gl-sp-right-Quillen of the paper) and~(lemma:restr-inj-gl-sp-left-Quillen of the paper) as in the proof of Lemma~(lemma:G-Top*-tensored of the paper). Moreover, if $X\in\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*$ is $\mathchoice{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{\hbox{\hfuzz=20pt\hbox{$\mathcal A\kern-.3pt$}\setbox0=\hbox{$\ell\kern-.75pt\ell$}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern-.075pt\unhcopy0}\hbox to 0pt{\hfuzz=8pt\kern.075pt\unhcopy0}\box0\kern.05pt}}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}{{\mathcal{A}}\kern-.3pt\ell\kern-.6pt\ell}$-cofibrant, then $X\smashp{-}\cong\Sigma^\infty X\smashp{-}$ is homotopical by Proposition~(prop:gl-flatness of the paper), as is ${-}\smashp Y$ for any flat $Y$. With these established, the pushout-product axiom for acyclic cofibrations then follows as in the proof of Proposition~(prop:smash-gl-left-Quillen of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma G-global-spectra-tensoring of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
[Lemma l:palm_conc of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple point process satisfying the Palm correlation bound (equation e:bd_palmcorr of the paper). Then for a bounded Borel set $B \subset \mathbb{R}^d$,

\begin{align}\nonumber \sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_p \in \mathbb{R}^d} \mathbb{P}_{\bk x1p} \bigl(\mathcal{P}(B) \geq \hat{\kappa}_p|B| + p + t \bigr) \le
& \exp\Bigl(-t\Bigl(\log(1+\frac{t}{\hat{\kappa}_p|B|})-1\Bigr)\Bigr), \ \ \ p \in \mathbb{N}, \ \ \ t > 0.
\end{align}

body:
[Lem prob expression of arXiv:2505.11700, 'Distribution of the cokernels of determinantal row-sparse matrices'] Let $\underline{n}=(n_a)_{a \in G}$ and $q \in S(\underline{n})$. Then
$$
\mathbb{P}(A_nq = 0) = \frac{1}{k_n}n^{-(k_n-1)n} \det(M) \prod_{a \in G_+} (n(k_n-1)_a^{n_a -1}). 
$$
Moreover, the matrix $M$ is positive semi-definite.

body:
[Corollary cor:lower_bounds of arXiv:2607.22908, 'Epidemic Phase Transitions in the Zero-Range Process'] For any relative deviation $\delta \in (0, 1)$ and corresponding absolute deviation $\varepsilon = \rho\delta \in (0, \rho)$:
  \begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P}(\bar{X} \le \rho(1-\delta)) \le \exp\braces*{ -n \frac{\rho \delta^2}{2\Gamma}},
    \qquad 
    \mathbb{P}(\bar{X} \le \rho - \varepsilon) \le \exp\braces*{ -n \frac{\varepsilon^2}{2 \Gamma \rho} }.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2607.22878, 'Clustering of large deviations in heavy-tailed moving averages: the catastrophe principle '] For every $M> \max(|a_0|, |a_L|)$, 
$0<\eps<\min_{l=0,\ldots, L+1}(a_l-a_{l-1})$ and $0<\delta<\delta_0$, 
\begin{align} 
  &\limsup_{n\to \infty} \, \bigl(n P(h^{(n)} \|Z\| > \lambda_
    n)\bigr)^{-1}\left[ \sum_{|i| 
          \leq Mn}E\bigl( e^{-g(i/n,    G_i^{(n)}Z_i/\lambda_n)}
  \one_{\Psi}(H_i^{(n)} Z_i/\lambda_n)\bigr) \right.\\
 \notag &\left. \hskip 0.05in - n\eps \sum_{l=0}^{L+1} \sum_{a_{l-1}/\eps\leq
                 k<a_l/\eps} \sum_{j=1}^{m_l} e^{-b_{lj}}P\bigl(
                 H_{[kn\eps]}^{(n)}Z_i/\lambda_n \in  \Psi^{\delta},  G_{[kn\eps]}^{(n)} Z_i/\lambda_n \in A_{lj}^\delta \bigr)\right] 
\leq f(\eps)  
  \end{align}
  and
\begin{align} 
  &\liminf_{n\to \infty}  \, \bigl(n P(h^{(n)} \|Z\| > \lambda_
    n)\bigr)^{-1}\left[ \sum_{|i| 
          \leq Mn}E\bigl( e^{-g(i/n,    G_i^{(n)}Z_i/\lambda_n)}
  \one_{\Psi}(H_i^{(n)} Z_i/\lambda_n)\bigr) \right.\\
 \notag &\left. \hskip 0.05in - n\eps \sum_{l=1}^L \sum_{a_{l-1}/\eps\leq
                 k<a_l/\eps} \sum_{j=1}^{m_l} e^{-b_{lj}}P\bigl(
                 H_{[kn\eps]}^{(n)}Z_i/\lambda_n \in \Psi^{-\delta}, G_{[kn\eps]}^{(n)} Z_i /\lambda_n \in A_{lj}^{-\delta} \bigr)\right] 
\geq -f(\eps)  
  \end{align}
  for a nonnegative function $f$ with $f(\eps)\to 0$ as $\eps\to
  0$. Here $a_{-1}=-M, \, a_{L+1}=M, \, m_{-1}=m_{L+1}=1$ and
  $b_{-1,1}=b_{L+1,1}=0$.

body:
[Corollary 2 of arXiv:2607.28992, 'Minimal inversion of a permuton sample'] Let $\mu$ be a permuton which admits a piece-wise continuous and strictly positive density $f:[0,1]^2\rightarrow(0,\infty)$ continuous at $(0,0)$ and at $(1,1)$.
    Let $\minv_n^\mu$ be the minimal inversion of $n$ points distributed according to $\mu$, as defined in~\eqref{eq:main}.
    Then, the random variable $\minv_n^\mu$ satisfies
    \begin{align*}
        n^{-1/2}\minv_n^\mu
        \dconv\ray[2,\frac{f(0,0)+f(1,1)}{2}]
    \end{align*}
    as $n$ goes to infinity, where the convergence occurs in distribution.

body:
[Lem 16 of arXiv:2608.15379, 'Stochastic Jacobi fields along discontinuous martingales on Riemannian submanifolds'] Let $D$ be an open set. Let $D_1,D_2$ be relatively compact open sets in $E$ satisfying \eqref{opensets}. Let $u \in \cF^D_{loc}(M) \cap L^{\infty}_{loc}(D)$ be an $\cE$-harmonic map on $D$.
Assume that the Dirichlet form $(\cE,\cF)$ satisfies \thetag{C} with a vector field  $\cH$ on $E$.
In addition, assume that $\cH u \in \cF^{D}_{loc}\cap L^{\infty}_{loc}(D)$ and satisfies \thetag{A} and \thetag{B}. Set $\bu:=(u,\cH u)$.
Let
\[
\bu = \bv + \bh
\]
be the componentwise decomposition defined by \eqref{HarmDecom}. Let $v=\pi_1\circ \bv, \bv_2=\pi_2 \circ \bv$. 
Then it holds that for any $\mathcal{X}\in \mathfrak{X}(M)$,
\begin{align*} 
\int_0^{t\land \tau_{D_1}} \langle \mathcal{X}(u(Z_-)), dN^{[\bv_2]}\rangle_{\delta_{\mathbb{R}^d}} = -\int_0^{t\land \tau_{D_1}} \langle \II(\mathcal{X}\circ u, \cH u), dN^{[v]}\rangle_{\delta_{\mathbb{R}^d}}
\end{align*}
for $t\geq 0,\ \Prob_z\text{-a.s. for q.e.}\ z\in E$.

body:
[Corollary 7 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\equiv c>0$ and $V\in C_b(\R)$. Then
\[
\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-\sup_\R V
\le\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)\le
\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-\inf_\R V.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)}{|\log\alpha|}\longrightarrow\frac{c}{R_+}
\qquad(\alpha\downarrow0).
\]
Under the edge hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:heteroHamiltonian},
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)
=\frac{c}{R_+}\left[\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}
+p\log\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}-p\log R_+-\log(R_+A)-1\right]+O(1).
\]
If, in addition, $V\equiv a_0$, then
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=\alpha d\,\cH\!\left(\frac{c}{\alpha d}\right)-a_0
=\sup_{s\in\R}\{cs-\alpha d(M(s)-1)\}-a_0.
\]
If $s_\alpha>0$ is the optimizer, then $\alpha dM'(s_\alpha)=c$ and
\[
(\Lambda_D^\R)'(\alpha)=-d(M(s_\alpha)-1)<0,\qquad
(\Lambda_D^\R)''(\alpha)=\frac{c^2}{\alpha^3dM''(s_\alpha)}>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=-a_0+\frac{c^2}{2\alpha dD_2(J)}
-\frac{D_4(J)c^4}{24\alpha^3d^3D_2(J)^4}+O(\alpha^{-5})
\qquad(\alpha\to+\infty),
\]
and, under the edge hypothesis,
\[
\Lambda_D^\R(\alpha)=\frac{c}{R_+}\left[\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}
+p\log\log\frac{c}{\alpha d}-p\log R_+-\log(R_+A)-1+o(1)\right]-a_0
\]
as $\alpha\downarrow0$. Finally, for
$\cA_{\sigma,m,\R}u=\sigma^{-m}(J_\sigma*u-u)+cu'+a_0u$,
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,\R})=\sigma^{-m}\cH(c\sigma^{m-1})-a_0.
\]

body: [Definition of arXiv:2412.02777, 'How to quantify the coherence of a set of beliefs'] Two coherent credence bases $(V, \boldsymbol q)$ and $(V', \boldsymbol q')$ are \textit{content equivalent} if $\langle\bar V\rangle=\langle\bar V'\rangle$ and the credence base $((V, V'), (\boldsymbol q, \boldsymbol q'))$ is coherent.

[Theorem thm:Push-TASEP-multipoint of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] The dressed edge weights satisfy the mixed diamond
equation
\begin{align}
& (\partial_t \mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a},
\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{1}})
\mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a},
\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{1}}^{-1}
- (\partial_t \mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{1},
\mathbf{n}})
\mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{1},
\mathbf{n}}^{-1} \notag \\
& \qquad + \mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{1},
\mathbf{n}}
\mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{1},
\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{1}}^{-1}
- \mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a},
\mathbf{n}}
\mathcal{M}_{t,\mathbf{a},
\mathbf{n}+\mathbf{1}}^{-1} = 0
\end{align}
at every $(t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n})$ with $t > 0$,
$1 \le n_1 < \cdots < n_m$, and
$a_i < y_{n_i+1} - 1$ for all~$i$.

body:
REFUTED AUXILIARY CLAIM: every density-one periodic force-balanced configuration for the repulsive three-dimensional Riesz potential |r|^{-s}, s>3, has nonnegative second variation under every finitely supported displacement. The sc-compact entry is a counterexample: Z^3 is force balanced and has a finite-support negative second variation. This false universal bridge is distinct from P0309 and from a properly conditional harmonic calculation.
This entry records a false auxiliary statement with its counterexample
It must not be used as a theorem
title: Refuted auxiliary bridge: force balance implies Hessian positivity

body:
[Lem L1L2 of arXiv:2504.19942, 'The edge-averaging process on graphs \\ with random initial opinions'] Fix a vertex $o\in V$. Then, for every $t>0$,
$$\|f_t(o)\|_1\leq \|f_0(o)\|_1\, .$$
If $\mathrm{Var}(f_0(o))<\infty$, then we also have
$$\mathrm{Var}(f_t(o))=\mathbb{E}[Q_t]\mathrm{Var}(f_0(o)).$$
title: Lem L1L2 of arXiv:2504.19942

[Theorem 10 (Classical central-section extremizers; see \cite{MeyerPajor,Koldobsky1998,Eskenazis,ChasapisNayarTkocz}) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $0<p<2$ and $n\ge2$. For every $\theta\in\sphere$,
\begin{equation}
 A_{p,n,0}(\diag)
 \le
 A_{p,n,0}(\theta)
 \le
 A_{p,n,0}(e_1).
\end{equation}
The right equality occurs exactly for coordinate directions $\{\pm e_i\}$, and the left equality occurs exactly for diagonal directions
\[
 \left\{\frac1{\sqrt n}(\pm1,\ldots,\pm1)\right\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Classical central-section extremizers; see \cite{MeyerPajor,Koldobsky1998,Eskenazis,ChasapisNayarTkocz}

body: [Corollary cor:stability of arXiv:2509.08430, 'One-dimensional particle clouds with elastic collisions'] The Markov chain~$\eta$ on ${\mathbb Z}_+^{N-1}$ is positive recurrent if and only if~(equation eq:stability_condition of the paper) holds. If positive recurrent, then~$\eta$ is geometrically ergodic, meaning that the stationary distribution has a finite exponential moment. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:stability of arXiv:2509.08430

body:
[Thm LSS of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'] Fix $\hat{D}, K' < \infty$. Then there exists a function $\sigma: [0,1] \to [0,1]$ (depending on $\hat{D}$ and $K'$)
   such that $\lim_{q \to 1} \sigma(q) = 1$
   with the following property. Let $\hat{G}$ be any graph with degree at most $\hat{D}$ and let
   $X$ be a random subset of sites of $\hat{G}$ which has ``dependence range $K'$'' in the sense that
   for any $K'$-separated subset $S \subset \hat{G}$, the collection of events
   \[
      \left \{ \{ s \in X \} : s \in S \right\}
   \]
   is mutually independent.
   Suppose also that for some $q \in [0,1]$, $\mathbb{P}( v \in X ) \ge q$ for all $v \in \hat{V}$.
   Then there exists a coupling of $X$ and $\hat{G}_{\sigma(q)}$ such that
   \[
      \hat{G}_{\sigma(q)} \subset X
   \]
   almost surely,
   where $\hat{G}_{\sigma(q)}$ is independent Bernoulli site percolation on $\hat{G}$ with parameter 
   $\sigma(q)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{LSS} Corollary 1.4

[Prop MDPcppp of arXiv:2412.09471, 'On the moderate deviation principles in the sparse multi-type Erd\H{o}s R\'enyi random gra'] Under the Assumption~(assump1 of the paper), for any sequence $a_n$ such that $1\ll a_n\ll\sqrt{n}$, suppose that $|\mu^n-\mu|=O\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)$ and $\alpha\in{\mathbb R}_+^d$ satisfy $\alpha_r\le\mu_r$ for all $r\in{\mathcal S}$. Let $\{\alpha^n\}\subset{\mathbb R}_+^d$ be a sequence such that $\alpha^n\rightarrow\alpha$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$ and $0<\alpha^n_r\le\mu^n_r$ for all $r\in{\mathcal S}$. Under condition $X_{i,r}^n\leq \alpha^n_r n$ for all $i\geq 1$ and $r\in{\mathcal S}$, 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item [(i)]  the sequence of random vectors 
        $$\frac{1}{a_n\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N(Z_n n)}X_i^{n}-c^n n\right)$$
        satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function  
        $$j_1(x)=\frac{1}{2}\<x, \Phi^{-1} x\>,$$
        where $\Phi^{-1}=D_{c}^{-1}-\kappa$;
        \item [(ii)] the sequence of random vectors 
        $$\frac{1}{a_n\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor(|c^n|-\frac12\langlec^n,\kappac^n\rangle)n+a_n\sqrt{n}x\rfloor}X_i^{n}-c^n n-\frac{c^n a_n\sqrt{n}x}{|c^n|-\frac 12\langle c^n, \kappac^n\rangle}\right)$$
        satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function 
        $$
       j_2(x)= \frac12 \bigg\langle x,\left(\Phi-\frac{cc^T}{|c|-\frac12\langlec,\kappac\rangle}\right)^{-1}x \bigg\rangle;
        $$
        
      \item [(iii)]the sequence of random vectors 
        \[\frac{1}{a_n\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N(Z_n n)}X_i^{n}\mathbbm{1}_{\{X^{n}_i\neq k\}}-(c^n-kh(k)) n\right)
        \]
        satisfies the moderate deviation principle with speed $a_n^2$ and rate function  
        \[
        j_3(x)=\frac{1}{2}\<x,(\Phi-kk^Th(k))^{-1}x\>.
        \]
        
        
    \end{enumerate}
title: Prop MDPcppp of arXiv:2412.09471

body:
Let n>=2, K>0, and let x=(x_1,...,x_n) and y=(y_1,...,y_n) be real random vectors whose 2n coordinates are mutually independent, each with a Lebesgue density bounded almost everywhere by K. Let Z be a deterministic real n by n matrix, u,v deterministic real n-vectors, and w a deterministic real scalar. Write sigma_1(Z)>=...>=sigma_n(Z)>=0 for its singular values, and assume r=rank(Z)>=2. Then Q=x^T Z y+x^T u+v^T y+w has a Lebesgue density satisfying ||p_Q||_infinity <= 2(C_RV K)^2 sqrt(2e*pi) min_{2<=j<=r} [j^(-1/2) (product_{i=1}^j sigma_i(Z))^(-1/j)], where C_RV is the universal constant in the Rudelson-Vershynin bounded-density projection theorem. Equivalently one may minimize over 2<=j<=n, interpreting terms with zero singular-value product as infinity. This is the k=1 corollary of Banks, Garza-Vargas, Kulkarni and Srivastava, arXiv:2005.08930. No bounded-density bound is available in general at rank one: if U,V are independent uniform(0,1), UV has density -log(t) on 0<t<1, which is unbounded near zero. Independence only between the two vectors is insufficient even at rank two: x=(U,U), y=(V,V), Z=diag(1,-1) gives Q=0 almost surely. A quadratic-form application must independently verify the coordinate independence and rank hypotheses.
n>=2 and K>0
All 2n coordinates of x and y are mutually independent and each has a Lebesgue density bounded a.e. by K
Z,u,v,w are deterministic real coefficients
rank(Z)>=2

[Proposition prop:c2fail of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] For $\varepsilon>0$ define directions in $\mathbb{R}^4$
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_0&=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_2), & d_1&=e_1,\ d_2=e_2,\\
d_3&=-\varepsilon(e_3+e_4), & d_4&=e_3,\ d_5=e_4,\\
d_6&=-\varepsilon(e_1+e_3), & d_7&=-\varepsilon(e_2+e_4),
\end{aligned}
\]
with masses $s_0=s_3=s_6=s_7=\frac1{4(1+2\varepsilon)}$ and
$s_1=s_2=s_4=s_5=\frac{\varepsilon}{2(1+2\varepsilon)}$, realized as a
whitened system through Lemma~(lem:realize of the paper). Exactly the four points
$d_0,d_3,d_6,d_7$ are strictly $4$-generated, and the four side points
$d_1,d_2,d_4,d_5$ are not generated by the other rays at all. The exact
Mahalanobis norms are
\[
\lVert v\rVert^2=\frac{2\varepsilon(3\varepsilon+2)}{\varepsilon+1}
\ \text{(generated points)},\qquad
\lVert v\rVert^2=\frac{\varepsilon^2+4\varepsilon+2}{\varepsilon(\varepsilon+1)}
\ \text{(side points)} .
\]
For $0<\varepsilon<\frac{\sqrt{33}-3}{12}\approx0.2287$, all generated
points have $t=1/\lVert v\rVert^2>1$ and all side points have $t<1$: no point is
simultaneously cheap and generated. At $\varepsilon=\frac1{100}$ the values
are exactly $t=\frac{5050}{203}$ and $t=\frac{101}{20401}$.

body: In computability theory, Rice's theorem states that all non-trivial semantic properties of programs are undecidable. A semantic property is one about the program's behavior, unlike a syntactic property. A non-trivial property is one that is neither true for every program, nor false for every program.
title: Rice's theorem

body: In mathematics, the pigeonhole principle states that if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item. For example, of three gloves, at least two must be right-handed or at least two must be left-handed, because there are three objects but only two categories of handedness to put them into. This seemingly obvious statement, a type of counting argument, can be used to demonstrate possibly unexpected results. For example, given that the population of London is more than one unit greater than the maximum number of hairs that can be on a human head, the principle requires that there must be at least two people in London who have the same number of hairs on their heads.
title: Pigeonhole principle

[Defn 3 (Model envelopes) of arXiv:2609.03296, 'Nonuniqueness of Model Potentials and Weak Geodesic Rays'] Let \((X,\omega)\) be a compact K\"ahler manifold. For an upper-semicontinuous
function \(f\), set
\[
 P_\omega(f)
 :=
 \left(
 \sup\{v\in\PSH(X,\omega)\mid v\leq f\}
 \right)^*.
\]
For \(\phi\in\PSH(X,\omega)\) with \(\sup_X\phi=0\), define
\[
 P_\omega[\phi]
 :=
 \left(
 \lim_{C\to\infty}P_\omega\bigl(\min\{\phi+C,0\}\bigr)
 \right)^*.
\]
We call \(\phi\) an \emph{\(\omega\)-model potential} if
\(P_\omega[\phi]=\phi\). It has positive mass if its non-pluripolar
Monge--Amp\`ere measure has strictly positive total mass.
title: Model envelopes

A single polynomial-time instance-uniform oracle sampler for all positive-normalizer {0,1,4}-weighted oracle circuits at TV accuracy 1/10 implies NP^O subset RP^O subset P^O/poly; this sampler-interface route cannot establish T410 Target 2. No Target 2 common oracle is constructed, and no novelty priority is claimed.
Uniform polynomial running-time/randomness bounds in the arbitrary weight-circuit description length, including hardwired instances
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:cd7babe876c3357d888afeb8ef19c6394e317abef58a458426469b0be2afe042","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/cd/cd7babe876c3357d888afeb8ef19c6394e317abef58a458426469b0be2afe042.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:5d544a0cbc0f2ffed98a3664ea50e70ceeb525f95c42c1200e5418673643b262","bundle_entry_key":"instance_uniform_weighted_sampler_barrier","bundle_id":"population.t410-oracle-sampling-barriers-protected-blocks-003","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"computational complexity; conditional sampling; relative entropy; autoregressive scoring","draft":"w739/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:instance_uniform_weighted_sampler_barrier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Instance-uniform sampling is incompatible with Target 2 circuit hardness

Claim C005 v1. Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: route-failure. Target: 2.
No novelty priority is claimed. This is an elementary necessary restriction
on an oracle construction, not a separation or an impossibility of C003 A.

## Exact hypothesis

Fix an oracle O. Suppose there is one randomized oracle algorithm U which,
given an explicit description of any deterministic oracle circuit C on m bits,
with output in {0,1,4} and positive total weight, samples a distribution within
total variation 1/10 of the law assigning probability C(z)/sum C to z.
Its time and randomness are bounded by one polynomial in the description
length and m. The quantifier includes circuits containing a fixed input x as
constants. Ordinary polynomial-size circuits may use O gates, in the usual
bit-query model. This is an INSTANCE-UNIFORM sampler interface.

Then NP^O is contained in RP^O, and consequently NP^O is contained in P^O/poly.
It is therefore incompatible with the circuit-hardness requirement of Target 2.

## Verifier reduction

Let A be any NP^O language, with a polynomial-time oracle verifier V(x,w)
and exactly p(|x|) witness bits after padding. Given x, construct in polynomial
time a circuit C_x with m=1+p(|x|) input bits. It assigns weight 1 to 0^m,
weight 4 to 1w when V(x,w) accepts, and zero to all other strings. The circuit
is polynomial-size: unroll the bounded verifier, with oracle gates for its
queries, and hardwire x. Its normalizer is 1+4 Z_x, where Z_x counts witnesses.
No normalizer computation is used by the reduction.

Run U on C_x. Accept only if the sampled word is 1w and V(x,w) actually
accepts. On a no input this never accepts. On a yes input the target event has
mass 4Z_x/(1+4Z_x)>=4/5. Total variation at most 1/10 leaves acceptance
probability at least 7/10. This proves A is in RP^O. The running time is
polynomial in |x| because U has one polynomial bound uniform over descriptions.

## Relativized randomized-to-advice step

For each input length n, repeat the preceding test independently k=n+2 times
and accept if any run accepts. A yes input is rejected with probability at
most (3/10)^k; a no input is never accepted. The union bound over all 2^n
inputs of length n gives probability of any mistake at most

    2^n (3/10)^(n+2) = (9/100)(3/5)^n < 1.

Thus there is one fixed polynomial-length collection of k random tapes that
works simultaneously for EVERY length-n input. Hardwire those tapes as advice
and unroll the oracle computation into a polynomial-size oracle circuit.
Only the independent repetitions on a single input were multiplied; inputs
need no independence. This proves A is in P^O/poly. The tape collection may
depend on n and O, exactly as the circuit model permits.

## Why this does not contradict C003

C003 A has quantifier form: for every fixed uniform weighted family W, there
exists a uniform polynomial-time sampler S_W. It supplies neither a computable
compiler W to S_W nor a polynomial bound uniform over weight descriptions.
In the reduction above x varies with the INSTANCE, not just with the length.
Replacing the family-specific samplers by a single sampler accepting C_x would
be an extra assumption, which is precisely what the theorem rules out.

C004 encoded a unary input into a polynomially related output length and so
did not require this additional uniformity. Encoding every binary x into its
own length requires exponentially many lengths; it does not yield a polynomial
time reduction and cannot silently convert C003 A into this stronger property.

Therefore an oracle construction for C003 must achieve family-specific
sampling without a polynomial-time instance-uniform weight-circuit interface.
It must also preserve hardness after all sampling/inversion interfaces are
available. Neither this proof nor C004 proves such a construction exists.
The joint oracle consistency problem for binary NP circuit hardness is OPEN.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:a709e45865929b025dd7f8ab22e9a633f013cb492fed61e532bf39a91f8c0201","revision_digest":"sha256:d9fe42072d4cba052697690bd26cd19d3d236739c096685e652aa411c85317b6","source_id":"own-work:T410-w739-C005-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T21:39:37.775816+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}
title: Instance-uniform weighted sampling forces NP into RP and P/poly (unaudited)

body:
[Theorem thm:CD_schur_averaging of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Suppose that (ass:fundamental of the paper) holds and $A^\varepsilon$ is constant.
Denote the Jacobian of the unscaled drift by
\[
\mathcal Jb(z)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\nabla_x b_1(z) & \nabla_y b_1(z)\\
\nabla_x b_2(z) & \nabla_y b_2(z)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Define
\[
\mathsf S(z)
:=\mathrm{diag}(a_1,a_2)^{1/2}\,\mathrm{Sym}\!\bigl(-\mathcal Jb(z)\bigr)\,\mathrm{diag}(a_1,a_2)^{1/2}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathsf S_{11}(z) & \mathsf S_{12}(z)\\
\mathsf S_{21}(z) & \mathsf S_{22}(z)
\end{pmatrix},
\]
and assume that there exist $\varepsilon_0>0$ and $\kappa\ge0$ such that for all $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$ and all $z\in E$,
\[
\mathsf S_{11}(z)\succ 0,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}\!\Bigl(\mathrm{Schur}(\mathsf S_{11})(z)\Bigr)\ge -\kappa,
\]
where $\mathrm{Schur}(\mathsf S_{11})(z):=\mathsf S_{22}(z)-\mathsf S_{21}(z)\mathsf S_{11}(z)^{-1}\mathsf S_{12}(z)$.
Then (ass:CDkappa of the paper) holds uniformly in $\varepsilon$, i.e.\ $(P_t^\varepsilon)_{t\ge0}$ satisfies $CD(-\kappa,\infty)$ for all $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$.

[Lemma 2 (Linearized forward equation) of arXiv:2604.00937, 'Infinite Horizon Optimal Control of Forward-Backward Stochastic Volterra Equations with De'] The process $\dot{X}$ satisfies
\begin{align*}
\dot{X}(t) &= \int_0^t \left[ \frac{\partial b}{\partial x}(t,s)\dot{X}(s) + \frac{\partial b}{\partial x_1}(t,s)\dot{X}_1(s) + \frac{\partial b}{\partial u}(t,s)\beta(s) \right] ds \\
&\quad + \int_0^t \left[ \frac{\partial \sigma}{\partial x}(t,s)\dot{X}(s) + \frac{\partial \sigma}{\partial x_1}(t,s)\dot{X}_1(s) + \frac{\partial \sigma}{\partial u}(t,s)\beta(s) \right] dB(s) \\
&\quad + \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{R}_0} \left[ \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial x}(t,s,e)\dot{X}(s) + \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial x_1}(t,s,e)\dot{X}_1(s) + \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial u}(t,s,e)\beta(s) \right] \tilde{N}(ds,de),
\end{align*}
where $\dot{X}_1(t) = \dot{X}(t-\delta)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Linearized forward equation

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2604.26549, 'Existence and uniqueness results of a stochastic nonlinear heat equation with a constraint'] Let $u_0\in \Vp\cap \bM$ be fixed. Then, we call that problem \eqref{eqn-main-prob-Ito}  has a \emph{strong solution} if and only if for every stochastic basis $(\Omega,\Fn,\Fb,\Pr)$  and every $\mathbb{R}^M-$valued $\Fb-$Wiener process $$W= (W_1, \dots, W_M),$$ there exists a $\Fb-$progressively measurable process $u :[0, T] \times\Omega \to D(A)$ with $\Pr-$a.e. paths
		$$u(\cdot,\omega)\in C([0,T];\Vp)\cap L^2(0,T;D(A))\cap L^{2p-2}(0,T;L^{2p-2}(\bO))$$ such that for all $t\in [0, T]$, $\Pr-$a.s.
		\begin{align}
			u(t)& =u_0+ \int_0^t\big( \Delta u(s) -|u(s)|^{p-2}u(s) + ( \norm{\nabla u(s)}_{L^2(\bO)}^2 + \norm{u(s)}_{L^p(\bO)}^p ) u(s)\big)ds\\
			& \quad + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^M\int_0^t\kappa_i(u(s))ds+ \sum_{i=1}^M\int_0^t\Nn_i(u(s))dW_i(s),
		\end{align}
		in $L^2(\bO)$, i.e., 
		\eqref{eqn-strong-form} is satisfied.

body: [Theorem thm:McCann of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $P,Q \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. There exists a coupling measure $\pi \in \Pi(P,Q)$ with cyclically monotone support contained in the graph of the subdifferential of a closed convex function $\psi$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$. If $P$ vanishes on all sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $d -1$, then $\psi$ is differentiable $P$-almost everywhere, $(\nabla\psi)_{\#}P=Q$, and the map $\nabla\psi$ is uniquely determined $P$-almost everywhere. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Brenier's Theorem, Main Theorem in \citet{McCann1995}

body: [Definition 4.1 (Statistically δ-hyperbolic) of arXiv:2606.10238, 'Hyperbolic Neural Population Geometry Benefits Computation'] Let S be a space equipped with a distance function d. [Definition 3 (Fixed nondegenerate \(C^2\) Jordan curve) of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] A map \(\gamma:\mathbb T\to\mathbb R^2\) is called a fixed nondegenerate
\(C^2\) Jordan curve if \(\gamma\) is a \(C^2\) embedding and satisfies
 \[
     \inf_{t\in\mathbb T}|\gamma'(t)|>0,
     \qquad
    \inf_{t\in\mathbb T}
     |\det(\gamma'(t),\gamma''(t))|>0.
 \]
When derivatives are written, \(\gamma\) is represented by the associated
\(1\)-periodic \(C^2\) map
\(\bar\gamma=\gamma\circ\pi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^2\), where
\(\pi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb T\) is the quotient map; the notation
\(\gamma'(t)\), \(\gamma''(t)\) refers to the derivatives of
\(\bar\gamma\) at any representative of \(t\in\mathbb T\).
title: Fixed nondegenerate \(C^2\) Jordan curve

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2505.21774, 'The friendship paradox for trees'] {\bf [Densities of vertex types for infinite trees]}

\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] 
Let $\mathcal{T}_\infty$ be the infinite Galton-Watson tree with offspring distribution $p$ satisfying \eqref{eq:pcond}. Then, for each $\chi \in S$, there exists $f^\chi$  such that 
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty} \frac{N_m^\chi}{N_m} = f^\chi \quad \PP\text{-}\mathrm{a.s.}
\] 
\item[(b)] 
For $k \in \N$, let $S_k= \sum_{l=1}^k X_l$, where $(X_l)_{l=1}^k$ are drawn independently from $p$, and let $\tilde{X}$ be drawn independently from $\tilde{p}$. Then
\[
f^\chi = \sum_{k \in \N_0} p_k\,\PP\Big({\rm sign}\big[\tX+S_k-k(k+1)\big] = \chi\Big).
\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2505.21774

body:
[Lemma lem:EA-term of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Let $G=G_{A,y_t,\beta}$ be the Gibbs measure of the planted SK model with tilt $y_t$ at time $t\in[0,T]$, with
\[
m:=\langle\sigma\rangle\in(-1,1)^n,
\qquad
P:=\mathop{{}\boldsymbol{\mathrm{Cov}}}(G),\qquad P_{ij}=\langle\sigma_i\sigma_j\rangle-\langle\sigma_i\rangle\langle\sigma_j\rangle.
\]
Let
\[
q:=\frac{\|m\|_2^2}{n},
\qquad
c:=\beta^2(1-q) = \frac{\beta^2}{n}\mathsf{Tr}[P],
\qquad
V:=\frac{2\beta^2}{n}mm^{\mathsf{T}},
\qquad
S:=D+cI_n-V.
\]
Then,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal E_A
= -\beta^2\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}[\mathsf{Tr}[P^2]] - 3\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\left[c^2\mathsf{Tr}[P^2]\right] + O(1)
+\mathcal R_A^{V}
+\mathcal R_A^{\mathrm{resp}},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{itemize}[itemsep=0.25em]
\item $\mathcal R_A^{V}$ is the collection of all contributions containing at least one copy of $V$, and
\item $\mathcal R_A^{\mathrm{resp}}$ is the collection of all ``response'' contributions coming from
Gaussian integration-by-parts in $A$ where at least one $A$--derivative hits either $D$, $c$,
or produces a non-diagonal spin-correlation response\,. 
\end{itemize}
title: Controlling the $\mathcal E_A$ term and exact cancellations

Own-work draft, C006 version 2, proof (unaudited); priority not established. Fix L>=3, d>=1, H=L-1, equal hidden widths m, a C2 activation with |sigma|, |sigma prime|, |sigma double prime|<=1, and data ||x||<=1, |y|<=1. Let h1_i=sigma(w_i dot x), hl_j=sigma(m^(-1)sum_i B^l_ji h(l-1)_i) for 2<=l<=H, and f=m^(-1)sum_j a_j hH_j, with half-squared population loss. Initialize two independent runs with w_i iid in [-1,1]^d, a_i iid in [-1,1] and entries of every B^l iid in [-1,1]; arrays are mutually independent and each array law is common across runs. Train all parameters by simultaneous fresh-sample SGD or finite minibatch averages, using multipliers m for a,w and m^2 for every middle matrix, with deterministic nonnegative steps summing to T<infinity. Set S2=sum eta_k^2, A=2exp(T), define M_l=1+2A^2 T product_{s=l+1}^H M_s backwards for l=H,...,2, W=sqrt(d)+2A^2 T product_{s=2}^H M_s, R=max(1,A,W,M_2,...,M_H), and r=6sqrt(d)m^(-1/(d+2))+6m^(-1/3)+6(L-2)m^(-1/2). A compatible tuple of hidden-layer permutations, selected only from the initial boundary arrays, has expected population loss-chord barrier <=8R^L exp(64L^2 R^(2L)T)[r+4L R^L sqrt(S2)]. Thus eta_max<=m^(-2/(d+2)) yields O_{L,d,T}(m^(-1/(d+2))) for every fixed depth. The boundary matchings and identity internal permutations suffice: each middle cut error adds linearly at initialization, and deterministic transpose cut estimates handle trained dependence. No bound uniform in growing depth, ReLU theorem, fixed-step independent-data limit, low-risk endpoint guarantee or independent audit is established.
All stated bounded smooth fixed-depth, fixed-horizon and independent iid initialization hypotheses
Fresh iid SGD data; deterministic steps; small-step condition required for width vanishing

[Lem 12 of arXiv:2511.22156, ''] There exists $\delta>0$ which is independent of $D_m(x)$ such that if $y,z\in G_m(x)$ and $\gamma (t),\ 0\leq t\leq 1$ is a continuous curve in $D_m(x)$ from $y$ to $\partial_o D_m(x)$, then 
\begin{equation}
    P^z(W\ hits \ \gamma \   before \ \tau) >\delta.
\end{equation}
\begin{proof}
Set 
\[
\partial_oG_m(x)= \partial([x_0^{(1)}-\frac{2}{3} 3^{m},x_0^{(1)}+\frac{2}{3} 3^{m}]\times [x_0^{(2)}-\frac{2}{3} 3^{m},x_0^{(2)}+\frac{2}{3} 3^{m}])\cap \tilde{F}_0.
\]
By applying the corner move (Theorem \ref{theorem3.3}) and knight move (Theorem \ref{theorem3.7}) construction inside the squares each of side length $3^{-m-2}$, surrounding $G_m(x)$ (see Figure \ref{fig:chain of squares}) for the process starting at $W_{\mathcal{T}_{\partial_oG_m(x)}}$, and by a same idea of \cite{barlow1989construction}, there is $\delta>0$ depending only on the number of small squares such that  
\[
P^z(W\hbox{ hits every }L\in \mathcal{H}_{m+2}\hbox{ that satisfies }L\cap \partial_oG_m(x)\neq\emptyset)>\delta.
\]
Noticing that in the above event $W$ divides $D_m(x)$ into two parts, one of which contains $G_m(x)$, it holds that
\[
P^z(W\ \hbox{hits} \ \gamma \   \hbox{before} \ \tau) \geq P^z(W\hbox{ hits every }L\in \mathcal{H}_{m+2}\hbox{ that satisfies }L\cap \partial_oG_m\neq\emptyset)>\delta.
\]
\end{proof}

Let $\hat{L}$ be the Finslerian metric induced by $L_0$ on the graph $G = \{(p,f(p)) : p \in M\} \subset M \times \mathbb{R}$. Since $\varphi(p) = (p,f(p))$ defines a diffeomorphism from $M$ onto $G$, it follows that
$$ \tilde{L}(v) = \varphi^*\hat{L} = L(v) + (df(v))^2 $$
is a Finslerian metric on $M$.

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \( (M^n, g) \) be a closed, connected, oriented, smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension \( n \geq 3 \), which is locally conformally flat with positive scalar curvature. Assume further that \( H_1(M^n; \mathbb{Z}) = 0 \) and that the fundamental group \( \pi_1(M) \) is finite.

\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] If \(n\) is even or \(n\equiv1\pmod4\), then \((M^n,g)\) is conformally equivalent to the standard sphere \((S^n,g_{st})\).

\item[(ii)] If \(n\equiv3\pmod4\), then \(\pi_1(M)\) is trivial or isomorphic to the binary icosahedral group \(I_{120}^*\cong\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_5)\); accordingly, \((M^n,g)\) is conformally equivalent to \((S^n,g_{st})\) or to a spherical space form \(S^n/\Gamma\) with \(\Gamma\cong I_{120}^*\). The congruence restriction is optimal: for every \(n\equiv3\pmod4\), both alternatives occur.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.00483, 'On Embedding Hamming Spheres with Applications to Positive Curvature'] Let $p$ be a prime and $k\ge2$, and set $m=(p^k-1)/(p-1)$. Let $\mathcal C_V$ be a projective code associated to $\mathrm{PG}(k-1,p)$. Then every $x\in\mathcal C_V$ has weight $w=p^{k-1}$, any two distinct $x,y\in\mathcal C_V$ satisfy $d(x,y)=b=p^{k-1}$, and
$$
|\mathcal C_V|=\gamma(p,b,w,m)=p^k-1.
$$
In particular,
$$
\gamma(p,b,w,m)<(p-1)m+1.
$$

body: Let (X, Sigma_X, mu) and (Y, Sigma_Y, nu) be sigma-finite measure spaces and let f be measurable on the product sigma-algebra of X times Y, with values in R or C. If the double integral of |f| over X times Y with respect to mu times nu is finite (f is integrable), then for a.e. x the slice y -> f(x,y) is integrable, for a.e. y the slice x -> f(x,y) is integrable, and integral_X integral_Y f dnu dmu = integral_Y integral_X f dmu dnu = integral over X times Y of f d(mu times nu). Tonelli's theorem gives the same conclusion for f merely nonnegative and measurable, integrals allowed to be +infinity.

[Lemstar lem:eigenfunctions of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Let $\Psi$ be a  branching mechanism. Recall $\rho\in [0,\infty]$ its largest zero.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Assume $\Psi$ supercritical: $\Psi'(0+)\in [-\infty,0)$ and $\rho\in (0,\infty]$.  Let $u_0\in (0, \rho)$ be fixed. Define for all $\theta\in \big(0,-\Psi'(0+)\big)$,
\begin{equation}f(x):=\int_0^{\rho} (1-e^{-xu})\frac{\theta}{-\Psi(u)}e^{-\int_{u_0}^{u}\frac{\theta}{\Psi(v)}\mathrm{d} v}\mathrm{d} u,\quad x\in (0,\infty).
\end{equation}
This is a well-defined increasing function, in $\mathrm{C}^2((0,\infty))$, which satisfies $x\mathrm{L}^{\Psi}f(x)=\theta f(x)$ for all $x\in (0,\infty)$.
Moreover, 
\[f(x)\underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\longrightarrow}\infty \Longleftrightarrow \int_0^{x_0}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{-\Psi(u)}=\infty \text{ for some } x_0\in (0,\rho).\]
\item Assume $\Psi$ non-immortal (not necessarily supercritical): $\rho\in [0,\infty)$. Let $u_0\in (\rho,\infty)$ be fixed. Define for all $\theta\in (0,\infty)$, \[f(x):=\int_{\rho}^{\infty}e^{-xu}\frac{1}{\Psi(u)}e^{\int_{u_0}^u\frac{\theta}{\Psi(v)}\mathrm{d} v}\mathrm{d} u,\ x\in (0,\infty).\]
This is a well-defined decreasing function, in $\mathrm{C}^2((0,\infty))$, which satisfies $x\mathrm{L}^{\Psi}f(x)=\theta f(x)$ for all $x\in (0,\infty)$. Moreover, \[f(x)\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\longrightarrow}\infty \Longleftrightarrow
\int_{x_0}^{\infty}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\Psi(u)}=\infty \text{ for some } x_0\in (\rho,\infty).\]
\end{enumerate}

The source has d unknown A/S context pairs, one arbitrary r-support A and one all-K S each, and N-2d known S contexts; it selects contexts uniformly then truths uniformly. Independently receive uniform ell-subsets of truths in BOTH variable contexts,ANY0<=ell<=r, and n actual iid untagged facts. Every realized generator must be source Mis_infinity<=c at exact score bins in ALL data-compatible worlds,0<=c<1/(2NrK),rational c. For each FIXED alphabet bound K0, C026 true-posterior native branch frontier and an attaining randomized robust policy are polynomial-time computable in growing d,n,N and rational budget bit size, for every verifier fraction in the coprime small-budget paired actual-iid model. Low whole contexts separate; whole choices are posterior prefixes per h; sorted-coefficient marked multiset DP solves allocation. No uniform polynomial-in-K, efficient global expectation or classical ERM/PAC claim. The C026 conditional Bayes minimum beta is min_branches,partitions(sum f*p/m-c*max f/m), where unresolved h=min union chooses paired residual (2(K-h),F,(2-h/r-h/K)/N), or F units(2,1,1/(NK)) at h=r, OR BOTH posterior-weighted whole contexts(K,F*pi,1/N),(K,F*(1-pi),1/N). Resolved A union j<r contributes(K-j,F,(r-j)/(Nr)),otherwise none. pi is the true original-data posterior defined by L(u,j)=(K/r)^u*binom(K-j,r-j)/binom(K-ell,r-ell). All lower-posterior whole contexts can be isolated. For any number of whole choices among pairs with the same h, keep the largest max(pi,1-pi) values. Enumerate those per-h prefix lengths. Remaining native types are at most2K-1. Sort selected high false counts, and candidate cell signatures by coefficient [lambda*m(s)-p(s)+e*c]/[m(s)+K*q],lambda=1/(NK),where q high whole objects and donor mark e are included. An ordered unbounded resource DP allocates contiguous high-count blocks with exactly one mark. Rearrangement and exchange arguments prove equality. This gives a polynomial-time estimator for every fixed K0 with growing VC d; polynomial degree depends on K0. Learning-policy symmetrization attains C026 global minimax E beta, without averaging generator laws. The global oracle penalty formula is unchanged. Aim: polynomial-time evaluation/attainment of beta_c(D) for every fixed

Write lambda=1/(NK). For each native object put deficit A=lambda*m-p>=0.

whereas every other high whole object and EVERY native paired/unit/A
object has risk>=F/(2K). All whole objects have zero deficit. Removing

weakly increases f_S/m_S on remaining pools, so increases (1); splitting

cannot decrease. Thus the exchange cannot worsen the objective.

## Proof details, exact evidence and limits

Low-context removal can be performed in increasing risk order: the
smallest low object in a cell has risk no larger than the mean of the
remaining components. Removing it increases the remaining mean risk
and leaves deficit A fixed. The isolated low object has deficit0.
Repeating yields all lows isolated. If a remaining pool is nonempty,
its components all have risk>=F/(2K), so the maximum risk is attained
among nonlow cells. A whole branch always supplies a high counterpart.
Thus low cells need not be marked even at positive c.

For the prefix exchange keep the old high object's pool assignment:
increasing its expected false count increases both its nonnegative
deficit benefit and its risk. Only an isolated low count decreases.
The multiset of unselected native components is identical for equal h,
including the F-unit saturated branch. Therefore neither budget nor
baseline invalidates the exchange.

For rearrangement, expand each cell coefficient b into q identical
slots. Swapping inverted high counts x>=y between coefficients b>=a
changes benefit by(x-y)*(b-a)>=0. This elementary identity proves the
needed assignment step without trusting an external formula. It also
applies to the single marked coefficient. Exactly one cell is marked;
optimizing its identity is equivalent to c*maximum risk. Native-only
cells have q0 and do not constrain the high order. Whole-only cells
have s0,q>0 and remain allowed.

For repeated knapsack choices, each step strictly increases
sum_t used_v_t+used_high. Processing resource states in that order
permits all repetitions of the current signature. Moving to the next
signature prevents decreasing coefficient order. Equal-coefficient
types may be canonically grouped because their total high contribution
does not depend on which of their equal-b slots receive particular
counts. This proves both directions of the DP correspondence.

The fixed-K type bound and polynomial cardinalities above concern
explicit data and rational c. Posterior numerators/denominators have
O(n log K+K) bits before common reductions. Rational DP path sums have
at most O(Kd) summands of polynomial bit size; exact comparisons and
sorting therefore preserve polynomial bit complexity. Uniform draws
of context swaps and atom permutations implement C026 policy
symmetrization in polynomial time. Backpointers reconstruct native
components, high-count slots and the marked cell; low whole objects
are isolated. C026 supplies the actual robust generator.

scripts/posterior_prefix_dp.py is a guarded exact prototype:
before resource allocation it bounds signature-times-state work by
two million per prefix choice. Reconstruction of the resource path
checks counts, contiguous high slots, single donor mark and benefit.
These box limits are not an asymptotic algorithm restriction.

logs/posterior_prefix_dp_check.json compares the sorted algorithm to
C026's UNRESTRICTED branch and multiset partition solver in1933 games,
including1340 below-half,529 saturated and1679 mixed-h cases.
It checks5510 prefix choices and200384 bounded state/signature products.
Cases include the C025 unit-splitting and internal budget-crossing
witness, plus three different true repetition posteriors at the same h.
This is a cross-check of different optimizations; it is not an
independent mathematical audit of their common C026 model reduction.

logs/posterior_prefix_controls_check.json uses genuine K3,r2,N7 data:
t_high=27/35,t_low=9/13. Keeping the lower posterior instead of the
higher at a fixed one-whole count loses1/13720; reversing high-count
assignment between two real native cell coefficients loses6/22295.
These strict controls show that the pruning and sorting are material.

q031 returned unrelated cards; q032 found the STANDARD rearrangement
inequality card claim_853521f6d5824f8aac2d37564a443ea7, walked in
recall/walk008.txt. Its printed statement lacks the promised displayed
inequality, so it supplies only a method-name pointer; the swap identity
above is the proof actually used. No duplicate rearrangement card is
queued. The inbox detector found a known-present own card before the
outside-inbox zero; no global absence or priority claim follows.

This establishes a fixed-alphabet efficient estimator in the specified
paired model IF the unaudited C026 characterization is correct. Its
global minimax value and learning penalty remain the expectations in
C026; this algorithm does NOT give polynomial-time exact evaluation of
those expectations for growing d,n. Uniform polynomial dependence on K,
noncoprime saturation, larger budgets and classical labeled ERM/PAC
remain open. Let \(S\) be the random walk with i.i.d.\ steps of law \(\calN(0,\beta)\). There are \(c>0, n_0\geq 1,\lambda_0\geq 0\) such that, for any \(\lambda\geq \lambda_0\) and \(n\geq n_0\),

[Prop prop_smooth_fit_2d of arXiv:2606.23648, '\textsc{Optimal Stopping for a Diffusion with Unobserved Bernoulli Drift}'] Let \(x\in\mathcal I\). Then \(U(x,\cdot)\) satisfies smooth fit at the
    upper boundary:
    \[
        \lim_{y\uparrow b(x)} D_y U(x,y)
        =
        \lim_{y\downarrow b(x)} D_y U(x,y)
        =
        k'(x+b(x)).
    \]
    If \(a(x)>-x\), then \(U(x,\cdot)\) also satisfies smooth fit at the lower
    boundary:
    \[
        \lim_{y\uparrow a(x)} D_y U(x,y)
        =
        \lim_{y\downarrow a(x)} D_y U(x,y)
        =
        k'(x+a(x)).
    \]

    Suppose, in addition, that the boundaries are \(C^1\) on an open interval \(J\subset\mathcal I\). Then \(U\) satisfies horizontal smooth fit as well. More precisely, if \(a(x)>-x\) on \(J\), then
    \begin{equation}
        Q'(x)G(a(x))+R'(x)=k'(x+a(x)),
        \qquad
        Q'(x)G(b(x))+R'(x)=k'(x+b(x)).
    \end{equation}
    If \(a(x)=-x\) on \(J\), then we have the upper-boundary identity
    \[
        Q'(x)G(b(x))+R'(x)=k'(x+b(x)), \qquad x \in J.
    \]

Let $f_{n}$ be a function with $||f_{n}||_{\infty} \leq 1$. Assume that $(n \pi_{n})$ is bounded. Then
$$n\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[(I_1^{(M_n)} - q_{n})\,\Delta_{n}(S_{M_n}) \mid S_n = -1\right]  \quad \mathop{\longrightarrow}_{n \rightarrow \infty} \quad0.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 84 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Let $\{f_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a family of complex, Lebesgue measurable functions $f_n$ on $[0,T]$.
Suppose that $\{f_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is uniformly integrable. Then the family $\{g_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of complex functions $g_n$ on $[0,T]$  defined in \eqref{eqn-g_n from f_n} 
 is uniformly absolutely continuous, that is, for every $\eps>0$, there exists $\delta> 0$ such that for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and for all pairwise disjoint segments $\{[x_i,y_i]\}_{1 \leq i \leq N }$: if 
\[
\sum_{i=1}^N \lvert y_i - x_i \rvert \leq \delta,
\]
then 
     \begin{equation*}
        \sum_{i=1}^N \lvert g_n(y_i) -  g_n(x_i) \rvert \leq \eps.
      \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop PropCarlo-Levy of arXiv:2506.08202, 'Stochastic dissipative systems in Banach spaces driven by L\'evy noise'] Let $d\in{\mathbb N}$, $H=L^2([0,1]^d)$ and $A$ be the realization of the Laplacian operator with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Assume that $\nu(H\backslash H_{1/4+\delta})=0$ and
\begin{equation}
\int_H {\left|z\right|}_\delta^2+{\left|z\right|}^4_{1/4+\delta}\nu(dz)<+\infty.
\end{equation}
The following two assertions hold true.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\{L_A(t)\}_{t\geq 0}$ is a càdlàg process in $H_\gamma$ with $\gamma<1/4+\delta$.
\item Let $\delta>\frac{d-1}{4}$. Then $\{L_A(t)\}_{t\geq 0}$ is a càdlàg process in $C([0,1]^d)$ and
\[
{\mathbb E}\left[\sup_{t\in [0,T]}{\left\|L_A(t)\right\|}^q_{C([0,1]^d)}\right]<+\infty,\qquad T>0,\, q\in [1,4).
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\bigcup_{\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}} \widehat{\amsmathbb{H}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})}.
\]
where $\epsilon$ is the unique bipartition of $\mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}$ such that $\epsilon(\boldsymbol{v}) = 1$. This is a bordered Riemann surface, whose boundary is the closure of the set of real points, that is the image in $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ of
\[
\bigcup_{\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}} \big(\widehat{\amsmathbb{R}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})} \setminus \amsmathbb{B}_{\boldsymbol{w}}^{\epsilon(\boldsymbol{w})}\big).
\]
See Figure~\ref{Fig:Half5} and \ref{Fig:Half7} for an example.
title: Half-spectral curve

[Corollary 69 of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] Let \(W\) be in the minimal Kahane--Peyri\`ere regime, and set
\(\chi=1-\mathbb E[W\log_2 W]\). In each of the following two settings---the fixed-arc setting of
Theorem~\ref{T:arc-main-endpoint} and the fixed-Jordan setting of
Theorem~\ref{T:jordan-main-endpoint}---the corresponding pushforward cascade
measure is Salem almost surely on the relevant non-extinction event if and
only if there exists \(a\in[1,2)\) such that
\[
    \mathbb P(W=a)=a^{-1},
    \qquad
    \mathbb P(W=0)=1-a^{-1}.
\]
Here Salem means that the Fourier dimension of the measure equals its
Hausdorff dimension.

Let M>=1 finite linear-regression tasks have matrices X_m in R^(n_m by d) and labels y_m. Suppose X_m*w_star=y_m for every m, put R=max_m||X_m||_2>0, and define L(w;m)=||X_m*w-y_m||^2/2 and L(w)=M^(-1)*sum_m L(w;m). Initialize w_0=0 and sample tau_1,...,tau_k independently and uniformly from{1,...,M}, with replacement. Scheme1 performs the exact update w_t=argmin_w {L(w;tau_t)+(lambda_t/2)*||w-w_(t-1)||^2}. Write D2=||w_0-w_star||^2. For a known integer horizon k>=3, choose lambda_t=lambda=R^2*(ln(k)-1)>0 and keep it fixed for all k rounds. Then E L(w_k)<=5*D2*R^2*ln(k)/k. Thus the coefficient is constant within a run and changes with the chosen horizon.
Finite jointly realizable linear tasks; R is the largest task-matrix operator norm and R>0.
Independent uniform task indices sampled with replacement; exact Scheme1 updates; w_0=0.
Known horizon k>=3; lambda=R^2*(ln(k)-1) used throughout the run.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Estimate the number of near-maximal configurations and compare with the connectivity threshold of the level set on the hypercube. Result: In the NK model with K = O(1) the fitness is a sum of n local terms each depending on K + 1 bits, so the field is a sum of n independent contributions (for the standard model with random neighbourhoods) and the level set at height M_n - delta_n with delta_n = o(n) but delta_n >> sqrt n contains exp(c delta_n^2/n)... the number of configurations within delta of the maximum is, by a large-deviation count, about exp(n I(delta/n)) for a rate I; bridges exist if this level set percolates on the hypercube, and a level set of density rho on the n-cube contains a giant connected component when the local structure allows, roughly when each configuration in the set has on average more than one neighbour in the set: the expected number of neighbours in the level set of a typical level-set point is n times the conditional probability that flipping one bit stays within delta of the maximum, which is n times (probability that the change of the K+1 affected local terms is at most delta), of order n delta/n = delta when delta is small compared to the local term scale... so bridges exist (heuristically) when delta_n >> 1, i.e. the level set within a constant deficit of the maximum is connected in the giant-component sense for deficits growing to infinity, while for bounded deficits the peaks are isolated. This suggests the answer depends on the deficit scale: bridges at deficit delta_n -> infinity, islands at bounded deficit. The argument is a branching heuristic (neighbour counts) without control of dependencies; making it rigorous would need a second-moment argument on the number of level-set paths, which I did not carry out. Key identity: Expected number of level-set neighbours of a level-set point is of order delta (the deficit); bridges expected iff the deficit tends to infinity. Obstruction: Second moment for level-set paths on the hypercube not done.

[Lemma 27 (Critical product lower divisor law) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Fix \(r\geq1\).  Suppose that, for every integer \(L\), compact
operators \(A_{j,L}\), \(1\leq j\leq r\), satisfy
\[
 s_k(A_{j,L})\geq\frac{c}{k},
 \qquad 1\leq k\leq L.
\]
For \(T_L=A_{1,L}\otimes\cdots\otimes A_{r,L}\), there are constants
\(b_r,B_r>0\), independent of \(L\), such that
\begin{equation}
 s_N(T_L)\geq b_r\frac{(\log(e+N))^{r-1}}{N}
 
\end{equation}
whenever
\[
 B_r\leq N\leq b_rL(\log(e+L))^{r-1}.
\]

[Proposition massTprop of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $(T, d, \rho, \mu)$ be a rooted finitely measured Polish $\mathbb{R}$-tree. 
For all $h\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$ we denote by $T_{\! \mu, h+}$ the closure of $T^o_{\! \mu, h+}\! := \!   \bigcup_{h^\prime >h} T_{\! \mu , h^\prime} $.
Then, the following holds true.
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$] Let $h\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$, and let $\rho\! \in \!  \mathtt{t}\! \subset \! T$ be a closed subtree such that $\mu (T\backslash \mathtt{t})\! < \!  h$. Then, $T_{\mathtt{P}_\mathtt{t} \mu, h}\! = \!  T_{\! \mu, h}$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] Let $\nu\! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_f (T)$. Then $\mu \! = \!  \nu$ iff $T_{\! \mu, h}\! = \!  T_{\! \nu,h}$ for all $h\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(iii)$] For all $h, h' \! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$ such that $h\! < \!  h'$, $T_{\! \mu, h'} \! \subset \! T_{\! \mu, h}$ and 
$\bigcap_{ h'' \in (0, h)} T_{\! \mu, h''} \! = \!  T_{\! \mu, h}$, which implies that 
$h\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+\! \mapsto \! T_{\!\mu , h}$ is $d_{\mathtt{Haus}}$-left-continuous with $d_{\mathtt{Haus}}$-right limits, it has at most countably many discontinuities and its $d_{\mathtt{Haus}}$-right limit at $h$ is $T_{\! \mu , h+}$. 
\item[$(iv)$] Let $h\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$. Then 
\begin{equation}

\bigsqcup_{\sigma \in \mathtt{Lf} (T_{\! \mu, h})}  \!\!\! ]\!] f_{T_{\! \mu, h+}}\!  (\sigma) , \sigma  ]\!] \; = T_{\! \mu, h} \backslash T_{\! \mu, h+} \subseteq 
 T_{\! \mu, h} \backslash T^o_{\! \mu, h+}\! = \!  \big\{ \sigma \! \in \!  T: \mu (\theta_\sigma T) \! = \!  h \big\}, 
 \end{equation}
where $f_{T_{\! \mu, h+}} $ stands for the projection onto $T_{\! \mu, h+}$.

\smallskip

\item[$(v)$]  If $\mathtt{Supp}\,   \mu$ is connected and contains $\rho$, then $T_{\! \mu, h} \! = \!  T_{\! \mu, h+}$  
for all $h\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(vi)$] The closure of $T^o\! :=\!  \bigcup_{h\in \mathbb{R}^*_+} T_{\! \mu , h}$ is $\mathtt{S}\, \overline{\! \mathtt{pan}\!  }\,  \, (\mathtt{Supp}\,  \mu)$, the closure of $\mathtt{Span} \, (\mathtt{Supp}\,   \mu )$.  

\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:polynomial-kernel-perturbation of arXiv:2602.14998, 'Random geometric graphs with smooth kernels: sharp detection threshold and a spectral conj'] Consider a kernel $\kappa$ with the expansion in Gegenbauer polynomials
\[
\kappa(t) = \sum_{k=1}^L \alpha_k C_k^\lambda(t) 
\]
satisfying $\lambda = (d-2)/2$ and 
\[
\alpha_1 = \zeta d^{-1} , 
\quad
|\alpha_k| \leq C_1 d^{-k}, k=2,\ldots,L,
\]
for a constant $C_1 > 0$. 
Let $X \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ be defined by $X_{ij} = \langle x_i, x_j \rangle$ where $x_1, \dots, x_n$ are i.i.d.\ uniform random points on $S^{d-1}$. {\sf\color{blue}[Slight abuse of notation: here $X$ has diagonal entries equal to $1$ for ease of notation.]}
Suppose that we observe 
$$
Y = \kappa(X) + Z ,
$$
where $\kappa$ is applied entrywise and $Z$ is a fixed noise matrix.  
Let $U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times d}$ be the matrix whose columns are the top-$d$ eigenvectors of $Y$. 
There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, the following holds.
If $d + \log(1/\delta) \le n$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$,
$$
\left\| U U^\top - \frac dn X \right\| \le C \left( \sqrt{\frac{d + \log(1/\delta)}{n}} + \frac{1}{|\zeta| d} + \frac{L^2 d}{|\zeta| n} \log \frac{d}{\delta} + \frac{d}{|\zeta| n} \|Z\| \right) .
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 64 (Critical second-order entrance) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] A stochastic source has a \emph{critical second-order entrance} in a real
separable Hilbert space \(H\) if its perfected degree-two anchor is an
adapted c\`adl\`ag path in \(\mathscr G^+_{\mathrm{crit}}(H)\), its
finite-rank spatial projections converge ucp in the critical metric, and its
relative increments are obtained from the anchor by the stopped causal law.
A \(\beta\)-controlled entrance additionally satisfies, for a control
\(\omega\),
\[
 \|X_{s,t}\|\lesssim\omega(s,t)^\beta,
 \qquad
 \|A_{s,t}\|_{1,\infty}\lesssim\omega(s,t)^{2\beta},
 \qquad \beta\in(1/3,1/2).
\]
The source-specific analysis ends at this entrance.  Higher ancestry and
spectral conclusions are supplied by the normal and response theories.

body:
[Lemma 3 (Chain-compatible cutoffs) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let $\mathsf O\subset\R^{3d}$ be a bounded smooth open set.  After the
reordering
\[
    x^1=r,\qquad x^2=p,\qquad x^3=\theta,
\]
there exist cutoff drifts, indexed by $0\le\delta\le1$,
\[
    B_1^{\mathsf O},B_2^{\delta,\mathsf O}
        \in C_b^\infty\left(\R^{3d};\R^d\right),
    \qquad
    B_3^{\delta,\mathsf O}
        \in C_b^\infty\left(\R^{2d};\R^d\right),
\]
with
\[
    B^{\delta,\mathsf O}(x)
    =\left(
        B_1^{\mathsf O}(x),
        B_2^{\delta,\mathsf O}(x),
        B_3^{\delta,\mathsf O}\left(x^2,x^3\right)
    \right),
\]
such that, for every $x\in\mathsf O$,
\begin{equation}
    B^{\delta,\mathsf O}(x)
    =
    \begin{pmatrix}
        -\gamma x^2-\gamma x^1\\
        -L^{-1}\nabla U(x^3)+\gamma x^1-\delta Lx^2\\
        x^2-\delta\nabla U(x^3)
    \end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every $k\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{0\le\delta\le1}
    \left(
        \left\|B_1^{\mathsf O}\right\|_{C_b^k}
        +\left\|B_2^{\delta,\mathsf O}\right\|_{C_b^k}
        +\left\|B_3^{\delta,\mathsf O}\right\|_{C_b^k}
    \right)<\infty.
\end{equation}
On $\mathsf O$,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
    J_{x^1}B_2^{\delta,\mathsf O}=\gamma I_{d},
    \qquad
    J_{x^2}B_3^{\delta,\mathsf O}=I_{d}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The same assertions hold for cutoff drifts $B^{\delta,\mathsf O,*}$ of the
adjoint dynamics, with
\begin{equation}
    B^{\delta,\mathsf O,*}(x)
    =
    \begin{pmatrix}
        \gamma x^2-\gamma x^1\\
        L^{-1}\nabla U(x^3)-\gamma x^1-\delta Lx^2\\
        -x^2-\delta\nabla U(x^3)
    \end{pmatrix},
    \qquad x\in\mathsf O,
\end{equation}
and hence with chain links $-\gamma I_d$ and $-I_d$.

body:
[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2609.04033, 'From configuration spaces to graph complexes via $\mathbf{FA}$-modules'] For $d$ odd there is an isomorphism of graded $S_n$-modules
	$$ 
H^\ast(\mathsf{T}_\Gamma(n)_d)\cong \bigoplus_{a+b=d-1} u_{(a,b)}\Sigma^{d}\Phi[n,(a,b)^\ast],
	$$
where
	$$u_{(a,b)} =
	\begin{cases}
		\left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b-2}{4}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b}{6}\right\rfloor+
		\delta_{a,b} & \text{ if }  a\equiv b \equiv 0 \text{ mod } 2 \\ 
		& \\
		\left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b-2}{4}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \ds\frac{a-b}{6}\right\rfloor+
		1 & \text{ if }  a\equiv b \equiv 1 \text{ mod } 2 \\ 	
		& \\
		0 & \text{ else.}
	\end{cases}
	$$
title: Lemma 25 of arXiv:2609.04033

body:
[Lem 38 of arXiv:2608.20552, 'One-point fluctuations for exponential last passage percolation under upper-tail condition'] There exist $C,c,L_0>0$ such that, for all $n_1,n_2\ge1$, $0\le a,b\le n_1\wedge n_2$ satisfying $n_1\vee n_2\ge2$ and $a\le n_1-1$, and $L\ge L_0$,
\beqq
	|\J^{12}_{21}(a,b,n_1,n_2)|
	\le
	e^{-\tDel L}
	C^{n_1+n_2}\sqrt{n_1!n_2!}\,
	(n_1+n_2-a-b)!e^{-c(n_1+n_2)L}.
\eeqq

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2605.09706, 'A dyadic construction of a three-dimensional attractive point interaction Markov family'] Fix $T,\beta,\varepsilon>0$ and $0\le s<t\le T$. The map 
$\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[s,t]}$ given by~\eqref{EqDefGlobalDyadicLimitKernel_Inf} is well defined and satisfies the following:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[s,t]}:\;
E_\varepsilon \times \mathcal B(E_\varepsilon)\to [0,1]$ is a sub-probability kernel on $E_\varepsilon$.

\item If $0\le r<s<t\le T$ with $r,s,t\in\mathbb D_T$, then for every $x\in E_\varepsilon$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(E_\varepsilon)$,
\begin{align}
\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[r,t]}(x,A)
\,=\,
\int_{E_\varepsilon}
\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[r,s]}(x,dy)\,
\widehat{\mathsf K}^{T,\beta,\varepsilon}_{[s,t]}(y,A)\, .
\end{align}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Aldous and Fill, Open Problem 4.30 (p. 137) asks whether there is an explicit function psi(b,s) tending to 0 as s tends to infinity, not depending on the chain, with sup_x |P(S_t/(sigma sqrt t) <= x) - P(Z <= x)| <= psi(||g||_inf, t/tau2) for standardized g and continuous-time reversible chains. Our result (id P0209, 2026-09-08): NO such psi exists. Take two independent reversible chains: Y two-state with rates epsilon and 1 - epsilon (spectral gap exactly 1) and Z a fair sign flip at rate R/2; set epsilon = s^-2, R = s^4, A = 2 epsilon + sqrt((1-epsilon)(1-4 epsilon)), B = (2-A)/(1-epsilon) and g = A Z + B (Y - epsilon). Then exactly, at every s: E g = 0, E g^2 = 1, ||g||_inf = 2 and tau2 = 1. Taking t = s sends t/tau2 to infinity with the sup norm pinned at 2, yet normality fails: S_t is compound Poisson with vanishing intensity (the mean number of visits to the rare state is epsilon t = 1/s, tending to 0), so with probability 1 - O(1/s) no visit occurs and S_t sits near the deterministic value -B epsilon t while the whole variance is carried by one rare excursion. Verification as the source words it: the identities were checked to seven decimals at every s, and the measured Kolmogorov distance to N(0,1) is 0.478, 0.505, 0.509, 0.506 at s = 30, 100, 300, 1000 - flat at about 1/2, not decreasing, while t/tau2 rises from 30 to 1000. Prior art not cleared. two independent reversible chains as specified (four states in total) g standardized: E g = 0, E g^2 = 1, sup norm 2, tau2 = 1 t = s, epsilon = s^-2, R = s^4

Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\|T_\phi:H^p\to H^2\|\asymp_p B_{2,p}(\phi)$, and
 boundedness of $T_\phi:H^p\to H^p$ implies
 $B_{2,p}(\phi)<\infty$.
 \item If $\operatorname{supp}\widehat\phi$ is contained in an analytic
 $\Lambda(p)$-set $E\subset\mathbb N_0$, then
 \[
  T_\phi:H^p\to H^p\text{ is bounded}
  \iff B_{2,p}(\phi)<\infty,
 \]
 with
 \[
  \|T_\phi:H^p\to H^2\|
  \le\|T_\phi:H^p\to H^p\|
  \le C_{E,p}\|T_\phi:H^p\to H^2\|.
 \]
 In this sector boundedness is equivalent to compactness.
 \item Hadamard-lacunary symbols are a special case of \textup{(ii)}.
 For a one-frequency-per-block symbol the test $h=1$ exactly norms the
 vector criterion, up to constants depending only on $p$.
 \item The blockwise condition
 \[
  \bigl(2^{-j/p'}\|\Delta_j\phi\|_{H^p}\bigr)_j\in\ell^t
 \]
 is sufficient in general and is not necessary, even for symbols with
 a consecutive interval occupying half of every sufficiently large hard
 block.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 19 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(\iota \colon X \to S\) be a morphism of $\F_p$-stacks.
Let
\[
X^{(1)} \defeq X\times_{S,F_S}S
\]
be the relative Frobenius twist, and let
\[
F_{X/S}\colon X \to  X^{(1)}
\]
be the relative Frobenius.
  \begin{itemize}
      \item   The \emph{(absolute) de Rham stack} of \(X\) is defined as a functor
  \begin{equation*}
    X^{\dR} \colon \CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p} \to \Ani; \  R \mapsto X(W(R)/^L p),
  \end{equation*}
  where \(W(R)\) is the ring of Witt vectors of \(R\), \(-/^L p\) is the derived quotient by \(p\), and \(X(W(R)/^L p)\) is the mapping space \(\Map_{\dSch_{\setF_p}}(\Spec(W(R)/^L p), X)\) in the \(\infty\)-category of derived schemes over \(\setF_p\).
  Since this is isomorphic to the relative Hodge--Tate stack \((X/\setZ_p)^{\HT}\) of \(X\) relative to the crystalline prism \((\setZ_p, (p))\) introduced in \cite{bhatt2022Prismatization}*{Construction 7.1}, this is a stack on \(\CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p}\) (\cite{bhatt2022Prismatization}*{Lemma 7.3}).

  This is equipped with natural morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    \pi_{X} \colon X \to X^{\dR} \quad \text{and} \quad \nu_X \colon X^{\dR} \to X
  \end{equation*}
  of \(\setF_p\)-stacks: For each \(R \in \CAlg^{an}_{\setF_p}\), each morphism is given by precomposition of morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    R \xrightarrow{\Phi_R} W(R)/^L p \quad \text{and} \quad W(R)/^L p \xrightarrow{\res} R,
  \end{equation*}
  where \(\Phi_R\) is the animation of the morphism \(a \mapsto [a^p] \bmod p\) and \(\res\) is the restriction morphism.
  Note that the composition \(\nu_X \circ \pi_X\) is the absolute Frobenius morphism \(F_X \colon X \to X\) of \(X\).
\item The \emph{de Rham stack} of $X$ over $S$ is defined by
\[
(X/S)^{\dR} \defeq X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR},\pi_S} S.
\]
We define natural morphisms
  \begin{equation*}
    \pi_{X/S} \colon X \to (X/S)^{\dR} \quad \text{and} \quad \nu_{X/S} \colon (X/S)^{\dR} \to X^{(1)}
  \end{equation*}
  of \(\setF_p\)-stacks as follows:
The morphism $\pi_{X/S}$ is defined by
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
X \arrow[r,"\pi_{X/S}"'] \arrow[rd,bend right,"\iota"] \arrow[rr,bend left,"\pi_X"] & X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR}} S \arrow[r,"\pr_1"] \arrow[d,"\pr_2"] & X^{\dR} \arrow[d,"\iota^{\dR}"] \\
& S \arrow[r,"\pi_S"] & S^{\dR}.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The morphism $\nu_{X/S} \colon (X/S)^{\dR} \to X^{(1)}$ is induced by the following commutative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
X^{\dR} \times_{S^{\dR}} S \arrow[r,"\pr_1"] \arrow[d,"\pr_2"] & X^{\dR} \arrow[d,"\iota^{\dR}"] \arrow[r,"\nu_X"] & X \arrow[d,"\iota"] \\
S \arrow[r,"\pi_S"] \arrow[rr,bend right,"F"] & S^{\dR} \arrow[r,"\nu_S"] & S.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
\item We assume that $\iota$ is smooth representable.
Then the cotangent complex \(L_{X/S}\) is a locally free \(\cO_X\)-module concentrated in degree \(0\).  
We set
\[
\Omega^1_{X/S} \defeq L_{X/S},
\qquad
\Omega^i_{X/S} \defeq 
\bigwedge_{\cO_X}^i\Omega^1_{X/S}.
\]
The universal \(S\)-derivation
\[
d_{X/S}\colon \cO_X \to  \Omega^1_{X/S}
\]
extends uniquely to the relative de Rham complex
\[
\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}
=
\left[
\cO_X
\xrightarrow{d_{X/S}}
\Omega^1_{X/S}
\xrightarrow{d_{X/S}}
\Omega^2_{X/S}
 \to \cdots
\right].
\]

We define a morphism of complexes of $\cO_{X^{(1)}}$-modules
\[
F^{\dR}_{X/S} \colon \cO_{X^{(1)}} \to F_{X/S,*}\Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}
\]
as follows:
We have
\[
d_{X/S}\circ F_{X/S}^{\sharp}=0
\]
by checking smooth locally on \(X\).  
Therefore, the morphism
\[
F_{X/S}^{\sharp}\colon
\cO_{X^{(1)}} \to  F_{X/S,*}\cO_X
\]
defines a morphism of complexes
\[
F_{X/S}^{\dR}\colon
\cO_{X^{(1)}}
 \to 
F_{X/S,*}\Omega^\bullet_{X/S},
\]
whose degree \(0\) component is \(F_{X/S}^{\sharp}\) and whose
positive-degree components are zero.
\end{itemize}

[Theorem disintegration of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Let \(\Omega\)  and \(\mathcal{X}\) be Polish spaces, and let \(\nu \in \mathcal{P}(\Omega)\). Consider any
	\(\mu \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times \Omega)\). Then, there exists a unique (up to \(\nu\)-a.e. equality)
	Borel family \((\mu^{\omega})_{\omega \in \Omega}\subset \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\) such that 
     	\[
     		\int_{\mathcal{X}\times \Omega} \varphi(x,\omega)d\mu(x,\omega)=\int_{\Omega} \int_{\mathcal{X}} \varphi(x,\omega)d\mu^{\omega}(x)d\nu(\omega),
     	\]
	for every bounded and measurable function \(\varphi:\mathcal{X}\times \Omega\to \mathbb{R}\). Conversely, given any Borel
	family \((\mu^{\omega})_{\omega \in \Omega}\subset \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\), we can associate a unique fibered probability
	measure \(\mu \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times \Omega)\) so that the above formula holds true, and it will be denoted
	by \(\mu(x,\omega)=\mu^{\omega}(x)\otimes d\nu(\omega)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Disintegration theorem

body:
[Definition def:dg of arXiv:2410.23509, 'Dynkin Games for L\'evy Processes'] Let 
$G_1(x)\leq G_2(x)$
be two real continuous payoff functions.
Consider a L\'evy process $X$ and a discount factor $r>0$, 
such that conditions (equation eq:ic of the paper) and (equation eq:limit of the paper) above hold.
Given two stopping times $\sigma$ and $\tau$, define the expected payoff

$$
{\operatorname{\mathbf{M}}_x}(\sigma,\tau)=\operatorname{\mathbf{E}}_x\left(
e^{-r\tau}G_1(X_{\tau})\mathbf{1}_{\{\tau\leq\sigma\}}
+
e^{-r\sigma}G_2(X_{\sigma})\mathbf{1}_{\{\sigma<\tau\}}
\right).
$$

The Dynkin game (DG) problem consists
in finding the value function $V(x)$ and two optimal stopping rules ${\sigma^*}$ and ${\tau^*}$ such that
\begin{align}
V(x)&=\inf_{\sigma}\sup_{\tau}{\operatorname{\mathbf{M}}_x}(\sigma,\tau)=\sup_{\tau}\inf_{\sigma}{\operatorname{\mathbf{M}}_x}(\sigma,\tau)={\operatorname{\mathbf{M}}_x}(\sigma^*,\tau^*).

\end{align}
title: Dynkin game

[Definition 10 (Weighted deterministic maximal $L^p$-regularity) of arXiv:2606.15425, 'Well-posedness of stochastic parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities and applicat'] Let $\mathcal B_1 \coloneqq D(A) \subset \mathcal B$. Given $p \in (1,\infty)$ and $\beta \in (-1,p-1)$, we say that $A$ has \textit{weighted deterministic maximal $L^p$-regularity} on $[0,T]$ if for every
$f\in L^p_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B)$ and $u_0\in (\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-(1+\beta)/p,p}$
there exists a unique
$$
u\in W^{1,p}_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B)\cap L^p_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B_1)
$$
such that $u(0)=u_0$ and
$$
u'(t)+Au(t)=f(t)\quad \text{for a.e. } t\in(0,T),
$$
and moreover, there is a constant $C_{MR}>0$ independent of $f$ and $u_0$ such that
\begin{equation}
\norm{u}_{W^{1,p}_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B)}+\norm{u}_{L^p_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B_1)}
\leq C_{MR}\left(\norm{f}_{L^p_\beta([0,T];\mathcal B)}+\norm{u_0}_{(\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-(1+\beta)/p,p}}\right).
\end{equation}
title: Weighted deterministic maximal $L^p$-regularity
