[Theorem 6 (\cite{DHKBrown},\cite{HoZhong2020Brown}) of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $b_{0,1}(t)$ be a free multiplicative Brownian motion, and let $u_0$ be a unitary operator freely independent from $b_{0,1}$.  Denote by $\mu_{u_0}$ the spectral measure of $u_0$, a probability measure on the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$.

Define $T(u_0,\cdot)\colon\C\to\R_+$ by
\begin{equation}  T(u_0,z) = \frac{\log |z|^2}{|z|^2-1}\left(\int_{\mathbb{T}} \frac{\mu_{u_0}(d\xi)}{|\xi-z|^2}\right)^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Also, for each $t>0$, define the open precompact set $\Sigma(u_0,t)$ by
\begin{equation}  \Sigma(u_0,t) = \{z\in\C\colon T(u_0,z)<t\}. \end{equation}
The Brown measure $\mu_{u_0b_{1,0}(t)}$ has support equal to $\overline{\Sigma(u_0,t)}$.  The Brown measure is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, and has density on $\overline{\Sigma(u_0,t)}$ that is real analytic in $\Sigma(u_0,t)$.  The density has the form $z=re^{i\theta}\mapsto w_t(\theta)/r^2$, with the radial function $w_t$ bounded by $w_t(\theta)<\frac{1}{\pi t}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{DHKBrown},\cite{HoZhong2020Brown}

[Proposition 3 (Approximation of forward processes) of arXiv:2606.28174, 'Moment duality and propagation of exchangeability'] Let $\{A^N\}_{N}$ be a sequence of block-counting processes associated with label-forgetful mappings $\{L^N\}_{N}$. 
For each $N\geq1$, define $\Theta^N$ as the de Finetti process dual to $A^N$ from Theorem \ref{thduality}.  Assume that there exists a continuous-time Markov process $\{A_t\}_{t}$ taking values in $\N$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[i)] $\{A_t\}_{t}$ is moment dual to a $[0,1]$-valued Feller Markov process $\{W_t\}_{t}$. 
    \item[ii)] There exists a diverging sequence $\{a_N\}_N$ such that for any fixed $t\in[0,T]$,
    
    $A^N_{ \lfloor a_Nt\rfloor }$ converges in distribution towards $A_t$
    
    whenever $A^N_0\overset{a.s.}{=}A_0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, defining $ W^N_t=\Theta^N_{\lfloor a_N t\rfloor}$, the sequence $\{W^N\}_{N}$ weakly converges towards $W$ in $\D([0,T],[0,1])$.

\[
   S=(a+V)\cap\{0,1\}^n.
\]
If \(S\neq\varnothing\), choose \(b_0\in S\) and define
\[
   U=\Span(S-b_0).
\]
Then \(U\) is a rational linear subspace, \(U\subseteq V\), and
\[
   (a+V)\cap\{0,1\}^n=(b_0+U)\cap\{0,1\}^n.
\]

[Lem 58 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] The defining polynomials of $X$ can be written as
\[
\begin{split}
\msF_1 &= y^3 x + y^2 f_4 + y f_7 + t^2 + f_{10}, \\
\msF_2 &= y^2 w + y (t \ell + g_9) + \ell_1 \ell_2 \ell_3 + g_{12},
\end{split}
\]
where $\ell = \ell (z, s), \ell_i = \ell_i (z, s)$ are linear forms in $z, s$, and $f_i, g_i \in \mbC [x, z, s, t, w]$ are such that $f_i, g_i \in (x, w)$ and no two of $\ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3$ are mutually proportional.

[Theorem thm:4 of arXiv:2504.12293, 'Near-existence of bigeodesics in dynamical exponential last passage percolation'] Consider dynamical exponential LPP and fix $\theta\in (-1,1),\varepsilon>0$. For $n\in \mathbb{Z}$, let $\ell_{n,\varepsilon}^\theta$ denote the line segment defined by $\ell_{n,\varepsilon}^\theta=\{p: \phi(p)=n, |\psi(p)-\theta n|\leq \varepsilon |n|\}$. Then there exists a constant $C$ such that for all large enough $n\in \mathbb{N}$, we have
  \begin{equation}
    
    \mathbb{P}(\exists t\in [0,1]\textrm{ and points } p\in \ell_{-n,\varepsilon}^\theta, q\in \ell_{n,\varepsilon}^\theta \textrm { with } \0\in \Gamma_{p}^{q,t})\geq C(\log n)^{-1}.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:4 of arXiv:2504.12293

Let X be standard Gaussian in R^d, u any unit vector, teacher y=sigma(u dot X), and student f_rho(X)=integral sigma(w dot X)rho(dw) for probability rho on the unit sphere. Outer coefficients are fixed at +1; the prior and initialization are uniform on the sphere. R is E(f_rho-y)^2 with no factor 1/2, and MFLD is partial_t rho=div_S(rho grad_S(delta R/delta rho))+lambda(t)Delta_S rho. For sigma(z)=alpha*z+beta*(z^2-1)/sqrt(2), A=alpha^2, B=beta^2, A+B=1 and A>=16B, define c=d/(d-1), gamma=A-4cB, C=2A+16B, delta=sqrt(eps)/4, T=log(2/delta)/(2gamma*delta), K=(1+4gamma*T)^6, H=min(delta^2,1/(C^2*T^2)), lambda0=H/(8dTK), lambda(t)=lambda0/(1+t/T). Population sphere MFLD from uniform initialization satisfies R(rho_T)<=3eps/8 uniformly on the entire coefficient cone; time and inverse temperature are polynomial in d and 1/eps.

body:
Owner draft: independently checked proof (C006 v1). For d>=1, the signed radial line law on [-1,1] with density f_d(t)=(d/2)|t|^(d-1) can be (2k+1)-CM only if (k/(k+1))^d>=1/(2k+1). A zero-sum tuple cannot have every |t_i|>k/(k+1), since at least k+1 share a sign and cannot be canceled by k bounded terms. Thus F_2 is not 3-CM (1/4<1/3) and F_4 is not 5-CM (16/81<1/5). These are the uniform disk/four-ball conditional laws on unoriented lines through the center. The full balls are mixable, so this refutes componentwise centered radial-needle mixing, not the convex-body conjecture. Projection onto a fixed line has a different marginal.
d positive integer
Odd order n=2k+1 with k>=1
Bounded scalar support [-1,1]
This is a conditional radial line law, not a projection marginal

[Theorem 23 of arXiv:2605.16072, 'Stochastic integration \\with respect to a L\'evy basis'] Let $\Theta\colon \Borel_b(\Rp\times \O) \to L_P^0(\Omega;\R)$ be a L\'evy basis and $(\Xi_k)_{k\in{\mathbb N}}$ a sequence of  predictable processes $\Xi_k\colon\Omega\times [0,T]\times\O\to\R$ satisfying:
	\begin{enumerate}[\rm (a)]
		\item  $(\Xi_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges $P\otimes \chi$-a.e.\ to a predictable process $\Xi$;
		\item  there exists a predictable, $\Theta$-integrable process $\Upsilon$ such that, for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$,
		\[
		(\zeta_\Theta+\eta_\Theta)(t,x,\abs{\Xi_k(\omega,t,x)})
		\leq
		(\zeta_\Theta+\eta_\Theta)(t,x,\abs{\Upsilon(\omega,t,x)}),
		\]
		for $P\otimes \chi$-a.a.\ $(\omega,t,x)\in \Omega\times [0,T]\times \O$.
	\end{enumerate}
	Then $\Xi$ is $\Theta$-integrable and
	\[
	\lim_{k\to\infty} \sup_{\Gamma \in \mathcal{S}_{{\rm prd}}^{1}}
	E\Bigg[\abs{\int_{(0,T]\times \O} \Gamma (\Xi_k-\Xi) \;{\rm d}\Theta}\wedge 1 \Bigg]=0.
	\]

$$

body:
[Theorem thm:limit-law of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $K$ be the Koenigs linearizer of $A$ at $\tfrac12$: the unique
		increasing solution of the Schr\"oder equation
		$K(2u) = A(K(u))$, $K(0)=\tfrac12$, $K'(0)=1$; then $K$ extends to a
		real-analytic increasing bijection $\mathbb{R}\to(0,1)$ and is the
		distribution function of a symmetric law $\mathcal{K}$ with analytic
		density. For every $f \in \mathcal{D}_{+}$,
		\begin{equation}
			2^{n} f(m)\,(X_{n} - m) \;\xrightarrow{\ d\ }\; \mathcal{K},
			
		\end{equation}
		and if $\mathbb{E}|X|^{\varepsilon} < \infty$ for some
		$\varepsilon>0$, all moments converge; in particular
		\begin{equation}
			\operatorname{Var}(X_{n})
			\;\sim\; \sigma_{\mathcal{K}}^{2}\, f(m)^{-2}\, 4^{-n},
			\qquad \sigma^{2}_{\mathcal{K}} \approx 0.166.
			
		\end{equation}
		Moreover, with $g = 1-K$, the symmetry of $A$ gives the exact tail
		recursion $g(2u) = A(g(u))$, whence
		\begin{equation}
			-\log\big(1 - K(u)\big)
			= u^{\log_{2}3}\,\Theta(\log_{2}u)\big(1 + O(u^{-\log_{2}3})\big)
			\qquad (u \to \infty)
			
		\end{equation}
		for a positive continuous $1$-periodic $\Theta$: the tails of
		$\mathcal{K}$ are compressed-exponential with exponent
		$\log_{2}3$, lighter than exponential and heavier than Gaussian, the
		exponent being the ratio of the logarithms of the endpoint degree and
		the interior multiplier; consistently, the excess kurtosis of
		$\mathcal{K}$ is positive ($\approx 0.164$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematical analysis, the alternating series test proves that an alternating series is convergent when its terms decrease monotonically in absolute value and approach zero in the limit. The test was devised by Gottfried Leibniz and is sometimes known as Leibniz's test, Leibniz's rule, or the Leibniz criterion. The test is only sufficient, not necessary, so some convergent alternating series may fail the first part of the test.
title: Alternating series test

[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Let $\nu$ denote the uniform probability
measure on \(\{-1,+1\}^{2N}\). Define

and

\[
 B_\rho
 =
 T\bigl(t_\rho(Q)\bigr)^\delta
 \Sigma_\rho(g_Q,g_P)
 E\bigl(e_\rho(P,Q)\bigr),
 \qquad
 \delta\in\{-1,+1\},
\]
where $g_P$ is the side of $P$ separating $P$ from $Q$ and $g_Q$ is
the corresponding side of $Q$.  Replace the slithering matrix by the
finite approximant from
Corollary~(cor:slithering-networks of the paper), and define
\[
 B_{\rho,N}
 =
 T\bigl(t_\rho(Q)\bigr)^\delta
 S_{\rho,N}(g_Q,g_P)
 E\bigl(e_\rho(P,Q)\bigr).
\]
Then $B_{\rho,N}$ is the weight matrix of a weighted planar network
$(\mathcal B_{\rho,N},\omega_{\rho,N})$. Moreover, the weight matrix of the planar network $(\mathcal B_{\rho,N}, \lvert \omega_{\rho,N} \rvert)$ is the corresponding generalized building block $B_{\rho_0,N}$ for $\rho_0$, the Hitchin representation in the bending fiber (see (equation eq:rho0coords of the paper)).

T : d(\rho, \sigma) \! = \!  a \}  \big)\! = \!  0$. We observe that $\mathbb{T}(\infty) \! = \!  \mathbb{T}$.

\item[$(b)$] We also denote by $\mathbb{T}^{1}_c(a)$ (resp.~by $\mathbb{T}^{0}_{c}(a)$)

$ \mathbb{T}^1_{\! c}(\infty)\! = \!  \mathbb{T}^1_{\! c}$ and $ \mathbb{T}^0_{\! c}(\infty)\! = \!  \mathbb{T}^0_{\! c}$.

[Proposition 14 (Transfer from singularity to corank) of arXiv:2606.25204, 'Exponential Rank Bounds for Random Matrices'] Fix \(b\in(0,1)\).  For each \(n\ge1\), let \(A=(A_{ij})\) be an
\(n\times n\) random matrix with independent real entries.  Assume that
\begin{align}
   \sup_{x\in\R}\PP\{A_{ij}=x\} &\leq b<1
   \qquad (1\leq i,j\leq n), \\
   \PP\{\rank A<n\} &\leq C_0\exp(-c_0 n)
   \qquad\text{for all }n\ge n_0 
\end{align}
for some constants \(C_0>0\), \(c_0>0\), and \(n_0\ge1\).  Then there exists
\(c_{5.1}=c_{5.1}(b,C_0,c_0,n_0)>0\) such that for all \(n\ge1\) and all
\(1\leq k\leq n\),
\begin{equation}
   \PP\{\rank A\leq n-k\}\leq \exp(-c_{5.1}nk).
\end{equation}
title: Transfer from singularity to corank

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: Omega bounded. The proofs use boundedness twice - the auxiliary function exp(gamma x_1) must be bounded on Omega, and the maximum must be attained on a compact set. On unbounded domains the conclusion is false even for harmonic functions with zero boundary data. Unbounded counterexample: on the half-space {x_n > 0} the function u(x) = x_n is harmonic and vanishes on the whole boundary, yet u > 0 inside; sup u = infinity while sup over the boundary of u = 0. Bounded counterexample (so boundedness of u does not rescue the statement in general): for n >= 3 let Omega = {|x| > 1} and u(x) = 1 - |x|^{2-n}. Then u is harmonic in Omega, continuous up to the boundary, bounded with 0 <= u < 1, u = 0 on the boundary sphere, and sup over Omega of u = 1 > 0 = sup over the boundary of u^+. In the plane, u(x) = log|x| on {|x| > 1} is an unbounded version of the same phenomenon. What restores the principle: treat infinity as a boundary point, i.e. assume limsup of u(x) as |x| tends to infinity is <= 0 (then the principle holds on any unbounded Omega, by exhausting with large balls), or impose a Phragmen-Lindeloef growth restriction adapted to the geometry. The admissible growth is set by the opening of the domain, and a thinner domain permits faster growth, not slower: in a plane sector of opening pi/a the threshold is exp(|x|^a), so a narrow sector allows faster growth than a half-plane, and in a strip of width d the threshold is exp(pi|x|/d), the extremal being exp(pi x_1/d) cos(pi x_2/d). The same caution applies to the H^1 weak maximum principle: its proof uses the Sobolev inequality together with the fact that the level sets have finite measure.
title: Pitfall: The Weak Maximum Principle Needs a Bounded Domain (or Control at Infinity)

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.31168, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality for surfaces in every codimension'] For every $N \geq 3$, there exist constants $\ve_N>0$ and $C_N<\infty$ with the following property.
For every $\Psi \in C^1(\bG(N,2) , (0,\infty) )$ with $\sup_{T \in \bG(N,2)} \|B_{\Psi}(T) - T \| \leq \ve_N$, every rectifiable $2$-varifold $V = v(M,\theta)$ in $\bR^N$ with finite total mass and finite first variation with respect to the anisotropy $\Psi$ satisfies
\[
\|V\| (\bR^N) \leq C_N \, \cH^2(M)^{\frac{1}{2}} \, |\delta_{\Psi} V|(\bR^N).
\]
In particular, if $\Theta^2(\|V\|,x) \geq \theta_0 > 0$ holds $\|V\|$-a.e.~$x$, then 
\[
\|V\|(\bR^N)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C_N \theta_0^{- \frac{1}{2}} |\delta_{\Psi} V|( \bR^N).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 24 (Fifth-chaos kernels) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] In the regime \eqref{eq:sbe-tree-response-regime}, the fifth-chaos
kernels of the three response coordinates are
\begin{subequations}
\begin{align}
 G_{\XoneFourB,5}^\eps
 &=
 \operatorname{Sym}_5\left[
  \chi_\odot(k_5,k_{1234})
  M_{12345}M_{1234}M_{12}M_{34}
  \prod_{i=1}^5H_i^\eps
 \right],
 \\
 G_{\XtwoThree,5}^\eps
 &=
 \operatorname{Sym}_5\left[
  \chi_\odot(k_{12},k_{345})
  M_{12345}M_{12}M_{345}M_{34}
  \prod_{i=1}^5H_i^\eps
 \right],
 \\
 G_{\XoneFourC,5}^\eps
 &=
 \operatorname{Sym}_5\left[
  \chi_\odot(k_5,k_{1234})
  M_{12345}M_{1234}M_{123}M_{12}
  \prod_{i=1}^5H_i^\eps
 \right].
 
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
Moreover, uniformly in \(\eps\),
\[
 \mathcal C_{G_{\XoneFourB,5}^\eps}(\zeta)
 +\mathcal C_{G_{\XtwoThree,5}^\eps}(\zeta)
 \lesssim
 \langle\zeta\rangle_\gamma^{
  -(\gamma+1)-2(5q-\delta)+},
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal C_{G_{\XoneFourC,5}^\eps}(\zeta)
 \lesssim
 \langle\zeta\rangle_\gamma^{-(\gamma+1)-4q+}.
\]

Monotonicity is still open, still interesting mathematics, and open even for the mean; it just buys this program nothing. THE PROBE'S CONTENT, CONFIRMED BY P3 AND UNCHANGED: monotonicity Var(X_{n+1}) >= Var(X_n) for planar FPP reduces exactly to a signed-covariance statement through the identity Var(X_{n+1}) - Var(X_n) = Cov(X_{n+1} + X_n, Delta) with Delta := X_{n+1} - X_n bounded by an O(1) triangle bound, equivalently monotonicity iff Cov(X_n, Delta) >= -Var(Delta)/2; and FKG/Harris positive association is structurally inapplicable, because Delta is not environment-monotone - the two-route gadget is constructible with bounded weights and raising a weight on X_n's geodesic makes Delta strictly fall. That is an obstruction to Harris, not a proof that no positive-association argument exists. Let X_1, \dots, X_n be independent Bernoulli random variables with \mathbb{P}(X_k = 1) = p_k = 1 - \mathbb{P}(X_k = 0). Let S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n X_k and \lambda = \sum_{k=1}^n p_k. Let Y \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda). Then the total variation distance between the distribution of S_n and Y satisfies d_{TV}(\mathcal{L}(S_n), \text{Poisson}(\lambda)) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{k=0}^\infty |\mathbb{P}(S_n = k) - \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!}| \le \sum_{k=1}^n p_k^2.

body:
[Lemma lem:moving-bump of arXiv:2609.00794, 'On operators whose adjoints or second adjoints attain their norms'] Let
\[
u:=\left(\frac1{2^n}\right)_{n=1}^\infty\in S_{\ell_1},
\qquad
b_n:=\frac12(e_{n+1}-e_{n+2})\in S_{\ell_1},
\]
where $(e_n)$ denotes the standard coordinate basis for $\ell_1$. 
Let $0<\kappa<1$, and let $S\in\mathcal L(\ell_1,\ell_1)$.
Suppose that there exist a set $A\subset\mathbb N$, a mapping
$\nu\colon A\to\mathbb N$, and scalars $(\lambda_j)_{j\in A}$ such that

\begin{enumerate}
\itemsep0.25em
\item  $Se_j=\kappa u+(1-\kappa)\lambda_j b_{\nu(j)}$ for every $j \in A$, and $|\lambda_j|\leqslant 1$ for every $j \in A$;

\item there exist $(j_n)\subset A$ and a sequence $(s_n)$ tending to
infinity such that
\[
Se_{j_n}=\kappa u+(1-\kappa)b_{s_n};
\]

\item $\sup_{j\notin A}\|Se_j\|<1$.
\end{enumerate}

Then $\|S\|=1$ and $S^*$ does not attain its norm.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Zero speed on every bounded-degree subexponential-growth subgraph Result: Let H be a connected subgraph of a bounded-degree graph G with |B_G(x,n)|=exp(o(n)). The Carne-Varopoulos bound gives P_x(X_n=y)<=2 sqrt(deg_H(y)/deg_H(x)) exp(-d_H(x,y)^2/(2n)). Summing over reachable vertices yields P(d_H(x,X_n)>=epsilon n)<=C exp(o(n)-epsilon^2 n/2), which is summable. Thus the intrinsic speed on H is zero almost surely. Check: Reachability in H implies membership in B_G(x,n), but distances in the exponential bound remain intrinsic to H. Bounded degrees control the prefactor. This is a consequence of the classical heat-kernel bound, not a novelty claim. Obstruction: It settles the zero-speed equivalence for subexponential-growth Cayley graphs and their clusters only. Exponential-growth cases need different information.

[Lemma lem:asymptotic-product-app of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] Let $x_{a,j}>0$, $1\leq a\leq r$, be functions on a compact space.  If
\[
 \prod_{a=1}^r x_{a,j}\to1
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \max_{a,b}|x_{a,j}-x_{b,j}|\to0
\]
uniformly, then $x_{a,j}\to1$ uniformly for every $a$.

body: [Defn def:hugging of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] For $\theta\in\Theta^\omega$, a point $(x,s)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ is a \emph{$\theta+$ hugging shock} if $(x,s)\in\IG\theta$ and $\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{-}\cap\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{+}\ne\{(x,s)\}$. Similarly, $(x,s)$ is a \emph{$\theta-$ hugging shock} if $(x,s)\in\IG\theta$ and $\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{-}\cap\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{+}\ne\{(x,s)\}$.
title: Defn def:hugging of arXiv:2604.12963

body:
[Proposition 14 (Radial calculus) of arXiv:2609.03332, 'Singularity Models of Finite-Time K\"ahler-Ricci Flows'] Let $Q = Q(s)$ be a radial function on $(M^0, g)$ with $g$ as in \eqref{eq:ansatz-metric}, and let $\nu = \partial_s$ be the unit normal of the leaves. Then
	\begin{align}
		\nabla Q &\;=\; Q'\, \nu \,, \qquad \big| \nabla Q \big|^2 \;=\; \big( Q' \big)^2 \,,\\
		
		\Delta Q &\;=\; Q'' \;+\; Q' \left( \frac{H'}{H} \;+\; \sum_{i=1}^r \frac{n_i\, \big( q_i H + \kappa_i \big)}{F_i^2} \right) \;=\; \frac{\big( V Q' \big)'}{V} \,, \qquad V \;:=\; H \prod_{i=1}^r F_i^{2 n_i} \,.
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Radial calculus

body:
Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T280-w716-C9 v1, kind route-failure, Target 3. For every k>=1, the prepared aligned finite scale law supported on 1,...,k+1, with zero output weights and biases and exp activation, has a positive risk threshold whose first hitting time for the normalized degree-k sphere harmonic tends to infinity with d. Thus k+1 occupied scales with fixed positive separation do not alone imply O(1)-in-d small-risk learning. For k=1 and scales 1,2 the Gaussian squared approximation floor exceeds 2/5, so risk 1/4 cannot be attained in dimension-uniform bounded time. For any fixed finite horizon T and positive minimum atom mass, d/dt E a^2<=1/2 implies pointwise bounded output coefficients and O(1/d) aligned-scale drift; the actual nonlinear output remains O(1/d) from its initial exponential span. The degree-k sphere harmonic has a strictly positive limiting Gaussian projection distance from the span at scales 1,...,k+1. For scales 1,2 and target Z the squared distance is 1-(1-4 exp(-2)+4 exp(-3))/(exp(1)-1)>2/5. This is a full-risk obstruction; no claim is made about a single harmonic projection hitting time. No novelty claim or independent certification.
Uniform unit sphere, ordinary all-parameter population mean-field flow, known axis and sqrt(d)-scaled initialization
Fixed finite positive atom masses, fixed scales, zero output and bias initialization
Threshold depends on k; assertion concerns full residual energy, not a claimed general mixing or frequency lower bound
title: Draft: separated scales do not ensure exponential mean-field polynomial fitting (T280 w716)

[Theorem thm:highdimEinstein of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] Let $n\geqslant 2$ be an integer, and $a>0$. There exists $0<\varepsilon:=\varepsilon(n,a)<1$ such that the following holds.
  
  Let $(M^n, g)$ be a closed $L^\infty$-Riemannian manifold, and $S\subset M$ a closed subset of Assouad codimension greater than $2+a$; see (def:Codimension of the paper). Suppose that $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = Kg$ on $M\setminus S$ for some $K\in\mathbb R$, and in addition suppose that one of the following conditions holds:
  \begin{itemize}
      \item[(a)] Either $(1 - \varepsilon)h \leqslant g \leqslant (1+\varepsilon) h$ for a smooth metric $h$ on $M$,
      \item[(b)] Or $g$ is continuous. 
  \end{itemize}
    Then $g$ extends to $M$ as a smooth Einstein metric, perhaps for a different smooth structure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:highdimEinstein of arXiv:2609.01464

body:
PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. By Aizenman's random-current identity the four-point Ursell function is expressed through the probability that the currents from x_1 to x_2 and from x_3 to x_4 share a cluster; non-triviality (nonvanishing renormalised coupling) is equivalent to inf over scales L of P(two independent random-current clusters at scale L intersect) > 0. The 4D case is now trivial (Aizenman-Duminil-Copin 2021); in 3D the heuristic is favourable because the current-cluster dimension (5 - eta)/2 = 2.48 exceeds 3/2, so independent fractals of that dimension would intersect with positive probability. A second-moment argument on the number of intersection points reduces the uniform lower bound to (a) a two-point function lower bound with exponent 2 - eps in d = 3 (Duminil-Copin's Conjecture 5, PIMS lectures) and (b) a variance bound on the intersection count, which involves six-point correlations beyond the Lebowitz inequality. Both inputs are open; (b) is the genuinely new obligation.

[Lemma 57 (A curve meets an ellipsoid in at most $2D$ points) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $V\subset\R^d$ and $C\subset\mathbb P^d_{\mathbb C}$ be as above,
		with $\deg C=D$.  For $R\succ0$ and $\rho>0$, set
		\[
		E_{R,\rho}:=\{x\in\R^d:x^\top R x=\rho\}.
		\]
		If $C$ is not contained in the projective quadric obtained by
		homogenizing $x^\top R x-\rho$, then
		\begin{equation}
			
			\#\bigl(V\cap E_{R,\rho}\bigr)\le 2D.
		\end{equation}
		In particular, this holds for every centered ellipsoid if $V$ is not
		contained in any centered ellipsoid.  A sufficient condition is that
		$V$ be unbounded.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2605.07059, 'Modified ruin probability for a Cram{\'e}r-Lundberg model driven by a compound mixed Poiss'] Fix $\ell\in(0,c/\mu)$. Assume that
\[
\psi_{\rm cl}(u,\ell)\sim c_\ell e^{-R_\ell u},\qquad u\to\infty,
\]
for some constants $c_\ell,R_\ell>0$. If $\psi$ is continuous or monotone on $(-\infty,0)$, then
\[
\psi_\ell(u)\sim C_\ell\,\psi_{\rm cl}(u,\ell),\qquad u\to\infty,
\]
where
\[
C_\ell:=\int_{(-\infty,0)}\psi(y)\,\nu_\ell(\rmd y)
\]
and the probability measure $\nu_\ell$ is determined by
\begin{align*}
&\nu_\ell(( -\infty,-x])
\\
&=\frac{1}{c-\ell\mu}\Bigl(ce^{-R_\ell x}
\\
&\qquad\qquad-\ell\int_0^x e^{-R_\ell(x-z)}\bar F(z)\,\rmd z
\\
&\qquad\qquad-\ell\int_x^{\infty}\bar F(z)\,\rmd z\Bigr),
\end{align*}
for $x\ge0$.

[Definition gsp of arXiv:2608.30777, 'Inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \\ in Fourier-Lebesgue and modulation space'] Let $1\leq p_{0} \leq 2.$
 Consider a pair of exponents $(Q_{p_{0}}(r),r)$ satisfying 
\begin{align*}
&\frac{2}{Q_{p_{0}}(r)} + \frac{1}{r} = \frac{1}{p_{0}} \\
  \text{either}\quad 
& 0 < \frac{1}{Q_{p_{0}}(r)} < \min \left( \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{r},\; \frac{1}{4} \right) \quad  \text{and}\quad
  0 < \frac{1}{r} < \frac{1}{2}\\
&  \text{or}\quad 
(Q_{p_0}(r), r)= (4, r) \quad  \text{and}\quad r > 4.
\end{align*}
The set of all such pairs is denoted by 
$\widehat{\mathcal{X}}(p_{0}).$
title: Generalized Strichartz pair, \cite{hyakuna2012existence, CFeffermanAM,grunrock2004improved}

 (X,g_i(s))\longrightarrow(\widehat X,\hat g_s),\qquad s<0,

be smooth spacetime convergence on an exhaustion of a complete smooth
limit, with time-preserving convergence embeddings \(\psi_i\) defined
on domains \(U_i\Subset\widehat X\times(-\infty,0)\).  Write
\(U_{i,t}=U_i\cap(\widehat X\times\{t\})\) and \(\psi_{i,t}\) for the
time-\(t\) maps.  Fix \(t_0<0\), \(D>0\), an integer \(k\ge0\), and

\(\Omega\Subset\widehat X\) such that, for all large \(i\),
\[
\overline{B_{g_i(t_0)}(p_i,D)}
\Subset
\psi_{i,t_0}(\Omega)
\Subset
\psi_{i,t_0}(U_{i,t_0}),
\]
\[
\left\|
\psi_{i,t_0}^{*}g_i(t_0)-\hat g_{t_0}
\right\|_{C^k(\overline\Omega,\hat g_{t_0})}
\leq\varepsilon.
\]

[Theorem 55 (connected full isometry group in the four-factor Cartan
families) of arXiv:2609.03593, '\textbf{New Homogeneous Einstein Metrics from Detection}'] Let $H/K$ be one of
\[
 \SU(n)/\SO(n),\quad n=3\text{ or }n\ge5,
\]
\[
 \SU(2n)/\Sp(n),\quad n\ge9,
\]
or
\[
 E_6/\Sp(4),\qquad E_7/\SU(8),\qquad E_8/\SO(16).
\]
Let $g$ be any positive $H^4$-invariant metric in the Cartan-fixed family
of Theorem~\ref{thm:Cartan-fixed-point}.  Then
\[
 \Lie\Isom_0(H^4/\Delta K,g)=\mathfrak h^4.
\]
Equivalently, the effective image of the displayed $H^4$ action is the
connected full isometry group.

Let p>0. Let X_n be real random variables in L^p on one probability space, and let X be a finite real random variable on that space. Then X is in L^p and E|X_n-X|^p tends to zero if and only if X_n converges to X in probability and {|X_n|^p:n>=1} is uniformly integrable. For 0<p<1, L^p convergence here means convergence of the pth absolute moments of the differences; no norm or Minkowski inequality is asserted.

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2609.02837, '2609.02837'] Let $\phi: \R^n_{+}\!\!\downarrow\, \to \R_{+}$ and define its extension to $\R^n$ by \eqref{E:UIN-extension-phi}. Then $\Phi$ is a symmetric gauge function on $\R^n$ if and only if the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]\addtolength{\itemsep}{3pt}
\item $\phi(\vec{x}) \geq 0$ for all $\vec{x} \in \R^n_{+}\!\!\downarrow$.
\item $\phi(\vec{x}) = 0$ if and only if $\vec{x}=0$. 
\item $\phi(a \vec{x}) = a\phi(\vec{x})$ for all $\vec{x} \in \R^n_{+}\!\!\downarrow$ and all $a \in \R_{+}$.
\item $\phi(\vec{x}+\vec{y}) \leq \phi(\vec{x}) + \phi(\vec{y})$ for all $\vec{x},\vec{y} \in \R^n_{+}\!\!\downarrow$.
\item $\phi(\vec{x}) \leq \phi(\vec{y})$ whenever $\vec{x},\vec{y} \in \R^n_{+}\!\!\downarrow$ and $\vec{x} \prec_{\w} \vec{y}$.
\end{enumerate}

maximum over $[-1,1]$ at the unique point $m^*$, and
\[
\max_{m\in[-1,1]}\Phi_h(\beta,m)=\Phi_h(\beta,m^*)=f(\beta,h)=\beta\gamma_{\max}(h).
\]
Consequently, for every $\eta\in(0,1)$,
\begin{equation}

c_1=c_1(\beta,h,\eta):=\Phi_h(\beta,m^*)-\sup_{m\in[-1,1],\,|m-m^*|>\eta}\Phi_h(\beta,m)>0 .
\end{equation}
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 47 (Local comparison for the one-step tilted spine law) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Fix $t>1$ and let $\nu_t=\mathrm{Beta}(t,\theta)$ on $(0,1)$, with density
$
f_t(x)$.
We set
\[
I_j^{(m)}:=\left(\frac{j-1}{m},\frac{j}{m}\right],\qquad 1\le j\le m.
\]
With the same notations as in 
Proposition~\ref{prop:ewens_onestep_beta}, 
the following estimates hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \textbf{Uniform cell-wise comparability.}
There exist constants \(0<c_t\le C_t<\infty\) such that for all sufficiently large \(k\) and all
\(1\le j\le m\),
\begin{equation}
c_t\,
\nu_t\!\left(I_j^{(m)}\right)
\le
\mu_{k,t}\!\left(\left\{\frac{j}{m}\right\}\right)
\le
C_t\,
\nu_t\!\left(I_j^{(m)}\right).

\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] \textbf{Sharp comparison in the bulk.}
There exist constants $C,\gamma>0$ such that for
every $\eta\in(0,\frac12)$, 
\begin{equation}
\sup_{\eta m\le j\le (1-\eta)m}
\left|
\frac{\mu_{k,t}(\{j/m\})}{\nu_t(I_j^{(m)})}-1
\right|
\le
C\,\eta^{-1}m^{-\gamma},

\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $k$.
\end{enumerate}

[Defin 55 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\op{s}_{\rho}$ be the dilation with scale $\rho > 0$: $\op{s}_{\rho}(x)=\rho x$. Given $\mu \in \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R})$, its pushforward by $\op{s}_{\rho}$
is the unique probability measure $\op{s}_{\rho \#}\mu$  such that

$$\Int{\mathbb{R}}{} f(x) \, \mathrm{d}\op{s}_{\rho \#}\mu( x)  \, =  \, \Int{\mathbb{R}}{} f(\rho  x) \,  \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, .$$

Note that $\mathrm{supp} \big[ \op{s}_{\rho \#} \mu \big] \,  =  \,  \rho \, \mathrm{supp} [ \mu ]$. For a probability measure $\mu$ and $\tau>0$, we denote by $\mu_\tau$
the probability measure obtained by the convolution

\begin{equation}

\mu_\tau=\frac{1}{2\tau} \mathbbm{1}_{[-\tau;\tau]} \ast \mu\,.

\end{equation}

body: Let X be a smooth projective curve of genus g over an algebraically closed field, equivalently a compact Riemann surface, and let D be a divisor on X. Write l(D) for the dimension of the space of meromorphic functions on X whose poles are bounded by D and which have no other poles, and let K be a canonical divisor of X. The Riemann-Roch theorem states l(D) - l(K - D) = deg(D) + 1 - g, where deg(D) is the sum of the coefficients of D. Once deg(D) > 2g - 2 this gives l(D) = deg(D) + 1 - g exactly, since l(K-D) then vanishes. Proved by Riemann and Roch in the 1850s-60s; vastly generalized by Hirzebruch and Grothendieck.
title: Riemann-Roch theorem

[Proposition prop:full_Busemann of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] On the space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ there exists a process
    \[
    \Bigl(W_\xi^c(\mathbf x,\mathbf y): \xi \in (0,\xi_{\max}^c], \mathbf x,\mathbf y \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\mathrm{HS}}\Bigr)
    \]
    measurable with respect to the weights $(\omega_{\mathbf x})_{\mathbf x \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\mathrm{HS}}}$ that satisfies the following:
\begin{enumerate}  [label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
    \item  For all $\xi \in (0,\xi_{\max}^c)$, and each $t \in \mathbb{Z}$, the process 
    $\bigl(W_\xi^c((t,t),(k + t,t))\bigr)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ has law $\mu_{c,s}$, where $s = (X_c \circ T_c)^{-1}(\xi)$. For $\xi = \xi_{\max}^c$, the process has law $\mu_{c,r_c}$.
    \item  The law of the Busemann process is invariant under diagonal shifts. That is, for $m \in \mathbb{Z}$,
    \[
    \Bigl(W_\xi^c(\mathbf x,\mathbf y): \xi \in (0,\xi_{\max}^c], \mathbf x,\mathbf y \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\mathrm{HS}}\Bigr) = \Bigl(W_\xi^c(\mathbf x +(m,m),\mathbf y + (m,m)): \xi \in (0,\xi_{\max}^c], \mathbf x,\mathbf y \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\mathrm{HS}}\Bigr).
    \]
    \item{\rm{(Continuity at fixed $\xi$)}}  For each $\zeta \in (0,\xi_{\max}^c]$ and $\mathbf x,\mathbf y \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\mathrm{HS}}$, the function $\xi \mapsto W_\xi^c(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ is continuous at $\xi = \zeta$ on a $\zeta$-dependent event of probability one.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 28 of arXiv:2607.29495, 'Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees'] Let $\Downg$  be the distribution of  $X\sim\Poisson(dp_\good)$.
Let $\Downgbig$ be the distribution of $X$ conditioned on $X\geq D$ and let $\Downgsmall$ be $\Downg$ conditioned on $X<D$. Let $\Downb$ be the distribution $\Poisson(dp_\bad)$.  The rooted random tree $\cT^{\down}$ is defined as follows.

\begin{itemize}
\item The root is set to be \emph{down-good} with probability $p_\good$ and \emph{down-bad} otherwise (with probability $p_\bad$).

\item From every down-good vertex, the number of down-good children is sampled independently from $\Downgbig$ and the number of down-bad children is sampled independently from $\Downb$.

\item From every down-bad vertex, the number of down-good children is sampled independently from $\Downgsmall$ and the number of down-bad children is sampled independently from $\Downb$.
\end{itemize}
title: Definition 28 of arXiv:2607.29495

Assume that there exists $\theta \in(0,1)$ such that $v \in C_{\mathrm{loc }}^{\theta}(\mathbb{R}^{d}, \mathbb{R}^{d})$, $\operatorname{div} v \in$ $L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{d}), g \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$. Then, for any $\rho \in C_{r}^{\infty}$ and any $R>0$ such that $\operatorname{supp}\left(\rho \circ \phi^{-1}\right) \subseteq B_R$, we have the uniform bound
\begin{align*}
\left|\int_{\mathbb R^d} \mathcal{R}_{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}[ v,g](\phi(x)) \rho(x) d x\right|

\end{align*}
and
in addition,
\begin{equation}
\lim _{\ensuremath{\varepsilon} \to  0} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \mathcal{R}_{\ensuremath{\varepsilon}}[v, g](\phi(x)) \rho(x) d x=0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:constant-scalar of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Suppose that the base-graph edge weights
$(c_k, \lambda_k)$ are constant scalars, that the
block-diagonal lifts to the product graph are
$C_k = c_k I_m$ and $D_k = \lambda_k I_m$, and that
the directed-path propagator satisfies
$\mathcal{T}$-covariance, $\mathcal{T}$-splitting, and
$\mathcal{S}_k$-invariance~(equation eq:Sk-invariance of the paper).
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},
leftmargin=*]
\item $\mathcal{S}_k$-compatibility holds.

\item $P(\mathcal{S}_k u) = P(u)$, and the corrected
edge weights satisfy
$\Lambda_k(u) = D_k(u) = \lambda_k I_m$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the diamond data on $\mathcal{G}^m$
is $(C_k, \Lambda_k) = (c_k I_m, \lambda_k I_m)$.

Let $\beta \in \{\beta^{\mathrm {geo}},\beta^{\mathrm {res}}\}$ be the scaling exponent of the CLE$_6$ geodesic (resp.\ resistance) metric defined in [my2025metric,my2025diffusion]. For each $q \in (0,1)$, we have
    \[
    \mathbf{E}[S_n \mid \partial_L \Lambda_n \leftrightarrow \partial_R \Lambda_n ]

[Lemma lem:cutmarked of arXiv:2608.12954, 'Rainbow percolation'] In the marked model of (def:marked of the paper), define, for $n/3\le i\le 2n/3$,
\[
   \mathcal C^\sharp_i:=\{R^\sharp_j<i+1-j\ \text{for }1\le j\le i\}
   \cap\{R^\sharp_{i+1}<1\}
   \cap\{R^\sharp_k<k\ \text{for }i+2\le k\le n-1\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal C^\sharp_i\subseteq\{\text{gap}^\sharp\text{ at }i+1\}$, and
the certificate count
\[
   N^\sharp_{\mathcal C}:=\#\{i\in[n/3,2n/3]:\ \mathcal C^\sharp_i\
   \text{occurs}\}
\]
satisfies $\mathbb P(N^\sharp_{\mathcal C}\ge1)\ge c(x_m)>0$; consequently
\[
   \mathbb P\big(\exists i:\ \text{gap}^\sharp\text{ at }i\big)\ \ge\ c(x_m)\ >\ 0,
\]
uniformly in $n$ and in the marked parameters $m,s$. In particular, on the
rainbow event intersected with $B$, each one-sided disconnection event of
the reduction satisfies
$\mathbb P(\mathcal D^L), \mathbb P(\mathcal D^R)\ \ge\ c(x_m)$, uniformly over
rainbows.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Equal level growth does not determine branching number Result: A geodesic spanning tree has exactly the Cayley graph sphere sizes at each level. But growth can exceed branching number for a bounded-degree tree: take a single infinite spine and at its nth vertex attach a finite b-ary tree of height n. Its level sizes have exponential rate sqrt(b)>1, while its only infinite ray is the spine and arbitrarily deep singleton cutsets give branching number one. Check: At level m the largest attached contribution starts around n=m/2 and has order b^(m/2), up to constant factors and a geometric sum. Every attachment is finite, so no additional infinite ray appears. Obstruction: This is not a geodesic Cayley spanning-tree counterexample. It proves that matching sphere counts alone cannot establish the conjectured branching number.

body: [Lemma lem:excess-chernoff of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Let $n$ be an integer, and let $Z_1,\dots,Z_n$ be components of a generalised multinomial  random variable. Let $\overline{\mu} \in (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0})^n$, and suppose $\mathbb{E}(Z_k) \le \mu_k$ for all $k \in [n]$. Fix $\delta \ge e$, and for all $k \in [n]$, let $Z_k^+ = \max\{0, Z_k - \delta\mu_k\}$. Let $Z^+ = \sum_{k=1}^n Z_k^+$. Then for all $z\geq 0$, $\mathbb{P}(Z^+ > z) \le 2^n\delta^{-z}$.
title: Lemma lem:excess-chernoff of arXiv:2602.21315

body:
[Lemma main_lemma of arXiv:2604.05921, 'Simplicity of random hypergraphs'] Let $\delta_1,\delta_2 \in \mathds{N}$. Given (possibly non-unique) vertices $v_1,v_2,\hdots,v_{\delta_1} \in V$, let the unique vertices be denoted by $v'_1,v'_2,\hdots,v'_{u(\vb*{v})}$, for some $u(\vb*{v}) \in \mathds{N}$. Similarly, let the unique vertices in $w_1,w_2,\hdots,w_{\delta_2}$ be denoted by $w'_1,w'_2,\hdots,w'_{u(\vb*{w})}$. Let $D(\vb*{v})=\frac{\delta_1!}{\prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{v})} m_{v'_i}(\vb*{v})!}$ and $D(\vb*{w})=\frac{\delta_2!}{\prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{w})} m_{w'_i}(\vb*{w})!}$. Let $\hat{R}(\cdot)$ be as in (equation def:B_hat of the paper) and let $U$ denote a uniformly chosen vertex in $V$. For any functions $f_1^{(i)}(v):V \rightarrow \mathds{N}$, $f_2^{(i)}(v):V \rightarrow \mathds{N}$ and $w \in \mathds{N}$,
    \begin{align}
        
        &\sum_{\vb*{v} \in V^{\delta_1}}  \sum_{\vb*{w} \in (V\backslash\{v_1,\hdots,v_{\delta_1}\})^{\delta_2}} (D(\vb*{v})D(\vb*{w}))^w \prod_{i=1}^{u(\vb*{v})} f_1^{(m_{v'_i}(\vb*{v}))}(v'_i) \prod_{j=1}^{u(\vb*{w})} f_2^{(m_{w'_j}(\vb*{w}))}(w'_j) \nonumber \\
        &=\sum_{\substack{\vb*{a} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}:\\ \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} ia_i = \delta_1}}  \frac{\delta_1!^{1+w}}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_1} k!^{(1+w)a_k}} \sum_{\substack{\vb*{b} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}:\\ \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_2} ib_i = \delta_2}}  \frac{\delta_2!^{1+w}}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_2} k!^{(1+w)b_k} } \nonumber \\
    &\hspace{1cm} \times \sum_{\gamma(\cdot) \in \hat{R}(\vb*{a},\vb*{b})} (-1)^{\sum{\vb*{g} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}, \vb*{h} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}}( \sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} g_i + \sum_{j=1}^{\delta_2} h_j -1) \gamma(\vb*{g},\vb*{h})} \nonumber \\
    &\hspace{1cm} \times  \prod_{\substack{\vb*{y} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_1}\\ \vb*{z} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_2}}} \Bigg( \frac{1}{\gamma(\vb*{y},\vb*{z})!} \Big(\frac{n\mathds{E} \big[\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_1} (f_1^{(i)}(U))^{y_i} \prod_{j=1}^{\delta_2} (f_2^{(j)}(U))^{z_j} \big] \big(\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_1} y_i + \sum_{j=1}^{\delta_2} z_j-1 \big)!}{\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_1} y_i! \prod_{j=1}^{\delta_2} z_j!} \Big)^{\gamma(\vb*{y},\vb*{z})} \Bigg).
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:class-number-reduction of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $P\nmid N$, with $P$ odd, $N$ squarefree, and $PN>4$.  For $m\geq1$, whenever the arguments are discriminants, one has
\[
h(-P^{2m}N)=P^{m-1}h(-P^2N),
\qquad
h(-4P^{2m}N)=P^{m-1}h(-4P^2N),
\]
and
\[
h(-P^{2m+1}N)=P^mh(-PN),
\qquad
h(-4P^{2m+1}N)=P^mh(-4PN).
\]

[Definition Type forest, type rays and paths of arXiv:2607.16911, 'Multipartite random graphs with given degrees: local limit, revisiting the giant, distance'] Consider the \emph{Ulam-Harris forest} $\mathscr{F}_S$ on the set of types $S$. That is to say, $\mathscr F_S$ is an infinite forest, consisting of $|S|$ many infinite tree components $\{\mathscr T(s):s\in S\}$. For any fixed $s_0 \in S$, the root of the tree $\mathscr T(s_0)$ is $s_0$, and for any $v\in \mathscr T(s_0)$, it has $|S|$ many offspring $\{vs:s\in S\}$. Observe that any $v\in \mathscr T(s)$ has the form of a word $v=s_0s_1\dots s_k$. We call the forest $\mathscr F_S$ the \textit{type forest} corresponding to the set of types $S$. 
    
    Furthermore any directed infinite path $\pi=(s_0\rightarrow s_0s_1 \rightarrow s_0s_1s_2\rightarrow \dots)$ starting at the root $s_0$ is called a \emph{type ray} in $\mathscr T(s_0)$, and a finite directed path of the form $(s_0\rightarrow s_0s_1 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow s_0s_1s_2\dots s_k)$ is called a \emph{type path} started at $s_0$. By $|\pi|$ we denote the length of $\pi$. Thus, if $\pi$ is a type ray, $|\pi|=\infty$, while for $\pi=(s_0\rightarrow s_0s_1 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow s_0s_1\dots s_k)$, $|\pi|=k$.
title: Type forest, type rays and paths

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2606.06231, 'Sensitivity of SDE Solutions to Perturbations of the Diffusion and Drift'] Under Assumptions \ref{assump:main_assumptions_1} and \ref{assump:h_assump1}, for all $T>0$ we have
\begin{align}
&\left|\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T h(t,\tilde X_t)dt\right]-\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T h(t,Y_t)dt\right]\right|  
\leq\frac{ L_h(1+1/\epsilon)^{1/2}}{K_{\kappa,\epsilon}^{1/2}}(  1+M_h D_{1,T}) \|\sigma-\eta\|_{F,\infty}\\
& +\frac{2L_h(1-e^{-K_{\kappa,\epsilon}T/2})}{K_{\kappa,\epsilon}} (1+M_hD_{2,T}) \frac{\mathbb{E}[\|X_0-Y_0\|^{2}]^{1/2}}{T} \notag\,,\\
&D_{1,T}\coloneqq \frac{ (1+1/\epsilon)^{1/2}\|\sigma-\eta\|_{F,\infty}}{K_{\kappa,\epsilon}^{1/2}} +  \frac{4(1-e^{-\tilde{K}_{\kappa,\delta}T/2})}{\tilde{K}_{\kappa,\delta}T} \mathbb{E}[\| X_0\|^{2}]^{1/2}\\
&+ \frac{2}{\tilde{K}_{\kappa,\delta}^{1/2}}\left(2A_G+ \|\sigma\|_{F,\infty}^2    +\frac{\kappa}{\delta } \left(\mathbb{E}[\|X_0-Y_0\|^{2}] +\frac{(1+1/\epsilon)\|\sigma-\eta\|_{F,\infty}^2}{K_{\kappa,\epsilon}} \right) \right)^{1/2}\,,\notag\\
&D_{2,T}\coloneqq   \frac{2}{ \tilde{K}_{\kappa,\delta}^{1/2}}\left(2A_G+ \|\sigma\|_{F,\infty}^2    +\frac{\kappa}{\delta } \left(\mathbb{E}[\|X_0-Y_0\|^{2}] +\frac{(1+1/\epsilon)\|\sigma-\eta\|_{F,\infty}^2}{K_{\kappa,\epsilon}} \right) \right)^{1/2} \\
&+  \frac{  (1-e^{-K_{\kappa,\epsilon}T})}{2(1-e^{-K_{\kappa,\epsilon}T/2})}\mathbb{E}[\|Z_0\|^{2}]^{1/2}+ \frac{2\left(1-e^{-(\tilde{K}_{\kappa,\delta}+K_{\kappa,\epsilon})T/2}\right)}{(1+\tilde{K}_{\kappa,\delta}/K_{\kappa,\epsilon}) (1-e^{-K_{\kappa,\epsilon}T/2})}\mathbb{E}[\| X_0\|^{2}]^{1/2}  \,.\notag
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2604.00642, 'Quantitative central limit theorem for an integrated periodogram via the fourth moment the'] Let
\[
f_\alpha(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{-\alpha}L(\lambda),
\qquad \lambda\in(-\pi,\pi),\quad \alpha\in\mathcal A,
\]
where $\mathcal A=[a,b]\subset[0,1)$, and assume that the true parameter value $\alpha_0$ belongs to $\mathcal A$. Suppose that $L\in \mathcal C^1([-\pi,\pi]\setminus\{0\})$ is positive on $[-\pi,\pi]$ and slowly varying at $0$.

Define the Whittle contrast by
\[
Q_n(\alpha)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}
\left[
\log f_\alpha(\lambda)+\frac{I_n(\lambda)}{f_\alpha(\lambda)}
\right]\dd\lambda,
\qquad \alpha\in\mathcal A.
\]
Let
\[
\widehat\alpha_n\in \arg\min_{\alpha\in\mathcal A} Q_n(\alpha)
\]
be any measurable minimizer of $Q_n$ over $\mathcal A$. Then
\[
\widehat\alpha_n \xrightarrow{\mathbb P} \alpha_0,
\]
and
\[
\sqrt n\,(\widehat\alpha_n-\alpha_0)
\;\Rightarrow\;
\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{4}{\sigma_0^2}\right),
\]
where
\[
\sigma_0^2
=
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} \bigl(\log|\lambda|\bigr)^2\,\dd\lambda.
\]

[Corollary cor:mass-no-killing of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $G$ be a graph with $\kappa=0$ and \(\mu(X)<\infty\).
Let $\phi\in\mathcal{I}$ with $\phi^{-1}(\mathbb R_+)\neq\emptyset.$ Then \(G\) satisfies
\hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{} if and only if one, and hence all, of the
statements {\rm(ii)}--{\rm(iv)} of
Theorem~(thm:generalized-mass-characterization of the paper) hold, with the
generalized mass identity~\hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{} reducing
to the conservation of mass:
\[
    \mathsf M_u(t)=\mathsf M_{u_0}
    \qquad \text{for } t\in[0,T].
\]

Moreover, if \(G\) does not satisfy \hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{}, then, for every \(T>0\)
and every \(c \in \mathbb R_+\) such that $0<\phi(c)<\sup_{\mathbb R}\phi,$ there exist bounded positive pointwise solutions
\(u_-\) and \(u_+\), both with initial datum \(u_0= c\), and times
\(t_-,t_+\in(0,T]\) such that
\[
    0\le u_-\le c\le u_+
    \qquad\text{on }[0,T]\times X
\]
and
\[
    \mathsf M_{u_-}(t_-)<c\,\mu(X)<\mathsf M_{u_+}(t_+).
\]
Thus, failure of \hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{} allows for both loss of mass to infinity and
creation of mass from infinity.

body:
[Theorem CPLT of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a compactly supported positive measure $\rho$, of mass $c=mass(\rho)$, the following compound Poisson limits converge,
$$p_\rho=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\left(1-\frac{c}{n}\right)\delta_0+\frac{1}{n}\rho\right)^{*n}
\quad,\quad 
\pi_\rho=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\left(1-\frac{c}{n}\right)\delta_0+\frac{1}{n}\rho\right)^{\boxplus n}$$
and if we write $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^sc_i\delta_{z_i}$ with $c_i>0$ and $z_i\in\mathbb R$ we have the formula
$$p_\rho/\pi_\rho={\rm law}\left(\sum_{i=1}^sz_i\alpha_i\right)$$
where the variables $\alpha_i$ are Poisson/free Poisson$(c_i)$, independent/free.

Let A be an N-by-n real random matrix whose rows a_i^T are independent, with integers N,n>=2, common uncentered second-moment matrix Sigma=E[a_i a_i^T], and Gamma=E max_i||a_i||_2^2<infinity. Put r=min(N,n). There is an absolute C such that, for delta=C sqrt(Gamma log(r)/N), E||A^T A/N-Sigma||_op<=max(||Sigma||_op^(1/2)delta,delta^2). With an absolute constant C, enlarged if necessary, the same hypotheses give (E||A||_op^2)^(1/2)<=sqrt(N||Sigma||_op)+C sqrt(Gamma log(r)). These are both conclusions of Vershynin1011.3027v7 Theorem5.48 p30. Sigma may be singular; zero row means, identical row laws and independence of coordinates are not assumed. The dimension restriction excludes the literal zero-log singleton endpoint.

body: [Definition 3.2 (δ-hyperbolic (Gromov, 1987) of arXiv:2606.10238, 'Hyperbolic Neural Population Geometry Benefits Computation'] ). A geodesic metric space (X , d) is δ-hyperbolic if every geodesic triangle in X is δ-thin. Equivalently for all x, y, z, w ∈X , d(x, z) + d(y, w) ≤ (3.1) max {d(x, y) + d(z, w), d(y, z) + d(x, w)} + 2δ, which is called the 4-point condition. In general, low δ means the geodesic metric space is more tree-like, as tree triangles (Chiswell, 2001) are 0-hyperbolic.

[Thm 7 (Universality of resultant distributions) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Let $Z\in\Z_p[x]$ be a fixed monic polynomial of degree $d$, whose constant term lies in $\Z_p^\times$. Then there exists a random variable $\mathcal{R}_Z\in\Z_{\geq 0}\cup\{\infty\}$ such that
$$
\val(\Res(P_n,Z))
\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}
\mathcal{R}_Z,\qquad n\rightarrow\infty.
$$
Furthermore, the sequence $\val(\Res(P_n^{\Haar},Z))$ also weakly converges to the same limit, i.e.,
$$
\val(\Res(P_n^{\Haar},Z))
\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}
\mathcal{R}_Z,\qquad n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

[Theorem th:upper of arXiv:2606.16259, 'Super-Arrhenius relaxation of the triangular plaquette model in any dimension'] For every $d\in \mathbb N$ there exists $a_d\in \mathbb N$ such that the following holds. For every $m\in \mathbb N$ and every $s\geqslant a_d$, if $t>0$ and $n\in \mathbb N$ satisfy
  \[t \leqslant 1-\frac{1}{m} \qquad\text{and}\qquad n \geqslant m^s,\]
  then
  \[
    G_{d,n}(t) \leqslant 1+n^{-s}.
  \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2605.26439, '2605.26439'] Assume that system \eqref{control equation} is null-controllable at time $T>0$. Then there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for any $\varphi\colon \mathcal H\rightarrow \R$ with $\|\varphi\|_{\infty}$ and $\|\nabla\varphi\|_{\infty}$ finite, the Markov semigroup $\{P_t\}_{t\geq 0}$ on $\mathcal H$ associated with $\{X_t\}_{t\geq 0}$ satisfies that
    \begin{equation*}
        \|\nabla P_T\varphi(x)\|_{\mathcal H} \leq C\|\varphi\|_{\infty}\quad 
        \forall\, x\in \mathcal H.
    \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 12 of arXiv:2605.25762, 'Brownian Convergence of Planar Domains and Stability of the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Pro'] Let $(x^{[n]}_{k})_{0\leq k\leq n}$ be a mesh.
Define
\[
\mu_{n}:=F(a)\delta_{a}+\sum^{n}_{k=1}\big(F(x_{k})-F(x_{k-1})\big)\delta_{x_{k}},
\]
and let $q_{n}$ be the quantile function of $\mu_{n}$. Then for
any $p\ge1$,
\[
\|q-q_{n}\|_{L^{p}(0,1)}\le\max_{1\le k\le n}(x_{k}-x_{k-1}).
\]
In particular, for the uniform mesh $x_{k}=a+\frac{b-a}{n}k$,
\[
\|q-q_{n}\|_{L^{p}(0,1)}\le\frac{b-a}{n}.
\]

	Let $U \subsetneq \BC$ be a simply connected domain. Let $z \in U$ be deterministic. Let $\tau$ be a stopping time for the filtration generated by 
	\begin{equation*}
		\left(\SCB_t(\SCL(z); D_{\Gamma_U}^U), \Gamma_U|_{\SCB_t(\SCL(z); D_{\Gamma_U}^U)}\right)_{t \ge 0}. 
	\end{equation*}
	Then the following is true: Let $V \subset U$ be a deterministic simply connected domain. Write $\{V_j\}_j$ for the connected components of $V^\star$ (recall~(equation eq:def-V-star of the paper) for the definition of $V^\star$).  Let $(\Gamma_U, D_{\Gamma_U}^U, \{D_{\Gamma_U|_{V_j}}^{V_j}\}_j)$ be coupled as in (def:weak_axioms of the paper), Axiom~(equation it:weak_axiom_locality of the paper) (locality). Then, on the event that $\SCB_\tau(\SCL(z); D_{\Gamma_U}^U) \cap V^\star = \emptyset$, conditionally on $\SCB_\tau(\SCL(z); D_{\Gamma_U}^U)$, on $V^\star$ and on the $\sigma$-algebra generated by~(equation eq:weak_axiom_locality of the paper), the $(\Gamma_U|_{V_j}, D_{\Gamma_U|_{V_j}}^{V_j})$'s are independent and their conditional laws are those of $(\Gamma_{V_j}, D_{\Gamma_{V_j}}^{V_j})$, respectively.
	The same is true with a deterministic connected arc of $\partial U$ in place of $\SCL(z)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 237 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\alpha,L,\epsilon,K>0$ and any sequence of $\epsilon$-approximate $L$-Lipschitz algorithms $(\cA_N)_{N\ge 1}$,
	\[
		\lim_{N\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)\Big) 
		= \lim_{N\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu_{\sym}(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon)\Big)
		= 0\,.
	\]

\begin{proof}
	We only prove that the first limit is zero, as the second limit is proved analogously.
	Suppose for contradiction that there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $\bbW_2(\mu(\cA_{N[K]}), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)) \ge \delta$ for infinitely many $N$.
	By \eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l4} from Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound}, there exists $C = C(\alpha,L,K) > 0 $ such that for sufficiently large $N$, $\mu(\cA_{N[K]}) \in \cP_4(\R,C)$.
Then, for infinitely many $N$, we have
	\[\mu(\cA_{N[K]})\in
		S_\delta 
		\equiv \Big\{ \mu \in \cP_4(\R,C) : \bbW_2(\mu, \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)) \ge \delta 
		\Big\}\,.
	\]
	By Lemma~\ref{l:confinement.cPp.compact.Wq}, the space $\cP_4(\R,C)$ endowed with the $\bbW_2$ metric is compact.
	The set $S_\delta$ is closed with respect to the $\bbW_2$ metric, hence also compact. Therefore
 we may find $\mu \in S_\delta$ and a subsequence $(N_j)_{j\ge 1}$ such that
	\[
		\lim_{j\to\infty} \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\mu\Big) = 0\,.
	\]
	As noted in Definition~\ref{d:truncated.lip.alg}, we have $\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j[K]}) = \mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j})$: thus, since each $\cA_{N_j}$ is an $\epsilon$-approximate $L$-Lipschitz algorithm, so is each $\cA_{N_j[K]}$. It follows by omitting finitely many $j$'s that we have
	\[
	\WERR(\cA_{N_j[K]},\mu)
	=\max\bigg\{
	\bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\mu\Big),
	\bbW_2\Big(
		\mu^\Ising(\cA_{N_j[K]}),
		\cP(\{\pm1\})
		\Big)
	\bigg\}\le\epsilon
	\]
for all $j$. Recalling the definition \eqref{e:cM.Lip} of  $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon)$, this implies
	\[
		\mu \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)\,,
	\]
	which contradicts that $\mu \in S_\delta$.
\end{proof}

[Defn of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:[0,T]\rightarrow V$ be a continuous path with bounded
variation. The \textit{signature transform} of $\gamma$ (or simply
the signature) is the formal tensor series defined by 
\[
S(\gamma)\triangleq\big(1,\gamma_{T}-\gamma_{0},\int_{0<s<t<T}d\gamma_{s}\otimes d\gamma_{t},\cdots,\int_{0<t_{1}<\cdots<t_{n}<T}d\gamma_{t_{1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes d\gamma_{t_{n}},\cdots\big),
\]
where the path integrals are defined in the Lebesgue-Stieltjes sense.
The tensor series $\log S(\gamma)$ is known as the \textit{logarithmic
signature} of $\gamma$.

body:
[Cor 10 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let \((\mathbf{G}_N)_{N\geq1}\) be any sequence of complex Ginibre
matrices: for each \(N\), its entries are independent centred complex
Gaussian variables satisfying
\[
 \E\!\left[|(\mathbf{G}_N)_{ij}|^2\right]=\frac1N,
 \qquad
 \E\!\left[(\mathbf{G}_N)_{ij}^2\right]=0.
\]
Let us set
\[
 p_N(z)=\det(z\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{G}_N),\qquad
 q_N(z)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{2N}\partial_z^2\right)p_N(z).
\]
Then, almost surely,
 $\nu_{q_N}\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}\mathfrak{sc}_1$.

body:
Every unbounded open convex set in finite-dimensional Euclidean space contains an infinite straight ray starting at each of its points. If such a set is a mirror-complement component, that ray never collides with a mirror and is an escaping launch direction. The assertion needs convexity and does not settle the general all-reflected-rays trapping problem.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

Lemma 1. Every unbounded open convex set C in R^d contains an unbounded straight ray starting at each x in C. Therefore, if a mirror-complement component is unbounded, open and convex, an origin in it has an unobstructed escaping launch direction and cannot have every reflected ray bounded.

Proof: choose r>0 with B(x,r) contained in C and y_k in C with |y_k-x| tending to infinity. A subsequence of d_k=(y_k-x)/|y_k-x| tends to a unit direction d. For fixed t>=0 and sufficiently large k, convexity gives a ball centered at x+t*d_k with radius (1-t/|y_k-x|)*r contained in C. Eventually this radius exceeds 3r/4 and the center is within r/4 of x+t*d, so B(x+t*d,r/2) is in C. This holds for every fixed t with the same subsequential direction d, proving the entire ray stays inside C. No collision occurs along it.

Lemma 2. C={(x,y): x>0 and |y-x^2|<1} is open, connected and unbounded but contains no unbounded straight ray.

Proof: (x,u)->(x,x^2+u) is a homeomorphism from (0,infinity) times (-1,1), proving the first three properties. For a ray (a+bt,c+dt), t>=0, with nonzero direction: b<0 eventually violates x>0; b=0 and d!=0 eventually violates the strip condition; b>0 makes y-x^2 a quadratic with leading coefficient -b^2, whose magnitude diverges. Thus all possible directions leave C in finite time.

This gives an explicit algebraic version of the previous spiral-corridor obstruction: unbounded connected vacancy alone does not supply a straight ray. The corridor is not represented as a permitted mirror arrangement, and absence of straight rays does not establish trapping of reflected rays. Convexity is a sufficient special-case condition, not a necessary one.

[Definition smr-inequality of arXiv:2606.28575, 'Global smooth solutions by high mode Lie-Transport noise for Logarithmically Hyperdissipat'] Let $p>2$. We write $(A, B) \in \mathcal{SMR}^\bullet_p$ if for every $f\in L^p(I_T\times \Omega, X_0)$, $u_0 \in L^p_{\mathcal{F}_0}(\Omega; X^{\operatorname{Tr}}_p)$ there exists a strong solution $u$ to the linear Cauchy problem 
    $$\mathrm{d}u - Au\mathrm{d}t = f_t\mathrm{d}t  + B(u)\mathrm{d}W_t,\qquad  u(0)=u_0.$$
    such that $u \in  L^p(\Omega ; H^{\theta, p}(I_T; X_{1-\theta}))$ for every $\theta \in [0, 1/2)$ and for all stopping times $\tau : \Omega \rightarrow I_T$ it holds 
    $$\|u\|_{L^p( \Omega; H^{\theta, p}(I_T; X_{1-\theta}))} \lesssim \|f\|_{L^p(I_T \times \Omega ; X_0)} + \|u_0\|_{L^p_{\mathcal{F}_0}(\Omega; X^{\operatorname{Tr}}_p)}$$
    and in particular 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{t\in[0, T]} \|u_t\|^p_{X^{\operatorname{Tr}}_p}\right]  +\expt{\int_0^t\|u_s\|^p_{X_1}\mathrm{d}s}  \lesssim \expt[]{\int_0^t \|f_s\|^p_{X_0}ds} + \expt{\|u_0\|^p_{ X^{\operatorname{Tr}}_p}}.
    \end{equation}

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2607.11283, 'Markov Properties of $k$-Record Processes via Order Statistics'] The process $(Y_n)_{n\ge k}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain with respect to the filtration $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n\ge1}$. More precisely, for every bounded Borel function $g:\mathcal{E}_k\to\mathbb{R}$ and every $n\ge k$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\bigl[g(Y_{n+1}) \mid \mathcal{F}_n\bigr]
=
\int_{\mathbb{R}} g\bigl(\psi_k(Y_n,x)\bigr)\, dF(x)
\quad \text{a.s.}
\]
In particular,
\[
\mathbb{P}(Y_{n+1}\in A \mid \mathcal{F}_n)
=
\int_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\psi_k(Y_n,x)\bigr)\, dF(x),
\quad A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{E}_k).
\]

[Lemma of arXiv:2604.24914, 'SPDEs with time-independent\\ L\'evy colored noise'] Under Hypotheses A to D, for any $(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}_{+} \times \mathbb{R}^d$,  $\{Y^{(t,x)}(s)\}_{s \in [0,t]}$ and $\{Z^{(t,x)}(s)\}_{s \in [0,t]}$ have jointly measurable modifications denoted by $\{\widetilde{Y}^{(t,x)}(s)\}_{s \in [0,t]}$, respectively $\{\widetilde{Z}^{(t,x)}(s)\}_{s \in [0,t]}$, and with probability 1,
\[
\int_0^t |\widetilde{Y}^{(t,x)}(s)|ds<\infty \quad \mbox{and} \quad \int_0^t |\widetilde{Z}^{(t,x)}(s)|ds<\infty.
\]
Moreover, for any $(t,x)\in \mathbb{R}_{+} \times \mathbb{R}^d$,
\[
v(t,x):=\int_0^t \widetilde{Y}^{(t,x)}(s)ds=\int_0^t \widetilde{Z}^{(t,x)}(s)ds \quad \mbox{in $L^2(\Omega)$}.
\]
The process $\{v(t,x); t\geq 0,x\in \mathbb{R}^d\}$ is the random field solution of equation (equation lin-eq of the paper).

[Definition def:fk_current of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $U\in C^1_b(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a bounded, continuously
differentiable vector field with bounded derivatives, and $k\in\mathbb{R}$.
The \emph{Feynman-Kac semigroup} associated with $U$ is the family
$(P_t^{k,J})_{t\geq 0}$ on $L^2(\mu)$ defined by
\begin{align}
  \bigl(P_t^{k,J} f\bigr)(x)
  \equiv
  \E^x\left[
    f(X_t)\exp\left(k \int_0^t U(X_s)\circ\mathrm{d} X_s\right)
  \right],
  
\end{align}
for $f \in L^2(\mu)$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $t \geq 0$, where $\circ$ denotes
Stratonovich integration and $U(X_\tau)\circ\mathrm{d} X_\tau=\sum_i U_i(X_\tau)\circ\mathrm{d} X^i_\tau$.
title: Feynman-Kac semigroup for current observables

[Proposition 1 (Pathwise conditional law map) of arXiv:2608.08040, 'A cylindrical neural approximation theorem for conditional laws of McKean–Vlasov equations'] Under the preceding assumptions, the frozen equation has a unique solution

$X^{\mu_0,w}$. For every $t\in[0,T]$, the map
\[
\rev{\Phi_{T,t}}:(\mathcal P_m(\mathbb R^d),\mathcal W_m)
\times\bigl(C^{0,\alpha}([0,T];\mathbb R^{q+1}),\rho_\alpha\bigr)
\longrightarrow(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d),\mathcal W_2),
\qquad
\rev{\Phi_{T,t}}(\mu_0,w):=\mathcal L(X_t^{\mu_0,w}),
\]
is well defined and continuous. The corresponding restricted map for the
equation posed on $[0,t]$ is
\[
\overline\Phi_t:(\mathcal P_m(\mathbb R^d),\mathcal W_m)
\times\bigl(C^{0,\alpha}([0,t];\mathbb R^{q+1}),\rho_\alpha\bigr)
\longrightarrow(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d),\mathcal W_2),
\qquad
\overline\Phi_t(\mu_0,v):=\mathcal L(X_t^{\mu_0,v}),
\]
which is also well defined and continuous. The two maps satisfy the causality
identity
\[
\rev{\Phi_{T,t}}(\mu_0,w)
=\overline\Phi_t(\mu_0,r_t w).
\]

When the deterministic driver is replaced by the random It\^o lift of the
\rev{time augmented} common noise, this pathwise law coincides almost surely with
the conditional law:
\[
\rev{\Phi_{T,t}}\bigl(\mu_0,
\widehat{W}^{0,\mathrm{It\hat{o}}}(\omega^0)\bigr)
=
\mathcal{L}(X_t\mid\mathcal{F}_t^{W^0})(\omega^0),
\]
where $X$ solves the associated classical It\^o common noise
McKean--Vlasov equation. No drift correction appears in this identification. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pathwise conditional law map

[Lemma app_S1 of arXiv:2609.01250, 'Global regularity for 2D gravity water waves with two retreating point vortices'] We have the following results:

(1) Assume each $\gamma_j (j=0,...,m)$ satisfies 
\begin{equation}
C_{0,j}|\alpha-\beta|\leq |\gamma_j(\alpha)-\gamma_j(\beta)|\leq C_{1,j}|\alpha-\beta|.
\end{equation}
Then both $\|S_1(A,f)\|_{L^2}$ and $\|S_2(A,f)\|_{L^2}$ are bounded by
$$C\prod_{j=1}^m \|A_j'\|_{X_j}\|f\|_{X_0},$$
where one of the $X_0, X_1, ...X_m$ is equal to $L^2$ and the rest are $L^{\infty}$. The constant $C$ depends on $\|\gamma_j'\|_{L^{\infty}}^{-1}, j=0,1,..,m$.

(2) Let $s\geq 3$ be given, and assume ((gammaj of the paper)) for each $\gamma_j$, then 
$$\|S_2(A,f)\|_{H^s}\leq C\prod_{j=1}^m \|A_j'\|_{Y_j}\|f\|_Z,$$
where for all $j=1,...,m$, $Y_j=H^{s-1}$ or $W^{[s-1]+1,\infty}$ and $Z=H^s$ or $W^{[s]+1,\infty}$. At most one of these $Y_j, Z$ norms is in $H^k$ ($k=s-1$ for $Y_j$ or $s$ for $Z$). The constant $C$ depends on $\left\lVert\partial_\alpha\gamma_j-1\right\rVert_{H^{s-1}},\ j=1,...,m$.

(3) Assume ((gammaj of the paper)) for each $\gamma_j$, then
\[
\left\lVertS_1(A,f)\right\rVert_{L^\infty}\le C\left(\prod_{j=1}^m\left\lVertA'_j\right\rVert_{W^{1,\infty}}\left\lVertf\right\rVert_{W^{1,\infty}}+\prod_{j=1}^m\left\lVertA_j'\right\rVert_{L^\infty}\left\lVertf\right\rVert_{L^\infty}\ln r+\prod_{j=1}^m\left\lVertA_j'\right\rVert_{L^\infty}\left\lVertf\right\rVert_{L^2}r^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right)
\]
for any $r>1$. The constant $C$ depends on $\|\gamma_j'\|_{L^{\infty}}^{-1}, j=0,1,..,m$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group
equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and let $\mu$ denote the Haar 
probability measure on $G$. 
For any $G$-valued random variables $X, Y$ with finite entropies 
there is a non-empty, closed subset $S$ of $G$ of positive Haar 
measure such that, if $U_S$ is uniformly distributed on $S$, then,
for any constant $C\geq 4$,
\begin{equation} 
\dR(U_S, Y) \leq (C+2)\dR(X, Y) + H_2(1 - 2/C), 
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\log \frac{\mu(S-S)}{\mu(S)} \leq (2C+4)\dR(X, Y) + 2H_2(1 - 2/C).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.22534

[Theorem thm:main-explosion of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] \phantomsection
Let $\sigma=1+2d\zeta$, where $(\zeta(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ are i.i.d.\ with $\mathbb{E}\zeta(0)=0$ and $0<\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$. In parts~\textup{(i)}, \textup{(ii)}, and~\textup{(iii)(a)--(b)}, assume additionally that
$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_0|\zeta(0)|}<\infty$ for some $\theta_0>0$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \underline{\textup{Dimensions one, two, and three.}}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The rescaled mean converges:
$\lim_{t\to\infty}t^{-(4-d)/4}\mathbb{E} u_t(0)$
exists and lies in $(0,\infty)$.
\item The parabolic scaling limit is a Brownian optimal-stopping value. Let
$\mathcal W$ be white noise on $\mathbb{R}^d$, let
\[
    Z(t,x)\coloneqq \sqrt{\Var(\zeta(0))}
    \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}g_t^{\rm BM}(x,y)\,\mathcal W(dy)\, ,
\]
with $g_t^{\rm BM}$ the finite-time Green kernel of Brownian motion (defined in Section~(sec:rw-rep of the paper)), and let
\[
    \mathcal U(T,x)\coloneqq
    \sup_{\tau\leq T}\mathbf E_x^{\rm BM}
    \bigl[Z(T,x)-Z(T-\tau,B_\tau)\bigr]\, ,
\]
where the supremum is over stopping times for Brownian motion. Then, for every $T>0$,
\[
    R^{-(2-d/2)}\,u^{(R)}_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}
    \Longrightarrow
    \mathcal U(T,\cdot)
    \qquad\text{in }C_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)\, ,
\]
where the field on the left denotes the multilinear interpolation from $R^{-1}\mathbb{Z}^d$ of the values
$x/R\mapsto R^{-(2-d/2)}u_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}(x)$.
\end{enumerate}

\item \underline{\textup{Dimension four.}}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item The mean odometer is of logarithmic order at each site: as $t\to\infty$
\[
    \mathbb{E} u_t(0)\asymp\log t\, ,
\]
and, for every fixed $x\in\mathbb{Z}^4$, $u_t(x)/\mathbb{E} u_t(0)\to1$ in $L^2$ and
almost surely.
\item The centered odometer $u_t(0)-\mathbb{E} u_t(0)$ has Gaussian fluctuations:
\[
    \frac{u_t(0)-\mathbb{E} u_t(0)}{\sqrt{\log t}}
    \Longrightarrow
    N\left(0,\frac{4\Var(\zeta(0))}{\pi^2}\right)\, ,
\]
and $\Var(u_t(0))/\log t\to4\Var(\zeta(0))/\pi^2$.
\item For every $T>0$ and $s>0$, the fields
$\bigl(u_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}-\mathbb{E} u_{\lfloor TR^2\rfloor}(0)\bigr)^{(R)}$ for
$R\geq1$ are tight in $H^{-s}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^4)$. Moreover, for every
$\alpha>2$, the fields $\bigl(u_{t_R}-\mathbb{E} u_{t_R}(0)\bigr)^{(R)}$ at the
superdiffusive times $t_R\coloneqq\lfloor R^\alpha\rfloor$ converge, modulo additive constants, to the four-dimensional membrane model $\mathcal G_4$ in $H^{-s}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^4)$.
\end{enumerate}

\item \underline{\textup{Dimensions five and higher.}}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
	\item The odometer is deterministic to first order at every fixed site. For
	each fixed $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, $u_t(x)/\mathbb{E} u_t(0)\to1$ in $L^2$ and almost surely.
	Moreover, the mean diverges: there is $c>0$ such that $\mathbb{E} u_t(0)\geq c(\log t)^{2/d}$ for all large $t$.

[Lemma lem:delta of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] Under any coupling between $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$, we have
\begin{align}
    \mleft|
        \operatorname{Cov}[X^i(0), X^j(t)]
    \mright|
    &\leqslant
    2 \sqrt{
        \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^i(0) (X^i(0) - Y^i(0)) \mright] \cdot
        \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^j(t) (X^j(t) - Y^j(t)) \mright]
    } \\
    
    &\qquad + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ Y^i(0) (X^j(t) - Y^j(t)) \mright]
        + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ (X^i(0) - Y^i(0)) Y^j(t) \mright] \\
    
    &\qquad + \mathbb{E}\mleft[Y^i(0)\mright] \mathbb{E}\mleft[ X^j(t) - Y^j(t) \mright]
    + \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^j(t) \mright] \mathbb{E} \mleft[ X^i(0) - Y^i(0) \mright].
\end{align}
Moreover, both factors appearing under the square root in (equation decom4631 of the paper) are nonnegative.

[Theorem thm:counterexample of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] For any $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ there exists a family of reversible Markov
chains $P_{\delta,N}$ (parameterized by $\delta\in(0,1)$ and integer
$N\ge 1$) on a finite state space, with
$M_{\delta,N}:=M(P_{\delta,N})$, such that
\[
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\;\lim_{\delta\to 0}\;L(P_{\delta,N})\;\le\;2\varepsilon,
  \qquad
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\;\lim_{\delta\to 0}\;\frac{\eta_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_{\delta,N})}{M_{\delta,N}}\;\ge\;2.
\]
Consequently, $L(P)\to 0$ does not universally imply
$\eta_{\mathrm{KL}}(P)/M\to 1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Near-square Gaussian extensive-rank reference has a C1 information limit and pointwise limiting MMSE at every fixed positive SNR, proof unaudited. For independent real standard Gaussian U of size N by M and V of size P by M, B=UV^T/sqrt(N), M/N->beta in (0,infinity), P/N->1, the per-entry MI tends to i_beta(s)=Sigma(dilation_sqrt(s)(mu_beta) free-plus semicircle_1)-Sigma(semicircle_1), where mu_beta is the compact symmetric limiting singular law of UV^T/N in the square model and has second moment beta. For s>0, i_beta is C1 and normalized Gaussian-reference MMSE converges to 2 i_beta_prime(s)=1/s-Phi(mu_beta free-plus semicircle_(1/s))/s^2. Input zero atoms are allowed. A real conditional population-Wishart theorem, exact random-profile density calibration021 and free-heat regularity020 pay the observation law, MI limit and derivative separately. Column-padding chain-rule bounds extend the square result to every P/N->1 sequence. With existing finite-fourth-moment spectral coupling008 and Haar comparison006, every centered fixed iid unit-variance finite-fourth-moment pair of factors has limsup normalized product-MMSE excess over the Gaussian reference <=0 at every fixed s>=0. Novelty unestablished; full rectangular aspect !=1 is not settled.
Real centered iid Gaussian reference factors, independent between arrays and of Gaussian channel noise.
M/N->beta>0 finite, P/N->1.
Per-entry risk for UV^T/sqrt(N); raw UV^T risk divided by N.
Iid-prior MMSE consequence uses fixed centered unit-variance finite-fourth-moment laws and unaudited claims006/008.
