body:
[Theorem thm: pinning-1 of arXiv:2602.04429, 'Disordered systems and (subcritical) polynomial chaos\\ with heavy-tail disorder'] Assume that \( \alpha > 1-\frac{1}{\gamma} \) in Example~(ex:pinning of the paper) and that \(\beta_{\delta} \downarrow 0\) with \(\lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} \beta_{\delta} \delta^{\alpha-1+\frac{1}{\gamma}} = \hat \beta \in (0,\infty)\).
	Then, we have the following convergence in distribution for the disordered partition function
	\[
	Z_{\Omega_{\delta}}^{\omega,\beta_{\delta}} \xrightarrow[\ \delta\downarrow 0\ ]{ (d) } {\ensuremath{\mathcal Z}}_{\Omega}^{\boldsymbol\zeta,\hat{\beta}} \,,
	\]
	where \({\ensuremath{\mathcal Z}}_{\Omega}^{\boldsymbol\zeta,\hat{\beta}}\) a \(\boldsymbol\zeta\) -measurable non-degenerate random variable expressed as a polynomial chaos~(equation eq: limiting chaos expansion of the paper), with \(\boldsymbol\zeta = \lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} \zeta_{\delta}\) a \(\gamma\)-stable Lévy white noise on \(\Omega=(0,1)\).

	Additionally, there exists a (disordered) continuum measure ${\ensuremath{\mathbf Q}} _0^{\boldsymbol\zeta,\hat{\beta}}$ on the space \(\mathcal{C}_{\infty}\) of closed subsets of \((0,1)\) (with the Matheron topology) such that we have the following convergence in distribution\footnote{on the set \(\mathcal{M}_1(\mathcal{C}_{\infty})\) of probability distributions on \(\mathcal{C}_{\infty}\) endowed with the weak topology.}:
	\[
	\mathrm{P}_{\Omega_{\delta}}^{\omega,\beta} \xrightarrow[\ \delta\downarrow 0\ ]{ (d) } {\ensuremath{\mathbf Q}} _0^{\boldsymbol\zeta,\hat{\beta}} \,.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defin 31 (Level change, step up, step down) of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\bs{\sg}_{N-1} \in \{ 0,1\}^{N-1}$.  One says that $\sigma_j$ with $j \in  \intn{1}{N-2}$
is a "level change" if $\sigma_j \neq \sigma_{j+1}$. Level changes come in two forms:

\begin{itemize}

\item "steps up" corresponding to $(\sigma_j, \sigma_{j+1}) = (0,1)$

\item "steps down" corresponding to $(\sigma_j, \sigma_{j+1}) = (1,0)$.

\end{itemize}

There is a natural identification $\bs{\sg}_{N-1} \mapsto \big(\sigma_1, X(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \big)$
where $X(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \subset \intn{1}{N-2}$ is the set of level changes.  That is, $\sigma_1$ is the first element in the sequence and

$$X(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \,  = \, \big\{ j \in \intn{1}{N-2} \, : \,  \sigma_j \neq \sigma_{j+1} \big\} \, .$$

Note that one has the partitioning $X(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \, = \,  X_\downarrow(\bs{\sg}_{N-1}) \cup X_{\uparrow}(\bs{\sg}_{N-1})$ where
$X_\downarrow(\bs{\sg}_{N-1})$ is the set of down steps and $X_{\uparrow}(\bs{\sg}_{N-1})$ is the set of up steps of $\bs{\sg}_{N-1}$.
title: Level change, step up, step down

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2606.08115, '2606.08115'] Let condition (C) be valid for a two-dimensional random walk $\left\{ \ov{S}_n\right\}$, the correlation coefficient of components of the random walk increments $\rho \in (0, 1)$. Let also $D \subset K$ be a measurable bounded set such that $\mathrm{dist}\left(D, \partial K\right) > 0$. Then for any $\alpha > 0$ and any $\ov{x} \in \mathcal{X}_V$ the equality
$$\lim_{T \to \infty} \pr_{\bfx}^{+}\left(\ov{S}_T + \ov{x} \in \sqrt{T}D, \exists j > T: \ov{S}_j + \ov{x} \in K \backslash K_{j, \alpha} \right) = 0$$
holds, where $K_{j, \alpha}$ for $j \in \mathbb{N}$ is defined by (\ref{Kdef}).
title: Lemma 23 of arXiv:2606.08115

[Thm th2 of arXiv:2510.10898, 'A central limit theorem for unbalanced step-reinforced random walks'] Suppose that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[$(A3).$]
$
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n W_{nk}^2 \stackrel{d}{\rightarrow} W,
$ where $W$ is some non-negative random variable;

\item[$(A4).$]
$
\lim\limits_{c\rightarrow \infty} \sup\limits_n \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n \mathbb{E} (W_{nk}^{2} I(|W_{nk}|>c))=0.
$
\end{enumerate}
If 
$
\sum_{k=1}^n \xi_k  /{a_n}\stackrel{d}{\rightarrow} N(0,1),
$
then
\begin{eqnarray*}
\frac{1}{a_n}\sum_{k=1}^n W_{nk} \xi_k  \stackrel{d}{\longrightarrow} \sqrt{W} N,
\end{eqnarray*}
where $N$ is a standard normal random  variable independent of $W$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm th2 of arXiv:2510.10898

    \be   \frac {1}  {2} (au)  \cdot  u \geq \delta |u|^2,   \ee
    
with $\delta >0$.  Let   $\nu_t$ be the measure  satisfying

[Def 31 (Local good approximations) of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Let $G_i$ be a sequence of locally compact Hausdorff local groups and $G$ a locally compact Hausdorff local group. We say a sequence of functions $\phi _ i : G_i \to G$ consists of \emph{local good approximations} if there are open, pre-compact, symmetric, multiplicative sets $A_i \subset G_i$, $A \subset G$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\Roman*${}_{\text{loc}}$]
        \item (Almost surjectivity) For all $U \subset A $ open nonempty, one has $\phi_i (A_i) \cap U \neq \emptyset$ for $i$ large enough.
        \item (No expansion) For all $V \subset G$ open with $\overline{A} \subset V$, one has $\phi_i (A_i) \subset V$ for $i$ large enough.
        \item (Almost homomorphism) For each identity neighborhood $U \subset G$, there is $i_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that if $i \geq i_0 $ and   $g, h \in A_i ^8 $, then $ [ \phi_i (gh)^{-1} \phi _i (g) \phi_i (h) ]  \in U $. 
        \item (No compression) For each compact $K\subset A$, there is $i_0 \in \mathbb{N}$  such that if $i \geq i_0$, and $g \in A_i^8$ satisfies  $\phi_i (g) \in K $,  then $g \in A_i$. 
        \item (Almost continuity) For each identity neighborhood $U \subset G$, there is a sequence of identity neighborhoods $U_i \subset G_i$ with $\phi_i (U_i) \subset U $ for $i$ large enough. 
    \end{enumerate}
    If properties (I${}_{\text{loc}}$--V${}_{\text{loc}}$) hold, we call the sets $A_i$ and $ A$ \emph{regular neighborhoods} with respect to the approximations $\phi_i$. 

    \emph{Small subgroups} and the \emph{NSS property} in the context of local good approximations are defined in exactly the same way as they were defined for good approximations (see Definition \ref{def:ss2}).
title: Local good approximations

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.23491, 'Stochastic Dynamics of Low Earth Orbit Near Full Capacity'] Under (A1)--(A3), as $N \to \infty$,
    \[ \sup_{t \leq T} \big| Z_I^{N,\gamma_I}(t) - \bar z_I(t) \big| \probc 0
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \sup_{t \leq T} \big| Z_F^{N,\gamma_I}(t) - z_{F,0} \big| \probc 0, \]
    where $\bar z_I$ is the unique solution of
    \[ \dot{\bar z}_I(t) = \kappa_1 - \kappa_4\, \bar z_I(t), \qquad \bar z_I(0) = z_{I,0}, \]
    namely $\bar z_I(t) = z_I^\star + (z_{I,0} - z_I^\star) e^{-\kappa_4 t}$.
    In particular, the fragments are frozen at their initial value on the intact clock.

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2512.01483, 'Scaling Limits of Line Models in Degenerate Environment'] Let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $Z_k$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, be a collection of i.i.d. random variables defined on the same probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ with tail behavior  $\mathbb{P}(Z_k > t) = t^{-\alpha + o(1)}$ as $t \to \infty$. Let $\alpha^{-} \in (0, \alpha) $. Then, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega$, there exists $C(\omega)>0$, such that, for all $k \geq 1$,
\[\max_{-k \leq i \leq k} Z_i \leq C(\omega) (1+ k^{\frac{1}{\alpha^{-}}}). \]

[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] The estimate 
		\[
			 |\overline{Z}(s,t) - \overline{Z}(s,u) - \overline{Z}(u,t)| 
			 	\lesssim 
			 |\overline{Z}(s,u)|\omega(u,t)^\frac{1}{p}
			 + |\widetilde{Y}(s)-Y(s)|\omega(s,t)^\frac{3}{p}
		\]
holds for every $(s,u,t)\in [S,T]^3$ such that $s\leq u\leq t$ and such that $\omega(s,t)\leq 1$. The constant in the above estimate depends only on $C, \widetilde{C}$, $m$, $\|f\|_3$, and $\|X\|$.

[Lemma lem:LDP of arXiv:2604.20094, 'Persistence and local extinction for superprocesses in random environments'] There are constants $N_0(d,\Theta)\geqslant 1$ such that for any $a\geqslant N_0$ and sufficient large $t$,
  	$$
  	{\mathbf P} \left(\sup_{|x|\leqslant t} v(t,x) > \mathrm{e}^{-\frac{a t}{3}} \right)\leqslant  \mathrm{e}^{-c t},
  	$$
  	where $c>0$ only depends on $d,a$ and $\Theta$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 2 (Linear error equation) of arXiv:2608.16256, 'Error Distribution of the Local Linearization Method for Stochastic Differential Equations'] \label[proposition]{prop:ll_exact_linear_reduction}
The scaled error satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \hat U_t^{n,i}
    =
    Z_t^{n,i}
    +
    \int_0^t
    f^i_j(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \hat U_s^{n,j}\,ds,
    \qquad
    0\le t\le1,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
    Z^n
    \coloneqq
    \bar M^n
    +
    \sum_{\ell=1}^5 R^{(\ell),n}.
\end{equation}
Here
\begin{align}
    \bar M_t^{n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    \frac{n\sqrt n}{2}
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \sigma^j_\alpha\sigma^k_\beta
    \\
    &\quad\times
    \biggl[
        \bigl(
            B_s^\alpha-B_{\varphi_n(s)}^\alpha
        \bigr)
        \bigl(
            B_s^\beta-B_{\varphi_n(s)}^\beta
        \bigr)
        -
        \delta^{\alpha\beta}
        \bigl(s-\varphi_n(s)\bigr)
    \biggr] ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(1),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    n\sqrt n
    \int_0^t
    \widetilde R_s^{n,i}\,ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(2),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    n\sqrt n
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \bigl(
        \hat X_s^{n,j}
        -
        \hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^{n,j}
    \bigr)
    \bigl(
        X_s^k-\hat X_s^{n,k}
    \bigr) ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(3),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    \frac{n\sqrt n}{2}
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \bigl(
        X_s^j-\hat X_s^{n,j}
    \bigr)
    \bigl(
        X_s^k-\hat X_s^{n,k}
    \bigr) ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(4),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    \frac{n\sqrt n}{2}
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \theta_s^{n,j}\theta_s^{n,k}\,ds,
    \\
    R_t^{(5),n,i}
    &\coloneqq
    n\sqrt n
    \int_0^t
    f^i_{jk}(\hat X_{\varphi_n(s)}^n)
    \theta_s^{n,j}\eta_s^{n,k}\,ds.
\end{align}

[Lem lm:maximizer of arXiv:2605.21366, 'The Martin boundary of the Directed Landscape'] The following holds on a full probability event.
   Suppose $\mathfrak h$ is an eternal solution. Let $s\in\mathbb{R}$. 
Let $\gamma:[s,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be an $\mathfrak h$-geodesic. Then, for any $t>r\ge s$, setting $u=y$ such that $(y,t)=\gamma(t)$ maximizes $u\mapsto\mathcal L(\gamma(r);u,t)+\mathfrak h(u,t)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2605.30121, 'Improved Survival Results for the One-Dimensional Renewal Contact Process'] Let $\mu$ be an interarrival distribution and let $U = \sum_{n\ge 0} \mu^{*n}$
be its renewal measure. If there exist $\kappa>0$ such that
\[
   \sup_{a\ge 0} U_{\mathrm{at}}\big( (a,a+\kappa] \big) \;<\; \eta/2,
\]
then $\lambda_c(\mu) \;<\; +\infty$. In particular, the conclusion holds for every non-atomic interarrival distribution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2605.30121

[Thm t1-tightening of arXiv:2411.14236, 'Size of chaos for Gibbs measures\\of mean field interacting diffusions'] Let $\mu \in \mathcal P_1(\mathcal X)$
and let $\rho > 0$, $\delta \geqslant 0$.
Suppose that for all $\nu \in \mathcal P_1(\mathcal X)$,
\begin{equation}

W_1^2(\nu, \mu) \leqslant \frac 2\rho
\bigl(H(\nu | \mu) + \delta\bigr).
\end{equation}
Then for all $\nu \in \mathcal P_1(\mathcal X)$,
\begin{equation}

W_1^2(\nu, \mu) \leqslant \frac 8\rho (2+\delta)^2 H(\nu|\mu).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm t1-tightening of arXiv:2411.14236

[Theorem 1 (F\"ollmer theorem) of arXiv:2604.14427, 'A criterion for proving entropy chaos on path space'] Assume $\mathbb P$ is the law of a Markov diffusion process and $\mathbb W$ the Wiener measure. Assuming \eqref{L2_condition}, then the following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The time reversed $\mathbb{\tilde{P}}=\mathbb{P}\circ R$ is such that $H(\mathbb{\tilde{P}}|\mathbb{W})<\infty, $ i.e. there exists and adapted process $\tilde{b}$ such that 
\begin{equation}
    \tilde{W}(t)=X(t)-X(0)-\int_0^t \tilde{b}(X(s),s) \dd s, \quad t\in [0,T],
\end{equation}
is a Wiener process under $\mathbb{\tilde{P}}$ and, for any $t < T,$ it holds that 
$$
   \mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{\tilde{P}}}\left[\int_0^T \tilde{b}(t)^2\dd t\right]< \infty. 
$$
\item For almost all $t\in [0,T]$, in $L^2(\mathbb P)$
    \[
{b}(t)=\lim_{h \downarrow 0}\mathbb{E}\left[\left.\frac{X({t+h})-X(t)}{h}\right|\mathcal{F}_t\right]
.
\]
\item For almost all $t\in [0,T]$, in $L^2(\mathbb P)$
    \[
\tilde{b}(t)=\lim_{h \downarrow 0}\tilde{\mathbb{E}}\left[\left.\frac{X({t+h})-X(t)}{h}\right|\mathcal{F}_t\right]
=\lim_{h \downarrow 0}\mathbb{E}\left[\left.\frac{X({T-(t+h))}-X({T-t})}{h}\right|\mathcal{\tilde{F}}_{T-t}\right]
,
\]
where $\tilde{\mathbb E}$ denotes the expectation with respect to the measure $\tilde{\mathbb P}$.
\item For almost all $t\in[0,T]$, there exists the density $\rho_t$ which is weakly differentiable.
    \item The following duality equality holds $$\tilde{b}(x,T-t)+b(x,t)={\nabla \log \rho(x,t)}.$$
    \item The osmotic velocity satisfies the following finite condition 
    $\mathbb{E}\left[\int_t^T|\frac{\nabla \rho_s}{\rho_s}|^2(X_s)\dd s\right]<\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
title: F\"ollmer theorem

[Definition item:WB1 of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] In the VEB setting, we say that $V$ is \emph{well-behaved} if the following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(WB1)]
\item For all $t \ge \tau_0$, $\textup{type}^{\Psi(t)} \ne \textup{failure}$.
\item For all $j \ge j_0$, there is a positive integer $t \le \tau_0 + (4/\lambda)^{2(j-1)}$ such that $\Psi(t)$ is $j$-filling or $j$-advancing.
\item For all $g \ge 0$ with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\tau_g)} \in \{\textup{refilling}, \textup{stabilising}\}$, there is a positive integer $g'$ with $g+1 \le g' \le g+2j$ such that $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\tau_{g'})} = \textup{filling}$.
\item For all $g \ge 0$ with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\tau_g)} = \textup{refilling}$, $\tau_{g+1} \le \tau_g + (j^{\Psi(\tau_g)})^{\phi+46}$.
\item For all $g \ge 0$ with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(\tau_g)} = \textup{stabilising}$, $\tau_{g+1} \le \tau_g + (j^{\Psi(\tau_g)})^{\phi+72}$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition item:WB1 of arXiv:2602.21315

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2604.10891, '2604.10891'] The joint transform $\theta_n(z,\omega)$ ($n=1,2,\ldots$) in
(\ref{eq:theta_n-def}) is determined recursively by

\begin{align}
\theta_1(z,\omega) 
&=
z h^*(\omega+\lambda) v^*(\omega+\lambda),

\\
\theta_n(z,\omega)
&=
\psi_n^H(z,\omega,0) \prod_{m=1}^n \psi_m^V(z,\omega,0)
-
\sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \theta_k(z,\omega)
\prod_{m=1}^{n-k} \psi_m^V(z,\omega,0),

body: In algebraic geometry, a projective variety is an algebraic variety that is a closed subvariety of a projective space. That is, it is the zero-locus in of some finite family of homogeneous polynomials that generate a prime ideal, the defining ideal of the variety.

body:
[Lem 124 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall the definition \eqref{e:bad.times.J}. 
If $(p^N)'$ converges to $p'$ in the L\'evy--Prohorov metric in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:levy.prohorov.derivs}, then  we have
	\[
	J^N\equiv
	J(p^N,\tep,\lambda)
		\subseteq 
		J\bigg(p,2\tep,\frac{\lambda}{2}\bigg)
	\equiv J
	\] for all $N$ large enough. 

\begin{proof}
The function $(p^N)'$ is nonincreasing, so there exists a nonnegative measure $\nu_N$ on $[q_0,1]$ with
	\[
	\nu_N( (s,t]) = -\Big[(p^N)'(t)-(p^N)'(s)\Big]
	\]
for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$, and with $\nu_N(\{0\})=0$. Define analogously the measure $\nu$ corresponding to the limiting function $p$.
The L\'evy--Prohorov convergence assumption implies that for all $N\ge N(\tep)$ we have
	\[
	\nu_N(A) \le \nu(A^{\tep})+\tep
	\]
where $A\subseteq[q_0,1]$ is any Borel set, and $A^{\tep}$ is the $\tep$-fattening of $A$. (The same inequality also holds with $\nu$ and $\nu_N$ exchanged.) It follows that
	\begin{align*}
	&-\Big[(p^N)'(t+\tep)-(p^N)'(t-\tep)\Big]
	= \nu_N([t-\tep,t+\tep])\\
	&\qquad\le \nu([t-2\tep,t+2\tep]) + \tep
	=-\Big[p'(t+2\tep)-p'(t-2\tep)\Big]+ \tep
	\le \frac{\lambda}{2}+\tep\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last bound holds provided $t\notin J$. Since $\tep\ll\lambda$ by Assumption~\ref{a:params}, this shows that if $t\notin J$ then $t\notin J^N$, as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 124 of arXiv:2608.29416

body: [Theorem 39 (Categorical form of the branching criterion) of arXiv:2604.10792, 'Variable-Length Markov Chains on Finite Quivers: Boundary-Window Identifiability, Exact De'] In the exact-depth regime, the depth-$m$ informative map is obtained from the depth-$r$ informative map by composition with the deterministic truncation of states together with stationary fiber averaging. If a tangent block satisfies the hypotheses of either \cref{thm:selected-criterion} or \cref{thm:selected-criterion-global}, then the induced first-order morphism exhibits strict kernel enlargement at depth $m$ relative to depth $r$ after quotienting by the directions already invisible at depth $r$.

[Lemma lem-EntProjImag of arXiv:2604.14318, '\large The free energy of the interacting Bose gas:\\\medskip a variational description \\'] Fix a box $W\Subset\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathfrak r, M,L,K,T,\vartheta\in(0,\infty)$ and $S\in\mathbb{N}$. Then there is a projection $\Pi=\Pi_{W;\mathfrak r,M,L,K,T,\vartheta, S}\colon{\mathcal L }_W\times{\mathcal S }_W\to A_{W;\mathfrak r,M,L,K;T}\cap({\mathcal L }_W\times {\mathcal S }_W^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({M,\vartheta,S}})}}})$ and there are $\varepsilon^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\mathcal L }})}}}_{M,W,L}$ and $\varepsilon_{M,\vartheta,S,T}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\mathcal S }})}}}\in (0,1)$ satisfying, for any $S$,
$$
\lim_{L\to\infty}\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{W\uparrow \mathbb{R}^d}\varepsilon_{M,W,L}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\mathcal L }})}}}=0\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad \lim_{M,\vartheta,T\to\infty}\varepsilon_{M,\vartheta,S,T}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\mathcal S }})}}}=0,
$$ 
such that, for any  $\xi\in{\mathcal M }_1({\mathcal L }_W \times{\mathcal S }_W)$ with finite expected total particle number $\langle \xi,\mathfrak N^{\ssup\ell}_W\rangle$, and for any $S\in\mathbb{N}$,
\begin{equation}
J_W(\xi\circ\Pi^{-1})\leq J_W(\xi)+\varepsilon^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\mathcal L }})}}}_{M,W,L}+\Big(\frac 1K+\varepsilon_{M,\vartheta,S,T}^{{{\scriptscriptstyle{({\mathcal S }})}}}\Big)\frac 1{|W|}\langle \xi,\mathfrak N^{\ssup\ell}_W\rangle.

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2605.27818, 'Exponential decay of mass for inertial coalescing particles with Hamiltonian noise'] There exists $\eta_2\in(0,\eta_0)$ and $\vt_2\in(0,\vt_1)$, and for each
midpoint $q\in\mathcal M$ a constant $\kappa_0(q)>0$, independent of  $\al,\eta,\vt,s$ and $x$, such that the
following holds.

For every $\al>0$, $\vt\in(0,\vt_2)$, $\eta\in(0,\min(\eta_2,c_*\vt^2))$,
$s\geq T_{\eta,\al}$, $x\in D_{\mathfrak{r}}$, and $q=(q_1,b_2)\in Z_1\times M_2$
\begin{equation}
\E\Big(\int_s^{s+1}\ind_{[b_2-\vt,b_2+\vt]}(\phi_{\al,2}(r,x))\,dr\,\big|\,\mathcal F_s\Big)\;\leq\;\kappa_0(q)\,\vt,\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \P\text{-a.s.}
\end{equation}
The symmetric statement for $q=(p_1,q_2)\in M_1\times Z_2$, with
$\phi_{\al,1}$ in place of $\phi_{\al,2}$ and $[p_1-\vt,p_1+\vt]$ in
place of $[b_2-\vt,b_2+\vt]$, also holds.

[Definition e:Nevanlinna_representation of arXiv:2411.10586, 'A convergence framework for Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble\\ via pole evolution'] A function $Y:\mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{H} \cup {\mathbb R}$ that is holomorphic is called a \emph{Nevanlinna function}.
Any Nevanlinna function $Y$ has the following integral representation
\begin{align}
    Y(w)=b+cw+\int_{\mathbb R}\left( \frac{1}{x-w}-\frac{x}{1+x^2}\right){\rm d} \mu(x),
\end{align}
where $b,c\in {\mathbb R}$, $c\geq 0$, and $\mu$ is a Borel measure satisfying the growth condition
\[
    \int_\infty^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \mu(x)}{1+x^2}<\infty.
\]

[Corollary 2 of arXiv:2605.23817, '\bfseries Visibility in the Boolean Model \\ on Harmonic Manifolds'] Let \(M\) be a simply connected non-compact homogeneous harmonic manifold
	with volume entropy \(h\geq 0\). Consider the Boolean model on \(M\) with
	intensity \(\lambda>0\) and fixed ball grains of radius \(\rho>0\), and let
	\(a_\rho\) be the tube coefficient from \eqref{eq:arho}. If \(h=0\), then $\EE[\vol_M(V_o)\mid o\notin Z]<\infty$ for every $\lambda>0$.
	If \(h>0\), then
	\[
	\EE[\vol_M(V_o)\mid o\notin Z]<\infty
	\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
	\lambda>\lambda_c(M,\rho):={h\over a_\rho}.
	\]

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2608.21787, 'Stability of extremal hyperplane projections of balls in $\ell_p^n(\R)$'] Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be i.i.d. square integrable Gaussian mixtures whose distribution is not Gaussian. Then there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on the distribution of $X_1$, such that for any real numbers $a_1, \ldots, a_n$, $b_1, \ldots, b_n$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^na_i^2 = \sum_{i=1}^nb_i^2 = 1$ and $\left(b_1^2, \ldots, b_n^2\right) \preceq \left(a_1^2, \ldots, a_n^2\right)$ we have
        \begin{align*}
            \E\left|\sum_{i=1}^nb_iX_i\right| - \E\left|\sum_{i=1}^na_iX_i\right| \ge C\left(\sum_{i=1}^na_i^4 - \sum_{i=1}^nb_i^4\right).
        \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] $\textbf{FIK} \cap \mathscr{L}_\Diamond = \textbf{iK}_\Diamond$.
  \begin{proof}
    ($\supseteq$) Trivial from the axiomatization. ($\subseteq$) Suppose $\textbf{iK}_\Diamond \nvdash \varphi$,
    then by Theorem (thm:ikb-ikd-completeness of the paper),
    there are $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ and $w \in W$ such that $\mathfrak{M}$ satisfies the $\Diamond$-p condition and $x \not \Vdash^e \varphi$.
    Since $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Diamond$, it is easy to see that $x \not \Vdash^{\text{h}} \varphi$. Therefore, $\textbf{FIK} \nvdash \varphi$ by soundness.

[Definition defn:sub-stop of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] Let $\mathcal{O}$ be an orbit of length $2^j$, and let
$\{\mathcal{O}_{s,t}\}$ denote its dyadic sub-orbits
(Definition~(def:dyadic-suborbit of the paper)). We say that $\mathcal{O}$ satisfies the \emph{sub-stopping condition}
(\textsc{SubStop}) if at least one dyadic sub-orbit satisfies the
\textsc{Stop} condition:
\[
\textsc{SubStop}(\mathcal{O},\varepsilon,w)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists\, s\in\{0,\dots,j\},\; t\in\{1,\dots,2^s\}
\text{ such that }
\textsc{Stop}\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{s,t},\varepsilon,w\bigr).
\]

[Theorem thm:main-canonical-bridge-limit of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] Assume~(ass:limiting-effective-kernel of the paper),
(ass:limiting-effective-density of the paper),
(ass:effective-marked-trace-convergence of the paper),
(ass:effective-spectral-LLT-criterion of the paper), and
(ass:canonical-density-regime of the paper). Fix \(\kappa > 0\) satisfies~(ass:background-density-concentration of the paper).  Let
\(\Xi_L = \Xi_{L,N_L}\)
be the canonical marked cycle point process at particle number \(N_L\).  Then,
under \(\mathbb{P}_{L,N_L}^{\mathrm{can}}\),
\[
    \Xi_L
    \Longrightarrow
    \Pi_{\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}}^{\mathrm{br}}
    \qquad
    \text{in } \mathcal{N}_\ell(\mathsf{E}).
\]
Here
\[
    \Pi_{\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}}^{\mathrm{br}}
    =
    \mathcal{L}\!\left(
        \Pi^{(\kappa)}
        \;\middle|\;
        T^{(\kappa)} = \rho_{\mathrm{eff}}
    \right)
\]
is the marked Poisson--Kingman bridge defined
in~(subsec:limiting-effective-bridge of the paper).

Moreover, the background part is invisible in every fixed macroscopic length
window: for every \(0 < \delta < R < \infty\),
\[
    \mathbb{P}_{L,N_L}^{\mathrm{can}}\!\left(
        \Xi_{L,\mathrm{bg}}
        \bigl([0,1] \times [\delta,R] \times \mathsf{M}\bigr) > 0
    \right)
    \longrightarrow 0.
\]
Thus the background contributes the deterministic density
\(\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}\), while the effective part carries the remaining
density \(\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}\): under
\(\mathbb{P}_{L,N_L}^{\mathrm{can}}\),
\[
    \left(
        \frac{B_L}{V_L},\;
        \frac{G_L}{V_L}
    \right)
    \longrightarrow
    \left(
        \rho_{\mathrm{bg}},\;
        \rho_{\mathrm{eff}}
    \right)
    \qquad
    \text{in probability}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Canonical marked Poisson--Kingman bridge limit

\[
\|Z_k(t_2) - Z_k(t_1)\|_{L^p(\Omega;\dot{H}^\nu)} \le C_{p,k} (t_2-t_1)^{\gamma},
\]
where
\[
\gamma = \min\left\{ \frac{2-(2-\nu)\alpha}{2},\ \frac{\alpha(1-\nu)+2H-2}{2} \right\}.
\]

body: In probability theory, statistics and related fields, a Poisson point process is a type of mathematical object that consists of points randomly located on a mathematical space with the essential feature that the points occur independently of one another. The process's name derives from the fact that the number of points in any given finite region follows a Poisson distribution. The process and the distribution are named after French mathematician Siméon Denis Poisson. The process itself was discovered independently and repeatedly in several settings, including experiments on radioactive decay, telephone call arrivals and actuarial science.

body: [Definition Dual graph of arXiv:2604.24743, 'The impact of disorder and non-convex interactions on delocalisation of height functions'] Consider the graph $(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2)^*$ defined to be the copy of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ translated by the vector $(1/2, 1/2)$. We refer to this graph as the dual lattice and denote by $E((\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2)^*)$ its edge set. Each edge $e^* \in E((\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2)^*)$ is naturally associated with an edge of $e$ of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ (which is the only edge of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^2$ intersecting the edge~$e^*$). We refer to Figure~(fig:duallattice of the paper) for an illustration.

[Theorem 2 (Universal survival of the incremental component) of arXiv:2607.25949, 'Block-hierarchical covariance decompositions for finite-block additive functionals'] Let \(\{X_t\}_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) be a stationary Markov chain. Then the intrinsic incremental space satisfies 
\begin{equation}
\mathcal I_k=\ker P_k\cap \ker P_k^* .
\end{equation}
Consequently, the Green--Kubo series converges trivially on \(\mathcal I_k\), and,
\[
B_k f=f,\qquad f\in \mathcal I_k .
\]
Hence 1 is an eigenvalue of $B_k$ whenever \(\mathcal I_k\neq\{0\}\), and every element of
\(\mathcal I_k\) is an eigenfunction associated with this eigenvalue. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Universal survival of the incremental component

body:
[Corollary 11 (Parseval-type identity and intrinsic reconstruction) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Assume that the family $\{\Psi_{j,k}\}_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$
is a Parseval $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-module frame, i.e.\ for every $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$ one has the reconstruction
\begin{equation}
f=\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\,\Psi_{j,k},
\end{equation}
with convergence in the Hilbert-module norm. For $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$ define
\[
C_{j,k}:=\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\in\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R}).
\]
Then:
\[
\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\langle f,\Psi_{j,k}\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\,
\langle \Psi_{j,k},f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}
=\langle f,f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})},
\]
and
\[
f=\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d} C_{j,k}\,\Psi_{j,k},
\]
with convergence in the Hilbert-module norm. In particular, the coefficient family $\{C_{j,k}\}$ uniquely determines $f$.

body:
[Thm 6 of arXiv:2511.20875, 'Double $q$-Wigner Chaos and the Fourth Moment'] Let $q\in[0,1)$, and let $m,n \in\N$ have opposite parities.  Let $H=L^2(\mathbb{R}_+)$.  For each $k\in\N$, let $f_k \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^m_+)\cong H^{\odot m}$ and $g_k \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n_+)\cong H^{\odot n}$ be fully symmetric functions, and let $X_k = I_q(f_k)$ and $Y_k=I_q(g_k)$ be the $q$-Wigner integrals in $\Gamma_q(H)$. Assume $\|f_k\|_{\mathcal{F}_q(H)}$ and $\|g_k\|_{\mathcal{F}_q(H)}$ converge and define
\[ \sigma_X = \lim_{k\to\infty}\|f_k\|_{\mathcal{F}_q(H)} \quad \& \quad \sigma_Y = \lim_{k\to\infty}\|g_k\|_{\mathcal{F}_q(H)}. \]
Then the following three conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} \tau_q[(X_k+Y_k)^4] = (2+q^{m^2})\sigma_X^4 + (2+q^{n^2})\sigma_Y^4 + (4+2q^{mn})\sigma_X^2\sigma_Y^2}$.
    \item $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} f_k \overset{p}{\frown} f_k = 0}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}_+^{2(m-p)})$ for $p=1,\ldots,m-1$ and $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} g_k \overset{p}{\frown} g_k = 0}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}_+^{2(n-q)})$ for $p=1,\ldots,n-1$.
    \item The sequence $(X_k+Y_k)_{k\in\N}$ converges in distribution to a mixed $Q$-Gaussian random variable with respect to the vector $[\sigma_X,\sigma_Y]$, where
    \[ Q = \begin{bmatrix} q^{m^2} & q^{mn} \\ q^{mn} & q^{n^2} \end{bmatrix}. \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 6 of arXiv:2511.20875

body:

body:
[Lemma 55 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] Let \(\nu\in M_{\chi,\sigma}(E)\) and consider:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm(i)]
\item
\(\nu=\nu_Z\) for some \(E\)-valued random element \(Z\).

\item
There is a finite-valued measurable \(h:E\to[0,\infty)\) such that
\[
L_h=1\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]

\item
There is a finite-valued measurable \(f:E\to(0,\infty)\) such that
\[
0<K_f<\infty\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Conditions \textup{(ii)} and \textup{(iii)} are always equivalent.
If \(\rho\not\equiv1\), all three conditions are equivalent.

If \(\rho\equiv1\), condition \textup{(i)} holds if and only if
there is an \(h\) as in \textup{(ii)} satisfying
\[
\int_Eh(x)\,d\nu(x)=1.
\]
Whenever positive representing measures exist, they have a common
total mass, and a probability representing measure exists precisely
when this common mass is one.

body:
Let U be an open subset of C and f holomorphic on U. If gamma is a closed piecewise smooth curve in U that is null-homotopic in U - in particular, any closed curve when U is simply connected - then the integral of f over gamma is zero. Homology form: the integral of f over a cycle gamma in U vanishes for every holomorphic f on U if and only if the winding number n(gamma, a) is zero for every point a outside U. Consequently, on a simply connected domain every holomorphic function has a holomorphic primitive.
f holomorphic on all of U (a single pole inside the curve breaks the conclusion)
gamma null-homotopic in U, or U simply connected

[Proposition prop:morse-count of arXiv:2609.00336, 'Critical points of point charge potentials along lines'] Let $p>0$, locations $x_1 , \ldots , x_m \in \mathbb{R}$ be pairwise distinct, and $q_1, \ldots , q_m$ all nonzero, and satisfying $Q:=\sum_{r=1}^m q_r\neq0$. Further suppose that all critical points of the potential 
		\[
		U(a,b)=\sum_{r=1}^m \frac{ q_r}{\big((a-x_r)^2+b^2\big)^{p/2}},
		\]
		are nondegenerate. Then, $U$ has exactly $m-1$ critical points, all of which are saddles.
title: Proposition prop:morse-count of arXiv:2609.00336

body:
[Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(U\subset Y^{\rm rv}\) be open.  We say that
\((\mathrm S)_U\) holds if there are \(t_U<T\) and \(c_U>0\), independent
of \(x\in\pi^{-1}(U)\) and \(t\in[t_U,T)\), such that
\begin{equation}
 S_{t,x}\ge c_U\eta,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
 Q_{t,x}\le c_U^{-1}\eta^{-1}.
\end{equation}
We say that \((\mathrm Q)_U\) holds if there are \(t_U<T\) and
\(C_U<\infty\), with the same uniformity, such that
\begin{equation}
 S_{t,x}\le C_U\eta,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
 Q_{t,x}\ge C_U^{-1}\eta^{-1}.
\end{equation}
When an estimate holds for all \(0\le t<T\), as will be the case for
the estimates proved below, we use the same notation.  Condition
\((\mathrm S)_U\) supplies the upper differential bound for pulled-back
base coordinates, whereas \((\mathrm Q)_U\) is the lower differential
bound that prevents loss of base rank.
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.02878

body: [Defn of arXiv:2607.25567, 'Random Trees in Hyperbolic FPP'] A path that realizes $d_{\omega}(x,y)$ will be called an {\bf $\omega-$ geodesic}, denoted $[x,y]_{\omega}$. Observe that under our hypothesis on $\rho$, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega\in \Omega$, there is a unique $\omega$-geodesic between each pair of points in ${\Gamma}$. For fixed vertices $x,y\in {\Gamma}$, this ($\mathbb{P}$-a.e. well-defined) random path $\Upsilon(x,y)$ (i.e., $\Upsilon(x,y)(\omega)$ denotes the $\omega$-geodesic between $x$ and $y$) will be called the {\bf FPP-geodesic} between $x$ and $y$.

body:
[Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.29361, 'Convergence of the subcritical $\gamma$-LQG metric to the critical $2$-LQG metric as $\gam'] Let $\mathcal{D}'(\CC)$ denote the space of distributions (generalized functions) on $\CC$, equipped with the standard weak topology. Fix $\xi>0$. A \textbf{(strong) LQG metric with parameter $\xi$} is a measurable function $h \rightarrow D_h$ from $\mathcal{D}'(\CC)$ to the space of lower semicontinuous metrics on $\CC$ such that the following hold whenever $h$ is a whole-plane GFF plus a continuous function on $\CC$.
    \begin{enumerate}[(I)]
        \item  
        \textbf{Length space.} A.s., $(\CC,D_h)$ is a length space.
        \item 
        \textbf{Locality.} Let $U \subseteq \CC$ be a deterministic open set. The $D_h$-internal metric $D_h(\cdot,\cdot ; U)$ is a.s. determined by $h|_U$.
        \item 
        \textbf{Weyl scaling.} For each continuous function $f : \CC \rightarrow \RR$, we define
        \begin{equation*}
            (e^{\xi f} \cdot D_h)(z,w):=\inf_{P : z \rightarrow w} \left\{\int_0^{\text{len}(P;D_h)} e^{\xi f(P(t))} dt \right\} \quad \text{for all} \quad z,w \in \CC,
        \end{equation*}
        where the infimum is over all $D_h$-rectifiable paths from $z$ to $w$ parameterized by $D_h$-length. Then, we have that $e^{\xi f} \cdot D_h = D_{h+f}$ for all continuous functions $f : \CC \rightarrow \RR$ a.s.
        \item 
        \textbf{Scale and translation invariance.} Let $Q$ be as in \eqref{eq:lfpp_normalizing_factor}. For each fixed and deterministic $r>0$ and $z \in \CC$, a.s.
        \begin{equation*}
            D_h(ru+z,rv+z) = D_{h(r \cdot +z)+Q \log r}(u,v) \quad \text{for all} \quad u,v \in \CC.
        \end{equation*}
        \item 
        \textbf{Finiteness.} Let $U \subseteq \CC$ be a deterministic, open, connected set and let $K_1, K_2 \subseteq U$ be disjoint, deterministic, compact, connected sets which are not singletons. Almost surely, $D_h(K_1,K_2 ; U) < \infty$.
    \end{enumerate}
title: Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.29361

body:
[Theorem thm:d_thin_dom_attract of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Let $\alpha \in (0,2)\setminus\{1\}$ and Assumption~(\nameref{asm:T}) hold for some $p>0$. Then, for any $q\in(0,1]$ satisfying the condition $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d\setminus B_{\bm{0}}(1)}|\bm{w}|^q\nu_{\bm{X}}^{\mathrm{d}}(\mathrm{d} \bm{w})<\infty$, we have $\mathds{E}\big[\sup_{s\in[0,1]} |\bm{R}_{st}/t^{1/\alpha}|^q\big] 
    = \mathcal{O} \big(t^{1-q/\alpha}\big)$ as $t \downarrow 0$. Moreover, for any real number $q\in(0,\alpha)\cap(0,1]$, we let $\kappa(t)\coloneqq t^r$ for $t\in(0,1]$ and some $r\geqslant -1/\alpha$. Then, as $t \downarrow 0$, we have
\begin{align}
\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{J}^{\bm{S}^t,\kappa(t)},\bm{J}^{\bm{Z},\kappa(t)}\big)
    &=\begin{dcases}
    \mathcal{O}\big(t^{1-q/\alpha}\big(1+\log(1/t)\1_{\{p+q=\alpha,\,r\ne -1/\alpha\}}\big)\big), & \text{for }p+q\geqslant\alpha,\\
    \mathcal{O}\big(t^{p/\alpha + r(p+q-\alpha)}\big), & \text{for }p+q< \alpha. 
    \end{dcases} 
\\
\mathcal{W}_2\big(\bm{D}^{\bm{S}^t,\kappa(t)},\bm{D}^{\bm{Z},\kappa(t)}\big)^2
    &=\mathcal{O}\big(t^{p/\alpha+r(p-\alpha+2)}\big), \\

    |\bm{\gamma}_{\bm{S}^t,\kappa(t)}-\bm{\gamma}_{\bm{Z},\kappa(t)}| 
&=\begin{dcases}
    \mathcal{O}\big(t^{1-1/\alpha}(1+\1_{\{p+1=\alpha,\,r\ne-1/\alpha\}}\log(1/t))\big),
    &p\geqslant \alpha-1>0,\\
    \mathcal{O}(t^{p/\alpha+ r(p-\alpha+1)}),&p<\alpha-1\text{ or }\alpha\in(0,1).
\end{dcases}
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:d_thin_dom_attract of arXiv:2411.03609

body:
[Lemma lem:sepstatdetcon of arXiv:2606.02472, 'Correlated uniform attachment trees'] From two sequences $(X_j^{i})_{j\geq 1}$, $i=1,2$ with $X_j^{i} \in \{0,1,\ldots, j-1\}$, generate a paired tree sequence $(T_k^{1}, T_k^{2})_{k\geq 1}$, where the edges of $T_k^{i}$ are $\{\{j, X_j^{i}\}\}_{j=0}^k$.
    Fix a sequence of time steps $0<K_0<K_1<\cdots< K_\ell< m<n$, and assume  $(X_j^{1},X_{j}^{2})_{j\geq 1}$  are such that the following hold. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item For all $j=0,\ldots, \ell$, the $K_j$ most central nodes of $(T_k^{i})_{k\geq 1}$, $i=1,2$, do not change after step $m$, meaning
        \[
        A_{K_j}^{i}(N) = A_{K_j}^{i}(m) \text{ for all } N \geq m, \, i=1,2, \, \text{and } j=0,\ldots, \ell.
        \]
        \item After time step $m$, the differences in the number of nodes connecting to $A_{K_j}^{i}$ in each of the two trees has the following uniform bound
        \ba{
         \max_{j \in \{0,\ldots, \ell \}} \left| \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{1} \in A_{K_j}^{1}(m) \right\} }  - \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{2} \in A_{K_j}^{2}(m)\right\} } \right| \leq \log(n)^{2/3}.
        }
         \item After time step $m$, the weighted sum of squares of the differences in the number of nodes connecting to $A_{K_j}^{i}(m)$ in each of the two trees satisfies the bound
        \[
        \frac{1}{\ell + 1} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{1}{K_j} \bbbclr{  \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{1} \in A_{K_j}^{1}(m) \right\} }  - \sum_{k=m+1}^{n} \mathbbm{1}_{ \left\{ X_k^{2} \in A_{K_j}^{2}(m) \right\} } }^2 > C\log(n),
       \]
       for some fixed  $C>0$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then
    \ban{
        \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{1}{K_j} &\bbbclr{ \sum_{x \in A_{K_j}^{1}(n)} \deg_{T_n^{1}}(x) -  \sum_{x \in A_{K_j}^{2}(n)} \deg_{T_n^{2}}(x)  }^2
            \\
         &> C  - \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{2(m+1) \log(n)^{2/3} + (m+1)^2}{K_j}. \notag
    } (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:sepstatdetcon of arXiv:2606.02472

For any formal series E in power sum symmetric functions, the plethystic exponential satisfies Exp(E + F) = Exp(E) * Exp(F), and Exp(sum_{k=1}^infinity p_k / k) = prod_{i} (1 - x_i)^(-1). The boundary Cauchy-Littlewood identity is equivalent to evaluating Exp on the specialized difference of alphabets representing boundary reflection charges.

[Theorem 2 (Consistency and rate of $\widehat\Delta$) of arXiv:2608.29465, 'Deciding When to Decide:\\Testing Operational Suboptimality Under Distributional Shift'] Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:compact} and~\ref{ass:f_regular} hold, and the moment conditions in Assumptions~\ref{ass:envelope} and~\ref{ass:f_lipschitz} hold under both $\mathbb P_0$ and $\mathbb P_1$. Assume the three samples are independent as described above and $n,m',m''\to\infty$. Then
\[
\left(\big|\widehat\Delta-\Delta^\star\big|-\delta_{\rm inv}\right)_+
=o_p(1).
\]
In particular, if $\delta_{\rm inv}=0$, then $\widehat\Delta \xrightarrow{p} \Delta^\star.$ Moreover, if the local inverse-stability condition in Assumption~\ref{assm:error_bound_P0} holds with exponent $\kappa\ge 1$, then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left(\big|\widehat\Delta-\Delta^\star\big|-\delta_{\rm inv}\right)_+
=O_p\big(&n^{-1/(2\kappa)}+(m')^{-1/2}\\
&+(m'')^{-1/2}\big),
\end{aligned}
\]
where $(x)_+:=\max\{x,0\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Consistency and rate of $\widehat\Delta$

title: Lemma l.priorstogmc of arXiv:2606.11043

body: [Theorem thm:frag-nonexplosive of arXiv:2511.10223, 'Stochastic Reaction Networks Within Interacting Compartments with Content-Dependent Fragme'] Let $N$ be the coarse-grained model associated to (equation eq:general-content-dependent-fragmentation of the paper), and let $\mathcal A$ denote the generator of the associated chemistry $\mathcal I_\mathcal K$. Suppose there exists $w\in\mathbb R_{>0}^d$ and $c,d\in\mathbb R_{>0}$ such that $\mathcal Af(x)\le cf(x)+d$ for every $x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d$, where $f:\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d\to\mathbb R$ is the function defined by $f(x):=w\cdot x$. Then $N$ is not explosive. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:frag-nonexplosive of arXiv:2511.10223

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2506.10511, '2506.10511'] For all $d\geq 1$ and all $\beta>0$, there exists a constant $\kappa=\kappa(d,\beta)\in (0,1)$ {\rm(}depending only on $d$ and $\beta${\rm)} such that
$$
\mathds{P}\left[\sum_{i=1}^K \xi_i\leq (1-\kappa)K/2\right]\leq \exp\left\{-(1-\kappa)^2K/2\right\}.
$$
We will refer to the event $\left\{\sum_{i=1}^K \xi_i\leq (1-\kappa)K/2\right\}$ as $E_1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 10 of arXiv:2506.10511

[Corollary cor:random-four-set-first-order of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix $h\geq2$.  As $q\to\infty$, a uniformly random
$A\in\binom{[q]}4$ satisfies
\[
 \mathbb P(|hA|=M_h-M_{h-r})
 =\frac{24\kappa_r}{q}+O_h(q^{-2})
 \qquad(2\leq r\leq h),
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb P(|hA|=M_h)
 =1-\frac{24K_h}{q}+O_h(q^{-2}).
\]
Every other attainable cardinality has probability
$\Theta_{h,n}(q^{-2})$.  In particular,
\[
 \mathbb P(A\text{ is not }B_h)
 =\frac{24K_h}{q}+O_h(q^{-2}),
 \qquad K_h\asymp h^2.
\]

[Definition The Generated $\Theta$-Expectation Operator of arXiv:2507.22577, 'A Mean-Field Theory of $\Theta$-Expectations'] Assume the conditions for global well-posedness (Assumptions (ass:mf_fbsde_standing of the paper), (ass:boundary_and_ndg of the paper), and (ass:monotonicity_fbsde of the paper)) hold. For any terminal condition $\xi \in L^2(\mathcal{F}_T)$, the \emph{conditional $\Theta$-Expectation} of $\xi$ given $\mathcal{F}_t$ is the mapping $\mathfrak{E}[\cdot|\mathcal{F}_t]$ defined as
\[ \mathfrak{E}[\xi|\mathcal{F}_t] \coloneqq Y_t, \]
where $(X,Y,Z,A)$ is the unique solution to the Mean-Field $\Theta$-FBSDE on $[0,T]$ with terminal value $Y_T = \xi$. The unconditional $\Theta$-Expectation is defined as $\mathfrak{E}[\xi] \coloneqq Y_0$.
title: The Generated $\Theta$-Expectation Operator

Let $A_n = \rho_n(1_S)$ be the adjacency operator of a uniformly sampled Schreier graph on the vertex set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with generator $S$.
Then, in probability, the Hausdorff distance between the spectrum of $A_{\mathrm F}$ and $(A_n)_{|\mathrm 1^\perp}$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 10 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Regularized Kullback-Leibler divergence between Gaussian measures on Hilbert spaces}\cite{Minh:LogDet2016,Minh:2020regularizedDiv}]
			
			Let $\Ncal(m_1,C_1), \Ncal(m_2,C_2) \in \Gauss(\Hcal)$,
			
			
			
			with corresponding mean vectors $m_1,m_2 \in \H$  
			and
			
			covariance operators $C_1, C_2 \in \Sym^{+}(\H) \cap \Tr(\H)$. 
			For any 
			
			fixed $\gamma \in \R$, 
			$\gamma > 0$, 
			the regularized 
			
			KL divergence, denoted by ${\KL}^{\gamma}(\Ncal(m_1, C_1)|| \Ncal(m_2, C_2))$, 
			
			is defined to be
			\begin{align}
				
				{\KL}^{\gamma}(\Ncal(m_1, C_1)|| \Ncal(m_2, C_2)) 
				
				&=\frac{1}{2}\la m_1 - m_2, (C_2 + \gamma I)^{-1}(m_1 - m_2)\ra 
				\nonumber
				\\
				&\quad + \frac{1}{2}d^1_{\logdet}[(C_1 + \gamma I), (C_2 + \gamma I)].
			\end{align}
title: Definition 10 of arXiv:2506.10494

Owner draft: independently checked proof (C011 v2). Let d>=2, p=d-1, A an invertible p-by-p matrix, c(y)=c_0+y*c_1, and r(y)=alpha+(beta-alpha)y with alpha,beta>=0 and alpha+beta>0. The uniform law on C={(y,z):0<=y<=1, z in c(y)+A(r(y)B_p)} is n-CM for every n>=d+1. This includes ellipsoidal cones, cylinders, frustums, all planar trapezoids and their invertible affine images. The height density is proportional to r(y)^(d-1), and Wang-Wang 2011 Corollary 2.9 p.13 mixes the heights at n>=d+1. Their radii have deterministic total >=d*max(alpha,beta), satisfying the polygon inequality. A Borel closed-vector polygon and one Haar rotation give simultaneous uniform scaled-ball sections (for p=1 use a sphere S^2 coordinate). Affine centers then sum to their centroid. General changing-shape/nonaffine sections are not covered; novelty UNKNOWN.

body:
Every bounded sequence of real numbers has a convergent subsequence. More generally, every bounded sequence in R^n has a convergent subsequence.

For any subset A of R^n, sequential compactness (every sequence in A has a subsequence converging to a point of A) is equivalent to A being closed and bounded. In every infinite-dimensional normed space, the closed unit ball is closed and bounded but not sequentially compact, so neither finite-dimensional formulation extends to all normed spaces.

At least one half of the interval contains infinitely many terms of the sequence; choose it and recurse. The nested intervals have lengths (b-a)/2^k -> 0, so by the nested interval property they intersect in a single point x. Choosing one term of the sequence from each stage (with strictly increasing indices) gives a subsequence converging to x. For R^n, apply the real case coordinate-wise, passing to successive subsequences n times. Closed bounded A: apply the keeper to a sequence in A and use closedness to put its limit in A. Conversely sequential compactness forces boundedness (otherwise choose ||x_k||>=k) and closedness (for x in closure choose x_k in A tending to x; a subsequential limit in A must equal x). In an infinite-dimensional normed space, each finite-dimensional span is closed and proper; Riesz's lemma inductively supplies unit vectors x_k at distance >1/2 from the preceding span. [Theorem thm:catcher-convergence of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] For \(0<\lambda\leq1\), fix \((D;a,b)\) as in Section~(subsec:continuum-main of the paper).  Let \(\delta\downarrow0\), and let
\(D^\delta\) be a finite connected induced subgraph of
\(\delta\mathbb{Z}^2\cap D\) such that the union of its mesh squares is a Jordan domain converging
to \(D\) both in the Carath\'eodory topology and in boundary Fr\'echet
  distance, equipped with exterior boundary vertices
  \(\widehat a^\delta,\widehat b^\delta\) converging to 
  \(a,b\).  Set \(Q^\delta_{xy}=\frac14\mathbf 1_{\{|x-y|=\delta\}}\) for
\(x,y\in D^\delta\), and assign weight \(\frac14\) to every edge entering
\(D^\delta\) from \(\widehat a^\delta\) or exiting \(D^\delta\) to
\(\widehat b^\delta\); these weights define the entrance and exit
vectors.  
  With \((D;a,b)\) fixed, let \(K_\lambda^\delta\) be its 
\(\lambda\)-random-walk loop-catcher on $D^\delta$, realized as the union of its closed mesh cells
  and two \(o_\delta(1)\)-diameter connectors from \(a\) and \(b\), respectively, to the corresponding endpoint cells.
Then in the Hausdorff topology on closed subsets of $\overline{D}$,
\[
 K_\lambda^{\delta}\ \Longrightarrow\ K_\lambda^{D;a,b}
 \qquad(\delta\downarrow0).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem deg_7_cubature_formula of arXiv:2411.13707, 'High-degree cubature on Wiener space \\ through unshuffle expansions'] Let $(z_i,\lambda)$, $(z_{ij},\mu)$ and $(z,\eta)$ be independent Gaussian cubature formulae of $(\text{deg}=7, \text{dim}=d)$, $(\text{deg}=3, \text{dim}=d^2)$ and $(\text{deg}=2, \text{dim}=1)$ respectively. Define,
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{L}^{(n,m,r)} \coloneqq{}& \epsilon_0 + \sum_{i}\Big (z_i^{(n)}\epsilon_i+\frac{1}{\sqrt 3}z_{ii}^{(m)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_0\epsilon_i)+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_0\epsilon_i\epsilon_i)\Big ) +\sum_{i,j}\Big[ \Big( \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}z_i^{(n)} z_{jj}^{(m)}+ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}z_{ij}^{(m)}\Big) \mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j)\\
&+\frac{1}{2} z_i^{(n)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_j)+\frac{1}{12}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_0\epsilon_i\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_j)+\frac{1}{24}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_i\epsilon_0\epsilon_j\epsilon_j)\Big] +\sum_{i,j,k} \Big (\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} z_{ij}^{(m)}z_k^{(n)}z^{(r)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_k)\\
&+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}z_{i}^{(n)}z_{jj}^{(m)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_k\epsilon_k)+\frac{1}{4\sqrt{3}}z_{i}^{(n)}z_{kk}^{(m)}\mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_j\epsilon_k)+\frac{1}{12}z_i^{(n)} \mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_j\epsilon_k\epsilon_k)\\
&+\frac{1}{24}z_j^{(n)} \mathrm{e}(\epsilon_i\epsilon_i\epsilon_j\epsilon_k\epsilon_k)\Big ).
\end{align*}
and $\theta_{n,m,r} = \lambda_n\mu_m\eta_r$ for each $(n,m,r)$ that indexes the product measure $(z_i,\lambda)\times (z_{ij},\mu)\times (z,\eta)$. Then
$\mathcal{L}^{(n,m,r)}$ and $\theta_{n,m,r}$ define the Lie polynomials and weights respectively of a degree-\(7\) cubature formula on \(d\)-dimensional Wiener space with drift. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Degree-7 cubature formula on \(d\)-dimensional Wiener space with drift

body: For large classes of random matrices (GUE, GOE, and universally many Wigner and sample-covariance ensembles), the largest eigenvalue, centered at the spectral edge and scaled by n^(2/3), converges in distribution to a Tracy-Widom law (beta = 1, 2, 4 by symmetry class). The Tracy-Widom distributions are expressed via Painleve II or as Fredholm determinants of the Airy kernel, and govern edge fluctuations far beyond matrices, e.g. the longest increasing subsequence of a random permutation.
title: Tracy-Widom Edge Fluctuations

body:
[Lemma lem:mixingtime of arXiv:2411.18563, 'Lower tails for triangles inside the critical window'] In the setting of Theorem~(thm:barbour2019longterm of the paper),
let $y_0\in\Omega_{\text{typ}}$ and let  $P=(Y_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ where we set $Y_0=y_0$.
Let $\nu$ denote the stationary distribution of $P$. For $k \geq 1$, we have
\[
W_1(\nu,Y_k) \leq \textup{diam}(\Omega)\left((1 - \rho)^{k} + 2k e_k + \nu(\Omega\setminus \Omega_{\text{typ}})\right).
\]
As a consequence, we have
\[
\left|\nu(f) - \mathbb{E}\left[f(Y_k)\right]\right| \leq L\cdot \textup{diam}(\Omega)\left((1 - \rho)^{k} + 2k e_k + \nu(\Omega\setminus \Omega_{\text{typ}}\right)\, ,
\]
where $\nu(f)$ denotes the expectation of $f$ with respect to $\nu$.
title: Lemma lem:mixingtime of arXiv:2411.18563

[Lem irr of arXiv:2411.07158, 'Markov chains on trees: almost lower and upper directed cases'] [Irreducibility criteria]
  \begin{itemize} \topsep0pt   \itemsep=0pt   \partopsep=0pt   \parsep=0pt \setcounter{c}{0}
  \addtocounter{c}{1}\item[($\roman{c}$)] An {\sf AUD}\xspace transition matrix ${\sf U}$ is irreducible iff, for all $u\neq \varnothing$, ${\sf U}_{u,p(u)}>0$ and, for each node $v\neq \varnothing$, there exists a strict ancestor $u$ of $v$ and an element $w$ in $T_v$ such that ${\sf U}_{u,w}>0$.
\addtocounter{c}{1}\item[($\roman{c}$)] An {\sf ALD}\xspace transition matrix ${\sf D}$ is irreducible iff, for all $u\neq \varnothing$, ${\sf D}_{p(u),u}>0$ and for each node $v$, there exists a descendant $w$ of $v$ and a strict ancestor $u$ of $v$, such that ${\sf D}_{w,u}>0$.~
\addtocounter{c}{1}\item[($\roman{c}$)] The transition matrix of a random walk on $T$ is irreducible iff for each $u\neq \varnothing$, ${\sf M}_{u,p(u)}>0$ and ${\sf M}_{p(u),u}>0$. \end{itemize}\vspace{-2em}~

body:
[Theorem thm:observable-distance-cs of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Suppose Assumptions~(assump:strong-convexity of the paper)--(assump:stepsize-bound of the paper) hold, and let $R_0$ be an $\mathcal{F}_{t_0-1}$-measurable quantity satisfying $R_0 \ge Z_{t_0}$ almost surely. Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$, the recursively defined process $\{\widehat U_{t+1}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\alpha)\}_{t \ge t_0}$ is well defined and fully observable from $R_0$ and the SGD trajectory. Moreover,
\[
    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        Z_{t+1}
        \le
        \widehat U_{t+1}^{\mathrm{dist}}(\alpha)
    \right)
    \ge
    1 - \alpha.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Observable confidence sequence for $\norm{x_{t+1} - x^\star}^2$

Then, we have a weak convergence
$$\val(\Res(P_{A_n},Z))\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}v,\qquad n\rightarrow\infty.$$

    \[\mathbb{E}\left[\left(e^{-\lambda t}Z(t)-Y\right)^2\right]=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\lambda}e^{-\lambda t}\]

	coordinates. Denote by $\mathcal{H}$ the scaled hexagon, that is,
	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathcal{H}\coloneqq \left\{
		(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\colon 0< \mathsf{t}<\mathsf{T},\
		\max(0,\mathsf{t}-\mathsf{T}+\mathsf{S})< \mathsf{x}<
		\min(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{N},\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{N})\right\}.
	\end{equation}
	Let
	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathsf{t}_l\coloneqq
		|\mathsf{N}-\mathsf{S}|
		,
		\qquad
		\mathsf{t}_r\coloneqq
		\min(\mathsf{N}+\mathsf{S},2\mathsf{T}-\mathsf{N}-\mathsf{S}).
	\end{equation}
	Denote the \emph{waterfall region} by
	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathcal{W}\coloneqq \left\{ (\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
			\mathsf{t}_l< \mathsf{t}< \mathsf{t}_r,
			\
			|2\mathsf{x}-\mathsf{S}-\mathsf{t}|< \mathsf{N}
		\right\}.
	\end{equation}
	Also, let the \emph{center line} be the following line segment of slope $\frac{1}{2}$:
	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathcal{C}\coloneqq
		\left\{ (\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})\in \mathcal{H}\colon
		\mathsf{t}_l< \mathsf{t}< \mathsf{t}_r,\
		\mathsf{x}=\tfrac12(\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{S})
		\right\}
		\subset \mathcal{W}.
	\end{equation}
	See (fig:waterfall_region of the paper) for illustrations of the waterfall
	region and the corresponding exact samples
	from the $q$-Racah measure generated by the
	shuffling algorithm of [borodin-gr2009q].
title: Waterfall region

[Corollary 5 (Convergence to the dynamical $ \Phi^{\kk+1}$ model) of arXiv:2605.28677, 'Weak universality for stochastic reaction-diffusion models\\ with long-range correlated no'] Let the random field $\zeta$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{ass_zeta}, 
and assume that its rescaling $\xi_\ve$ defined in \eqref{rescaled_noise} converges in law in the sense of Schwartz distributions to a random field $\xi$. 
Then 

\begin{itemize}
\item the smooth model $(\Pi^\ve,\Pi^{-,\ve},\Gamma^\ve)$ of Theorem~\ref{prop_main_reg} 
converges in law to a model $(\Pi,\Pi^-,\Gamma)$ with respect to the distance induced by

\begin{equation}
\max_{|\beta|\leq2} \big\{\|\Pi\|_\beta+\|\Pi^-\|_\beta+\|\Gamma\|_\beta\big\} \, ,
\end{equation}

\item $\Pi$ and $\Pi^-$ satisfy almost surely \eqref{pde_Pi} for $[\beta]\geq0$.
\end{itemize}
The convergence in the first item also holds in probability (respectively in $L^p$ for all $p<\infty$), provided the underlying sequence of random fields $\xi_\ve$ converges in probability (respectively in $L^p$ for all $p<\infty$) to a random field $\xi$.

Moreover, if we repeat the construction of $(\Pi^\ve,\Pi^{-,\ve},\Gamma^\ve)$ in Theorem~\ref{prop_main_reg} with multiindices only over $\{\kk\}\cup\NN^{1+d}$ 
(in particular all sums and products over $k\geq\kk$ collapse to $k=\kk$)
to obtain a model $(\Pi^\ve_{\kk},\Pi^{-,\ve}_{\kk},\Gamma^\ve_{\kk})$ for \eqref{eq_limit}, 
then $(\Pi^\ve_{\kk},\Pi^{-,\ve}_{\kk},\Gamma^\ve_{\kk})$ converges to a limiting model $(\Pi_{\kk},\Pi^-_{\kk},\Gamma_{\kk})$ which coincides with 
$(\Pi,\Pi^-,\Gamma|_{\RR[\![z_{\kk},z_\n]\!]})$ in the following sense:
For multiindices $\beta$ with $\sum_{k>\kk}\beta(k) = 0$ it holds 

\begin{equation}
\Pi_\beta=\Pi_{\kk,\beta} \, , \quad
\Pi^-_\beta=\Pi^-_{\kk,\beta} \, , \quad
\textnormal{and}\quad (\Gamma)_\beta^\gamma = (\Gamma_{\kk})_\beta^\gamma 
\quad\textnormal{for all $\gamma$ with $\sum_{k>\kk}\gamma(k)=0$} \, , 
\end{equation}

while for $\beta$ satisfying $\sum_{k>\kk}\beta(k)>0$ it holds

\begin{equation}
\Pi_\beta=0 \, , \quad
\Pi^-_\beta=0 \, , \quad
\textnormal{and}\quad (\Gamma)_\beta^\gamma=0 
\quad\textnormal{for all $\gamma$ with $\sum_{k>\kk}\gamma(k)=0$} \, .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence to the dynamical $ \Phi^{\kk+1}$ model

[Lemma 2q:moment of arXiv:2510.09818, 'On the Fourier dimension of fractional Brownian graphs'] [LL25].
Let $B$ be a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (0,1)$, and recall that the Fourier transform of $\mu_{G}$ is given by~(equation b1 of the paper). Then for any $q\in \mathbb N_+$ and $\xi_1, \xi_2 \in \mathbb R \setminus\{0\}$, we have
\begin{align}
	\mathbb E\left[ |\hat{\mu}_G(\xi_1,\xi_2)|^{2q} \right]
	= \frac{(q!)^2}{|\xi_2|^{2q/H}} \sum_{\varepsilon\in \mathcal{A}_{2q}} \mathcal{I}_{T}^{\lambda}[\varepsilon, G_\varepsilon],
\end{align}
where the parameters $\lambda, T$ and the function $G_{\varepsilon}$ are chosen as
\begin{align}
	\lambda = \frac{\xi_1}{|\xi_2|^{1/H}}, \qquad
	T = |\xi_2|^{1/H} ,\quad \text{ and }\quad
	G_\varepsilon(u) = e^{-\pi\mathrm{Var}(\sum_{i=1}^{2q} \varepsilon_i B_{u_i})}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 2q:moment of arXiv:2510.09818

For 0 < p < 1 the functional ||f||_p = (int |f|^p)^{1/p} is NOT a norm and the triangle inequality is false. Counterexample: on [0,1] with Lebesgue measure take f = 1_{[0,1/2]} and g = 1_{(1/2,1]}. Then ||f+g||_p = ||1_{[0,1]}||_p = 1, while ||f||_p + ||g||_p = 2 * (1/2)^{1/p} = 2^{1 - 1/p} < 1 for every p < 1 (e.g. 2^{-1} = 0.5 at p = 1/2). What survives: (i) the reverse inequality ||f+g||_p >= ||f||_p + ||g||_p for nonnegative f, g when 0 < p < 1; (ii) the quasi-triangle inequality ||f+g||_p <= 2^{1/p - 1}(||f||_p + ||g||_p); (iii) the p-th power is subadditive, int |f+g|^p <= int |f|^p + int |g|^p, so d(f,g) = ||f - g||_p^p is a complete translation-invariant metric and L^p (0 < p < 1) is a complete metric topological vector space - but it is not locally convex on a nonatomic space, and its dual is {0}. Related trap: the generalized Hölder inequality with 1/r = sum 1/p_i remains valid for r < 1, but the TWO-exponent Hölder inequality with a negative conjugate exponent (0 < p < 1, q = p/(p-1) < 0) points the other way under the appropriate positivity and finiteness hypotheses, so the standard direction may not be quoted when p < 1.
Lebesgue measure on [0,1] for the counterexample
0 < p < 1
title: Pitfall: Minkowski's inequality needs p >= 1 (and the quasi-norm constant below it)

[Defn of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] The conformal group \( \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}) \) satisfies the following properties, see [S85]:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \( \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}) \) is isomorphic to \( PSL_2(\mathbb{R}) \). Each element \( \tau \in \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}) \) can be written as:
    \[
    \tau(z) = T_v \circ \rho_{\theta}(z),
    \]
    where \( \rho_\theta(z) = e^{i\theta} z \) and \( T_v(z) = \frac{z - v}{1 - \overline{v} z} \).

    Geometrically, \( \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D}) \) is an \( S^1 \)-bundle over \( \mathbb{H} \), and it naturally acts on \( \partial \mathbb{D} \cong S^1 \) by extending the conformal maps to the boundary.

    \item The universal cover \( \widetilde{\mathrm{Aut}}(\mathbb{D}) \) is isomorphic to \( \widetilde{SL}_2(\mathbb{R}) \). Each element \( \tau \in \widetilde{\mathrm{Aut}}(\mathbb{D}) \) can be decomposed as:
    \[
    \tau = T_v \circ A_\theta,
    \]
    where \( \theta \in \mathbb{R} \), and \( A_\theta \) represents addition by \( \theta \) on \( \mathbb{R} \).

    Geometrically, \( \widetilde{\mathrm{Aut}}(\mathbb{D}) \) is an \( \mathbb{R} \)-bundle over \( \mathbb{H} \), and it naturally acts on \( \mathbb{R} \), the universal cover of \( S^1 \).

    \begin{itemize}
        \item For \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), \( A_\theta(x) = x + \theta \).
        \item For \( v \in \mathbb{D} \), there exists a unique \( |y - x| < \pi \) such that \( e^{iy} = T_v(e^{ix}) \).
    \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
title: Unnumbered defn of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherlan'

[Lem equalfnbootstrap of arXiv:2508.04954, 'Conditional exponential directed last passage percolation under a one-point upper large de'] Let $\Omega$ be an open subset of ${\mathbb R}^2$. 
Let $\{Z_n(x,y)\}_{(x,y)\in \Omega}$, $n\in {\mathbb N}$, and $\{Z(x,y)\}_{(x,y)\in \Omega}$ be random fields.  
Let $g: \Omega^2\to {\mathbb R}$ be continuously differentiable functions such that 
$(x,y)\mapsto (x,g(x,y))$ is invertible with continuously differentiable inverse function for $(x,y)\in \Omega$, and the following two conditions hold:
Suppose that the following two conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item For every $(x_1,y_1), (x_2,y_2) \in \Omega$ satisfying $g(x_1, y_1) \ne g(x_{2},y_{2})$,  as $n\to \infty$, 
\begin{equation} 
		(Z_n(x_1, y_1), Z_n(x_2, y_2))  \xrightarrow{d}  (Z(x_1, y_2), Z(x_2, y_2)) 
\end{equation}
\item For every $x_1, x_2 \in \pi_x(\Omega)$ and $r_1, r_2 \in {\mathbb R}$, 
\begin{equation*}
    		(y_1, y_2) \mapsto \mathbb{P} (Z(x_1,y_1)\le r_1, \, Z(x_2, y_2)\le r_2)
\end{equation*}
is a jointly continuous function of $(y_1, y_2)\in \prod_{i=1}^2 \pi_y(\Omega \cap (\{x_i\} \times {\mathbb R}))$. 
\end{enumerate}
Then, (equation eq:convergenced2 of the paper) holds for all $(x_1,y_1), (x_2, y_2)\in \Omega$.
title: Lem equalfnbootstrap of arXiv:2508.04954

For iid weights equal to a>0 with probability p in (0,1) and b>a otherwise, suppose northeast directed bond percolation on the a-edges has positive forward survival probability theta(p). Then almost surely some global bi-infinite FPP geodesic exists. At the origin, forward and backward surviving-ray events depend on disjoint edge time levels and intersect with probability theta(p)^2. Their concatenation is monotone and every finite segment has Manhattan distance many a-edges, the minimum possible cost. Translation ergodicity upgrades positive probability of existence to probability one. This is a boundary obstruction to dropping nonatomicity, not a counterexample to the nonatomic-law target.

Hasebe, Ueda and Wang, Log-unimodality for free positive multiplicative Brownian motion (arXiv:2009.13848), Problem 4.7 asks: if nu is a probability measure supported on [alpha, beta] with 0 < alpha < beta, must there be a number D >= 0 (depending on nu) such that sigma_t (free multiplicative convolution) nu is log-unimodal for all t >= D? Our result (id P0193, 2026-09-08): NO. For nu = (delta_{1/10} + delta_{10})/2 on [1/10, 10] the convolution is log-unimodal for no t >= 5 pi. Using the authors' own Lemma 4.1(3) criterion with r = e^u and atoms e^{+-a}, a = log 10, the relevant integral equals F_R(u) = (K_R(u-a) + K_R(u+a))/2 with K_R(s) = 1/(2(cosh s - cos R)); choosing the unique R in [pi/2, pi) with R / sin R = t/10 (which exists exactly for t >= 5 pi) gives F_R(0) <= 1/(2 cosh a) = 10/101 < 1/10 while F_R(+-a) >= 1/8 > 1/10 and F_R tends to 0 at +- infinity, so the level set has four roots against the criterion's at most two. Verification as the source words it: both bounds are uniform over the whole admissible range of R (measured max F(0) = 0.099010, min F(a) = 0.129901), so this is a proof and not a numerical observation; and a control both ways - on the three cases where the authors' Theorem 4.4 applies (alpha = 1, beta = 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3) the same root counter returns at most 2 roots at t = 1.01 D and t = 10 D, agreeing with their proved theorem. Prior art not cleared.

sigma_t the free positive multiplicative Brownian motion

body: [Definition eq:PsiRad of arXiv:2509.04155, 'An Approach to Sub-Gaussian Heat Kernel Estimates via Analysis on Metric Spaces'] We say that $\Psi : (0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ is a \emph{radial scale function} if it is an increasing homeomorphism satisfying the following doubling type property for some $\beta_U,\beta_L > 1$. There is $C \geq 1$ such that for all $0 < r \leq R$,\begin{equation}C^{-1}\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{\beta_L} \leq \frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(r)} \leq C\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^{\beta_U}.\end{equation}Given such $\Psi$, we associate it a function $\Phi$ given by\begin{equation}\Phi(s) := \sup_{r > 0} \left(\frac{s}{r} - \frac{1}{\Psi(r)}\right).\end{equation}
title: Definition eq:PsiRad of arXiv:2509.04155

body:
[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2506.10856, 'The space of multifurcating ranked tree shapes: enumeration, lattice structure, and Markov'] The space $\mathcal{T}_{N,K}$ of ranked tree shapes with $N$ leaves and $K$ internal nodes is in bijection with the space $\mathcal{F}_{N,K}$ of $K\times K$ lower triangular matrices with non-negative integer entries that obey the
following constraints:
\begin{enumerate}[label={F\arabic*.}]
    \item The diagonal elements $F_{i,i}$ are strictly increasing: $F_{1,1}< F_{2,2}<...<F_{K,K}$ with $F_{K,K}=N$. The subdiagonal elements satisfy $F_{i+1,i} = F_{i,i}-1$ for all $i=1,...,K-1$.
    \item The elements $F_{i,1}, i=3,...,K$ in the first column satisfy \[ \max\{0, F_{i-1,1}- 1\} \leq F_{i,1} \leq F_{i-1,1}\] This just implies the column elements are decreasing by at most 1 if $F_{i-1,1}$ is non-zero. 
    \item All other elements $F_{i,j}, i=4,...,K, j=2,...,i-2$ satisfy these three conditions. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label={\alph*.}]
        \item $\max\{0, F_{i,j-1} \} \leq F_{i,j}$: Row-wise non-decreasing. 
        \item $F_{i-1, j}-1 \leq F_{i,j} \leq F_{i-1, j}$: Column-wise change is either 1 or 0.
        \item $0\leq (F_{i-1, j} - F_{i,j}) - (F_{i-1, j-1}- F_{i,j-1}) \leq 1$: in any $2\times 2$ grid, sum of off-diagonal elements minus sum of on-diagonal elements is 1 or 0. 
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
The space of such matrices is denoted $\mathcal{F}_{N,K}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 21 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\sR=(R,\alpha_R\colon N\to R)$ be as in \eqref{eq;SN} and write $\sR/p=(R/p,N)$. The restriction on the subcategory $\mathrm{lSm}^{\rm Cart}_{\sR/p}$ of affine fine log-smooth algebras of Cartier type of the log-crystalline cohomology functor
      	\[
      	R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR) \colon \PreLog_{\sR/p} \to \mathcal{D}(R)^\wedge_p
      	\]
      	is the left Kan extension of its restriction to $\mathrm{lPoly}_{\sR/p}$. In particular, derived log crystalline cohomology and underived crystalline cohomology coincide for log smooth algebras of Cartier type.  
         Moreover, the algebra structure of $R\Gamma_{crys}(X/\sR)$ for $X\in \mathrm{lSm}^{\rm Cart}_{\sR/p}$ is left Kan extended from that for polynomial objects. 
     	\begin{proof}This is basically well-known, and follows the same argument of the non-logarithmic counterpart. We give a proof for the convenience of the reader. 
      		Considering the restriction of $R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ to  polynomial pre-log algebras and the resulting left Kan extension, (here, we use the fact that $\mathcal{D}(R)^\wedge_p$ admits colimits)
      		we obtain a natural comparison map from derived log crystalline cohomology $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ to $R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$. Both functors satisfy étale descent: this is clear for the underived version. As for derived log crystalline cohomology, it is enough to note that, since $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ takes value in $p$-complete $\sR$-modules, we can check descent by reduction modulo $p$. Since by construction derived log crystalline cohomology is obtained by Kan extension from polynomials pre-log algebras over $\sR/p$, on any such algebra 
      		$\sP$,  we can choose a polynomial algebra $\widetilde{\sP}$ over $\sR$ as its smooth lift. Then, the derived log crystalline cohomology $R\Gamma_{\text{crys}}(\sP/\sR)$ is exactly computed by the $p$-completion of $\omega_{\widetilde{\sP}/\sR}^{*}$ as \eqref{eq;omegalogcryscomparison}. 
      		Reducing modulo $p$ again, this is precisely $\omega_{\sP/(\sR/p)}^{*}$, thus $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)/p$ is $L\omega^*_{-/(\sR/p)}$, which satisfies étale descent. At this point, the claim of the Lemma follows again from the fact that         for log smooth pre-log algebras $\sA$ of Cartier type over $\sR/p$,
      		the comparison map 
      		$L\omega^*_{\sA/(\sR/p)}\to \omega^*_{\sA/(\sR/p)}$ is an equivalence (see for example \cite[Proposition 4.6]{BLPO-HKR}).
            Finally, the last statement follows from Remark \ref{rmk;multiplicativity}). 
                 	\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 6 (Pathwise uniqueness in the non-sticky class) of arXiv:2605.23529, 'Generalized Bessel-Dunkl diffusions'] Assume that one of the following two uniqueness regimes holds.

    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
        \item The Yamada-Watanabe alternative \textup{(a)} in
        Assumption~\ref{ass:uniq:sigma} holds, together with
        Assumptions~\ref{ass:uniq:b} and \ref{ass:uniq:k}.

        \item The locally Lipschitz alternative \textup{(b)} in
        Assumption~\ref{ass:uniq:sigma} holds, together with
        \ref{ass:uniq:b:euclidean} and Assumption~\ref{ass:uniq:k:dissipative}.
    \end{enumerate}
    Let $(X,B)$ and $(\widetilde X,B)$ be two solutions of
    \eqref{eq:degenerate-existence-indicator}, defined on the same filtered
    probability space, driven by the same Brownian motion, and with the same
    initial condition. Assume moreover that \eqref{eq:zero:leb} holds for both
    $X$ and $\widetilde X$. Then
    \begin{align}
        X(t) &= \widetilde X(t), \qquad 0\le t<\life{X}\wedge\life{\widetilde X}, \qquad \text{a.s.}
        
    \end{align}
    In particular,
    \begin{align*}
        \life{X} &= \life{\widetilde X}, \qquad\text{a.s.}
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pathwise uniqueness in the non-sticky class

[Proposition prop:multiport-closed of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a scalar rooted centered orthogonal-Weingarten ribbon map $\Gamma$ and
remove passive singleton color components by centering.  Before estimating
anything, cut simultaneously every row or trace wire joining distinct
coefficient components, record every resulting port, choose a maximizing
smoothing and all prime tags, and record one base on each original
$p\vee r$ circuit.  This declares $\tau$.  For every pure-Weyl component
$P$ with $m_P\ge2$, discard the forbidden-pair zero terms and apply
(lem:two-carrier-packet of the paper); hence $c^{\!*}(P)\ge2$ and
(thm:packet of the paper) gives a presentation
$\zeta_{P,\tau}$ satisfying
\[
 \|\zeta_{P,\tau}\|_{\mathscr P_\tau}
 \le A^{m_P}n^{c^{\!*}(P)-2}
 \|C_P\|_2^2\|C_P\|_\mathrm{op}^{m_P-2}.
\tag{2.6.14a}
\]
All cut interfaces can be reclosed at once by a normalized scalar
projective contraction $\mathcal G_\Gamma$ with
\[
 \mathcal A_\Gamma
 =\omega_\Gamma\,
 \mathcal G_\Gamma\!\left(
   \widehat\bigotimes_P\zeta_{P,\tau}\right),
 \quad
 \|\mathcal G_\Gamma\|_\pi\le1,
 \quad
 |\omega_\Gamma|
 \le C^m n^{F-4m+\ell_\Gamma-g_{\rm Wg}}.
\tag{2.6.14b}
\]
No component is estimated inside a gap of another component and no
component token is split.

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T280-w716-C2 v2, independent review pending; novelty not asserted. Let input be uniform probability measure on S2 and let the neuron feature be a ReLU(w.x+b). Train all Euclidean parameters including bias. Suppose the initial law is invariant under (a,w,b)->(a,Qw,b) for every Q in O(3), with E[a^2+|w|^2+b^2]<infinity; use derivative zero at ReLU zero. Its population tangent operator has harmonic eigenvalues mu_k. Put r=|w|, s=-b/r only on {r>0, |b|<r}. Then mu_2-mu_3=E[1_{r>0,|b|<r}(1-s^2)^3{r^2(1-s^2)^2+a^2(28s^4+14s^2+6)}/256], with integrand defined as zero elsewhere, including r=0. Hence mu_2>=mu_3, strictly iff the crossing event has positive probability. The coefficient formula uses q_2(s)=(1-s^2)^2/16 and q_3(s)=s q_2(s) and conditional eigenvalue r^2 q_k^2+a^2[(q_k-s q_k_prime)^2+q_k_prime^2+k(k+1)q_k^2]. The q_k_prime^2 term is the trained-bias contribution. Symbolic Legendre integration and polynomial identities plus 1,365 exact rational/boundary cases passed. The harmonic-analysis argument remains unaudited; no Lean certificate is asserted. This excludes initial bias/radius tuning as a route to degree-3-before-degree-2 learning under rotational initialization; it does not exclude a later anisotropic feature-learning reversal or settle T280 Target 2.
Draft: proof (unaudited), not independently checked
All model, measure, metric and moment conditions are stated in the statement

body: Publication record. S. Bubeck, Y. Li and D. Nagaraj conjectured that, for generic data, any two-layer neural network with m neurons that fits n noisy labels must have Lipschitz constant at least of order sqrt(n/m), with no restriction on the size of the weights; Bubeck and Sellke proved a universal version for Lipschitz-parameterized classes under a polynomial bound on the parameters. Y. Shmalo, A law of robustness for two-layer neural networks with arbitrary weights (arXiv:2607.07778, July 2026) proves the conjectured law up to one logarithmic factor for every continuous piecewise-linear activation, ReLU in particular, for data uniform on S^{d-1} (d >= 3) or drawn from N(0, I_d/d), labels in [-1, 1] with noise level sigma^2 > 0, and width-m two-layer networks with arbitrary real weights, biases and an affine skip connection. ResearchGate record 408594034. Not refereed.
title: Bubeck-Li-Nagaraj law of robustness conjecture proved up to one logarithmic factor for two-layer neural networks with arbitrary weights (Shmalo 2026, arXiv:2607.07778)

[Lem lem-1d-reduction of arXiv:2608.30807, 'Isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues'] Let $0\leq \gamma<1$. Then there exists a constant $C(\gamma)>0$ such that, for every positive function $a\in L^1(0,1)$ satisfying
\[
\int_0^1a(t)dt=1,
\]
there exists $f\in H_0^1(0,1)\setminus\{0\}$ such that
\[
\frac{\int_0^1a(t)|f'(t)|^2dt}{\int_0^1a(t)^{\gamma}f(t)^2dt}\leq C(\gamma).
\]

body:
[Cor nmlinfinf of arXiv:2412.00822, '\textsc{Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations \\ beyond hyperbolic spaces}'] Let $(\theta_{1},\phi_{1},r_{1})$ and $(\theta,\phi,r)$ be two corona points.
In the model of $\mathcal{M}$ given by the product of upper-half planes $\mathbb{U}_{2} \times \mathbb{U}_{2}$:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] If $(\theta_{1},\phi_{1})$ is sent at $(\infty,\infty)$,

$$
\emph{\text{NML}}((\infty,\infty, r_{1}),(\theta,\phi, r)) = \left \lbrace (z_{1},z_{2})\in \mathcal{M}\,;\;  |z_{1}-\theta|^{2} \cdot |z_{2}-\phi|^{2}=\frac{r_{1}}{r}\left(1+|\theta|^{2} \right)\left(1+|\phi|^{2} \right)\right \rbrace \; ;
$$
\item[(ii)] If $(\theta_{1},\phi_{1})$ is sent at $(\infty,y)$, for $y\in \mathbb{R}$,
{
$$
\emph{\text{NML}}((\infty,y, r_{1}),(\theta,\phi, r)) = \left \lbrace (z_{1},z_{2})\in \mathcal{M} \,;\;  \frac{|z_{1}-\theta|^{2} \cdot |z_{2}-\phi|^{2}}{|z_{2}-y|^{2}}=\frac{r_{1}}{r}\frac{\left(1+|\theta|^{2} \right)\left(1+|\phi|^{2} \right)}{1+|y|^{2}}\right \rbrace \;.
$$
}

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsc{Geometry of the no man's land in the product of upper-half planes}

body:
[Cor Cor_Lips of arXiv:2411.09640, 'Random Lipschitz functions on graphs with weak expansion'] There is a constant $c>0$ for which the following holds. Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $d=d(n)$. Fix $v_0 \in V(G)$ and let $f$ be chosen uniformly at random from $\mbox{\rm{Lip}}_{v_0}(G;\infty)$. Then,
    \[\mathbb{P}\left[R(f)< \frac{c\log\log n}{\log d}\right]=o_n(1).\]
title: Cor Cor_Lips of arXiv:2411.09640

[Lemma lem:gegenbauer-term-spectral-bound of arXiv:2602.14998, 'Random geometric graphs with smooth kernels: sharp detection threshold and a spectral conj'] In the setting of Proposition~(prop:polynomial-kernel-perturbation of the paper), there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for any $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $k \ge 1$, we have
$$
\|C^\lambda_k(X)\| \le n + C \Big( \sqrt{n d^k \log (d^k/\delta)} + d^k \log(d^k/\delta) \Big) .
$$

body:
[Lemma lem:moment-sharpness of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, connected graph.  Assume:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(A\arabic*)}]
			\item \textup{(Upper heat kernel)}\; $\sup_{x\in V}\mathbb{P}_x(X_n=x)/\deg(x)\leq A\,n^{-\alpha}$ for all $n\geq 1$, for some $\alpha>0$ and $A<\infty$.
			\item \textup{(Local time lower bound)}\; There exist $d_w\geq 2$ and $a>0$ such that
			\[
			\mathbb{E}_o[L_n(v)]/\deg(v)\geq a\,n^{1-\alpha}\,.
			\]
			for every $v\in B(o,n^{1/d_w})$ and all sufficiently large~$n$.
			\item \textup{(Volume lower bound)}\; $|B(o,r)|\geq c_{\mathrm{vol}}\,r^{d_f}$ for all $r\geq 1$, for some $d_f>0$ and $c_{\mathrm{vol}}>0$.
		\end{enumerate}
		Let $(\sigma(v))_{v\in V}$ be i.i.d.\ with $\mathbb{E}[\sigma(v)]\in(-\infty,\infty]$.
		If $\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\sigma(v)^+)^{(d_f+d_w)/(d_w\alpha)}\bigr]=\infty$, then $\mathbb{E}[u_\infty(o;\sigma)]=\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:moment-sharpness of arXiv:2604.13968

        \E T\left(\bs\right) = \exp\left(-\frac{\beta^2}{4N^2\theta_N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}W\left(\frac{i}{N},\frac{i}{N}\right)
        -\frac{\beta^2}{2N^2}\sum_{i> j}W^2\left(\frac{i}{N},\frac{j}{N}\right)-\frac{\beta^4}{12 N^4\theta_N^3}\sum_{i> j} W\left(\frac{i}{N},\frac{j}{N}\right)\right.\\

    \end{multline*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

 \begin{eqnarray}
  \inf_{n\geq n_0} \bigg|1-\int_0^\infty e^{\mathtt{i}zt -\frac{\beta}{n}  t} \cdot \gamma_n \overline\varPi_n(t)\, dt\bigg| \geq C  \cdot \big( |z|\wedge 1 \big).
 \end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition Prop.LowerBound of arXiv:2411.15485

\[ 
f(t) = \int_{S^{d-1}} \Psi\big(v + t^{1/2}x\big) \dd x, \qquad t > 0.

\end{align}
