body:
[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] For every $t\in(0,t_0)$, the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[(i)] If $G\subset\Omega(\Gamma_1)$ has finite perimeter and finite
 measure and contains a one-sided neighborhood of $\Gamma_1$ in
 $\Omega(\Gamma_1)$, then adjoining $K_0$ does not increase $\mathscr F_t$:
 \begin{equation}
  \mathscr F_t(G\cup K_0)\leq\mathscr F_t(G).
  
 \end{equation}
 Equality holds if and only if $K_0\subset G$ almost everywhere.

 \item[(ii)] If $F$ is an inner end region, then truncation at
 either fixed leaf does not increase $\mathfrak J_t$:
 \begin{equation}
  \mathfrak J_t\bigl(F\cap\Omega(\Gamma_i)\bigr)
  \leq\mathfrak J_t(F),\qquad i=0,1.
  
 \end{equation}
 For each $i$, equality holds if and only if
 $F\setminus\Omega(\Gamma_i)$ has measure zero.

 \item[(iii)] Every $\mathscr F_t$-minimizer $G$ among finite-perimeter sets
 $G'$ satisfying
 \[
  K_0\subset G'\subset\Omega(\Gamma_1),
  \qquad |G'|<\infty,
 \]
 contains a slab extending across $\Gamma_0$: there is a minimal leaf
 $\Gamma_-\prec\Gamma_0$ in the extension across $\Gamma_0$ such that
 \[
  \Omega(\Gamma_1)\setminus\Omega(\Gamma_-)\subset G
  \quad\text{almost everywhere}.
 \]
\end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.26565

[Definition of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] For convex $\mathcal{P}\subset \mathcal{P}(G)$ and $\mu\in \mathcal{P}$, the set $\Sym_{\mathcal{P}}(\mu)$ of symmetrizers for $\mu$ is defined by 
$$
\Sym_{\mathcal{P}}(\mu)=\{\nu\in\mathcal{P}:\mu*\nu(B)=\mu*\nu(-B) \forall B\in \mathcal{B}(G)\} .
$$
The {\em $\Phi$-asymmetry} of $\mu$ with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ is defined by
$$
A_{\Phi, \mathcal{P}}(\mu) := \inf_{\{\nu\in \Sym_{\mathcal{P}}(\mu)\}} \Phi(\nu) . 
$$

[Proposition 8 (The small-parameter boundary) of arXiv:2607.17630, 'Higher-Order Hankel Obstructions to Free Infinite Divisibility\ for Beta Distributions'] Fix $p>0$ and let $Y_{p,q}=1-X_{p,q}\sim\beta_{q,p}$.  For every fixed
$N\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac1qH_N(Y_{p,q})\longrightarrow
 \bigl[B(i+j+2,p)\bigr]_{i,j=0}^{N}\qquad(q\downarrow0).
\end{equation}
The limiting matrix is strictly positive definite.  In particular, for
fixed $p$ and $N$, $H_N(\beta_{p,q})$ is positive definite for all
sufficiently small $q>0$.

body:
[Theorem 14 (Aligned anisotropic Gaussian allocation) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Let $X_0\sim\calN(0,\Sigma)$, where
\[
\Sigma=V\diag(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d)V^\top,
\qquad \lambda_i>0.
\]
Let $A\in\R^{d_y\times d}$ have full row rank and suppose the measurement
is aligned with the prior eigenbasis,
\[
A=U\begin{bmatrix}\diag(s_1,\ldots,s_{d_y})&0\end{bmatrix}V^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma=\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y},
\]
with $s_i=0$ for $i>d_y$.  Define
\begin{equation}

B_{i,t}=a_t^2\lambda_i+\Delta_t,
\qquad
v_{i,t}=\frac{\lambda_i\Delta_t}{B_{i,t}},
\qquad
\tau_i^2=\left(\lambda_i^{-1}+s_i^2/\sigma_y^2\right)^{-1},
\qquad
\widetilde B_{i,t}=a_t^2\tau_i^2+\Delta_t,
\end{equation}
where $\tau_i^2=\lambda_i$ when $s_i=0$.  Under the joint law of $(X_t,R)$,
\begin{equation}

\E|s_{t,i}^{\rm prior}(X_t)|^2=\frac1{B_{i,t}},
\qquad
\E|g_{t,i}(X_t,R)|^2
=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}
{B_{i,t}^2(s_i^2v_{i,t}+\sigma_y^2)},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

\rho_i(t)
=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}
{B_{i,t}(s_i^2v_{i,t}+\sigma_y^2)}
=
\frac{B_{i,t}}{\widetilde B_{i,t}}-1.
\end{equation}
Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}
\item As $a_t\to0$,
\[
\rho_i(t)=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}{s_i^2\lambda_i+\sigma_y^2}+O(a_t^4).
\]
\item For $s_i>0$, $\rho_i(t)$ is strictly increasing along the reverse
trajectory, with low-noise limit $s_i^2\lambda_i/\sigma_y^2$, and
\begin{equation}

\rho_i(t)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\widetilde B_{i,t}=\frac12B_{i,t}.
\end{equation}
Thus, within this aligned linear-Gaussian model, $\rho_i=1$ is a
variance-halving, equal-Fisher-energy reference level.  It is crossed at a
unique interior noise level iff $s_i^2\lambda_i>\sigma_y^2$; when
$s_i^2\lambda_i=\sigma_y^2$, it is attained only at the clean endpoint.
\item Since the exact force is null on unmeasured aligned coordinates,
\begin{equation}

\rho_t^{\rm global}=\omega_t\rho_t^{\rm row},
\qquad
\omega_t=
\frac{\sum_{i:s_i>0}B_{i,t}^{-1}}{\sum_{i=1}^dB_{i,t}^{-1}}.
\end{equation}
For an isotropic prior, $\omega_t=d_y/d$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Aligned anisotropic Gaussian allocation

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Correlation of leaf heights at mesoscopic separation in the critical beta-splitting tree (October 2026). In the critical beta-splitting random tree on n leaves, closed into a cycle, take a uniformly random leaf and the leaf r places further round the cycle. Aldous and Janson (The critical beta-splitting random tree II: overview and open problems, arXiv:2303.02529, Section 3.9, Open Problem 1) asked for a proof that the correlation of the two leaf heights tends to 1 - alpha when log r_n / log n tends to alpha in [0, 1]. The paper proves that, uniformly in 1 <= r <= n/2, the covariance of the two heights is sigma^2 log(n/r) + O(sqrt(log n)) and the variance of one height is sigma^2 log n + O(sqrt(log n)), with sigma^2 = 2 zeta(3)/zeta(2)^3, so the correlation equals 1 - log r / log n + O((log n)^(-1/2)). The proof uses a potential of each leaf's position in its clade that decreases at rate zeta(2) up to square-integrable errors, and compares the two martingales it produces up to the cut that separates the two leaves. Exact rational checks, a Monte Carlo simulation and a Lean 4 file accompany the paper. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/beta-splitting-leaf-correlation (commit e337fd88d00f). Not refereed.
title: Correlation of leaf heights at mesoscopic separation in the critical beta-splitting tree tends to 1 - alpha, answering Aldous-Janson Open Problem 1 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/beta-splitting-leaf-correlation)

[Lem l1-contraction of arXiv:2604.20629, 'Rates of forgetting for the sequentially Markov coalescent'] Let $q(t\mid x)$ be a probability distribution
in $t$ and assume that it is stochastically monotone, i.e.
\[
F_{x}(y):=\int^{y}_{0}q(t|x) dt
\]
is non-increasing in $x$ for fixed $y>0$. Further define the mean
map 
\[
m(x):=\int^{\infty}_{0}t q(t|x) dt.
\]
If there exists $0<r<1$ such that 
\begin{equation}
|m(a)-m(b)|\le r |a-b|,\qquad a,b>0,
\end{equation}
then the quantile coupling 
\[
X_{n+1}=F^{-1}_{X_{n}}(U_{n}),\qquad Y_{n+1}=F^{-1}_{Y_{n}}(U_{n}),\qquad U_{n}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1),
\]
satisfies ((eq:contractive-coupling of the paper)).

[Definition of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Let $X_n$ be a discrete Markov chain on $\mathbb{N}$, with transition probabilities
    \[
    \mathbb{P}_{ij} := \mathbb{P}\left(X_{n+1} = j | X_n = i\right).
    \]
    We say that $X_n$ is a birth-death chain if its transition probabilities $\mathbb{P}_{ij}$ is tridiagonal; that is, 
    \[
    P_{ij} = 0, \text{if} \quad |i-j|>1.
    \]
    In this case, the nonzero entries are given by $P_{i,i} = r_i, P_{i,i+1} = p_i, P_{i,i-1} = q_i$. We also define the m step transition probabilities,
    \[
    \mathbb{P}^{m}_{ij} := \mathbb{P}\left(X_{n+m} = j | X_n = i\right).
    \]
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'

[Proposition 26 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] Suppose that $0 < \eps \le \delta$ and that $\psi_H(\delta+\varepsilon) \ge -\log(\varepsilon p^{e_H})$ and $\psi_H(\delta+\varepsilon) \gg 1$.
  There exists a $D=D(\delta,\varepsilon)$ such that, letting $t \coloneqq (\delta-\varepsilon)\Ex[X]$ and $m \coloneqq \lceil D \psi_H(\delta+\varepsilon) \rceil$, we have
  \[
    \Pr\bigl(G_{n,p} \in \langle\cS_{t,m}\rangle \mid X\geq (1+\delta)\Ex[X]\bigr) =1-o(1).
  \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2506.12145, 'Functional central limit theorem for dependent models with finite memory'] We have the distributional convergence in $D([0,\infty[)$ the Skorokhod space of right-continuous functions with left-hand limits, as $n \to \infty$,
\begin{equation}

\left( \sqrt{n}\Big(\frac{S_{\lfloor nt \rfloor}}{\lfloor nt \rfloor}-p\Big), t \geq 0\right) \overset{d}{\longrightarrow} \big( W_t, t \geq 0 \big),
\end{equation}
where $\big( W_t, t \geq 0 \big)$ is a real-valued centered Gaussian process starting at the origin with covariance given by $\dE[W_s W_t]= \frac{1}{t}\sigma^2_{p,\theta,k}$, for all $0<s \leq t$.
In particular, as $n \to \infty$,
\[\sqrt{n}\Big(\frac{S_n}{n}-p\Big) \overset{d}{\longrightarrow} N\left(0,\sigma^2_{p,\theta,k}\right).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 1 of arXiv:2506.12145

[Theorem 48 of arXiv:2604.01685, 'Probability with Measure\footnote{Lecture notes. University of Ljubljana.}'] Let $(\Omega,\FF,\mu)$ be a measure space. The integral enjoys the following properties.
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item Additivity: $\mu[ f+g ]=\mu[f]+\mu[g]$ whenever $\{f,g\}\subset \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ and $\mu[f^-]\lor \mu[g^-]<\infty$.
			\item Integral of indicator: $\int \mathbbm{1}_A\dd \mu=\mu(A)$ for all $A\in \FF$ (in particular $\int 0\dd \mu=0$, hence $\int f\dd\mu=\int f^+\dd\mu-\int f^-\dd\mu$ for all $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$). 
			\item Integrals vanishing, integrals finite: For $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[0,\infty]}$, $\int f\dd \mu=0$ iff $f=0$ a.e.-$\mu$, while $\int f\dd \mu<\infty$ implies that $f<\infty$ a.e.-$\mu$.  
			\item Triangle inequality: $\vert \int f\dd\mu\vert\leq \int \vert f\vert \dd\mu$ for all $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$.
			\item Measure zero sets are ``invisible'': $\int f\dd\mu=\int g\dd \mu$ whenever $\{f,g\}\subset \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ and $f=g$ a.e.-$\mu$. 
					\item  Monotonicity: $\int g\dd\mu\leq\int f\dd \mu$ whenever  $\{g,f\}\subset \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$, $g\leq f$ and $\int g^-\dd\mu <\infty$.
			\item Homogeneity: $\int cf\dd\mu=c\int f\dd\mu$ for all $f\in \FF/\mathcal{B}_{[-\infty,\infty]}$ for which $\int (cf)^-\dd \mu\land \int (cf)^+\dd\mu<\infty$,  for all $c\in [-\infty,\infty]$.	
		\end{enumerate}
		Furthermore, the integrals appearing in  \eqref{lebesgue:additivity}-\eqref{properties:indicator}-\eqref{properties:v} \& \eqref{properties:iii} are all well-defined. The same is true for \eqref{properties:ii} except  when $c=0$  and $\mu[f^+]= \mu[f^-]=\infty$. Finally, in \eqref{properties:vi}, $\int f\dd\mu$ is well-defined iff $\int g\dd\mu$ is well-defined. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 48 of arXiv:2604.01685

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2506.20146, 'Parabolic Anderson Model in the Hyperbolic Space. Part I: Annealed Asymptotics'] For any $p\geqslant1$, the following second order
asymptotics holds true for the solution $u(t,x)$ to the PAM (\ref{eq:GlobalPAM}):
\begin{equation}
\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{\beta(pt)}\log\big(e^{-H(pt)}\langle u(t,o)^{p}\rangle\big)=-\sqrt{-\frac{Q''(0)}{2}}d,
\end{equation}
where $H(t)$, $\beta(t)$ are defined by (\ref{eq:CGF}), (\ref{eq:BetaScale})
respectively and $\langle\cdot\rangle$ means taking expectation with
respect to the $\xi$-randomness. In other words, the $p$-th moment
of $u(t,o)$ satisfies the asymptotics
\begin{equation}
\langle u(t,o)^{p}\rangle=\exp\Big(\frac{1}{2}\sigma^{2}p^{2}t^{2}-d\sqrt{-\frac{Q''(0)}{2}}p^{3/2}t^{3/2}(1+o(1))\Big)\ \ \ \text{as }t\rightarrow\infty.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 4 of arXiv:2506.20146

Unreviewed draft reduction. Let T be a stopping time for a discrete process and B a deterministic finite set of M>=1 states. At every kth visit to any x in B before T, assume conditional probability at least h, 0<h<1, of no further visit to x before T, using that visit's sigma-field. Then for integer t>=M, P(T>t and all pre-exit states lie in B)<=M(1-h)^(floor(t/M)-1). Iterate conditional next-visit bounds and use a union bound over B. This controls time only after the visit hazard and confinement are proved.

[Lem 93 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recalling Definitions \ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}--\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, we have
\begin{align*}
\sM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0) 
&\subseteq \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,,\\
\sM^{\sideal,\sym}(\alpha,0) &\subseteq \sM^{\sx,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.\end{align*}

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification.sym} for the first assertion: 
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
\MSRheader\\
\hline
\GREATdefn{sy}\\
\SPRdefn{sy}
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The $\svi$ and $\svii$ classes
 differ only in the constraint on $p$: the $\svi$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6} (i.e. $p(\epsilon) \ge 1-\epsilon$, among other conditions) while the $\svii$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.7} (i.e. $p\equiv 1$). Consider any
	\[\mu = \mu^\sym(q_*=0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta=\zeta_0)
	 \in \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\,,\]
corresponding to controls
	\[(q_*=0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta=\delta_0,\zeta^\Ising=\delta_0) \in \Adm^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\,.\]
In particular, $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6}.
Recall the notation of Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}: 
we have $(b,\sigma) \in \Adm(0;p,f)$
for budget function $f(t) = (\bbE w_t)^2 / \alpha$, so
    \[
        \acute\mu = \mu(q_*=0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta=\zeta_0) \in \cM(0;p,f)\,.
    \]
Note that $\mu = \sym(\acute\mu)$.
Now consider the functions $\tilde p, \hat p \in \incr([0,1];[0,1])$ given by $\tilde p \equiv 1$ and
    \[
        \hat p(t) = \begin{cases}
            p(\epsilon) & t\in [0,\epsilon) \,, \\
            p(t) & t \in [\epsilon,1]\,.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    Since the restrictions of $p$ and $\hat p$ to $[\epsilon,1]$ agree, Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p.near.0} implies
    \beq
        d_\cH\Big(\cM(0;p,f),\cM(0;\hat p,f)\Big) 
        \le \Big(9(1+1/\alpha) \epsilon\Big)^{1/2}\,,
    \eeq
    for $\cM(0;p,f)$ specified in Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}.
    Since $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6}, we have $p(\epsilon) \ge 1-\epsilon$, and so
    \[
        \|\hat p' - \tilde p'\|_1
        =\|\hat p' \|_1 
        = \hat p(1) - \hat p(\epsilon)
        = p(1) - p(\epsilon)
        \le \epsilon\,.
    \]
    Then Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p} implies
    \beq
        d_\cH\Big(\cM(0;\hat p,f),\cM(0;\tilde p,f)\Big) 
        \le \Big(6(1+1/\alpha) \epsilon\Big)^{1/2}\,.
    \eeq
    For some $\tilde\epsilon = \tilde\epsilon(\epsilon)$ tending to $0$ as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$, \eqref{e:grt.in.spr.hausdorff1} and \eqref{e:grt.in.spr.hausdorff2} imply the existence of $\tilde \mu \in \cM(0;\tilde p,f)$ such that
    (since $\sym$ is a contraction)
    \beq
        \bbW_2\Big(
        \mu=\sym(\acute{\mu}), 
        \sym(\tilde \mu)
        \Big) 
        \le \bbW_2(\acute \mu,\tilde \mu)
        \le \tilde\epsilon\,.
    \eeq
    Let $\tilde\mu$ be attained by controls $(\tilde b,\tilde \sigma) \in \Adm(0;\tilde p,f)$, i.e.,
    \[
        \tilde\mu = \mu(q_*=0,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde p,\zeta=\zeta_0)\,.
    \]
Since $\tilde{p}\equiv1$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.7}, we have 
    \[
        (q_*=0,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,w,\tilde p,\zeta=\delta_0,\zeta^\Ising=\delta_0) 
        \in \Adm^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon)\,,
    \]
    and therefore $\sym(\tilde\mu) \in \cM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon)$. 
    Since for all $\mu \in \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ we can find such $\sym(\tilde\mu)$ satisfying \eqref{e:great.in.spr.sym.W2}, we conclude
    \[
        \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) 
        \subseteq 
        \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big( \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon) \Big)\,.
    \]
Adjusting $\tilde\epsilon$ gives
    \[
        \cB_\epsilon\Big( \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) \Big)
        \subseteq 
        \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big( \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\tilde\epsilon) \Big)\,.
    \]
Recalling Definition~\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, 
taking a union over $L$ and an intersection over $\epsilon$ proves the first assertion.

[Theorem 8 (Non-stationary case) of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] Let \( \bm{X} \) be a continuous centered Gaussian process satisfying
  assumptions~\ref{D1}--\,\ref{D3}, let \( \Gamma \) satisfy
  assumptions~\ref{B1}--\ref{B2}, and let \( L \in \mathcal{L} \).
  \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item If \( \alpha < \beta \) and Assumptions~\ref{B3}--\ref{B4} hold on
    every interval \([0,S]\), \(S\ge0\), for the limiting model
    \[
      \bm Z=\bm Y_{\alpha,V_{I,I}},
      \qquad
      \bm q(t)=S_{\alpha,V_{I,I}}(t)\bm w_I,
    \]
    and this limiting model is non-trivial,
    then with \( L_u = L \cdot u^{-2 \lambda_\Gamma / \alpha} \) holds
    \begin{equation*}
      \pk{
        \Gamma_{[0, T]} ( \uu ( \bm{X} - u \bm{b} ) ) > L_u
      }
      \sim
      \mathcal{H}_{\Gamma, L, \alpha, V_{I, I}, \Sigma, \bm{b}} \, 
      \Gamma ( 1 / \beta + 1 ) \,
      \tau_{\bm{w}}^{-1 / \beta} \,
      u^{2 / \alpha - 2 / \beta - |I|} \, 
      \varphi_{\Sigma} ( u \bb ),
\end{equation*}
    where \( \tau_{\bm{w}} = \bm{w}^\top A \bm{w} \).
    \item If \( \alpha = \beta \), \(\bm d(t)=t^\beta A\bm w\), and
    Assumptions~\ref{B3}--\ref{B4} hold on every interval \([0,S]\), \(S\ge0\),
    for the limiting model
    \[
      \bm Z=\bm Y_{\alpha,V_{I,I}},
      \qquad
      \bm q(t)=S_{\alpha,V_{I,I}}(t)\bm w_I+\bm d_I(t),
    \]
    and this limiting model is non-trivial,
    then with \( L_u = L \cdot u^{-2 \lambda_\Gamma / \beta} \) we have
    \begin{equation*}
      \pk{
        \Gamma_{[0, T]} ( \uu ( \bm{X} - u \bm{b} ) ) > L_u
      }
      \sim
      \mathcal{P}_{\Gamma, L, \alpha, V_{I, I}, \bm{d}_I, \Sigma, \bm{b}} \, 
      u^{-|I|} \,
      \varphi_{\Sigma} ( u \bb ).
\end{equation*}
    \item If \( \alpha > \beta \), \(\bm d(t)=t^\beta A\bm w\), and
    Assumptions~\ref{B3}--\ref{B4} hold on every interval \([0,S]\), \(S\ge0\),
    for the deterministic limiting model
    \[
      \bm Z\equiv\bm0,
      \qquad
      \bm q(t)=\bm d_I(t),
    \]
    and this limiting model is non-trivial,
    then with \( L_u = L \cdot u^{-2 \lambda_\Gamma / \beta} \) we have
    \begin{equation*}
      \pk{
        \Gamma_{[0, T]} ( \uu ( \bm{X} - u \bm{b} ) ) > L_u
      }
      \sim
      \mathcal{C}_{\Gamma, L, \bm d, \Sigma, \bm{b}} \,
      u^{-|I|} \,
      \varphi_{\Sigma} ( u \bb ),
\end{equation*}
    where
    \begin{equation}
      
      \mathcal{C}_{\Gamma, L, \bm d, \Sigma, \bm{b}}
      = 
      \lim_{S \to \infty} 
      \int_{\R^d}
      \exp \left( 
        \bm{x}_I^\top \bm{w}_I
        - \frac{1}{2} \, \bm{x}_J^\top ( \Sigma^{-1} )_{J J} \, \bm{x}_J
      \right) 
      \Ind{
        \Gamma_{[0, S]} \left( 
          -\bm{d}_I - \bm{x}_I,
          -\bm{x}_{\Jtan},
          ( \bb - \bm{b} )_{\Jsl}
        \right) 
        > L
      }
      \, d \bm{x}.
    \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}
  The displayed constants are finite and, by the non-triviality assumptions in
  the corresponding cases, positive. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Non-stationary case

z^\top\big(S + K_{\min} M_\omega\big) z \ge

\qquad \forall z\in\mathbb{R}^N,

and the largest such constant is
\[
\alpha_{\omega,N} = \lambda_{\min}(S + K_{\min}M_\omega).
\]

[Lemma lem:arithmetic of arXiv:2609.02041, 'Sparse $k$-AP Covering Sets and the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture'] There exists a constant $c>0$ 
such that for all sufficiently large $k$,
there exists a positive integer $Q$, $N$ and a subset 
$B\subseteq \{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$ such that 
$$|B| < N^{1-\frac{c}{\log\log k}}$$
and for every $x\in\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}$,
there exists a nonnegative integer $d$ such that 
$x-d$, $x-2d$, \dots, $x-(k-1)d$ are all in $B$.

[Lemma 212 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider a discrete ensemble as described in Section~\ref{Section_general_model}, satisfying Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic} and \ref{Assumptions_analyticity}. This means in particular that the derivative of the potential in the $h$-th segment is
\[
V_h'(x) = U_h'(x) + \iota_h^- \log|x - \hat{a}_h'| + \iota_h^+ \log |x - \hat{b}_h'|,
\]
where $U_h$ has a holomorphic extension in a complex neighborhood of $[\hat{a}_h',\hat{b}_h']$. Then, the Stieltjes transform of the equilibrium measure provided by Theorem~\ref{Theorem_equi_charact} satisfies for any $h \in [H]$ and $x$ in a band of the $h$-th segment
\[
\theta_{h,h}\big(\mathcal{G}_{\mu_h}(x^+) + \mathcal{G}_{\mu_h}(x^-)\big) + \sum_{g \neq h} 2\theta_{h,g} \mathcal{G}_{\mu_g}(x) = V'_h(x).
\]

body:
[Proposition 5 (Plane septic model) of arXiv:2609.03455, '2609.03455'] The Klein--V\'elu curve \eqref{eq:KV-uv} is birational over
$\Q(\psi,\u)$ to the plane septic
\begin{multline}
C_7:\ 
\psi^3\bigl(\u(\u-1)^2x_0^7+x_1^7+
 \u(\u-1)^2x_2^7\bigr)
-\u^2(\u^2-3\u-3)(\u-1)^2
 x_0^3x_1x_2^3 \\
+\psi(\u-1)(3\u^3-4\u^2-3\u-1)
 x_0^2x_1^3x_2^2
-\psi^2(3\u^2-2\u-2)x_0x_1^5x_2=0.
\end{multline}
It has fourteen ordinary double points, and its normalization is of genus $1$.
The points corresponding to $O,S,T$ are
\[
 O=(0:\psi^3:-\psi\u),\quad
 S=(\psi^3:-\psi\u:-\u^2),\quad
 T=(0:\psi^3:-\psi\u\zeta_7).
\]

[Lemma lem:factorial-box-divisibility of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $d,t\geq0$ be integers, let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t$ be positive
integers, put $R=\ell_1\cdots\ell_t$, and, for an indeterminate $x$, set
\[
 \Psi_{\boldsymbol\ell,d}(x)
 =\sum_{0\leq j_i<\ell_i}
   \binom{x-j_1-\cdots-j_t+d}{d}.
\]
Here $\binom{X}{d}=X(X-1)\cdots(X-d+1)/d!$ is the generalized binomial
polynomial (with $\binom{X}{0}=1$).
There is a universal polynomial
\[
 F_{d,t}(X,L_1,\ldots,L_t)
 \in\mathbb Z[X,L_1,\ldots,L_t]
\]
of degree $d$ in $X$ such that, after the specialization
$X=x$ and $L_i=\ell_i$,
\begin{equation}
 (d+t)!\,\Psi_{\boldsymbol\ell,d}(x)
 =R F_{d,t}(x,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t).
\end{equation}
Its leading coefficient in $X$ is $(d+t)!/d!$.

[Lemma lem:zan of arXiv:2608.11198, '(Non-)coincidence of critical parameters for Poisson Zoos and Loop Soup Percolation\\ on \'] Assume $C_*(\mu)<\infty$. Let $(V_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a
increasing finite connected
exhaustion of $V(G)$ with $\0\in V_1$, and let
\[
\widehat\chi_n^\mu(\alpha)
:=
\max_{x\in V_n}\sum_{y\in V_n}\mathbb{P}^{(n)}(x\leftrightarrow y \text{ at level }\alpha),
\]
where $\mathbb{P}^{(n)}$ is the probability measure underlying the finite-volume zoo
using only animals $A\in\mathfrak A$ with $V(A)\subseteq V_n$, and
$\{x\leftrightarrow y \text{ at level }\alpha\}$ denotes the event of $x$ and $y$ being contained in the same connected component of the graph induced by the
corresponding occupied edge set at level $\alpha$. Then for every $n$ and Lebesgue-a.e.\
$\alpha\ge0$,
\begin{equation} 
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm d\alpha}\widehat\chi_n^\mu(\alpha)
\le
C_*(\mu)\,\widehat\chi_n^\mu(\alpha)^2.
\end{equation}

body:
Owner campaign draft, literature-based proof (unaudited), no novelty claim. Let P be the uniform Euclidean probability on [0,1]^2 and P_n the empirical measure of n iid P draws. Ambrosio, Stra and Trevisan, arXiv:1611.04960v1 Theorem 1.1 PDF p.3, prove lim_(n->infinity) (n/log n) E W2^2(P_n,P)=1/(4 pi); this is empirical-to-uniform, whereas their bipartite constant is 1/(2 pi). For Q_n=P_n*N(0,h_n^2 I_2), the explicit Gaussian coupling yields |sqrt(E W2^2(Q_n,P))-sqrt(E W2^2(P_n,P))|<=sqrt(2)h_n. Thus if h_n^2=o(log n/n), the smoothed expected squared-W2 cost has the same 1/(4 pi) limit after multiplication by n/log n. Taking h_n=1/n and fresh fraction r=1 contradicts a bound C(n^(-1)+h_n^2) with C independent of n,h. Hence the unqualified all-bandwidth T356 Target 1 fails in ambient dimension two even for a connected full-dimensional constant density on its compact domain. A logarithmic sampling term, a bandwidth regime that absorbs it, or a restricted law class is necessary. This does not refute the Lipschitz-curve law theorem: a Lipschitz image of an interval cannot carry uniform square probability. The local Gaussian transfer is the draft being checked, not a new claim to the established matching theorem. Evidence: w703 T356 C008 v1, with primary PDF and hash in SOURCES.jsonl.
P uniform on Euclidean [0,1]^2
P_n iid empirical law
Gaussian covariance h_n^2 I_2
h_n^2=o(log n/n)
r=1, C independent of n,h for the target contradiction

[Proposition prop:singular-p-Lap of arXiv:2608.21805, 'Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equati'] For $2 < p < 4$, consider the regularised $p$-Laplacian $\mathcal{A}_\eta(u) = -\mathrm{div}\bigl((\lvert \nabla u \rvert^2 + \eta)^{(p-2)/2}\nabla u\bigr)$ for $\eta > 0$, and let $X^\eta$ denote the unique variational solution of the regularised SPDE under the standing hypotheses applied to $(\mathcal{A}_\eta, \mathcal{B})$, with covering field $v_h^\eta(r) := (\Phi_r^\eta)^{*}(\gamma_t^\eta)^{\dagger}h$ (where $\Phi_r^\eta := D_r X^\eta(t)$). The regularisation removes the coefficient singularity and supplies the required Fr\'echet differentiability of the drift, each $\mathcal{A}_\eta$ at $\eta > 0$ satisfying Assumptions~(ass:LR of the paper), (ass:diff1 of the paper), and (ass:diff2 of the paper) with $\mathcal{A}''_{\eta, uu}$ uniformly bounded on bounded subsets of $V$. Assume, for each fixed $\eta > 0$, that the regularised equation satisfies the remaining structural and non-degeneracy hypotheses of Theorem~(thm:main of the paper), Part~II, for the chosen deterministic direction $h$, so that the theorem yields a regularised logarithmic derivative $\beta_h^\eta \in L^2(\mu_t^\eta)$. Assume moreover that
\begin{equation}
  X^\eta(t) \;\longrightarrow\; X(t) \qquad \text{in probability in } H \quad \text{as } \eta \downarrow 0 .
\end{equation}
Suppose, in addition to the standing hypotheses, the following \emph{uniform-in-$\eta$ stability conditions} hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(S\arabic*)}, leftmargin=3em]
  \item \textup{(Convergence of the HS-Malliavin fibres.)} As $\eta \downarrow 0$,
  \[
    \lVert \Phi^\eta - \Phi \rVert_{\mathbb{D}^{1, p^*}(L^2([0,t]; L_2(U,H)))} \;\longrightarrow\; 0,
  \]
  and
  \[
    \sup_{\eta > 0}\;\lVert \Phi^\eta \rVert_{\mathbb{D}^{1, p^*}(L^2([0,t]; L_2(U,H)))} \;<\; \infty.
  \]
  \item \textup{(Pseudoinverse $L^q$-convergence.)} $(\gamma_t^\eta)^{\dagger}h \to \gamma_t^{\dagger}h$ in $L^q(\Omega; H)$, with
  \[
    \sup_\eta\mathbb{E}[\norm{(\gamma_t^\eta)^{\dagger}h}_H^q] < \infty.
  \]
  \item \textup{(Uniform Cameron--Martin compatibility dominator.)} The Tikhonov-regularised trace integrands $\mathcal{I}^{(\varepsilon), \eta}_r$ for the regularised pair $(\Phi^\eta, \gamma_t^\eta)$ admit a single dominator $\Psi_r$ as in~(equation eq:CM-compat-axiom of the paper)--(equation eq:CM-compat-dominator of the paper), valid uniformly in $(\varepsilon, \eta) \in (0, \eta_0)^2$ for some $\eta_0 > 0$, and converge as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ at each fixed $\eta$ in the sense of~(equation eq:CM-compat-limit of the paper); and their Tikhonov limits converge, $\mathcal{I}^{(0),\eta}_r \to \mathcal{I}^{(0)}_r$ in probability as $\eta \downarrow 0$, for almost every $r \in [0,t]$.
  \item \textup{(Conditioning stability.)} $\mathbb{E}[\delta_U(v_h) \mid X^\eta(t)] \to \mathbb{E}[\delta_U(v_h) \mid X(t)]$ in $L^2(\Omega)$ as $\eta \downarrow 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, under~(equation eq:p-Lap-state-conv of the paper) and \textup{(S1)}--\textup{(S3)} alone, $\delta_U(v_h^\eta) \to \delta_U(v_h)$ in $L^2(\Omega)$ and the Fomin derivatives converge as measures: for every $\varphi \in C_b(H)$,
\begin{equation}
  \int_H \varphi\,\beta_h^\eta\,\mathrm{d}\mu_t^\eta \;\xrightarrow[\eta \downarrow 0]{}\; \int_H \varphi\,\beta_h\,\mathrm{d}\mu_t .
\end{equation}
If in addition \textup{(S4)} holds, the logarithmic derivatives converge on the probability space:
\begin{equation}
  \beta_h^\eta(X^\eta(t)) \;\xrightarrow[\eta \downarrow 0]{L^2(\Omega)}\; \beta_h(X(t)).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 9 (Covering-to-measure principle, \cite{dadush2022matrix} Lemma 3.3) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] Let $K\subset\R^s$ be symmetric and convex.  The following are equivalent,
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[\textup{(1)}] $N\!\left(K^\circ,\frac1sB_\infty^s\right)\le 2^{O(s)}$,
    \item[\textup{(2)}] $N\left(K^\circ,\frac{1}{\sqrt s}B_2^s\right)\le 2^{O(s)}$,
    \item[\textup{(3)}] $\gamma_s(K)\ge 2^{-O(s)}$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, we will use the following parameterized form of the implication \(\textup{(2)}\Rightarrow\textup{(3)}\). If \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^s\) is a symmetric convex body, and for some $r\ge s$, $N\left(K^\circ,\frac{1}{\sqrt s}B_2^s\right)\le 2^{Cr}$, then $\gamma_s(cK)\ge 2^{-C'r}$, where $c,C'>0$ depend only on $C$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:time-change-transport of arXiv:2604.05941, 'Banach spaces of continuous paths with finite $p$-th variation'] Let $q\ge2$, let $\mathbb P$ be a dense $q$-refining partition sequence, and let $\phi$ be the associated homeomorphism from Proposition~(prop:q-refining-homeomorphism of the paper). If $x\in V_{\mathbb{T}_q}^p$ satisfies
    \[
        [x]_{\mathbb{T}_q}^{(p)}(t)=h(t),\qquad t\in[0,1],
    \]
    for some continuous non-decreasing function $h$ with $h(0)=0$, then $y:=x\circ\phi\in V_\mathbb P^p$ and
    \[
        [y]_\mathbb P^{(p)}(t)=h(\phi(t)),\qquad t\in[0,1].
    \]
    Equivalently, if $H:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous, non-decreasing, and $x\in V_{\mathbb{T}_q}^p$ satisfies
    \[
        [x]_{\mathbb{T}_q}^{(p)} \equiv H\circ\phi^{-1},
    \]
    then $x\circ\phi\in V_\mathbb P^p$ and $[x\circ\phi]_\mathbb P^{(p)} \equiv H$.

body:
[1 16 of arXiv:2606.10058, 'Mean First Passage Times and Fundamental Tensors of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Let ${\cal A}=[a_{i_1i_2\ldots i_m}] \in \mathbb R^{u \times w \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $w \le n$, be an $m$th order tensor and ${\cal E} \in \mathbb R^{1 \times u \times n \times \cdots \times n}$ be an $m$th order tensor of all ones. Then, ${\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A} \in \mathbb R^{1 \times w \times n \times \cdots \times n}$ is an $m$th order tensor such that 
$${\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A}=\left[\sum_{j=1}^u a_{ji_2\ldots i_m}\right],$$
i.e., it effects a summation operation over the first index of $\cal A$. In particular, for an $m$th order identity tensor ${\cal I} \in \mathbb R^{u \times u \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $u \le n$, 
\be

{\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal I}={\cal E}.
\ee
Moreover, if ${\cal B} \in \mathbb R^{w \times v \times n \times \cdots \times n}$, where $v \le n$, is an $m$th order tensor too, then 
\be

({\cal E} \boxtimes {\cal A}) \boxtimes {\cal B}={\cal E} \boxtimes ({\cal A} \boxtimes {\cal B}),
\ee
i.e., there is associativity for such a special case of $\boxtimes$ multiplication. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

level set. Hence
\[
D\!\left(a(Du_\varepsilon)\right)=0
\qquad\text{a.e. on }\{Du_\varepsilon=0\}.
\]
The equation
\[
-\varepsilon^2\operatorname{div} a(Du_\varepsilon)+W'(u_\varepsilon)=0

body:
[Lem estLpIb of arXiv:2411.08725, 'Berry-Esseen bounds for large-time asymptotics of one-dimensional diffusion processes via '] Let Assumption~{\rm (ass1 of the paper)} hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm (i)]
Suppose that (equation ass:s1 of the paper) is satisfied with some $\alpha >\frac{1}{2}$. 
Then for any $p\in [1,\infty )$, 
\[
\sup _{x\in [x_0, \infty )} \sup _{t\in [0,\infty )} E\left[ \left| \int _0^t \left( \sigma (s,X_s^x) - \sigma _\infty (s) \right) dB_s \right| ^p \right] \leq C_p .
\]

\item[\rm (ii)]
Suppose that (equation ass:b1 of the paper) is satisfied with some $\beta >1$. 
Then for any $p\in [1,\infty )$, 
\[
\sup _{x\in [x_0, \infty )} \sup _{t\in [0,\infty )} E\left[ \left| \int _0^t \left( b(s,X_s^x) - b_\infty (s) \right) ds \right| ^p \right] \leq C_p .
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Lem estLpIb of arXiv:2411.08725

Let  $\Psi_0$ be the initialising state

Let $V$ be a volume process from~$\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. 
For any
$t \geq \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Then  the following statements hold  for
every $t >  \tau_0$ and
every tuple
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states

$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$.

conditioned on
$\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}$,

the transition is via

$\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}$,
is at most $\exp(- \lambda(j^{\psi_{t-1}}-1)/400)$. 
\end{itemize}

body:
[Lemma lem:CBess of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Let $d\ge 1$ and $\nu = (d-2)/2$.
Let $x,\eta\in\mathbb{R}^d$ with $x\neq 0$,
and also $\eta \neq 0$ if $d\le 2$.
Let $\Lambda \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ be symmetric and positive-definite.
Then
\begin{equation} 
\mathbb{C}(x; \eta, \Lambda)
= \frac { 2} { (2\pi)^{d/2}   \sqrt{\det \Lambda }  }
\left( \frac ab \right)^\nu
K_\nu(ab)  e^{ x \cdot \Lambda^{-1} \eta }.
\end{equation}
In particular, for $d=1$ and $d=3$ we have
\begin{alignat}2
\mathbb{C}(x; \eta, \Lambda)
&=
\frac{ 1 } { |\eta| }
	e^{ x \cdot \Lambda^{-1} \eta -ab},
   &&(d=1),
    \\
    \mathbb{C}(x; \eta, \Lambda)
&= \frac { 1} { 2\pi \sqrt{\det \Lambda } }
\frac{ 1 } {\sqrt{x \cdot \Lambda^{-1} x} }  e^{ x \cdot \Lambda^{-1} \eta -ab}
    \qquad&& (d=3).
\end{alignat}
title: Lemma lem:CBess of arXiv:2605.15545

body:
[Lem dual of arXiv:2609.01791, 'Minimum $b_2$ of symplectic fillings of lens spaces'] Let $p>q>0$ be coprime integers. Let $[c_1,\dots,c_{l_1}]^-$ be the Hirzebruch-Jung expansion of $p\slash q$, and $[d_1,\dots,d_{l_2}]^-$ be the Hirzebruch-Jung expansion of $p\slash(p-q)$.

Let $a_i\ge 0$, $b_i\ge 3$ be integers satisfying
$$(c_1,\dots,c_{l_1})=(2^{[a_0]},b_1,2^{[a_1]},\dots,b_k,2^{[a_k]}).$$
Then,
$$adjusted((d_1,\dots,d_{l_2}))=(a_0+1,0^{[b_1-3]},a_1+1,\dots,0^{[b_k-3]},a_k+1).$$

body:
[Openquestion 31 (Minimal maximum length for common-bias cycles) of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Fix a common bias $p\in(0,1)\setminus\{\tfrac12\}$ and use random tie-break.
Let $L_{\max}(p)$ be the smallest integer $L$ such that there exist patterns $A,B,C$ with
$\max(|A|,|B|,|C|)\le L$ that form a non-transitive $3$-cycle under this common bias $p$.
Does $L_{\max}(p)$ exist for every $p\ne\tfrac12$?
Determine $L_{\max}(p)$ (or give meaningful bounds) and describe the length profiles that achieve it.
We exhibited cycles of profiles $(2,5,5)$ and $(3,6,6)$, and we classified all common-bias cycles with $\max(|A|,|B|,|C|)\le 8$. (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Minimal maximum length for common-bias cycles

body:
[Cor Corollary: Commensurable factors have almost same decomposition of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $X$ be a $\mathbb{Z}^d$-system and $\pi_i: X \to Y_i$, $i = 1, 2$, be two nilfactors over a common base $\Omega$, with bundle decompositions
    $$ Y_i = \bigsqcup_{n \geq 0} \Omega^i_n \rtimes_{\rho^i_n} N^i_n / \Gamma^i_n.$$
    If the joining of $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ over $\Omega$ induced by $X$ is finite-to-finite, then for every $n, l \geq 0$ with $\nu(\Omega^1_n \cap \Omega^2_l) > 0$, the nilpotent Lie groups $N^1_n$ and $N^2_l$ are isomorphic.

body:
[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2607.11756, 'Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model'] Suppose that
\[
 0<a<b\le1,
 \qquad
 \alpha(s)=m\in(0,1)
 \quad(a<s<b).
\]
Set
\[
 T=\beta^2(b-a),
 \qquad
 \sigma(t)=a+\frac{t}{\beta^2},
 \qquad
 U(t,x)=u(\sigma(t),x),
 \qquad 0\le t<T.
\]
Let $\widehat X_t=X_{\sigma(t)}$, denote its density by $p(t,\cdot)$,
and define
\begin{equation}
 f(t,x)=p(t,x)\e^{-mU(t,x)},
 \qquad
 V(t,x)=-\log f(t,x).
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 U_t=-\frac12(U_{xx}+mU_x^2),
 \qquad
 f_t=\frac12f_{xx}
\end{equation}
on $(0,T)\times\R$, and
\begin{equation}
 V_x\ge0,
 \qquad V_{xx}\ge0,
 \qquad V_{xxx}\le0
 \qquad\text{on }(0,T)\times(0,\infty).
\end{equation}

For $0\le B<1$, let $x=x(t,B)\ge0$ be the inverse slope coordinate
\[
 B=U_x(t,x),
\]
and set
\[
 C(t,B)=U_{xx}(t,x(t,B)).
\]
Define
\begin{align}
 z&=-\frac12C_B=(m+K)B,
 &J&=K+BK_B,                                      \\
 \Phi&=2z^2-mC,
 &N&=V_x+KB,                                      \\
 R_1&=KBV_x+\frac12(KB)^2,
 &R_V&=\frac12(V_x^2-V_{xx}),                     \\
 R_0&=2CJ-\frac m2C-\frac12z^2,
 &G&=2Cz(3zJ-CJ_B),                               \\
 L&=CJ-z(N+z),                                    \\
 w(t,B)&=2p(t,x(t,B))C(t,B).                      
\end{align}
Every derivative of $V$ appearing in slope coordinates is evaluated at
$(t,x(t,B))$.

Fix a compact interval $I\subset[0,T)$, so that $\max I<T$. There are constants
$c_I,C_I>0$ such that, for every $t\in I$ and $x\in\R$,
\begin{align}
 c_I\e^{-C_Ix^2}
 &\le f(t,x)\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix^2},                 \\
 p(t,x)&\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix^2},                     \\
 |V_x(t,x)|&\le C_I(1+|x|),                      \\
 0\le V_{xx}(t,x)&\le C_I,                       \\
 |V_{xxx}(t,x)|&\le C_I.                         
\end{align}
Consequently, for every $A\ge0$ and integer $k\ge0$, there are
constants $c_{I,A,k},C_{I,A,k}>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_R^\infty
 p(t,x)(1+x)^k\e^{Ax}\dd x
 \le C_{I,A,k}\e^{-c_{I,A,k}R^2},
 \qquad R\ge0.
\end{equation}

There are constants $A_I,C_I'<\infty$ such that, for $t\in I$ and
$0\le B<1$,
\begin{align}
 &|N|+|\Phi|+|G|+|R_0|+|(R_0)_B|
 +|R_1|+|(R_1)_B|\notag\\
 &\qquad
 +|R_V|+|(R_V)_B|+|L|+|L_B|
 \le C_I'\e^{A_Ix(t,B)}.                         
\end{align}
If $I\Subset(0,T)$, then, with the time derivative taken at fixed
$B$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\frac{\partial_t(w\Phi)}w\right|
 \le C_I'\e^{A_Ix(t,B)}.
\end{equation}

More generally, suppose $Q$ is continuous on $I\times[0,1)$ and
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 |Q(t,B)|\le C\e^{Ax(t,B)}
\end{equation}
for some $A,C<\infty$. Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_0^1w(t,B)|Q(t,B)|\dd B<\infty.
\end{equation}
If
\[
 B_I(R)=\sup_{t\in I}U_x(t,R),
\]
then
\[
 B_I(R)<1,
 \qquad
 B_I(R)\uparrow1
 \quad(R\to\infty),
\]
and
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_{B_I(R)}^1w(t,B)|Q(t,B)|\dd B
 \le C_{I,Q}\e^{-c_{I,Q}R^2}.
\end{equation}

Define
\begin{equation}
 F(t,B)=\int_B^1w(t,D)\Phi(t,D)\dd D.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 |F(t,B)|\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix(t,B)^2}.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $Q$ satisfies \eqref{eq:admissible-Q}, then
\begin{equation}
 F(t,B)Q(t,B)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(B\uparrow1),
\end{equation}
uniformly for $t\in I$, and
\begin{equation}
 w(t,B)C(t,B)z(t,B)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(B\uparrow1)
\end{equation}
uniformly for $t\in I$.

If $I\Subset(0,T)$, the function
\begin{equation}
 H(t)=\int_0^1w(t,B)\Phi(t,B)\dd B
\end{equation}
belongs to $C^1(I)$, with
\begin{equation}
 H'(t)=\int_0^1\partial_t(w\Phi)(t,B)\dd B.
\end{equation}
At any $t\in(0,T)$ for which $H(t)=0$, one has $F(t,0)=0$ and
\begin{equation}
 \int_0^1w\Phi R_0\dd B
 =\int_0^1F(R_0)_B\dd B
 =\int_0^1w\tau(R_0)_B\dd B,
 \qquad \tau=\frac Fw.
\end{equation}
At such a centered time, the function
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H(B)=w(B)C(B)z(B)-F(B)
\end{equation}
extends to an absolutely continuous function on $[0,1]$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H_B=wL
 \qquad\text{a.e.\ on }(0,1),
\end{equation}
and has
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H(0)=\mathcal H(1)=0.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 9 (Universal-cover noncollapsing for torus bundles) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(B\geq1\).  There is a number \(i_B>0\) with the following property.  Let
\(M\) be the total space of a \(\TT^2\)-bundle over \(S^1\), let \(h\) be an
invariant metric for that bundle structure, and let \(g\) be
another metric satisfying
\[
        B^{-1}h\leq g\leq Bh.
\]
If \(|\sec_g|\leq\Lambda\) for some \(\Lambda>0\), then the universal cover
satisfies
\[
        \inf_{\widetilde x\in\widetilde M}
        \inj_{\widetilde g}(\widetilde x)
        \geq i_B\Lambda^{-1/2}.
\]

body:
For security parameter lambda, a secret-key zero-bit pseudorandom code for a channel C consists of polynomial-time KeyGen, randomized Enc and Dec, with polynomial block length n(lambda). There is only one message, denoted 1. For k generated by KeyGen and fresh x=Enc(k), Dec(k,C(x))=1 except with negligible probability. For every fixed string y independent of k, Dec(k,y)=bottom except with negligible probability (a bound uniform over y). Any polynomial-time adversary with oracle access to fresh encodings under one fixed k has negligible advantage over an oracle returning fresh independent uniform n-bit strings. The decoder is secret; public-key encoding is an additional property, not part of this definition.
The channel and all algorithm interfaces are fixed
Negligibility is in lambda; fresh encoder coins on every call
title: Christ?Gunn secret-key zero-bit pseudorandom code: soundness and repeated-encoding security

[Theorem caffarellisregularity of arXiv:2411.10235, '\textbf{Smooth transport map via diffusion process}'] Let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be two probability measures being absolutely continuous with respect to the $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure and that are supported on open bounded sets $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ respectively. Provided that

[Lemma 6 ({\cite[Lemma 4.1) of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] {AM92}}] 
For a smooth measure \(\mu \in \mathcal{S}\) and its corresponding PCAF \(A^\mu\), the following equalities hold:
\[
\|R_\alpha \mu\|_{\infty, q} = \|R_\alpha \mu\|_{\infty} \quad \text{for any } \alpha > 0,
\]
and
\[
\|\mathbb{E}_{\cdot}[A_t^{\mu}]\|_{\infty, q} = \|\mathbb{E}_{\cdot}[A_t^{\mu}]\|_{\infty} \quad \text{for any } t > 0.
\]
Here, $\|\cdot\|_{\infty}$ denotes the essential supremum norm with respect to the underlying measure $m$.

Result: Duminil-Copin-Smirnov's parafermionic observable exists for all n in [0,2] at the critical x with spin sigma = 1 - 3 arccos(-n/2)/(4 pi)... (the spin depends on n) and satisfies the contour relations; full holomorphicity holds for none except the Ising-related n = 1 dilute? (n = 1 corresponds to the Ising model's low-temperature expansion on the honeycomb, for which the observable is the Ising fermion and IS holomorphic — that is how Smirnov's Ising result and Chelkak-Smirnov work; on the honeycomb the n = 1 loop model at x_c is the critical Ising model, so the n = 1 case at the critical point IS known via Ising, contrary to the naive reading; the source's remark 'n = 1 site percolation' refers to the dense phase x = 1, kappa = 6). So: n = 1 critical (Ising, SLE(3)) and n = 1 dense (percolation, SLE(6)) are both known; n = 2 corresponds to kappa = 4 (GFF level lines) and is open; n in (0,1) union (1,2) open in both phases; n = 0 critical open (P0003), n = 0 dense (kappa = 8, uniform spanning tree-like, x = 1: the dense O(0) model at x = 1 is the Hamiltonian-cycle-type model... open). Load-bearing hypothesis: Re a(u, u) ≥ α‖u‖² for all u in the Hilbert space H, with a fixed α > 0 and the norm of H itself (the trial and test space). What fails: strict positivity a(u, u) > 0 for u ≠ 0, or injectivity of the associated operator, is not enough - the solution operator need not be bounded and the problem need not be solvable. Counterexample 1: H = ℓ², a(u, v) = Σ_{n ≥ 1} n^{-1} u_n conj(v_n). Then a is bounded (C = 1), Hermitian, and a(u, u) > 0 for every u ≠ 0, but the associated operator is the injective compact diagonal operator with entries 1/n, whose range is not closed. For f = (1/n)_n ∈ ℓ², the equation a(u, v) = ⟨f, v⟩ for all v forces u_n = 1 for all n, which is not in ℓ²: no solution exists. Counterexample 2 (the practical one): on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain Ω, a(u, v) = ∫_Ω ∇u·∇v̄ on H = H¹(Ω) is bounded and positive semidefinite but not coercive, since a(1, 1) = 0; the Neumann problem −Δu = f, ∂_ν u = 0 is solvable only under the compatibility condition ∫_Ω f = 0, and is never uniquely solvable in H¹(Ω) (constants can be added). Coercivity is recovered only on the subspace {u ∈ H¹(Ω) : ∫_Ω u = 0} via the Poincaré-Wirtinger inequality; on H_0^1(Ω) it is recovered via the Poincaré inequality, which is why the Dirichlet problem is the easy case. Other silent hypotheses: H must be complete (a coercive bounded form on a dense non-closed subspace gives no existence), and the coercivity constant α must be uniform, not depending on u. Note a is not assumed symmetric - that part is genuinely unnecessary. For non-coercive but well-posed problems (e.g. mixed or saddle point formulations, convection dominated problems, different trial and test spaces), the correct replacement is the Banach-Necas-Babuska inf-sup theorem: an inf-sup condition on a plus injectivity of the adjoint form, of which coercivity is only a sufficient condition.
H is a Hilbert space
a is bounded sesquilinear on H × H
the claimed coercivity constant α > 0 must hold on all of H
title: Pitfall: Lax-Milgram Needs Coercivity on the Whole Space, Not Mere Positivity or Injectivity

[Definition 8 (Weighted Besov spaces \cite{HZZZ22}) of arXiv:2607.13379, 'Quantitative Propagation of Chaos and Fluctuations for Kinetic McKean--Vlasov SDEs with Si'] For $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ and $p,q\in[1,\infty]$, define
\begin{align*}
\bB_{p;a}^{\alpha,q}:=\Big\{f\in\mathcal{S}':\ \|f\|_{\bB_{p;a}^{\alpha,q}}:=\Big(\sum_{j\ge-1}2^{\alpha j q}\|\mathcal{R}_j^a f\|^q_{L^p}\Big)^{1/q}<\infty\Big\},
\end{align*}
with the usual modification when $q=\infty$.
Moreover, for $\ell\in\mR$, we also define weighted Besov spaces with the norm
$$
    \|f\|_{\bB^{\alpha,q}_{p;a,\ell}}
    :=
    \|\langle z\rangle^{\ell}f\|_{\bB^{\alpha,q}_{p;a}},
    \qquad
    \langle z\rangle=(1+|z|^2)^{1/2}.
$$
For $p=q=\infty$, we write
$$
\bC^\alpha_a:=\bB^{\alpha,\infty}_{\infty;a}.
$$
title: Weighted Besov spaces \cite{HZZZ22}

with $\theta(x) := \int_{\XX}k(y \mid x)\pi(\dd y)$ and $r := 1-\theta$, one has

$\pi$ is invariant for $T$, i.e.\ \hyp{A3}{A3} holds, and $T$ is reversible with respect to
$\pi$.

body: Let X and Y be Banach spaces, U a subset of X open in the norm topology, and F: U -> Y. F is Frechet differentiable at a point x in U if there exists a bounded linear operator A: X -> Y such that the limit, as h in X tends to 0, of ||F(x+h) - F(x) - A h||_Y / ||h||_X equals 0. The operator A, when it exists, is unique and is called the Frechet derivative of F at x, denoted DF(x). [standard, e.g. Brezis, Functional Analysis, Sobolev Spaces and PDEs]
title: Frechet Derivative of a Map Between Banach Spaces

\[

body:
[Corollary cor:finite-type-spectral-label-pk-limit of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] Assume (equation eq:finite-type-band-parameter-convergence of the paper),
\[
  \Theta:=\sum_{r=1}^Q\theta_r\ge1,
\]
and \((ass:background-density-concentration of the paper)\).  If
\(N_L/V_L\to\rho>\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}\), then
\[
  \Xi_{L,N_L}^{\mathrm{ft}}
  \Longrightarrow
  \Pi_{\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}}^{\mathrm{ft}\text{-}\mathrm{br}}
  \qquad
  \text{in }\mathcal N_\ell(E_{\mathrm{ft}}).
\]
The limiting ranked lengths \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\) are the ranked jumps of the
Poisson--Kingman bridge with scalar profile
\[
  \phi_{\mathrm{ft}}(x)
  =
  \sum_{r=1}^Q
  \theta_r e^{-\beta\lambda_r x}
\]
conditioned to have total mass \(\rho-\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}\).  Conditionally on
the ranked lengths, the auxiliary variables \(U_i\) are independent uniform
variables on \([0,1]\), and the spectral labels are conditionally independent
with
\[
  \mathbb P\bigl(M_i^{\mathrm{ft}}=r\,\big|\,X_i\bigr)
  =
  \frac{
    \theta_r e^{-\beta\lambda_r X_i}
  }{
    \sum_{s=1}^Q \theta_s e^{-\beta\lambda_s X_i}
  },
  \qquad r=1,\ldots,Q.
  \]
  If all positive weight $\lambda_r$ equal a common value $\lambda_*$, then $\phi_{\mathrm ft}(x)=\Theta e^{-\beta \lambda_* x}$ and the ranked normalized length have law $PD(0,\Theta)$. If at least two positive weight are distinct, the limit law is not a Poisson Dirichlet type. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-type spectral-label marked Poisson--Kingman bridge

[Theorem Thm 1.2 of arXiv:2608.30491, 'The Daugavet property in symmetric operator spaces'] Let $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be a semi-finite atomless von Neumann algebra and let $E$ be a symmetric function space on $(0,\tau(\mathbf{1}))$. Assume that $E(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ has the Daugavet property.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm(i)]
\item If $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is $\sigma$-finite and $E$ is KB, then $L_1\subseteq E$ on $(0,\tau(\mathbf{1}))$.
\item If $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is non-$\sigma$-finite, $E$ is KB, and $E\cap L_\infty\neq L_1\cap L_\infty$, then $L_1\subseteq E$ on $(0,\infty)$.
\item If $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is non-$\sigma$-finite and $E$ is uniformly monotone, then $L_1\subseteq E$ on $(0,\infty)$.
\item If $\tau(\mathbf{1})<\infty$ and $E$ is KB, then $E=L_1$ on $(0,\tau(\mathbf{1}))$, up to equivalence of norms.
\item If $\tau(\mathbf{1})<\infty$, $E$ has a Fatou norm, and either $E^\times$ is strictly monotone or $E^\times$ is order continuous, then $E=L_\infty$ on $(0,\tau(\mathbf{1}))$, up to equivalence of norms.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Thm 1.2 of arXiv:2608.30491

[Definition def:paired-resource of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] A safe gate and its $C$-degree are as in
(def:circuit-primitives of the paper); the amplified estimate is proved in
(lem:safe of the paper).

For an active eigenframe of an arbitrary self-adjoint pure-Weyl $C$, put
\[
 (F_Cx)_a=\lambda_aA_a^Tx,
 \qquad
 F_C^*F_C=Q_2:=-\sum_a\lambda_a^2A_a^2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Tr} Q_2=2\|C\|_2^2.
\tag{2.2.1}
\]
A concrete carrier for these two fronts is obtained as follows.  Let
$E_C=\ell^2(I_C)$ be the active label space,
$J_C:E_C\to\Lambda^2H$ the isometry $J_Ce_a=A_a$, and
\[
 \iota_\wedge A=2^{-1/2}\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}e_i\otimes e_j,
 \qquad
 \mathsf W_C=(\iota_\wedge J_C)\otimes I_H,
\]
and define the one-hole column
\[
 (T_Cx)_{ijk}=\sum_\ell C_{ij,k\ell}x_\ell.
\tag{2.2.2}
\]
With the ordered-pair convention
$C_{ij,k\ell}=\sum_a\lambda_a(A_a)_{ij}(A_a)_{k\ell}$,
one has the exact typed identity
\[
 \mathsf W_CF_C=-2^{-1/2}T_C,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak q_C^{\rm hole}
 :=\mathsf W_CF_CF_C^*\mathsf W_C^*
 =\frac12T_CT_C^*.
\tag{2.2.3}
\]
Thus the open token is a specified three-strand operator, up to the signed
leg permutations recorded by its port state; it is not defined merely by
having a prescribed scalar cap.  Moreover
\[
 T_C^*T_C=2Q_2,
 \qquad
 T_C=P_{[2,1]_0}T_C,
\tag{2.2.4}
\]
where $P_{[2,1]_0}$ is the trace-free hook projection on the first three
indices.

A paired-front atom contains the two correlated Hilbert--Schmidt fronts
of this single $F_C$ pair, equivalently the concrete hole
$\mathfrak q_C^{\rm hole}$ in (eq:2.2.3 of the paper), any safe left and right gates, and
an untouched typed ancillary boundary $E$.  Let $\mathfrak M_C^{\rm alg}(E)$ be
the algebraic span of these atoms.  Its projective norm is the infimum,
over all atomic presentations, of the sum of the products of the two
front Hilbert--Schmidt norms and all safe-gate operator-norm bounds.  The
completion is denoted $\mathfrak M_C(E)$.  Its distinguished token
$\mathfrak q_C$ satisfies
\[
 \|\mathfrak q_C\|_{\mathfrak M_C}\le\operatorname{Tr} Q_2=2\|C\|_2^2.
\tag{2.2.5}
\]
The two fronts form one resource: they may move or fuse but are never
duplicated.  Equality in (eq:2.2.5 of the paper) is not asserted, and the cap identity
does not identify this open pair with a differently typed polar pair.
title: Paired resource and safe module
Two-slab and two-disk estimate

body:
[Lem 11 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] Let 
${\sf d}$ be a distance function consistent with the given topology on 
 $E$.
Suppose that the jumping measure $J$ satisfies 
$$
\frac{D_1}{{\sf d}(x,y)^{p_1}}{\m}({\d} x)\m({\d} y)\leq
J({\d} x{\d} y)\leq \frac{D_2}{{\sf d}(x,y)^{p_2}}{\m}({\d} x){\m}({\d} y)
$$ 
for some $D_1,D_2>0$ and $0<p_1\leq p_2<\infty$. 
Assume $1\land\frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}}\in L^1(E;{\m})$ 
for a fixed $o\in E$ and take $u\in L^1_{\loc}(E;{\m})$. Then the following are equivalent. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(1)] $\left(1\land \frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}} \right)|u|\in L^1(E;{\m})$.
\item[\rm(2)] For any $U\Subset V\Subset E$ with $o\in V$, 
\begin{align}
\int_{U\times V^c}|u(x)-u(y)|J({\d} x{\d} y)
<\infty.
\end{align} 
\end{enumerate}
Assume $1\land\frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}}\in L^2(E;{\m})$ and 
take $u\in L^2_{\loc}(E;{\m})$. Then the following are equivalent. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(3)] $\left(1\land \frac{1}{{\sf d}(\cdot,o)^{p_1}} \right)|u|^2\in L^1(E;{\m})$.
\item[\rm(4)] For any $U\Subset V\Subset E$ with $o\in V$, 
\begin{align}
\int_{U\times V^c}|u(x)-u(y)|^2J({\d} x{\d} y)
<\infty.
\end{align} 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 11 of arXiv:2506.17979

[Definition 23 of arXiv:2607.22441, 'The martingale representation theorem for cylindrical martingale valued measures'] Let $P$ be a probability distribution on $C([0,T],G)$. We say that $P$ solves the \emph{weak martingale problem} for $(a,b,Q,\lambda)$ if for any $G$-valued continuous adapted process $X$ defined on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ whose probability distribution is $P$, we have for  
every $f\in C_{u,loc}^{2}(G)$,
\[
M^f_t = f(X_t) - f(\xi) - \int_0^t A_s f(X_s)\, ds
\]
is a $G$-valued continuous martingale on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, where the infinitesimal generator $A_t$ satisfies
$$
\int_0^t A_s f(x_s)\, ds = \tfrac{1}{2} \int_0^t \int_U 
\operatorname{Tr}_{b(s,u,x_s)\, Q^{1/2}}\left( f''(x_s)\right) \lambda(du) ds
+ \int_0^t f'(x_s)\, a(s,x_s)\, ds,
$$
for any $x\in C([0,T],G)$. In such a case, we also say that $X$ solves the martingale problem.
title: Definition 23 of arXiv:2607.22441

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), standard concentration reduction, no novelty claim. Let iid labels I_s have task probabilities p_t>0. Let N_t(s) count task t up to integer s and T_t(h)=min{s:N_t(s)>=h}, integer h>=1. For 0<epsilon<1, P(T_t(h)<=floor((1-epsilon)*h/p_t))<=exp(-epsilon^2*h/2), and P(T_t(h)>ceil((1+epsilon)*h/p_t))<=exp(-epsilon^2*h/4). For any M listed task-threshold pairs with h>=hmin, all brackets hold simultaneously except on an event of probability at most 2*M*exp(-epsilon^2*hmin/4), without independence across task clocks. If an already decoupled learner transitions between local counts floor((1-delta)H) and ceil((1+delta)H), retains its learned loss thereafter, H tends to infinity, delta tends to zero and log(4*n/zeta)=o(H), then with failure at most zeta the global transition widths are uniformly o(H/p_t). This does not prove the learner is decoupled or that isolated parity learning has such a transition.

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2608.27880, 'Precise universal edge asymptotics for planar $\beta=2$ Coulomb gases with radial external'] Let $V$ be in  $C^3(0, +\infty)$ and suppose that $V'=0$ has a unique solution $t_1>0$ and $r V'(r)$ is strictly increasing on $(0, +\infty).$	Let $t_1, \tau_n$ be defined as above. Then 
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] Berry-Esseen bound:
$$\aligned 
\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|\mathbb{P}(\min_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i|\ge t_1-\frac{\sqrt{\tau_n}}{\sqrt{V''(t_1) n}}+\frac{t}{\sqrt{V''(t_1)n\tau_n}})-e^{-e^{t}}|&\sim\frac{2\log\log n}{e\log n}.
\endaligned $$ 
\item[(2)] For any $0<t<t_1,$ we have 
$$\mathbb{P}(\min_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i|\le t)\sim \frac{\sqrt{V''(t_1)}\,t_1 t}{\sqrt{2\pi n}(t_1^2-t^2)(-V'(t))}
\exp(-nV(t)+nV(t_1)).$$ 
\item[(3)] Given $t>1,$ we obtain \[
\mathbb{P}\bigl( \min_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i| \le t_1-\frac{t\sqrt{{\tau}_n}}{\sqrt{V''(t_1) n}} \bigr)
\sim
t^{-2}(\frac{8\pi (\log n)^2}{V''(t_1) n t_1^2 })^{\frac{t^2-1}{2}}.
\]
\item[(4)] Given $1\ll v_n\ll \log n$:
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl( \min_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i| \le t_1-\frac{\sqrt{{\tau}_n}}{\sqrt{V''(t_1) n}}-\frac{v_n}{\sqrt{V''(t_1) n {\tau}_n}} \bigr)
\sim
\exp\bigl(-v_n-\frac{v_n^2}{2{\tau}_n}\bigr).
\]
\item[(5)] Given $d_n>0$:
\[\aligned
&\quad\mathbb{P}\bigl(\min_{1\le i\le n}|\sigma_i| \le t_1 - d_n \bigr)\\
&
\sim
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{t_1}{2\sqrt{2\pi V''(t_1) n} \, d_n^2 }
\exp\bigl(-\frac{1}{2}V''(t_1) n d_n^2\bigr), & \frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{\sqrt{n}} \ll d_n \ll n^{-\frac13},\\[1.2em]
\displaystyle \frac{t_1\exp(-n V(t_1-d_n)+nV(t_1))}{2\sqrt{2\pi V''(t_1) n} \,  d_n^2 }
, & n^{-\frac13}\lesssim d_n\ll 1.
\end{cases}
\endaligned\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

		d\hat{X}_t={\sigma(\hat{X}_t)\over F(\hat{X}_t,t;t_n)}dW_t+{\sigma^2(\hat{X}_t)\over F^2(\hat{X}_t,t;t_n)}\left[g(\hat{X}_t,t;t_n)+{b(\hat{X}_t)\over \sigma^2(\hat{X}_t)}\right]dt,\quad t\in(t_n,t_{n+1}],
	\end{equation}
	where $\sigma:\mathbb{R}_{+}\to\mathbb{R}_{+}$, $\sigma(x)=\theta\sqrt{x}$, $b:\mathbb{R}_{+}\to\mathbb{R}$, $b(x)=\alpha-kx$, and
	\begin{align}
		& F(x,t;t_n)=1+{k\over 2}(t-t_n)+{(4\alpha-\theta^2)(t-t_n)\over 8x}, \nonumber \\
		&g(x,t;t_n)=-{k(t-t_n)\over 2\theta^2}+{1\over 2x}-{2(2+k(t-t_n))\over 4x(2+2k(t-t_n))+(4\alpha-\theta^2)(t-t_n)} \nonumber \\
        &~~~~~~~~~~~~~~+{(4\alpha-\theta^2)^2(t-t_n)\over 32\theta^2 x^2}. \nonumber
	\end{align}
	Moreover, 

\[
\frac{1}{F(x,t;t_n)}\le 1,~
|g(x,t;t_n)|\le K\left(1+\frac{1}{x}+\frac{t-t_n}{x^2}\right),~
\sup_{t\le T,\,N} g(x,t;t_n)\le K\left(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^2}\right),
\]
\[
\inf_{x\ge0} g(x,t;t_n)
=
-\frac{k}{2\theta^2}(t-t_n)
\ge
-\frac{kT}{2\theta^2}.
\]
where $K>0$ is a constant depending only on $\alpha$, $\theta$ and $T$.

AUTHOR-CHECKED CANDIDATE COUNTEREXAMPLE; NO INDEPENDENT REVIEW OR NOVELTY CLAIM. A stationary four-state reversible family has E g=0, E g^2=1, exactly ||g||_infinity=2 and relaxation time1. At times s tending to infinity, its additive functional divided by its positive asymptotic standard deviation times sqrt(s) converges in probability to0, so its Kolmogorov distance from N(0,1) has liminf at least1/2. A rare slow coordinate carries asymptotic variance while a fast coordinate supplies bounded instantaneous variance. Uniformizing all rates preserves the obstruction. Each individual chain still has a usual fixed-chain central limit theorem.
Chain and function may depend on s
Stationary initialization
Normalization by asymptotic variance rate
Aldous-Fill Open Problem4.30 literal uniform quantifiers

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6d7c6860e2f24dab6c7065a1a81281f6f1721b7b4d6d510c186affdd00fb73d1","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/6d/6d7c6860e2f24dab6c7065a1a81281f6f1721b7b4d6d510c186affdd00fb73d1.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:782e3ef5bbb0faf01a685eb529732c0d77bfa3843ab0c5c3cb1c854a588ec117","bundle_entry_key":"uniform-clt-counter","bundle_id":"population.probability-candidate-obstructions-and-spatial-lemmas-005","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-1000-20h-20260906/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.markov:candidate-gap-and-bounded-observable-insufficient-uniform-clt","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0209: a four-state obstruction to the proposed uniform normal approximation

Status: complete negative-answer candidate, author checked by spectral covariance and a direct rare-event argument. No independent review or novelty certificate. The construction responds to the literal historical question, whose current status is unverified.

Source: Aldous and Fill, *Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs*, 2002 unfinished monograph, 2014 recompilation, Open Problem 4.30, PDF p.137, https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.pdf . The chapter is internally dated October 11, 1994. With a stationary finite reversible continuous-time chain and a function g satisfying Eπg=0 and Eπg²=1, the source asks for a universal bound

\[
 \sup_x\left|\mathbb P_\pi\left\{\frac{\int_0^t g(X_u)\,du}
 {\sigma\sqrt t}\le x\right\}-\Phi(x)\right|
 \le\psi(\|g\|_\infty,t/\tau_2),
 \qquad \psi(b,s)\longrightarrow0\quad(s\longrightarrow\infty).
\]

Here σ² is the asymptotic variance rate and τ2 is the relaxation time. We keep the first argument exactly equal to two, so there is no hidden assumption of uniformity or continuity in b.

## Four-state reversible family

For an integer s at least three, set ε=s^{-2} and R=s^4. Let Y be a stationary two-state chain on {0,1}, with rates 0→1 equal to ε and 1→0 equal to 1-ε. Its stationary success probability is ε and its nonzero generator eigenvalue is -1. Independently let Z be a fair stationary sign chain, flipping at rate R/2, with nonzero generator eigenvalue -R. The product X=(Y,Z) has four states, is irreducible and reversible, and has generator eigenvalues 0,-1,-R,-(R+1). Thus τ2=1.

Define

\[
 A=2\varepsilon+\sqrt{(1-\varepsilon)(1-4\varepsilon)},\qquad
 B=\frac{2-A}{1-\varepsilon},\qquad
 g(Y,Z)=AZ+B(Y-\varepsilon).
\]

For 0<ε≤1/9, A and B are positive. The positive root A solves

\[
 A^2-4\varepsilon A+5\varepsilon-1=0,
\]

which is equivalent to A²+B²ε(1-ε)=1. Independence and centering therefore give Eπg=0 and Eπg²=1. Also A+B(1-ε)=2. Every possible absolute value of g is at most max{A+Bε,A+B(1-ε)}=2 because ε<1/2, and the value 2 occurs when Y=1,Z=1. Hence ||g||∞=2 exactly for every s. Finally A→1 and B→1.

## Exact variance rate

The stationary autocovariance is

\[
 \mathbb E[g(X_0)g(X_u)]
 =A^2e^{-Ru}+B^2\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)e^{-u}.
\]

This follows directly from the two nonconstant coordinate eigenfunctions. Integrating twice over the covariance triangle gives

\[
 \sigma^2=2\int_0^\infty\mathbb E[g(X_0)g(X_u)]\,du
 =\frac{2A^2}{R}+2B^2\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)>0.
\]

Each fixed member of the family has the ordinary asymptotic normal limit. The issue is uniformity over chains at a time depending on the member.

## Collapse at time t=s

Observe the chain until t=s. Write F=A∫₀ˢZ_u du and H=B∫₀ˢ(Y_u-ε)du. The probability that Y is ever one on this interval is at most

\[
 \mathbb P(Y_0=1)+\mathbb E[\#\{0\to1\hbox{ transitions in }[0,s]\}]
 \le\varepsilon+s\varepsilon=\frac1{s^2}+\frac1s.
\]

On the complementary event, H=-Bεs, and

\[
 \left|\frac{H}{\sigma\sqrt s}\right|
 \le\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon s}{2(1-\varepsilon)}}\longrightarrow0.
\]

The fast component is negligible in L²:

\[
 \mathbb E F^2
 =2A^2\int_0^s(s-u)e^{-Ru}\,du
 \le\frac{2A^2s}{R},
\qquad
 \mathbb E\left(\frac F{\sigma\sqrt s}\right)^2
 \le\frac{A^2}{RB^2\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)}\longrightarrow0.
\]

Here Rε=s². Combining the rare-event bound with Chebyshev yields

\[
 \frac{\int_0^s g(X_u)\,du}{\sigma\sqrt s}
 \longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability}.
\]

For any fixed x>0 its distribution function thus tends to one. The limiting inferior of its Kolmogorov distance from a standard normal is at least 1-Φ(x). Letting x decrease to zero shows that this limiting inferior is at least one half. Yet ||g||∞=2 and t/τ2=s→∞. No function ψ of the stated kind can therefore exist.

## Second checks and rate normalization

The apparent conflict with variance convergence is illusory. For a coordinate with covariance c e^{-λu}, the exact finite-time variance is 2c[t/λ-(1-e^{-λt})/λ²]. Substitution shows Var(∫g)/(σ²s)→1. Rare visits carry the variance while their probability tends to zero; the normalized squares are not uniformly integrable. Variance convergence alone cannot force a central limit theorem.

Page 26 explicitly permits nonnegative transition rates with no constraint on their sums. Even imposing total jump rate at most one would not rescue the proposed bound. Replace the generator Q by Q/R and observe for time Rs. Every outgoing rate is at most (R/2+1)/R≤1. The relaxation time becomes R, the variance rate becomes Rσ², and the time integral has the same law as R times the old integral. Both the standardized law and the ratio t/τ2=s are unchanged.

The independent coordinate construction also makes clear the missing quantity: an asymptotic variance scale relative to the function and the slow rare-event mode. A gap and a bounded instantaneous variance do not prevent the asymptotic variance from concentrating in rare excursions. This observation is explanatory, not a claim that any particular modified bound has been proved here.

Focused primary-source searches on September 6, 2026 found the original statement and the author's chapter notes, which discuss fixed-chain Berry–Esseen constants. No later resolution of this precise uniform question was verified. This is not a novelty certificate. A future reviewer should recheck the exact fixed L∞ normalization, stationary initialization, spectral gap, covariance integral, and uniform-limit quantifiers.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:556c6b1fcc6b4db785822e5b4cae963c5ea31477c78e3e04ba1fa72416f504a4","revision_digest":"sha256:e2e1e42036cb94def4ac57cca1bd36d04103293e439a270fdb1bda6190ee4056","source_id":"owner-original-probability-research-20260906:uniform-clt-counter","source_revision":"author-checked-20260906-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Corollary 20 (Exponential-moment bound) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] Let $k\ge1$ and $\phi_1,\dots,\phi_k\in\Ccg$ be supported in $\overline B_{R_0}$ with
$\|\phi_i\|_\infty\le M_0$. Then
\begin{equation}
\bN\Bigl[\prod_{i=1}^k|\mu(\phi_i)|\Bigr]
\;\le\;\gamma^{k-1}\,(2k-3)!!\,\bigl(C_\star M_0\bigr)^{k}
\;\le\;A^{\,k}\,k!\,,
\end{equation}
for $A=A(R_0,M_0)$. Consequently, for every
$\varphi\in\Ccg$ supported in $\overline B_{R_0}$ with $\|\varphi\|_\infty\le M_0$, the
moment generating function of $\mu(\varphi)$ under the size-biased measure
$\Nh=\mu(\varphi_0)\,\bN$ is finite near the origin:
\begin{equation}
\Nh\bigl[e^{\theta\,\mu(\varphi)}\bigr]
=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{\theta^k}{k!}\,\bN\bigl[\mu(\varphi_0)\,\mu(\varphi)^k\bigr]
<\infty\qquad\text{for } |\theta|<1/A',
\end{equation}
where $A'=A'(R_0,M_0,\varphi_0)$. The same holds jointly: for
$\varphi^1,\dots,\varphi^j\in\Ccg$ supported in $\overline B_{R_0}$ with
$\|\varphi^i\|_\infty\le M_0$, the joint MGF
$\Nh[\exp(\sum_i\theta_i\mu(\varphi^i))]$ is finite for $|\theta|$ small
enough, by H\"older's inequality.

[Proposition hull_well_defined of arXiv:2606.27357, '\textbf{Typical distances in high-genus triangulations}'] For any $\varepsilon > 0$ and $n \ge 1$, let us assume that the event $\mathbf{Iso}_{n}(\frac{\varepsilon}{2})$ occurs. Let us also fix $r \ge 0$ such that $|B_r^{+}| \le n^{1-\varepsilon}$. Then, we have $B_r^{\bullet} \neq T_{n,g_n}$. Moreover, if $K_{\theta}\log(n) \le |B_r^{\bullet}|$, then we have
\begin{align}
\big|\log(|B_r^{\bullet}|)-\log(|\partial^{*}B_r^{\bullet}|)\big| \le \log(3w_{\theta}^{-1}).
\end{align}
In particular, we have 
\[
\big|\log(|B_r^{+}|)-\log(|B_r^{\bullet}|)\big| \le \log(3w_{\theta}^{-1}).
\]
title: Proposition hull_well_defined of arXiv:2606.27357

\[
\kappa_{1,a_*}(u)

 \frac{\E[T_m^*]}{m+2}\longrightarrow2,

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02755, 'The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation'] One of the most common descriptions of solutions of singular SPDEs is their characterisation as the limit of solutions of renormalised smooth random PDEs. We quantify the speed of this convergence in the case of the KPZ equation. In particular, we show that the na\"ive guess that the rate is given by the distance of the noise regularity from the endpoint regularity for well-posedness is not correct. Instead, we obtain convergence at the larger rate $1/2$ and show that this rate is sharp. This is achieved by considering the equation satisfied by the rescaled error, which is critical for variance blowup, and showing that this equation has a limit given by an affine linear singular SPDE driven by a new, independent noise. This result can be alternatively interpreted as identifying the asymptotic size and law of fluctuations of the solutions of the KPZ equation driven by mollified noise around their singular limit.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.02755: The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation

body:
[Corollary 44 (No finite-dimensional triangular family is lossless in infinite dimension) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Assume that at least one central axis $E_A$ or $E_Q$ is infinite dimensional.
Then no finite family of coefficient-defined finite-dimensional tests of the
form \eqref{eq:finite-dimensional-triangular-test} is lossless on the full
operational state space.  More precisely, for any finite collection
$(C_j,B_j)_{j=1}^N$ there is a nonzero finite-rank pure central state whose
complete restarted response is zero for every one of these tests.  Likewise,
no finite product family of scalar area/covariance probes is norming.
Consequently no fixed finite-dimensional scalarization admits a continuous
decoder to the full operational state whenever a central axis is infinite
dimensional.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2606.15432, 'A Concavity Theorem for the Parisi PDE'] Fix \(\gamma\in\Opendenseset_\alpha\), and set
\[
    \sfq(s):=\int_0^s\gamma(r)\,\dd r,
    \qquad
    q_\gamma:=\sfq(1),
    \qquad
    \sfp(s):=\frac{\sfq(s)}{q_\gamma},
    \qquad
    \zeta:=\sfp^{-1}.
\]
Let \(\Phi_\gamma\) solves the following conventional Parisi PDE
\[
\begin{cases}
-\partial_t\Phi_\gamma(t,x)
=
\dfrac{q_\gamma}{2}
\left(
\partial_{xx}\Phi_\gamma(t,x)
+
\zeta(t)\bigl(\partial_x\Phi_\gamma(t,x)\bigr)^2
\right),
& (t,x)\in[0,1)\times\mathbb R,
\\[0.5ex]
\Phi_\gamma(1,x)=\log\cosh x,
& x\in\mathbb R.
\end{cases}
\]
Then,
\[
    \Psi^\gamma(s,x)=\Phi_\gamma(\sfp(s),x),
    \qquad (s,x)\in[0,1]\times\mathbb R .
\]

[Lemma lem:index_kernel of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] Let $(\sigma,\rho,m,b)$ specify a NURS orbit
\[
\mathcal{O}=(\sigma\circ\rho^j)_{j=a}^b,
\qquad a=b-2^m+1.
\]
Conditional on $(\sigma,\rho,m,b)$, the index selected by NURS satisfies
\[
p_{\mathrm{index}}(i \mid \sigma, \rho, m, b)
=
\frac{P_{\beta}(\sigma \circ \rho^i)}
{\sum_{j=a}^{b} P_{\beta}(\sigma \circ \rho^j)}
=
\frac{w(\sigma \circ \rho^i)}
{\sum_{j=a}^{b} w(\sigma \circ \rho^j)},
\qquad i\in\{a,\dots,b\},
\]
and $p_{\mathrm{index}}(i \mid \sigma, \rho, m, b)=0$ for $i\notin\{a,\dots,b\}$.

[Prop propThreeAnnulus of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] For every $\beta>0$, every integer $n\geqslant 2$, and $\mathcal{K}>0$, $\rho_0>0$, $0\leqslant c<n-2$ there are $0<r_0<1$, $0<\delta<1$, and $C>0$ such that the following holds. 
    
    Let $(X,\mathrm{d},\mathcal{H}^n)$ be an $\mathrm{RCD}(-\eta,n)$ space, with $\eta\geqslant 0$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\Sigma \subset X$ satisfies (def:Codimension of the paper) with $k=2$ and the choices of $\mathcal{K},\rho_0,c$ above: in particular, $\Sigma$ has codimension greater than $2$. Moreover, $X\setminus\Sigma$ is (locally isometric to) a smooth Riemannian manifold;
        \item $|\mathrm{Ric}| \leqslant \eta$ on $X\setminus \Sigma$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Let $x\in X$, and assume $\{f_i\}_{i=1}^n$ are harmonic functions on $B_4(x)$. Denote
    \[ 
    D:=\sum_{i,j} \fint_{B_4(x)} |\nabla f_i \cdot \nabla f_j - \delta_{ij}|\mathrm{d}\mathcal{H}^n.
    \]
    Assume $D+\eta\leqslant \delta$. Then there is a symmetric matrix $A_{ij}$ with $\|A_{ij}\| < C(D+\eta^{1/2})$ such that $\widetilde{f}_i := f_i + \sum A_{ij}f_j$ satisfy
    \[ \sum_{i,j} \fint_{B_{r_0}(x)} |\nabla \widetilde{f}_i\cdot \nabla \widetilde{f}_j - \delta_{ij}|\ensuremath{\mathrm d}\mathcal{H}^n \leqslant r_0^{1-\beta} (D+\eta^{1/2}). \]

[Proposition prop:Higgs-cutoff-detailed of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] After passing to one subsequence, there are a nonzero orthogonal projection
$q\in W^{1,2}(M,\operatorname{End} E)$ and $\pi=\operatorname{Id}_E-q$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \pi^*=\pi=\pi^2,
 \qquad q\bar\partial_E\pi=0,
 \qquad q\theta\pi=0
\end{equation}
in the distributional sense.  The projection $\pi$ defines a coherent
Higgs subsheaf $\mathcal F\subset E$, and $q$ represents the nonzero Higgs
quotient $\mathcal Q=E/\mathcal F$.  On a Riemann surface this quotient is
an honest Higgs vector bundle.

body:
[Lem positive density of arXiv:2604.21663, 'Large deviations for non-irreducible Markov chains on Euclidean spaces'] Assume~(hyp: pseudo lsc density of the paper). 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item 
		The sets $(\rho^k)^{-1}((0,\infty))$ are open subsets of $(\mathbb R^d \cup\{x_{\mathrm{init}}\})\times \mathbb R^d$ for all $k\in \mathbb N$.
		\item The set $\tilde \rho^{-1}((0,\infty))$ is an open subset of $(\mathbb R^d \cup\{x_{\mathrm{init}}\})\times \mathbb R^d$.
		\item Let $x\in \mathbb R^d \cup\{x_{\mathrm{init}}\}$, $y\in \mathbb R^d$, and $u\in \mathcal W$. If $\rho(x,uy)>0$, then $\rho^{k}(x,y)>0$, where $k=|u|+1$.
		\item 
		Let $x\in \mathbb R^d \cup\{x_{\mathrm{init}}\}$, and $y,z\in \mathbb R^d$.
		If $\rho^k(x,y)>0$ for some $k\in \mathbb N$ and $\rho^l(y,z)>0$ for some $l\in\mathbb N$, then $\rho^{k+l}(x,z)>0$.
	In particular,  
	\begin{equation*}
		\big(\tilde \rho(x,y)>0,\ \tilde \rho (y,z)>0\big)\Rightarrow\tilde \rho(x,z)>0.
	\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}
title: Lem positive density of arXiv:2604.21663

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] We keep the above notation: recall that $(\bT,\boo)$ is an infinite GW tree whose offspring distribution $\nu$ is supercritical, that we denote by $\tau_n$ is a GW tree with offspring distribution $\mu$ conditioned to have $n$ vertices for all sufficiently large $n$, and that $(\bT,\boo)$ and $\tau_n$ are independent. We assume that $\mu$ satisfies (\ref{hypostaintro}) and that $\nu$ satisfies (\ref{defmusiintro}).  We furthermore assume that there exists $\ttb \ino \big(\tfrac{2\alpha}{\alpha -1} , \infty \big)$ such that $\sum_{k\in \bbN} k^{1+ 2\ttb} \nu (k) \leko \infty$. 
Recall from (\ref{spacdefintro}) the definition of the spaces $\ftau_n$ and $\bcR_n$. 
We denote by $(T_H, d_H, \mathtt r_h, \ttm_H)$ the normalized $\alpha$-stable L\'evy tree and by 
$(T_{H, W} , d_{H, W}, \mathtt r_{H, W}, \ttm_{H, W})$ the normalized Brownian cactus with $\alpha$-stable branching mechanism as defined above. Recall that $\bbM$ is the space 
of isometry classes of pointed measured compact metric spaces equipped with the Gromov--Hausdorff--Prokhorov distance. 
Then, \emph{conditionally given the environment} $(\bT, \boo)$, the following joint convergence 
\begin{equation}

\big( \ftau_n, \bcR_n \big) \underset{n\rightarrow \infty}{- \!\!\! - \!\!\! - \!\!\! \longrightarrow }  \Big(\big(T_H,d_H,\mathtt r_H,\ttm_H\big)\, ;\, \big(T_{H,W},d_{H,W},\mathtt r_{H,W},\ttm_{H,W}\big)\Big)
\end{equation}
holds weaky on $\bbM^2$ equipped with the product topology. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition def:classicalStochStab of arXiv:2604.28068, 'Mean-square Stability and Bifurcations for Dissipative SDEs'] Suppose that $x^*$ is an equilibrium of the SDE (equation eq:main_d of the paper) and let
$X$ be a global solution with initial data $X_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Then $Y=X-x^*$ is a solution of the centered SDE (equation eq:main_YSDE of the paper) with $Y_0=X_0-x^*$. We say that the equilibrium  $x^*$ is
\begin{enumerate}
\item stable in probability for $t\geq 0$ if  for any  $s\geq 0$ and $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\lim_{Y_0\to 0}\mathbb{P}\left[\sup_{t>s}\|Y(t)\|>\varepsilon\right]=0;
\]
\item asymptotically stable in probability if  it is stable in probability and 
\[
\lim_{Y_0\to 0}\mathbb{P}\left[\lim_{t\to\infty}\|Y(t)\|=0\right]=1;
\]
\item pth-moment stable if for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a $\delta> 0$ such that
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\|Y(t)\|^p\right]<\varepsilon,\quad t\geq 0,
\]
whenever $\|Y_0\|^p<\delta$; if $p=2$, the equilibrium is said to be mean-square stable;
\item globally pth-moment asymptotically stable if  it is pth-moment stable, and for all $Y_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\|Y(t)\|^p\right]=0;
\] 
if $p=2$, the equilibrium is said to be mean-square asymptotically stable;
\item a.s.~stable if  for any $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta> 0$ such that
\[
\|Y(t)\|<\varepsilon,\quad t\geq 0,\quad a.s,
\] 
whenever $\|Y_0\|<\delta$;
\item globally a.s.~asymptotically stable if  for all $Y_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$, 
\[
\lim_{t\to \infty}\|Y(t)\|=0\quad a.s.
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:classicalStochStab of arXiv:2604.28068

body:
[Definition def:partialflow of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(N\) be a compact manifold.
A \emph{semiflow} on \(N\) is a continuous map \(\varphi\) mapping a subset \(U\subset N\times \mathbb{R}\) to \(N\), which satisfies that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for each \(x\in N\), \(\{t\in \mathbb{R}:(x,t)\in U\}\) is a closed interval of \(\mathbb{R}\) and contains \(0\).
\item if \((x,t)\in U\), then \((\varphi(x,t),-t)\in U\),
\item \(\varphi(x,0)=x\) and \(\varphi(\varphi(x,t_{1}),t_{2})=\varphi(x,t_{1}+t_{2})\).
\end{enumerate}
title: Semiflow

[Definition 12 (Schur multiplier) of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let \(\mathcal{M}_n\) denote the space of \(n \times n\) real matrices and \(E_{i,j}\) the elementary matrix whose only non-zero entry is in position \((i,j)\). 
Let \(d,n \in \mathbb{N}\) and let
\[
\mathfrak{m}(d) = \{m_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}}\}_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}=1}^n
\]
be a multi-dimensional matrix with real entries. The \(d\)-linear Schur multiplier \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathfrak{m}(d)} : \mathcal{M}_n \times \cdots \times \mathcal{M}_n 
\to \mathcal{M}_n\) is
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak{M}_{m(d)}(X_1,\dots,X_d) = \sum_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}=1}^n m_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}} x^{(1)}_{j_1,j_2} \cdots x^{(d)}_{j_d,j_{d+1}} E_{j_1,j_{d+1}}.
\end{equation}
title: Schur multiplier
