Then, for $\eta > 0$ small enough, there exist constants $r_0 > 0$ and $D > 0$ such that for all $(a,b)$ satisfying $r > r_0$, $\alpha(a,b) > 0$, and $|\alpha(a,b) - \alpha_0| < \eta$, we have:
$$\Big|\frac{1}{2i\pi}\int_{x_c + i\R}\frac{\phi^{z_0}(x)\gamma(x,Y^+(x),Z^+(x))e^{-ax-bY^+(x)}}{\partial_y\gamma_+(x,Y^+(x))} dx\Big| + |I_2(a,b)| \leq D e^{-r(\cos(\alpha)x_c + \sin(\alpha)Y^+(x_c))}$$

body:
[Lem 29 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The function $V$ defined by \eqref{e:freeprob.V} is strictly convex on the interval $(z_0,+\infty)$, with $V(z)\to\infty$ as $z\to\infty$.
As a consequence, $V$ has a unique minimizer on the interval $[z_0,+\infty)$, which we denote $z_{\min}$.

\begin{proof} For $z>z_0$, we calculate
    \beq
        
        V'(z)
        = 1 - \alpha \frac{m_2(z)}{m(z)^2} \sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j
            \bigg(\frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2\,.
    \eeq
Recall that $m:(\hw_1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ is strictly decreasing, and we have
$\alpha - \hv_j m(z) > 0$ for all $z>z_0$. It follows that, on  the interval
$(z_0,\infty)$, the function
    \[
    \frac{m(z)}{\alpha-\hv_j m(z)}
    = \frac{1}{\alpha/m(z)-\hv_j}
    \]
is strictly decreasing, \emph{regardless of the sign of $\hv_j$}. Consequently, in \eqref{e:fp-V-pr}, each term
    \[      \bigg(\frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2\]
is strictly decreasing on $(z_0,\infty)$, again \emph{regardless of the sign of $\hv_j$}. In the special case $s=1$, we have $m_2(z)=m(z)^2$, so we conclude in this case that $V'$ is strictly increasing on the interval $(z_0,\infty)$. For $s\ge2$, we note that $m_2(z)/m(z)^2$ is positive, and
    \[
        \frac{d}{dz}\bigg[ \frac{m_2(z)}{m(z)^2}\bigg]
        = \frac{2}{m(z)^3} \Big(m_2(z)^2 - m(z)m_3(z)\Big)
        < 0
    \]
by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. It therefore follows in this case as well that $V'$ is strictly increasing, and so $V$ is strictly convex, on the interval $(z_0,\infty)$.
Finally, as $z\to\infty$, $m(z) \to 0$. Therefore the first term of $V(z)$ tends to $\infty$ while the second term remains bounded, and so $V(z) \to \infty$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 29 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.06489, 'The Missing Central Limit Theorems for Local Functionals of Berry's Random Wave Model'] For any order $q\geq 2$ and space dimension $d\geq 2$, the random variable $\frac{h(q,R)}{\sqrt{\var h(q,R)}}$ converges in total variation and 1-Wasserstein distance
    to a standard Gaussian random variable as $R\to\infty$.

    Moreover, if $F(R)=\int_{B_R}f(u_1(x))dx$ is given by a nontrivial local observable with Hermite decomposition
    \begin{equation*}
        f(x)=\sum_{q\geq 2}\frac{a_q}{q!}H_q(x),
        \qquad
        a_q=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_\R f(z)H_q(z) e^{-z^2/2}dz,
    \end{equation*}
    such that either $d=2$ and $a_4\neq 0$ or $\sum_{q\geq 3}\frac{a_q^2C_{q,d}}{(q!)^2}<\infty$,
    then $\frac{F(R)}{\sqrt{\var F(R)}}$ converges in 1-Wasserstein distance to a standard Gaussian random variable as $R\to\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.06489

[Theorem theorem-1invasion of arXiv:2504.04943, 'Emergence of \bl microbial \bl host dormancy \\ \bl during \bl a persistent virus epidemic'] Assume $(\widetilde n_{2a}, \widetilde n_{2d}, \widetilde n_{2i}, \widetilde n_{3})$ to be a coordinatewise positive and asymptotically stable equilibrium of~(equation 4dimvirus of the paper) (so that (equation viruscoexcond2 of the paper) holds, which implies $mv>r+v$),
    
    and $\lambda_2 - \lambda_1 \neq \frac{qD \widetilde n_3 (r\kappa\mu_1-v\sigma)}{(r+v)(\kappa\mu_1+\sigma)}$. Then we have for all sufficiently small $\beta>0$ that 
    \[ 
    \lim_{K\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\Big( T_\beta < T_0^{1} \, \Big| \, \mathbf N^K(0) = \widetilde{\mathbf M}_K \Big) = 1-s_{1a}, \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\thesection.\arabic{equation}}
    \]
    where the number $s_{1a} \in (0,1]$ is uniquely characterized as the first coordinate of the 
    smallest positive solution of the system of equations~(equation s1as1i of the paper) below. Here,
    \begin{enumerate}[(I)]
    \item $s_{1a} = 1$ holds if the \mbox{$(\rm{Inv}_{1 \nrightarrow 2,3})$\color{black}}\ condition~(equation 1doesn'tinvade2 of the paper) holds,
    \item whereas $s_{1a}<1$ holds if the \mbox{$(\rm{Inv}_{1 \rightarrow 2,3})$\color{black}}\ condition~(equation 1invades2 of the paper) holds.
    In this case, conditional on the event $\{ T_\beta < T_0^1 \}$ we have
    \[ \lim_{K\to\infty} \frac{T_\beta}{\log K } = \frac{1}{\widetilde \lambda} \qquad \text{ in probability}, \] where $\widetilde \lambda$ is the largest eigenvalue of the matrix $\widetilde J$ defined in~(equation Jtildedef of the paper) below (which is positive if~(equation 1invades2 of the paper) holds).
    \end{enumerate}
    Finally, in both cases, conditional on the event $\{ T_0^1 < T_\beta \}$, we have
    \[ \lim_{K\to\infty} \frac{T_0^1}{\log K } = 0 \qquad \text{ in probability}.        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\thesection.\arabic{equation}} \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

r_n^{\mathrm{opt}}\in\{\lfloor\ell n\rfloor,\lfloor\ell n\rfloor+1\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\{\ell n\}<1-c-\frac{\varepsilon_n}{|A|}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
r_n^{\mathrm{opt}}=\lfloor\ell n\rfloor,
\]
whereas
\[
\{\ell n\}>1-c+\frac{\varepsilon_n}{|A|}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
r_n^{\mathrm{opt}}=\lfloor\ell n\rfloor+1.
\]
Consequently, whenever
\[
\left|\{\ell n\}-(1-c)\right|>\frac{\varepsilon_n}{|A|},
\]
the optimal threshold is unique and satisfies
\[
r_n^{\mathrm{opt}}
=
\lfloor\ell n+c\rfloor.
\]

[Corollary 19 (Finite volume OZ for a single crossing) of arXiv:2604.21669, 'Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts:\\ II. order-order interface convergence'] Let \(0<J<U\) satisfy \(\sinh 2J=e^{-2U}\). There are \(c_0,c>0\) such that for any sequence \(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{c_0}\geq k_n\geq c_0\ln(n)\), there exists \(n_0\geq 1\) such that for \(n\geq n_0\), \(m_n \geq c_0n\), there exists a probability measure \(\bndMeas_n\) on \(\SetRootMarkBackCont \times \SetRootMarkForwCont\) satisfying
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \(\bndMeas_n\) is supported on pairs \((\eta_L,\eta_R)\) with \(\norm{\displace(\eta_L)}_{\infty},\norm{\displace(\eta_R)}_{\infty} \leq k_n^2\),
		\item defining \(v(\eta_L,\eta_R) = v_R-v_L-\displace(\eta_L)-\displace(\eta_R)\), for any \(f\) function of \(\calC\),
		\begin{multline*}
			\Big|\sum_{m\geq 0}\sum_{\eta_L,\eta_R} \bndMeas_n(\eta_L,\eta_R) \OZ_{v(\eta_L,\eta_R)}\big[f(v_L + \eta_L\concatenate\bar{\eta}_1^M \concatenate \eta_R)\big]
			\\
			-\Phi_{n}\big[f(\calC)\bgiven v_R\in \calC\big]\Big|
			\leq
			\norm{f}_{\infty}e^{-ck_n},
		\end{multline*}where \(\eta_1^M \sim \OZ_{v(\eta_L,\eta_R)}\).
	\end{itemize}
	The same result holds for \(\calC', v_L',v_R'\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite volume OZ for a single crossing

$$
\Hol(\C^{mn})\oplus \oplus_{i<j} \overline{\C[\partial_{z^1_j},\cdots, \partial_{z^n_j}]\omega_{ij}},
$$ 
subject to the following relations:
\begin{itemize}
\item $f(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij}\cdot g(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij}=0$, for $f(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij}, g(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij}\in \overline{\C[\partial_{z^1_j},\cdots, \partial_{z^n_j}]\omega_{ij}}$,
\item $ 
\zz_{ij}^{\xalpha}\partial_{\zz_j}^{\xbeta}\omega_{ij}=

(-1)^{\alpha_1+\cdots +\alpha_n} \prod_{i=1}^n \frac{\beta_i!}{(\beta_i-\alpha_i)!} \, \partial_{\zz_j}^{\xbeta-\xalpha}\omega_{ij} & \alpha_i\le \beta_i \text{ for all } i \\
0 & \alpha_i>\beta_i \text{ for some } i \\

$$g(\partial_{\zz_j})(f(\partial_{\zz_i})\omega_{ij}h(\partial_{\zz_k})\omega_{jk})+h(\partial_{\zz_k})(g(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{jk}f(\partial_{\zz_i})\omega_{ki})+f(\partial_{\zz_i})(h(\partial_{\zz_k})\omega_{ki}g(\partial_{\zz_j})\omega_{ij})=0.$$

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C002 v1. For every fixed alpha>=1024 and c>0, m=ceil(alpha d), iid a_i~N(0,I_d), and fixed unit x_*, use f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2 and eta=c/log d. With probability tending to one there is a sample-dependent point x_0 with ||x_0-x_*||=1/10 whose unmodified GD iterates diverge in norm. Take x_0=x_*+(1/10)u, where u is the signed unit direction of a_1 aligned with its signal projection. Its first update has norm Omega_(alpha,c)(d/log d). Writing S=A^T A/m and B=H_*/2, on S>=I/2 and ||B||=O_alpha(log d), every x of norm R satisfies ||x-eta grad f(x)|| >=eta R^3/4-(1+eta||B||)R. The first update enters the region where this lower bound is at least 2R. The logarithmic bound on B uses C001. This refutes a simultaneous guarantee for every point in the fixed ball; it does not refute random independent starts or convergence along incoherent trajectories.

    \begin{enumerate}

        \item if it is $\delta$-slim, then it is $2\delta + \frac{1}{2}$-hyperbolic.

[Definition d.fpc of arXiv:2510.07682, 'From tug-of-war to Brownian Boost: \\ explicit ODE solutions for player-funded stochastic-'] For $h \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$, the forward play-cone $F_h$ of $h$ is set equal to 
$$
F_h \, = \, \Big\{ \, (k,\ell) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \times \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}_+: \vert k - h \vert \leq \ell \, , \, \vert k-h \vert + \ell  \in 2\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}} \, \Big\} \, .
$$

Let $S \in \mathcal{S}$ (and recall the formulation of the strategy space~$\mathcal{S}$ from Section~(s.tlp of the paper)). A  {\em Mina deviation point} is an element $(q,\ell) \in F_h$ for which 
there exists a trajectory $\psi: \llbracket 0, \ell \rrbracket \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $\psi(0) = h$ and $\psi(\ell) = q$
such that $S(\psi) \neq b_q$.
Write  $\mathsf{D}_-(S,h) \subseteq F_h$ for the set of Mina deviation points. The strategy $S$ is  {\em deviating for Mina} if  $\mathsf{D}_-(S,h) \neq \emptyset$.
 A {\em Maxine deviation point} is an element $(q,\ell) \in F_h$ such that  $S(\psi) \not= a_q$ for some path~$\psi$ as above. Write $\mathsf{D}_+(S,h)$ for the set of these points; if  $\mathsf{D}_+(S,h) \not= \emptyset$, then $S$ is deviating for Maxine.

[Lemma lem.inv_lo of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $N$ be a fixed positive integer, $c > 0$ and $\epsilon > 0$.
    Then there exist $r=r(N, c, \epsilon)$ and  $v=v(N, c, \epsilon)$ such that the following holds.
    
    For any sequence $X_1, \dots, X_n$ of independent random variables on $\mathbb{Z}$
    such that $\mathbb P(X_i = j) = \frac {a_{i,j}} N$ where $a_{i,j} \in \mathbb{Z}$, 
    $\mathcal{Q}(X_i) = \max_{j} \frac{a_{i,j}} N \le \frac 1 2$
    and $\mathcal{Q}(X_1 + \dots + X_n) \ge \frac c {\sqrt n}$
    there
    exists a symmetric GAP ${\bf A}$
    of rank at most 
    $r$ and volume at most $v$
    such that all but at most $\epsilon n$ of random variables $X_i$
    have their support contained in ${\bf A}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let G be a finite simple graph on n >= 3 vertices. The closure cl(G) is obtained from G by repeatedly adding an edge between any two non-adjacent vertices u, v with deg(u) + deg(v) >= n, until no such pair remains; the resulting graph cl(G) does not depend on the order in which edges are added. Then G is Hamiltonian if and only if cl(G) is Hamiltonian. [Bondy and Chvatal (1976); see Diestel, Graph Theory]
title: Bondy-Chvatal Closure Lemma

Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). After the optimism reading was refuted (P20), the gain was located row by row: the per-evaluation-row relative-score gain of the long-only stack over least squares against the bootstrap variance of the least-squares stack at that row. P22 (a) REFUTED at the pre-registered 0.2: the within-cell median Spearman between a row's gain and the least-squares variance load at that row is 0.13 over the 40 EMIT cells (positive in 36 of 40; 0.37 on Y2, 0.01 on Y1); (b) HELD on Y2, REFUTED as an every-group claim: the top-decile-load rows carry 47 pct of Y2's gain (a uniform spread gives 10) but only 11 pct on Y1 (20 on Y3, 32 on Y4); (c) HELD: across the 40 EMIT cells the gain rank-correlates 0.54 with the variance-load share of least squares' error, and 0.65 with the share the constraint removes (least squares minus nn1) - the between-cell statistic that optimism (P20) failed to be; (d) REFUTED as written: the OCO-2 top-decile share reaches 0.40 on sco2, but as the share of a gain of -0.55 pct it is the ratio of two near-zero numbers and does not test the clause; falsifier (within-cell correlation at or below zero) not triggered. Reading: where the gain is large (Y2, +18) it sits where least squares is uncertain - row-level rank correlation 0.37, 47 pct of the gain on the tenth of rows with the largest variance; where it is modest (+5 to +6) it is spread over the rows; between cells the variance-load share of least squares' error predicts the gain (0.54) and the variance the constraint removes predicts it better (0.65). The calibration and evaluation rows share the same target-norm distribution, so this is not a split shift; the gain leans toward the small-norm evaluation rows the reported metric weights most. Cell level: the variance the constraint removes (least squares' bootstrap variance share minus the long-only stack's) predicts the gain within every output group (Spearman 0.79, 0.87, 0.54, 0.43 on Y1-Y4; 0.69 across 40 cells with the group effect removed), while the L1 norm of the least-squares weights does not survive the group adjustment (0.02): the constraint pays what it saves in estimation variance at the rows it is scored on. Fresh-split replication (split C, SPLIT_SEED 11): P23 (a) REFUTED at the per-group 0.5, HELD in the aggregate: on split C the within-group Spearman between the gain and the variance removed is +0.59, +0.49, +0.64, +0.22 on Y1..Y4 and +0.74 across the 40 cells with the group effect removed (split B: +0.69); (b) REFUTED: the split-B variance-removed share predicts the split-C gain only on Y1 and Y2 (+0.72, +0.47; Y3 +0.09, Y4 -0.24; demeaned +0.17), and the split-B gain itself predicts the split-C gain only weakly (Y1 +0.82, Y4 +0.47, Y2 +0.15, Y3 -0.14); (c) HELD: the long-only stack beats least squares on 35 of 40 split-C cells (mean +9.59 against +8.83 on split B); falsifier (any group at or below 0.2, or the demeaned correlation at or below 0.3) not triggered.

[Proposition 15 (The radial pole need not be subadditive) of arXiv:2609.02595, 'Minimal Radial Sub-Gamma Envelopes for Infinitely Divisible Random Vectors'] Let \(N_1,N_2\) be independent Poisson variables with mean one, put
\[
 x_1=(-2,-2),\qquad x_2=(-2,-1),
\]
and define
\begin{equation}
 X=N_1x_1+N_2x_2-(x_1+x_2).
\end{equation}
Then \(\Sigma\) is positive definite, but for
\[
 t_1=(-2,1),\qquad t_2=(-1,2),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 C_X(t_1)=\frac{35}{39},\qquad
 C_X(t_2)=0,
 \qquad C_X(t_1+t_2)=1.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 C_X(t_1+t_2)>C_X(t_1)+C_X(t_2).
\end{equation}

[Definition ATTRACTOR of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let $\Phi$ be an RDS. A random compact set $\mathcal{A}$ is { called pullback attractor} if 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [1)] $\mathcal{A}$ is invariant under \( \Phi \).
		\item [2)] For every compact set $K\subseteq  \mathcal{X}$ 
		we have
		\[ \lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \sup\limits_{x\in K} d(\Phi^t_{\theta_{-t}\omega}(x), \mathcal{A}(\omega)  )=0~~~\mathbb{P}-a.s. \]
	\end{enumerate}
	We call $\mathcal{A}$ a {weak attractor} if the convergence in 2) holds in probability instead of almost surely. The set $\mathcal{A}$ is called a {(weak) point attractor} if it satisfies the properties stated above, assuming that the compact set $K$ in condition 2) consists of a single point.~A (weak) point attractor is said to be {minimal} if it is contained in every other (weak) point attractor.
title: Definition ATTRACTOR of arXiv:2603.12774

\cref{old-lem:wall-defect-splitting}, and suppose that $F$ and $K$ are global
minimizers for $\Phi$ and $\Phi^-$, respectively.  For $s>0$,
write $s^{-1}A:=\{x/s:x\in A\}$.  Given $s_j>0$ with $s_j\to\infty$, set
\begin{equation}
 F_j:=s_j^{-1}F,
 \qquad K_j:=s_j^{-1}K.
\end{equation}
After passing to one common subsequence, there exist global minimizers
$G,L\subset H$ for $\Phi$ and $\Phi^-$, respectively, such that
\begin{align}
 \chi_{K_j}&\to\chi_L\quad\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}},&
 D\chi_{K_j}&\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}D\chi_L,&
 |D\chi_{K_j}|&\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}|D\chi_L|,
 \\
 \chi_{F_j}&\to\chi_G\quad\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}},&
 D\chi_{F_j}&\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}D\chi_G,&
 |D\chi_{F_j}|&\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}|D\chi_G|
 
\end{align}
and
\begin{equation}
 G=H\setminus L,
 \qquad
 |D\chi_G|=\HH^n\llcorner P+|D\chi_L|.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2608.17562, '2608.17562'] Let
  $Z \sim \mathcal{F}(\alpha)$ for some $\alpha > 0$,
  and let 
  $W$ be a random variable whose distribution function $F_W$
  is absolutely continuous on $[K, +\infty)$ for some $K>0$, with 
    density function~$f_W$.

 Let also $\mathcal{H}$ be a set of functions $h : \R \to \R$ such that $\esp[\vert h(W) \vert] < \infty$ for every $h$, the Stein solution $g_{h}$ exists, is absolutely continuous and satisfies \eqref{H_1} 

 for almost every $x > 0$,
 for some $\beta \in (-\infty, \alpha)$ and $C_{1} > 0$ independent of $h$.
 Then, we have 
\begin{align*}
\underset{h \in \mathcal{H}}{\sup} \ \vert \esp[h(W)] - \esp[h(Z)] \vert \leq \underset{h \in \mathcal{H}}{\sup}\ \vert &\esp[h(W)\ind_{\lb W \leq K \rb}] - \esp[h(Z)]F_{W}(K)\vert\\
		&  + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - \beta}C_{1}F_{W}(K) + C_{1}\int_{K}^\infty  r^{\beta}F_{W}(r)\bigg\vert\frac{f_{W}(r)}{F_{W}(r)} - \frac{\alpha}{r^{\alpha + 1}}\bigg\vert \dif r.\numberthis
\end{align*}
title: Lemma 16 of arXiv:2608.17562

body:
Let X and Y be Banach spaces and T : X -> Y a bounded linear operator that is surjective. Then T is an open map: the image of every open subset of X is open in Y; equivalently there is c > 0 such that the image of the unit ball of X contains the ball of radius c in Y. Corollaries: a bounded linear bijection between Banach spaces has a bounded inverse (the bounded inverse theorem), and two complete norms on one vector space that are comparable in one direction are equivalent. Completeness of BOTH spaces is needed: the identity from (C[0,1], sup norm) to (C[0,1], L^1 norm) is bounded and bijective and its inverse is unbounded, the target not being complete.
X and Y Banach (complete normed) spaces
T bounded, linear and surjective

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2609.02423, '2609.02423'] Let $1<\sigma<s$, $z_N=P_NJ^\sigma u$, and
$z_{\nu,N}=\chi_{\nu,N}(D)z_N$.  On an $x$ chart take the single
weight scale $\lambda\simeq N$.  If $\tau\in\{\pm1\}$ is the sign of
$v_x$ on the chart, the commutator with
$\tau a_{\lambda,x_0}$ has the form
\begin{equation}
 \ip{i[\omega(D),\tau a_{\lambda,x_0}]z_{\nu,N}}{z_{\nu,N}}
 =\norm{Q_{x,\nu,x_0}z_N}_2^2
 +\ip{R_{x,\nu,x_0}z_N}{z_N},
\end{equation}
where
\[
 Q_{x,\nu,x_0}
 =\Op\left(
 \left(\frac\lambda R\right)^{1/2}
 \psi_0\left(\frac{\lambda(x-x_0)}R\right)
 |v_x|^{1/2}\chi_{\nu,N}\right).
\]
This uses the smooth factorization $a'=\psi_0^2$ from
\eqref{eq:aprime-square}; in particular, no nonsmooth choice of the
square root of $a'$ is involved.  On a $y$ chart the analogous
identity holds with $\mu\simeq N^{1/2}$, $y_0$, and $v_y$.  For $R$
sufficiently large,
\begin{equation}
 |\ip{R_{r,\nu,r_0}z_N}{z_N}|
 \le \frac14\sup_{r_0'\in\R}\norm{Q_{r,\nu,r_0'}z_N}_2^2
 +C_R\norm{z_N}_2^2,
\end{equation}
where $r=x$ or $y$ and $r_0=x_0$ or $y_0$.  The constants are
uniform in $N$ and the spatial centres.  For every smooth
frequency-truncated function,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{r_0\in\R}\norm{Q_{r,\nu,r_0}z_N}_2^2
 \le C_RN^3\norm{z_N}_2^2<\infty.
\end{equation}
Thus the supremum in \eqref{eq:remainder-absorb} is finite before any
absorption is performed.

Finally, the statement holds verbatim with $\chi_{\nu,N}$ replaced by
any of the auxiliary symbols $\Theta_{\nu,N,\ell}$,
$\ell\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, of \cref{def:chart-ladder}, with constants
uniform in $\ell$.  Indeed, the proof uses only the symbol bounds
\eqref{eq:chart-symbol} and the fact that $v_\nu$ has a fixed sign on
the support, both of which are imposed on every level in
\cref{def:chart-ladder}.

[Dfn 3. dfn: Polish functor of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Polish functor}] 
  We say that a functor $\tau$ is \textit{Polish} if there exist a functor $\tilde{\tau}$
  and, for each $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$,
  a sequence $(\tilde{\tau}_{k}(S))_{k=1}^{\infty}$ of open subsets in $\tilde{\tau}(S)$
  satisfying the following conditions.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (P\arabic*), leftmargin = *]
    \item 
      The functor $\tilde{\tau}$ is complete, separable and continuous. 
    \item 
      The functor $\tau$ is a topological subfunctor of $\tilde{\tau}$.
    \item 
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$,
      it holds that $\tau(S) = \bigcap_{k \geq 1} \tilde{\tau}_{k}(S)$.
    \item 
      Let $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$ be a root-and-distance-preserving map
      between $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}) \in \mathfrak{M},\, i=1,2$.
      Then, $\tilde{\tau}_{f}^{-1}(\tilde{\tau}_{k}(S_{2})) = \tilde{\tau}_{k}(S_{1})$
      for each $k \geq 1$. 
      In particular,
      $\tilde{\tau}_{f}^{-1}(\tau(S_{2})) = \tau(S_{1})$.
  \end{enumerate}
  We call $(\tilde{\tau}, (\tilde{\tau}_{k})_{k \geq 1})$ a \textit{Polish system} of $\tau$.
title: Dfn 3. dfn: Polish functor of arXiv:2412.08236

Let $h_{\mu_{\mathfrak{s},a}}(x_{3},x_{4},\ldots,x_{d})$ be the dominant height on the layer whose last $d-2$ coordinates are given by $x_{3},\ldots,x_{d}$. Then, we have
$$

$$

The earlier C0135-A001 says both that a clock has size m^2 log(m) and that its inverse is sqrt(t)/log(t), and later uses the different scale sqrt(t) log(t). These cannot be equivalent scales.

Let f(x)=x^2 log(x), x>=1. It is strictly increasing for x>1. If a deterministic increasing clock T_m is asymptotic to m^2 log(m), its generalized inverse is asymptotic to sqrt(2t/log(t)). [Lemma 14 of arXiv:2506.18834, '\large\bf On the random-time and finite-time ruin probability for widely dependent claim s'] Let $\xi_{i},i\geq1$ be WUOD random variables with a common distribution $V$ on $(-\infty,\infty)$
such that $E\xi_1s_1(\xi_1)<\infty$ for some positive even function $s_1(\cdot)$ on $(-\infty,\infty)$
satisfying $s_1(x)\underline{\uparrow}\infty$.
Then the following three conclusion hold.

(1) There exists a positive even function $s_2(\cdot)$ on $(-\infty,\infty)$ such that
\begin{eqnarray}
s_2(x)\underline{\uparrow}\ \infty,\ \ s_2(x)s_1^{-s+1}(x)\overline{\downarrow}\ 0\ \ \ \text{for any}\ \ \ s>1\ \ \
\text{and}\ \ \ E\xi_1s_1(\xi_1)s_2(\xi_1)<\infty.
\end{eqnarray}

(2) Write $s(\cdot)=s_1(\cdot)s_2(\cdot)$ and $V_{s(\cdot)}^+(x)=s^{-1}(x)\int_{0\le y\le x}ys(y)V(dy)+x\overline{V}(x),\ x\ge0$, then
\begin{eqnarray}
V^+_{s(\cdot)}(x)=o\big(s^{-1}_1(x)\big)\ \ \ \ \ \text{and}\ \ \ \ \ s_1^{-l}(x)=o\big(V^+_{s(\cdot)}(x)\big)
\ \ \ \text{for any}\ \ l>1,
\end{eqnarray}

(3) If $E\xi_1=0$ and there is an integer $m\ge1$ such that
$$x^ms^{-1}(x)\underline{\uparrow}\ \infty\ \ \ \ \text{and}\ \ \ x^{m-1}s^{-1}_1(x)\overline{\downarrow}\ 0,$$
then for any $\gamma>0$, $v>0$ and $0<\theta<1$, there exist $x_0=x_0\big(v,\gamma,m,\theta,V,s_1(\cdot),s_2(\cdot)\big)\ge 1$
and $C=C(x_0)>0$ such that for each integer $n\ge1$,
\begin{eqnarray}
P\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\xi_i>x\Big)\le n\overline{V}(vx)+Cs_{U,V}(n)\big(V_{s_{(\cdot)}}^+(vx)\big)^{(1-\theta)v^{-1}}
\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \text{for all}\ \ x\ge \max\{\gamma n,x_0\}.
\end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Derive d_s in d = 2 from known exponents via the Einstein relation and locate what is rigorous. Result: On the IIC of two-dimensional critical percolation (which exists, Kesten) the walk is subdiffusive with d_s = 2 d_f/d_w where d_f = 91/48 is the fractal dimension of the IIC and d_w is the walk dimension; the Einstein relation d_w = d_f + zeta with zeta the resistance exponent gives d_s = 2 d_f/(d_f + zeta), and the conjectured resistance exponent of the 2D IIC is zeta ~ 0.98 (numerically the backbone resistance exponent), giving d_s = 2 x 1.896/(1.896 + 0.98) = 1.318, matching the numerics quoted by the source; the rigorous status: Kesten proved subdiffusivity with d_w > 2, and the resistance exponent is only known to lie in an interval (zeta > 0 from Kesten; zeta <= something from the one-arm/backbone dimension). A rigorous upper bound: d_s <= 2 d_f/(d_f + zeta_min) where zeta_min is any rigorous lower bound on the resistance exponent; with zeta >= (d_f - d_backbone)?? no, the rigorous lower bound of Kesten for the resistance across an annulus of the IIC uses the number of disjoint crossings (the backbone), giving resistance >= (log n)^c at least... Kesten's bound is R(0, B(n)^c) >= n^{epsilon} for some small unexplicit epsilon. So no explicit rigorous bound on d_s beyond d_s < 4/3?? not even that. Recorded: d_s in 2D is determined by the resistance exponent through d_s = 2 d_f/(d_f + zeta) (rigorous given that the Einstein relation holds, which is a theorem for strongly recurrent graphs with the volume and resistance exponents, Barlow-Coulhon-Kumagai), so the open content is the value of zeta; for 3 <= d < 6 the existence of the IIC is the first obstacle. Key identity: d_s = 2 d_f/(d_f + zeta) on the 2D IIC (Einstein relation); d_f = 91/48 known, zeta unknown (numerically about 0.98). Obstruction: Resistance exponent of the 2D IIC unknown; IIC existence unproved for 3 <= d < 6.

body:
[Corollary 10 (Exhaustive finite-time breakdown alternative) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Let $F\colon[0,T_{\max})\times\Sigma\to\Sph^3$ be a maximal smooth
MIWF with
\[
 T_{\max}=T_{\max}(F_0)<\infty,
 \qquad W(0)\leq8\pi.
\]
Then exactly one of the following mutually exclusive alternatives
holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\Alph*)}]
 \item there are $t_j\nearrow T_{\max}$ and $x_j\in\Sigma$ such that
 \[
  |A^0_{F_{t_j}}(x_j)|^2\longrightarrow0;
 \]
 \item uniform nonumbilicity holds and the unique limit is zero:
 $\Var_{T_{\max}}=0$;
 \item uniform nonumbilicity holds, $\Var_{T_{\max}}\neq0$, and
 $\spt\Var_{T_{\max}}$ is a closed embedded orientable Lipschitz
 surface of genus zero;
 \item uniform nonumbilicity holds, $\Var_{T_{\max}}\neq0$, and
 $\spt\Var_{T_{\max}}$ is a closed embedded orientable Lipschitz
 surface of genus one.
\end{enumerate}
In alternatives \textup{(C)} and \textup{(D)}, the limit has unit
density.  No assertion made here excludes alternative \textup{(D)}.

[Theorem 2 (Large deviations principle) of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(a>1\) and \(I_a=[1,a]\). Then \(N_a(L)/L\) satisfies a large deviations principle on \([0,\infty)\) with speed \(L\) and good rate function
\[
J_a(x):=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb{R}}\{\theta x-\Lambda_a(\theta)\},
\qquad x\geq0.
\]
That is, for every Borel set \(A\subset[0,\infty)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
-\inf_{x\in A^\circ}J_a(x)
&\le \liminf_{L\to\infty}\frac{1}{L}\log\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{N_a(L)}{L}\in A\right) \\
&\le \limsup_{L\to\infty}\frac{1}{L}\log\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{N_a(L)}{L}\in A\right) \le -\inf_{x\in \overline{A}}J_a(x),
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(A^\circ\) and \(\overline A\) denote the interior and closure of \(A\) in the relative topology of \([0,\infty)\). Moreover, \(J_a\) is strictly convex on \((0,\infty)\) and vanishes only at \(\lambda_a=\frac{1}{4\pi}\left(1-\frac{1}{a}\right)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Kind:moved. Target:1. Status:proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.

## Statement

Let E be any real m-by-p matrix, B any m-by-r matrix and A any r-by-p matrix. Set e=||E||op and h=||B||op^2+||A||op^2. For any eta>0 with eta(e+h)<=1/2, put

 Phi(E,B,A)=E-eta(BB^T E+E A^T A)+eta^2 E A^T B^T E.

Then ||Phi(E,B,A)||op<=||E||op. In particular, when E=BA-Delta, Phi is exactly the residual after one simultaneous GD step for ||BA-Delta||F^2/2. No rank assumption, Gaussian assumption, balance or commutation is required. The lemma gives a sufficient small-step condition, not an optimal one. It does not claim spectral monotonicity at an arbitrary loss-decreasing step.

The hardest point is that orthogonal dilation commutes with this particular nonlinear update after compression. The proof explicitly checks the quadratic term. The algebraic dilation is the classical Julia/Halmos construction; its primary provenance is P. L. Robinson, "Julia operators and Halmos dilations", arXiv:1803.09329, Theorem0 p.1 and Theorem1 p.2. The rectangular block here is the Julia operator with its column blocks switched; Theorem2 concerns the square-space special case. The construction and its properties are proved below from an SVD rather than assumed from a named theorem. The primary source gives the classical dilation, not this GD contraction. Literature overlap and independent correctness remain unaudited.

## 1. Orthogonal residuals

First suppose m=p=N and E=eQ for an orthogonal N-by-N matrix Q, with e>0. Multiplying Phi/e on the right by Q^T gives

 (Phi/e)Q^T=I-eta(DD^T+CC^T)+eta^2 e C D^T,

where D=B and C=Q A^T. Indeed E A^T B^T E/e=e Q A^T B^T Q, which becomes e C D^T after right multiplication by Q^T. This checks the order of the quadratic term.

Let W=[D C] be N-by-2r and set

 H = [[I_r,0],[-eta e I_r,I_r]].

The preceding matrix equals Z=I-eta W H W^T. Direct expansion gives

 I-Z^T Z = eta W[H+H^T-eta H^T W^T W H]W^T.

Now ||W||op^2<=||D||op^2+||C||op^2=h,

 H+H^T >=(2-eta e)I, and ||H||op<=1+eta e.

The first bound follows either from the 2-by-2 scalar block eigenvalues 2+eta e and 2-eta e, or the quadratic-form inequality 2|x^T y|<=||x||^2+||y||^2. The second follows by writing H=I+N, where the sole nonzero off-diagonal block of N has operator norm eta e. Consequently

 H+H^T-eta H^T W^T W H
 >=[2-eta e-eta h(1+eta e)^2]I
 >=[2-1/2-(1/2)(3/2)^2]I
 =(3/8)I>=0.

Only eta e<=1/2 and eta h<=1/2 are used in this estimate; they follow from the stated sufficient condition. It follows that Z^T Z<=I and ||Z||op<=1. Right multiplication by Q^T preserves the norm, so ||Phi||op<=e in this orthogonal case.

## 2. Explicit orthogonal dilation of an arbitrary rectangular contraction

Suppose e>0 and let F=E/e, so ||F||op<=1. The matrices I_m-FF^T and I_p-F^TF are positive semidefinite. Their positive semidefinite square roots define the (m+p)-by-(p+m) real matrix

 Q = [[F, (I_m-FF^T)^(1/2)],[(I_p-F^TF)^(1/2),-F^T]].

This is square because m+p=p+m. It is orthogonal. For a direct verification, take an SVD F=U Sigma V^T. It gives the exact intertwining identity

 F(I_p-F^TF)^(1/2)=(I_m-FF^T)^(1/2)F,

since each paired singular direction contributes the scalar sigma_i sqrt(1-sigma_i^2) on both sides, and the unmatched zero singular directions contribute zero. Multiplying Q Q^T therefore gives identity diagonal blocks and zero cross blocks. Thus Q Q^T=I, which for a finite square real matrix also implies Q^T Q=I. In particular the upper-left m-by-p compression of eQ is E. This proof also covers rectangular F with singular value1; no inverse of a defect square root is used.

## 3. Compression preserves the nonlinear update

Use the orthogonal residual Etilde=eQ, the padded factor Btilde=[B;0_(p-by-r)], and Atilde=[A,0_(r-by-m)]. These are compatible factors in the enlarged N=m+p dimensional problem, with ||Btilde||op=||B||op and ||Atilde||op=||A||op. The step condition is unchanged, so section1 gives ||Phi(Etilde,Btilde,Atilde)||op<=e.

Consider its first m rows and first p columns. The linear terms compress to BB^T E and E A^T A because Btilde Btilde^T and Atilde^T Atilde are zero off their leading diagonal blocks. For the quadratic term, the first m rows of Etilde Atilde^T equal E A^T, and the first p columns of Btilde^T Etilde equal B^T E. Hence the leading m-by-p block of

 Etilde Atilde^T Btilde^T Etilde

is exactly E A^T B^T E, not a block contaminated by the defect square roots. Therefore the full compressed residual is exactly Phi(E,B,A). Compression by orthogonal coordinate projections cannot increase operator norm, proving the lemma. If e=0, every term of Phi is zero, completing the missing degenerate case.

## Relation to GD and limitations

Multiplication of B_next=B-eta E A^T and A_next=A-eta B^T E gives the displayed Phi with its positive quadratic term. Thus the lemma applies to ordinary simultaneous GD without replacing it by alternating updates, a continuous flow, or a split contraction. At larger steps the proof does not give monotonicity. It provides no statistical-risk or convergence theorem without a separate factor bound and positive-margin argument. The application is saved separately as C025. [Lemma lem6.5 of arXiv:2411.03528, '\textbf{On a boundary of the central limit theorem for strictly stationary, reversible Mar'] Suppose $\phi: [1,\infty) \to (-\infty, 0]$ is a function
that satisfies the following conditions: \hfil\break
(a) $\phi$ is strictly decreasing and convex on $[1, \infty)$; and \hfil\break
(b) one has that
\begin{equation}

\lim_{x \to \infty} \phi(x)\ =\ -\infty 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac {\phi(x)} {x}\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}

   Let $\Gamma$ denote the set of all points $x \in (1, \infty)$ (the open half line) 
such that $\phi$ is {\rm not} differentiable at $x$.
Refer to Notations (nt6.4 of the paper)(A)(B).   
For each $y \in (1, \infty) - \Gamma$, let 
$L^{(y)}: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ denote the affine function whose graph is tangent to that 
of $\phi$ at the point $(y, \phi(y))$ --- that is, the affine function that satisfies
\begin{equation}

L^{(y)}(y)\ =\ \phi(y) \indent {\rm and} \indent 
L^{(y)}(x)\ \leq\ \phi(x)\ \ {\rm for\ all}\ x \in [1, \infty). 
\end{equation}
 
   Then the following statements (I) and (II) hold:
\medskip

   (I) The following statements hold: \hfil\break 
(i) For each $x \in (1, \infty)$, $\phi(x) < \phi(1) \leq 0$. \hfil\break 
(ii) For each $y \in (1,\infty) - \Gamma$,  
$[{\rm slope\ of}\ L^{(y)}] = \phi'(y) < 0$. \hfil\break   
(iii) The function $x \mapsto \phi'(x)$ for $x \in (1,\infty) - \Gamma$, 
is nondecreasing. \hfil\break  
(iv) One has that $\lim_{x \to \infty,\, x \notin \Gamma} \phi'(x) = 0$. 
\medskip

   (II) For any negative number $D$ and any positive number 
$s$, there exists a number    
$T = T(\phi, D, s) > 1$ with the following property:

   For each $y \in [T,\infty)  - \Gamma$, the affine function 
$L^{(y)}$ in (the entire sentence of) eq.\ ((eq6.502 of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}

-s\ \leq\ [{\rm slope\ of}\ L^{(y)}]\ =\ \phi'(y)\ <\ 0 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
L^{(y)}(0)\ \leq\ D. 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem6.5 of arXiv:2411.03528

\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathbb E_\beta \sum_{x\in K} d_\mathrm{chem}(o,x)\leq (\mathbb E_\beta|K|)^2$.

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let X and Y take finitely many values with joint pmf p and marginal p_X, entropies in natural logarithms with 0 ln 0 = 0. For each x choose a pmf K_x on the values of Y with K_x(y) = p(x, y)/p_X(x) whenever p_X(x) > 0, and K_x arbitrary when p_X(x) = 0. Then H(X, Y) = H(X) + sum over x of p_X(x) H(K_x), and this sum, the conditional entropy H(Y | X), equals -sum over (x, y) with p(x, y) > 0 of p(x, y) ln(p(x, y)/p_X(x)) whatever the choices at zero-probability x. Hence H(Y | X) >= 0 and H(X, Y) >= H(X). By induction, H(X_1, ..., X_k) = sum over j of H(X_j | X_1, ..., X_{j-1}) for finitely-valued X_1, ..., X_k. Dividing every term by ln 2 gives the statement in bits.
X and Y take finitely many values
natural logarithms with 0 ln 0 = 0
K_x the conditional pmf where p_X(x) > 0 and any pmf where p_X(x) = 0

[Thm large_time_limit_non_L1 of arXiv:2605.29073, 'Volterra clocks and their pure-jump limits: \\hitting times of curved boundaries'] Assume $K \in L^1_{loc}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+\,,\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+)$ is completely monotone with $\int_0^{\infty}\,K(s)\,ds = + \infty\,$, and $\lambda > 0\,$. Then the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\widetilde{G_0}(t) \to G_0^* \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+$ as $t \to + \infty\,$, then $(W^n \,, X^n) \Rightarrow (W^*\,, X^*)$ in $D^{\circ}[0\,,T]\,$, where $W^*$ is standard Brownian motion, and $X^*$ is the constant process
        $$
        X^*_t := \inf\{s \geq 0 \,:\, \lambda s - \nu W^*_{f(s)} > G_0^* \}\,, \quad t \leq T\,.
        $$
        \item If there exists a sequence $c_n \downarrow 0$ such that, defining
        $$
        \widetilde{G_0}^n(t) := c_n\,\widetilde{G_0}(nt)\,, \quad f^n(x) := c_n^2\,f(x / c_n)\,, \quad \widetilde{W}^n_t := c_n\,W^n_{t / c_n^2}\,, \quad t\,,x \geq 0\,,
        $$
        we have $\widetilde{G_0}^n \to G_0^*$ pointwise on $[0\,,T]$ for some continuous $G_0^*\,$, and $f^n \to_{l.u.} f^*$ on $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+\,$, then $(\widetilde{W}^n\,, c_n\,X^n) \Rightarrow (W^*\,, X^*)$ in $D^{\circ}[0\,,T]\,$, where $W^*$ is a standard Brownian motion, and
        $$
        X^*_t := \inf\{s \geq 0\,:\, \lambda s - \nu W^*_{f^*(s)} > G_0^*(t) \}\,, \quad t \leq T\,.
        $$
    \end{enumerate}

PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. Via the Kruskal/invasion coupling the MST on T_{n,d}, d > 6, is governed by the critical window p = p_c(1 + O(V^{-1/3})): the V^{1/3} diameter (Heydenreich-van der Hofstad Open Problem 16.3) follows from (a) a window cluster of size V^{2/3} with intrinsic diameter V^{1/3} existing with positive probability (torus plateau plus the Kozma-Nachmias intrinsic one-arm exponent applied on the torus), (b) subcritical clusters at p_c(1 - eps) having intrinsic diameter O(eps^{-1} log V), summable over the geometric ladder of levels, and (c) uniqueness and concentration of the giant just above the window (Open Problem 13.2), the same three ingredients as in the complete-graph proof of Addario-Berry, Broutin, Goldschmidt and Miermont. The scaling limit (Open Problem 16.4) additionally needs metric-space (Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov) convergence of the window clusters and the product merging rule, both unproved on the torus and both consequences of the wrapping mechanism if it could be made quantitative.
Uniform i.i.d. edge weights on T_{n,d}, d > 6
Kruskal/invasion coupling between the MST and percolation

[Lem 49 (Polynomial tail control on the random sum) of arXiv:2506.19123, 'The longest increasing subsequence of Brownian separable permutons'] The random sum 
\[
\sum_{k=1}^\infty (\sttm_k)^{\frac{1}{2}-\alpha }\left(\sum_{n=\sttm_k}^{\sttm_{k+1}-1} r(n) f(T_n)\right)
\]
is almost surely finite.
Furthermore, there exists $\eps>0$ such that almost surely, for $k_0$ large enough,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{k=k_0}^\infty (\sttm_k)^{\frac{1}{2}-\alpha }\left(\sum_{n=\sttm_k}^{\sttm_{k+1}-1} r(n) f(T_n)\right) \leq k_0^{-\eps}.
\end{align*}
title: Polynomial tail control on the random sum

body:
[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] Assume that $\mu\in{\cal S}$ and its $\alpha$-potential
    $R_\alpha\mu$ belongs to $L^\infty(E;m)$ for  all $\alpha>0$. 
    Let $\{F_\ell\}$ be a (compact) nest attached 
    to $\mu$, namely, $1_{F_\ell}\mu \in {\cal S}_0$ for all $\ell \in{\mathbb N}$.
    Then for any compact set $K$ and $\alpha>0$,
    there exists a $C=C(\alpha, K)>0$ such that
    the following hold for all $\ell \in{\mathbb N}:$ 
    \begin{equation} 
      \mu(K\cap F_\ell) \le
      C \sqrt{\form_\alpha(U_\alpha(1_{F_\ell \cap K}\mu), U_\alpha(1_{F_\ell \cap K}\mu))}
    \end{equation}
    and 
    \begin{equation} 
      \form_\alpha(U_\alpha(1_{F_\ell \cap K}\mu), U_\alpha(1_{F_\ell \cap K}\mu))
      \le \Big(1+\frac{|\alpha-1|}{\alpha} \Big) \|R_1\mu\|_{\infty} \mu(K \cap F_\ell).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 16 of arXiv:2605.05864

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.00988, 'Covering Projective Height Balls by Subspaces in Rigid Adelic Spaces'] There is a constant $c_7>0$, effectively computable from $d, r_2, |D_K|$, with the following property. For every nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset\cO_K$, with
$q=\Nm\mathfrak p$, and every $R\ge1$, there is a subset
$S(R,\mathfrak p)\subset\cO_K/\mathfrak p$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]
\[
|S(R,\mathfrak p)|\ge c_7\min\{q,R^d\};
\]
\item[(ii)] every class in $S(R,\mathfrak p)$ has a representative
$a\in\cO_K$ with $\|a\|_\infty\le R/2$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 1 (GOE Matrix) of arXiv:2606.16018, 'A non-asymptotic bound on the TV distance between a \\Wishart matrix and an appropriately '] A random matrix \(\mG\in\bbR^{n \times n}\) is drawn from the \emph{Gaussian orthogonal ensemble} if it is a symmetric matrix with independent entries on the upper triangle such that for any \(i < j\)
	\[
		[\mG]_{ii} \sim \cN(0,2)
		\qquad
		\text{and}
		\qquad
		[\mG]_{ij} \sim \cN(0,1).
	\]
	We will denote this random matrix as \(\mG \sim \mathrm{GOE}(n)\).
	A GOE matrix is also distributed as \(\mG = \frac1{\sqrt 2} (\mH + \mH^\top)\) where \(\mH\in\bbR^{n \times n}\) has iid \(\cN(0,1)\) entries.

[Proposition 46 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Fix a limiting point \(\xi=(\mu_t)_{t<1}\) based at
\(q\in Y^{\rm prod}\), let
\(\tau_i\searrow0\), and set
\[
 g_i(s)=\tau_i^{-1}g(1+\tau_i s).
\]
Choose \(H_{2m+2}\)-centres \(p_i\) of the time-\((-1)\) measures
\(\mu_{i,-1}:=\mu_{1-\tau_i}\) with respect to \(g_i(-1)\).
After passing to a subsequence realizing a tangent space at \(\xi\), fix
a finite \(A\ge0\) and any \(q_i\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 d_\eta(q_i,q)\le A\sqrt{\tau_i}.
\end{equation}
There is \(D_A<\infty\) such that
\begin{align}
 \operatorname{diam}_{g_i(-1)}F_{q_i}&\le D_A,
 \\
 F_{q_i}&\subset B_{g_i(-1)}(p_i,D_A).
 
\end{align}
For every finite \(B\ge0\), there is \(C_{A,B}<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{B_{g_i(-1)}(p_i,D_A+B)}
 |\Rm(g_i(-1))|_{g_i(-1)}\le C_{A,B}.
\end{equation}
The constants may depend on the fixed limiting point and the realizing
subsequence, but not on \(i\).

[Defn 2 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Let $H$ be a Hilbert space, and let
$\{s_j(T)\}_{j\geq1}$ denote the singular values of a compact
operator $T:H\to H$, that is, the eigenvalues of
$(T^*T)^{1/2}$, counted with multiplicity. The operator $T$ is
called \emph{trace--class} if
\[
    \sum_{j\geq1}s_j(T)<\infty,
\]
and \emph{Hilbert--Schmidt} if
\[
    \sum_{j\geq1}s_j(T)^2<\infty.
\]
If $T$ is self-adjoint, then its singular values are the absolute
values of its eigenvalues $\{\lambda_j(T)\}_{j\ge 1}$, and hence these conditions are equivalent
to
\[
    \sum_{j\geq1}|\lambda_j(T)|<\infty
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \sum_{j\geq1}\lambda_j(T)^2<\infty,
\]
respectively.

[Df 34 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $E$ be a finite set.
    Let $E = E_0 \sqcup E_1 \sqcup E_2$ be a tripartition of $E$.
    Write $E_{01} = E_0 \cup E_1$ and $E_{12} = E_1 \cup E_2$.
    Suppose $M$ is a matroid on $E_{01}$ and $N$ is a matroid on $E_{12}$ such that
    $E_1$ is a modular flat of $M$ and
    $M|_{E_1} = N|_{E_1}$.
    
    One defines the \textbf{generalized parallel connection} of $M$ and $N$ along $E_1$---denoted $P_{E_1}(M, N)$---to be the unique matroid on $E$ whose flats are the subsets $F \subseteq E$ such that 
    $F \cap E_{01}$ is a flat of $M$ and 
    $F \cap E_{12}$ is a flat of $N$.
    The rank of this matroid is $\rk P_{E_1}(M, N) = \rk M + \rk N - \rk_M E_1$.
    When $E_1$ is modular in $N$ also, we say (following Ziegler) that $M$ is the \textbf{modular join} of $M$ and $N$ along $E_1$.
    In this case, $P_{E_1}(N, M)$ also exists and is equal to $P_{E_1}(M, N)$.

FPP chi=1/3 campaign, 2026-08-30: the engine's inequality is TIGHT at the conjectured answer, which is a structural reason the route resists. Iterating CRUX 9.3's Var(X_Mn) <= (beta/2) M Var(X_n) from n_0 with n_j = M^j n_0 gives the exponent 2 chi = 1 + log(beta/2)/log M, so M is a FREE DESIGN PARAMETER selecting which exponent is proved rather than an obstruction; at beta = 1 it takes M = 8 to deliver 2 chi = 2/3 exactly. If Var ~ n^(2 chi) exactly then Var(X_Mn) = M^(2 chi) Var(X_n), so the inequality is tight precisely when beta = 2 M^(2 chi - 1): at chi = 1/3 that is 1.587 at M=2, 1.260 at M=4, EXACTLY 1.000 at M=8, 0.794 at M=16. So 'beta <= 1 at M = 8' is not a sufficient condition for chi <= 1/3 that some other route might reach - it IS the statement chi <= 1/3, with zero slack. An inequality that is an equality at the truth cannot be established by an argument that loses constants, and every technique in reach loses constants somewhere. This also explains BETA_MEASURED_20260815's numbers: beta falling 1.76, 1.58, 1.45, 1.38 toward about 1.22 is, against beta = 2 M^(-1/3), the tight value at M near 4.4, consistent with KPZ holding and the block geometry sitting near M = 4.

[Lemma lem:longinequali of arXiv:2512.12124, 'A discontinuous percolation phase transition on the hierarchical lattice'] Let $\varpi \in \Lambda_{M_g+jr,\infty}$ for some $jr \in \{r,\ldots, \bar{r}_{g+1} - r\}$. Then
    \begin{align}
        &\notag \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varpi \textnormal{ bad} \right)  
        \\
        & \notag 
        \leq
        \sum_{\varphi, \varphi^\prime \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ not good} \right) \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi^\prime \textnormal{ not good} \right) 
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{7mm}
        + \sum_{\varphi \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ not good} \right) \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( G^{\mathrm{bl}} \left( \chi_{r}(\varpi) \setminus \{\varphi \} \right) \textnormal{ not connected} \right)
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{7mm}
        + \sum_{\gamma \in \{L^{-r}, \ldots, 1- L^{-r} \} }  \sum_{\varphi \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ is $\gamma$-mediocre} \right) \sum_{A \subset \chi_{r}(\varphi) : |A|\geq \gamma L^r } \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( A \nsim \chi_{r}(\varpi) \setminus \{ \varphi \} \right) 
        \\
        & \hspace{7mm}
        +
        \sum_{m \in \{0,r,\ldots, jr - r \} } \left( L^{jr - m} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \Lambda_{M_{g}+m}(0) \textnormal{ bad} \right) \right)^N
    \end{align}
    and, for every $\gamma \in \{L^{-r},\ldots,1-L^{-r} \}$,
    \begin{align}
        \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varpi \textnormal{ is $\gamma$-mediocre} \right)
        \leq
        \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( G^{\mathrm{bl}} \left( \chi_{r}(\varpi) \right) \textnormal{ has a cluster of density at most $\gamma$} \right).
    \end{align}
    If $\varpi \in \Lambda_{M_{g+1},\infty}$, then, for every $\gamma \in \{ L^{-r},\ldots, 1-L^{-r} \}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varpi \textnormal{ is $\gamma$-mediocre} \right)
        \leq
        \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( G^{\mathrm{bl}} \left( \chi_{r}(\varpi) \right) \textnormal{ has a cluster of density at most $\gamma$} \right),
    \end{equation}
    and
    \begin{align}
        
        &\mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varpi \textnormal{ bad} \right)  
        \\
        & \notag \leq
        \sum_{\varphi, \varphi^\prime \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ not good} \right) \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi^\prime \textnormal{ not good} \right) 
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{4mm}
        + \sum_{\varphi \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ not good} \right) \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( G^{\mathrm{bl}} \left( \chi_{r}(\varpi) \setminus \{\varphi \} \right) \textnormal{ not connected} \right)
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{4mm}
        + \sum_{\gamma \in \{L^{-r}, \ldots, 1- L^{-r} \} }  \sum_{\varphi \in \chi_{r}(\varpi)} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \varphi \textnormal{ is $\gamma$-mediocre} \right) \sum_{A \subset \chi_{r}(\varphi) : |A|\geq \gamma L^r } \mathbb{P}_{\bar{J}} \left( A \nsim \chi_{r}(\varpi) \setminus \{ \varphi \} \right) 
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{4mm}
        +
        \sum_{m \in \{M_{g}, M_{g}+r,\ldots, M_{g+1} - r \} }  \hspace{-12mm} \left( L^{M_{g+1} - m} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \Lambda_{m}(0) \textnormal{ bad} \right) \right)^N
        \\
        & \notag \hspace{4mm}
        +
        \sum_{m \in \{M_{g-1}, M_{g-1}+r,\ldots, M_{g} - r \} } \hspace{-12mm} \exp \left( e L^{\bar{r}_{g+1}} L^{M_{g}-m} \mathbb{P}_{q,J} \left( \Lambda_{m}(0) \textnormal{ bad} \right) - \log(g)^3 \lceil L^{\bar{r}_{g+1} + M_{g} - m} g^{-1-\varepsilon} \rceil \right) .
    \end{align}

[Theorem Polynomial approximation to $C^k$ functions of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Suppose that $f:\RR\to \RR$ is a $k$-th order differentiable function with $|f^{(k)}|\le M $. 
  Let $\mu$ be a distribution on $\RR$. 
  Then there exists a polynomial $p$ of degree 
  
  
  \begin{enumerate}
    
    
    \item $O(\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)) $ under strictly sub-exponential $\mu$; 
    \item $O(\exp\{\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)\})$ under sub-exponential marginal $\mu$.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Polynomial approximation to $C^k$ functions

[Def $G$-gerbe of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Let $G$ be a finite group scheme, and suppose $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$ is a morphism between two smooth separated Deligne--Mumford stacks. 
Then, equipping $\mathcal{Z}$ with the \'etale topology, the morphism $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$ is a {\em $G$-gerbe} if there exists an \'etale covering $\{Z_i \to \mathcal{Z}\}$ such that there is an isomorphism $\mathcal{Y} \times_{\mathcal{Z}} Z_i \simeq BG$ over $\mathcal{Z}/Z_i$ for every $i$.
title: $G$-gerbe

[Definition 15 (Regularity used in this paper) of arXiv:2609.03361, 'Grassmann--Pl\"ucker Parametrization of Convolutional Filter Subspaces:\ Regularity and Cl'] Let $f:X\to Z$ be a morphism from a smooth algebraic variety $X$ to an
algebraic variety $Z$. If the differential
\[
  \dd f|_x:T_xX\longrightarrow T_{f(x)}Z
\]
is injective for every $x\in X$, then $f$ is called a \emph{regular
parametrization}. Equivalently,
\[
  \rank(\dd f|_x)=\dim X
\]
for every $x\in X$.
title: Regularity used in this paper

body:
[Lemma 36 of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:tet}
 Let $w,w'>0$ and $u,u'\geq 0$, let $a^2 = w^2 + u^2$, $b^2 = (w')^2 + (u')^2$, and let $f - d = \delta = u + u'$. 
There is a unique positive solution in $x$ for the equation 
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\Delta_{abx}^2}{abx} \frac{\Delta_{xdf}^2}{xdf}
 =
 \left(\frac{9 \diamondplus_{abfd}^2}{4a b fd}\right).
\end{equation}
Denote it $c_*$. Then,
$$c_{**} := \lim_{\substack{f \rightarrow \infty\\ f - d = \mathbf{\delta}} } c_*$$ exists. 
Also,  for a target right-angled or obtuse triangle \((a,b,c_{**})\),  where $c_{**}^2 \geq a^2 + b^2$,     the required 
\(\delta^2\) is given by
\[
\delta^2
=
\frac{
2c_{**}^4(c_{**}^2-a^2-b^2)
}{
(c_{**}^2-a^2+b^2)(c_{**}^2+a^2-b^2)
}.
\]
Moreover, suppose
\[
a_n=a\sqrt n,\qquad b_n=b\sqrt n,
\]
and
\[
Q_n=n^{21}+O(n^{20}),\qquad
d_n^2=Q_n-2u'n^{11}+O(n^{10}),
\qquad
f_n^2=Q_n+2u n^{11}+O(n^{10}).
\]
If \(c_n\) is the maximizer of
\[
x\longmapsto
\frac{\Delta_{a_nb_nx}^2}{a_nb_nx}
\frac{\Delta_{xd_nf_n}^2}{xd_nf_n},
\]
then
\[
c_n=c_{**}\sqrt n+O(n^{-1/2}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 36 of arXiv:2607.04138

[Definition 45 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Let \( N \geqslant 1 \) be an integer. Suppose \( V = (V_1, \ldots, V_d) \) is a collection of vector fields on \( \mathbb{R}^N \), each of class \( \mathcal{C}^{N-1}(\mathbb{R}^N;\mathbb{R}^N) \). Let \( \mathbf{g} \in T^{(N)}(\mathbb{R}^d) \), the step-\( N \) free nilpotent group over \( \mathbb{R}^d \), and let \( y \in \mathbb{R}^N \). Then the (increment of the) step-\( N \) Euler scheme is defined by
\[
\mathcal{E}_{(V)} (y, \mathbf{g}) := \sum_{k=1}^{N} \sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_k \in \{1, \ldots, d\}} V_{i_1} \cdots V_{i_k} I(y)\, \mathbf{g}^{k; i_1, \ldots, i_k}.
\]
title: Definition 45 of arXiv:2512.07202

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Let $p\geq 2$ and let $(X_N=I_p(f_N),N\geq 1)$ satisfy 
	\eqref{c1}. Let $Y_N=I_q(g_N)$ with $p<q<2p$ and 
	$\sup_N\|g_N\|_{H^{\otimes q}}<\infty$  with the decomposition (\ref{decomp}). Assume that
	\begin{equation}
		(Y_N, Y_{1,N})
		\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{(d)}(Y, Y_1).
	\end{equation}
	Then:

 $(X_N,Y_N)\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{(d)}(Z,Y)$ 
		where $Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ and $Y$ admits the decomposition 
		\begin{equation}
			Y = \frac{Z}{p\sigma^2}Y_1 + \varepsilon, 
		\end{equation}
		where $\varepsilon$ is independent of $Z$.  The characteristic function of $(Z,Y)$ is
		\begin{equation}
			\varphi(u,v) = e^{-\frac{\sigma^2 u^2}{2}}\,
			\mathbf{E}\!\left[e^{iv\varepsilon - \frac{uv}{p}Y_1 
				- \frac{v^2}{2p^2\sigma^2}Y_1^2}\right].
		\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 16 of arXiv:2606.14812

[Prop Probability of hitting the origin, driftless case of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] When the drift is zero, i.e., $\mu=0$, we have
$$
\mathbb{P}[T<\infty]= \begin{cases}1 & \text { if } \alpha>0, \\ 0 & \text { if } \alpha \leqslant 0. \end{cases}
$$
If $\alpha \leqslant 0$, the vertex is not reached.  
If $0<\alpha<2$, the vertex is reached, but the amount of time spent at the vertex has zero Lebesgue measure.  
If $\alpha \geqslant 2$, the process hits the vertex and stays there. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Probability of hitting the origin, driftless case

[Proposition prop:singular-block-gauge of arXiv:2607.03639, '\vspace{-0.6in}An AI-Assisted Solution to the Signed BAR Conjecture: Uniqueness in the Har'] Assume that $R$ is nonsingular and that $R_{AA}$ is singular for some nonempty proper set $A\subsetneq J$. Choose
\[
 0\ne v\in\ker R_{AA},\qquad w=R_{TA}v\in\mathbb R^T.
\]
Then $w\ne0$. Let $\phi\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty)^T)$ satisfy $w\cdot\nabla_T\phi\not\equiv0$. For $i\in A$, define a finite signed measure $\zeta_i$ on $F_i$ by
\begin{equation}
 \int_{F_i}g(x)\,d\zeta_i(x)
 =v_i\int_{(0,\infty)^T}g(\iota_A(y))\phi(y)\,dy,
\end{equation}
and set $\zeta_i=0$ for $i\notin A$. Define $\chi\in\mathcal M(E)$ by
\begin{equation}
 \int_E g(x)\,d\chi(x)
 =-\int_{(0,\infty)^T}g(\iota_A(y))
       \bigl(w\cdot\nabla_T\phi(y)\bigr)\,dy.
\end{equation}
Then $\chi$ is finite, nonzero, supported on $S_A$, and satisfies $\chi(E)=0$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=1}^d\int_{F_i}D_i f\,d\zeta_i
 =\int_E f\,d\chi,
 \qquad f\in C_b^2(E).
\end{equation}

Let sigma be a continuous sigmoidal function (sigma(t) tends to 1 as t goes to +infinity and to 0 as t goes to -infinity). The width required may grow with the target accuracy; the theorem asserts density, not efficiency.

[Lemma Glem1 of arXiv:2411.06089, '{\Large \bf Averaging principle for semilinear slow-fast rough partial differential equati'] Let $T> 0$ and $\mathbf B \in \mathscr{C}^\gamma([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$ for some $\gamma \in (1/3, \gamma_0)$. Then for any $(Y, Y^\prime) \in \mathcal{D} _{\mathbf B}^{2\gamma , \eta }([ 0, T] ; \mathcal{H} )$ with $\eta \in [0,\gamma)$ and $ G_1 \in C_{- 2\gamma , 0}^3( \mathcal{H} ; \mathcal{H}^d)$, we have
$$\Big(\int_0^\cdot S_{\cdot-u} G_1 (Y_u) d\mathbf{B}_u, G_1(Y) \Big) \in \mathcal{D}_{\mathbf B}^{2\gamma,\eta}([0,T];\mathcal{H}),$$
and
\begin{align}
&\Big\| \int_0^{\cdot} S_{\cdot-u} G_1 (Y_u) d\mathbf{B}_u , G_1 (Y) \Big\|_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathbf B}^{2\gamma,\eta}}  \nonumber\\
 \lesssim & \|G_1 (Y)_0^\prime\|_{\mathcal H_{-2\gamma}^{d \times d}}+\|G_1 (Y)\|_{\infty,0}
+T^{\gamma-\eta}(1+|B|_\gamma+|B^2|_{2\gamma})\|G_1 (Y),G_1 (Y)^{\prime}\|_{\mathscr{D}_{S,\mathbf B}^{2\gamma,2\gamma,0}}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 10 (Weyl's Inequality) of arXiv:2606.25810, 'Spectral Collapse Under Geometric Alignment of Extreme Events'] For symmetric matrices \(A\) and \(E\),

\[
\lambda_k(A) + \lambda_n(E) \le \lambda_k(A+E) \le \lambda_k(A) + \lambda_1(E).
\]

In particular, when \(E\) is positive semidefinite,
\[
\lambda_k(A) \le \lambda_k(A+E) \le \lambda_k(A) + \lambda_1(E).
\]

Draft counterexample awaiting independent review: For the same parameter p=99/100 every finite-width strip S_k=Z x {-k,...,k} has no infinite Bernoulli bond cluster, while their increasing union Z^2 percolates. An enclosing closed dual circuit count gives theta_Z2(p)>=1-10557/2352250000>0.99999. Consequently unrestricted transfer of nonpercolation from every approximating graph to its union is false, even when every graph is infinite, connected, locally finite and quasi-transitive. This example is supercritical in the plane and the strip critical probabilities do not converge to the planar critical probability; it does not refute critical nonpercolation on higher-dimensional lattices or a bridge with additional threshold hypotheses.

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2608.11637, '\bf Uniform Local Asymptotics for L\'evy Processes with Subexponential Jumps'] For any $ \theta>0$, $K\geq 0$ and $\delta_1\geq \delta_0>0$, we have as $n\to\infty$,
 	\beqlb
 	\sup_{x\geq \theta n} \sup_{|y|\leq Kb(x)}\sup_{\delta\in[\delta_0,\delta_1]}
 	\bigg| \frac{  \mathbf P\big(  \widetilde{S}_n \in x-y+\Delta_\delta\big)}{n\cdot \nu\big(x+\Delta_\delta\big)}-1
 	\bigg| \to 0.
 	\eeqlb
 	Moreover, there exists a constant $C>0$ such  that for all $n\geq 1$, $x\geq \theta n$ and $\delta \in [\delta_0,\delta_1]$, 
 	\beqlb
 	\sup_{|y|\leq Kb(x)} \mathbf P\big(  \widetilde{S}_n \in x-y+\Delta_\delta\big) \leq C\cdot n\cdot \nu\big(x+\Delta_\delta\big). 
 	\eeqlb (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:Lq-J-comonotonic of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] Pick $q \in (0,1]$. Assume that 
 the L\'evy measures of $\nu_{\bm{X}}$ and $\nu_{\bm{Y}}$ admit the radial decomposition in~(equation eq:radial_decomp of the paper)
and construct the processes $(\bm{L^X},\bm{L^Y})$ 
by~(equation eq:comono_coupling_2 of the paper).
For any $\varepsilon\in(0,\infty)$ (we may have $\varepsilon=\infty$ when $\bm{X}$ and $\bm{Y}$ are of finite variation), the coupling $(\bm{L^X},\bm{L^Y})$ satisfies 
\begin{equation}

\mathds{E}\bigg[\sup_{t \in [0,1]}\big|\bm{L^X}_t-\bm{L^Y}_t\big|^q\bigg]\leqslant  \int_{(0,\varepsilon)\times \mathbb{S}^{d-1}} |\rho_{\bm{X}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})-\rho_{\bm{Y}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})|^q \mathrm{d} x \otimes \sigma(\mathrm{d} \bm{v}).
\end{equation}
In particular, the following inequality holds
\begin{equation}

\begin{split}
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X},\bm{Y})
&\leqslant |\bm{\varpi_X}-\bm{\varpi_Y}|^q
+\bigg(4\int_{[\varepsilon,\infty)\times \mathbb{S}^{d-1}}(\rho_{\bm{X}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})-\rho_{\bm{Y}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v}))^2 \mathrm{d} x \otimes \sigma(\mathrm{d} \bm{v})\bigg)^{q/2}\\
&\qquad+2^qd^{q/2}|\bm{\Sigma_X}-\bm{\Sigma_Y}|^q
+\int_{(0,\varepsilon)\times \mathbb{S}^{d-1}} |\rho_{\bm{X}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})-\rho_{\bm{Y}}^{\leftarrow}(x,\bm{v})|^q \mathrm{d} x \otimes \sigma(\mathrm{d} \bm{v}).
\end{split}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:Lq-J-comonotonic of arXiv:2411.03609

body:
[Lemma lem:distinct-translation-budgets of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] After equal-time fusion, fix one relative weak order with $h\ge1$
ordered supernodes.  Reparametrize its physical translation orbit by the
first occupied time $a=t_1$.  If
$t_{j+1}-t_j=1+g_j$ with $g_j\ge0$, and $q$ is the total slack recorded
by the common one-variable Green series, admissibility in
$\{1,\ldots,m\}$ is
\[
 a+(h-1)+q\le m.
\]
Thus its Taylor budget is
\[
 M(a)=m-h+1-a,
 \qquad M(a+1)=M(a)-1.
\tag{3.2.10q$_{20}$}
\]
In particular distinct physical translations have distinct budgets.
If a root time was initially used to name the orbit, replacing it by
$t_1$ is a bijective reparametrization and changes no local state or
multiplicity.

[Theorem 39 (Convergence for a strictly positive density plus an atom) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \hyp{A}{A} and \hyp{M}{M}. Then
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{A\in\XXA} \bigl| (T^{n}\circ\mu)(A) - \pi(A) \bigr| = 0
  \qquad\text{for every } \mu \in \Prob,

singular mass is bounded by the probability that no move has yet been made:
\[
  \sing\bigl( T^{n}\circ\mu \bigm| \pi\bigr) \;\le\; \int_{\XX} r^{n} \dd\mu
  \qquad (\mu \in \Prob,\ n \in \Nz) ,
\]
and the right-hand side tends to $0$ for every $\mu \in \Prob$.

[Proposition prop:flat-core of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] Fix $n\geq1$, $C\geq0$, and $0<\eta<1$.  Let $Q$ be a finitely supported
random variable in a torsion-free abelian group, write $q$ for its probability
mass function, let $Q'$ be an
independent copy, and suppose
\[
 H(Q+Q')-H(Q)\leq nC.
\]
Then there are a proper affine GAP datum $B$ and a probability mass
function $q_{\rm g}$ such that
\begin{align}
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(q,q_{\rm g})&\leq\eta,\\
 \supp q_{\rm g}&\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(B),\\
 \rank B&\leq d_\eta,\\
 \|q_{\rm g}\|_\infty&\leq\frac{\kappa_\eta}{|B|}.
 
\end{align}
The constants $d_\eta,\kappa_\eta<\infty$ depend only on $n,C,\eta$.
No uniform control as $\eta\downarrow0$ is asserted.

body:
[Theorem thm:min_sample of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~(thm:ci of the paper), 
we fix a desired accuracy (or tolerance)
$\varepsilon>0$ at a confidence level $1-\alpha$, with $\alpha\in(0,1)$, and introduce
\begin{align}
  \Theta_A(\varepsilon)
  \equiv
  \frac{1}{2\varepsilon^2}
  \left(\sqrt{\tilde\sigma_A^2} 
  + \sqrt{\tilde\sigma_A^2 + 2c_A\varepsilon}\right)^{2},
  
\end{align}
such that the minimal required time for a single trajectory (Theorem~(thm:tmin of the paper))
reads $t_{\textrm{min},A}(\varepsilon,\alpha) = \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log(2N_\nu/\alpha)$. 

Then $\mathbb{P}^\nu(-\varepsilon \leq \widehat{A}_{n,t} - \E^\mu[\overline{A}_t] \leq \varepsilon) \geq 1-\alpha$, i.e., 
the confidence radius stays below the tolerance level, $r_A(\alpha,n,t) \leq \varepsilon$, with 
probability of at least $1-\alpha$, if and only if

\begin{align}
  nt \geq \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\left(\log\frac{2}{\alpha} + n\log N_\nu\right).
  
\end{align}
This fixes the minimal sample size and the minimal per-trajectory time as follows.

For fixed $t > \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log N_\nu$, the
guarantee holds if and only if $n \geq n_{\min,A}$, where
\begin{align}
n_{\min,A}(\varepsilon,\alpha,t)
=\left\lceil\frac{\Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log(2/\alpha)}{t - \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log N_\nu}
\right\rceil.

\end{align}
denotes the \emph{minimal sample size}. In the case that $t \leq \Theta_A(\varepsilon)\log N_\nu$, 
no finite number of independent trajectories is sufficient. 
At stationarity $N_\mu = 1$ we recover 
    \begin{align}
      n_{\min,A}(\varepsilon,\alpha,t)
      =\left\lceil\frac{t_{\textrm{min},A}(\varepsilon,\alpha)}{t}\right\rceil,
      
    \end{align}
and the required sample size is simple the minimal time of a single trajectory
(Theorem~(thm:tmin of the paper)) divided by the per-trajectory length, and any $t>0$ 
has a finite sample size.

For fixed $n$, Eq.~(equation eq:uq_full of the paper) holds if and only if $t \geq t_{\min,A}(n,\varepsilon, \alpha)$,
where
\begin{align}
  t_{\min,A}(n, \varepsilon, \alpha)
  =\frac{\Theta_A(\varepsilon)}{n}\left(\log\frac{2}{\alpha} + n\log N_\nu\right).
  
\end{align}
Notably, in the case $n=1$ this recovers $t_{\textrm{min},A}(\varepsilon,\alpha)$ from 
Eq.~(equation eq:tmin of the paper).
The corresponding one-sided guarantees hold under the same conditions with
$\log(2/\alpha)$ replaced by $\log(1/\alpha)$.

body:
[Theorem thm:two-vortex of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\boldsymbol\kappa=(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$ satisfy
$\kappa_1>0>\kappa_2$, and let
$(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\in\Lambda_2(D)$ be a strict local
minimum point of $W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}$.  Choose $\rho>0$ such that
\[
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})
  \Subset\Lambda_2(D),
\]
and
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  &>W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\\
  &\quad\text{for every }(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \overline{B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})}
  \setminus\{(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\}.
  \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Fix $M_i,R_i>0$ for $i=1,2$.  Then there exist positive constants
$C$, $\eta_0$, and $\varepsilon_0$, depending only on
$D,\rho$, and $\mathbf a_{*,i},\kappa_i,M_i,R_i$, $i=1,2$,
such that the following holds.

For every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, let
$(\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
\in B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})$, and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(D)$ be nonnegative and satisfy
\[
  \int_D\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=|\kappa_i|,
  \qquad
  \|\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty
  \leq M_i\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R_i\varepsilon}(\mathbf a_{i,\varepsilon}),
  \quad i=1,2.
\]
Set
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
:=\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,0}-\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,0}$.
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of (equation eq:euler-intro of the paper), and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t}$ denote the transport of
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}$ by the associated Euler flow map.
If
\begin{equation}
  \eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}
  :=\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0})
  +\Bigl[W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\Bigr]
  +\varepsilon
  \leq\eta_0,
\end{equation}
then, for every $t\in\mathbb R$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})
  \times\mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})
  \subset B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2}),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
  &\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t})
  +\sup_{(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})\times
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})}
  \Bigl[
  W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})
  \Bigr] \leq C\eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}.
  
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Quantitative estimates: two opposite-sign vortices

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.27249, 'Torus actions, almost non-negative curvature and fundamental groups'] For all \(m\in \mathbb{N}\), there is a constant \(0<C(m)<\infty\), such that the fundamental group of every almost non-negatively curved closed manifold \(M\) of dimension \(m\), which admits an action of a torus \(T\) satisfying the above assumption, contains a abelian subgroup of index \(<C(m)\).
  
  Moreover, a finite index abelian subgroup of \(\pi_1(M)\) acts trivially on \(\pi_2(M)\).
  If the torus action on \(M\) is slice-maximal, then the action of \(\pi_1(M)\) on \(\pi_2(M)\) is \(C(m)\)-trivial. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.27249

$H$ \textcolor{black}{be} monotone  increasing,   $G$ monotone

body:
[Definition 27 (Language relating to polymer models from \cite{ks}) of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] In these definitions, we use the notation $N(A)$ to denote the \emph{set of neighbors} of $A$ in $\Q$, rather than
the number of neighbors.
Additionally, $\cH$ denotes either $\cE$ or $\cO$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item
    A subset $A \sse \cH$ is said to be \emph{2-linked} if there is no decomposition $A = A_1 \cup A_2$ into
    nonempty sets $A_1$ and $A_2$ which satisfy $N(A_1) \cap N(A_2) = \emptyset$.

    \item 
    For a subset $A \sse \cH$, we denote by $[A]$ the \emph{closure} of $A$,
    defined to be the largest subset of $\cH$ with the same neighborhood set as $A$.
    In other words, $[A] = \{ v \in \cH : N(v) \sse N(A) \}$.

    \item
    A 2-linked set $\fp \sse \cH$ with $|[\fp]| \leq \fr{3}{4} 2^{d-1}$ is called a \emph{polymer}.

    \item
    Polymers $\fp_1$ and $\fp_2$ are said to be \emph{compatible} if $\fp_1 \cup \fp_2$ is not 2-linked.

    \item
		We denote by $\Sep[\cH]$ the set of pairwise compatible collections of polymers.
    
    \item
    The \emph{weight} of a polymer $\fp$ is $\omega(\fp) = \E[\phi_\fp]$, where $\phi_\fp = 2^{-\N(\fp)}$.
    We remind the reader that $\N(\fp)$ denotes the (random) number of vertices neighboring $\fp$
    in the percolated graph $\Qp$.

    \item
    We define \emph{clusters} and their weights as in the previous section, which is a general construction that
    works for all polymer models.
    The set of clusters will be denoted by $\cC^\cH$.
\end{itemize}
title: Language relating to polymer models from \cite{ks}

Thus P_x^omega(A_l)=P_x^omega(A_-l)=0, including any iid law supported on such rows.

[Proposition prop:continuityVarSolns of arXiv:2609.03094, 'Discrete Gromov--Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing'] Let $(\mu_{0,n})_{n\in\mathbb N}\subset \mathcal P(\mathcal X_0)$ and $(\mu_{1,n})_{n\in\mathbb N}\subset \mathcal P(\mathcal X_1)$ be such that  $\mu_{0,n}\stackrel{w}{\to} \mu_0\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X_0),$ $\mu_{1,n}\stackrel{w}{\to} \mu_1\in \mathcal P(\mathcal X_1)$.   
    For each $n\in\mathbb N$, let $(u_n,v_n)$ solve
    \[ 
    \inf_{u\in\mathbb R^{r_0}}\sup_{v\in\mathbb R^{r_1}}\left\{ \frac12\|u\|^2-\frac 12 \|v\|^2+\inf_{x\in\mathcal K_n}\left\{\left( \mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}v-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal} u \right)^{\intercal}x  \right\} \right\}=\mathsf{GW}_p(\mu_{0,n},\mu_{1,n})^p,
    \]
    where $x\in\mathcal K_n$ is understood as the vector representation for $\pi\in\Pi(\mu_{0,n},\mu_{1,n})$. 
    Then, every cluster point of the sequence $(u_n,v_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ solves  
    \begin{equation}
    
    \inf_{u\in\mathbb R^{r_0}}\sup_{v\in\mathbb R^{r_1}}\left\{ \frac12\|u\|^2-\frac 12 \|v\|^2+\inf_{x\in\mathcal K}\left\{\left( \mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}v-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal} u \right)^{\intercal}x  \right\} \right\}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 14 (Moment-generating function) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The \textsc{mgf} of $T_{m,p}$ is
  \[
    M_{T_{m,p}}(t) \coloneqq
    \E\left[\exp(t\,T_{m,p})\right]
    = \left[
        \sum_{\ell=0}^m
        \binom{m-m\,e^{-t}}{\ell}
        (-1)^\ell
        \left(\frac{1}{1-p}\right)^\ell
      \right]^{-1}, \quad t \in \left(-\infty, \delta_{m,p}\right),
  \]
  for some positive $\delta_{m,p} > 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 17 (Global well-posedness for the periodic SBE) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \((\gamma,\alpha)=(2,0)\), let \(u_0\in L^2(\T)\) have zero spatial
mean, and let \(\mathbb X_{0,2}\) be the canonical periodic Burgers
enhancement.  Then the canonical stochastic Burgers equation
\[
 (\partial_t-\partial_x^2)u
 =\partial_x(u\diamond u)+\partial_x\xi,
 \qquad u(0)=u_0,
\]
admits, almost surely, a unique global paracontrolled solution in the sense of
\cite{GubinelliPerkowski2017KPZReloaded}.  On every finite interval it has
the representation
\[
 u=X+\Xone+\ell+Jm^\Psi,
\]
where
\[
 m\in L^\infty_tL^1\cap L^\infty_tL^2\cap L^2_tH^1,
 \qquad
 m\in L^3_tB^s_{3,3}\quad\text{for every }0<s<\frac12.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\eps_n\downarrow0\) and every sequence of smooth,
mean-zero initial data \(u_0^n\to u_0\) strongly in \(L^2\), the full
canonical mollified solution sequence converges to \(u\) in probability in
the local solution topology of
\cite[Theorem~3.7]{GubinelliPerkowski2017KPZReloaded} on each finite interval.

[Corollary corollaryofthelcd of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] Let $X,Y$ be uniformly sampled from an $(N,N_1,\kappa,\kappa',D_1,D_2,D_3)$ box pair with $N\geq N_1\geq 2$, and let $\alpha>0$ satisfy $\alpha d\geq 4,2^{16}B^2\kappa'Nd^{-1/2}/\alpha \leq 3^d$. Let $t_1=N^{-1}$ and $t_2=N_1^{-1}$. Then whenever $\log N$ is small enough relative to $\alpha$ in the sense that
$
\sqrt{\alpha c_0^2n/8}\geq (\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\nu p}}+\frac{256\sqrt{2}B^2}{\sqrt{c_0}})\sqrt{\log_+\frac{c_{\rho,\delta}^2c_0^42^{-11}N}{\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\nu p}}+\frac{256\sqrt{2}B^2}{\sqrt{c_0}}}}
$, the following probability estimate holds true: 
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{P}_{X,Y}(\operatorname{LCD}&^\mathbf{t}_{\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\nu p}}+\frac{256\sqrt{2}B^2}{\sqrt{c_0}},c_{\rho,\delta}^2c_0^42^{-16}}(r_nX_D,r_nY_D)\leq 2^{11}B^2, \\&|\sin(X_D,Y_D)|\geq c_{\rho,\delta}^2c_0^2/128)\leq (10^{12}\alpha(2+\frac{4\kappa'}{\kappa})^2)^{d/4},
\end{aligned}$$
where we take $r_n=\frac{c_0}{32\sqrt{n}}$ and in the probability we take an intersection with the event where the lower bound on $|\sin(X_D,Y_D)|$ holds. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.01166, 'Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions'] Suppose that the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:dnn} hold, and let \(\xi_m\), \(m\geq m_0\geq 1\), be the corresponding graded approximant. Define \(G_m(r)=g_{\xi_m}(r)-g_{\Xi_0}(r)\) 
and let \(\rho_t=(1-t)\rho_{\Xi_0}+t\rho_{\xi_m}\) and \(\xi_t(r)=(r\rho_t(r))^{-1}\) for \(0\leq t\leq1\). Finally, let \(\Pi_t\) be the stationary law for \(\xi_t\). Then it holds that
\begin{equation}
 \norm{G_m}_{\infty,[0,U]} =o(1), \quad
 \sup_{0\leq t\leq1}\norm{G_m}_{L^2(\nu_t)} \leq C_{\mathrm{path}} m^{-(\beta+1)},
\end{equation}
and, consequently, given~\eqref{eq:app_fwd}, 
\(\KL(\pi_0\Vert\pi_{\xi_m}) \leq C_{\mathrm{KL}} m^{-2(\beta+1)}\).
Here  
\(C_{\mathrm{path}},C_{\mathrm{KL}}\) are constants depending on \(\kappa\), K, as well as 
\(C_{\mathrm{app}},
C_{\mathrm{fwd}}\)
from Lemma~\ref{lem:dnn}, and independent of \(m\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 7 of arXiv:2609.01166

body:
[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2512.08745, 'Variance strikes back: sub-game--perfect Nash equilibria in time‑inconsistent $N$‑player g'] Let {\rm\Cref{assumpDPP_NplayerGame}.\ref{Glip_NplayerGame}} and {\rm\Cref{assumption:borelMeasurability_Lip}} hold. Let $(\Y^N,\Z^N,\M^{\star,N},\N^{\star,N},\Z^{m,\star,N},\Z^{n,\star,N})$ be a solution to the following system of {\rm BSDEs}
\begin{align}
\notag Y^{i,N}_t &= g^i\big(X^i_{\cdot \land T}, L^N(\X^N_{\cdot \land T})\big) + G^i\big(\varphi^i_1(X^i_{\cdot \land T}),\varphi^i_2\big(L^N(\X^N_{\cdot \land T})\big)\big) \\
\notag &\quad+ \int_t^T f^i_s\big(X^i_{\cdot \land s},L^N(\X^N_{\cdot \land s},\hat\balpha^N_s),\hat\alpha^{i,N}_s\big) \d s - \int_t^T \partial^2_{m,n}G^i\big(M^{i,\star,N}_s,N^{i,\star,N}_s\big) \sum_{\ell =1}^N Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_s \cdot Z^{i,n,\ell,\star,N}_s \d s \\
\notag &\quad- \frac{1}{2} \int_t^T \Bigg(\partial^2_{m,m}G^i\big(M^{i,\star,N}_s,N^{i,\star,N}_s\big) \sum_{\ell =1}^N \big\|Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_s\big\|^2 +\partial^2_{n,n}G^i\big(M^{i,\star,N}_s,N^{i,\star,N}_s\big) \sum_{\ell=1}^N \big\|Z^{i,n,\ell,\star,N}_s\big\|^2 \Bigg)\d s \\
\notag &\quad- \int_t^T \sum_{\ell = 1}^N Z^{i,\ell,N}_s \cdot \d \big(W_s^{\hat\balpha^\smalltext{N},N}\big)^\ell, \; t \in [0,T], \; \P \text{\rm--a.s.}, \\
\notag M^{i,\star,N}_t &= \varphi^i_1(X^i_{\cdot \land T}) - \int_t^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_s \cdot \d \big(W_s^{\hat\balpha^\smalltext{N},N}\big)^\ell, \; t \in [0,T], \; \P \text{\rm--a.s.}, \\
\notag N^{i,\star,N}_t &= \varphi^i_2\big(L^N\big(\X^N_{\cdot \land T}\big)\big) - \int_t^T \sum_{\ell=1}^N Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_s \cdot \d \big(W_s^{\hat\balpha^\smalltext{N},N}\big)^\ell, \; t \in [0,T], \; \P \text{\rm--a.s.} \\
\notag \hat\balpha^N_t &\coloneqq \mathfrak{a}^N\big(t,\X^N_{\cdot \land t},\Z^N_t,\M^{\star,N}_t,\N^{\star,N}_t,\Z^{m,\star,N}_t,\Z^{n,\star,N}_t\big),  \\
\frac{\d \P^{\hat\balpha^\smalltext{N},N}}{\d \P} &\coloneqq \cE\Bigg( \int_0^\cdot \sum_{\ell =1}^N b^\ell_t\big(X^\ell_{\cdot \land t},L^N\big(\X^N_{\cdot \land t},\hat\balpha^N_t\big),\hat\alpha^{\ell,N}_t\big) \cdot \d W^\ell_t \Bigg)_T.
\end{align}
In addition, for each $i \in \{1,\ldots,N\}$, there exists $p \geq 1$ such that 
\begin{align}
\notag &\sup_{\balpha \in \cA^\smalltext{N}_\smalltext{N}} \E^{\P^{\smalltext{\balpha}}} \Bigg[ \sup_{t \in [0,T]} \big|Y^{i,N}_t\big|^p + \bigg(\int_0^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N \big\|{Z}_t^{i,\ell,N}\big\|^2 \d t\bigg)^\frac{p}{2} \Bigg] \\
&+\esssup_{\balpha \in \cA^\smalltext{N}_\smalltext{N}} \Bigg\{\sup_{t \in [0,T]} \Big\{ \big| M^{i,\star,N}_t\big| + \big| N^{i,\star,N}_t \big| \Big\} + \sup_{\tau \in \cT_{0,T}} \E^{\P^{\smalltext{\balpha}\smalltext{,}\smalltext{N}\smalltext{,}\smalltext{\tau}}_{\smalltext{\cdot}}} \Bigg[ \int_\tau^T \sum_{\ell =1}^N \Big( \big\|Z^{i,m,\ell,\star,N}_t\big\|^2 + \big\|Z^{i,n,\ell,\star,N}_t\big\|^2 \Big) \d t \Bigg] \Bigg\} <+ \infty.
\end{align}
Consequently, it holds that $\hat\balpha^N \in \mathcal{N}\!\mathcal{A}_{s,N}$, and for any player index $i \in \{1,\ldots,N\}$, $J^i(t,\cdot,\hat\alpha_t^{i,N};\hat\balpha_t^{N,\smallertext{-}i}) = Y^{i,N}_t$, $\P\text{\rm--a.s.}$, for every $t\in [0,T]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
