[Definition Non-bidirectional chemical system of arXiv:2607.02367, 'Flux solutions for stochastic chemical systems with sources and sinks'] Assume that $\mathcal R$ is a set of chemical reactions i.e. 
 $\mathcal R := \{ S_\rho \}_{\rho=1}^r $. Assume that $ \mathcal R_s $ is a set of sources and sinks, i.e.  $\mathcal R_s := \{e_k \}_{k \in \Omega_c}  \cup  \{ - e_{ k  }\}_{\Omega_c }  $ with $ \Omega_c \subset \Omega$.  
 Assume that $\mathcal K := \{ R_\rho  \}_{ \rho =1 }^r $ is the set of the kinetics associated with the chemical reactions $S_\rho \in \mathcal R $ and $\mathcal K_s := \{ \alpha_k  \}_{ k \in \Omega_c }  \cup \{ \beta_k  \}_{ k \in \Omega_c } $ is the set of the chemical rates associated with the sources and sinks. 
 We say that $(\Omega, \mathcal R,  \mathcal R_s , \mathcal K, \mathcal K_s )$ is a non-bidirectional chemical system with sources and sinks.
title: Non-bidirectional chemical system

[Prop char-mu-tilde of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] There exists a constant $c>0$ such that for all balls or boxes $B\subset[0,1]^2$,

    \widetilde{\mu}(\pi^{-1}(B)) = \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\frac{cY_k(B)}{2^{2k}A^{\CLE}_1(2^{-k},1)} \qquad\text{in probability}.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:one-face-normal-form of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Let $\mathbb G_0$ be a connected one-face topological map on the compact
oriented surface $\Sigma_{g,n}$ and suppose that every boundary component is
carried by $\mathbb G_0$. After contracting a spanning tree, the resulting
one-vertex ribbon graph has $2g+n$ oriented loop edges. There is a free basis
\[
 a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_g,b_g,c_1,\ldots,c_n
\]
of its edge-path group such that, with the face and boundary orientations induced by the orientation of the surface, the unique face word is, up to cyclic
permutation,
\[
 \prod_{i=1}^g[a_i,b_i]\prod_{j=1}^n c_j,
\]
and $c_j$ represents the $j$-th oriented boundary component. The
corresponding change of edge variables preserves product Haar measure.

body: [Lemma coupleab of arXiv:2603.05467, 'Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph'] For $ \varepsilon>0 $ and $\alpha=(c_2+\varepsilon)n^{-1/d}$ we can choose $t\geq t_0(\varepsilon,d)$ sufficiently close to 1 such that there exists a coupling of $ G_t $ with an continuum AB percolation model with intensity $ \lambda=\lambda(\varepsilon,t)>\lambda_c$ on $ B(\underline{0},\rho(t,n)) $ such that for any two points $ x,y $ that are adjacent in the continuum AB percolation model, it holds that $ g^{-1}(x),g^{-1}(y) $ are adjacent vertices in $ G_t $.
title: Lemma coupleab of arXiv:2603.05467

body:
[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] For every $\delta > 0$, there exists a positive constant $c$ such that the following holds for every $G \in \mathcal{L}$ satisfying $\Ex_G[X] \ge (1+\delta)\Ex[X]$:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
  \item
    
    If $Lp_H \le p \ll 1$ for some $L \ge (\log n)^{1/c}$ and $e_G \le f(\log n)^2$, then
    \[
      e_G\log(1/p)-v_G\log(en/g)\geq ce_G \min\{\log L, \log(1/p)\}.
    \]
  \item
    
    If $H$ is stable and $p_H \ll p \ll 1$, then
    \[
      e_G\log(1/p)-v_G\log(en/g)\geq ce_G\log(1/p).
    \]
  \end{enumerate}

We use freely the language of \cite[Chapter VI]{Hel01}. 
Let $\frak g$ be the Lie algebra of $G$ and let $\frak k \subset \frak g$ be the Lie algebra of $K$.
Also, denote by $\frak p \subset \frak g$ the orthogonal subspace to $\frak k$ with respect to the Killing form. 
The restriction of the Killing form to $\frak k$ is negative definite

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Burdzy and Scheutzow, Forward Brownian motion (arXiv:1302.6958), Problem 7.5 (p. 26) asks: for any process {X_t, t >= 0} whose law is equivalent to Brownian motion, can one find a random piece to put in front of X so that the new process is a Brownian motion? Our result (id P0032, 2026-09-08): YES - and under absolute continuity rather than equivalence, which is weaker than the problem assumes. The mechanism is a filling-scheme lemma: for theta an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a standard Borel space (E, P) and Q = f P, there is an almost surely finite integer N >= 0 with law(theta^N Z) = Q for Z distributed as P. Apply it with E = C_0(R) under two-sided Wiener measure and (theta w)(t) = w(t+1) - w(1), lifting the one-sided density of X's law to two-sided paths; the lemma returns a finite N for which {Z(N+t) - Z(N)} has X's law while {Z(t) - Z(0)} is a Brownian motion whose first N units are exactly the prefix. Verification as the source words it: the filling construction was implemented on a finite ergodic system (Z/n with the +1 shift) for n = 5, 7, 12, 60 with random densities - total accepted mass 1.000000000000 every time, the law of theta^N Z matching f P to about 1e-16, E[N] finite - and the negative control is the informative one, since with a non-ergodic theta exactly half the mass is ever accepted and half survives forever. The L^1 ergodic-theorem step in the infinite-dimensional setting was not verified, only read; it is standard but checked by eye only. NOVELTY IS THE WEAK POINT and the campaign's own proof file volunteers it: the lemma is a filling construction related to classical work of Chacon-Ornstein, Rost and Thorisson - sound mathematics, very likely a known consequence. X's law absolutely continuous with respect to Brownian motion (weaker than the problem's equivalence) theta the unit shift with recentering on two-sided Wiener space, ergodic and invertible

body: Let X be the passage time between fixed endpoints and X^L its value after resampling a block L, and let U_L be the event that the geodesic uses an edge of L. If the geodesic avoids L then the original path survives unchanged in the resampled field, so X^L <= X on the complement of U_L. Hence the positive part (X^L - X)^+ vanishes off U_L, and any functional of the form E[1(U_L) f((X^L - X)^+)] with f(0) = 0 equals E[f((X^L - X)^+)] - the indicator carries no information. Combined with exchangeability this gives E[((X^L - X)^+)^k] = (1/2) E[|X^L - X|^k] for every k >= 1.

=

\]
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 13 (Asymptotics of $\Var(D_n)$) of arXiv:2606.18047, 'Analysis of the asymmetric shelf shuffle'] Let $D_n$ be the number of descents of an $(m, p)$-shelf shuffle with $n$ cards. Put $q=1-p$. Then the following limits hold, uniformly in the choice of $p=p(n)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $m/n\to0$, then
\[
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(D_n)}{n}-pq\longrightarrow0.
\]
In particular, for fixed $p$, $\operatorname{Var}(D_n)/n\to pq$.
\item If $m/n\to\infty$, then
\[
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(D_n)}{n}\longrightarrow \frac1{12}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Asymptotics of $\Var(D_n)$

[Theorem thm:Ricci of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Assume that, for each $\varepsilon>0$, the semigroup $P_t^\varepsilon$ falls into the smooth diffusion setting of this paragraph and
admits an invariant probability measure $\pi^\varepsilon(dz)=e^{-V^\varepsilon(z)}\,dz$ with strictly positive smooth density.
Let
\[
  \mathfrak{R}^\varepsilon(z):=\mathfrak{R}_z\bigl(V^\varepsilon,F^\varepsilon,A^\varepsilon\bigr)
\]
be the corresponding Ricci matrix field in the sense of [ArnoldCarlenJu2008LargeTime]. If there exist
$\varepsilon_0>0$ and $\kappa\ge0$ such that
\begin{equation}
  \mathfrak{R}^\varepsilon(z)+\kappa\,A^\varepsilon(z)\ \succeq\ 0,
  \qquad \forall\,z\in E,\ \ 0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0,
\end{equation}
then (ass:CDkappa of the paper) holds uniformly in $\varepsilon$; cf.\ [bolley-gentil-phi-entropy]. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Unreviewed independent derivation: for n>=2 work on H={x in R^(n+1):sum x_i=0} with its Euclidean metric, and take X uniform on vertices v_i=sqrt((n+1)(n+2))(e_i-1/(n+1)). Covariance on H is identity. Put u=(e_0-e_1)/sqrt(2), T=<X,u>, Y=X-Tu and S=lambda_0+lambda_1 in barycentric coordinates. Conditional on Y, T is uniform on an interval of length sqrt(2(n+1)(n+2)) S, and S~Beta(2,n-1). Thus ess sup conditional C_P=2(n+1)(n+2)/pi^2, mean conditional C_P=12/pi^2, ess sup conditional variance=(n+1)(n+2)/6 and mean conditional variance=1. Cheeger uses boundary/min(mass,1-mass): ess inf conditional h=sqrt(2/((n+1)(n+2))). Near-extremal fibers have positive marginal probability: P(S>1-delta)=delta^(n-1)[n-(n-1)delta] for 0<delta<1. This blocks transferring global isotropy to a uniform conditional bound; it is not a KLS refutation or novelty claim.
Euclidean metric on H; n>=2; orthogonal conditioning onto u-perp; marginal-almost-everywhere conditional laws.
C_P uses variance/Dirichlet energy; h uses boundary/min(mass,1-mass).

[Theorem 6 (Sequential mixed coincidence identity) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let the one-step likelihood ratios $R_1,\dots,R_T$ be strictly positive, and let $\alpha \in \R^T$ satisfy $0 < Z_T(\alpha) < \infty$ for $Z_T$ of~\eqref{eq:seqZ}.
Then for every path measure $\widetilde Q \ll P|_{\cF_T}$,
\begin{equation}
  \log Z_T(\alpha)
  = \sum_{t=1}^T \alpha_t\,\E_{\widetilde Q}[\log R_t]
    - \KL(\widetilde Q\|P|_{\cF_T})
    + \KL(\widetilde Q\|R^*_\alpha)
  \;=\; \max_{\widetilde Q \ll P}
    \Bigl\{\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^T \alpha_t\,\E_{\widetilde Q}[\log R_t]
      - \KL(\widetilde Q\|P|_{\cF_T})\Bigr\},
\end{equation}
the maximum attained uniquely at $\widetilde Q = R^*_\alpha$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sequential mixed coincidence identity

[Thm t:thm_q_sup of arXiv:2504.07255, 'A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme\\ for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Dri'] Let assumptions
$\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{Lip}_+}_A$,
$\mathbf{H}_{A_x,A_{xx}}$,
$\mathbf{H}_{a,b,c}^{\mathrm{Lip}_b}$, and
$\mathbf{H}_{\nu,p}$
 hold.
 Then, for any $T\in[0,\infty)$ and $q\in (0,p)$ there is uniform convergence
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
 \mathbf{E} \sup_{t\in[0, T]}\|X_t^n-X_t\|^q \leq_C h_n^{\delta}(1+\|x\|^p),
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
with the convergence rate
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\delta=\frac{p-q}{\chi}\wedge\frac{q}{4}\wedge \frac{1}{2}.
\end{aligned}\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2605.17155, '2605.17155'] Let \((\xi_{k,r})_{k\geq0,\ 0\leq r<p^{k+1}}\) be independent copies of a
real random variable \(\xi\), and extend periodically by
\[
   \xi_{k,n}=\xi_{k,r}\quad\hbox{if }n\equiv r\pmod {p^{k+1}} .
\]
Assume \(\E[|\xi|]<\infty\) and let \(H>0\).  Then
\begin{equation}
   X_n=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}p^{-kH}(\xi_{k,n}-\xi_{k,0}),
   \qquad n\geq0,
\end{equation}
converges absolutely a.s.~for every fixed \(n\), and
\((X_n)_{n\geq0}\) is a real-valued \(p\)-adic \(H\)-sssi process. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 10 of arXiv:2605.17155

body:
[Theorem thm:maxwell of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $w$ be a kernel whose reaction $\varphi_{w}$ is bistable:
		$w(0) < 1$, $w(1) < 1$, and a single interior zero of
		$\varphi_{w}$. Then the equation~(equation eq:cdf-equation of the paper) admits a
		traveling law $F(x,t) = F_{c}(x - ct)$, unique up to translation,
		with monotone profile, globally stable among laws, and its speed
		obeys
		\begin{equation}
			c = \frac{\mathbb{E}_{w}[Z] - \tfrac12}
			{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}}(F_{c}')^{2}\,dx},
			\qquad
			\operatorname{sign}(c)
			= \operatorname{sign}\big(\mathbb{E}_{w}[Z] - \tfrac12\big),
			
		\end{equation}
		where $\mathbb{E}_{w}[Z]$ is the mean rank of the kernel: the
		Maxwell equal-area construction of bistable fronts collapses, for
		rank dynamics, to a single moment, and the law stands still
		precisely when the kernel is rank-balanced. For the phase-shifted
		family $w_{1,\alpha}$,
		\begin{equation}
			c(\alpha)
			= -\frac{\pi\sqrt D}{4}\,\sin(2\pi\alpha) + O(\alpha^{2})
			\qquad (\alpha \to 0).
			
		\end{equation}

body:
[Corollary 27 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let
\(
  u_0:\Sigma\to S
\)
be an orientation-preserving covering of degree \(d\) between
closed surfaces, and let \(X_g\in\mathcal T(\Sigma)\) be the conformal
structure determined by the domain metric \(g\). Denote by
\(u_0^*\Delta_q\) the pullback measured foliation on \(\Sigma\). Then
\begin{equation}

  \mathscr E_{\Delta_q}(u_0)
  =
  \frac12\,
  \operatorname{Ext}_{X_g}\!\left(u_0^*\Delta_q\right).
\end{equation}
More explicitly, write the pullback  multicurve as
\(u_0^*\Delta_q=\sum_{i=1}^r\sum_{a=1}^{r_i}\widehat\delta_{i,a}\). Let
\(\widehat\Phi=\Phi_{u_0^*\Delta_q,X_g}\) be the Hubbard--Masur
differential on \(X_g\), and let \(\widehat A_{i,a}\) be its characteristic
cylinder with core curve \(\widehat\delta_{i,a}\). If
\(\widehat M_{i,a}=\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat A_{i,a})\) denotes its
actual conformal modulus, then
\begin{equation}

  \mathscr E_{\Delta_q}(u_0)
  =
  \frac12\int_{X_g}|\widehat\Phi|
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^{r}\sum_{a=1}^{r_i}
  \frac{1}{\widehat M_{i,a}}.
\end{equation}

Suppose, in addition, that the  conformal structure on $\Sigma$ is the pullback
of the initial target structure, namely \(X_g=u_0^*X_0\in T(\Sigma)\). Then
\begin{equation}

  \mathscr E_{\Delta_q}(u_0)
  =
  \frac d2\,
  \operatorname{Ext}_{X_0}(\Delta_q)=\frac d2
  \sum_{i=1}^{r}\frac1{M_i}.
\end{equation}

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] Let $\Omega$ be the state space of a Rook's Walk with parameters $n$ and $d$ (i.e., $\Omega=\{1,\dots, n\}^d$). Define the $i^\text{th}$ Hamming shell $H_i$ to be,
   \[H_i = \{x\in \Omega \mid i= ||\hat{1}-x||_0\}, \quad \forall i\in \{0,\dots,d\}\]
   where $||\cdot||_0$ denotes Hamming distance and $\hat{1}:=\{1\}^d$. Furthermore, define $\varphi : \{0,\dots,d\} \to \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ such that 
   \[\varphi(i) = |H_i|, \quad  \forall i\in \{0,\dots,d\}\]

Author-derived conditional result, pending independent review: let a capacity-2 chordal Loewner driver be a continuous semimartingale dW=mu dt+dN, with N a continuous local martingale and d<N>=v dt, v>=0 and locally integrable coefficients. Fix constant alpha>0. Before three fixed obstacles are hit, let h_i be their hydrodynamic maps, analytic at W with positive derivative. If each h_i'(W)^alpha is a local martingale on a common positive interval and the matrix with rows (h_i''/h_i',h_i'''/h_i',(h_i''/h_i')^2) is invertible for a.e. time there, then mu=0 and v=8/3 a.e. there and alpha=5/8. Global Brownian-driver/SLE identification additionally needs such intervals to cover all finite times.
Continuous semimartingale driver with absolutely continuous drift/quadratic variation
Capacity normalization partial_t g=2/(g-W)
Common constant alpha>0
Reflected analytic conformal derivatives and local boundedness stops
Three local martingales over an interval
A.e. nondegenerate jet matrix
Globalization requires explicit coverage of all finite times

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The functor $((eq:ext-orth-spc of the paper))$ is topologically enriched.
    \begin{proof}
        Recall that mapping spaces in enriched functor categories are topologized as a subspace of the product. By the universal property of the latter, the claim therefore amounts to saying that
        \[
            \textbf{\textup{maps}}_{\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}}(X,Y)\to\textbf{\textup{maps}}_{\textbf{\textup{Top}}}(\overline{X}(V),\overline{Y}(V))
        \]
        is continuous for all $X,Y\in\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ and $V\in{\widehat{{\smash{\textbf{\textup{L}}}\vphantom{t}}\kern-1.75pt}\kern1.75pt}$. Adjoining over and plugging in the definition of $\overline{X}(V)$, this is equivalent to continuity of
        \[X(U)\times\textbf{\textup{maps}}_{\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}}(X,Y)\to \overline{Y}(V)\]
        for all finite-dimensional $U\subset V$. But this map is simply the composite
        \[

body: In first-passage percolation on Z^2 with edge weights confined to [a, b] with a > 0, any geodesic from the origin to (0, r) satisfies a DETERMINISTIC bound on its transversal excursion: it never attains transversal level D > r(b - a)/(2a). The proof is elementary counting: reaching transversal level D forces at least r + 2D edges, each of weight at least a, giving passage time at least a(r + 2D), while the straight path gives at most b r; the two are incompatible beyond the stated level. No probabilistic input is used, so the bound holds for every realisation.

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2604.19308, '\textbf{On McKean--Vlasov SDEs with polynomial drifts for SIS epidemic models}'] Let $a,b,c,d\in\R$ and $y>0$ satisfy $a + dy^{\frac{3}{2}} > 0$. Then $f\colon [0,y]\rightarrow\R$ given by $f(x) := a + bx + cx^{2}+d(y-x)^{\frac{3}{2}}$ admits a unique zero in the following two cases:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $d = 0$ and either $c\leq 0$ and $f(y)\leq 0$ or $c > 0$ and $f(y) < 0$.

\item $c\leq 0$, $d\neq 0$ and $f(y) < 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, in the first case, the zero $x_{0}$ of $f$ is of the form $x_{0} = \frac{-b-\sqrt{b^{2} - 4ac}}{2c}$, if $c\neq 0$, and $x_{0} = - \frac{a}{b}$, otherwise.
title: Lemma 21 of arXiv:2604.19308

body:
[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2608.01516, 'Nondegeneracy and regularity of polynomial pushforwards'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb N$, let $\theta\in\mathbb R^k$ satisfy $|\theta|=1$, and
let $\varrho\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^k)$ be a nonnegative integrable
log-concave function on $\mathbb R^k$. Let
$
f\in\mathcal P_d(\mathbb R^k;\mathbb R^k),
$
let $J_f$ be the Jacobian matrix of $f$, let
$
A_f:=\operatorname{adj}(J_f),
$
and set
\[
Q_j(x):=\langle A_f(x)\theta,e_j\rangle,
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every $t>0$, and every
$\varphi\in C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^k)$ satisfying
\[
\|\varphi\|_\infty\le t,
\quad
\|\partial_\theta\varphi\|_\infty\le 1,
\]
one has
\begin{align*}
\biggl|
\int_{\mathbb R^k}(\partial_\theta\varphi)(f)\varrho\,dx
\biggr|
&\le
\int_{\mathbb R^k}
I_{\{(\det J_f)^2\le 2\varepsilon^2\}}\varrho\,dx
+
t\varepsilon^{-1}
\sum_{j=1}^k
\int_{\mathbb R^k}|\partial_{x_j}Q_j|\varrho\,dx
\\
&\quad
+
(2+18\pi kd)t\varepsilon^{-1}
\sum_{j=1}^k
\int_{\mathbb R^{k-1}}
\sup_{x_j\in\mathbb R}|Q_j(x)\varrho(x)|\,d\hat{x}^j,
\end{align*}
where
\[
\hat{x}^j:=(x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1},x_{j+1},\ldots,x_k)
\in\mathbb R^{k-1},
\quad j=1,\ldots,k.
\]

Own work draft, proof (unaudited), conditional on C010 v2 and C012 v2; no independent PASS or novelty assertion. In noiseless isotropic Gaussian homogeneous max-margin learning with fixed probe angle theta in (0,pi/2], let E(alpha,theta) be the infimum of limiting fresh-Gaussian test errors over fixed absolute-probe-margin thresholds, dimension limit first at retained aspect alpha. With an unlimited unlabeled source pool and only selected teacher labels, for alpha>=32, sin(theta)/(2*pi*e*alpha)<=E(alpha,theta)<=8*sin(theta)/alpha. The achievable upper choice is threshold b=4*sin(theta). For any output with teacher angle delta, a Gaussian disagreement subwedge of angle gamma=min(delta,theta) has probability gamma/pi and conditional probe second moment <=8*sin(theta)^2; Markov gives selected-law error r>=gamma/(2*pi*f), where f=P(|Z|<=b)<4*sin(theta). The classical Vapnik support-vector leave-one-out bound, reproduced in Burges 1998 Sec.7.4 Eq.(93), plus at most d active iid continuous selected rows, gives expected selected risk<=d/(n+1). C010 continuity and concentration give limiting selected risk<=1/alpha. Since alpha>=32, delta>=theta would force risk>1/(8*pi)>1/32; hence delta<theta and fresh risk<=2*f/alpha. C012 supplies the lower bound. Constants are uniform over fixed positive theta, not a dimension-varying-theta theorem. Original source cost is alpha/f, diverging on order alpha/theta at small theta. A finite source cap, exact crossover, initial exponential regime, and optimal fraction are not settled.

body: [Theorem theo:main_meso of arXiv:2605.21265, 'The non-Hermitian minor process'] Let $X$ be a complex or real $N\times N$ i.i.d. matrix satisfying Assumption~(ass:chi of the paper). Fix (small) $c_0, \tau>0$, an exponent $a\in (0,1/2)$ and an open bounded domain $\Omega\subset \mathbf{C}$. For $x_0\in [c_0,1)$ and $z_0\in\mathbf{C}$ with $|z_0|\le (1-\tau)\sqrt{x_0}$, there exists the centered Gaussian process $L_{x_0,z_0}(y,f)$ indexed by $\mathbf{R}\times H^2_0(\Omega)$ with the covariance structure given by $C_{x_0,z_0,\beta}$ defined in (equation eq:C_beta_meso of the paper). The process of mesoscopically scaled centered linear statistics $L^{\lceil xN\rceil}(f_{z_0,a})$ with $x:=x_0+N^{-2a}y$ converges to $L_{x_0,z_0}(y,f)$ in the sense of moments (equation eq:main_macro of the paper). The implicit constant in the error term may depend only on the moment degree, $c_0,\tau,a$, model parameters from Assumption~(ass:chi of the paper) and $H^2(\Omega)$ norms of test functions. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$\mu_1,\mu_2 \in\bN_{<\infty}$ have disjoint support and set
$\mu:=\mu_1+\mu_2$. Assume that $\xi_{\mu_1}$ and $\xi_{\mu_2}$ are independent RCMs with distributions $\xi^{\mu_1}$ and $\xi^{\mu_2}$, respectively.

V^\mu_n(\xi^\mu)\le_{st} V_n^{\mu_1}(\xi_{\mu_1})+ V_n^{\mu_2}(\xi_{\mu_2}),\quad n\in\N_0,\\

V^\mu_{\le n}(\xi^\mu)\le_{st} V_{\le n}^{\mu_1}(\xi_{\mu_1})+ V_{\le n}^{\mu_2}(\xi_{\mu_2}),\quad n\in\N_0.
\end{align}

In \cref{ex:quadratic-mean-flow}, suppose deterministic $0<M_2,M_4<\infty$
satisfy $P_0Z^2\leq M_2$ and $P_0Z^4\leq M_4$.  For
$\delta\in(0,1)$ define
\[
 u_{n,\delta}=\sqrt{\frac{2M_2}{n\delta}},
 \qquad
 v_{n,\delta}=\sqrt{\frac{2M_4}{n\delta}}.
\]
With probability at least $1-\delta$,
\begin{multline}
 \sup_{0\leq t\leq T}|\widetilde\Score_n(t)-\Risk_S(t)|
 \leq \frac{v_{n,\delta}}2
 +\bigl(\sqrt{M_2}+u_{n,\delta}\bigr)u_{n,\delta}\\
 {}+\left\{\frac1{n-1}+\frac1{2(n-1)^2}\right\}
       (M_2+v_{n,\delta}).
\end{multline}
For fixed $\delta$, the bound in \eqref{eq:quadratic-unbounded-band} is
$O(n^{-1/2})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unbounded quadratic-loss risk curve

[Proposition 19 of arXiv:2608.29972, '\bf Cram\'er transform, half-space depth and threshold phenomena for convex bodies'] Let $K$ be a body in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then, for every $a\in(0,1)$,
$$\int_K\exp\left(\frac{a}{n}\Lambda_K^*(x)\right)\,dx\leq 2^a\Gamma(1-a)n^a.$$
In particular,
$$\mathbb{E}_{\mu_K}\left[\exp\left(\frac{a}{n}\Lambda_K^*(X)\right)\right]\leq C(a)n^a.$$

[Proposition 3 (Phase function and its maximizer) of arXiv:2605.11995, 'Intrinsic volumes of \(\ell_p\)-balls and a continuum of Maxwell--Poincar\'e--Borel laws f'] Fix \(1<p<\infty\) and \(\beta\in(0,1)\). Define the function $\Psi_{p,\beta}:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$
by
\begin{equation}
\Psi_{p,\beta}(\theta)
=
\frac{1-\beta}{2}\log \theta
+\beta\log \mathcal I_p(\theta)
+(1-\beta)\log \mathcal J_p(\theta),
\qquad \theta>0.
\end{equation}
Then \(\Psi_{p,\beta}\) has a unique global maximizer \(\theta_{p,\beta}\in(0,\infty)\). Moreover, $\Psi_{p,\beta}''(\theta_{p,\beta})<0$,
and \(\theta_{p,\beta}\) is the unique solution in \((0,\infty)\) of the equation
\begin{equation}
\theta_{p,\beta}\,\frac{\mathcal J_p(\theta_{p,\beta})}{\mathcal I_p(\theta_{p,\beta})}
=
\frac{(1-\beta)p}{2(p-1)\beta}.
\end{equation}
For $p=2$, this simplifies to $\theta_{2,\beta}=(1-\beta)/\beta$ and
\begin{equation}
\Psi_{2,\beta}(\theta)=\frac{1-\beta}{2}\log\theta+\frac{1}{2}\log\pi-\frac{1}{2}\log(1+\theta),\quad \theta>0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 13 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Consider a distribution $\mu$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ and a sample $X\sim\mu$. Assign, for each $v\in[n]$, an independent random variable $U_v\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]$. Then the vertex field denoising process with respect to $\mu$ is defined by the following process $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$:
    $$
Y_t:=\{v\in[n]:X_v=1\wedge U_v\leq t\}.
    $$
title: Definition 13 of arXiv:2605.02002

body:
[Lemma restr-cleft-sym-mon of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $i\colon S\hookrightarrow T$ be a cleft. Then the strong symmetric monoidal functor $i^*\colon\CAT_T^\times\to\CAT_S^\times$ restricts to a strong symmetric monoidal functor $\CAT_T^{\textup{$S$-cc},\otimes}\to\CAT_S^{\textup{$S$-cc},\otimes}$.
    \begin{proof}
        This proof is an elaboration on [CLL_Clefts]*{Remark 4.23}.  Unravelling definitions, the lemma amounts to proving the following:
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item The unique $S$-cocontinuous $T$-functor $\ul\Spc_S\to i^*(\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T})$ preserving the terminal object is an equivalence.
            \item For any ${\mathcal{C}}_1,{\mathcal{C}}_2\in\CAT_T^\text{$S$-cc}$, `the' universal $S$-bilinear map $\beta\colon{\mathcal{C}}_1\times{\mathcal{C}}_2\to{\mathcal{D}}$ forgets to the universal $S$-bilinear map $i^*{\mathcal{C}}_1\times i^*{\mathcal{C}}_2\to i^*{\mathcal{D}}$.
        \end{enumerate}
        The first statement is clear, while for the second statement it will suffice to show that for any $S$-cocomplete $S$-$\infty$-category ${\mathcal{D}}$ the induced map 
        \[
            -\circ i^*\beta\colon{\textup{Fun}}_S^\text{$S$-bilinear}(i^*{\mathcal{C}}_1\times i^*{\mathcal{C}}_2,{\mathcal{E}})\to{\textup{Fun}}_S^\text{$S$-cc}(i^*{\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})
        \]
        is an equivalence. By [CLL_Clefts]*{Construction~4.21 and Corollary~4.22}, the equivalence $\ul{\textup{Fun}}_T({\mathcal{D}},i_*{\mathcal{E}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;} i_*\ul{\textup{Fun}}_S(i^*{\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$ obtained as the total mate of the obvious equivalence $i^*{\mathcal{D}}\times i^*(-)\cong i^*({\mathcal{D}}\times-)$ restricts to $\ul{\textup{Fun}}_T^\text{$S$-cc}({\mathcal{D}},i_*{\mathcal{E}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;} i_*\ul{\textup{Fun}}_S^\text{$S$-cc}(i^*{\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$, and evaluating at the terminal presheaf $1\in\PSh(T)$ yields a natural equivalence ${\textup{Fun}}_T({\mathcal{D}},i_*{\mathcal{E}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;} {\textup{Fun}}_S(i^*{\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$ restricting to ${\textup{Fun}}_T^\text{$S$-cc}({\mathcal{D}},i_*{\mathcal{E}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;} {\textup{Fun}}_S(i^*{\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$. On the other hand, applying this observation twice, Remark~(rk:charact-bilinear of the paper) shows that also the equivalence ${\textup{Fun}}_S(i^*{\mathcal{C}}_1\times i^*{\mathcal{C}}_2,{\mathcal{E}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\textup{Fun}}_T({\mathcal{C}}_1\times{\mathcal{C}}_2,i_*{\mathcal{E}})$ restricts to subcategories of $S$-bilinear functors. In summary, we obtain a commutative square
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                 {\textup{Fun}}_S^\text{$S$-bilinear}(i^*{\mathcal{C}}_1\times i^*{\mathcal{C}}_2,{\mathcal{E}})\arrow[r,"-\circ i^*\beta"]\arrow[d,"\sim"'] &[.5em] {\textup{Fun}}_S^\text{$S$-cc}(i^*{\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})\arrow[d,"\sim"]\\[-.05ex]
                 {\textup{Fun}}_T^\text{$S$-bilinear}({\mathcal{C}}_1\times {\mathcal{C}}_2,i_*{\mathcal{E}})\arrow[r,"-\circ\beta"'] & {\textup{Fun}}_T^\text{$S$-cc}({\mathcal{D}},i_*{\mathcal{E}})
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        The bottom map is invertible by the defining property of $\beta$, whence so is the upper map by $2$-out-of-$3$, as desired.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma restr-cleft-sym-mon of arXiv:2608.28504

[Definition 6 (Good boxes) of arXiv:2607.02477, 'Mixing times of spin systems on dynamical percolation'] Let $i\in\T_M^d$ and $n\in\N$. We say that a box $\B_{i,n}=\Lambda_i\times\II_n$ is \textit{good} if the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(A\arabic*), ref=A\arabic*]
    \item For any $\tilde\eta\in\{0,1\}^{E(\T_N^d)}$ and $\Upsilon\in\mathcal{E}_{i,n}$, the process $(\tilde\eta_t)_{t\in\II_n}$ started from $\tilde\eta$ and evolved using $\upd_{i,n}(\eta)\cup\Upsilon$ is such that for all $k$ with $\I_k\subset\II_n^{(2)}$ and all $x\in\Lambda_i$,
    $$|\tilde\C_k^\ajar(x)| ~\leq~ \log^2 L, $$
    where $\tilde\C_k^\ajar(x)$ refers to the $\I_k$-ajar cluster of $(\tilde\eta_t)_{t\geq 0}$ containing $x$.
    \item For any $\tilde\sigma,\hat\sigma\in S^{\T_N^d}$, $\tilde\eta\in\{0,1\}^{E(\T_N^d)}$, $\Xi,\Xi'\in\mathcal{S}_{i,n}^{(2)}$ and $\Upsilon\in\mathcal{E}_{i,n}^{(2)}$, the processes $(\tilde\sigma_t,\tilde\eta_t)_{t\in\II_n^{(2)}}$ and $(\hat\sigma_t,\tilde\eta_t)_{t\in\II_n^{(2)}}$, started from $(\tilde\sigma,\tilde\eta)$ and $(\hat\sigma,\tilde\eta)$, respectively, and evolved using $\upd_{i,n}^{(2)}(\sigma)\cup\Xi$ and $\upd_{i,n}^{(2)}(\eta)\cup\Upsilon$ for $(\tilde\sigma_t,\tilde\eta_t)_{t\in\II_n^{(2)}}$, and $\upd_{i,n}^{(2)}(\sigma')\cup\Xi'$ and $\upd_{i,n}^{(2)}(\eta)\cup\Upsilon$ for $(\hat\sigma_t,\tilde\eta_t)_{t\in\II_n^{(2)}}$, are such that 
    $$\tilde\sigma_\frac{(n+1)C}{\lambda}(x) ~=~ \hat\sigma_\frac{(n+1)C}{\lambda}(x), \quad \forall x\in\overline{\Lambda_i^\core}.$$
    \item For any $\tilde\sigma,\hat\sigma\in S^{\T_N^d}$ such that $\tilde\sigma(\overline{\Lambda_i^\core})=\hat\sigma(\overline{\Lambda_i^\core})$, $\tilde\eta\in\{0,1\}^{E(\T_N^d)}$, $\Xi,\Xi'\in\mathcal{S}_{i,n}^{(2)}$ and $\Upsilon\in\mathcal{E}_{i,n}^{(2)}$, the processes $(\tilde\sigma_t,\tilde\eta_t)_{t\in\II_n^{(2)}}$ and $(\hat\sigma_t,\tilde\eta_t)_{t\in\II_n^{(2)}}$ defined as in Condition (\ref{A2}) are such that for all $t\in\II_n^{(2)}$,
    $$\tilde\sigma_t(x) ~=~ \hat\sigma_t(x), \quad \forall x\in\Lambda_i^\core.$$
\end{enumerate}
If any of those conditions fail, we say that $\B_{i,n}$ is a \textit{bad} box.
title: Good boxes

[Corollary cor:final-theory of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $L \supseteq \textbf{FIK}$.
  For any $L$-consistent theory $(\Gamma, \Delta)$
  there is a maximal and $L$-final theory $(\Gamma^*, \Delta^*)$ such that
  $(\Gamma, \Delta) \subseteq (\Gamma^*, \Delta^*)$.
  \begin{proof}
    In the proof of Lindenbaum lemma, choose $(\Gamma_i, \Delta_i \cup \set{\varphi_i})$ if and only if $(\Gamma_i \cup \set{\varphi_i}, \Delta_i)$ is not $L$-consistent.
    Then it is easy to see that $(\Gamma_\omega \cup \Pi, \Delta_\omega \setminus \Pi)$ is not $L$-consistent for any nonempty $\Pi \subseteq \Delta_\omega$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:final-theory of arXiv:2608.29708

[Openproblem 10 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Let $\ka>0$.
Does there exist an asymptotic expansion
\begin{align}

\msf T_\ka(t)-\msf T_0(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\msf a_n(\ka,t)\qquad\text{as }t\to0,

body:
[Theorem 26 (Stokes--Betti coordinate formula) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Under the preceding hypotheses,
\begin{equation}
 [\gamma_u]
 =
 \sum_{\alpha=1}^{\mu}
 C^{\mathrm{Betti}}_{u\alpha}[\Gamma_\alpha].
 
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}\in
 \operatorname{Mat}_{N\times\mu}(\mathbb Z)
\]
is locally constant on \(\mathfrak C\).  If the representatives are
transverse, then
\begin{equation}
 C^{\mathrm{Betti}}_{u\alpha}
 =
 \#_{\mathrm{or}}
 \bigl(\gamma_u\pitchfork\check\Gamma_\alpha\bigr),
 
\end{equation}
the finite signed intersection count.  Its rank, integral kernel,
cokernel, and elementary divisors are therefore computed exactly by the
Smith normal form.

Across a Stokes wall, write the change of integral descending basis as
\[
 \boldsymbol\Gamma^+
 =
 S_{\mathrm{top}}\boldsymbol\Gamma^-,
 \qquad
 S_{\mathrm{top}}\in\operatorname{GL}_\mu(\mathbb Z).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^+
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^-S_{\mathrm{top}}^{-1}.
 
\end{equation}
Along a generic path crossing successively walls with matrices
\(S_1,\ldots,S_k\),
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}(\lambda_1)
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}(\lambda_0)
 S_1^{-1}\cdots S_k^{-1}.
 
\end{equation}

If an analytically normalised thimble frame is related to the integral
frame by
\[
 \boldsymbol\Gamma^{\mathrm{an}}
 =
 G\,\boldsymbol\Gamma^{\mathrm{top}},
 \qquad
 G\in\operatorname{GL}_\mu(\C),
\]
then its selected-cycle coordinate matrix is
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}G^{-1}.
 
\end{equation}
Thus nonintegral multipliers caused by analytic normalisations do not
contradict the integral Picard--Lefschetz coefficients.

body:
[Definition 44 ($\delta$-coalescent vertices) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] For \(n \ge 1\) and \(\delta > 0\),  define
\begin{equation}  H = H(n,\delta) := \left\lfloor \frac{h(q_n)}{\lfloor\delta n\rfloor} \right\rfloor. 
\end{equation}
The interval $\big[s\lfloor\delta n\rfloor,(s+1)\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\big)$ is called the \textit{$s$-th height interval}. We focus on the coalescent process starting from height \((s+1)\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\) for \(s = 1, \dots, H-2\). Recall that $\cX_{s\lfloor\delta n\rfloor}\big(n, (s+1)\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\big)$
 consists of all vertices at height \(s\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\) that have at least one descendant at height \((s+1)\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\). Those vertices are referred to as the \textit{\(\delta\)-coalescent vertices} at the \( s \)-th height interval. The collection of all \(\delta\)-coalescent vertices at these height intervals is denoted by
    \[
        \bar{\cX}(n,\delta) := \bigcup_{s=1}^{H-2} \cX_{s\lfloor \delta n \rfloor}\big(n,(s+1)\lfloor \delta n \rfloor\big).
    \]
title: $\delta$-coalescent vertices

[Proposition 6 (Convex case) of arXiv:2511.13559, 'Asymptotic analysis of rare events in high dimensions'] Let $N\geq1$ and $\sup_{u\in D}|g(u)|\leq1$. Suppose Assumption~\ref{assume1} is satisfied and $D$ is star-shaped about $0_{d+1}$. Also, suppose the restriction of $z$ to any line segment in $D$ emanating from $0_{d+1}$ is convex. Let $R=24+2(1+2N)(\log\la)/d$ and suppose $\g\in C^{2N}(\us(R\e)\times[0,(R\e)^2))$, $\z\in C^{2N+2}(\us(R\e)\times[0,(R\e)^2))$. Suppose there are constants $\CR$, $C_{\g,\ell}$, $\ell=0,\dots,2N$ and $C_{\z,\ell}$, $\ell=0,\dots,2N+2$ such that
 \begin{align}
 R\e&\leq\min(1,\rho_0),\qquad R\e\delta_2(R\e/2)\leq 2,\\
 R\e &\leq 3/C_{\z,3},
 \end{align}
and~\eqref{BC},~\eqref{forq},~\eqref{forw}, are satisfied.

 Then the conclusion of Proposition~\ref{prop:main} follows. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2608.30898, 'Necessity of Ladyzhenskaya \& Ural'tseva's sufficient conditions in nonuniform ellipticity'] Let $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a bounded, Lipschitz domain and $u_{0}\in C(\partial \Omega)$ be a function. Introduce class
\eqn{0.33}
$$
\mathcal{D}_{\infty}(u_{0};\Omega):=\left\{w\in \mathbb{X}(\Omega)\colon w=u_{0}\mbox{ on }\partial \Omega\right\}.
$$
Then there exists a unique maximizer $u\in \mathcal{D}_{\infty}(u_{0};\Omega)$ of Dirichlet problem
$$
\mathcal{D}_{\infty}(u_{0};\Omega)\ni w\mapsto \max_{w\in \mathcal{D}_{\infty}(u_{0};\Omega)}\mathcal{J}_{q}(w;\Omega).
$$
iff $\mathcal{D}_{\infty}(u_{0};\Omega)\not =\emptyset$.

[Lemma 33 of arXiv:2608.18834, 'The Parabolic Anderson Model's Total Mass at Small Times: Geometry, Fluctuations, and Reno'] For every bounded open set $G\subset\mbb R^d$,
define
\[\mf c(G)=\left(\int_{G^2}\msf g(x-y)\d x\dd y\right)^{1/2}=\left(\int_{\mbb R^d}|\hat{\mbf 1_G}(\om)|^2\dd\mu(\om)\right)^{1/2};\]

\[\lim_{\eps\to0}\mbf E\left[\left(\int_{G^2}\al^\eps_t(x)\d x\right)^m\right]^{1/m}\sim \mf c(G)^2\,t^{2H_0}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
        H_C(p)>H_C(u)=\frac{C}{N}.
\]
Thus $u$ is the unique global minimizer of the LRU hit rate on
$\Delta_N^\circ$.  Equivalently, the LRU miss rate $1-H_C(p)$ is uniquely
maximized at $u$ on $\Delta_N^\circ$.

body:
[Theorem sec1-thm.2 of arXiv:2602.04303, '\Large\textbf{Strong solutions to SDEs with singular drifts driven by fractional Brownian '] Let $X_{s,t}^x$ be a unique strong solution to the SDE
			\begin{equation}
				\mathrm{d} X_{s,t}^x=b(t,X_{s,t}^x)\mathrm{d} t+\mathrm{d} B_t^H,\qquad 0\leq s\leq t\leq T,\qquad X_{s,s}^x=x\in\mathbb{R}^d,
			\end{equation}
			where $b\in L^p_xL^q_t$ with $p,q$ satisfying (equation cond1 of the paper) and (equation cond2 of the paper). Then, the map $\phi_{s,t}(x,\omega):[0,T]^2\times\mathbb{R}^d\times\Omega\ni(s,t,x,\omega)\mapsto X_{s,t}^x(\omega)$ is a stochastic flow of homeomorphisms for the SDE (equation sec1-eq.1 of the paper), that is, there exists a universal set $\Omega^*\in\mathcal{F}$ of full Wiener measure such that for all $\omega\in\Omega^*$, the following states are true:
			\begin{enumerate}
				\item $\phi_{s,t}(x,\omega)$ is continuous in $(s,t,x)\in[0,T]^2\times\mathbb{R}^d$.
				\item $\phi_{s,t}(\cdot,\omega)=\phi_{u,t}(\phi_{s,u}(\cdot,\omega),\omega)$ for all $s,u,t\in\mathbb{R}^d$.
				\item $\phi_{s,s}(x,\omega)=x$ for all $(s,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$.
				\item $\phi_{s,s}(\cdot,\omega):\mathbb{R}^d\mapsto\mathbb{R}^d$ are homeomorphisms for all $s,t\in[0,T]$. 
			\end{enumerate}
			Moreover, $\phi_{s,t}(\cdot,\omega):\mathbb{R}^d\mapsto\mathbb{R}^d$ is Sobolev differentiable, i.e.
			$$\phi_{s,t}(\cdot,\omega)\text{ and } \phi_{s,t}^{-1}(\cdot,\omega)\in L^2(\Omega;W^{1,p_1}(\mathbb{R}^d,w)),\qquad\forall\; s,t\in[0,T],\,p_1\in(1,\infty)$$ 
			where $W^{1,p_1}(\mathbb{R}^d,w)$ is a  weighted Sobolev space with weight $w$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem sec1-thm.2 of arXiv:2602.04303

body:
[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.26001, 'The kernel of the Birman--Craggs--Johnson homomorphism'] Fix $g \geq 2$ and $b \in \{0,1\}$.  Set $H = \HH_1(\Sigma_g^b;\bbF_2)$.
Consider a separating twist $T_x \in \Torelli_g^b$ and a BP map $T_y T_z^{-1} \in \Torelli_g^b$.
Let $H = U \oplus V$ be the symplectic splitting associated to $x$ and let 
$h \in H$ be the $\bbF_2$-homology class of $T_y T_z^{-1}$.  Then 
$[T_x,T_y T_z^{-1}]$ is a basic commutator if and only if the following are
satisfied:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(c$\hspace{2pt}'$)] $\igeom(x,y) \leq 2$ and $\igeom(x,z) \leq 2$; and
\item[(d$\hspace{2pt}'$)] writing $h = u+v$ with $u \in U$ and $v \in V$, we have $u \neq 0$ and $v \neq 0$.
\end{itemize}
title: Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.26001

[Proposition 3 (Kaimanovich--Savchuk ray decomposition {\cite[Section~5) of arXiv:2606.23896, 'The one-point Schreier Poisson boundary of Thompson's group \(F\)'] {Kaimanovich2017}; \cite{Savchuk2010,Savchuk2015}}]
The Schreier graph \(\Gamma\) contains
two families of attached one-dimensional rays. The negative type rays are the
connected components of the subgraph on
\((-\infty,0]\cap\mathbb Z[1/2]\), attached to vertices in
\((0,1]\cap\mathbb Z[1/2]\). The positive type rays are the connected
components of the subgraph on \([2,\infty)\cap\mathbb Z[1/2]\), attached to
vertices in \([1,2)\cap\mathbb Z[1/2]\). The only vertex to which one ray of
each type is attached is \(1\).

[Satz 2 of arXiv:2511.20322, 'Dissertation'] Let $\be \in (0,1)$, $c > 0$, $L, \la > 0$ and $\cR : \R^d\to \R \in \dC 2$ be $\la$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth such that $\nabla^2 \cR$ is Hölder continuous.
Let $Y$ be the solution to the Young differential equation
\begin{equation}

dY_t = - \frac{1}{(1+ct)^\be} \nabla \cR(Y_t)\,dt + \frac{1}{(1+ct)^\be} \si\,d\hat W_t,
\end{equation}
driven by an epoched Brownian motion $\hat W$ with period $T$. Then
\[\left|Y_t - (\nabla \cR)^{-1}(T^{-1}\si \hat W_T)\right| \leq T^{1/2-\be} |\si| \left(4.7\frac{L}{\la} + 1.2\right)c^{-\be}\frac{\sqrt{\log t}}{t^{\be}} + o\left(\sqrt{\log t}\cdot  t^{-\be}\right), t\to \infty, \quad a.s.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Satz 2 of arXiv:2511.20322

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2506.10856, 'The space of multifurcating ranked tree shapes: enumeration, lattice structure, and Markov'] The space $\mathcal{T}_{N,K}$ is in bijection with the set of vectors $\{t, l\}$, each of length $K$ that satisfy the following constraints:  
\begin{enumerate}[label={S\arabic*.}]
    \item $t_1=0$ and $1\leq t_i\leq i-1$: the parent of the root is labeled 0 and the parent of node $i$ must have smaller rank (label) than $i$. 
    \item $\sum_{i=1}^K l_i=N$: the total number of leaves is $N$.
    \item $l_j\geq 2$ if $| \{ i: t_i= j\} | =0$: an internal node must subtend at least 2 leaves if it does not subtend an internal node. This also implies $l_K \geq 2$: the last internal node subtends at least 2 leaves and no internal nodes.
    \item $l_j\geq 1$ if $| \{ i: t_i= j\} | = 1$: an internal node must subtend at least 1 leaf if it is the parent of only one other internal node. 
\end{enumerate}

Let N1,N2 each have rate lambda Poisson marginals. If independent, Var(N1(t)+N2(t))=2*lambda*t; if N1=N2, the variance is 4*lambda*t. Both inputs have identical individual IDCs equal to one, but the total IDC is respectively one and two. Thus any multi-bottleneck diffusion approximation based solely on the marginal IDC data has a missing covariance parameter before reflection is even applied. Check: Expand Var(A+B)=Var A+Var B+2 Cov(A,B). The independent and common-input examples make the cross term respectively zero and lambda*t. They are auxiliary arrival models, not claimed counterexamples to an analyzer that retains cross covariances. Obstruction: Need a consistent joint covariance model and its propagation through multidimensional reflected Brownian flow limits. This information obstruction does not provide those estimates or an approximation error bound.

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] A variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ follows the uniform law of $[a,b]$ precisely when the following happens, for any measurable function $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$:
$$E(\phi(f))=\frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b\phi(x)dx$$
Equivalently, we must have $f:X\to[a,b]$, up to a set of null measure, and given a measurable set $Y\subset[a,b]$, the following must happen, $\lambda$ being the Lebesgue measure:
$$P(f\in Y)=\frac{\lambda(Y)}{b-a}$$
Also, in this latter statement, we can restrict the attention to the intervals $Y\subset[a,b]$.

[Lemma lem:young of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] The product of smooth functions  
$$ (f_1,f_2)\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)\times C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n) \mapsto f_1f_2\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n) $$ extends uniquely as a bilinear continuous map
from $\mathcal{C}^\alpha(\mathbb{R}^n)\times \mathcal{C}^\beta(\mathbb{R}^n) \mapsto \mathcal{C}^{\inf(\alpha,\beta)}(\mathbb{R}^n) $ for $\alpha+\beta>0$.    

A consequence of the above is that for all compact set $K\subset \mathbb{R}^n$, the set $\mathcal{C}^\alpha_K(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of H\"older distributions of regularity $\alpha<0$ and supported by $K$ injects continuously in the dual of $\mathcal{C}^\beta(\mathbb{R}^n)$ provided $\alpha+\beta>0$.

body:
[Theorem 40 (Optional stopping for nonnegative supermartingales) of arXiv:2608.20337, 'Information on trajectories:\\ martingales and random times'] Let $(M_t)$ be a nonnegative supermartingale and $\tau$ a stopping time (possibly infinite, with $M_\infty := \liminf_{t\to\infty} M_t$).
Then
\[
  \E[M_\tau] \leq M_0 .
\]
If $(M_t)$ is a nonnegative martingale, the matching equality $\E[M_\tau] = M_0$ holds in each of the following cases.
\emph{(a)} $\tau$ is bounded.
\emph{(b)} The stopped family $\{M_{\tau\wedge n}\}_{n\geq 0}$ is uniformly integrable (in particular when $(M_t)$ is closed by an integrable terminal variable, or $\tau$ is a.s.\ finite and $(M_t)$ is uniformly integrable).
Integrability of $M_\tau$ alone does \emph{not} suffice: a nonnegative martingale can leak mass to $\{\tau = \infty\}$, so that $\E[M_\tau] < M_0$ even though $\E[M_\tau] < \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:perimeter of arXiv:2606.11248, 'Persistent Homology of the Planar Wiener Sausage: Brownian Scaling and a Logarithmic Expec'] Let $0<a<b<\infty$. There exist constants $C_{a,b}<\infty$ and $T_{a,b}<\infty$ such that, for all $T\ge T_{a,b}$ and all $r\in[a,b]$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathcal{H}^{1}\bigl(\partial K_{T}^{(r)}\bigr)\bigr]\le C_{a,b}\frac{T}{(\log T)^{2}}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every fixed $r>0$,
\[
\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{(\log T)^{2}}{T}\,\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathcal{H}^{1}\bigl(\partial K_{T}^{(r)}\bigr)\bigr]<\infty.
\]

body: Let (X_n)_{n >= 0} be a submartingale with respect to a filtration (F_n)_{n >= 0} with E[|X_n|] < infinity for every n. Then X_n admits a decomposition X_n = M_n + A_n, where (M_n) is a martingale with respect to (F_n), (A_n) is a predictable, non-decreasing process (A_{n+1} >= A_n almost surely, A_n is F_{n-1}-measurable for n >= 1) with A_0 = 0, and this decomposition is almost surely unique. If (X_n) is itself a martingale, A_n is identically 0. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]

[Lemma lem:rkhs_decomposition of arXiv:2608.23938, 'Generalization, memorization, and overfitting \\for diffusion models trained in the lazy h'] Suppose that Assumption~(ass:kernel_func_vanishing_kappa of the paper) holds. Then, every function $f \in {\mathcal H}$ can be uniquely represented as
    \[
        f({\boldsymbol x}) = \<{\boldsymbol \theta}, {\boldsymbol x}\> + \sum_{k\in\mathcal A_h} \sqrt{\frac{\alpha_k}{d^k}} \<{\boldsymbol W}_k, {\boldsymbol x}^{\otimes k}\>,
    \]
    where \({\boldsymbol \theta} \in \mathbb{R}^d\) and \({\boldsymbol W}_k \in \mathrm{Sym}^k(\mathbb{R}^d)\) is a symmetric tensor for all \(k \geq 3\). Furthermore, the associated RKHS norm of \(f\) is given by
    \[
        \|f\|_{{\mathcal H}}^2 = d\|{\boldsymbol \theta}\|_2^2 +  \sum_{k\in\mathcal A_h} \|{\boldsymbol W}_k\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2.
    \]

[Lemma 71 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Suppose $\phi \in L^2(0,T;\zero{H}{2}(\domO)) \cap L^{\frac32}(0,T;\newone{V})$ and $\bu \in L^2(0,T;\StokesV)$. Assume also that 
\begin{trivlist} 
\item[(i)] the sequence $(\bu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is bounded in $L^2(0,T;\StokesV)$, i.e. 
\[
\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \int_0^T \Vert \bu_n(s) \Vert_{\StokesV}^{2}\, \d s< \infty,
\]
\item[(ii)] the sequence $(\phi_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is bounded in $L^2(0,T;\zero{H}{2}(\domO)) \cap L^{\frac32}(0,T;\newone{V})$, i.e.  
\[
\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \left\{\int_0^T \Vert \phi_n(s) \Vert_{\zero{H}{2}}^{2}\, \d s + \int_0^T \Vert \phi_n(s) \Vert_{\newone{V}}^{3/2}\, \d s
\right\}< \infty
\]
and
\item[(iii)]  $\bu_n \to \bu$ in $L^2(0,T;\StokesH)$ and $\phi_n \to \phi$ in $L^2(0,T;\newone{H})$. 
\end{trivlist}
Then, for every $z_2 \in \newone{V}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \lim_{ n \to \infty} \int_0^T \lvert \duality{B_{1,n}(\bu_n(s),\phi_n(s)) - B_1(\bu(s),\phi(s))}{z_2}{\newone{V}}{\newonep{V}} \rvert\,\d s= 0.
     \end{equation}

Work as d->infinity with integers N=N(d)->infinity and M=M(d)>=1. Let (X_d,nu_d) and (Omega_d,tau_d) be probability spaces and sigma_d in L2(nu_d times tau_d). Use its singular expansion sigma_d(x,theta)=sum_j sqrt(mu_j) psi_j(x) phi_j(theta), with ordered nonnegative mu_j, sum_j mu_j<infinity, positive mu_(M+1) and positive denominators in the displayed tail conditions, and orthonormal families psi_j in L2(nu_d), phi_j in L2(tau_d). Let D_d be the closed span of the psi_j and P_<=M its orthogonal projection onto the first M modes. Define the feature kernel U_d(theta,thetaprime)=E_x~nu_d sigma_d(x,theta)sigma_d(x,thetaprime), its spectral tail U_>r=sum_(j>r) mu_j phi_j phi_j^T, and kappa_r=sum_(j>r)mu_j>0 for each cutoff used. Draw theta_1,...,theta_N independently from tau_d and let K_ij=U_d(theta_i,theta_j). All stochastic rates below are as d->infinity. (H) There is one sequence u(d)>=M(d) such that, for every fixed real q>=1, all g in span{phi_1,...,phi_u} satisfy ||g||_(L2q(tau_d))<=C_q||g||_(L2(tau_d)), with C_q independent of d and g. (E) For the same u there is a fixed delta_E>0 such that N^(2+delta_E)<=kappa_u^2/sum_(j>u)mu_j^2 eventually. (Dupper) For every epsilon>0, max_i U_>M(theta_i,theta_i)/kappa_M=O_P(N^epsilon). (Sa) There is a fixed delta_a>0 with N^(1+delta_a)<=kappa_M/mu_(M+1) eventually. (Sb) There is a fixed delta_b>0 with M<=N^(1-delta_b) and kappa_M/mu_M<=N^(1-delta_b) eventually. For each fixed deterministic target sequence f_d in D_d, independent of the random features, define R_App(g,Theta)=inf_(a in R^N) E_x~nu_d[(g(x)-sum_i a_i sigma_d(x,theta_i))^2]. Then 0<=R_App(P_<=M f_d,Theta)<=o_P(1)||f_d||_(L2(nu_d))||P_<=M f_d||_(L2(nu_d)). This is the separate population upper statement Theorem5(b). Its hypotheses include Dupper and both spectral-gap clauses; Dlower is not assumed. There is no assertion at an integer-degree transition that violates these spectral-gap conditions.

PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Consider one FCFS server with Poisson arrival rate lambda>0 and independent exponential service rate mu>lambda. After becoming empty it remains on for deterministic grace g in [0,infinity], then switches off. A cold arrival triggers deterministic setup tau>=0, which is never cancelled; arrivals during setup wait. Put p=exp(-lambda g), x=lambda tau, rho=lambda/mu and y=p/(1+xp), with p=0 at g=infinity. The stationary mean queueing wait is lambda/[mu(mu-lambda)] + tau(1+x/2)y. If busy, on-idle, off and setup powers are B,I,O,U, average power is rho B+(1-rho)I+(1-rho)[O+xU-(1+x)I]y. Hence varying the grace period traces an affine waiting-power curve. The formula includes arrivals during setup and the subsequent busy period. It addresses k=1 and does not claim the many-server frontier or optimality among other policies.

Label: proof for a specified M/M/1 DelayedOff model, awaiting w346. It does not solve the source's many-server question.

Assume Poisson arrivals of rate lambda>0, independent exponential service of rate mu>lambda, FCFS, and a single server. After becoming empty, it remains on for a deterministic grace period g in [0,infinity], then switches off. An arrival to an off server starts a deterministic setup of duration tau>=0. Setup is not cancelled; arrivals during setup wait and are served when setup ends. Define p=exp(-lambda g) (p=0 for g=infinity), x=lambda tau, v=mu-lambda, and rho=lambda/mu.

The stationary mean queueing wait, excluding service, is

W(g)=lambda/[mu(mu-lambda)] + tau(1+lambda tau/2) p/(1+lambda tau p).

The long-run fractions of time busy, on-idle, off, and in setup are respectively

rho, (1-rho)(1-p)/(1+xp), (1-rho)p/(1+xp), (1-rho)xp/(1+xp).

If their powers are B,I,O,U, average power is

P(g)=rho B+(1-rho) I+(1-rho)[O+xU-(1+x)I] p/(1+xp).

Thus W and P lie on an affine line as g varies (power may be constant when the bracket vanishes); all later arrivals and the busy period are included.

Proof: Use iid regenerative cycles starting when a busy period ends. The next-arrival gap A is exponential(lambda). Its expected on-idle and off durations are (1-p)/lambda and p/lambda. Setup occurs with probability p and contributes tau p expected time. After setup the initial busy-period queue is K=1+Poisson(x), whereas after a hot arrival it is K=1.

For the birth-death queue killed at zero, its expected busy duration from k is k/v. Its expected area under the queue length is

F(k)=k^2/(2v)+(lambda+mu)k/(2v^2).

The generator satisfies LF(k)=-k and F(0)=0. A justification avoiding an unbounded optional-stopping assumption is as follows: embed at jump epochs, whose increments are iid with probabilities lambda/(lambda+mu) and mu/(lambda+mu). Negative drift and bounded increments give an exponential tail for the hitting time of zero from each fixed k, by a Chernoff bound on the unconstrained walk when survival forces its position to stay positive. Queue height is at most k plus the number of jumps. This tail makes the stopped quadratic boundary term vanish and the queue area integrable; apply the stopped generator identity and let the cutoff tend to infinity. The Poisson initial queue also has all moments and exponential moments sufficiently near zero, so the same formulas can be averaged over K.

E[K]=1+x, E[K^2]=1+3x+x^2 after setup, and the expected setup queue area is tau+lambda tau^2/2. Thus the expected cycle duration is

C=mu/[lambda v] (1+xp),

and its expected queue area is

A=mu/v^2 [1+mu tau p+lambda v tau^2 p/2].

Renewal reward gives E[N]=A/C. Little's law gives response time E[N]/lambda, and subtracting 1/mu yields the displayed W. Dividing each expected state duration by C yields the power fractions and their sum one. This also verifies busy fraction rho, g=0, g=infinity, and tau=0.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:531a5ddd276062b8b8612e5e597231bc49324742e8374f26aff0274068818a3d","revision_digest":"sha256:ee901e9ab6079a52e8000f515d63eeed51c6cfe36449a529fc20f5c928a510cc","source_id":"own-work:w340:mm1-deterministic-delayedoff-stationary-waiting-power-curve","source_revision":"2026-10-10-draft-awaiting-w346","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: The conditional expectation E[X | G] of an integrable X given a sub-sigma-algebra G is the (a.s. unique) G-measurable random variable Y with E[Y 1_A] = E[X 1_A] for all A in G. Key properties: the tower/law of total expectation E[E[X | G]] = E[X] (and E[E[X|H]|G] = E[X|G] for G subset H); it is linear, order-preserving, pulls out G-measurable factors (E[ZX | G] = Z E[X | G]), and equals E[X] when X is independent of G. It is the L^2 orthogonal projection onto G-measurable functions.

[Theorem 5 (Hard edge, \(q=1\)) of arXiv:2511.12623, 'The eigenvector bead process'] Fix \(K\in\mathbb{N}\) and an integer \(\alpha > K\).
Let \(T - N = \alpha\).
For each \(s\in\{0,\dots,K\}\), let \(\{\lambda^{(s)}_{j}\}_{j=1}^{N+s}\) denote the spectrum of the matrix \(X_{N+s}^\top X_{N+s}\),
and define the point process
\[
\Theta_{N}^{(s)} \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{N+s} \delta_{\,4N\,\lambda_{j}^{(s)}}.
\]
Then the process \(\big(\Theta_{N}^{(s)}\big)_{s=0}^{K}\) forms a Markov chain in \(s\) and converges in distribution to the Markov chain driven by the operator \(\mathcal{T}\).
The limiting point process of eigenvalues
\(
\Theta^{(s)} \;=\; \lim_{N\to\infty} \Theta_{N}^{(s)}
\)
is the \emph{Bessel point process} of parameter~\(\alpha\), describing the universal statistics at the hard edge of the spectrum. \cite{forrester1993hard,tracy1994bessel,forrester2010log} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Hard edge, \(q=1\)

[Definition 19 (Likelihood ratio dominance order $\leq_{\textnormal{lrd}}$) of arXiv:2605.16560, 'Seasonal Statistics of Shannon Rate in a Dynamical Poisson-Voronoi Cellular Network'] We say that two non-negative random variables $X,Y$ satisfy  likelihood ratio dominance order ({\em lrd order}), 

\[
X\leq_{\textnormal{lrd}} Y \mbox{ if } \frac{f_Y(z)}{f_X(z)} \mbox{ is an increasing function }
\]

on their common support. Note that lrd order implies stochastic domination~\cite{ShakedShanthikumar2007}.
title: Likelihood ratio dominance order $\leq_{\textnormal{lrd}}$

[Corollary coro:lower_bound_on_expected_size_of_fat_worms_on_nonamenable_graphs of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Consider a nonamenable graph $G$ with a subgroup of its automorphisms $\Gamma \leq \mathrm{Aut}(G)$ that acts transitively and unimodularly on $G$. Let $\eta \, : \, \mathbb{N}_{>0} \rightarrow [0,1]$ be a probability mass function and $\mathcal{X} = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{(x,H)_i} \sim \mathcal{P}_{\eta}^\lambda$.
Assume also that we are given some $R \in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$, a finite connected set $A \subset \subset V(G)$ and a subset of its exterior boundary $B \subseteq \partial_{\mathrm{ext}} A$.
There exists a constant $c(G) > 0$ depending only on the graph such that, for the restricted process $\check{ \mathcal{X} }_{A,B}^R$ defined in Definition (def:point_measure_restricted_to_hit_B_but_not_the_closure_of_A of the paper), we have
\begin{equation}
	
	\mathbb{E} \left[ \left| \mathrm{Tr}( \check{ \mathcal{X} }_{A,B}^R ) \right| \right] \geq
	c(G) \cdot \tfrac{ \lambda \cdot \mathbb{E} \left[ \mathcal{L}^2 \mathds{1} \left[ \mathcal{L} \leq R \right] \right] }{ \lambda \cdot m_1 + 1 } \cdot 
	\left[  
	\tfrac{ (1-\rho(G))^2 \cdot (1 + \mathrm{h} (G))}{2} \cdot |A| - \left( | \partial_{\mathrm{ext}} A | - |B| \right)
	\right],
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{L}$ denotes a random variable that has law $\eta$.
title: Corollary coro:lower_bound_on_expected_size_of_fat_worms_on_nonamenable_graphs of arXiv:2505.07145

[Theo 2 of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Assume that $0<\alpha<1$, $m\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, $m\leq0$ a.e. in
	$\Omega$, and that
	\[
	\Omega^0:=\operatorname{int}\{x\in\Omega:m(x)=0\}
	\]
	is a nonempty connected $C^{1,1}$ domain compactly contained in $\Omega$, $|\Omega^0|>0$. Assume also that
	$m<0$ a.e. in $\Omega\setminus\overline{\Omega^0}$.
Suppose that there exist $\rho_0>0$ and $m_{\rho_0}^->0$ such that
\begin{equation}
	\mathcal C_{\rho_0}\subset\Omega^-
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
	-m(x)\geq m_{\rho_0}^-
	\qquad\text{for a.e. }x\in\mathcal C_{\rho_0}.
\end{equation}
Then there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every $\lambda\in
(\lambda_{1,\Omega^0}-\varepsilon,\lambda_{1,\Omega^0}),$
the non-negative weak solution $u_\lambda^-$ given by
Theorem~\ref{thm:Main2} has compact support in $\Omega$. More precisely, there exists $\rho\in(0,\rho_0)$, independent of $\lambda$
sufficiently close to $\lambda_{1,\Omega^0}$, such that
$u_\lambda^-=0$ in $\mathcal C_\rho$. Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{supp}u_\lambda^-
\subset
\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)\geq\rho\}
\Subset\Omega.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theo 2 of arXiv:2608.30578

[Lemma lem:mass-selection of arXiv:2608.28330, 'Realising atomless laws as distance distributions on metric measure spaces'] Let $I=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ for some $N\in\mathbb N$, or let
		$I=\mathbb N$.  Let $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and let
		$(c_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of positive numbers satisfying $\sum_{i\in I}c_i=1-\alpha$.
		There is a constant $\gamma_0(\alpha)>0$ such that, if
		$\sup_{i\in I}c_i\le\gamma_0(\alpha)$, then there exist $p_0>0$
		and a family $(p_i)_{i\in I}$ of positive numbers satisfying
		\[
		\begin{alignedat}{2}
			&p_0+\sum_{i\in I}p_i
			=1,
			&\qquad
			&p_0^2+\sum_{i\in I}p_i^2
			=\alpha,
			\\
			&c_i
			=2p_i\Big(
			p_0+\sum_{\substack{j\in I\\j<i}}p_j
			\Big),
			\quad i\in I,
			&\qquad
			&\sum_{i\in I}p_i^2
			\le
			\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\sup_{i\in I}c_i.
		\end{alignedat}
		\]

   $D_{\lambda h} (\R^{2n} )$ with $\lambda >0$. If
   $\lambda $ is sufficiently large then the series in the right hand side of (\ref{comp-Miz}) is absolutely convergent and we have,    
\be( F \sharp _h^{\rm Wick} G ) (X) =  \sum _{\alpha} 
    \frac  {h^{|\alpha|}}   { 2^{|\alpha|} \alpha! }  
        \partial _X^{\alpha}   F  ( X)  \ 
         \partial _{\overline X}^{\alpha}  G (X), \ee
     
where
     
     $$ \partial _{X_j} = \partial _{x_j} - i \partial _{\xi_j},\quad
      \partial _{\overline X_j} = \partial _{x_j} + i \partial _{\xi_j} .$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    Fix $K>1,L>0$. Let $q\in \mathbb{Z}^2$ be such that $\phi(q)=2n$, $\mathrm{slope}(0,q)\in (K^{-1},K)$. Consider the point $p_{n,L}$ satisfying $\phi(p_{n,L})=0$ and $\psi(p_{n,L})=Kn^{2/3}$ and let $\ell_{n,L}$ denote the line segment joining $-p_{n,L}$ and $p_{n,L}$. [Definition 18 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $\{(S_\lambda,\mathcal{E}_\lambda)\}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ be a family of coarse spaces.
    Fix a notation:
    \[
    \otimes_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\mathcal{E}_\lambda :=\{E\subset \Pi_{\lambda \in \Lambda} S_\lambda\times \Pi_{\lambda \in \Lambda} S_\lambda\mid \text{for all }\lambda \in \Lambda, \Ad_{\pi_{\lambda}}(E)\in \mathcal{E}_\lambda \}.
    \]
    Then this forms a coarse structure on $\Pi_{\lambda \in \Lambda} S_\lambda$, and $(\Pi_{\lambda \in \Lambda} S_\lambda,\otimes_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\mathcal{E}_\lambda)$ is called the \emph{product coarse structure} of $\{(S_\lambda,\mathcal{E}_\lambda)\}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$.
    Here, $\pi_{\lambda}$ is the projection to $S_{\lambda}$ for each $\lambda\in \Lambda$.
title: Definition 18 of arXiv:2608.25785

[Theorem thm:basic_properties_of_PPPs of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Let $\mathcal{X} = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{(x,H)_i} \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^\lambda$ be as in Definition (def:Poisson_zoo_as_PPP of the paper) and given any $A \in \mathcal{Z}$ introduce the restricted measure $\nu_A(\cdot) := \nu ( \cdot \cap A)$.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item 
		
		If $A \in \mathcal{Z}$, then the restricted process $\mathcal{X} \mathds{1} [A]$ has law $\mathcal{Q}_{\nu_A}^\lambda$.
		\item 
		
		If $A_1, A_2, \ldots \in \mathcal{Z}$ are such that $A_i \cap A_j = \emptyset$ for $i \neq j$, then the restricted processes $\mathcal{X} \mathds{1} [A_1], \mathcal{X} \mathds{1}[A_2], \ldots$ are independent.
		\item 
		
		Let $p \in [0,1]$ and $\{ \xi_i \}_{i \in I}$ a collection of independent $\mathsf{Bernoulli}(p)$ random variables, and consider the following decomposition:
		\begin{equation}
			\mathcal{X} = \mathcal{X}_1 + \mathcal{X}_2 := \sum_{i \in I} \xi_i \delta_{(x,H)_i} + \sum_{i \in I} (1 - \xi_i) \delta_{(x,H)_i}.
		\end{equation}
		Then $\mathcal{X}_1 \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^{p v}$ and $\mathcal{X}_2 \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^{ (1-p)v }$ in law, and they are independent of each other.
		\item
		
		If $A \in \mathcal{Z}$, then $\mathcal{X}(A)$ follows a Poisson distribution.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:basic_properties_of_PPPs of arXiv:2505.07145

body:
[Lemma L_cEL of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] Suppose that $L$ is not contained in $S$. 
Let $x$ denote the number of vertices in 
$S\cap L$ that are not in $e'$.
Then 
\[
e(S\cap L) \leqslant \lambda x, 
\] 
with equality if and only if 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x=0$; or else
\item $x=r-2$ and $e(S\cap L)=\binom r2 -2$,
\end{enumerate}
and in all other cases,
\[
e(S\cap L) \leqslant \lambda x-\xi,
\] 
for some $\xi>0$ depending only on $r$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Efficiency within a leaf

For an iid uniform sign n by n matrix, projective equality within row partition pi with a blocks and column partition tau with b blocks has probability 2^(-((n-1)^2-(a-1)(b-1))).
n>=1; real mutually independent uniform {-1,1} entries; pi and tau fixed deterministic partitions.

Two sign rows (or columns) are projectively equal if one equals plus or minus the other. Fix any partitions pi and tau of the n row and n column labels into a and b nonempty blocks, respectively. Demand projective equality within every row block of pi and every column block of tau. Then the probability of all demands is exactly

    2^(-((n-1)^2 - (a-1)(b-1))).                      (P1)

Proof. Write B_ij=(-1)^X_ij with iid uniform bits, and perform all bit addition modulo two. Define D_ij=X_ij+X_i1+X_1j+X_11. Its first row and first column vanish. The map from X to its first row, its first column excluding the repeated corner, and D_ij for i,j>=2 is a bijection. Consequently the (n-1)^2 interior D bits are independent uniform bits.

Original rows i,k are projectively equal precisely when D_i*=D_k*: subtracting the two normalized bit rows removes their difference in column one. The analogous statement holds for columns. Thus all demands say that D is constant on each pi-block times tau-block rectangle. Rectangles meeting the block containing row 1 or the block containing column 1 must be zero. Each of the remaining (a-1)(b-1) rectangles has one free bit. Counting assignments proves P1. This also treats cycles of pair constraints without incorrectly multiplying them.

In particular, one specified row-pair event and one specified column-pair event have joint probability 2^(3-2n). Each marginal is 2^(1-n). Their joint probability is twice the product, for every n>=2. [Lemma lem:horiz of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] There is $C=C(d)<\infty$ such that the following holds. Let
$B,B'\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\times[0,\Lambda]$ and let $A,A'$ be increasing events determined, in the sense
of (lem:Hprops of the paper), by $B$ and $B'$ respectively. By (lem:Hprops of the paper) the regions on which
$A$ and $A'$ depend are the $6r$-neighbourhoods of the spatial projections of $B$ and $B'$, and
not those projections themselves. Suppose that these two regions are contained in cubes of side
$W$ and lie at distance $D$ from one another. Then
\begin{equation}

  \mathbb{P}_\eta(A\cap A')\ \le\ \mathbb{P}_\eta(A)\,\mathbb{P}_\eta(A')
  +C\eta\big(W^d+\Lambda^{d/2}\big)e^{-D^2/(2d\Lambda)} .
\end{equation}

[Corollary cor_fourmomentwienerchaos of arXiv:2509.18045, 'Density convergence on Markov diffusion chaos via Stein's method'] Assume $L$ is the infinite-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck generator (defined in Appendix (appendix_malliavin of the paper)) and $\Gamma$ is the associated carr\'{e} du champ operator. $X_n,n\geq 1$ is a sequence of eigenfunctions of $L$ with the same eigenvalue $q$ (in other words, $X_n,n\geq 1$ is a sequence of multiple Wiener integrals of a fixed order order $q$). Let  $\mathcal{Z}$ be a random variable distributed either as a normal distribution with density $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{(x-\alpha)^2}{2}}$ or a Gamma distribution with density $\frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)}x^{\alpha-1}e^{-x}\mathds{1}_{ \{x> 0\} }$. Set $F_n=Z_n+\alpha,n\geq 1$. 

Under the conditions that 
\begin{itemize}
  \item the first four moments of $F_n$ converge to the first four moments of $\mathcal{Z}$, 
    \item $\sup_{n\geq 1} \E{\frac{1}{\Gamma(F_n)^3}}<\infty$ in the case $\mathcal{Z}$ is normally distributed; and \\$\sup_{n\geq 1} \brac{\E{\frac{1}{F_n^6}\mathds{1}_{\{F_n\leq 0 \}}}+\E{\frac{1}{\Gamma(F_n)^4}}+\E{\frac{1}{F_n^4}} }<\infty $ in the case $\mathcal{Z}$ is Gamma distributed,
\end{itemize}
then the densities $p_{F_n}(x)$ converges to the density $p_\mathcal{Z}(x)$ for every $x\in \mathbb{R}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 16 (Arizmendi--P\'erez-Abreu squaring identity) of arXiv:2604.22114, 'Free compressions of R-diagonal random variables and the semigroup of Brown measures'] Let $\mu$ be a symmetric probability measure on $\R$, and let $S_\mu$ denote the $S$-transform of $\mu$
\emph{in the sense of} \cite{arizmendi_perez-abreu2009}.
Then there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and an open set $U\subset i\C^{+}$ with $(-\varepsilon,0)\subset U$ such that
$S_\mu$ and $S_{\mu_{sq}}$ are well-defined on $U$, and for every $z\in U$,
\begin{equation}

S_{\mu_{sq}}(z) \;=\; \frac{z}{1+z}\,\big[S_\mu(z)\big]^2,
\end{equation}
where $\mu_{sq}$ is the push-forward of $\mu$ under the map $t\mapsto t^2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Arizmendi--P\'erez-Abreu squaring identity

[Dfn 8 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] \begin{itemize}
   \item[(D1)] Let $b_{n} = n (\log n)^{-2}$ and $M = (\log n)^{2}.$ We divide the time interval $[0,n]$ into $M$ subintervals of equal length ($= b_{n}$) as follows. Let 
$$I^{1} (j) = \big[ n - j b_{n}, n - (j-1) b_{n} \big] =: [t^{1}_{j}, t^{1}_{j-1}] \ \ \ \text{ for \ \  $j =1, 2, \cdots , M$.} $$
 Note that $ 0 = t^{1}_{M} < t^{1}_{M-1} < \cdots < t^{1}_{1} < t^{1}_{0} = n. $

Similarly, we divide the time interval $[n,2n]$ in the same way as follows. Let 
$$I^{2} (j) = \big[ n + (j-1) b_{n}, n + j b_{n} \big] =: [t^{2}_{j-1}, t^{2}_{j}] \ \ \ \text{ for \ \  $j =1, 2, \cdots , M$.}$$
 Note that $ n= t^{2}_{0} < t^{2}_{1} < \cdots < t^{2}_{M-1} < t^{2}_{M} = 2n.  $

\item[(D2)] We set 

$$ L^{1} (j) = \text{len} \, \Big( \text{LE}^{\ast} \big( S [t^{1}_{j}, t^{1}_{j-1}  ] \big) \Big) \ \ \ \text{and } \ \ \ L^{2} (j) = \text{len} \, \Big( \text{LE}^{\ast} \big( S [t^{2}_{j-1}, t^{2}_{j}  ] \big) \Big). $$

As in (20) of \cite{DS-SW-4d}, we let 
$$ L^{\ast} = \max \big\{ j + k \ : \ I^{1} (j) \leftrightarrow I^{2} (k) \big\} $$
denote the size of the longest intersection. Here, for two intervals $I, J \subset [0, \infty)$, we write 
$$ I \leftrightarrow J \ \ \text{ if } \ \ \{ S(i) \ : \ i \in I \} \cap \{ S(j) \ : \ j \in J \} \neq \emptyset.$$
Clearly, $ 2 \le L^{\ast} \le 2M $. 

\item[(D3)] Set 
$$ L_{n}' = \text{len} \, \Big( \text{LE}^{\ast} \big( S[n,2n] \big) \Big). $$
Note that $L_{n}$ and $L_{n}'$ have the same distribution.

\item[(D4)] A time $k \in [0,n]$ is called a cut time (up to $n$) if $S[0,k] \cap S[k+1,n] = \emptyset$.

\end{itemize}
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2604.01748

[Lemm Bounds on the diameter, \cite{riordan2010diameter} of arXiv:2412.05746, 'Hyperbolicity, slimness, and minsize, on average'] Given $\lambda > 1$, let $\lambda_* < 1$ satisfy $\lambda_* e^{-\lambda_*} = \lambda e^{-\lambda}$ (i.e., the conjugate). Then there exists a constant $C_\lambda$ that depends only on $\lambda$, such that for $G_n \in \ER(n, \lambda/n)$ and its giant component $\mathscr{C}_{max}$,
    \[ \diam(\mathscr{C}_{max}) \leq  \left(\frac{1}{\log \lambda} + \frac{2}{\log (1/\lambda_*)} \right) \log n + C_\lambda \]
    with high probability. Note that for $\lambda \geq 4.67, \frac{2}{\log (1/\lambda_*)} < \frac{1}{\log \lambda}$ holds. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bounds on the diameter, \cite{riordan2010diameter}

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check what the OSSS route needs and whether it survives for q < 1. Result: The DRT proof uses (i) the FKG property of the random-cluster measure for q >= 1 (to make the model monotone so that the OSSS inequality applies to increasing events with the correct sign) and (ii) a differential inequality obtained from OSSS. For q < 1 the measure is expected to be negatively associated (C0091), the opposite of FKG, and the OSSS inequality's use of monotonicity fails: the covariance terms Cov(f, omega_e) can be of either sign. A conceivable replacement is a randomised-algorithm inequality for negatively associated measures, which does not exist in the literature to my knowledge, and even the existence of the infinite-volume measure and its monotonicity in p are delicate for q < 1 (the source notes this). A rigorous partial fact: for q < 1 the comparison inequalities of Fortuin give the random-cluster measure sandwiched between product measures with parameters p and p/(p + q(1-p)), which yields a non-trivial interval for both thresholds but not their equality. No progress on equality. Obstruction: No monotonicity, hence no OSSS-type inequality, for q < 1.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0092-sharp-phase-transition-for-the-random-cluster-model-with-q-1
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

[Prop of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] In Example (ex:different-stability-in-each-environment of the paper), the mixed process is exponentially ergodic for any choice of $\kappa>0$.
\begin{proof}
    Fix $\kappa>0$, and consider the function defined by
    \[
        h_\kappa(x,i)=\begin{cases}
            90 x^{\kappa/3} & i=1\\
            57 x^{\kappa/3} & i=2
        \end{cases}.
    \]
    Notice that
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal L_\kappa h_\kappa(x,1)
        &=(2x+1)(90(x+1)^{\kappa/3}-90x^{\kappa/3})
        +x(90(x-1)^{\kappa/3}-90x^{\kappa/3})
        +\kappa(57x^{\kappa/3}-90x^{\kappa/3})\\
        &=(2x+1)(30\kappa x^{\kappa/3-1}+o(x^{\kappa/3-1}))
        -x(30\kappa x^{\kappa/3-1}+o(x^{\kappa/3-1}))
        -33\kappa x^{\kappa/3}\\
        &=-3\kappa x^{\kappa/3}+o(x^{\kappa/3}),
    \end{align*}
    and similarly
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal L_\kappa h_\kappa(x,2)
        &=(x+1)(57(x+1)^{\kappa/3}-57x^{\kappa/3})
        +3x(57(x-1)^{\kappa/3}-57x^{\kappa/3})
        +\kappa(90x^{\kappa/3}-57x^{\kappa/3})\\
        &=(x+1)(19\kappa x^{\kappa/3-1}+o(x^{\kappa/3-1}))
        -3x(19\kappa x^{\kappa/3-1}+o(x^{\kappa/3-1}))
        +33\kappa x^{\kappa/3}\\
        &=-5\kappa x^{\kappa/3}+o(x^{\kappa/3}).
    \end{align*}
    The desired result follows from Theorem (thm:Lyapunov-exponential-ergodicity of the paper).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered prop of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks'

[Lemma 2 (Weighted-ratio expansion) of arXiv:2608.30916, 'Selection-Aware Stress Testing for Interactive Agents'] Let $a_g=P s_g>0$, $P^g h=P(s_gh)/a_g$, and $P_n^g h=P_n(s_gh)/P_ns_g$. Whenever $P_ns_g>0$,
\begin{equation}
 P_n^g h-P^g h
 =\frac{a_g}{P_ns_g}(P_n-P)
 \left\{\omega_g(h-P^gh)\right\},
 \qquad \omega_g=s_g/a_g.
 
\end{equation}
If $P\{\omega_g^2(h-P^gh)^2\}<\infty$ and $P_ns_g\to_p a_g$, then
\begin{equation}
 \sqrt n(P_n^g h-P^g h)
 =\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \omega_g(W_i)\{h(W_i)-P^gh\}+o_p(1).
 
\end{equation}
The same statement holds coordinatewise for a fixed-dimensional vector $h$.

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2604.19220, 'Split merge dynamics for expanding intervals and point processes on the real line.'] \textup{(a)} {\bf Deterministic stratified fragmentation}. 
Assume that the averages $\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^np_k$ converge as $n\to\infty$, with limit $\bar p$ say.
Then, as $n\to\infty$, 
$$ 
g_n \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d} \begin{cases}
    \bar{p}\beta_{\left(1,\frac{1}{c}\right)}(0,1-q)+(1-\bar{p})\beta_{\left(\frac{1}{c},1\right)}(1-q,1) &\text{if }\ 0<c<\infty
    \\\bar{p}\d_0+(1-\bar{p}) \d_1 &\text{if }\ c=0
    \\\d_{1-q} &\text{if }\ c=\infty
\end{cases}
\; \text{weakly on }[0,1].
$$
\textup{(b)} {\bf Random stratified fragmentation and fully random fragmentation}. 
Define $\bar p=\EE(P_1)$ or $\bar p=\EE(P_{1,1})$ according to the case in hand.
Then, almost surely, as $n\to\infty$, 
$$
G_n \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d}   \begin{cases}
    \bar{p}\beta_{\left(1,\frac{1}{c}\right)}(0,1-q)+(1-\bar{p})\beta_{\left(\frac{1}{c},1\right)}(1-q,1) &\text{if }\ 0<c<\infty
    \\\bar{p}\d_0+(1-\bar{p}) \d_1 &\text{if }\ c=0
    \\\d_{1-q} &\text{if }\ c=\infty
\end{cases}
\;\text{weakly on }[0,1].
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Defn def:persistence of arXiv:2410.24170, 'Persistent hubs in CMJ branching processes with independent increments and preferential at'] Suppose that $(\mathcal{T}_{n})_{n \in \mathbb{N}_{0}}$ is a sequence of directed trees. We say $u \in \bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}_{0}} \mathcal{T}_{n}$ is a \emph{persistent hub} if $\outdeg{u, \mathcal{T}_{n}} = \max_{v \in \mathcal{T}_{n}} \outdeg{v, \mathcal{T}_{n}}$ for all but finitely many $n \in \mathbb{N}_0$.  A persistent hub $u$ is unique if it is a persistent hub, and for any other persistent hub $u'$, we have $u = u'$. If $u$ is a persistent hub, or unique persistent hub we say $(\mathcal{T}_{n})_{n \in \mathbb{N}_{0}}$ contains a persistent hub, or unique persistent hub respectively.
title: Defn def:persistence of arXiv:2410.24170

body:
[Thm 6 of arXiv:2608.15379, 'Stochastic Jacobi fields along discontinuous martingales on Riemannian submanifolds'] Let $(E,h)$ be a second countable Riemannian manifold and $D$ an open set in $E$. Let $(M,g)$ be a properly embedded Riemannian submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$. Let $(\cE,\cF)$ be a regular Dirichlet form satisfying \thetag{C} for a vector field $\cH \in \mathfrak{X}(E)$.
Let $u \in \cF^D_{loc}(M)\cap L^{\infty}_{loc}(D)$ be an $\cE$-harmonic map on $D$ satisfying \thetag{A} and \thetag{B}.
Let $\cH u$ be the distributional derivative of $u$ with respect to $\cH$.
We assume that
$\cH u$ is in $\cF^{D}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^d) \cap L^{\infty}_{loc}(D)$ and satisfies conditions \thetag{A} and \thetag{B}. We fix a $TM$-valued Borel measurable quasi-continuous modification of $(u,\cH u)$ and set $\bJ=(u(Z), \cH u(Z))$. Then for each relatively compact open set $D_1$ with $\overline{D_1} \subset D$, the process $\bJ^{\tau_{D_1}}$ is a $\left(\Prob_z, \{\cF^Z_t\}_{t\geq 0} \right)$-$\gamma^{\bcl}$-martingale for q.e. $z \in E$. In particular, $\bJ^{\tau_{D_1}}$ is a $TM$-valued semimartingale. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 6 of arXiv:2608.15379

Let phi be a C^2 local diffeomorphism of a neighborhood of 0 in R^d, with phi(0)=0 and Dphi(0) diagonalizable over R with positive eigenvalues. Split R^d=E_cs direct-sum E_u into eigenspaces with eigenvalues <=1 and >1. There are a neighborhood U of 0 and a C^1 embedded local stable-center disk W_cs tangent to E_cs at 0 such that every point whose nonnegative iterates remain in U lies in W_cs. If E_u is nonzero, that forward-trapped set is Lebesgue-null. This local trapping statement, together with a countable neighborhood cover and inverse iterates of a diffeomorphism, excludes convergence to any point of an unstable critical family when pointwise convergence is already known.

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2609.04153, '\vspace*{-3cm}Smooth autonomous fast dynamo action on the three-torus'] Let $u_N$ be given by \eqref{eq:velocity}, and define
$$
\ell(b)
:=
\int_{\TT^2}f_1'(x)b_1(x,y)\,\dd x\,\dd y,
\qquad
h_g(x,y)
:=
\e^{2\pi i g(x,y)}
\begin{pmatrix}
f_2'(y)\\
0
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Then, as $N \to \infty$, $N^{-2}\mathcal{M}_{N,g}$ converges in the $X \to Y$ operator norm to the rank-one operator
$$
\mathcal M_\infty b:=\e^{2\pi i g}\mathcal L_\infty b=\ell(b)h_g.
$$
The only possible nonzero eigenvalue of $\mathcal M_\infty$ is
$$
\lambda_g
:=
\ell(h_g)
=
\int_{\TT^2}
\e^{2\pi i g(x,y)}
f_1'(x)f_2'(y)\,\dd x\,\dd y.
$$
If $\lambda_g\neq0$, then it is an algebraically simple eigenvalue of
$\mathcal M_\infty$. Moreover, for every pair of nonconstant functions
$f_1,f_2$, there exists $g\in C^\infty(\TT^2;\RR)$ such that
$\lambda_g\neq0$.

[Lemma 17 (Boundary reaction; cf.\ Proposition A.8 of \cite{Brendle2019}, Lemma 4.8 of \cite{Chen2024}) of arXiv:2608.26598, 'Pinching cones for positive isotropic curvature in dimensions seven and eight'] Let $n\ge5$, let $S\in\CB(\mathbb R^n)$, and let $H$ be a symmetric two-tensor. Suppose that
    \begin{equation*}
        \Phi_\lambda(S)+(1-\lambda^2)\bigl(H_{11}+H_{22}\bigr)\ge0

        +2(1-\lambda^2)\bigl((S*H)_{11}+(S*H)_{22}\bigr)
        \ge(1+\lambda^2)\bigl(H_{11}+H_{22}\bigr)^2\ge0.
