body:
Let $X = Z\Sigma^{1/2}$ be $n \times p$ with $Z$ having i.i.d. entries of mean $0$ and variance $1$, $\Sigma$ positive semidefinite, and let $S = \frac{1}{n}X^T X$. Assume $p/n \to c \in (0, \infty)$ and that the empirical spectral distribution of $\Sigma$ converges weakly to a probability measure $H$ on $[0, \infty)$. Then almost surely the empirical spectral distribution of $S$ converges weakly to a nonrandom probability measure $F = F^{c, H}$, characterised as follows: with $\underline F = (1 - c)\delta_0 + cF$ (the limiting spectral distribution of the $n \times n$ companion $\frac{1}{n}XX^T$) and $\underline m(z) = \int \frac{d\underline F(t)}{t - z} = -\frac{1 - c}{z} + c\,m_F(z)$, for every $z \in \mathbb{C}^+$ the value $\underline m(z)$ is the unique solution in $\mathbb{C}^+$ of $$z = -\frac{1}{\underline m} + c\int \frac{\tau\, dH(\tau)}{1 + \tau\,\underline m}.$$ Equivalently, $m_F$ solves $m_F(z) = \int \frac{dH(\tau)}{\tau\,(1 - c - c z\, m_F(z)) - z}$. For $H = \delta_1$ (identity population covariance) the equation reduces to the quadratic $z\,\underline m^2 + (z + 1 - c)\,\underline m + 1 = 0$ for the companion transform (equivalently $c z\, m_F^2 + (z - 1 + c)\, m_F + 1 = 0$ for $m_F$ itself), whose solution is the Stieltjes transform of the Marchenko-Pastur law with ratio $c$; the support of $F$ and its density are read off by Stieltjes inversion, and the density is analytic inside the support and behaves like a square root at its edges.

[Theorem 25 of arXiv:2605.30616, 'Brownian motion: the hyperbolic number setting'] Let, as in Corollary \ref{cor-78}, be given two probability measures on the cylinder sigma-algebra of $\mathcal S^\prime_{\mathbb R}$, and let $Z_1,Z_2,\ldots$ and
  $W_1,W_2,\ldots$ be the corresponding sequences of pairwise orthogonal Gaussian variables. Define (with $p=\lambda_1e_++\lambda_2e_-$)
\begin{equation}
B_{p}(\w)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}U\begin{pmatrix}\left(\int_{0}^{\lambda_{1}}\zeta_{n}(u)du\right)Z_{n}(\w) & 0\\
0 & \left(\int_{0}^{\lambda_{2}}\zeta_{n}(u)du\right)W_{n}(\w)
\end{pmatrix}U.
\end{equation}
Then, $(B_{p})$ 
is $\mathbb{H}$-valued Gaussian and has covariance
function \eqref{wertyuio}.

[Theorem thm:cassidy of arXiv:2510.12520, '\Large Strong Convergence: A Short Survey\thanks{Contribution to the Proceedings of the In'] Let $\sigma_1^N,\ldots,\sigma_r^N$ be i.i.d.\ uniform random 
elements of $\mathbf{S}_N$, and ${\pi_N:\mathbf{S}_N\to 
\mathrm{U}(D_N)}$ be any irreducible unitary representation of 
$\mathbf{S}_N$ of dimension $1<D_N\le \exp(N^{1/21})$. Define
$\boldsymbol{U}^N=(U_1^N,\ldots,U_r^N)$ by $U_k^N=\pi_N(\sigma_k^N)$, and
let $\boldsymbol{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ be free Haar unitaries. Then
$\boldsymbol{U}^N$ converges strongly to $\boldsymbol{u}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem spde WP of arXiv:2605.13479, '\LARGE Dean-Kawasaki Equation with Biot-Savart and Keller-Segel Interactions: Existence an'] Assume that (equation eq:small-KS of the paper) holds. Fix $\varepsilon > 0$ and let $\rho_0 \in \mathrm{Ent}(\mathbb{T}^2)$ be a nonnegative initial datum, where $\mathrm{Ent}(\mathbb{T}^2)$ is defined in (equation eq:def-Ent-space of the paper). We consider the following two cases.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For the mollified equation, namely $\eta > 0$ in (equation SPDE-1 of the paper), there exists a probabilistically weak renormalized kinetic solution $\rho^{\eta}$ to (equation SPDE-1 of the paper) with initial data $\rho_0$. Moreover, $\rho^{\eta}$ coincides with a weak solution of (equation SPDE-1 of the paper).
\item For the limiting equation (equation SPDE-0-intro of the paper), corresponding to $\eta = 0$ in (equation SPDE-1 of the paper), there exists a probabilistically weak renormalized kinetic solution.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:construction-until-explosion of arXiv:2608.05105, 'Cluster-Cluster model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$'] Let \(\alpha<0\), and write \(\beta=-\alpha>0\). The Cluster-Cluster dynamics
admits a maximal local construction as follows. For every finite
\(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d\) there is a stopping time
\(\tau^\Lambda\in[0,\infty]\) such that the restriction of the process to
\(\Lambda\) is well defined on \([0,\tau^\Lambda)\), has càdlàg paths there,
and has only finitely many jumps on every compact subinterval of
\([0,\tau^\Lambda)\). If \((\Lambda_j)_{j\ge1}\) is an increasing exhaustion of
\(\mathbb Z^d\) by finite boxes, the maximal lifetime is
\[
    \tau_{\rm exp}:=\inf_{j\ge1}\tau^{\Lambda_j}.
\]
For every \(T<\tau_{\rm exp}\), the process is defined on every finite set up to
time \(T\). If \(\tau_{\rm exp}<\infty\), then local stabilization of the cutoff
processes fails at \(\tau_{\rm exp}\); equivalently, arbitrarily large cutoff
levels influence the evolution in finite boxes arbitrarily close to
\(\tau_{\rm exp}\).

[Proposition prop:d of arXiv:2604.17253, 'Large Deviations for the Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation with Randomized Quasi-Periodic Ini'] Let $\dim_{\mathbb Z^\nu}\mathrm D^{(k,\gamma^{(k)})}$ denote the number of $\mathbb Z^\nu$-components of $\mathrm D^{(k,\gamma^{(k)})}$. Then
\[
\dim_{\mathbb Z^{\nu}} \mathrm D^{(k,\gamma^{(k)})} = 2\sigma(\gamma^{(k)}).
\]
That is, 
\begin{align*}
\mathrm D^{(k,\gamma^{(k)})} \cong (\mathbb Z^{\nu})^{2\sigma(\gamma^{(k)})}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem boundsrho of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Assume $\mathrm{a}=0$ and $\neg \hatHone$. 

	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Let $\eta$ be the L\'evy measure associated to $\Sigma$. Then, $$\overline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma,\hat\Phi}=\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\limsup}\,x\int_0^{\infty}\bar{\eta}(u)\Big(\frac{1}{\hat\Phi(x)}-\frac{1}{\hat{\Phi}(x+u)}\Big)\mathrm{d} u,$$
        and similarly for $\underline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma,\hat\Phi}$ with $\liminf$.
        \item
		If $\Sigma\sim \Sigma_1$ at $\infty$, then $$\overline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma, \hat{\Phi}}=\overline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle \Sigma_1,\hat\Phi}\text{ and } \underline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle \Sigma, \hat{\Phi}}=\underline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma_1, \hat{\Phi}}.$$ 
		
		\item  There is no loss of generality in assuming that the measure $\hat{U}$ admits a density $\hat u$, moreover
\[\underline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma,\hat\Phi}=\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\liminf}\,\mathbb{E}[B(\mathbbm{e}_x)], \quad \overline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma,\hat\Phi}=\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\limsup}\,\mathbb{E}[B(\mathbbm{e}_x)],\]
where 
\begin{center}
$B:(0,\infty)\ni z \mapsto \frac{\Sigma(z)\hat{u}(z)}{z}$ and $\mathbbm{e}_x$ is an exponential r.v. with parameter $x$.\end{center}
One has also the bounds
		\[\liminf_{z\rightarrow \infty}\frac{\Sigma(z)\hat{u}(z)}{z}\leq \underline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}\leq \overline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Phi, \hat{\Sigma}}\leq \underset{z\rightarrow \infty}\limsup\frac{\Sigma(z)\hat{u}(z)}{z}.\]    
		In particular, if $\varrho:=\underset{x\rightarrow \infty}{\lim}\frac{\Sigma(z)\hat{u}(z)}{z}\text{ exists in } [0,\infty]$, then $\underline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma, \hat{\Phi}}=\overline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle \Sigma, \hat{\Phi}}=\varrho.$
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem boundsrho of arXiv:2605.06488

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2609.03243, 'Weighted Ces\`aro type operators on the weighted Bergman spaces in the unit ball'] Let \(\alpha>-1\), \(\beta>0\), \(0<p<1\), \(p<q\le\infty\), and
\(M>(n+1+\alpha)/p\). Suppose that \(\mu\) is
\(\lambda\)-Carleson, where
\[
    \lambda=\beta+(n+1+\alpha)\left(\frac{1}p-\frac{1}q\right),
    \qquad \frac{1}{\infty}=0.
\]
Then
\[
    \sup_{w\in\mathbb B_n}
    \|\mathcal C_{\mu,\beta}^{\xi}a_{w,M}^{(p)}\|_{q,\alpha}
    \lesssim
    \sup_{0\leq r<1}\frac{\widehat\mu(r)}{(1-r)^\lambda}.
\]

body: In information theory, the noisy-channel coding theorem, establishes that for any given degree of noise contamination of a communication channel, it is possible to communicate discrete data nearly error-free up to a computable maximum rate through the channel. This result was presented by Claude Shannon in 1948 and was based in part on earlier work and ideas of Harry Nyquist and Ralph Hartley.
title: Noisy-channel coding theorem

body: In mathematics, the Mordell–Weil theorem states that for an abelian variety over a number field , the group of K-rational points of is a finitely-generated abelian group, called the Mordell–Weil group. The case with an elliptic curve and the field of rational numbers is Mordell's theorem, answering a question apparently posed by Henri Poincaré around 1901; it was proven by Louis Mordell in 1922. It is a foundational theorem of Diophantine geometry and the arithmetic of abelian varieties.
title: Mordell–Weil theorem

body:
[Prop evanescent of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] Let $X$ be a CTMC on $\mathbb S\subseteq \mathbb Z^d$, and let $x\in\mathbb S$. Then $x$ is evanescent for $X$ iff when started from state $x$ with positive probability the process never enters a recurrent state.
\begin{proof}[Proof Sketch]
    First, assume that $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty}\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{X(t)}_{\ell^1}\to\infty$ occurs with positive probability. Given this event, the process almost surely does not enter a recurrent state because if a recurrent state is visited once then it is a.s.~visited infinitely many times [Norris_1997].
    
    For the reverse implication, suppose that $\liminf\limits_{t\to\infty}\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{X(t)}_{\ell^1}$ is finite with probability one. Note that for all $R\in\mathbb R$, the event that the process ever enters a recurrent state contains, up to a set of measure zero, the event that $\liminf\limits_{t\to\infty}\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{X(t)}_{\ell^1}\le R$. Indeed, otherwise we could use the fact that $\{y\in\mathbb Z^d:\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*} y_{\ell^1}\le R\}$ is finite to conclude that there existed a specific transient state $y$ which was visited infinitely often with positive probability, contradicting transience of $y$. Sending $R\to\infty$, the result follows from continuity of probability. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop evanescent of arXiv:2507.09421

[Theorem 17 (Bernstein inequalities, Lemma 2.1, \cite{MR2768550}) of arXiv:2609.02197, '2609.02197'] Let $\left(n,\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3\right) \in \mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{R}_+^*\times\mathbb{R}_+^*\times\mathbb{R}_+^*$ such that $\gamma_2<\gamma_3.$
\begin{enumerate}
\item There exists $\mu \in \mathbb{R}_+^*$ such that for any $\left(r,\beta\right) \in \left[1,+\infty\right[^2$ and all $\varphi \in \mathscr{S},$ if \\ $\left\{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d,\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi\left(y\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2\pi \mathrm{i}\left\langle x,y\right\rangle}\,\mathrm{d}y\neq 0\right\}\subset \left\{x \in \mathbb{R}^d,\left|x\right|\leq \beta\gamma_1\right\},$ then $$\max_{\substack{q\in\mathbb{N}^d \\ \left|q\right|=n}}\left\Vert \partial^q \varphi\right\Vert_{L^\infty\left(\mathbb{T}^d\right)}\leq \mu\beta^{n+\frac{d}{r}}\left\Vert \varphi\right\Vert_{L^r\left(\mathbb{T}^d\right)}.$$
\item There exists $\left(\mu_1,\mu_2\right) \in \left(\mathbb{R}_+^*\right)^2$ such that for any $\beta \in \left[1,+\infty\right[$ and all $\varphi \in \mathscr{S},$ if \\ $\left\{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d,\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\varphi\left(y\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2\pi \mathrm{i}\left\langle x,y\right\rangle}\,\mathrm{d}y\neq 0\right\}\subset\left\{x \in \mathbb{R}^d,\beta\gamma_2\leq \left|x\right|\leq\beta\gamma_3\right\},$ then $$\mu_1\beta^{n}\left\Vert \varphi\right\Vert_{L^\infty\left(\mathbb{T}^d\right)}\leq \max_{\substack{q\in\mathbb{N}^d\\\left|q\right|=n}}\left\Vert \partial^{q}\varphi\right\Vert_{L^\infty\left(\mathbb{T}^d\right)}\leq \mu_2\beta^{n}\left\Vert \varphi\right\Vert_{L^{\infty}\left(\mathbb{T}^d\right)}.$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bernstein inequalities, Lemma 2.1, \cite{MR2768550}

For a complex n by n matrix A and epsilon >= 0, the closed epsilon-pseudospectrum is Lambda_epsilon(A) = {z in C : sigma_min(zI - A) <= epsilon}, sigma_min the smallest singular value and ||.|| the spectral norm. Hence Lambda_epsilon(A + E) is contained in Lambda_{epsilon + delta}(A) and Lambda_epsilon(A) in Lambda_{epsilon + delta}(A + E), for every epsilon >= 0.

[Corollary 73 (Evaluated matching reconstruction below the Hilbert endpoint) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $1\le r<2$, let $I\subset\Lambda\times\cM$, and let
$\mathscr D=(I_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ be a matching partition as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:matching-gap-reconstruction}.  Retain the finite-rank
block projections and put
$d_i:=\min\{\rank P_\lambda,\rank Q_\mu\}$ for
$i=(\lambda,\mu)$.  If
\[
 K_i\in\mathfrak W_{m,2}
 (\cH_{\R};Q_\mu\cC,P_\lambda\cE),
 \qquad
 b_i:=d_i^{1/r-1/2}\Prof_{m,2}(K_i),
\]
and $b\in\mathsf M_r(\mathscr D)$, then the evaluated block series
converges in $L^p(\Omega;\Sch_r)$ for every $1\le p<\infty$.  With
$p_*:=\max\{p,r\}$,
\begin{equation}

 \norm{\sum_{i\in I}I_m(K_i)}_{L^p(\Omega;\Sch_r)}
 \le
 A_m(p_*+2)^{m/2}\norm b_{\mathsf M_r(\mathscr D)}.
\end{equation}
For finite-overlap supports, the right-hand side is multiplied by
$(\chi_+\chi_-)^{1-1/r}$.  In particular, the assertion applies with
$\mathsf M_r(\mathscr D)=\mathsf{Gap}_r$.
title: Evaluated matching reconstruction below the Hilbert endpoint

Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. Let A_q be a random set, independent of X, containing each coordinate independently with probability q in [0, 1], and M(q) = E over A_q of E Var(f | X_{A_q^c}). Then M(q) = sum over nonempty S of [1 - (1 - q)^|S|] w_S = Var(f) - J(1 - q), with J the Bernoulli reveal profile, and M(q) = (1/2) E[(f(X) - f(X^(A_q)))^2], where X^(A) redraws X_A independently from its own law. For every r >= 1, (-1)^(r+1) M^(r)(q) = sum_{k=r}^n (k)_r (1 - q)^(k - r) W_k >= 0 with (k)_r = k(k - 1)...(k - r + 1); so M is increasing and concave, M'(0) = sum_k k W_k = sum_i E Var(f | X_{-i}), and the derivatives at any q determine the spectrum. For a pure order-d function, J(p) = p^d Var(f) and M(q) = [1 - (1 - q)^d] Var(f).

[Lem pcp-cumulant-functional of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] Let
\[
N=\sum_j\vartheta_{U_j}C_j
\]
be a stationary Poisson cluster process with immigrant rate $\nu$, where the $C_j$ are i.i.d. copies of a finite simple cluster $C$ and $\mathbb{E} C(\mathbb{R})<\infty$; if multiplicities are allowed, products and sums below are over atoms counted with multiplicity. Whenever the following logarithms are finite, for instance for bounded compactly supported $q$ with $-1<q\le0$ and bounded compactly supported $f\le0$ under the preceding finite-mean assumption, the Poisson product formula gives
\[
K_{\mathrm{fac}}^N(q)
=
\nu\int_\mathbb{R}
\left\{
\mathbb{E}\prod_{y\in C}(1+q(u+y))-1
\right\}\,du
\]
and
\[
K_{\mathrm{comp}}^N(f)
=
\nu\int_\mathbb{R}
\left\{
\mathbb{E}\exp\big(C(f(u+\cdot))\big)-1
\right\}\,du .
\]
The derivative identities used below require only finite moments: for every $n\ge1$ with $\mathbb{E}[C(\mathbb{R})^n]<\infty$ and bounded compactly supported $f_0,\ldots,f_{n-1}$,
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\prod_{j=0}^{n-1} f_j(t_j)\,
\kappa_n(dt_0,\ldots,dt_{n-1})
=
\nu\int_\mathbb{R}
\mathbb{E}\sum_{x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}\in C}^{\neq}
\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}f_j(u+x_j)\,du,
\]
whereas
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\prod_{j=0}^{n-1} f_j(t_j)\,
\gamma_n(dt_0,\ldots,dt_{n-1})
=
\nu\int_\mathbb{R}
\mathbb{E}\sum_{x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}\in C}
\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}f_j(u+x_j)\,du.
\]
Equivalently, for $n\ge2$,
\[
\kappa_n^{\mathrm{red}}(d\tau_1,\ldots,d\tau_{n-1})
=
\nu\,\mathbb{E}\sum_{x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}\in C}^{\neq}
\prod_{r=1}^{n-1}\delta_{x_r-x_0}(d\tau_r),
\]
and
\[
\gamma_n^{\mathrm{red}}(d\tau_1,\ldots,d\tau_{n-1})
=
\nu\,\mathbb{E}\sum_{x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}\in C}
\prod_{r=1}^{n-1}\delta_{x_r-x_0}(d\tau_r).
\]
In particular, if $\mathbb{E}[C(\mathbb{R})^3]<\infty$ and
\[
W(\omega):=\widehat C(\omega)=\sum_{x\in C}e^{-\mathrm{i}\omega x},
\]
then
\[
\widehat{\gamma_3^{\mathrm{red}}}(\omega_1,\omega_2)
=
\nu\,\mathbb{E}\{W(\omega_1)W(\omega_2)W(-\omega_1-\omega_2)\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cumulant functionals for Poisson cluster processes

body: [Thm main-random-walk of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] There exists a sequence $(b_n)_{n\in\mathbf N}$ such that the following is true. Let $m \in \mathbf N$ and sample $\rho_n \in \mathcal{X}^{(m)}_n$ and $\rho \in \mathcal{X}^{(m)}$ such that $(\mathcal{X}^{(m)}_n,d^{{\mathrm {path}}}_n,\pi_n,\rho_n) \to (\mathcal{X}^{(m)},d^{{\mathrm {path}}},\pi,\rho)$ in law in the rooted GHf topology. Then there exists a coupling such that the following holds almost surely. Let $X^{(n)}$ be the continuous-time simple random walk on $\mathcal{X}^{(m)}_n$ that jumps to each open neighboring site at rate $b_n$, started from $\rho_n$. Then there exists a diffusion process $X$ on $\mathcal{X}^{(m)}$ with $X_0=\rho$ such that $\pi_n(X^{(n)})$ converges in law to $\pi(X)$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$ in the space of c\`adl\`ag processes on $[0,1]^2$ equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work proof draft (unaudited); no novelty priority claimed. Fix one oracle O. Assume that for every NP^O predicate and every strict uniform polynomial-time O-samplable ensemble there is one deterministic O-relative heuristic scheme, polynomial in input length and inverse error, whose error is bounded by the requested tolerance at every length. Then every uniform nonnegative rational efficient-weight law with polynomial numerator/denominator bit bounds and positive normalizer has uniform strict polynomial-time approximate samplers at every inverse-polynomial TV accuracy. Every uniform polynomial-time O-map also has all-length distributional inverters at every inverse-polynomial joint-TV accuracy. A conditional-set affine-hashing sampler proves both: random bucket counting, unique-witness extraction, and an explicit virtual-row union bound avoid assuming a sampler or CDF for the target weighted law. Under the existing C003 AR conversion this gives nonuniform polynomial-size forward-KL approximations in the SAME oracle. The 1995 Impagliazzo survey defines DistNP using samplable ensembles and reports an IR2 heuristic oracle with NP circuit hardness, but its unpublished construction and full O-relative sampler coverage have not been verified here. This card proves the bridge under the precise hypothesis; it does not claim an independently established Target 2 oracle.
One fixed final oracle O; full O-relative NP and strict uniform polynomial-time samplable ensembles
For every such distributional NP problem, one fixed deterministic scheme with runtime polynomial in input length and inverse error and error <=eta for every length and every eta in (0,1)
For A: uniform nonnegative rational weight evaluator with polynomial numerator/denominator bounds and positive normalizer; for B: a uniform polynomial-time map on fixed polynomial-length uniform seeds

T410-w739-C013 v3. Kind: moved. Target: 2.
Status: proof (unaudited). Own-work derivation; no novelty
priority claimed for the hashing method or the resulting bridge.

## Exact hypothesis and conclusions

Fix one oracle O. Use the following fully quantified hypothesis H:
for every language K in NP^O and every uniform, strict polynomial-time
O-samplable ensemble D_N, there is one deterministic O-relative scheme
H_K,D(z;eta) with runtime polynomial in |z| and 1/eta and

    Pr_{z~D_N}[H_K,D(z;eta) != K(z)] <= eta

for EVERY N>=1 and 0<eta<1. The algorithm is fixed for the pair (K,D),
not chosen separately at each length or accuracy. Invalid answers count
as errors. An ensemble may concentrate at exactly N-bit strings, a special
case of distributions on strings of length at most N.

Under H the following statements hold for the SAME final oracle O:
A. Every uniform nonnegative polynomial-bit rational polynomial-time
   O-relative weight family w_L, with Z_L>0, has a uniform strict
   polynomial-time O-relative sampler within any requested TV error rho.
   Runtime is polynomial in L and 1/rho. No normalizer or target CDF is used.
B. Every uniform deterministic polynomial-time O-relative map F_L on
   uniform polynomial-length binary inputs has a uniform distributional
   inverter at every inverse-polynomial TV accuracy, at all lengths.

Thus H discharges BOTH premises of C003 v2, rather than introducing an
additional weighted-law sampling hypothesis. C003 then supplies nonuniform
polynomial-size AR approximations with forward KL <=L^(-c) for every fixed c.
If there is an O satisfying H and NP^O not in P^O/poly, this proves Target 2.

This proof does NOT construct that oracle. Impagliazzo's 1995 primary
survey reports such a heuristic oracle on page 12, but its [IR2] construction
is listed as in preparation. The published definition of DistNP on page 11
uses SAMPLABLE distributions, not the PComp convention of another survey.
Whether the oracle assertion covers fully O-relative samplers and all the
scheme quantifiers above must not be silently strengthened. Those are the
remaining source-level conditions in applying this bridge to the report.

## 1. A conditional uniform-set sampling lemma

Let Y_{L,q} have a uniform strict polynomial-time O-relative sampler, and
let S_{L,q,y} be a uniformly polynomial-time O-recognizable subset of
{0,1}^{m(L,q)}, nonempty for every y in the support of Y_{L,q}.
Lengths m and the challenge size have known polynomial bounds in L+q.
Use a polynomial-time computable witness length, padding with required
zero bits if needed, so padding preserves each set cardinality.
There is, under H, one strict polynomial-time O-relative procedure I
whose joint output (Y,I(Y)) is within TV rho of
(Y,U_{S_{L,q,Y}}). Its runtime is polynomial in L+q and 1/rho.
For this lemma take dyadic accuracy 0<rho<=1. Any requested tolerance
is met by a dyadic rho below it. The input convention is thus canonical
and its bit length is bounded by a polynomial in 1/rho.

### A single query language and a single samplable ensemble

Choose monotone integer polynomial bounds M(n)>=m(L,q) and V(n) for
challenge length, for all L,q<=n. Increase M(n) to at least one.
Let ell=ceil(log2(n+1)) and ellM=ceil(log2(M(n)+2)). A query contains:

* the header 1^n 0;
* fixed-width fields L,q,j (ell bits each) and type (ellM bits);
* a padded, self-delimited challenge y in a fixed polynomial V(n) space;
* an n by M(n) binary matrix and n-bit affine offset.

All queries at parameter n have one fixed polynomial length N(n), made
strictly increasing by padding if needed. Invalid fields, malformed padding,
or an incorrect total length denote a constant-false instance. For valid
L,q,j with L,q>=1 and j<=n, use the first j rows and first m(L,q) columns
to define the affine hash h on m(L,q) bits. Type 0 asks whether the zero
bucket S intersect h^{-1}(0) is nonempty. Type 1 asks whether it contains
two distinct witnesses. Type a+1, 1<=a<=m, asks whether it contains a
witness with bit a equal to one. These are all NP^O predicates: at most
two polynomial-length witnesses suffice, with distinctness checked explicitly.

Define D_{N(n)} by sampling all four fields uniformly from their entire
bit ranges, sampling y from Y_{L,q} on valid L,q (dummy otherwise), and
sampling the full matrix and offset uniformly. This is a strict uniform
O-relative polynomial-time sampler, including unused rows and columns.
At lengths outside the image of N(n), use a point mass. Monotone N(n)
lets a sampler find n by a polynomial-time search. Padding and a challenge
length field make parsing and the NP verifier uniform. There is ONE D and
ONE K for the entire set family, independent of the requested accuracy.

Conditioning on any valid tuple (L,q,j,type) costs exactly

    C(n)=2^(3ell+ellM) <=16(n+1)^3(M(n)+2),

which is polynomial. Conditional on those fields, y has exactly the
specified Y_{L,q} law and the active hash is a uniform affine hash.
Therefore a scheme with error eta under D_{N(n)} has average error at
most C(n)eta under any such fixed tuple, averaging over y and the hash.
For the unconditional-set special case, y is a fixed empty challenge;
then D is a uniform subcube and has an exact polynomial-time CDF as well.

### Pairwise independent affine hashes

For uniform binary A,b, h(v)=Av+b maps any fixed v uniformly to j bits;
for distinct v,w, (h(v),h(w)) is a uniform independent pair. To check this,
each row's nonzero dot product A_row(v-w) is uniform, and its independent
offset makes the first output bit uniform independently of the difference.
Rows are independent. This remains true for j=0 and j>m.

Fix a nonempty S of size s and put lambda=s 2^(-j). If T is its zero
bucket size, E T=lambda and E T^2<=lambda+lambda^2. Cauchy-Schwarz applied
to T*1{T>0}, with lambda>0 because S is nonempty, gives

    lambda/(1+lambda) <= Pr[T>0] <= lambda.                (1)

The upper bound is Markov. No independence of three or more witnesses
is used. For each v in S, pairwise independence and a union bound give

    2^(-j)(1-lambda) <= Pr[zero bucket={v}] <= 2^(-j).     (2)

When 0<lambda<1 this implies strictly positive singleton success
probability alpha between lambda(1-lambda) and lambda. Only this range
is used for normalization below. The conditional singleton-output law mu
satisfies mu(v)>= (1-lambda)/s because alpha<=s 2^(-j). Thus
TV(mu,U_S)=1-sum_v min(mu(v),1/s)<=lambda.

### Calibration and singleton extraction with exact NP answers

For each j=0,...,m+3, take

    J=ceil(128(m+4)/rho)

independent hashes and estimate Pr[T>0] by its empirical frequency. A
Bernoulli mean has variance <=1/(4J). Chebyshev and a union bound imply
all estimates are within 1/8 of their means except with probability rho/8.
Choose the smallest j0 with estimated probability <=1/2. Such a j exists:
at j=m+3, lambda<=1/8 and the good estimate is <=1/4. At j=0 the exact
estimate equals 1, so j0>=1. On the good event, at j0 the true probability
is <=5/8, so (1) implies lambda0<=5/3<2. At j0-1 it is >3/8, so Markov
and halving lambda give lambda0>3/16>1/8. In particular

    1/8 <= lambda0 <=2.

Let delta=rho/8 and t=ceil(log2(4/delta)); equivalently t is the least
integer with 2^t>=4/delta. Then delta/8<2^(-t)<=delta/4. At j=j0+t,

    delta/64 < lambda <=delta/2,
    alpha>=lambda(1-lambda)>=delta/128.

Run T0=ceil(1024/(delta rho)) independent fresh final buckets. In each,
ask all the NP queries above before reading their answers. Reject empty
or non-singleton buckets. On a singleton, the m bit answers recover its
unique witness, which is checked for membership and bucket membership.
Return the first successful witness, or a fixed fallback after T0 trials.

The exhaustion probability is <=rho/8: for alpha>0,
(1-alpha)^T0 <=1/(1+alpha T0)<=rho/8, using Bernoulli's inequality
on (1-alpha)^(-T0), with the alpha=1 case immediate. Given any successful
calibration result, the first singleton has the same law as one bucket
conditioned on being singleton; truncation changes it by at most the
exhaustion probability. By (2), its TV distance from uniform S is at most
delta/2=rho/16. Calibration failure, truncation, and singleton bias give
total error at most 5rho/16 for the ideal exact-NP procedure. These bounds
hold for every supported y, hence also for their joint mixture.

### Replacing all queries by one heuristic scheme

Choose n polynomially large enough that L,q<=n and every possible final
row count j0+t is <=n. Choose it from the known m bound, not from the
unknown set cardinality. Use the scheme for the single (K,D) above.

The final row count depends on y and calibration hashes. We must NOT
apply a fixed-row average error bound after conditioning on that choice.
Instead, sample virtual final batches for EVERY row count j=0,...,n.
Only the selected batch is used. For each fixed row count and type, each
virtual query has the unconditioned distribution (Y,uniform affine hash)
covered by the C(n) bound. It is harmless that queries with different
types share a hash. Include all virtual queries in the union bound:

    Qstar=(m+4)J+(n+1)T0(m+2),
    eta=rho/(8 C(n) Qstar).

There are at most Qstar queries. The probability of ANY wrong heuristic
answer in this joint experiment is at most Qstar C(n)eta=rho/8. The
algorithm need only evaluate the chosen final batch, and can generate its
hashes after calibration; this has the same distribution as selecting
one of the independent virtual batches. With the same random tapes the
actual and ideal algorithms agree unless some counted query is wrong.
Coupling adds at most rho/8 in TV, without conditioning their output
law on the correctness event. The joint error is at most 7rho/16<rho.

All loops and bit lengths are polynomial in L+q and 1/rho. Arithmetic for
the ceilings and dyadic field widths is exact; t can be found by repeated
doubling. The scheme's inverse-eta dependence remains polynomial because
C, Qstar and N(n) are polynomial. This proves the conditional-set lemma.

## 2. Efficient rational weights: prove A without normalization

For the desired dyadic accuracy rho<=1 choose integer q>=1 with
2^-q<=rho/8. Let k=L+b(L)+q and W(x)=floor(2^k w_L(x)). Define

    S_{L,q}={(x,u): |x|=L, |u|=k+b(L)+1, 0<=u<W(x)}.

Its witness length m=2L+2b(L)+q+1 is polynomial in L+q and its predicate
is in P^O. Since a positive rational weight is at least 2^(-b), some
W(x)>=1, so S is nonempty. Its uniform law projected onto x is proportional
to W(x). With w'=2^(-k)W, the missing mass E=sum_x(w(x)-w'(x)) is at most
2^(L-k). Since Z>=2^(-b), E/Z<=2^(L+b-k)=2^-q<=rho/8.
For nonnegative w'<=w, normalization changes TV by at most E/Z; this
follows directly by retaining the common subprobability w'/Z.

Apply the conditional-set construction with empty challenge and requested
error rho. Its actual proof bound is 7rho/16, not merely rho. Projection
cannot increase TV; adding rounding gives error <=9rho/16<rho for P.
The algorithm uses the weight evaluator, not an exact normalizer, an
advice value, or an NP-complete solver on all possible instances. Its
heuristic scheme is specific to this ONE uniform weight family. Hence
the universal-compiler collapse in C005 does not apply.

## 3. Uniform maps: prove the distributional inversion premise B

For a uniform map F_L:{0,1}^{r(L)}->{0,1}^{s(L)}, let
Y_L=F_L(U_{r(L)}) and S_{L,y}={u:F_L(u)=y}. This challenge is uniformly
O-samplable, and every supported y has a nonempty P^O-recognizable set.
Apply the conditional-set lemma, with q a dummy precision parameter.
Given y, the resulting I_L(y) is within joint TV rho of a uniform preimage.
The ideal joint law is exactly (F_L(U),U), since conditional on its image
a uniform seed is uniform over its preimage. Thus

    TV( (F_L(U), I_L(F_L(U))), (F_L(U),U) ) <=7rho/16.

Here the first pair uses fresh coins for I conditional on its challenge;
no independence between image and original seed is asserted. This is
C003 B, with polynomial runtime in L and inverse accuracy, for every
fixed uniform map family and every length. Unlike the empty-challenge
case, this use of H requires samplers allowed to query O.

## 4. Scope, checks, and remaining target-level issue

Finite diagnostics must check actual affine hash distributions for all
small subsets, including singleton and full sets, zero rows and rows beyond
the witness length, and exact rational weight-rounding instances. They
must also exhibit failure of the unadjusted conditioning argument when
an average-accurate answer's query index is chosen from its challenge.
A Lean check certifies only the displayed real calibration implication,
not this full probabilistic theorem, source interpretation, or an oracle.

The hardest remaining external step is the precise final-oracle existence
statement: the 1995 survey reports DistNP subset HP with NP not in P/poly,
but the proof of [IR2] has not been obtained. We record the definition
and assertion with their exact locators. No independent review or new
oracle construction is claimed. This bridge can be checked separately
from that literature premise and from C003's AR conversion.

## Validation record and v3 side conditions

72,877 exact finite checks passed: 1,110 affine-hash subset cases,
4,276 pointwise singleton bounds, 1,110 second-moment checks, 65,805
rational weight-rounding instances, and 576 calibration constant cases.
For the average-query selection negative control, Y is uniform on 16
indices and a query j is wrong exactly when j=Y. Each fixed j has error
1/16, but choosing j(Y)=Y has error 1. This is why the proof pays for
all virtual row counts rather than conditioning a fixed-index estimate.
The Lean calibration attempt returned RUNTIME_UNVERIFIED after 130.2s;
it supplied NO Lean certificate. The rung is a written proof (unaudited),
with exact finite diagnostics, not a Lean-checked theorem or oracle.

Version 3 states the strict load range 0<lambda<1 where division by
singleton success probability is used; the final load already satisfies
this range. It also fixes the accuracy-input convention to dyadics. The
algorithm and constants are unchanged. Five additional exact boundary
checks cover a zero-bit witness set, with zero through four hash rows.
The adaptive-selection negative control was explicitly recomputed over
all 16 fixed indices and all 16 challenges, not inferred from its label.

For the H invocation, eta>0 and eta<1 because C and Qstar are positive
and eta=rho/(8 C Qstar). If a scheme accepts only dyadic tolerances,
round eta downward to the next dyadic; its inverse grows by less than
a factor of two. This leaves every error bound and polynomial runtime
unchanged. Nonemptiness of S also ensures the rounded-weight normalizer
is nonzero. No limit exchange or infinite probability-space argument
is used: every random tape and every virtual query table here is finite.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:bc29281e466374e5470dde0b6c49a018719480c9c6b7449f931fa08628ec0b65","revision_digest":"sha256:efca2756691cfef91b468ca218ece09d5496ca7c006dcdabe80658783d662fb9","source_id":"own-work:T410-w739-C013-v3","source_revision":"2026-10-20T23:24:48.316680+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

\begin{itemize}

\item[(ii)] Setting

body:
[Theorem 6 (The spectral/dimension dichotomy) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Assume uniform ellipticity ($p_{d,d'}\ge p^{\mathrm{tr}}_{\min}>0$) and bounded weights. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Quenched limit.) For $\nu_h$-a.e.\ ray, $n^{-1}\big(n\log m_*+S_n(\xi)\big)\to\ell$, and consequently the harmonic-measure-dimension expression equals the quenched rate:
\[
p_{\min}^{-\dimH(\partial T,\nu_h;\,p^{\ex})}=e^{\ell},\qquad \dimH(\partial T,\nu_h;\,p^{\ex}):=\frac{\ell}{\log(1/p_{\min})}.
\]
\item (Annealed criticality.) The cascade is critical iff $\bar m=1$, where $\bar m$ is the Perron root $\rho(M)$ of \eqref{eq:M} (with $w\equiv1$).
\item (The gap.) $\bar m\ge e^{\ell}$, i.e.\ $\rho(M)\ge p_{\min}^{-\dimH}$, with equality if and only if $p_ew_e$ is $\nu_h$-almost surely constant. Hence the identity $\rho=p_{\min}^{-\dimH}$ holds exactly on boundary-homogeneous trees (in particular the Bethe lattice) and strictly undercounts criticality otherwise.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition defcroiss of arXiv:2609.03492, 'A conjecture implying $\theta(p_c)=0$ for Bernoulli bond percolation on $\Z^d$'] Let $\tau$ be a stopping time, and let $X$ be a real-valued random
variable measurable with respect to $\sigma(\pi)$.
We say that $X$ is \emph{increasing up to $\tau$} if, for every
configuration $\omega\in\{0,1\}^E$ and every edge
$e\in \mathcal{H}_\tau(\omega)$,
\[
X(\omega^{(e\to0)})
\le
X(\omega^{(e\to1)}).
\]

If $A$ is an event measurable with respect to $\sigma(\pi)$, we say
that $A$ is \emph{increasing up to $\tau$} if its indicator function
$\mathbf{1}_A$ is increasing up to $\tau$.

DRAFT candidate bridge, not a certified theorem. Let G,H be countable connected locally finite simple undirected graphs on the same vertex set. Fix for every H-edge h a simple G-path P_h joining its endpoints, with length <=L, and suppose each G-edge lies in <=M routes, for integers L,M>=1. For p in [0,1], set t=1-(1-p)^(1/M), q=t^L. Assign distinct independent Bernoulli(t) slots to routes at every base edge; OR M slots to realize iid G-percolation at p, and independently thin shorter route indicators to obtain iid H-percolation at q. This couples every H-open route inside a G-open path, hence p_c^bond(G)<=1-(1-(p_c^bond(H))^(1/L))^M. The written countable-product proof in bridge_derivation.md awaits w563. This transfers existence only; different H-clusters may merge in G.

In the case $1\le \alpha\le 2$, we have for $r\ge 2$
\begin{align}
		\Big\Vert \sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\xi_{i}\tilde{\xi}_{j}\Big\Vert_{L_{r}}\asymp_{\alpha}&r^{1/2}\Vert A\Vert_{F}+r\Vert A\Vert_{l_{2}\to l_{2}}+r^{1/\alpha}\Vert A\Vert_{l_{\alpha^{*}}(l_{2})}\nonumber\\
		&+r^{(\alpha+2)/2\alpha}\Vert A\Vert_{l_{2}\to l_{\alpha^{*}}}+r^{2/\alpha}\Vert A\Vert_{l_{\alpha}\to l_{\alpha^{*}}},\nonumber
	\end{align}
    where $\Vert A\Vert_{F}$ is the Frobenius norm, $\Vert A\Vert_{l_{p}(l_{2})} = \big(\sum_{i}(\sum_{j}a_{ij}^{2})^{p/2}\big)^{1/p}$, $\Vert A\Vert_{l_{p}\to l_{q}} = \sup\{\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}x_{j}y_{i} : \Vert x\Vert_{p}\le 1, \Vert y\Vert_{q^{*}}\le 1\}$ is the operator norm from $l_{p}$ to $l_{q}$ ($q^{*}$ the conjugate of $q$), and $\asymp_{\alpha}$ means that each side is at most a constant depending only on $\alpha$ times the other. [Theorem 54 of arXiv:2512.05466, 'Stochastic Flows and Marked Stable Processes'] Let $\alpha =\frac{\delta}{2}\in (0,1)$. 
Fix any $z<0$ and consider the spindle partition of the region to the left of the flow line $(\cR_{z,z+y} (0), y\ge 0)$.  
For $y\ge 0$, set 
\begin{equation}
   \beta^y:= \{ (\cR_{r,z+y}(a-), \cB_{r,z+y}(a)) \colon  
 \cT_{(a,r)}\text{ a spindle, } \, \cB_{r,z+y}(a)\le \cR_{z,z+y} (0))\} .
\end{equation}
Then the process $\big(\beta^y,\, y\in [0,|z|)\big)$ is an $\mathrm{SSIP}^{(\alpha)}(\alpha)$-evolution starting from zero; and $(\beta^y,\, y\ge |z|)$ is an $\mathrm{SSIP}^{(\alpha)}(0)$-evolution. 
The total mass process $\big(\|\beta^y\|,\, y\ge 0)\big)$ is equal to $(\cR_{z,z+y} (0), y\ge 0)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Th th_2d_structure of arXiv:2606.23648, '\textsc{Optimal Stopping for a Diffusion with Unobserved Bernoulli Drift}'] In the setting of Theorem~(th_fixed_x_solution of the paper), the two-dimensional continuation region $\mathcal{C}$ has the sectional representation
    (equation C_sectional_representation of the paper), where each nonempty section \(\mathcal C_x\) is a bounded interval \((a(x),b(x))\). On this region the value function is given by
    \[
        U(x,y)=Q(x)G(y)+R(x)-cyG(y),
        \qquad a(x)<y<b(x),
    \]
    in the notation of (equation def_q_R_coefficients of the paper), (equation def_G of the paper),
    while \(U(x,y)=k(x+y)\) outside \(\mathcal C\).

    \noindent \textbf{(i)} \quad 
    The continuation region expands diagonally: if \((x,y)\in\mathcal C\) and
    \(h\ge0\), then
    \(
        (x+h,y-h)\in\mathcal C.
    \)
    Consequently, \(\mathcal I\) of (equation def_I_active of the paper) is a right-interval, \(d(x)=x+a(x)\) is non-increasing on \(\mathcal I\), and diagonal contact is sticky: if
    \(a(\bar x)=-\bar x\) for some \(\bar x\in\mathcal I\), then
    \(
        a(x)=-x,\, x\in\mathcal I,\, x\ge\bar x.
    \)
    
    \noindent If, in addition, (ass_3 of the paper) holds, then the continuation region expands vertically:
    \[
        (x,y)\in\mathcal C,\ h\ge0
        \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
        (x+h,y)\in\mathcal C.
    \]
    In particular,
    \[
        a(x+h)\le a(x),
        \qquad
        b(x+h)\ge b(x),
        \qquad x\in\mathcal I,\ h\ge0.
    \]

    \noindent \textbf{(ii)} \quad 
    The free boundaries satisfy the integral equations (equation interior_boundary_system_2d of the paper), (equation active_boundary_system_2d of the paper) below. If the relevant side branches of \(y\mapsto\Phi(x,y)\) have no flat portions, then the boundary functions are continuous on intervals where the boundary regime is fixed. At regular points, where the corresponding values of \(H\)  of (equation def_H_2d of the paper) do not vanish, the boundaries are of class \(C^1\) and satisfy the differential equations of Proposition~(prop_boundary_regular_odes of the paper).

    \noindent \textbf{(iii)} \quad 
    The value function is non-decreasing in both $x$ and $y$ variables. Moreover, it satisfies smooth fit in the displacement variable $y$ at the upper boundary and at every interior lower boundary. At regular boundary points it also satisfies horizontal smooth fit.

    \noindent \textbf{(iv)} \quad 
    Finally, if \(k'(0+)\le c\), then the lower boundary never touches the diagonal:
    \[
        a(x)>-x,\qquad x\in\mathcal I.
    \]
    If \(k'(0+)>c\) and \(k(r)=o(e^{2r})\) as \(r\to\infty\), then the lower
    boundary eventually coincides with the diagonal:
    \[
        a(x)=-x
        \quad\text{for all sufficiently large }x\in\mathcal I.
    \]
    In the non-contact case, under the same subcritical growth condition and assuming that
    \(
    \rho
    \coloneqq
    \sup\{r\ge0:k'_+(r)\le c\}
    \)
    is finite, one has
    \(
        x+a(x)\to\rho
    \)
    as $x\to\infty.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Th th_2d_structure of arXiv:2606.23648

Let N be a nonnegative integer-valued random variable with finite second moment, mu = E[N] and beta = E[binom(N, 2)]. For every integer r >= 1, P(N > 0) >= 2 mu/(r+1) - 2 beta/(r(r+1)). Pointwise, for every integer n >= 0, 1_{n > 0} >= 2n/(r+1) - 2 binom(n, 2)/(r(r+1)), with equality exactly at n = 0, r and r + 1.
N is nonnegative and integer valued
E[N^2] < infinity
r is an integer, r >= 1

[Theorem 7 (Abstract Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula) of arXiv:2608.02417, 'A Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for linear stochastic evolution equations in Banach spaces'] Let Assumption \ref{ass:fixed-time-integrability} hold, and fix \(t>0\).
Suppose that \(\xi\in E\) and \(h\in\scrH_t\) satisfy
\[
    S(t)\xi=R_th.
\]
Then, for every bounded Borel function \(f:E\to\R\), the derivative
\(D_\xi P_tf(x)\) exists and
\[
    D_\xi P_tf(x)
    =
    \E[f(U_t^x)W_t(h)]
    =
    \E\Bigl[
    f(U_t^x)
    \int_0^t \iprod{\Pi_t h(s)}{\dd W_{H}(s)}_{H}
    \Bigr],
\]
where \(W_t\) is the \(\scrH_t\)-isonormal process associated with \(W_H\) and
\(\Pi_t\) denotes the orthogonal projection of \(\scrH_t=L^2(0,t;H)\)
onto \((\Ker (R_t))^\perp\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Abstract Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula

body:
[Theorem thm:hybrid-monotonicity of arXiv:2609.00399, 'Shannon's problem on the monotonicity of entropy and a Conjecture of Tao'] Let $\mathcal G$ be a second-countable locally compact abelian group and let
$e:\mathbb R\to\mathcal G$ be a topological group embedding with closed image such that
$D=\mathcal G/e(\mathbb R)$ is discrete.  Let $\pi:\mathcal G\to D$ be the quotient map,
choose a section $s:D\to\mathcal G$ of $\pi$, and write each $v\in\mathcal G$ uniquely
as $v=s(d)+e(x)$.  Let $V_1,V_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d.\ $\mathcal G$-valued random
variables.  Assume that the quotient label of $V_1$ has finite support and
that, conditional on each positive-probability label, the real coordinate
has a bounded, compactly supported Lebesgue density.  If
$Y_k=V_1+\cdots+V_k$, then
\begin{equation}
 h(Y_{k+1})-h(Y_k)\geq\frac12\log\frac{k+1}{k},\qquad k\geq1,
\end{equation}
where both entropy terms are finite and are computed relative to the same
Haar measure on $\mathcal G$.  Their difference is independent of the Haar
normalization. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-real-direction hybrid monotonicity

[Theorem thm:GFE_block of arXiv:2412.04579, 'Solvable Families of Random Block Tridiagonal Matrices'] Let $\mathbf{M}$ have G${\mathbb{F}}$E$(rn)$ distribution, and consider the matrix $\mathbf{S}$ defined via~(equation eq:S1234 of the paper). Then $\mathbf{S}$ is a.s.~invertible, and the $r$-block Jacobi matrix $\mathbf{T}$ produced by Theorem~{\rm(thm:block_basic_1 of the paper)} has~$\mathtt{H}_{n,\beta}(r,0)$ distribution.

The eigenvalues of $\mathbf{T}$ are distributed as $G\beta E(rn)$, and the normalized eigenvector matrix $\mathbf{V}=[\mathbf{v}_{i,j}]_{i,j\in [\![rn ]\!]}$ can be chosen in a way so that the first $r$ rows of $\mathbf{V}$ are independent of the eigenvalues and have the same distribution as the first $r$ rows of an $rn\times rn$ Haar ${\mathbb{F}}$-unitary matrix. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Agresti and Veraar, Nonlinear parabolic stochastic evolution equations in critical spaces (journal version 2025, p. 130), Problem 4 asks whether in the variational setting of their Theorem 6.4 there is a constant C_T with E sup_{t <= T} ||u(t)||_H^2 <= C_T (1 + E ||u_0||_H^2) for all u_0 in L^2(Omega; H). Our result (id P0266, 2026-09-08): the bound FAILS, on the authors' own named unresolved example - Allen-Cahn on the one-dimensional torus with one-dimensional quadratic noise, du = (Laplacian u + u - u^3) dt + gamma u^2 dW, at the critical gamma^2 = 2. With deterministic constant data u_0 = a > 0 the solution stays spatially constant, and the substitutions Y = 1/U, Y = e^{-t} V, time change s = (e^{2t} - 1)/2 and R = V / sqrt 2 turn the SDE into R being a four-dimensional Bessel process started at R_0 = 1/(sqrt 2 a), with U_t = e^t / (sqrt 2 R_s). Since sup_{t <= T} U_t^2 >= 1/(2 inf_{s <= S} R_s^2) and a BES(4) enters a ball of radius x with probability of order x^2 (Newtonian capacity), P(sup U^2 > y) is of order 1/y - tail index one - so E sup_{t <= T} ||u(t)||_H^2 = infinity for every T > 0 while E ||u_0||_H^2 = a^2 is finite. Verification as the source words it: checked in the reverse direction by Ito as well; and an instrument note - a first simulation appeared to contradict the x^2 scaling, but refining the steps at fixed x drives P/x^2 toward the exact constant 2.0 (1.204, 1.579, 1.697 at x = 0.2 and 0.725, 1.285, 1.455 at x = 0.1), so the scaling is real. NOT Lean-checked: this one has no finite arithmetic core, being Ito calculus plus a capacity estimate. [Lem 146 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] Let $h>0,\delta>0,\eta>0,{\hat x}_0\ge 0,w\in\mathbb R$, write ${\hat x}'={\hat x}_0+w$, and choose 
		$M=-2{\hat x}_0-\eta$. 
                There exists a constant $c>0$ such that
		 for fixed $h$, ${\hat x}_0$, and $w$ satisfying $w+{\hat x}_0>\delta-\sqrt{2h/\gamma''}$, it holds for $\eta$ small enough
		\begin{align}
			&\bigl(U_{h;M,Q}({\hat x}')-U_{h;M,Q}({\hat x}_0)\bigr)
			-\bigl(U_{h;0,0}({\hat x}_1+w)-U_{h;0,0}({\hat x}_1)\bigr)
			\ge c \delta^{1/2} Q w^2
                          +\mathcal{O}(Q^2),
			
		\end{align}
                as $Q\to0$,
		where ${\hat x}_1={\hat x}_1^{[-2{\hat x}_0-\eta]}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 55 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Fix $N,n\ge1$, $K_{\rm feat}<\infty$, $\beta>0$, and
		$\vartheta\ge1$.  Let
		$W\in\R^N$ be a $(K_{\rm feat},\tau)$-regular feature with
		covariance matrix $\Sigma$, put
		$\lambda_{\Sigma}=\|\Sigma\|_{\op}>0$, and let $G$ be the matching centered
		Gaussian feature.  Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ and $G_1,\ldots,G_n$ be
		independent arrays of iid copies of $W$ and $G$, respectively.
		There are constants $C<\infty$ and $c_0>0$, depending only on
		$K_{\rm feat}$, with the following property.

		Let
		$\mathcal D\subset\R^N$ be nonempty, bounded, convex, and relatively
		open in its affine hull, and let
		$\mathcal B:\mathcal D\to[0,\infty)$ be a
		$\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier.  Fix $(\theta_{\rm ref},b_{\rm ref})\in\mathcal D\times\R$, and set
		\[
			K_{\rm ref}:=
			1+\lambda_{\Sigma}\|\theta_{\rm ref}\|_2^2+b_{\rm ref}^2
			+\mathcal B(\theta_{\rm ref}).
		\]
		Put
		\[
			\mathfrak L_n:=1+\vartheta\log n
		\]
		and
		\[
			\Delta_n:=
			(1+\beta^{-1})^2K_{\rm ref}^2\left[
			\frac{\sqrt{\dim\mathsf V_{\mathcal D}}(\tau/\lambda_{\Sigma}+1)}{n}
			+\left(\frac{\mathfrak L_n}{n}\right)^{1/3}
			\right]
			+\frac{(1+\beta)K_{\rm ref}}{n}.
		\]
		If $\mathfrak L_n\le c_0n$, then
		\begin{equation}
			
			\left|
			\E\Phi_W(\mathcal D;\beta)
			-\E\Phi_G(\mathcal D;\beta)
			\right|\le C\Delta_n.
		\end{equation}
		Moreover, for every $t>0$,
		\begin{equation}
			
			\Pp\left\{
			\left|\Phi_W(\mathcal D;\beta)-\Phi_G(\mathcal D;\beta)\right|
			>C\Delta_n+t
			\right\}
			\le\frac{C(1+\beta^{-1})^2K_{\rm ref}^2}{nt^2}.
		\end{equation}

[Lemma 3 (Rate normalization) of arXiv:2606.29635, 'Extremality and Limit Laws for the Siblings of the Coupon Collector'] For positive rates $r=(r_1,\ldots,r_N)$ define
\[
        I_j(r)=\sum_{k=1}^N\int_0^\infty r_k\e^{-r_kt}\frac{(r_kt)^{j-1}}{(j-1)!}\prod_{i\ne k}(1-\e^{-r_it})\dd t.
\]
Then $I_j(cr)=I_j(r)$ for every $c>0$. Consequently, if $p_i=r_i/\sum_\ell r_\ell$, then $\E_pU_j^N=I_j(r)$.

STATUS: proof (unaudited). Conditional radial-locking theorem: if a_n(T)=(1/n)*sum_{l<nT} E[1-rho_l] tends to zero for the Gaussian ReLU Gram chain, then the maximum normalized log-diagonal ratio tends to zero in probability, with threshold failure bound 1536*a_n(T)/epsilon^2+C_T*n*exp(-c*n)*(1+epsilon^-2). Together with qualitative positive-time correlation collapse and the settled single-input limit, the two preactivations converge jointly to sqrt(M_t)*xi*(sqrt(q1),sqrt(q2)), M_t=exp(-5t/2+sqrt(5t)*Z), xi independent of Z. Scope and unresolved checks: Qualitative angular collapse is an explicit premise; C006 is unaudited. No novelty clearance or finite-n scalar-limit rate. This does not identify scale/fine-angle joint Brownian coupling.
Zero-bias independent Gaussian ReLU layers at critical variance; positive initial diagonal variances tending to q1,q2>0; fixed T; stated angular-defect and scalar-limit premises.
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:c3156b201e8345dedeeb7e501931cdc1356631992e378628f9f2875840105c46","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c3/c3156b201e8345dedeeb7e501931cdc1356631992e378628f9f2875840105c46.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7e185a76f632fc458b19fe969e975e29336e6a75bb44e60aea49001f47687453","bundle_entry_key":"radial-locking","bundle_id":"population.t244-relu-entrance-and-radial-drafts-002","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:gaussian-relu-radial-locking-conditional-joint-output-law","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Radial locking and the conditional two-output limit

Status: proof (unaudited). Target 1. This identifies a missing architecture step, without claiming literature novelty. The qualitative angle-collapse premise is stated explicitly; C006 is a separate, still unaudited way to verify it for the network.

Let a zero-bias Gaussian ReLU network have width n and initial diagonal preactivation-variance parameters q_{1,n},q_{2,n}>0, tending to q_1,q_2>0. Write K_{j,l} for the corresponding diagonal Gram entries; equivalently the next preactivation covariance is G_l with diagonals K_{1,l},K_{2,l} and correlation rho_l. For each fixed T suppose

    a_n(T)=(1/n) sum_{l<floor(nT)} E[1-rho_l] -> 0.

Assign rho=1 after extinction for defining this bounded expectation. Then, uniformly for l<=floor(nT),

    log[(K_{2,l}/q_{2,n})/(K_{1,l}/q_{1,n})] -> 0 in probability,

on nonextinction, whose probability tends to one. More explicitly the failure probability at threshold epsilon is bounded by

    1536 a_n(T)/epsilon^2 + C_T n exp(-c n)(1+epsilon^-2).

If additionally, for fixed t>0, rho_floor(nt)->1 in probability and K_{1,floor(nt)}/q_{1,n} converges to M_t=exp(-5t/2+sqrt(5t)Z), then the pair of final preactivations converges jointly to

    sqrt(M_t) xi (sqrt(q_1),sqrt(q_2)),

where xi,Z are independent standard normals. The single-input scale premise is settled in the dossier and appears in Li-Nica-Roy, arXiv:2206.02768, section 2.2, Eq.(2.6). No moment-determinacy argument is used.

## Symmetric one-step truncation

Given a current angle theta, let (a_i,b_i), i=1,...,n, be independent standard bivariate Gaussian pairs with correlation rho=cos(theta). Define S_a=sum(a_i)_+^2 and S_b=sum(b_i)_+^2 and the symmetric event

    H={n/4<=S_a,S_b<=n}.

Each sum has the marginal law chi-square_B with B~Bin(n,1/2), independently of rho. Its moment-generating function is

    E exp(lambda S_a)=[(1+(1-2lambda)^(-1/2))/2]^n, lambda<1/2.

Markov's inequality with lambda=-1/2 for the lower tail and lambda=1/8 for the upper tail gives P(H^c)<=C exp(-cn), uniformly in rho. The same bounds hold at rho=+/-1, since only marginals were used.

Define D=log(S_b/S_a) on H and D=0 off H. Exchangeability of the bivariate Gaussian pair and symmetry of H give E[D|theta]=0 exactly. On H, the mean-value theorem for log gives |D|<=4|S_b-S_a|/n.

For h_i=(b_i)_+^2-(a_i)_+^2, E h_i=0 and

    |h_i|<=|b_i-a_i|(|a_i|+|b_i|),
    E h_i^2 <= sqrt(E(b_i-a_i)^4 * E(|a_i|+|b_i|)^4)
              <= sqrt(12(1-rho)^2 * 48)=24(1-rho).

Here E(b-a)^4=12(1-rho)^2 and (|a|+|b|)^4<=8(a^4+b^4). Coordinate independence therefore yields

    E D^2 <= (16/n^2) E(S_b-S_a)^2 <= 384(1-rho)/n.

No inverse angle or untruncated logarithm of a zero norm is taken.

## Layerwise coupling and martingale bound

Modify the entire Gram update to a self-loop whenever H fails. On H use the exact update, including its angle and both diagonal entries. This gives a positive-diagonal chain at every layer. It couples with the true chain through floor(nT) layers with disagreement probability at most C Tn exp(-cn), by a conditional union bound. Exact angle zero on H is allowed; subsequent proportional inputs have rho=1 and D=0.

For the modified chain, Gaussian rotational invariance and ReLU homogeneity give

    log[(K_{2,l}/q_{2,n})/(K_{1,l}/q_{1,n})]=sum_{i<l} D_i.

The increments D_i have conditional mean zero and the conditional second-moment bound above. Thus this is a square-integrable martingale. The expected sum of its variances is at most 384 times the angular-defect average of the modified chain. At layer l the bounded defect 1-rho in [0,2] differs in expectation from the true chain by at most 2Cl exp(-cn). Summing and dividing by n changes a_n(T) by at most C_T n exp(-cn).

Doob's L2 inequality and Markov's inequality now give the displayed 1536 a_n(T)/epsilon^2 bound, plus C_T n exp(-cn)(1+epsilon^-2). Transfer by the coupling proves radial locking for the true network. Extinction itself is contained in a coupling failure, since H excludes zero norms.

If rho_floor(ns)->1 in probability for every fixed s>0, the assumption a_n(T)->0 follows automatically: regard the sum as the integral of a bounded step function on [0,T], use bounded convergence of E[1-rho_floor(ns)] at each s>0, and then dominated convergence in s. The initial layer has zero limiting time measure.

## Joint preactivation law

Radial locking, the positive single-input limit, and Slutsky's theorem give

    (K_1,K_2,rho) => (q_1 M_t,q_2 M_t,1),
    G_floor(nt) => M_t v v^T, v=(sqrt(q_1),sqrt(q_2)).

For a pair of final preactivations, the exact conditional characteristic function at w in R^2 is exp(-w^T G_floor(nt) w/2), by Li-Nica-Roy section 2.3, Eq.(2.7). This is a bounded continuous function of G, so its expectation converges to E exp(-M_t (w dot v)^2/2), which identifies the claimed Gaussian scale mixture. The same argument handles any fixed number of conditionally independent output coordinates.

## Scope

This proof is conditional on qualitative angular collapse and the single-input limit, not on the n^-2 angular rate. Section 2.3 of Li-Nica-Roy observes collapse at positive depth-to-width time; priority of this radial consequence has not been cleared. C006 would also imply the required angle premises once its proof is independently checked. No finite-n convergence rate for the scale law and no joint law of the Brownian scale with the fine angle process are proved here.

Prior-literature update (C012): Li-Nica arXiv2310.12079 Section4.1 already states the positive-time rescaled-correlation SDE and explicitly leaves the entrance unresolved. Its displayed q/log-q equations have an Ito discrepancy awaiting Claude review. [Proposition 5 of arXiv:2606.10313, '\textbf{Invariance principles for additive functionals of voter models}'] (Clifford and Sudbury, 1973; Holley and Liggett, 1975).
For any integer $m\geq 1$, $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_m\in G$, $0\leq t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_m\leq s$, given $\eta\in \{0, 1\}^G$ and $H:\{0, 1\}^m\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, we have
\begin{align}
&\mathbb{E}_\eta H\left(\eta_{t_1}(x_1), \eta_{t_2}(x_2)\ldots, \eta_{t_m}(x_m)\right) \notag\\
&=\hat{\mathbb{E}}H\left(\eta(\mathcal{X}_s^{s-t_1, x_1}), \eta(\mathcal{X}_s^{s-t_2, x_2})\ldots, \eta(\mathcal{X}_s^{s-t_m, x_m})\right).
\end{align}
Consequently, for any probability distribution $\mu$ on $\{0, 1\}^G$,
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb{E}_{\mu} H\left(\eta_{t_1}(x_1), \eta_{t_2}(x_2)\ldots, \eta_{t_m}(x_m)\right) \notag\\
&=\hat{\mathbb{E}}\mathbb{E}_{\mu}H\left(\eta_0(\mathcal{X}_s^{s-t_1, x_1}), \eta_0(\mathcal{X}_s^{s-t_2, x_2})\ldots, \eta_0(\mathcal{X}_s^{s-t_m, x_m})\right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:isometry of arXiv:2602.14617, 'Stochastic Burgers equation driven by multiplicative Rosenblatt noise: local existence, un'] Let $\Phi \in \mathbb{D}^{2,2}(L^2([0,T]))$. Then
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[ \left( \int_0^T \Phi_s \, \delta \mathcal{R}_s \right)^2 \right] = \mathbb{E}\left[ \|\Phi\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 \right] + \mathbb{E}\left[ \|\nabla_H \Phi\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 \right] + \mathbb{E}\left[ \|\nabla_H^2 \Phi\|_{\mathcal{H}}^2 \right],
\]
where $\nabla_H$ and $\nabla_H^2$ are fractional derivative operators of order $H$ and $2H$ respectively, defined by
\[
(\nabla_H \Phi)_u = \frac{2c_H^R}{\Gamma(H/2)} \int_u^T \Phi_s (s-u)^{H/2-1} ds,
\]
\[
(\nabla_H^2 \Phi)_{u,v} = \frac{4c_H^R}{\Gamma(H/2)^2} \int_{\max(u,v)}^T \Phi_s (s-u)^{H/2-1} (s-v)^{H/2-1} ds,
\]
with $c_H^R$ a normalization constant (see Table (tab:constants of the paper)). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem Fubini, Tonelli of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a function $f:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R$ which is measurable and integrable, in the sense that the following integral is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^N}|f(z)|dz<\infty$$
we have the following equalities, for any decomposition $N=N_1+N_2$:
$$\int_{\mathbb R^{N_1}}\int_{\mathbb R^{N_2}}f(x,y)dydx=\int_{\mathbb R^{N_2}}\int_{\mathbb R^{N_1}}f(x,y)dxdy=\int_{\mathbb R^N}f(z)dz$$
Moreover, the same holds when $f:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb R$ is assumed positive, and measurable.

[Thm conformal invariance aut H of arXiv:2505.16093, 'Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system'] For conformal map $\tau \in {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H})$, the drift term
$b(\boldsymbol{\theta},u)$ is a pre-schwarz form, i.e.
$$b_i=\tau^{\prime} \widetilde{b}_i \circ \tau+ \frac{6-\kappa}{2}\left(\log \tau^{\prime}\right)^{\prime}$$
\begin{itemize}

\item[(i)]
   
Equivalently, in terms of partition function $\psi$, there exists a smooth function  $F(\tau,u): {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H})\times \mathbb{H} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that:
\begin{equation}
   \log(\psi)-\log(\psi \circ \tau)+\frac{\kappa-6}{2\kappa}\sum_i \log(\tau'(z_i)) = F(\tau,u) 
\end{equation}
    and $F$ satisfies the following functional equation:
   \begin{equation} 
      F(\tau_1 \tau_2 ,u)= F(\tau_1,\tau_2(u))+F(\tau_2,u)
   \end{equation}
\item[(ii)]
There exists a rotation constant \( \lambda(\infty) \) such that:
    \[
    F(D_a, \infty) = -d\cdot\log(a).
    \]
    \item[(iii)] Suppose \( F_1(\tau, u) \) and \( F_2(\tau, u) \) correspond to partition functions \( \psi_1 \) and \( \psi_2 \). If their dilatation constants \( d_1 = d_2 \), then there exists a function \( g(u) \) such that:
    \[
   \psi_2 = g(u) \cdot \psi_1.
    \]

    \item[(iv)] For \( \tau \in \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{H}) \) and $u \in \overline{\mathbb{H}}$, we define:
    \begin{itemize}
    \item if $\tau(u) \neq \infty, u \neq \infty$
    \[
    F(\tau, u) = d \cdot \log \left(\tau'(u)\right),
    \]
    \item If $\tau(u)=\infty$, $u \neq \infty$ 
    \[
    F(\tau, u)= F(-\frac{1}{\tau},u)
    \]
    \item If $\tau(u)\neq \infty$, $u= \infty$
    \[
    F(\tau, u)= F(-\frac{1}{\tau},0)
    \]
    \item If $\tau(z)=az+b$ and $u=\infty$,
    \[
    F(\tau,\infty) = -d \cdot \log(a)
    \]
        \end{itemize}
    Then $F(\tau,u)$ satisfy equation ((functional equation for F of the paper)), with dilatation constant $d$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma LemGroundStateVisitation of arXiv:2608.11178, 'A submartingale for the probability of avoiding the origin in one-point interaction ground'] Fix \(d\in\{2,3\}\), \(T,\gamma>0\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). The following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]

\item
Under the conditional law \(\widehat{\mathbb P}_{x}^{T,\gamma} := \mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma} [\,\cdot\,|\,\tau>T]\), the coordinate process
\(X=\{X_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}\) satisfies
\begin{align}
X_t
=
x
+
\int_0^t
\widehat b_{T-s}^{\gamma}(X_s)\,ds
+
\widehat M_t^{T,\gamma},
\qquad
t\in[0,T],\nonumber
\end{align}
where
\(\{\widehat M_t^{T,\gamma}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\) is a continuous
\(d\)-dimensional martingale with respect to
\(\{\mathcal F_t^{T,x}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\).

\item Let \(\rho\) be an
\(\{\mathcal F_t^{T,x}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\)-stopping time taking values in
\([0,T]\) such that \(\mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma}[\rho<\tau]>0\). Then the stopped coordinate process \(\{X_{t\wedge\rho}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\) has the same law under $\widehat{\mathbb P}_{x}^{T,\gamma,\rho} := \mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma}
\bigl[\,\cdot\,\bigm|\rho<\tau\bigr]$ as it does under the path measure
\[
\frac{
\bigl(S_{T-\rho}^{\gamma}(X_\rho)\bigr)^{-1}
}{
\widehat{\mathbb E}_{x}^{T,\gamma}
\left[
\bigl(S_{T-\rho}^{\gamma}(X_\rho)\bigr)^{-1}
\right]
}
\,\widehat{\mathbb P}_{x}^{T,\gamma}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma LemGroundStateVisitation of arXiv:2608.11178

[Theorem 33 of arXiv:2609.02197, '2609.02197'] Let $d=5$ and $\theta \in \left]-\infty,-\frac{1}{2}\right[.$

There exists a stochastic process $\left(\text{\gls{sto12}}\right)_{r \in \mathbb{R}_+}$ with state space $\left(\mathscr{C}^\theta,\mathcal{B}\left(\mathscr{C}^\theta\right)\right)$ such that the sample paths of $\left(\widetilde{\Xi}_{q,3}\right)_{q \in \mathbb{R}_+}$ are continuous and for every $\left(U,\varsigma\right) \in \mathbb{R}_+\times \mathbb{R}_+^*,$ $$\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow 0}\mathds{P}\left(\sup_{r \in \left[0,U\right]}\left\Vert\widetilde{\Xi}_{r,\epsilon,3}-\widetilde{\Xi}_{r,3}\right\Vert_{\mathscr{C}^\theta}>\varsigma\right)=0.$$

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2604.02312, 'A weak transport approach to the Schrödinger--Bass bridge'] Let $(x,\eta) \in \R^d \times \cP_2(\R^d)$. Then 
    \[
        \beta \longmapsto C_{\rm SB}^\beta(x,\eta),
    \]
    is non-decreasing whereas 
    \[
        \beta \longmapsto \frac1\beta C_{\rm SB}^\beta(x,\eta), 
        \qquad 
        \beta \longmapsto \frac1\beta \left( C_{\rm SB}^\beta(x,\eta) - \frac12 |x - \bar\eta|^2 \right)
    \]
    are non-increasing. Moreover,
    \begin{gather*}
        \lim_{\beta \uparrow \infty} C_{\rm SB}^\beta(x,\eta) = H(\eta \,|\, \gamma_x), 
        \qquad 
        \lim_{\beta \downarrow 0} C_{\rm SB}^\beta(x,\eta) = \frac12 |x - \bar\eta|^2, \\
        \qquad \lim_{\beta \downarrow 0} \frac1\beta \Big( C_{\rm SB}^\beta(x,\eta) - \frac12 |x - \bar\eta|^2 \Big) = \frac12 \Wcal_2^2(\eta,\gamma_{\bar\eta}).
    \end{gather*}

body:
Let X_1, X_2, ... be iid copies of a discrete source X with entropy H(X). For every eps > 0 and all large n, blocks of n symbols can be encoded using at most n (H(X) + eps) bits with error probability tending to zero, and conversely any encoding using at most n (H(X) - eps) bits has error probability tending to one. Entropy is thus the exact asymptotic limit of lossless compression per symbol.

    $$\eta^*(T) \coloneqq \lambda(T) - \sup\{\Re \lambda \mid \lambda \in \sigma(T), \Re\lambda \neq \lambda(T)\} \,,$$
    and for $z \in \mathbb{R}^d$ we set $\eta^*(z) \coloneqq \eta^*(A(z))$.

body: [Defn of arXiv:2609.00884, 'The weakness of typicality'] Let $\mathcal{C}\subseteq 2^{\omega}$. We say $\mathcal{C}$ is an $X_0$-\emph{computational class} if for any $X\in\mathcal{C}$ and any $Y$ with $X_0\oplus Y\ge_{\mathrm{T}} X$, $Y\in\mathcal{C}$; that is, if $\mathcal{C}$ is closed upwards under Turing reducibility relative to~$X_0$.

[Lemma descentera of arXiv:2608.09856, '\bf Mass erasure on measured $\bbR$-trees,\\ applications to L\'evy forests'] Let $(T, d, \rho)$ be a rooted Polish $\mathbb{R}$-tree, with bordification $(T^*\! , d^*\! , \rho)$. We recall the definition of $\mathcal{M}_f^{\mathtt{era}}(T)$ from ((meraspace of the paper)). 
Then the following holds true. 
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$(i)$] $\mu \! \in \!   \mathcal{M}_f^{\mathtt{era}}(T)$ iff ${\cal E}_h \mu \! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_f(T)$ for all $h\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$. In this case, 
$T^*_{\! \mu, h}$ is a compact subset of $T$ and we simply denote it by $T_{\! \mu,h}$. 

\smallskip

\item[$(ii)$] For all $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$, let $\nu_p \! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_f(T)$ and let $h_p\! \in \!  \mathbb{R}^*_+$ be such that 
$h_{p+1} \! < \!  h_p$, ${\cal E}_{h_p-h_{p+1}}\nu_{p+1}\! = \!  \nu_p$ and $\lim_{p\rightarrow \infty} h_p\! = \!  0$. Then, there exists a unique $\mu\! \in \!  \mathcal{M}_f^{\mathtt{era}}(T) $ such that ${\cal E}_{h_p} \mu \! = \!  \nu_p$ for all $p\! \in \!  \mathbb{N}$. Moreover $\nu_p \! \to \! \mu$ weakly in $\mathcal{M}_f(T^*)$. 
\end{compactenum} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma descentera of arXiv:2608.09856

body:
Let H be a complex Hilbert space and T a trace-class operator on H. Then for every orthonormal basis (e_i) of H the family (<T e_i, e_i>) is absolutely summable and its sum tr T is the same for every orthonormal basis; |tr T| <= ||T||_1; tr is linear on S_1(H); tr(T*) = conjugate of tr T; and tr T = sum_i <T e_i, e_i> with at most countably many nonzero terms. Moreover, for B in B(H) the products BT and TB are trace class, with ||BT||_1 <= ||B|| ||T||_1 and ||TB||_1 <= ||B|| ||T||_1, and tr(BT) = tr(TB). If A and B are both Hilbert-Schmidt then AB and BA are trace class and tr(AB) = tr(BA) = <B, A*>_2, where the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product is <X, Y>_2 = sum_i <X e_i, Y e_i> = tr(Y*X), so that indeed <B, A*>_2 = tr(AB) (note the order: <A*, B>_2 is the complex conjugate of tr(AB), not tr(AB) itself). If T >= 0 is a positive trace-class operator then tr T >= 0 and tr T = 0 forces T = 0.
H is a complex Hilbert space
T is trace class on H
B is a bounded operator on H; A, B are Hilbert-Schmidt in the two-factor statement
the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product is linear in its first argument, <X, Y>_2 = tr(Y*X)

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2609.03248, 'Connections between colored restricted $b$-ary and ordinary partitions'] Let $\rho\geq 1$, $\ell\geq 1$, and $b\geq 2$ be integers. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] the sequence $C_b^{\Lambda}(n)$ of $\rho$-color $b$-ary 
partitions of $n$ (where the multiplicity of each part with color $i$ is one 
of $i, 2i, \ldots, \ell i$) and
\item[(b)] the sequence $Y_n$ of ordinary partitions with each part bounded by
$\rho$ and occurring at most $\ell$ times
\end{enumerate}
are connected by the recurrence relation
\begin{equation}
C_b^\Lambda(bn+j)=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor\lambda/b\rfloor}Y_{bk+j}C_b^\Lambda(n-k)
\qquad (j=0, 1,\ldots b-1),
\end{equation}
where $\lambda=\ell\rho(\rho+1)/2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theo dqgsrt of arXiv:2507.00737, 'Dispersion models on a circle: universal properties and asymptotic results'] Take the same hypothesis as (theo:excha of the paper). Let $M_0,\cdots,M_{b-1}$ be some non-negative masses. For all $a_0\preceq 0\preceq a_1\preceq \cdots \preceq a_{b-1}\preceq a_0 \preceq 0 \cdots$ and such that
	$\Leb\left( \fleche{[a_i,a_{i+1 {~\sf mod~} b}]}\right)> M_i$ for all $i\in \{0,\cdots,b-1\}$, 
	\begin{equation}
	\mathbb{P}\left( \bA{k}_j \in \mathrm{d} a_j,  \left|\textbf{O}^{(k)}_j\right|=M_j, 0\leq j \leq b-1\right)= \sum_{(J_0,\cdots,J_{b-1}) \in P(k,b)} \prod_{j=0}^{b-1} Q(m(J_j)) \mathds{1}_{W(m(J_j)) = M_j}\, \mathrm{d} a_j
	\end{equation} where $P(k,b)$ is the set of partitions of $\{0,\ldots, k-1\}$ into $b$ parts. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 16 (Eigen-expansion of $d_\varepsilon(\varrho)$) of arXiv:2603.29473, '$\chi^2$--cut-off phenomenon for Galerkin projections of Fokker--Planck equations with mon'] \hfill

	\noindent
	Let $\varepsilon>0$ be fixed.
	Let $\psi_{k,\varepsilon}$, $k=0,1,\ldots$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2_{\varrho_{\varepsilon,\infty}}$ with $\psi_{0,\varepsilon}=1$. Then for a density $\varrho \in L^2_{\varrho^{-1}_{\varepsilon,\infty}}$, the $\chi^2$-discrepancy \cref{eq:Sepdist} satisfies
	\begin{equation*}
		(d_\varepsilon(\varrho))^2 = \sum_{k=1}^\infty \left ( \int \varrho(x) \psi_{k,\varepsilon}(x) \dx \right )^2.
	\end{equation*}

[Lemma rogozin1961increase of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] [esseen1968concentration]
    There exists an absolute positive constant $C_{(rogozin1961increase of the paper)}$ such that the following holds. Let $n\ge 1$ and let $\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n$ be independent random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$.  Then for any $t\ge t_0>0$, one has
    \[
    \mathcal{L}\lr{\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i, t}\le \frac{C_{(rogozin1961increase of the paper)} (t/t_0)^2}{\sqrt{n-\sum_{i=1}^n\mathcal{L}(\xi_i,t_0)}}.
    \]
    In particular, if $\alpha\ge  \max_{1\le i\le n}\mathcal{L}(\xi_i,t_0)$, then
    \[
     \mathcal{L}\lr{\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i, t}\le \frac{C_{(rogozin1961increase of the paper)}}{\sqrt{n(1-\alpha)}}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma rogozin1961increase of arXiv:2604.10446

[Proposition prop:sc-backtracking-residual of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Define \[ 
	\Delta_{\mathsf{BacktrackingInt}} \coloneqq  \sum _{\tau \in \mathcal{B}(K)} (c_\tau)^2 \cdot  \mathsf{M} _{\mathsf{BacktrackingInt}(\tau)} - I_d \,,	\]
	we have \[ 
	\|\Delta_{\mathsf{BacktrackingInt}}\|_{sp} = o_d(1)\,.
	\]
	provided $\mathrm{Var}(K)=1$. Suppose each shape has at most $D_V$ vertices. Then, with high probability,
\[
    \|\Delta_{\mathsf{BacktrackingInt}}\|_{\mathrm{sp}}
    \leq
    \frac{\operatorname{poly}(q,D_V)}{\sqrt d}
    +
    O\left(
        \frac{D_V^2}{d}
        +
        \frac{D_V^2}{m}
    \right).
\]
In particular, if \(m=\Theta(d^2)\) and \(q,D_V=\operatorname{polylog}(d)\), then
\[
    \|\Delta_{\mathsf{BacktrackingInt}}\|_{\mathrm{sp}}
    \leq
    \frac{\operatorname{polylog}(d)}{\sqrt d}
    =
    o_d(1).
\]

[Theorem 8 (Integration regimes) of arXiv:2512.04646, '\textbf{Canonical Rough Path over Tempered Fractional Brownian Motion: Existence, Construc'] Let $B_{H,\lambda}$ be a tfBm and $X$ a suitable integrand path.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
  \item For $H > 1/2$, the rough path integral
    $\int X\,d\mathbf{B}_{H,\lambda}$ coincides with the Young
    integral $\int X\,dB_{H,\lambda}$ and equals the limit of
    left Riemann sums.
  \item For $H \in (1/4,1/2]$, the Young integral does not exist in
    general, but the rough path integral
    $\int X\,d\mathbf{B}_{H,\lambda}$ is well-defined via the
    Sewing Lemma \cite[Lemma~4.2]{FrizHairer2014}.
  \item For adapted square-integrable integrands and $H > 1/4$,
    the rough path integral agrees with the stochastic integral of
    \cite{MeerschaertSabzikar2014}.
\end{enumerate}

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): After the one-batch exchange on A_r, every signed-selector residual certificate has dimension d >= r - floor(log_2(2r)) (tag 43). Proof: let R be the residual span and pi the quotient map of rank q = r - d. Selector feasibility says every member of D~(A_r) has the same quotient image, up to sign, as one of the r members of the exchanged basis, so |pi(D~(A_r))| <= 2r (44). But (37) is an invertible linear image of the r-cube, and every rank-q linear image of a cube has at least 2^q distinct points (pick q input directions with independent images, fix the other signs, vary those q). Hence 2^{r-d} = 2^q <= 2r. Notes: For r = 2^{2t} the bound is r - (2t+1) while the number of batches remains ONE. The cube-image counting step (every rank-q linear image of a cube has >= 2^q points) is a reusable tool.

body: In BOND percolation on a graph G with parameter p in [0,1], each edge is declared open with probability p and closed otherwise, independently; P_p denotes the resulting product measure on {0,1}^{E(G)}. The open cluster C(x) of a vertex x is the set of vertices reachable from x through open edges. Write theta(p) = P_p( |C(0)| = infinity ) for a fixed origin. Coupling all parameters on a common family of independent uniform variables - edge e open at level p exactly when U_e <= p - shows theta is nondecreasing, so the CRITICAL PROBABILITY p_c(G) = sup{ p : theta(p) = 0 } = inf{ p : theta(p) > 0 } is well defined. SITE percolation is defined analogously with vertices; the two have different critical values on the same graph, and p_c^{bond} <= p_c^{site} on any graph. On Z^d with d >= 2 one has 0 < p_c < 1, with the explicit elementary bounds 1/(2d-1) <= p_c^{bond}(Z^d) < 1. The value is known exactly only in special cases, most famously p_c^{bond}(Z^2) = 1/2. Whether theta(p_c) = 0 in every dimension is a celebrated open problem: it is known for d = 2 (Harris and Kesten) and, by lace-expansion methods, in high dimensions - Hara and Slade for large d, later reduced to d >= 11 by Fitzner and van der Hofstad - and it was still open for the intermediate dimensions 3 <= d <= 10 at the time this node was written. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Chapters 1 and 8]

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ be bounded and open, $T>0$, and let $\partial_t+L$, $Lu=-a^{ij}u_{x_ix_j}+b^iu_{x_i}+cu$, be uniformly parabolic with coefficients continuous and bounded on $U_T$. Let $u\in C^2_1(U_T)\cap C(\overline{U_T})$. (i) If $c\equiv0$ and $u_t+Lu\le0$ in $U_T$, then $\max_{\overline{U_T}}u=\max_{\Gamma_T}u$ (and if $u_t+Lu\ge0$, then $\min_{\overline{U_T}}u=\min_{\Gamma_T}u$). (ii) If $c\ge0$ and $u_t+Lu\le0$, then $\max_{\overline{U_T}}u\le\max_{\Gamma_T}u^+$ (and if $u_t+Lu\ge0$, then $\min_{\overline{U_T}}u\ge-\max_{\Gamma_T}u^-$). (iii) Comparison principle, any bounded $c$: if $u_t+Lu\le0$ in $U_T$ and $u\le0$ on $\Gamma_T$, then $u\le0$ in $U_T$; consequently the classical initial-boundary value problem has at most one solution in $C^2_1(U_T)\cap C(\overline{U_T})$.

coefficients a^{ij}, b^i, c continuous and bounded on U_T, a^{ij} symmetric

u in C^2_1(U_T) cap C(closure of U_T)

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2607.21392, 'Gaussian Convexity Principles for Sharp Moderate Deviations of Gaussian Maxima and Critica'] Let $t>\sqrt{2}$ be fixed, and define
\[
    q_t=\sqrt{(t^2-2)\log N-2\log\log N}.
\]
Then, for all sufficiently large $N$,
\begin{equation}
    \Phi^{-1}\left(
    \mathbb P\left(\max_{1\le i\le N}X_i\le t\sqrt{\log N}\right)
    \right)
    \ge q_t .
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
    \Phi^{-1}\left(
    \mathbb P\left(\max_{1\le i\le N}X_i\le t\sqrt{\log N}\right)
    \right)
    =
    \sqrt{t^2-2}\sqrt{\log N}+o(\sqrt{\log N}),
    \qquad N\to\infty .
\end{equation}

is metastable in the following sense:
\begin{enumerate}

\]

		\[

		\frac{u}{\|A\|_{\op}}

		\[
		\|\langle W,A\rangle\|_{\psione}
		\le \frac{C}{\sqrt d}\|A\|_F.
		\]

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2606.30349, 'Attenuated Poisson Dirichlet approximations for divisibility configurations'] Let $B\subset \mathbf N(\mathbbm{X})$ be measurable, and let $X_0,\dots,X_m$ be $\mathbf N(\mathbbm{X})$-valued random variables defined on a common probability space. Then
\begin{align*}
\Pb\big[\{X_0\in B\}\Delta\{X_m\in B\}\big]
\le
\sum_{i=1}^m \Pb \big[\{X_{i-1}\in B\}\Delta\{X_i\in B\}\big].
\end{align*}
Equivalently,
\begin{align*}
\mathcal E_B[X_0,X_m]
\le
\sum_{i=1}^m \mathcal E_B[X_{i-1},X_i].
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let V be an R^n-valued random vector with ||V||_2>0 almost surely, and let W be an independent q by n matrix whose entries are independent N(0,1) variables. Put Y=WV/sqrt(n) and Z=WV/||V||_2. Then Z has independent N(0,1) coordinates and is independent of the entire random vector V. Hence Y=(||V||_2/sqrt(n))Z exactly, with a Gaussian vector factor independent of the random radial scale. For any deterministic a>0, writing G=log(||V||_2^2/(n a^2)) yields Y=a exp(G/2)Z and Z is independent of G. This is an exact finite-dimensional Gaussian scale-mixture identity; it does not assert that G itself is Gaussian.
Positive integers n,q
V is a measurable random vector with positive norm almost surely
