body:
Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d, d >= 2, with edge-weight law nu. Assume the two conditions (i) E min{ t_1^d, ..., t_{2d}^d } < infinity, where the t_i are 2d independent copies of tau_e - equivalently E[Y^d] < infinity where Y is the MINIMUM of 2d copies, the two being the same because x -> x^d is increasing on [0, infinity) - and (ii) F(0) < p_c(d). Let B(t) = {x : T(0, x) <= t}, the random ball. Then there is a DETERMINISTIC, convex, COMPACT set B_nu in R^d with NON-EMPTY INTERIOR, symmetric about the axes, such that for every eps > 0, P( (1-eps) B_nu is contained in B(t)/t which is contained in (1+eps) B_nu for all large t ) = 1. The set B_nu is the unit ball of the time constant. Condition (i) is NOT merely convenient: if it fails then for every C > 0 the sum over x of P(m(x) > C|x|) diverges, where m(x) is the minimum weight over the edges at x, and Borel-Cantelli forces T(0,x)/|x| > C for infinitely many x almost surely, so the shape statement itself fails. Condition (ii) is what keeps the shape bounded: if F(0) >= p_c the time constant vanishes (Kesten) and B_nu is all of R^d; zero-weight edges percolate when F(0) > p_c, but at F(0) = p_c they do not in d = 2 or in high dimensions, so it is the vanishing time constant, not percolation of zero-weight edges, that unbounds the shape. What is NOT known, and is repeatedly imported elsewhere as an unproven hypothesis: whether the boundary of B_nu is STRICTLY CONVEX, whether it is DIFFERENTIABLE, and whether it has uniformly positive CURVATURE. Those are open for every non-degenerate weight distribution in every dimension, which is why the Newman-Piza exponent bounds and the directed-geodesic results carry non-constructive curvature or differentiability hypotheses. B_nu is not computed explicitly for any non-trivial F. [Cox and Durrett (1981), verified against Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation, Section 2.2]
i.i.d. nonnegative weights on Z^d, d >= 2
F(0) < p_c(d), so the time constant is a norm and the shape is bounded
E min{t_1^d, ..., t_{2d}^d} < infinity, equivalently E[Y^d] < infinity for Y the minimum of 2d independent copies of tau_e - and this condition is necessary, not just sufficient
no curvature, strict convexity or differentiability of B_nu is asserted; those are open

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:aa10d1f5315ac0588c10fde2a2896218ab29202df5951f2b7dce8e91f884dcd0","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/aa/aa10d1f5315ac0588c10fde2a2896218ab29202df5951f2b7dce8e91f884dcd0.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:69a0f29fcd282535c895ebd66e8e75b2d3fc0abad3eaa9a899b76a390bcc07a1","bundle_entry_key":"cc","bundle_id":"population.rwre-escape-clock-w447-001","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability / random walks in random environment","draft":"w447/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.rwre:nonstopping-rwre-clock-exit-count-moment-equivalence","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Clock-to-exit-count equivalence, without a stopping-time horizon

Claim CC (proved by w447; independent review pending).

Fix a uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor kernel on Z^d with lower bound kappa>0. Let sigma_0=0. At the finite stopping time sigma_i choose a set S_i containing X_sigma_i, measurably from the history and environment. Keep S_i fixed until its first exit, and assume its escape radius is at most the deterministic integer r>=1. Define sigma_{i+1} to be that exit time. The S_i may overlap, and the choice may depend on the whole past. Write D_i=sigma_{i+1}-sigma_i and a=kappa^r.

For any integer-valued random horizon tau>=1 finite almost surely, even if tau depends on the future and is not a stopping time, put K_tau=min{m>=1:sigma_m>=tau}. Then

E tau < infinity  if and only if  E K_tau < infinity.

Moreover let B be any event of probability p>0 on which tau is finite, under a law obtained by averaging the uniformly elliptic kernels and their paths. The same equivalence holds under conditional expectation given B. No conditional Markov or iid assertion is made under B.

Proof. ER gives conditionally at sigma_i

P(D_i>mr | F_sigma_i, omega) <= (1-a)^m.

Thus ceil(D_i/r) is conditionally dominated by a geometric variable on {1,2,...} with success probability a. With lambda=a/(4r) we get

E(exp(lambda D_i) | F_sigma_i,omega)
 <= a exp(a/4)/(1-(1-a) exp(a/4)) <= 4/3.

For the last inequality use exp(a/4)<=1/(1-a/4); the geometric denominator is positive, since (1-a)/(1-a/4)<1. The formula is increasing in exp(a/4), and at 1/(1-a/4) it is exactly 4/3. Tower iteration at the actual sigma_i now proves

E exp(lambda sigma_m) <= (4/3)^m.

At each tower step exp(lambda sigma_i) is measurable with respect to F_sigma_i (which retains omega), so E[exp(lambda sigma_{i+1})] = E[exp(lambda sigma_i) E(exp(lambda D_i)|F_sigma_i)] <= (4/3) E[exp(lambda sigma_i)]. Induction proves the displayed bound. This is a conditional moment argument, not independence between episodes.

Let C=2 log(4/3)/lambda. For every integer m>=1,

P(tau>Cm | B)
 <= P(K_tau>m | B) + p^(-1) exp(-lambda C m)(4/3)^m
 = P(K_tau>m | B) + p^(-1)(3/4)^m.

Indeed if K_tau<=m then tau<=sigma_m, regardless of whether tau is a stopping time. The second term follows by an unconditional Chernoff bound followed by division by p ONCE. In the unconditioned case take B to be the whole sample space.

Put L=ceil(C). Tail summation in blocks of L, using the bound above, gives the explicit estimate

E[tau | B] <= L ( E[K_tau | B] + 3/p ).

For the reverse implication, every D_i>=1, so sigma_m>=m and K_tau<=tau pathwise. Therefore E[K_tau | B]<=E[tau | B]. The argument also applies if tau is only finite on B, by defining it arbitrarily off B and defining K accordingly there.

Application to the C0041 route. Fixed-size balls centered at successive sigma_i satisfy the hypotheses uniformly. One may put tau equal to a directional regeneration horizon and B equal to a positive-probability no-backtracking event; neither is incorrectly treated as an ordinary stopping-time law. Proving finite conditional mean of the exit count K_tau is the single remaining moment problem for this route. Directional transience only gives its almost-sure finiteness. The equivalence does not yet establish that mean, or prove ballisticity. With S_i a singleton the criterion is tautological; balls with radius at least two separate residence from returns but do not make their exit skeleton iid.

[Definition Merger of arXiv:2505.16585, 'Expanded regimes of area law for lattice Yang--Mills theories'] Let $\ell_i, \ell_j$ be loops of $s$ which both contain some lattice edge $e$. Thus, $\ell_i = a \mbf{e} b$ and $\ell_j = c \mbf{e}' d$, where $\mbf{e}, \mbf{e}'$ are the same lattice edge. Define $\ell_i \oplus_{\mbf{e}, \mbf{e}'} \ell_j := a \mbf{e}' d c \mbf{e} b$. The \textit{positive merger} of $s$ at $(\mbf{e}, \mbf{e}')$ is defined to be the string $s' := ([\ell_i \oplus_{\mbf{e}, \mbf{e}'} \ell_j], \ell_1, \ldots, \hat{\ell}_i, \ldots, \hat{\ell}_j, \ldots, \ell_n)$, where here $\hat{\ell}$ denotes omission.

Similarly, if $\ell_i = a \mbf{e} b$, $\ell_j = c \mbf{e}' d$ where $\mbf{e}, (\mbf{e}')^{-1}$ are the same lattice edge, then define $\ell_i \ominus_{\mbf{e}, \mbf{e}'} \ell_j := adcb$. The \textit{negative merger} of $s$ at $(\mbf{e}, \mbf{e}')$ is defined to be the string $s' := ([\ell_i \oplus_{\mbf{e}, \mbf{e}'} \ell_j], \ell_1, \ldots, \hat{\ell}_i, \ldots, \hat{\ell}_j, \ldots, \ell_n)$.

Given an edge $\mbf{e}$ of $s$, we let $\mbb{M}_{+}(s, \mbf{e})/\mbb{M}_-(s, \mbf{e})$ be the sets of all positive/negative mergers of $s$ at $(\mbf{e}, \mbf{e}')$ for some other edge $\mbf{e}'$. We will frequently use the notation $\mbb{M}_{\pm}(s, \mbf{e})$ to denote the set of positive or negative mergers of $s$ at $\mbf{e}$.
title: Merger

endowed with the norm
\[
\|u\|_V^2 := \|u'\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)}^2 + \|u\|_{\mathbb{H}}^2.

condition that is, there exist some positive constants $\alpha>0$ and

\alpha \|u\|_V^2,

[Theorem 22 (existence for the auxiliary system) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $n\ge2$, $\frac{n+1}2<s\le\frac n2+1$, $\breg\in(\frac12,1)$, $\varepsilon=1-\breg$,
let $\Binf\in\Rn\setminus\{0\}$ be fixed, and let
$v_0\in H^{s}(\Rn)$ be divergence-free, of arbitrary size, and with no relation to
$\Binf$. Put
$R:=2C_{\rm lin}\|v_0\|_{H^{s}}$ and let $\delta$ be as
fixed above. There is $T_*>0$, depending on $n,s,\breg,v_{\rm A}$, on
$\|v_0\|_{H^{s}}$ and on the modulus $\omega_{v_0}$, such that $\mathcal M$ carries $\mathcal U_{R,\delta}$
into itself and has a unique fixed point $\Ufield$ in it.  The potential reconstructed from this
fixed point solves \eqref{eq:auxiliary-system} on $[0,T_*]$ and satisfies
$\Ufield=dw$ on $[0,T_*]\times\Rn$. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 dw\in C\big([0,T_*],Y^{s-1,1}\big)\cap C^1\big([0,T_*],H^{s-1}\big),
 \qquad
 E_i\partial_tX^j\in C\big([0,T_*],H^{s-1}\big).
\end{equation}
If $\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}<\infty$ for some
$\rpar\in(0,1]$, then $T_*$ may be chosen to satisfy
\eqref{eq:Tstar}, \eqref{eq:Tstar-R2} and
\eqref{eq:Tstar-enhanced}; in particular, it depends only on the listed
parameters and on
$\|v_0\|_{H^s}+\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}$.  For this choice,
\begin{equation}
 \|\Ufield\|_{H^{s-1,1+\rpar}_{\breg}}
 \le 2C_{\rm lin}\|\nabla v_0\|_{Y^{s-1,\rpar}}.
\end{equation}
This is additional Lagrangian spacetime regularity of the differentiated
displacement; no Eulerian anisotropic norm is asserted.

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2608.03922, 'Absolute continuity of two-dimensional polynomial random vectors'] Let $M>0$ and let $d,n\in\mathbb N$. Let
$\mu=\mu_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mu_n$,
where each $\mu_j$ is a probability measure with density $\varrho_j$ satisfying
\[
0\le \varrho_j(x_j)\le M
\quad \forall x_j\in\mathbb R,
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
\]
Then, for every nonconstant $f\in \mathcal{P}_d(\mathbb{R}^n)$
and for every Borel set $A\subset\mathbb R$, one has
\[
[f]_\infty^{1/d}\mu(f\in A)
\le
2d^2(1+M)\bigl(\lambda_1(A)\bigr)^{1/d}.
\]

body:
[Prop 13 of arXiv:2607.13849, 'Rearranged Stochastic Heat Equation with an Entropy Gradient Structure'] For $\delta >0$, let $(X_t, W_t,\zeta_t,{\mathscr J}_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ be a weak limit in $\mathbb{D}([0,T], \mathcal{H}^{-1}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})\times L^2_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})
\times 
{\mathcal H}^{-2}_{\rm Sym}(\mathbb{S})
    \times 
    \mathcal{H}^{-(3+\delta)}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})
    )$ of the family $\{(X_t^{(h)},W_t,\zeta_t^{(h)},{\mathscr J}_t(X^{(h)})_{0 \le t \le T}\}_{{h \in T/{\mathbb N}^*}}$ when $h\searrow 0$. Assume (without any loss of generality) that it is constructed on the same probability space $(\Omega,\mathfrak{F},\mathbb{P})$ as the approximation scheme. Then: 
    \begin{itemize}
    \item[1.] With probability 1, $(X_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ is in $\mathcal{C}([0,T], \mathcal{H}^{-1}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S}))
    \cap L^\infty([0,T], 
    \mathcal{U}^2(\mathbb{S}))
    \cap L^2([0,T],\mathcal{H}^{1}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S}))$. It satisfies  
\begin{equation}
    
\mathbb{E}\bigl[\|X_{t}\|_2^2\bigr] + 
2\int_0^{t} \mathbb{E} \bigl[\|D_{\mathbf{x}}X_{r}\|_2^2\bigr] \mathrm{d}r \leq \mathbb{E}\bigl[\|X_0\|_2^2\bigr] +t  + c_{\lambda}t, \quad t \in [0,T]. 
\end{equation}
Moreover,
    $$\mathbb{E}
    \left[ \sup_{t \in [0,T]}
    \| X_t \|_2^2 + 
    \int_0^T \|D_{\mathbf{x}}X_t\|_2^2\mathrm{d}t 
    \right] \leq C(1+\mathbb{E}\|X_0\|_2^2),$$ for a constant $C$ independent of $X_0$.  
    \item[2.] The process $(W_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ is an $L^2_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})\text{-valued}$ $Q\text{-Brownian}$ motion.
    \item[3.] With probability 1, $(\zeta_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ takes values in $\mathcal{C}([0,T], \mathcal{H}^{-2}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S}))$.
Moreover, if $\varphi \in \mathcal{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})$ is non-decreasing, then, almost-surely, the path $(\langle \zeta_t,\varphi\rangle)_{0 \le t \le T}$ is non-decreasing on $[0,T]$.
    \item[4.] With probability 1,  for any $\varphi \in \mathcal{H}^{2}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S})$, for all $0\leq s\leq t\leq T$,
    \begin{align*}
 \langle X_t -X_s,\phi \rangle = \langle \zeta_t-\zeta_s,\phi\rangle  + \int_{s}^{t} \langle X_r,\Delta_{\mathbf{x}} \phi \rangle \mathrm{d}r + \langle W_{t}-W_{s},\phi \rangle.
\end{align*}
\item[5.] With probability 1, 
$({\mathscr J}_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ is in 
$\mathcal{C}([0,T],\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{Sym}}^{-(3+\delta)}(\mathbb{S}))$. Moreover, if $\varphi \in \mathcal{H}^{3+\delta}_{\mathrm{Sym}}(\mathbb{S}) \cap {\mathcal U}^2({\mathbb S})$, then, almost-surely, the paths $(\langle {\mathscr J}_t,\varphi\rangle)_{0 \le t \le T}$
and $(\langle 
\eta_t ,\varphi \rangle := \langle \zeta_t - {\mathscr J}_t, \varphi \rangle)_{0 \le t \le T}$
are non-decreasing on $[0,T]$, and 
\begin{equation*} 
\forall s,t \in [0,T] \ {\rm with} \ s <t, \quad 
\max \left( \langle {\mathscr J}_t - {\mathscr J}_s,\varphi \rangle, 
\langle \eta_t - \eta_s,\varphi \rangle \right) \leq 
\| \zeta_t - \zeta_s \|_{2,-2}
\| \varphi \|_2.
\end{equation*}
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 13 of arXiv:2607.13849

[Theorem Théorème Fixation RMS of arXiv:2504.03627, 'Richardson’s model and the contact process with stirring: long time behavior.'] Let $\lambda>0$ and $(\xi_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be $\mathrm{RMS}(\lambda,1)$ starting from a non-empty initial configuration.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item All sites fix on the infected state or all sites fix on the healthy state.
    \item Suppose that $d\in \{1,2\}$. Then all sites fix on the infected state.
    \item Suppose that $d\ge 3$ and $\lambda>2d\lambda_c(d)$. Then all sites fix on the infected state.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Théorème Fixation RMS of arXiv:2504.03627

[Theorem 83 (Reconstruction-lattice tensor--Pfaffian transfer) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] Let $E$ be a separable real Hilbert space, fix $2\le\sigma<\infty$ and
$\rho>0$, and let $A\in\Sch_2(E)$ be a strongly measurable random
skew-adjoint operator.

\emph{(a) Decoupled branch.}  For every $N\ge1$, let
$I_N^{\rm dec}$ be a countable two-sided block system and let
$\mathsf E_N^{\rm dec}(I_N^{\rm dec})$ be an order-continuous
$\sigma$-reconstruction lattice with reconstruction constant
$C_N^{\rm dec}$.  Let $(K_{2N;i})_{i\in I_N^{\rm dec}}$ be order-$2N$
block coefficients with input $\C$ and output $\wedge^{2N}E$, and put
\[
 b_{2N;i}^{\rm dec}:=\Prof_{2N,\sigma}(K_{2N;i}),
 \qquad
 R_{2N}^{\rm dec}:=C_N^{\rm dec}
 \big\|(b_{2N;i}^{\rm dec})_{i\in I_N^{\rm dec}}\big\|_{\mathsf E_N^{\rm dec}}.
\]
Assume $(b_{2N;i}^{\rm dec})_i\in\mathsf E_N^{\rm dec}$, let
$\mathbf K_{2N}:=\sum_iK_{2N;i}\in\mathfrak T_{2N,\sigma}$ be the
reconstructed coefficient, realize all decoupled evaluations on one common
product Gaussian space, and set
$\Xi_{2N}:=\cT_{\mathbf K_{2N}}^{(2N)}$.  Suppose that, on one event of
probability one,
\begin{equation}

 (\alpha_A)^{\wedge N}=\frac{N!}{2^N}\Xi_{2N}
 \qquad(N\ge1).
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}

 \mathcal L_{\rho,\sigma}^{\rm dec}
 :=\sup_{N\ge1}N^{1/\rho}(R_{2N}^{\rm dec})^{1/N}<\infty,
\end{equation}
then, for every finite $p\ge1$,
\begin{equation}

 \bigl\|\|A\|_{\Sch_{\rho,\infty}}\bigr\|_{L^p}
 \le C_\rho(1+p+\sigma)\mathcal L_{\rho,\sigma}^{\rm dec}.
\end{equation}

\emph{(b) Same-field branch.}  For every $N\ge1$, let
$I_N^{\rm W}$ be a countable two-sided block system and let
$\mathsf E_N^{\rm W}(I_N^{\rm W})$ be an order-continuous
$\sigma$-reconstruction lattice with reconstruction constant
$C_N^{\rm W}$.  Let $(L_{2N;i})_{i\in I_N^{\rm W}}$ be symmetric block
kernels, all evaluated by one real isonormal Gaussian process, and put
\[
 b_{2N;i}^{\rm W}
 :=\Prof_{2N,\sigma}(\Dec_{2N}L_{2N;i}),
 \qquad
 R_{2N}^{\rm W}:=C_N^{\rm W}
 \big\|(b_{2N;i}^{\rm W})_{i\in I_N^{\rm W}}\big\|_{\mathsf E_N^{\rm W}}.
\]
Assume $(b_{2N;i}^{\rm W})_i\in\mathsf E_N^{\rm W}$, let
$\mathbf L_{2N}:=\sum_iL_{2N;i}\in\mathfrak W_{2N,\sigma}$ be the
reconstructed same-field coefficient, and set
$\Xi_{2N}:=I_{2N}(\mathbf L_{2N})$.  Retain
\eqref{eq:reconstruction-lattice-pfaffian-compatibility}.  If
\begin{equation}

 \mathcal L_{\rho,\sigma}^{\rm W}
 :=\sup_{N\ge1}N^{1+1/\rho}(R_{2N}^{\rm W})^{1/N}<\infty,
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}

 \bigl\|\|A\|_{\Sch_{\rho,\infty}}\bigr\|_{L^p}
 \le C_\rho(1+p+\sigma)\mathcal L_{\rho,\sigma}^{\rm W},
 \qquad 1\le p<\infty.
\end{equation}
Both estimates are dimension free.
title: Reconstruction-lattice tensor--Pfaffian transfer

[Theorem thm:main-joint-clt of arXiv:2507.12502, 'Quantitative Edge Eigenvector Universality for Random Regular Graphs: Berry-Esseen Bounds '] Let $G$ be as in Theorem (thm:main-berry-esseen of the paper). For any $K = K(N)$ satisfying $K \leq N^{1/10-\delta}$ for some fixed $\delta > 0$, and any collection of deterministic unit vectors $\mathbf{q}^{(1)}, \ldots, \mathbf{q}^{(m)} \in \mathbb{R}^N$ orthogonal to $\mathbf{e}$, the random vector
\[
\mathbf{Z}_N := \left(\sqrt{N}\langle \mathbf{q}^{(\alpha)}, \mathbf{u}_i \rangle : 1 \leq \alpha \leq m, 2 \leq i \leq K+1\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{mK}
\]
converges in distribution to $\mathbf{Z} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_{mK})$ as $N \to \infty$.

Moreover, the rate of convergence in the multivariate Berry--Esseen theorem is
\[
\sup_{A \in \mathcal{C}} \left|\mathbb{P}(\mathbf{Z}_N \in A) - \mathbb{P}(\mathbf{Z} \in A)\right| \leq C_{d,m} K^{3/2} N^{-1/6+\varepsilon}
\]
where $\mathcal{C}$ denotes the class of convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{mK}$ and $C_{d,m}$ depends only on $d$ and $m$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Joint Central Limit Theorem

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); no independent PASS or established priority. Let m>=2, w>=2 be fixed finite integers. Let M in R^(m-by-2) have rank two, and Sigma be real symmetric positive definite of size two. Assume the positive singular values of M Sigma satisfy s1>s2>0. Fix ONE pair of independent iid standard Gaussian matrices B0 in R^(m-by-w), A0 in R^(w-by-2), then for alpha tending to zero solve the Euclidean factor gradient flow
 B'=-(BA-M)Sigma A^T, A'=-B^T(BA-M)Sigma
from (alpha B0,alpha A0). For almost every fixed seed, there exist a balanced nonzero-product rank-one critical factor zstar=(bstar;astar), physical times T_alpha>=0, p_alpha>0 tending to zero, and fixed-in-time hidden orthogonal rotations R_alpha such that on every fixed compact interval in t,
 (B_alpha;A_alpha^T)(T_alpha+log(1/p_alpha)/s+t) R_alpha -> Ustar(t).
Here s is the positive singular value of Gstar=(bstar astar^T-M)Sigma. The canonical limit has only two nonzero hidden columns and all its output columns in col(M). It is a complete nonconstant factor-flow connection from [zstar,0,...] at minus infinity to finite factors with product M at plus infinity.

At the chosen arrivals, in the first fixed seed rotation before the later dormant rotation, the active error is O(p_alpha^2), dormant norm is O(p_alpha), and projected dormant row norm is exactly p_alpha. Thus with Z_alpha=(B_alpha;A_alpha^T)(B_alpha;A_alpha^T)^T and Z1=zstar zstar^T,
 Z_alpha(T_alpha)->Z1,
 liminf vstar^T Z_alpha(T_alpha)vstar / ||Z_alpha(T_alpha)-Z1||_F>0.
Writing a_alpha=vstar^T Z_alpha(T_alpha)vstar gives a_alpha=p_alpha^2+O(p_alpha^4); the Gram clock log(1/a_alpha)/(2s) differs from log(1/p_alpha)/s by O(p_alpha^2).

The covariance need not be isotropic or commute with the target. Repeated positive origin singular values, rank-deficient M or covariance, input dimension larger than two, depth >=3, and independently resampling the seed with alpha are outside this statement. The endpoint of the first rank-one path need not minimize among rank-one products. No data-uniform quantitative convergence rate is asserted.

T232-w704-C018 v1. Kind: narrowed; Target 1. Status: proof (unaudited). This is a candidate whole-range m-by-2 extension, not an independently checked theorem, a priority finding, or a complete solution of T232. Rectangular dependencies C014-C017 require independent audit.

## Exact statement
Let m>=2, w>=2 be fixed finite integers. Let M in R^(m-by-2) have rank two, and Sigma be real symmetric positive definite of size two. Assume the positive singular values of M Sigma satisfy s1>s2>0. Fix ONE pair of independent iid standard Gaussian matrices B0 in R^(m-by-w), A0 in R^(w-by-2), then for alpha tending to zero solve the Euclidean factor gradient flow
 B'=-(BA-M)Sigma A^T, A'=-B^T(BA-M)Sigma
from (alpha B0,alpha A0). For almost every fixed seed, there exist a balanced nonzero-product rank-one critical factor zstar=(bstar;astar), physical times T_alpha>=0, p_alpha>0 tending to zero, and fixed-in-time hidden orthogonal rotations R_alpha such that on every fixed compact interval in t,
 (B_alpha;A_alpha^T)(T_alpha+log(1/p_alpha)/s+t) R_alpha -> Ustar(t).
Here s is the positive singular value of Gstar=(bstar astar^T-M)Sigma. The canonical limit has only two nonzero hidden columns and all its output columns in col(M). It is a complete nonconstant factor-flow connection from [zstar,0,...] at minus infinity to finite factors with product M at plus infinity.

At the chosen arrivals, in the first fixed seed rotation before the later dormant rotation, the active error is O(p_alpha^2), dormant norm is O(p_alpha), and projected dormant row norm is exactly p_alpha. Thus with Z_alpha=(B_alpha;A_alpha^T)(B_alpha;A_alpha^T)^T and Z1=zstar zstar^T,
 Z_alpha(T_alpha)->Z1,
 liminf vstar^T Z_alpha(T_alpha)vstar / ||Z_alpha(T_alpha)-Z1||_F>0.
Writing a_alpha=vstar^T Z_alpha(T_alpha)vstar gives a_alpha=p_alpha^2+O(p_alpha^4); the Gram clock log(1/a_alpha)/(2s) differs from log(1/p_alpha)/s by O(p_alpha^2).

The covariance need not be isotropic or commute with the target. Repeated positive origin singular values, rank-deficient M or covariance, input dimension larger than two, depth >=3, and independently resampling the seed with alpha are outside this statement. The endpoint of the first rank-one path need not minimize among rank-one products. No data-uniform quantitative convergence rate is asserted.

## 1. Actual Gaussian arrival and the nonzero-product endpoint
C014 proves fixed-compact canonical origin matching, including the extra m-2 zero eigenvalues, and exact output contraction. C017 proves the missing active O(epsilon) bound with epsilon=alpha^(1-s2/s1), using exact top cancellation rather than inferring a rate from qualitative convergence. Its reduced canonical pair, via any orthonormal basis Q of col(M), is exactly the square pair for Mtilde=Q^T M. The reduced target is invertible and Mtilde Sigma has the same positive singular values.

The balanced bounded analytic first path converges. Its nonconstant gradient orbit has a fixed strict energy margin below the zero product; hence its endpoint has nonzero product. This is stronger than merely a nonzero stationary factor, a distinction necessary in rectangular output space. C015 supplies the simple positive dormant residual rate s and strict active top gap r<s at that endpoint. C003 applies to the exactly reduced ideal variational pair and gives alignment of the ideal remnant with vstar. C017 then uses one fixed late entrance, before alpha tends to zero, to meet all of C016's uniform entrance hypotheses. C016 supplies the actual later arrival, strong Gram alignment and O(p_alpha^2) active endpoint error on its own growing local interval.

The Gaussian event is fixed at initialization: the two positive-origin eigenrows are independent standard Gaussian rows. Their Gram determinant is a nonzero polynomial, so the event that the top row vanishes or its projected second row vanishes is a proper algebraic null set for w>=2. There is no later-flow independence claim.

## 2. Full parameter Jacobian and exact top projection
Write the first hidden rotation as R0 and theta1=[zstar,0,...,0]. Since all dormant columns vanish at theta1, their first product variation is zero. The full parameter Jacobian is therefore block diagonal: one full active Jact and w-1 copies of Lstar. It is symmetric because the field is a Euclidean negative gradient. C015 gives top(Jact)=r<s, while Lstar has simple top s, one -s and m zeros. Consequently the FULL largest parameter eigenvalue is s with multiplicity w-1, and its entire eigenspace consists of vstar in the dormant columns.

At arrival, set p_alpha=||vstar^T X_alpha||. Choose a dormant orthogonal rotation D_alpha taking that full row to (p_alpha,0,...,0). Applying diag(1,D_alpha) leaves theta1 fixed. All factor errors remain O(p_alpha), with active error O(p_alpha^2), and the complete top spectral projection is EXACTLY p_alpha u for one fixed unit parameter vector u supported in the first dormant column. A right hidden rotation is a symmetry of the whole flow: B maps to B R and A to R^T A, so BA is unchanged. Thus each chosen R_alpha=R0 diag(1,D_alpha) is fixed for the subsequent flow, not a time-dependent change of coordinates.

## 3. Canonical escape and both invariant subspaces
Apply the general finite-dimensional C011 lemma to the polynomial field centered at theta1. Its hypotheses are a C2 field, symmetric Jacobian, positive top rate s of arbitrary multiplicity, a fixed FULL normalized top projection, and O(p_alpha) total error. All have just been verified. Its weighted Volterra limit after log(1/p_alpha)/s is unique in the class with leading term exp(st)u and remainder O(exp(2st)). Initially it exists on a negative half-line and then on its maximal forward interval. Global forward existence is not inferred from this local lemma.

Consider the linear affine-in-parameters subspace in which all hidden columns beyond the active and first dormant columns vanish, and all output columns belong to col(M). It contains theta1 and u. It is invariant under the exact nonlinear flow: zero hidden columns have zero derivative; if B=Q C and M=Q Mtilde, then B'=Q[-(CA-Mtilde)Sigma A^T], and A'=-C^T(CA-Mtilde)Sigma. Its restricted field is isometric to the square width-two factor field.

To justify confinement at the negative-infinite boundary, do NOT infer it merely from finite-time invariance. Construct the restricted canonical Volterra solution using C011 on that restricted finite-dimensional field. The same top direction u and local weighted bounds apply; the restricted top remains s, since it contains the single first dormant vstar and its active rates are below s. Embed this restricted solution into the full parameter space. Because the field and its derivative preserve the subspace, its semigroup and Volterra equation agree with the full ones on it. It is therefore a full weighted Volterra solution with the SAME leading term and remainder. Uniqueness in C011 forces equality with the full canonical limit. Forward ODE uniqueness preserves confinement for the rest of its maximal interval. This proves both output-space and two-hidden-column confinement rather than assuming them.

## 4. Apply the endpoint theorem only after reduction
Reduce the canonical pair by Q. Its active endpoint is (Q^T bstar,astar), and its residual top vector is the reduced vstar. Its backward expansion is exactly the square canonical expansion in C011:
 z(t)=zstar+O(exp(2st)), x(t)=exp(st)vstar+O(exp(2st)).
The output residual vector lies in range(Gstar), perpendicular to bstar, and the input one lies in range(Gstar^T), perpendicular to astar. Both are nonzero. The two square reduced factors consequently have nonzero determinant leading terms of order exp(st) and are invertible at a sufficiently negative but finite time.

Conserved balance has value zero at the backward endpoint, and hence is exactly zero on the canonical orbit. C011's square determinant identity gives the graph determinant sign det(Mtilde), NOT a nonexistent determinant of the rectangular M. The orbit is nonconstant. Strict gradient descent places its finite-time loss below the first critical loss, which itself is strictly below C(0), by the stationary nonzero-product energy identity.

Thus the reduced canonical factors meet every C010 hypothesis at one finite time: square width two, balance, invertibility, correct orientation relative to Mtilde, and loss below C(0). C010 requires only invertibility of Mtilde and SPD Sigma, not distinct singular values. It proves global boundedness and finite factor convergence with reduced product Mtilde. Re-embedding by Q gives finite rectangular factor limits with product Q Mtilde=M. This extends the canonical flow globally; C011 continuous-dependence convergence extends to every fixed compact because the canonical orbit is now known to exist there. No finite-alpha infinite-time endpoint is substituted for a canonical endpoint by interchanging limits.

## 5. Arrival Gram and clock
The full top residual vector is perpendicular to zstar. Hence at arrival
 a_alpha=(vstar^T z_alpha)^2+||vstar^T X_alpha||^2=p_alpha^2+O(p_alpha^4).
The O(p_alpha^2) active endpoint bound is used here, not merely the O(p_alpha) total error allowed by C011. Positivity gives a_alpha>=p_alpha^2. If a_alpha/p_alpha^2=1+d_alpha, then 0<=d_alpha<=C p_alpha^2 and
 -C p_alpha^2/(2s)<=log(1/a_alpha)/(2s)-log(1/p_alpha)/s<=0.
This follows from 0<=log(1+d)<=d. The clock difference tends to zero. Multiplication of factors is continuous on the fixed bounded canonical comparison intervals, so compact shifted Gram convergence follows as well. This algebraic clock estimate is not a quantitative nonlinear escape-error rate.

## Status and strongest unresolved checks
The proof depends on unaudited rectangular C014-C017 and the output/hidden-subspace Volterra composition in Section 3, which is a new use of the checked general C011 lemma. The square C012 PASS alone does not certify those steps. This entire C018 theorem requires independent review; no PASS, full T232 solution, or literature novelty is claimed. Primary literature priority remains unresolved. The hardest remaining verification is the exact full-space versus restricted canonical Volterra uniqueness handoff together with all rectangular entrance hypotheses at the same fixed time.

        \lim_{n\to \infty}\sup_{t\geq 0}\left| \mathbb P(\hat L_n\leq t|Y_1,\dots,Y_n)-\mathbb P(L\leq t)\right|= 0,$

(Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 119 of arXiv:2605.03236, 'Stochastic It\^o Equations and Parabolic Second-Order Equations with singular Drift'] Suppose that the   assumptions of
Theorem \ref{theorem 1.20.1} are satisfied
and
take $R\in(0,\infty)$. Suppose we are given
 $u_{0},u_{1},...\in D$ and $f\in L_{(q,p)}(C_{R})$ such that, for 
$f_{n}:=\cL u_{n} $, we have
$$
\sup_{n\geq1}\sup_{\partial'C_{R}}|u_{n}|<\infty,
\quad \|f_{n}-f\|_{L_{(q,p)}(C_{R})}+\|u_{n}-u_{0}\|_{L_{(q,p)}(C_{R})}
\to 0
$$
as $n\to\infty$. Then $\cL u_{0} =f$ in $C_{R}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 119 of arXiv:2605.03236

body:
[Prop model-categorical-model of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] In the situation of the previous construction, assume in addition that all model structures are right proper and admit functorial factorizations. Then the map ${N_\textup{top}}(\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y})\to{\mathcal{C}}_{/Y}$ is degreewise a localization at the given weak equivalences. Moreover, if we write $\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}^\circ\subset\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}$ for the full subcategory given in degree $A\in\textbf{\textup{T}}$ by those $X\to Y$ such that $X$ defines a terminal object in the localization of $\textbf{\textup{C}}(A)$, then also the induced map ${N_\textup{top}}(\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}^\circ)\to{\mathcal{C}}_{/Y}^\circ$ is a localization (at the same weak equivalences).
    \begin{proof}
        We will only prove the second statement, the proof of the first one being analogous. By Lemma~(lemma:fgt-simpl-structure of the paper), the canonical map $N\big((\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}^\circ)(A)_0\big)\to N_{\textup{top}}\big((\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}^\circ)(A)\big)$ from the nerve of the underlying unenriched category induces an equivalence on localizations, so it will suffice to show that the canonical map $\smash{N(\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}^\circ(A)_0)\to{\mathcal{C}}_{/Y}^\circ(A)}$ is a localization. For $N(\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}(A)_0)\to{\mathcal{C}}_{/Y}(A)$ this is an instance of Lemma~(lemma:slice-over-fibrant of the paper); [g-global]*{Proposition~A.1.15} then shows that the induced map from the localization of $(\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}^\circ(A)_0)$ to ${\mathcal{C}}_{/Y}(A)$ is fully faithful, and so it only remains to show that every object of ${\mathcal{C}}_{/Y}^\circ(A)$ is contained in its essential image. Indeed, any object is equivalent to the image of some $(X\to Y)\in\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}(A)$, and since $\textbf{\textup{C}}_{/Y}(A)\to{\mathcal{C}}_{/Y}(A)$ lives over the localization $\textbf{\textup{C}}(A)\to{\mathcal{C}}(A)$, $X$ is weakly contractible.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop model-categorical-model of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
[Lem 15 of arXiv:2512.05687, '$L^p$-Boltzmann-Gibbs principle \\ via Littlewood-Paley-Stein inequality'] (Iteration lemma,
cf.\ Lemma 5.5 of \cite{BFS})
Let $p\ge 4$ and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function on
$\mathcal{X}_N$ for some $p'>p$ depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}$ 
such that $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ and $\tilde f'(u_0)=0$.
Then, there exists a constant $C=C(u_0, \ell_0)>0$ such that, for $\ell \geq \ell_0$, 
and a function $h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x) \\
& \hskip 20mm \times \Big\{ E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)] 
-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x \eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(2\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag  \\
&\hskip 10mm \leq \ CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^{p/2} \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
On the other hand, when only $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x)\\
&\hskip 20mm  \times \Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]
-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(2\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag \\
&\hskip 10mm  \leq \ CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^p \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
title: Lem 15 of arXiv:2512.05687

body:
[Prop p:holder of arXiv:2411.10586, 'A convergence framework for Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble\\ via pole evolution'] For any $B>0$, there exist large and small $C,c>0$ such that the following holds.
Take any particle-generated $\{Y_t\}_{t\in{\mathbb R}}$ satisfying (a:SDE of the paper), and that its poles are given by a line ensemble $\{x_i(t)\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}, t\in{\mathbb R}}$, and that $Y_0(w)=\sum_{i=1}^\infty\frac{1}{x_i(0)-w}-\frac{1}{{\mathfrak a}_i}-\frac{\Ai'(0)}{\Ai(0)}$ for any $w\in\mathbb{H}$.
Take $k\in\mathbb{N}$ large enough and any $0<\xi<ck^{-4/3}$.
Then conditional on the event that
\begin{equation}  
|x_i(0)-{\mathfrak a}_i| \le B, \quad \forall i \in \llbracket k/2, 2k\rrbracket,
\end{equation}
with probability at least $1-e^{-ck^{1/6}}$ we have
    \[ \max_{0\leq s\leq \xi} |x_k(s)-x_k(0)|\leq C k^{2/3}\xi^{1/2}.\]

[Lemma 27 of arXiv:2608.26693, '2608.26693'] Fix $p$ and $\Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^p$.  If $X,Y,K_0,K_1$ range over operator-norm-bounded subsets of the symmetric matrices, then, uniformly as $\varepsilon\to0$,
\begin{align}
d_B^2(\Sigma+\varepsilon X,\Sigma+\varepsilon Y)
&=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}\ip{X-Y}{\mathcal L_\Sigma^{-1}(X-Y)}+O(\varepsilon^3),\\
\KL\!\left(\N(0,\Sigma+\varepsilon X)\mid\N(0,\Sigma+\varepsilon K_i)\right)
&=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4}\tr[\Sigma^{-1}(X-K_i)\Sigma^{-1}(X-K_i)]+O(\varepsilon^3).
\end{align}
The second-order covariance action is the minimum of the quadratic model obtained from \eqref{eq:bures-local}--\eqref{eq:kl-local}.

body:
[Defn def.Lp-stabilizing_marking of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $\xi$ be a marking function and, depending on whether $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ is a finite or infinite marked point process, $\xi$ is defined on either finite or infinite point sets, i.e., $\xi: \mathbb{R}^d \times\mathbb{K}\times \hat{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \longrightarrow \mathbb{K}'$ or $\xi: \mathbb{R}^d \times\mathbb{K}\times\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}} \longrightarrow \mathbb{K}'$.
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item 
We say that  $\xi$ is a {\em bounded Lipschitz-localizing marking function ({\em \textnormal{BL}-localizing} for short)} on the point process $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ if 
there 
is an increasing-decreasing family of 
functions~$\varphi_p: [0, \infty) \to [0,1], p \in \mathbb{N},$ such that 
\begin{align} 
 \sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_p \in \mathbb{R}^d} 
 d_{\textnormal{BL}, \bk x1p}( \bk\xi1p(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}),\bk{\xi^{(r)}}1p( \tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}))  \leq 2\varphi_p(r), \ r  \geq 0, 
\end{align}
where the extra notation $\bk x1p$ in $d_{\textnormal{BL}, \bk x1p}$ accounts for the distribution of the vector of scores  $\bk {\xi}1p(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})$ and $ \bk{\xi^{(r)}}1p( \tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}))$ under the Palm distribution $\mathbb{P}_{\bk x1p}$ of $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$. 

\item  We say that   $\xi$  is {\em  \textnormal{BL}-localizing  on the finite  windows}
  of $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$ if there is an increasing-decreasing family of functions  $\varphi_p: [0, \infty) \to [0,1], p \in \mathbb{N}$,
  such that
\begin{align} 
  \sup_{1 \leq n < \infty} \sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_p \in W_n} d_{\textnormal{BL}, \bk x1p}\big( \bk{\xi}1p(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_n),\bk{\xi^{(r)}}1p( \tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_n)) \big)  \leq 2\varphi_p(r), \ r  \geq 0.
\end{align}

\item  We say that $\xi$ is {\em fast \textnormal{BL}-localizing} on $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$, or on the finite windows of $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}$, if $(\varphi_p)_{p \in \mathbb{N}}$ are  fast decreasing. 

\item  Exponential \textnormal{BL}-localization signifies that  $\varphi_p$ is exponentially decreasing to zero  for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$.   
\end{enumerate}

 As elsewhere, in~(equation Lp-stab-infinite of the paper) and~(equation Lp-stab of the paper) we adopt the
convention that the supremum over $\bk{x}{1}{p}$ is understood as an
$\mathrm{ess\,sup}$ with respect to the factorial moment measures of the
common ground process~$\mathcal{P}$, which are tacitly assumed to have  the form $\rho^{(p)}(\bk x1p)\mathrm{d} \bk{x}{1}{p}$ with $\rho^{(p)}$ uniformly bounded by $\kappa_p$.
title: \BL-localization of marking functions

\[

\]
is immediate. Indeed, if \((\mathcal A_n)\) is an admissible sequence of partitions of \(T\), then its restriction to \(F\),
\[
\mathcal A_n|_F
:=
\{A\cap F:\ A\in\mathcal A_n,\ A\cap F\neq \varnothing\},
\]
is an admissible sequence of partitions of \(F\), and for every \(t\in F\),
\[
\operatorname{diam}\bigl((\mathcal A_n|_F)(t)\bigr)
\le
\operatorname{diam}\bigl(\mathcal A_n(t)\bigr).

[Dfn 118 (occupation measures, continuous-time) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\vY^\frozen$ be the subsequential limit from Theorem~\ref{t:tightness}. Similarly to Definitions~\ref{ss:sde.abstract}
and \ref{d:discrete.occ},
let $\rho_{\vY}$ be the occupation measure for $\vY^\frozen=(\vY^{\frozen,\RomI:\RomIII},Y^{\frozen,\Ising})$. We also let
$\rho_D$, $\rho_V$, $\rho_U$, $\rho_\rrr$, $\rho_\www$
be the occupation measures for
$D^{\frozen,\RomI}$, $Q^{\frozen,\RomII}$, $Q^{\frozen,\RomII,\RomIII}$, $Q^{\frozen,\RomIII}$, and $Q^{\frozen,\Ising}$ respectively: for instance, $\rho_D$ is the signed measure such that
	\[\int_{\R^5}
	f(t,\vy)\rho_D(dt\,d\vy)
	= \bE\int_0^1
	f(t,\vY^\frozen,(t))
	\,dD^\frozen(t)\]
for any bounded continuous function $f$ on $\R^5$. Note it 
follows from Theorem~\ref{t:tightness} that $D^\frozen$, $Q^{\frozen,\RomII}$, $Q^{\frozen,\RomII,\RomIII}$, $Q^{\frozen,\RomIII}$, and $Q^{\frozen,\Ising}$ are finite-variation processes, so the integrals with respect to these processes are well-defined. Denote the conditional measures $\rho_t\equiv \rho_{\vY,t}$, $\rho_{D,t}$, etc. Note that since $(Y^{\frozen,\RomI},Y^{\frozen,\RomII},Y^{\frozen,\RomIII})$ evolves independently of $Y^{\frozen,\Ising}$,
we can factorize
 $\rho_t=\varrho_t\otimes\varsigma_t$,
 $\rho_{D,t}=\varrho_{D,t}\otimes\varsigma_t$, and so on.
title: occupation measures, continuous-time

[Theorem thm:pole-calibration of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Let $x_0=0$, let $b_a$ be defined by (equation eq:pole-reference-drift of the paper), and suppose
(equation eq:pole-coefficient-class of the paper) holds.  There exists
$K_{\mathrm{th}}=K_{\mathrm{th}}(T,\lambda,\Lambda)\geq1$ such that the following
holds.  For each $0<\theta<1$, define the threshold
\begin{equation}
 K_\theta^\star(a):=K_{\mathrm{th}}\theta^{-1}\mathcal M_d(a).
 
\end{equation}
Choose any $K\geq K_\theta^\star(a)$.  Set
$\omega_K(t):=e^{-K(T-t)/2}$ and, for
$\alpha\geq0$, write
$\overline w_{\alpha,K}(t):=t^\alpha\omega_K(t)$.  For
$\kappa\geq0$, set
$w_{\alpha,K;\kappa}:=(\overline w_{\alpha,K})_\kappa$ according to
Definition~(def:regular-time-weight of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The reference pair $(b_a,a)$ satisfies
Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) and~(ass:bochner-regularity of the paper).
Its time-$t$ diffusion law is $\mu_t=\gamma_t=N(0,tI_d)$, with current
velocity $c(t,y)=y/(2t)$.
\item If $\alpha\geq1/2$, then
\begin{equation}
 C_{\overline w_{\alpha,K}}(X^a)\leq2/\sqrt{1-\theta}.
 
\end{equation}
\item If $0\leq\alpha<1/2$ and
$0<\theta<1-4/(C_\alpha^{\mathrm{Br}})^2$,
put
\begin{equation*}
 \Delta_{\mathrm{hi}}
 :=1-\theta-\frac4{(C_\alpha^{\mathrm{Br}})^2}>0.
\end{equation*}
There are constants with the following dependencies:
\begin{equation*}
 C=C\bigl(T,\lambda,\Lambda,\alpha,\theta,\Delta_{\mathrm{hi}}^{-1}\bigr)>0,
 \qquad
 \kappa_0=\kappa_0\bigl(
   T,\lambda,\Lambda,\alpha,\theta,\Delta_{\mathrm{hi}}^{-1},\mathcal M_d(a)
 \bigr)\geq1
\end{equation*}
For every $\kappa\geq\kappa_0$, these constants give
\begin{equation}
 C_{w_{\alpha,K;\kappa}}(X^a)
 \leq C_\alpha^{\mathrm{Br}}
 +C\mathcal M_d(a)
  \left(\frac{\log(2+\kappa)}{\kappa}\right)^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}
The same $C$ and $\kappa_0$ apply to every $K\geq K_\theta^\star(a)$ in
(equation eq:pole-weight-threshold of the paper).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:pole-calibration of arXiv:2608.16119

[Lemma lem_convergence of arXiv:2608.09105, 'Longest convex chains with i.i.d.\ points'] For any $f\in\mathcal{F}$ and any sequence $(f_n)_{n\geqslant1}$ in $\mathcal{F}$, the following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]

\item 
$d(f_n,f)\to0$ as $n\to\infty$.

\item 
$f_n(x)\to f(x)$ as $n\to\infty$, for every $x\in[0,1)$.

\item 
$\partial^+f_n(t)\to f'(t)$ as $n\to\infty$, for every differentiability point $t\in(0,1)$ of $f$.

\end{enumerate}

[Definition 14 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] We define the following two bornologies:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For a family of bornological spaces $\{(S_\lambda, \mathcal{B}_\lambda)\}_{\lambda\in \Lambda}$, the set-theoretical direct product $\Pi_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\mathcal{B}_\lambda$ forms a bornological base on $\Pi_{\lambda\in \Lambda} S_\lambda$.
        We call $\langle \Pi_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\mathcal{B}_\lambda\rangle$ the \emph{direct product bornology} on $\Pi_{\lambda\in \Lambda} S_\lambda$.
        \item Let $P$ be a set and $f$ a map from $P$ to the bornological space $S$.
        Then the family $f^*\mathcal{B}_S:=\{f^{-1}(B)\subset P\mid B\in \mathcal{B}_S\}$ forms a bornological base on $P$.
        We call $\langle f^*\mathcal{B}_S \rangle $ the \emph{inverse image bornology} of $\mathcal{B}_S$ by the map $f$. 
        In particular, if $P$ is a subset of $S$ and the map $f$ is the inclusion map, the bornology $f^*\mathcal{B}_S =\langle f^*\mathcal{B}_S \rangle $ is called the \emph{subbornology} of $\mathcal{B}_S$.
    \end{enumerate}

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited). Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K be integers. There are d pairs of contexts, one arbitrary A and one systematic S per pair, and N-2d known S contexts. S has all K candidates true; each A has an independent uniform r-subset. The target p chooses contexts uniformly and then truths uniformly. The orientation class has VC dimension d. Observe n iid factual context/candidate samples WITHOUT partition tags. Independently conditional on the world, a perfect verifier supplies a uniform r-subset T_x of truths in EVERY variable context, including S, without orientation labels. This reveals every A truth. Set kappa=1-r/K. A pair is resolved exactly if a training sample lies outside either T_x. If U pairs remain unresolved, exactly 2^U worlds are compatible, though their actual posterior probabilities need not be equal. For arbitrary generator g, source Mis_infinity is TV(g,p_Pi), with p uniformly coarsened within exact g-probability level sets. Require Mis_infinity<=c in EVERY compatible world. The exact conditional worst-world false-mass frontier is V(c,U)=(kappa*U/N-c)_+/2 for 0<=c<=1. A uniform COMPATIBLE-WORLD average is an artificial lower-bound device, not an assertion about the actual posterior. An invariant-group generator attains V in every world. At c=0 every robustly feasible g has false mass at least kappa*U/(2N) in EACH actual compatible world, by a separate finite-cell inequality. Therefore the exact GLOBAL minimax expected false mass at zero budget is kappa*d/(2N)*(1-kappa/N)^n. The joint occupancy PGF is sum_{j=0}^d binom(d,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-j*kappa/N)^n, without independence of missing-pair indicators. For c>0 only E[(kappa*U/(2N)-c)_+] <= global value <= E[(kappa*U/N-c)_+]/2 is claimed. Expected conditional worst-world value need not equal global minimax expectation. The zero-budget value is kappa/2 times the error of the specified fair completion of support-consistent ERM, not a claim about optimal statistical classification error. This is full verification with extra S certificates, robust calibration, and an explicit paired VC family; it is not the general partial-verifier or actual-world-only calibration problem. Independent audit and priority review pending.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:ce641672c77772014d04c0f0fc8229c909dd1c1453222974535345804389f4b3","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/ce/ce641672c77772014d04c0f0fc8229c909dd1c1453222974535345804389f4b3.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:53d58ec2cda38bfc21fe0da89da7bb92798ef336c1b995aec1105ac63f2c6488","bundle_entry_key":"untagged-full-verifier-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-untagged-full-verifier-frontier-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; verified truth supports","draft":"w709/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:untagged-full-support-verifier-frontier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Full truth supports without orientation labels: untagged all-sample frontier

Candidate T379-C013 v2, proof (unaudited). Exact rational checks PASS;
independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending.
Target 2, with target-1 interaction. This treats ell=r, not arbitrary
partial verification. The hardest open extension is the unresolved
untagged posterior with ell<r and arbitrary positive calibration budgets.

## Experiment and compatible worlds

Integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2 and 1<=r<K. There are d pairs with
exactly one A and one S context; other contexts are known S. Each S has
all K truths; each A has an independent uniform r-subset of truths. The
factual law is uniform on contexts then uniformly true within context.
Observe n iid factual samples with NO A/S tags. Independently after
training a perfect verifier supplies an r-subset T_x of true candidates
in EVERY variable context, uniformly among r-subsets of truths, without
orientation tags. Thus it reveals ALL truths in A, and r truths in S.
The verified fraction of arbitrary truths is one; the additional S
truths are explicitly part of this information protocol.

A context containing an observed candidate outside T_x must be S.
An A context can never do so. If neither sibling in a pair has such an
observation, both orientations are compatible, even if observations
inside T_x make their LIKELIHOODS unequal. Let U count these unresolved
pairs. Resolved pairs have known S and A supports; in an unresolved
pair the A support would be exactly T_x under either orientation.
Consequently the compatible world set has exactly 2^U orientations,
and no other unknown support variables.

Put kappa=1-r/K, lambda=1/(NK) and p0=kappa/N. The proposed exact
conditional WORST-WORLD robust Mis_infinity frontier over all g is

 V(c,U)=(kappa*U/N-c)_+/2,         0<=c<=1.                (1)

Here feasibility requires source miscalibration <=c for EVERY compatible
world; output bins are the exact g-probability levels. The actual
posterior-average game is not asserted to have this value: its
orientation weights can be unequal after untagged factual observations.

At ZERO calibration budget a stronger pointwise conclusion holds:

 H_theta(g)>=kappa*U/(2N) for EVERY compatible theta,       (2)

for every robustly zero-calibrated g. An attainer has equality in every
world. Therefore the GLOBAL minimax expected value at zero budget is

 inf_A sup_world E[H(A(data,T))]
       =kappa*d/(2N)*(1-kappa/N)^n.                       (3)

This global value does not follow just by averaging a conditional
worst-world lower bound; the separate pointwise argument below is needed.

## Conditional frontier with an artificial uniform compatible prior

For a conditional worst-world lower bound, average the compatible
orientations UNIFORMLY. This is an admissible proof device even though
it is generally NOT the Bayesian posterior given the actual samples.
Let mu be the mean factual law under this artificial distribution. There
are three atom types:

 F: known false atoms of resolved A contexts, mu=0;
 M: atoms outside T_x in unresolved pairs, mu=lambda/2;
 S: all atoms safe in every compatible world, mu>=lambda.

In M the uniform-compatible-prior false risk is 1/2; in F it is one;
in S it is zero. The mu mass of M is kappa*U/N. In any uniform
coarsening Pi, mu_Pi(F union M)>=mu(F union M), since inside densities
are <=lambda/2 and outside safe densities are >=lambda. Linearity and
TV convexity show TV(mu_Pi,g)<=c for every robustly feasible g, using
its fixed bins Pi(g). Hence

 max_theta H_theta(g)>=average_theta H_theta(g)
    =g(F)+g(M)/2 >= (kappa*U/N-c)_+/2.

For attainment, begin from mu, remove min(c,kappa*U/N) uniformly from
M and add it uniformly to the fixed S reservoir. Keep F at zero.
Within each unresolved pair, both siblings' certified atoms have equal
g, and both siblings' outside atoms have equal g; their pairwise p
masses are invariant across orientations. Known safe/false groups have
invariant p masses too. Every exact score bin is a union of these
groups, so p_Pi=mu_Pi for every theta, including merged or zero scores.
Since g_Pi=g, Mis_infinity<=TV(mu,g)<=c. Every actual world has half
of M's candidate atoms false, giving H_theta=V(c,U) worldwise.
This proves (1), without substituting actual posterior weights.

## Pointwise zero-budget lower bound

Suppose g is robustly calibrated with budget zero, and fix ANY actual
compatible world theta. Then g=p_theta,Pi for all theta, with Pi the
exact score partition. Averaging worlds uniformly gives g=mu_Pi.

In a cell B, let c_B count M-atoms false in this actual theta, d_B
count M-atoms true there, f_B count globally false F-atoms, and t_B
count universally safe S-atoms. Put L=c_B+d_B+f_B+t_B>0. We have

 mu(B)>=lambda*((c_B+d_B)/2+t_B).

The false mass assigned by mu_Pi in this cell is therefore at least

 lambda*(c_B+d_B+2*t_B)*(c_B+f_B)/(2*L)
                  >=lambda*c_B/2,

because the numerator difference after multiplying by 2L/lambda is

 d_B*f_B+c_B*t_B+2*t_B*f_B >=0.

Sum cells. Exactly U*(K-r) M-atoms are false in each world. Thus
H_theta(g)>=lambda*U*(K-r)/2=kappa*U/(2N), proving (2).
This is an analytic finite-cell inequality, not a sample-based claim.
It allows arbitrary cells and known-false dilution atoms.

For positive c, TV(mu_Pi,g)<=c instead gives the useful pointwise
bound H_theta(g)>=(kappa*U/(2N)-c)_+. It does NOT give the stronger
conditional-worst-world expression (1) for each theta. We do not infer
an exact global positive-budget minimax value from (1).

## Actual sampling and exact expectation at zero budget

Fix an actual world and verifier output T. Its training samples remain
iid, since T was independently drawn conditional on the world. Pair j
is resolved exactly when a sample hits its S context outside T_x, an
event of mass (K-r)/(NK)=p0 per draw. These distinguishing categories
are disjoint across pairs. Thus, without any independence assumption on
missing-category indicators,

 E[U]=d*(1-p0)^n,
 E[z^U]=sum_{j=0}^d binom(d,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-j*p0)^n.        (4)

The joint missing event for j specified categories has probability
(1-j*p0)^n; expand the product of missing-indicator factors to obtain
the PGF. This law is independent of the actual supports, orientations
and identity of T. Pointwise (2) supplies the expected lower bound in
EVERY fixed world; the preceding generator attains equality in every
outcome at c=0. This proves (3) for the global minimax game.

For c>0 the global expected minimax is bracketed by

 E[(kappa*U/(2N)-c)_+] <= value
                  <= (1/2)*E[(kappa*U/N-c)_+].           (5)

These agree at c=0, but are not generally the same elsewhere.
The expectation of the conditional worst-world value IS the upper
expression; it is a different objective from global minimax expectation.

A specified fair completion of unresolved support-consistent ERM bits
has expected classification error d/N*(1-p0)^n, so (3) is kappa/2
times that specified ERM error. This is NOT claimed to be the minimax
statistical classification error: likelihoods of inside-T observations
can help classify unresolved pairs. Robust calibration retains all
compatible worlds regardless of their likelihood.

Union bound P(U>0)<=d*(1-p0)^n gives a probability >=1-delta regime
of completely known partition when n>=(N/kappa)*log(d/delta). The
algorithm uses certificate flags and group sampling in polynomial time,
with O(n+d*r) explicitly supplied truth identities. No NK table is needed.

## Scope and primary-source basis

The source coarsening definition is Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3,
Definitions 1--2,pp.8--9. This experiment has a strong full-support
verifier that also reveals r truths in every S context; revealing only
A truth sets WITH their types is a different and easier protocol.
The result assumes robust calibration over all compatible worlds, not
merely calibration in the actual world with high probability. No novelty
is claimed for coupon occupancy or the elementary TV inequalities.
The proposed result is the exact explicit untagged verifier frontier and
its pointwise lower bound at zero error. The exact check log is
logs/untagged_full_verifier_check.txt: 6560 integer-cell inequalities,
all 203 six-atom partitions, 9842 ten-atom partitions with at most three
cells, 16 attainer/world checks and 21 joint occupancy laws pass.
Negative controls cover safe-density removal and a genuinely skewed
posterior whose mean law fails robust calibration. These finite checks
support, and do not replace, the general derivation above. Independent

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.29406, 'Partially Totally Real Submanifolds of Sasakian Manifolds'] For $X,Y\in\Gamma(\Dtilde)$ define
\[
 \mathcal Q(X,Y)=h(X,PY)-h(Y,PX)+\nabla_X^\perp FY-\nabla_Y^\perp FX.
\]
Then $\Dtilde$ is integrable if and only if
\begin{align}
 g(\mathcal Q(X,Y),\phi Z)&=0 \quad\text{for all }Z\in\Gamma(\Dperp),\\
 g(PX,Y)&=0
\end{align}
for all $X,Y\in\Gamma(\Dtilde)$.

[Proposition prop:tailbnd of arXiv:2608.13452, 'Wasserstein stability of the zero cell of a Poisson hyperplane tessellation under directio'] Let \(\Phi\) be a coupling of \(\phi_1\) and \(\phi_2\) which is antipodally symmetric, i.e., \(\Phi\) is invariant under the antipodal map \(T: (v_1,v_2) \mapsto (-v_1,-v_2)\) for all \((v_1,v_2) \in (S^{d-1})^2\).
    Given the coupling $(Z_0^{(1)},Z_0^{(2)})$ defined by (equation eq:couplingZeroCells of the paper) using \(\Phi\), we have for all $u \in S^{d-1}$ and $t > 0$,
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{P}[ \rho_{Z_0^{(1)}}(u)- \rho_{Z_0^{(2)}}(u) \geq t]
        &= 2 \gamma \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{-\gamma F_u(y+t,y)} \int_{(S^{d-1})^2} \langle u,v_2 \rangle   \indic{ 0 < \langle  u , v_2\rangle < \frac{y+t}{t} \langle u,v_2-v_1 \rangle} \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \Phi (v_1 , v_2) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} y,
    \end{align*}
    where $F_u(\cdot,\cdot)$ is defined as in (equation def:Fu of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:tailbnd of arXiv:2608.13452

[Theorem thm:positive-random-measure-realization of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $(X,\mu,Y)$ be a separated cross-section system. For every
$R>0$, there is an equivariant Borel map
$\Phi_R:X\to\mathcal M_+(\mathbb R^d)$ such that
\[
    \Phi_R(x)=g_x\,\lambda_d,
    \qquad
    0<
    \inf_{\substack{x\in X\\u\in\mathbb R^d}}
    g_x(u),
    \qquad
    \sup_{\substack{x\in X\\u\in\mathbb R^d}}
    |\partial^\alpha g_x(u)|
    <\infty
    \quad
    (\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^d).
\]
The pushforward
$\zeta_R:=(\Phi_R)_*\mu$ has local second moments and satisfies
\[
    \sigma_{\zeta_R}\bigl(B_R(0)\bigr)=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
    \Phi_R(x)=\Phi_R(x')
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    \kappa_Y(x)=\kappa_Y(x').
\]
Consequently, if $Y$ is generating, then $\Phi_R$ is a measurable
$\mathbb R^d$-isomorphism from $(X,\mu)$ to
$\bigl(\mathcal M_+(\mathbb R^d),\zeta_R\bigr)$. The measure
$\zeta_R$ is ergodic whenever $\mu$ is ergodic.

[Prop CLEcoupling1 of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Consider a zero boundary GFF $\Phi_D$ on $D$ and the nested CLE$_4$ determined by exploring consecutively two-valued sets $A_{-2\lambda, 2\lambda}$. Then, for all boundary conditions $v \in 2\lambda \mathbb{Z}$, we have the following properties in coupling with $\Phi_D + v$: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item The labels $s_\ell \in \{-2\lambda, 2\lambda\}$ attached to each loop $\ell \in \text{CLE}_4^{n}$ are i.i.d. symmetric conditionally on the loops, 
and in terms of distributions,
$$\sum_{\Gamma \in \text{CLE}^{\rm nest}_4}(v1_{\Gamma \text{ outermost}}+s_\Gamma)
\1_{\operatorname{Int}(\Gamma)} = \Phi_D +v.$$
\item 
We assign the height $v$ to the boundary of the domain. Thereby, each gasket in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ can be uniquely attached a height corresponding to the sum of labels of loops $s_\ell$ in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ strictly surrounding this gasket, including the boundary of the domain. If this sum equals $h$, then we say that the gasket is at height $h$. Equivalently we can attach a height to each loop in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ by considering the sum of labels of loops surrounding and including this loop and the boundary. This way the height of the gasket corresponds to the height of its outermost loop.   
\item In this coupling, conditionally on the loops, for each $z \in D$, the heights $h$ of the gaskets in 
CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ surrounding $z$ form a simple symmetric random walk $S^z(m)$ with step-size $2\lambda$ and starting point $v$. 
\item For $v \neq 0$, consider $A_0$, the first passage set of $\Phi_D + v$ with boundary values $0$. Then $A_0$ is almost surely equal to taking the connected component of the boundary of the closed union of all gaskets of non-zero height. In particular, for each $z \in D \cap \mathbb{Q}^2$, the boundary of the connected component of 
$D \setminus A_0$ containing $z$ is constructed as follows: we consider the nested loop sequence surrounding $z$ until the first time that a loop of height $0$ appears and that is the boundary. 
\item Further, the sign excursion sets of $\Phi_D + v$ have the following description using nested CLE$_4$: we consider the closed union of all the gaskets in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ of height different than zero. The connected components have then the law of sign excursion sets.
\item Finally, the dual of the excursion sets, i.e. the complement of the excursion sets in $D$, is given by the disjoint union of all the gaskets of height $0$ in the nested CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Prop CLEcoupling1 of arXiv:2604.15146

[Lemma 18 (Affine contraction) of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] Let $\pi=\mu(\d x)\pi_x(\d y)\in\Pi_S(\mu,\nu)$ and let $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
Define $\pi_x^{\alpha}:=(T_{x,\alpha})_\#\pi_x$, the push-forward of $\pi_x$ by the map $T_{x,\alpha})$, where $T_{x,\alpha}(y):=\alpha y+(1-\alpha)x$.
Set $\pi^\alpha:=\mu(\d x)\pi_x^\alpha(\d y)$ with second marginal $\nu^\alpha$.
Then $\pi^\alpha\in\Pi_S(\mu,\nu^\alpha)$ and
\[
AW_1(\pi^\alpha,\pi)\le (1-\alpha)\Big(\int_{\R}|x|\,\mu(\d x)+\int_{\R}|y|\,\nu(\d y)\Big).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 5 (Chebotarev density theorem) of arXiv:2609.02444, 'The Hasse norm principle for $A_4$-quartic extensions of global function fields'] Let \(G\) be a finite group, \(\phi \colon X \to Y\) a \(G\)-torsor defined over \(\FF_q\), and \(\Phi \subset G\) a conjugacy class.
  \begin{enumerate}
      \item  Suppose that \(X\) is geometrically connected.
  Then
  \[ \lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{|\{y \in Y(\FF_{q^m}) \mid \varphi(y) = \Phi\}|}{|Y(\FF_{q^m})|} = \frac{|\Phi|}{|G|}. \]
  \item More generally, suppose that \(Y\) is geometrically connected and \(X\) has \(r\) geometric components, all defined over \(\FF_q\).
  Then
  \[ \lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{|\{y \in Y(\FF_{q^{m}}) \mid \varphi(y) = \Phi\}|}{|Y(\FF_{q^{m}})|} \leq r\frac{|\Phi|}{|G|}, \]
  with equality if and only if $\Phi$ is contained in the stabiliser of a geometric component of $X$.
  \end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem kernel of arXiv:2606.19507, 'The $t$-Split Two-Periodic Aztec Diamond Model'] Let $-N \leq \xi,\xi' \leq -1$ and $0 < m, m' < N$. The correlation kernel $t$-split two-periodic Aztec diamond of size $2N$ with $t < 1/2$ can be written as a piecewise expression depending on whether $m' \leq tN$ or $m' > tN$. For $0 < m' \leq tN$ the kernel is:
    \begin{multline} 
        \left[\mathbb{K}_N(4m',2\xi'+j;4m,2\xi+i)\right]_{i,j=0,1} = -\frac{\1_{m>m'}}{2\pi \mathrm{i}} \oint_{\gamma_{0,1}}\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z} z^{\xi'-\xi}\phi_{m'\to m,N}(z)\\
        +\frac{1}{(2\pi\mathrm{i})^2}\oint_{\gamma_1} \mathrm{d}w \oint_{\gamma_{0,1}} \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z(z-w)}\frac{w^{\xi'+N}(z-1)^N}{z^{\xi+N}(w-1)^N}r_{\alpha,1}(w)^{tN-m'}F_{\alpha,1}(w) \\
        \times \Phi_{\beta}(w)^{(1/2-t)N} \Phi_{\beta}(z)^{(t-1/2)N}\Phi_{\alpha}(z)^{-tN}\phi_{0\to m,N}(z) \\
        + \frac{1}{(2\pi\mathrm{i})^2}\oint_{\gamma_1}\mathrm{d}w\oint_{\gamma_{0,1}} \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z(z-w)}\frac{w^{\xi'+N}(z-1)^N}{z^{\xi+N}(w-1)^N}r_{\alpha,2}(w)^{tN-m'} c(w) F_{\alpha,2}(w) F_{\beta,1}(w)F_{\alpha,1}(w) \\
        \Phi_{\beta}(w)^{(1/2-t)N} \Phi_{\beta}(z)^{(t-1/2)N} \Phi_{\alpha}(z)^{-tN}\phi_{0\to m,N}(z).
    \end{multline}
    For $tN < m' < N$ the kernel is:
    \begin{multline} 
        \left[\mathbb{K}_N(4m',2\xi'+j;4m,2\xi+i)\right]_{i,j=0,1} = - \frac{\1_{m>m'}}{2\pi\mathrm{i}} \oint_{\gamma_{0,1}}\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z} z^{\xi'-\xi} \phi_{m' \to m,N}(z) \\
        + \frac{1}{(2\pi\mathrm{i})^2}\oint_{\gamma_1} \mathrm{d}w \oint_{\gamma_{0,1}} \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z(z-w)}\frac{w^{\xi'+N}(z-1)^N}{z^{\xi+N}(w-1)^N}r_{\beta,1}(w)^{N/2-m'} F_{\beta,1}(w)\\
        \Phi_{\beta}(z)^{(t-1/2)N}\Phi_{\alpha}(z)^{-tN}\phi_{0\to m,N}(z) \\
        + \frac{1}{(2\pi\mathrm{i})^2}\oint_{\gamma_1}\mathrm{d}w\oint_{\gamma_{0,1}} \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z(z-w)}\frac{w^{\xi'+N}(z-1)^N}{z^{\xi+N}(w-1)^N}r_{\beta,1}(w)^{(2t - 1/2)N - m'}c(w)F_{\beta,1}(w)F_{\alpha,1}(w)F_{\beta,2}(w)\\
        \times \Phi_{\beta}(z)^{(t-1/2)N}\Phi_{\alpha}(z)^{-tN}\phi_{0\to m,N}(z). 
    \end{multline}
    In both cases, $\gamma_1$ is a simple, positively oriented contour surrounding $1$ but not $0$, while $\gamma_{0,1}$ is a simple, positively oriented contour surrounding both $0$ and $1$ with $\gamma_1$ in its interior. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem kernel of arXiv:2606.19507

body: Let f be a continuous complex-valued function on an open connected subset U of C. If for every closed triangular path T whose closed solid triangle lies inside U, the contour integral of f around the boundary of T equals zero, then f is holomorphic on U. Morera's theorem is essentially the converse of the Cauchy-Goursat theorem, and it is commonly used to prove that a function built as a locally uniform limit, series, or integral of holomorphic functions is itself holomorphic.
title: Morera's theorem

[Lemma 8 (Trajectory lemma, simplified form) of arXiv:2606.02856, 'Geometric Routing in Geometric Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] Let \(w_0\) and \(D_0\) be sufficiently large constants, and let \(M:=\min\{w_0,D_0\}\). Let \(\om{1} \leq f_0(n) \leq \oh{\log\log n}\) be any growing function. Suppose that the geometric path \(P\) first enters
\(\overline{V}(w_0,D_0)\) at a vertex \(u_1\). Then, with probability
\(1-\Oh{M^{-\Omega(1)}}\), the following holds:

\(P\) follows the layered trajectory: it visits the layers in the prescribed order, visiting each first-phase layer and each second-phase layer at most once, except possibly the layer \(A_{2,\star}\), which may be visited twice. Moreover, before leaving the main part, \(P\) reaches a vertex \(u_\ell\) s.t.
\[
	\mathbb{E}_{<D_0}\big[\,\abs{N(u_{\ell}) \cap V_{<D_0}}\,\big] = \Om{M^{\Om{1}}},
\]
where the expectation is w.r.t. uncovering the vertices whose distance to target is at most \(D_0\), conditioned on the position and weight of \(u_\ell\). The number of hops from \(u_1\) to \(u_\ell\) is at most
\[
	\frac{1+\oh{1}}{\abs{\log(\tau-2)}} \left( \log\log_{w_0}(D_{u_1}^d) + \log\log_{D_0}(D_{u_1}) \right) 
	+\Oh{f_0(n)}.
\]
In particular, since \(D_{u_1}\le n^{1/d}\), this is at most \( \frac{2+\oh{1}}{\abs{\log(\tau-2)}}\log\log n\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Trajectory lemma, simplified form

[Lem 102 (SDE for coordinate sum) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let
$\hvY(t) = \vY(t-\sss)+\xxx$
where $(\sss,\xxx)\sim\varphi$, and let 	\[
	\iY(t)
	\equiv \sum_{i=1}^d \iY^i(t)\,.
	\]
Let $\iX$ be the SDE solution from Definition~\ref{d:projected.coeffs}.
Assume the coefficients $B$ and $A^{1/2}$ of \eqref{e:proj.coef.drift} and \eqref{e:proj.coef.qv} are bounded and Lipschitz.
Then the processes $\iX$ and $\iY$ satisfy the same Fokker--Planck equations. 
Consequently, for each fixed $t$, the marginal law of $\iX(t)$ agrees with the marginal law of\/ $\iY(t)$.

body:
Let U be an open subset of R^D and L be C^3 on a neighborhood of the gradient-flow trajectories in question. For every x in U suppose the solution phi_t(x) of d phi_t/dt=-grad L(phi_t), phi_0=x, exists for all t>=0 and converges to Phi(x). Assume the resulting endpoint map Phi:U->R^D is C^2. Then for every x in U, D Phi(x) grad L(x)=0 and D^2 Phi(x)[grad L(x),grad L(x)]=-D Phi(x) Hess L(x) grad L(x). Here the second derivative of the vector-valued map is a bilinear map. The identities hold on the domain of the endpoint map, not merely at its limiting minima. They assert annihilation of grad L; they do not assert annihilation of every individual noise direction in a multi-output loss. Source: Li, Wang and Arora, What Happens after SGD Reaches Zero Loss? -- A Mathematical Framework, Lemma C.2, PDF p29.
U is open; L is C^3 on a neighborhood of the trajectories
Gradient flow from every point of U exists for all nonnegative times and has an endpoint
The endpoint map Phi is C^2 on U

    \begin{enumerate}[label=\alph*)]
        \item $\Theta_i \leqslant_{st} \Theta_j$,
        \item $V_i \mid \{\Theta_i = \theta\} \leqslant_{st} V_j \mid \{\Theta_j = \theta\}$ for every fixed $\theta$,
         \item $V_i \mid \{\Theta_i = \theta\} \leqslant_{st} V_i \mid \{\Theta_i = \theta'\}$ for every $\theta \leqslant \theta'$ and $i$.
    \end{enumerate}
    \noindent Then $V_i \leqslant_{st} V_j$ for $i \leqslant j$.

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2607.28215, 'Almost stochastic dominance via optimal transport'] The following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item A function $\psi$ is $c$-convex, if and only if $-\psi \in  \mathcal{L}_1(E,c)$.
\item For a $c$-convex function $\psi$ we have $\psi^c = \psi$.
\item  Any function $\psi \in  \mathcal{L}_1(E,c)$ is $\le_c$-monotone. 
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ which follows the exponential law of parameter $\lambda>0$, its moments are given by the following formula:
$$M_k=\frac{k!}{\lambda^k}$$
In particular, the mean is $E=1/\lambda$, and the variance is $V=1/\lambda^2$.

[Lem 64 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $q_0 \in [0,1)$, we have
$\sM^{\si}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\sii}(\alpha,q_0)$.

\begin{proof} We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification} for this proof:
	\begin{center}
	\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
	\MSRheader\\

	\FAIRdefn\\
	\TMPONEdefn

We see that the $\si$ and $\sii$ classes differ only in the condition on the Ising initialization $Y(q_*)\sim\zeta^\Ising$: the $\si$ class satisfies the condition~\ref{it:7.1} (i.e., $\zeta^{\Ising} \in \cP_2(\R)$), while the $\sii$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:7.2} (i.e., $\zeta^{\Ising} \in \cP([-1,1])$).

Therefore, let us suppose we have controls $(q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfying the $(\alpha,q_0,L,\epsilon)$-$\si$ conditions, which drive processes $X,Y$ as in \eqref{e:formal.sde.main}, \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising}. We will construct controls $(\tilde q_*,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde w,\tilde p,\tilde \zeta,\tilde \zeta^\Ising)$ satisfying the $(\alpha,q_0,L,\tilde{\epsilon})$-$\sii$ conditions, for some $\tilde{\epsilon}$ that will tend to zero as $\epsilon\to0$. The latter controls will drive processes $\tilde X, \tilde Y$ that will approximate $X,Y$.

Let $(\tilde q_*,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde p,\tilde \zeta) = (q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)$.
    We then take 
    \[\tilde\zeta^{\Ising}
    =f_\# \zeta^{\Ising},\quad
        f(x) = \begin{cases}
            1 - \epsilon/x
            & 
            \textup{for $x \in (1,+\infty)$,} \\
            (1-\epsilon) x &
            \textup{for $[-1,1]$,} \\
            -1 + \epsilon/x &
            \textup{for $x \in (-\infty,1)$.}
        \end{cases}
    \]
Thus $\tilde\zeta^{\Ising} \in \cP([-1,1])$, so it satisfies condition~\ref{it:7.2}. We couple the initializations $Y(q_*)\sim\zeta^\Ising$ and 
	\[
	\tilde{Y}(q_*)
	=f(Y(q_*))
	\sim \tilde{\zeta}^\Ising\,.
	\]
Note that for $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, the function $f$ is an invertible mapping from $\bbR$ to $(-1,1)$.
    Recall from the definition \eqref{e:filt.X.Y} of $\cF_Y$ that we can write
    \[
        w_t = w_t\Big((W(s))_{s\in [q_*,t]},U',Y(q_*)\Big)\,,
    \]
where the $w_t$ on the right-hand side is a measurable function. We then define $\tilde w$ by setting
    \[
        \tilde w_t\Big((W(s))_{s\in [q_*,t]},U',\tilde Y(q_*)\Big)
        = w_t\Big(
        (W(s))_{s\in [q_*,t]},
        U',
        f^{-1}(\tilde Y(q_*))
        = Y(q_*) 
        \Big)\,.
    \]
Therefore $w=\tilde{w}$ as processes.
We let $\tilde X, \tilde Y$ be defined by \eqref{e:formal.sde.main} and \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising} with $(\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde w)$ in place of $(b,\sigma,w)$; and we couple them to
$X,Y$ by taking the initializations $\tilde X(q_*) = X(q_*)$ and $\tilde Y(q_*) = f(Y(q_*))$, as well as the same 
Brownian motions $B,W$. It is clear from these definitions that conditions \ref{it:1.2}, \ref{it:2.1}, \ref{it:3.2}, \ref{it:4.1}, \ref{it:8.1} remain satisfied for $(\tilde q_*,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde w,\tilde p,\tilde \zeta,\tilde \zeta^\Ising)$; so it remains to verify that conditions \ref{it:5.1} and \ref{it:6.1} remain satisfied.

From the above definitions and \eqref{e:formal.sde.main}, it is clear that $X=\tilde{X}$ as processes. Since we already noted that $w=\tilde{w}$ as processes, it follows from \eqref{e:formal.sde.ising} that
	\beq
	Y(t)-Y(q_*)
	= \int_{q_*}^t w_u\,d W(u)
	=\tilde{Y}(t)-\tilde{Y}(q_*)
	\eeq
for all $t\in[q_*,1]$. Thus, conditions
\ref{it:5.1} and \ref{it:6.1} will essentially follow from showing that
$Y(q_*)$ and $\tilde{Y}(q_*)$ are close in $L^2$, so we turn to this next.

Let $g(x) = (|x|-1)_+^2$. Recall from Remark~\ref{r:true.mg} that $Y$ is an $L^2$-bounded continuous martingale. Since $g$ is nonnegative and convex, it follows that $g(Y(t))$ is a nonnegative submartingale. Thus
    \[

[Corollary projected-unit-sphere of arXiv:2609.00108, 'The double sphere solution in the liquid drop model'] Let
		\(
		\bar g=\bar g(\omega_3)
		\in C^{0,\beta}(S)
		\)
		be axially symmetric. Define
		\begin{equation}
			{\rm c}[\bar g]
			=
			-
			\frac{
				\displaystyle
				\int_S\bar g\,\omega_3\,d\sigma
			}{
				\displaystyle
				\int_S\omega_3^2\,d\sigma
			}.
		\end{equation}
		Then there exists a unique axially symmetric
		\(
		\bar h\in C^{2,\beta}(S)
		\)
		satisfying
		$$
		J_S[\bar h]
		=
		\bar g
		+
		{\rm c}[\bar g]\,\omega_3,
		\qquad
		\bar h(P_S)=0.
		$$
		Moreover,
		\begin{equation}
			\|\bar h\|_{C^{2,\beta}(S)}
			+
			|{\rm c}[\bar g]|
			\le
			C
			\|\bar g\|_{C^{0,\beta}(S)}.
		\end{equation}
		We denote this linear solution operator by
		\begin{equation}
			\mathcal T_S[\bar g]
			=
			(\bar h,{\rm c}[\bar g]).
		\end{equation}

body: The axiom of choice (AC) states: for every family {A_i : i in I} of nonempty sets, indexed by any set I, there exists a choice function c defined on I with c(i) in A_i for every i. Equivalently: every Cartesian product of nonempty sets is nonempty; every surjection has a right inverse; every set of nonempty pairwise disjoint sets has a transversal selecting one element from each. Over the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms ZF, the axiom of choice is equivalent to Zorn's lemma and to the well-ordering theorem, and also to Tychonoff's theorem for arbitrary compact spaces. AC is independent of ZF: Godel (1938) showed ZF plus AC is consistent if ZF is (constructible universe), and Cohen (1963) showed ZF plus the negation of AC is consistent if ZF is (forcing). Countable and finite choices do not follow from ZF alone in general, but AC is provable in ZF for finite index sets I by induction.
title: Axiom of choice

				\leq V(\|u_0\|^2_{H^s}), \qquad t\ge0.
			\end{equation*}
			Moreover, the problem (equation SPDE-general of the paper) on $\mathbb T^d$ admits an invariant measure $\mu$ in the sense of Definition (IM definition of the paper) with $E=H^s$. 
			
			\item  If (Hypo-DNI-3 F-h of the paper) holds, then  
			\begin{equation*} 
				\int_0^t\mathbb{E}  \left[V\left(\frac{\|u(t')\|^2_{W^{p,\infty}}}{M^2}\right)\Bigg|\mathcal{F}_0\right]{\,\rm{d}} t'
				\leq  \frac{V(\| u_0\|^2_{H^\theta})}{\mathscr{G}_3}\left(1-{\rm e}^{-\mathscr{G}_3t}\right),
				\quad t>0.
			\end{equation*}
			As a result, the Dirac measure centered at $0$ is the \textbf{unique invariant probability measure} on both $\mathbb T^d$ and $\mathbb R^d$ when $h(0)=0$.
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textbf{Long-time dynamics of \eqref{SPDE-general}}

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2506.09609, 'Schramm-Loewner evolution contains a topological Sierpi\'nski carpet when $\kappa$ is clos'] Fix $s \in (0,1)$, there exists a universal constant $C = C(s)>0$ such that the following holds.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Let $\mathfrak h$ be a whole-plane GFF normalized so that $\mathfrak h_R(0) = 0$. For any $B(z,r) \subset B(0,R)$, let $\mathfrak h^{z,r}$ be the harmonic extension of $\mathfrak h|_{\mathbb{C} \setminus B(z,r)}$ in $B(z,r)$. Then, for any $t \geq 1$,
        $$
        \mathbb{P} \Big[ \sup_{u,v \in B(z, sr)} |\mathfrak h^{z, r}(u) - \mathfrak h^{z,r}(v)| \geq t \Big] \leq C e^{-t^2 / C}.
        $$ 
        \item Let $B(z,r)$ and $B(y,l)$ be two boxes such that $B(z,r) \subset B(y,l)$. Let $h_{y,l}$ be a zero-boundary GFF on $B(y,l)$ and let $h^{z,r}_{y,l}$ be the harmonic extension of $h_{y,l}|_{B(y,l) \setminus B(z,r)}$ on $B(z,r)$. Then, for any $t \geq 1$,
        $$
        \mathbb{P} \Big[ \sup_{u,v \in B(z, sr)} |h^{z, r}_{y,l}(u) - h^{z,r}_{y,l}(v)| \geq t \Big] \leq C e^{-t^2 / C}.
        $$ 
    \end{enumerate}

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2608.12070, 'Central limit theorems for a heavy-tailed subcritical Galton-Watson process with state-dep'] [{\cite[Proposition D.3]{Barczy}}]

 

Let $\tau$ be a non-negative integer-valued random variable and let  $\{\zeta, \zeta_i,i\ge 1\}$ be a sequence of  i.i.d. non-negative random variables, independent of $\tau$, such that $\tau$ has regularly varying tail of index $\kappa\in [0,\infty)$ and $0<\E(\zeta) <\infty$. In case of $\kappa\in [1,\infty)$, assume additionally that  there exists $r>\kappa$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}(\zeta^r)<\infty$. Then we have
$$
\P\left(\sum_{i=1}^\tau \zeta_i>x\right)\sim (\E \zeta)^\kappa\P(\tau>x),\quad x\to \infty.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 26 of arXiv:2609.00254, 'On the geometry and cohomology of almost abelian solvmanifolds'] Let $\rho$ be a non-degenerate integrable pure spinor and let
$X+\xi\in\left(\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak g^*\right)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ be such that
$\d\rho=(X+\xi)\cdot\rho$. Then the character of Lemma \ref{lem:bicomplex}(d) is
\begin{equation}
\chi(v)=2\left\langle X+\xi,\,v\right\rangle,\qquad v\in \mathfrak L .
\end{equation}
In particular, $\chi=0$ if and only if $\rho$ is closed, that is, if and only if the structure is
generalized Calabi--Yau, in which case
$GH^{\,n-\bullet}_{\overline\partial}(\mathfrak g)\cong H^\bullet\left(\mathfrak L,\mathbb C\right)$.

body: Let X be a square-integrable function of independent coordinates and let X^L denote X with the coordinates in a block L replaced by an independent copy. Then (X, X^L) is an exchangeable pair, and E[(X - X^L)^2] = 2 Var(X) - 2 Cov(X, X^L). Consequently E[(X - X^L)^2] <= 4 Var(X) always, and E[(X - X^L)^2] <= 2 Var(X) whenever Cov(X, X^L) >= 0. The identity requires no independence beyond that of the resampled block and no structure on X beyond square-integrability.
