[Definition 100 (Admissible dyadic spectral resolution) of arXiv:2606.29292, 'Intrinsic Gaussian Tensor Geometry and Random Operator Spectra'] A family $(\rho_L)_{L\in\mathbb D}\subset C_c^\infty((0,\infty);\R)$,
$\mathbb D=\{1,2,4,\ldots\}$, is an \emph{admissible inhomogeneous dyadic
resolution} if $\sum_L\rho_L(\lambda)=1$ for $\lambda\ge1$, the sum is
locally finite, and there are fixed $0<c_0<1<C_0<\infty$ such that
\[
  \operatorname{supp}\rho_1\subset[c_0,C_0],\qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\rho_L\subset[c_0L,C_0L]\quad(L\ge2),
\]
with
\begin{equation}

  \sup_{L\ge2}\sup_{\lambda\ge0}
  L^j|\partial_\lambda^j\rho_L(\lambda)|<\infty
  \qquad(j=0,1,2,\ldots).
\end{equation}
Set $\Delta_L:=\rho_L(\Lambda_g)$.  The resolution has finite overlap, the
operators $\Delta_L$ have finite rank, and $\sum_L\Delta_L=\Id$ strongly on
$L^2(M)$.
title: Admissible dyadic spectral resolution

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.03403, 'Hyperpositive functions, sector bounded functions and a trace formula'] Let $K(z,w)$ be a $\mathbb C^{m\times m}$-valued function positive definite on $\Omega$.
  In the above notation there is  a uniquely defined Hilbert space, denoted by $\mathcal H(K)$ and called the reproducing kernel Hilbert space associated to
  $K(z,w)$ with the following properties:\\
  $(1)$ The elements of $\mathcal H(K)$ are functions defined on $\Omega$.\\
  $(2)$  For every $z\in\Omega$ and $f\in\mathcal H(K)$
  \begin{equation}
    
f(z)=\langle f,K_z\rangle_{\mathcal H(K)}.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, given any orthonormal basis $(f_a)_{a\in A}$ (where $A$ is an index set with the dimension of $\mathcal H(K)$) it holds that
\begin{equation}
  K(z,w)=\sum_{a\in A}f(z)f(w)^*.
  
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.03403

In the width-one strip of the exact-variance lemma, perturb all Gaussian vertex weights by g^s=e^(-s)g+sqrt(1-e^(-2s))g' with independent copy g'. The number B_r(s) of diamonds where the maximizing choice differs has Binomial(r,q(s)) law, q(s)=arccos(e^(-s))/pi. The probability of identical maximizing paths is (1-q(s))^r, and their expected shared-vertex fraction is 1-rq(s)/(2r+1). For s=r^(-alpha) with fixed 0<alpha<2, the path-equality probability tends to zero, shared fraction tends to one, and Var(M_r) remains linear in r. This refutes only the unqualified path-change auxiliary bridge.
All assumptions of the width-one exact-variance lemma
Independent Gaussian copy in the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck perturbation
Fixed alpha in (0,2) for the asymptotic claim

If ||E_0||_2=q<1, then ||X_t-B^(-1)||_2 <= ||B^(-1)||_2 q^(2^t), hence X_t converges to B^(-1). The source initialization X_0=alpha B^T satisfies q<1 whenever 0<alpha<2/lambda_max(B^T B). The residual identity itself holds for arbitrary square B and X_t; invertibility and the strict contraction condition are required for this inverse-convergence conclusion.

Let n,d>=1 and T>=2 be integers, and m>=1 an integer factor width. Fix tokens x_it in R^d, queries z_i in R^d, labels Y_i in {-1,+1}, and a linear head v in R^d. Select opt_i in argmax_t Y_i v^T x_it. Let C be the set of real d-by-d matrices satisfying (x_i,opt_i-x_it)^T W z_i>=1 for all i and t!=opt_i. Consider (Att-SVM), minimizing ||W||_F over C, and (Att-SVM-star), minimizing ||W||_* over C subject to rank(W)<=m. The nuclear norm ||W||_* is the sum of singular values. For each problem separately assume its feasible set is nonempty. Every global optimizer W of either problem has row(W) contained in S=span{z_1,...,z_n}. Consequently rank(W)<=dim(S)<=min(n,d), with the additional rank cap m in the nuclear problem. No uniqueness is asserted for nuclear-norm optimizers. The conclusion concerns global solutions of these margin problems, not arbitrary KKT points or gradient-descent limits.
finite real dataset and fixed linear head; opt_i chosen by token scores
nonempty feasible set for the particular stated optimization problem
global optimum, not merely a stationary point; nuclear problem retains rank cap m

Then the map $\varepsilon_0^W: Z(Y) \to Z(Y')$  sends $J_n^{(3)}(Y)$ into $J_{n-1}^{(3)}(Y')$. Equivalently, for any $\vartheta \in Z(Y)$ we have \[q_3(Y; \vartheta) \le q_3(Y'; \varepsilon_0^W(\vartheta)) + 1.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition Order of a tempered distribution of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Let \(T\in\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^d)\) be a tempered distribution (i.e.\ a continuous linear functional on \(\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d)\)).  We say that \(T\) is of \emph{order} at most \(m\) if there exists a constant \(C>0\) such that
\[
  \bigl|T \varphi\bigr|
  \;\le\;
  C \,\sum_{\substack{|\alpha|\le m \\|\beta|\le m}}
  \;\sup_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}
  \bigl|\,x^{\alpha}\,\partial^{\beta}\varphi(x)\bigr|
  \quad
  \text{for all }\varphi\in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^d).
\]
The \emph{order} of \(T\) is the least integer \(m\) for which such an estimate holds.

[Theorem 1 (EPI on compact groups) of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group, equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Assume that $G$ has no open subgroups except $G$ itself and possibly $\{0\}$. Let $X,Y$ be independent random variables on $G$ with finite entropies. Then
$$h(X+Y)-\frac{1}{2}h(X)-\frac{1}{2}h(Y) \geq 0.$$
Moreover:
\begin{itemize}
\item[$(i)$]
If $G$ is connected, then there is equality if and only 
if $X$ and $Y$ are both uniform on $G$.
\item[$(ii)$]
If $G$ is finite, then there is equality if and only if 
either both $X$ and $Y$ are uniform on the whole group $G$ 
or both $X$ and $Y$ are deterministic.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: EPI on compact groups

	Let $S,T \in \Sym(\Hcal) \cap \HS(\Hcal)$, with eigenvalues $\{\alpha_k\}_{k \in \Nbb}$, $\{\beta_k\}_{k \in \Nbb}$
	and corresponding orthonormal eigenvectors $\{\phi_k\}_{k \in \Nbb}$, $\{\psi_k\}_{k \in \Nbb}$, respectively.
	Let $A \in \Sym(\Hcal)$.
	Then
	\begin{align}
		
		\trace(ASAT) =\trace(SATA) = \sum_{k,j=1}^{\infty}\alpha_k \beta_j \la A\phi_k, \psi_j\ra^2.
	\end{align}
	If, in addition, $A \in \Sym(\Hcal)\cap \HS(\Hcal)$, then $\trace(AS) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\alpha_k\la \phi_k, A\phi_k\ra$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 33 of arXiv:2609.02785, 'Characterization of Stanley-Reisner varieties by their automorphism group'] Let $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_2$ be the complexes of \cref{ex:rigid-invisible}. For parameters $t\in(\KK^{\times})^5$ and $h,g\in\KK[x]$, and for $\Delta\in\{\Delta_1,\Delta_2\}$, the formulas
$$
\varphi_{t,h,g}\colon\quad
\overline{x}_1\mapsto t_1\overline{x}_1,\quad
\overline{x}_2\mapsto t_2\overline{x}_2+\overline{x}_1h(\overline{x}_1),\quad
\overline{x}_3\mapsto t_3\overline{x}_3,\quad
\overline{x}_4\mapsto t_4\overline{x}_4+\overline{x}_5g(\overline{x}_5),\quad
\overline{x}_5\mapsto t_5\overline{x}_5
$$
define automorphisms of $\KK[\Delta]$, and, with $\tau:=\rho_{(1\,5)(2\,4)}$,
$$
\Aut(X_{\Delta_1})\;=\;\{\varphi_{t,h,g}\}\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\Aut(X_{\Delta_2})\;=\;\{\varphi_{t,h,g}\}\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle,
$$
given by the same formulas. In particular $\Aut(X_{\Delta_1})$ and $\Aut(X_{\Delta_2})$ are isomorphic as ind-groups, while $X_{\Delta_1}\not\cong X_{\Delta_2}$. Consequently, the fully exposed hypothesis cannot be removed from \cref{thm:main}.

[Definition 6 (Rhombus concavity) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{def:rhomb}
Given a function $h:T \ra \R$, and a positive integer $n$,  let $h_n$ denote the function from $T_n$ to $\R$ such that for $(nx, ny) \in T_n$, $h_n(nx, ny) = n^2 h(x, y).$
A function $h:T \ra \R$ is called {\bf rhombus concave} if for any positive integer $n$, 
and any $i$, $\De_i h_n$ is nonpositive on $E_i(T_n),$ and $h$ is continuous on $T$.
The corresponding function $h_n$ is called {\bf discrete (rhombus) concave}.  
Note that a necessary and sufficient condition for a function $h_n$ from $T_n$ to $\R$ to be discrete concave,  is that the piecewise linear extension (which we denote $\tilh_n$) of $h_n$ to $nT$ is  concave.
Here each piece is an isosceles right triangle with a $\sqrt{2}-$length  hypotenuse parallel to the vector $(1, 1).$
title: Rhombus concavity

body:
[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Set
\(
  U_1
  :=
  |\Phi_1|_{\sigma_0}^2
  =
  \frac{|\phi_1|^2}{\rho^2}.
\)
Then
\begin{equation}
  \dot H_0=0,
  \qquad
  \ddot H_0
  =
  -4(\Delta_0-2)^{-1}U_1.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every $k\ge 0$,
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  \widehat\sigma_t
  ={}&
  \sigma_0
  +2t\operatorname{Re}\Phi_1
  \\
  &+
  \frac{t^2}{2}
  \left[
    2\operatorname{Re}\Phi_2
    +
    \left(
      2U_1-4(\Delta_0-2)^{-1}U_1
    \right)\sigma_0
  \right]
  +O_{C^k}(t^3).
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
Here $O_{C^k}(t^3)$ means that, after subtracting the displayed
terms up to order two, the remainder $R_t$ satisfies
\(
  \|R_t\|_{C^k(X_0,\sigma_0)}\le C_k |t|^3
\)
for $|t|$ sufficiently small. Equivalently, all covariant derivatives
of $R_t$ up to order $k$, computed with respect to $\sigma_0$, are
uniformly $O(t^3)$.
Equivalently, in the coordinate $z$,
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  \widehat\sigma_t
  ={}&
  \rho\,dz\,d\bar z
  +
  t\left(
    \phi_1\,dz^2+\overline{\phi_1}\,d\bar z^2
  \right)
  +
  \frac{t^2}{2}
  \Bigg[
    \phi_2\,dz^2+\overline{\phi_2}\,d\bar z^2
  \\
  &+
    \left\{
      \frac{2|\phi_1|^2}{\rho^2}
      -
      4(\Delta_0-2)^{-1}
      \left(
        \frac{|\phi_1|^2}{\rho^2}
      \right)
    \right\}
    \rho\,dz\,d\bar z
  \Bigg]
  +O_{C^k}(t^3).
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}

[Ppn 230 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Fix $\alpha, L, \epsilon > 0$ and $\fq\in [1,2)$. 
	For any $\epsilon$-approximate $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA_N$, we have
	\[
		\max\bigg\{
			\bbW_\fq\Big(\mu(\cA_N), \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)\Big),
			\bbW_\fq\Big(\mu_{\sym}(\cA_N), \cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon)\Big) 
		\bigg\} \le o_N(1)\,,
	\]
	where $o_N(1)$ is a term tending to $0$ as $N\to\infty$ (which may depend on $\alpha,L,\epsilon,\fq$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $0 < a \leq b$ and let $\{k(n)\}_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ satisfy $\lim_{n \to \infty} k(n) = \infty$ and $\lim_{n\to\infty} k(n)/n = 0$. Then

    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Satz 2 of arXiv:2506.13661, 'Box-Covariances of Hyperuniform Point Processes'] Let $\eta$ be a stationary hyperuniform point process on $\mathbb{R}$ with 
	truncated pair correlation measure $\beta$ such that $|\beta|(\mathbb{R})<\infty$. If   
	
	
	\quad \emph{(i)} the function $H(y)=-\int_0^y \beta([x,\infty))\mathrm{d}x= \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Var}(\eta(\Lambda_y))$ is regularly varying with parameter $a\in[0,1],$ then,
	
	\quad \emph{(ii)} for all $z\in\mathbb{R}$ we have  
	\begin{align}
		\mathrm{cov}(z)=
		\frac{|z-1|^{a}}{2}+ \frac{|z+1|^{a}}{2}-|z|^{a},
	\end{align}
    for $a\in (0,1]$, and $\mathrm{cov}(z)=\delta_0(z)-\frac{1}{2} \delta_{-1}(z)-\frac{1}{2}\delta_{+1}(z)$ for $a=0$ (as in \eqref{eq:thm_cov}).
	
	Conversely, if we additionally assume that $\beta([x,\infty))$ is non-positive (or non-negative) for $x$ sufficiently large, then \emph{(i)} and \emph{(ii)} are equivalent. Moreover, if
	
	\quad \emph{(iii)} the limit $\mathrm{cov}(z)<\infty$ 
	exists for $z=1$ and $z=2$,
	
	then both \emph{(i)} and \emph{(ii)} follow.
	In either of these cases, neighboring boxes 
	have $\mathrm{cov}(1)=2^{a-1}-1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Satz 2 of arXiv:2506.13661

[Lemma lem:Galerkin of arXiv:2411.02459, 'Existence and higher regularity of statistically steady states for the stochastic Coleman-'] For all $U_0=(u_0,\eta_0)\in\mathcal{H}^0_\mu$ and $t\ge 0$, there exists a unique strong solution pair $(V_N,\eta_N)\in C([0,t];H\timesM^0_\mu)$. Furthermore, there exists a positive constant $c(U_0,t)$ independent of $N$ such that the following holds
\begin{align*}
&\mathbb{E}\sup_{0\le r\le t}\|(V_N(r),\eta_N(r))\|^2_{\mathcal{H}^0_\mu}\\
&+\int_0^t\mathbb{E}\big(\|V_N(r)\|^2_{H^1}+\|\eta_N(r)\|^2_{M^0_\mu} +\|V_N(r)\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}+\|\varphi(V_N(r)+\xi(r))\|^q_{L^{q}}\big)\emph{d} r\\
&\le c(U_0,t),
\end{align*}
where $q=(p_0+1)/p_0$ and $p_0$ is as in \nameref{cond:phi:2}.

[Lemma 3 (Truncation comparison) of arXiv:2608.05866, 'The Berry--Esseen Estimate \\in the Free Central Limit Theorem'] Let $T>0$. For each $j$, let $\nu_j$ be the probability measure obtained from $\mu_j$ by moving all mass outside $[-T,T]$ to the point zero. Let $Y_j$ have distribution $\nu_j$, and set
\[
 \alpha_j:=\int x\,\nu_j(dx),
 \qquad
 \beta_j^2:=\int x^2\,\nu_j(dx)-\alpha_j^2,
\]
\[
M_n:=\sum_{j=1}^n\alpha_j,
 \qquad
N_n^2:=\sum_{j=1}^n\beta_j^2>0,
 \qquad
\Gamma_n:=\sum_{j=1}^n\mu_j([-T,T]^c).
\]
Let $\widetilde\nu_{n,j}$ be the distribution of $(Y_j-\alpha_j)/N_n$, and let
\[
\widetilde\nu^{(n)}:=\widetilde\nu_{n,1}\bp\cdots\bp\widetilde\nu_{n,n}.
\]
Then $N_n\le B_n$, and
\begin{equation}
 \Delta(\mu^{(n)},\omega)
 \le \Delta(\widetilde\nu^{(n)},\omega)
 +\Gamma_n+\frac{|M_n|}{\pi N_n}
 +\frac{2}{\pi}\left(\frac{B_n}{N_n}-1\right).
\end{equation}

By using the indicator trick, we first write the expectation as the partial sum of the probabilities $\\mathbb{P}(S_{k}=M_{k})$. This is the probability of the event that the sample path of the walk, if traversed backwards in time, stays above the running minimum $M_k$. body:
Let Q_n = [-1/2,1/2]^n (the centred cube of volume 1), n >= 2. For every unit vector a in R^n, 1 <= vol_{n-1}(Q_n \cap a^perp) <= sqrt(2). The upper bound is attained exactly when a = (+-e_i +- e_j)/sqrt(2) (for example the hyperplane orthogonal to (1,1,0,...,0)); the lower bound 1 (Hadwiger, Hensley; Ball gives a simpler proof) exactly when a = +-e_j. Probabilistic form: if U_1,...,U_n are independent and uniform on [-1/2,1/2] and a_1^2 + ... + a_n^2 = 1, the density of a_1U_1 + ... + a_nU_n is largest at 0, where it equals vol_{n-1}(Q_n \cap a^perp); so this density is at most sqrt(2), with equality for (U_1 + U_2)/sqrt(2).

Assumes: central sections (hyperplanes through the centre of the cube); cube normalised to volume 1: Q_n = [-1/2,1/2]^n; the density statement is for independent uniform inputs

[Lemma lem:fgorth of arXiv:2603.05467, 'Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph'] Suppose that $0 < a < 0.01, 0 < r < 0.01/\sqrt{d}$, the finite set $V \subseteq [0,\infty)^d$
and the function $f :S^{d-1} \to (-0.1,0.1)$ are such that  
$f$ is odd and $a$-Lipschitz and moreover

$$ \left|B\left( (1+f(u))\cdot u, r \right) \cap V\right| \leq 1, $$

\noindent
for all $u \in S^{d-1}$.
Then there also exists a function $g : S^{d-1} \to \ensuremath{ \mathbb R}$ that is odd, $(9a)$-Lipschitz and satisfies 

$$ \left|f(u)-g(u)\right| < ar \quad \text{ and } \quad 
B\left( (1+g(u)) \cdot u, (a/2) \cdot r  \right) \cap V = \emptyset, $$

\noindent 
for all $u \in S^{d-1}$

[Prop of arXiv:2411.09988, 'A Study in Markov Chains, Loop-Erased Random Walk and Loop Soups'] Order the vertices $A = \{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}$ and define the measure on ordered loops $m^*$ as follows. Let $A_j = A\backslash\{x_1,...,x_{j-1}\}$. If $l$ is a loop in $A_j$ rooted at $x_j$, then
    \[m^*(l) = \frac{p(l)}{\beta(l)}\]
    where $\beta(l) = \# \{k:1\leq k \leq |l|, l_k = x_j\}$, and $m^*(l)=0$ for all other loops. Then
    \[\sum_{l} m^*(l) = \log \det G_A.\]

body: Coarea bound for a definite rank-two core. If (Y_1, Y_2) has density rho on R^2 and lambda_1, lambda_2 > 0, then S = lambda_1 Y_1^2 + lambda_2 Y_2^2 has density p_S(s) = (2 sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2))^{-1} int_0^{2 pi} rho(sqrt(s/lambda_1) cos th, sqrt(s/lambda_2) sin th) d th <= pi ||rho||_inf/sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2) (substitute u = sqrt(lambda_1) y_1, v = sqrt(lambda_2) y_2 and use polar coordinates; in two dimensions the length of the level curve and the gradient cancel, which is why ||rho||_inf suffices, and in three dimensions this fails). For an orthonormal two-dimensional projection of independent coordinates with densities <= 1, ||rho||_inf <= 2 (Livshyts-Paouris-Pivovarov), attained by ((X_1 + X_2)/sqrt2, (X_3 + X_4)/sqrt2) with uniform laws on unit intervals, so a definite rank-two core has density <= 2 pi/sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2). Passing from the core to the full form Q = core + R, with R depending on the same coordinates, is where the conjecture is hard.

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $Q$ be a quiver with stability parameters $\theta_i\in\bR$, $i\in Q_0$, functions $f_a$, $a\in Q_1$ as before, and a representation $(E,\rho)$ over $K$ with a non-Archimedean norm on each $E_i$, $i\in Q_0$.
Remove any arrows $a\in Q_1$ with $\rho(a)=0$.
We define a quiver $Q^\star$ with $\theta_i^\star$, $i\in Q^\star_0$, and a representation $E^\star$ of $Q^\star$ over $\bC$ as follows.

The $\lambda_{a,k}$ are as before and, by Lemma~(lem:limsvd of the paper) and its proof, are the well-defined values where the increasing filtration $\cF^-(\rho(a))_{\lambda}$ (equivalently: the decreasing filtration $\cF^+(\rho(a))_{\lambda}$) jumps.
The quiver $Q^\star$ has vertices of three types:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item A vertex for each vertex $i\in Q_0$ with 
    \[ 
    \theta_i^\star \coloneqq \theta_i+\sum_{\substack{a\in Q_1: s(a)=i}} f_a'(\lambda_{a,k_a}),
    \]
    and $E^\star_i\coloneqq(E_i)_0$.
    \item A vertex $(a,k,-)$ for each pair $(a,k)$, $a\in Q_1$, $0\leq k\leq k_a-1$, with
    \[ 
    \theta_{a,k,-}^\star \coloneqq \begin{cases} -f_a'(\lambda_{a,1}), & k=0\\ f_a'(\lambda_{a,k})-f_a'(\lambda_{a,k+1}), & k=1,\ldots,k_a-1 \end{cases}
    \]
    and with an arrow to $s(a)$.
    We set 
    \[
    E^{\star}_{a,k,-}\coloneqq\begin{cases} \cF^-(\rho(a))_{-\infty}\coloneqq\cF^-(\rho(a))_{<\lambda_1}, & k=0 \\ \cF^-(\rho(a))_{\lambda_k}, & k=1,\ldots,k_a-1 \end{cases} 
    \]
    and assign the inclusion map to the arrow.
    \item A vertex $(a,k,+)$ for each pair $(a,k)$, $a\in Q_1$, $1\leq k\leq k_a$, with 
    \[
    \theta_{a,k,+}^\star \coloneqq \begin{cases} -f_a'(\lambda_{a,1}), & k=1 \\ f_a'(\lambda_{a,k-1})-f_a'(\lambda_{a,k}), & k=2,\ldots,k_a \end{cases}
    \]
    and with an arrow to $t(a)$.
    We set $E^{\star}_{a,k,+}\coloneqq\cF^+(\rho(a))_{\lambda_k}$ and assign the inclusion map to the arrow.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition d.zdef of arXiv:2510.07682, 'From tug-of-war to Brownian Boost: \\ explicit ODE solutions for player-funded stochastic-'] For a sequence $h$, write as usual $\prod_{i=0}^k h_i = h_0 \cdots h_k$ for $k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$. A device extends this notation to negative $k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$: we set 
$$\prod_{i=0}^k h_i \, = \, \begin{cases}
  \, 1  &  \text{for $k=-1$} \\
 \,  h_{k+1}^{-1} \cdots h_{-1}^{-1}  &  \text{for $k \leq -2$} \, .
\end{cases}
$$
Let $x \in (0,\infty)$. This parameter will index four real-valued  sequences 
$$
a^{\rm def}(x),b^{\rm def}(x),m^{\rm def}(x),n^{\rm def}(x) :\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \to (0,\infty)
$$ 
which we denote in the form $\big\{ *^{\rm def}_i(x): i \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \big\}$  for $* \in \{a,b,m,n\}$. The resulting~$(a,b,m,n)$ is a normalized or `default' quadruple that (as we will state shortly) solves the \textrm{ABMN}  system. 

We first specify $m^{\rm def}(x):\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$. This increasing sequence is given by
\begin{equation}
m^{\rm def}_{-\infty}(x) = 0 \, , \, \, \, \, \textrm{and} \, \, \, \, m^{\rm def}_{k+1}(x)- m^{\rm def}_k(x) \, = \,  \kappa \prod_{i=0}^k \big( c_i(x) - 1 \big) \, \, \,  \textrm{for $k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$} \, ,
\end{equation}
in the notation of Definition~(d.stabc of the paper).
Note that $m^{\rm def}_0(x) - m^{\rm def}_{-1}(x) = \kappa$ in view of the product notation.

The decreasing sequence   $n^{\rm def}(x):\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ satisfies 
$$
n^{\rm def}_\infty(x) = 0 \, , \, \, \, \,   \textrm{and} \, \, \, \, n^{\rm def}_k(x)- n^{\rm def}_{k+1}(x)  \, = \, x \prod_{i=0}^k \big( d_i(x) - 1 \big) \, \, \,  \textrm{for $k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$} \, . 
$$
Note that $n^{\rm def}_{-1}(x) - n^{\rm def}_0(x) = \kappa x$.

To specify $a^{\rm def}(x),b^{\rm def}(x):\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} \to (0,\infty)$, we set 
$$
M_i(x) = m^{\rm def}_{i+1}(x) - m^{\rm def}_{i-1}(x)
  \, \, \, \, \textrm{and} \, \, \, \, N_i(x) = n^{\rm def}_{i-1}(x) - n^{\rm def}_{i+1}(x)
$$ 
for $i \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$. We further write 
$$
a^{\rm def}_i(x) = \frac{\kappa \rho \, M_i(x)^{1+\rho} N_i(x)^\rho}{\big(M_i(x)^\rho+N_i(x)^\rho\big)^2} \, \, \, \, \textrm{and} \, \, \, \, 
b^{\rm def}_i(x) = \frac{\kappa \rho  \,  M_i(x)^\rho N_i(x)^{1+\rho}}{\big(M_i(x)^\rho+N_i(x)^\rho\big)^2} \, .
$$
title: Definition d.zdef of arXiv:2510.07682

[Lemma lem:cond-pr-remask of arXiv:2608.23554, 'Provably adaptive sampling with uniform and remasking \\ discrete diffusion models'] Consider the remasking process with parameter \(p_M\) and let \(\rho = \sqrt{1 - p_M}\).
    Let \(0 \leq u < \ell\) with \(\Delta = \ell - u > 0\) and \(a, b \in \cV\). Then,
    \begin{equation*}
        \Pr(X_{\ell}^i = b \mid X_u^i = a) = \begin{cases}
             e^{-\Delta} \bI\{a = b\} + \frac{e^{-\Delta}}{S} (\cosh(\Delta \rho) - 1)&\text{if } a,b \in [S] \\
             e^{-\Delta} \rho \sinh(\Delta \rho)&\text{if } a \in [S], b = \mathrm{REMASK} \\
             1 - e^{-\Delta}(\cosh(\Delta \rho) + \rho \sinh(\Delta \rho))&\text{if } a \in [S], b = \mathrm{MASK}, \\
             \frac{e^{-\Delta}}{S} \frac{\sinh(\Delta\rho)}{\rho} &\text{if } a = \mathrm{REMASK}, b \in [S], \\
            e^{-\Delta} \cosh(\Delta \rho) &\text{if } a = b = \mathrm{REMASK}, \\
             1 - e^{-\Delta}\left(\cosh(\Delta \rho) + \frac{\sinh(\Delta \rho)}{\rho}\right)  &\text{if } a = \mathrm{REMASK}, b = \mathrm{MASK} \\
             1 &\text{if } a = b = \mathrm{MASK} \\
             0 &\text{otherwise.} \\
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation*}

[Theorem thm:exchangeable-reserve of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Let $d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H})=d<\infty$. Suppose that among the examples received by the learner are $r$ clean examples $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$, and let $Z_0$ be a fresh clean example. Assume that, after fixing all remaining examples and the clean information used to choose them, the examples $Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ remain exchangeable. Then the canonical one-inclusion learner satisfies
\[
    \mathbb{E} L_D(\widehat h,h^\star)
    \le
    \frac{d}{r+1}.
\]
The learner need not be told which observed examples constitute the exchangeable reserve. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exchangeable clean reserve

$\int_{\R}x\,\mu_j(dx)=0$,
and $\sigma_j^2:=\int_{\R}x^2\,\mu_j(dx)\in(0,\infty)$,

\begin{equation}
 \Delta(\mu^{(n)},\omega)
 \le  \frac{C}{B_n^{2+\delta}}\sum_{j=1}^n
 \int_{\R}|x|^{2+\delta}\,\mu_j(dx).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Fix 0<kappa<1/4. On Z^2 consider the homogeneous kernel

p(+e_1)=1/4+delta, p(-e_1)=1/4-delta,
p(+e_2)=p(-e_2)=1/4,

where 0<delta<=1/4-kappa. Its environment law is a Dirac mass at that row at each site, hence is spatially iid and kappa-uniformly elliptic. Its increments are iid. The strong law gives X_n/n -> (2delta,0), so it is directionally transient and ballistic in e_1. Nevertheless

sup_{0<delta<=1/4-kappa} E_0[sum_{n>=0} 1_{X_n=0}] = infinity,

while first exit from the singleton {0} takes exactly one step for every delta. Thus no law-independent upper bound for total occupation can follow from kappa, dimension, directional transience and the singleton residence bound alone. Every individual law in this example has finite Green function: it is not a counterexample to C0041 or to finiteness under a fixed iid law.

Proof of the divergence with explicit constants. At delta=0 the transformed coordinates Y=X^(1)+X^(2), Z=X^(1)-X^(2) are independent simple symmetric walks. Consequently

P_0(X_{2n}=0) = [binom(2n,n)/4^n]^2 >= 1/(4n), n>=1.

The elementary central-binomial lower bound binom(2n,n)>=4^n/(2sqrt(n)) follows by induction from n=1, since

binom(2n+2,n+1)/binom(2n,n)=4(1-1/(2n+2))
and (1-1/(2n+2))^2 >= n/(n+1).

Every path of length 2n under p_delta has probability at least (1-4delta)^(2n) times its p_0 probability. If delta<=1/(16N) and n<=N, Bernoulli's inequality gives (1-4delta)^(2n)>=1-8delta n>=1/2. Therefore its Green function is at least

1 + (1/8) sum_{n=1}^N 1/n.

Choose delta_N=min((1/4-kappa)/2,1/(16N)); these are positive, preserve the same ellipticity lower bound, and give the divergent harmonic lower bound.

Proof of finiteness for fixed delta. For theta=(1/2)log((1/4+delta)/(1/4-delta))>0,

P_delta(X_n=0) <= E_delta exp(-theta X_n^(1))
 = [1/2+2sqrt(1/16-delta^2)]^n.

The base is strictly below one, so the Green series is finite. The obstruction is to a uniform or purely local inference, not to each law separately.

Source: owner campaign derivation, w447, 2026-10-10. Original self-contained proof, no novelty asserted.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:047fe7ba9301b69651dcccf4db6a294172a65f26b81749f8dee021fee20973f4","revision_digest":"sha256:f148b099951e62f0e1d9faebed3462d371972d3ff40dda42036061d3570a739f","source_id":"urn:mb-source:e7d77f3a07e37aa4:w447:C0041:GO","source_revision":"2026-10-10","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2608.30551, 'Critical Discrete Hardy Inequalities in $L^p$'] Let $N \in \N$ and define $\xi_N \in C_c(\Z)$ as 
\[
\xi_N(x)
:=
\begin{cases}
1,
    & |x|\leq N,\\[1mm]
2-\dfrac{|x|}{N},
    & N<|x|<2N,\\[2mm]
0,
    & |x|\geq2N.
\end{cases}
\]
Then $0 \leq \xi_N(x) \leq 1$ and converges pointwise to $1$. Moreover, if 
$$
\alpha \leq \frac{2\sigma+a_p}{2(a_p+1)},
$$
then
$$
\sup_{N \in \N} \mathcal{M}_{p, \sigma, \alpha}(\xi_N) < \infty.
$$

[Lemma 15 (Global Gibbs tail) of arXiv:2607.20882, 'An Eyring--Kramers Law for the Hypoelliptic Third-Order\\ Langevin Diffusion'] Fix $\eps_0>0$.  For every $h_0>\inf_{z\in\R^{3d}}H(z)$ and
$0<\eps<\eps_0$, where $\inf_{z\in\R^{3d}}H(z)=\inf_{\theta\in\R^d}U(\theta)$,
\[
\int_{\{H(z)\ge h_0\}}e^{-H(z)/\eps}\,dz
\le Z_{\eps_0}
\exp\!\left(-\left(\frac1\eps-\frac1{\eps_0}\right)h_0\right).
\]
In particular, if $h_0>U(m)$, this tail is
$o(e^{-U(m)/\eps}\eps^N)$ for every fixed $N$.
title: Global Gibbs tail

Let (X,d) be a compact metric space of diameter at most one, with covering numbers N(X,epsilon)<=epsilon^(-d_x) for 0<epsilon<=1, where d_x>0. Let P be a Borel probability measure, and W:X x X->[0,cmax] a measurable symmetric kernel with 0<cmin<=d_P(x)=integral W(x,y)dP(y) and cmax<=1. Assume there is ONE partition X=X_1 union ... union X_q into q>=1 measurable pieces such that |W(x,y)-W(xprime,y)|<=cLip d(x,xprime) for every y and every x,xprime in the same piece. Let x_1,...,x_n be independent samples from P, and fix 0<rho<=1/2. For any fixed bounded Borel f:X->R, define T_X f(x)=n^(-1)sum_i W(x,x_i)f(x_i) and T_P f(x)=integral W(x,y)f(y)dP(y). There is a universal C such that, with probability at least 1-rho, sup_x |T_X f(x)-T_P f(x)| <= C ||f||_sup [cLip sqrt(d_x)+(cmax+cLip)sqrt(log(q/rho))]/sqrt(n). The card uses a common partition explicitly; it does not assert this bound merely from separate, y-dependent partitions. The confidence range rho<=1/2 is retained to absorb the standard two-sided tail constants.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation or source-specific limiting obstruction Result: Linear Debye screening gives the formal structure factor S(k)=|k|^2/(|k|^2+m^2), with m^2 proportional to beta times the background density. Its truncated-correlation Fourier transform is proportional to -m^2/(|k|^2+m^2). In two dimensions the inverse transform is a multiple of the modified Bessel function K0(m*r), whose large-distance behavior is proportional to exp(-m*r)/sqrt(m*r). Check: The resolvent of -Delta+m^2 has Fourier multiplier1/(|k|^2+m^2); its heat-kernel integral yields the positive radial K0 kernel. Thus screening formally creates an exponential length m^-1 rather than a Riesz power tail. Obstruction: The linear-response closure is not proved for the interacting Gibbs law. A rigorous result needs a uniform control of nonlinear correlations and error terms at distances beyond the screening length. The calculation identifies a mechanism, not a clustering theorem.

[Prop e:moment_main_bound of arXiv:2411.03482, 'Ergodicity of 2D singular stochastic Navier--Stokes equations'] For any initial data $u[0] = u_{\mathfrak{r}}[0] + u_{\mathfrak{s}}[0]$ with $\|u_{\mathfrak{s}}[0]\| = \lambda$ and $\|u_{\mathfrak{r}}[0]\|_{\mathcal{C}^{-\kappa}} \leq 2\alpha_0$, define $w^{\mathcal{L}}$ and stopping time $T$ as previously. Then there exists some constant $C$ which is independent of $N$, such that for any $0 < a < 1$ and $\alpha_0$ small enough (the smallness is independent of $N$), we have 
	\begin{equs}
	
		\mathbb{E} \Big(e^{\frac{T\wedge a}{2}} \|w^{\mathcal{L}}[T\wedge a]\|^{2N} &- \|w^{\mathcal{L}}[0]\|^{2N} \Big) \leq (C\alpha_0)^{2N} \lambda_+^{2N}a + (CN)^{N}a \quad \\
		&+ C^N \lambda_+^{2N} \int_0^a \mathbb{E} \left(\lambda_+^{\kappa} \|\mathcal{P}_{\lambda, K} \Tilde X\|_{\Besov{-\kappa}{4, \infty}} \right)^{2N/(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{500\kappa}{3})} \mathrm{d} t \\
		&+ C^N \lambda_+^{2N} \int_0^{a} \mathbb{E} \big( \lambda_+^{3N} \|\mathcal{H}_{\lambda} \Tilde X\|_{\Besov{-1/2}{4, 6N}}^{6N} \big)\mathrm{d} t \;.
	\end{equs} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

A continuous planar path and its one-dimensional polygonal approximations do not by themselves produce a one-dimensional Jordan arc contained in the path image. For the standard Koch arc, the similarity dimension is log(4)/log(3)>1 and every nontrivial internal Jordan arc has that dimension. This deterministic obstruction refutes the generic polygonal-approximation route; it asserts no dimension above one for a Brownian trace.
The standard Koch arc satisfies the stated self-similar Jordan-arc hypotheses
The usual open-set self-similar dimension theorem is an input

[Theorem LOT of arXiv:2604.11761, 'The smallest singular value of signed random combinatorial matrices'] For any $b>0$ and $\gamma \in(0,1)$ there exists $C>0$ depending only on $b$ and $\gamma$ for which the following holds. Let $v \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $\|\mathrm{D}(v)\|_2 \geq b \sqrt{n}$. Then for every $\alpha>0$ and $\varepsilon \geq 0$, we have

\begin{align*}
\mathcal{L}\left(W_{v}, \varepsilon\right) \leq C \varepsilon+\frac{C}{\operatorname{CLCD}_{\alpha, \gamma}(v)}+C e^{-2 \alpha^2 / n}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Thm aldous-efr-pfr of arXiv:2510.18856, 'Evolution of recursive trees with limited memory'] Fix a fringe distribution $\varpi \in \mathcal{M}_{\pr, {\sf fringe} }(\mathbb{T})$. Suppose a sequence of trees $\left\{\mathcal{T}_n:n\geqslant 1\right\}$ converges in the expected fringe sense $\mathcal{T}_n \stackrel{\mbox{$\E$-\bf fr}}{\longrightarrow} \varpi$ as $n\to\infty$. If $\varpi$ is extremal in the space of fringe measures, then the above convergence in expectation automatically implies $\mathcal{T}_n \stackrel{\mbox{$\operatorname{P}$-\bf fr}}{\longrightarrow} \varpi$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.00976, '\bfseries Lipshitz-Sarkar refines mirrors more than Khovanov'] The prime knot \(K=17nh_{0009090}\) is such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item for every pair of grading indices \((i,j)\),
\[
       \operatorname{Kh}^{i,j}(K;\mathbb Z)\cong \operatorname{Kh}^{i,j}(mK;\mathbb Z)
\]
as abelian groups, including all torsion (the isomorphisms need not be
canonical);
\item with coefficients in \(\mathbb F_2\),
\[
\begin{array}{c@{\qquad}c}
\toprule
\text{object} &
\operatorname{rank}\!\left(\operatorname{Sq}^2:\operatorname{Kh}^{-6,-9}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Kh}^{-4,-9}\right)\\
\midrule
K  & 1\\
mK & 0\\
\bottomrule
\end{array}
\]
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the quantum-graded Khovanov stable homotopy types of \(K\) and
its mirror are not equivalent, although their integral Khovanov homology
groups are identical.

body: In combinatorial mathematics and extremal set theory, the Sauer–Shelah lemma states that every family of sets with small VC dimension consists of a small number of sets. Here, the VC dimension is the largest size $k$ of a set with the property that all of its subsets can be formed by intersecting it with a member of the family. If the family has $n$ elements in its union, then the Sauer–Shelah lemma states that its number of sets is at most proportional to $n^{k}$.

[Theorem thm:krylov_lp_estimate of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] Let $p\ge2$, $\eta\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $\tau\le T$ be a bounded stopping time.
Assume that the coefficients of $L$ satisfy
Assumption (asp:coefficients of the paper). Suppose
\[
    u_0\in U_p^\eta,
    \qquad
    f\in\mathbb H_p^{\eta-2}(\tau),
    \qquad
    g\in\mathbb H_p^{\eta-1}(\tau,\ell_2).
\]
If $u\in\mathcal H_p^\eta(\tau)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm{d} u=(L u+f)\,\mathrm{d} t+\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}g^k\,\mathrm{d} w_t^k,
    \qquad
    u(0)=u_0,
\end{equation}
then
\[
    \|u\|_{\mathcal H_p^\eta(\tau)}
    \le
    N\left(
        \|u_0\|_{U_p^\eta}
        +
        \|f\|_{\mathbb H_p^{\eta-2}(\tau)}
        +
        \|g\|_{\mathbb H_p^{\eta-1}(\tau,\ell_2)}
    \right),
\]
where $N=N(p,\eta,\nu,T)$. 

Moreover, under the same assumptions, the equation (equation eq:SPDE1 of the paper) has a unique solution
$u\in\mathcal H_p^\eta(\tau)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Krylov's $L_p$-estimate, Theorem~5.1 of \cite{kry1999analytic}

[Proposition 12 (Risk recursion for Polyak) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] Under the gradient-noise covariance assumption, the expected excess risk obeys the two-sided recursion:
\begin{equation} 
    \EE[\cE(\btheta_k)]
    \eqsim
    \cS_{\polyak}(k)
    +
    \frac{\eta^2\sigma^2}{B}\sum_{\tau=0}^{k-1}\mathcal{K}_{\polyak}(\tau)
    +
    \frac{\eta^2}{B}\sum_{\tau=0}^{k-1}\mathcal{K}_{\polyak}(\tau)\EE[\cE(\btheta_{k-1-\tau})].
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the right-hand side provides both rigorous upper and lower bounds for the expected excess risk up to universal constant factors.

[Theorem thm : PointPoint of arXiv:2412.03320, 'Large deviation principle at speed $n$ for the random metric in first-passage percolation'] There exists a function $J_{\mathrm{pp}}  : \mathcal{X} \rightarrow \intervallefo0\infty$, such that for all $x,y\in X$ and $\zeta > a \norme[1]{x-y}$,
    \begin{equation}
        
        \lim_{n\to\infty}-\frac1n \log\Pb{ \vphantom{\BoxPT} \mathbf T\p{\!\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor nx \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor\!, \!\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor ny \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor\!} \le n \zeta } =  \lim_{n\to\infty} -\frac1n \log\Pb{ \BoxPT\p{\!\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor nx \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor\! ,\!\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor ny \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor\! } \le n\zeta } = J_{\mathrm{pp}} (x-y, \zeta),
    \end{equation}
    where $\floor\cdot$ denotes the componentwise floor function. Moreover:
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item
        
         $J_{\mathrm{pp}} $ is convex and absolutely homogeneous.
        \item
        
         For all $(x,\zeta)\in \mathcal{X}$,
        \begin{equation}
            J_{\mathrm{pp}} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft( x, \zeta \aftergroup\egroup\originalright) = J_{\mathrm{pp}} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft( \module x,\zeta \aftergroup\egroup\originalright),
        \end{equation}
        where $\module x$ denotes the vector of $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose components are the modules of $x$'s components. 
        
        \item 
        
        For all $(x_1,\zeta_1), (x_2,\zeta_2)\in \mathcal{X}$, if $0\le x_1 \le x_2$ for the componentwise order and $\zeta_1 \ge \zeta_2$, then
        \begin{equation}
            J_{\mathrm{pp}} (x_1, \zeta_1) \le J_{\mathrm{pp}} (x_2, \zeta_2).
        \end{equation}
        
        \item 
        
        For all $(x,\zeta) \in \mathcal{X}$, $J_{\mathrm{pp}} (x,\zeta)=0$ if and only if $\zeta \ge \mu(x)$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm : PointPoint of arXiv:2412.03320

[Lemma 44 of arXiv:2511.05386, 'CLT for $\beta$-ensembles with Freud weights, application to the KLS conjecture in Schatte'] Let $p>2$.
	For any $\alpha\in[0,1]$, the function $r_{\alpha}$ is $\cC^1(\R)\cap\cC^\infty(\R^*)$.
	Moreover, there exists $C,c>0$ such that for any $\alpha\in[0,1]$ and $\lambda\in \R$, 
	\[
	c \left( 1+\alpha \abs{\lambda}^{p-2} \right) \leq r_{\alpha}(\lambda) \leq C \left( 1+\alpha \abs{\lambda}^{p-2} \right), 
	\qquad
	\abs{r_{\alpha}'(\lambda)} \leq \begin{cases}
	    C \alpha & \text{if } p \leq 3, \\
	    C \alpha (1+\abs{\lambda})^{p-3} & \text{if } p > 3, 
	\end{cases} 
	\]
	and, if $\lambda \neq 0$, 
	\[
	\abs{r_{\alpha}''(\lambda)} 
	\leq \begin{cases}
	    C \alpha \abs{\lambda}^{p-3} & \text{if } p < 3, \\
	    C \alpha (1+(\log1/\abs{\lambda})_+) & \text{if } p = 3, \\
	    C \alpha (1+\abs{\lambda})^{p-4} & \text{if } p >3.
	\end{cases}
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:singleton-order-sum of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $\mathsf M_j$ be any typed passive copy of the coordinate pure-Weyl
multiplier in (lem:singleton-renewal of the paper), with arbitrary passive
Hilbert-space amplification.  Put
\[
 \mathsf V_j=\mathsf Q\mathsf M_j\mathsf Q,
 \qquad A_j=\mathscr E\mathsf M_j\mathscr T,
 \qquad \mathfrak H_a=\mathscr G\mathcal K^a\mathscr G^*.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathscr T^*\mathsf M_j\mathscr T
 =\mathscr E\mathsf M_j\mathscr E^*=0,
 \qquad
 \mathscr G^*\mathsf V_j\mathscr G
 =-\mathcal KA_j-A_j^*\mathcal K.
\tag{3.2.10q$_1$}
\]
There is a numerical $C$ such that
\[
 \sum_{a,b\ge0}
 \|\mathfrak H_a\mathsf V_j\mathfrak H_b\|
 \le C\frac{\log(n+2)}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{3.2.10q$_2$}
\]
Consequently, for every fixed $L<\infty$ there is $A_L<\infty$ such
that a passive-singleton component with $2\le s\le L\log n$ labelled
vertices satisfies, after summing every strict chronological order and
every allowed finite-gap simplex,
\[
 \sum_{\sigma\in S_s}
 \|\mathcal X_{s,\sigma}\|
 \le \frac{A_L^s}{N}.
\tag{3.2.10q$_3$}
\]
After the proved circuit-anchored root/pass rewrite, its one free
translation, and a fixed terminal ribbon gluing, its scalar contribution is at most
$A_L^s(m/N)\mathfrak a_\Gamma$, where
$\mathfrak a_\Gamma$ is the positive projective majorant of the already
normalized non-temporal atom.
The same conclusion holds for several Haar-separated passive-singleton
components after their labelled vertex sets have been fixed, with one
factor $m/N$ per component and no interleaving multinomial.  This last
sentence does not sum over varying component-label decompositions; the
physical maximal passive-only components are instead annihilated exactly
in (lem:haar-passive-zero of the paper) below.

body: Publication record. In the critical beta-splitting random tree a clade of m leaves splits into clades of i and m - i leaves with probability proportional to 1/(i(m - i)); the drawn length of a binary tree is the total length of the vertical lines of its cladogram, each vertex drawn at the level of its height. Open Problem 14 of D. J. Aldous and S. Janson, The critical beta-splitting random tree II: overview and open problems, asks for a proof that the expected drawn length L_n grows roughly like n log^4 n. Y. Shmalo, The drawn length of the critical beta-splitting tree grows linearly (2026) shows instead that L_n/n converges to a finite constant lambda with 4.800 < lambda < 5.372 (lambda ≈ 4.88 numerically). Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/beta-splitting-drawn-length (commit 536da55fafcf). Not refereed; an independent read is owed.
title: Aldous-Janson Open Problem 14 (critical beta-splitting tree) answered: the expected drawn length grows linearly, L_n/n -> lambda with 4.800 < lambda < 5.372, not like n log^4 n (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/beta-splitting-drawn-length)

body:
[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2604.10891, '2604.10891'] If $\rho < 1$ and $\E[V] < \infty$, the LST $d^*(s)$ of the system delay $D$
in the stationary FIFO system is given by

\begin{equation}
d^*(s) 
=
\frac{(1-\rho)s h^*(s)}{s - \lambda + \lambda h^*(s)}
\bigg[
\frac{\ell_{\rm E}^*(0)}{\lambda\E[V]+\ell_{\rm E}^*(0)}
+
\frac{\lambda\E[V]}{\lambda\E[V]+\ell_{\rm E}^*(0)}
\cdot
\frac{d_{\rm E}^*(s)}{v^*(s)}
\cdot
\frac{1-v^*(s)}{\E[V]s}
\bigg],

\end{equation}

where 

\[
d_{\rm E}^*(s)
=
\prod_{k=1}^{\infty} \zeta_k^V(s)
-
\ell_E^*(0)
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
\big( 1 - \zeta_n^H(s) \big) \prod_{k=1}^n \zeta_k^V(s),
\]

and $\zeta_k^H(s)$ and $\zeta_k^V(s)$ are determined recursively by

\begin{align*}
\zeta_1^H(s) 
&=
h^*(s)
\qquad
\zeta_n^H(s) 
= 
\psi_{n-1}^H\big(h^*(s)\big),
\quad 
n=2,3,\ldots
\\
\zeta_1^V(s) 
&=
v^*(s), 
\qquad 
\zeta_n^V(s) = v^*\big(\lambda-\lambda \zeta_{n-1}^H(s)\big),
\quad 
n=2,3,\ldots.
\end{align*}

The $n$th ($n=1,2,\ldots$) moment $\overline{D}^{(n)}$ of $D$ is given by

\begin{equation}
\overline{D}^{(n)}
=
\frac{\overline{L}^{(n)}}{\lambda^n},
\quad
n=1,2,\ldots.
}
\end{equation}

$$
where $C_n\to 0$
and  $H_{j}$ are polynomials not depending on $n$.

[Theorem thm.highdim of arXiv:2609.01189, 'The lower mean curvature bound in Gromov's mean-of-the-mean-curvature conjecture'] For each integer $n\ge3$, there exists a compact connected $n$-dimensional spin manifold $X$ with nonempty smooth boundary and a $1$-parameter family of Riemannian metrics $g_a$ on $X$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item
the scalar curvature $\ScalOp_{g_a}\equiv 0$ for every $a>0$,
\item
the induced metric on the boundary $\partial X$ is independent of $a$,
\item
$\int_{\partial X}H_{g_a}\to\infty$ as $a\to0$, where $H_{g_a}$ is the mean curvature of $\partial X$ w.r.t.\ the outward unit normal,
\item
$\min_{\partial X}H_{g_a}\to-\infty$ as $a\to0$.
\end{enumerate}
If $n\ge5$, then (thm.highdim1 of the paper) can be replaced by 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)']
\item
the scalar curvature $\ScalOp_{g_a}\equiv C$ for every $a>0$ and any prescribed constant $C\in\mathbb{R}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm.highdim of arXiv:2609.01189

[Theorem thm:boltzmann_gibbs of arXiv:2601.04997, 'Fluctuations of the Boundary-Driven Symmetric Zero-Range Process from the NESS'] If (equation assumption:g_bdd of the paper) holds, then for every continuous function $G:[0, 1]\to\mathbb{R}$ and every $t>0$,
\begin{equation}
    \mylim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E}_{\bar\nu_N }\left[\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\int_0^t\sum_{x=2}^{N-2}G\left(\frac{x}{N}\right)\tau_x V_N(\eta_s)\de s\right)^2\right]=0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Boltzmann-Gibbs Principle

Own-work auxiliary proof draft (unaudited); no novelty priority claimed. Fix any oracle O. Let P_L be given by a uniform polynomial-time O-relative evaluator of nonnegative rational weights with polynomial numerator/denominator bit bounds and positive normalizer. Suppose a polynomial-size nonuniform dyadic AR proposal R_L has polynomial next-bit precision and P_L(x)<=D(L)R_L(x) pointwise, for an integer-valued polynomial D>=1. For every fixed positive integer c there is a polynomial-size nonuniform dyadic AR Q_L with KL(P_L||Q_L)<L^(-c). Conditional importance sampling with K=(1024 D L^(2c+2))^2 samples per position, globally shared random tapes, and one dyadic normalizer-scale exponent suffices; smoothing and output rounding bound KL by (47/120)L^(-c). Exact normalization, a sampler for P and distributional inversion are not assumed. The domination premise itself also yields nonuniform inverse-polynomial-TV sampling by bounded rejection. No common oracle with NP circuit hardness and domination proposals for all efficiently weighted laws has been constructed. This does not settle Target 2 or assert that the premise follows from IR2.
Uniform polynomial-time O-relative rational weight evaluator; known polynomial numerator/denominator bit bound; Z_L>0
Polynomial-size nonuniform O-relative AR proposal with polynomial dyadic precision and pointwise P_L<=D(L)R_L for an integer polynomial D>=1

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:7f48ea00b06eac61a7d3de865d18e29f986464964f5d95df60f3913c79888486","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/7f/7f48ea00b06eac61a7d3de865d18e29f986464964f5d95df60f3913c79888486.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:e6f8938fd0964f6bdec71311b16a459f94b9a6dcb22372c6c194227f52f9e1ff","bundle_entry_key":"importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","bundle_id":"population.t410-importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"autoregressive distributions; importance sampling; oracle computational complexity; forward KL; nonuniform circuits","draft":"w739/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:importance-weighted-dominated-autoregressive-proposals","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Polynomial domination by an AR proposal suffices for forward-KL approximation

T410-w739-C012 v1. Kind: auxiliary sufficient-condition lemma. Target: 2.
Status: proof (unaudited). Own-work draft; no novelty priority claimed.
This is an alternative sufficient condition, not a construction of the target oracle.

## Statement and unpaid obligation

Fix an oracle O. For each integer L>=1 let P_L(x)=w_L(x)/Z_L on
{0,1}^L. The nonnegative rational weights w_L are uniformly polynomial-time
computable relative to O, not all zero, and their numerator and positive
denominator have bit lengths at most a known polynomial b(L).

Assume a polynomial-size nonuniform oracle autoregressive proposal R_L:
its next-bit probabilities are exactly evaluable dyadics with common
precision B(L), a polynomial. Assume further that

    P_L(x) <= D(L) R_L(x) for every x,                         (1)

where D>=1 is an integer-valued polynomial. Then for each fixed positive
integer c there is a polynomial-size nonuniform oracle autoregressive Q_L
whose next-bit probabilities are dyadic and

    KL(P_L || Q_L) <= (47/120) L^(-c) < L^(-c).              (2)

Natural logarithms are used. All circuits use the same oracle O. Their
size exponent may depend on c and on the polynomial bounds. The uniform
weight evaluator is a single algorithm; the proposal and resulting Q may
have length-dependent advice. For any fixed positive real requested
exponent one can instead use its integer ceiling.

The hardest unpaid step for Target 2 is to construct ONE oracle with
NP^O not contained in P^O/poly and, for EVERY efficient-weight law, a
proposal satisfying (1). This proof supplies no such oracle or universal
proposal. It does not derive (1) from the reported IR2 result, assert
equivalence with C003's sampler/inverter criterion, or settle Target 2.

## 1. Only a short scale advice is needed

The weight representation implies 2^(-b)<=Z_L<=2^(b+L). Choose the
integer a=ceil(log_2 Z_L) as nonuniform advice and set A=2^a. Then

    Z_L <= A <= 2 Z_L,       z:=Z_L/A belongs to [1/2,1].

The signed exponent a uses O(log(b+L+1)) bits; the rational A itself has
polynomial representation length. We do NOT assume the exact rational Z
has polynomial bit length: arbitrary rational weight denominators need
not share a small common denominator.

For R(x)>0 put h(x)=w(x)/(A R(x)); set h=0 when R(x)=0. Domination
ensures P(x)=w(x)=0 on the latter set. Consequently

    0 <= h(x) <= D,          E_R h = z.

Computing h takes polynomial-size exact rational arithmetic: R(x) is a
product of L polynomial-bit dyadics, and w,A have polynomial bit length.
Hereafter L subscripts are omitted.

## 2. Conditional importance estimates and change of measure

For a prefix s of length i<L with R(s)>0, define

    a_s=E_R[h(X)|s],    b_s=E_R[h(X) 1{X_(i+1)=1}|s].

Then P(s)=R(s)a_s/z. When P(s)>0 the true next-bit probability is
p_s=b_s/a_s. Draw K independent suffix samples from R(.|s). This is an
exact ancestral sampler: each next-bit dyadic of precision B uses B fair
bits, so at most LB random bits per sample. Let ahat_s,bhat_s be the
sample means of h and h times the next-bit indicator. Define

    g_s=bhat_s/ahat_s if ahat_s>0; otherwise g_s=1/2.

We always have 0<=g_s<=1 and ahat_s*g_s=bhat_s, including the zero
denominator case because nonnegative h forces bhat_s=0 there. Thus

    a_s |g_s-p_s| <= |a_s-ahat_s|+|b_s-bhat_s|.             (3)

This follows by writing a_s*g_s-b_s as
(a_s-ahat_s)*g_s+(bhat_s-b_s). Each sample variable lies in [0,D], so
variance of each mean is at most D^2/K. By Cauchy-Schwarz its mean
absolute error is at most D/sqrt(K). Multiply (3) by R(s)/z and sum over
prefixes with P(s)>0. Since their R masses sum to at most one and z>=1/2,

    sum_s P(s) E |g_s-p_s| <= 4D/sqrt(K)                   (4)

at every position. Prefixes of zero P mass contribute zero. At an
R-null prefix output 1/2 directly; it is P-null by (1).

No sample from P, normalizer computation, or distributional inversion
was used. In particular we did not require an accuracy guarantee at
each one of exponentially many prefixes.

## 3. One polynomial table of shared tapes

At each position select K independent tapes of length LB. Use these
SAME tapes to evaluate the conditional sampler at every prefix of that
length. For each FIXED prefix its K samples have exactly the independent
law used above. Evaluations at different prefixes may be correlated;
only linearity of expectation over prefixes is used in (4).

There are L*K*L*B advice bits, not a tape table indexed by all prefixes.
For any fixed advice table, evaluation runs K ancestral samplers and
computes their exact rational sample means. Adding K polynomial-bit
rationals can increase bit length by at most a polynomial factor K;
division and the other arithmetic therefore have polynomial circuits.
This remains true when the proposal itself has nonuniform advice.

## 4. Smoothing, KL, and explicit sample count

Write eta=L^(-c), epsilon=eta/(16L), and choose the perfect square

    K = (1024 D L^(2c+2))^2.

This is polynomial for fixed c. Let q_s=epsilon+(1-2epsilon)g_s at
R-positive prefixes, so q_s is in [epsilon,1-epsilon]. Also

    |p_s-q_s| <= |p_s-g_s|+epsilon,
    (p_s-q_s)^2 <= 2|p_s-g_s|+2epsilon^2.

For Bernoulli parameters p in [0,1], q in (0,1), the inequality
log t<=t-1, applied to each nonzero P term, gives

    kl(p||q) <= (p-q)^2/[q(1-q)].                          (5)

The same formula holds at p=0,1 by the zero-mass convention. Chain rule
for forward KL, (4), and (5) yield

    E KL(P||Q) <= [8DL/sqrt(K)+2L epsilon^2]
                         /[epsilon(1-epsilon)].          (6)

Here sqrt(K)=64DL/(eta epsilon). Each of the two terms in (6) equals
eta/[8(1-epsilon)]. Since epsilon<=1/16, their sum is at most
(4/15)eta. This calculation averages over a finite, polynomial-length
random table, not over independent conditional errors along a P path.

## 5. Polynomial-bit dyadic outputs

Choose an integer t with Delta=2^(-t)<=eta epsilon/(16L), for example
t=ceil(log_2(256 L^(2c+2))). Replace q_s by

    qhat_s = floor(2^t q_s)/2^t.

Then |qhat_s-q_s|<=Delta and qhat_s>=epsilon/2, while both complementary
probabilities are at least epsilon/2. The derivative of log on this
range is at most 2/epsilon. For every fixed random table, each next-bit
log probability changes in absolute value by at most 2Delta/epsilon.
The chain rule therefore gives

    KL(P||Qhat) <= KL(P||Q)+2L Delta/epsilon
                <= KL(P||Q)+eta/8.

Use qhat=1/2 at R-null prefixes. Averaging shows

    E KL(P||Qhat) <= (4/15+1/8)eta = (47/120)eta.

Some single finite table has loss at most this average. Fix it as advice.
The resulting Qhat is a normalized AR law with polynomial-size oracle
circuits and t-bit dyadic next probabilities. This proves (2).

## Scope and validation

The proposal premise already implies NONUNIFORM approximate sampling of
P, although the proof above does not invoke such a sampler. Indeed draw
X from R and accept it with probability h(X)/D, using a fresh uniform
number in [0,1]. The acceptance probability is z/D>=1/(2D), and the
accepted law is exactly P. Rational acceptance probabilities can instead
be rounded DOWN to dyadics of mesh delta. The acceptance probability
decreases by at most delta and the accepted law changes in total
variation by at most 2D delta, provided delta<=1/(4D): if v(x) is the
unnormalized accepted mass and v'(x)<=v(x), their missing total mass e
is at most delta, and TV(v/alpha,v'/(alpha-e))<=e/alpha<=2D delta.
The rounded success probability is at least 1/(4D). Truncating after
T independent proposals adds at most (1-1/(4D))^T to the TV error.
For a requested inverse-polynomial error rho, choose dyadic
delta<=rho/(4D) and T>=4D ln(2/rho). Thus a strict polynomial-time
NONUNIFORM dyadic sampler with TV error at most rho follows. Its
normalizer-scale advice and the proposal advice need not be uniform.
This implication is an explicit limitation of the sufficient condition,
not a contradiction to it or a uniform sampling theorem for the oracle.

This proof is a sufficient-condition derivation, not a novelty claim or
an independently checked proof. Finite rational diagnostics check (3),
the prefix change-of-measure identity, and the constants, with an omitted-
denominator negative control. They do not prove the asymptotic theorem
by enumeration. No enormous K sample run is proposed or performed.
The condition (1) must be established before applying this to any
particular oracle or weight family. Target 1 C001 v2 remains subject to
independent review; Target 2 remains OPEN.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:cd6159c155b54a445d85ded8bfe2169b8fbff887b41d8a66fa0cb61f5b912613","revision_digest":"sha256:f19892a156489aea3c44cdeab77ef7112d4b9e56b7b483fe2d21b6bdf47d45f1","source_id":"own-work:T410-w739-C012-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T22:53:13.841333+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma lem.nondeg of arXiv:2609.01007, 'Global universality of the expected number \\of zeros of non-analytic random signals'] Suppose that the base function $f$ satisfies Condition $(\mathbf{H2})$, in particular $f$ is of class $\mathcal C^{q}$, with $q=7$. Then, for $n$ large enough, the covariance matrix with respect to $\mathbb{P} \otimes \mathbb{P}_X$ of the random vector $Z_n=\left(g_n(0),g_n'(0),\dots, g_n^{(q-1)}(0)\right)$ is positive definite. In other words, there exists $\kappa>0$ such that, for $n$ large enough and for all $\lambda=(\lambda_0,\dots, \lambda_{q-1})\in {\rm I\kern-0.16em R}^{q}$, we have
\[
\sigma_n^2(\lambda) :=\mathbb{E}_{\mathbb{P}_X\otimes \mathbb{P}}\left[\left(\lambda \cdot Z_n\right)^2\right] \geq \kappa \sum_{i=0}^{q-1} \lambda_i^2 .
\]

AUTHOR PROOF; independent audit pending. For each epsilon in (0,1), delta_star=1-sqrt(1-epsilon) is the largest delta in (0,1] such that the following implication holds for every finite forest G, independent Bernoulli edge probabilities in [0,1], vertices o,b and nonempty relay set A: if P(o connects to A)>1-delta and P(a connects to b)>1-delta for all a in A, then P(o connects to b)>1-epsilon. A two-edge path rules out every larger delta, so delta_star is also a necessary upper bound on any proposed all-finite-graph modulus. Its sufficiency for arbitrary cyclic graphs is not asserted.
Independent Bernoulli bond states with arbitrary edge probabilities in [0,1]
Nonempty relay set
Strict premises and conclusion as in Kozma-Nitzan Conjecture 3

body:
[Theorem 36 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Assume that the family of vector fields \( \{V_\alpha\}_{\alpha=1}^d \) is equiregular and satisfies Hypotheses \ref{h1} and \ref{1.2}. Let \( Y \) be the solution to equation \eqref{density1}, driven by a \( d \)-dimensional fractional Brownian motion \( B \) with Hurst parameter \( H \in \left(\frac{1}{4}, 1\right) \). Then, for any fixed real numbers \( 0 < a < b \), \( M > 0 \), \( \eta_1 > 0 \), and \( 0 < \eta_2 < 1/H \), there exist strictly positive constants
\[
C_1 = C_1(a, b, V, H, M, n, \eta_1, Q), \quad C_2 = C_2(a, b, V, H, M, n, \eta_2, Q)
\]
such that for all compact sets \( A \subset B_d(o,M) \),
\begin{equation}
C_2 \, \mathrm{Cap}_{Q - 1/H + \eta_2}(A)
\ \leqslant\
\mathbb{P}(Y([a,b]) \cap A \neq \emptyset)
\ \leqslant\
C_1 \, \mathrm{Cap}_{Q - 1/H - \eta_1}(A),
\end{equation}
where \( Q \) is the homogeneous dimension defined in Definition~\ref{defofhomodim}. In particular, if $Q=N$, then $\eta_2$ can be chosen to be $0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 36 of arXiv:2512.07202

body:
[Proposition 201 (Identification of the most difficult error terms in the commuted wave equations) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\velocityarray \eqdef (v^1,v^2,v^3)$ 
be solutions to the covariant wave equations \eqref{E:COVARIANTWAVEEQUATIONSWAVEVARIABLES}. We denote the product of $\upmu$ and the RHS of the covariant wave equation satisfied by 
$v^i$ by $\mathfrak{G}_{i}$, 
i.e., 
$\upmu \Box_{\gfour} v^i = \mathfrak{G}_{i}$. \begin{subequations}  
\begin{align} 
\upmu \Box_{\gfour} (\tanderY^{N-1} \Lunit v^i) 
& 
= 
\angrmd^{\sharp} v^i  \cdot \upmu \angrmd \tanderY^{N-1} \mytr_{\gtorus}\upchi 
+ 
\tanderY^{N-1} \Lunit \mathfrak{G}_{i} 
+ 
\HarmlessWave{N},	
	\\
\begin{split} 
\upmu \Box_{\gfour} (\tanderY^{N-1}\Yvf{A} v^i) 
& 
= 
(\muX v^i)  \tanderY^{N-1} \Yvf{A} \mytr_{\gtorus} \upchi 
+ 
(\Speed^{-2} X^A) \angrmd^{\sharp} v^i \cdot \upmu \angrmd \tanderY^{N-1} \mytr_{\gtorus}\upchi 
\\
& \ \
+ 
\tanderY^{N-1}\Yvf{A} \mathfrak{G}_{i} 
+ 
\HarmlessWave{N}. 
\end{split}
\end{align}Moreover, if $1 \leq N \leq \Ntop$ and $\tander^N$
denotes any order $N$ string of $\mathcal{P}_u$-tangent commutator
other than the ones appearing on LHSs~\eqref{E:TOPCOMMUTEDWAVELFIRSTTHENALLYS}--\eqref{E:TOPCOMMUTEDWAVEALLYS},
(i.e., if $\tander^N$ features at least two copies of $\Lunit$ or only a single $\Lunit$ but does not act first like it does in
\eqref{E:TOPCOMMUTEDWAVELFIRSTTHENALLYS}), 
then $\tander^N v^i$ obeys the following wave equation:
\begin{align} 
\upmu \Box_{\gfour} (\tander^N v^i) 
	& = 
	\tander^N \mathfrak{G}_i
	+ 
	\HarmlessWave{N}.
\end{align}
\end{subequations}

[Definition1 Defbad of arXiv:2603.05491, '\textbf{Local limits of uniform triangulations with boundaries in high genus}'] Fix $A,a > 0$ and $t \in \mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{p}^n}(n,g_n)$. Let $i \in \{1,\cdots,\ell_n\}$ and $e \in \partial_i t$. Fix a peeling algorithm $\mathcal{A}$. Fix $j \ge 0$ and assume that $\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e)$ is a planar triangulation with one hole. We say that step $j+1$ is $\mathbf{BAD}^{\mathcal{A}}(A,a)$ (see Figure~(badcases of the paper)) if it satisfies one of the conditions below:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item  The triangulation $\bigg((t,e) \backslash \bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e),\mathcal{A}(\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e))\bigg)$ satisfies $\mathcal{L}_k^{\mathrm{nsep}}$ or $\mathcal{R}_k^{\mathrm{nsep}}$ with $k \in \{0,\cdots,A-1\}$.
    \item  The triangulation $\bigg((t,e) \backslash \bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e),\mathcal{A}(\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e))\bigg)$ satisfies $\mathcal{L}_k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ (resp. $\mathcal{R}_k^{\mathrm{sep}}$) with $k \in \{0,\cdots,A-1\}$, and writing $t_1$ for the component filling the left hole (resp. the right hole), we have $t_1 \notin \bigsqcup_{i=0}^{a}\mathcal{T}_{k+1}(i,0)$.
     \item  The triangulation $\bigg((t,e) \backslash \bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e),\mathcal{A}(\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e))\bigg)$ satisfies $(\mathcal{H}_{A+1})$.
    \item  The triangulation $\bigg((t,e) \backslash \bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e),\mathcal{A}(\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j}(t,e))\bigg)$ satisfies $(\mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}
 Otherwise, it is said to be $\mathbf{GOOD}^{\mathcal{A}}(A,a)$. Note that if step $j+1$ is $\mathbf{GOOD}^{\mathcal{A}}(A,a)$, then $\bar{\mathcal{E}}^{\mathcal{A}}_{j+1}(t,e)$ is again a planar triangulation with one hole.
title: Definition1 Defbad of arXiv:2603.05491

body:
Let Z be a random finite measure on D with total mass T>0 almost surely and 0<E[T]<infinity. Put U_A=Z(A)/T. Then E[Z(A)]/E[T]-E[U_A]=Cov(T,U_A)/E[T] for each measurable A. Consequently mean normalized measure equals normalized mean measure exactly when Cov(T,U_A)=0 for every A. Independence of total mass and normalized measure is sufficient but unnecessary: three equally likely outcomes T=(1,2,3), U_first=(1,0,1) on two sites give both averages (2/3,1/3), yet T and the normalized measure are dependent. No integrability or independence claim for DGFF extremal mass is inferred from this finite example.

body:
[Thm 7 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional $(n \geq 2)$ forward complete Finsler metric measure manifold with $\Lambda_F<\infty$. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$.
Given constants $p \in (\frac{n}{2}, n]$, $\alpha\in [\frac{1}{2},1)$ and a fixed point $x_{0}\in M$. Then,  for $0 \leq r < R_{0}$ and an arbitrarily fixed point $x\in M$ satisfying that $d_{F}(x_{0}, x) \leq \Lambda_{F}^{-1}\left( R_{0}-r\right)$, there exist positive constants $D_{1}=D_{1}(n, p, \vartheta , R_{0})$ and $D_{2}=D_{2}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$, such that, when $\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}<D_{1}^{-\frac{2p-1}{p}}$, we have
\beq
&& \left(\frac{m\left(B_{\Lambda_{F}^{-1}r}^{+}(x)\right)}{m\left(B_{R_{0}}^{+}(x_{0})\right)}\right)^{\frac{1}{2 p-1}} \geq  \Big[\frac{1}{4} \left(1-D_{1} \overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}\right)
e^{-\frac{\vartheta R_{0}}{2 p-1}}\Lambda_{F}^{-\left(2 \vartheta R_{0}b(p,\alpha)+\frac{5n}{2p-1}\right)}   \nonumber \\
&& \times \left(\frac{r}{R_{0}}\right)^{\vartheta R_{0} b(p,\alpha)+\frac{4n-2p}{2p-1}}  -  \frac{D_{2}\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}}{1-D_{1} \overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}} \Big] \left(\frac{r}{R_{0}}\right)^{\frac{2p-n}{2p-1}}, 
\eeq
where
\beqn
&& D_{1}(n,p,\vartheta,R_{0}):=D(n, p) e^{\frac{2 p+1}{2 p-1} \vartheta R_{0}} R_{0}^{\frac{2p}{2 p-1}},  \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ D(n, p):=\frac{n(n-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2 p-1}}(2 p-1)^{\frac{p}{2 p-1}}}{(2 p-n)^\frac{3p-2}{2p-1}},    \\
&& D_{2}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0}):=\frac{D_{1}(n,p,\vartheta,R_{0}) e^{\frac{\vartheta R_{0}}{2 p-1}} \Lambda_{F}^{-\frac{2p-n}{2p-1}}}{1-e^{-\frac{\vartheta R_{0}}{2p-1}}(2-\alpha)^{\frac{2p-2n}{2p-1}}\alpha^{\frac{n}{2p-1}} }, \ \ \  b(p,\alpha):=\frac{1}{(2p-1)\ln(2-\alpha)}.
\eeqn

[Lemma 25 (Stage preparation, stability, and regular restart) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] There are constants
\[
        K_{\mathrm{st}}<\infty,\qquad \Lambda_*<\infty,
        \qquad \beta_{\mathrm{reg}}>0,\qquad C_{\mathrm{st}}<\infty,
\]
depending only on \(K,N,\sigma\), with the following property.  For every
\(0<\beta_*\leq\beta_{\mathrm{reg}}\), there is a constant
\(\eta_{\mathrm{st}}>0\), depending only on \(K,N,\sigma,\beta_*\), such that the following holds.
Let \(p(\tau)\) be any parabolically rescaled \(\delta_0\)-large block, for
some \(\delta_0\geq c_0\), under the standing fixed-threshold application.
Fix the torus structure used during this
stage and put
\[
        q(1)=p(1),\qquad r(1)=\overline{q(1)}.
\]
Put
\[
        b:=\|q(1)-r(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r(1))}.
\]
Assume that \(r(1)\) is Riemannian,
\(\BG_N(r(1);\Lambda_*)\) holds, and \(b<\eta_{\mathrm{st}}\).  These are
exactly the analytic start conditions in
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-stage-start}, with
\(\Lambda=\Lambda_*\) and \(\eta=\eta_{\mathrm{st}}\).
Then the invariant Ricci flow \(r(\tau)\) and the Ricci--DeTurck flow
\(q(\tau)\) relative to it exist on \([1,100]\), and
\begin{align}
        |\sec_{r(\tau)}|&\leq K_{\mathrm{st}}/\tau,
                &&1\leq\tau\leq100,                               \\
        \|q-r\|_{X_r^N[1,100]}
                &<\beta_*,                                         \\
        \|q-r\|_{X_r^N[1,100]}
                &\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.                                 
\end{align}
If
\[
        q^+(1)=100^{-1}q(100),\qquad
        \rho^+=100^{-1}r(100),\qquad
        r^+(1)=\overline{q^+(1)},
\]
then \(r^+(1)\) is Riemannian, \(\BG_N(r^+(1);\Lambda_*)\) holds,
\(|\sec_{r^+(1)}|\leq K_{\mathrm{st}}\), and
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 &\|q^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N+5,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}
 +\|r^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N+5,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}\\
 &\qquad\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
        \|r^+(1)-\rho^+\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,\rho^+)}
        \leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:usa-facts of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\mathcal{Y},\hat\mathcal{Z},T)$ satisfy Condition~(cond:usa-minimax of the paper).
  Let $t \in \{0,\ldots,T-1\}$.
  Let $X:\mathcal{Y}^T\to\mathbb{R}$ be bounded and upper semi-analytic.
  Then the following hold.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item Per-round minimax duality: $\overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}}[X \mid s] = \overline{\mathbb{E}}^* [X \mid s]$ when $t=T-1$.
  \item The map $\mathcal{Y}^t \ni s \mapsto \overline{\mathbb{E}}^*[X \mid s]$ is upper semi-analytic.
  \item The tower property of $\overline{\mathbb{E}}^*$: $\overline{\mathbb{E}}^*[\overline{\mathbb{E}}^*[X \mid Y_{1..t}]] = \overline{\mathbb{E}}^* X$.

Abel's theorem (the Abelian direction): if the series sum a_n converges to s, then the power series f(x) = sum a_n x^n converges for |x| < 1 and f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below. The converse is false in general: f(x) = sum (-1)^n x^n = 1/(1 + x) tends to 1/2 while sum (-1)^n diverges. Tauber's theorem (the Tauberian direction): if f(x) = sum a_n x^n converges for |x| < 1, f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below, and n a_n -> 0, then sum a_n converges to s. Littlewood strengthened the condition to a_n = O(1/n) (Littlewood's Tauberian theorem, 1911), and Hardy and Littlewood showed that a one-sided bound n a_n >= -C also suffices. 'Abelian' theorems pass from a summability method's convergence to a weaker one; 'Tauberian' theorems go back under an extra growth condition on the terms.
Abel: sum a_n converges
Tauber: f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below and n a_n -> 0 (Littlewood: a_n = O(1/n) suffices, with a harder proof)

[Lemma 6 (Localized empirical-process bound) of arXiv:2608.22179, '\bf Token-Level Likelihood-Array Regression for Membership Inference and AI-Generated Text'] Let \(Z\) be a centered Hilbert-space feature with covariance operator \(\Gamma_Z\),
and let
\(f^\circ(Z)=\alpha^\circ+\ip{\theta^\circ}{Z}\) be any fixed score. For
\(a,b>0\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\E\sup_{\delta,h}\Big[&(P-P_n)
\left\{
\ell_Y\bigl(f^\circ(Z)+\delta+\ip{h}{Z}\bigr)
-\ell_Y\bigl(f^\circ(Z)\bigr)
\right\}\\
&-a\{\delta^2+\norm{h}_{\Gamma_Z}^2\}-b\norm{h}^2\Big]
\leq
\frac{C}{an}\{1+\mathcal N_{\Gamma_Z}(b/a)\}.
\end{aligned}

\end{equation}
The supremum may be restricted to any subset of \(\R\oplus\mathcal H\). The
constant \(C\) is universal and the result does not require \(f^\circ\) to be the
true conditional log odds.

[Theorem 2 (Distance theorem for sparse simple random tensors) of arXiv:2606.24090, 'Sparsity-adaptive concentration inequalities for random polynomials'] Let \(0<\alpha\le 1\), \(p\in(0,1]\), and let
\[
     X=X^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes X^{(d)}\in\mathbb R^{n^d},
\]
where \(X_i^{(k)}=\delta_i^{(k)}\xi_i^{(k)}\), the variables \(\delta_i^{(k)}\) are i.i.d. Bernoulli\((p)\), and the variables \(\xi_i^{(k)}\) are independent, mean zero, variance one, and satisfy  $\|\xi_i^{(k)}\|_{\Psi_\alpha}\le 1$. All variables are assumed to be mutually independent.
Set
\[
    \Lambda_{n,p,d}:=\max_{0\le s\le d-1}(np)^{s/2}.
\]
Then for every deterministic nonzero matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{n^d\times n^d}\) and every \(t\ge 0\),
\begin{align}
&\mathbb P\left\{
\left|\|B X\|_2-p^{d/2}\|B\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\right|\ge t
\right\}\nonumber\\
&\qquad\le 2\exp\left[
-c_{\alpha,d}
\min\left\{
\frac{t^2}{\Lambda_{n,p,d}^2\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2},
\left(\frac{t}{n^{(d-1)/2}\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}}\right)^\alpha,
\left(\frac{t}{\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}}\right)^{\alpha/d}
\right\}
\right].
\end{align}
In particular, if \(np\ge 1\), then
\[
    \Lambda_{n,p,d}=(np)^{(d-1)/2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Distance theorem for sparse simple random tensors

Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph, q>=2 an integer, K>=0, u the uniform independent q-color law, and gamma_K the free ferromagnetic Potts law proportional to exp(K times the number of agreeing edges). Then D(u||gamma_K)>=|E|[log((exp(K)+q-1)/q)-K/q]. Equality holds on forests; for K>0 and a graph with a cycle it is strict. Thus on growing Z^d boxes at any fixed K>0, liminf D(u||gamma_K)/|V|>=d[log((exp(K)+q-1)/q)-K/q]>0. This is a product-law obstruction and does not establish critical discontinuity.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.28992, 'Minimal inversion of a permuton sample'] Let $\mu$ be a $(\alpha,\phi)$-standard permuton as defined in Section~\ref{sec:ass}.
    Let $\minv_n^\mu$ be the minimal inversion of $n$ points distributed according to $\mu$, as defined in~\eqref{eq:main}.
    Finally, denote by $\Delta=\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^2:x+y\leq1\}$ the unit square triangle.
    Then, the random variable $\minv_n^\mu$ satisfies
    \begin{align*}
        n^{-\alpha/(\alpha+1)}\minv_n^\mu
        \dconv\ray[\alpha+1,\int_\Delta\phi]
    \end{align*}
    as $n$ goes to infinity, where the convergence occurs in distribution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] The following absolute continuity relationships hold:
	\begin{itemize}
	\item Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ be two disjoint non-trivial segments of $\partial \BD$. Let $\tau$ be the first time $t\ge 0$ that the ball $\SCB_t(\alpha; D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$ hits $\beta$. Let $X$ be a deterministically selected point (e.g., the leftmost in some parameterization) in $\beta \cap \SCB_\tau(\alpha;D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$. Then the law of $X$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\beta$. 
	\item Similarly, let $\tau'$ be the first time $t\ge 0$ that $\SCB_t(\alpha;D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$ hits $\SCL(0)$ and let $X$ be a deterministically selected point in $\SCL(0) \cap \SCB_{\tau'}(\alpha;D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$. Then, conditionally on $\SCL(0)$, the conditional law of $X$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the harmonic measure on $\SCL(0)$ seen from $\infty$ in $\BC \setminus \overline{\mathop{\mathrm{int}}(\SCL(0))}$.
	\item Furthermore, let $\tau''$ be the first time $t\ge 0$ that $\SCB_t(\SCL(0); D^\BD_{\Gamma_{\BD}})$ hits $\partial \BD$ and let $X$ be a rotationally equivariant selected point on $\partial \BD \cap \SCB_{\tau''}(\SCL(0); D^\BD_{\Gamma_\BD})$ (i.e., the selection commutes with rotations of $\BD$). Then, the law of $X$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\partial \BD$ and is actually the uniform distribution on $\partial \BD$.
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.04139

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.14254, '2605.14254'] The process $\xi^{\lambda,z}$ is a semi-martingale and it has the following dynamic:
		\begin{equation}
			\xi^{\lambda,z}_{t}=b^{\lambda,z}_t+\lambda\,\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t\wedge\sigma_z^{\lambda} }\text{sgn}(z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_{s})\,\mathrm{d}s,\, t\geq 0,
		\end{equation}
		where $b^{\lambda,z}$ is an $\mathbb{F}^{\xi^{\lambda,z}}$-Brownian motion stopped at $\sigma_z^{\lambda}$. Here, the sgn function is defined as
		$$
		\text{sgn}(x):=\left\{\begin{aligned}
			-1, & \text { for } x<0 \\
			0, & \text { for } x=0 \\
			+1, & \text { for } x>0
		\end{aligned}\right..
		$$

such that, whenever
\begin{align}
\sqrt{N/\log N}\le\Delta_t\le KN/\sqrt{\log N},

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $t_n\to\infty$, $\mu\in\mathbf M(\mathbf D)$ be such that $\mu_{t_n}\overset{v}\to \mu$ and let $\Upsilon$ be a Poisson point process on ${\bf D}$ with intensity $\mu$.
    Then $\Upsilon$ and $\Upsilon_{t_n}$ are a.s.~admissible and we may write 
    $$\Upsilon=\sum_{i=1}^\infty \delta_{X_i},$$
    with $\{X_i(o)\}_{i\in \mathbb{N}}$ strictly increasing.

body:
Own-work research draft; status proof (unaudited), independent review and priority assessment pending. Fix k>=1 and D>=k+1. In R^(k+1) let M0 be the smooth closed surface z^2+Phi(|x|^2)=1, where Phi(s)=0 for s<=1 and Phi(s)=(s-1)exp(-1/(s-1)) for s>1. Let V0 be its surface volume. Put ell=1/(2sqrt(k)), A=1/12, Q=[-ell/2,ell/2]^k, and b(t)=64t^3(1-t)^3 on [0,1], zero outside. For n>=1 put h=ell/n and partition Q into n^k cells with lower corners c_i. For every sigma in {-1,+1}^(n^k), define f_sigma(x)=A h^2 sum_i sigma_i product_j b((x_j-c_ij)/h), T_sigma(x,z)=(x,z+f_sigma(x)), Vn=area(T_sigma(M0)), and t_n=(V0/Vn)^(1/k). Let mu_(sigma,n) be exactly uniform surface probability on t_n T_sigma(M0), isometrically embedded into R^D. There are constants C,W0 depending only on k,D and this fixed base such that, for W>=W0, a common scalar-input ReLU feedforward DAG architecture with at most W charged edge weights and biases has sup_(n,sigma) inf_theta W1((G_theta)#Unif[0,1],mu_(sigma,n))<=C W^(-4/k), with depth O(W). All fixed coefficients are charged; absent edges are absent; skip connections, unrestricted real weights and discontinuous target-to-weight assignments are allowed. The exact squared-gradient graph area density is C2 across every cell face with bounds independent of n; uniformly positive C2 chart densities have uniformly C2 inverse triangular transports. Apply Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk Theorem 3.3 (arXiv:1906.09477, p.5) at r=2,d=k, then a logarithmic-size tent-map scalar-source conversion and a fixed finite chart mixture with positive-time connectors. The source-conversion coupling uses the exact smooth map Lipschitz constant, not the coding network Lipschitz constant. This is a candidate theorem only for this entire explicit packing family, not all reach-bounded C2 surfaces. No bounded-bit, efficient weight-computation, complete T339 solution or novelty claim is made.
Exactly the explicit smooth base and signed cubic-endpoint bump family in the statement; k>=1, D>=k+1; scalar uniform latent source; unrestricted real-weight sparse feedforward DAG parameter count including fixed coefficients. Analytic proof unaudited, depending on unaudited T2-007 regularity and the known Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk theorem.

[Theorem thm:ck-and-wk-enjoy-lip of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Both $\textbf{CK}$ and $\textbf{WK}$ enjoy LIP.
  \begin{proof}
    Let $L \in \set{\textbf{CK}, \textbf{WK}}$ and suppose $L \vdash \varphi \to \psi$,
    then $\varphi \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \psi$ is provable in $\mathrm{G}_L$.
    Consider the partition $\varphi;\emptyset$ of $\varphi$,
    then by Lemma (lemma:maehara of the paper), there is $\chi$ such that
    $\varphi \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \chi$ and $\chi \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \psi$ are provable in $\mathrm{G}_L$,
    which imply $L \vdash \varphi \to \chi$ and $L \vdash \chi \to \psi$, respectively,
    and $\mathrm{V}^\bullet(\chi) \subseteq \mathrm{V}^\bullet(\varphi) \cap \mathrm{V}^\bullet(\psi)$ for each $\bullet \in \set{+, -}$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:ck-and-wk-enjoy-lip of arXiv:2608.29708

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2609.03556, 'An Effective SPDE Model for a Schr\"odinger Equation with a Fluctuating Magnetic Potential'] \label[lemma]{lem:rmse_viscous}
Assume \cref{hp:noise} and $\psi_0\in L^2(\R^d)$. There exists a unique
progressively measurable process $\psi^{\tau,\nu}$ with paths in
$C([0,T];L^2)\cap L^2(0,T;H^2)$ $\mathbb{P}-a.s.$ satisfying, for each
$\phi\in \mathscr{S}(\R^d)$ and $t\in [0,T]$,
\begin{align*}
i\langle \psi^{\tau,\nu}_t,\phi\rangle-i\langle \psi_0,\phi\rangle
&=-i\nu \int_0^t
\langle\psi^{\tau,\nu}_s,\Delta^2\phi\rangle ds
-\int_0^t \langle\psi^{\tau,\nu}_s,\Delta\phi\rangle ds\\
&\quad-2i\int_0^t
\langle \psi^{\tau,\nu}_s,A^{\tau}_s\cdot\nabla\phi\rangle ds+\int_0^t
\langle|A^{\tau}_s|^2\psi^{\tau,\nu}_s,\phi\rangle ds
\quad \mathbb{P}-a.s.,
   \end{align*}
   where $A^{\tau}_t$ is the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process \eqref{eq:OU_prel}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
