body:
For an integral operator T_k on L^2 with kernel k, the formula tr T_k = integral of k(x,x) dx is not a definition and not automatic. (1) An L^2 kernel is an equivalence class modulo null sets, and on a nonatomic space the diagonal is a null set, so k(x,x) has no meaning at all without choosing a distinguished representative; different representatives give different 'diagonal integrals'. (2) Continuity of the kernel is not enough for trace class. Carleman's example: there are continuous 2pi-periodic functions g whose Fourier coefficients are not absolutely summable. The convolution operator (T f)(x) = (1/(2 pi)) times the integral over the circle of g(x - y) f(y) dy has the continuous kernel k(x,y) = g(x - y)/(2 pi), is normal with eigenvalues the Fourier coefficients of g and eigenfunctions the exponentials, so its singular values are the moduli of those coefficients; hence T is Hilbert-Schmidt but not trace class, while the naive diagonal integral is the finite number g(0). (3) What does hold: if T is trace class on L^2([a,b]) and has a continuous kernel on [a,b] x [a,b], then tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx; and by Mercer's theorem, if k is continuous, symmetric and positive semidefinite on a compact interval (more generally on a compact metric space with a finite Borel measure of full support), then the associated operator is trace class, the eigenfunction series converges absolutely and uniformly, and tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx = sum of the eigenvalues. So the safe routes are positivity plus continuity (Mercer), or an independent proof of trace class plus continuity; 'the kernel is nice' by itself is not a proof.
the operator is trace class, or the kernel is continuous and positive semidefinite (Mercer) on a compact space with a finite Borel measure of full support
the kernel is a continuous representative, so that its diagonal values are defined
an L^2 kernel alone determines only a Hilbert-Schmidt operator, whose diagonal is undefined

[Theorem thm2 of arXiv:2609.02136, 'Gamma approximation and Poisson--Gaussian invariance principle on Poisson chaos'] Fix an integer $q\geq1$ and $\nu\in(0,\infty)$.  Let
$F_n\in\mathcal{C}_q^\eta\cap L^4(\Omega)$ satisfy
\noindent
\begin{align}
 \mathbb{E}[F_n^2]=2\nu
\quad{\rm and}\quad
 \mathcal J_4(F_n)\longrightarrow0.
 
\end{align}
Then $\Delta_\nu(F_n)\to0$ implies $F_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}Z_\nu$.
If, in addition, $\{F_n^4:n\geq1\}$ is uniformly integrable, then the
following assertions are equivalent:
\begin{align*}
\begin{aligned}
 {\rm(i)}\ F_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}Z_\nu
 &\Longleftrightarrow {\rm(ii)}\ d_2(F_n,Z_\nu)\to0\\
 &\Longleftrightarrow {\rm(iii)}\ \mathbb{E}[F_n^3]\to8\nu
 \quad{\rm and}\quad \mathbb{E}[F_n^4]\to12\nu^2+48\nu
 \Longleftrightarrow {\rm(iv)}\ \Delta_\nu(F_n)\to0.
\end{aligned}
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm2 of arXiv:2609.02136

[Lemma 2 (Disintegration of conditional independence) of arXiv:2609.00946, 'Embedded Conditional Independence Tests for Large Language Model Generated Text with an Ap'] Let $(E_A,\mathcal{E}_A)$, $(E_B,\mathcal{E}_B)$, $(E_C,\mathcal{E}_C)$ be
standard Borel spaces and write
$(E,\mathcal{E}) = (E_A\times E_B\times E_C,\,
\mathcal{E}_A\otimes\mathcal{E}_B\otimes\mathcal{E}_C)$, with coordinate
projections $A,B,C$. Let
\[
  \mathcal{P}_0 := \bigl\{\,\mu \text{ probability measure on }(E,\mathcal{E})
  \;:\; A \indep B \mid C \text{ under } \mu \,\bigr\}.
\]
Let $V$ be an $E$-valued and $W$ a $(\mathcal{W},\mathcal{G})$-valued random
variable on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, where $(\mathcal{W},\mathcal{G})$
is an arbitrary measurable space, and let $\mathbb{P}^{V\mid W}$ be a regular
conditional distribution of $V$ given $W$. Then
$\{w\in\mathcal{W}:\mathbb{P}^{V\mid W=w}\in\mathcal{P}_0\}\in\mathcal{G}$ and
\[
  A \indep B \mid (C,W)
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \mathbb{P}^{V\mid W}\in\mathcal{P}_0 \quad \mathbb{P}^{W}\text{-a.s.}
\]

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2608.11071, 'Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents'] For each $\kappa,\alpha, n>0$, there exists a non-negative function $\psi\in C^3[-n^{1/4}\kappa,0]$ such that the following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The function $\psi$ solves the ODE (Stein's equation)
    \begin{equation}
        \psi''(z)-\alpha z^3 \psi'(z)=-1,
        
    \end{equation}
    with boundary conditions $\psi'(-n^{1/4}\kappa)=\psi(0)=0$.
     \item We have $\psi'(z)\leq 0$ for all $z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]$ and $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]}|\psi'(z)|<C_1$ for some positive constant $C_1$ independent of $n$.
    \item We have $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa, 0]}\psi(z)<C_2$ for some positive constant $C_2$ independent of $n$.
    \item  For all sufficiently large $n$ we have $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/4}\kappa,0]}|\psi'''(z)|=\alpha\kappa^3n^{3/4}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm intro-coupling of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] Let  \(d=4,5\) and fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\).  Let \(G_1\) be the
coarse-grained self-intersection graph of the simple random walk path $S[0,n]$ constructed
from the block length
\[
    a_n =
    \begin{cases}
    \varepsilon n(\log n)^{-1}, & d=4,\\
    \varepsilon n^{2/3}, & d=5,
    \end{cases}
\]
and let \(G_2\) be the corresponding long range percolation graph, with
nearest-neighbor edges present deterministically and with the dimension-dependent
connection probabilities specified below.  Then \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) can be
constructed on the same probability space so that
\[
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\bigl(G_1\neq G_2\bigr)=0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop p:efron-stein-classical of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $X_0,X_1,\dots,X_n, Y$ be random vectors (possibly with different and/or infinite lengths) on the same probability space, such that $X_0,\dots,X_n$ are conditionally independent given $Y$.
    Write $\mathbf{X} \coloneqq  (X_0,\dots,X_n)$.
    Let $\widetilde{\mathbf{X}} = (\widetilde{X}_0,\dots,\widetilde{X}_n)$ be a conditionally independent copy of $\mathbf{X}$ given $Y$.
    Write
    \begin{align*}
        \widetilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(k)} \coloneqq  (X_0,\dots,X_{k-1},\widetilde{X}_k, X_{k+1},\dots,X_n).
    \end{align*}
    Note that we have the equality of unconditional joint laws
    \begin{align*}
        (\mathbf{X},Y)\overset{d}{=} (\widetilde{\mathbf{X}},Y) \overset{d}{=} (\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(0)}, Y)\overset{d}{=} \cdots \overset{d}{=} (\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(n)},Y).
    \end{align*}
    

    Let $Z=Z(\mathbf{X},Y)$ be a square-integrable function of $(\mathbf{X},Y)$.
    Then
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}[\Var(Z \mid Y)]
        = \frac12
        \mathbb{E}\left[
            \left(
                Z(\mathbf{X},Y)
                - Z(\widetilde{\mathbf{X}},Y)
            \right)^2
        \right]
        &\leqslant
        \frac12
        \sum_{k=0}^n 
        \mathbb{E}\left[
            \left(
                Z(\mathbf{X},Y)
                - Z(\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}^{(k)},Y)
            \right)^2
        \right].
    \end{align*}
    In fact, the above holds almost surely with $\mathbb{E}[\,\cdot\,|\,Y]$ in place of $\mathbb{E}[\,\cdot\,]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Efron--Stein inequality

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2607.20646, 'The Independence-Preserving Property and Planar Web Geometry'] Let $(\mu_X,\mu_Y,\mu_U,\mu_V)$ be probability measures on $(0, \infty)$ having positive continuous density.
Then $\HIp|_{(0,\infty)^2}$ preserves their independence if and only if there exist $p,q,r\in\R$ with $\max\{p, 0\} < \min\{q, r\}$ such that
\begin{alignat*}{3}
    \mu_X(\dd x)
        &\propto (1 + \alpha x)^{p}\Big(\frac{1}{1+x}\Big)^q\Big(\frac{\alpha x}{1+\alpha x}\Big)^r\frac{\dd x}{x} &
        &\propto x^{r-1}(1+x)^{-q}(1+\alpha x)^{p-r}\,\dd x,\\
    \mu_Y(\dd y)
        &\propto (1 + \beta y)^{p}\Big(\frac{\beta y}{1+\beta y}\Big)^q\Big(\frac{1}{1+y}\Big)^r\frac{\dd y}{y} &
        &\propto y^{q-1}(1+y)^{-r}(1+\beta y)^{p-q}\,\dd y,\\
    \mu_U(\dd u)
        &\propto (1 + \alpha u)^{p}\Big(\frac{\alpha u}{1+\alpha u}\Big)^q\Big(\frac{1}{1+u}\Big)^r\frac{\dd u}{u} &
        &\propto u^{q-1}(1+u)^{-r}(1+\alpha u)^{p-q}\,\dd u,\\
    \mu_V(\dd v)
        &\propto (1 + \beta v)^{p}\Big(\frac{1}{1+v}\Big)^q\Big(\frac{\beta v}{1+\beta v}\Big)^r\frac{\dd v}{v} &
        &\propto v^{r-1}(1+v)^{-q}(1+\beta v)^{p-r}\,\dd v.
\end{alignat*}

body:
[Corollary 58 of arXiv:2508.04938, 'Perfect t-embeddings of doubly periodic Aztec diamonds'] Let~$D_p=p_0-p_\infty$,~$D_q=q_0-q_\infty$, and~$D=p_0+p_\infty-q_0-q_\infty$. The 1-forms~$\omega^{\mathcal Z}$ and~$\omega^{\vartheta}$ can be expressed as

\begin{multline*}
\omega^{\mathcal Z}=\frac{\sqrt{a^2+1}(a+\i)}{2\pi\i}\omega_{D_q}-\frac{\sqrt{a^2+1}(a-\i)}{2\pi\i}\omega_{D_p} \\
+\frac{\sqrt{a^2+1}}{2\pi\i}\left(a\nabla \log\theta(t+u(p_\infty)-u(q_\infty))-a\nabla\log\theta(t+u(p_0)-u(q_0)) \right.\\
\left.+\i\nabla \log\theta(t+u(p_0)-u(q_\infty))-\i\nabla \log\theta(t+u(p_\infty)-u(q_0))\right)\vec{\omega},
\end{multline*}
and
\begin{multline*}
\omega^{\vartheta}=\frac{(a^2+1)}{2\pi\i}\omega_{D} \\
+\frac{(a+\i)}{2\pi\i}\left(a\nabla \log \theta(t+u(p_0)-u(q_0))+a\nabla \log \theta(t+u(p_\infty)-u(q_\infty))-2a\nabla \log\theta(t)\right. \\
\left.-\i\nabla \log\theta(t+u(p_0)-u(q_\infty))-\i\nabla \log \theta(t+u(p_\infty)-u(q_0))+2\i\nabla\log \theta(t)\right)\vec{\omega}.
\end{multline*}

In particular,~$\vartheta$ is real-valued if and only if
\begin{multline*}
\nabla \log\theta(t+u(p_0)-u(q_\infty))+\nabla \log\theta(t+u(p_\infty)-u(q_0)) \\
-\nabla \log\theta(t+u(p_0)-u(q_0))-\nabla \log\theta(t+u(p_\infty)-u(q_\infty))=0.
\end{multline*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 58 of arXiv:2508.04938

body:
[Lemma lem:commutator-transfer of arXiv:2608.22910, 'A Commutator Framework for Selective Spectral Alignment in Deep Neural Networks'] Fix \(t\geq0\) and \(\ell\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\), and set
\[
C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}:=[\mathcal S_\ell,\mathrm{NFM}_\ell],
\qquad
C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}:=[Q_\ell,P_\ell].
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}
=W_\ell^\top C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}W_\ell
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}\|_F
\leq
\|W_\ell\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}\|_F.
\end{equation}
If \(W_\ell\) has full row rank, and \(\sigma_{\min}(W_\ell)\) denotes
its smallest singular value, then
\begin{equation}
\sigma_{\min}(W_\ell)^2\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}\|_F
\leq
\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}\|_F
\leq
\sigma_{\max}(W_\ell)^2\|C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}\|_F,
\end{equation}
and hence \(C_\ell^{\mathrm{feat}}=0\) if and only if
\(C_\ell^{\mathrm{int}}=0\).

[Definition 32 (Coordinate-free operational second-order state) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] The $(\eta;\mathfrak I,1)$ state space
$\mathsf Z_{\eta;\mathfrak I,1}(H)$ consists of continuous paths starting at the group identity
\[
 g:[0,T]\longrightarrow\Gito_{\mathfrak I,1}(H)
\]
such that the geometric readout $\Theta_H^S(g)$ belongs to
$G\Omega^2_{\eta,\mathfrak I}(H)$ and the covariance path
$q_t:=\Theta_H^Q(g_t)$ belongs to
$C_0^{0,2\eta}([0,T];\mathcal S_{1,\rm sa})$.  For
$g_{s,t}:=g_s^{-1}\star g_t$, write its canonical cocycle chart as
\[
 g_{s,t}=(x_{s,t},A_{s,t},q_{s,t}).
\]
The state metric is
\begin{equation}

 d_{\eta;\mathfrak I,1}(g,\widetilde g)
 =|x-\widetilde x|_{\eta;H}
 +|A-\widetilde A|_{2\eta;\mathfrak I}
 +|q-\widetilde q|_{2\eta;\mathcal S_1}.
\end{equation}
Stopping is group-path stopping.  The resulting space is causal Polish.
title: Coordinate-free operational second-order state

[Dfn 4 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] Let $\lambda = [\lambda(0), \lambda(1), \cdots, \lambda(m)]$ be a path of length $m$ in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$. We define the chronological loop-erasure of $\lambda$, denoted by $\text{LE} (\lambda)$, in the following manner. First, set
$$ t_0 \coloneqq \max\{t \ge 0 \, : \, \lambda(t) = \lambda(0)\}.$$
For each $i \geq 1$, define
$$ t_i \coloneqq \max\{t \ge 0 \, : \, \lambda(t) = \lambda(t_{i-1}+1)\}. $$
Let 
$$n = \min\{i \, : \, t_i = m\}.$$
    Then, the chronological loop-erasure of $\lambda$ is given by
    $$\text{LE} (\lambda) \coloneqq [\lambda(t_0), \lambda(t_1), \ldots, \lambda(t_n)].$$
title: Definition 4 of arXiv:2604.01748

Let X_1, \dots, X_n be independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_k] = 0 and \text{Var}(X_k) = \sigma_k^2 < \infty. Let S_k = \sum_{j=1}^k X_j. Then for every \epsilon > 0, \mathbb{P}\left( \max_{1 \le k \le n} |S_k| \ge \epsilon \right) \le \frac{1}{\epsilon^2} \sum_{k=1}^n \sigma_k^2 = \frac{\text{Var}(S_n)}{\epsilon^2}.

Preserved duplicate statement and commentary:
Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent random variables with E[X_i] = 0 and Var(X_i) < infinity for each i, and let S_k = X_1 + ... + X_k. Then for every lambda > 0, P(max_{1 <= k <= n} |S_k| >= lambda) <= Var(S_n) / lambda^2 = (sum_{i=1}^n Var(X_i)) / lambda^2. This strengthens Chebyshev's inequality applied to S_n alone into a bound on the whole running maximum. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have $S_1\sim\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}(n-\sqrt{n})^{1/2}$
    \begin{proof}
        We may compute $S_1$ explicitly. We have, via a combinatorial identity,
        \[S_1=\frac{n-2m-3}{2^{n-2m-4}}\binom{n-2m-4}{\frac{n}{2}-m-2}\]
        By a special case of Stirling's estimate, we have
        \[\binom{n}{n/2}\sim 2^n(\pi n/2)^{-1/2}\] 
        This gives
        \[S_1\sim \frac{(n-2m-3)(2^{n-2m-4})}{(2^{n-2m-4})\sqrt{\pi(\frac{n}{2}-m-2)}}=\frac{(n-2m-3)}{\sqrt{\pi(\frac{n}{2}-m-2)}}\]
        \[=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\left(\frac{n-2m-3}{\sqrt{n-2m-4}}\right)\]
        \[=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\left(\frac{n-\left\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\right\rceil-2}{\sqrt{n-\left\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\right\rceil-3}}\right)\]
        \[\sim\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}(n-\sqrt{n})^{1/2}\]
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered proposition of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a nonnegative random variable X, typically a count of some combinatorial structure written as X = sum_i X_i for indicator random variables X_i, the Paley-Zygmund inequality gives P(X > 0) >= (E[X])^2 / E[X^2]. Expanding E[X^2] = E[X] + sum_{i != j} E[X_i X_j], the method succeeds in proving P(X>0) is bounded away from 0 exactly when the pair-correlation sum sum_{i != j} E[X_i X_j] is of the same order as (E[X])^2, that is, when correlations between the indicators do not overwhelm the square of the mean. This is the standard route to existence results, such as an infinite cluster, a long crossing, or a large clique, once a first-moment computation has already established that E[X] is large or diverging, complementing the first-moment method, which by Markov's inequality only ever gives upper bounds on P(X>0). The method does not give any rate of convergence beyond the crude Paley-Zygmund ratio, gives no lower bound at all if the correlation structure is not controlled, and can produce a vacuous (near-0) bound whenever the variance is dominated by rare, strongly correlated configurations even though the mean itself is large. Typical failure: Computing a large or diverging first moment E[X] and declaring existence of the structure without bounding E[X^2]; if the indicators X_i are strongly positively correlated (a common situation for overlapping structures), the pair-correlation term can dominate (E[X])^2, making the Paley-Zygmund bound vacuous even as E[X] -> infinity, which is exactly the situation where a large first moment gives a false sense of near-certain existence. Canonical reference: Paley and Zygmund, 1932, Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society; Alon and Spencer, The Probabilistic Method, fourth edition, Wiley.
a well-defined nonnegative counting or indicator-sum random variable X = sum_i X_i
a computable or boundable first moment E[X]
a computable or boundable second moment E[X^2], in particular control of the pairwise correlations E[X_i X_j]
the correlation sum not growing asymptotically faster than (E[X])^2
title: Technique: The Second-Moment Method

body:
[Lemma 3 (Replica Wick polynomial) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] For
\[
 M_{P,r}(\Sigma)
 =
 \E\prod_{a=1}^{r}P(X_a^\Sigma),
 \qquad \Sigma\in\Sym_r^{++}(\R),
\]
one has the polynomial identity
\begin{equation}
 M_{P,r}(\Sigma)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{E=(e_{ab})\\k_a(E)\leq m}}
 N(E)\,\Contr_E(P)
 \prod_{1\leq a\leq b\leq r}\Sigma_{ab}^{e_{ab}},
 
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 N(E)
 =
 \frac{\prod_{a=1}^{r}k_a(E)!}
 {\displaystyle
  \prod_{a=1}^{r}2^{e_{aa}}e_{aa}!\,
  \prod_{1\leq a<b\leq r}e_{ab}!}
 \in\N_{>0}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, every complete contraction of copies of the tensors
\(T_0(P),\ldots,T_m(P)\) is, up to the explicit positive factor
\eqref{eq:wick-multiplicity}, a coefficient of one of the polynomials
\(M_{P,r}\).

body:
Let P be a locally finite poset, R a nonzero commutative ring with 1, and Q a subset with the induced order. Restricting an element of the incidence algebra I_R(P) to the comparable pairs of Q is a unital R-algebra homomorphism onto I_R(Q) if and only if Q is order-convex: x <= z <= y with x, y in Q forces z in Q. In that case mu_Q(x, y) = mu_P(x, y) for all x <= y in Q.

[Corollary 37 (Convergence, stated with a reference measure; Theorem \ref{thm:posdens}) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $\XX$ be a set, $\XXA$ a $\sigma$-algebra on $\XX$, and $\lambda$ a
$\sigma$-finite measure on $(\XX,\XXA)$. Let
\[
  p : \XX \longrightarrow [0,\infty)
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \tau : \XX\times\XX \longrightarrow [0,\infty), \quad (x,y) \longmapsto \tau(y \mid x),
\]
be measurable, respectively $\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable, and define the probability
measure $\pi$ and the Markov kernel $T$ by
\[
  \pi(A) := \int_{A} p \dd\lambda,
  \qquad
  T(A \mid x) := \int_{A} \tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX),
\]
where $\int_{\XX} p \dd\lambda = 1$ and $\int_{\XX}\tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) = 1$
for every $x \in \XX$. Write $\Xp := \{ y \in \XX : p(y) > 0 \} \in \XXA$ and assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item \emph{(invariance)} $\displaystyle\int_{\XX} \tau(y \mid x)\,p(x)\,\lambda(\dd x) = p(y)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX$;
  \item \emph{(the support is not left)} for every $x \in \XX$: $\ \tau(y \mid x) = 0$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX\setminus\Xp$;
  \item \emph{(positivity)} $\tau(y \mid x) > 0$ for $(\lambda\otimes\lambda)$-almost every $(x,y) \in \Xp \times \Xp$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$, and
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty} \tv{T^{n}\circ\mu - \pi} = 0 \qquad\text{for every } \mu \in \Prob .
\]
Theorem \ref{thm:posdens} of the introduction is the special case in which $p > 0$
everywhere, so that $\Xp = \XX$ and hypothesis (ii) is vacuous.

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.24549, 'Persistent Cross Entropy'] A map $k:\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{Z}\to(0,1]$ is called a
\textbf{similarity function} if it satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\textit{\roman*})]
\item there exist a metric $\rho$ on $\mathcal{Z}$ and a strictly decreasing function
$h:[0,\infty)\to(0,1]$ with $h(0)=1$ and
$\lim\limits_{r\to\infty}h(r)=0$ such that
$$
k(u,v)=h(\rho(u,v));
$$

\item $k$ is Lipschitz in its second argument: there exists $L_0>0$ such that
$$
|k(u,v)-k(u,v')|
\leq
L_0\Vert v-v' \Vert
$$
for all $u,v,v'\in\mathcal{Z}$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.24549

[Corollary 8 of arXiv:2609.02801, 'Ratio and limiting zero distribution asymptotics for symmetric multiple orthogonal polynom'] Suppose $a < 2^{-r}$ and $(c_n)_{n \geq 0}$ is a positive sequence for which $\lim_{n \to \infty} c_n = 0$. If
\[    0 \leq  a_{n+1} \leq c_n + a \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} a_{n-k}, \qquad  n \geq 0,  \]
then $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n= 0$.

[Theorem gdvAc of arXiv:2607.00753, 'Threatening excursions in large population\\ quasi-stationary birth and death systems.\\ O'] Let $A$  be an open subset of $\mathds R_{+}^{d}$ satisfying Assumption ${\bf (HS)}$. Then there exists a number $\rho_{A}>0$ independent of
$K$ such that for $K$ large enough
$$
\frac{\rho_{A}}{3\,K^2\,M_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\,\eta_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A) }\le
\mu_{K}(K*A^{c})\le\frac{2\;\delta_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}}{M_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\,\eta_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)}\;.
$$
Moreover,
$$
\lim_{K\to\infty}\frac{\log\big(\mu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(K*A^{c})\big)}{K}
=\lim_{K\to\infty}\frac{\log\big(\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(K*A^{c})\big)}{K}=-V^{*}(A)\;.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem UM of arXiv:2608.30491, 'The Daugavet property in symmetric operator spaces'] Let $({\mathcal M}, \tau)$ be an  infinite  semi-finite      atomless von Neumann algebra and let \({\mathcal{E}}\subseteq S({\mathcal M}, \tau)_h \) be a  strongly
		symmetric 
		operator   space.  
		Assume  that \( {\mathcal{E}} \) has the following properties:
		\begin{enumerate}[\rm(a)]
			\item For any \( p\in{\mathcal P}({\mathcal M}) \) with \( \tau(p) < \infty \), the space \( {\mathcal{E}}_p \) is order continuous.
			\item Let \( p\in{\mathcal P}({\mathcal M})  \) with \(  \tau(p) < \infty \). 
			If \( x \in S_{\mathcal{E}} \) and for every \( \varepsilon > 0 \), \( y_\varepsilon \in S_{\mathcal{E}} \), then 
			$$
			\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \|x + p y_\varepsilon p\|_{\mathcal{E}} = 2 $$
			whenever $  	\mathop{\lim}\limits_{\varepsilon \to 0} \|p y_\varepsilon p\|_{\mathcal{E}} = 1$  and  
			$	\mathop{\lim}\limits_{\varepsilon \to 0} \|x + y_\varepsilon\|_{\mathcal{E}} = 2.
			$ 
		\end{enumerate}
		If \( {\mathcal{E}} \) has the Daugavet property, then it is isometrically isomorphic to \( L_1({\mathcal M}, \tau)_h \). In particular,
		if \( \phi_{\mathcal{E}}(1) = 1 \), then \( {\mathcal{E}} = L_1({\mathcal M}, \tau)_h   \) with equality of norms.

[Dfn 4 of arXiv:2608.29148, '2608.29148'] A $\Theta$-metric $g$ on $(\ol X, [\Theta])$ is called an {\it asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) metric} with CR infinity $(M, H, J)$ if it satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]  For any boundary defining function $r$, we have 
\[
\Bigl|\dfrac{dr}{r}\Bigr|^2_g=\dfrac{1}{4}\quad \textrm{on}\ M,
\]
or, equivalently, $|\nu|^2_g=4$. 
\item[(ii)] For any $p\in M$, the map
\[
L_p\longrightarrow {}^\Theta T_p \ol X, \quad Z\longmapsto [\nu_p, Z]
\]
gives the identity map on $L_p$.
\item[(iii)] For any contact form $\th$ on $M$, we have 
\[
\lambda_\th^*(g|_{L})=2h_{\a\ol\b}\th^\a\cdot\th^{\ol\b},
\]
where the right-hand side denotes the Levi form on $H$ associated with $\th$.
\end{enumerate}
We call $(\ol X, [\Theta], g)$ an {\it ACH manifold}.

Finite-dimensional local corollary of van den Berg-Hetebrij-Rink parameterization theorem. Let F be a C^k map, integer k>=2, on a neighborhood of 0 in R^c x R^s, fixing 0, with DF(0)=diag(I_c,A_s) and spectral radius(A_s)<1. Then, after restricting to a neighborhood, there is a C^k center graph h with h(0)=0,Dh(0)=0 and a local C^k center map R, DR(0)=I_c, such that F(u,h(u))=(R(u),h(R(u))) wherever both sides remain local. The graph is parameterized by its center coordinate u. For k=3 this gives a C3 center graph. This assertion is a graph-existence and reduced-map theorem; it does not by itself assert a phase projection or stable foliation for nearby points.

[Lemma lem:doubling-metric-dim of arXiv:2512.06984, 'Infinite Dimensional Multifractal Analysis of the Wiener measure'] Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space.
		
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm (A)] (Doubling $\Rightarrow$ finite metric dimension)
Assume that there exists an integer $N\ge 1$ such that for every $x\in X$ and $R>0$, the ball $B(x,R)$ can be covered by at most $N$ balls of radius $R/2$.
Then $(X,d)$ is $(C,s)$-homogeneous in the sense of Assouad, with
\[s=\log_2 N, \qquad C=N,\]
hence $\Dim(X,d)<\infty$.
			
\item[\rm (B)] (Finite metric dimension $\Rightarrow$ doubling)
Assume that $(X,d)$ is $(C,s)$-homogeneous: for all $0<a<b$ and all $Y\subset Z\subset X$ with $\mathrm{diam\, }(Z)\le b$ and $Y$ $a$-separated, one has $\#Y\le C(b/a)^s$.
Then $(X,d)$ is doubling: every ball $B(x,R)$ can be covered by at most
\[N_0:=C\,2^{s}\]
balls of radius $R/2$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Doubling $\Longleftrightarrow$ finite Assouad/metric dimension

[Lem number-crossings-check of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] Consider an annulus $A(x;r,2r)$. Let $\check{F}_1(\check{M})$ be the event that there are at most $\check{M}$ distinct clusters (open or closed) that cross this annulus. If there exist both an open crossing and a closed crossing of $A(x;r,2r)$, then for any open (resp.\ closed) cluster that crosses this annulus, one can find two (not necessarily disjoint) open (resp.\ closed) crossings of the annulus $\eta_c$ and $\eta_a$ that serve as the clockwise most and counterclockwise most boundaries of this cluster. 
Define the event $\check{F}_2(\check{b})$ as follows. If there are at least 2 crossing clusters of $A(x;r,2r)$, then for every open (resp.\ closed) crossing cluster of $A(x;r,2r)$, let $v$ be the endpoint of $\eta_a$ on the inner boundary of $A(x;r,2r)$. On $\check{F}_2$, we require that there exists an open (resp.\ closed) path from $\eta_a$ to the inner boundary of $A(x;r,2r)$ that stays at distance at least $10\check{b}r$ away from $v$. We also require the same assertion when we swap $\eta_a$ with $\eta_c$. In particular, this implies that for points $v$ that are the endpoints of the interfaces of crossing clusters at the inner boundary of $\check{A}$, no crossing clusters apart from the ones whose interface $v$ is on enter the box $B(v,10\check{b}r)$. 

The following holds for $R$ large enough. For each $\check{p}>0$, there exist $\check{M}$ large enough and $\check{b}>0$ small enough so that $$\mathbf{P}\!\left(\check{F}_1(\check{M})\cap \check{F}_2(\check{b})\right)\geq 1-\check{p}$$ for all annuli $A(x;r,2r)$ of radius $r\geq \frac{R}{\check{b}n}$.

[Theorem thm:2nd_mom_formula of arXiv:2504.14457, 'Abstract'] Consider a Poisson process $(N_t)_{t \geq 0}$ with rate 1, and let $(\tau_n)_{n \geq 0}$ denote its jump times. Also, consider $B^{(i)} = \left(B^{(i)}_t\right)_{t \geq 0}$ to be i.i.d copies of a standard Brownian motion. We define a stochastic process $X = (X_t)_{t \geq 0}$ as follows: for $0 < t \leq \tau_1$, let
$$X_t = X_0 + B^{(1)}_t.$$
For $i \geq 1$ and $\tau_i < t \leq \tau_{i+1}$, let
$$X_t = X_{\tau_i} + B^{(i+1)}_{t - \tau_i}.$$
We denote by $P_x$ the probability measure under which $X_0 = x$ and $E_x$ the expected value under $P_x$.
We have
\begin{align}
\nonumber \lefteqn{E[u(t,x)u(t,y)] }\\
&= e^t E_x\left[\lambda^2 w(t - \tau_{N_t}, X^{1}_{\tau_{N_t}}) w(t - \tau_{N_t}, X^{2}_{\tau_{N_t}}) \prod_{i=1}^{N_t} \left((t-\tau_i)^{2H-1} f(X^1_{\tau_i} - X^2_{\tau_i})\right)\right],
\end{align}
where $X^1$ and $X^2$ are two i.i.d copies of the process $X$ defined above.

Notice that for the heat equation,
$p_h(t,\mathbb{R}^d)=1$ for all $d\geq 1$.\\ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:2nd_mom_formula of arXiv:2504.14457

        \item  When $\xi \notin \Xi$, there is exactly one equivalence class of $\xi$-eternal solutions, namely that of $(x,t) \mapsto W^\xi(0,0;x,t)$.

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.03831, 'On flows generated by square-integrable vector fields'] Let $\rho \in L^1_\loc(I\times \R^d)$ be a weak solution of \eqref{CE}.
Let $N\subset I$ be given by Proposition~\ref{prop-CE-int} and let $s\in I\setminus N$.
Then for any $t\in \overline{I}$ the distribution
\begin{equation}
\langle \rho|_t, \fhi \rangle := \int_{\R^d} \rho(s,x) \fhi(x) \, dx + \int_s^t \int_{\R^d} \rho(\tau, x) \v(\tau, x) \cdot \nabla \fhi(x) \, dx \, d\tau,
\qquad \fhi \in \mathscr{D}(\R^d),
\end{equation}
is called the trace of $\rho$ at time $t$.

[Thm 4 (Basse-O'Connor, Kramer-Bang, Svedsen, \cite{basseoconnor2025fourthmoment}) of arXiv:2511.20875, 'Double $q$-Wigner Chaos and the Fourth Moment'] Let $m,n \in\N$ have opposite parities.  For each $k\in\N$, let $f_k \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^m_+)$ and $g_k \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n_+)$ be fully symmetric functions, and let $X_k = I^W(f_k)$ and $Y_k=I^W(g_k)$.  Assume $\mathbb{E}[X_k^2] + \mathbb{E}[Y_k^2] = \sigma^2$ for all $k\in\N$.  Then the following three conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} c_4[X_k+Y_k] = 0}$.
    \item $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} f_k \overset{p}{\frown} f_k = 0}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}_+^{2(m-p)})$ for $p=1,\ldots,m-1$,  and $\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to\infty} g_k \overset{p}{\frown} g_k = 0}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R}_+^{2(n-p)})$ for $p=1,\ldots,n-1$.
    \item The sequence $(X_k+Y_k)_{k\in\N}$ converges in distribution to a centered Gaussian random variable with variance $\sigma^2$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\begin{equation}

\left\{\begin{array}{lll} (-1)^{\textnormal{par}(\textnormal{X}_1,\textnormal{X}_2)}\bigg( -\dfrac{1}{4\pi} \displaystyle\int_{z_1^*}^{z_1}\int_{z_2^*}^{z_2} \mathcal{F}^{(q,q)}(w_1,w_2)\dd w_1 \dd w_2 - \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\log\left|\frac{z_1 - z_2}{z_1 - z_2^*}\right|\bigg) && \textnormal{if}\,\,q_1 = q_2 = q, \\[12pt]

f:\Gamma_n(\alpha)\to\mathbb C

\),

\lVert f\rVert_{\ell^r(\Gamma_n(\alpha))}
=
\left(\sum_{\eta\in\Gamma_n(\alpha)}\lvert f(\eta)\rvert^r\right)^{1/r}.
\]

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.01346, '2609.01346'] For every pair of integers satisfying \eqref{eq:nk-range}, there is a compact
embedded rotational torus $\Sigma^n\subset\R^{n+1}$ whose homothetic
dilations form a shrinking solution of the unnormalised $\sigma_k$-curvature
flow \eqref{eq:sigma-k-flow} in the Sobolev almost-everywhere sense defined in
Section~\ref{sec:weak}.  More precisely, $\Sigma$ has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item The torus is smooth away from two rotational latitudes and satisfies
  $\langle X,\nu\rangle=-\sigma_k(S)$ there.
  \item If $\Omega$ is the bounded domain enclosed by $\Sigma$ and
  $S_{\mathrm w}$ is the weak shape operator of $\partial\Omega=\Sigma$, then
  $\langle X,\nu\rangle=-\sigma_k(S_{\mathrm w})$ almost everywhere with
  respect to the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal H^n$.
  \item Set $X_t=((k+1)(T-t))^{1/(k+1)}X$ and
  $\Sigma_t=X_t(M)$.  If $\nu_t$ and $S_{\mathrm w,t}$ are the outward unit
  normal and weak shape operator of $\Sigma_t$, respectively, then
  $\langle\partial X_t/\partial t,\nu_t\rangle
  =\sigma_k(S_{\mathrm w,t})$ at $\mathcal H^n$-almost every point, for every
  $t<T$.
  \item Its profile curve has H\"older regularity $C^{1,1/k}$ and belongs
  to the Sobolev class $W^{2,p}$ for every $1\leq p<k/(k-1)$.
\end{enumerate}
If $s$ is arclength along the profile curve and $s_0$ is either singular
parameter, then the profile curve is
not $C^2$ at $s_0$, and the magnitude of its meridional principal curvature
is asymptotic to a positive multiple of $|s-s_0|^{-(k-1)/k}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.01346

        +(1/n)[10u f'(u)+11u^2 f''(u)+4u^3 f'''(u)
                            +(u^4/2)f''''(u)] + O_(f,d,K)(n^(-3/2)). (B)

The exact conditional raw moments, for k large enough, are

    E M     = (k-1)/(k-2),
    E M^2   = k/(k-3),
    E M^3   = (k^2-1)/[(k-2)(k-4)],
    E M^4   = k(k+2)/[(k-3)(k-5)].                  (G)

These follow from E(chi-square_r)^z=2^z Gamma(r/2+z)/Gamma(r/2),
independence, and Gamma(x+1)=x Gamma(x). In particular the first formula
is exact; approximating its two gamma ratios separately is unnecessary.
Expansion in 1/k gives

    E(M-1)   =1/k+2/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^2 =1/k+5/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^3 =6/k^2+O(k^-3),
    E(M-1)^4 =3/k^2+O(k^-3).

For central binomial k,

    E[1/k; central]=2/n+2/n^2+O(n^-3),
    E[1/k^2; central]=4/n^2+O(n^-3).

For example expand around mu=n/2 with k-mu, whose odd central moments
vanish and whose second moment is n/4. The fourth central moment is O(n^2);
central-k Taylor denominators are bounded below by n/3, and the remaining
binomial tails are exponential. Thus the four mixed moments are respectively

    2/n+10/n^2+O(n^-3),
    2/n+22/n^2+O(n^-3),
    24/n^2+O(n^-3),
    12/n^2+O(n^-3).

Also E|M-1|^5=O(n^(-5/2)). To verify this last bound, split on central
S/k and R/k. There, M-1 is Lipschitz in their centered deviations and has
fifth absolute moment of this order. The chi-square exponential tails,
Holder, and higher inverse moments on central k bound the omitted part
exponentially. This is possible for all sufficiently large n, since k
then exceeds every fixed inverse-moment threshold used.

Fourth-order Taylor expansion with fifth-derivative remainder now proves
(B), including the factors 1/2,1/6,1/24. The fourth-order term is of size
1/n in the scaled generator, exactly the same order as the signed third
moment term. Therefore a derivation using only a third-order Taylor term
cannot give the complete weak 1/n correction, even before ReLU flips.

This partial expansion does not upgrade C004's full O(n^-1/2) error to
O(1/n). The unresolved pieces are the mixed baseline/flip moments and
angular geometry terms, uniformly enough to match the singular entrance.
If such a complete expansion is obtained, a time-step weak-error formula
also needs the discrete-vs-continuous semigroup correction, not only the
coefficient displayed in the one-step generator.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:3d7df9f2e51673034c933127493e891f934b33deb918593bd355f53d6e87ca80","revision_digest":"sha256:f282992730d5aa78d8c74a31004934b8f1d577dbbef911eb63487680c57725d0","source_id":"own-work:T244-w691-C030:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v1-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma area Lemma of arXiv:2605.29095, 'Asymptotics of the number of components of random polynomial lemniscates'] [Area Theorem] [Ahlfors], [crane-polynomialpreimage] 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item Let \( f \) be a univalent (injective holomorphic) function on a domain \( D \subseteq \mathbb{C} \), and let \( K \subset D \) be a measurable set. Then the area of the image \( f(K) \) is given by:
\[
\text{Area}\big(f(K)\big) = \int_K |f'(z)|^2 \, dA(z),
\]
where \( dA(z) = dx \, dy \) denotes the Euclidean area element in \( \mathbb{C} \).
\item Let \( p \) be a polynomial of degree \( n \) over \( \mathbb{C} \), and let \( K \) be any measurable subset of the complex plane. Let \( n(z, p, K) \) be the number of preimages of \( z \) under \( p \) that lie in \( K \) counted with multiplicity. Then,
\begin{align}
    \int_{\mathbb{C}} n(z, p, K)\, dA(z) = \int_K |p'(z)|^2\, dA(z).
\end{align}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition infinity squared of arXiv:2608.25889, 'Slope Inequalities for the Geography Problem of Spin Symplectic 4-Manifolds'] We say that a smooth oriented $4$-manifold $M$\/ has $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ if there exist infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible smooth $4$-manifolds
that are all homeomorphic to $M$.  
We say that $M$\/ has $\infty^2$-\emph{property}\/ if there exist infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible symplectic $4$-manifolds and infinitely many pairwise nondiffeomorphic irreducible nonsymplectic $4$-manifolds, all of which are homeomorphic to $M$.  
We also say that a symmetric bilinear form has $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ or $\infty^2$-\emph{property}\/ if it is the intersection form of a 
simply connected smooth $4$-manifold with $\infty$-\emph{property}\/ or $\infty^2$-property, respectively.
title: Definition infinity squared of arXiv:2608.25889

body:
[Lemma lem:thinned of arXiv:2608.12954, 'Rainbow percolation'] Let $c\in(0,1)$ and
$\varepsilon_1:=16e^{-\beta/32}+32N(1-c)^{N/2}+15(1-c)^{N^2}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $N(1-c)^{N/2}\le\tfrac12$, then $\mathbb P(W_{k,i})\ge1-\varepsilon_1$
  for all $k,i$.
\item[(ii)] $\mathbb P\big(O^N_u\cap O^N_v\setminus L_e\big)\le(1-c)^{N^2}$
  for every edge $e=\{u,v\}$ of $\mathsf H$.
\item[(iii)] No pair of points is assigned twice: not to two distinct
  window events, not to two distinct edges of $\mathsf H$, and not to
  a window event and an edge.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma L:basis-for-comparison of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take $x \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $y_1 \le y_2 \in \mathbb{Z}, t \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $[x,1]_{\textsf{L}}\le [y_1,t]_{\textsf{L}}$ and $[x,1]_{\textsf{L}}\le [y_2,t]_{\textsf{L}}$, and take $f:\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$. Then for any $E:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathbb{R}$,
$$
E[x, 1; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E[x, 1; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}} \le E^f[0,0; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E^f[0,0; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}},
$$
on the event where a geodesic in $E^f$ from $[0,0]_{\textsf{L}}$ to $[y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}}$ intersects $\{[r, 1]_{\textsf{L}} : r \ge x\}$. Similarly, 
$$
E[x, 1; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E[x, 1; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}} \ge E^f[0,0; y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}} - E^f[0,0; y_1, t]_{\textsf{L}},
$$
on the event where a geodesic in $E^f$ from $[0,0]_{\textsf{L}}$ to $[y_2, t]_{\textsf{L}}$ intersects $\{[r, 1]_{\textsf{L}} : r \le x\}$.

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.28578, 'On two differing geometric descriptions of the passage from microscopy to macroscopy in Ma'] Let $M$ be a connected closed Riemannian manifold, let $\Prob^{\infty}_+(M)$ be its Fr\'echet manifold of smooth positive probability densities and let $\Hspace_k\hookrightarrow C^1(M;TM)$ be a vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Then the following statements hold.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item The continuity operator $\Aop_{\rho}v=-\Div(\rho v)$ is the differential of the pushforward action, is surjective on the smooth core and identifies a density tangent with a particle velocity modulo the $\rho$ divergence free kernel.
		\item The weighted $L^2(\rho)$ norm and the reproducing kernel Hilbert norm produce fibrewise Otto and Stein tangent--cotangent Hilbert pairs by quotient and Riesz representation; their Onsager maps factor as $\Kop^{\bullet}_{\rho}=\Aop_{\rho}\Bop^{\bullet}_{\rho}$.
		\item Let $\Mop_{\rho}=\mathsf{P}^{\mathrm{hor}}_{\rho}\Iop_{\rho}\Iop_{\rho}^{*}$ on the Otto horizontal space. A regular covector $[f]$ induces the Otto tangent $\Aop_{\rho}\grad f$ and the Stein tangent $\Aop_{\rho}\Mop_{\rho}\grad f$. These tangents agree exactly when $\Mop_{\rho}\grad f=\grad f$, whilst the particle fields agree exactly when $\Iop_{\rho}\Iop_{\rho}^{*}\grad f=\grad f$.
		\item Positive proportionality of the two tangents gives the same unparametrised law curve, equality after a differentiable observation gives the same prescribed evolution of that observation, and spectral bounds on $\Mop_{\rho}$ compare dissipation and tangent cost. Agreement for every regular force in a closed force space is equivalent to $\Mop_{\rho}=\id$ there. Any positive self-adjoint response on a finite dimensional smooth force subspace can be realised by a finite rank reproducing kernel.
		\item Relative entropy supplies the common covector $[\log(\rho/\pi)]$. Its Wasserstein and Stein descents agree according to the preceding criterion; equality of their instantaneous dissipations is weaker than equality of their law tangents.
		\item Every regular minimal exponential family has smooth gradient solutions of the required Stein equations on the closed-manifold core. Membership in a prescribed kernel space is an additional range condition; when it holds, covector descent in expectation coordinates is realised by particle transport and agrees with the prescribed Fisher mirror evolution on the model.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.28578

Let $X$ be $n$ i.i.d. rows in $\mathbb{R}^M$ with covariance $\Sigma$. Split the rows into two independent parts of sizes $m$ and $n - m$ with sample covariances $S_1 = V_1\Lambda_1 V_1^T$ and $S_2$. The nonparametric eigenvalue-regularised covariance estimator is $\hat\Sigma = V_1 \operatorname{diag}(V_1^T S_2 V_1)\, V_1^T$, averaged over $K$ random splits. Then: (i) $\mathbb{E}[V_1^T S_2 V_1 \mid V_1] = V_1^T \Sigma V_1$, so each diagonal entry $v_i^T S_2 v_i$ is an unbiased estimate of the population variance in the direction $v_i$ - the Ledoit-Peche oracle $d_i^* = v_i^T\Sigma v_i$ evaluated on independent data; (ii) as $M, n \to \infty$ with $M/n \to c > 0$ and $m/n \to r \in (0,1)$, $\hat\Sigma$ is asymptotically optimal in Frobenius loss among estimators of the form $V_1 D V_1^T$ with $D$ diagonal (Lam 2016, Theorem 1); (iii) $\hat\Sigma$ is positive semidefinite and carries no bandwidth, floor or shrinkage constant beyond the split fraction (Lam recommends choosing $m$ by minimising $\|\hat\Sigma_m - S\|_F$ over a grid; $m = n/2$ is the usual default). A population direction of genuinely small variance keeps a small estimate (its held-out variance is small too); a direction whose small sample variance was a finite-sample cancellation receives the variance it actually has out of sample.
rows i.i.d. with finite fourth moments
M/n -> c > 0, m/n -> r in (0,1)
the two parts of the split are disjoint (independence of V_1 and S_2 is what carries the argument)

[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2608.18075, '2608.18075'] The stochastic convolution driver $Y=(Z,Z_\tau)$ has a centred Radon
Gaussian version in $\mathsf Y^+$.  Consequently, for every $\delta>0$
there is a compact set $\mathfrak L\subset\mathsf Y^+$ such that
\begin{align}
 p_{\mathfrak L}:=\mathbf P\{Y\in\mathfrak L\}>0,
 \qquad
 \sup_{y\in\mathfrak L}\|y\|_{\mathsf Y}<\delta.
\end{align}
The version in $\mathsf Y^+$ may be chosen from the same Fourier partial
sums as the canonical $\mathsf Y$ valued version, and hence the two agree
almost surely.

[Thm replaceprinciple of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] [TVuniversality] 
 For every  $n\geq 1$  let $A_n, B_n$ be two random $n \times n$  matrices. 
 Assume that the following two conditions hold. 
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item The sequence 
     \[\frac{1}{n} \left(\|A_n\|_{HS}^2 + \|B_n\|_{HS}^2\right)
     \]
     is bounded in probability, where $\|\cdot\|_{HS}$ denotes the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a matrix.
     \item For almost all complex number $z$,
     \[
     \frac{1}{n}\log \left|\det\left(A_n-zI_n\right)\right|-\frac{1}{n}\log \left|\det\left(B_n-zI_n\right)\right|
     \]
     converges in probability to $0$.
 \end{enumerate}
 Then $\mu_{A_n}-\mu_{B_n}$ converges in probability to $0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 34 of arXiv:2608.18075, '2608.18075'] Put
\begin{align*}
 s_*=\frac{\alpha_{\rm H}}2-\frac14,
 \qquad s_*<\gamma<\frac{\alpha_{\rm H}}2,
 \qquad \lambda_0=\frac{\alpha_{\rm H}}2+5,
 \qquad t_M=\lambda_0M^{-2}\log M.
\end{align*}
Fix $R_0<\infty$.  Let
$z\in C_0([0,t_M];C^\gamma)$ be a deterministic, mean zero,
divergence free compatible path with
$\|z\|_{C([0,t_M];C^\gamma)}\le R_0$, let $Z^0$ be the
stochastic convolution generated by the radial noise $d_0Q_0\dd W^0$, and
put
\begin{align*}
 D_t=P_tu_0+z_t,
 \qquad X=D+Z^0,
 \qquad U_0=1+\|u_0\|_{C^\gamma}.
\end{align*}
Let $u$ be the Navier--Stokes solution with linear part $X$, and let $\rho$
solve its linearised vorticity equation from $0\ne\rho_0\in L^2$.  There
are deterministic $M_0,K_{R_0},r_0<\infty$ and
$a_0,\alpha_0>0$, depending only on the fixed equation parameters, such
that, whenever
\begin{align}
 M\ge M_0\vee M^{(2)}(\rho_0)\vee K_{R_0}U_0^{r_0},
 
\end{align}
one has
\begin{align}
 \mathbf P_0\left\{
  \|\Pi_0\rho_{t_M}\|_2
  \ge a_0M^{-3}
       \|\rho_0\|_{H^{-(\alpha_{\rm H}/2+1)}}
 \right\}\ge\alpha_0.
 
\end{align}
The constants are uniform over all such compatible paths in the fixed
$R_0$ ball.  Here ``compatible'' means a limit, in the displayed topology,
of smooth Fourier truncated velocity paths; this class contains the
residual stochastic convolutions used below.
title: Lemma 34 of arXiv:2608.18075

body:
Let $E$ be a symmetric $p \times p$ matrix with eigen-decomposition $E = \sum_k \lambda_k u_k u_k^T$ (for instance a sample covariance) and let $C$ be any symmetric $p \times p$ matrix (the population covariance). Among all estimators of the form $\Xi = \sum_k \xi_k u_k u_k^T$ - the same eigenvectors as $E$, free eigenvalues - the Frobenius loss $\|\Xi - C\|_F^2$ is minimized by the oracle choice $\xi_k^{\mathrm{or}} = u_k^T C u_k$, the projection of the population matrix onto the $k$-th sample eigenvector, with minimal loss $\|C\|_F^2 - \sum_k (u_k^T C u_k)^2$. In particular the oracle eigenvalues are convex combinations of the population eigenvalues (they lie between the smallest and largest population eigenvalue) and their sum equals $\operatorname{tr} C$: a rotationally invariant estimator that is optimal in Frobenius loss never moves the trace and always shrinks the spread of the sample spectrum toward the population spread.
E and C symmetric p x p; the estimator class is restricted to the eigenvectors of E

[Thm 11 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Let $\alpha$ be a quadratic irrational, let $ax^2+bx+c$ be its minimal polynomial with $a,b,c \in \mathbb{Z}$, $\mathrm{gcd}(a,b,c)=1$ and $a>0$, and let $Q(x,y)=ax^2+bxy+cy^2$ be the corresponding binary quadratic form. For any constant $\theta>1$ and any integer $M \ge 1$, we have
\[ \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{1}{m^{\theta} \| m \alpha \|^{\theta}} = c(\alpha, \theta) \log M +O(1) \]
with an implied constant depending only on $\alpha$ and $\theta$. The constant $c(\alpha, \theta)$ is given by
\[ c(\alpha, \theta) = \frac{D^{\theta/2}}{\log \varepsilon} \sum_{\substack{n \in \mathbb{Z} \\ n \neq 0}} \frac{R_Q(n)}{|n|^{\theta}}, \]
where $D=b^2-4ac>0$ is the discriminant, $R_Q(n)$ is the number of primary representations of $n$, and $\varepsilon=(t_0+u_0\sqrt{D})/2$ with the smallest positive solution $(t_0,u_0)$ of Pell's equation $t^2-Du^2=4$.

Fix theta in (0,pi/2] and unit probe q; teacher w=cos(theta)q+sin(theta)u, u uniform on S^(ell-1) in q-perp, ell=d-1>=2. An unlabeled isotropic Gaussian pool and independent seed select m indices without teacher labels. The learner sees only those m teacher labels, plus q, theta and the unlabeled pool, and outputs a unit linear normal. Conditional on the pool and seed, at most (e*max(1,m/ell))^ell selected-label patterns occur. The latitude cap argument gives expected error at least sin(theta)*(2*(e*max(1,m/ell))^ell)^(-1/(ell-1))/(2*pi). For a rotation-equivariant protocol this applies to each fixed teacher-probe pair. If m/ell->alpha>0 in probability, liminf expected error>=sin(theta)/(2*pi*e*max(1,alpha)), independent of source-pool size. Threshold max-margin is equivariant. The same bound applies to each fixed-fraction deterministic limit and their infimum at retained alpha, excluding an asymptotic exponential envelope at fixed theta>0. No extra unselected labels, label-adaptive selection, or teacher-dependent side information are allowed. No matching upper rate or actual crossover is proved.
theta in (0,pi/2] fixed
Noiseless isotropic Gaussian teacher; fixed independent probe
Retained indices depend on unlabeled covariates and probe, not teacher labels
Learner observes only retained teacher labels plus unlabeled source pool and probe
Unit-normal linear output; rotation equivariance for fixed-teacher statement

[Theorem 60 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] We fix $\alpha \ino (1, 2]$. Let $\mu$ satisfy (\ref{hypostaintro}). 
Let $\tau_n$ be as in (\ref{defratr}) (i.e., ~namely, a GW($\mu$)-tree conditioned to have $n$ vertices). 
Let $\nu$ be a supercritical offspring distribution whose mean is denoted by $\ttm_\nu$. We assume that there is  $\ttb\ino ( \frac{2\alpha}{\alpha-1}, \infty)$ such that $\sum_{k\in \bbN} k^{1+2\ttb} \nu(k)\leko \infty$.
Let $(\bT, \boo)$ be an invariant GW($\nu$)-tree that is independent from $\tau_n$. 
We recall the $a_n$ and $b_n$ from (\ref{remindcv}) and we recall 
from (\ref{vutchi}) the definition of $\sigma_\nu$. We also recall the notation $\mathscr Q_n'$ from (\ref{VHCGDcv}) in Theorem \ref{VHCcvstable} $(iv)$. We keep the above notation. 
Then, conditionally given $(\bT, \boo)$, the following convergence 
\begin{eqnarray}

\Big(\mathscr Q_n'  ,  \tfrac{1}{ \sigma_\nu \! \sqrt{a_n}} \widehat{\cW}_{2n\cdot }(\tau_n),   \tfrac{1}{ \sigma_\nu \! \sqrt{a_n}}\widehat{\cW}^*_{n\cdot }(\tau_n)   \!\!  \!\!  \!\!  \!\!  \!\!   \!\! \! & , &\!   \!\!   \!\!  \!\!  \!\!  \!\!  \!\!  \tfrac{\sigma_\nu}{ \sqrt{a_n}} \widehat{W}_{2n\cdot }(\tau_n),\!  \tfrac{\sigma_\nu}{ \sqrt{a_n}} \widehat{W}^*_{n\cdot }(\tau_n)\Big)  \nonumber  \\
&\underset{n\to \infty}{-\!\!\!-\!\!\!-\!\!\!\longrightarrow}& \big( X', H', H', \widehat{W}',  \widehat{W}' , \widehat{W}',  
\widehat{W} '\big)
\end{eqnarray}
a.s.~holds weakly on $\bD([0, 1], \bbR) \! \times \! \bC ([0, 1], \bbR)^6$ equipped with the product topology. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 44 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] There exist positive constants $\eta$ and $\sigma$ such that the following holds for all $p_H \le p \le p_H \cdot n^\eta$.
  For all $J' \subseteq J \in \cJ^*$, all large enough $n$, and all $G \subseteq K_n$ with at most $f \cdot \bigl(\log(1/p)\bigr)^2$ edges,
  \[
    \left|\bigl\{\varphi \in \Emb(J,K_n) : \varphi(J) \cap G = \varphi(J')\bigr\} \right| \cdot p^{e_J - e_{J'}} \le
    \begin{cases}
      n^\sigma & \text{if $J' \in \cJ_\emptyset^*$,}\\
      n^{-3\sigma} & \text{otherwise}.
    \end{cases}
  \]

[Lemma lem:time-inhomogeneous of arXiv:2411.01364, 'Global Dynamics of Granular Media Equations via Stochastic Order'] Suppose Assumption (asp:potential of the paper) holds, and let $\{\nu_t\}_{t\in \mathbb R}\in C_b(\mathbb R;\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R))$. Consider the following time-inhomogeneous SDE
    \begin{equation}
        \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} X_t=-V'(X_t)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} t-(W'*\nu_t)(X_t)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} t+\sigma(X_t)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} B_t.
    \end{equation}
     Let $X_t^{s,\mu}$ be the unique solution of equation (equation eq:sde-1 of the paper) at time $t$ with starting time $s$ and initial distribution $\mu$ and $P^*(t,s)$ be the dual semigroup of equation (equation eq:sde-1 of the paper), i.e., $P^*(t,s)\mu:=\mathcal L(X_t^{s,\mu})$. Then the equation (equation eq:sde-1 of the paper) has a unique entrance measure $\{\rho^{\nu}_t\}_{t\in \mathbb R}$ in $C_b(\mathbb R;\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R))$, i.e., $P^*(t,s)\rho^{\nu}_s=\rho^{\nu}_t$ for all $t\geq s$ and there exist $C,\lambda>0$ such that for all $\mu\in \mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$, $t\geq s$, we have
     \begin{equation}
         d_2\big(\mathcal L(X_t^{s,\mu}), \rho^{\nu}_t\big)\leq C(1+\|\mu\|_2^2)e^{-\lambda (t-s)},
     \end{equation}
    where $d_2(\cdot,\cdot)$ is defined by
      \[
      d_2(\mu_1,\mu_2):=\int_{\mathbb R}(1+|x|^2)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} |\mu_1-\mu_2|(x), \ \text{ for all } \ \mu_1,\mu_2\in \mathcal P_2(\mathbb R).
      \]
    In particular,
     \begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
        \item if $\{\nu_t\}_{t\in \mathbb R}$ is an entrance measure of (equation eq:mvsystem of the paper), i.e., $P^*_t\nu_s=\nu_{t+s}$ for all $t\geq 0, s\in \mathbb R$, then $\rho^{\nu}_t=\nu_t$ for all $t\in \mathbb R$;
        \item if $\{\nu_t\}_{t\in \mathbb R}$ is a singleton $\{\nu\}\subset\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$, then  the unique entrance measure $\{\rho^{\nu}_t\}_{t\in \mathbb R}$ is also a singleton $\{\rho\}\subset \mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$ such that $\rho$ is the unique invariant measure of (equation eq:sde-1 of the paper) in $\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$.
     \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:time-inhomogeneous of arXiv:2411.01364

[Lemma lem:VEB-escape of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] There exists a real number $\lambda_0 \in (0,1/2)$ such that the following holds. Consider any $\lambda \in (0,\lambda_0)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ such $p_0=1$ and, for all $i \ge 1$, $W_i \le (4/\lambda)^i$. Suppose that $\overline{p}$ has finitely many bins which are strongly exposed. 
Let $X$ be the backoff process with
birth rate~$2 \lambda$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and cohort set~$\mathcal{C}=\{A,B\}$ (Definition~(def:backoff-cohorts of the paper)).
Let $j_0\geq 5$ be a sufficiently large positive integer such that all strongly-exposed bins are in $[j_0-1]$.
Let $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{init}}$ be the event that, for every step $t' \in [T^{\overline{p},j_0}]$, $n^{X^B} \ge 2$. 
We will condition on $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{init}}$.
Let
$\tau_0 =  T^{\overline{p},j_0}$. 
Let
$\Psi_0$ be the  initialising high-level state   
with $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be   the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper) and let $\ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$  (Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-state-space of the paper)) be the  $\Psi_0$-closure (Definition~(def:hls-closed of the paper)) of~$\mathrm{hls}$.  
The $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule~$\mathrm{hls}$ is a transition rule (Definition~(def:transition-rule of the paper)) by Observation~(obs:BB-bounding-is-transrule of the paper) and 
it is $\ensuremath{\Psi^{\mathrm{BB}}(\Psi_0)}$-valid (Definition~(def:valid of the paper)) by
Lemma~(lem:backoff-bounding-valid of the paper).

Conditioned on $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{init}}$,
the VEB-coupling (Definition~(equation def:VEB-couple of the paper)   couples $X$ with a volume process $V$ from $\Psi_0$ with  transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$ and with a sequence $E_1, E_2,\ldots $ of escape processes with send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. 
The coupling uses $b_i^{E_0}(\tau_0+1)$ as a synonym for $\mathbf{e}_i^X(\tau_0+1)$.

With probability at least~$2/3$,  
both of the following hold.
 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item for all $t> \tau_0$ such that 
$\textup{type}^{\Psi(t)}  = \textup{advancing}$
and the $S\in \mathcal{S}^{\Psi(t)}$,
$\sum_{k \in  S } p_kb_k^{E_{g^{\Psi(t-1)}}}(t) \leq \lambda | S  |/80$. Moreover, $S$ is non-empty.
\item for all $t> \tau_0$ such that 
$\textup{type}^{\Psi(t)} \notin \{\textup{failure},\textup{advancing}\}$ and all $k \in [j^{\Psi(t-1)}-1]$ such that $W_k \ge (j^{\Psi(t-1)})^\chi$, $p_kb_k^{E_{g^{\Psi(t-1)}}}(t) \le \lambda/80$. Moreover, there is at least one such $k\in [j-1]$.
\end{enumerate}

Own-work research draft, proof (unaudited). Fix k,D>=1, b>0, K>=0 and 0<lambda<=1<=Lambda. For all b-Lipschitz maps F:[0,1]^k to R^D and probability densities p with lambda<=p<=Lambda and Lip(p)<=K, a common scalar-input ReLU feedforward DAG with at most W charged edge weights and biases achieves sup_(F,p) inf_theta W1((G_theta)#Unif[0,1],F#(p dx))<=C W^(-2/k) for W>=W0. C,W0 depend only on these fixed constants. Depth O(W), unrestricted real weights, skip connections and discontinuous target-to-weight assignments are allowed; every fixed coefficient is charged. Exact inverse triangular sampling has Lipschitz constants bounded by L0=0, Lj=(1+B/c)L_(j-1)+1/c, where c=lambda/Lambda and B=K/lambda+Lambda*K/lambda^2. Apply the known Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk arXiv:1906.09477 Theorem 3.3 p.5 at r=1,d=k to F composed with that sampler; a logarithmic-size tent-map conversion from scalar noise uses the Lipschitz constant of the exact map, not the coding network. For an (a,b)-bi-Lipschitz C1 chart with Lip(DF)<=M, its exactly uniform surface law satisfies the hypotheses with lambda=(a/b)^k, Lambda=(b/a)^k and K=k*b^(k-1)*M/a^k. This covers controlled C1,1 cube images with boundary. It does not cover arbitrary closed reach-bounded manifolds or merely bounded densities, establish finite-bit rates or optimality, or claim novelty. Independent review and priority assessment pending.
Fixed constants stated above, Euclidean Lipschitz norms, scalar uniform latent source, sparse DAG count including fixed coefficients. Uniform-surface corollary requires an injective bi-Lipschitz chart and a Lipschitz derivative.

[Lemma lem:cesaro_ell of arXiv:2509.03048, 'Elephant random walks on infinite Cayley trees'] Let $p \in [0, 1)$ and $m \ge 1$. There is a constant $\tilde{C}_{p, d, m} > 0$, such that
    \[
        \mathbb{E}|\Xi_n|^m \le (\tilde{C}_{p, d, m})^m \cdot r_n^{-m}.
    \]
    In fact, for any $m \ge 2$, one may take $\tilde{C}_{p, d, m} = \tilde{C}_{p, d} \cdot m$ for some constant $\tilde{C}_{p, d} > 0$. Consequently, for any $u \ge \frac{2\tilde{C}_{p, d}\exp(1)}{r_n}$, one has
    \[
        \mathbb{P}(|\Xi_n| \ge u) \le \exp\bigg(-\frac{ur_n}{\tilde{C}_{p, d}\exp(1)}\bigg).
    \]
title: Lemma lem:cesaro_ell of arXiv:2509.03048

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional Finsler metric measure manifold. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$.
Then for $p>\frac{n}{2}$ and $K>0$, we have the following inequalities.
\ben
\item[{\rm (1)}] If $0< r\leq R\leq \frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{K}}$, then
\beq
& &\left[\frac{A(R)}{e^{\vartheta R} \sin^{n-1}(\sqrt{K} R)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2p-1}} -\left[\frac{A(r)}{e^{\vartheta r} \sin^{n-1}(\sqrt{K} r)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2p-1}} \nonumber\\
&&  \leq \left(\frac{n-1}{(2p-1)(2p-n)}\right)^{\frac{p-1}{2 p-1}}\left(\left\|{\rm Ric}_{\infty}^{K}\right\|_{p, R, \vartheta}(x_{0})\right)^{\frac{p}{2p-1}} \int_{r}^{R}\left(\frac{1}{\sin (\sqrt{K} s)}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{2p-1}} ds. 
\eeq

\item[{\rm (2)}] If $\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{K}}<r \leq R <\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{K}}$, then
\beq
&& \left[\frac{A(R)}{e^{\vartheta R} \sin^{n-1}(\sqrt{K} R)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2p-1}}-\left[\frac{A(r)}{e^{\vartheta r} \sin^{n-1}(\sqrt{K} r)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2p-1}}\nonumber\\
&& \leq  \left(\frac{n-1}{(2 p-1)(2 p-n)}\right)^{\frac{p-1}{2p-1}}\left(\left\|{\rm Ric}_{\infty}^{K}\right\|_{p, R, \vartheta}(x_{0})\right)^{\frac{p}{2p-1}} \int_{r}^{R} \frac{1}{\sin^{2}(\sqrt{K} s)} ds. 
\eeq

body:
[Definition def:simple-sequential-gambles of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $\mathcal{Y}$ be a set of per-round outcomes, $T\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$ a time horizon, and $\{\hat\mathcal{Z}_t\subseteq(\mathcal{Y}\to\overline{\mathbb{R}})\}_{t=1}^T$ sets of per-round gambles.
  The \emph{simple sequential gamble space} $(\mathcal{Y},\{\hat\mathcal{Z}_t\}_t,T)$ is the sequential gamble space $(\mathcal{Y},\hat\mathcal{Z},T)$ given by
  $\hat\mathcal{Z}^{(s)} = \hat\mathcal{Z}_{|s|+1}$ for all $s\in\mathcal{Y}^{<T}$.
  When we have some $\hat\mathcal{Z}\subseteq(\mathcal{Y}\to\overline{\mathbb{R}})$ such that $\hat\mathcal{Z}_t = \hat\mathcal{Z}$ for all $t\leq T$, we call it a \emph{simple repeated gamble space} and write it more simply as $(\mathcal{Y},\hat\mathcal{Z},T)$.
title: Simple sequential gamble space

body:
[Definition 66 of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For a sequence $f=(f_r)_{r\ge0}$ with values in $\Bbbk=\Q(q)$, let
\[
 (Lf)_r=f_{r+1},\qquad (Mf)_r=q^rf_r;
\]
then $LM=qML$.  In one discrete variable, the standard
$q$-Weyl-algebra definition of $q$-holonomicity is equivalent to the
existence of a nonzero recurrence
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a=0}^{d}p_a(q,q^r)f_{r+a}=0,
 \qquad p_a(q,M)\in\Q(q,M),
\end{equation}
after clearing denominators if necessary.  This equivalence and the
multivariate $q$-Weyl-algebra definition used below are recalled in
\cite[Section~3]{GLsurvey}.
title: Definition 66 of arXiv:2608.29585

body:
[Lemma L:abstract-convergence of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $f_n:\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$ be a sequence of functions satisfying (equation E:MC-lambda of the paper) which converge uniformly on compact sets to continuous limit $f:\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R}$ which also satisfies (equation E:MC-lambda of the paper). Suppose that additionally $f$ satisfies the following shape bound: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item For all $c_0 > 0$, there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for all $u = (x, a, t; y, b; t + s) \in \mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow$ with $s < c_0$ we have that
		$$
		\left|f(u) + \frac{(x-y)^2}{s} \right|\le C s^{1/3} \log^2\left(\frac{{2\|u\|_2}}{s}\right).
		$$
	\end{itemize}
	Suppose $\pi_n$ is a sequence of continuous geodesics for $f_n$ between points $(u_n, s)$ to $(v_n, t)$, where the sequence $(u_n, s; v_n, t)$ is precompact in $\mathbb{H}^{2+}_\uparrow$.
	Then:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The sequence $\pi_n$ is precompact in the uniform topology on functions from $[s, t] \to \Lambda$.
		\item If $\pi:[s, t] \to \Lambda$ is a subsequential limit of $\pi_n$, then $\pi$ satisfies (equation E:f-equality of the paper) for any finite set $\{s = t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_k = t\} \subset [s, t]$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma L:abstract-convergence of arXiv:2604.10020

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2609.02878 (conjecture environment labelled conj:intro-kpolystable-fibres).] Assume that every fibre \(F_y\) is K-polystable with respect to
\(-K_{F_y}\). Then the finite-time K\"ahler--Ricci flow is Type I:
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{0\le t<T}\sup_{x\in X}
 (T-t)|\Rm(g(t))|_{g(t)}(x)<\infty.
\end{equation}
Moreover, fix \(q\in Y\), and let
\(\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}\in2\pi c_1(F_q)\) be a normalized
K\"ahler--Einstein metric,
\[
 \Ric(\omega_{q,{\rm KE}})=\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}.
\]
Write \(g_{q,{\rm KE}}=2g_{\omega_{q,{\rm KE}}}\), so that
\(\Ric(g_{q,{\rm KE}})=\tfrac12g_{q,{\rm KE}}\). After forgetting the
conjugate heat measures, every Type-I-scale blowup at \(\xi\) based at
\(F_q\) is isomorphic, as a K\"ahler metric flow, to
\begin{equation}
 \left(
 \C^m\times F_q,\,
 J_0\oplus J_{F_q},\,
 g_{\rm E}+(-s)g_{q,{\rm KE}}
 \right)_{s<0}.
\end{equation}
Thus the residual factor is the central fibre with its own complex
structure. (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)
title: Open problem: K-polystable smooth fibres

[Thm 5 (Skorokhod representation theorem) of arXiv:2606.27078, 'Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Jumps: A General Framework and Equivalent Formulatio'] Let $\{\overline{\mathbb{P}}^{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}$ be a sequence of probability measures on the enlarged space $\overline{\Omega}$ introduced in Section~2.
Assume that $\overline{\mathbb{P}}^{n}\to \overline{\mathbb{P}}^{0}$ weakly in $\mathcal{P}(\overline{\Omega})$.
Then there exist a probability space $([0,1],\mathcal{B}([0,1]),\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is the Lebesgue measure, and $\overline{\Omega}$-valued random variables $\{z^{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0}$ defined on this space such that
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] $\lambda\circ(z^{n})^{-1}=\overline{\mathbb{P}}^{n}$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}$.
\item[(2)] $z^{n}\to z^{0}$ pointwise (i.e., in the product topology of $\overline{\Omega}$) $\lambda$-a.s.\ as $n\to\infty$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Skorokhod representation theorem

A Strichartz estimate for a wave equation $\Box_{\bar{g}} \phi = F$ on a curved spacetime $(\bar{M}, \bar{g})$ is an inequality of the form $\|\phi\|_{L^p_t L^q_x(I \times \Sigma)} \le C (\|\phi(0)\|_{H^s(\Sigma)} + \|\partial_t \phi(0)\|_{H^{s-1}(\Sigma)} + \|F\|_{L^{\tilde{p}'}_t L^{\tilde{q}'}_x(I \times \Sigma)})$, where $(p, q)$ and $(\tilde{p}, \tilde{q})$ are wave-admissible exponents satisfying $2/p + (n-1)/q = (n-1)/2 - s$.
g_bar is a Lorentzian metric with bounded geometry
(p, q) is an admissible exponent pair
s is the Sobolev regularity of initial data
title: Strichartz Estimates on Curved Spacetimes

[Lemma lem:cutoff-gradient-product of arXiv:2605.03718, 'Potential Hessian Ascent III:\\ Sampling the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model at $\beta < 1/'] Let $N\in\mathbb N$, let $\operatorname{Sym}_N$ be the set of real symmetric $N \times N$ matrices, and let $(\operatorname{Sym}_N,\schnorm{\cdot})$ be the normalized Schatten-2 norm metric on $\operatorname{Sym}_N$. Let $\mathcal H$ be a real Hilbert space.
Let $f: \operatorname{Sym}_N\to\mathcal H$ be $L_f$-Lipschitz on $S$ with respect to the stated metric and let $\chi:\operatorname{Sym}_N\to\mathbb R$ be globally $L_{\chi}$-Lipschitz.
Fix open measurable sets $\mathcal L\subseteq S\subseteq \mathbb R^N$ and assume:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $0\leqslant \chi\leqslant 1$ everywhere and $\chi=0$ on $S^{c}$,
\item $d\chi=0$ a.e.\ on $\mathcal L^{c}$ (equivalently, $\supp(d\chi)\subseteq\mathcal L$),
\item $\sup_{x\in S}\|f(x)\|_{\mathcal H}\leqslant J$ for some $J<\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $h:=\chi f$ is locally Lipschitz, and for every random variable $X$ with values in $M_N(\mathbb R)$,
\begin{equation}

\mathop{{}\mathbb{E}}\bigl[\|d(\chi f)(X)\|_{\mathrm{HS}(\operatorname{Sym}_N,\mathcal H)}^2\bigr]
\ \leqslant\
2(\dim \mathcal H)L_f^2 \;+\; 2\,J^2\,L_{\chi}^2\,\mathop{{}\mathbb{P}}\{X\in\mathcal L\},
\end{equation}
where $\left\lVert{\cdot}\right\rVert_{\mathrm{HS}(\operatorname{Sym}_N,\mathcal H)}$ is as in \pref{eq:intrinsic-gradient-norm-coordinates}.

Let X and Y be Banach spaces and T in K(X,Y). If x_n -> x weakly in X, then ||T x_n - T x|| -> 0. Conversely, if X is reflexive and T in B(X,Y) maps every weakly convergent sequence to a norm convergent sequence, then T is compact. Without reflexivity the converse fails (the identity of l^1 maps weakly convergent sequences to norm convergent ones by Schur's property but is not compact).
X and Y are Banach spaces
T is bounded and linear
for the converse, X is reflexive

The corresponding class parameter is
\[
    d_{\mathrm{OD}}^\star(\Hc)
    :=
    \inf_{\psi}d_{\mathrm{OD}}(\psi),
\]
where the infimum ranges over all regularizers attaining their minima on realized version spaces.

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C005 v1. Exact obstruction reduction for Target 3, not an escape theorem; no novelty claimed for Gaussian conditioning. Let d>=3, m>=1, eta>0, x_* a deterministic unit vector, A have iid N(0,1) entries, and independently x0~N(0,I_d/d). Use f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2 and unmodified GD. Set e1=x_*, q0=<e1,x0>, rho0=||x0-q0 e1||, e2=(x0-q0 e1)/rho0, E an orthonormal basis of their perpendicular space, g=Ae1, h=Ae2, B=AE, z0=q0*g+rho0*h, v0=z0*(z0^2-g^2) coordinatewise, s=||v0||, u=v0/s, P=I-u*u^T, w=B^T*u, q1=q0-eta*g^T*v0/m, p1=rho0-eta*h^T*v0/m. Excluding null events rho0*s=0, conditional on F1=sigma(x0,g,h,w), z1=A*x1 has Gaussian law with mean mu=q1*g+p1*h-eta*||w||^2*v0/m and covariance tau^2*P, where tau=eta*s*||w||/m. Also w is standard Gaussian in dimension d-2, independently of sigma(x0,g,h). Consequently E[q2|F1]=q1-eta/m sum_i g_i*mu_i*(mu_i^2+3*tau^2*(1-u_i^2)-g_i^2). This retains the residual-direction memory term; centering at q1*g+p1*h with conditionally mean-zero error for the same F1 is false. No claim rules out a different conditioning history or center. At m=ceil(alpha*d), ||w||^2/m converges in probability to 1/alpha for fixed alpha>0. Growing-horizon response and overlap-noise control, and random-start escape, remain open.

d>=3, m>=1, eta>0

body:
[Prop DL-top of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] The topology of $\partial {\rm DL}(p,q)$ is as follows
		\begin{itemize}
			\item $\rho_{x_0}$ and $\rho'_{x'_0}$ are isolated points. 
			\item $\rho_i\to \rho_{\omega_0}$ if $i\to\infty$, and $\rho_i\to \rho'_{\omega'_0}$ if $i\to-\infty$.
			\item $\rho_{\omega_n}\to\rho_{\omega}$ if $\omega_n\to\omega$, and $\rho'_{\omega'_n}\to\rho'_{\omega'}$  if $\omega'_n\to\omega'$.
			\item $\rho_{x_0}\to\rho_{\omega}$ for $\omega\neq \omega_0$ if $x_0\to\omega$.
			\item $\rho_{x_0}\to\rho_{\omega_0}$ if $x_0\to\omega_0$ and $h(x_0)\to-\infty$.
			\item $\rho_{x_0}\to\rho'_{\omega'_0}$ if $x_0\to\omega_0$ and $h(x_0)\to+\infty$.
			\item $\rho_{x_0}\to \rho_i$ if $x_0\to\infty$ such that $h(x_0)=i$.
		\end{itemize}
		and similarly for $\rho'_{x'_0}$. Also, every sequence of distinct points in $\partial {\rm DL}(p,q)$ has a subsequence of one of these types. See Figure~(fig:DLboundary of the paper) for a portrait in the case $(p,q)=(2,2)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsc{Topology of $\partial {\rm DL}(p,q)$}

[Defn 20 of arXiv:2608.30380, 'Morita Induction and Geometric Ideals in $\ell^p$ Roe-Type Algebras'] A Banach space $V$ has the \emph{uniform projection property} if there exist a constant $K\geq1$ and a function $f:\N\to\N$ such that, for every finite-dimensional subspace $F\subseteq V$, there is a finite-rank projection $P\in B(V)$ satisfying
\[
 F\subseteq\ran P,
 \qquad
 \|P\|\leq K,
 \qquad
 \rank P\leq f(\dim F).
\]

Conditional counterexample, independent review pending: for kappa>=0, kappa!=6, fix 0<a<b<c and stop in 0<X<Y<Z. Solve locally dX=[2/X-beta]dt-sqrt(kappa)dB and dY=[2/Y-beta]dt-sqrt(kappa)dB with beta=(6-kappa)(1/X+1/Y)/3, X_0=a,Y_0=b. Set W=integral beta dt+sqrt(kappa)B and Z=g_t(c)-W. These X,Y are real Loewner marks for W. For C(u)=B(1/3,1/3)^(-1) integral_0^u [v(1-v)]^(-2/3)dv, C(X/Y) is a local martingale, although W has bracket kappa dt and nonzero drift. The second Cardy observable C(X/Z) has normalized drift (6-kappa)(1/Z-1/Y)/3, which is nonzero. This refutes only one-observable identification, not percolation conformal invariance.

\[
\begin{split}
\msF_1 &= z w + s t + t f_4 + f_8, \\
\msF_2 &= z^2 s + z (t g_3 + g_7) + t^2 y + t g_6 + g_{10},
\end{split}
\]
where $f_4, f_8 \in \mbC [x, y, w]$ and $g_3, g_7, g_6, g_{10} \in \mbC [x, y, s, w]$.

[Defn d.omegatmixing-field of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] \ 
 \begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item  The random field $M=\{M(x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ with values in $\mathbb {M} $  
satisfies  {\em $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations}  if
there exists an increasing-decreasing family of 
 functions $\omega_k :  [0, \infty) \to [0,2]$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, 
(called correlation decay functions), such that $\lim_{s \to \infty}\omega_k(s) = 0$ for all $k \in\mathbb{N}$ and for all $p,q \in \mathbb{N}$, $x_1,\ldots,x_{p+q} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and all $f \in \textnormal{BL}(\mathbb {M} ^p)$, and
  $g \in \textnormal{BL}(\mathbb {M} ^q)$ we have

\begin{align} 
\left| \mathbb {E} [f(\bk {M(x_i)}1{p}) \, g(\bk  {M(x_i)}{p+1}{p+q})] - \mathbb {E} [f(\bk  {M(x_i)}1p)] \, \mathbb {E} [g(\bk  {M(x_i)}{p+1}{p+q})] \right| \le \omega_{p+q}(s),
\end{align}

where $s := d(\bk x1p,\bk x{p+1}{p+q})$ is at (equation defs of the paper).
\item  The random field $M$
satisfies {\em $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations}  if~(equation e.field-mixing of the paper) holds when \textnormal{BL}\ is replaced by $\mathbb{B} $.
 \item  Under Item~(i)  (resp. Item (ii)), the random field  $M$  has  {\em fast $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations}  (resp.  {\em fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations}) 
 if $(\omega_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ are fast decreasing. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Mixing correlations of the random field

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2511.02725, 'Mixing of general biased adjacent transposition chains'] There exists a constant $C'(\eps) = e^{O(1/\ep)}$ such that the following holds. 
Consider two permutations $\eta,\bar\eta\in \vloc$ and let $A=[i+1,n-j]$, $A^c=[n]\bs A$, and 
$A_r = [i+1+r, n-j-r]$. Then for $r\ge \ell_{\max}$, $r\le \fc{n-j-i-\ell_{\max}-1}2$, 
\begin{multline*}
\big\|
\mu\pa{\si({A_r})\in \cdot \mid \si(A^c) = \eta, \si\in \vloc} - 
\mu\pa{\bar\si({A_r})\in \cdot \mid \bar\si(A^c)  = \bar\eta,   \bar\si\in \vloc}
 \big\|_{\tv} \\
\le 
\exp(-r/C'(\eps)\ell_{\max}).
\end{multline*}
If $i=0$, the above holds with $A_r=[1,n-j-r]$, and if $j=0$, the above holds with $A_r=[i+1 + r,n]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let (X_n)_{n >= 0} be a martingale for a filtration (F_n) and let F_infinity be the sigma-algebra generated by the union of the F_n. The following are equivalent: (i) the family {X_n} is uniformly integrable; (ii) X_n converges almost surely AND in L^1 to some X_infinity; (iii) there exists Y in L^1 with X_n = E[Y | F_n] almost surely for every n, that is the martingale is CLOSED. When these hold one may take Y = X_infinity, and X_infinity = E[Y | F_infinity]. Consequences: for a UI martingale, E[X_infinity] = E[X_0], and the optional stopping identity E[X_tau] = E[X_0] holds for EVERY almost surely finite stopping time tau, with no boundedness assumption on tau or on the martingale - this is a genuinely stronger conclusion than the standard three sufficient conditions (bounded tau, bounded martingale, or E[tau] finite with bounded increments). An L^1-bounded martingale need not be UI, and then only the almost sure half of (ii) survives. For p > 1, an L^p-bounded martingale is automatically UI by de la Vallee Poussin and converges in L^p as well; p = 1 is the exceptional case. [standard; e.g. Williams, Probability with Martingales, Theorems 13.3 and 14.1]
(X_n) a martingale with respect to (F_n)
for the optional stopping consequence: tau an almost surely finite stopping time and the martingale uniformly integrable

OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Prove a quenched invariance principle for simple random walk on the random interlacement set and on an infinite component of the vacant set of random interlacements. Source: Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems, Open Problem 16.7, p. 248. Status notes: Procaccia, Rosenthal and Sapozhnikov (PTRF 2016) proved a quenched invariance principle for random walk on the interlacement set for every u > 0 and on the vacant set for u small; combined with the 2023 sharpness result of Duminil-Copin, Goswami, Rodriguez, Severo and Teixeira (which gives the required decoupling and local uniqueness for all u < u*), the vacant-set case throughout the supercritical phase appears to follow, but this combination was not verified in a fetched source. Admitted for the vacant set with u in the whole phase (0, u*) as the residual question.
Posed in Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems

[Proposition prop:stat of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] When the condition $\mathbb{E} \sigma_1  = \int_0^\infty \big(1-G(t)\big)dt < \infty$ 
is satisfied then the discrete time Markov chain $\{K_n\}$ is positive recurrent 
and its stationary distribution $\pi$ has finite mean: 
$\sum_{k=1}^\infty k \pi_k < \infty$. Similarly, the sequence of service stages 
posesses a unique stationary distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^+$ which has finite mean 
$\int_0^\infty y dF(y)<\infty$. 

Further, if for some $m>1$ 
$\mathbb{E}[\sigma_1^m]= \int_0^\infty m t^{m-1} \big(1-G(t)\big) dt <\infty$, then 
$\int_0^\infty y^m dF(y)<\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:stat of arXiv:2603.20078

body: Let C be a convex subset of a real vector space X and f: C -> R. f is convex if f(lambda x + (1-lambda) y) <= lambda f(x) + (1-lambda) f(y) for all x, y in C and lambda in [0,1]. If X is a normed space with dual X*, the subdifferential of f at a point x_0 in C is the set partial f(x_0) = {v in X* : f(x) >= f(x_0) + v(x - x_0) for all x in C}, whose elements are called subgradients of f at x_0; partial f(x_0) may be empty, a single point, or contain more than one point. [standard, e.g. Rockafellar, Convex Analysis]
title: Convex Function and Its Subdifferential

[Proposition 46 of arXiv:2607.08536, 'Soft edge limit of the Laguerre beta-ensemble at the lower edge'] Fix $\beta>0$ and assume $a_n\le (\log n)^{1/2}$. 
    Let $B^{(\cdr_n)}(t)$ be standard Brownian motion with drift $\cdr_n=-a_n\beta$ and let $U$ be an independent $\textup{Unif }[0, 1]$ random variable. Let $\mathcal{F}_t,t\ge 0$ be the filtration of $B$ enlarged with $U$.
    Let $\xi_k, \lfloor\log^6 n\rfloor\le k\le n-1$ be independent $\log\mathrm{beta}'(p_k,q_k)$-distributed random variables with $p_k=\beta k/2,q_k=\beta(k+2a_n)/2$. 
    
    Then there exists a sequence of stopping times $\{\tau_{n,k},\lfloor\log^6 n\rfloor\le k\le n\}$ with respect to $\mathcal{F}_t,t\ge 0$ such that the following statements hold for all $n$ larger than a fixed $\beta$ dependent constant.
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item We have $0=\tau_{n,n}<\tau_{n,n-1}<\dots<\tau_{n,\lfloor\log^6 n\rfloor}$. For $\lfloor\log^6 n\rfloor\le k\le n-1$ the differences $\Delta \tau_{n,k} := \tau_{n,k}-\tau_{n,k+1}$ are independent, and
        \[
            B^{(\cdr_n)}(\tau_{n,k}) - B^{(\cdr_n)}(\tau_{n,k+1})\ed \xi_k.
        \]
        \item Let $t_{n,k} = \frac{1}{\beta}\log\frac{n}{k}$ for $\lfloor\log^6 n\rfloor\le k\le n$, then  we have 
        \begin{align*}
               \pr\left(t_{n,k} -\frac{a_n}{k\beta }\le \tau_{n,k}\le t_{n,k} + \frac{\log^{4+1/2}n}{k}, \quad \lfloor\log^6 n\rfloor\le k\le n\right)\ge 1-e^{-\log^{10/9}n}.
        \end{align*}    
    \end{enumerate}
title: Proposition 46 of arXiv:2607.08536
