[Theorem 77 (Filtered critical realization theorem) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Fix \(N\ge2\) and \(\beta\in(1/3,1/2)\).  The assignment
\eqref{cc:eq-critical-rees-compiler} has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.7em]
\item It is a well-defined map from controlled critical entrances to
\(\mathscr R^{\rm cr}_{\le N}(H)\), and
\begin{equation}
 \|P_{n,r}L_n(s,t)\|_{\mathfrak W^{[r]}_{\rm mf}(n)}
 \le C_{N,\beta,P}\,\omega(s,t)^{n\beta}
 
\end{equation}
for every \(2\le n\le N\) and every exact depth \(r\).
\item If the input area is little weak trace on every interval, each Rees
coefficient belongs to the corresponding little logarithmic grade.
\item The construction is natural under bounded linear maps: the induced
map on every coefficient is the tensor pushforward, and its norm is bounded
by the appropriate power of the operator norm.
\item If \(x=L_n(s,t)\ne0\) and \(r_0=\nu_F(x)\), then
\(P_{n,r}x=0\) for \(r<r_0\), while the class of
\(P_{n,r_0}x\) in \(F_{r_0}L_n/F_{r_0+1}L_n\) is the intrinsic initial
normal symbol of \(x\).  Thus the least nonzero Rees cost is canonical even
though the full split lift is not.
\item Optional evaluation, a selected singular lift, and the split Rees realization
commute under the hypotheses of
\Cref{cc:prop-causal-normal-completion}.  In particular, no source application needs a second stopped or
gauge-covariance proof for its compiled logarithm.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition 8 (Windowed Microcanonical Ensemble) of arXiv:2607.23526, 'Equivalence of Canonical and Microcanonical Ensembles for Euclidean Lattices'] Let $\Delta>0$. For $E\in\R$ and $N\geq1$, denote
\[\Omega_N(E,\Delta):=\{x\in\Lambda^N:E\leq H_N(x)<E+\Delta\},\quad G_N(E,\Delta):=\#\Omega_N(E,\Delta).\]
Whenever $G_N(E,\Delta)>0$, define the windowed microcanonical ensemble as the uniform measure
\[\mu^{\mc}_{N,E,\Delta}(x):=G_N(E,\Delta)^{-1}\one_{\Omega_N(E,\Delta)}(x)\]
on $\Omega_N(E,\Delta)$, and define its entropy as $R_{N,E,\Delta}^{\mc}:=\log G_N(E,\Delta)$.
title: Windowed Microcanonical Ensemble

body:
[Corollary 7 (\textsf{Law of small chaotic blocks}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Fix an order $r\geq1$.  For each $n$, let
$F_{n,1}$, $\ldots$, $F_{n,K_n}$ be independent centered variables in
order-$r$ chaoses
over mutually independent component spaces, 
and
suppose that

\noi
\begin{align}
 X_{n,k}:=F_{n,k}+\theta_{n,k}\in\N_0.
\notag
\end{align}
Put
$F_n:=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n} F_{n,k}$,
$\theta_n:=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n}\theta_{n,k}$, and
$X_n:=F_n+\theta_n$.
In the Poisson setting, assume

\noi
\begin{align}
 \theta_n\to\lambda,
 \quad
 \sum_km_2(F_{n,k})\to\lambda,
 \AND
 \sum_k\cP(F_{n,k})\to0.
\notag
\end{align}
Then $X_n$ converges to $\Pois(\lambda)$ in total variation.  In the
Rademacher setting, the same conclusion holds with $\cP$ replaced by
$\cR$, provided that the maximal coordinate influence $\cM(F_n)$ of $F_n$ tends
to zero. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsf{Law of small chaotic blocks}

body: [Theorem 1.2 (Colorful Tverberg theorem) of arXiv:2607.29403, 'Strong invariants and Tverberg numbers in convexity spaces'] Let $d,t\geq 1$, let $(X,\mathcal{C})$ satisfy $\textup{VC}(\mathcal{C})\leq d$, and let $S_{1},\ldots,S_{d+1}\subseteq X$ be pairwise disjoint finite sets. If $|S_{i}|\geq d(t-1)+1$ for every $i\in[d+1]$, then there exist pairwise disjoint transversals $T_{1},\ldots,T_{t}$ of the color classes whose convex hulls have a common point; that is, $\bigcap_{j=1}^{t}\operatorname{conv}(T_{j})\neq\varnothing.$

body:
[Prop basechange-surj of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let 
    \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            A\arrow[r,"g"]\arrow[d,"q"']\arrow[dr,pullback] & B\arrow[d,"p"]\\
            C\arrow[r,"f"'] & D
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    be a pullback in the 1-category of compact Lie groups\footnote{Note that the full subcategory of the category of topological groups spanned by the compact Lie groups is closed under finite limits because it is closed under finite products as well as passage to closed subgroups.} such that $p$ is \emph{surjective}. Then the Beck--Chevalley map $\textbf{\textup{L}}q_!g^*\to f^*\textbf{\textup{L}}p_!$ of functors ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{$B$-gl}\to{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{$C$-gl}$ is an equivalence.
    \begin{proof}
        If $X\in\cat{$\bm B$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ is cofibrant, then it is Hausdorff and $B$-free the above; thus, the $A$-orthogonal space $g^*X$ is Hausdorff, and it is $\ker(q)$-free as $g$ is injective when restricted to $\ker(q)$. It thus follows from Proposition~(prop:quotient-we-global of the paper) that the (derived) Beck--Chevalley map $\textbf{\textup{L}}q_!g^*X\to f^*\textbf{\textup{L}}p_!X$ is already modelled by the \emph{underived} Beck--Chevalley map $q_!g^*X\to f^*p_!X$ on the pointset level. To complete the proof, we will show that this map is even an isomorphism (without any assumptions on $X$).

        For this note that since $p$ is surjective, $p_!(-)=(-)/\ker(p)$ with unit $\textup{id}\to p^*p_!$ given by the quotient map, and similarly for $q$. For this choice of adjunction data, one then directly computes that the Beck--Chevalley map is in fact the identity map of $(g^*X)/\ker(q)=X/g(\ker(q))=X/\ker(p)$. 
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop basechange-surj of arXiv:2608.28504

[Definition 2 (Cauchy hypersurfaces and Globally hyperbolic regions) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\mathcal{M} \subset \R^{1+3}$ be an open subset of spacetime on which the fluid variables
	$\vec{\Psi} := \{s,\uprho,v^1,v^2,v^3\}$ are defined and $C^1$,
	and let $\gfour(\vec{\Psi})$ be the acoustical metric defined in \eqref{E:ACOUSTICALMETRICANDMATERIALDER}.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item  We say that a surface $\Sigma \subset \mathcal{M}$ is a \emph{Cauchy hypersurface} for $\mathcal{M}$ (with respect to $\gfour$) if every $\gfour$-timelike inextendible curve in $\mathcal{M}$ intersects $\Sigma$ exactly once.
		\item We say that $(\mathcal{M},\gfour(\vec{\Psi}))$ is \emph{globally hyperbolic} whenever $\mathcal{M}$ contains a Cauchy hypersurface.
	\end{itemize}
title: Cauchy hypersurfaces and Globally hyperbolic regions

body:
[Lemma lem:parameter-family of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] There is $s_0>0$ such that, for every $|s|<s_0$, the zeros of
$F_{z,s}$ admit an indexing
\[
    L_{z,s}
    =
    \{p_{\lambda,s}(z):\lambda\in\Lambda\}
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
the sets $L_{z,s}$ are real and uniformly Delone, with constants
independent of $z$ and $s$;

\item for all $z \in Z$, 
\[
    L_{Tz,s}=L_{z,s}-1;
\]

\item for all $z \in Z$,
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{L_{z,s}}
    =
    4\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }(-1,1);
\]

\item
if $s\neq0$ and
\[
    L_{w,s}=L_{z,s}-u,
\]
then
\[
    u\in\mathbb Z
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    w=T^uz;
\]

\item
for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $z\in Z$, the map
$s\mapsto p_{\lambda,s}(z)$ is real analytic and satisfies
\[
    p_{\lambda,0}(z)=\lambda,
    \qquad
    \left.
    \frac{d}{ds}p_{\lambda,s}(z)
    \right|_{s=0}
    =
    -\frac{H_z(\lambda)}{S'(\lambda)}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

Their separate Question 15 asks for chi>0 in suitable dimensions; the canonical P0104 card combines them. A power saving in rotationally invariant Riemannian FPP and finite-size straight-path identities for lattice FPP do not establish a fixed-law lattice chi=1/3 result. [Theorem 10 (Oracle bound over the three fixed statistical comparators) of arXiv:2609.00402, '2609.00402'] Let \(T\geq5\) and let \(\mathcal D_N=\{(\bm X^{(i)},Y^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^N\) consist of independent copies of \((\bm X,Y)\). Before observing \(\mathcal D_N\), fix fully specified deterministic comparators \(\overline h_S,\overline h_V,\overline h_{AR}\) of the forms introduced above. Their specifications include every threshold and calibration constant, the clipping radius, and the selected approximation networks. There exists a fixed CNN classifier class with parallel branches \(\mathcal H\), with the head specification fixed as in Definition~\ref{def:cnn}, such that \(\overline h_S,\overline h_V,\overline h_{AR}\in\mathcal H\). Let \(d_{\mathcal H}=\operatorname{VCdim}(\mathcal H)\), where \(1\leq d_{\mathcal H}\leq N\), and let \(\widehat h_{\mathrm{ERM}}\in\arg\min_{h\in\mathcal H}N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbb I\{h(\bm X^{(i)})\neq Y^{(i)}\}\). Then, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[
\operatorname{err}(\widehat h_{\mathrm{ERM}})
\leq\inf_{h\in\mathcal H}\operatorname{err}(h)+2r_N(d_{\mathcal H},\delta)
\leq\min_{G\in\{S,V,AR\}}\operatorname{err}(\overline h_G)+2r_N(d_{\mathcal H},\delta).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

for all $t\in(0,t_0(x))$.

Status: proof (unaudited). Claim w730-T355-C005 v1. Novelty unestablished.

Let d,q be positive finite integers. Let H be a constant symmetric positive
definite q by q matrix with extreme eigenvalues 0<m<=M. Let
A:R^d -> R^{q x q} be C^1, A(u)^T A(u)=H, and

    sup_u sum_i ||partial_i A(u)||_op^2 <= D^2 < infinity.

Let z_k be iid R^q-valued labels, independent of the past, with
E z_k=0 and E z_k z_k^T=I_q. No symmetry or higher moment is assumed.
Fix sigma>=0, 0<rho<2, 0<eta<=rho/M, deterministic u_0 and v_0=0.
Consider label-noise SGD

    h_{k,i}:=u_{k+1,i}-u_{k,i}=-eta sigma z_k^T partial_i A(u_k)v_k,
    v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta sigma A(u_k)^T z_k, B=I-eta H.       (1)

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}) define f(u)=F(u,0), a(u)=D_v F(u,0), and

    F_2=sup_u ||D^2 f(u)||_op,
    F_vv=sup_{u,v} ||D_v^2 F(u,v)||_op,
    F_uv=sup_u ||D_u a(u)||_op,
    c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho),
    gamma=min{m, M(2-rho)/rho} > 0.

For every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=k<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_k,v_k)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),               (2)

    C(T)=c [F_vv/2 + T sigma^2 D^2 F_2/2
                       + F_uv sigma D/gamma].         (3)

Thus the slow-clock weak rate is a=1 with an explicit constant linear
in T, with only centered second-moment labels. Covariance proportionality
to the loss Hessian is asserted ON the minimizing manifold v=0, where
the noise covariance is sigma^2 diag(0,H). No off-manifold covariance
proportionality is asserted. The ambient loss is L=v^T H v/2.

The limiting constant tangential process is the known trace-Hessian

not a verified priority claim. General T355 remains open.

Claim w730-T355-C005, version 1. Kind: narrowed. Target: 1.
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unestablished; independent review required.

## Statement

Let d,q be positive finite integers. Let H be a constant symmetric positive
definite q by q matrix with extreme eigenvalues 0<m<=M. Let
A:R^d -> R^{q x q} be C^1, A(u)^T A(u)=H, and

    sup_u sum_i ||partial_i A(u)||_op^2 <= D^2 < infinity.

Let z_k be iid R^q-valued labels, independent of the past, with
E z_k=0 and E z_k z_k^T=I_q. No symmetry or higher moment is assumed.
Fix sigma>=0, 0<rho<2, 0<eta<=rho/M, deterministic u_0 and v_0=0.
Consider label-noise SGD

    h_{k,i}:=u_{k+1,i}-u_{k,i}=-eta sigma z_k^T partial_i A(u_k)v_k,
    v_{k+1}=B v_k-eta sigma A(u_k)^T z_k, B=I-eta H.       (1)

For F in C_b^2(R^{d+q}) define f(u)=F(u,0), a(u)=D_v F(u,0), and

    F_2=sup_u ||D^2 f(u)||_op,
    F_vv=sup_{u,v} ||D_v^2 F(u,v)||_op,
    F_uv=sup_u ||D_u a(u)||_op,
    c=sigma^2 q/(2-rho),
    gamma=min{m, M(2-rho)/rho} > 0.

For every T>=0,

    sup_{integer 0<=k<=T/eta^2}
      |E F(u_k,v_k)-F(u_0,0)| <= eta C(T),               (2)

    C(T)=c [F_vv/2 + T sigma^2 D^2 F_2/2
                       + F_uv sigma D/gamma].         (3)

Thus the slow-clock weak rate is a=1 with an explicit constant linear
in T, with only centered second-moment labels. Covariance proportionality
to the loss Hessian is asserted ON the minimizing manifold v=0, where
the noise covariance is sigma^2 diag(0,H). No off-manifold covariance
proportionality is asserted. The ambient loss is L=v^T H v/2.

The limiting constant tangential process is the known trace-Hessian
flow: Li-Wang-Arora, arXiv:2110.06914v4, Corollary 5.2, pp.8-9 and 33.
The quantitative estimate and removal of symmetry are candidate results,
not a verified priority claim. General T355 remains open.

## Proof

### Normal second moments and tangential martingale increments

These calculations are the same as C004 v2, equations (2)-(5); they use
centering and unit covariance, not central symmetry. They are included
to make this version independently readable. Conditional expectation
in (1), with the fresh label independent of (u_k,v_k), gives

    Q_{k+1}=B Q_k B+eta^2 sigma^2 H, Q_0=0,
    Q_k=eta sigma^2 (I-B^{2k})(2I-eta H)^{-1},
    E|v_k|^2=tr Q_k<=eta c.                             (4)

The middle formula follows by diagonalizing H and summing a finite
geometric series. For each eigenvalue lambda, its contribution is
eta sigma^2[1-(1-eta lambda)^{2k}]/(2-eta lambda), whose bracket is
in [0,1] and denominator at least 2-rho. Finite second moments follow
inductively from the first equality; no fourth moments enter.

Similarly conditional mean zero and unit covariance give

    E[h_k|past]=0,
    E[|h_k|^2|past]
      =eta^2 sigma^2 sum_i |partial_i A(u_k)v_k|^2,
    E|h_k|^2<=eta^3 sigma^2 D^2 c.                     (5)

All states are finite almost surely at finite k. These bounds also give
the integrability needed below. Taylor expansion of f and conditional
centering imply, for K eta^2<=T,

    |E f(u_K)-f(u_0)|<=T eta sigma^2 D^2 c F_2/2.       (6)

Here the first-order term has zero expectation since grad f is bounded
and adapted, and the second-order remainder is bounded by F_2|h_k|^2/2.

### Mixed normal-linear observable: the new step

Set r=||B||_op=max_lambda |1-eta lambda|<1. For lambda in [m,M],

    1-|1-eta lambda|=min{eta lambda, 2-eta lambda}
       >=min{eta m, 2-rho}>=eta gamma.

The last inequality uses eta<=rho/M. Thus 1-r>=eta gamma.

Let a:R^d->R^q be any bounded globally Lipschitz function with Lipschitz
constant L_a. Define the q by q matrix N_k=E[v_k a(u_k)^T]. Since v_0=0,
N_0=0. Add and subtract a(u_k) in N_{k+1}. Conditional centering of z_k
then gives the exact recurrence

    N_{k+1}=B N_k+R_k,
    R_k=E[v_{k+1}(a(u_{k+1})-a(u_k))^T].               (7)

Every matrix entry is integrable by boundedness of a and (4). For the
remainder, Lipschitz continuity and Cauchy-Schwarz give

    E[|v_{k+1}| |a(u_{k+1})-a(u_k)|]
      <=L_a sqrt(E|v_{k+1}|^2 E|h_k|^2)
      <=L_a sigma D c eta^2.                          (8)

No factorization of these correlated factors is used. Iterate (7) as
a finite matrix identity and take its trace. For any j>=0,

    |tr(B^j R_k)|
      =|E[(a(u_{k+1})-a(u_k))^T B^j v_{k+1}]|
      <=r^j L_a sigma D c eta^2.

Consequently, for every integer K>=0,

    |E[a(u_K)^T v_K]|=|tr N_K|
      <=L_a sigma D c eta^2 sum_{j=0}^{K-1} r^j
      <=L_a sigma D c eta/gamma.                      (9)

The empty sum handles K=0. This reusable bound replaces the exact
cancellation by central symmetry used in C004. It is uniform in K.

### Finish the ambient observable estimate

For the particular a(u)=D_v F(u,0), boundedness and the mixed derivative
bound imply L_a<=F_uv. Taylor's theorem in v yields

    |F(u,v)-f(u)-a(u)^T v|<=F_vv |v|^2/2.

Take expectations and use (4), (9), and (6). The resulting sum is
exactly eta times (3). This proves (2). Sigma=0, D=0 and T=0 require
no division by these quantities; gamma is strictly positive regardless.
Only finite second moments and fresh-label independence were used.

## Scope and hardest step for review

The hardest new step is the matrix recurrence (7), followed by taking
the trace AFTER its finite iteration. Replacing N_k by the scalar
E[a(u_k)^T v_k] before iterating would be unjustified for general H.
The proof keeps the matrix until the final trace.

The constant-Hessian target is addressed in its dossier's on-manifold
covariance interpretation, including rotating output frames. Fixed
off-manifold initial conditions, general curved manifolds and a

[Theorem 1 (Representative lifts and quotient geodesics) of arXiv:2608.26961, 'Gromov--Monge Flow Matching for Equivariant Graph Generation'] Let \(\bmu,\bnu\in\mP_2(Q)\), fix \(\mu\in[\bmu]\), and let
\(\Gamma\in\mathrm{c}_Q(\bmu,\bnu)\). There exist
\(\nu_\Gamma\in[\bnu]\) and
\(\gamma_\Gamma\in\mathrm{c}_{\R^D}(\mu,\nu_\Gamma)\) such that
\((\mathfrak q,\mathfrak q)_\sharp\gamma_\Gamma=\Gamma\) and
\[
\int_{\R^D\times\R^D}\|x-y\|^2\,\d\gamma_\Gamma(x,y)
=
\int_{Q\times Q}d_Q(\bx,\by)^2\,\d\Gamma(\bx,\by).
\]
If \(\Gamma\) is optimal, then \(\gamma_\Gamma\) is optimal between its
representative marginals. Moreover, in this case, with
\(\pr^t(x,y)=(1-t)x+ty\) and
\(\mu_t\coloneqq\pr^t_\sharp\gamma_\Gamma\), the projected curve
\(\bmu_t\coloneqq\mathfrak q_\sharp\mu_t\) is a constant-speed
\(\W_{2,Q}\)-geodesic, and the flow-matching field associated with the lifted
coupling \(\gamma_\Gamma\) satisfies
\[
\int_I\int_{\R^D}\|v_t^{\gamma_\Gamma}(z)\|^2
\,\d\mu_t(z)\,\d t
=\W_{2,Q}^2(\bmu,\bnu).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem workload-difference of arXiv:2505.04942, '\textbf{Randomized Routing to Remote Queues}'] Assume the conditions of Theorem~(theorem:load-balancing of the paper) hold. Then for $T > 0$, $ \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \tilde{\Gamma}^{\star}_{n}(t) \Rightarrow 0 $ as $ n \to \infty $. If conditions~(equation eq:fourth-moments of the paper) and (equation eq:log-log-n-bound of the paper) also hold, then with probability 1, 
	\[
	\sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \tilde{\Gamma}^{\star}_{n}(t)< \max \Big\{ 2C \mu \chi_{n}, 2C' \mu \frac{\log \log n + \log (n \chi_{n}^{2})}{\sqrt{n} \chi_{n}} \Big\} \quad \mbox{for $n$ sufficiently large,}
	\]
	where $C$ and $C'$ are specified in Theorem~(theorem:load-balancing-gap of the paper). The order of this upper bound is minimized with $ \chi_{n} = C'' n^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log n} $ for $ C'' > 0 $, in which case $ \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \tilde{\Gamma}^{\star}_{n}(t) = O(n^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log n}) $ with probability~1. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2608.10183, '2608.10183'] Assume the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:elephant-nonexplosion}. Fix $j\in\mathbb N$ and suppose that
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb E\left(
N_0^j+|S_0^j|
\right)
<\infty.
\end{equation*}
Then the functions
\begin{equation*}
t\longmapsto\mathbb E\left(N_t^j\right)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
t\longmapsto\mathbb E\left(S_t^j\right)
\end{equation*}
are absolutely continuous on every bounded time interval.

For almost every $t\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
\frac{d}{dt}
\mathbb E\left(N_t^j\right)
=\mathbb E\left(
\Lambda_j(X_t)
\right),

\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\frac{d}{dt}
\mathbb E\left(S_t^j\right)
=
(2p-1)
\mathbb E\left(
r_j(N_t,S_t)\Lambda_j(X_t)
\right).

\end{equation}
where \begin{equation*}
\Lambda_j(x)
:=
\sum_{k\in\mathcal P_j}\phi_k(x^k).
\end{equation*}
Equivalently, for every $t\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\left(N_t^j\right)
=
\mathbb E\left(N_0^j\right)
+
\int_0^t
\mathbb E\left(
\Lambda_j(X_u)
\right)du,

\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
\mathbb E\left(S_t^j\right)
=
\mathbb E\left(S_0^j\right)
+
(2p-1)
\int_0^t
\mathbb E\left(
r_j(N_u,S_u)\Lambda_j(X_u)
\right)du.

\end{align}

[Theorem 31 (Kernel-uniform quantitative weak CLT) of arXiv:2604.20634, 'Distributional Statistical Models:\\ \large Weak Moments, Cumulants, and a Central Limit T'] Fix $T\in\mathcal{S}'(\R)$ and a family of kernels
$\mathcal{K}\subset\mathcal{S}(\R)$ such that, for every
$\varphi\in\mathcal{K}$, the pair $(T,\varphi)$ has
${}^{(\varphi)}\phi(0)\ne0$, ${}^{(\varphi)}\kappa_2>0$, and
${}^{(\varphi)}K$ is $C^3$ in a neighbourhood of the origin.  Suppose that for
some $T_0>0$,
\[
   c_0:=\inf_{\varphi\in\mathcal{K}}{}^{(\varphi)}\kappa_2>0,
   \qquad
   \overline{M}:=\sup_{\varphi\in\mathcal{K}}\;
   \sup_{|u|\le T_0/\sqrt{c_0}}
   \bigl|{}^{(\varphi)}K^{(3)}(u)\bigr|<\infty .
\]
Let $Z_n^{(\varphi)}=\bigl(S_n-n\,{}^{(\varphi)}\kappa_1\bigr)/
\sqrt{n\,{}^{(\varphi)}\kappa_2}$ denote the sum normalised by the
instrument's own first two weak cumulants.  Then
\[
   \sup_{\varphi\in\mathcal{K}}\;\sup_{|t|\le T_0}
   \Bigl|\,{}^{(\varphi)}\phi_{Z_n^{(\varphi)}}(t)-e^{-t^2/2}\,\Bigr|
   \;=\;O\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\right),
\]
with the implied constant depending only on $T_0$, $c_0$ and $\overline{M}$.

[Lem 13 (Endpoint residual estimates) of arXiv:2607.28865, 'First-Passage Percolation on Spread-out line graphs: Microscopic Regime'] Assume $\ell\ge2$. Recall the residual terms $\sfRT_n$ and $\sfRH_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:residual-def}.
\begin{enumeratei}
    \item Under Condition~\textup{B.\ref{ass:B1}}, the sequence $\{\sfRT_n\}_{n\ge1}$ is tight, and the sequence $\{\sfRH_n\}_{n\ge1}$ is uniformly bounded in $L^q$ for every $q\ge1$.
    \item Under Condition~\textup{B.\ref{ass:B2}}, both residual sequences have uniformly bounded moments of all orders. That is, for every $q\ge1$,
    \[
        \sup_{n\ge1}\E\left[\big(\sfRT_n\big)^q+\big(\sfRH_n\big)^q\right] < \infty.
    \]
\end{enumeratei}

[Lemma lem:zmoncp of arXiv:2608.11198, '(Non-)coincidence of critical parameters for Poisson Zoos and Loop Soup Percolation\\ on \'] There is a coupling of the Poisson zoos
\((\mathcal O^\mu_\alpha)_{\alpha\ge0}\) such that
\[
\mathcal O^\mu_{\alpha_1}\subseteq \mathcal O^\mu_{\alpha_2}
\qquad\mathbb{P}\text{-a.s. whenever }\alpha_1\le \alpha_2.
\]
Moreover, if \(\alpha \in (0,\infty)\) and \(\alpha_n\uparrow \alpha\), then
\begin{equation} 
C^\mu_\alpha(\0)
=
\bigcup_{n\ge1} C^\mu_{\alpha_n}(\0)
\qquad\mathbb{P}\text{-a.s.}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
\chi_\mu(\alpha)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\chi_\mu(\alpha_n).
\]

body:
Let f_n : [a,b] -> R be Riemann integrable, uniformly bounded (|f_n| <= M for all n), and suppose f_n -> f pointwise on [a,b] where f is ALSO Riemann integrable. Then integral_a^b f_n -> integral_a^b f. The Riemann integrability of the limit must be ASSUMED and does not follow: enumerate the rationals of [0,1] as q_1, q_2, ... and let f_n be the indicator of {q_1, ..., q_n}. Each f_n is Riemann integrable with integral 0, the family is bounded by 1, and f_n increases pointwise to the indicator of the rationals, which is not Riemann integrable. This is the essential defect that the Lebesgue integral repairs: the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem needs only measurability of the limit, which is automatic for a pointwise limit of measurable functions. Historically Arzela proved this in 1885 by a direct and rather delicate covering argument, before the Lebesgue theory existed. [Arzela (1885); see e.g. Luxemburg, 'Arzela's dominated convergence theorem for the Riemann integral', Amer. Math. Monthly 78 (1971)]
each f_n Riemann integrable on the compact interval [a,b]
uniform bound |f_n| <= M
pointwise convergence to f, AND f Riemann integrable - an independent hypothesis

Therefore f_n and f are Lebesgue integrable with Lebesgue integrals equal to their Riemann integrals. The constant function M is Lebesgue integrable on the bounded interval [a,b] and dominates every |f_n|, and f_n -> f pointwise, so the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem gives integral f_n -> integral f in the Lebesgue sense, hence in the Riemann sense. [Lem 17 of arXiv:2609.02173, 'Bounding Selmer Groups of Superelliptic Jacobians via Class Groups'] For \(1\leq i\leq r_v\), let
	\(L_{v,i}\) be a factor of \(L_v\), and let
	\(e_{v,i}=e(L_{v,i}/K_v)\) denote the ramification index of
	\(L_{v,i}/K_v\). Let \(k_{v,i}\) and \(k_v\) denote the residue
	fields of \(L_{v,i}\) and \(K_v\), respectively. Write
	\(\overline{T}_{v,i}\) for the reduction of \(T_{v,i}\).
	One has
	\[
	\sum_{i=1}^{r_v}
	e_{v,i}
	\operatorname{Tr}_{k_{v,i}/k_v}(\overline {T_{v,i}})
	=
	0
	\quad
	\text{in } k_v.
	\]

[Theorem th:main of arXiv:2504.11107, 'An Invariance Principle for some\\% Reaction-Diffusion Equations with a Multiplicative Ran'] Suppose that Assumption (ass:par of the paper) holds, and
	recall the definition of the constant ${\rm L}_g$ from part (2) of 
        that assumption. Suppose that
	\begin{equation}
		\sup_{z>0} |f(z)/z|<  {\rm L}_g^2/64.
	\end{equation}
	Then, for every $\varepsilon\in(0\,,1)$
	there exist nonrandom numbers $S=S(\varepsilon)>0$ and $\beta
	=\beta(\varepsilon) \in (0\,, 1)$, 
	and a coupling $(u\,,w)$ -- that depends on the choice of $\varepsilon$ --
	where the space-time random field $w = \{w(t\,,x)\}_{t\geqslant0,x\in\mathbb{T}}$ solves (equation SHE of the paper) and 
	the space-time random field $u=\{u(t\,,x)\}_{t\geqslant S,x\in\mathbb{T}}$ is a solution to (equation PAM of the paper)
	shifted by $S$ time units and started at $w(S)$; that is,
	\begin{equation}\left[\begin{split}
		&\partial_t u = \partial^2_x u + \mu u  + \sigma u\dot{W}_0
			\hskip.45in\text{on $(S\,,\infty)\times\mathbb{T}$},\\
		&\text{subject to }u(0)=w(S)\hskip.9in\text{on $\mathbb{T}$},
	\end{split}\right.\end{equation}
	for a suitably constructed
	space-time white noise $\dot{W}_0$, such that
	\[\textstyle
		\mathrm{P}\left\{ \| \log w(t) - \log u(t) \|_{C(\mathbb{T})} 
		=O( t^{-\beta})\text{\ as $t\to\infty$} \right\} \geqslant 
		1 - \varepsilon. 
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:main of arXiv:2504.11107

[Theorema 4 (\Cref{GPS-to-ANV}) of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(k\) be a perfect field of characteristic \(p > 0\) and let \(X\) be a smooth projective
scheme over \(W(k)\).
If \(X\) is globally \(+\)-regular, then its closed fiber $X_k \defeq X\times_{W(k)}k$ is HT-split.
Furthermore, we obtain the following Akizuki--Nakano-type vanishing in mixed characteristic: for every ample line bundle \(L\) on \(X\),
\[
R^i\Gamma_{(p)}R\Gamma\left(
X,
\Omega^j_{X/W(k)}\otimes L^{-1}
\right)
=0
\qquad
\text{whenever }i+j<\dim X.
\]
In particular, this vanishing implies \(H^i(X, \Omega^j_{X/W(k)} \otimes L^{-1}) = 0\) for \(i + j < \dim X - 1\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \Cref{GPS-to-ANV}

[Definition 14 (Generated tree with a spine) of arXiv:2605.09459, 'Multipoint connectivity in the branching interlacement process'] Let $1 \leq k,m \leq n$. Let $T \in \mathbb{T}_{m,n}$ and $v_1,\dots,v_k$ distinct vertices of $T$. The \textbf{tree generated by $v_1,\dots,v_k$ in $T$} is the tree $T\langle v_1,\dots,v_k\rangle$ with vertex set
  \[
    \{v_1,\dots,v_k\} \cup \{v_i \wedge v_j, i \neq j\} \cup \{s_{v_i}, i \leq k\},
  \]
  and where two vertices are connected if the geodesic between the two in $T$ does not contain any other vertex of $T\langle v_1,\dots,v_k\rangle$.
title: Generated tree with a spine

For n>=2, let J_n be the nilpotent matrix with ones on the superdiagonal, and C_n=J_n+e_n e_1^T. Their difference has rank one, but the empirical eigenvalue laws differ by one on the bounded 1-Lipschitz test f(z)=min(|z|,1): J_n has only zero eigenvalues and C_n has all nth roots of unity. Thus a Hermitian-style rank/n bound cannot control nonnormal empirical eigenvalue laws in general. This deterministic example is not an iid circular-law lower bound.

[Definition 49 (Trunk paths and vertices) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] Under $\q^m_n$, we have 
\[
X_j = m, \quad \text{for all } \bar{h} \le j \le \bar{h} + \lfloor c_0 n \rfloor.
\]
In other words, for each $j$ between $\bar{h}$ and $\bar{h}+\lfloor c_0 n\rfloor$, there are exactly $m$ vertices in $\cX_j$. These vertices belong to $m$ distinct ancestral lineages that remain separate at height $\bar{h}$. 
Let $\mathsf{T}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{T}_m$ be the $m$ coalescent subtrees at height $\bar{h}$.  
For $\bar{h}\le j \le \bar{h}+\lfloor c_0 n \rfloor$ and $1\le i\le m$, denote by 
\(z^j_i \in V(\mathsf{T}_i)\)
the unique vertex of $\mathsf{T}_i$ at height $j$. 
The sequence
\[
Z_i := \big(z^{\bar{h}+\lfloor c_0 n \rfloor}_i, z^{\bar{h}+\lfloor c_0 n \rfloor-1}_i, \ldots, z^{\bar{h}}_i\big)
\]
is called the trunk path of $\mathsf{T}_i$, and its elements are referred to as the trunk vertices of $\mathsf{T}_i$.  
The remaining $q_n(j)-m$ non-trunk vertices at height $j$ are denoted by $y^j_1, \ldots, y^j_{q_n(j)-m}$, where the subscripts are assigned arbitrary.
title: Trunk paths and vertices

[Proposition 75 (Exact restart law with memory) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $u,v\ge0$ with $u+v\le T$.  Then
\begin{align}
 \mathscr D_{u+v}^\eps(d,\eta)
 &=\mathscr D_v^\eps\bigl(
     \mathscr D_u^\eps(d,\eta),\theta_u\eta
   \bigr),
 \\
 \mathscr Y_{u+v}^\eps(d,\eta)-\eta_u
 &=\mathscr Y_v^\eps\bigl(
     \mathscr D_u^\eps(d,\eta),\theta_u\eta
   \bigr).
 
\end{align}
In particular, for every raw path $x$, seam $s$, and
$0\le v\le T-s$,
\begin{align}
 D_{s+v}^\eps(x)
 &=\mathscr D_v^\eps\bigl(D_s^\eps(x),\theta_sx\bigr),
 \\
 Y_{s+v}^\eps(x)-x_s
 &=\mathscr Y_v^\eps\bigl(D_s^\eps(x),\theta_sx\bigr).
 
\end{align}
Thus the boundary layer obtained by restarting with zero memory is exactly
the discarded term $e^{-v/\eps}D_s^\eps(x)$.

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] For $\bs{q}\in\Delta_d$, $\pi\in\on{Sym}(d)$, and $t\in[d]$, define
the {suffix mass}
\[
  s_t^\pi(\bs{q})
  :=\sum_{r=t}^d q_{\pi(r)}.
\]
Thus, $s_t^\pi(\bs{q})$ is the total $\bs{q}$-mass of the elements in
position $t$ or later in the ordering $\pi$. Define
\begin{align*}
  F(\bs{q})
  &:=\E_\pi\left[
       \sum_{t=1}^d q_{\pi(t)}
       \log\frac{s_t^\pi(\bs{q})}{q_{\pi(t)}}
     \right]
     -S(\bs{q})
  =\E_\pi\left[
       \sum_{t=1}^d q_{\pi(t)}
       \log s_t^\pi(\bs{q})
     \right]
     +H_{\mr c}(\bs{q}),
\end{align*}
where $\pi$ is uniformly distributed on $\on{Sym}(d)$.
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2609.02017

[Proposition propF1 of arXiv:2412.06701, 'Matsumoto-Yor processes on Jordan algebras'] $ $
\begin{enumerate}
\item An element $x$ in $E$ is invertible if and only if the quadratic representation $\mathrm P(x)$ is invertible. If $x$ in $E$ is invertible then $\mathrm P(x)^{-1}=\mathrm P(x^{-1})$.
\item If $x$ is invertible then $\mathrm P(x)(x^{-1})=x$.
\item If $x,y\in E$ then $\mathrm P(\mathrm P(y)(x))=\mathrm P(y)\mathrm P(x)\mathrm P(y)$.
\item If $x,y\in E$ are invertible then $(\mathrm P(x)(y))^{-1}=\mathrm P(x^{-1})(y^{-1})$.
\item The differential of $x\in E^{\times} \mapsto x^{-1}$ at $x$ is $-\mathrm P(x^{-1})$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.28245, 'I-FLOP: Fast Learning of Order and Parents from Interventional Data'] Fix $v\in V$ and $Z\subseteq V\setminus\{v\}$.
	Let $\widehat{P}_{v,N}(Z)$ be the parent set returned by target-filtered grow--shrink using $s_v^{\mathrm{tf\text{-}pool}}$.
	Under Assumptions~\ref{assump:data-generating process}--\ref{assump:env-proportions}, starting from any initial parent set $P_0\subseteq Z$,

\[
    \max_{\substack{n,m\in[N,2N]\\ |n-m|\leqslant\Delta_N N}}\max_{x\in[-1,1]} |f_n(x)-f_m(x)|
    < C\sqrt{\Delta_N N}\sqrt{\log(1/\Delta_N)+\log\log N}.
\]

body:
[Thm 5 of arXiv:2608.26723, 'Extrinsic upper bounds for the harmonic mean of eigenvalues in curved manifolds'] Let $M$ be an $m(\ge 2)$-dimensional closed orientable submanifold in an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $N$ of the sectional curvature $K_N \le \delta$, where $\delta > 0$.
	We assume that $M$ is contained in a convex ball of radius $\le \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\delta}}\arctan \frac{m}{\sqrt{2m+1}}$.
	Then we have
	\begin{equation*}
		\mathfrak{H}(\lambda_1,\cdots,\lambda_m)\le \frac{m}{\vol(M)}\int_M\big(\delta+|\mathbf{H}|^2\big).
	\end{equation*}
	Equality holds implies that $\lambda_1=\cdots=\lambda_m$ and $M$ is minimally immersed in a geodesic sphere of $N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2608.03922, 'Absolute continuity of two-dimensional polynomial random vectors'] Let $M>0$ and let $d,n\in\mathbb N$. Let
$\mu=\mu_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\mu_n$,
where each $\mu_j$ is a probability measure with density $\varrho_j$ satisfying
\[
0\le \varrho_j(x_j)\le M
\quad \forall x_j\in\mathbb R,
\quad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
\]
Then, for every $f\in \mathcal{P}_d(\mathbb{R}^n)$
and every $\varepsilon>0$, one has
\[
[f]_\infty^{1/d}\mu(|f|\le \varepsilon)
\le
4d^2(1+M)\varepsilon^{1/d}.
\]

Let d>=2, N>=2, and let C be a set of N distinct points on the unit sphere S^(d-1). Let t_1<...<t_m<1 be exactly the distinct inner products between distinct points of C, m>=1, and assume C is a spherical (2m-1)-design: every polynomial on R^d of degree<=2m-1 has the same average over C as under normalized uniform surface measure. Put F(t)=product_(i=1)^m(t-t_i). Let p_j be the monic orthogonal polynomials for the nonnegative measure (1-t)(1-t^2)^((d-3)/2)dt on [-1,1]. There is a real alpha such that F=p_m+alpha p_(m-1). Equivalently F is orthogonal to every polynomial of degree<=m-2 for this modified measure. For m=1 this orthogonality condition is empty and the displayed representation still holds. No sign condition on alpha is asserted. This is Lemma6.3 of Cohn-Kumar.
d,N>=2; C distinct equally weighted unit vectors, spherical (2m-1)-design
t_i list all off-diagonal inner products; m>=1
p_j monic for the modified measure with factor (1-t)

[Definition d:chart of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] A \emph{chart of dimension $n$} on a metric measure space $(X,d,\mu)$ is a pair $(U,\phi)$ where:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item $U \subset X$ is measurable, $m(U) >0$, and $\phi:X \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is Lipschitz.
			\item For every Lipschitz function $f: X \to \mathbb{R}$, there exists a measurable function $\partial_\phi f: U \to \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $f$ is differentiable with respect to $\phi$ at $m$-almost every $x_0 \in U$ and with derivative $\partial_\phi f(x_0)$.
		\end{enumerate}
		A \textbf{measurable differentiable structure}	on $(X,d,\mu)$ is a  countable collection $\{(U_\alpha,\phi_\alpha)\}$ of charts with uniformly bounded dimension such that $$\mu \left( X \setminus \bigcup_{\alpha} U_\alpha\right)=0.$$
title: Definition d:chart of arXiv:2510.13659

body:
[Conjecture 1 (Gaussian ellipsoid fitting conjecture) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d}}{\sim}N(0,I_d)$, where
	$n=n(d)$. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, as $d\to\infty$:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
		\item If $n\le(1-\varepsilon)\frac{d^2}{4},$	then an ellipsoid fit exists with probability tending to one.
		
		\item If $n\ge(1+\varepsilon)\frac{d^2}{4}$, then no ellipsoid fit exists with probability tending to one.
	\end{enumerate} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

Then, the operator $A:\mathcal{D}\to C^2_b(\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal{S}^{d,+}_{1})$ defined by
\begin{align*}
&Af(x,\boldsymbol{\theta}) \\
&=c_1\Bigg[ \int_0^\infty \Bigg\{\sum_{j=1}^d f\big(x,\boldsymbol{v}_{j,y}^{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\big)-f(x,\boldsymbol{\theta}) \\
&\qquad\qquad-\Big(\boldsymbol{e}_0+(1-\theta_j)\boldsymbol{e}_j-\sum_{k\neq j} \theta_k \boldsymbol{e}_k\Big)\cdot \grad{f}(x,\boldsymbol{\theta}) \mathbbm{1}_{\big(0,\log(1+e^x)-x\big)}(y)\Bigg\}\frac{e^{y}}{(e^{y}-1)^{\alpha}}dy\Bigg], 
\end{align*}
solves the martingale problem for $(\xi^R,\Xi^R)$, where $c_1=\pi^{-1}\Gamma(1+\alpha)\sin(\pi\alpha)$, and the vector $\boldsymbol{v}_{j,y}^{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$ is from (\ref{frequent_vector}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 2 of arXiv:2605.23659, '2605.23659'] For each \(i\in I\), define the restricted point process
\[
N^{(i)} := N(\cdot\cap ([0,\infty)\times D_{0}^{(i)})),
\]
and let
\[
n^{(i)} := n(\cdot \cap D_{0}^{(i)}).
\]
Then \(\{N^{(i)}\}_{i\in I}\) is a family of independent Poisson point processes with intensity measures \(dt\otimes n^{(i)}\). Moreover,
\[
N=\sum_{i\in I} N^{(i)}
\]
as random measures, almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition M1 of arXiv:2412.04212, 'Rectangular Gilbert Tessellation'] Let 
$\mathcal{V}$ be a locally finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (i.e., within any finite square, there is a finite number of points of $\mathcal{V}$ ), and let a constant $0<p<1$ be fixed arbitrarily. For each $u\in \mathcal{V}$ 
a random vector $$d_u \in \{(0,1), (1,0)\}$$ is assigned independently of the rest with the probability
\begin{equation}\notag
\mathbb{P}\{d_u= (0,1) \}=p=1-\mathbb{P}\{d_u= (1,0) \}.
\end{equation}
Set 
$G(0):=\mathcal{V}.$
At time $t=0$, from every point $u\in \mathcal{V}$ into each side of the assigned direction ($\pm d_u$), a ray $\mathcal{L}^{\pm}_{u,d_u}(t)$
grows
with constant speed $1$ until it reaches another ray;
at this moment, the growth stops, and the ray remains unchanged thereafter. 

For any $t>0$, we define a collection of 
rays
\begin{equation}
G_{\mathcal{V}}(t):=  \left\{ \mathcal{L}^{+}_{u,d_u}(t),
\mathcal{L}^{-}_{u,d_u}(t),
u\in \mathcal{V}
\right\}.
\end{equation}
We call process $\left( G_{\mathcal{V}}(t), \ t\geq 0\right)$ 
the process of planar quadrangulation.

[Lemma lem:hill-paths of arXiv:2608.08375, 'Algebraic formulas for first-passage times of Markov processes in the linear framework: ge'] Under the conditions stated previously, if $k \in \overline{Z}$, then $u \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} k$ if, and only if, $u \leadsto_G k$.

\proof If $u = k$, the conclusion is trivial, so assume that $u \neq k$. If $u \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} k$, then there is a path, $u = j_1 \to \dotsb \to j_n = k$, of edges in $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$. We may assume that this path does not revisit $u$, so that $u \neq j_2, \dotsc, j_{n-1}$, for otherwise we can simply consider the portion of this path starting from the last visit to $u$. Since none of these edges now enter $u$, it follows from Definition~(def:hill of the paper).1 that they must have arisen from edges in $G$, so that $u \leadsto_G k$. Now suppose that $u \leadsto_G k$, so that there exists a directed path, $u = i_1 \to \dotsb \to i_m = k$, of edges in $G$. As before, we may assume that $u \neq i_2, \dotsc, i_m$, so that none of the edges enter $u$. Since $k$ is non-terminal, each vertex along the path must also be non-terminal. It then follows from Definition~(def:hill of the paper).1 that each edge must also exist in $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$, so that $u \leadsto_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} k$.
\hfill \qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: Potts free energy for general configuration-model degrees structural reduction Result: For a finite forest at zero field, Z=q^(number of components)*(exp(beta)+q-1)^(number of edges), by successively summing leaf colors. body:
[Defn eq:Ae-def of arXiv:2609.00110, 'Phase Transition and Fluctuation Results for First-Passage Percolation on Spread-Out Cycle'] Let $e=\{u,v\}$ be a bridge, where $u$ has label $1$ and $v$ has label $2$. 
Its original activation time and the lower bound recorded at activation are
\begin{align*}
 \gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}
 &:=
 \max\{\widehat\mathsf{T}_1(u),\widehat\mathsf{T}_2(v)\},\\
 L_e^{\mathrm{act}}
 &:=
 \big(\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}-\widehat\mathsf{T}_1(u)\big)
 +
 \big(\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}-\widehat\mathsf{T}_2(v)\big).
\end{align*}
The corresponding residual in the cumulative-hazard scale is
\begin{align*}
 R_e
 := H(\go_e)-H(L_e^{\mathrm{act}}) 
 = \go_e^\theta-(L_e^{\mathrm{act}})^\theta.
\end{align*}

For $q\geqslant\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}$, define the collision threshold
\begin{align*}
 L_e(q)
 :=
 \big(q-\widehat\mathsf{T}_1(u)\big)
 +
 \big(q-\widehat\mathsf{T}_2(v)\big).
\end{align*}
In particular, $L_e(\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}})=L_e^{\mathrm{act}}$.

For $s\geqslant\mathfrak{a}_\ell\gt_e^{\mathrm{act}}$, define the rescaled bridge age by
\begin{align}
 A_e(s)
 :=
 \big(s-\mathfrak{a}_\ell\widehat\mathsf{T}_1(u)\big)
 +
 \big(s-\mathfrak{a}_\ell\widehat\mathsf{T}_2(v)\big).
\end{align}
Then $ L_e(s/\mathfrak{a}_\ell)=\frac{A_e(s)}{\mathfrak{a}_\ell}$.

The cumulative bridge hazard at rescaled time $s$ is
\begin{align}
 \gL_s
 &:= \sum_{e\in\mathcal{B}_s}
 \left[ H\left(\frac{A_e(s)}{\mathfrak{a}_\ell}\right) - H(L_e^{\mathrm{act}}) \right]
 =\sum_{e\in\mathcal{B}_s}\left[\left(\frac{A_e(s)}{\mathfrak{a}_\ell }\right)^\theta
 -(L_e^{\mathrm{act}})^\theta\right]
 \notag\\
 &=\int_0^s \frac{2\theta}{\mathfrak{a}_\ell ^\theta}
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal{B}_q} A_e(q)^{\theta-1}\,\mathrm d q.
\end{align}
title: Bridge thresholds, residuals, and cumulative hazard

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.17192, 'Geometric Regime--Switching Diffusions on Stratified Riemannian Spaces with an Application'] Let $I$ be a countable index set and suppose
		\(
		E = \bigsqcup_{\alpha\in I} S_\alpha
		\)
		is a partition into pairwise disjoint subsets such that:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(S\arabic*),ref=S\arabic*]
			\item for every $\alpha\in I$, $S_\alpha$ is a connected, smooth, finite--dimensional
			manifold without boundary, equipped with a Riemannian metric $g_\alpha$;
			\item the inclusion $\iota_\alpha: S_\alpha \hookrightarrow E$ is a homeomorphism onto its image
			and this image is a Borel subset of \(E\).
		\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma equivalentconditionsail1 of arXiv:2608.30491, 'The Daugavet property in symmetric operator spaces'] For  a  Banach space \((X, \left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert)\), the following  are equivalent:	
		\begin{enumerate}[\rm(i)]
			\item There exist a null sequence \(\{ \varepsilon_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) of positive numbers in \((0,1)\)  and a sequence \(\{x_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) in \(X\) such that
			\[
			\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=1}^{m}(1-\varepsilon_n)|a_n|\leq\left\|\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=1}^{m}a_nx_n\right\|\leq\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=1}^{m}|a_n|
			\]
			for all  \(\{a_n\}_{n=1}^{m}\in \ell_1\), where 
			$m\in \mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}$.
			
			\item There exist a null sequence \(\{\varepsilon_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) of positive numbers in \((0,1)\)  and a sequence \(\{x_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) in \(X\) such that
			\[
			\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=1}^{m}|a_n|\leq\left\|\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=1}^{m}a_nx_n\right\|\leq\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=1}^{m}(1+\varepsilon_n)|a_n|
			\]
			for all  \(\{a_n\}_{n=1}^{m}\in \ell_1\), where 
			$m\in \mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}$.
			
			\item There exist a null sequence \(\{\varepsilon_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) of positive numbers in \((0,1)\) and a sequence \(\{x_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}\) in \(X\) such that
			\[
			\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=k}^{m}|a_n|\leq\left\|\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=k}^{m}a_nx_n\right\|\leq(1+\varepsilon_k)\mathop{\sum}\limits_{n=k}^{m}|a_n|
			\]
			for all  \(\{a_n\}_{n=k}^{m}\in \ell_1\),  where  \(k\in\mathbb{N}\) and 
			$m\in \mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}$.
			
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Prop ergodic of arXiv:2411.04157, 'Stochastic homogenization of dynamical discrete optimal transport'] Let $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega,\sigma_\omega,\theta_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ be stationary, with $(\mathcal X_\omega,\mathcal E_\omega)$ satisfying Assumption (ass: graph of the paper) (equation path of the paper), (equation ball of the paper) almost surely. Let $({\mathcal X_{\omega,\varepsilon}},\mathcal E_{\omega,\varepsilon})$ be the rescaled random graph with the same weights and means. Then almost surely the limit  in the cell formula (equation eq: cell of the paper) exists, is finite, and is independent of the orthotope. If in addition the graph, the weights, and the mean functions are ergodic, then the limit in the cell formula is deterministic almost surely.

[Lemma lem:leave-loop-quickly of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j_0$ be a
sufficiently large integer.  
Let  
$\Psi_0$ be the initialising state with
$j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$ and $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$.  
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be  
the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).
Let $V$ be a volume process from~$\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Then  the following statement holds  for
every $t \geq  \tau_0+2$ and
every tuple
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-2}} = \textup{filling}$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} = \textup{refilling}$, and $j = j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.
Conditioned on $\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} $, with 
probability at least $1-\exp(-\lambda j(\log j )^2/202)$,  
the following events occur.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\mathrm{exit}(t-1) \le t-1+j^{\phi+74}$,
\item for all $\hat{t}$ 
in the range $t-1 \leq \hat{t} < \mathrm{exit}(t-1)$  with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(t)} = \textup{stabilising}$, $\mathrm{trans}(\hat{t}) \le \hat{t} + j^{\phi+72}$,
\item for all $\hat{t}$ 
in the range $t-1 \leq \hat{t} < \mathrm{exit}(t-1)$ 
with $\textup{type}^{\Psi(t)} = \textup{refilling}$, $\mathrm{trans}(\hat{t}) \le \hat{t} + j^{\phi+46}$, and
\item $|\{\Psi(t') \colon t-1 \le t' \le \mathrm{exit}(t-1)-1\}| \le 2j$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm: two function reverse hypercontractivity of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] For any $r \in (-1,1)$ and any non-negative functions \( f, g \in L^2({\mathbb{S}^{n-1} }) \), the following reverse hypercontractivity inequality holds:
\[
\mathop{\mathbb E\/}_{x \cdot y = r}[f(x) g(y)] = \langle f, A_r g \rangle \geq \|f\|_p \|g\|_p - O_r\left(\frac{1}{n}\right) \|f\|_2 \|g\|_2,
\]
as \( n \to \infty \), for all \( 0 < p \leq 1 - |r| \).

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: an interior ball touching the boundary at the point x0 in question (and, for the strong maximum principle, the fact that such a ball can always be produced inside the open set where the solution is strictly below its maximum). Without it the conclusion 'the inward derivative at a boundary minimum is strictly positive' is false. Counterexample at a convex corner: in the plane let Omega be the sector {0 < theta < beta, 0 < r < 1} with 0 < beta < pi and u(r, theta) = r^{pi/beta} sin(pi theta/beta). Then u is harmonic in Omega, continuous on the closure, u > 0 inside and u = 0 on both straight edges, so 0 is a strict boundary minimum of u; but pi/beta > 1, so for every direction e pointing into Omega the difference quotient (u(te) - u(0))/t = O(t^{pi/beta - 1}) tends to 0: there is no Hopf gain at the vertex. No interior ball touches the vertex, exactly as the hypothesis requires. How far the hypothesis can be relaxed: the interior sphere condition may be replaced by an interior C^{1,Dini} (or interior paraboloid/cone-with-Dini) condition, but not by mere C^1 regularity of the boundary; there are C^1 domains where a positive harmonic function vanishing on the boundary has vanishing gradient at a boundary point - for instance the image of the upper half-plane near 0 under the conformal map z -> z log(1/z), whose boundary is C^1 but not Dini smooth at 0, and for which the inverse map has derivative tending to 0. Practical rule for an auditor: a proof that invokes Hopf's lemma (to get strict inequality, strict monotonicity, a sign of the normal derivative, simplicity of the first eigenvalue, or the strong maximum principle at the boundary) must say why the domain has the interior ball property at the relevant point; convex corners and cusps of the domain are where this silently breaks.
title: Pitfall: The Hopf Lemma Needs an Interior Sphere Condition

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2606.09121, 'Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths'] Let
\[
    \varphi_2=(\Delta X(h_0)^2,\ldots,\Delta X(h_{L-1})^2)^\top.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
    \Omega_2(\theta):=\Cov_\theta(\varphi_2)
    =2C(\theta)\circ C(\theta),
\end{equation}
where $\circ$ denotes the Schur product.  Moreover $\Omega_2(\theta)$ is positive definite.

\[   \left| \frac{d}{dp} \mathbb{E}[\tilde{D}_p(o,x)] \right| \le
   \frac{1}{p} \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{e =\{u,v\} \in \pi} 
   \mathbbm{1}_{\left\{u \connectsthru{G_p \setminus \{e\}} v\right\}} d_{G_p \setminus \{e\}}(u,v) \right]
   + \frac{1}{1-p} o(d_G(o,x)),
\]
where the implicit constant in the little o notation may depend on $p_0$ and $G$ but not on $p$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 1 (Admissible local-footprint family) of arXiv:2607.16502, 'Asymptotic Behavior of Path Functionals for Vector-Valued Gaussian Processes at High Level'] For \(E\in\mathcal K\) and \(F\in\mathcal K_0\), equip
\(C(E+F,\R^d)\) with the uniform norm and let
\[
  \Gamma_{E;F}:C(E+F,\R^d)\to\R
\]
be Borel measurable.  If coordinate deletion is used, the notation
\(\Gamma_{E;F}(\bm f_{K^c},\bm\infty_K)\) denotes a separate Borel map
\(\Gamma_{E;F}^{(-K)}:C(E+F,\R^{|K^c|})\to\R\), as above.
We call \(\{\Gamma_{E;F}\}\) an admissible local-footprint family, with
admissible levels \(\mathcal L\) and exponent \(\lambda_\Gamma\), if the
following conditions hold whenever the displayed restrictions are defined.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item[(\namedlabel{LF1}{\(\mathbf{LF}_1\)})]
  \textbf{Long-set union structure.}  For every fixed \(F\in\mathcal K_0\),
  all \(A,B\in\mathcal K\), \(L\in\mathcal L\), and
  \(\bm f\in C((A\cup B)+F,\R^d)\),
  \[
    \Gamma_{A;F}(\bm f)>L
    \Longrightarrow
    \Gamma_{A\cup B;F}(\bm f)>L
    \Longrightarrow
    \Gamma_{A;F}(\bm f)>L
    \quad\hbox{or}\quad
    \sup_{t\in B}\min_i f_i(t)>0,
  \]
  and
  \[
    \Gamma_{A;F}(\bm f)>L
    \Longrightarrow
    \sup_{t\in A}\min_i f_i(t)>0.
  \]
  No inclusion, monotonicity, or decomposition property is imposed in the
  footprint variable.

  \item[(\namedlabel{LF2}{\(\mathbf{LF}_2\)})]
  \textbf{Joint affine scaling.}  For all \(a>0\), \(b\in\R\),
  \(E\in\mathcal K\), \(F\in\mathcal K_0\), and \(L\in\mathcal L\),
  \[
    \Gamma_{aE+b;aF}(\bm f)>a^{\lambda_\Gamma}L
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    \Gamma_{E;F}\bigl(\bm f(a\,\cdot+b)\bigr)>L.
  \]

  \item[(\namedlabel{LF3}{\(\mathbf{LF}_3\)})]
  \textbf{Local regularity for the exact limiting element.}  On each pair
  \(([0,S],F)\) used in a theorem, let \(\mathcal W_{\bm x}\) denote the
  coordinate-reduced shifted limiting path appearing in the corresponding
  local constant, regarded as a random element of
  \(C([0,S]+F,\R^d)\).  Then, for every \(L\in\mathcal L\) and
  Lebesgue-a.e. shift vector \(\bm x\),
  \[
    \pk{\Gamma_{[0,S];F}(\mathcal W_{\bm x})=L}=0,
    \qquad
    \pk{\mathcal W_{\bm x}\text{ is a continuity point of }
       \Gamma_{[0,S];F}}=1.
  \]
\end{enumerate}
As in Remark~\ref{rem:scaled-level-B1}, Assumptions~\ref{LF1}--\ref{LF2}
imply the long-set union structure at the scaled level
\(a^{\lambda_\Gamma}L\) for the scaled footprint \(aF\).  This is the form used
for a physical footprint \(\rho_uF\).
The coordinate-reduction property analogous to Assumption~\ref{B5}, when it
is used, is required only for the path coordinates and with \(F\) fixed.
A one-set family canonically lifts to a local-footprint family by
\[
  \Gamma_{E;F}(\bm f)=\Gamma_E(\bm f|_E),
\]
provided its affine scaling is read in the equivalent threshold-scaled form
used in~\ref{LF2}.
title: Admissible local-footprint family

body:
On any finite time horizon [0, T], the collection of set-valued non-decreasing processes D: [0, T] -> 2^V forms a complete lattice under inclusion. The Picard cascade operator Gamma is monotone, and by the Knaster-Tarski theorem, the set of all solutions to Gamma[D] = D is a non-empty complete lattice whose infimum is the unique minimal solution D^{min}.
G is countable
Gamma is monotone

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent review pending. Half-alphabet partial verifier, all n and arbitrary VC d: for coprime r,K-r and ell>=ceil(K/2), exact pointwise/global robust small-budget frontier is a finite native residual PARTITION optimization sum f*p/m-c*max(f/m), with saturated unknown units split. Marked-cell multiset DP and pair-type count convolution give a polynomial-time estimator/global evaluation for each FIXED alphabet bound K0; no uniform polynomial-in-K claim. Exact oracle plus expected learning penalty. d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K,gcd(r,K-r)=1 Independent uniform ell truth certificates in BOTH variable contexts,ell>=ceil(K/2); actual untagged iid factual samples,ANY n>=0 Pathwise robust source Mis_infinity<=c in every compatible world,0<=c<1/(2NrK); efficiency only for fixed K<=K0. Precisely, native objects (size,false weight,source mass) are U_h=(2(K-h),F,(2-h/r-h/K)/N) for each unresolved pair with h=min(jL,jR)<r; F units (2,1,1/(NK)) for h=r; and A_a=(K-a,F,(r-a)/(Nr)) for each resolved A with known union a<r. Resolved a=r contributes no residual. For a pooled cell S sum each coordinate and set w=f*p/m,rho=f/m. Every robust generator has actual false mass at least V_c=min_partitions(sum w-c*max rho) in each compatible world; an observable native policy attains equality in all worlds. Empty family has value0. Thus global minimax is E[V_c], with the exact pair-type coefficient law and marked-cell multiset DP in the proof. Known-partition oracle is sum F(r-jA)/(Nr(K-jA))-c*max({F/(K-jA):jA<r} union {0}); expected difference is the exact learning penalty. Arithmetic polynomial-time claims assume rational c and each fixed alphabet bound K0. Source chooses contexts uniformly then truths uniformly, with N-2d fixed known S contexts. Side certificates are independent uniform ell-subsets in BOTH contexts including S. Exact score-bin source Mis_infinity robustness is pathwise in every compatible world. This does not settle arbitrary verifier fractions, noncoprime supports, larger budgets or classical labeled ERM/PAC.

This removes C024's additional size/density-order threshold by explicitly
optimizing native residual pooling. Efficiency is polynomial for each
FIXED alphabet bound K0, not uniformly polynomial in K.

## Experiment and statement candidate

Integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r,gcd(r,F)=1,
ceil(K/2)<=ell<=r and arbitrary n>=0. There are d unknown A/S pairs,
one arbitrary r-truth A and one all-K-truth S per pair, and known S
contexts elsewhere. Source chooses contexts uniformly then truths
uniformly. Independent uniform ell-subsets of truths are certified in
BOTH variable contexts, including S. Observe n actual iid untagged facts.
Each realized learned generator must be source Mis_infinity<=c in ALL
compatible worlds, at exact generator-score bins,0<=c<1/(2NrK).

From the observed truth unions, a pair is resolved iff one union exceeds
r. For unresolved pairs h=min(jL,jR)>=ell. For resolved pairs a is the
known union size in the identified arbitrary context.

Build observable native objects with (size m,false weight f,source mass p):

 U_h,ell<=h<r: (2(K-h), F, (2-h/r-h/K)/N), one per unresolved pair.
 U_r unit: (2,1,1/(NK)), F copies per unresolved h=r pair.
 A_a,ell<=a<r: (K-a,F,(r-a)/(Nr)), one per resolved arbitrary context.
 Resolved a=r contributes NO object, since its entire truth support is known.

For a nonempty pooled native cell S define
 m_S=sum m, f_S=sum f, p_S=sum p,
 w(S)=f_S*p_S/m_S and rho(S)=f_S/m_S.
The proposed exact conditional POINTWISE frontier is

 V_c(v)=min_native_partitions P [
              sum_{S in P}w(S)-c*max_{S in P}rho(S)],       (1)

with value0 if there are no native objects. EVERY robustly feasible
generator has actual false mass>=V_c(v(D)) in EACH compatible world,
and an observable policy attains equality in all worlds simultaneously.

Thus the exact global expected robust minimax is E[V_c(v(D))].
The same-data known-partition oracle remains
 O(D,c)=sum_allpairs F*(r-jA)/(Nr(K-jA))
       -c*max({F/(K-jA):jA<r} union {0}).
Their expected difference is the exact experiment-specific learning penalty.

## Hardest step: why arbitrary score bins reduce to native partitions

Remove globally false atoms without increasing any actual risk or robust
calibration, as in C022. Pure-false mass can be transferred to a remaining
cell; mixed-cell mass is redistributed uniformly on nonremoved atoms.
Small-budget lattice forces the resulting zero-score cell to have zero
source mass in every world. Every other score bin has common source mass
by the1/(NrK) bin-mass lattice and2c triangle bound.

Known-A unsaturated supports force outside-known atoms into one bin.
C019's coprime reduction balances each unresolved pair at h=min(jL,jR)
while preserving the same generator's source bin masses and actual
false-count vectors. Fix ANY actual world in that expanded game.
Common residual, whole-context and balanced-saturated components are
those classified in C023/C024; source bin masses can be computed using
the fair compatible-orientation mean without assuming it is the true
sampling posterior.

Every risk-bearing component has source mean density<=lambda=1/(NK).
Safe components have density>=lambda, so analytically removing safe
components weakly lowers its bin's baseline false mass and raises its
actual false fraction (unless the bin becomes empty).

Replace common residuals peeling k<h by native U_h, removing only
2(h-k) known truths of density sigma=(1/(Nr)+lambda)/2>=lambda.
Replace a whole actual-A context by native U_h: its native size
2(K-h)<=K because h>=K/2, and the removed source/size differences satisfy

 Delta_p-lambda*Delta_m=2(K-h)*(lambda-b_h)>=0.

Thus replacing also weakly lowers that bin's baseline false cost while
preserving its false weight F and raising its false fraction. Whole
actual-S contexts are safe and removed analytically. Identified-A
residuals are already native. Saturated balanced outside components
split into units (m2,f1,p=lambda); do NOT force the whole outside set
into one cell.

These analytic operations may use the actual orientation solely in the
LOWER argument. They do not construct a hidden-label algorithm. After
them each nonempty old bin corresponds to a cell of the observable
native object multiset, with the same actual false weight.

Let p0 be the common coarsened source of the post-removal original g,
and alpha the maximum actual false fraction of its nonzero bins.
TV gives H(g)>=H(p0)-c*alpha (after accounting for the risk-decreasing
globally-false removal). For the mapped native partition P,

 H(p0)>=sum_P w(S), alpha<=max_P rho(S).

Therefore H(g)>=sum_P w-c*max_P rho>=V_c(v), pointwise. This avoids
assuming native objects have ordered density or fair actual posterior.

Saturated unit pairing can depend on old bins in the LOWER proof. Any
canonical pairing of opposite-context outside atoms works for the UPPER,
because each unit has invariant source mass lambda and exactly one
actual false atom, regardless of orientation. All units share one type.

## Observable upper policy and donor feasibility

Choose an optimal partition of the observable native objects. Give each
cell uniform score p_S/m_S, remove c mass uniformly from a cell with
maximum rho and add it to fixed S. Selected certified truth groups of
unresolved pairs are paired at sigma; resolved-A known truths use their
native1/(Nr), known S uses lambda, known false atoms use zero.

Every positive native cell has source mass>=1/(NrK)>c. A fixed S
reservoir exists and has at least1/N>c capacity available for transfer.
All nominal group masses are source-invariant; exact-score mergers
contract source calibration and do not change the output law or loss.
Every native object has the stated false weight in EVERY compatible
world. Thus actual false mass is exactly the objective in (1). If the
native family is empty, emit the known true source and attain zero.

## Exact multiset DP

There are T<=2(r-ell)+1<=K-1 native TYPES. Let v_t be counts of a type.
The unit type can have dF copies; other counts are <=d. Costs w(s)
and rho(s) depend only on a nonzero sub-multiset s, not object labels.
Define the unpenalized partition DP

 D(0)=0,
 D(v)=min_{0<s<=v, s contains the first nonempty type}
                    [w(s)+D(v-s)].

Mark the cell that receives the budget reduction:

 V_c(v)=min_{0<s<=v}[w(s)-c*rho(s)+D(v-s)].              (2)

For every complete partition, minimizing over its marked cell chooses
a maximum-risk cell. Hence (2) equals (1), even though D has no budget
term. Reconstruction gives the marked cell and a minimizing D partition.
At a positive-budget optimum the marked cell can be chosen with maximum
rho; otherwise marking a larger-risk cell in that same partition would
strictly improve the global marked minimum.

States are bounded by prod_t(v_t+1). All state/subcell transitions are
bounded by prod_t((v_t+1)(v_t+2)/2). For each FIXED K<=K0 this is
polynomial in d and the explicit input size, with degree depending on
K0; memory is polynomial as well. It is not a polynomial-in-K theorem.
All rational costs have denominators dividing a common multiple of
NrK and the integers1..NK (and the input budget denominator), so their
bit lengths are polynomial in the explicit atom/input size. This does
not justify running an exponentially large-in-K computation on this box.

## Exact global occupancy computation for fixed K

Use C024's pair-type polynomials Q_Uh(z),Q_Aa(z),Q_zero(z), with actual
A/S union occupancies and degree truncated at n. Form the multivariate
pair polynomial

 Q(z,y)=Q_zero(z)+sum_{h<r}Q_Uh(z)*y_Uh
              +Q_Ur(z)*y_unit^F+sum_{a<r}Q_Aa(z)*y_Aa.

Then the exact native type-count law is

 Pr(v)=n!/N^n *[z^n y^v] exp((N-2d)z)*Q(z,y)^d.        (3)

This handles all multinomial context-count dependence. It is the same
in each fixed actual world by support/label symmetries. Since the lower
bound and upper policy match POINTWISE, global minimax equals
sum_v Pr(v)V_c(v), without an invalid conditional-max averaging step.
For fixed K0, type-count convolution and each native multiset DP have
polynomial state/transition bounds in d,n,N; arithmetic bit lengths
remain polynomial. The global oracle uses C024's A-only coefficient
formula. No classical labeled-data ERM/PAC rate is claimed.

## Exact evidence and limits

Five exact-arithmetic suites are saved in logs:

native_pooling_dp_check.json compares1052 multiset games to10954 labeled
partitions, including ordered/full-verifier reductions. It verifies a
genuine greedy failure with gap1/6059157 and a saturated-unit splitting
improvement; forcing one whole outside block can lose optimality.

native_saturated_atomic_check.json permits broader invariant atomic-bin
allocations and safe-atom mixing for K11,r8,ell6,N5,d2. It visits11592
balanced states and about8.5million balanced transitions. Both zero and
positive budget match the native optimum. The positive-budget optimizer
relaxes to a free safe recipient: this is a LOWER bound matched by the
feasible native upper. Outside-block rigidity remains an analytic input,
not an unrestricted Bell-number enumeration.

native_global_type_counts_check.json compares32 global type laws to
13080 independent joint occupancy outcomes, including10 ordered global
reductions. For K11,r8,ell6,d2,n7 the first strict global pooling event has
probability15750/(11^5*N^7); native improvement on that event is
3/(2420N)-3c/55. Independent direct sampling coefficients and all affine
endpoint comparisons verify the stated event law and improvement.

native_unit_raw_worlds_check.json explicitly constructs generator scores
and checks calibration and false mass in ALL14112 compatible worlds of
the K18,r13,ell9,N7,d3 splitting witness, at zero and positive budget:
28224 raw-atom checks. Native baseline2999/46410 beats the unsplit value
8045/124488. These are checks of the actual generator, not just a DP.

native_budget_phase_check.json verifies the exact two-line lower envelope
for that witness: min(2999/46410-3c/5,8045/124488-5c/8),
crossing at53/264537. Optimizing the zero-budget partition first and then
spending c=1/4095 loses29/26453700. All2631 labeled-partition endpoint
comparisons pass; the right endpoint is used only for affine comparison,
not an extension of the strict source-budget theorem.

The analytic identity applies to real c in the stated interval. The
algorithmic bit-complexity claim assumes rational input c; its denominator
is included in the input size. All computations use integers/Fraction.
Finite checks do not replace independent mathematical review.

priority certificate. Standard partition dynamic programming and

The model still requires half-alphabet certificates in BOTH contexts,

[Lem 11 (Limit of the magnetic energies) of arXiv:2608.30445, 'Derivation of a linearly elastic elliptic membrane shell theory in the framework of magnet'] Let
			$(\boldsymbol v(\varepsilon),\boldsymbol m(\varepsilon))
			\in\boldsymbol{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon;\Omega)$ as in Lemma \ref{sec5-lem1}, and set
			\[
			\boldsymbol{\mathfrak m}_\varepsilon(x)
			:=
			m_i(\varepsilon)(x)\boldsymbol g^i(\varepsilon)(x).
			\]
			Then, up to a subsequence (not relabeled),
			$\boldsymbol{\mathfrak m}_\varepsilon$ converges weakly in $(H^1(\Omega))^3$ to $\boldsymbol m_S = m_i \boldsymbol{a}^i$, 
			\begin{align}
				
				&\liminf_{\varepsilon\to0}
				\frac12\int_\Omega
				g^{ij}(\varepsilon)g^{pq}(\varepsilon)
				m_{p\|i}(\varepsilon;\boldsymbol m(\varepsilon))
				m_{q\|j}(\varepsilon;\boldsymbol m(\varepsilon))
				\sqrt{g(\varepsilon)}\,\mathrm{d} x\nonumber\\
				&\hspace{35mm}\geq
				\int_\omega|\nabla_S\boldsymbol m_S|^2\sqrt a\,\mathrm{d} y,
			\end{align}
			and
			\begin{equation}
				
				\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}
				\frac{\mu_0}{2\varepsilon}
				\int_{\mathbb R^3}
				|\nabla v_{\varepsilon,\boldsymbol m(\varepsilon)}|^2\,\mathrm{d} \xi
				=
				\frac1{\mu_0}\int_\omega m_3^2\sqrt a\,\mathrm{d} y.
			\end{equation}
			Conversely, for each
			$\boldsymbol m\in\boldsymbol M_S(\omega)$, define $\boldsymbol{m}^\varepsilon = (m_i^\varepsilon)$ by
			\begin{equation}
				
				m_i^\varepsilon(y,x_3)
				:=
				\boldsymbol m_S(y)\cdot
				\boldsymbol g_i(\varepsilon)(y,x_3).
			\end{equation}
			Then
			$\boldsymbol m^\varepsilon
			\in\boldsymbol M(\varepsilon;\Omega)$,
			$\boldsymbol m^\varepsilon\to\boldsymbol m$ strongly in
			$(H^1(\Omega))^3$, and equality is attained in
			\eqref{sec5-eqn7} in the limit; moreover,
			\eqref{sec5-eqn8} holds for this sequence.

[Theorem WP_H^1 of arXiv:2606.00325, 'Ergodicity for a class of stochastic Hasegawa-Mima equations with dissipation'] For every $p>2$, $T>0$ and $\phi_0\in L_{\mathcal{F}_0}^{2p}(\Omega, V)$ there exists a pathwise unique solution of (eq:main of the paper) in the sense of (def-sol-H1 of the paper). Moreover $\phi$ is a Markov process in $V$ and it satisfies,  
    \begin{align}
        &\mathbb{E}\left[ \left\| \phi(t)\right\|_V^2 + 2\int_0^t|A^{1/2 }\phi(s)|^2ds\right] =  \mathbb{E}\left[ \left\| \phi_0\right\|_V^2 \right] + \kappa t \\
        &\mathbb{E}\left[ \sup_{t\in [0, T]} \|\phi(t)\|_V^p + \left(\int_0^T |A^{1/2} \phi(t)|^2 dt\right)^{p/2}\right] \lesssim 1
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2609.03403, 'Hyperpositive functions, sector bounded functions and a trace formula'] A $\mathbb C^{m\times m}$-valued function $K(z,w)$  defined for $z,w$ in some non-empty set $\Omega$ is said to be a positive definite
kernel\index{positive definite kernel}\index{kernel!positive definite} (or positive definite function) if for every
$N\in\mathbb N$, $z_1,\ldots, z_N\in\Omega$ and $c_1,\ldots, c_N\in\mathbb C^m$, it holds that
\begin{equation}

\sum_{u,v=1}^N c_v^*K(z_v,z_u)c_u\ge 0.
\end{equation}

[Coro cor:Feller of arXiv:2411.19543, 'Feller property and convergence for semigroups of time-changed processes'] Let $\Omega$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with boundary $F$ and $\mu$ the $(d-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of $F$. Consider the second order elliptic operator $\mathscr{L}^V:= -\sum_{l,k=1}^d \partial_l(c_{kl}\partial_k) + V$, where $c_{kl}=c_{lk}:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ are real valued bounded smooth functions satisfying the uniform ellipticity condition
\begin{align*}
	C^{-1}|\xi|^2\leq\sum_{k,l=1}^dc_{k,l}(x)\xi_k\xi_l\leq C|\xi|^2,\quad \xi\in\mathbb{R}^d
\end{align*}
for some $C>0$
and $V:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ is a real valued bounded non-negative measurable function. Assume further that the operator induced by $\mathscr{L}^V$ in $L^2(\Omega):=L^2(\Omega,dx)$ with Dirichlet boundary condition, say $L_D^V$, is injective. Let  $S_t^V$ be the semigroup of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on $L^2(F):=L^2(F,\mu)$ related to $\mathscr{L}^V$ (see [Ouhabaz] and references therein). Then $S_t^V$ maps $C(F)$ into itself and 
$S_t^V|_{C(F)}:C(F)\to C(F)$ has Feller property.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited). In the Fong-Yang scalar Adam normalization, retain q=w_t*y_previous and h=w_next*y as separate bounded coordinates in a limit with e=V=y=y_previous=0. Use the high-branch potential and the exact lifted position relation y_next=-(1+b)*h. For 0<b<1, the limiting potentials and work satisfy phi=-q^2/2, phi_next=(1+b-b^2/2)*h^2, work=h^2, and margin Psi=phi_next-phi-work=(b-b^2/2)*h^2+q^2/2. In particular at b=.9, Psi=99*h^2/200+q^2/2; zero margin forces q=h=0 and y_next=0. This excludes a nonzero position jump on a full zero-margin singular-origin path, not on every origin limit edge.
0<b<1
high-branch source potential as stated
e=V=y=y_previous=0
retained ratios q,h finite
lifted update y_next=-(1+b)h and variance_next=0

Under the assumptions, define f_t=f(.;z_t) and x_(t+1)=x_t-eta_t*grad f_t(x_t). fix T>=2 and 0<alpha<1/2. Put v_t=(T-t+2)^(-alpha) for t=0,...,T-1 and v_T=v_(T-1). Write G_t^2=E||grad f_t(x_t)-grad f_t(x_star)||^2. Then sum_(t=1)^T v_t*[sum_(s=1)^t (v_s-v_(s-1))*E||grad f_t(x_t)-grad f_t(x_s)||^2+v_0*G_t^2] >= (1-2*alpha)*v_T^2*G_T^2+sum_(t=1)^(T-1) [(1-4*alpha)*v_t^2+(v_t-v_(t-1))*sum_(s=t)^T v_s]*G_t^2. The statement uses the natural v_0=(T+2)^(-alpha) explicitly substituted in the source proof of Theorem1. The comparator need not minimize any loss, and no common minimizer is assumed.
Each f(.;z):R^d->R is convex and beta-smooth, beta>0; Euclidean norms.
For every s<=t, conditional on z_1,...,z_(s-1), z_s and z_t have the same distribution. This is conditional equality of marginal laws, not conditional independence.
Fixed comparator x_star and initialization x_1 in R^d; deterministic positive step sizes eta_1,...,eta_T. All displayed expectations are finite.
T>=2, 0<alpha<1/2 and the stated deterministic power weights, including v_0.

[Lemma 6l3d of arXiv:2609.03926, 'Overcolored Partition $k$-tuples Restricted by Parity of the Parts'] We have
	\begin{align}
		\psi(q)&=\frac{f_2^2}{f_1}\\
		\psi(-q)&=\dfrac{f_1f_4}{f_2}\\
		P(q)&=\dfrac{f_2f_3^2}{f_1f_6}\\
		P(-q)&=\dfrac{f_1f_4f_6^5}{f_2^2f_3^2f_{12}^2}\\
		\psi(q)&=P(q^3)+q\psi(q^9)\\
		\dfrac{1}{\psi(q)}&=\dfrac{\psi(q^9)}{\psi(q^3)^4}\left(P(q^3)^2-qP(q^3)\psi(q^9)+q^2\psi(q^9)^2\right)\\
		F(q)&=F(q^9)\left(X(q^3)^{-1}-q-2q^2X(q^3)\right), 
	\end{align}
	 where $P(q)=\displaystyle\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}q^{\frac{3n^2+n}{2}}$,  $F(q)=f_1f_2$ and $X(q)=\dfrac{f_1f_6^3}{f_2f_3^3}$.

[Lemma 38 of arXiv:2604.21669, 'Discontinuous transition in 2D Potts:\\ II. order-order interface convergence'] Let \(0<J<U\) satisfy \(\sinh 2J=e^{-2U}\). There exist \(n_0\geq 1, c,c_0\in (0,+\infty)\) such that for any \(n\geq n_0\), \(m_n\geq c_0n\), any \(\eta_L,\eta_L'\in \SetRootMarkBackCont, \eta_R,\eta_R' \in \SetRootMarkForwCont\) satisfying
	\begin{equation*}

		>0,
	\end{equation*}
	one has
	\begin{equation*}
		\condPrimalDualClusterMeas_{\eta_L,\eta_L'}^{\eta_R,\eta_R'}\big(\goodCl_n \big)
		\geq
		e^{-c\scale_n^{100}},
		\quad
		\OZDec^2_{\eta_L,\eta_R,\eta_L',\eta_R'}\big(\goodCl_n\big)
		\geq
		e^{-c\scale_n^{100}}.
	\end{equation*}

[Thm Main of arXiv:2609.02882, 'A new proof that more than $2/3$ of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and '] We have 

$$ \liminf_{T\to \infty} \frac{N_0^{\textup{s}}(T)}{N(T)}\geqslant C_0=0.67250\ldots
\quad \textup{ and } \quad \liminf_{T\to \infty} \frac{N_d(T)}{N(T)}\geqslant C_1:=\frac{C_0+1}{2}=  0.83625\ldots,
$$
where $C_0$ is defined in (equation Eq:DefinitionC_0 of the paper). That is, more than $67.25\%$ of the non-trivial zeros of the zeta function are simple and on the critical line, and more than $83.62\%$ are distinct. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop shape of arXiv:2609.00672, 'Deciding superellipticity and computing the Weierstrass normal form'] Let $g\ge2$, let $C:y_2^2=f(x_2)$ with $f\in K[x_2]$ separable of degree $2g+1$ or $2g+2$, let $n\in\{2g+1,2g+2\}$, and put $m=n-1$. Let $T_n$ be the set of $t\in\mathbb P^1(K)$ for which

\[
f_t=a\,(x-\beta)^n+b,\qquad a,b\in K^\times,\ \beta\in K .
\]

\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item There are $u,v\in K(C)$ with $K(u,v)=K(C)$ and $v^n=(u^2-b)/a$ for some $a,b\in K^\times$ if and only if $T_n\ne\emptyset$.
\item $T_n$ is finite. It contains $\infty$ only if $\deg f=n$, and a finite $t\in T_n$ is a root of $f$ if $n=2g+1$ and satisfies $f(t)\ne0$ if $n=2g+2$.
\item Let $n=2g+2$ and let $t\in K$. Then $t\in T_n$ if and only if $p_t=f_t'$ satisfies

\begin{equation}
m\,p_t\,p_t''=(m-1)\,(p_t')^2 .
\end{equation}

The coefficients of $m\,p_t\,p_t''-(m-1)(p_t')^2$ as a polynomial in $x$ are polynomials in $t$ over $K$, not all zero, and $T_n\cap K$ is the set of their common roots in $K$.
\end{enumerate}

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). To study the empirical spectral distribution of a non-Hermitian random matrix M, such as an i.i.d.-entry matrix in the circular law problem, Girko's Hermitization method associates to each z in C the 2n x 2n Hermitian matrix H_z with off-diagonal blocks M-zI and (M-zI)^*, whose eigenvalues are plus and minus the singular values of M-zI. The identity log|det(M-zI)| = (1/2) sum_i log(s_i(M-zI)^2) relates the real part of the logarithmic potential of M's empirical spectral distribution at z to the empirical distribution of singular values of M-zI, a Hermitian and hence more tractable object accessible via Stieltjes transform and local law techniques from Hermitian random matrix theory. Establishing, first, convergence of the singular-value distribution of M-zI for almost every z, and second, a uniform bound preventing accumulation of small singular values near 0, needed because log is singular there, together imply, via potential-theoretic uniqueness, convergence of the empirical spectral distribution of M itself, for example to the circular law for i.i.d. entries. It does not work without the delicate small-singular-value control, typically the hardest and most technical part of the proof, requiring separate anti-concentration or least-singular-value estimates, and the method inherently gives information about the logarithmic potential, from which the actual distribution is recovered only via a separate potential-theoretic uniqueness argument. Typical failure: Establishing convergence of the singular-value distribution of M-zI and concluding convergence of the eigenvalue distribution of M without separately proving the required small-singular-value control; without a quantitative lower bound on the least singular value, which can be genuinely delicate for matrices with dependent or heavy-tailed entries, the logarithmic potential argument can fail even though the easier half of Girko's method has been verified, historically the main obstruction in proving circular-law universality under weak entry assumptions. Canonical reference: Girko, 1984, Theory of Probability and its Applications; Bai, 1997, Annals of Probability; Tao and Vu, 2010, Annals of Probability.
i.i.d., or otherwise well-structured, entries of the non-Hermitian matrix M with matching moment and normalization conditions, e.g. mean 0, variance 1/n
convergence, for almost every z or in an appropriately averaged sense, of the empirical singular-value distribution of M-zI, established via Hermitian random matrix methods
a uniform bound preventing the smallest singular values of M-zI from concentrating excess mass near 0, i.e. a least-singular-value or anti-concentration estimate
sufficient regularity to justify exchanging limits with the singular logarithm in the potential-theoretic identity
title: Technique: Hermitization (Girko's Method) for Non-Hermitian Random Matrices

[Thm smasympexGUE of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] There exist universal constants $C,c>0$, and a compactly supported 
distribution $\nu_k$ for every $k\in\mathbb{Z}_+$, such that the following 
holds. Fix any bounded $h\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$, and define
$$
	f(\theta):= h(K\cos\theta)
	\qquad\text{with}\qquad
	K := (Cr)^{q_0}\|X_{\rm F}\|.
$$
Then for every $m, N\in \mathbb{N}$ with $m\le\frac{N}{2}$, we have
\begin{multline*}
       \left| \mathbf{E}[\mathop{\textnormal{tr}} h(X^N)]
	- \sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \frac{\nu_k(h)}{N^k} \right| 
       \le
	\frac{(Cq_0)^{2m}}{m! N^m} \|f^{(2m+1)}\|_{[0, 2\pi]} 
	\\ +
	Cre^{-cN}\big(\sobnorm{h}{0}{(-\infty,\infty)}
		+ \sobnorm{f^{(1)}}{0}{[0, 2\pi]} \big).
\end{multline*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Smooth asymptotic expansion for GUE

[Corollary 28 (Curvature reduction criterion) of arXiv:2608.29406, 'Partially Totally Real Submanifolds of Sasakian Manifolds'] Assume that at a point $p\in M$ there exist
\[
 0\neq X\in\Dtilde_p,\qquad 0\neq Z\in\Dperp_p,
\]
with $PX\neq0$.  Then
\[
 g\bigl(\widetilde R(X,PX)Z,\phi Z\bigr)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c=1.
\]
In particular, on a proper PTR region, any geometric hypothesis forcing this mixed curvature component to vanish forces the ambient Sasakian space form to have $\phi$-sectional curvature $1$.

body: [Conjecture 45 of arXiv:2506.09609, 'Schramm-Loewner evolution contains a topological Sierpi\'nski carpet when $\kappa$ is clos'] The function $\underline{\kappa} \mapsto \rho_c(\underline{\kappa})$ is continuous for $\underline{\kappa} \in (0,4)$. There exists $\underline{\kappa_c} \in (2,4)$ such that $\rho_c(\underline{\kappa}) > \underline{\kappa}/2 - 4$ for $\underline{\kappa} \in (2, \underline{\kappa_c})$ and $\rho_c(\underline{\kappa}) = \underline{\kappa}/2 - 4$ for $\underline{\kappa} \in (\underline{\kappa_c}, 4)$. Moreover, for $\kappa \in (4, 16/ \underline{\kappa_c})$, the SLE$_{\kappa}$ curve is almost surely conformally removable and the adjacency graph of its complementary is connected.
