[Prop second of arXiv:2507.18080, 'An upper bound for the lower tail of the mass of balls under the Critical $2d$ stochastic '] [BC98]
Let $u^{\vartheta,\varepsilon}$ be the solution of  (equation eq:SHEbetae of the paper) with initial condition  $u_0\in L^2({\mathbb{R}}^2)$. 

Then, for $\phi\in L^2({\mathbb{R}}^2)$, we have\begin{align}
&\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}\mathrm{Var}\left( \int_{{\mathbb{R}}^2}u^{\vartheta,\varepsilon}(t,x)\phi(x)\text{\rm d} x\right)\\
&=4\pi\iint_{{\mathbb{R}}^2\times {\mathbb{R}}^2}\text{\rm d} x\text{\rm d} y\iint_{0<u<v<t}\text{\rm d} u\text{\rm d} v \left(P_uu_0(x)\right)^2 G_{\vartheta}(v-u,y-x)\left(P_{t-v}\phi(y)\right)^2\notag\\
&=\mathrm{Var}\left(\mathscr{Z}_t^\vartheta(u_0,\phi)\right),
\end{align}
where the semigroup is defined by $P_t\phi(x)=\int_{{\mathbb{R}}^2}\phi(y)p_t(x,y)\text{\rm d} y $.

The same identity  holds when $u_0\in C_b({\mathbb{R}}^2)$ and $\phi\in C_c({\mathbb{R}}^2).$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop second of arXiv:2507.18080

[Definition 15 (Good metrics) of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] An admissible metric \(\widetilde g\) is called \emph{good} if
	\[
	g=h, \qquad \text{and} \qquad a^c\equiv0.
	\]
Thus, for a good metric, the horizontal and vertical components are determined by the same metric on the base, and the horizontal--vertical cross term vanishes identically.

[Corollary 9 (Winkler (1988)) of arXiv:2608.13358, 'Extreme points of sets of probability measures and $\phi$-divergences'] Assume that $\cI=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and that the extreme points of $\cP$ are exactly the Dirac measures.\ Then, $p\in \cM$ is an extreme point of $\cM$ if and only if
\[
p=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_j\delta_{\omega_j}
\]
with $m\in \N$ satisfying $m\leq n+1$, $\alpha_1,\ldots, \alpha_m>0$, and pairwise distinct $\omega_1,\ldots, \omega_m\in \Omega$, such that the
vectors
\[
v_j:=\big(1,f_1(\omega_j),\ldots,f_n(\omega_j)\big)^\top\in\R^{n+1},
\qquad j=1,\ldots,m,

body:
[Conjecture conj of arXiv:2510.05850, 'Three-point connectivity constant for $q$-state Potts spin clusters'] Let $\omega^\delta$ be the fuzzy Potts configuration on $\delta \mathbb{Z}^2$ with parameters $q \in (1,4)$ and $r=1/q$.
    Define $P_n^\delta(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ to be the probability that the points $z_i^\delta$ are all in the same red cluster of $\omega^\delta$, and let $\pi_\delta$ be the probability that there is a red nearest-neighbor path connecting the origin and the unit circle. Then the following limit exists:
    \begin{equation}
    P_n(z_1,\ldots,z_n) := \lim_{\delta \to 0} \pi_\delta^{-n} P_n^\delta(z_1,\ldots,z_n).
    \end{equation}
    
    Furthermore, let $\{\mathcal{C}_i^\delta\}$ be the collection of red clusters of $\omega^\delta$, and let $\mathcal{M}_i^\delta$ be the counting measure on vertices in $\mathcal{C}_i^\delta$, normalized by $\delta^2\pi_\delta^{-1}$. Then, under the weak Hausdorff topology,
    \[ (\omega^\delta, \{\mathcal{M}_i^\delta\}) \overset{d}{\rightarrow} (\omega, \{C \cdot \mathcal{M}_i\}), \quad \mbox{as } \delta\to 0. \]
    Here, $\omega$ is the continuum fuzzy Potts configuration, $\mathcal{M}_i$ is the Miller--Schoug measure on $\mathcal{C}_i$ (the scaling limit of $\mathcal{C}_i^\delta$), and $C>0$ is a constant. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture conj of arXiv:2510.05850

body:
[Prop function doesn't work of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] There exists a process in the \nameref{setting} Setting such that additionally:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item each constituent CRN of the process is endowed with mass-action kinetics and has at-most-monomolecular reactions,

        \item for each $i$ there exists a vector $v^i\in\mathbb R^d_{\ge0}$ such that $(v^iM_i)_m>0$ for each $m\in\operatorname{supp}(v^i)$, where $(v^iM_i)_m$ is the $m$-th entry of the vector $v^iM_i$,

        \item $\bigcap_j \operatorname{supp}(v_j)\ne\varnothing$,
    \end{itemize}
    but nevertheless, if $h$ is the function $h(x,i):=1-(1+v^i\cdot x)^{-1}$ then for any choices of $\kappa>0$ and $b$ there exists a state $(x,i)$ such that $v^i\cdot x>b$ but $\mathcal L_\kappa(x,i)<0$.
\begin{proof}
    Consider the mixed process from Example (ex:IDK man of the paper). Notice that if $v^1:=(2,1,0)$ and $v^2:=(0,1,2)$, then one has $v^1M_1=(7,1,0)$ and $v^2M_2=(0,1,7)$. Let $h(x,i)=1-(1+v^i\cdot x)^{-1}$, and notice that
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal L_\kappa(x,1)
        &=\frac1{1+2x_1+x_2}\left(\frac{\kappa(-2x_1+2x_3)}{1+x_2+2x_3}+\frac{7x_1}{1+2x_1+x_2+7}+\frac{x_2}{1+2x_1+x_2+1}+\frac{\alpha x_3(0)}{1+2x_1+x_2}\right)\\
        &=\frac1{1+2x_1+x_2}\left(\frac{2\kappa(x_3-x_1)}{x_2+2x_3+1}+\frac{7x_1}{2x_1+x_2+8}+\frac{x_2}{2x_1+x_2+2}\right)\\
        &\le\frac1{1+2x_1+x_2}\left(\kappa-\frac{2\kappa x_1}{x_2+2x_3+1}+\frac{7}{2}+1\right).
    \end{align*}
    This upper bound is evidently negative iff the expression inside the parentheses is negative. Moreover, for any fixed values of $\kappa$, $x_2$, and $x_3$, the expression will be negative for all sufficiently large values of $x_1$. The result follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $v_1,\dots,v_N\in\{-1,0,1\}^d$, set $z=\sum_{i=1}^N v_i$, and suppose $\|z\|_\infty\le b$ for some integer $b\ge0$.

[Proposition prop:local_energy of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Let $Q=I \times B$ be a parabolic cylinder with side length $\varrho\in (0,1/2]$, and fix $r\in (1,\infty)$.
Suppose that (equation eq:ass_caccioppoli1 of the paper)-(equation eq:ass_caccioppoli4 of the paper) holds. Then there is a constant $C>0$ depending only on $d,M,\varrho,\nu,\nu_0$ and $r$ such that, for all $\phi\in C^\infty_{{\rm c}}(B)$ such that $\int_B \phi^2=1$, all $\psi\in C^\infty_{{\rm c}}((t_0-\varrho^2,t_0])$, and all local solutions $(v,\pi,\widetilde{\pi}_n)$ to the stochastic Stokes system (equation eq:turbulent_stokes_caccioppoli of the paper), the following localized energy inequality holds a.s.\
\begin{align}
\nonumber
&\sup_{I}\int_{B} \psi^2\phi^2|\widetilde{v}_\phi|^2 
+\int_{Q}\psi^2\phi^2  \, |\nabla v|^2 
\leq 
C \int_Q \psi^2 |\nabla \phi|^2 \|(\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n\|_{\ell^2}^2
\\
\nonumber
&\ \   
+  C \int_{Q} |\widetilde{v}_\phi|^2 \big( \phi^2 |\partial_t\psi^2 | +\psi^2 |  \nabla  \phi|^2 \big) + C \int_I \psi^2  \|(\nabla \phi) \pi\|_{H^{-1}(B)}^2\\
\nonumber
&  \ \  
+ C \int_{Q}\psi^2  \big( |\nabla \phi|^2 |F|^2+ |\phi|^2 \|(G_n)_n\|_{\ell^2}^2\big) 
\\
&\ \   
+C\sup_I \Big|\sum_{n} \int_{t_0-\varrho^2}^\cdot \psi^2 \Big[\int_B \big( \widetilde{\pi}_n \widetilde{v}_\phi-\zeta_n \frac{|\widetilde{v}_\phi|^2}{2}\big) \cdot \nabla (\phi^2) +(G_n\cdot \widetilde{v}_\phi) \phi^2\Big]\,\mathrm{d} W^{n}\Big|.

\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Candidate source-faithful mixed-bin transfer: with q=p^Pi, false F subset arbitrary block A and rho_B=|F intersection B|/|A intersection B| (zero when denominator0), g(F)>=sum_B p(B)rho_B|Ahat intersection B|/|B|-q(A triangle Ahat)-TV(q,g). For N uniform contexts, K candidates/context, at least r truths/context sampled uniformly, and partition errors on WHOLE contexts, q(error)<=(K/r)p(error) for every data-dependent binning. Expected source Mis_b<=eps and a separately justified ERM error a_n therefore cost at most eps+(K/r)a_n in this transfer. The rho_B are true within-bin false fractions, not assumed observable or constant. The formula is pointwise and needs no independence between g, learned partition and data. It does not prove an ERM rate, matching bounds, or an exact expected known-partition frontier. The bin source coarsening, rather than raw p, measures generic partition error; the K/r comparison uses the whole-context structure. No full Lean certificate.
Finite nonempty cells; p,g probability laws; F subset A
Pi=V_b(g) when identifying TV(q,g) with source Mis_b
Context comparison: equal context masses, uniform truths per context,1<=r<=K, whole-context partition errors

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:247e82cbf98b79debe0935a4ac5270d59fc42fa0f91d67bfe980847ad08f4e4c","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/24/247e82cbf98b79debe0935a4ac5270d59fc42fa0f91d67bfe980847ad08f4e4c.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:2c4fc927b131230fc51f77b2068375180fabbeb4df3a4fffa8cf9f06efbd52db","bundle_entry_key":"source-coarsened-mixed-bin-partition-error","bundle_id":"population.t379-source-faithful-mixed-bin-context-error-transfer-20261022","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"calibrated generation; mixed probability bins; VC partitions; distribution comparison","draft":"w709/bundle_022.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:kalai-vempala-mixed-bin-context-partition-error-transfer","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Mixed-bin transfer under the source calibration statistic

T379-C031 v2, proof (unaudited), Target1. One deterministic statement.
This is an elementary source-statistic lemma with a context-union
comparison, not a matching frontier or a claim of new mathematical priority.

## Statement

Let Y be finite, p and g probability distributions, and Pi any finite
partition into NONEMPTY cells. Let q=p^Pi be the uniform-per-bin
coarsening in Kalai--Vempala Definition1. Let A be the true arbitrary
block, Ahat its estimate, and F a false-fact set with F subset A.
For B in Pi put

 a_B=|A intersection B|, ahat_B=|Ahat intersection B|,
 rho_B=|F intersection B|/a_B if a_B>0, and rho_B=0 otherwise.

Then

 g(F) >= sum_B p(B) rho_B ahat_B/|B|
          - q(A triangle Ahat) - TV(q,g).                 (1)

In particular Pi may be the source's data-dependent V_b(g), in which
case the last term is exactly Mis_b(g,p). The assertion is pointwise
in the realized data and true world; it does not require independence
between g, Ahat and the data. The rho_B are true within-bin false
fractions, NOT assumed observable or constant across bins.

## Per-bin proof with both blocks visible

Define a nonnegative deficit for each bin:

 d_B=sum_{y in B}(q(y)-g(y))_+.

For each B, uniformity of q and F subset A give

 g(F intersection B) >= q(F intersection B)-d_B
                     = p(B) rho_B a_B/|B| - d_B.

Split the bin as a_B systematic-complement atoms and |B|-a_B systematic
atoms. Replacing the former count by ahat_B introduces exactly
p(B)rho_B(a_B-ahat_B)/|B|. Because 0<=rho_B<=1 and
|a_B-ahat_B|<=|(A triangle Ahat) intersection B|, this change is at least

 -p(B)|(A triangle Ahat) intersection B|/|B|.

Sum the resulting per-bin inequalities. Both q and g have total mass1,
so sum_B d_B=TV(q,g), with coefficient1 rather than2.
The partition-error sum is exactly q(A triangle Ahat).
This proves (1). No products of probabilities or conditional-to-joint
independence assumptions are used.

Equivalently the unperturbed mixed-bin expression is
q(F)=sum_B p(B)[a_B/|B|]rho_B: it accounts explicitly for dilution by
the systematic part |B|-a_B in every bin, including mixed cells.

## Expected calibration and precisely what it does not supply

Taking expectation preserves (1), so an expected Mis_b bound eps
subtracts eps. An expected q-partition-error bound eta subtracts eta.
But a bound on E p(A triangle Ahat) cannot replace eta without another
argument. A simple metric control is p=(1,0), g=(1/2,1/2), one bin:
q is uniform, Mis_1=0, and E={second atom} satisfies p(E)=0 but q(E)=1/2.
This is a metric counterexample, not a counterexample to an entire
two-block statistical model with additional assumptions.

Nor does (1) supply rho_B lower bounds after data-dependent binning.
Those need an arbitrary-fact posterior/missing-mass argument, such as
the hypotheses actually used in Kalai--Vempala Theorem1. It would be
invalid to assert binwise independence of false identities from g.

## Failure checks and scope

The exact verifier checks all partitions of three atoms, rational
source/generator distributions, and all set triples F subset A,Ahat.
It tests the true per-atom TV definition and per-bin deficit sum.
Controls must fail when the calibration term is dropped, when the
partition-error term is dropped, and when aggregated bin TV replaces
the source statistic. All arithmetic is rational.

The Lean probe is limited to the scalar step
rho*a >= rho*b-e from 0<=rho<=1 and |a-b|<=e, e>=0.
Its acceptance, if any, does not formalize (1), the bin construction,
or the ERM statistical theorem. Its exact outcome is in the run log;
the full lemma is not claimed Lean-checked.

## Uniform-context specialization of the same transfer statement

Suppose Y consists of N contexts with K candidate atoms each. The source
chooses a context uniformly, then a truth uniformly among that context's
k_x truths, with r<=k_x<=K, r>=1. The two partitions A,Ahat are unions
of WHOLE contexts. Writing R_p(h,hat h)=p(A triangle Ahat), (1) gives

 g(F) >= sum_B p(B)rho_B ahat_B/|B|
          -(K/r) R_p(h,hat h)-Mis_b(g,p)                 (2)

when Pi=V_b(g). To see this, max_y p(y)<=1/(Nr) implies
q(y)=p(B)/|B|<=1/(Nr) in every bin. If exactly m contexts are
misclassified, the error union has mK atoms and p-error m/N.
Consequently q(error)<=mK/(Nr)=(K/r)R_p.
This holds for every data-dependent g and every partition Pi: no
independence or uniform convergence over bins is required.

Taking expectation yields a penalty at most (K/r)E R_p+eps under
expected source Mis_b<=eps. Thus a separately established ERM rate
E R_p<=a_n would give an explicit (K/r)a_n term in this lower transfer.
No ERM rate is inferred from the unlabeled factual sample itself.

Load-bearing conditions: equal context masses, at least r truths per
context, and errors that are unions of whole contexts. The earlier
single-atom metric counterexample violates the last condition and
therefore does NOT refute (2). When r=K, q=p is globally uniform and
the error comparison is equality.

The proof is an application of total variation and counting. Its role
is to name the exact error distribution that the unpaid ERM step must
control. Matching upper/lower rates, a closed H^*, posterior rho_B
bounds and an observable ERM loss remain unproved.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:ce502524661dbd572fa8e6970726384b6100a27c07dfd1a168cbec2c22d75f76","revision_digest":"sha256:f438e44e1fab2d216371493a747b33a72ebb8b0bad5275c336626892d7d6fedd","source_id":"owner:w709:T379-C031:v2","source_revision":"2026-10-22T02:52:48.178817+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

we have

[Definition 36 (Weight) of arXiv:2605.09459, 'Multipoint connectivity in the branching interlacement process'] Given a tree $T$ equiped with functions $\varphi : V(T) \to \mathbb{Z}^d$, and $\alpha : E(T) \to \mathbb{R}$, we define the \textit{weight} of $T$, as
  \[
    p^{\alpha}_\varphi(T) = \prod_{(u,v) \in E(T)} \frac{1}{1 + \|\varphi(u)-\varphi(v)\|^{\alpha(u,v)}}.
  \]
  For a tree $T$ with vertices in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, we write $p^{\alpha}(T)$ for $p^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{Id}}(T)$. When there is no possible ambiguity, we omit the exponent $\alpha$. Furthermore, if the weight is constant equal to $c$, we simply write $p^c_\varphi$.
title: Weight

[Definition of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] Let $v=e_-\cap e_+\in V(N)$ be a vertex of the Newton polygon. We say that a chamber ${\mathsf{R}}$ has a \emph{sign (or color) change} at $v$ if
\[
\operatorname{sign}_{\mathsf{R}}(e_-)\neq \operatorname{sign}_{\mathsf{R}}(e_+).
\]
We write $\operatorname{SC}({\mathsf{R}})\subset V(N)$ for the set of sign changes of ${\mathsf{R}}$.

[Theorem thm:main-result of arXiv:2607.24018, 'Jeu de taquin forests \\ and the inverse infinite RSK correspondence'] Let $T$ be a Plan\-che\-rel-distributed random IYT, and let 
	$(z_1,z_2,\ldots) = \RSK^{-1}(T)$ be the associated sequence of i.i.d.
	$U(0,1)$-distributed random variables. The following statements hold almost
	surely:
	
	\begin{enumerate}
	
	\item Each of the trees $\tau$ in $\Phi(T)$
possesses an asymptotic direction $\alpha_\textnormal{asym}(\tau)$ (see
(subsec:asymptotic-direction of the paper) for the definition).
	
	\item We have the equality of sets
	\[
	\left\{ \alpha_\textnormal{asym}(\tau) \,:\, \tau \textrm{ is a tree in }\Phi(T)
	\right\}
	= \{ z_1, z_2, \ldots \}.
	\]

	\item Distinct trees have distinct asymptotic directions;
	in particular, the map $\tau \mapsto \alpha_\textnormal{asym}(\tau)$
	is a bijection between the set of trees of $\Phi(T)$
	and the set $\{ z_1, z_2, \ldots \}$.

	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Partial inverse of the RSK map

[Proposition l:cumuredu of arXiv:2411.08848, 'Stationary random measures: Covariance asymptotics, variance bounds and central limit theo'] (Cumulant reduction, [Krishnapur2007])

Assume that ${\mathcal X}$ is a simple point process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying Assumption (asmpt:integrationofrhokT of the paper).  Let $Y_i={\mathcal X}(h_i), i =1,\ldots,m$ for some compactly supported \textcolor{black}{continuous} functions $h_i:\mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R},  $ and $Y = (Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)$ be the corresponding random vector.   Then we have that,  

\begin{equation}

{\boldsymbol \kappa}_m[Y] = \<Q_m[(h_i(x_j))_{1\le i,j\le m}], \rho_m^T\>,  
\end{equation}
where 
\[
Q_m[(y_{i,j})_{1\le i,j\le m}]=\sum_{\tau:[m]\to [m-1]}c_{\tau} \prod_{i=1}^{m}(y_{i,\tau(i)}-y_{i,m})
\]
with $c_{\tau}=(-1)^{m-\ell(\tau)}\frac{(\ell(\tau)-1)! \ (m-\ell(\tau))!}{m! \ (m-1)!}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 26 (Schatten classification from orthogonal direct-sum laws) of arXiv:2608.04993, '2608.04993'] Let $1\le r\le\infty$.  Replace the area square-sum law by the $\ell^r$ block
law and normalize a standard skew two-plane by $2^{1/r}$ for $r<\infty$, or by
$1$ for $r=\infty$.  Then the finite-dimensional coefficient norm is
$\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal S_r}$.  The analogous symmetric law, normalized in one
dimension, also gives $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal S_r}$.  On finite-rank state
coordinates the dual gauge is the Schatten $r'$ gauge; completing finite ranks
gives $\mathcal S_{r'}$ when $r'<\infty$ and $\mathcal K(H)$ at the endpoint
$r'=\infty$.

For the principal pair $(r_A,r_Q)=(2,\infty)$, the state geometry is therefore
$\mathcal S_2/\mathcal S_1$.  At the coefficient endpoint $r_Q=\infty$, the
finite-rank norm completion is $\mathcal K(H)$, while the full normal test space
may be taken to be $\mathcal L(H)=\mathcal S_1(H)^*$; both unit balls induce the
same trace norm on $\mathcal S_1(H)$.

[Lemma lem:gyration_derivative3 of arXiv:2508.18807, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation I: High effective dimension}'] If Case 2 or 3 of (equation HD+ of the paper) holds then for each $u\in \mathbb R^d$ we have that
\begin{multline*}

 \frac{d}{dr} \mathbb E_{\beta_c,r} \left[\sum_{x\in K} \langle x,u\rangle^2 \right]
=  \frac{2 \alpha}{r}  \mathbb E_{\beta_c,r} \left[\sum_{x\in K} \langle x,u\rangle^2 \right] + \frac{\alpha^2}{\beta_c} r \int_{B} \langle y,u\rangle^2 \dif y 
\\\pm O\left(\frac{\|u\|^2_2}{r(\log r)^2} \mathbb E_{\beta_c,r}\sum_{x\in K}\|x\|_2^2\right)
\end{multline*}

as $r\to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition def:volume-process of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] (short version of Definition~(def:volume-process-ext of the paper), without the explanation)
Fix a real number $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. 
Fix an initialising state 
$\Psi_0 = (0, \tau_0,j,\overline{z},\emptyset,\textup{initialising})$.
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be a transition rule on a set of high-level states which includes~$\Psi_0$. Let $\Psi^*$ be the $\Psi_0$-closure of~$\mathrm{hls}$. Suppose that $\mathrm{hls}$ is $\Psi^*$-valid.
A \emph{volume process} $V$ 
from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$ is defined as follows. 

Choose the initial population as follows.
Choose 
a random vector 
$\overline{\mathrm{arr}} = (\mathrm{arr}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{arr}_j)
\sim\mathsf{Po}(F_{[j]}^{\Psi_0}(\tau_0))$.
Let $\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^V(\tau_0)$ be a tuple
of $j$~disjoint sets
$\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^V(\tau_0) = (\mathbf{arr}^V_1(\tau_0),\ldots,\mathbf{arr}^V_j(\tau_0))$ 
where each $\mathbf{arr}^V_i(\tau_0) \subseteq \mathcal{B}(\tau_0)$ and has size 
$\mathrm{arr}^V_i(\tau_0)$.

Let ${\overline{\mathbf{b}}}^V_{[j]}(\tau_0) = \overline{\mathbf{arr}}^V(\tau_0)$.
For all $i>j$, let   ${\mathbf{b}^V_i}(\tau_0) = \emptyset$. 
Let the initial high-level state 
$\Psi(\tau_0)$ be~$\Psi_0$. 
 

For all $t> \tau_0$ the evolution of 
$\newsym{V}{Volume process - Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper)}{V}$ at step~$t$ is as follows, having 
already defined $\Psi(t-1)$ and  ${\overline{\mathbf{b}}}^V(t-1)$.

\begin{itemize}

\item Let $j = j^{\Psi(t-1)}$.

\item Let
$\newsym{Y-t}{part of volume process
- Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper)
}{Y_{t-1}}$ be a $j$-jammed process with 
send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$t-1$, 
birth rate~$\lambda$, and initial population  $\mathbf{arr}^{Y_{t-1}}(t-1) = {\overline{\mathbf{b}}}_{[j]}^V(t-1)$.

 

 
\item  Let $\newsym{Psi-t}{high-level state determined by volume process - Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper) }
{\Psi(t) }
= \mathrm{hls}(\Psi(t-1), {\overline{b}}^{Y_{t-1}}_{[j]}(t), t)$.

 

\item Let ${\overline{b}}^V_{[j]}(t) = \phi_{\Psi(t-1),\Psi(t),t}({\overline{b}}^{Y_{t-1}}_{[j]}(t))$.

  

\item  For all $i\in [j]$,  let  $\mathbf{b}_i^{V}(t)$ be the lexicographically least
subset of $\mathbf{b}_i^{Y_{t-1}}(t)$ 
of size $b^V_i(t)$. 
 

\item {For all $i > j$, let $\mathbf{b}^V_i(t) = \emptyset$.}
\end{itemize}
title: Definition def:volume-process of arXiv:2602.21315

[Theorem theo.SRWBRW of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] Let $(R_\infty^k)_{k\ge 1}$, and $(\mathcal R_c^k)_{k\ge 1}$, be respectively SRW and critical BRW ranges on $\mathbb Z^d$. 
\begin{enumerate}  
\item[(i)] If $d\ge 5$, then for any $i\ge 2$, and any $j\ge 1$, there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$, such that for any $t>1$, 
$$\exp(-c_1\, t^{1-\frac 2d}) \le \mathbb P(|R_\infty^1\cap \dots \cap R_\infty^i \cap \mathcal R_c^1 \cap \dots\cap \mathcal R_c^j|>t) \le  \exp(-c_2\, t^{1-\frac 2d}). $$ 
\item[(ii)] If $d\ge 7$, then for any $k\ge 1$, there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$, such that for any $t>1$, 
$$\exp(-c_1\, t^{1-\frac 2{d-2}} ) \le \mathbb P(|R_\infty^1\cap \mathcal R_c^1 \cap \dots \cap \mathcal R_c^k|>t) \le  \exp (-c_2\, t^{1-\frac 2{d-2}}). $$ 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theo.SRWBRW of arXiv:2411.19145

[Prop 7 (Brunn-Minkowski inequality) of arXiv:2609.00743, '$L_p$ Brunn-Minkowski inequality for the eigenvalue of generalized Monge-Ampère equation'] Let $K$ and $L$ be nonempty bounded measurable sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that $(1-\lambda)K+\lambda L$ is also measurable for $\lambda\in(0,1)$. Then
    \[
    V_n((1-\lambda)K+\lambda L)^{\frac1n}\ge (1-\lambda)V_n(K)^{\frac1n}+\lambda V_n(L)^{\frac1n}.
    \]
    Here $V_n(\cdot)$ denotes the Lebesgue measure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality

body: [Defn of arXiv:2412.04527, 'Critical Drift for Brownian Bees and a Reflected Brownian Motion Invariance Principle'] Let $X$ be a random variable taking values in a partially ordered space $\mathcal{E}$ with partial ordering $\leq_o$. A function $f:\mathcal{E}\to \mathbb{R}$ is called \textbf{increasing} if for $e_1,e_2\in \mathcal{E}$, we have $e_1 \leq_o e_2 \implies f(e_1)\leq f(e_2)$. An event $A$ is called increasing if the indicator of $A$ is an increasing function. We call the random variable $X$ \textbf{associated} if we have $\mathbb{E}[f(X)g(X)]\geq \mathbb{E}[f(X)]\mathbb{E}[g(X)]$ for all increasing functions $f,g$.

body: [Defi def: Poisson tree of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] A $(d-1)$-\emph{rooted Poisson tree} with parameter $\lambda > 0$ is a $(d-1)$-rooted random $d$-dimensional simplicial complex $(X, \tau)$ constructed as follows: Start with a root $(d-1)$-simplex $\tau$. At each step $k = 0, 1, \dots$, to every $(d-1)$-simplex $\tau'$ of distance $k$ from $\tau$, add $\mathsf{Poi}(\lambda)$ new vertices $v_1, \dots, v_m$ and the $d$-dimensional simplices $\tau' \cup \{v_1\}, \dots, \tau' \cup \{v_m\}$ along with all their lower-dimensional simplices to the simplicial complex constructed in the previous step. The process is independent across different $(d-1)$-simplices at each step.
title: $(d-1)$-rooted Poisson trees

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.06823, 'On spectrum of sample correlation matrices from large fold tensor vectors'] (\cite{Jiang2004}*{Lemma 2.1}) 
Let $A$ be an $n \times p$ complex random matrix. Denote by $A_j$ the $j$-th column of $A$, and $A_{ij}$ the $(i,j)$-th entry of $A$. Let $B$ be the matrix whose $j$-th column is $A_j/\|A_j\|$. Then for any $n \times n$ diagonal matrix $\Lambda = \diag (\Lambda_{11},\ldots,\Lambda_{nn})$
\begin{align*}
    \Tr \left( \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}} A - B \right) \Lambda_n \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}} A - B \right)^* \right)
    = \sum_{j=1}^p \Lambda_{jj} \left( \dfrac{1}{n} \|a_j\|^2 - 1 \right) - 2 \sum_{j=1}^p \Lambda_{jj} \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \|a_j\| - 1 \right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.06823

[Lemma 51 (no hidden equivariant gauge directions) of arXiv:2609.03593, '\textbf{New Homogeneous Einstein Metrics from Detection}'] Let $H/K$ be an effective irreducible compact symmetric pair with $H$ and
$K$ simple, and put $G=H^s$, $L=\Delta K$.  Then
\[
 N_{\mathfrak h^s}(\Delta\mathfrak k)=\Delta\mathfrak k.
\]
Consequently the connected group of $G$-equivariant diffeomorphisms of
$G/L$ is trivial.  More generally, the invariant metric tangent space
contains no nonzero infinitesimal pure-gauge tensor $\mathcal L_Xg$.
After fixing homothety, the response kernel therefore contains neither a
scale direction nor a diffeomorphism-gauge direction.

body:
[Definition 2 of arXiv:2606.00586, 'Stein's Method for Convergence Rates of Invariant Measures in the Nonlocal-to-Local Limit'] Given a fixed measurable function $m: \mR^d \to \mR$. The corresponding multiplier operator $T_m$ with $m$ is given by
\[
T_m [f]:= \mathcal{F}^{-1}\bigl( m  \hat f  \bigr), \quad f \in \sS (\mathbb{R}^d),
\]
where $\hat f = \sF f$ denotes the Fourier transform of $f$, and $\sF^{-1}$ is the inverse Fourier transform. If $T_m$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, we call $m$ an $L^p$ Fourier multiplier.

body:
Own-work draft: proof (unaudited); independent correctness and novelty review pending. General T267 remains open.

Self-contained model definitions for this obstruction: 0<e<1/4, D=1+e^2+e^4, uniform population on
x_(s,t)=(1,es,e^2 t)/sqrt(D), one training observation at each of these
four inputs, and u_e=(0,e,1)/sqrt(1+e^2). The teacher is
 g_e(x)=ReLU(u_e.x)-c_e/2, c_e=e^2/sqrt(D(1+e^2)), alpha_e=c_e/2.
Fix 0<nu<=1 and kappa>0. For each of the sixteen sign vectors
xi in {-1,1}^4, train a separate network with labels
 y_i=g_e(x_i)+sigma_e xi_i, sigma_e=2 alpha_e sqrt(kappa/sqrt(e)).
All sixteen networks share their initial parameters. At width m these are
 f_m(x)=m^(-1/2) sum_(j=1)^m a_j ReLU(w_j.x),
 w_j(0) iid N(0,I_3), a_j(0) iid uniform {-nu,nu}, independent of w_j(0).
Train BOTH layers by simultaneous discrete GD with step gamma=1/2 on
(1/8) sum_i (f_m(x_i)-y_i)^2. Set the derivative at a zero gate to zero.
No pairing, tying or resetting of the readout is imposed.

# C019 v1: the averaged central peak is absent from each realized-label curve
Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: route-failure. Target: 1. Novelty unestablished.
This is a local-window obstruction, not a global no-double-descent theorem.

## 1. Exact claim and dependencies
Use exactly C018's four stratified inputs, unit-norm single-index ReLU
teacher, fixed nu,kappa>0 (nu<=1), independent Gaussian hidden weights,
iid signed heads, both-layer GD step1/2 and sigma_e=2alpha_e sqrt(rho_e),
rho_e=kappa/sqrt(e). Unlike C018 retain the individual label realization:
 R_(e,m,xi)(k)=(1/4)sum_i(f_(m,xi)(x_i;k)-g_e(x_i))^2.
All sixteen networks share initialization. For any fixed bounded interval
I=[A,B] with A<B, let J_e(I) be the integers k with
 b_s k-(3/2)log(1/e) in I.
Then
 lim_(e downarrow0) liminf_(m to infinity)
 P(each of the sixteen sequences (R_(e,m,xi)(k))_(k in J_e(I))
   is strictly monotone in one direction) = 1.             (1)
The direction may depend on xi and initialization. For small e, J has
many consecutive integers. In particular none of the sixteen individual
curves has decrease/rise/decrease witnesses entirely inside this window,
with probability tending to one in this iterated-limit sense.
C018's sixteen-trajectory average may nevertheless have such witnesses.
No single-realized-label theorem follows from that average. This claim
concerns only a bounded s window around (3/2)log(1/e)/b_s, not other times.

## 2. Exact unaveraged risk derivative
Write c_h=(1/4)sum_i h(i)xi_i for h=0,s,t,st, N_h=2sqrt(rho_e)c_h,
and U_(e,h)=Z_(e,h)/alpha_e-theta_h/alpha_e in the Gaussian width limit.
The frozen residual in mode h divided by alpha_e is
 q_h U_(e,h)+(1-q_h)N_h, q_h=exp(-b_h t).
Thus, with eta_e=(b_t+b_st)/b_s, the derivative normalized by
2alpha_e^2(b_t+b_st) is exactly
 D_(e,xi)(s)=sum_h [b_h/(b_t+b_st)]
       {q_h N_h(N_h-U_(e,h))-q_h^2(U_(e,h)-N_h)^2},       (2)
at t=t_e(s)=((3/2)log(1/e)+s)/b_s.
C016/C017 give a joint Gaussian coupling, locally uniformly in s,
 e U_(e,s)->L_s=sqrt(2)nu G_s,
 U_(e,t)->L_t=sqrt(2)nu G_t-1, U_(e,st)->-1,
 b_t/(b_t+b_st), b_st/(b_t+b_st)->1/2, eta_e~e.
Let a=L_s^2 and B0=(L_t^2+1)/2; B0 is C017's B.
The constant-mode term is negligible faster than any power of e, even
with N_0=O(e^(-1/4)), because b_0 is bounded away from zero and
Z_(e,0)=O(1) in this coupling.

## 3. Exhausting the sixteen sign patterns
The four-dimensional Walsh transform of a sign vector has just two types.
If xi has an odd number of + signs (eight patterns), all four c_h are
+/-1/2. If xi has an even number, xi is one of the eight signed Walsh
characters, so exactly one c_h equals +/-1 and the others vanish.
Consequently there are ten patterns with c_s!=0, four with c_s=0 and
one of c_t,c_st nonzero, and two with only c_0 nonzero.
This finite classification is verified exactly in the accompanying script;
it also follows by direct enumeration of the sixteen vectors.

For c_s!=0, (2) gives the locally uniform limit
 e^(3/4) D_(e,xi)(s) -> -2sqrt(kappa)c_s L_s exp(-s).      (3)
Indeed q_s=e^(3/2)exp(-s), N_s=2sqrt(kappa)e^(-1/4)c_s,
U_s=e^(-1)(L_s+o(1)), and eta_e~e. The cross term
-q_s N_s U_s/eta_e has size e^(-3/4) and gives (3).
The terms q_s N_s^2/eta_e and q_s^2 U_s^2/eta_e are O(1);
all remaining fast terms are smaller. Slow-mode terms are O(e^(-1/4))
and disappear after multiplication by e^(3/4). These estimates are
uniform on each fixed compact s interval.

If c_s=0 and either c_t or c_st is nonzero, the corresponding limit is
 e^(1/4) D_(e,xi)(s) -> sqrt(kappa)(c_t L_t-c_st).         (4)
To check the slow terms without losing cancellations, rewrite their braces
in (2) as
 N_h U_h q_h(2q_h-1)-U_h^2 q_h^2+N_h^2 q_h(1-q_h).
Here q_h=1-O(e log(1/e)). After multiplication by e^(1/4), the
first term converges to 2sqrt(kappa)c_h times its U_h limit;
the second vanishes, and the third is O(e^(3/4)log(1/e)).
The weights tend to1/2. The fast contribution is only O(1) because N_s=0.
For these four patterns, exactly one of c_t,c_st is +/-1, so (4) is
nonzero unless L_t=0 in a t-pattern; that Gaussian event has probability0.

For the two constant patterns all nonconstant N_h vanish. Directly (2)
then gives, locally uniformly,
 D_(e,xi)(s) -> -a exp(-2s)-B0 <0.                       (5)
The constant-label term is again exponentially negligible.

Outside the null events L_s=0 and L_t=0, each of (3)-(5) has a strictly
nonzero, constant sign throughout any fixed compact interval. Uniform
convergence makes each frozen derivative have that sign for all sufficiently
small e. There are finitely many patterns, so this holds for all sixteen
simultaneously. Their integer-time frozen risks are therefore strictly
monotone throughout J_e(I). The Gaussian probability of this event tends
to one, by the coupling and bounded convergence.

## 4. Transfer of the LOCAL obstruction to actual nonlinear GD
For fixed e and finite integer horizon T, C018 Section3 proves joint weak
convergence of all actual risk values to their frozen Gaussian-width-limit
values. The proof works for each label pattern before averaging: prediction
transfer is uniform over the sixteen patterns, and squaring finitely many
prediction vectors is continuous. Choose T to include J_e(I).
The event that each of sixteen finite risk sequences is strictly monotone
in some direction is a finite union (over choices of direction) of finite
intersections of strict adjacent-value inequalities. It is therefore open
in this finite joint risk array. The open-set Portmanteau inequality gives
 liminf_m P(actual monotonicity event)>=P(frozen monotonicity event).
The right side tends to one as e decreases by Section3, proving (1).
Strict adjacent gaps need not have a uniform size in e: width is sent to
infinity at each fixed e first. No derivative of actual nonlinear GD is
introduced, and no uniform-width assertion is being made.

## 5. Consequence and exact scope
The dominant signed cross term in (3) disappears under noise averaging;
its sign is not controlled for a realized dataset. Slow signed cross terms
similarly survive in (4). C017/C018 obtain an averaged quadratic profile
only after these cancellations. Thus a high-probability peak in the mean
of sixteen trajectories is compatible with local monotonicity of every
constituent trajectory. Equation (1) is the exact obstruction to reusing
that proof as a single-dataset result. It does not rule out single-dataset
double descent in a DIFFERENT window or under another noise/initialization
scaling, nor for other input laws or feature-learning regimes.
Dependencies C009,C016,C017,C018 are unaudited. Independent mathematical
and novelty review remain pending. The finite check certifies only the
sign-pattern classification and exponent bookkeeping, not the CLT, limits,
nonlinear transfer or this full proof. No training experiment was performed.
Exact four-point stratified model in proofs/REALIZED_NOISE_CENTRAL_OBSTRUCTION.md
Fixed bounded s interval around b_s k=(3/2)log(1/e); width limit precedes small-e limit
Independent Gaussian hidden weights and iid signed fixed-nu heads; both layers trained; sigma_e=2alpha_e sqrt(kappa/sqrt(e))

[Corollary cor:half-normalized of arXiv:2607.13990, 'Effective Resistance in Fixed-Rank External-Field Measures\\ and Constant-Stretch Correlat'] For every fixed-rank external-field law with positive weights,
\begin{equation}
    \Sigma
\succeq
    \frac12\left(D-\frac{vv^\top}{V}\right).

\end{equation}
Equivalently, every nonzero eigenvalue of $D^{-1/2}\Sigma D^{-1/2}$ is at least $1/2$.
Since this matrix is a normalized graph Laplacian, its eigenvalues are also at most $2$, and hence
\begin{equation}
    \operatorname{spec}\left(D^{-1/2}\Sigma D^{-1/2}\right)
\subseteq
    \{0\}\cup[1/2,2].

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Half-normalized covariance bound

body:
[Theo 1 of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Assume that $0<\alpha<1$ and $m\in L^\infty(\Omega)$.

\begin{itemize}
\item[i)]
If $|\Omega^+|>0$, then, for every $\lambda<\lambda^*$, problem
\eqref{Eq1} possesses a non-negative weak solution
$u_\lambda^+\in H_0^1(\Omega)\cap C^{1,\gamma}(\overline{\Omega})$ for any
$\gamma\in(0,1)$, such that
\[
E_\lambda(u_\lambda^+)<0,
\qquad
E_\lambda''(u_\lambda^+)>0.
\]
Moreover, the minimum energy level $(-\infty,\lambda^*)\ni\lambda
\longmapsto E_\lambda(u_\lambda^+)$ is continuous and strictly decreasing, and
\[
E_\lambda(u_\lambda^+)\longrightarrow0
\qquad\text{as }\lambda\to-\infty.
\]
\item[ii)]
Suppose that
\[
\int_\Omega m(x)\varphi_{1,\Omega}^{\alpha+1}\,dx<0,
\qquad
|\Omega^+\cup\Omega^0|>0.
\]
Then
$0<\lambda_{1,\Omega}<\lambda^*<+\infty$.
For every $\lambda\in(\lambda_{1,\Omega},\lambda^*)$, problem
\eqref{Eq1} possesses a non-negative weak solution
$u_\lambda^-\in H_0^1(\Omega)\cap C^{1,\gamma}(\overline{\Omega})$ for any
$\gamma\in(0,1)$, such that
\[
E_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)>0,
\qquad
E_\lambda''(u_\lambda^-)<0.
\]
Moreover, the corresponding minimum energy level $(\lambda_{1,\Omega},\lambda^*)\ni\lambda
\longmapsto E_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)$ is continuous and strictly decreasing, and
\[
E_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)\longrightarrow+\infty
\qquad\text{as }\lambda\downarrow\lambda_{1,\Omega}.
\]
If, in addition, condition
\begin{equation}
\lambda_{1,\Omega^0}>
\lambda_{1,\Omega^0\cup\Omega^+}
\tag{M}

\end{equation}
holds, then
\[
E_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)\longrightarrow0
\qquad\text{as }\lambda\uparrow\lambda^*.
\]
\end{itemize}
In the degenerate case $m\leq0$ a.e. in $\Omega$, assume that
$\Omega^0=\operatorname{int}\{m=0\}$ is a nonempty connected Lipschitz
domain compactly contained in $\Omega$ and that
$m<0$ a.e. in $\Omega\setminus\overline{\Omega^0}$.
Then
\[
\lambda^*=\lambda_{1,\Omega^0},
\qquad
E_\lambda(u_\lambda^-)\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{as }\lambda\uparrow\lambda_{1,\Omega^0},
\]
without assuming condition {\rm (M)}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2609.02808, 'Minimizers of Laplace eigenvalues under a lower curvature bound'] Every $g\in\overline\Cc$, equipped with its area measure
$\mathfrak m=e^{2u}\dd$, is a compact $\mathrm{RCD}(1,2)$ metric measure
space. Consequently, it is also an $\mathrm{RCD}(1,\infty)$ space.
Moreover, $\diam(g)\le\pi$ and $\Area(g)\le4\pi$.

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.03634, 'Joint Laws of Maximum Drawdown and Maximum Drawup for Spectrally Negative L\'{e}vy Process'] Fix $a<0<b$. Under $\mathbb{P}_{a,b}^{>}$, the pre-$H_S$ process, the intermediate process, and the post-$H_I$ process are independent and their laws are as follows;
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The pre-supremum process is the Doob transform of the spectrally negative L\'{e}vy process killed when it reaches $b$ before the exponential time $T$, with excessive function
\[
h^*(x)=\frac{\gamma}{\Phi(\gamma)}W^{(\gamma)}(x-a)
\frac{\left(W^{(\gamma)\prime}(b-a)\right)^2-W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)W^{(\gamma)\prime\prime}(b-a)}
{\left(W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)\right)^2},
\qquad a<x<b.
\]

\item The intermediate process is the Doob transform of the post-supremum process killed at $\tau_a$, with excessive function
\[
h^{**}(x)=\frac{\left(Z^{(\gamma)}(b-a)-1\right)
\left[
W^{(\gamma)\prime}(x-a)W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)
-
W^{(\gamma)}(x-a)W^{(\gamma)\prime}(b-a)
\right]}
{\left(W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)\right)^2},
\qquad a<x<b.
\]

\item The post-infimum process is the Doob transform of the spectrally negative L\'{e}vy process issued from $a$ and killed at $T\wedge\tau_b^+\wedge\tau_a^-$, with excessive function
\[
h^{***}(x)=1-Z^{(\gamma)}(x-a)
+\left(Z^{(\gamma)}(b-a)-1\right)
\frac{W^{(\gamma)}(x-a)}{W^{(\gamma)}(b-a)},
\qquad a<x<b.
\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Proposition prop:U-expression of arXiv:2608.18320, 'Asymptotics for Beta-Splitting Trees via Homogeneous Fragmentations and Meromorphic Potent'] Let $\xi$ be an unkilled meromorphic subordinator with Laplace exponent
    $\phi$ and finite mean $\mu=\phi'(0)$. Let $(-\rho_k)$ and
    $(s_k)$ denote its nonzero poles and zeros, respectively, and put $s_0=0$.
    The sequences may be finite or infinite and are indexed so that
    \[
            0>-\rho_1>s_1>-\rho_2>s_2>\cdots.
    \]
    The displayed inequalities are truncated if either sequence terminates.
    Then, for $\operatorname{Re} z>0$,
    \begin{equation}
            \frac1{\phi(z)}
            =
            \eta+
            \sum_{k\ge0}
            \frac1{\phi'(s_k)(z-s_k)},
            \qquad
            \text{where }
            \eta:=\lim_{z\to+\infty}\frac1{\phi(z)},
    \end{equation}
    and the potential measure of $\xi$ is
    \begin{equation}
            U(\mathrm{d} x)
            =
            \eta\delta_0(\mathrm{d} x)
            +
            \left[
            \sum_{k\ge0}
            \frac{e^{s_kx}}{\phi'(s_k)}
            \right]\mathrm{d} x.
    \end{equation}
    Moreover, the residues $1/\phi'(s_k)$ are positive and the series converge
    locally uniformly in their respective domains. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Potential measure of a meromorphic subordinator

[Definition def:ising-rpc of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Consider a tree with $L$ levels, rooted at $\varnothing$, in which every vertex before the last level has
		countably many children. We label the children of each vertex by $\mathbb{N}$, so a vertex at level $\ell$ is a sequence
		$(n_1,\ldots,n_\ell)\in\mathbb{N}^\ell$.
		
		For every $1\le\ell\le L$, attach to each vertex at level $\ell-1$ an independent Poisson point process on $\mathbb{R}$
		with intensity
		\[
		\theta_\ell e^{-\theta_\ell u}\,\mathrm{d} u.
		\]
		Order its points decreasingly and assign them in this order to the edges leading to its children. All these point
		processes are independent.
		
		For a leaf $\alpha=(n_1,\ldots,n_L)$, set $\alpha|0=\varnothing$ and
		$\alpha|\ell=(n_1,\ldots,n_\ell)$. Let $u_{\alpha|\ell}$ denote the label of the edge from
		$\alpha|_{\ell-1}$ to $\alpha|\ell$, and define
		\[
		u_\alpha:=\sum_{\ell=1}^L u_{\alpha|\ell}.
		\]
		For two leaves $\alpha^1$ and $\alpha^2$, let $\alpha^1\wedge\alpha^2$ be the largest
		$\ell\in\{0,\ldots,L\}$ for which $\alpha^1|\ell=\alpha^2|\ell$, and set
		\[
		s_{\alpha^1\wedge\alpha^2}:=q_{\alpha^1\wedge\alpha^2}.
		\]

[Theorem 5 (Exact dynamic-kernel mismatch identity) of arXiv:2608.30261, 'Estimating Population-Risk Curves Along Nonconvex Gradient Flows from the Training Sample'] Fix $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $x\in\mathcal X$.  Suppose
$F_{P^\eps,\lambda}$ is twice continuously
differentiable near every point
$\theta_s^{P,\lambda}+u\Delta_s^\lambda$ and
$f_\theta(x)$ is continuously differentiable near every point in
$\{\theta_t^{P,\lambda}+u\Delta_t^\lambda,
    \theta_t^{P,\lambda}+ud_t^\lambda\}$,
for $s,t\in[0,T]$ and $u\in[0,1]$.
Suppose, for $|h|$-almost every $z$ and every $s\in[0,T]$, that
$\theta\mapsto f_\theta(x_z)$ is differentiable at
$\theta_s^{P,\lambda}$ and $\varphi(\cdot,y_z)$ is differentiable at
$f_{\theta_s^{P,\lambda}}(x_z)$.
For $0\leq s\leq t\leq T$ and $|h|$-almost every $z\in\mathsf Z$, define the
chord and resummed dynamic-kernel operators
$\mathcal K^{\rm ch,\lambda}(t,s;x,z),
\mathcal K^{\rm res,\lambda}(t,s;x,z):
\R^k\to\R^k$ by
\begin{align}
 \mathcal K^{\rm ch,\lambda}(t,s;x,z)
 &=\overline J_t^{\Delta,\lambda}(x)
   \overline U^\lambda(t,s)J_s^\lambda(x_z)^*,
 \\
 \mathcal K^{\rm res,\lambda}(t,s;x,z)
 &=\overline J_t^{d,\lambda}(x)
   U^{0,\lambda}(t,s)J_s^\lambda(x_z)^*.
 
\end{align}
Then
\begin{align}
 f_{\theta_t^{P^\eps,\lambda}}(x)-f_{\theta_t^{P,\lambda}}(x)
 &=-\eps\int_0^t\int
   \mathcal K^{\rm ch,\lambda}(t,s;x,z)a_s^\lambda(z)
   \,\dd h(z)\,\dd s,
 \\
 f_{\theta_t^{P,\lambda}+d_t^\lambda}(x)
  -f_{\theta_t^{P,\lambda}}(x)
 &=-\eps\int_0^t\int
   \mathcal K^{\rm res,\lambda}(t,s;x,z)a_s^\lambda(z)
   \,\dd h(z)\,\dd s.
 \\
 f_{\theta_t^{P^\eps,\lambda}}(x)
  -f_{\theta_t^{P,\lambda}+d_t^\lambda}(x)
 &=-\eps\int_0^t\int
   \{\mathcal K^{\rm ch,\lambda}
      -\mathcal K^{\rm res,\lambda}\}(t,s;x,z)
   a_s^\lambda(z)\,\dd h(z)\,\dd s.
 
\end{align}
for every $t\in[0,T]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact dynamic-kernel mismatch identity

Let f_theta(x)=v1 ReLU(w1.x)+v2 ReLU(w2.x), with w1,w2 in R^2, train both layers without biases, on x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), with both labels +1, using exponential or logistic loss and gradient flow. If w1.x1>0 and w1.x2>0, w2.x1<0 and w2.x2<0, and v1>0 initially (v2 arbitrary), the loss tends to zero and the parameter direction converges to the direction represented by w1=(0,2), v1=2, w2=0, v2=0. This is a KKT point of minimizing squared Euclidean parameter norm subject to both training margins being at least one, but it is not a local optimum of that constrained problem. The first neuron is initially active on both points and the second on neither. This is a sufficient initialization basin; no claim is made that these inequalities characterize all bad initializations.
Exactly two hidden ReLU neurons, input dimension two, no biases, both hidden and output weights train
Training points (1,1/4) and (-1,1/4), both with label +1
Exponential or logistic loss, continuous gradient flow
First hidden weight has strictly positive inner product with both points; second strictly negative with both
First output weight initially strictly positive; second output weight arbitrary

[Theorem thm:jackson of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Fix any $D\ge 1$. 
For any $f\in C^k([0,2\pi])$ such that $f^{(l)}(0) = f^{(l)}(2\pi)$ for all $l\le k$ and $\norm{f^{(k)}}_\infty \le M$, there exists a trigonometric polynomial $T_D$ of degree $D$ on $[0,2\pi]$ such that 
\begin{align}
\norm{T_D - f}_{\infty} &\le   C_k  D^{-k} M , 
\end{align}  
where $\sup_k C_k < \infty$.
Moreover, we have that $\sum_{1\le m \le D} |a_m| +|b_m| \le 2^{k+2}M/\pi \, \sum_{1\le m \le D} m^{-k}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2608.31164, 'The anisotropic Michael-Simon inequality'] Let $F: \bR^N \to [0,\infty)$ be a strictly convex norm that is $C^1$ away from the origin and let $\Gamma \subset \bG(N,N-1)$.
    Suppose that there are hyperplanes $\{ P_{\alpha} \}_{\alpha=1}^J \in \bG(N,N-1)$ with orthogonal projections $\pi_{\alpha} : \bR^N \to P_{\alpha}$ such that, for every $\nu \in \bS^{N-1}$ with $\nu^{\perp} \in \Gamma$, there is some $\alpha$ for which $F(\pi_{\alpha} \nu) < F(\nu)$.
Then, the Michael-Simon inequality with respect to $F$ holds for every rectifiable codimension-$1$ varifold whose tangent planes almost everywhere are contained in $\Gamma$.

In particular, the Michael-Simon inequality holds for codimension-$1$ varifolds whenever the anisotropy $F$ is invariant under reflections $\{ R_{\alpha} \}_{\alpha=1}^J$ across hyperplanes $\{ P_{\alpha}\}_{\alpha=1}^J$ with $\bigcap_{\alpha=1}^J P_{\alpha} = \{  0\}$.

[Proposition prop:LT of arXiv:2510.10299, '\Large Sparse graphs and their Benjamini-Schramm limits: a spectral tour'] Let $S$ be a finite symmetric generating set of $\Gamma$ such that $\mathrm{e} \in S$. The  following statements are equivalent: 
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item $\lim_{n} \| \rho_n(a) \| = \| \lambda(a) \|$ for all $a \in  \mathbb{C}[\Gamma]$.
\item $\lim_{n} \| \rho_n(a) \| = \| \lambda(a) \|$ for all  $k \geq 1$ and $a \in M_k(\mathbb{C})[\Gamma]$.
\item  $\lim_{n} \| \rho_n(a) \| = \| \lambda(a) \|$ for all $k \geq 1$ and $a \in M_k(\mathbb{C})[\Gamma]$ with support in $S$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:consistencyLimitLawsGraphs of arXiv:2609.03094, 'Discrete Gromov--Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing'] Fix $\lambda\in(0,1)$, $N\neq 4$,  $\mu_{i,n} = (1-\lambda)\hat \mu_{i,n}+\lambda \mathcal U$ for $i\in\{0,1\}$,  
       $\hat \Sigma_n = \Sigma_{w_{\hat \mu_{0,n}}}$, and $\hat u_n=u_{\mu_{0,n}}$ (defined by analogy with $u_{\tilde \mu_0}$ in (assn:generalSettingLimitLaw of the paper)). Then, 
         $\hat \Sigma_n\to \Sigma_{w_{\mu_0}}$ and $\hat u_n\to u_{\tilde \mu_0}$ conditionally on the data given almost every realization of $G_{0,1},G_{0,2},\dots,$ and, if $\mathsf{GW}_p(\tilde \mu_0,\tilde \mu_1)=0$,  the conservative testing procedure from (sec:consistencyConservativeQuantiles of the paper) yields a test for graph distribution isomorphism of any given asymptotic level upon scaling $\hat L_n$ by $(1-\lambda)$. If $\mathsf{GW}_p(\tilde \mu_0,\tilde \mu_1)>0$, the probability that the test rejects the null hypothesis converges to $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Consistent Isomorphism Testing

body: [Definition of arXiv:2609.03755, 'The Scramble Number of Outerplanar Graphs'] A \emph{separator} is a set of vertices such that the removal of the vertices disconnects the graph into at least $2$ distinct non-empty components. body:
[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] Let $(M_j)_{j\geq1}$ be independent and identically distributed positive
  random variables with $\Ee\log M_1<0$, and assume $\log(M_1+\eps)$ has
  exponential moments in a neighborhood of the origin for each fixed
  $\eps>0$. For every $b<\infty$, there exist $K_\ast<\infty$ and
  $c_1,c_2,c_3>0$, depending only on $b$ and the law of $M_1$, such that the
  affine recursion
  \begin{equation*}
    U_{t+1}=M_{t+1}U_t+b,
    \qquad
    U_0=K,
  \end{equation*}
  satisfies, uniformly for $K\geq2$,
  \begin{equation}
    \Pp\left(\inf\{t:U_t\leq K_\ast\}>c_1\log K+r\right)

body:
[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2608.27156, 'Traveling Waves in Equity Markets with\\Rank-Based Entry and Exit'] For each $t \in [0,T]$ let $\xi_t$ be the finite measure on $\R$ with scaled CDF $H(t,y) = m_t\, V(t,y)$, where $m$ is continuous and positive and $V$ is jointly continuous, nondecreasing in $y$, with $V(t, -\infty) = 0$ and $V(t, +\infty) = 1$ for every $t$. Let $(\xi^n_t)_{t \leq T}$ be paths of finite measures with scaled CDFs $H_n(t,y) = \xi^n_t((-\infty, y])$ and masses $m^n_t = \xi^n_t(\R)$. If
\begin{equation*}
    \sup_{t \leq T} \big| \langle \xi^n_t, \varphi \rangle - \langle \xi_t, \varphi \rangle \big| \;\longrightarrow\; 0
    \quad \text{for every } \varphi \in C_c(\R),
    \qquad \text{and} \qquad
    \sup_{t \leq T} \big| m^n_t - m_t \big| \;\longrightarrow\; 0,
\end{equation*}
then $\sup_{t \leq T} \sup_{y \in \R} \big| H_n(t,y) - H(t,y) \big| \to 0$.

this is a dated literature claim by the authors of arXiv:2604.01214, not a theorem
it describes the position immediately BEFORE their own rotationally invariant result
'exactly solvable planar models in last passage percolation' is where Theta(n^{2/3}) is known - not in first-passage percolation

WHY THIS IS FILED AS ITS OWN NODE: it is the single most load-bearing world-model sentence for the chi = 1/3 campaign, it is dated, and it is written by the people with the most reason to know. It settles two questions the campaign keeps re-asking - whether anyone has beaten n/log n on the lattice (no) and whether Theta(n^{2/3}) is known anywhere in FPP (no; it is known in exactly solvable LPP).
WHAT IS QUOTED AND WHAT IS INFERRED: the sentence in the statement above is quoted verbatim and describes the position BEFORE the authors' own theorem. The further clause 'after it, the lattice bound is still n/log n' is lane P4's INFERENCE from the scope of their theorem - it is proved for rotationally invariant Riemannian FPP on the plane, and Z^d has no rotational invariance - not a sentence the authors wrote. The inference is corroborated separately by the arXiv sweeps of 2026-04-01 to 2026-08-22 recorded in this lane's recon note, which found no lattice variance result at all.
THE SAME ABSTRACT INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATES TWO HYPOTHESIS SETS in this layer: it attributes the O(n) variance bound to 'Kesten's O(n) upper bound (Ann. Appl. Probab., 1993)', and it attributes the log improvement to Benjamini, Kalai and Schramm 'when passage times take two values with equal probability' - the two-point hypothesis that gets dropped in casual quotation.
SOURCE: abstract of arXiv:2604.01214v1, retrieved from the official arXiv API by lane P4 on 2026-08-22. Quoted verbatim above.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source, in the sense that the quoted sentence was read in the authors' own text. It is a literature claim; it is not itself proved anywhere.

Before their own theorem nothing beat the BKS log factor in any non-trivial FPP variant; after it, the LATTICE bound is still n/log n.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2506.14859, 'A note on Polya urns: the winner may lead all the time'] Consider a \Polya{} urn with balls of two colours, black and white, 
with the replacement rule that if a ball of colour $i\in\set{\xb,\xw}$ is
drawn, it is replaced together with $m_i$ 
additional balls of the same colour, for some given positive integers
$m_\xb,m_\xw$. 
Let $B_n$ and $W_n$ be the numbers of black and white balls after $n$ draws,
with initial conditions $B_0=b_0$ and $W_0=w_0$ for some given $b_0,w_0$.
Suppose that $m_\xb\ge m_\xw$ and that $b_0>w_0\ge0$.
Then there is a positive probability that $B_n>W_n$ for all $n\ge0$.

[Theorem 4 (well-posedness of the sticky CIR
process) of arXiv:2605.13648, 'Sticky CIR process with potential: invariant measure and exact sampling'] The sticky CIR process defined by \cref{eq-CIR4} has a unique
weak solution \(u_t\) for \(\delta\in(1,2)\) and  \(\mu> 0\). The solution \(u_t\) is a regular
diffusion process with a Feller transition semigroup
$P_t\varphi(x)\coloneqq\mathbb{E}[\varphi(u_t)\mid u_0=x]$: it is a strongly continuous
contraction semigroup on $C_0([0,\infty))$, the continuous functions on $[0,\infty)$
vanishing at infinity, and $x\mapsto P_t\varphi(x)$ is continuous for every bounded
continuous $\varphi$.

Claudio Altafini, Multistability of Self-Attention Dynamics in Transformers, arXiv:2511.11553 (2025), studies finite self-inclusive spherical attention dot x_i=(I-x_i x_i^T) V sum_j a_ij(X) x_j, where a_ij=exp(x_i^T Q^T K x_j)/sum_l exp(x_i^T Q^T K x_l). Clustering directions need not be value-matrix eigenvectors. Section 5 Remark 6, PDF p22, explicitly reports that analytical stability of the clustering equilibria was not verified in that paper; Section 6 Example 1 and Figure 1(d) give a numerical three-clustering attractor. This is a source-scope statement, not a theorem that every clustering configuration is stable or a claim about all later literature.

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2607.11283, 'Markov Properties of $k$-Record Processes via Order Statistics'] The process $(U_n)_{n\ge k}$ is a time-homogeneous Markov chain 

with respect to its natural filtration
$\mathcal{G}_n=\sigma(U_k,\dots,U_n)$, $n\ge k$.
Its transition kernel $Q_k$ is given by
\begin{equation}

Q_k(x,A)
=
F(x)\,\delta_x(A)
+
\int_{A\cap(x,\infty)}
k\frac{(1-F(y))^{k-1}}{(1-F(x))^{k-1}}\,dF(y),
\qquad A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}),
\end{equation}
for every $x$ such that $F(x)<1$, where $\delta_x$ denotes the Dirac measure at $x$.

body:
[Corollary 7 (Assembly through retained states and fixed interfaces) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] Consider finitely many ReLU modules whose parameter slots are affine functions
of one common code vector.  Form a computation by repeatedly applying the
following operations: run modules in parallel; retain a terminal hidden state
instead of applying its scalar affine readout; route or split retained states
through fixed affine/ReLU layers; merge consecutive affine maps when at least
one is fixed; and align depths by fixed signed transport.  Then the resulting
computation is realized by one fully connected scalar-output ReLU architecture,
and every slot of that architecture is affine in the same code vector.

If a hidden layer of the resulting architecture is enlarged by adding channels
that are identically zero, the enlarged architecture realizes the same
function.  More precisely, if the original pair is $(\Psi,\calA)$ with
$\calA\in\aff(M,P_\Psi)$ and the enlarged architecture is
$\Psi^{\mathrm{pad}}$, inserting fixed zeros into the new slots defines
\[
 \calA^{\mathrm{pad}}
 \in\aff(M,P_{\Psi^{\mathrm{pad}}})
\]
such that
$\Psi^{\mathrm{pad}}_{\calA^{\mathrm{pad}}(\bmxi)}
=\Psi_{\calA(\bmxi)}$ for every $\bmxi\in\R^M$.

[Theorem AC eqivalence on Cantor is not classifiable of arXiv:2608.30346, '\textbf{Classification complexity of homeomorphism group actions}'] Let \(N\) be the set of non-atomic,  locally positive, probability Borel measures on the Cantor space. Then we have
    \[\equiv|_{N} \leq_B E^H_{\AC(2^\mathbb{N})}.\]
    Thus, \(E^H_{\AC(2^\mathbb{N})}\) is not classifiable by countable structures.

[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2609.03187, 'Duality for a Martingale Transport Problem with Moment Constraints'] Let $\lambda^*$ be a dual optimizer for \eqref{eq:strong-dual}, and choose the corresponding optimal coupling in the form: 
\[
\pi^*(dx,dy)=\mu(dx)\,(T_{\lambda^*}(a_{\lambda^*}(x)+\cdot))_\#\gamma(dy).
\]
Then, for $\mu$-a.e. $x\in\mathbb R$, the conditional measure $\pi^{*,x}$ has the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}[label={\rm(\arabic*)}]
    \item atoms may occur only at the strike prices $K_1, \ldots, K_N$;
    \item away from the strike prices, it is obtained from $\gamma$ by a piecewise-shift transformation.
\end{enumerate}

body: [Lem sing of arXiv:2411.06571, 'Moment-based approach for two erratic KPZ scaling limits'] Let $\Phi_\epsilon := \varphi_\epsilon * \varphi_\epsilon$, with $\varphi_\epsilon$ as in Theorem (mr3 of the paper). Then for $\psi:\Bbb R\to \Bbb R$ bounded and continuous, and $x_1,...,x_n\in\Bbb R$, we have that$$\int_{\Bbb R^n} \Bbb E\bigg[ \prod_{j=1}^n \mathcal Z_{0,t}^\epsilon (x_j, y_j) \bigg]\prod_{j=1}^n \psi(y_j) dy\cdots dy_n = \mathbf E^{(x_1,...,x_n)}_{\mathrm{Sing}(\epsilon)} [ e^{  \sum_{1\le i<j\le k}\int_0^t \Phi_\epsilon (X^i_s-X^j_s)ds}\prod_{j=1}^n \psi(X^j_s)].$$Here the expectation on the right side is with respect to a diffusion process on $\Bbb R^n$ whose generator is $$L^{(n,\epsilon)}_{\mathrm{Sing}}f(y_1,...,y_n):= L^{(n,\epsilon)}_{\mathrm{Cen}}f(y_1,...,y_n) + \sum_{i\ne j} \epsilon^{1/2} \Phi_\epsilon(y_i-y_j) (\partial_i f)(y_1,...,y_n). $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.29855, 'Growth of Simple Closed Geodesics in closed Hyperbolic $3$-Manifolds'] If $A_g$ projects to a nonsimple geodesic in $M$, then there are
$$
i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\},
\qquad
0\le k\le n/2,
\qquad
\sigma\in\Sigma,
$$
and a decomposition
$$
\omega^{(i)}=BC,
\qquad
|B|=k,
\qquad
|C|=n-k,
$$
such that, with $b=[B]$ and $c=[C]$,
$$
A_{bc}\cap(\sigma b^{-1})A_{bc}\ne\varnothing
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sigma b^{-1}\notin\Stab_\Gamma(A_{bc}).
$$
Consequently, only $O(n^2)$ triples $(i,k,\sigma)$ need be considered,
with the implied constant depending on $S$.

[Lemma 11 (Collapse to the quotient circle) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(\pi:(M,h)\to(S^1,h_{S^1})\) be the metric quotient of an invariant
torus-bundle metric, and suppose
\[
        \sup_{y\in S^1}\diam_h\bigl(\pi^{-1}(y)\bigr)\leq\delta,
\]
where the fiber diameters are ambient diameters in \((M,h)\).  Then, for all
\(x,x'\in M\),
\begin{equation}
 0\leq d_h(x,x')-
 d_{h_{S^1}}\bigl(\pi(x),\pi(x')\bigr)\leq2\delta.
\end{equation}
Consequently, \(\pi\) has distortion at most \(2\delta\) and
\[
        d_{\mathrm{GH}}\bigl((M,h),(S^1,h_{S^1})\bigr)\leq\delta.
\]

[Theorem thm:DP2-proof of arXiv:2604.25108, 'Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality\\in the Double Dixie Cup '] For every $m\ge1$, $N\ge2$, and every positive probability vector $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_N)$,
\[
        \operatorname{Var}_p(T_m(N))\ge \operatorname{Var}_u(T_m(N)),
        \qquad
        u=(1/N,\ldots,1/N),
\]
with equality iff $p=u$.

[Definition 29 of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] For
\(I\in\mathcal D_\ell([0,1])\),
\(M_I=\widetilde\nu_\ell(I)\),
define
\[
    C_{I,n}
    =
    \begin{cases}
    \displaystyle
    L_n\frac{2T_{\ell+1,n}}{M_I},
    & M_I>0,\\[6pt]
    +\infty,
    & M_I=0.
    \end{cases}
\]
For a child \(J\subset I\), set
\(
    U_{J,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}=U_J\wedge C_{I,n},
\)
and define
\(
    \overline U_{I,n}
    =
    \mathbb E\left[
        U_{J,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}
        \mid
        \mathcal F_\ell
    \right].
\)
The quantity \(\overline U_{I,n}\) is independent of the choice of child
\(J\subset I\).  Define
\[
    X_{J,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}(\xi,d,\ell)
    =
    c_J(\xi,d,\ell)M_I
    \left(
        U_{J,n}^{\mathrm{cap}}
        -
        \overline U_{I,n}
    \right).
\]

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2606.11845, 'Stochastic epidemic model with varying infectivity and waning immunity: the law of large n'] The system of integral equations \eqref{eq:limit2} has a unique solution which belongs to $\mathbf{D}^2$, and 
for all $t\ge0$, $0\le x(t)\le 1$ and $0\le y(t)\le \overline{\lambda}^{\ast}_0 \exp(\overline{\lambda}^\ast t)$. Moreover, the solution of this system is continuous whenever $\overline{\lambda}_0(t)$ is continuous, and $\gamma_0(t)$ is continuous in probability.\footnote{In the statement of Theorem 3.1 of \cite{FPPZ}, the stated condition ``$\gamma_0$ has bounded variation and the map $t\mapsto(\E[\gamma_0(t)],\overline{\lambda}_0(t))$ is continuous'' does not imply the continuity. The last inequality in the proof of that theorem is wrong, and counterexamples are easy to find.}

body: For a subgroup H of G and g in G, the left coset gH = {gh : h in H} and right coset Hg = {hg : h in H}. The left cosets partition G into disjoint blocks each of size |H| (the map h -> gh is a bijection), so |G| = [G:H] |H| when finite - this is the counting behind Lagrange's theorem. H is normal exactly when left and right cosets coincide, which is what lets the cosets form the quotient group G/H.

[Mytheo 1 of arXiv:2607.00495, 'Rank deficiency of Bernoulli random matrices for growing corank'] For every $p \in (0,1/2]$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, there are $n_{\ref{Theorem A}}$ and $c_{\ref{Theorem A}} >0$ depending only on $p$ and $\varepsilon$ with the following property. Let $n \ge n_{\ref{Theorem A}}$, $1 \le k \le c_{\ref{Theorem A}}\sqrt{\log{n}}$, and let $B_{n}(p)$ be $n \times n$ random matrix with independent entries $b_{ij}$ such that $\mathbb{P}(b_{ij}=0)=1-p$ and $\mathbb{P}(b_{ij}=1)=p$. Then we have 
   \begin{align*}
       \mathbb{P}\left(  \mathrm{rank}\left(B_{n}(p) \right) \le n-k   \right) \le \left( 1-p+\varepsilon \right)^{kn}.
   \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

  \qquad \tau\longmapsto P^\tau ,
\]
is continuous and linear.  More precisely,
\begin{equation}
 \|P^\tau\|_{\mathcal V_p(I;\mathcal E_{\mathrm{jet}})}
 +\|R^{P^\tau}\|_{q\text{-var};I;\mathcal E_{\mathrm{jet}}}
 \le C_I\|\tau\|_{\mathbb T_{\mathbf x}^p}.                        
\end{equation}
Every finite-norm joint-lift representative of \(\tau\) yields the same
path \(P^\tau\).  On a bounded tangent set, \(C_I\) can be chosen uniformly
over \(I\in\Pi(\mathbf x)\) and over representatives with the prescribed
quantitative realization budget. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theo 1 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (sharpened Malliavin-Stein bounds for Poisson functionals)
    Let $(\X,\nu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space and $(\MM,\QQ)$ a space of marks with probability measure $\QQ$. Let $\hat{\mathcal{P}}$ be a Poisson measure on $\X \times \MM$ of intensity $\nu \otimes \QQ$. Let $F$ be a measurable function of $\hat{\mathcal{P}}$ such that $\E F^2 < \infty$ and $\E F = 0$ and
    \[
    \int_{\X \times \MM} \E \left[\left( D_{(x,m_x)} F \right)^2\right] (\nu \otimes \QQ)(dx,dm_x) < \infty.
    \]
    For any point $x\in \X$, define a random variable $M_x$ independent of everything else, distributed according to $\QQ$.
    Then it holds that
    \[
    \mathbf{d}_W(F,N) \leq \sqrt{\tfrac{2}{\pi}}\hat{\gamma}_0+ \sqrt{\tfrac{2}{\pi}}\hat{\gamma}_1 + \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\hat{\gamma}_2 + \hat{\gamma}_3
    \]
    and
    \[
    \mathbf{d}_K(F,N) \leq \hat{\gamma}_0 + \hat{\gamma}_1 + \tfrac{1}{2} \hat{\gamma}_2 + \hat{\gamma}_4 + \hat{\gamma}_5 + \hat{\gamma}_6,
    \]
    where
    \begin{align*}
        \hat{\gamma}_0 &:= \E \left| 1- \Var(F) \right|\\
        \hat{\gamma}_1 &:= 2 \bigg(\int_\X \bigg(\int_\X \E \big[ |D_{(y,M_y)}F|^4\big]^{1/4} \cdot \E \big[|\DD_{(x,M_x),(y,M_y)}F|^4\big]^{1/4} \nu(dy) \bigg)^2 \nu(dx) \bigg)^{1/2}\\
        \hat{\gamma}_2 &:= 2  \bigg(\int_\X \bigg(\int_\X \E \big[|\DD_{(x,M_x),(y,M_y)}F|^4\big]^{1/2} \nu(dy) \bigg)^2 \nu(dx) \bigg)^{1/2}\\
        \hat{\gamma}_3 &:= 2 \int_\X \E|D_{(y,M_y)}F|^3 \nu(dy)
    \end{align*}
    and
    \begin{align*}
        \hat{\gamma}_4 &:= \bigg(4\int_\X \E|D_{(y,M_y)}F|^4 \nu(dy)\bigg)^{1/2}\\
        \hat{\gamma}_5 &:= \bigg(8\int_\X\int_\X \E|\DD_{(x,M_x),(y,M_y)}F|^4 \nu(dy)\nu(dx)\bigg)^{1/2}\\
        \hat{\gamma}_6 &:= \bigg(32\int_\X\int_\X \E\big[|\DD_{(x,M_x),(y,M_y)}F|^4\big]^{1/2} \cdot \E\big[|D_{(x,M_x)}F|^4\big]^{1/2} \nu(dy)\nu(dx)\bigg)^{1/2}.
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theo 1 of arXiv:2605.23292

Let f ∈ C^1(R;R^n) and u0 ∈ L^∞(R^n). A function u ∈ L^∞(R^n × (0,∞)) is a Kruzhkov entropy solution of u_t + div f(u) = 0, u(·,0) = u0, if for every k ∈ R and every φ ∈ C_c^∞(R^n × [0,∞)) with φ ≥ 0: ∫_0^∞ ∫_{R^n} ( |u - k| φ_t + sgn(u-k) ( f(u) - f(k) )·∇_x φ ) dx dt + ∫_{R^n} |u0(x) - k| φ(x,0) dx ≥ 0. Equivalently (for C^1 flux), η(u)_t + div q(u) ≤ 0 in the sense of distributions, with the initial datum taken in L^1_loc, for every convex entropy η ∈ C^1(R) with entropy flux q determined by q' = η' f'; the Kruzhkov family η_k(u) = |u-k| generates all convex entropies. Every entropy solution is a weak solution (take k larger than ||u||_∞ and k smaller than -||u||_∞ and combine the two resulting inequalities). The inequality has a sign: it expresses dissipation, and it is exactly the condition selected by the vanishing-viscosity limit u^ε_t + div f(u^ε) = ε Δ u^ε.
f ∈ C^1 (Lipschitz flux suffices for the theory)
u ∈ L^∞; the test functions must be NONNEGATIVE, otherwise the inequality would force equality and lose all selection power
sgn is the usual signum, so the pair (|u-k|, sgn(u-k)(f(u)-f(k))) is the Kruzhkov entropy/entropy-flux pair
title: Kruzhkov Entropy Solution

	$$
		\mathcal{C}(\tilde{\sK})_\times := \{ f \colon {\tilde{\sK}}\to \{0,1\}: f(\tilde{\sK}^{\times}) = \{0\} \}.
	$$
	Then $\Gammas \simeq \mathcal{C}(\tilde{\sK})_\times$.
